name: csv-to-xlsx
description: Convert a CSV/JSON table into a real Excel .xlsx workbook (typed columns, optional sheet name).
example_prompt: turn this CSV into an Excel file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (rust_xlsxwriter) emitting a .xlsx blob. — via rust_xlsxwriter crate
rationale: Reverse of the existing xlsx-to-csv and a constant office need.

name: pdf-table-extractor
description: Detects tabular layouts in a text-based PDF and extracts them as CSV using positional clustering.
example_prompt: Extract the tables from this PDF report into CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM PDF text/position extraction plus row/column clustering heuristics; fully offline. — via lopdf crate
rationale: Getting tables out of PDFs is one of the most-requested and least-served data chores.

name: text-redactor
description: Masks emails, phone numbers, credit-card-like numbers, and IPs in text with configurable redaction placeholders.
example_prompt: Redact the emails and phone numbers in this support transcript
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: PII regex set with masking, fully offline so data never leaves the browser — via regex crate
rationale: Sharing logs and transcripts safely requires masking PII, and doing it locally guarantees nothing is uploaded.

name: pii-tokenize
description: Replaces detected PII with deterministic, format-preserving pseudonyms so the text stays linkable but de-identified.
example_prompt: tokenize the names and emails in this log so they're consistent but anonymized
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using keyed HMAC-derived tokens — deterministic pseudonymization computed locally.
rationale: Mirrors Databunker's tokenization vault, letting analysts keep referential integrity without ever exposing real identities.

name: sql-query
description: Run a SQL query over a CSV or pasted table and return results.
example_prompt: SELECT region, SUM(sales) FROM data GROUP BY region — over this CSV: <csv>
loader_feasibility: pyodide bundles a WASM sqlite3; load the CSV into an in-memory DB and query, all client-side. — via gluesql crate
rationale: SQL over ad-hoc data is a powerful analysis interface that needs no backend with sqlite-in-WASM.

name: csv-pii-redactor
description: Masks or salted-hashes emails, phone numbers, and ID-like values in chosen columns for safe sharing.
example_prompt: Redact the email and SSN columns in this CSV before I send it externally
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM regex detection + masking/SHA hashing; runs locally so PII never leaves the browser.
rationale: Local-only redaction lets people share datasets without ever uploading sensitive fields anywhere.

name: qif-ofx-convert
description: Converts QIF/OFX bank exports into clean normalized CSV ready for import into budgeting apps.
example_prompt: Convert this OFX file from my bank into a CSV I can import
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM format parsing/serialization; pure text transform, offline.
rationale: GnuCash/Firefly III imports constantly break on legacy QIF/OFX, and a local converter unblocks setup without uploading bank data.

name: fuzzy-doc-search
description: Full-text fuzzy search across one or more uploaded txt/markdown/PDF documents, returning ranked matching snippets with context.
example_prompt: Search these 3 PDFs for anything about 'retention policy' and show me the surrounding lines.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: in-memory tokenization, fuzzy scoring, and pure-Rust PDF text extraction all run in the wasmi sandbox with no network. — via pdf-extract crate
rationale: docfd-style cross-document fuzzy search is exactly the kind of private, local-only search users won't paste into a server.

name: files-to-prompt
description: Bundles multiple uploaded files into one LLM-ready digest with a directory tree, fenced contents, and a token estimate.
example_prompt: Pack these source files into a single prompt-ready block
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: builds the tree and concatenates file contents from the browser file picker in-memory.
rationale: Turning a directory dump (dir2txt) into a single pasteable, token-counted context block is a hugely common LLM prep step.

name: log-parser
description: Auto-detects and parses raw log files (JSON, logfmt, syslog, common/combined access) into a structured, filterable table.
example_prompt: Parse this nginx access log and show me all 5xx requests sorted by response time
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pure text tokenizing/regex with no network or backend; the whole file stays in the browser.
rationale: Observability platforms like OpenObserve exist because people drown in unstructured logs; structuring them locally is the first useful step.

name: document-scan
description: Detect a document's edges in a photo and apply perspective correction to produce a flat, cropped scan.
example_prompt: straighten and crop this photo of a receipt into a clean scan
loader_feasibility: ONNX/Rust corner detection plus a WebGPU perspective warp — all client-side. — via imageproc crate
rationale: CamScanner-style flattening is a top mobile use, and deskew only fixes rotation, not perspective.

name: image-to-webp
description: Converts PNG, JPG, or BMP images to WebP with adjustable quality.
example_prompt: convert this PNG to WebP
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (wasm) with libwebp encodes WebP entirely client-side via the wasmi bridge, no upload. — via image crate
rationale: Direct match to the convert-to-webp demand term and a top web-performance optimization.

name: video-convert
description: Converts video between mp4, webm, mov and mkv.
example_prompt: Convert this mov to mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM transcodes containers/codecs in the browser.
rationale: Container/codec conversion is a top VideoToolbox request and avoids slow uploads.

name: convert-image-format
description: Converts an image between PNG, JPEG, WebP, BMP, GIF and TIFF with optional quality control.
example_prompt: Convert this PNG to a JPEG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM image crate decodes and re-encodes locally.
rationale: Format conversion for compatibility and file size is one of the most-searched image tasks.

name: video-merge
description: Concatenates multiple video clips into one.
example_prompt: Join these clips into a single video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg concat joins compatible streams locally in WASM.
rationale: Stitching clips is a core editing task and keeps large source files off any server.

name: auto-enhance
description: Automatically improve a photo with auto-levels, contrast stretch, and saturation correction.
example_prompt: Auto-enhance this dull photo
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute — histogram analysis and tone-curve application run as local GPU passes.
rationale: One-click "make it look better" is one of the most-used photo features and easy to do well locally.

name: video-to-captions
description: Extracts the audio track from an uploaded video and produces a timestamped caption file for it.
example_prompt: Generate captions for this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (WASM) strips/decodes the audio track locally, then transformers-js Whisper transcribes it with timestamps in-browser — model Xenova/whisper-tiny
rationale: Pairs the ffmpeg and Whisper demand directly: captioning video privately is a top use of local ASR stacks.

name: 7z-extract
description: Extracts files from a .7z archive (including AES-encrypted ones) entirely in the browser.
example_prompt: Extract the files from this .7z archive
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sevenz-rust is pure Rust and LZMA/LZMA2 decoding compiles to WASM with no native deps. — via sevenz-rust crate
rationale: Directly serves the 7z/sevenz-rust demand and lets users open 7z archives without uploading sensitive files to a server.

name: image-resize-to-filesize
description: Iteratively resizes and re-encodes an image to hit a target file size in KB.
example_prompt: Get this photo under 200 KB while keeping it as sharp as possible
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg/plain Rust→WASM: binary-search dimensions+quality and re-encode locally. — via image crate
rationale: Meets hard upload/attachment size limits without guesswork.

name: heic-to-png
description: Decodes HEIC/HEIF images to lossless PNG, preserving the alpha channel when present.
example_prompt: Turn this .heic screenshot into a png
loader_feasibility: Same ffmpeg/libde265 HEVC path as heic-to-jpeg; decode and PNG re-encode happen in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: Editors and design tools that reject HEIC often accept PNG, and users want a lossless target.

name: duplicate-image-finder
description: Scans a batch of images and reports exact and near-duplicate pairs above a similarity threshold with a suggested keep/delete list.
example_prompt: Find the duplicate and near-duplicate photos in this folder so I can clean it up.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM hashes every image and does pairwise comparison locally; no upload of the gallery needed. — via image crate
rationale: De-duplicating a photo dump is a common chore and doing it client-side keeps private photos off any server.

name: audio-gain-adjust
description: Raises or lowers volume by a precise dB amount, optionally with soft-clip protection.
example_prompt: Make this clip 6 dB louder
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg volume filter, or plain Rust→WASM linear-gain scan; trivial
rationale: Exact-dB gain changes are a constant need that GUI sliders make imprecise.

name: video-target-filesize-encoder
description: Re-encodes a video to land under a chosen file-size budget by computing the right bitrate from the clip duration and doing a two-pass encode.
example_prompt: compress this video to under 8MB so I can post it on Discord
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — duration probe + bitrate math + two-pass libx264/aac all run in the ffmpeg WASM build entirely in-browser.
rationale: The single most common 'make it fit' request (Discord/email/forum limits) and nobody wants to do the bitrate arithmetic by hand.

name: invoice-data-extractor
description: Extracts invoice number, dates, vendor, line items, and amount due from a scanned or photographed invoice.
example_prompt: Extract the invoice number, date, and total from this invoice image
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime OCR feeds plain-Rust label/value matching; no server round-trip needed for the document. — via ocrs crate
rationale: Bookkeeping workflows need structured invoice fields without sending financial documents to a cloud OCR API.

name: voice-note-transcriber
description: Transcribes a chat voice message to text directly in the browser.
example_prompt: transcribe this telegram voice note to text
loader_feasibility: transformers-js/onnx-runtime — a Whisper model runs on-device so the audio never leaves the browser. — model Xenova/whisper-tiny
rationale: Reading voice notes instead of listening is a huge convenience, and local transcription keeps private audio off any server.

name: mov-to-mp4
description: Rewraps a QuickTime MOV into an MP4 container, stream-copying H.264/HEVC when possible and transcoding only if needed.
example_prompt: Convert my iPhone .mov screen recording to .mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm reads the MOV atom structure and writes an MP4, copying compatible streams in-browser.
rationale: MOV files from Apple devices are huge and poorly supported on Windows/web, so a fast remux is valuable.

name: video-to-h264
description: Re-encodes any video to the most universally compatible H.264 High profile MP4 with yuv420p pixels.
example_prompt: Re-encode this to the most compatible mp4 that plays everywhere
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm's libx264 encoder runs in the browser to produce a baseline-compatible MP4.
rationale: Many files use exotic codecs that fail on TVs and old devices; normalizing to H.264 fixes broad playback issues.

name: unzip-archive
description: Lists the contents of a ZIP archive and lets the user extract and download individual files.
example_prompt: Show me what's inside this zip and let me grab one file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the zip crate (with miniz_oxide) inflating entries in memory; no server.
rationale: Inspecting an untrusted archive without extracting it to disk is a real safety win.

name: video-title-card
description: Overlays styled title or lower-third text onto a video at a given time range.
example_prompt: Add the title 'Vacation 2026' to the first 3 seconds of this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg drawtext filter with a bundled font renders text locally.
rationale: Titles and captions are core editor output and awkward to produce in chat otherwise.

name: vocal-separator
description: Separates vocals from the instrumental backing of a song.
example_prompt: Remove the vocals from this track
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a Spleeter/Demucs-lite separation model client-side.
rationale: Top-demand karaoke and remix use case (musdb demand).

name: gpu-image-resize
description: Resizes an image to a target size with high-quality Lanczos/bicubic filtering.
example_prompt: Resize this to 1024px wide with Lanczos.
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute performs the multi-tap resampling kernel as a shader on the GPU client-side.
rationale: Sharp downscaling beats the browser's default and is a constant need before publishing images.

name: video-caption-burner
description: Burns title text or an SRT subtitle track permanently onto a video.
example_prompt: Add the caption 'Summer 2026' to the bottom of this clip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg-wasm's drawtext/subtitles filters render text into frames client-side.
rationale: Hardcoded captions are a top editly feature and impossible to do privately in most web tools.

name: indonesian-summarizer
description: Generates a concise summary of an Indonesian article or document.
example_prompt: Summarize this Indonesian news article in a short paragraph
loader_feasibility: transformers-js summarization with an IndoSum/multilingual mT5 model converted to ONNX, running on onnxruntime-web.
rationale: IndoSum demand shows clear need for Bahasa summarization, delivered here without uploading content anywhere.

name: sqlite-query
description: Run SQL queries against an uploaded SQLite (.sqlite/.db) file and return result tables.
example_prompt: run 'SELECT * FROM users LIMIT 10' on this .db file
loader_feasibility: sql.js / sqlite-wasm runs the full SQLite engine in-browser.
rationale: Querying real SQLite files locally is hugely useful; sql-query only handles CSV/pasted tables.

name: action-items
description: Extract action items, decisions, and owners from a meeting transcript or notes as a structured checklist.
example_prompt: pull the action items out of this meeting transcript
loader_feasibility: transformers-js instruction model runs in-browser; no server.
rationale: Meeting-notes-to-tasks is a top productivity AI use and complements the summarize tool.

name: transaction-categorizer
description: Auto-labels each transaction description into budget categories using a local zero-shot classifier.
example_prompt: Categorize these transaction descriptions into groceries, rent, dining, etc.
loader_feasibility: transformers-js zero-shot classification (MNLI model) running in-browser; no data leaves the device.
rationale: Categorization is the most tedious budgeting step, and doing it locally keeps spending data private while showcasing on-device ML.

name: image-metadata-dumper
description: Dumps all EXIF, XMP, and IPTC tags from an image as structured JSON.
example_prompt: Show me every metadata tag in this JPEG as JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via a kamadak-exif-style reader: parse tag blocks, serialize JSON — no calls out. — via kamadak-exif crate
rationale: A complete tag dump is the fastest way to inspect camera settings and provenance without a desktop app.

name: photo-slideshow-video
description: Builds a slideshow video from uploaded photos with per-image hold time, crossfade transitions, and an optional music track.
example_prompt: Make a slideshow video from these 12 photos with 3s each and crossfades, plus this mp3
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg xfade + concat + amix runs client-side on the uploaded files.
rationale: A wedding/holiday slideshow is one of the most common consumer video tasks and is fully doable offline.

name: photo-geotag-extractor
description: Reads the GPS EXIF block and reports latitude/longitude, altitude and bearing in decimal and DMS form.
example_prompt: Where was this photo taken? Get the GPS coordinates
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM decodes only the GPS IFD from EXIF; coordinates are computed locally with no geocoding call. — via kamadak-exif crate
rationale: Pinpointing where a photo was shot is a high-value, frequently-requested single-purpose extraction.

name: ofx-to-csv
description: Parses an OFX/QFX bank statement into a CSV of transactions with date, amount, payee, type, and balance.
example_prompt: Convert this bank OFX statement into CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM SGML/XML parse of OFX locally—financial data never leaves the browser.
rationale: Banks export OFX/QFX but budgeting spreadsheets need CSV, and uploading statements to a website is a real privacy concern.

name: jpg-compressor
description: Re-encodes a JPG at a chosen quality level to reduce file size while keeping dimensions.
example_prompt: compress this jpg to about 200 KB
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (wasm): quality-targeted MJPEG re-encoding runs client-side. — via image crate
rationale: Shrinking JPGs for upload limits and web pages is one of the most common image chores.

name: auto-white-balance
description: Removes color casts by neutralizing the image's average or gray-point to restore natural colors.
example_prompt: This photo looks too orange, fix the white balance
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — gray-world / white-patch estimation is per-channel scaling math, no model needed — via image crate
rationale: Indoor and tungsten-lit photos almost always have a color cast and users want a one-click neutral fix.

name: speech-to-english-translation
description: Transcribes foreign-language speech and outputs an English translation of what was said.
example_prompt: Translate this Spanish audio clip into English text
loader_feasibility: transformers-js Whisper's built-in translate task runs entirely client-side, mapping non-English speech directly to English — model Xenova/whisper-small
rationale: Whisper/Parakeet/Moonshine users frequently want speech-translation, which Whisper does natively with no extra model.

name: voice-note-cleaner
description: Transcribes a rambling voice note and tidies it into punctuated, paragraphed, bulleted notes.
example_prompt: Turn this voice note into clean bullet-point notes
loader_feasibility: transformers-js Whisper for ASR plus a small transformers-js summarizer, both in-browser; formatting in Rust→WASM — model Xenova/whisper-base
rationale: OpenWhispr/Sasayaki demand is about dictation-to-usable-notes, not just raw transcripts.

name: gps-location-remover
description: Strips only the GPS/geolocation tags from a photo, leaving camera and exposure data intact.
example_prompt: Remove the location data from this photo but keep the camera info
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: selective EXIF tag deletion, no full re-encode required — via little_exif crate
rationale: Many users want to keep useful EXIF but scrub where the shot was taken — a precise privacy need Scrambled Exif over-deletes.

name: pin-image-resizer
description: Resizes and crops an image to Pinterest's recommended pin ratios (2:3, 1000×1500).
example_prompt: Resize this image to a Pinterest pin size
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (WASM) scale and crop filters — image processed in the browser.
rationale: Correctly sized pins perform far better, and manual cropping is fiddly.

name: strip-image-metadata
description: Removes EXIF/GPS and other metadata from a batch of images to protect privacy before sharing.
example_prompt: Strip GPS and EXIF data from these photos before I post them
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (WASM) — re-encodes without metadata, fully client-side so location data never leaves the device.
rationale: Strong privacy use case that is actively harmful to do via an upload-based tool.

name: log-file-analyzer
description: Searches, filters, and highlights large plain-text log files with regex, severity, and time-range filters.
example_prompt: Show only ERROR and WARN lines from this log between 14:00 and 15:00
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — chipmunk-style streaming search runs over the in-memory file buffer client-side, keeping logs private. — via regex crate
rationale: Engineers triage huge logs daily and want fast filtering without uploading sensitive log data anywhere.

name: receipt-parse
description: OCR a receipt photo and extract structured merchant, date, line items, tax, and total.
example_prompt: Extract the line items and total from this receipt photo
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime OCR + plain-Rust structured parsing; offline. — model naver-clova-ix/donut-base-finetuned-cord-v2
rationale: Major expense-tracking use case far beyond generic OCR.

name: stem-separator
description: Splits a song into separate vocal and instrumental stems using an AI model.
example_prompt: Separate this track into vocals and backing instruments
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a quantized Demucs/UVR model entirely in the browser on decoded PCM.
rationale: True stem separation is the premium version of vocal-removal demand and keeps copyrighted audio on-device.

name: smart-crop
description: Crop an image to a target aspect ratio while keeping the most salient subject centered.
example_prompt: Crop this to 1:1 but keep the person in frame
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime — a small saliency/segmentation model picks the focal region, then crop runs locally.
rationale: Subject-aware cropping for thumbnails/social is far better than naive center crop and is a common batch need.

name: video-rotate-orientation
description: Rotates the picture 90, 180, or 270 degrees and re-encodes so the new orientation is baked into the pixels.
example_prompt: Rotate this sideways phone video 90 degrees clockwise
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader uses the transpose filter in the browser; a short re-encode is well within ffmpeg.wasm limits.
rationale: Phone clips recorded in the wrong orientation are a universal annoyance fixable locally.

name: nsfw-detect
description: Score an image for explicit/NSFW content so it can be flagged or filtered before sharing.
example_prompt: is this image safe for work?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime / transformers-js NSFW classifier; small model runs client-side. — model Falconsai/nsfw_image_detection
rationale: Local image moderation is a practical safety building block for any UGC or upload flow.

name: image-montage
description: Combines multiple images into a single grid/contact-sheet montage with configurable rows and spacing.
example_prompt: Make a 2x2 montage from these four images
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's tile/xstack filters stitch the decoded images into one canvas entirely in-browser.
rationale: ImageMagick montage demand maps to a useful collage/contact-sheet tool with no upload.

name: subscription-finder
description: Detects recurring and subscription charges in a transaction list and projects their annual cost.
example_prompt: Find recurring subscriptions in my transactions and tell me the yearly total
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM pattern/interval detection over parsed transactions; offline.
rationale: Surfacing forgotten subscriptions is one of the highest-value insights in expense apps, and it runs entirely on local data.

name: csv-to-vcard
description: Convert a CSV/JSON contact list into a single .vcf file of vCards for bulk import.
example_prompt: turn this CSV of contacts into a vCard file
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust to WASM — pure text transform.
rationale: Bulk contact import is common; the existing vcard tool makes only one card.

name: timesheet-calculator
description: Parses a freeform or structured work log of start-stop times and tags, then totals hours per project and computes billable amounts.
example_prompt: Total my hours from this log: 9:00-12:30 client-A, 13:00-17:00 client-B, 17:00-18:15 client-A
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure string/time-interval parsing and arithmetic, no network or server needed.
rationale: Six different time-trackers were harvested as demand; a stateless 'paste log → get totals' tool covers the universal need without an account.

name: document-embeddings
description: Generates dense vector embeddings for text chunks using a local sentence-embedding model.
example_prompt: Generate embeddings for these paragraphs.
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — runs a small embedding model (e.g. all-MiniLM) in-browser via WASM/WebGPU, no API key or server. — model Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
rationale: Embeddings are the backbone of semantic search/RAG and doing them locally keeps data private and free.

name: sqlite-table-to-csv
description: Reads an uploaded SQLite .db/.sqlite file by parsing the on-disk page format and exports a chosen table as CSV.
example_prompt: Export the orders table from this SQLite file as CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decoding the documented SQLite file format directly in-memory; no SQL engine or server.
rationale: People receive SQLite files (browser history, app exports) and just want one table as a spreadsheet without installing tooling.

name: video-onscreen-text-ocr
description: Runs OCR on sampled frames to extract any on-screen text (titles, lower-thirds, signs) with timestamps.
example_prompt: Extract all the on-screen text in this video with timecodes
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes frames and a transformers-js/onnx OCR model reads text locally; weights ship to the browser, no API.
rationale: Extracting burned-in text enables search, translation, and indexing, and goes beyond merely detecting captions.

name: password-file-decrypt
description: Decrypts files produced by the password encryptor back to their original plaintext.
example_prompt: Decrypt this .enc file, the password is hunter2
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; symmetric XChaCha20-Poly1305 decrypt runs entirely client-side — via chacha20poly1305 crate
rationale: Pairs with the encryptor so encrypted files stay usable offline.

name: docx-text-extract
description: Extracts the plain text and Markdown structure from a .docx Word document.
example_prompt: Pull the text out of this .docx file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: docx is a zip of XML, parsed with the zip + quick-xml crates fully in-memory. — via quick-xml crate
rationale: Maps the wv/Vertopal document-viewer demand to a browser-local extractor with no upload to a server.

name: svg-rasterizer
description: Renders an SVG file to a crisp PNG at any resolution, faithfully handling gradients, fonts, and filters.
example_prompt: Render this SVG logo to a 1024x1024 PNG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — resvg is a pure-Rust SVG renderer that compiles to wasm and rasterizes entirely in the browser with no server. — via resvg crate
rationale: Reliable, font-accurate SVG→PNG conversion is a constant need for designers exporting icons and graphics.

name: csv-cleaner
description: Cleans a CSV by trimming whitespace, deduplicating rows, normalizing delimiters/line endings, and dropping or filling empty cells.
example_prompt: Clean up this CSV: trim spaces and remove duplicate rows
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via rust-csv — row/field rewriting is local CPU work, no server — via csv crate
rationale: Messy CSVs are universal and a deterministic local cleaner is more trustworthy and private than pasting data into a web app.

name: zip-extract
description: List and extract the contents of a .zip archive (with optional password).
example_prompt: extract this zip and show me what's inside
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust (zip crate) to WASM — pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: Inspecting and unpacking zips in-browser is broadly useful.

name: video-mux-external-audio
description: Combines a separate audio file with a video track into one file, matching durations as needed.
example_prompt: mux this narration.mp3 onto my screen-recording mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — maps the video stream and external audio stream into one container in the WASM runtime.
rationale: Recording video and audio separately then muxing them is a standard workflow this makes one-click.

name: mt940-statement-parse
description: Parses a SWIFT MT940 bank statement into opening/closing balances and individual :61:/:86: transaction lines.
example_prompt: Turn this MT940 statement into a transaction table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line/tag parsing of the MT940 field structure; banking data is parsed locally so account details never touch a server
rationale: Accountants and fintech devs reconcile MT940 files constantly and a privacy-preserving local parser is genuinely valuable.

name: video-first-last-frame-extractor
description: Exports the very first and very last decodable frames of a video as images.
example_prompt: Give me the first and last frame of this clip as images
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm decodes frame 0 and seeks to EOF for the final frame; client-side decode.
rationale: First/last frames are needed for crossfades, thumbnails, and truncation checks and are awkward to grab manually.

name: extractive-summary
description: Pick and highlight the most important verbatim sentences from a document (TextRank), no rewriting.
example_prompt: Highlight the 5 key sentences of this article without paraphrasing
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust TextRank (or transformers-js embeddings) entirely in-browser.
rationale: Verbatim extractive summarization is a distinct technique/output from the abstractive summarize tool and needs no LLM.

name: ip-log-anonymizer
description: Masks or salted-hashes IP addresses inside a log for GDPR-compliant analytics.
example_prompt: Anonymize the IPs in this access log: <paste>
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM octet-zeroing and HMAC hashing; the data stays entirely local.
rationale: IP anonymization is both a privacy-analytics requirement and a legal one, making client-side processing the ideal place to do it.

name: eml-msg-parser
description: Parses .eml and Outlook .msg messages to extract headers, bodies, and decoded attachments.
example_prompt: Extract the attachments and sender details from this .msg email
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: MIME and OLE (.msg) structures are parsed from the uploaded file with no host access. — via mail-parser crate
rationale: Phishing and email-evidence analysis needs local extraction so suspect attachments never leave the box.

name: action-item-extractor
description: Pulls action items, owners, and decisions out of freeform meeting or daily notes into a structured task list.
example_prompt: Extract the action items and owners from these meeting notes

name: denoise-image

name: image-watermark

name: vcard-to-json

name: video-background-blur

name: image-side-by-side

name: pdf-sign

name: ecc-keygen

name: resume-ats-check

name: image-chroma-key

name: jpg-to-png

example_prompt: convert this jpg to png

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (lopdf) overlay, or pyodide pikepdf. — via lopdf crate
rationale: Branding/draft-stamping PDFs is a frequent business task absent from the set.

name: audio-noise-reduce
