description: Converts an image to a base64 data URI for inlining, and extracts images back out of data URIs.
example_prompt: Turn this PNG into a data URI I can paste into my CSS
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM base64 + image sniffing; or ffmpeg for format conversion, all in-browser
rationale: Inlining small assets to cut requests is a standard static-hosting optimization for sites on Vercel and similar platforms.

name: invoice-builder
description: Generates a clean printable HTML invoice from line items, with tax, totals and seller/buyer details.
example_prompt: make an invoice for ACME, 3 line items, 8% tax, due in 30 days
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — HTML invoice template plus the line-item arithmetic, no server.
rationale: Producing a tidy invoice without signing up for a billing SaaS is a common small-seller need.

name: weak-password-detector
description: Checks a password against a bundled list of the most common and breached passwords.
example_prompt: Is 'password123' a commonly breached password?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with an embedded top-N breached-password list; fully offline, no HIBP call.
rationale: Reuse of breached passwords is the single biggest real-world account risk and can be screened locally without leaking the password.

name: phishing-header-inspector
description: Scans an email's headers for spoofing and phishing indicators such as From/Return-Path mismatch, display-name spoofing, and inconsistent Received hops.
example_prompt: Is this email phishing? Here are the full headers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via mail-parser + mail-auth with local heuristics — no DNS lookups required because it reasons over the pasted headers only — via mail-parser crate
rationale: Quick local triage of a suspicious message is high-value for everyday users and keeps potentially sensitive mail off external scanners.

name: gpx-to-geojson
description: Convert GPX/KML GPS tracks and waypoints into GeoJSON (and back).
example_prompt: Convert this GPX hike track to GeoJSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via georust gpx/kml + geojson — parsing/serialization only. — via gpx crate
rationale: Turning GPS exports into GeoJSON is a common first step for mapping personal tracks privately.

name: dir-checksum-report
description: Takes a set of uploaded files and produces a Markdown table of filename, size and CRC32/SHA-256 for verification.
example_prompt: Make a checksum report for these files I'm uploading
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: reads each file's bytes locally and emits Markdown; no upload to any server.
rationale: One-step manifest for verifying a batch of downloads or release artifacts offline (the DirCrcMd use case).

name: image-alt-text
description: Generates a descriptive caption or alt text for an uploaded image.
example_prompt: Write alt text describing this image
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs an image-to-text caption model (BLIP-style) fully in-browser via WASM/WebGPU; no API call. — model Xenova/vit-gpt2-image-captioning
rationale: Text browsers like w3m/browsh need image descriptions to be usable, and accessible alt text is broadly valuable beyond terminals.

name: crypto-keypair-generator
description: Generates fresh cryptographic keypairs and addresses for chains like Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana entirely offline.
example_prompt: Generate a new Ethereum keypair and address
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — secp256k1/ed25519 crates compile to wasm32, and offline generation is actually safer than any web service. — via ed25519-dalek crate
rationale: Air-gapped key generation (the wagyu use case) is exactly the kind of task you want running locally, never on a server.

name: whatsapp-chat-analyzer
description: Parses an exported WhatsApp _chat.txt and reports messages per person, busiest hours/days, word and emoji frequency.
example_prompt: analyze my exported whatsapp chat and show who texts the most
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — text parsing and counting only; the chat never leaves the browser.
rationale: WhatsApp chat stats are a popular curiosity and these exports are deeply personal, so on-device analysis is the right model.

name: bulk-file-renamer
description: Applies regex, find/replace, sequential-numbering, or case rules to a list of filenames (or files inside an uploaded zip) and outputs the rename mapping plus a re-zipped result.
example_prompt: rename all these files to lowercase and replace spaces with dashes, show me the mapping
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM does the string transforms and re-zips in memory; vidir-style bulk editing with no editor or FS.
rationale: vidir demand — bulk rename is tedious and error-prone by hand, and previewing the mapping before applying it is safer.

name: markdown-to-pptx
description: Convert a Markdown outline into a real PowerPoint .pptx deck, splitting slides on headings.
example_prompt: turn this markdown outline into a PowerPoint deck
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (pptx is zipped XML); local.
rationale: Generating an editable .pptx is distinct from the existing HTML reveal.js slides export and widely wanted.

name: business-card-ocr
description: OCR a business card photo and output a structured vCard contact.
example_prompt: Turn this business card photo into a contact
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime OCR + field parsing into vCard; offline.
rationale: Popular networking task chaining OCR to the existing vCard format.

name: resume-parse
description: Extract structured fields (name, contact, skills, experience, education) from a resume/CV into JSON.
example_prompt: parse this resume into structured JSON
loader_feasibility: transformers-js NER + section heuristics over extracted text; local.
rationale: Resume parsing is a staple of recruiting/ATS workflows and isn't covered by the generic entity or card-OCR tools.

name: bpm-detect
description: Detects the tempo (BPM) of a music track.
example_prompt: What's the BPM of this track?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes to PCM, then plain Rust→WASM onset-autocorrelation computes BPM locally.
rationale: BPM detection is the entry tool for DJ apps like YOU.DJ and Until AM and is pure DSP.

name: csv-chart-generator
description: Generates bar, line, scatter, or histogram charts from chosen CSV columns as SVG.
example_prompt: Make a scatter plot of height versus weight from this CSV.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses data and renders the chart as SVG locally.
rationale: Producing basic charts from data is a core visualization skill (CS171/OpenIntro).

name: screenshot-beautify
description: Wrap a screenshot in a polished frame with padding, rounded corners, shadow, and a gradient/solid backdrop.
example_prompt: make this screenshot look nice with a purple gradient background and shadow
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM compositing (or webgpu for the gradient); all pixel work is local.
rationale: Tools like Screely/Shots.so are wildly popular for making screenshots presentation-ready, and it's pure compositing.

name: transcript-clean
description: Clean a raw transcript: remove filler words, fix capitalization/punctuation, and merge speaker turns.
example_prompt: Clean up this messy auto-transcript and remove the ums
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust rules + optional transformers-js punctuation model; browser-local.
rationale: Polishing raw transcripts into readable text is a common step after transcription.

name: image-pad-to-square
description: Pads a rectangular image to a perfect square (or chosen aspect) with a selectable background color, without cropping content.
example_prompt: Pad this image to a square with a white background
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: create a square canvas, fill, and blit the source centered — pure pixel ops in-memory. — via image crate
rationale: Marketplaces and Instagram demand square images; padding (vs cropping) preserves the whole subject.

name: audio-dereverb
description: Reduces room reverb and echo from a dry-intended speech or vocal recording.
example_prompt: Take the room echo out of this recording I made in a hallway.
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a dereverb model locally on the audio frames.
rationale: Reverb removal rescues otherwise-unusable takes and is the inverse of the existing reverb-adding tool, with no current cleanup option.

name: saturation-vibrance-adjust
description: Adjusts saturation globally and vibrance (protecting skin tones and already-saturated areas).
example_prompt: Boost the vibrance of this landscape
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM converts to HSL/HSV and scales saturation with a vibrance falloff; runs locally.
rationale: Vibrance (smart saturation) is a staple edit that one-click tools rarely expose with control.

name: device-mockup-framer
description: Frames a screenshot inside a clean device mockup (phone, tablet, laptop, browser window) with shadow and background.
example_prompt: Put this screenshot inside an iPhone mockup on a soft gradient
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — perspective-fit the screenshot into the bundled bezel art and composite; offline.
rationale: Device mockups are constant marketing output and the popular tools all require an upload to a web app.

name: image-horizon-tilt-checker
description: Detects a tilted horizon or dominant line and reports the angle so the photo can be leveled.
example_prompt: Is the horizon in this photo level, and by how many degrees is it off?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs edge detection and a Hough-style line vote — CPU-only, fully local.
rationale: A crooked horizon is an instantly-noticeable flaw, and measuring the exact angle enables a precise straighten.

name: portrait-background-blur
description: Applies a depth-of-field-style background blur while keeping the foreground subject sharp.
example_prompt: Blur the background behind the person in this photo
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime: a person/segmentation model produces a mask, then the background is Gaussian-blurred in Rust, client-side. — model briaai/RMBG-1.4
rationale: Faux-bokeh portraits are highly desirable and reuse local segmentation without the full background-removal output.

name: audio-pause-shortener
description: Detects overly long silences in speech and shortens each to a fixed maximum to tighten pacing.
example_prompt: Cut all the long pauses in my podcast down to half a second
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg silencedetect to find gaps + atrim/concat to rebuild, fully client-side
rationale: Tightening dead air is a standard podcast edit that otherwise needs a DAW.

name: video-set-crf-quality
description: Re-encodes at a chosen constant-quality CRF value, trading file size against visual quality on a simple slider.
example_prompt: re-encode this at crf 23 for a good size-quality balance
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — libx264/x265 -crf re-encode in the WASM build.
rationale: CRF is the cleanest quality knob and exposing it directly lets users dial size without bitrate math.

name: spoken-language-identifier
description: Identifies the spoken language of a speech recording and returns the top candidate languages with confidence scores.
example_prompt: What language is being spoken in this clip?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — a small language-ID model (e.g. Whisper/wav2vec head) runs on WASM/WebGPU entirely client-side — model Xenova/mms-lid-126
rationale: Sorting multilingual recording archives needs language tagging, and doing it locally keeps sensitive audio private.

name: audio-hiss-reducer
description: Reduces broadband tape/preamp hiss using spectral gating tuned to the high band.
example_prompt: Reduce the tape hiss on this old cassette transfer.
loader_feasibility: pyodide STFT spectral gating with numpy; runs fully in the browser.
rationale: Hiss reduction targets a noise type the speech denoiser and notch tools don't, key for archival transfers.

name: video-scene-cut-detector
description: Detects hard scene cuts in a video and reports each cut's timestamp and confidence score.
example_prompt: Find all the scene cuts in this video and list their timestamps
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — the `scdet`/`select='gt(scene,...)'` filters compute frame-to-frame difference entirely in the wasm decoder, no server.
rationale: Editors and archivists constantly need an exact cut list to split or index footage without scrubbing manually.

name: filler-word-counter
description: Transcribes speech locally and counts filler words (um, uh, like, you know) with timestamps.
example_prompt: Count the filler words in my presentation recording
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs Whisper in-browser then tallies filler tokens, fully local — model Xenova/whisper-tiny.en
rationale: Filler-word reports help speakers and podcast editors tighten delivery.

name: tldr-headline-generator
description: Produces a single-line tl;dr or headline for a block of text.
example_prompt: Write a one-line tl;dr for this thread: <paste>
loader_feasibility: transformers-js abstractive model in-browser with a short max-length decode keeps it fast and fully local. — model Xenova/distilbart-cnn-6-6
rationale: Maps the 'your tl;dr by an AI: deep reinforced abstractive summarization' demand into a focused one-liner output.

name: wavelet-denoise
description: Removes broadband noise from audio using wavelet-threshold denoising.
example_prompt: Clean up the hiss in this recording
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM wavelet decomposition, soft thresholding, and reconstruction run fully client-side.
rationale: Wavelet thresholding is a classic, effective denoiser that preserves transients better than spectral gating.

name: speech-segmenter
description: Splits a long recording into separate utterance clips at natural speech boundaries.
example_prompt: Split this interview into separate speech chunks.
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime VAD finds speech regions and ffmpeg cuts the clips, all in the wasm runtime.
rationale: Utterance segmentation prepares audio for captioning and dataset building without server round-trips.

name: file-lock
description: Password-encrypts a file into a self-contained blob you can share, and decrypts such blobs back to the original.
example_prompt: Encrypt this PDF with a password so I can send it safely
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — AES-GCM with PBKDF2 key derivation (fast in WASM) runs client-side; bytes never leave the browser. — via aes-gcm crate
rationale: Captures croc/share's secure-transfer intent — the encryption — while staying fully local; the transfer itself is out of band.

name: pdf-form-data-extract
description: Reads the filled values of an AcroForm PDF and outputs the field name/value pairs as JSON or CSV.
example_prompt: Extract the field values from this filled-in PDF form
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM enumerates the AcroForm field tree and reads /V values in-browser — via lopdf crate
rationale: Lets people pull structured data out of completed forms without retyping it.

name: key-format-convert
description: Converts cryptographic keys between PEM, DER, and JWK representations.
example_prompt: convert this rsa pem key to jwk
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (der/pkcs8/spki + serde_json for JWK); transcoding in-page. — via pkcs8 crate
rationale: jsrsasign's PEM↔JWK conversion is a frequent dev chore, and private keys must not be uploaded to convert them.

name: video-strip-metadata
description: Remove embedded metadata (location, device, timestamps) from a video by remuxing it clean.
example_prompt: Strip the GPS and device metadata from this video before I share it
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — stream-copy remux with -map_metadata -1, fast and local.
rationale: Privacy parity with the existing image-strip-metadata tool, which video lacks.

name: ppt-to-text
description: Extracts text from legacy binary PowerPoint .ppt (97–2003) presentations.
example_prompt: Get the text out of presentation.ppt
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs a pure-Python OLE2 parser over the .ppt streams in the WASM sandbox (replaces catdoc's catppt).
rationale: Old .ppt files are common in archives and nearly impossible to open without legacy Office.

name: epub-extract
description: Extracts readable text and chapter structure from an EPUB ebook so it can be searched, summarized, or quoted.
example_prompt: Pull the chapter list and text out of this EPUB so I can summarize chapter 3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the zip crate plus HTML stripping; EPUB is just zipped XHTML processed locally
rationale: Turns the bookworm ebook-reader demand into a practical text-extraction tool that feeds the rest of the chat.

name: evtx-parser
description: Converts Windows Event Log .evtx files into readable JSON/CSV with filtering by Event ID and time.
example_prompt: Show me all logon events (4624/4625) in this Security.evtx file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: evtx is a binary chunk/template format parsed in-memory from the upload; mature Rust evtx crates compile to wasm cleanly. — via evtx crate
rationale: Event-log triage is the single most common DFIR task and a browser-local EvtxECmd avoids installing tooling on an evidence host.

name: pivot-table
description: Builds a pivot table from tabular data with chosen row/column dimensions and an aggregation (sum/avg/count/min/max).
example_prompt: Pivot this CSV with region as rows, month as columns, summing revenue
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM groups and aggregates the parsed rows in memory
rationale: Pivoting is the go-to way to summarize tabular data and is a deterministic in-memory operation.

name: url-extractor
description: Finds and normalizes all URLs in free text, including bare and parenthesized links.
example_prompt: Extract every URL from this block of notes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — autolink detection regexes, no network required.
rationale: URL extraction (twitter-text and knwl.js feature) is a recurring need for link harvesting and cleanup.

name: markdown-preview
description: Renders Markdown to clean, sanitized HTML for preview.
example_prompt: render this markdown so I can see how it looks
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pulldown-cmark plus sanitizer produce HTML entirely in-browser. — via pulldown-cmark crate
rationale: glow-style rendering from the terminal lists; lets users preview docs without any service.

name: voice-activity-detector
description: Produces a precise speech-presence timeline (start/end timestamps of spoken segments) using a VAD model.
example_prompt: Give me the timestamps of every spoken segment in this audio
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a lightweight Silero-style VAD model fully client-side on decoded PCM (ffmpeg decodes). — model onnx-community/silero-vad
rationale: Accurate VAD segments drive transcription chunking, silence trimming, and turn-taking analysis.

name: ini-parser
description: Parses INI/conf files (sections, keys, comments) into structured JSON and reports duplicate keys.
example_prompt: Convert this .ini config to JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a small INI parser crate compiles to WASM and runs on the pasted text.
rationale: INI is everywhere in tooling but has no native JSON bridge, so a local converter is handy.

name: pdf-outline-extract
description: Extract a PDF's bookmark/outline table of contents as a structured list.
example_prompt: List the table of contents/bookmarks in this PDF
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM PDF object parsing, offline. — via lopdf crate
rationale: Pulling a PDF's navigation tree is distinct from extracting body text or Markdown.

name: exif-photo-organizer
description: Reads EXIF from uploaded photos and proposes date/camera-based filenames and folder structures (e.g. 2026/06/IMG_20260624_…).
example_prompt: Rename these photos by the date they were taken
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — EXIF is metadata parsing only (kamadak-exif), no pixel decoding required. — via kamadak-exif crate
rationale: Date-based media organization is the marquee use case of photo-library managers like spacedrive.

name: tcx-to-gpx
description: Converts Garmin TCX workout files into GPX, preserving track points and timestamps.
example_prompt: Convert this TCX from my watch into GPX
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM XML schema mapping; fully local.
rationale: Fitness exports come as TCX while most map tools want GPX, a constant friction point.

name: audio-effects-rack
description: Applies classic effects — reverb, echo/delay, chorus, tremolo, and compression — to a clip.
example_prompt: Add a small room reverb and a slap-back echo to this guitar
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader — aecho/chorus/acompressor/afir effects run locally in wasm. — via fundsp crate
rationale: pySox-style effect chains are a popular creative need that maps cleanly to ffmpeg filters.

name: env-json-converter
description: Converts a .env file to a JSON object and back, preserving comments where possible.
example_prompt: Convert this .env into JSON: <paste .env>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parse/serialize; no network access needed.
rationale: Round-tripping env vars between dotenv and JSON is a common glue task adjacent to dotenv tooling.

name: key-insights-extractor
description: Extracts the main ideas and key takeaways from text as a bulleted list.
example_prompt: Pull the key insights out of this transcript
loader_feasibility: transformers-js summarization model post-processed into bullets; in-browser inference. — model Xenova/distilbart-cnn-6-6
rationale: Implements fabric's extract_wisdom/extract_main_idea demand with a distinct bullet output.

name: telegram-export-reader
description: Parses a Telegram chat export (result.json) into a clean transcript plus per-sender message and word stats.
example_prompt: summarize the stats from my telegram export result.json
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — JSON parsing and aggregation, no Telegram API access required. — via serde_json crate
rationale: Telegram's JSON export is unwieldy; turning it into a transcript and stats locally protects private conversations.

name: email-translator
description: Translates an email body into another language.
example_prompt: Translate this German email to English
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs an opus-mt/NLLB translation model in-browser. — model Xenova/nllb-200-distilled-600M
rationale: Foreign-language email needs translation without leaking its contents to a cloud service.

name: markdown-to-docx
description: Convert a Markdown document into a styled Microsoft Word (.docx) file.
example_prompt: convert this markdown to a Word document
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust docx builder to WASM — pure compute (docx is zip+XML). — via docx-rs crate
rationale: Exporting to Word is a frequent need; only markdown-to-pdf exists today.

name: yaml-to-json
description: Parses YAML into equivalent JSON, preserving types and nested structures.
example_prompt: convert this YAML to JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via serde_yaml + serde_json — pure parsing, no network — via serde_yaml crate
rationale: Config-file conversion between YAML and JSON is a daily devops task with strong recurring demand.

name: add-audio-to-video
description: Adds or replaces the audio track of a video with an uploaded audio file.
example_prompt: put this song over my video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader muxes a new audio stream onto the video locally.
rationale: Adding background music to clips is a core editing task.

name: csv-join-report
description: Full-outer-joins two CSVs on a key and reports matched rows, left-only, and right-only counts and samples.
example_prompt: Reconcile these two member lists on email and show what's unmatched on each side
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: hash-join over rows, no database needed.
rationale: Reconciling two lists for unmatched records is a universal task usually done with a spreadsheet kludge.

name: extract-numbers-from-text
description: Pulls every numeric value (integers, decimals, scientific notation, signed, separator-formatted) out of arbitrary prose or logs into a clean list.
example_prompt: extract all the numbers from: revenue rose to $1,234.5 from 1.1e3 (-3% YoY)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — regex scan and numeric parsing over the input string, fully local.
rationale: Grabbing figures buried in a paragraph or report to feed further math is a frequent first step with no general numeric extractor in the catalog.

name: csv-cell-diff
description: Aligns two CSVs column-by-column and highlights every individual cell that differs.
example_prompt: Show me a cell-level highlight of what changed between yesterday's and today's price sheet
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; column alignment plus per-cell string comparison produces an HTML/SVG grid client-side
rationale: Row-level diffs hide which field actually moved; cell highlighting is what reviewers really need.

name: xlsx-sheet-diff
description: Compares two spreadsheet sheets cell-by-cell and reports value, formula, and structural differences.
example_prompt: Compare Sheet1 of these two Excel files and tell me which cells differ
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM calamine reads xlsx in-browser; cell-grid comparison is local — via calamine crate
rationale: Spreadsheet version comparison is a daily finance/ops need with no client-side option today.

name: image-sequence-to-video
description: Encodes a numbered sequence of PNG/JPG frames into a video at a chosen frame rate.
example_prompt: turn these frame_0001.png … frame_0240.png images into a 24fps mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — the image2 demuxer reads the numbered frames from the in-browser FS and encodes to MP4.
rationale: Render farms, Blender, and ML pipelines emit frame sequences that need assembling into a playable clip — distinct from a timed slideshow.

name: csv-delimiter-converter
description: Reparses CSV/TSV/semicolon data and re-emits it with a different delimiter, preserving quoting.
example_prompt: convert this semicolon-separated file into a proper comma csv
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSV reader/writer with configurable delimiters; offline.
rationale: European semicolon CSVs and TSV exports constantly need re-delimiting, and naive replace breaks quoted fields.

name: find-replace-with-diff
description: Runs batch regex find-and-replace across pasted text and shows a diff preview before you accept the result.
example_prompt: Replace all 'foo_bar' with 'fooBar' in this code and show me the diff: <pasted code>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM regex replace plus diff rendering; operates only on pasted text in-browser. — via regex crate
rationale: Preview-before-apply find/replace (the 'sad' workflow) prevents the blind sed mistakes that corrupt files.

name: csv-diff
description: Compare two CSV/tables and report added, removed, and changed rows (optionally keyed by a column).
example_prompt: diff these two CSV exports and show me what rows changed
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: in-memory row hashing/keying, no network.
rationale: Row-level data diffing is a real analyst pain point and parallels the backlog's json-diff.

name: face-bounding-box-detector
description: Detects faces in an image and returns their bounding-box coordinates (no identification).
example_prompt: Give me the bounding boxes for every face in this photo
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a lightweight face detector (e.g. BlazeFace) entirely client-side.
rationale: Face boxes drive offline redaction/blur workflows where uploading photos is unacceptable.

name: code-screenshot-ocr
description: Extracts source code from a code screenshot while preserving indentation and line breaks.
example_prompt: Get the code out of this screenshot keeping the formatting
loader_feasibility: transformers-js OCR with whitespace-aware line reconstruction runs in-browser. — model Xenova/trocr-base-printed
rationale: Developers constantly need to recover runnable code from screenshots and slides.

name: monophonic-audio-to-midi
description: Transcribes a single-voice recording (hum, whistle, solo) into a MIDI note sequence via pitch tracking and segmentation.
example_prompt: Convert this humming recording into a MIDI melody
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes to PCM, Rust→WASM does pitch tracking + note segmentation and emits an SMF — no server.
rationale: Hum-to-MIDI is a high-value creative tool that is fully feasible for monophonic input on-device.

name: env-file-parser
description: Parses a .env file into structured JSON and flags malformed or duplicate keys.
example_prompt: Turn this .env into JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: dotenv parsing (envy-style) is pure text processing in wasmi.
rationale: Converting and validating env files is a common dev need that runs fully offline.

name: hmac
description: Compute an HMAC (SHA-256/384/512/MD5) of a message with a secret key.
example_prompt: compute the HMAC-SHA256 of this payload with key 's3cret'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HMAC; no network. — via hmac crate
rationale: Webhook/API signature verification is common and not covered by plain hashing.

name: paste-link
description: Compress text and encode it into a self-contained shareable URL fragment so the content travels in the link itself with no server storing it.
example_prompt: turn this snippet into a shareable paste link
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM deflate (miniz_oxide) + base64url into a '#' fragment; everything is local and the data lives only in the URL, never on a host. — via miniz_oxide crate
rationale: Captures the appeal of feuille/paste69/GoCatGo (quick text sharing) without any backend, since the fragment is decoded purely client-side.

name: password-hash
description: Hash a password with bcrypt or Argon2 (and verify a password against a hash) for seeding or testing auth.
example_prompt: bcrypt-hash the password 'hunter2' with cost 10
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (bcrypt/argon2 crates compile to wasm32); CPU-bound but local, fine for one-off. — via argon2 crate
rationale: Generating/verifying password hashes for fixtures and migrations is distinct from the existing message-digest hash tool.

name: chat-translator
description: Translates a customer message between languages so agents can support multilingual chats.
example_prompt: Translate this customer message to English
loader_feasibility: transformers-js translation models (opus-mt/NLLB) — run on-device. — model Xenova/nllb-200-distilled-600M
rationale: Real-time translation is a costly add-on in chat suites; here it's free and private.

name: extract-emails
description: Scans arbitrary text and pulls out every email address into a deduplicated list.
example_prompt: Pull all the email addresses out of this support thread
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM regex pass over the input string; no network or server needed
rationale: Harvesting contacts from pasted logs, emails, or docs is a constant micro-task.

name: column-pseudonymize
description: Replaces identifier values with stable salted hashes so a dataset can be analyzed or shared without raw IDs.
example_prompt: Pseudonymize the email column with a salted hash so I can share this
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM SHA-256 with a user-supplied salt; deterministic and local. — via sha2 crate
rationale: Consistent pseudonymous keys preserve joinability while protecting identities, entirely offline.

name: video-black-frame-timeline
description: Produces a timeline of fully or near-black frame ranges, useful for finding fades and segment boundaries.
example_prompt: List every black-frame range in this video with timestamps
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg blackdetect filter computes luma statistics per frame entirely within the WASM runtime.
rationale: Black-frame ranges mark ad breaks, fades, and act boundaries — distinct from freeze detection and widely needed for editing.

name: env-to-configmap
description: Converts a .env file into a Kubernetes ConfigMap (or Secret) manifest.
example_prompt: turn this .env into a Kubernetes ConfigMap
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse key=value lines + template manifest (base64 for Secret), client-side
rationale: Moving local env vars into k8s manifests is a routine deploy step and the catalog only covers shell-export conversion.

name: har-validator
description: Validates a HAR (HTTP Archive) file's structure: log/entries shape, required request/response fields, and timing totals.
example_prompt: Validate this HAR file's structure
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: HAR is JSON with a fixed schema, validated entirely in-browser. — via serde_json crate
rationale: Malformed HAR exports break analysis tools and a structural check confirms a capture is usable before deep work.

name: video-face-presence-timeline
description: Detects which frames/segments contain faces, producing a timeline useful for redaction or highlight prep.
example_prompt: Mark where people's faces appear in this footage
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg samples frames for an onnx face-detection model run in-browser via WASM.
rationale: A face-presence map preps blur/redaction passes and works fully offline so footage never leaves the device.

name: csv-type-inferrer
description: Sniffs a CSV's delimiter/quote dialect, infers per-column types (int/float/bool/date/string), and emits typed JSON.
example_prompt: Detect the delimiter and column types in this CSV and give me typed JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; dialect sniffing and type inference are pure local string analysis. — via csv crate
rationale: Loading messy CSVs always starts with guessing the dialect and column types, a boilerplate step worth automating client-side.

name: sqlite-schema-extractor
description: Reads a SQLite database file's header and sqlite_master to extract its tables, indexes, and DDL without executing it.
example_prompt: What tables and schema are in this .sqlite file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the SQLite on-disk B-tree pages directly, no SQL engine or server required.
rationale: Recovering the schema from a raw .db file is a common forensics/migration need that shouldn't require running it.

name: image-composite
description: Overlay or blend two images with position, scale, opacity, and blend mode (multiply, screen, overlay).
example_prompt: Place this logo onto that background at 60% opacity in the corner
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — per-pixel blend-mode math on two decoded images, fully local. — via image crate
rationale: Combining/blending two images is a fundamental editing op the existing collage/watermark tools don't fully cover.

name: html-to-pdf
description: Render an HTML snippet or fetched page into a paginated PDF.
example_prompt: Convert this HTML invoice into a PDF
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM lightweight HTML/CSS layout engine to printpdf; heaviest path but client-side. — via printpdf crate
rationale: HTML-to-PDF is one of the most-requested converters and only markdown/text/docx paths exist.

name: email-attachment-extractor
description: Extracts every attachment from an .eml or mbox and offers them as downloads.
example_prompt: Pull all the attachments out of this mbox
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM walks MIME parts and reconstructs attachment bytes locally. — via mail-parser crate
rationale: Bulk-saving attachments from an archive has no easy, private local tool.

name: cluster-similar-values
description: Fuzzy-clusters near-duplicate text values in a column (typos, casing, spacing) and proposes a canonical form per cluster.
example_prompt: Cluster the company-name column to merge variants like 'IBM' and 'I.B.M.'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs key-collision and edit-distance clustering in-sandbox.
rationale: Replicates OpenRefine's signature clustering feature, the hardest part of dataset reconciliation.

name: pandas-csv-explorer
description: Applies pandas operations (filter, group, pivot, sort) to a CSV from a natural request.
example_prompt: group this csv by region and sum revenue
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs pandas on the uploaded CSV locally.
rationale: Interactive pandas exploration without a setup is a frequent learner and analyst need.

name: pandas-sandbox
description: Runs user-written Python/pandas code against an uploaded CSV in a sandbox and returns the printed output or resulting table.
example_prompt: Run this pandas snippet on my data.csv
loader_feasibility: pyodide executes Python with pandas/numpy fully in the browser sandbox; the CSV never leaves the page.
rationale: Lets learners practice the Pandas exercises from the harvested courses without a server or notebook.

name: entity-anonymizer
description: Replaces named entities with consistent placeholders (PERSON_1, ORG_2) to de-identify text while preserving structure.
example_prompt: Anonymize the names and companies in these interview notes but keep them consistent
loader_feasibility: transformers-js NER plus Rust→WASM consistent substitution map, fully browser-local. — model Xenova/bert-base-NER
rationale: Dataset de-identification is a core Comprehend/annotation workflow and benefits from staying offline.

name: pdf-object-analyzer
description: Maps a PDF's object tree and flags JavaScript, embedded files, OpenActions, and launch triggers.
example_prompt: Does this PDF contain JavaScript or embedded files? Show the suspicious objects
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the PDF object/xref structure is parsed from the upload; no rendering or network needed. — via lopdf crate
rationale: Malicious PDFs hide JS and launch actions that this surfaces locally, a Remnux pdfid/pdf-parser equivalent.

name: text-normalizer
description: Cleans and normalizes text: Unicode NFKC, case folding, accent stripping, whitespace and punctuation normalization.
example_prompt: Normalize this messy text for processing.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; Unicode transforms run client-side with no dependencies. — via unicode-normalization crate
rationale: Consistent normalization is the unglamorous-but-essential preprocessing step every NLP pipeline in the demand terms relies on.

name: search-index-builder
description: Builds a serialized full-text search index (inverted index JSON) from a folder of documents so a static site can search offline.
example_prompt: build a prebuilt search index from these markdown docs so my static site can search them client-side
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tokenizes, stems and emits a compact inverted-index JSON like lunr/tinysearch/minisearch produce; pure data transform.
rationale: Static-site authors repeatedly need a prebuilt index for offline search and currently reach for a Node toolchain to get it.

name: vcard-normalize
description: Normalizes names, phone numbers to E.164, and emails across a vCard address book for consistency.
example_prompt: Clean up the phone number formatting in my contacts
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM phone/email normalization, no network — via phonenumber crate
rationale: Consistent contact formatting improves search, dedupe, and cross-device sync.

name: regex-search
description: Searches pasted text or uploaded files with a regex or literal pattern and returns matching lines with line numbers, context, and highlights.
example_prompt: Find every line that matches TODO|FIXME in this file and show 2 lines of context
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using the regex crate; pure string scanning needs no network or server
rationale: Consolidates the demand behind ripgrep/ag/ack/sift/krep/hypergrep/ugrep/vgrep into the single most-requested search primitive.

name: csv-to-ledger
description: Converts a bank/credit-card CSV export into double-entry ledger/hledger journal entries with guessed accounts.
example_prompt: Convert this bank CSV into hledger journal entries
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — CSV parsing and ledger text emission run locally, keeping financial data on-device.
rationale: importing bank CSVs is the biggest friction in plain-text accounting and doing it locally keeps statements private.

name: text-pipeline-playground
description: Runs pasted text through a chain of Python transforms (split, grep, map, sort, regex) with live preview, like Ultimate Plumber.
example_prompt: Take this log text and pipe it through filters to get just the error lines, sorted and deduped
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs the user's Python transform steps on the pasted text in a sandbox, entirely client-side.
rationale: Ultimate Plumber's live-preview pipe building is genuinely useful and pyodide makes the same iteration possible in-browser.

name: dotenv-validator
description: Lints a .env file for duplicate keys, unquoted values with spaces, bad interpolation, and missing-variable references.
example_prompt: Check this .env file for problems
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parser plus lint rules; runs locally on the file text.
rationale: Broken .env files cause silent runtime failures and the checks are simple and offline.

name: file-compressor
description: Compresses or decompresses files with zstd, gzip, xz, or brotli.
example_prompt: Compress these files with zstd.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pure-Rust codec crates operate on in-memory buffers, no native libs. — via flate2 crate
rationale: The compression stage zbackup and bup are built around, useful standalone.

name: html-email-to-text
description: Converts an HTML email body into clean, readable plain text.
example_prompt: Convert this HTML email to plain text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM strips HTML and normalizes whitespace entirely client-side.
rationale: HTML emails are unreadable as source and people just want the plain version.

name: concat-files
description: Concatenates multiple uploaded text files into one document with clear per-file header separators.
example_prompt: Combine these files into one with filename headers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: joins user-provided file contents in-memory; files come from the browser file picker.
rationale: Merging a folder of files into a single readable blob (catdir) is a common prep step for review or sharing.

name: csv-derive-column
description: Add a computed column to a CSV from a formula referencing other columns.
example_prompt: Add a 'total' column = price * quantity to this CSV
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM expression evaluator over rows, offline.
rationale: Adding calculated fields is a core spreadsheet task not covered by clean/pivot/groupby.

name: csv-sample
description: Take a random, stratified, or top/bottom-N sample of rows from a large CSV.
example_prompt: Give me a random 100-row sample of this big CSV
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — reservoir sampling over parsed rows runs locally with no network.
rationale: Sampling big files for quick inspection is a frequent practical need.

name: colorize
description: Add realistic color to a black-and-white or grayscale photo using a colorization model.
example_prompt: colorize this old black and white photo
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime in-browser (DeOldify/colorization ONNX); inference runs client-side, no server.
rationale: Photo colorization is a crowd-pleasing AI feature and ONNX models exist that fit a browser runtime.

name: csv-to-pdf-table
description: Renders a CSV file as a formatted table inside a PDF.
example_prompt: Turn this CSV into a nicely formatted PDF table
loader_feasibility: pyodide — fpdf2 draws the CSV rows as a styled table client-side. — via printpdf crate
rationale: Producing a presentable PDF report from raw data is a common business reporting need.

name: video-thumbnail-extractor
description: Grabs still frames or a contact-sheet of thumbnails from a video at chosen times or intervals.
example_prompt: Pull a thumbnail every 10 seconds from this video as a contact sheet
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: frame extraction and tile filter render images locally.
rationale: mpv users take screenshots and want preview sheets; this does both without any install.

name: pdf-redact
description: Permanently redact a PDF by removing the underlying text/images beneath black boxes (true redaction).
example_prompt: redact the SSNs in this PDF so the text underneath is gone
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust PDF library to WASM — pure compute. — via lopdf crate
rationale: True redaction (not just an overlay) is critical for safely sharing documents.

name: data-chart
description: Generate a chart (line/bar/scatter/pie) from supplied data.
example_prompt: Plot a bar chart of these monthly sales: Jan 10, Feb 14, Mar 9
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs matplotlib in-browser and renders a PNG inline; no server-side plotting service. — via plotters crate
rationale: Turning numbers into visuals is a top data request and matplotlib in pyodide handles it locally.

name: js-css-minifier
description: Minifies JavaScript and CSS and reports before/after byte sizes.
example_prompt: Minify this CSS and tell me how much smaller it got
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a minifier crate runs the transform entirely in the browser.
rationale: Quick, build-step-free minification for one-off assets, in the vite-plus tooling space.

name: spreadsheet-to-sql
description: Reads an uploaded Excel (.xlsx/.xls) file and emits CREATE TABLE plus INSERT statements per sheet.
example_prompt: convert the first sheet of this Excel file into a SQL table
loader_feasibility: pyodide with pandas/openpyxl parses the workbook in WASM and generates SQL locally; the file is never uploaded. — via calamine crate
rationale: Business data lives in spreadsheets, and getting it into a real DB schema is exactly what driver/ORM users need first.

name: mesh-convert
description: Converts 3D meshes between Wavefront OBJ and STL (both directions, ASCII or binary STL output).
example_prompt: Convert this OBJ to a binary STL for printing
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM combining wavefront_rs + stl_io readers/writers; the whole conversion happens in memory in the browser. — via stl_io crate
rationale: OBJ↔STL conversion is a constant friction point in the 3D-printing pipeline and pairs naturally with the inspector tools.

name: format-js
description: Formats JavaScript/TypeScript to a Prettier-compatible style and returns the result.
example_prompt: Format this TypeScript snippet
loader_feasibility: Biome is a pure-Rust formatter with an official @biomejs WASM bundle, so it runs in the wasmi/WASM runtime. — via biome_js_formatter crate
rationale: JS/TS formatting is Prettier's primary use case and Biome makes it available as browser-local Rust→WASM.

name: audio-time-stretch
description: Speeds up or slows down audio without changing its pitch.
example_prompt: Slow this down 20% but keep the pitch.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's atempo filter time-stretches the decoded audio in-browser without altering pitch. — via symphonia crate
rationale: Musicians transcribing solos and learners slowing down speech rely on pitch-preserving tempo change.

name: image-pixelate
description: Applies a mosaic/pixelation effect with a chosen block size, optionally to a region.
example_prompt: Pixelate this image into 16px blocks.
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute averages each block in a shader on the GPU locally.
rationale: Pixelation is widely used to redact faces and sensitive details, which is exactly when staying browser-local matters.

name: gpx-merge
description: Merges multiple GPX files or tracks into one, ordered chronologically by timestamp.
example_prompt: Combine these three GPX files from my trip into a single track
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM parse-and-concatenate; deterministic and offline. — via gpx crate
rationale: Multi-day or multi-device logs arrive as separate files that users want stitched into one track.

name: video-to-hevc
description: Re-encodes a video to H.265/HEVC in an MP4 to roughly halve file size at the same visual quality.
example_prompt: Convert this to HEVC to shrink the file
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm includes libx265, performing the HEVC encode locally (slow but fully client-side).
rationale: HEVC cuts storage and bandwidth dramatically, a clear win for users archiving large footage.

name: phone-number-extractor
description: Finds phone numbers across common international formats and normalizes them to a canonical form.
example_prompt: Extract every phone number from this directory dump
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; format-aware pattern matching in-memory. — via phonenumber crate
rationale: Phone formats vary wildly and are tedious to collect and normalize manually.

name: json-to-yaml
description: Converts JSON into clean, indented YAML with proper multiline-string handling.
example_prompt: Convert this JSON to YAML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via serde_json + serde_yaml; serialization runs in the wasmi sandbox. — via serde_yaml crate
rationale: Reverse of yaml-to-json and avoids pasting secrets into web converters.

name: pronounceable-password-generator
description: Produces pronounceable, easy-to-type passwords from phoneme patterns with adjustable length and digit/symbol injection.
example_prompt: Make me 5 pronounceable 12-character passwords.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — syllable assembly plus CSPRNG, no external data.
rationale: A common request from people who hate random gibberish from their manager but still want decent entropy.

name: pdf-strip-metadata
description: Removes all metadata and hidden document info for privacy before sharing.
example_prompt: Strip all metadata from this PDF
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — lopdf clears the info dictionary and XMP stream in-browser. — via lopdf crate
rationale: Scrubbing author and software fingerprints is a privacy task that must not be uploaded.

name: passport-photo
description: Crop and format a portrait to passport/ID-photo specs (size, head ratio, plain white background).
example_prompt: Make a US passport photo from this selfie
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime segmentation for clean background + Rust resize/crop to spec; browser-local and private.
rationale: Passport/ID photo makers are high-demand and benefit hugely from staying private/on-device.

name: image-film-grain
description: Add adjustable film grain / analog noise to an image.
example_prompt: Add subtle film grain to this photo
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust noise overlay (or webgpu) in-browser. — via image crate
rationale: Common stylization opposite of denoise; not present in the filter set.

name: audio-highpass-filter
description: Applies a high-pass filter to remove low-frequency rumble and handling noise.
example_prompt: Cut everything below 80 Hz to kill the rumble in this recording.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg highpass biquad filter; runs locally.
rationale: Low-cut rumble removal is the first move in any voice cleanup chain and has no standalone tool.

name: spectral-subtraction-denoise
description: Removes steady background noise using a noise profile sampled from a silent region of the file.
example_prompt: Use the first second of silence as a noise print and subtract that hiss from the whole recording
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (or pyodide): STFT, estimate noise spectrum from the profile region, spectral-subtract per frame, ISTFT. — via rustfft crate
rationale: Noise-print subtraction is the classic, model-free denoiser and excels at constant hiss/hum/air conditioning.

name: iban-extractor-validator
description: Extracts IBANs from text and checks each with the ISO 13616 mod-97 checksum.
example_prompt: Find and validate the IBANs in this document
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans for IBAN patterns and runs the mod-97 check in-page; financial data never leaves the device.
rationale: Validating bank account numbers from invoices/statements is a real finance task best done locally.

name: prores-to-mp4
description: Compresses a large ProRes master into a shareable H.264 MP4.
example_prompt: Convert this ProRes file to a normal mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader — ProRes decode and H.264/AAC encode run entirely in wasm.
rationale: ProRes editing exports are huge and need a delivery-sized MP4 for sharing or upload.

name: av1-to-mp4
description: Transcodes an AV1 video into a broadly-compatible MP4 for devices that can't decode AV1.
example_prompt: This AV1 video won't play on my TV, convert it to mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader — native AV1 decode plus H.264 encode run locally in wasm.
rationale: AV1 downloads increasingly fail on older TVs/phones, so a compatibility transcode is genuinely needed.

name: json-to-json-schema
description: Infers a draft JSON Schema from one or more JSON examples.
example_prompt: Generate a JSON Schema from this example object
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM analyzing value types/required keys to emit a schema, no server.
rationale: Authoring JSON Schema by hand is painful; deriving a starting schema from real data is a high-value head start.

name: image-gaussian-blur
description: Applies a precise Gaussian blur at a chosen sigma for smoothing or background softening.
example_prompt: Blur this image with a radius of 8 pixels
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: separable Gaussian convolution, fully in-browser.
rationale: A reliable, exact-radius blur primitive people constantly need.

name: largest-files-finder
description: Scans a dropped folder and lists the top-N largest files with their full paths so you can quickly reclaim space.
example_prompt: Find the 20 biggest files in this folder I'm giving you.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; file sizes are read locally via the File System Access API and sorted in WASM — content never leaves the browser.
rationale: The core job of gdu/dua/ncdu (find the space hogs) maps directly to a fast, private, install-free browser tool.

name: image-color-quantizer
description: Reduces an image to a target number of distinct colors using median-cut/k-means for a flat poster or smaller-file look.
example_prompt: Reduce this image to 16 colors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: median-cut palette generation and nearest-color mapping run on the decoded buffer.
rationale: Color reduction shrinks files and creates a stylized look, and existing tools only check/inspect palettes rather than build them.

name: webp-to-png
description: Decodes a WebP image (lossy or lossless) and re-encodes it as a standard PNG.
example_prompt: Convert this .webp to PNG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the `image` crate decodes WebP and encodes PNG entirely in-memory, no server. — via image crate
rationale: WebP is everywhere on the web but many editors and tools still won't open it, so a one-click decode is in constant demand.

name: jwt-claims-diff
description: Decodes two JWTs and reports which claims were added, removed, or changed between them.
example_prompt: Compare the claims in these two JWT tokens
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — base64url decode + JSON claim comparison, tokens stay client-side
rationale: Debugging auth flows often means comparing token payloads, and doing it locally keeps tokens off any server.

name: video-beat-detector
description: Analyzes the audio track to detect tempo (BPM) and beat timestamps for syncing cuts to music.
example_prompt: Detect the BPM and beat times in this music video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg extracts audio; Pyodide runs librosa beat tracking entirely in the browser sandbox.
rationale: Editing cuts to the beat is a staple of montage editing, and a beat-time list lets editors place cuts precisely.

name: vcard-contact-extractor
description: Parses one or more vCard (.vcf) contact cards into a flat table of name, phone, email, org, and address fields.
example_prompt: Turn this exported .vcf contacts file into a CSV table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM text parsing of vCard grammar; runs entirely on the local file
rationale: Exported phone/email contacts are personal data users want flattened to a spreadsheet without a third-party converter site.

name: pdf-links-extract
description: Lists every hyperlink and its anchor text or page target found inside a PDF.
example_prompt: List all the links in this PDF
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM walks the PDF annotation dictionaries to read URI actions in-browser — via lopdf crate
rationale: Useful for auditing documents or harvesting references without opening and clicking each link.

name: video-remove-embedded-subs
description: Strips all embedded subtitle/caption streams from a video container while keeping video and audio intact.
example_prompt: Remove the baked-in subtitle tracks from this MKV
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's -sn / -map negation drops subtitle streams in ffmpeg.wasm via stream copy.
rationale: Unwanted forced or duplicate subtitle tracks are common in rips and break some playback setups.

name: audio-fade-tool
description: Adds fade-in and fade-out of specified lengths to an audio file.
example_prompt: Add a 2-second fade-in and 3-second fade-out to this song.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg afade filter; sample-level gain envelope in wasm.
rationale: Fades are a universal finishing touch and currently unavailable as a standalone tool.

name: rtf-to-text
description: Strips RTF control words and groups to produce plain Unicode text.
example_prompt: Extract the plain text from this RTF file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM RTF tokenizer handling \uN escapes and group nesting; local only.
rationale: RTF is still produced by legacy editors and clipboard exports and lacks a clean offline extractor.

name: gpx-to-csv
description: Extracts track/waypoint coordinates, elevation, and timestamps from a GPX file into CSV.
example_prompt: Convert this GPX track into a CSV of points
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing GPX XML (quick-xml); pure local parse. — via quick-xml crate
rationale: Athletes and surveyors analyze GPS tracks in spreadsheets and want it done without uploads.

name: mts-to-mp4
description: Converts AVCHD camcorder .mts/.m2ts footage into an editor-friendly MP4 container.
example_prompt: Convert my camcorder .mts files to mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm demuxes the AVCHD transport stream and remuxes H.264/AC-3 to MP4 in-browser.
rationale: AVCHD camcorders output .mts that most consumer software refuses, so this unblocks home video editing.

name: opus-to-wav
description: Decodes Opus voice notes to WAV/PCM for use in editors and DAWs.
example_prompt: decode this opus voice note to wav
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader's libopus decoder outputs PCM WAV in wasm.
rationale: Opus messenger recordings need to become PCM before they can be edited, trimmed, or imported into a DAW.

name: job-skill-extractor
description: Pulls technology and soft-skill keywords from a job description or resume using on-device NER/classification.
example_prompt: What skills does this job ad ask for?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a token-classification model in WASM on the input text locally. — model Xenova/bert-base-NER
rationale: Skill extraction powers matching and gap analysis and is a top job-data use case.

name: legal-doc-summarizer
description: Summarize long legal/case documents into a plain-language brief with key holdings.
example_prompt: Summarize this court judgment into a plain-English brief
loader_feasibility: transformers-js with chunked long-input summarization runs in-browser. — model Xenova/distilbart-cnn-6-6
rationale: 'Legal Case Reports Data Set' demand — summarizing dense legalese is high-value and privacy-sensitive (local-only).

name: vcard-contacts-converter
description: Parses, converts, splits, and merges vCard (.vcf) contact files, including vCard⇄CSV conversion and de-duplication.
example_prompt: Convert this contacts.vcf into a CSV and remove duplicates
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: text-based vCard/CSV parsing and serialization done locally, keeping contacts private.
rationale: Switching dialers/launchers means migrating contacts, and users want a private way to reshape .vcf exports without uploading them.

name: face-blur-video
description: Detects and blurs faces across the frames of a short video clip.
example_prompt: Blur the faces in this 15-second clip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes frames, onnx-runtime detects faces per frame, and ffmpeg re-encodes — all in the browser sandbox.
rationale: Sharing video of protests, kids, or bystanders demands face redaction, and existing tools require uploading sensitive footage to a server.

name: json-lint
description: Validates JSON syntax and pinpoints errors by line and column with fix suggestions.
example_prompt: Why is this JSON invalid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using a streaming JSON parser that surfaces precise error spans; local.
rationale: Syntax errors are the first wall users hit before schema validation even matters.

name: json-repair
description: Repairs malformed JSON by fixing trailing commas, single quotes, unquoted keys, and comments to produce valid output.
example_prompt: Fix this broken JSON so it parses
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with a lenient parser (sonic-rs/serde) — repair logic runs locally, no server
rationale: LLM and log output is full of nearly-valid JSON, and a local repair tool salvages it without re-running anything.

name: encrypted-zip
description: Packs files into a password-protected AES-encrypted zip archive, or extracts one, in memory.
example_prompt: Zip these files into an encrypted archive with password secret123
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the `zip` crate with AES encryption builds and reads the archive entirely client-side. — via zip crate
rationale: The closest browser-local analog to encfs — encrypt a bundle of files without uploading them anywhere.

name: llm-output-extractor
description: Extracts and repairs JSON embedded in messy LLM output (markdown fences, trailing commas, prose).
example_prompt: Pull the clean JSON out of this LLM response.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a tolerant JSON scanner/repairer running entirely client-side.
rationale: Recovering structured data from imperfect model output is a universal pain in structured-generation tooling.

name: postman-collection-converter
description: Converts a Postman or Insomnia collection export into curl commands or fetch/axios code.
example_prompt: Convert this Postman collection JSON into curl commands
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — reads the exported JSON and emits commands/code with no execution.
rationale: ATAC and similar clients import Postman/Insomnia, and many devs need to escape those formats into portable curl.

name: resume-to-json

name: cartoonify

name: video-autocrop-bars

name: text-to-sql

name: json-csv-converter
description: Convert a JSON array to CSV and CSV back to JSON.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: serde_json plus the csv crate, no backend.
rationale: Frequent data-wrangling step that should stay on the user's machine.

name: md5-hash
description: Computes the MD5 digest of text or a file.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the md-5 RustCrypto crate is pure-Rust and deterministic, running fully in wasmi.

name: url-codec

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — percent-encoding is a byte-level transform with no network access.

name: base64-text-converter
description: Encodes text to Base64 or decodes Base64 back to text, with URL-safe variant support.
example_prompt: base64 encode "hello world"
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure byte/string transform with the base64 crate, no I/O or network needed so it runs entirely in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: Base64 encode/decode is one of the most frequent developer lookups and is trivially correct offline.

name: audio-ringtone
description: Trim, fade, and export an audio clip as a phone ringtone (<=30s, m4r/mp3).

loader_feasibility: ffmpeg trim + afade + encode; browser-local.
rationale: Ringtone makers are a perennially popular one-step utility bundling trim/fade/encode.

name: png-to-jpg
description: Flattens transparency onto a chosen background color and encodes the result as JPEG.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the `image` crate composites and encodes JPEG in-memory — via image crate
rationale: Naive PNG→JPEG turns transparency black; correct background flattening is the actual user need.

name: webp-to-jpg
description: Decodes WebP images and saves them as widely-compatible JPG files.
example_prompt: Save this downloaded WebP as a JPG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM image crate decodes WebP and encodes JPEG locally
rationale: Many apps and printers still reject WebP, so converting back to JPG for compatibility is a recurring need.

name: html-table-from-csv
description: Converts pasted CSV into a semantic HTML <table> with thead/tbody, scope attributes, and optional caption.
example_prompt: Turn this CSV into an HTML table with a header row and a caption 'Sales'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — CSV parsing plus HTML generation with proper escaping, fully in-browser.
rationale: Pasting tabular data into pages is common and hand-built tables miss accessibility scopes/escaping.

name: mp3-to-opus
description: Re-encodes an MP3 to Opus at a chosen bitrate for much smaller files at similar quality.
example_prompt: convert this mp3 to opus to save space
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader decodes MP3 and encodes libopus in wasm.
rationale: Opus is dramatically more efficient than MP3, so shrinking voice/podcast libraries is a common ask.

name: vietnamese-english-translator
description: Translates between Vietnamese and English.
example_prompt: Translate this Vietnamese paragraph into English
loader_feasibility: transformers.js: an opus-mt / NLLB-200 distilled vi↔en model runs in-browser — model Xenova/opus-mt-vi-en
rationale: Offline Vietnamese↔English translation is broadly useful and avoids sending text to a server.

name: markdown-table-generator
description: Builds and aligns Markdown tables from CSV, TSV, or row input, with column alignment controls.
example_prompt: Turn this CSV into a nicely aligned markdown table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSV parse + table formatting; fully local
rationale: hand-writing markdown tables is tedious, and the mdt demand shows people want a dedicated table helper.

name: still-image-audio-video
description: Loops a single cover image for the full length of an audio file to produce a static-image music/podcast video for upload.

loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loops the image and copies the audio stream in the browser.
rationale: Musicians constantly need a 'static image + track' MP4 just to put audio on YouTube.

name: camt053-parse

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML walk of the Ntry/Amt/Bal tree; runs entirely in-browser keeping financial XML off any backend — via quick-xml crate
rationale: camt.053 is replacing MT940 across SEPA and there's no easy local viewer for its deeply nested XML.

name: har-request-extract
description: Extracts the request list (method, URL, status, size, timing) from a browser HAR capture.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON parse over the HAR, fully offline

name: env-template-generator
description: Generates a .env.example (keys, placeholder values, comments) from an existing .env or key list, stripping secret values.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; parses and rewrites locally so real secrets never leave the page.
rationale: Standard repo hygiene that also prevents committing real credentials.

name: data-anonymizer
description: Masks PII columns and generalizes quasi-identifiers, then reports the dataset's k-anonymity level.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM performs masking, generalization, and the k-anonymity computation in memory with no data leaving the browser.

name: keyword-extractor
description: Pulls the most important keywords and phrases from a document.

loader_feasibility: transformers-js embeddings rank candidate phrases (KeyBERT-style) entirely client-side. — model Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
rationale: Keyword extraction supports SEO, tagging, and indexing and is fully offline-capable.

name: loudness-matched-ab-prep

rationale: Removes the louder-sounds-better bias that ruins informal A/B listening tests.

name: calendar-freebusy-overlap
description: Compares two ICS calendars and finds the common free time windows.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses both calendars and intersects busy intervals locally; calendar data stays private.
rationale: Finding a mutual opening between two calendars is a real scheduling task distinct from event-by-event diffing.

name: video-audio-sync-offset-finder
description: Cross-correlates the audio of two videos to find the time offset that best aligns them.
example_prompt: Find how many milliseconds the audio is offset between these two captures
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg extracts PCM and Rust→WASM (or pyodide numpy) runs cross-correlation, all client-side.
rationale: An exact audio offset lets you re-sync two recordings of the same event automatically.

name: video-speech-segment-detector
description: Runs voice-activity detection on the audio and outputs timestamps of speech vs non-speech segments (no transcription).

name: har-body-stripper

example_prompt: Strip the response bodies out of this HAR file to make it smaller
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON walk over the HAR structure; runs fully in-browser.
rationale: HAR files are huge and contain secrets in bodies, so trimming them before sharing is essential and safer done locally.

name: document-skew-detector
description: Estimates the skew/rotation angle of a scanned document or text image.
example_prompt: What angle is this scanned page skewed by?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM uses projection-profile/Hough-style angle scoring on decoded pixels in-browser.
rationale: Knowing the skew angle is the prerequisite for deskewing scans before OCR.

name: downsample-timeseries
description: Reduces a large time-series to a target point count using LTTB while preserving visual shape, returning the downsampled data.
example_prompt: Downsample this 50k-point sensor log to 1000 points for plotting
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs the Largest-Triangle-Three-Buckets algorithm in-sandbox.
rationale: Solves the dygraphs large-series problem so big datasets stay chartable in the browser.

name: health-record-summarizer
description: Summarizes a pasted clinical note, discharge summary, or visit record into a short plain-language overview.
example_prompt: Summarize this discharge summary in a few bullet points
loader_feasibility: transformers-js (local summarization model in-browser) — the model runs client-side so the medical text never leaves the device. — model Xenova/distilbart-cnn-6-6
rationale: Aggregated health records like Fasten's are sensitive, and on-device summarization makes them readable without a privacy tradeoff.

name: office-macro-extractor
description: Extracts and de-obfuscates VBA macros from OLE and OOXML Office documents to expose malicious code.

loader_feasibility: pyodide: runs oletools/olevba in the in-browser Python sandbox against the uploaded document, no server.

name: browser-artifact-parser

name: regex-to-json

name: json-anonymize
description: Redacts or pseudonymizes PII fields (emails, names, phone numbers, IDs) in a JSON document using configurable field rules.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with regex/heuristic redaction over serde_json; sensitive data never leaves the browser.
rationale: Directly realizes 'jsonymize' and is especially valuable browser-local since the whole point is not sending PII to a server.

name: note-action-extractor
description: Scans free-form notes for action markers (TODO, FIXME, AI:, action:) and extracts them into a clean task list.
example_prompt: Pull all the action items out of these meeting notes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pattern matching over text lines, deterministic.
rationale: Turning memo-style notes into actionable tasks is the bridge between note tools (memo, geek-life) and todo tools.

name: spending-categorizer

rationale: Finance Tracker/gocost demand plus privacy concerns make a local-only spend categorizer genuinely valuable.

name: data-summary

loader_feasibility: pyodide runs pandas describe()/info() in-browser; returns a markdown table.
rationale: Quick data profiling is the first thing analysts do and pandas does it locally and reliably.

name: subtitle-translator

name: template-renderer

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — uses an embedded template engine (minijinja/handlebars), no network. — via minijinja crate

name: diceware-passphrase

rationale: Distinct from manual image-crop; auto-trim is a high-frequency cleanup step.

name: sql-injection-scanner

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — line-split parse with serde_json, streaming-friendly and fully local. — via serde_json crate

name: encoded-payload-decoder

name: csv-eda

name: mail-merge

description: Embeds subtitle tracks into a video as soft subs or extracts existing subtitle streams.
