loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: subtitle stream muxing/demuxing is a container operation done in WASM on the local file.
rationale: mpv viewers want soft-subbed files; muxing subs in without a desktop tool is genuinely useful.

name: bip39-mnemonic-validate
description: Validates a BIP39 mnemonic's checksum and word list and shows the recovered entropy in hex.
example_prompt: is this seed phrase valid: legal winner thank year wave sausage worth useful legal winner thank yellow
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — checksum/wordlist math only, fully offline. — via bip39 crate
rationale: People routinely need to confirm a backed-up phrase is intact without exposing it to a server.

name: openapi-to-typescript
description: Generates TypeScript interfaces and request/response types from an OpenAPI spec.
example_prompt: generate TypeScript types from this openapi.yaml
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse the spec and emit TS source text, no codegen server.
rationale: Typed API clients are a daily need and this avoids running a Node codegen toolchain.

name: folder-size-treemap
description: Renders an interactive treemap of a dropped folder so you can see at a glance which subfolders and files eat the most space.
example_prompt: Show me a treemap of where the space goes in this Downloads folder I'm dropping in.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; the browser File System Access API / <input webkitdirectory> enumerates every file and its size client-side, and the WASM tool aggregates the size tree — no upload, no server.
rationale: Treemap disk-usage analyzers (diskus, dua, gdu, vizex, diskroaster) are repeatedly demanded yet nobody offers one that runs locally in a tab on a folder you choose.

name: phone-e164-normalize
description: Normalizes free-form phone numbers to E.164 given a default country, flagging ones that can't be parsed.
example_prompt: Standardize these US phone numbers to E.164
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with a phonenumber crate/metadata bundled; fully offline.
rationale: Phone columns are a mess of formats and consistent E.164 is required for dedupe and messaging.

name: import-graph-extractor
description: Extracts the import/require/use dependency graph from one or more pasted source files and lists who depends on what.
example_prompt: Build the import graph for these Python files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses import statements with pure text/regex analysis client-side.
rationale: Understanding module coupling before a refactor is a common analysis task that needs no server.

name: csv-column-type-validator
description: Validates that each CSV column matches a declared type (int, float, date, bool, enum) and lists the offending cells.
example_prompt: Check that column 3 is all integers and column 5 is ISO dates in this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: per-cell type parsing is pure computation on the uploaded text.
rationale: Type drift in one cell corrupts whole pipelines and there's no lightweight way to assert column types client-side.

name: json-array-to-jsonl
description: Splits a single JSON array into one compact JSON object per line (JSONL).
example_prompt: Convert this JSON array into JSONL
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM streaming array elements to per-line serialization; deterministic and offline.
rationale: Many bulk-load APIs (Elasticsearch, OpenAI fine-tune) require JSONL but data arrives as a JSON array.

name: png-chunk-stripper
description: Losslessly strips ancillary PNG chunks (time, text, gamma, profiles) to shrink the file without touching pixels.
example_prompt: Remove all the non-essential chunks from this PNG to make it smaller
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: walk chunks, keep only critical ones, rewrite — pure byte surgery.
rationale: Quick lossless size win that also removes editor-injected metadata.

name: audio-edge-silence-trimmer
description: Removes only the leading and trailing silence below a threshold, leaving the body untouched.
example_prompt: Trim the dead air off the start and end of this recording
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — `silenceremove` configured for start/stop edges only; runs in ffmpeg.wasm.
rationale: Tight head/tail trimming is the cleanup people want before publishing a clip, distinct from detecting or extracting interior silence.

name: dotenv-normalizer
description: Sorts, dedupes, groups by prefix, and aligns a .env file, flagging duplicate keys.
example_prompt: clean up and sort this .env file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — line parsing and string formatting; no secrets leave the browser.
rationale: Keeps env files tidy and surfaces duplicate keys that silently override.

name: duplicate-row-finder
description: Detects exact and near-duplicate rows in a table, groups them, and reports which key columns drive the duplication.
example_prompt: Find duplicate and near-duplicate rows in this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM hashes and fuzzy-compares rows in memory with no external service
rationale: Hidden duplicates inflate counts and corrupt joins; surfacing them is a common data-cleaning inspection.

name: sprite-sheet-from-video
description: Extracts evenly spaced frames from a clip and packs them into a single sprite-sheet/atlas image plus a CSS keyframe snippet.
example_prompt: Make a 5x5 sprite sheet from this short clip for a CSS animation
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg samples frames and tiles them; a plain-Rust step emits the matching CSS, all in-browser.
rationale: Frame atlases drive lightweight web/game animations and differ from a preview contact sheet by being playback-ready.

name: multi-photo-scan-splitter
description: Detects multiple photos placed on one flatbed scan, then auto-straightens and crops each into a separate image.
example_prompt: I scanned four old photos at once — split them into separate files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: background thresholding plus connected-component/contour detection on the pixel buffer runs on CPU; an optional onnx edge model can refine borders.
rationale: Digitizing photo albums by scanning several at once is hugely common and tediously manual today, so an auto-splitter is a big time-saver.

name: otpauth-migration-decoder
description: Decode a Google Authenticator otpauth-migration:// export payload into individual otpauth:// URIs for each account.
example_prompt: decode this otpauth-migration link into separate otp uris
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM base64 + protobuf (prost) decode of the migration payload; fully offline so 2FA secrets stay on-device.
rationale: Escaping Google Authenticator's bulk-export format into portable per-account URIs is a common, fiddly migration need the existing QR tools don't cover.

name: image-canvas-resize
description: Changes the canvas dimensions without scaling pixels, adding margin or cropping with a chosen anchor and fill color.
example_prompt: Extend this image's canvas to 1200x630 anchored top-left on black
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: allocate a new canvas of target size and copy the source at the anchor offset — no resampling, no server.
rationale: Designers frequently need exact canvas sizes (OG images, ad slots) without distorting the artwork.

name: jpeg-lossless-rotate
description: Rotates a JPEG by 90/180/270 degrees losslessly via DCT-block transposition, no re-compression.
example_prompt: Rotate this JPEG 90 degrees clockwise without quality loss
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: operate on the entropy-coded DCT blocks (jpegtran-style) entirely in-memory.
rationale: Lossless rotation preserves quality that a decode/re-encode would degrade — a meaningful distinction users want.

name: sas7bdat-to-csv
description: Reads proprietary SAS .sas7bdat binary data files and exports their rows and typed columns to CSV.
example_prompt: Open this .sas7bdat file and save it as CSV
loader_feasibility: pyodide: pandas.read_sas runs entirely in the WASM Python sandbox with no SAS install or server.
rationale: Researchers receiving SAS datasets have no easy offline way to read them without licensed SAS; the backlog only covers the XPT transport format, not native sas7bdat.

name: js-object-to-json
description: Converts a JavaScript object literal (unquoted keys, single quotes, trailing commas) into valid JSON.
example_prompt: turn this JS object I copied from code into proper JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the relaxed object syntax and emits strict JSON without eval
rationale: Copying a config object out of source code into a JSON file is a daily friction point.

name: ken-burns-slideshow-video
description: Builds a Ken Burns slideshow video from a set of images, applying slow pan-and-zoom to each with crossfades.
example_prompt: Turn these 8 photos into a Ken Burns slideshow, 4 seconds each, with crossfades, 1080p
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg 'zoompan' plus xfade transitions process the user's images entirely in the WASM ffmpeg loader.
rationale: Photo-to-video slideshows are one of the most common consumer video tasks and fully local-doable.

name: exif-gps-presence-checker
description: Quickly reports whether an image embeds GPS location coordinates, without revealing the coordinates themselves unless asked.
example_prompt: Does this picture have my location in it?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the EXIF GPS IFD presence flag locally. — via kamadak-exif crate
rationale: A focused yes/no privacy gate is faster than a full metadata dump for the most common concern.

name: wav-to-ogg-vorbis
description: Encodes WAV PCM into Ogg Vorbis at a selected quality for broad open-format playback.
example_prompt: convert this wav to ogg vorbis q6
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader's libvorbis encoder writes Ogg Vorbis client-side.
rationale: Vorbis remains the required audio format for many games and open-source apps that won't take WAV.

name: tsv-to-json
description: Converts a TSV table into a JSON array of objects keyed by the header row.
example_prompt: convert this TSV to JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — header/row parsing and JSON serialization are pure in-memory operations.
rationale: Exact demand term; bridges spreadsheet copy-paste into API-ready JSON without uploading data anywhere.

name: ini-env-diff
description: Diffs two .env or .ini config files key-by-key, flagging added, removed, and changed settings.
example_prompt: What's different between my staging and prod .env files?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM key/value parser; set comparison over parsed maps runs locally
rationale: Config drift between environments causes outages; a side-by-side key diff is a fast sanity check.

name: before-after-slider
description: Produces a self-contained interactive HTML/SVG before-after slider that wipes between two images.
example_prompt: Make a draggable before/after slider from these two photos
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM base64-embeds both images into a static HTML slider, no hosting needed
rationale: Interactive wipe sliders are far more convincing than a static diff and are trivial to share.

name: apache-log-parser
description: Parses Apache/Nginx common and combined access log lines into fields (IP, method, path, status, UA).
example_prompt: Break these access log lines into structured fields
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: regex against the known log grammars, runs on pasted log text.
rationale: Quick ad-hoc analysis of access logs shouldn't require shipping logs to an external parser.

name: video-silence-detector
description: Scans the audio track and outputs a timestamped list of silent segments (start/end/duration) above a chosen threshold.
example_prompt: Find all the silent gaps in this video and list their timestamps
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader's silencedetect filter emits segment timestamps to the log, parsed client-side.
rationale: A read-only silence map lets editors locate dead air and plan cuts without destructively trimming like a trimmer tool would.

name: video-audio-compress-dynamics
description: Applies dynamic-range compression to a video's audio so quiet and loud passages sit closer together.
example_prompt: Compress the dynamic range of this video so the quiet parts are easier to hear
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's acompressor filter runs in ffmpeg.wasm with all DSP done client-side.
rationale: Interviews and lectures with wildly varying levels become listenable after a single compression pass.

name: audio-bleep-censor
description: Mutes or bleeps specified time regions to censor words or sensitive content.
example_prompt: Bleep out the audio from 0:42 to 0:44 in this clip.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg volume enable-window plus optional tone overlay; client-side.
rationale: Region censoring is a common, currently-unserved editing task for podcasts and shared recordings.

name: markdown-table-formatter
description: Reflows a markdown table so columns are padded and aligned, fixing ragged pipes and inconsistent spacing.
example_prompt: Clean up the alignment of this messy markdown table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM column-width computation and re-render; runs locally
rationale: Hand-edited markdown tables drift out of alignment quickly, and a formatter makes them readable in source form.

name: content-trim-bounds-detector
description: Finds the tight bounding box of non-background/non-transparent content and reports suggested trim margins.
example_prompt: What's the content bounding box for trimming this PNG?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans decoded pixels for the content extent against the background locally.
rationale: Auto-trim bounds eliminate wasted padding in icons and sprites.

name: chord-recognizer
description: Detects a time-stamped chord sequence (major/minor/7th) from a recording.
example_prompt: Give me the chords for this guitar recording
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM templates chroma frames against chord profiles with a smoothing pass, all local
rationale: Auto chord charts save musicians hours of transcription by ear.

name: statistical-test-runner
description: Runs hypothesis tests (t-test, ANOVA, Mann-Whitney, chi-square, normality) on pasted or uploaded data.
example_prompt: Run a one-way ANOVA on these three groups of numbers
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs scipy.stats locally on the parsed data with no server round-trip.
rationale: On-device significance testing is a constant analyst need and scipy makes it fully browser-local.

name: tabular-predictor
description: Trains a gradient-boosted model on an uploaded CSV and predicts a chosen target column (auto-detecting classification vs regression).
example_prompt: Train a model on this CSV to predict the 'churn' column and score these new rows.
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs scikit-learn HistGradientBoosting (the in-browser equivalent of XGBoost/LightGBM) plus pandas entirely in WASM; no data leaves the device.
rationale: Directly serves the dominant XGBoost/LightGBM/PerpetualBooster/pytorch_tabular demand with a privacy-preserving local trainer.

name: big-csv-profiler
description: Streams a very large CSV in chunks to compute column stats (count, min/max, mean, nulls, cardinality) without loading it all at once.
example_prompt: Profile this 200MB CSV's columns without choking the browser
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM processes the file as a stream, keeping memory bounded locally
rationale: Translates the Dask 'data at scale' demand into a practical browser-local out-of-core profiler.

name: sd-png-metadata-reader
description: Reads Stable Diffusion generation parameters (prompt, seed, model, sampler) embedded in a PNG's text chunks.
example_prompt: What prompt and settings made this PNG?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the PNG tEXt/iTXt chunks; no decoding of pixels needed.
rationale: InvokeAI and other generators bury full recipes in PNG metadata, and reproducing or auditing an image starts with reading them.

name: text-secret-decrypt
description: Decrypts an armored password-protected ciphertext block back to readable text.
example_prompt: Decrypt this armored secret block, the password is swordfish
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; decrypt happens locally in the wasmi sandbox
rationale: Completes the offline secret-sharing loop with the text encryptor.

name: otpauth-qr-generator
description: Renders a scannable QR-code image from an otpauth:// URI or its individual fields for importing into an authenticator app.
example_prompt: Make a QR code for otpauth://totp/Mail:bob?secret=JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (qrcode crate → PNG) — pure encoding to image bytes, fully offline.
rationale: The reverse of the decoder, needed to push a stored secret back onto a phone authenticator without trusting a web QR site with the secret.

name: obs-recording-remux
description: Remuxes an OBS .mkv or .flv recording into a streamable .mp4 without re-encoding.
example_prompt: Convert my OBS .mkv recording to mp4 without re-encoding
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (compiled to WASM) does a stream-copy container remux in-browser — fast and lossless.
rationale: OBS records to MKV/FLV by default and the constant pain point is getting a shareable MP4 without a slow re-encode.

name: glb-gltf-packer
description: Packs separate glTF JSON + bin + textures into a single GLB, or unpacks a GLB back into glTF parts.
example_prompt: Pack these glTF and bin files into one GLB
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: binary chunk (re)assembly, pure byte ops.
rationale: Switching between GLB and loose glTF is a routine asset-pipeline chore with no good in-browser tool.

name: totp-secret-setup
description: Creates a random TOTP secret with its otpauth:// enrollment URI for authenticator apps.
example_prompt: make a new totp secret for my app login
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (CSPRNG + Base32 + otpauth URI assembly); secret generated locally.
rationale: Enrolling 2FA requires a freshly generated secret that should originate on the user's device, not a server log.

name: email-list-cleaner
description: Validates, normalizes, lowercases, and de-duplicates an email address list, flagging malformed entries.
example_prompt: Clean and dedupe this list of email addresses
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM syntax validation and dedup — runs locally with no deliverability lookup.
rationale: Bounce-prone lists hurt every Mailchimp/AWeber sender, and cleaning them locally keeps PII off third parties.

name: dicom-anonymizer
description: Strips patient-identifying tags (name, ID, dates, institution) from a DICOM file and returns a sanitized copy safe to share.
example_prompt: Remove all the patient info from this DICOM file so I can share it.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — dicom-rs rewrites the data set in-browser; the original PHI is never transmitted anywhere. — via dicom crate
rationale: De-identifying scans for research or teaching is a common, compliance-sensitive task that is only truly safe when done locally.

name: log-merger
description: Interleaves multiple pasted log files into one unified timeline, sorted by parsed timestamps with source tags.
example_prompt: Merge these three service logs into one timeline ordered by timestamp
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — timestamp parsing and k-way merge are pure in-memory text operations.
rationale: multitail's core value is watching many logs together; merging them chronologically is exactly what's needed to debug cross-service issues.

name: search-in-documents
description: Searches a regex or keyword inside PDFs, DOCX, EPUB, and ZIP archives, returning matches with the document and page/section they came from.
example_prompt: Search this PDF and the docx for every mention of 'indemnity' and show where they appear
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM combining the zip crate plus PDF/Office text extraction; all parsing runs in the wasmi sandbox client-side
rationale: Directly delivers ripgrep-all's killer feature — searching binary document formats — which nothing else in the catalog does.

name: csv-to-sqlite
description: Builds a downloadable SQLite database file from one or more CSV/JSON tables with inferred types.
example_prompt: Turn these three CSVs into a single .sqlite database
loader_feasibility: pyodide's sqlite3 creates the database file in the browser sandbox and returns it for download.
rationale: Directly serves the Turso/libSQL/TrailBase audience that wants portable SQLite without standing up a server.

name: 7z-create
description: Packs uploaded files into a .7z archive with optional LZMA2 compression level and password (AES-256) protection.
example_prompt: Compress these files into a password-protected 7z
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sevenz-rust's LZMA encoder and AES support run in WASM with no native dependencies. — via sevenz-rust crate
rationale: Creating encrypted 7z archives client-side keeps files private and completes the 7z round-trip the demand term implies.

name: flashcard-generator
description: Turns study text into question-and-answer flashcards for spaced repetition.
example_prompt: Make flashcards from these notes on Rust ownership.
loader_feasibility: transformers-js for question generation plus local extractive logic; the model runs in-browser.
rationale: Self-study from Rust books is a stated demand and flashcards are a proven learning aid.

name: pdf-flatten-form
description: Flattens form fields and annotations into static, non-editable page content.
example_prompt: Flatten this filled PDF form so the fields can't be edited
loader_feasibility: pyodide — pypdf merges field appearances into the page content stream in-browser.
rationale: Locking a completed form before sending it is a routine step many tools get wrong.

name: duplicate-track-finder
description: Finds duplicate songs across uploaded files by comparing tags, durations, and audio similarity, suggesting which to keep.
example_prompt: Find duplicate songs in this batch of files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: fuzzy tag matching plus lightweight audio-signature comparison on decoded samples runs locally with no DB lookups.
rationale: De-duplicating a messy library is a headline beets feature and a top pain point for cmus/mpd users.

name: jwt-decoder
description: Decodes a JWT into its header and payload, shows expiry/issued times, and optionally verifies an HMAC signature.
example_prompt: Decode this JWT and tell me when it expires
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; base64url decoding and HMAC verification are local crypto operations.
rationale: Developers inspect tokens constantly and pasting them into a random website is a real security risk.

name: data-reshape
description: Parses JSON/YAML/CSV/XML and reshapes it with a query/template into a new structured output.
example_prompt: Flatten this YAML and output the names and emails as CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (serde multi-format readers + a template/filter engine) runs entirely client-side (BaFi-style universal parse+transform).
rationale: A jq-like transform that works across formats covers a huge swath of everyday data-wrangling needs.

name: email-auto-tagger
description: Auto-tags emails by topic or category using zero-shot classification against labels you provide.
example_prompt: Tag these emails as work, personal, or finance
loader_feasibility: transformers-js zero-shot model (bart-mnli) classifies locally. — model Xenova/bart-large-mnli
rationale: Gives Notmuch-style tagging without writing rules or running a mail server.

name: json-format
description: Pretty-prints, minifies, or sorts keys of JSON, with optional duplicate-key and trailing-comma repair.
example_prompt: Pretty-print this JSON with 2-space indent and sort all keys alphabetically.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM serde_json parse/serialize; fully local.
rationale: JsonGenius-style formatting/repair is the highest-traffic JSON chore and ideal for offline use with sensitive data.

name: password-pwned-check
description: Check whether a password appears in known breaches via the Have I Been Pwned k-anonymity range API.
example_prompt: Has the password 'hunter2' been leaked in any breach?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM computes SHA-1, then a single fetch sends only the 5-char hash prefix to the free no-key HIBP range endpoint; runs client-side.
rationale: Hugely popular security check, privacy-preserving by design, and trivially browser-local with no API key.

name: csv-encoding-fix
description: Repair a broken CSV: detect the delimiter, fix mojibake/encoding (Latin-1↔UTF-8), and normalize line endings.
example_prompt: This CSV has garbled accents and weird separators — fix it
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM encoding detection/transcode; offline.
rationale: Encoding/delimiter breakage is one of the most common real CSV headaches.

name: audio-joiner
description: Concatenates multiple audio files into one, optionally gapless or with crossfade.
example_prompt: Join these tracks into one continuous gapless mix
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: concat and crossfade filters run client-side on the uploaded files.
rationale: DJ-style mixes, audiobook stitching, and gapless album joins are common requests the TUI players can't do.

name: sticker-maker
description: Turn a photo into a die-cut sticker: cut out the subject and add a white contour outline on a transparent background.
example_prompt: Make a sticker out of my dog in this photo
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime segmentation (shared with background-remove) + Rust outline/contour; browser-local.
rationale: Die-cut sticker makers (Telegram/WhatsApp style) are very popular and add the distinctive contour border beyond a plain cutout.

name: budget-split
description: Split take-home pay into the 50/30/20 (or custom) needs/wants/savings buckets.
example_prompt: Split $4200 monthly income into 50/30/20
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM arithmetic, offline.
rationale: A hugely popular personal-budgeting framework with no dedicated tool.

name: thai-english-translator
description: Translates between Thai and English.
example_prompt: Translate this Thai paragraph to English
loader_feasibility: transformers.js: an opus-mt / NLLB-200 distilled th↔en model runs in-browser — model Xenova/nllb-200-distilled-600M
rationale: Offline, private Thai↔English translation is valuable for travelers and anyone handling confidential text.

name: ts-to-mp4
description: Converts an MPEG transport stream (.ts) capture into a seekable MP4 by stream-copying into the new container.
example_prompt: Make this .ts recording into a normal mp4 I can scrub
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm demuxes MPEG-TS and writes MP4 with stream copy, fixing timestamps locally.
rationale: DVR and IPTV captures land as .ts files that don't scrub well until rewrapped to MP4.

name: ogg-to-mp3
description: Converts Ogg Vorbis files to MP3.
example_prompt: convert this ogg file to mp3
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader decodes Vorbis and encodes MP3 fully in wasm.
rationale: Ogg is common from open-source games and Bandcamp but poorly supported on phones and car stereos.

name: wma-to-mp3
description: Converts legacy Windows Media Audio (.wma) files to MP3.
example_prompt: convert my old wma music files to mp3
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader includes WMA v1/v2 decoders and MP3 encoder, no server.
rationale: Old ripped CD libraries are full of WMA that modern phones and streaming-sync tools can't play.

name: wav-to-mp3-encoder
description: Encodes a WAV into an MP3 at a chosen bitrate or VBR quality.
example_prompt: Encode this WAV to a 192 kbps MP3
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (wasm) bundles a lame-style MP3 encoder, so encoding runs entirely in the browser.
rationale: Producing a shareable, small MP3 from a working WAV is one of the most common audio export needs.

name: avif-to-png
description: Decodes a modern AVIF image and writes a lossless PNG copy.
example_prompt: I downloaded an .avif but my editor can't open it — make it a PNG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the `image` crate's dav1d-backed AVIF decoder runs client-side.
rationale: AVIF adoption is rising fast while desktop app support lags, so users frequently hit files they can't open.

name: whitespace-collapser
description: Collapses runs of internal spaces and tabs to a single space and trims each line, optionally preserving code indentation.
example_prompt: Clean up all the double spaces and stray tabs in this text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: single-pass regex/scan over the string, fully local
rationale: Pasted-from-PDF and copy-merged text is riddled with irregular spacing that needs one-click normalizing.

name: flac-to-wav-decoder
description: Losslessly decodes a FLAC file into PCM WAV.
example_prompt: Turn this lossless.flac into a wav
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader decodes FLAC frames to PCM and writes WAV client-side; no quality loss — via claxon crate
rationale: Many editors and embedded players accept WAV but not FLAC, and the decode is exact and offline.

name: m4v-to-mp4
description: Renames and remuxes Apple's .m4v container into a standard .mp4, stripping iTunes-specific atoms if present.
example_prompt: Change this .m4v file into a regular mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM copies the H.264/AAC streams into an MP4 container locally. — via mp4 crate
rationale: M4V is essentially MP4 but some players reject the extension/atoms, so a clean remux unlocks playback.

name: targz-tool
description: Creates or extracts .tar.gz / .tgz archives from uploaded files or an uploaded tarball.
example_prompt: pack these files into a tar.gz
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (tar + flate2/miniz) streams bytes in memory; gzip and tar are pure computation, no OS needed. — via flate2 crate
rationale: tar.gz is the Unix archive format people actually ship, and no major browser tool produces it client-side.

name: json-to-sql-insert
description: Generate parameterized or literal SQL INSERT statements from a JSON array of rows.
example_prompt: Make INSERT statements for this JSON array targeting a 'users' table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — schema inference and SQL string building over in-memory rows. — via serde_json crate
rationale: Seeding a database from JSON sample data is common and generating safe INSERTs by hand is tedious and error-prone.

name: social-image-resize
description: Crop and resize one image to all the standard sizes for a chosen platform (Instagram post/story, Twitter, LinkedIn, etc.) at once.
example_prompt: resize this banner for Instagram feed, story, and a Twitter header
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM resize with preset aspect ratios; local. — via image crate
rationale: Multi-platform sizing is a daily social workflow; responsive-images outputs arbitrary sizes, not platform presets.

name: photo-restore
description: Restore old or damaged photos: reduce scratches/blur and enhance faces.
example_prompt: Restore this scanned old family photo

name: debt-payoff

name: video-background-remove

name: ui-screen-recording-to-gif
description: Converts a screen-recording video into an optimized, palette-reduced GIF for READMEs and demos.

loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — palettegen/paletteuse and fps/scale filters run in the WASM ffmpeg build.

name: avi-to-mp4
description: Converts a legacy AVI file to MP4, transcoding old codecs like DivX/Xvid/MJPEG to H.264 as required.

name: wmv-to-mp4
description: Transcodes a Windows Media WMV/VC-1 file into an H.264/AAC MP4 for cross-platform playback.
example_prompt: Convert this old .wmv to mp4 so it plays on my Mac
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm decodes WMV2/VC-1 and WMA and re-encodes to H.264/AAC in the browser.

name: youtube-thumbnail-generator
description: Builds a YouTube-style thumbnail image from a chosen video frame plus large outlined headline text and an accent bar.
example_prompt: Make a clickbait thumbnail from the frame at 0:30 with the text 'I TRIED IT'
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg extracts the frame and composites drawtext with outline/box styling, fully local.
rationale: Every video upload needs a thumbnail and this produces one without a design app.

name: resume-scaffolder
description: Builds a clean, print-ready résumé (HTML) from structured inputs for experience, education, and skills.
example_prompt: Scaffold a one-page résumé from my job history and skills
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: renders structured input into a styled HTML layout, printable to PDF locally.
rationale: People want a fast, private résumé starting point without uploading their work history to a site.

name: mpeg-to-mp4
description: Converts legacy MPEG-1/MPEG-2 program-stream files (.mpg/.mpeg) into an H.264/AAC MP4.
example_prompt: Convert this old .mpg video to mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM decodes MPEG-1/2 and re-encodes to MP4 locally with no server.
rationale: Old .mpg archives are common and need re-encoding to play and share on current platforms.

name: json-query
description: Query/transform JSON with a jq-style filter expression.
example_prompt: From this JSON, get .users[].email — <json>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust (jaq, a jq implementation) compiles to WASM and runs filters locally. — via jaq-core crate
rationale: jq-style extraction is a beloved power-user tool and jaq makes it browser-local.

name: hl7-v2-parse
description: Parses a pipe-delimited HL7 v2.x message into named segments, fields, and components (MSH, PID, OBX, etc.).
example_prompt: Parse this HL7 message and show me the PID and OBX segments as a table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string splitting on segment/field/component separators; pure text parsing with no network, ideal for privacy-sensitive health data that should never leave the browser
rationale: Clinicians and integration engineers constantly hand-decode HL7 and a local-only parser keeps PHI off any server.

name: ioc-extractor
description: Pulls IPs, domains, URLs, file hashes, emails, and CVE IDs out of free-form text or reports.
example_prompt: Extract all indicators of compromise from this incident report
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: regex/parsing over pasted text, fully local with no lookups. — via regex crate
rationale: Harvesting IOCs from reports is a constant IntelMQ-style chore that parses instantly in-browser.

name: data-aggregate
description: Group records by a column and aggregate (count/sum/avg/min/max) without writing SQL.
example_prompt: group this CSV by region and sum the revenue
loader_feasibility: pyodide — pandas groupby runs in the in-browser Python sandbox on the uploaded file.
rationale: RecordStream/rq/csvtk aggregation demand; group-and-sum is the most common analytics ask, made SQL-free.

name: directory-tree-view
description: Prints a clean indented tree of a chosen folder with per-entry sizes and counts, like a size-annotated `tree`.
example_prompt: Give me a tree view of this project folder with file sizes next to each entry.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; folder contents and sizes come from the File System Access API client-side and the tool formats the tree string in WASM.
rationale: erdtree-style annotated trees are a popular ask and trivially browser-local once the folder is enumerated.

name: toxicity-detect
description: Score text for toxicity, insults, threats, and hate so it can be flagged or moderated before posting.
example_prompt: is this comment toxic? <paste comment>
loader_feasibility: transformers-js (toxic-bert / unbiased-toxic-roberta); classification model runs in-browser. — model Xenova/toxic-bert
rationale: Content-moderation scoring is a common need for forums and UGC that the existing sentiment/redact tools don't address.

name: csv-to-sql
description: Generate SQL CREATE TABLE and INSERT statements from a CSV/JSON table with inferred column types.
example_prompt: turn this CSV into SQL insert statements for a table called customers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (type inference + SQL emit); pure compute.
rationale: Seeding a database from a spreadsheet is a frequent task that complements the existing sql-query tool.

name: support-intent-classifier
description: Labels a customer message with an intent (billing, bug, refund, how-to, sales) for routing.
example_prompt: What is this customer asking about: 'I was charged twice this month'
loader_feasibility: transformers-js zero-shot classification (bart-mnli) — on-device. — model Xenova/bart-large-mnli
rationale: Auto-routing tickets is the headline upsell of every live-chat suite.

name: format-validator
description: Validates whether input is a well-formed email, URL, IPv4/IPv6, phone number, or credit card (with Luhn check).
example_prompt: Is 4111 1111 1111 1111 a valid credit card number?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM combines bundled regexes with a Luhn checksum locally — no validation service involved.
rationale: Format validation is the bread-and-butter use case behind every RegexLib category and is far more reliable bundled than hand-written each time.

name: code-formatter
description: Beautifies and re-indents HTML, CSS, JavaScript, or JSON snippets.
example_prompt: Format this minified CSS so I can read it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using pure-Rust formatters/pretty-printers; operates on the pasted string with no build step.
rationale: CodePen/JSFiddle demand is about quickly tidying front-end snippets, which is a stateless text transform ideal for browser-local use.

name: forced-aligner
description: Aligns a provided transcript to audio and outputs word/line timestamps as SRT or VTT subtitles.
example_prompt: Sync this transcript to the audio and give me an SRT
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a Whisper model with word timestamps in the browser to align text to audio. — model Xenova/whisper-base
rationale: Forced alignment turns a plain transcript into captions and karaoke timing without any server.

name: gpx-split
description: Splits a GPX track into segments by distance, elapsed time, or detected stop gaps.
example_prompt: Split this all-day GPX into separate tracks wherever I stopped for more than 20 minutes
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM segmentation over parsed points; no network.
rationale: Continuous loggers record one giant track that users need broken into per-activity pieces.

name: data-uri-codec
description: Encodes pasted text or base64 bytes into a data: URI and decodes data: URIs back to content.
example_prompt: make a data URI for this SVG markup
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: MIME-prefix assembly plus base64, no server needed.
rationale: Inlining assets as data URIs is routine for CSS/HTML and avoids a build step for one-off embeds.

name: video-ken-burns
description: Animate a still image with a smooth pan-and-zoom (Ken Burns) effect into a short video clip.
example_prompt: Make a 5-second slow zoom-in video from this photo
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — zoompan filter generates frames from a single image locally.
rationale: Turning photos into motion is popular for reels/intros and complements the slideshow tool.

name: audio-bass-adjust
description: Boosts or cuts low frequencies with a simple shelving control.
example_prompt: Add more bass to this track
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg bass (lowshelf) filter; trivial DSP in wasm
rationale: A one-knob bass shelf covers the most common quick tonal fix users want.

name: fit-file-decoder
description: Decodes binary Garmin/ANT FIT activity files into readable records and exports them as GPX or CSV.
example_prompt: Decode this .fit file from my bike computer and give me the GPS track
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust FIT decoder compiled to WASM; binary parsing runs entirely client-side. — via fitparser crate
rationale: FIT is the dominant fitness-device format but is opaque binary, so an offline decoder is genuinely valuable.

name: video-mux-audio
description: Adds an audio track to a silent video without re-encoding the picture.
example_prompt: add this music track to my silent video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm muxes the audio stream alongside -c:v copy locally.
rationale: Silent screen recordings and renders frequently need an audio track muxed in.

name: credit-card-validate
description: Runs the Luhn check on a card number and identifies the issuing network (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, etc.) by prefix and length, fully offline.
example_prompt: Does this card number pass the Luhn check and what network is it?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM Luhn algorithm and prefix table; never leaves the browser, which matters for sensitive numbers.
rationale: Local-only validation of card numbers is both useful and privacy-preserving versus any web tool.

name: cue-sheet-splitter
description: Splits a single full-album audio file into per-track files using an accompanying .cue sheet, carrying over tags.
example_prompt: Split this album.flac into tracks using album.cue
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: reads the cue timestamps and slices the decoded stream in WASM, no server involved.
rationale: CUE+single-file rips are ubiquitous on the cmus/mpd/foobar crowd and painful to split without desktop tools.

name: normalize-peak
description: Scales a file so its loudest sample hits a target dBFS peak.
example_prompt: Peak-normalize this to -1 dBFS
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: find max absolute sample, compute gain to target, multiply through.
rationale: Peak normalization is the simplest, most-requested level fix before export or mastering.

name: tabs-to-spaces
description: Converts leading and inline tabs to a configurable number of spaces, or spaces back to tabs, respecting tab stops.
example_prompt: Convert all the tabs in this snippet to 2 spaces
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM column-aware tab expansion; runs locally
rationale: Indentation-style mismatches are a daily annoyance for anyone pasting code between editors and style conventions.

name: video-metadata-privacy-check
description: Scans container and stream metadata for GPS coordinates, device serials, and personal tags before sharing.
example_prompt: Does this phone video leak any location or device info?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM (with ffmpeg.wasm probing) reads metadata tags entirely in-browser.
rationale: Videos quietly carry GPS and device IDs, and a pre-share privacy lint prevents accidental doxxing.

name: passport-photo-validator
description: Checks a photo against passport/visa specs: pixel dimensions, head-size ratio, centering, plain uniform background, and single forward face.
example_prompt: Does this photo meet US passport requirements?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a face/landmark model in-browser; plain Rust→WASM does the geometry and background-uniformity math. — model qualcomm/MediaPipe-Face-Detection
rationale: Rejected passport/visa photos are costly and frustrating, and the exact spec checks are tedious to do manually.

name: dataframe-diff
description: Loads two tabular files (CSV/TSV/Parquet) as dataframes and reports added rows, dropped rows, and changed cells with column alignment.
example_prompt: do a dataframe diff of these two datasets and summarize what changed
loader_feasibility: pyodide running pandas to align and compare; fully in-browser sandbox
rationale: Pandas-grade dataset reconciliation in the browser serves analysts who can't upload sensitive data.

name: svg-minifier
description: Minifies an SVG by stripping editor metadata, collapsing whitespace, and rounding path precision.
example_prompt: Minify this Illustrator-exported SVG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse XML, drop noise, re-serialize compactly — pure text/tree work.
rationale: Design-tool SVG exports are bloated and shipping them minified noticeably cuts page weight.

name: video-split-into-segments
description: Splits a video into equal-duration segments for upload limits or chunked sharing.
example_prompt: Split this video into 60-second segments
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader uses the segment muxer with -c copy in ffmpeg.wasm, producing parts in MEMFS.
rationale: Breaking a long video into platform-sized chunks is a frequent, fiddly task.

name: alpha-trim-bounds
description: Computes the bounding box of non-transparent pixels so you know the true visible extent of a transparent image.
example_prompt: What's the actual content bounding box ignoring the transparent margins?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans the alpha channel for min/max opaque coordinates in-memory.
rationale: Sprites and logos ship with excess transparent padding, and the trim bbox is the basis for tight packing.

name: blurred-padding-reframe-video
description: Reframes a landscape video to square or vertical by centering it over a blurred, scaled copy of itself as the background.
example_prompt: Convert this 16:9 video to 9:16 vertical with a blurred background
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg overlays the scaled clip onto a gblur'd background pad, all client-side.
rationale: The blurred-bar reframe is the default way to post horizontal footage to Reels/TikTok/Shorts.

name: letterbox-bars-video
description: Adds cinematic black letterbox or pillarbox bars to pad a video to a target aspect ratio without cropping.
example_prompt: Add 2.39:1 cinematic black bars to my 16:9 clip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg pad fills the new canvas around the source frame locally.
rationale: Aspect-ratio padding for a cinematic look or platform-fit is a simple but constantly needed edit.

name: ico-builder
description: Combines several PNGs into a single multi-resolution Windows .ico file.
example_prompt: build an ico from these 16, 32, and 48 pixel pngs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM image crate ICO encoder writes the multi-image container
rationale: Building a proper multi-size ICO is the reverse of the existing ico-extractor and is needed for app/site icons.

name: jsonl-deduplicator
description: Removes duplicate records from an NDJSON/JSONL stream by whole-line equality or a chosen set of key fields, keeping first or last.
example_prompt: Deduplicate this JSONL file by the id field, keeping the last occurrence
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: streaming line parse with a key-hash set, no server.
rationale: Log and export pipelines emit JSONL with repeated records; key-based dedup is a common need that existing JSON-array dedup tools don't cover line-oriented.

name: html-prettify
description: Re-indents and formats messy or minified HTML into clean, readable markup.
example_prompt: Format this minified HTML so I can read it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML tokenizer + indenter; runs entirely client-side
rationale: Inspecting scraped or minified markup is far easier when it's pretty-printed.

name: video-silence-segment-finder
description: Finds silent audio segments throughout a video and lists their start/end times for chaptering or dead-air trimming.
example_prompt: Find the silent gaps in this video's audio
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: the silencedetect filter scans decoded audio locally in WASM.
rationale: Silence boundaries drive auto-chaptering and dead-air removal, and a timestamp list makes both fast.

name: csv-anti-join
description: Returns the rows in CSV A whose key has no match in CSV B (and optionally the reverse).
example_prompt: Show me the orders in file A that aren't present in file B
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; build a key set from B and filter A — pure in-memory join
rationale: Anti-joins answer 'what's missing/extra' and are awkward to do without a database.

name: video-loudnorm-ebur128
description: Normalizes the audio loudness to a broadcast/streaming target (e.g. -14 LUFS) using two-pass EBU R128 measurement, keeping the video untouched.
example_prompt: normalize this video's audio to -14 LUFS for YouTube
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — two-pass loudnorm filter measures then corrects loudness, video stream-copied, all in the WASM build.
rationale: Platforms target specific LUFS levels and consistent loudness is a top complaint, distinct from dynamics compression.

name: http-header-parser
description: Parses a raw HTTP request or response header block into a structured, case-normalized map.
example_prompt: Parse these raw HTTP headers into a readable table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: line splitting and folding logic run on the pasted block, no network.
rationale: Reading raw headers from curl -v or devtools is a constant debugging need.

name: mbox-dedup
description: Finds and removes duplicate messages in an mbox by Message-ID.
example_prompt: Remove duplicate emails from this mbox
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM hashes Message-IDs and rewrites the archive locally.
rationale: Merged archives accumulate duplicates that are tedious to clean by hand.

name: video-audio-peak-normalize
description: Applies a single gain so the loudest sample of the video's audio hits a chosen peak ceiling (e.g. -1 dBFS) without changing dynamics.
example_prompt: Peak-normalize this clip's audio to -1 dB
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's volumedetect + volume filters run in ffmpeg.wasm; peak measurement and gain apply are local.
rationale: A lightweight, dynamics-preserving alternative to loudness normalization for users who just want maximum safe volume.

name: video-audio-sync-offset
description: Shifts the audio track earlier or later relative to the video by a millisecond offset to fix lip-sync drift.
example_prompt: Delay the audio in this video by 250 ms to fix the lip sync
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's -itsoffset / adelay handling runs in ffmpeg.wasm by remapping audio PTS locally.
rationale: A/V desync from bad muxes or screen recordings is a frequent, frustrating defect with no easy consumer fix.

name: video-audio-fade
description: Applies an audio-only fade-in at the start and/or fade-out at the end of a video without touching the picture.
example_prompt: Add a 2-second audio fade-in and fade-out to this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's afade filter runs in ffmpeg.wasm, re-encoding only the audio stream locally.
rationale: Abrupt audio starts/ends sound unpolished, and an audio-only fade keeps video bytes untouched.

name: video-bake-rotation
description: Bakes a video's rotation metadata into the actual pixels and clears the rotate flag, fixing players that ignore it.
example_prompt: This phone video shows sideways in some players — bake in the rotation
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg applies transpose per the side-data angle then resets metadata in ffmpeg.wasm, all local.
rationale: Rotation-metadata-only orientation breaks in many editors and web players; baking pixels fixes it permanently.

name: audio-fit-to-length
description: Pads with silence or trims an audio file to an exact target duration.
example_prompt: Pad this jingle out to exactly 15 seconds.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg apad/atrim to the computed length; runs in-browser.
rationale: Hitting an exact duration for ads, loops, or slots is a common precise edit with no current tool.

name: har-redact
description: Strips cookies, auth headers, and response bodies from a HAR capture for safe sharing.
example_prompt: redact the cookies and auth headers from this HAR file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with serde_json over the HAR schema; in-memory, client-side. — via serde_json crate
rationale: HAR files leak tokens and PII, so safe redaction before sharing is essential.

name: true-peak-checker
description: Measures inter-sample (true) peaks via 4x oversampling per ITU-R BS.1770 and flags dBTP overs that survive lossy encoding.
example_prompt: Does this master have any true-peak overs above -1 dBTP?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: polyphase oversampling FIR + peak detect runs entirely on decoded PCM client-side
rationale: Sample peaks pass while true peaks clip after MP3/AAC; mastering engineers need this exact compliance check.

name: loudness-spec-compliance
description: Validates integrated LUFS, true-peak, and gating against a named broadcast standard (EBU R128, ATSC A/85, -23/-24 LKFS) and returns pass/fail per criterion.
example_prompt: Does this file pass EBU R128 for broadcast delivery?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: BS.1770 K-weighting + gated integration is pure DSP on decoded PCM, no server
rationale: Delivery to broadcasters fails on exact spec thresholds; a pass/fail compliance report prevents rejected submissions.

name: best-shot-picker
description: Rank a set of similar photos and pick the best ones by sharpness, aesthetics, and open-eyes/smile detection.
example_prompt: pick the best 2 of these 8 burst photos
loader_feasibility: onnx/transformers aesthetic + face/blur models in-browser.
rationale: Photo culling across near-duplicates is a real photographer pain point not solved by single-image scoring or dedup.

name: cyberchef-pipeline
description: Chains multiple decode/transform steps (e.g. from-base64 → gunzip → XOR) into a single client-side recipe.
example_prompt: from base64 then gunzip then show me the result
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; composes deterministic transforms locally, a CyberChef-style flow with no server. — via flate2 crate
rationale: A composable transform pipeline covers the long tail of decoding puzzles in one tool.

name: gps-track-stats
description: Computes total distance, duration, moving time, average/max speed, and elevation gain from a GPX or GeoJSON track.
example_prompt: How far and fast was this GPS track? (paste GPX)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — haversine distance and aggregation math run in-browser.
rationale: PhoneTrack/OwnTracks users want trip summaries without sending GPS history to an analytics service.

name: enex-to-markdown
description: Converts Evernote ENEX export files into Markdown, noting attachments and tags.
example_prompt: Convert this Evernote .enex export to Markdown
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the ENEX XML client-side.
rationale: Joplin, Notesnook, and Obsidian migrations commonly start from ENEX, and doing it locally avoids handing private notes to cloud importers.

name: ai-text-detector
description: Estimates whether a passage is AI-generated using a local classifier and perplexity-based heuristics.
example_prompt: Is this paragraph likely written by an AI?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js/onnx-runtime: runs a small detector/scoring model in-browser, no upload.
rationale: Demand for distinguishing human vs machine text ('Not Human Search') is high, and local scoring keeps the checked text private.

name: parametric-eq
description: Applies a multi-band parametric equalizer with adjustable frequency, gain, and bandwidth per band.
example_prompt: Boost 3kHz by 4dB and cut 200Hz by 3dB on this vocal
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader — the equalizer/anequalizer filters run client-side in wasm.
rationale: Multi-band EQ (AudioTK) is the most-used mixing operation and naturally chat-driven.

name: hash-ioc-match
description: Hashes an uploaded file and flags it if its hash appears in a pasted blocklist of known-bad MD5/SHA values.
example_prompt: Check if this file's hash is in my list of bad hashes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — hashing plus set lookup, fully local
rationale: Hash-based IOC scanning (Loki/THOR/Redline) on a single suspect file shouldn't require installing an endpoint agent.

name: fuzzy-name-matcher
description: Matches and deduplicates person/organization names using Jaro-Winkler, Levenshtein and Soundex.
example_prompt: Match these customer names against my master list allowing typos
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string-similarity algorithms, offline.
rationale: Reproduces Rosette's name-matching capability for entity resolution, fully on-device.

name: compound-interest-calculator
description: Computes future value with compound interest and optional periodic contributions.
example_prompt: future value of $5000 at 7% compounded monthly for 10 years
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — compounding formulas run instantly client-side.
rationale: One of the most-searched finance calculators, exact and private as a local tool.

name: social-card-image
description: Renders a branded social share / OG card image with a headline and subtitle laid out over a background.
example_prompt: Make a Twitter share card that says 'Launching v2 today'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM image and font rasterization (image + ab_glyph) — drawn entirely locally. — via image crate
rationale: OG and Twitter card generation usually needs a server screenshot service; this does it offline.

name: survey-tabulator
description: Tabulates survey response CSVs into per-question counts, percentages and cross-tab summaries.
example_prompt: tabulate this survey CSV — counts and percentages for each question
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — CSV parsing and group-by aggregation in memory, no server.
rationale: Turning raw response exports into readable result summaries is exactly what users want after a survey closes.

name: har-secret-scanner
description: Scans a .har capture for leaked auth tokens, cookies, and API keys so they can be redacted before the file is shared.
example_prompt: Check this HAR for any secrets before I send it to support
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via har-rs plus local regex/entropy heuristics — scanning happens in-browser, no server — via har crate
rationale: HAR files routinely leak credentials, and a local scanner that never uploads the capture is exactly the right safety tool.

name: sbom-generator
description: Generates a CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM from a dependency lockfile such as package-lock.json, Cargo.lock, or requirements.txt.
example_prompt: Generate a CycloneDX SBOM from my package-lock.json: <paste file>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the lockfile format and serializes the SBOM JSON; pure parsing/serialization, fully offline.
rationale: syft's popularity shows strong SBOM demand, and producing one locally lets teams inventory private lockfiles without uploading them.

name: sbom-diff
description: Compares two lockfiles or SBOMs and reports added, removed, and version-bumped dependencies.
example_prompt: Diff these two package-lock.json files and show what changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses both inputs and computes a set diff; pure in-memory comparison, no network.
rationale: tracking dependency drift between releases is a core syft/supply-chain need that's naturally offline and deterministic.

name: seamless-loop-video
description: Makes a clip loop perfectly by crossfading its end back into its start so the join is invisible.
example_prompt: Make this 4-second clip into a seamless loop
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg overlaps the tail and head with xfade in the wasm runtime.
rationale: Seamless loops are wanted for backgrounds, livestream stingers, and ambient art and are fiddly to make by hand.

name: yaml-to-csv
description: Flattens a YAML list of records (or mapping of records) into a CSV with a unioned column header.
example_prompt: Turn this YAML list of users into a CSV table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: serde_yaml parse plus tabular flattening, no server. — via serde_yaml crate
rationale: Config and seed data live in YAML lists that people need in spreadsheets; the backlog has csv-to-yaml but not the reverse.

name: markdown-table-to-csv
description: Parses a markdown (or pipe-delimited) table back into clean CSV, stripping alignment rows and padding.
example_prompt: Convert this markdown table into CSV I can open in Excel
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM table-row parse + CSV emit with quoting; client-side
rationale: Getting tabular data out of docs and back into a spreadsheet is the inverse chore people hit just as often.

name: parquet-to-json
description: Streams Parquet rows out as JSON or NDJSON for quick inspection or piping into JS tools.
example_prompt: Show this parquet file as NDJSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM `parquet` reader emitting serde_json; fully local row decoding. — via parquet crate
rationale: JSON is the easiest format to eyeball or feed to web code, and no current tool bridges Parquet→JSON client-side.

name: json-schema-batch-validate
description: Validates an array or NDJSON stream of records against one schema and returns a pass/fail summary plus per-record error list.
example_prompt: Validate every row in this NDJSON file against this schema and show me which records failed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — loops the same in-process validator over each record; pure CPU work, no server — via jsonschema crate
rationale: Maps the json-schema-benchmark / bulk-validation demand into the common real task of checking a whole dataset at once.

name: ipynb-to-script
description: Extracts the code cells from a Jupyter .ipynb file into a clean .py script (or markdown), dropping outputs.
example_prompt: Convert this notebook into a plain Python script
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the notebook JSON and concatenates cells; no execution or network.
rationale: A second Euporie mapping that solves the common need to get runnable code out of a notebook.

name: feature-encoder
description: Encodes categorical columns via one-hot, label, ordinal, or target encoding.
example_prompt: One-hot encode the categorical columns in this dataset
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs pandas/scikit-learn encoders locally on the uploaded CSV.
rationale: Categorical encoding is a feature-engine staple every ML pipeline needs and is fully client-side.

name: ocr-to-hocr
description: Runs OCR and outputs text with word-level bounding-box coordinates in hOCR/ALTO format.
example_prompt: OCR this page and give me the text with bounding boxes as hOCR
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime OCR produces per-word boxes that plain Rust serializes to hOCR — all client-side. — via ocrs crate
rationale: Document-processing pipelines need positioned OCR output, not just flat text, for layout-aware downstream steps.

name: document-layout-analyzer
description: Segments a document image into regions — title, paragraphs, tables, figures, and captions — with reading order.
example_prompt: Detect the text, table, and figure regions on this scanned page
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a small layout-detection model in WASM and emits region boxes locally.
rationale: Structured document extraction needs layout regions first, and doing it on-device keeps documents private.

name: semantic-search
description: Index a set of passages/documents and return the most relevant ones for a natural-language query using embeddings.
example_prompt: Search these 20 notes for the ones about deployment rollbacks
loader_feasibility: transformers-js sentence embeddings + cosine similarity in-browser; local. — model Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
rationale: End-to-end semantic search over a user's own corpus is a higher-level need than the embed/rerank primitives alone.

name: pdf-search
description: Searches a PDF for a word or phrase and lists matching pages with surrounding context.
example_prompt: Find every mention of 'liability' in this PDF
loader_feasibility: pyodide — pdfplumber extracts page text and locates matches locally. — via lopdf crate
rationale: Full-text search across a long PDF is a fast, high-utility lookup users do constantly.

name: screenshot-link-extractor
description: OCRs an image and extracts all URLs, emails, and phone numbers it contains into a clean list.
example_prompt: Pull every link and email out of this screenshot
loader_feasibility: transformers-js OCR plus plain-WASM regex parsing runs fully in-browser. — model Xenova/trocr-base-printed
rationale: Recovering clickable contacts/links from a non-selectable screenshot is a common everyday chore.

name: missing-value-imputer
description: Fills missing values in a CSV using mean, median, most-frequent, or KNN imputation.
example_prompt: Fill the missing values in this CSV using KNN
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs scikit-learn's SimpleImputer/KNNImputer on the parsed DataFrame in-browser. — via csv crate
rationale: Imputation is the most common feature-engine task and runs fully offline on the user's data.

name: video-crop-difference-detector
description: Detects whether one video is a cropped or padded version of another and reports the crop/pad box.
example_prompt: Is the second clip just a cropped version of the first, and by how much?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg samples frames and Rust→WASM searches for the best matching crop offset locally.
rationale: Recovering the exact crop relationship lets you reconcile two reframed versions automatically.

name: har-to-csv
description: Converts a browser HAR (HTTP Archive) capture into a CSV of requests with URL, method, status, size, and timing.
example_prompt: Turn this network.har into a CSV of requests
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM serde_json over the HAR file; flattening the entries is pure local work. — via serde_json crate
rationale: HAR files from DevTools are huge JSON blobs that are far easier to analyze as a flat request table.

name: data-normalize
description: Scale numeric columns with min-max, z-score, or robust scaling for ML and comparison.
example_prompt: Z-score normalize the numeric columns in this table
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — column statistics and rescaling are pure local arithmetic over parsed rows.
rationale: Feature scaling is a standard preprocessing step for the embedding/ML pipelines users build.

name: log-format-converter
description: Converts access logs between combined, common, and JSON formats and exports to CSV for spreadsheets.
example_prompt: Convert this nginx combined log to CSV: <paste>
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM line parsing and re-serialization; offline.
rationale: A practical preprocessing step that makes the user's own log data portable without ever uploading it.

name: text-corpus-cleaner
description: Cleans raw text corpora by deduplicating lines, normalizing whitespace/encoding, stripping boilerplate, and filtering by language.
example_prompt: Clean and dedupe this big dump of Spanish text into a tidy corpus.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — streaming text normalization and dedup with optional bundled language detection, offline.
rationale: Mirrors the 'Compilation of Spanish Unannotated Corpora' demand, a practical prep tool for anyone building NLP datasets client-side.

name: paste-link-decode
description: Decode a paste-link URL fragment back into the original text.
example_prompt: decode this paste link back to text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM base64url + inflate; pure local decode with no network round-trip. — via flate2 crate
rationale: The reader side of paste-link completes a fully serverless pastebin entirely inside the browser.

name: html-extract
description: Extracts text or attributes from pasted HTML using CSS selectors, like jq for markup.
example_prompt: From this HTML, give me the text of every <a> inside .results and their href attributes.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the scraper/html5ever crate; operates on supplied HTML string, no fetching.
rationale: pup-style selector extraction is the standard way to scrape pasted markup and runs perfectly offline.

name: smart-task-categorizer
description: Auto-tags untagged tasks into categories (work, home, errands, finance, etc.) via in-browser zero-shot classification.
example_prompt: Categorize these loose tasks into work, home, and errands
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — a small zero-shot text-classification model runs entirely in the browser, no API calls. — model Xenova/nli-deberta-v3-xsmall
rationale: Adds intelligent +project/@context suggestions that plaintext CLIs can't, while keeping tasks private on-device.

name: http-request-parse
description: Parses a raw HTTP request (request line, headers, query params, cookies, form/JSON body) into structured JSON.
example_prompt: Parse this raw HTTP request into its fields.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Rocket-style request parsing is pure text processing with no network.
rationale: Inspect and understand captured HTTP requests without external tooling.

name: value-counts
description: Count distinct values in a chosen column with counts and percentages.
example_prompt: Show the value counts for the 'country' column in this CSV
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM hash-count; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: A pandas value_counts equivalent is a constant first step in data exploration.

name: ssh-keygen
description: Generate an OpenSSH ed25519 or RSA key pair in authorized_keys / OpenSSH PEM format.
example_prompt: Generate an ed25519 SSH key pair
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM ed25519/RSA crypto + OpenSSH encoding; offline. — via ssh-key crate
rationale: keypair-generate outputs PEM/JWK, not the OpenSSH formats developers actually paste.

name: markdown-query
description: Extracts specific elements from Markdown — all links, code blocks, headings, or tables — into a clean list.
example_prompt: Pull every link out of this markdown file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM Markdown AST walk (pulldown-cmark) filtering node types; in-memory only — via pulldown-cmark crate
rationale: Auditing a doc's links, harvesting its code samples, or listing its sections is a frequent and fiddly manual task.

name: markdown-to-image
description: Render a Markdown snippet (headings, lists, code, tables) as a shareable PNG.
example_prompt: Render these release notes as an image
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM Markdown parse plus raster layout, offline. — via pulldown-cmark crate
rationale: Sharing formatted notes as images on social/chat is common and not covered by html/pdf/slides exports.

name: table-format
description: Render tabular data (CSV/JSON) as a clean Markdown or ASCII table.
example_prompt: Turn this CSV into a Markdown table
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM formatting; instant and offline.
rationale: Pasting data into docs/READMEs/issues as aligned tables is a frequent, low-effort win.

name: image-classifier
description: Classifies the main subject of an image using a MobileNet/ResNet model.
example_prompt: What's in this photo?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime — a quantized classification model runs in WASM/WebGPU with the image processed locally. — model Xenova/resnet-50
rationale: On-device image classification keeps photos private and demonstrates the ONNX path (tensorflow/rust).

name: ics-to-csv
description: Flattens calendar events from an .ics file into a CSV spreadsheet with one row per event.
example_prompt: Turn my calendar.ics into a CSV I can open in Excel
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; parses iCalendar text and serializes CSV entirely in the browser. — via ical crate
rationale: Spreadsheet analysis of one's schedule is a common need that no built-in calendar app exposes.

name: hex-tool
description: Converts between text/bytes and hexadecimal, both directions.
example_prompt: hex encode "crypto"
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the hex crate — pure transform, runs client-side
rationale: Hex is the default representation for keys, hashes and ciphertext throughout every cryptography reference.

name: photo-gps-mapper
description: Extracts GPS coordinates from a batch of photos and outputs them as a coordinate list or GeoJSON for mapping.
example_prompt: Pull the GPS coordinates out of these photos as GeoJSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: read EXIF GPS tags from each image and serialize locally; no reverse-geocoding network call. — via kamadak-exif crate
rationale: Aves' map view is a beloved feature, and users want to export where photos were taken for their own mapping tools.

name: json-to-xml
description: Renders a JSON object as well-formed XML with configurable root and item element names.
example_prompt: Convert this JSON to XML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM building XML strings from serde_json values; pure computation. — via serde_json crate
rationale: Many legacy APIs still consume XML, so JSON→XML is a recurring need that should stay offline.

name: markdown-to-confluence
description: Convert Markdown into Confluence wiki/storage markup.
example_prompt: Convert this Markdown to Confluence format
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM Markdown parse + Confluence emit; offline. — via pulldown-cmark crate
rationale: Teams paste docs into Confluence constantly; not covered by existing Markdown converters.

name: audio-compressor
description: Applies dynamic-range compression with adjustable threshold, ratio, attack and release.
example_prompt: Compress this vocal so the quiet and loud parts are more even.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg acompressor filter; entirely in the wasm DSP build.
rationale: Evening out dynamics is essential vocal/podcast processing and the catalog only measures dynamic range, never adjusts it.

name: html-table-to-json
description: Parses an HTML <table> into a JSON array of row objects keyed by header cells.
example_prompt: extract this HTML table into JSON records
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; DOM table walking and JSON serialization run client-side. — via scraper crate
rationale: Scraped tables often need to become structured data, and doing it locally avoids pasting into a server tool.

name: fastq-to-fasta
description: Strips per-base quality lines from FASTQ reads and emits clean FASTA, with optional length and quality filtering.
example_prompt: Convert this FASTQ file to FASTA and drop reads shorter than 50bp
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: 4-line-record streaming text transform, no server needed.
rationale: Downstream aligners and BLAST often want FASTA only, and dropping quality lines plus length-filtering is a daily preprocessing chore.

name: image-average-color
description: Computes the single mean color of an image (and a gamma-correct variant) as a hex/RGB value.
example_prompt: What's the average color of this picture?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM averages all pixel values in one pass offline. — via image crate
rationale: A go-to value for placeholder backgrounds, theming, and quick at-a-glance color summaries.

name: cookie-string-to-json
description: Parses a raw Cookie header string into a JSON object of name/value pairs, decoding values.
example_prompt: Parse this Cookie header string into JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM splits on the cookie grammar and decodes; deterministic local transform
rationale: Reading and editing the cookie jar from a captured request is a frequent web-debugging need.

name: csv-to-ndjson
description: Emits one JSON object per CSV row as newline-delimited JSON for streaming pipelines.
example_prompt: convert this CSV to NDJSON, one record per line
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; csv parse → per-row serialize, fully client-side — via csv crate
rationale: NDJSON is the ingest format for many log/search systems.

name: html-table-to-csv
description: Parses the first or all <table> elements in pasted HTML and outputs CSV.
example_prompt: pull this HTML table into CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM html parser (scraper/tl) extracting rows; runs on pasted markup locally — via scraper crate
rationale: Scraped/copied HTML tables are awkward to reuse without a clean CSV export.

name: html-entity-decoder
description: Decodes HTML character entities (&, ©, —) into their literal characters.
example_prompt: Decode the HTML entities in this string
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — named/numeric entity table, no I/O
rationale: Scraped or exported HTML often leaves entities unresolved, making text unreadable.

name: gpu-image-diff
description: GPU-accelerated per-pixel diff that handles very high-resolution image pairs far faster than a CPU pass.
example_prompt: Diff these two 8K renders quickly
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute: a compute shader subtracts the two textures on the GPU entirely in the browser.
rationale: For 4K/8K assets a CPU diff is sluggish; offloading to WebGPU keeps it instant and local.

name: swagger2-to-openapi3
description: Upgrades a Swagger 2.0 spec (JSON or YAML) into an equivalent OpenAPI 3.0 document.
example_prompt: convert this swagger 2.0 spec to OpenAPI 3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; structural transform of the parsed spec, fully in-memory.
rationale: Many legacy APIs are still Swagger 2.0 and modern tooling expects OpenAPI 3.

name: aiff-to-flac
description: Compresses AIFF audio into lossless FLAC with identical samples, preserving any tags.
example_prompt: compress this aiff to flac for archiving
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader decodes AIFF PCM and encodes FLAC entirely client-side.
rationale: AIFF masters are large, and FLAC stores the same samples far smaller for portable archives.

name: json-from-logs
description: Scans mixed log/console text for embedded JSON objects/arrays and extracts each as a separately pretty-printed, validated block.
example_prompt: This log has JSON blobs buried in it—find and pretty-print every JSON object
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM bracket-balancing scan plus JSON validation; runs on the pasted text
rationale: Logs and stack traces routinely embed JSON inline, and isolating each blob to read it is a daily debugging chore.

name: video-cea608-caption-extractor
description: Extracts CEA-608/708 closed captions embedded in the video bitstream to an SRT/VTT file.
example_prompt: Pull the embedded CEA-608 closed captions out of this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg reads the in-stream caption side-data and writes a subtitle file entirely in wasm.
rationale: Broadcast and screen-recorded files often carry in-stream captions that no consumer tool exposes offline.

name: date-column-validate
description: Checks that every value in a CSV date column parses against a chosen format.
example_prompt: Verify the order_date column all matches YYYY-MM-DD
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM date parsing (chrono); client-side — via chrono crate
rationale: Inconsistent date formats silently break downstream parsing; a column-level check stops it.

name: arrow-feather-to-csv
description: Reads Arrow IPC / Feather files and writes their tables out as CSV.
example_prompt: Convert this .feather file to CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the `arrow` crate's IPC reader; zero-copy table decoding runs locally. — via arrow crate
rationale: Feather is pandas/R's fast-interchange format and has no convenient standalone viewer.

name: named-entity-recognition
description: Extracts people, organizations, locations, and dates from text.
example_prompt: find the named entities in this news paragraph: ...
loader_feasibility: transformers-js token-classification NER model runs client-side via ONNX/wasm. — model Xenova/bert-base-NER
rationale: Stanford NLP / OpenNLP / CogcompNLP / Epic NER without uploading sensitive documents to a server.

name: aes-gcm-decrypt
description: Decrypts AES-256-GCM ciphertext given the key, nonce and tag, verifying integrity before output.
example_prompt: decrypt this aes-gcm blob with my key and nonce
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the aes-gcm crate's authenticated decrypt; runs fully client-side.
rationale: Round-trip decryption is required for the same AES interop scenarios the harvested crypto libraries cover.

name: av1-video-encoder
description: Re-encodes an uploaded video to efficient AV1 (WebM/MP4) at a chosen quality to dramatically shrink file size.
example_prompt: Convert this MP4 to AV1 to make it smaller
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — SVT-AV1/libaom encoding runs CPU-bound but fully local inside ffmpeg.wasm.
rationale: AV1 yields large size savings and local encoding avoids uploading big videos to a cloud transcoder.

name: aws-sigv4-signer
description: Computes the AWS Signature Version 4 canonical request, string-to-sign, and final Authorization header for a given request and key.
example_prompt: Build the SigV4 Authorization header for this GET request to S3 with my test secret key.
