loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with sha2/hmac crates: the whole signing chain is deterministic crypto with no network, keeping secrets on-device. — via sha2 crate
rationale: SigV4 mismatches are a top AWS debugging pain and a local step-by-step signer lets you compare against your client's output safely.

name: qr-backup-restore
description: Decodes a set of scanned QR-code images back into the original file or text.
example_prompt: Reassemble my file from these QR backup photos.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a Rust QR decoder (rqrr) reads the uploaded images and reconstructs the byte stream offline. — via rqrr crate
rationale: The decode half of paperbackup, keeping sensitive restored data on-device.

name: text-to-json
description: Parse pasted INI, key=value, logfmt, CSV, or passwd-style text into structured JSON.
example_prompt: Convert this INI config into JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — dedicated format parsers run locally; only the file/text-format subset of jc that needs no shell is supported.
rationale: jc demand: a lot of real data lives in ad-hoc text formats, and turning it into JSON unlocks every other tool here.

name: markdown-formatter
description: Normalizes and prettifies Markdown — consistent headings, list markers, spacing, and table alignment.
example_prompt: Clean up and reformat this messy markdown
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parse-then-reprint formatter; pure text transformation
rationale: directly serves the mdformat demand and standardizes docs before committing or publishing.

name: multiple-regression
description: Fit a multiple linear regression across several predictor columns and report coefficients, R², and significance.
example_prompt: regress price on sqft, bedrooms, and age from this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM linear algebra; local.
rationale: Multi-variable regression is core analytics; curve-fit only handles a single x/y trendline.

name: audio-channel
description: Convert between stereo and mono, swap, or isolate left/right channels.
example_prompt: convert this stereo file to mono
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg pan/channelmap filters. — via symphonia crate
rationale: Channel fixes (mono podcasts, one-sided recordings) are frequent and simple.

name: pdf-header-footer
description: Adds custom header and footer text to every page of a PDF.
example_prompt: Add a footer with my company name to this PDF
loader_feasibility: pyodide — reportlab overlays text that pypdf merges onto each page client-side. — via lopdf crate
rationale: Branding and labeling documents is a common professional formatting task.

name: eisenhower-matrix-sorter
description: Sorts a list of tasks into urgent/important quadrants with recommended do/schedule/delegate/drop actions.
example_prompt: Put these 12 tasks into an Eisenhower matrix
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — zero-shot classification of each task into urgency/importance runs in-browser.
rationale: Prioritization is the unmet need behind every task manager; the matrix is a recognizable, decision-ready output.

name: pdf-grayscale
description: Convert a color PDF to grayscale to save ink and reduce size.
example_prompt: Make this PDF black-and-white for printing
loader_feasibility: Rust PDF library recolors content streams/images in-browser.
rationale: Common print-prep need not covered by pdf-compress or pdf-redact.

name: pdf-metadata-edit
description: View and edit a PDF's title, author, subject, and keywords metadata.
example_prompt: set the title and author on this PDF
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM PDF library (lopdf-style), runs locally on the uploaded file. — via lopdf crate
rationale: Document metadata editing is common for publishing; exif-edit covers images but not PDFs.

name: critical-path-calculator
description: Computes the critical path plus earliest/latest start times from a task graph with durations.
example_prompt: Find the critical path of this project schedule.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — CPM forward/backward passes over the parsed graph.
rationale: Project and pipeline planning needs CPM, and doing it manually is error-prone (dagrs).

name: geojson-to-csv
description: Flattens GeoJSON features into a CSV of properties plus geometry coordinates.
example_prompt: Convert this GeoJSON to a CSV of points
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — geojson crate to read, csv crate to write, fully client-side.
rationale: Getting geo features into a spreadsheet or BI tool is a routine GIS interchange need with no quick clipboard option.

name: gpx-to-kml
description: Converts a GPX file to KML for Google Earth and other KML-aware viewers.
example_prompt: Convert my GPX track to KML
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM XML-to-XML transform; fully offline. — via quick-xml crate
rationale: KML remains a common interchange target and a recurring one-off conversion need for GPS tracks.

name: emoji-remover
description: Strips emoji and pictographic symbols from text, optionally leaving a single space where each was removed.
example_prompt: remove all the emoji from this message
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM filtering over Unicode emoji ranges/properties; offline and deterministic.
rationale: Cleaning emoji out of names, filenames, and data fields is needed before importing into systems that reject them.

name: python-dict-to-json
description: Converts a Python dict/list literal (True/False/None, single quotes, tuples) into valid JSON.
example_prompt: convert this python dict I printed into JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses Python literal syntax and maps None/True/False to JSON null/booleans locally
rationale: Pasting a printed Python structure into JSON tooling otherwise requires manual True→true edits.

name: ascii-table-renderer
description: Renders rows and headers into a fixed-width ASCII/box-drawing table for terminals and plain-text docs.
example_prompt: Render this data as an ASCII box table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: column-width computation and border drawing, fully offline.
rationale: Plain-text tables for CLIs, comments, and emails differ from Markdown tables and are widely needed.

name: video-mute-section
description: Silences the audio over a chosen time range while leaving the rest intact.
example_prompt: Mute the audio from 00:10 to 00:15 in this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader uses the volume filter with an enable-between expression in the browser.
rationale: Bleeping out a name or noise in one stretch is needed often and awkward in consumer apps.

name: list-dedupe-merge
description: Merges two lists into one deduplicated list and reports how many overlapping entries were collapsed.
example_prompt: Merge these two mailing lists and remove duplicates
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — set union with overlap counting, no I/O
rationale: Combining lists while tracking overlap is a frequent, error-prone manual chore.

name: video-ab-side-by-side
description: Renders two videos synchronized side-by-side (or stacked top/bottom) into a single comparison clip with optional labels.
example_prompt: Put these two renders next to each other so I can compare them
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — ffmpeg.wasm hstack/vstack + drawtext filters run fully in-browser, no server
rationale: The most common review need: watching an original and an edit play together frame-for-frame.

name: remove-empty-lines
description: Deletes all blank or whitespace-only lines, compacting the text.
example_prompt: delete all the blank lines from this
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line filter, no API
rationale: Tidies double-spaced exports and sparse lists into dense, scannable text.

name: round-decimals
description: Rounds numeric columns to a chosen number of decimal places using a selectable rounding mode.
example_prompt: Round every number in the amount column to 2 decimals
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM numeric formatting; deterministic and local.
rationale: Float noise and over-precise exports need consistent rounding before reporting or reconciliation.

name: numeric-row-deduplicator
description: Removes exact duplicate numeric rows (optionally keyed on selected columns), preserving first-occurrence order.
example_prompt: Drop duplicate rows from this numeric table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: hash-set of row keys in a single pass, no network.
rationale: De-duplicating numeric records is a core cleanup task distinct from set-operations on values.

name: csv-to-json-matrix
description: Converts a numeric CSV grid into a JSON array-of-arrays (with optional row/column header objects).
example_prompt: Turn this CSV table into a JSON 2D array
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: CSV parse plus JSON serialization, no external services.
rationale: Front-end charting and JS numeric libs expect nested-array JSON, not CSV.

name: danish-english-translator
description: Translates between Danish and English.
example_prompt: Translate this Danish paragraph to English
loader_feasibility: transformers.js: an opus-mt da↔en model runs in-browser — model Xenova/opus-mt-da-en
rationale: Offline Danish↔English translation is useful for readers and anyone handling confidential text.

name: schema-inferrer
description: Infers a JSON Schema and a SQL CREATE TABLE statement from a sample dataset.
example_prompt: Generate a SQL table schema from this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM type inference over parsed rows; runs client-side.
rationale: Loading any open dataset into a database first requires a schema, which this auto-derives.

name: monte-carlo-sim
description: Run a Monte Carlo simulation of a model and report the outcome distribution and percentiles.
example_prompt: Simulate 10000 trials of a project that's 3 tasks of 2-5 days each
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM random sampling and histogram, offline.
rationale: Risk/estimate modeling is widely useful and absent from the existing stats tools.

name: table-to-image
description: Render a CSV/JSON table as a clean, styled image (with header styling and zebra rows) for sharing.
example_prompt: render this CSV as a nice table image
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM table layout + raster render; local. — via fontdue crate
rationale: Sharing data as an image is common; existing tools render Markdown or code, not data tables directly.

name: chart-image-digitizer
description: Extracts numeric data points from a line or scatter plot image (with user-set axis calibration) into CSV.
example_prompt: Get the data points out of this line chart screenshot as a CSV
loader_feasibility: pyodide: runs WebPlotDigitizer-style color/peak detection with numpy in the Python sandbox, fully client-side.
rationale: Recovering data from published chart images is a real research/journalism need with no client-side tool in the catalog.

name: image-rounded-corners
description: Rounds the corners of an image to a chosen radius, outputting a transparent PNG with the corners masked.
example_prompt: Give this thumbnail rounded corners with a 24px radius
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: build a rounded-rect alpha mask and apply it to the buffer.
rationale: Rounded-corner image assets are everywhere in UI work and tedious to produce manually.

name: round-to-nearest-multiple
description: Rounds each value to the nearest multiple of a given step (e.g. 0.25, 5, 1000).
example_prompt: Round these prices to the nearest 0.05
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: divide, round, multiply per element, offline
rationale: Snapping to arbitrary increments is common for pricing/grids and isn't expressible with decimal-place rounding.

name: ipynb-to-markdown
description: Converts a Jupyter notebook into clean Markdown with fenced code blocks and output sections.
example_prompt: Convert this .ipynb to markdown
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON-to-markdown transform, runs locally
rationale: Notebook-to-markdown export is a frequent step for docs, blogs and PRs.

name: csv-to-parquet
description: Converts CSV/JSON tables into a compressed columnar Parquet file.
example_prompt: Convert this CSV to Parquet with snappy compression
loader_feasibility: pyodide (pyarrow) performs the conversion client-side and returns the file for download.
rationale: Serves the Arrow/Tonbo analytics audience that wants efficient columnar files without a data pipeline.

name: hex-byte-inspector
description: Converts between hex, raw bytes, and text and displays byte length and grouping for cryptographic values.
example_prompt: decode this hex string and show me the byte length
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM hex/encoding crate; trivial byte manipulation that runs instantly in wasmi.
rationale: Crypto work produces endless hex blobs and a quick local decoder/inspector saves constant manual conversion.

name: xpath-extractor
description: Runs an XPath query against an XML/HTML document and returns the matched nodes as a CSV or JSON list.
example_prompt: Pull every //book/title from this XML with XPath
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM DOM walk plus a small XPath evaluator; no DOM API or server needed. — via sxd-xpath crate
rationale: Lets users surgically extract fields from large XML feeds without writing a script.

name: dbf-table-parser
description: Parses dBase/.dbf table files into column definitions and rows, exportable as CSV or JSON.
example_prompt: Parse this .dbf file into rows and columns
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reading the DBF header and fixed-width records from bytes; offline parsing.
rationale: DBF still ships with shapefiles and legacy data; a browser parser saves installing GIS/legacy tooling.

name: data-validator
description: Validates pasted CSV or JSON rows against type, range, regex, and required-field rules and lists violations.
example_prompt: Check this CSV — emails must be valid and age must be 0-120
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applying nutype-style constraints row by row; validation is pure logic with no network.
rationale: Constraint validation (nutype) catches dirty data before it reaches a system and is fully browser-local.

name: video-trim-black-frames
description: Detects and trims leading and trailing fully-black frames from a video.
example_prompt: Cut off the black frames at the start and end of this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's blackdetect filter finds the ranges and trims them in ffmpeg.wasm, fully local.
rationale: Exports and screen recordings frequently begin/end with dead black frames that look unprofessional.

name: data-clusterer
description: Clusters tabular data with KMeans, DBSCAN, or hierarchical methods and visualizes the result.
example_prompt: Cluster this data into groups with DBSCAN
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs scikit-learn clustering on the parsed CSV and plots with matplotlib in-browser. — via linfa-clustering crate
rationale: Clustering is the headline mlpack/Shogun capability and a top exploratory-analysis need served offline.

name: owntracks-to-gpx
description: Converts an OwnTracks location export (JSON or .rec recorder format) into a standard GPX track.
example_prompt: Convert my OwnTracks export to GPX so I can open it in a map app
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — JSON/line parsing and GPX XML emission, fully offline.
rationale: OwnTracks and Nextcloud PhoneTrack users want their own location history in a portable format without uploading it anywhere.

name: container-object-extractor
description: Recursively decomposes containers (ZIP, OLE, PE resources, archives) into their nested objects for scanning.
example_prompt: Break this Office file into all its embedded objects and streams
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: container formats are unpacked in-memory from the upload, mirroring Laika BOSS object decomposition. — via zip crate
rationale: Decomposing nested objects exposes hidden payloads, the core idea behind Laika BOSS, runnable on one uploaded file.

name: midi-to-json
description: Converts a MIDI file into structured JSON of notes, timing, control changes, and meta events.
example_prompt: Convert this MIDI to JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — deterministic binary parse, runs entirely locally. — via midly crate
rationale: JSON makes MIDI scriptable for downstream tools and LLM reasoning (Mido/Pretty-MIDI demand).

name: nacl-secretbox-encrypt
description: Encrypts or decrypts data with a shared symmetric key using NaCl secretbox (XSalsa20-Poly1305).
example_prompt: secretbox encrypt this with our shared key
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (crypto_secretbox/xsalsa20poly1305 crate); AEAD in-page.
rationale: secretbox is libsodium's symmetric workhorse and a distinct demand from box, run locally to protect the shared key.

name: keypair-generator
description: Generates X25519 or Ed25519 keypairs and shows them in hex, base64, and PEM for use in secure channels and signing.
example_prompt: generate an Ed25519 keypair
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with RustCrypto curve crates seeded by the browser CSPRNG; keys never leave the device. — via ed25519-dalek crate
rationale: Generating identity/signing keypairs offline mirrors Ockam's identity model and is safer done client-side.

name: ansi-log-renderer
description: Parses raw terminal output containing ANSI escape codes and renders it to clean colored HTML, or strips the codes to plain text.
example_prompt: This pasted log is full of escape codes — render it with the colors or strip them out.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: ANSI escape-sequence parsing and HTML/plain emission are pure text transforms.
rationale: procmux, pueue, and Steam TUI all surface ANSI-colored process output, and cleaning or rendering captured logs is a common, fully-local need.

name: bitcoin-address
description: Derives Bitcoin addresses (P2PKH, P2WPKH) and WIF from a secp256k1 key using SHA-256, RIPEMD-160, and Base58Check/Bech32.
example_prompt: derive the bitcoin address from this public key
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM chaining RustCrypto hashes, secp256k1, and base58/bech32 crates, all pure computation in wasmi. — via bitcoin crate
rationale: Wallet developers and learners need to reproduce the full key-to-address pipeline locally to avoid leaking key material.

name: chunk-text
description: Split a long document into overlapping chunks by token or character count for RAG/embedding pipelines.
example_prompt: split this article into 500-token chunks with 50-token overlap
loader_feasibility: transformers-js tokenizer (or plain Rust for char mode) runs fully client-side; no server tokenization.
rationale: Core preprocessing step for anyone building AI/embedding workflows, directly complementing count-tokens and text-embed.

name: ics-parse
description: Parse an .ics calendar file into a structured list of events (title, times, location, recurrence).
example_prompt: what events are in this .ics file?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust to WASM — pure compute.
rationale: Reading calendar files is the inverse of ical-generate.

name: currency-converter
description: Converts amounts between currencies using a rate table you supply or paste, including multi-leg conversions.
example_prompt: Convert 250 EUR to USD and JPY using these rates: EUR/USD 1.08, USD/JPY 156
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — multiplication and cross-rate math run locally; rates are user-provided since WASM has no network.
rationale: moeda/cash-cli demand is currency conversion, and the math (cross-rates, rounding) is the actual value once a rate is known.

name: pptx-to-text
description: Extract text and slide outline from a PowerPoint .pptx file.
example_prompt: pull the text out of this PowerPoint
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (zip + OOXML XML parse). — via zip crate
rationale: Completes the office-doc extractors (docx/xlsx) with the missing slides format.

name: csv-column-split
description: Split one column into several by a delimiter, or concatenate multiple columns into one.
example_prompt: Split the 'full_name' column into first and last name
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM string ops; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: Splitting/merging columns is a frequent cleaning task not covered by csv-clean.

name: json-sort
description: Recursively sort JSON object keys (and optionally arrays) to produce stable, diff-friendly output.
example_prompt: Sort all the keys in this JSON config alphabetically
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM serde reserialize; pure compute, browser-local. — via serde_json crate
rationale: Canonical key ordering makes config diffs readable and is distinct from pretty-printing.

name: font-subset
description: Subset a font to only the glyphs actually used by given text, shrinking the file for web use.
example_prompt: Subset this font to just the characters in my headline
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM font subsetting; offline. — via allsorts crate
rationale: Real web-performance win for self-hosted fonts with no existing tool.

name: nmap-output-parser
description: Parses nmap XML or greppable output into a clean, sortable table of hosts, open ports, services, and versions.
example_prompt: Turn this nmap XML into a readable host/port/service table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with a pure-Rust XML parser over the pasted scan results; no scanning is performed in-browser. — via quick-xml crate
rationale: Captures the post-scan value of rustscan/nmap workflows by making raw scan output instantly readable without a tool install.

name: csv-window-functions
description: Computes running totals, moving averages, lag/lead, and rank over partitions of CSV data.
example_prompt: Add a 7-day moving average of sales and a running cumulative total to this CSV.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — ordered in-memory passes over parsed rows, no external compute.
rationale: Window calculations are core analytics that are awkward to do by hand in a spreadsheet.

name: code-chunker
description: Splits source into function- and class-aligned chunks suitable for embedding or LLM context windows.
example_prompt: Chunk this file into pieces I can feed to a RAG pipeline
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tree-sitter boundaries drive the chunking, all in the browser.
rationale: Prepares code for retrieval/embedding (octocode-style) without sending it to a server.

name: audio-filter
description: Applies a low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, or notch filter to audio.
example_prompt: Low-pass this audio at 2 kHz
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg biquad filters run entirely in-WASM.
rationale: Quick cleanup or tonal shaping without a DAW (Selected Topics in Audio Signal Processing demand).

name: music-tagger
description: Classifies a clip's genre, mood, or instruments using an in-browser audio model.
example_prompt: What genre is this clip?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs an audio-classification model (AST/wav2vec) client-side. — model Xenova/ast-finetuned-audioset-10-10-0.4593
rationale: Auto-tagging and recommendation are core MIR tasks (MIR Notebooks/musdb demand).

name: location-history-parser
description: Parses Google Takeout / Dawarich location-history JSON into a daily summary of places visited and distance traveled.
example_prompt: Summarize my Google location history JSON by day and total distance
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM JSON streaming + aggregation; keeps highly sensitive history on-device. — via serde_json crate
rationale: Dawarich users import this exact export, and parsing it locally avoids handing years of movements to a server.

name: histogram-equalizer
description: Enhances contrast in a photo via global and adaptive (CLAHE) histogram equalization.
example_prompt: Boost the contrast on this dark photo
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes and remaps the intensity histogram over the pixel buffer client-side.
rationale: Contrast enhancement is universally useful and a classic scikit-image exposure routine.

name: embeddings-similarity-search
description: Embeds a set of texts and finds the most semantically similar items to a query, ranked by cosine similarity.
example_prompt: Among these support tickets, which are most similar to 'cannot reset password'?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a sentence-embedding model in-browser, no API — model Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
rationale: Semantic search is a modern data-science staple and a strong showcase of fully-local ML.

name: geofence-check
description: Test whether latitude/longitude points fall inside a polygon (point-in-polygon).
example_prompt: Is 40.71,-74.00 inside this polygon?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM ray-casting, offline.
rationale: Geofencing is a common geo task absent from the distance/geohash tools.

name: persian-text-normalizer
description: Normalizes Persian/Farsi text by fixing half-spaces (ZWNJ), replacing Arabic characters with Persian equivalents (ك→ک, ي→ی), and correcting punctuation spacing.
example_prompt: Normalize this Persian text and fix the half-spaces: مي خواهم كتاب بخوانم
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure character-class rewrite and spacing rules (virastar/Parsivar/Hazm style), no model or network needed.
rationale: Inconsistent Arabic-vs-Persian codepoints and missing ZWNJ break search, NLP, and display for nearly every Persian text pipeline.

name: levels-adjust
description: Remaps black point, white point, and midtone gamma from explicit input/output levels.
example_prompt: Set the black point to 20 and white point to 235 on this image
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a single per-pixel linear+gamma lookup table, pure arithmetic
rationale: Precise Photoshop-style levels control is something casual editors lack but power users want.

name: image-format-validator
description: Verifies that an image file's bytes match its claimed format, reports dimensions, color depth, and corruption.
example_prompt: Is this actually a valid PNG and what are its dimensions?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg/plain Rust (image crate); decodes header in-page
rationale: Mislabeled or truncated images break uploads, and header validation is fast and fully client-side.

name: bot-traffic-filter
description: Flags and strips bot/crawler hits from a log or event list and reports the human-versus-bot split.
example_prompt: Remove bot traffic from this list of hits and tell me the human count: <paste>
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM UA and heuristic matching against a bundled crawler list; offline.
rationale: Bot filtering is a headline feature of Pirsch/Shynet/Swetrix-style analytics and a common data-hygiene need.

name: http-headers-diff
description: Compares two sets of HTTP headers and reports added, removed, and changed header values.
example_prompt: Diff the response headers from these two requests
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — header block parse + case-insensitive map comparison, local only
rationale: Header drift between environments or deploys causes subtle bugs that a normalized diff makes obvious.

name: glob-filter
description: Filters a path list by glob and gitignore-style include/exclude patterns and previews exactly which paths match.
example_prompt: From these paths show only **/*.rs but not anything under target/
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using globset-style matching — pattern engine over provided strings. — via globset crate
rationale: Pattern-based locate/filtering covers plocate/bfs demand and lets users validate globs before scripting them.

name: qr-paper-backup
description: Encodes a file or secret into a printable sheet of numbered QR codes for offline paper archival.
example_prompt: Make a paper QR backup of this recovery key.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the qrcode crate chunks bytes and renders QR matrices to SVG/PNG with no network.
rationale: Direct browser-local realization of paperbackup — exactly the kind of offline-only task that should never touch a server.

name: video-audio-track-splitter
description: Splits a video that contains multiple audio tracks (languages/commentary) into separate per-track audio files.
example_prompt: This movie has 3 audio tracks — split each one out into its own file
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader enumerates and demuxes each audio stream separately, all client-side.
rationale: Multilingual rips bundle several audio tracks, and separating them per language is needed for archiving or remixing.

name: code-outline-extractor
description: Produces a structured outline of functions, classes, and methods from pasted source code.
example_prompt: Show me an outline of all the functions in this file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tree-sitter parses the AST in-browser; purely syntactic so it runs fully local
rationale: kwaak/unibear navigation features map to a fast symbol outliner that needs only a parser, not an LLM.

name: markdown-to-jira
description: Convert Markdown into Jira wiki markup (and back).
example_prompt: Convert this Markdown into Jira ticket formatting
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM transform; offline.
rationale: Frequent friction point for developers writing Jira issues, with no existing tool.

name: apply-alpha-mask
description: Uses a grayscale mask image as the alpha channel of another image to create a cutout.
example_prompt: Apply this grayscale mask as transparency to my photo
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM copies the mask's luminance into the target's alpha channel; runs in-browser.
rationale: The natural counterpart to mask extraction, letting users reapply or hand-author cutouts locally.

name: kobo-highlights-extractor
description: Extracts highlights, annotations, and reading stats from a KoboReader.sqlite file into Markdown or CSV.
example_prompt: Pull my highlights out of this KoboReader.sqlite
loader_feasibility: pyodide's built-in sqlite3 opens the uploaded DB file fully in-browser; nothing leaves the device.
rationale: Kobuddy exists precisely because Kobo locks highlights inside an SQLite file; doing it locally avoids handing your reading history to a script.

name: weighted-random-sampler
description: Draws a weighted random sample of rows from a CSV or JSON dataset, with or without replacement.
example_prompt: Sample 100 rows from this CSV weighted by the population column
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; reservoir/alias sampling with seeded RNG.
rationale: Building representative subsamples for testing and surveys.

name: csv-collapse-rows
description: Groups CSV rows by key columns and collapses a chosen column's values into a single delimited cell.
example_prompt: Group by order_id and combine all item names into one comma-separated cell
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; group-by accumulation in memory, no network
rationale: The inverse of explode, needed to roll line-items back up into one row per entity.

name: video-onscreen-text-detector
description: Detects frames containing burned-in on-screen text/graphics to locate titles, captions, or watermarks.
example_prompt: Find where there's text on screen in this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg frames feed an onnx text-detection model executed locally.
rationale: Locating on-screen text segments speeds re-versioning, watermark spotting, and OCR scoping without a server.

name: json-schema-faker
description: Generates N rows of realistic fake data that conform to a JSON Schema, respecting formats like email, uuid, and date-time.
example_prompt: Generate 20 fake records matching this user JSON Schema
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — schema-driven value synthesis with built-in format generators, deterministic seed optional, no server.
rationale: Seeding test databases and mocking APIs needs schema-faithful fake data, which is otherwise a separate tooling install.

name: bank-statement-reconcile
description: Reconciles a bank-statement CSV against a bookkeeping ledger by date and amount with fuzzy memo matching, listing unmatched items and suggested matches.
example_prompt: Reconcile this bank statement against my ledger and show what doesn't match
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM matches rows by amount + date window + fuzzy description in-browser; sensitive financial data never leaves the device.
rationale: Bank reconciliation needs date-tolerance and memo-fuzzy matching that a generic two-column reconcile doesn't provide, and privacy makes client-only ideal.

name: pem-bundle-splitter
description: Splits a multi-block PEM bundle into individual labeled blocks (certificates, keys, CSRs) and reports the type and order of each.
example_prompt: Split this PEM bundle into its individual certificates
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM PEM boundary parsing; the bundle never leaves the browser.
rationale: Concatenated cert chains and key bundles must often be separated, and getting the order/type right by hand is fiddly and sensitive.

name: regex-column-validate
description: Flags CSV column values that don't match a supplied regex pattern.
example_prompt: Check that every value in the phone column matches my pattern
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSV parse plus regex; client-side — via regex crate
rationale: Per-column format validation is a core data-quality step not covered by generic CSV tools.

name: ocr-text-cleaner
description: Fixes common OCR substitution errors such as 'rn'→'m', 'l'/'1', '0'/'O', and stray spacing around punctuation.
example_prompt: Clean up the obvious OCR mistakes in this scanned text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM rule-based confusable-substitution pass; runs locally
rationale: OCR output has predictable, repetitive error classes that a focused rule set can repair faster than re-typing.

name: json-to-dynamodb-batch
description: Converts a JSON array of items into a DynamoDB BatchWriteItem request payload with typed attributes.
example_prompt: make a DynamoDB batch-write request from these 5 JSON items for table Orders
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM: builds typed-attribute JSON and the batch structure locally.
rationale: Bulk-loading DynamoDB requires the verbose typed batch format that is painful to write manually.

name: target-mean-encoder
description: Replaces a categorical column with the mean of a numeric target per category (with optional smoothing) to produce model-ready numeric features.
example_prompt: Target-encode the city column using the conversion column in this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a group-by mean with smoothing over the table, computed in-browser.
rationale: Target encoding is a staple feature-engineering step that the backlog's one-hot/feature encoders don't cover, and smoothing is easy to get wrong.

name: class-rebalancer
description: Balances an imbalanced label column by random over-sampling the minority class or under-sampling the majority to a target ratio, with a fixed seed.
example_prompt: Balance this dataset by oversampling the rare label class
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: deterministic seeded row resampling over the table, fully in-browser.
rationale: Class imbalance wrecks classifier training and resampling is the first fix people reach for, yet no over/under-sampling tool exists in the backlog.

name: person-name-splitter
description: Parses a free-form full-name column into title, first, middle, last, and suffix components, handling particles like "van"/"de" and "Jr.".
example_prompt: Split the full_name column into first and last name columns
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: rule-based name tokenization over the column, runs client-side.
rationale: Contact and CRM imports arrive with one name field that must be split for mail-merge and matching, and only address parsers (not name parsers) exist.

name: bson-inspector
description: Parses a BSON document into a typed tree showing element names, BSON types, and nested documents.
example_prompt: Decode this BSON document into readable JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: BSON is a length-prefixed typed format parsed deterministically in the browser
rationale: MongoDB exports and dumps are BSON, and reading them without a Mongo install is frequently needed.

name: speech-audio-quality-checker
description: Pre-flights a recording for ASR by checking sample rate, channel count, SNR, and clipping against transcription-readiness thresholds.
example_prompt: Is this audio clean enough to transcribe accurately?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — combines header inspection and level/SNR DSP over PCM, fully browser-local.
rationale: Knowing upfront whether audio meets ASR quality bars avoids wasted transcription passes on hopeless recordings.

name: flac-to-ogg-vorbis
description: Transcodes lossless FLAC into Ogg Vorbis for smaller, broadly playable lossy files.
example_prompt: make ogg vorbis files from my flac album
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader decodes FLAC and encodes Vorbis losslessly-to-lossy in wasm.
rationale: Lossy Vorbis copies of a FLAC archive are handy for game assets and bandwidth-limited playback.

name: msgpack-to-json
description: Decodes a MessagePack binary blob (hex or uploaded file) into pretty-printed JSON for inspection.
example_prompt: Decode this MessagePack payload to JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (rmp-serde + serde_json) decoding the bytes in-memory. — via rmp-serde crate
rationale: Debugging MessagePack wire payloads is otherwise a manual binary-reading nightmare.

name: enum-domain-check
description: Flags CSV column values that fall outside an allowed set of categories.
example_prompt: Find rows where the status column isn't one of active/inactive/pending
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM set membership over parsed CSV; local
rationale: Categorical columns drift to typos and stray values that only a domain check catches.

name: video-embed-cover-art
description: Embeds a chosen image as the poster/cover thumbnail of an MP4 or MKV file.
example_prompt: set this png as the thumbnail/cover image for my mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — attaches the image as an attached_pic/cover stream in the WASM runtime.
rationale: A baked-in cover thumbnail makes files look right in players and media servers instead of showing a blank frame.

name: video-audio-bitrate-set
description: Re-encodes just the audio at a chosen bitrate (e.g. 128k) to shrink oversized soundtracks while keeping the video.
example_prompt: drop the audio bitrate to 96k to save space
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — audio-only re-encode with -b:a, video copied, in the WASM runtime.
rationale: Bloated 320k+ audio is wasted bytes for spoken-word video, and trimming it is an easy size win.

name: wav-to-csv-samples
description: Exports decoded PCM samples to CSV with one column per channel and a time/index column.
example_prompt: Export this WAV's samples to a CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: decodes PCM and writes comma-separated rows, no external dependency.
rationale: Engineers and students need sample values in a spreadsheet for plotting and analysis.

name: video-chapter-export
description: Parses embedded chapter markers and exports them to a CSV/JSON/cue/text file without splitting the video.
example_prompt: Export the chapter markers from this MP4 to a CSV
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader (ffprobe -show_chapters) reads chapter metadata directly, client-side.
rationale: Existing chapter markers are useful as a standalone index for YouTube descriptions or re-muxing, distinct from generating or splitting.

name: sql-schema-extractor
description: Parses CREATE TABLE / ALTER statements from a SQL dump and emits a clean table/column/constraint model.
example_prompt: Extract the table and column definitions from this SQL dump.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs a SQL DDL parser over the text locally, producing a structured schema.
rationale: Turning a messy DDL dump into a structured schema feeds diagrams, migrations, and type generation.

name: dotenv-to-shell
description: Converts a .env file into export-prefixed shell statements (and back), handling quoting and special characters.
example_prompt: Turn this .env into export statements I can source <pastes .env>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — key/value parsing and shell-quoting rules are pure text transformation.
rationale: sauce's per-directory env management maps cleanly to a browser-local env-format converter with correct quoting.

name: video-audio-track-selector
description: Keeps a single chosen audio track (e.g. the English one) from a multi-track video and drops the rest.
example_prompt: Keep only the second audio track in this video and remove the others
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg stream mapping (-map) selects one track in ffmpeg.wasm, copying streams locally.
rationale: Multi-language rips carry several audio tracks that confuse players; isolating one is common cleanup.

name: audio-resampler
description: Converts an audio file to a different sample rate with high-quality resampling.
example_prompt: Resample this 48 kHz file down to 44.1 kHz.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg aresample (soxr) in the wasm build; no server. — via rubato crate
rationale: Sample-rate conversion is a frequent compatibility fix for editors, games, and telephony with no current tool.

name: uniform-border-detector
description: Detects a solid uniform frame/border around an image and measures its thickness on each side.
example_prompt: How thick is the white border around this scan?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM walks inward from each edge over decoded pixels to find border extent.
rationale: Border measurement guides automatic deframing of scans and screenshots.

name: clipping-detector
description: Scans decoded PCM for clipped (full-scale) samples and consecutive-over runs, reporting count, timestamps, and worst regions.
example_prompt: Check this WAV for clipping and tell me where it's distorted
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: symphonia decodes to PCM in-browser, then a simple sample-threshold scan flags overs with no server needed — via symphonia crate
rationale: Clipping is the single most common audio defect and a fast objective pass/fail check before release.

name: genomic-vcf-to-tsv
description: Flattens genomic Variant Call Format (.vcf) records, including INFO/sample fields, into a tidy TSV.
example_prompt: Flatten this variants.vcf into a TSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line parser splitting the structured INFO/FORMAT columns; runs offline.
rationale: Genomic VCFs pack key data in compound columns that analysts must explode before any spreadsheet work.

name: posthoc-pairwise-comparison
description: After an omnibus test, runs post-hoc pairwise comparisons (Tukey HSD, Dunn) with corrected p-values.
example_prompt: Which of these four groups differ? Run Tukey HSD
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs statsmodels' pairwise_tukeyhsd (precompiled for WASM) on the in-browser dataset.
rationale: Post-hoc comparison (the scikit-posthocs demand) is the missing step after ANOVA and runs entirely offline.

name: dataset-quality-checker
description: Audits a CSV for missing values, duplicates, type issues, high cardinality, and leakage warnings.
example_prompt: Run a data-quality check on this CSV
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs pandas-based profiling and validation checks locally on the uploaded data.

name: ics-merge-dedupe

rationale: Reusable rule-based data validation is exactly the automated-validation demand, with no infrastructure needed.

name: simplenote-export-to-markdown

name: grayscale-convert

name: qr-styled

name: pie-donut-chart-svg

name: tiff-to-png

name: aac-to-mp3

name: molecular-weight-calculator
description: Computes molecular weight, exact mass and elemental composition from a molecular formula or SMILES.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; formula tokenizing and atomic-mass lookup run locally with a built-in element table.

name: text-to-hex

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure byte-to-hex formatting, no dependencies or network needed

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure hex parsing and UTF-8 reconstruction, fully client-side

name: bar-chart-svg

example_prompt: Bar chart of total sales by region from this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM aggregates and draws the bars into SVG locally.
rationale: Categorical comparison charts are core to the business-analytics programs on the list.

name: mortgage-calculator
description: Computes monthly mortgage payment (principal, interest, taxes, insurance) and total cost.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — payment math runs locally with no backend.
rationale: The highest-volume finance calculator query, served privately without a server.

name: quiz-generator
description: Builds a multiple-choice or short-answer quiz with an answer key from any text you provide.

loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a question-generation model client-side and plain Rust assembles distractors — fully local.
rationale: 'Cognitive Sandbox' learning demand; self-quizzing from your own material, offline and private.

name: timezone-converter
description: Converts a datetime across time zones, including DST handling and a multi-city comparison view.

rationale: Extends the date-picker demand into timezone math, a high-frequency need for scheduling across regions.

name: pixel-art-editor

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM manages the pixel buffer and PNG encoding behind a canvas UI; all editing and export happen in the browser. — via png crate

name: format-css
description: Formats CSS/SCSS/LESS with consistent indentation, spacing, and declaration ordering.
example_prompt: Format this CSS for me

name: rent-affordability

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM arithmetic, offline.

name: html-validate

name: rent-vs-buy

loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM scenario math.
rationale: A classic high-value decision calculator with no current equivalent.

name: format-code
description: Auto-format source code (JS/TS, JSON, CSS, Markdown, etc.) to a consistent style.

name: gdrive-link-converter

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure URL pattern parsing and rewriting; no Google API call needed.

name: zip-explorer
description: An interactive in-page browser for an uploaded archive: navigable tree, per-file size, and inline preview of text and images.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the archive index and decodes entries on demand; the tool page renders the tree and previews client-side. — via zip crate

name: net-worth-tracker

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: summation and grouping of entered line items, no backend.

name: salary-convert

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM arithmetic; browser-local.
rationale: Hourly-to-salary conversion is a common everyday financial calculation.

name: youtube-transcript

name: image-translate

name: image-color-replace

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM per-pixel color match/replace. — via image crate
rationale: Quick recolor/cleanup task distinct from chroma-key (video) and background-remove.

name: xml-beautify

rationale: XML/SOAP/config files remain widespread and are painful to read unformatted.

name: regex-playground

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the `regex` crate compiles and runs entirely client-side. — via regex crate
rationale: Regex testing is a daily dev need that should never require a server round-trip.

name: email-syntax-validate

rationale: List hygiene needs syntactic validation that stays private (no upload to a verifier).

rationale: RAW metadata is hard to read without bulky desktop apps; this does it instantly in-browser.

name: nmea-to-csv

example_prompt: Turn this NMEA GPS log into a CSV of coordinates
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM sentence parser with checksum validation; runs on the uploaded log.
rationale: Raw GPS receiver logs are NMEA and unusable until decoded into coordinates.

name: chorus

example_prompt: Add a chorus effect to make this synth sound wider and lush
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg chorus or Rust modulated-delay lines — fractional-delay DSP runs in WASM.
rationale: Chorus is a staple richness/width effect for vocals, guitars, and synths.

name: scrypt

name: language-detect

rationale: A natural companion to translation that is small and fully offline.

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM (image crate) applies LUT-from-curve per pixel, offline.

name: address-parse

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM libpostal-style parser; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: Address normalization is a frequent data-cleaning and form-processing need.

name: responsive-images

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM batch resize/encode + HTML emit; browser-local.

name: html-sanitizer

name: log-timeline

rationale: Separates meaningful logic changes from cosmetic churn, which line diffs hopelessly conflate after a reformat.

name: network-config-parser

name: html-diff

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — date diffs against a user-supplied reference date.
rationale: Surfacing what's overdue or imminent is the first thing every task tool user looks for.

name: url-analyzer

name: chat-transcript-formatter

name: video-frame-fingerprint

rationale: Automates the tedious hunt for compositionally similar frames between two pieces of footage.

name: column-value-diff
description: Joins two tables on a key column and reports where a chosen value column disagrees, with old/new pairs.
example_prompt: join these two CSVs on id and show me where the price column differs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSV parse + keyed join; offline table work
rationale: Verifying a single field across two datasets (price, status, count) is a focused, frequent reconciliation.

name: video-duration-fix-remux
description: Rebuilds a container to repair missing or wrong duration metadata without re-encoding.
example_prompt: This webm shows 00:00 duration — fix it
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM remuxes with a stream copy entirely in-browser.
rationale: Streamed/recorded webm files routinely have broken duration headers that break seeking.

name: csv-fill-down
description: Forward-fills empty cells in chosen columns with the last non-empty value above them, like a spreadsheet fill-down.
example_prompt: Fill the blank category cells down from the value above in this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; single linear pass over rows, no server
rationale: Merged-cell exports leave huge gaps that must be filled before the data is usable for grouping.

name: sort-json-array
description: Sorts a JSON array of objects by one or more keys, ascending or descending.
example_prompt: sort this json array of users by age descending
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; serde_json parse, key-based sort, re-serialize locally
rationale: Reordering record arrays by a field is a frequent data-prep step before display or import.

name: csv-column-mapping-suggest
description: Given two CSVs with differently-named columns, suggests a column mapping using header similarity and value-overlap so they can be aligned before diffing or joining.
example_prompt: These two CSVs use different column names — suggest how to map them onto each other
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM compares headers (fuzzy) and samples value distributions to score candidate mappings in-browser; pure data analysis.
rationale: Real-world dataset comparison stalls on schema mismatch; auto-suggesting the column mapping is the missing precursor to every existing CSV diff/join tool.

name: video-two-pass-encode
description: Performs a 2-pass encode at a target average bitrate for accurate, evenly distributed quality.
example_prompt: Two-pass encode this to an average 2 Mbps
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg-wasm runs the analysis and encode passes over the file in-browser.
rationale: Two-pass yields far better bitrate accuracy than CRF/CBR for size-targeted delivery and is distinct from existing single-knob tools.

name: video-audio-rms-timeline
description: Extracts windowed RMS and peak audio levels from a video's audio track into a CSV time series.
example_prompt: Export an RMS/peak audio level timeline for this video as CSV
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (loaded) astats filter reports per-window RMS/peak; tabulated in WASM locally
rationale: Level timelines drive auto-ducking, clipping detection, and finding the loud moments without leaving the browser.

name: syslog-triage
description: Parses and filters Linux syslog/auth.log, highlighting sudo, SSH auth, and cron events for a quick intrusion review.
example_prompt: Find failed SSH logins and sudo use in this auth.log
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — line parsing and pattern matching
rationale: UAC/unix_collector dump /var/log, and reading the security-relevant lines fast is the actual triage need.

name: sql-linter
description: Parses SQL and flags syntax errors plus anti-patterns like SELECT *, missing aliases, and implicit joins.
example_prompt: lint this query and tell me what's wrong with it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with sqlparser-rs for the AST plus rule checks; entirely static analysis with no execution. — via sqlparser crate
rationale: ORM users writing raw fragments want fast feedback on correctness and style without spinning up a database.

name: geojson-merge
description: Combine multiple GeoJSON files or features into one FeatureCollection.
example_prompt: Merge these two GeoJSON files into a single FeatureCollection
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via georust/geojson — collection concatenation is pure compute. — via geojson crate
rationale: Stitching layers together is a routine GIS prep task with no good no-upload web tool.

name: video-faststart
description: Moves the MP4 moov atom to the front of the file so it starts playing before fully downloading (web-optimized).
example_prompt: Optimize this mp4 so it streams instantly on the web
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm runs -movflags +faststart with stream copy, rewriting the atom order locally and instantly.
rationale: Progressive web playback breaks when moov is at the end; faststart is a tiny but high-impact fix.

name: bulk-artifact-extractor
description: Scans any file or disk-image blob for emails, URLs, IPs, domains, phone numbers, Bitcoin addresses, and Luhn-validated credit-card numbers, reporting each with its byte offset.
example_prompt: Extract all emails, URLs, and credit card numbers from this disk image
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: regex scanning over uploaded bytes needs no network or OS and runs entirely in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: Reproduces bulk_extractor's most-used PII/IOC triage pass without sending sensitive evidence to a server.

name: lua-runner
description: Executes a snippet of Lua entirely in the browser and returns its output and any errors.
example_prompt: Run this Lua: `local t={} for i=1,5 do t[i]=i*i end return table.concat(t,',')`
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a pure-Rust Lua VM (e.g. `hematita`) compiles to wasm32 and runs sandboxed in wasmi; supports a core subset of the standard library. — via hematita crate
rationale: mlua/hlua/rust-lua53 all exist to run Lua, and a zero-install in-browser Lua sandbox is a directly useful, demand-aligned tool (with honest stdlib-subset limits).

name: markdown-strip
description: Strip all Markdown formatting (headings, emphasis, links, code fences, tables) to produce clean plain text.
example_prompt: Remove the markdown formatting from this README and give me just the plain text
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: parse the Markdown AST (pulldown-cmark) and emit text nodes only; pure compute, fully browser-local. — via pulldown-cmark crate
rationale: Common need when pasting docs into plain-text fields or TTS; markdown-to-html exists but the reverse (to plain text) does not.

name: pickle-to-json
description: Loads a Python pickle file containing plain data (dicts, lists, numbers, strings, DataFrames) inside a sandboxed interpreter and serializes it to readable JSON.
example_prompt: Show me what's inside this .pkl file as JSON
loader_feasibility: pyodide: unpickling and json conversion happen in the isolated WASM Python runtime, so nothing leaves the browser. — via serde-pickle crate
rationale: Pickle is opaque without running Python; a sandboxed viewer lets people inspect saved data files they'd otherwise have to spin up an interpreter for.

name: correlated-feature-pruner
description: Computes the pairwise correlation matrix of numeric columns and drops one column from each pair above a chosen threshold to reduce collinearity.
example_prompt: Drop highly correlated numeric columns above 0.9 in this dataset
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Pearson correlation over numeric columns and greedy pruning, computed client-side.
rationale: Removing redundant correlated features is routine pre-modeling hygiene, and the only `collinear` tool in the backlog is for geometry points, not feature columns.

name: duplicate-column-detector
description: Finds columns whose values are identical (optionally ignoring header name) and reports or removes the redundant copies.
example_prompt: Find and drop duplicate columns in this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: column-hash comparison across the table, runs locally.
rationale: Joins and exports often produce silently duplicated columns under different names; detecting them by content is something no existing tool does.

name: video-gps-metadata-extractor
description: Extracts GPS location metadata embedded by phones (QuickTime ©xyz and udta atoms) and reports latitude/longitude.
example_prompt: Does this video have GPS location data in it?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: reads the QuickTime metadata atoms straight from the file, no network geocoding.
rationale: Users often need to find or audit location data leaking from phone videos before sharing them.

name: video-audio-loudness-compare
description: Measures integrated LUFS and true peak for two videos' audio and reports the loudness gap.
example_prompt: Is the audio louder in the new version than the old one?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg ebur128/loudnorm analysis on both audio tracks runs fully in the wasm build.
rationale: Loudness mismatches between versions break consistent playback across an edit.

name: video-scene-cut-diff
description: Detects scene-cut timestamps in two edits of the same footage and lists added, removed, or moved cuts.
example_prompt: Compare the cut points between the rough cut and the final cut
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg scene-detection on both files plus Rust→WASM list alignment runs in the wasm build.
rationale: A cut-level diff documents exactly how an edit evolved between versions.

name: collage-splitter
description: Detects the cells of a photo-grid collage and exports each original photo back out individually.
example_prompt: Split this 2x2 collage back into the four separate photos
loader_feasibility: plain Rust finds border/gutter lines and crops the cells entirely in WASM. — via image crate
rationale: People often receive a collage but want the source photos back, which is annoying to crop by hand.

name: funnel-conversion-analyzer
description: Computes step-by-step conversion and drop-off rates from an event CSV.
example_prompt: Compute the signup funnel conversion from this events CSV: <paste>
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM CSV parsing and per-step counting; offline.
rationale: Funnel analysis is a premium analytics feature (Matomo/Swetrix) that is just computation over the user's own event data.

name: nostr-key-encoder
description: Converts Nostr identifiers between hex and NIP-19 bech32 forms (npub/nsec/note/nprofile/nevent).
example_prompt: convert this nostr npub to hex: npub1sn0wdenkukak0d9dfczzeacvhkrgz92ak56egt7vdgzn8pv2wfqqhrjdv9
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bech32 + hex codec is pure computation, no network, and keeps secret keys (nsec) on-device. — via bech32 crate
rationale: Nostr users constantly swap between hex and bech32, and doing it offline avoids ever pasting a private key into a website.

name: geocode
description: Convert an address to latitude/longitude or coordinates back to an address.
example_prompt: What are the coordinates of the Eiffel Tower?
loader_feasibility: Calls the free OSM Nominatim API via the HTTP host import; parsing client-side.
rationale: Foundational location lookup that feeds static-map, geo-distance, and weather.

name: image-dedupe
description: Find near-duplicate images in a set using perceptual hashing and report similarity clusters.
example_prompt: Which of these photos are duplicates or near-duplicates?
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — pHash/dHash computation and Hamming-distance clustering run locally on decoded pixels.
rationale: Cleaning up duplicate photos is a real recurring chore and perceptual hashing is lightweight.

name: video-audio-hum-remover
description: Removes 50/60 Hz mains hum and its harmonics from a video's audio with a tuned notch filter chain.
example_prompt: Remove the electrical hum from this video's audio
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's anequalizer/highpass notch filters run in ffmpeg.wasm, processing audio locally.
rationale: Ground-loop hum is a pervasive recording flaw with a deterministic, well-known fix.

name: video-add-silent-audio
description: Adds a silent audio track to a video that has none, so platforms requiring an audio stream will accept it.
example_prompt: This silent video gets rejected on upload — add a silent audio track
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg generates anullsrc and muxes it in ffmpeg.wasm without re-encoding video.
rationale: Many platforms and editors choke on audioless video, and a silent track is the standard workaround.

name: numeric-string-sanitizer
description: Strips thousands separators, currency symbols, units, and stray whitespace from messy number cells and parses them into clean floats.
example_prompt: Clean this column of '$1,234.50 USD' style values into plain numbers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — regex/parse on text columns, fully local
rationale: Imported financial/scientific CSVs are full of unparseable formatted numbers and this is the standard pre-analysis fix.

name: broken-image-batch-checker
description: Tries to decode a batch of images and returns a pass/fail list of which files are unreadable or corrupt.
example_prompt: Tell me which of these images won't open
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg/plain Rust→WASM attempts to decode each file in turn fully in-browser. — via image crate
rationale: Finding the one broken file in a folder of hundreds is painful manually; a batch checker isolates it fast.

name: env-schema-validate
description: Validates a .env file against a declared schema of required keys, types, and allowed values.
example_prompt: check my .env against these required variables
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM dotenv parse plus rule check; text-only and offline.
rationale: Missing or mistyped env vars cause confusing runtime failures that an upfront schema check eliminates.

name: sas-xpt-reader
description: Reads SAS XPORT (.xpt) transport files and converts them to CSV.
example_prompt: Convert this FARS .xpt file to CSV
loader_feasibility: pyodide (pandas.read_sas) decodes the SAS transport format in-browser.
rationale: FARS crash data and most federal health datasets ship as SAS .xpt, which is unreadable without SAS or Python.

name: data-profile
description: Produces a profiling report: inferred types, missing %, cardinality, distribution summaries, and top values per column.
example_prompt: Profile this dataset and tell me what's in each column.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM multi-pass over columns; fully local.
rationale: A lightweight pandas-profiling clone is exactly what New/Junior Data Scientist audiences reach for first.

name: shapefile-to-geojson
description: Converts an uploaded .shp/.dbf/.shx shapefile set into GeoJSON.
example_prompt: Convert this census tract shapefile to GeoJSON
loader_feasibility: shapefile Rust crate→WASM parses geometry + attributes locally. — via shapefile crate
rationale: Census/government boundary data ships almost exclusively as shapefiles, but the web needs GeoJSON.

name: cookieless-visitor-counter
description: Counts unique visitors from a log using the daily-salted-hash method, storing no cookies or PII.
example_prompt: Count unique visitors in this log without cookies: <paste>
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM daily-salted hashing of IP+UA then distinct-count; offline.
rationale: This is exactly how Plausible and GoatCounter count uniques privately, and it is pure local computation over the user's own data.

name: gpx-simplify
description: Reduces the point count of a GPX track with the Douglas-Peucker algorithm at a chosen tolerance while preserving shape.
example_prompt: Simplify this huge GPX track to fewer points without losing the route shape
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — geometric simplification math runs entirely client-side.
rationale: Dense OwnTracks/PhoneTrack exports are heavy to render or share, and local simplification shrinks them privately.

name: keep-to-markdown
description: Converts a Google Takeout Keep export (JSON/HTML) into Markdown notes with labels and checkboxes preserved.
example_prompt: Convert my Google Keep export to Markdown
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the Takeout JSON/HTML and emits Markdown, fully offline.
rationale: The 'Google Keep Exporter' demand is literally people leaving Keep for Obsidian/Joplin who need clean Markdown without trusting a random web converter with their notes.

name: payment-qr
description: Builds a BIP21 (or generic text) payment URI and renders it as a scannable QR code image.
example_prompt: Make a Bitcoin payment QR for address bc1q... requesting 0.005 BTC
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the pure-Rust qrcode crate rendering to a PNG buffer; no server needed.
rationale: Generating a payment QR offline avoids leaking the receiving address to a third-party QR service.

name: spectral-eq-match
description: Matches a track's EQ curve and loudness to a chosen reference, deriving and applying a corrective filter.
example_prompt: Make my mix sound tonally like this reference track
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — spectrum estimation, filter derivation, and FFT convolution all run in wasmi.
rationale: This is exactly what matchering does, and reference-matched mastering has strong creator demand.

name: registry-hive-parser
description: Opens raw Windows registry hives (NTUSER.DAT, SYSTEM, SOFTWARE) and lets you browse keys, values, and RunKeys.
example_prompt: Browse the Run keys and recent docs in this NTUSER.DAT hive
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: registry hives are a self-describing binary (regf) format read directly from the uploaded file.
rationale: Registry hives hold persistence, user activity, and config evidence (Zimmerman RECmd) that analysts repeatedly hand-parse.

name: shellbags-parser
description: Extracts shellbag entries from a registry hive to reconstruct folders a user browsed, including deleted/removable paths.
example_prompt: Reconstruct the folders this user opened from the shellbags in this UsrClass.dat
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: shellbags are nested ITEMIDLIST blobs inside the registry binary, parsed entirely client-side.
rationale: Shellbags prove folder access even after deletion, a high-value Zimmerman SBECmd artifact.

name: amcache-parser
description: Parses Amcache.hve to list installed and executed programs with SHA-1 hashes and first-run times.
example_prompt: List every executable that ran on this system from Amcache.hve with hashes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Amcache is a registry hive variant read directly from the uploaded bytes.
rationale: Amcache gives program-execution evidence with hashes for malware triage (AmcacheParser) without a desktop install.

name: usnjrnl-parser
description: Parses the NTFS $UsnJrnl change journal to show file creation, rename, and deletion events over time.
example_prompt: Show every file that was deleted according to this $UsnJrnl
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the journal is a stream of USN records parsed sequentially from the upload.
rationale: The change journal captures file activity (incl. deletions) the MFT alone misses, key for anti-forensics detection.

name: pcap-file-extractor
description: Reassembles and carves files transferred over HTTP, FTP, and SMB inside a PCAP capture for download.
example_prompt: Extract any files that were downloaded in this pcap
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: TCP stream reassembly and protocol carving are pure computation.
rationale: NetworkMiner's signature file-extraction feature, run locally so exfiltrated artifacts never leave the analyst's machine.

name: csv-data-explorer
description: Loads a CSV and returns summary stats, dtypes, and a describe() table.
example_prompt: Summarize this CSV
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs pandas in-browser, data never leaves the device.
rationale: Mirrors the exploratory workflows taught in data-science courses (Python Data Science Handbook demand).

name: stl-repair
description: Recomputes normals, removes degenerate and duplicate triangles, and reports watertightness for an STL.
example_prompt: Clean up this STL — fix normals and remove duplicate triangles
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: triangle-soup cleanup is pure geometry.
rationale: Dirty STLs from scanners/exporters are a constant headache and repair is otherwise a desktop-app task.

name: faceted-filter
description: Runs faceted search over a JSON dataset: returns filtered results plus facet value counts, sorting and pagination.
example_prompt: give me facet counts by brand and price-range for this product JSON, filtered to in-stock items
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — group-by and counting over an in-memory array, exactly itemsjs's model, entirely local.
rationale: Faceted browsing over a dataset is a common need with no good offline tool today.

name: fuzzy-csv-join
description: Joins two CSVs on a key column using approximate (fuzzy) matching instead of exact equality, surfacing matched and unmatched rows.
example_prompt: Fuzzy-join these two CSVs on the 'name' column with a 0.85 similarity threshold
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — CSV parsing plus string distance, no server required.
rationale: Record-linkage on messy spreadsheets is a frequent, painful task with no good browser-local tool.

name: json-transform-rules
description: Reshapes JSON from a source structure to a target using declarative match/transform rules (json-transforms/jsontl).
example_prompt: Transform this nested API response into {id, name, total} using a mapping rule.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM rule interpreter walks the tree and emits the target locally.
rationale: Declarative shape mapping is the core of API/ETL glue and avoids hand-written loops.

name: eth-wallet
description: Generates an Ethereum wallet — a secp256k1 private key, public key, and checksummed address.
example_prompt: generate a new ethereum wallet for me
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via RustCrypto's `k256` + keccak hashing seeded by the browser CSPRNG; never touches a network. — via k256 crate
rationale: Maps the Privy wallet demand; generating a wallet that the key never leaves the device for is exactly what browser-local enables.

name: age-encrypt
description: Encrypt text with the modern age format using either a passphrase or one or more X25519 recipient public keys, producing an armored ciphertext.
example_prompt: encrypt this note with age to age1ql3z7...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (the rage/age crate is pure Rust); scrypt/X25519 + ChaCha20-Poly1305 all run client-side so plaintext never leaves the browser.
rationale: age is the backend behind `passage` and the standard modern alternative to GPG, and no age tool exists in the catalog (only PGP).

name: compose-to-diagram
description: Turns a docker-compose.yml into a Mermaid diagram of services, dependencies, and networks.
example_prompt: Draw a diagram of the services in this docker-compose file: [paste yaml]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; parses compose and emits Mermaid text, all local. — via serde_yaml crate
rationale: Gives lazydocker/dockly-style visibility into a multi-service stack at a glance, with no tooling.

name: spreadsheet-formula-audit
description: Scans a workbook for circular references, broken references, and formula errors and reports the offending cells.
example_prompt: Find any circular references or #REF! errors in this workbook.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — IronCalc builds the cell dependency graph in-memory to detect cycles and error states. — via ironcalc crate
rationale: Debugging broken spreadsheets is tedious by hand and a precise engine catches every bad cell.

name: chunk-list
description: Splits a list of lines or comma-separated items into fixed-size chunks (e.g. for batching).
example_prompt: split these 500 ids into chunks of 50
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM slices the parsed item list into N-sized groups locally
rationale: Batching IDs for paginated APIs or IN-clauses is a recurring need with awkward manual counting.

name: numeric-column-coercer
description: Forces a text column to numeric, stripping stray whitespace and flagging or quarantining cells that can't be parsed.
example_prompt: Coerce this column to numbers and tell me which cells failed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: per-cell parse attempt + error report, no I/O.
rationale: Type coercion with an error report is the first cleanup step on almost any messy export and isn't covered yet.

name: pdf-javascript-extractor
description: Locates and extracts embedded JavaScript from a PDF, de-obfuscating common encodings for review.
example_prompt: Extract any JavaScript embedded in this PDF
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: stream decoding (FlateDecode etc.) and JS extraction are local byte operations. — via lopdf crate
rationale: Embedded JS is the classic PDF attack vector; pulling it out safely for inspection is a core pdf-parser workflow.

name: job-posting-parser
description: Extracts title, company, location, salary, and listed skills from a pasted job posting.
example_prompt: Parse this job posting into structured fields
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM rule/regex extraction over the posting text, no network.
rationale: The 250k+ job-postings demand reflects a real need to structure free-text listings.

name: text-generate
description: Continue or generate text from a prompt using a small local language model.
example_prompt: continue this story: 'The lighthouse keeper noticed…'
loader_feasibility: transformers.js small causal LM (e.g. distilgpt2/SmolLM, WebGPU); no server. — model Xenova/distilgpt2
rationale: Adds genuine generation (vs the transform-only paraphrase/summarize) fully offline.

name: json-remove-nulls
description: Recursively removes keys whose values are null (optionally also empty strings/arrays/objects) from JSON.
example_prompt: strip out all the null fields from this JSON response
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM walks the parsed tree and prunes null nodes before re-serializing
rationale: API payloads are full of null noise that obscures the data you actually care about.

name: fixed-width-to-csv
description: Splits fixed-width / column-positional text records into CSV using a supplied or inferred column spec.
example_prompt: Parse this fixed-width COBOL report into CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM byte-offset slicing; deterministic and fully offline.
rationale: Legacy mainframe/banking exports are fixed-width and notoriously painful to convert correctly.

name: topojson-to-geojson
description: Expands compact TopoJSON (with shared arcs) into standard GeoJSON features.
example_prompt: Convert this TopoJSON map to GeoJSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM arc-stitching over the TopoJSON structure; pure local computation.
rationale: TopoJSON is a common compact map distribution format that most mapping libraries still need as GeoJSON.

name: image-skin-tone-analyzer
description: Detects skin-tone pixels and reports their average hue, suggesting a warm/cool white-balance correction.
example_prompt: Are the skin tones in this portrait too orange?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: skin-color thresholding in YCbCr plus averaging — offline math. — via image crate
rationale: Portrait correction hinges on neutral, natural skin tones.

name: background-color-detector
description: Determines the likely background color by sampling corners and edges and checking for a dominant uniform fill.
example_prompt: What's the background color of this product shot?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM samples border pixels and clusters them locally.
rationale: Knowing the exact background color is essential for matting, padding, and seamless web placement.

name: geo-cluster
description: Clusters lat/long points using grid or DBSCAN and returns cluster assignments and centroids.
example_prompt: Cluster these GPS points into hotspots.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM spatial clustering with haversine distance; local only.
rationale: Hotspot detection is a natural extension of the taxi-data demand and runs client-side.

name: multilingual-sentiment
description: Scores the sentiment (1–5 stars / positive–negative) of reviews and comments in many languages including Hindi, Bangla, and Spanish.
example_prompt: Is this Hindi movie review positive or negative?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js loads the multilingual BERT sentiment ONNX model and runs inference in-browser; no API key, no server. — model Xenova/bert-base-multilingual-uncased-sentiment
rationale: Maps the Hindi Movie Reviews, IIT Patna Movie Review Sentiment, and SAIL 2015 demand into a single working classifier instead of a static dataset.

name: verify-signature
description: Verifies an Ed25519/RSA signature over a message against a public key.
example_prompt: verify this signature against the public key
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM RustCrypto verification — pure CPU check, client-side — via ed25519-dalek crate
rationale: Signature verification is the counterpart to signing and a common release/identity check developers need.

name: python-lint
description: Lint a Python snippet for errors and style issues (undefined names, unused imports, PEP8) with line-precise findings.
example_prompt: lint this Python function
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs pyflakes/pycodestyle in-browser.
rationale: Python is the most popular language and has no linter here yet; pyodide makes it fully local.

name: image-embed
description: Produce a CLIP vector embedding for an image for similarity search, clustering, or dedup.
example_prompt: give me the embedding vector for this image
loader_feasibility: transformers-js / onnx CLIP image encoder runs in-browser; mirrors the existing text-embed tool. — model Xenova/clip-vit-base-patch32
rationale: An image-side counterpart to text-embed unlocks visual similarity and cross-modal matching locally.

name: zero-shot-classifier
description: Sorts text into any labels you provide without training, using an entailment model.
example_prompt: Classify this email as billing, support, or sales.
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs an NLI model (bart-mnli) entirely in-browser. — model Xenova/bart-large-mnli
rationale: Flexible labeling without training data covers a huge range of triage and tagging use cases.

name: time-series-resample
description: Resample/aggregate a timestamped series to a coarser interval (e.g. minute→hour, day→week).
example_prompt: resample this daily CSV to weekly sums
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM time bucketing.
rationale: A fundamental time-series operation distinct from categorical groupby-aggregate and data-smooth.

name: tar-archive-lister
description: Enumerates tar archive members with paths, sizes, modes, owners, and types without unpacking.
example_prompt: Show me what's inside this tar file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the `tar` crate iterating headers in the byte stream; offline parsing only. — via tar crate
