rationale: A safe, private way to inspect tarball contents before committing to extraction.

name: question-answering
description: Answers a question using only the passage you provide and quotes the supporting span.
example_prompt: Based on this contract, what is the notice period?
loader_feasibility: rust-bert/transformers-js extractive QA model (DistilBERT-SQuAD) runs in WASM. — model Xenova/distilbert-base-cased-distilled-squad
rationale: Extractive QA over a pasted document gives grounded answers without sending the document anywhere.

name: docx-comment-extractor
description: Extracts tracked review comments from a .docx into a CSV with author, anchored text, and date.
example_prompt: Pull all the reviewer comments out of this Word doc
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM ZIP plus comments.xml parse; fully client-side. — via zip crate
rationale: Consolidating reviewer comments from a doc into a list is tedious to do by hand.

name: cookie-parser
description: Splits a Cookie or Set-Cookie string into individual cookies with their attributes (Domain, Path, Expires, flags).
example_prompt: parse this Set-Cookie header and show the flags
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string parsing per RFC 6265, no server
rationale: Inspecting cookie attributes for security review is a precise, common dev need.

name: json-mask
description: Selects a subtree of JSON using GitHub-style field syntax like a,b(c,d).
example_prompt: Mask this JSON to only url,owner(login) fields.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM mask parser prunes the value tree locally.
rationale: Field-masking trims big API payloads to just what's needed, mirroring partial-response APIs.

name: ledger-balance
description: Parses a ledger/hledger plain-text journal and computes balances for every account and sub-account.
example_prompt: Give me account balances from this hledger journal
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the ledger journal format is plain text parsed and summed client-side.
rationale: ledger/hledger's balance report is the most-used command and works perfectly on pasted text with zero install.

name: embedding-export
description: Embeds each row/document of an uploaded dataset and exports the vectors as CSV/JSON ready to load into a vector database.
example_prompt: Generate embeddings for the 'description' column of this product CSV and give me a JSON I can import into Qdrant
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs the embedding model client-side; plain Rust->WASM assembles the export file in memory. — model Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
rationale: People adopting Qdrant/ruvector need vectors first, and producing them locally avoids shipping private text to an embedding API.

name: question-answer
description: Answer a question by extracting the relevant span from a supplied context passage (extractive QA).
example_prompt: given this paragraph, when was the company founded?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js (DistilBERT-SQuAD); small extractive model runs fully client-side. — model Xenova/distilbert-base-uncased-distilled-squad
rationale: Grounded extractive QA over pasted text is a top agent use case and needs no large generative model.

name: rerank
description: Re-rank a list of passages/documents by relevance to a query using a cross-encoder.
example_prompt: rank these 6 paragraphs by relevance to 'refund policy'
loader_feasibility: transformers.js cross-encoder (ONNX) running on WASM/WebGPU; fully local. — model Xenova/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2
rationale: Core RAG-pipeline step with no in-catalog equivalent; pairs with the existing embed/chunk tools.

name: profanity-filter
description: Flags or masks profane and unsafe words in a block of text using a built-in wordlist.
example_prompt: check this comment for profanity and mask any bad words
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM matches against a bundled wordlist; no model or network.
rationale: 'Word Safety' demand maps to a lightweight client-side content filter for user-generated text.

name: ledger-register
description: Produces a filtered, running-total transaction register from a ledger/hledger journal by account or date range.
example_prompt: Show all Expenses:Food transactions this quarter from this ledger file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — filtering and running-balance math over parsed journal text, offline.
rationale: the register view is hledger's second core report and answers 'where did my money go' without any tooling.

name: form-field-validator
description: Validates form values (email, phone, URL, postal code, credit card) against locale rules and returns per-field errors.
example_prompt: Check if these form entries are valid: email john@, phone 555-12
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with regex and Luhn checks — deterministic validation runs entirely in the browser.
rationale: Client-side validation is the one part of a form pipeline that should never depend on a SaaS backend.

name: full-text-search
description: Searches across pasted documents with BM25/TF-IDF ranking, stemming, and snippet highlighting, returning ranked results.
example_prompt: Search these support articles for 'refund not processed' and rank the best matches
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — ranking math and tokenization run entirely in the browser.
rationale: Delivers Algolia/CloudSh-style search results with zero server and full privacy over the user's own corpus.

name: persian-ner
description: Extracts named entities (people, organizations, locations) from Persian text.
example_prompt: Find all the people and places in this Persian news paragraph
loader_feasibility: transformers-js token-classification with a Persian NER model (trained on Arman/PEYMA-style data) converted to ONNX, run client-side. — model HooshvareLab/bert-fa-base-uncased-ner-peyma
rationale: Persian NER (ArmanPersoNERCorpus, FarsiYar) is core to information extraction, search, and redaction over Persian documents.

name: x25519-ecdh
description: Generates X25519 keys and derives a shared secret from your private key and a peer's public key.
example_prompt: derive the shared secret between my x25519 key and this peer public key
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the x25519-dalek crate; scalar multiplication computed in-sandbox
rationale: ECDH key agreement is the basis of every modern secure channel (gocrypto/kyber-adjacent) and is meaningless if the private key leaves the device.

name: audio-limiter
description: Applies a brick-wall true-peak limiter to prevent clipping while maximizing level.
example_prompt: Limit this master to -1 dBTP so it never clips.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg alimiter filter; runs in-browser.
rationale: A safety limiter is the standard last step before export and pairs with the loudness/peak tools.

name: typescript-to-json-schema
description: Converts a TypeScript interface or type alias into an equivalent JSON Schema.
example_prompt: Turn this TypeScript interface into a JSON Schema
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a Rust TS type-syntax parser emits the schema; no compiler service needed
rationale: Closes the loop on the codegen demand from the other direction — devs constantly need runtime validation matching their existing TS types.

name: env-file-sort
description: Sorts, deduplicates, and groups keys in a .env file while preserving comments.
example_prompt: sort and dedupe the keys in this .env file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line transform; fully client-side.
rationale: Tidy, ordered .env files reduce merge conflicts and missed-duplicate bugs.

name: code-comment-extractor
description: Strips out and lists all comments from a source file across common comment syntaxes.
example_prompt: Extract just the comments from this code.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: lexer-style comment detection per language runs offline.
rationale: Useful for reviewing documentation density or generating comment-only summaries.

name: voice-activity-validator
description: Runs a small VAD model over a file to confirm it actually contains speech and reports the proportion of speech vs non-speech.
example_prompt: Confirm this file labeled as speech actually contains voice
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a compact VAD model on decoded frames entirely in the browser, no server. — model onnx-community/silero-vad
rationale: Speech datasets and voicemail dumps contain mislabeled silent or music-only files, and a VAD validator filters them out.

name: video-pixel-diff-csv
description: Exports a per-frame CSV of percent changed pixels and mean/max pixel delta between two aligned videos.
example_prompt: Export per-frame difference stats between these two clips as a CSV
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — blend=difference + signalstats metadata logged per frame in ffmpeg.wasm
rationale: Turns visual diffs into chartable numbers for QC pipelines and regression tracking.

name: diff-to-markdown
description: Renders a unified diff as a clean Markdown document with fenced diff blocks and a per-file change summary.
example_prompt: Format this patch as markdown for a PR description
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse the diff and template Markdown output in-memory
rationale: Drops patches straight into PR bodies, issues, or docs with proper formatting and a summary header.

name: env-file-merger
description: Merges multiple layered .env files with last-wins override semantics and shows the resolved environment plus which file set each value.
example_prompt: Merge .env then .env.local then .env.prod and show me the final values and where each came from
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — in-memory map merge over pasted file contents, no filesystem access required.
rationale: rs-env/direnv layering is exactly this override chain, and reasoning about which layer won is the #1 source of 'why is this variable wrong' bugs.

name: frequency-encoder
description: Replaces categorical values with their occurrence count or relative frequency, turning high-cardinality columns into a single numeric feature.
example_prompt: Replace the product_id column with its frequency in this dataset
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: single-pass value counts mapped back over rows, fully local.
rationale: Frequency/count encoding is a go-to for high-cardinality categoricals where one-hot explodes, and nothing in the backlog provides it.

name: constant-column-dropper
description: Detects and removes zero-variance columns — those with a single repeated value (or all-null) — from a CSV.
example_prompt: Remove all columns that have the same value in every row of this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: per-column distinct-count scan with row rewrite, no server.
rationale: Constant columns add noise and break some models; pruning them is a standard cleanup that no current tool automates.

name: wav-samples-to-json
description: Exports PCM samples as a JSON array alongside format metadata for use in code.
example_prompt: Give me this WAV's samples as a JSON array
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: decodes PCM and serializes to JSON locally, no server round-trip.
rationale: Web developers loading audio into JS visualizers want a ready-to-import JSON sample array.

name: face-embedding-extractor
description: Computes a numeric face-identity embedding vector for each detected face for matching and clustering.
example_prompt: Give me the face embedding vector for the person in this photo
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a face-recognition embedding model in WASM, keeping biometric vectors on-device. — model immich-app/buffalo_l
rationale: Local face-clustering and dedup of a photo library needs embeddings that should never leave the user's machine.

name: nostr-event-signer
description: Builds and schnorr-signs a Nostr event from your nsec, emitting publish-ready JSON to copy into any relay client.
example_prompt: sign this nostr kind-1 note 'gm' with my nsec (stays local)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — secp256k1 schnorr signing runs entirely client-side so the private key never leaves the browser. — via k256 crate
rationale: Signing locally is the safe way to craft events; the key stays on the device instead of in a server-side tool.

name: json-to-query-string
description: Serializes a JSON object into a properly percent-encoded URL query string.
example_prompt: Build a query string from this JSON object
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM encoder; deterministic, fully client-side.
rationale: Constructing correctly-encoded query params by hand routinely breaks on spaces and special chars.

name: json-to-markdown-table
description: Turns a JSON array of objects into a Markdown table, using union of keys as columns.
example_prompt: Convert this JSON array into a Markdown table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via serde_json + formatting; pure local transform. — via serde_json crate
rationale: Frequently needed to drop API responses into documentation without a server.

name: spline-smoother
description: Fits smoothing splines to noisy series to reveal the underlying trend.
example_prompt: Smooth this noisy time series and show the trend
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs scipy's UnivariateSpline on the parsed series and plots in-browser. — via csaps crate
rationale: Smooth additive trends (the pyGAM demand) are a common analytics need scipy handles fully offline.

name: data-format-sniffer
description: Detects whether pasted or uploaded data is CSV, TSV, JSON, JSONL, XML, Parquet, or Avro and reports delimiter/encoding.
example_prompt: What format is this file and how is it delimited?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM magic-byte + heuristic sniffing; no network.
rationale: Open datasets arrive with wrong or missing extensions; knowing the real format unblocks every other tool.

name: onnx-image-classifier
description: Runs a bundled or uploaded ONNX image classifier on a photo and returns the top-k labels.
example_prompt: What's in this image? Classify it
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime (web) executes the model with WASM/WebGPU fully client-side.
rationale: Demonstrates real model inference and deployment in the browser, a headline applied-ML topic.

name: clip-zero-shot-image-classifier
description: Classifies an image against user-supplied text labels using an in-browser CLIP model.
example_prompt: Is this photo a cat, a dog, or a fox?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs the CLIP image and text encoders entirely client-side. — model Xenova/clip-vit-base-patch32
rationale: Directly maps Prompt Engineering for Vision Models — text-prompted, training-free vision.

name: naive-bayes-text-classifier
description: Trains a Naive Bayes text classifier on labeled examples in-browser and classifies new text.
example_prompt: Train a spam classifier on these labeled messages, then classify this one.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; bag-of-words counting and Bayes math train and predict locally.
rationale: Building a classifier from scratch is the central 'Understand & Implement NLP' lesson and needs no model download.

name: secretbox-decrypt
description: Decrypts a libsodium crypto_secretbox ciphertext given the nonce and key, verifying the Poly1305 tag.
example_prompt: open this libsodium secretbox with my key and nonce
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the crypto_secretbox crate's verifying open; no server involved.
rationale: Reading libsodium-encrypted blobs is the inverse of the Kalium/halite secretbox demand.

name: json-coerce-types
description: Cleans up loosely-typed JSON by coercing stringified numbers, booleans, and nulls into native JSON types.
example_prompt: Fix this JSON where numbers and booleans are quoted strings.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (serde_json with serde-aux-style coercion) rewrites values locally.
rationale: APIs and CSV imports often emit everything as strings, and auto-coercing them saves tedious manual cleanup.

name: recurring-task-expander
description: Expands recurrence rules (e.g. rec:1w, rec:+2m, weekday patterns) on tasks into the next N concrete dated instances.
example_prompt: Expand the recurring tasks in this todo.txt for the next 8 weeks
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — date arithmetic on a supplied 'today'; the local clock is passed in, no network.
rationale: Recurrence (topydo/Ultralist 'rec:') is fiddly to compute by hand and is a clear value-add done locally.

name: semantic-dedupe
description: Finds near-duplicate or paraphrased entries in a text list using embedding similarity above a threshold.
example_prompt: Find near-duplicate questions in this support FAQ list
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — embeddings computed locally, then pairwise similarity filtering in WASM with no upload. — model Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
rationale: Exact-match dedup misses paraphrases; semantic dedup catches them and is a genuine pain point for content lists.

name: json-log-formatter
description: Pretty-prints, aligns, and filters structured JSON log lines by level or field for readable inspection.
example_prompt: Pretty-print these JSON logs and only show entries where level is error
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with serde_json parsing and formatting the pasted log lines client-side.
rationale: Reproduces fblog's job of making dense JSON logs human-readable without piping potentially sensitive logs through a server.

name: xlsx-recalculate
description: Opens an uploaded .xlsx workbook, recomputes every formula cell, and returns the workbook with refreshed values.
example_prompt: Recalculate all the formulas in this budget.xlsx and show me the updated totals.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — IronCalc parses and recalculates xlsx workbooks in-memory; file bytes never leave the browser. — via ironcalc crate
rationale: Frequently needed when a spreadsheet was edited by a tool that didn't refresh cached formula results.

name: yaml-resume
description: Renders a YAML or JSON Resume document into a styled, print-ready HTML/PDF resume.
example_prompt: render my YAML resume into a clean PDF
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM templates the structured data to HTML and uses the browser's print-to-PDF; no service.
rationale: YAMLResume/JSON-Resume users want polished output without committing to a hosted renderer.

name: mv-script-generator
description: Turns a before→after filename mapping into a safe bash `mv` (or PowerShell `Rename-Item`) script plus the matching undo script.
example_prompt: Generate a bash mv script and an undo script for these renames
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string assembly with shell-quoting; fully local
rationale: massren-style tools ultimately produce rename commands, and emitting a reviewable script (with rollback) is the safest browser-local form of that.

name: diff-hunk-selector
description: Splits a pasted unified diff into individual hunks and lets you pick a subset to export as a smaller patch.
example_prompt: Let me pick just some hunks from this diff to make a partial patch
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses and re-emits valid patch text in-browser.
rationale: Reproduces git-crecord / `add -p` hunk surgery without a repo, useful for splitting changes apart.

name: markdown-link-extractor
description: Lists every link and image in a Markdown document and flags broken reference-style definitions.
example_prompt: List all the links in this markdown and find any broken references
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM markdown AST walk; intra-document link validation done locally
rationale: auditing links in long docs is tedious by hand and complements the markdown tooling suite.

name: subdomain-extractor
description: Extracts unique, deduplicated hostnames and subdomains from pasted logs, source or scan output and groups them by registrable domain.
example_prompt: pull all unique subdomains out of this log dump
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — regex extraction and dedup over text, fully local.
rationale: Harvesting hostnames from artifacts is a foundational recon prep step and pure text processing.

name: self-signed-cert
description: Generate a self-signed X.509 certificate plus its private key from subject/SAN fields.
example_prompt: Make a self-signed cert for localhost valid 1 year
loader_feasibility: Rust rcgen/x509 compiled to WASM; outputs PEM in-browser. — via rcgen crate
rationale: Common dev/test need distinct from the CSR-only and keypair-only tools.

name: album-art-tool
description: Extracts embedded cover art from audio files or embeds a chosen image as the album cover.
example_prompt: Embed this cover.jpg into all the tracks in this album
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: cover art lives in the file's metadata atoms/frames and is read/written entirely in the WASM runtime. — via lofty crate
rationale: ncmpcpp/musikcube users obsess over correct embedded artwork; extracting and embedding covers is a frequent library-grooming task.

name: email-syntax-validator
description: Validates email address syntax and flags disposable or role-based domains against a bundled list.
example_prompt: Check whether these email addresses are validly formatted and which are disposable
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: RFC syntax checks and local domain-list lookup, no DNS/SMTP
rationale: socialscan also validates emails; the format/disposable check is fully local and useful for list cleaning.

name: sentence-split
description: Segment text into individual sentences, correctly handling abbreviations and decimals.
example_prompt: Split this paragraph into one sentence per line
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM rule-based segmenter with an abbreviation list, offline.
rationale: A common preprocessing primitive for NLP pipelines not covered by token/char chunking.

name: rtf-to-markdown
description: Convert RTF documents to clean Markdown or plain text.
example_prompt: Convert this .rtf file to Markdown
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust RTF parser → Markdown in-browser.
rationale: Fills a doc-format gap alongside docx/epub/pptx converters.

name: red-eye-remove
description: Detect and neutralize red-eye in flash photos of people.
example_prompt: Remove the red-eye from this flash photo
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime/plain WASM — eye detection plus red-channel desaturation in the iris region, all local.
rationale: A classic, narrowly-scoped photo fix that's satisfying to automate offline.

name: html-to-jsx
description: Convert raw HTML into React JSX (class→className, self-closing tags, style objects).
example_prompt: Convert this HTML snippet to JSX for React
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust HTML parse + JSX serialization in-browser; no server.
rationale: Ubiquitous React workflow (transform.tools) distinct from html-to-markdown/html-to-text.

name: json5-convert
description: Convert JSON5/JSONC (comments, trailing commas, unquoted keys) to strict JSON and back.
example_prompt: convert this JSON5 with comments to strict JSON: <paste>
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM json5 parser.
rationale: Config files (tsconfig, VS Code) use JSONC; strict json-format chokes on them.

name: svg-to-jsx
description: Convert an SVG into a ready-to-use React component (or JSX), camelCasing attributes.
example_prompt: Turn this SVG icon into a React component
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust SVG parse + JSX serialization in-browser.
rationale: Routine React workflow (svgr) distinct from svg-optimize/svg-to-png.

name: explain-query-plan
description: Runs EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on a query against a provided schema and explains how the engine would execute it.
example_prompt: explain the query plan for this SELECT and tell me if it uses an index
loader_feasibility: pyodide's sqlite3 builds the schema in memory and returns the real EXPLAIN output, rendered client-side.
rationale: Query-plan understanding is core to ORM/query-builder performance work and rarely available without a live database.

name: facial-landmark-detector
description: Locates facial landmark points (eyes, nose, mouth, jaw) on faces in an image.
example_prompt: Mark the facial landmarks on this portrait
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a 68-point landmark ONNX model client-side on the cropped face region.
rationale: Landmarks power alignment, filters, and measurement use cases and are dlib's other headline feature.

name: video-to-hls
description: Segments a video into HLS .ts chunks plus an .m3u8 playlist for adaptive web streaming, all packaged in-browser.
example_prompt: Split this video into HLS segments with a playlist
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm's hls muxer writes segments and the m3u8 to the virtual filesystem, zipped for download locally.
rationale: Self-hosting streaming video requires HLS packaging that normally needs a server-side encoder.

name: guitar-tab-to-midi
description: Converts ASCII guitar tablature into a MIDI file by mapping string/fret positions to pitches.
example_prompt: Convert this guitar tab into MIDI so I can hear it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the tab grid, maps frets to MIDI notes per tuning, and writes a Standard MIDI File locally.
rationale: Huge amounts of music exist only as ASCII tab and players want to audition it as MIDI.

name: wav-to-raw-pcm-extractor
description: Strips the WAV header and chunks to output the bare interleaved PCM sample bytes.
example_prompt: Give me just the raw PCM bytes from this WAV file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses the data chunk offset and slices out the payload, fully local.
rationale: DSP pipelines and embedded players frequently need headerless PCM rather than a container.

name: media-integrity-checker
description: Probes an audio/video file's streams to detect truncation, missing moov atoms, or codec/container mismatches.
example_prompt: Is this MP4 corrupt or truncated?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (ffprobe-style demux) compiled to WASM; runs on the uploaded file locally
rationale: Corrupt media is hard to diagnose and a local probe avoids uploading large private files to a service.

name: phylip-to-fasta
description: Converts PHYLIP sequential or interleaved multiple-sequence-alignment files into standard FASTA.
example_prompt: Convert this interleaved PHYLIP alignment to FASTA
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: header-driven block parsing of the PHYLIP grid into FASTA records, fully local.
rationale: Phylogenetics pipelines emit PHYLIP but most viewers want FASTA, and interleaved-vs-sequential parsing trips people up.

name: nexus-to-fasta
description: Extracts the sequence matrix from a NEXUS file's DATA/CHARACTERS block and writes it out as FASTA.
example_prompt: Pull the alignment out of this NEXUS file as FASTA
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: block-scanning text parser for the NEXUS command grammar, runs in the sandbox.
rationale: NEXUS bundles trees, data, and assumptions blocks together; isolating just the alignment as FASTA is a recurring need with no current tool.

name: audio-frequency-band-isolator
description: Isolates a single frequency band with a band-pass filter to extract or solo a sound (e.g. just the bass or just sibilance).
example_prompt: Isolate just the 100-250Hz band from this mix so I can hear the bass
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — `bandpass` with center frequency and width; pure in-browser ffmpeg.wasm filtering.
rationale: Soloing a band is invaluable for diagnosing problem frequencies or extracting a part, and a dedicated band-pass is simpler than fighting a full EQ.

name: timestamp-extractor
description: Extracts dates and timestamps from text and lists them in a normalized format.
example_prompt: Pull all the dates and timestamps out of this log.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: multi-format date pattern matching and parsing runs client-side.
rationale: Reconstructing a timeline from logs or notes requires structured timestamp extraction.

name: drawdown-analyzer
description: Computes maximum drawdown, drawdown duration, recovery time, and the underwater curve from an equity or returns series.
example_prompt: What's the max drawdown of this equity curve?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM running-max scan; fully local.
rationale: Drawdown is the headline risk metric for any strategy/portfolio and needs only the series itself.

name: cumulative-percent-builder
description: Sorts values descending and adds running count, cumulative sum, and cumulative percentage columns for Pareto analysis.
example_prompt: Build a Pareto cumulative-percent table from these counts
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: sort + cumulative arithmetic, no I/O.
rationale: The 80/20 Pareto cumulative-percent table is a frequent analysis with no current tool.

name: graphql-mock-from-sdl
description: Generates mock JSON response data for every type in a GraphQL SDL schema.
example_prompt: Here's my GraphQL schema — give me mock data for a User and its nested posts.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: SDL parsing and field-type-to-value mapping are deterministic and local. — via graphql-parser crate
rationale: Front-end devs need realistic GraphQL mocks before the backend exists, with no live endpoint required.

name: ldif-to-csv
description: Parses an LDAP LDIF export into CSV, mapping each entry to a row and attributes to columns.
example_prompt: Convert this LDIF directory export to CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: LDIF is line-oriented text with base64 attribute decoding, all done in-memory.
rationale: Directory admins need LDIF dumps in CSV to review users and groups in a spreadsheet.

name: merge-conflict-resolver
description: Parses Git conflict markers in pasted text and lets the user keep ours/theirs/both side by side.
example_prompt: Help me resolve these merge conflicts
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing of <<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>> markers; pure text, no repo access.
rationale: Conflict resolution is a top git-addon ask and is just structured text editing.

name: yaml-path-query
description: Query or edit YAML values by a path expression while preserving the rest of the file.
example_prompt: get the value at spec.containers[0].image in this YAML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — `serde_yaml` + path resolver run in-sandbox. — via serde_yaml crate
rationale: Direct map of YAML Paths; surgically reading/editing deep YAML (k8s, CI configs) is high-value.

name: magic-bytes-fixer
description: Detects corrupted or wrong file headers and repairs the magic bytes/structure for PNG, JPEG, ZIP, PDF, and more.
example_prompt: This PNG won't open — fix its header so it renders
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: header detection and byte patching operate on the file buffer in memory.
rationale: Deliberately broken headers are a staple of forensic challenges and this also rescues genuinely damaged files, all without an upload.

name: arff-converter
description: Converts Weka ARFF machine-learning datasets to and from CSV, preserving attribute types.
example_prompt: Convert this ARFF dataset to CSV
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM text parsing; runs fully in-browser.
rationale: ARFF is a common classic-ML dataset format with almost no modern converters.

name: youtube-upload-spec-checker
description: Validates a video against YouTube's recommended upload specs (codec, frame rate, bitrate, color, audio) and lists each deviation.
example_prompt: Is this video optimized for YouTube upload?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: ffprobe metadata from ffmpeg.wasm is checked against the spec ruleset client-side.
rationale: Matching the recommended specs avoids a quality-degrading re-encode on YouTube's side.

name: tiktok-video-spec-checker
description: Validates a video's vertical aspect ratio, resolution, duration, and codec against TikTok's upload requirements.
example_prompt: Check if this clip meets TikTok's video specs
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: ffprobe metadata from ffmpeg.wasm is compared to TikTok's ruleset client-side. — via mp4 crate
rationale: Wrong aspect ratio or over-length clips get letterboxed or trimmed by TikTok, hurting reach.

name: image-region-change-grid
description: Divides two aligned images into a grid and reports which cells changed and by how much, giving a compact 'what changed where' summary.
example_prompt: Break these two images into a grid and tell me which cells changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM diffs per cell and tabulates change scores locally
rationale: A cell-level summary is more actionable than a raw heatmap for triaging regressions.

name: audio-declick
description: Detects and repairs clicks, ticks, and crackle (vinyl/digital glitches) by interpolating over them.
example_prompt: Remove the clicks and crackle from this vinyl rip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg adeclick filter; impulse detection + interpolation in wasm
rationale: Declicking is essential for digitized vinyl and dropout-laden recordings.

name: notes-to-html-export
description: Bundles a set of markdown notes into a single styled, self-contained HTML page with a table of contents.
example_prompt: Export these markdown notes as one HTML page I can share
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — markdown-to-HTML rendering, fully local — via pulldown-cmark crate
rationale: note/Noted/NoteSH users want a portable, shareable export without cloud services.

name: pgp-decrypt
description: Decrypts an ASCII-armored PGP message using your private key and passphrase.
example_prompt: Decrypt this PGP block with my private key, my passphrase is hunter2
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (rPGP); private-key decryption is local CPU crypto, so the secret key stays in the browser tab. — via pgp crate
rationale: Pairing decrypt with encrypt is essential and keeping the private key client-side is the whole point of GnuPG.

name: base64-to-audio-file
description: Decodes a base64 string or data: URI back into a downloadable audio file.
example_prompt: Decode this base64 audio string into a playable file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: strips any data-URI prefix and base64-decodes to bytes, fully local.
rationale: Audio pulled from JSON payloads or data URIs needs decoding back to a real file to use.

name: json-schema-to-sample
description: Generates a minimal valid example JSON instance that satisfies a given JSON Schema, honoring required fields and defaults.
example_prompt: Give me an example JSON object that validates against this JSON Schema
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — walks the schema tree and constructs a conforming instance, no validator service.
rationale: Producing a valid example by hand from a deep schema is tedious; a generator makes API docs and fixtures trivial.

name: yaml-deep-merge
description: Deep-merges multiple YAML documents with override semantics, mirroring how Helm layers values files.
example_prompt: Merge these base values.yaml and override.yaml the way Helm would
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — YAML parsing and recursive merge run fully client-side. — via serde_yaml crate
rationale: Helm's most reused mechanic is values-file layering; a standalone deep-merge is useful far beyond Kubernetes.

name: json-transform-pipeline
description: Applies a chain of functional transforms (map, filter, pluck, group-by, sort-by, unique, flatten) to a pasted JSON array.
example_prompt: Group these orders by `customer` and sum each group's `total`
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a declarative transform interpreter over the parsed JSON runs entirely client-side.
rationale: ramda-cli, underscore-cli, and fx all express demand for composable data wrangling without writing a script.

name: video-grayscale
description: Converts a color video to grayscale/black-and-white.
example_prompt: Make this video black and white
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's hue=s=0 / format=gray runs in ffmpeg.wasm with local pixel transforms.
rationale: A simple, frequently-requested stylistic transform with an unambiguous result.

name: number-to-currency-formatter
description: Formats a raw number as a currency string with chosen symbol, grouping, and decimal places (no live rates).
example_prompt: format 1234.5 as EUR with comma decimals
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure string formatting, no network, fully local.
rationale: Presentation-only currency formatting is common and needs no exchange-rate server.

name: license-plate-reader
description: Detects vehicle license plates in an image and reads the plate text with region formatting.
example_prompt: Read the license plate in this photo
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime handles plate detection and OCR in WASM, keeping potentially sensitive footage local.
rationale: Parking, logistics, and personal use cases need plate reading and on-device keeps surveillance data private.

name: number-words-to-digits
description: Parses spelled-out numbers ("two hundred forty-three", "one point five million") into numeric digits.
example_prompt: Convert 'two hundred forty-three' to a number
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — word-to-value grammar with an embedded lexicon, no model needed.
rationale: Legal, financial, and transcript text writes amounts in words that need digitizing for computation.

name: dummy-csv-generator
description: Generates a CSV of N rows with user-specified typed columns for testing and demos.
example_prompt: Make a 1000-row CSV with columns id (int), price (float), category (A/B/C).
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: typed value generation and CSV serialization are pure local computation.
rationale: Quick throwaway CSVs for testing imports and charts are needed often with no good offline tool.

name: er-diagram-from-sql
description: Generates a Mermaid entity-relationship diagram from SQL CREATE TABLE statements and foreign keys.
example_prompt: Make a Mermaid ER diagram from these CREATE TABLE statements.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: DDL parsing and Mermaid text emission require no rendering server, just string output.
rationale: Visualizing an existing schema's relationships is valuable for documentation and onboarding.

name: histogram-maker
description: Plots a histogram (with optional KDE) of a chosen numeric column to show its distribution.
example_prompt: Show the distribution of customer ages in this dataset
loader_feasibility: pyodide numpy bins the data and matplotlib renders the histogram PNG locally.
rationale: Distribution inspection is step one of statistical thinking from Regression, a Friendly Guide.

name: cagr-calculator
description: Computes compound annual growth rate and period-over-period growth for a value series.
example_prompt: What's the CAGR of this GDP column from 2000 to 2023?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM math; runs locally.
rationale: Growth-rate computation is the most-requested derivation from economic time series.

name: histogram-svg
description: Bins a numeric column and renders a histogram as an SVG image.
example_prompt: Histogram of the age column with 20 bins
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM bins values and draws bars into SVG client-side.
rationale: Distribution plots are the most common first chart a data-science learner makes.

name: z-score-calculator
description: Computes z-scores for values given a mean and standard deviation, or standardizes a dataset.
example_prompt: z-score for 85 when mean is 70 and sd is 10
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — arithmetic standardization runs instantly in-browser.
rationale: Common stats-class operation that's quick and exact as a dedicated tool.

name: cloud-share-direct-link
description: Rewrites a Nextcloud, Dropbox, Google Drive or OneDrive share-page URL into its direct-download URL.
example_prompt: Turn this Nextcloud share link into a direct download URL for curl
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM URL/string transformation against known share-link patterns — pure local rewriting.
rationale: The 'Nextcloud share URL downloader' demand is literally a URL-pattern transform that needs no server.

name: php-formatter
description: Reformats PHP source to a consistent PSR-style layout entirely in the browser.
example_prompt: Format this PHP: `<?php function f($a,$b){if($a){return $a+$b;}return 0;}`
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a pure-Rust PHP parser/formatter (the Mago toolchain / php-parser-rs) compiles to wasm32 and runs without a PHP runtime. — via mago-formatter crate
rationale: phper lets developers build PHP extensions in Rust, and that audience edits PHP stubs/tests that benefit from a no-install formatter.

name: ruby-runner
description: Executes a snippet of Ruby in the browser and returns its output, powered by a pure-Rust Ruby implementation.
example_prompt: Run this Ruby: `puts (1..10).select(&:even?).sum`
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Artichoke is a pure-Rust, mruby-compatible Ruby that already targets wasm32 (it ships a web playground), so it runs sandboxed in wasmi. — via artichoke crate
rationale: anima-engine/mrusty embeds mruby in Rust, and a zero-install in-browser Ruby sandbox is the natural user-facing realization of that capability.

name: least-squares-regression
description: Fits a linear (or polynomial) least-squares model to data points and reports coefficients and R².
example_prompt: Fit a line to these (x,y) points and give me the slope and intercept
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: faer-rs/nalgebra solve the normal-equations/QR least-squares (LAPACK gels role) client-side. — via nalgebra crate
rationale: Linear regression is one of the most common quantitative tasks and works perfectly offline on pasted data.

name: fft-analyzer
description: Computes the discrete Fourier transform of a signal and returns the frequency-magnitude spectrum.
example_prompt: Give me the frequency spectrum of this list of samples
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the rustfft crate (the GSL FFT equivalent) compiles to WASM and transforms the signal in-browser.
rationale: FFT-based spectral analysis is a frequent need in audio, sensor, and signal work and runs instantly client-side.

name: html-entity-codec
description: Encodes characters to HTML entities and decodes named, decimal, and hex entities back to text.
example_prompt: decode these HTML entities: <div>&copy;2026
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — uses a bundled named-entity table; no DOM or network required.
rationale: Entity encode/decode is a perennial need when sanitizing or un-mangling copied web/markup content.

name: json-validate
description: Validate a JSON document against a JSON Schema and report each failing path with a clear message.
example_prompt: validate this JSON payload against this schema and list the errors
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: the jsonschema crate runs Draft validation entirely locally.
rationale: The execution counterpart to the backlog's json-schema-generate, closing the schema loop.

name: pdf-bookmarks
description: Adds a bookmark/outline tree to a PDF for easier navigation.
example_prompt: Add bookmarks for each chapter in this PDF
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — lopdf writes outline objects into the document catalog locally. — via lopdf crate
rationale: Navigable outlines make long documents far more usable, especially on e-readers.

name: base64-validator
description: Validates base64/base64url strings and reports padding and alphabet errors.
example_prompt: Is this a valid base64url string?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — decode/validate, local
rationale: Encoding errors are a frequent debugging dead-end that a quick validator resolves.

name: image-to-embedded-array
description: Converts an image into a C/C++ byte array (RGB565, RGB888, mono, or XBM) for embedded TFT/OLED displays.
example_prompt: Convert this icon.png to an RGB565 C array for a 128x64 OLED
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM uses the `image` crate to decode and re-encode pixels into the chosen array format with no server. — via image crate
rationale: Embedded/IoT developers constantly need image-to-array conversion and existing converters are clunky desktop or web-upload tools.

name: email-spam-score
description: Scores an email's spamminess with transparent heuristics: link ratio, caps, trigger phrases, header anomalies.
example_prompt: How spammy does this email look?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies a rule set locally with no SpamAssassin server.
rationale: A quick, private spam estimate for a suspicious message has no good local equivalent.

name: boxplot-chart
description: Render box-and-whisker plots showing distribution, quartiles, and outliers per group.
example_prompt: show a box plot of scores by class from this CSV
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust rendering to PNG/SVG, client-side.
rationale: Box plots are a standard distribution visualization not in the current chart tools.

name: audio-reverse
description: Reverses an audio clip.
example_prompt: Play this clip backwards
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg areverse filter reverses decoded samples client-side.
rationale: Reversal is a quick creative/editing effect that runs instantly on-device.

name: tailwind-palette-generator
description: Produces a full 50–950 tint/shade scale from one base color, matching Tailwind/shadcn token conventions.
example_prompt: Generate a Tailwind color scale from #2563eb
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — lightness/chroma interpolation in OKLCH done entirely in-WASM.
rationale: Every Tailwind/shadcn project needs consistent numbered color ramps and hand-tuning them is tedious.

name: http-header-explainer
description: Explains each header in a request/response, including what it does and any security or caching implications.
example_prompt: Explain these response headers: Strict-Transport-Security, Cache-Control: no-store, X-Frame-Options: DENY
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with an embedded header-reference table; pure lookup and formatting, no network.
rationale: Bundles HTTP knowledge offline so devs debugging clients/servers stop tab-hopping to MDN for every header.

name: regex-literal-escape
description: Escapes arbitrary text into a regex-safe literal for PCRE, JS, or RE2 flavors.
example_prompt: regex-escape the string a.b*c+(d)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: metacharacter table substitution, fully in-sandbox.
rationale: Matching user-supplied text literally requires correct escaping that varies by regex flavor.

name: iqr-outlier-trimmer
description: Removes rows whose values fall outside Q1-k·IQR to Q3+k·IQR (Tukey fences) for a chosen column.
example_prompt: Drop the IQR outliers from the price column
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: quartile computation plus row filtering, fully client-side
rationale: IQR/Tukey-fence row removal is the textbook outlier-deletion method and differs from clipping or NaN cleaning.

name: ceil-floor-to-multiple
description: Rounds each value up (ceil) or down (floor) to the nearest multiple of a given step, with direction selectable.
example_prompt: round these up to the next multiple of 50: 120, 201, 350
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — divide/ceil-or-floor/multiply per element, fully offline.
rationale: Directional snapping (always up for capacity/billing, always down for buckets) is distinct from nearest-multiple rounding and a common pricing/grid need.

name: text-region-detector
description: Finds and outlines all text regions in an image, returning their bounding boxes.
example_prompt: Show me where all the text is in this image
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a DBNet/CRAFT text-detection model locally to produce boxes.
rationale: Box detection is a reusable building block for redaction, cropping, and targeted OCR.

name: regex-capture-to-csv
description: Applies a regex with named capture groups across text and emits one CSV row per match.
example_prompt: Use this regex with named groups to extract a CSV from my log lines
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM regex engine; pure text scanning, fully local. — via regex crate
rationale: A general regex-to-table extractor covers countless ad-hoc parsing needs in one tool.

name: pkcs12-inspect
description: Lists the bag structure of a PKCS#12 (.p12/.pfx) container — cert bags, key bags, and friendly names — without requiring the password to read the outer structure.
example_prompt: What's inside this .pfx file's structure?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM ASN.1 walk of the PFX SafeContents; purely structural inspection in-browser, keys never exported or uploaded
rationale: People often need to know what bags a .pfx holds before importing it, and doing that locally avoids exposing a key store.

name: limiter
description: Applies brickwall peak limiting to a ceiling so the signal never clips.
example_prompt: Limit this mix so nothing goes above -0.3 dBFS
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: look-ahead peak detection with fast gain reduction to the ceiling — in-buffer.
rationale: A limiter is the final safety/loudness stage before export and pairs naturally with normalize.

name: apply-patch
description: Apply a unified diff/patch to a pasted source file and return the patched result (and detect conflicts).
example_prompt: Apply this diff to my file and show the result
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — local unified-diff parser and hunk application, fully in-block.
rationale: Useful for reviewing AI-suggested patches in chat without leaving to a terminal; text-diff only shows diffs.

name: blurhash
description: Generate a compact BlurHash/ThumbHash placeholder string (and preview) for progressive image loading.
example_prompt: generate a blurhash for this image
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (blurhash/thumbhash crate); pure DCT math on decoded pixels.
rationale: BlurHash placeholders are a standard front-end pattern (Unsplash, Mastodon) that's trivial to compute locally.

name: license-checker
description: Checks the SPDX license IDs in an SBOM or dependency list against user-supplied allow/deny rules.
example_prompt: Flag any GPL or unknown licenses in this dependency list against my allowlist
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM matching SPDX identifiers against local policy lists; pure parsing and comparison.
rationale: grant-style license policy enforcement is just local matching and is useful for compliance without uploading the bill of materials.

name: sops-encrypt
description: Encrypts only the values in a YAML, JSON, or .env file with a passphrase/key, leaving keys readable.
example_prompt: SOPS-encrypt the values in this YAML config with this passphrase
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (serde for structure + age/AES for values); structure-preserving encryption runs in-tab. — via aes-gcm crate
rationale: SOPS-style selective config encryption is widely used and the plaintext secrets should be encrypted before leaving the machine.

name: video-fragmented-mp4
description: Converts a standard MP4 into a fragmented MP4 (fMP4) suitable for streaming and MSE-based players.
example_prompt: Make this a fragmented mp4 for my MSE video player
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm applies -movflags frag_keyframe+empty_moov with stream copy in the browser.
rationale: Media Source Extensions and CMAF pipelines require fMP4, a precise format need not covered by generic converters.

name: null-fill-numeric
description: Replaces blank/NA cells in a numeric column with a chosen strategy: constant, column mean, median, or mode.
example_prompt: Fill the missing values in this column with the median
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: scan + statistic + substitute, all in-memory.
rationale: Missing-value imputation is a universal cleanup chore with no current gizza tool.

name: prisma-schema-to-sql
description: Translates a Prisma schema's models and relations into CREATE TABLE DDL for the chosen dialect.
example_prompt: Generate SQL DDL from this Prisma schema
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Prisma schema parsing and DDL emission are deterministic text work.
rationale: Devs want to inspect or hand-apply the raw SQL behind a Prisma model without running migrate.

name: edge-detection
description: Detects edges in an image using Canny or Sobel and returns the edge map.
example_prompt: Run edge detection on this image.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — imageproc implements Canny/Sobel purely in Rust over image-rs buffers. — via imageproc crate
rationale: Edge maps are a core computer-vision primitive that hobbyists and devs want without a Python/OpenCV setup.

name: persian-tokenizer
description: Splits Persian text into sentences and words, correctly handling ZWNJ-joined compounds and Persian punctuation.
example_prompt: Tokenize this Persian paragraph into sentences and words
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — rule-based segmentation (Hazm/Parsivar style) with no external resources.
rationale: Persian word boundaries are ambiguous due to half-spaces, so a correct tokenizer is the prerequisite for every downstream NLP task.

name: toml-parser
description: Parses TOML into JSON with clear error locations for malformed input.
example_prompt: Turn this Cargo.toml into JSON so I can read the dependency tree
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the toml crate is native Rust and compiles cleanly to WASM, no network.
rationale: Inspecting TOML config as JSON makes diffing and querying far easier for developers.

name: sam-to-csv
description: Parses SAM sequence-alignment records into a CSV table with named columns (QNAME, FLAG, RNAME, POS, CIGAR, etc.) plus optional decoded flag bits.
example_prompt: Turn this SAM alignment file into a CSV table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: tab-delimited text with a fixed 11-field layout plus optional tags, parsed locally.
rationale: Inspecting alignments in a spreadsheet needs the SAM lines columnized and the bitwise FLAG decoded, which is tedious by hand.

name: csv-null-standardizer
description: Standardizes assorted missing-value tokens (NA, N/A, null, -, NaN) into a single chosen representation.
example_prompt: Turn all the NA, N/A and -- values in this CSV into empty cells
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; configurable token matching per cell, runs in-browser
rationale: Inconsistent null markers silently break aggregation and type inference across merged sources.

name: video-luma-histogram-report
description: Builds an aggregate luma (and optional RGB) histogram across the video to reveal exposure distribution.
example_prompt: Show me the brightness histogram for this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg signalstats/histogram over decoded frames produces the data locally inside the wasmi runtime.
rationale: An exposure histogram is the standard way to judge over/under-exposure, and it's read-only analysis distinct from auto-levels correction.

name: cartesian-product-generator
description: Generates the full Cartesian product of multiple input lists as a test matrix in CSV or JSON.
example_prompt: Generate all combinations of [Chrome,Firefox] x [Windows,Mac] x [light,dark]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; combinatorial enumeration locally.
rationale: Building exhaustive test and config matrices by hand is error-prone.

name: csv-row-index-adder
description: Adds a sequential index, UUID, or composite key column to a CSV.
example_prompt: Add a row_id column numbering each row in this CSV from 1
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; counter or local UUID generation per row, no network
rationale: Stable row identifiers are needed for joins and dedup tracking yet exports rarely include them.

name: image-blank-detector
description: Detects blank, solid-color, all-white, or all-black images that indicate a failed render or export.
example_prompt: Flag any blank or solid-color images in this batch.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes and computes pixel variance/entropy — trivial local computation.
rationale: Empty exports silently slip into pipelines, and a blank check catches broken renders before they ship.

name: video-audio-language-list
description: Lists each audio and subtitle track's language tag and title so users can pick the right one before extracting.
example_prompt: What audio languages are in this movie file?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg/ffprobe (loaded) reads per-stream language and title tags; runs in wasm ffmpeg locally
rationale: Multi-language files need a clean language inventory to decide which track to keep or strip.

name: rest-file-to-curl
description: Expands a .http/.rest/ain request file with {{variables}} and an environment into concrete curl commands.
example_prompt: Turn this .http file into curl commands using base_url=https://api.dev and token=abc
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the request DSL and interpolates variables locally, sending nothing.
rationale: Tools like ain and HTTP Prompt store requests in files, and devs often need them as portable curl for sharing or CI.

name: strip-console-logs
description: Removes console.log/debug/info/warn statements from JavaScript or TypeScript source.
example_prompt: strip all the console.log calls out of this JS before I ship it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans and deletes matched console.* call statements without executing code
rationale: Debug logging routinely leaks into production diffs and clearing it manually is error-prone.

name: exponential-smoother
description: Applies exponentially-weighted moving average (EWMA) smoothing with a configurable alpha or span.
example_prompt: EWMA-smooth this series with alpha 0.3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: single recursive pass, no server
rationale: EWMA is the standard recency-weighted smoother for streaming/financial series and isn't offered yet.

name: video-changed-region-bbox
description: Outputs per-frame bounding boxes of regions that differ between two aligned videos as JSON.
example_prompt: List the bounding boxes of what changed each frame between original and edited
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg extracts difference frames and Rust→WASM runs connected-component labeling to emit boxes, all local.
rationale: Machine-readable change regions enable automated diff review and targeted re-renders.

name: video-trim-diff-finder
description: Compares two cuts of the same footage to find which segments were inserted or removed and where.
example_prompt: Tell me what was cut out between the long and short versions
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg per-frame fingerprints plus a Rust→WASM longest-common-subsequence align both timelines client-side.
rationale: An edit-decision diff turns 'what changed in this cut' into a precise segment list.

name: video-set-keyframe-interval
description: Re-encodes with a fixed keyframe (GOP) interval, e.g. one keyframe every 2 seconds, for clean seeking and streaming segmentation.
example_prompt: force a keyframe every 2 seconds in this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — -g and force_key_frames during re-encode in the WASM runtime.
rationale: Streaming/HLS packaging and frame-accurate editing both depend on regular keyframes that source files rarely provide.

name: video-perceptual-hash-list
description: Computes a perceptual hash (pHash) per sampled frame or scene to enable similarity matching and duplicate detection across files.
example_prompt: Generate perceptual hashes for this video's keyframes so I can match it against another clip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg extracts frames client-side; a plain Rust→WASM pHash routine hashes them in-browser.
rationale: Perceptual hashes let users find re-encoded duplicates or matching content where exact hashes fail.

name: speech-music-classifier
description: Segments a recording into speech versus music regions with timestamps.
example_prompt: Mark which parts of this radio clip are talking versus music
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a small audio-classification model fully in-browser on decoded frames
rationale: Speech/music segmentation drives podcast chaptering, ad detection, and selective processing.

name: canned-response-suggester
description: Suggests the most relevant saved reply from your canned-response list for an incoming message.
example_prompt: Pick the best canned reply for: 'do you offer student discounts?'
loader_feasibility: transformers-js embeddings similarity — local ranking, no network. — model Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
rationale: Speeds agent replies, the exact productivity feature live-chat tools meter.

name: code-language-detect
description: Detects the programming language of a pasted code snippet, GitHub-Linguist style.
example_prompt: What programming language is this snippet?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM applies Linguist-style keyword/heuristic classifiers locally; no network or model download required.
rationale: Language detection for snippets is the core of GitHub Linguist and useful for syntax-highlight selection and dataset cleanup.

name: feature-selector
description: Ranks and selects the most predictive columns in a labeled dataset using mutual information, chi-squared, and Relief scores.
example_prompt: Which columns matter most for predicting 'price' in this CSV?
loader_feasibility: pyodide — scikit-learn's feature_selection + a Relief implementation run in the Python sandbox, fully local.
rationale: scikit-feature/scikit-rebate demand maps to a concrete data-prep tool that trims and explains feature sets offline.

name: regression-model-trainer
description: Fits linear/ridge/random-forest regression to predict a numeric column and reports R², RMSE, and coefficients.
example_prompt: Fit a model to predict house price from these features and show R²
loader_feasibility: pyodide — scikit-learn regressors train and evaluate in the Python sandbox, keeping data client-side.
rationale: Numeric prediction is a distinct, high-frequency scikit-learn use case complementing the classification tools.

name: super-timeline-builder
description: Merges timestamps from multiple parsed artifacts into a single sorted CSV super-timeline.
example_prompt: Combine these MFT, evtx, and prefetch outputs into one timeline
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: it normalizes and merges already-parsed records in-memory, no host access.
rationale: Super-timelining (plaso/log2timeline) is the heart of DFIR analysis and a lightweight merger is widely useful.

name: rncryptor-encrypt
description: Encrypts data into the password-based RNCryptor v3 container format (AES-CBC + HMAC + PBKDF2).
example_prompt: encrypt this text in rncryptor format with password pass123
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM composing aes/cbc/hmac/pbkdf2 crates to the documented RNCryptor spec; local compute. — via aes crate
rationale: RNCryptor is a widely shipped iOS/Android container format with no convenient web tool to produce it.

name: json-normalize
description: Flattens deeply nested JSON into normalized entity tables keyed by id, given an entity schema (normalizr).
example_prompt: Normalize this nested posts→comments→author JSON into entity tables.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM schema-guided walk produces entity maps client-side.
rationale: Redux/state apps need normalized stores, and doing it by hand is tedious and bug-prone.

name: age-keygen
description: Generate a new age X25519 identity, returning the secret key and its shareable public recipient string.
example_prompt: make me a new age keypair
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the browser CSPRNG seeding X25519 keygen; deterministic pure-Rust crypto, fully offline. — via age crate
rationale: Users need an age identity before they can use age-encrypt/decrypt, and generating it locally guarantees the secret key was never transmitted.

name: lazy-load-attributer
description: Adds loading="lazy" and decoding="async" to images and iframes that lack them.
example_prompt: Add lazy-loading attributes to the images in this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM DOM walk + attribute insertion; deterministic, client-side.
rationale: Retrofitting lazy loading across a long page by hand is tedious and easy to miss elements.

name: cartesian-to-polar-csv
description: Converts a CSV of (x,y) points into polar (r,θ) coordinates, with degree/radian choice.
example_prompt: Convert these x,y points to polar coordinates
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: computing hypot and atan2 per row is closed-form math evaluated locally.
rationale: Plotting and signal work frequently needs the polar view of Cartesian point data.

name: absolute-value-transformer
description: Applies absolute value, sign extraction, or negation to a numeric column.
example_prompt: Take the absolute value of this column
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — elementwise abs/sign, fully local
rationale: Flipping signs or taking magnitudes in bulk is a tiny chore users currently do row-by-row.

name: gap-finder
description: Finds missing values and gap ranges in a sequence that should be consecutive (e.g. invoice or ID numbers).
example_prompt: Which invoice numbers are missing from this list?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: sort and adjacent-difference scan, client-side.
rationale: Spotting gaps in expected-consecutive sequences is a common audit task that's tedious manually.

name: video-qr-scanner
description: Scans video frames for QR codes and outputs each decoded payload with the timestamp where it first appeared.
example_prompt: Find and decode any QR codes that show up in this screen recording
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg extracts sampled frames client-side, then a plain Rust→WASM QR decoder (rqrr) reads them in-browser. — via rqrr crate
rationale: Recorded presentations and ads often flash QR codes the viewer couldn't capture in time; extracting them automatically is genuinely useful.

name: grayscale-detector
description: Detects when an RGB image is effectively grayscale (R≈G≈B everywhere) so it can be stored as single-channel.
example_prompt: Is this RGB image actually grayscale?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM measures per-pixel channel divergence over decoded pixels in-browser.
rationale: Catching wastefully-RGB grayscale images enables big storage savings on export.

name: wireguard-config-generator
description: Generates a WireGuard keypair (or derives the public key from a pasted private key) and builds a complete client/server config with an optional QR code for mobile import.
example_prompt: Generate a WireGuard client config and a QR code I can scan on my phone
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM x25519-dalek for keygen plus a qrcode crate emitting SVG; private keys are generated and stay in the browser.
rationale: WireGuard keys must never touch a server, so a local-only generator (from wireguard-rs) is exactly the right trust model and saves CLI fiddling.

name: mongodb-query-to-sql
description: Translates MongoDB find filters into an equivalent SQL WHERE clause.
example_prompt: convert this MongoDB query to SQL: {age:{$gt:21}, status:'active'}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM: parses the filter object and emits SQL deterministically.
rationale: Teams migrating off MongoDB or querying both stores need a reliable filter translation.

name: pdf-extract-attachments
description: Extracts embedded file attachments bundled inside a PDF.
example_prompt: Get the files attached inside this PDF
loader_feasibility: pyodide — pypdf reads the embedded-files name tree and writes each attachment out locally. — via lopdf crate
rationale: Many invoices and government PDFs carry hidden attachments users don't know how to retrieve.

name: rss-feed-summarizer
description: Parses pasted RSS/Atom XML and produces a clean, deduplicated digest with optional AI summaries per item.
example_prompt: Summarize the latest items in this RSS feed XML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM for XML parsing plus transformers-js for on-device summarization; operates on pasted feed text so it sidesteps browser CORS. — via quick-xml crate
rationale: newsboat users want a fast readable digest of feeds; summarizing pasted feed content works fully offline.

name: flask-session-sign
description: Builds a valid Flask session cookie from a JSON payload and a secret key, replicating itsdangerous URLSafeTimedSerializer's key derivation, HMAC, and base64url encoding.
example_prompt: Sign this Flask session payload {"user":1,"admin":true} with secret key 'dev-key-123'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: it needs only HMAC-SHA1/SHA256 key derivation, base64url, and optional zlib — all pure-Rust crates that run offline in the browser. — via hmac crate
rationale: Crafting signed cookies for local testing of your own Flask app is a common dev task, and keeping the secret key in-browser avoids leaking it to a server.

name: aspect-sentiment
description: Extracts aspects/targets from reviews and assigns sentiment to each one.
example_prompt: Break down the sentiment by aspect in: 'Great battery but the screen is dim.'
loader_feasibility: transformers-js for aspect detection + sentiment, both run as local ONNX inference.
rationale: Aspect-based sentiment is a more actionable, research-grade variant beyond document-level polarity, matching the NLP-group demand.

name: topic-modeler
description: Discovers latent topics across a collection of documents using LDA.
example_prompt: Find the main topics in these meeting notes.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a Gibbs-sampled LDA implementation runs offline in the browser.
rationale: Direct map of gensim, BigARTM, and Multilingual-LDA demand for unsupervised theme discovery.

name: notebook-runner
description: Executes the Python code cells of an uploaded notebook in order and shows the produced outputs.
example_prompt: Run this notebook and show me the output of each cell
loader_feasibility: pyodide — runs the cell code in the in-browser Python WASM sandbox with numpy/pandas available.
rationale: Lets users actually execute the 'Data Science IPython Notebooks' they collect without any Jupyter install.

name: progressive-jpeg-converter
description: Re-encodes a baseline JPEG as progressive (or vice-versa) without changing pixels' quality.
example_prompt: Make this jpg progressive
loader_feasibility: mozjpeg/jpeg-encoder in WASM re-scans coefficients locally — via jpeg-encoder crate
rationale: Progressive JPEGs render faster on the web and are smaller, but no easy client tool toggles the mode.

name: mono-to-stereo-duplicator
description: Duplicates a mono WAV into a two-channel stereo file with identical left and right.
example_prompt: Make this mono recording into a dual-mono stereo WAV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: interleaves each sample twice and updates the channel-count header, no network.
rationale: Some players and pipelines require stereo input even for inherently mono sources.

name: histogram-bin-calculator
description: Recommends histogram bin counts and widths for a dataset using the Sturges, Scott, and Freedman–Diaconis rules, then shows the resulting bin edges and counts.
example_prompt: Suggest histogram bins for this data: 1,2,2,3,3,3,4,5,7,9,12.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: range, IQR, and standard-deviation math driving three binning formulas, fully local.
rationale: Choosing bin width is a recurring decision and seeing three principled rules at once speeds it up.

name: query-string-builder
description: Converts between a JSON object and an application/x-www-form-urlencoded query string, handling arrays and nesting.
example_prompt: build a query string from this JSON object
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; serialization with percent-encoding done locally. — via serde_json crate
rationale: Constructing and parsing form-encoded params correctly (arrays, nesting) is fiddly by hand.

name: document-term-matrix
description: Builds a document-term matrix (bag-of-words counts or binary) from a collection of documents and exports it.
example_prompt: Turn these 10 paragraphs into a document-term matrix I can download as CSV.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM tokenize-and-tabulate with CSV output, entirely local.
rationale: The DTM is the standard input format for tidytext/TextAnalysis modeling and is pure local computation.

name: chinese-ner
description: Recognizes person, place, and organization names in Chinese text.
example_prompt: Find the names of people and places in this Chinese text.
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — a compact Chinese token-classification model runs entirely in the browser. — model Xenova/bert-base-chinese-ner
rationale: Named-entity recognition is a headline HanLP capability and is valuable client-side for privacy-sensitive documents.

name: video-pgs-subtitle-image-extractor
description: Extracts image-based subtitle tracks (Blu-ray PGS / DVD VobSub) as a sequence of timed PNG images.
example_prompt: Export the PGS subtitle track from this MKV as timed images
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader demuxes and renders the bitmap subtitle stream to images in-browser.
rationale: Bitmap subtitle tracks can't be edited as text, and extracting the images is the prerequisite step before OCR or restyling.

name: graphql-formatter
description: Formats and validates the syntax of a GraphQL query, mutation, or schema.
example_prompt: format and check this GraphQL query
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — GraphQL lexing/parsing (graphql-parser crate) is pure text processing.
rationale: Another reading of GQL as a query language; GraphQL formatting/validation is a frequent API-development chore.

name: train-test-split
description: Split a CSV into train/test (and optional validation) sets with stratification and a reproducible seed.
example_prompt: Split this dataset 80/20 into train and test, stratified by label
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM seeded shuffle + partition; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: A reproducible train/test split is a routine first step in any ML workflow.

name: video-bit-depth-convert
description: Re-encodes a video between 8-bit and 10-bit pixel formats with correct dithering.
example_prompt: Convert this 10-bit video to 8-bit so it plays on my TV
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM applies the pixel-format conversion in-browser.
rationale: 8-bit-only players choke on 10-bit files and a clean dithered downconvert is the fix.

name: paraphrase-detector
description: Classifies whether two sentences are paraphrases, near-duplicates, or unrelated using a local embedding model.
example_prompt: Are these two support-ticket sentences saying the same thing?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — embed both and threshold cosine similarity, all client-side — model Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
rationale: Detecting duplicate phrasings is valuable for FAQ dedup, plagiarism, and content review.

name: one-time-pad
description: Encrypts/decrypts a message with a one-time pad and can generate a truly random pad of matching length.
example_prompt: make a one-time pad and encrypt this message
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the browser CSPRNG (getRandomValues) — pad and plaintext stay local
rationale: The OTP is the canonical perfect-secrecy demo in Understanding Cryptography and needs local randomness to be meaningful.

name: pydantic-validator
description: Validates JSON data against a Pydantic model definition and returns typed, field-level errors.
example_prompt: Validate this JSON against this pydantic model.
loader_feasibility: pyodide — runs CPython plus pydantic in WASM, executing real model validation in the browser sandbox.
rationale: Pydantic is the de-facto Python validation layer for LLM apps and has no client-side equivalent (pydantic/monty).

name: markdown-code-extractor
description: Extracts all fenced code blocks from markdown, optionally filtered by language.
example_prompt: Extract just the python code blocks from this answer
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM markdown fence parsing of pasted text; client-side only.
rationale: Chatblade-style 'give me only the code' extraction is a pure-text, high-frequency need.

name: file-metadata-query
description: Runs SQL-like queries (WHERE/ORDER BY on name, size, type, modified date) over a folder of files you drag into the chat.
example_prompt: From this folder, show files bigger than 1MB modified this month, sorted by size
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM query engine; the browser File API exposes name/size/type/lastModified without uploading file contents anywhere.
rationale: fselect's SQL-over-files is intuitive and the metadata it needs is exactly what the browser exposes locally.

name: xml-numeric-value-extractor
description: Extracts numeric element and attribute values from XML by tag/attribute path into a numeric column.
example_prompt: Pull all <price> values out of this XML product feed as a list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a small XML walker plus numeric filtering, runs offline.
rationale: Many feeds and configs are XML where you just want one numeric field as a clean series.

name: stream-editor
description: Applies an ed/sed-style command script (substitute, delete, print, insert by line/regex) to pasted text in one pass.
example_prompt: Run `s/foo/bar/g` and delete every blank line on this text.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; line/regex transforms run in-browser with the Rust regex engine — no server. — via regex crate
rationale: ed is the archetypal scriptable editor and a batch sed-style transformer is a genuinely useful, scriptable text tool.

name: mongo-query
description: Filters a JSON array of documents using a MongoDB-style query object with operators like $gt, $in, $and, and dotted field paths.
example_prompt: Filter these docs with the Mongo query {age:{$gte:21}, country:{$in:['US','CA']}}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM implementing the Mongo query operator subset over serde_json values; fully client-side.
rationale: MongoDB users expect to paste a query object verbatim, a distinct interface from jq/JSONPath that directly serves the strongest demand term.

name: ssh-public-key-parser
description: Parses OpenSSH/authorized_keys public keys into algorithm, key size, comment, and SHA256 fingerprint.
example_prompt: Parse this SSH public key and give me its fingerprint
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM Base64-decoding the wire format and hashing locally; fully offline. — via sha2 crate
rationale: Verifying key type/fingerprint before adding it to a server is a common, security-relevant check.

name: thousands-separator-normalizer
description: Detects US vs European grouping/decimal styles (1,234.56 vs 1.234,56) and normalizes to canonical floats.
example_prompt: Normalize these mixed-format numbers to plain decimals: 1.234,56 and 12,345.67 and 1 234,5
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — locale heuristics and string rewriting, no locale library or server needed.
rationale: Numbers copied from European reports break parsers; auto-normalizing separators is a frequent pain point.

name: multilingual-stemmer
description: Stems words in many languages via Snowball algorithms (German, Spanish, Danish, Arabic, and more).
example_prompt: Stem this German text to its word roots.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the rust-stemmers Snowball crate is pure Rust with no network.
rationale: A single robust multilingual stemmer covers most language-NLP preprocessing demand here in one place.

name: sentence-tokenizer
description: Splits text into sentences and word/punctuation tokens with character offsets.
example_prompt: split this paragraph into sentences and count the tokens: ...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM rule+abbreviation tokenizer; pure compute, no network.
rationale: Foundational OpenNLP/Stanford-style sentence detection that every other text tool depends on.

name: pcap-summary
description: Summarizes an uploaded pcap: protocol breakdown, top talkers, conversations, and busiest ports.
example_prompt: Summarize this capture — which hosts and ports dominate the traffic?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — aggregation over parsed packet headers is pure computation on the input file. — via etherparse crate
rationale: Beyond ngrep's matching, users want a quick capture overview; a local summarizer triages a pcap without Wireshark or uploads.

name: wif-key-decode
description: Decodes a WIF private key to its raw bytes (and back), reporting network and compression flag.
