example_prompt: decode this WIF key: L1aW4aubDFB7yfras2S1mN3bqg9nwySY8nkoLmJebSLD5BWv3ENZ
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Base58Check encode/decode only; never sends the private key anywhere.
rationale: Converting between WIF and raw private keys is a common wallet task that must stay strictly offline.

name: log-pattern-miner
description: Clusters thousands of log lines into a handful of Drain-style templates with occurrence counts to reveal the dominant message shapes.
example_prompt: Group these 10k log lines into patterns so I can see what's actually being logged most
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the Drain tree algorithm is pure CPU string work, ideal for client-side execution.
rationale: Pattern mining is the core value OpenObserve/Vector add to noisy logs, and it needs no server to run.

name: logfmt-converter
description: Converts log/event data between logfmt, JSON, NDJSON and CSV in either direction.
example_prompt: Turn these logfmt lines into NDJSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: format parsing and serialization are pure data transforms with no I/O.
rationale: Vector pipelines constantly reshape between these observability formats, a frequent one-off chore for engineers.

name: log-to-metrics
description: Aggregates parsed logs into counts, rates and latency percentiles grouped by any field.
example_prompt: From this log, give me request count and p95 latency per endpoint
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: grouping and percentile math are pure compute over the in-memory dataset.
rationale: Turning logs into metrics is Vector's headline capability and is trivially browser-local for a single file.

name: diff-code
description: Produces a unified or side-by-side diff between two code/text snippets with word-level highlighting.
example_prompt: Show me a diff between these two versions of the function
loader_feasibility: The pure-Rust `similar` crate compiles to WASM and diffs text locally. — via similar crate
rationale: Diff/VCS integration underlies every editor in the harvest (rustic, gitpod, IDEs); a standalone diff is the portable core of it.

name: column-aligner
description: Aligns whitespace- or delimiter-separated columns into a neat fixed-width layout, like `column -t`.
example_prompt: Line up these space-separated columns into even columns
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure text layout, no host access.
rationale: Aligning ad-hoc columnar text is a daily terminal task that comfy-table-style layout solves.

name: tar-create
description: Combines multiple files into a single uncompressed .tar archive preserving names and paths.
example_prompt: Bundle these files into a tar archive
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: alexcrichton/tar-rs writes the tar/ustar/pax container in pure Rust in the browser. — via tar crate
rationale: Tar is the canonical bundling format on Unix and a local builder avoids any upload.

name: principal-component-analysis
description: Runs PCA on a dataset and returns principal components, explained variance, and projected coordinates.
example_prompt: Run PCA on this CSV and show the top 2 components
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: faer-rs SVD computes the components in pure Rust, keeping the dataset entirely in the browser. — via faer crate
rationale: PCA is a staple of exploratory data analysis and dimensionality reduction that benefits from staying local and private.

name: geojson-format
description: Pretty-print, minify, or re-key GeoJSON and round coordinate precision.
example_prompt: Minify this GeoJSON and trim coordinates to 6 decimals
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via georust/geojson + serde_json — serialization only, no server. — via geojson crate
rationale: Trimming coordinate precision shrinks map payloads dramatically and is a common optimization step.

name: entropy-calculator
description: Calculates Shannon entropy in bits of a string or file to gauge randomness of keys, passwords, or data.
example_prompt: What's the Shannon entropy of this API key?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM; a single frequency pass over bytes, fully local.
rationale: Entropy is the core measure behind 'is this random enough' security questions and is pure math.

name: chat-log-analyzer
description: Computes who-talked-most, activity-by-hour, and word stats from a chat or IRC log.
example_prompt: Analyze this irc log and show activity by hour
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM aggregates counts from the parsed log entirely client-side.
rationale: Useful analytics over private chat logs without sending them to any service.

name: prose-linter
description: Flags clichés, weasel words, passive voice, and redundancies in writing using an embedded rule set.
example_prompt: Lint this paragraph for clichés and weak writing: <paste text>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — runs proselint-style rules over the text entirely in-browser.
rationale: Maps the Prosaic/prose-tooling demand into a deterministic style checker that keeps drafts private.

name: worklog-summarizer
description: Parses a timestamped activity or 'doing' log and summarizes time spent per tag, project, and day.
example_prompt: Summarize how many hours I spent per project from this doing log
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses timestamps and aggregates durations client-side.
rationale: doing-style activity logs are only useful once summarized into time totals, which is the tedious part.

name: timesheet-to-invoice
description: Turns tracked hours plus an hourly rate and client details into a formatted Markdown or plain-text invoice with line items and totals.
example_prompt: Make an invoice: 12h dev at $90/hr, 3h meetings at $60/hr, for Acme Corp
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — templating and currency math run entirely client-side.
rationale: Time-tracking demand (Watson, utt, Timetrap) almost always ends in billing; this closes the loop locally and privately.

name: otpauth-uri-parser
description: Parses an otpauth:// URI into its fields (issuer, account, secret, algorithm, digits, period).
example_prompt: Decode this otpauth:// URI into its parts
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM URI/query-string parsing; pure string analysis with no external calls
rationale: Inspecting and migrating 2FA secrets requires breaking otpauth URIs into readable fields without pasting them into a website.

name: file-finder
description: Searches the file names and paths of a dragged-in folder using glob and regex expressions.
example_prompt: Find all `*.test.ts` files under this folder
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM glob/regex over the directory listing provided by the browser's webkitdirectory File API; no contents leave the device.
rationale: fd/rawhide's fast name search is a daily-use operation that works fine on a client-side directory listing.

name: semantic-code-search
description: Finds the function or snippet that best matches a natural-language intent across a pasted set of code blocks using code embeddings.
example_prompt: Across these functions, which one parses the auth token? Describe it in plain English
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a code-embedding model in-browser via WASM/WebGPU; ranking by cosine similarity is local. — model Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
rationale: semantic-grep applied to code lets you locate behavior by intent, which keyword/AST search can't do.

name: text-similarity-scorer
description: Scores how semantically similar two texts are and ranks a list of candidates against a reference.
example_prompt: Which of these three answers is closest in meaning to my question?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js produces embeddings locally and computes cosine similarity in WASM, no server — model Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
rationale: A focused, fast embedding utility drawn from leettools' retrieval demand that is purely deterministic offline.

name: code-metrics-analyzer
description: Computes lines of code, cyclomatic complexity, and function counts for pasted source across common languages.
example_prompt: Give me complexity and LOC metrics for this Rust file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with tree-sitter grammars parses the source locally; static analysis needs no network
rationale: kwaak's code-agent demand includes understanding code health, and metrics are a deterministic, offline static-analysis task.

name: markdown-flashcards
description: Parses Q/A markdown notes into a flashcard deck and exports an Anki-importable CSV (or .apkg).
example_prompt: Turn these markdown notes into an Anki deck
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the markdown and builds the deck (CSV, or .apkg via bundled sqlite+zip) — notes stay on-device.
rationale: mdfc/GoCard/py_flashcards demand; lets people keep study notes in plain text and study them in Anki.

name: mattermost-export-reader
description: Parses a Mattermost bulk export (JSONL) into a readable per-channel transcript with author and timestamp resolution.
example_prompt: convert this mattermost export.jsonl into readable channel logs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — line-delimited JSON parsing and formatting run fully offline.
rationale: Self-hosted Mattermost exports are hard to read; a private local reader avoids re-uploading internal chat data.

name: twitter-archive-reader
description: Parses a Twitter/X data export (tweets.js) into readable Markdown plus posting stats and top tweets.
example_prompt: turn my twitter archive tweets.js into a readable markdown file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — strips the JS wrapper, parses JSON, and renders, all locally. — via serde_json crate
rationale: People want to browse and back up their tweets without handing the full archive to a web service.

name: shell-script-linter
description: Lints a bash/sh script for common pitfalls: unquoted variables, useless cat, missing set -euo pipefail, and subshell scope traps.
example_prompt: Check this bash script for bugs: [paste script]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM static analysis over tokenized shell; no execution, fully offline.
rationale: Subshella-style subshell gotchas plus general shell mistakes are a constant source of bugs; a lite shellcheck in chat is high value.

name: text-token-extractor
description: Scans a blob of text and pulls out all URLs, emails, IP addresses, file paths, and hashes.
example_prompt: Extract every URL and email from this log dump
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM regex (regex crate); pure in-memory scan, no system clipboard or shell needed.
rationale: Captures extrakto's core value (fuzzy token extraction) as a stateless processing tool that fits chat input.

name: ini-json-converter
description: Converts between INI/config files and JSON, and can get, set, or delete individual keys.
example_prompt: Turn this INI config into JSON and set database.port to 5432
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with rust-ini + serde_json; pure text parsing client-side. — via rust-ini crate
rationale: Directly maps crudini's get/set/del workflow that has no good browser-local equivalent.

name: config-merge
description: Merge layered config files (JSON/YAML/TOML/env) with override precedence and variable substitution.
example_prompt: merge this base config with this prod override and substitute the variables
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — deep-merge + templating over parsed configs, no server. — via toml crate
rationale: Konfigo's core job; composing environment-layered configs is a real pain point with no good client-side tool.

name: word-diff
description: Computes an inline word- and character-level diff between two texts, highlighting exactly which words changed inside each line rather than marking whole lines.
example_prompt: Word-level diff between these two paragraphs: <paste old> --- <paste new>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tokenizes both texts and runs a Myers diff over word tokens; pure computation, no server. — via similar crate
rationale: Existing line-diff tools can't show small edits inside a sentence; intra-line word granularity is what writers and reviewers actually want for prose and config.

name: diff-stat
description: Parses a unified diff or git patch and produces a diffstat summary: per-file lines added and removed, total churn, and the most-changed files.
example_prompt: Give me a diffstat for this patch: <paste git diff>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the hunk headers and +/- lines of a unified diff and tallies counts; pure text processing.
rationale: Reviewers and changelog writers want a quick churn summary of a patch without reading every hunk (a delta/diff-so-fancy staple), and no current tool summarizes an existing diff's statistics.

name: mbox-splitter
description: Splits a multi-message mbox archive into individual downloadable .eml files.
example_prompt: Split this mbox into separate email files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM splits on the `From ` separators and packs results into an in-browser zip. — via zip crate
rationale: mbox is the universal export format but nearly every other tool wants one email per file.

name: frequent-contacts-ranker
description: Ranks the people you email most by frequency and recency to build an autocomplete address list.
example_prompt: Rank my most-emailed contacts from this mbox
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tallies From/To/Cc across messages locally — a maildir-rank-addr port.
rationale: Reproduces maildir-rank-addr's useful ranked output without any shell tooling.

name: file-list-sorter
description: Sorts a list of filenames or paths by natural/numeric order, extension, depth, or size, with options like directories-first and case-insensitive.
example_prompt: Sort these filenames in natural order with directories first
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sorting/comparator logic only.
rationale: Natural sorting (img2 before img10) is exactly the Files-Sort-py/nat demand and is trivially browser-local.

name: markdown-notes-index
description: Scans uploaded markdown notes and builds a linked index with titles, tags, headings, and a table of contents.
example_prompt: Build an index of these markdown notes with their tags and headings
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM markdown parsing over uploaded file contents — no IO. — via pulldown-cmark crate
rationale: Maps lsnotes to a genuinely useful note-organizing output that browsers can produce from attached files.

name: log-summarizer
description: Summarizes a noisy log dump or error trace into a plain-English account of what happened and the likely cause.
example_prompt: Summarize what went wrong in these logs
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a small summarization model in-browser over the pasted logs; inference is fully client-side. — model Xenova/distilbart-cnn-6-6
rationale: Beyond stats, engineers want a human-readable narrative of a log, and local inference keeps potentially sensitive logs off any server.

name: journal-sentiment-tracker
description: Runs sentiment analysis over dated journal entries and reports mood trends across time.
example_prompt: Analyze the mood in my diary entries over the last month
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — a sentiment classification model runs in-browser via WASM/WebGPU, entries never leave the device — model Xenova/distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english
rationale: Mood tracking is the most-requested feature around digital diaries and benefits from staying fully local for privacy.

name: csv-to-ics
description: Builds a standards-compliant .ics calendar from a CSV or pasted list of events with dates and times.
example_prompt: Turn this list of events into a calendar file I can import
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM emitter producing RFC 5545 text; no network needed
rationale: Bulk-create importable calendar entries from a spreadsheet, fully offline.

name: password-export-convert
description: Convert password-manager exports between Bitwarden JSON, KeePass CSV, and generic CSV so users can migrate between managers.
example_prompt: convert this bitwarden export to a keepass-importable csv
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM format mapping (serde_json + csv crates); deterministic transform with no network, keeping the credential file local. — via csv crate
rationale: Switching between the many managers in the demand set (rbw, kpcli, pass, SpicyPass) is painful because export formats differ, and doing it locally avoids pasting secrets into a web converter.

name: multi-translate
description: Translates a phrase into several target languages at once, entirely in-browser.
example_prompt: Translate 'good morning' into Spanish, French, German, and Japanese
loader_feasibility: transformers-js translation models run client-side per language pair, no API keys — model Xenova/nllb-200-distilled-600M
rationale: One-shot multi-language output is handy for UI copy and travel without external services.

name: log-timestamp-normalizer
description: Detects mixed timestamp formats across log lines, normalizes them to ISO-8601/UTC, and annotates the elapsed delta between consecutive lines.
example_prompt: normalize all timestamps in this log to UTC and show the gap between each line
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM date parsing/formatting; no network or system clock dependency beyond user input. — via chrono crate
rationale: Timestamp wrangling is lnav's headline feature and a common real pain when correlating logs from multiple sources, ideal as a focused offline transform.

name: extract-matches
description: Pull every regex match (or all emails/URLs/IPs/numbers via presets) out of text into a clean deduplicated list.
example_prompt: Extract all the URLs from this email thread
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM regex with built-in preset patterns; in-memory only — via regex crate
rationale: A common 'grep but give me just the matches, not whole lines' need that the search-tool cluster implies and that no live process is required for.

name: ndjson-viewer
description: Pretty-prints and filters newline-delimited JSON streams, with key search across records.
example_prompt: Pretty-print and filter these NDJSON records by status field
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (or pyodide) parses each JSON line and applies filters in-browser on pasted content. — via serde_json crate
rationale: This is the honest browser-local analog of Yozefu's record-stream browsing, useful for any log or event-stream export.

name: lua-minifier
description: Shrinks Lua source by stripping comments/whitespace and optionally renaming locals, producing a compact equivalent script.
example_prompt: Minify this Lua module so it's as small as possible.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse with `full_moon` and re-emit the AST compactly; pure Rust, runs client-side. — via full_moon crate
rationale: games and embedded apps shipping Lua via these crates care about script payload size, and minification is a natural complement to the formatter/linter.

name: linear-regression
description: Fits a linear regression to CSV data and reports coefficients, R², and predictions.
example_prompt: Fit a regression predicting price from size and bedrooms in this CSV.
loader_feasibility: linfa/smartcore/anofox-regression compiled to WASM (plain Rust→WASM); least-squares is pure compute. — via smartcore crate
rationale: Regression on a pasted dataset is a staple analytics task that needs no server.

name: gpt-token-counter
description: Counts the exact number of BPE tokens a text uses for a chosen GPT/Claude model.
example_prompt: How many tokens is this paragraph for gpt-4o?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the tiktoken-rs BPE merge tables compile to WASM and tokenize entirely in-memory, no network. — via tiktoken-rs crate
rationale: Token counting is the single most common pre-flight check before sending a prompt and has clear standing demand (tiktoken-rs).

name: css-color-converter
description: Converts a color between hex, rgb(a), hsl, oklch, and the 0xAARRGGBB integer form used by Flutter/Dart and Android.
example_prompt: Convert rgb(37, 99, 235) to oklch and to a Flutter Color value
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — deterministic numeric conversions, no dependencies.
rationale: The Flutter and Rust-GUI demand terms all juggle colors across CSS, Dart, and native formats, and conversion is constant friction.

name: image-auto-orient
description: Auto-rotate a photo to its correct orientation using the EXIF orientation flag and bake it in.
example_prompt: fix the sideways rotation on this phone photo
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM EXIF read + re-encode; local. — via image crate
rationale: Sideways phone uploads are a perennial annoyance; image-rotate only does manual rotation.

name: web-readability
description: Fetch a URL and extract the clean article text (title, byline, body), stripping nav/ads.
example_prompt: Give me the readable article from this URL: <url>
loader_feasibility: web-fetch (already wired) gets the HTML; a plain-Rust readability/dom-content-extraction pass in WASM cleans it locally. — via scraper crate
rationale: Readable extraction makes web-fetch dramatically more useful and feeds summarize/translate.

name: video-scene-split
description: Detect scene/shot changes and split a video into per-scene clips.
example_prompt: split this video at every scene change
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg scene-detect filter, client-side.
rationale: Scene-based splitting is far more useful than fixed-length splits for editing.

name: video-reframe
description: Auto-reframe a landscape video to vertical 9:16 (or 1:1) by tracking and keeping the main subject centered.
example_prompt: reframe this 16:9 clip to vertical for Reels, keeping the speaker centered
loader_feasibility: ONNX subject detect/track plus ffmpeg dynamic crop, client-side.
rationale: Premiere-style auto-reframe for Shorts/Reels is in huge demand.

name: recipe-extract
description: Fetch a recipe page and extract clean structured recipe data (ingredients, steps, time, yield), stripping the blog filler.
example_prompt: Extract just the recipe from this cooking-blog URL
loader_feasibility: web-fetch + Rust JSON-LD/Recipe-schema + readability parse; browser-local. — via serde_json crate
rationale: Stripping the life-story preamble from recipe pages is a famous pain point and a purpose-built improvement over generic JSON-LD extraction.

name: visual-question-answering
description: Answer a free-form question about an uploaded image (multimodal VQA).
example_prompt: How many people are in this photo and what are they doing?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime or transformers-js multimodal model (tiny BLIP/ViLT) in-browser; local, no upload. — model Xenova/vilt-b32-finetuned-vqa
rationale: Asking questions about an image is a flagship multimodal capability distinct from plain captioning.

name: image-segment
description: Segment an image into labeled regions/masks (e.g. person, sky, road) with a semantic model.
example_prompt: Show me a segmentation mask of this scene
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime or transformers-js segmentation model (e.g. SegFormer) runs in-browser; segmentation is a supported transformers.js task. — model Xenova/segformer-b0-finetuned-ade-512-512
rationale: Pixel-level scene understanding underpins masking/editing workflows and extends the existing vision-model lineup.

name: pose-estimate
description: Detect human body keypoints (skeleton/pose) in a photo and overlay them with joint coordinates.
example_prompt: detect the body pose in this photo
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime (MoveNet/MediaPipe pose ONNX); keypoint inference runs in-browser. — model Xenova/yolov8l-pose
rationale: Pose detection powers fitness, AR, and animation use cases and is distinct from object/segment tools.

name: image-dither
description: Apply Floyd-Steinberg or ordered dithering to an image for retro, pixel-art, or e-ink looks and palette reduction.
example_prompt: apply 1-bit floyd-steinberg dithering to this photo
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: pixel-buffer error-diffusion, no model needed.
rationale: Popular aesthetic effect and genuinely useful for e-ink/embedded-display prep.

name: flatten-json
description: Flatten nested JSON into dot/bracket key paths (and unflatten back) for spreadsheets and config diffs.
example_prompt: flatten this nested JSON into dot-notation keys
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: recursive key walk on parsed JSON, fully local.
rationale: Common bridge step between nested APIs and flat CSV/config tooling.

name: log-parse
description: Parse and summarize access/app logs (Apache/Nginx/JSON): top IPs, paths, status codes, errors, and time range.
example_prompt: Summarize this nginx access log: top paths, status codes, and errors
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM regex/field parsing + aggregation; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: Quick local log triage without shipping logs to a server is a common ops need.

name: font-info
description: Inspect a TTF/OTF/WOFF font: family, weights/styles, glyph count, metrics, and embedded license.
example_prompt: What's inside this .ttf file?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM font-table parser (ttf-parser class); offline. — via ttf-parser crate
rationale: Useful for designers/devs vetting fonts; no font tooling exists yet.

name: gif-extract-frames
description: Split an animated GIF into its individual frame images.
example_prompt: extract all the frames from this gif as PNGs
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes the GIF locally; video-extract-frames only handles video. — via gif crate
rationale: Editing or reusing GIF frames is common and not covered by the video-only frame tools.

name: image-vectorize
description: Traces a bitmap (logo/icon/sketch) into a scalable SVG.
example_prompt: Vectorize this PNG logo into an SVG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the pure-Rust `vtracer` tracer; runs entirely on-device. — via vtracer crate
rationale: Bitmap-to-vector is a high-value logo/icon operation and a strong local-only differentiator.

name: mix-audio
description: Overlays two audio tracks together so they play at the same time with adjustable volume.
example_prompt: mix my voiceover under this background music
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader uses the amix/amerge filter locally.
rationale: Layering voice over music is a distinct, frequently requested operation.

name: code-line-counter
description: Counts code, comment, and blank lines by language for pasted code, with a complexity and rough COCOMO estimate like scc.
example_prompt: Count the SLOC and comment ratio of this file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — language detection and line classification run on the supplied text; offline.
rationale: scc/cloc are everyday metrics tools; an instant in-chat SLOC/complexity report helps with sizing snippets and reviews.

name: image-watermark-remove
description: Auto-detect a repeating watermark or logo overlay and inpaint it away.
example_prompt: remove the stock-photo watermark from this image
loader_feasibility: onnx inpainting model (e.g. LaMa) in-browser. — model Carve/LaMa-ONNX
rationale: Watermark removal is among the most-searched image tools; differs from manual object-remove by auto-detecting the overlay.

name: video-fade
description: Add fade-in/fade-out (to black) on video and audio at the start and end of a clip.
example_prompt: add a 1-second fade in and fade out to this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (already wired): fade/afade filters, fully in-browser.
rationale: Tiny but constantly wanted polish step, mirroring the backlog's audio-fade.

name: jsonl-convert
description: Convert between JSONL/NDJSON and a JSON array (and split/merge line-delimited records).
example_prompt: convert this JSON array into JSONL for my fine-tuning dataset
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: streaming line parse, no server.
rationale: JSONL is the standard LLM dataset format, making this a natural fit for gizza's AI users.

name: video-deinterlace
description: Remove interlacing combing artifacts from a video, producing clean progressive frames.
example_prompt: Deinterlace this old camcorder footage
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — yadif/bwdif deinterlace filter runs locally on the decoded stream.
rationale: Old/broadcast footage frequently needs deinterlacing and ffmpeg handles it cleanly.

name: image-drop-shadow
description: Add a realistic soft drop shadow behind a transparent-PNG cutout (product shots, stickers).
example_prompt: add a soft drop shadow under this cut-out product image
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust blur/composite (image crate) to WASM — local pixel work.
rationale: E-commerce and product imagery commonly need a shadow after background removal.

name: histogram-chart
description: Bin a list of numbers and render a histogram with auto or explicit bin counts.
example_prompt: Plot a histogram of these response times
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM binning + plotting; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: A distribution histogram from raw numbers is a basic stats need distinct from image-histogram.

name: fixed-width-parse
description: Parse fixed-width or whitespace-aligned column output (console tables, log dumps) into CSV/JSON.
example_prompt: Turn this whitespace-aligned terminal output into a CSV
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM column detection; offline.
rationale: text-to-table targets prose; aligned console/report output is a distinct, common case.

name: kml-to-geojson
description: Convert KML/KMZ map data to GeoJSON (and the reverse).
example_prompt: Convert this Google Earth KML to GeoJSON
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM XML parse; offline. — via kml crate
rationale: Common format bridge for mapping that pairs with the existing geojson-preview.

name: image-channel-split
description: Split an image into separate R, G, B, and alpha channel images (and recombine).
example_prompt: Show me the red, green, and blue channels of this image
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM pixel extraction, offline.
rationale: A staple inspection/compositing tool for designers and developers.

name: pr-description-generate
description: Draft a pull-request title and description from a pasted git diff.
example_prompt: Write a PR description for this diff [diff]
loader_feasibility: transformers-js small model in-browser (or hand off to the chat LLM).
rationale: Distinct from commit-message and changelog generation and a frequent developer chore.

name: ts-decompose
description: Decompose a time series into trend, seasonal, and residual components and plot them.
example_prompt: decompose this monthly sales series into trend and seasonality
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM STL/classical decomposition + SVG plot; local.
rationale: Seeing trend vs seasonality is fundamental to forecasting and isn't provided by the forecast or smoothing tools.

name: nanoid-generate
description: Generate NanoIDs with configurable alphabet and length (and batches).
example_prompt: Generate 5 nanoids of length 12
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust RNG in-browser; no network.
rationale: NanoID is a very common ID scheme not covered by uuid-generate (uuid/ulid only).

name: image-watermark-tile
description: Apply a repeating/tiled text or logo watermark across the whole image (anti-theft).
example_prompt: Tile my logo as a faint watermark over this image
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust tiled compositing in-browser.
rationale: Full-coverage tiling is distinct from the single-position image-watermark tool.

name: currency-convert
description: Convert an amount between currencies using current exchange rates.
example_prompt: convert 250 USD to EUR and JPY
loader_feasibility: web-fetch loader pulls a public rates feed; conversion runs client-side.
rationale: Currency conversion is one of the most common everyday lookups; unit-convert covers only physical units.

name: deflate-inflate
description: Compresses or decompresses raw DEFLATE and zlib streams (the format inside PDFs, PNGs, and many protocols).
example_prompt: Inflate this raw zlib stream I pulled out of a PDF
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: flate2-rs exposes raw deflate and zlib codecs that run fully in the browser. — via flate2 crate
rationale: Raw deflate/zlib streams turn up constantly when reverse-engineering file formats and have no friendly online tool.

name: decompress-auto
description: Detects the format of a compressed blob from its magic bytes and decompresses it automatically.
example_prompt: Just decompress this file, I'm not sure what format it is
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a single WASM module sniffs headers and dispatches to flate2/brotli/zstd-rs/bzip2-rs decoders in-browser. — via flate2 crate
rationale: Users often don't know whether a blob is gzip/zstd/brotli/bzip2, and auto-detection removes that friction.

name: geojson-validate
description: Validate GeoJSON against the spec and report structural errors, winding issues, and bad coordinates.
example_prompt: Is this GeoJSON valid? <paste GeoJSON>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via georust/geojson — parsing and validation are pure compute. — via geojson crate
rationale: GeoJSON is everywhere in mapping and a fast offline linter saves debugging round-trips.

name: stl-inspector
description: Parses ASCII or binary STL files and reports triangle count, bounding box, surface area, volume, and whether the mesh is watertight.
example_prompt: Check if this STL is watertight and tell me its volume
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (stl_io-style) decoding plus geometry math; fully client-side on the uploaded mesh.
rationale: Watertightness and volume are the first things a 3D-printing user checks before slicing, and there's no quick local tool for it.

name: docker-cli-output-parser
description: Parses `docker ps`, `docker images`, or `docker stats` text output into structured tables or JSON.
example_prompt: Turn this docker ps output into JSON: [paste docker ps output]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM columnar text parsing; pure text-to-data.
rationale: dry exists because raw docker output is hard to read; parsing it into clean data is the offline, scriptable version.

name: disk-usage-by-filetype
description: Aggregates a folder's space usage by file extension/category and shows it as a sorted colored bar chart.
example_prompt: Break down this folder by file type — how much is video vs images vs code?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; extensions and sizes are gathered client-side from the chosen folder and grouped in WASM, rendered with the chat's chart host.
rationale: vizex's colored-bar 'what type of stuff fills my disk' view is highly demanded and needs no server to compute.

name: email-phishing-link-scanner
description: Scans an email for suspicious URLs, mismatched display-vs-target links, and lookalike domains.
example_prompt: Check this email for phishing links
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses links and runs heuristics fully offline.
rationale: A private phishing pre-check before clicking is broadly valuable and defensive.

name: json-remap
description: Restructures a JSON document into a new shape using a declarative key-mapping/template spec.
example_prompt: Remap this JSON so each item only has id, name, and a combined fullAddress field
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM template/spec interpreter over serde_json values; pure transform, no server.
rationale: Serves 'json2json' and 'json-sharp' transformation-language demand for adapting one API's shape to another.

name: nacl-box-encrypt
description: Performs libsodium public-key authenticated encryption (crypto_box, Curve25519+XSalsa20-Poly1305) to a recipient key.
example_prompt: box-encrypt this to a recipient public key
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via `dryoc`; sodium-compatible and runs entirely in the browser. — via dryoc crate
rationale: Gives libsodium-net users interop for sending encrypted messages between known keypairs without a server.

name: ecies-encrypt
description: Encrypts a message to a recipient's elliptic-curve public key (ECIES) and decrypts with the private key.
example_prompt: ECIES-encrypt this payload to this secp256k1 public key
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM composing RustCrypto ECDH + HKDF + AES-GCM, all pure-Rust and wasm-ready. — via p256 crate
rationale: Maps the PyElliptic demand; one-shot encrypt-to-a-public-key is a frequent ad-hoc need not covered by symmetric tools.

name: text-splitter-regex
description: Splits text into rows or fields using a regex delimiter, handling multi-character and whitespace separators.
example_prompt: Split this text on one-or-more commas/semicolons using regex
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs the split operation in-memory — fully local. — via regex crate
rationale: Regex splitting is a distinct, frequent operation (tokenizing, field separation) that complements the extract/replace tools.

name: regex-bulk-match
description: Tests one regex against many input lines and reports match/no-match plus captures per line.
example_prompt: Which of these 50 strings are valid emails per this regex?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM loops the compiled pattern over each line in-memory; client-side. — via regex crate
rationale: A practical batch-validation workflow (e.g., cleaning a list) that single-string testers don't cover.

name: faq-semantic-search
description: Embeds a provided FAQ list and returns the best-matching answer to a question by meaning, not keywords.
example_prompt: Given this FAQ, answer: 'how do I reset my password?'
loader_feasibility: transformers-js embeddings (all-MiniLM) plus cosine match — vectors computed locally. — model Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
rationale: A self-serve FAQ deflects chats, and semantic match beats the keyword search these widgets ship.

name: chat-language-detector
description: Detects the language of an incoming chat message so it can be routed to the right agent.
example_prompt: What language is this message in?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM n-gram detection (whatlang) — pure local, no model download. — via whatlang crate
rationale: Language routing is a prerequisite for multilingual support and is trivially local.

name: autocomplete-trie
description: Builds a prefix trie from a wordlist and returns ranked autocomplete suggestions for a typed prefix.
example_prompt: give me autocomplete suggestions for 'inv' from this list of product names
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — trie construction and prefix walk over an in-memory list, the suggestion engine flexsearch ships, fully local.
rationale: Prefix autocomplete data is needed for search boxes and is trivial to generate offline.

name: hcl-to-json
description: Converts HashiCorp HCL (Terraform-style) configuration into equivalent JSON.
example_prompt: convert this Terraform HCL into JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the hcl-rs crate; parses and emits JSON entirely offline
rationale: HCL is widely used in infra-as-code and an HCL→JSON converter directly serves the harvested HCL demand.

name: survey-form-builder
description: Generates a self-contained HTML survey or poll form from a simple question spec (multiple choice, rating, free text).
example_prompt: build an HTML survey: one NPS question, one multiple choice on plan, one free-text comment
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — renders an HTML form from a question list, the authoring half of SurveyMonkey/Qualaroo, no backend.
rationale: Authoring a clean survey form by hand is tedious and a spec-driven generator is instantly useful.

name: stopword-filter
description: Removes stopwords from text using built-in multilingual stoplists or a custom list.
example_prompt: Strip the stopwords out of this English text.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; set-membership filtering over bundled stoplists, no network.
rationale: Stopword removal is a ubiquitous preprocessing step paired with the NLTK and scikit-learn workflows in the demand terms.

name: rule-based-extractor
description: Applies user-defined regex/pattern rules to extract structured fields (dates, codes, entities) from text.
example_prompt: Extract every invoice number matching INV-#### and every date from this document.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM regex engine applying the rule set locally, no external calls. — via regex crate
rationale: VisualText/NLP++ are rule-based extraction environments, and a lightweight pattern extractor brings that power browser-local.

name: audio-augment
description: Applies data-augmentation transforms (noise, pitch shift, time stretch, gain, reverb) to create training variants of a clip.
example_prompt: Make 5 augmented versions of this sample with noise and pitch shift
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM applies the audio filters locally; nothing is uploaded.
rationale: Augmentation expands small audio datasets and is a routine step before training.

name: midi-note-extract
description: Extracts every note as a CSV row of pitch, start, duration, and velocity.
example_prompt: Export the notes from this MIDI as CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure in-memory parse, no decode needed. — via midly crate
rationale: Lets musicians pull MIDI into spreadsheets or DAWs for analysis (Pretty-MIDI demand).

name: midi-tempo-change
description: Changes the tempo/BPM of a MIDI file while preserving note relationships.
example_prompt: Make this MIDI play at 90 BPM
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — edits tempo meta events in-place. — via midly crate
rationale: Quickly creates slowed practice tracks (Mido demand).

name: midi-track-splitter
description: Splits a multi-track MIDI file into separate single-track MIDI files.
example_prompt: Split this MIDI into one file per instrument
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — partitions and re-emits standard MIDI chunks locally. — via midly crate
rationale: Isolates parts for remixing or printing individual scores (Mido demand).

name: elf-analyzer
description: Parses Linux ELF binaries to show sections, symbols, dynamic imports, and RELRO/NX/PIE security flags.
example_prompt: Inspect this ELF binary's sections and security mitigations
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: ELF is parsed from uploaded bytes via a pure-Rust object crate, no host access.
rationale: ELF triage covers Linux malware and CTF reversing, complementing the Remnux/Tsurugi toolset browser-local.

name: csv-timeline-viewer
description: Loads a large CSV/JSONL of timestamped events and lets you sort, filter, and full-text search across columns and time ranges.
example_prompt: Load this forensic timeline CSV and filter to events on 2026-06-18
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: streaming CSV parse plus in-memory indexing handles large files locally without a server. — via csv crate
rationale: Recreates Eric Zimmerman's Timeline Explorer cross-platform in the browser, the standard way analysts triage huge event CSVs.

name: article-to-epub
description: Packages article text or cleaned HTML into a valid EPUB ebook file.
example_prompt: Turn this article into an EPUB I can read on my e-reader
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM builds the EPUB zip + container/OPF/XHTML structure in-memory. — via zip crate
rationale: Wallabag's most-loved export is 'send to e-reader', and EPUB generation is pure zip+XML that fits perfectly in WASM.

name: file-metadata-inspect
description: Surfaces all embedded metadata in a file — image EXIF/XMP, PDF author/producer, document properties.
example_prompt: What hidden metadata is in this PDF?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM metadata parsers, no upload
rationale: Shows what identifying data you'd leak before sharing a file publicly.

name: markdown-task-extractor
description: Extracts all `- [ ]`/`- [x]` checkboxes from Markdown into a task list with completion stats.
example_prompt: List all the open todos in these notes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line scan; pure text, no network.
rationale: Vikunja/TinyList users keep tasks inline in notes and want them pulled out as an actionable list.

name: odt-to-markdown
description: Converts an OpenDocument Text (.odt) file into Markdown.
example_prompt: Convert this LibreOffice document to markdown
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (zip + ODF XML parse); fully local. — via quick-xml crate
rationale: LibreOffice is the canonical ODF producer and ODT→Markdown has no good privacy-respecting converter.

name: xpub-derive
description: Derives receive and change addresses from an extended public key for watch-only inspection.
example_prompt: Derive the first 20 receive addresses from this xpub
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with pure-Rust secp256k1 (k256); EC point math is deterministic and runs entirely in the browser. — via k256 crate
rationale: Sparrow-style watch-only address derivation lets users verify an xpub belongs to their wallet without exposing private keys.

name: stepwise-feature-selection
description: Runs forward/backward stepwise regression to automatically pick the predictor columns that best explain the target by AIC/BIC.
example_prompt: Use stepwise regression to find which of these 12 columns predict sales
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — it just refits OLS over candidate subsets and compares information criteria, all in-memory. — via nalgebra crate
rationale: Automated predictor selection answers the perennial 'which variables actually matter' question.

name: per-capita-normalizer
description: Normalizes raw counts into per-capita or per-100k rates given a population column.
example_prompt: Convert these disease counts to cases per 100,000 using the population column
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM arithmetic across columns; offline. — via csv crate
rationale: GHDx and UNICEF health figures are only comparable across regions once normalized by population.

name: video-to-vp9
description: Re-encodes a video to VP9 in a WebM container for high-efficiency, royalty-free web delivery.
example_prompt: Encode this as VP9 webm for streaming on my site
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm's libvpx-vp9 encoder runs in the browser, no server transcoding needed.
rationale: VP9 gives HEVC-like compression without licensing concerns, ideal for self-hosted web video.

name: video-to-prores
description: Transcodes a video into Apple ProRes 422 in a MOV for high-quality, edit-friendly intermediate footage.
example_prompt: Convert this to ProRes so I can edit it without recompression artifacts
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm includes the ProRes encoder and MOV muxer, producing an editing master locally.
rationale: Editors need a robust intermediate codec, and ProRes conversion avoids generation loss during cutting.

name: video-to-dnxhd
description: Transcodes a video into Avid DNxHD/DNxHR in a MOV/MXF wrapper for professional NLE workflows.
example_prompt: Make a DNxHD version of this clip for Avid
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm bundles the dnxhd encoder, generating the intermediate file client-side.
rationale: Avid and DaVinci editors require DNxHD/HR masters, an unmet pro conversion the browser can handle.

name: wavpack-to-flac
description: Converts WavPack (.wv) lossless files to FLAC with no quality loss.
example_prompt: convert my wavpack rips to flac
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader decodes WavPack and encodes FLAC losslessly in-browser.
rationale: WavPack collections are unplayable on most mobile/streaming players, where FLAC just works.

name: dts-to-wav
description: Decodes DTS Coherent Acoustics audio to PCM WAV.
example_prompt: convert this dts audio track to wav
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader includes the DTS decoder, outputting PCM WAV client-side.
rationale: DTS tracks demuxed from Blu-ray/DVD need decoding to PCM before any standard editor can touch them.

name: json-error-locator
description: Pinpoints the exact line, column, and cause of a JSON syntax error (trailing comma, unquoted key, bad escape).
example_prompt: This JSON won't parse — tell me exactly where it's broken
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM streaming JSON parser surfaces precise error spans entirely client-side
rationale: Browser JSON.parse only gives a vague position; a precise locator turns a frustrating hunt into one glance.

name: image-text-legibility-checker
description: OCRs text in an image and flags text that renders too small (in pixels) to be legible at typical viewing sizes.
example_prompt: Is the text in this infographic large enough to read?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a text-detection model in-browser to measure glyph heights, no server.
rationale: Tiny embedded text fails on mobile and a measured legibility check catches it before publishing.

name: embedded-artwork-validator
description: Validates embedded cover art for format, dimensions, aspect ratio, file size, and presence against store/library requirements.
example_prompt: Check the embedded album art meets a minimum 1400x1400 requirement
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: extract the APIC/PICTURE block and read image header dimensions client-side
rationale: Distributors reject undersized or wrong-format cover art, and embedded checks prevent a failed submission.

name: correlated-sample-generator
description: Generates multivariate-normal samples matching a supplied mean vector and covariance matrix by Cholesky-transforming independent normals.
example_prompt: Generate 500 samples with covariance [[1,0.8],[0.8,1]]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Cholesky factorization plus a seeded Box–Muller normal generator, fully local.
rationale: Producing correlated synthetic data is a frequent need for testing statistics pipelines without a server.

name: mermaid-from-data
description: Generates Mermaid diagram source (flowchart, class, or ER) from a structured list of nodes and edges.
example_prompt: Generate a Mermaid flowchart from this list of steps and arrows
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM text emission from parsed edges; no rendering engine needed to produce source
rationale: Turning data into diagram-as-code is a common docs task and the Mermaid syntax is easy to fumble.

name: time-series-generator
description: Generates synthetic time-series data with configurable trend, seasonality, and noise.
example_prompt: Generate 365 daily values with an upward trend, weekly seasonality, and some noise.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: deterministic signal composition plus seeded noise runs fully client-side.
rationale: Realistic time-series fixtures are needed to demo dashboards and test forecasting code.

name: video-thumbnail-suggester
description: Picks the most representative, sharp, and well-exposed frames as ranked thumbnail candidates.
example_prompt: Suggest the best thumbnail frames for this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg `thumbnail` filter pre-selects candidates, onnx-runtime scores aesthetics/sharpness in-browser; all local.
rationale: Choosing a good thumbnail by hand is tedious, and an automatic ranked shortlist runs fully offline.

name: tempo-map-extractor
description: Tracks a variable tempo curve over time and exports BPM-versus-time rather than one global tempo.
example_prompt: Show how the tempo changes through this live performance
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs windowed beat tracking on the onset envelope locally
rationale: Live and classical recordings drift in tempo, which a single BPM value cannot capture.

name: wireguard-keygen
description: Generate a WireGuard Curve25519 key pair (and preshared key) with a sample config snippet.
example_prompt: Generate a WireGuard key pair and a starter config
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM Curve25519 crypto; offline. — via x25519-dalek crate
rationale: WireGuard is widely self-hosted and there's no key tool for it.

name: color-transfer
description: Transfers the color mood of a reference image onto a target by matching channel statistics.
example_prompt: Make this photo's colors match this sunset reference image
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Reinhard Lab-space mean/std matching between the two images
rationale: Stat-based color matching is a powerful grading trick with no client-side tool today.

name: video-vfr-to-cfr
description: Converts a variable-frame-rate video to a constant frame rate so it edits and syncs cleanly.
example_prompt: Convert this variable frame rate phone video to constant 30 fps
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's fps/vsync cfr handling runs in ffmpeg.wasm, retiming frames locally.
rationale: VFR phone/screen-capture video causes audio drift in most editors; CFR conversion is the canonical fix.

name: csv-header-sanitizer
description: Cleans column names into valid, consistent snake_case identifiers, deduplicating collisions.
example_prompt: Clean up these messy column headers into snake_case database-safe names
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM string normalization of the header row; no network.
rationale: Sanitized headers are required before loading into databases or code and are tedious to fix manually.

name: csv-date-normalizer
description: Parses mixed and ambiguous date/time formats in a column and rewrites them to ISO 8601.
example_prompt: Normalize the messy dates in the 'order_date' column to YYYY-MM-DD
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM date parsing (chrono-style) over column values; entirely client-side.
rationale: Inconsistent date strings break sorting and analysis, and normalizing them is fiddly without code.

name: csv-regex-replace
description: Applies a find-and-replace regex across selected columns with capture-group substitution.
example_prompt: In the 'phone' column replace any non-digit characters with nothing
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM regex engine over targeted columns; fully client-side. — via regex crate
rationale: Scoped regex replace is far safer than whole-file replace and is hard in spreadsheet apps.

name: html-comment-stripper
description: Removes all HTML comments, including conditional and CMS-injected ones, from markup.
example_prompt: Remove every comment from this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizer scan; pure string filtering, no network.
rationale: Exported pages carry author notes and tooling markers you want gone before publishing.

name: relative-to-absolute-urls
description: Rewrites relative href and src values in HTML to absolute URLs against a given base.
example_prompt: Rewrite all the relative links in this HTML to absolute using https://example.com/blog/
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM URL resolution per RFC 3986 over the parsed tree; no network.
rationale: Saved or syndicated HTML breaks its links unless relative paths are resolved to absolute ones.

name: ip-address-extractor
description: Pulls IPv4 and IPv6 addresses out of logs or text and flags private vs public ranges.
example_prompt: Extract every IP address from this access log
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: regex plus range checks against reserved CIDR blocks, all in-memory.
rationale: Triaging logs for offending IPs is a frequent ops task that needs no server.

name: markdown-table-extractor
description: Finds GitHub-flavored Markdown tables in a document and exports each as CSV or JSON.
example_prompt: Turn the tables in this README into CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a small Markdown table parser over the text, no rendering or server.
rationale: Getting tabular data out of Markdown into a spreadsheet is painful by hand and very common.

name: zip-archive-lister
description: Reads a ZIP file's central directory to list every entry with its size, compressed size, ratio, and modified time, without extracting.
example_prompt: List the contents of this zip file with sizes without unzipping it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reading the ZIP central directory with the zip crate; metadata-only, fully local
rationale: Peeking inside an archive before extracting (size, contents, suspicious paths) is a frequent, useful check.

name: postman-collection-extractor
description: Parses a Postman collection JSON into a flat list of requests with method, URL, headers, and body.
example_prompt: List all the requests in this Postman collection
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON walk.
rationale: API inventory and migration off Postman.

name: animated-webp-to-frames
description: Extracts every frame of an animated WebP as separate PNGs with timing info.
example_prompt: Split this animated webp into individual frames
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg demuxes animated WebP frames in WASM
rationale: Editing or re-timing a WebP animation requires its frames, which no simple client tool exposes.

name: video-to-animated-webp
description: Encodes a short clip as an animated WebP, a smaller modern alternative to GIF that keeps transparency.
example_prompt: make this 3-second clip into an animated webp
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — libwebp_anim encoder produces the animated WebP fully client-side.
rationale: Animated WebP gives GIF-like inline playback at a fraction of the size and is now broadly supported in browsers.

name: video-duplicate-content-detector
description: Decides whether two videos are the same content (re-encoded or rescaled) and reports a confidence score.
example_prompt: Are these two files the same video just re-encoded?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg samples frames and Rust→WASM compares perceptual hashes plus duration/aspect heuristics locally.
rationale: De-duplicating near-identical re-encodes saves storage and avoids redundant uploads.

name: git-diff-parse
description: Parses a raw git diff into structured per-file hunks with line ranges and change types.
example_prompt: Parse this git diff into structured hunks per file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tokenize diff headers and hunks into a model, local only
rationale: Turning an opaque diff into structured hunks enables targeted review and downstream tooling without git.

name: mjpeg-to-mp4
description: Converts Motion-JPEG video (often from webcams or microscopes) into efficient H.264 MP4.
example_prompt: convert this mjpeg avi to mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm decodes MJPEG and re-encodes to H.264/AAC client-side.
rationale: MJPEG captures are huge and incompatible, and H.264 MP4 shrinks and standardizes them.

name: sql-create-table-from-csv
description: Infers a CREATE TABLE statement with column names and guessed types from a CSV header and sample rows.
example_prompt: give me a CREATE TABLE for this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSV parsing plus per-column type inference; no server.
rationale: Bridges the common gap between having a CSV and needing a schema to load it into a database.

name: sql-insert-from-csv
description: Generates INSERT statements for a named table from CSV rows, with proper quoting and escaping.
example_prompt: make INSERT statements for table users from this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSV-to-SQL emission with correct string escaping; client-side.
rationale: A frequent data-loading need where correct SQL escaping is easy to botch by hand.

name: date-format-normalizer
description: Detects assorted date strings in text and rewrites them all to one chosen format (e.g. ISO 8601).
example_prompt: Normalize every date in this document to YYYY-MM-DD
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: multi-pattern date parser plus formatter, no network
rationale: Documents mixing '3/4/24', 'March 4 2024', and '4 Mar' need a single consistent date format for data work.

name: markdown-link-flattener
description: Replaces Markdown links with their visible text (or with 'text (url)'), removing the link syntax.
example_prompt: Flatten the Markdown links in this text so only the visible words remain
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: inline-link regex/parse and rewrite, runs locally
rationale: Converting Markdown to clean prose or footnoted text means flattening link syntax, distinct from just listing the links.

name: csv-coalesce-columns
description: Creates one column from the first non-empty value across a list of source columns (in priority order), optionally dropping the sources.
example_prompt: Make a phone column from the first non-empty of mobile, home, work in this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: row-wise first-non-null selection over the table, runs in-browser.
rationale: Spreadsheets with several partially-filled equivalent columns are everywhere, and SQL-style COALESCE over columns isn't offered by existing CSV tools.

name: strip-trailing-commas
description: Removes trailing commas before closing brackets/braces to make JSON strictly valid.
example_prompt: remove the trailing commas from this JSON so it parses
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizes and drops comma tokens preceding closers locally
rationale: Trailing commas are the single most common reason a hand-edited JSON file won't parse.

name: cumulative-sum-column
description: Computes a running cumulative sum (prefix sum) of a numeric column, optionally resetting per group.
example_prompt: Add a running total of the amount column
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: single accumulating pass, fully client-side
rationale: Cumulative sum is a fundamental running aggregation (and the inverse of first-difference) not covered by running-extrema.

name: video-creation-time-extractor
description: Extracts the original recording date and time stored in a video's container metadata.
example_prompt: When was this video originally recorded?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the mvhd/udta creation-time and com.apple.quicktime tags; pure parse, local
rationale: Recording timestamps drive media organization and chain-of-custody, and survive even when filesystem dates are lost.

name: sql-ddl-parse
description: Parses SQL CREATE TABLE statements into a structured schema of columns, types, keys, and constraints.
example_prompt: Extract the columns and types from this CREATE TABLE script
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM sqlparser-rs; pure local AST extraction — via sqlparser crate
rationale: It's the reverse of the existing csv-to-sql tools and useful for documenting or diffing schemas.

name: html-form-field-extractor
description: Lists every field of every HTML form with its name, type, required flag, default value, and validation attributes.
example_prompt: Show me all the form fields and their types in this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the form/input/select/textarea tree locally. — via lol-html crate
rationale: Documenting or scripting against an existing HTML form means manually hunting through markup, which this turns into one table.

name: html-image-inventory
description: Builds a table of every img/picture source with its alt text, width/height, and loading/decoding hints, flagging images missing alt or dimensions.
example_prompt: Inventory the images and alt text in this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM markup parse; inspects attributes only, fully offline. — via lol-html crate
rationale: An alt-text and explicit-dimensions audit is a recurring accessibility and layout-shift chore that no current extractor covers.

name: ndjson-formatter
description: Validates, pretty-views, and converts between NDJSON/JSON Lines and a JSON array.
example_prompt: turn these JSON lines into one array
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — line-by-line JSON parsing, fully client-side.
rationale: Log pipelines and ML datasets use NDJSON and need quick conversion/validation.

name: pwa-icon-set
description: Produces the PWA manifest icon set (192/512 plus maskable) and a manifest JSON snippet.
example_prompt: generate pwa app icons and manifest entries from this image
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM resizing/padding plus JSON text generation — via image crate
rationale: Installable web apps require an exact set of icon sizes and manifest entries that are error-prone to make manually.

name: image-format-size-compare
description: Re-encodes one image to PNG, JPEG, WebP and AVIF and reports the file size and a quality metric for each to pick the best format.
example_prompt: Encode this image as WebP, AVIF and JPEG and tell me which gives the smallest file at good quality.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (or plain Rust codecs) re-encodes to each format in the browser and measures sizes + PSNR locally.
rationale: Choosing the right delivery format is a real size/quality tradeoff people guess at; this measures it directly.

name: api-response-diff
description: Diffs two JSON API responses while ignoring user-specified volatile fields (timestamps, ids, request-ids) so only meaningful changes surface.
example_prompt: Diff these two API responses but ignore timestamp and id fields
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON parse + masked recursive comparison; client-side
rationale: Noise-filtered response diffing is the core of contract testing and is awkward to do manually.

name: base64-diff
description: Decodes two base64 (or base64url) blobs and shows a byte-level diff of the underlying payloads.
example_prompt: Compare these two base64 strings and tell me where the decoded bytes differ
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes both blobs and runs a byte diff entirely in memory; no server needed.
rationale: Devs often get two base64 tokens (JWT parts, certs, configs) and need to know if the real content differs, not just the encoding.

name: iban-validate
description: Validates an IBAN's country length and mod-97 check digits and formats it in standard groups.
example_prompt: Is DE89370400440532013000 a valid IBAN?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (mod-97 arithmetic); pure local
rationale: A mistyped IBAN causes failed or misdirected transfers that the checksum would catch.

name: audio-rms-level-report
description: Reports per-channel RMS, sample-peak, and average levels in dBFS as a JSON summary.
example_prompt: Give me the RMS and peak levels of this track per channel
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: single pass over decoded samples accumulating squares and peaks; trivial CPU.
rationale: A precise objective level readout underpins gain staging and comparisons.

name: jsonl-stats
description: Summarizes a JSON Lines file: record count, per-key presence frequency, and value-type distribution.
example_prompt: give me stats on this jsonl file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing each line and tallying key/type counts.
rationale: JSONL is the dominant ML/log format and lacks a quick local profiler.

name: check-digit-validator
description: Validates and computes check digits for Luhn (credit cards), ISBN-10/13, EAN, IBAN, and routing numbers, reporting which scheme matches.
example_prompt: Is 4539578763621486 a valid Luhn number?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; the weighted-modulo checksum algorithms are tiny integer routines, fully local with no data leaving the browser.
rationale: Check-digit verification is a constant data-entry and validation task and running it locally avoids sending sensitive identifiers to a server.

name: keyvalue-text-parser
description: Parses freeform `key: value` or `key=value` text blocks into structured JSON, grouping repeats.
example_prompt: Parse these label: value lines into a JSON object
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; tolerant line parsing with configurable separators, local only
rationale: Pasted metadata, headers, and form dumps arrive as key-value text that needs structuring.

name: log-return-calculator
description: Converts a price or level series into continuously-compounded log returns ln(p_t/p_{t-1}).
example_prompt: compute the log returns of 100, 102, 99, 105
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — adjacent-ratio logarithms over the parsed series, no network.
rationale: Log returns are additive over time and the standard input to volatility/quant work, distinct from the simple percent-change tools already present.

name: apple-touch-icon-generator
description: Produces the 180×180 apple-touch-icon PNG with optional safe-area padding and background fill.
example_prompt: Make an apple-touch-icon from this logo with white padding
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: composite onto a square canvas, resize, encode PNG — no network. — via image crate
rationale: iOS home-screen icons need a specific size and opaque background most logos lack.

name: raw-rgb-to-png
description: Assembles raw RGB/RGBA byte data plus width/height into a viewable PNG.
example_prompt: I have a raw RGBA dump that's 256x256 — turn it into a PNG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: wrap the byte buffer with the given dimensions and encode PNG — pure in-memory. — via image crate
rationale: Framebuffer and shader/render dumps come out as headerless raw bytes that need wrapping to inspect.

name: png-to-rgba-bytes
description: Decodes a PNG and dumps its pixels as a raw RGBA byte buffer (binary or hex).
example_prompt: Export this PNG as raw RGBA bytes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: decode and emit the flat pixel buffer — no external dependency. — via image crate
rationale: Engine/texture loaders and tests often need the raw pixel buffer rather than an encoded file.

name: diff-extract-versions
description: Reconstructs the full before-text and after-text from a unified diff that includes enough context.
example_prompt: From this diff, give me the original and the new version of the file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — walk hunks and emit the two reconstructed sides
rationale: People often have only a patch and want either side of it without manually reverse-engineering hunks.

name: sqlite-schema-diff
description: Opens two SQLite database files and diffs their schemas — tables, columns, indexes, and triggers.
example_prompt: Compare the schema of these two .sqlite files
loader_feasibility: pyodide — bundled sqlite3 reads both files in the sandbox and introspects sqlite_master with no server
rationale: Comparing real database file schemas usually needs a desktop tool; running sqlite in-browser keeps the data private.

name: video-resolution-target-check
description: Compares the video resolution against a target list (1080p, 720p, 4K) and reports exact, over, or under.
example_prompt: Is this exactly 1920x1080?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm reads dimensions in-browser and the comparison is trivial WASM logic.
rationale: Off-by-a-few resolutions slip past visual checks but get rejected by strict ingest specs.

name: authorization-header-decode
description: Decodes an Authorization header, splitting the scheme and revealing Basic credentials or Bearer token structure.
example_prompt: decode this Basic auth header to show the username
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM base64 decode for Basic and structure display for Bearer; no verification
rationale: Quickly confirming which user/scheme an auth header carries is a frequent debugging step.

name: image-histogram-analyzer
description: Generates per-channel RGB and luminance histograms and reports exposure stats (clipping, dynamic range).
example_prompt: Show the RGB histogram for this image and tell me if highlights are clipped
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes pixels and bins them into histograms client-side — via image crate
rationale: A histogram with clipping warnings is a core photo-QA tool that's surprisingly hard to get without an editor installed.

name: image-format-metadata
description: Reports structural metadata for any common image (dimensions, bit depth, color mode, interlacing, frame count, compression) across PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/BMP/TIFF.
example_prompt: What are the technical specs of this image file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads each format's header without full decode, all in-browser
rationale: A unified 'image specs' readout saves people from opening five different tools to learn bit depth or frame count.

name: sorted-order-checker
description: Verifies a numeric list is sorted ascending or descending and pinpoints the first out-of-order element.
example_prompt: Check if these numbers are sorted: 3,7,5,9
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — linear comparison pass, deterministic in-sandbox.
rationale: A simple, high-frequency data-quality check that returns the offending position, not just yes/no.

name: peak-detector
description: Finds local maxima/minima in a 1-D signal with configurable prominence, height, and minimum-distance thresholds.
example_prompt: Find the peaks in this signal column with prominence above 0.5.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM local-extrema scan with prominence calc; local.
rationale: Peak finding underlies spectroscopy, ECG, and counting tasks and is distinct from FFT analysis.

name: pdf-metadata-extractor
description: Extracts a PDF's document info dictionary and XMP metadata: title, author, dates, producer, and page count.
example_prompt: Show me the metadata and page count of this PDF
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM PDF object parsing of the trailer/info dictionary; no rendering needed. — via lopdf crate
rationale: Quick metadata inspection helps with provenance, redaction checks, and cataloging.

name: grade-to-gpa-parser
description: Maps letter grades (A, B+, C-) to GPA points on a configurable scale and averages them.
example_prompt: Turn these grades into a GPA: A, A-, B+, B, C
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — lookup table and weighted mean, fully local.
rationale: Computing GPA from transcripts is a routine task with a clear deterministic mapping.

name: trim-each-line
description: Trims leading and trailing whitespace from every line independently.
example_prompt: trim whitespace from both ends of every line
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string ops, fully local
rationale: Cleans ragged indentation and padding from copied tables and lists in one pass.

name: indent-block-text
description: Adds a configurable number of spaces or a fixed prefix to the start of every line.
example_prompt: indent every line of this by 4 spaces
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line mapping, no server
rationale: Quickly nests a block into code, quotes, or a YAML/Markdown level.

name: json-array-pluck-field
description: Extracts a single field by key or dotted path from every object in a JSON array into a flat list.
example_prompt: pluck the email field from this array of objects
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM path traversal, runs in-browser
rationale: Pulls one column out of JSON records for quick reuse.

name: chromatic-aberration-fix
description: Removes purple/green color fringing at high-contrast edges from lens chromatic aberration.
example_prompt: Fix the purple fringing on the edges of this photo
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM detects fringe colors near edges and desaturates/realigns channels; runs locally.
rationale: CA fringing is a frequent optical defect that is rarely offered as a focused, standalone fix.

name: de-esser
description: Reduces harsh sibilance by compressing only the 5–8 kHz band on vocal tracks.
example_prompt: The S sounds are too sharp on this vocal — de-ess it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: split-band crossover plus level-dependent gain on the high band, all in-buffer DSP.
rationale: Sibilance is a near-universal vocal problem and a dedicated de-esser fixes it without dulling the whole track.

name: bitcrush
description: Reduces effective bit depth and sample rate for a deliberate lo-fi/retro effect.
example_prompt: Give this an 8-bit lo-fi crushed sound
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: quantize amplitude to fewer bits and sample-and-hold to a lower rate — pure math.
rationale: Bitcrushing is a popular creative transformation for chiptune, lo-fi, and SFX design.

name: zero-pad-ids
description: Pads (or strips) leading zeros on an ID/code column to a fixed width so codes sort and join correctly.
example_prompt: Pad the zip codes to 5 digits with leading zeros
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string padding per cell; local.
rationale: Spreadsheets strip leading zeros from ZIP/SKU codes, breaking joins until re-padded.

name: category-canonicalize
description: Collapses spelling/case/whitespace variants of a categorical column to canonical values via a supplied mapping plus fuzzy suggestions for the rest.
example_prompt: Standardize the country column so USA, U.S., and United States all become one value
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with edit-distance grouping; runs locally on the column.
rationale: Inconsistent category spellings wreck group-bys and require tedious manual mapping to fix.

name: list-to-json-array
description: Converts a newline- or comma-separated list into a JSON array, with optional numeric/boolean type inference.
example_prompt: Turn this list of values into a JSON array
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM split + serde_json emit; deterministic and offline.
rationale: Moving a pasted list into JSON config/test fixtures is a tiny but constant friction point.

name: forward-backward-fill
description: Fills missing numeric cells by carrying the last observation forward and/or the next observation backward.
example_prompt: Forward-fill the blanks in this column and back-fill any leading gaps
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: sequential scan carrying last/next value, fully local.
rationale: Forward/backward fill is the standard imputation for stepwise data (prices, status) and is distinct from interpolation.

name: one-hot-encoder
description: Expands a categorical column into one binary indicator column per distinct category.
example_prompt: One-hot encode the category column in this table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: build vocabulary then emit indicator matrix, fully local.
rationale: One-hot encoding is the most common categorical-to-numeric transform for ML and has no current gizza tool.

name: image-text-overlay-contrast-checker
description: Scans a photo for the worst-case region where overlaid text would fail WCAG contrast, given a text color.
example_prompt: Where on this hero image would white caption text be hard to read?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: sliding-window luminance vs target text color — offline math.
rationale: Banner designers need to know where text-over-image will be illegible.

name: cyclomatic-complexity-analyzer
description: Computes cyclomatic complexity per function for a pasted source file and ranks the most complex functions.
example_prompt: Compute the cyclomatic complexity of each function in this JavaScript file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: tokenizes source and counts branch points in pure Rust, no external tooling.
rationale: Spotting the riskiest functions to refactor is a core code-quality inspection with no setup.

name: ffmpeg-filtergraph-builder
description: Builds a validated ffmpeg -filter_complex string from an ordered list of described filter steps.
example_prompt: build a filtergraph that scales to 720p, then crops to square, then adds a fade
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — composes and syntax-validates the filtergraph string, no execution required.
rationale: Filtergraph syntax is error-prone, so scaffolding it saves trial-and-error.

name: video-codec-whitelist-check
description: Verifies the video and audio codecs are within an allowed set (e.g. H.264/AAC) for a target platform.
example_prompt: Are the codecs in this file allowed for web upload (H.264 + AAC)?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm probes codec names locally and the whitelist comparison runs in WASM. — via mp4 crate
rationale: An off-list codec (HEVC, AC-3, VP9 in MP4) is a frequent silent rejection cause for upload pipelines.

name: video-fps-target-check
description: Verifies the average frame rate matches an expected target (24/25/30/60) within tolerance and flags 29.97 vs 30 traps.
example_prompt: Is this video really 30fps or is it 29.97?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm reads avg/r_frame_rate locally and the tolerance check runs in WASM. — via mp4 crate
rationale: The 30 vs 29.97 distinction breaks sync in conform workflows and is easy to mis-assume.

name: video-burned-in-caption-detector
description: Samples frames and runs on-device OCR to detect hardcoded/burned-in subtitles versus a clean unsubbed master.
