example_prompt: Does this video have burned-in subtitles hardcoded into the picture?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a text-detection model over sampled frames decoded by ffmpeg.wasm, fully in-browser.
rationale: Burned-in captions ruin a master meant for re-subtitling, and they're invisible to any metadata-only check.

name: zip-integrity-checker
description: Validates a ZIP archive's central directory and verifies each entry's stored CRC32 against its data.
example_prompt: Is this ZIP file intact? Check the CRCs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: ZIP parsing and CRC32 verification run entirely on the uploaded bytes. — via zip crate
rationale: Silent ZIP corruption is common after partial downloads and per-entry CRC checks pinpoint the damaged file.

name: percent-difference-calculator
description: Computes absolute difference, percent change, and symmetric percent difference between two values.
example_prompt: Percent difference between 240 and 300?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; ratio arithmetic, no dependencies.
rationale: Percent change vs percent difference vs relative error are routinely confused, and disambiguating them is genuinely useful.

name: json-schema-compat-check
description: Compares an old and new JSON Schema to determine whether the change is backward-compatible for producers and consumers.
example_prompt: Is this new JSON schema a breaking change compared to the old one?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — schema parse plus compatibility ruleset evaluation, no server
rationale: Schema evolution safety is hard to reason about manually and a rules-based checker prevents broken contracts.

name: npy-array-decoder
description: Decodes a NumPy .npy binary array file into JSON/CSV numbers, reporting its dtype and shape.
example_prompt: Decode this .npy file and show me the array values
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the .npy magic header, dtype string, and little-endian payload entirely client-side; no Python or server needed
rationale: Lets people inspect ML/scientific .npy dumps without spinning up a Python environment.

name: ndjson-to-matrix
description: Converts NDJSON numeric records into an aligned 2D matrix/CSV with a unified column set.
example_prompt: Turn this NDJSON of numbers into a matrix
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses each JSON line and aligns keys into columns
rationale: Streaming NDJSON logs of metrics need flattening into a rectangular matrix for analysis.

name: mp4-to-flv
description: Encodes an MP4 into an FLV stream for legacy RTMP/Flash-based ingest pipelines.
example_prompt: Make an .flv version of this video for our old streaming server
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader — FLV mux with H.263/H.264 runs in wasm, no server.
rationale: Legacy broadcast and RTMP encoders still demand FLV, an awkward format to produce locally.

name: data-drift-summary
description: Compares two tabular datasets and reports per-column type, null-rate, cardinality, range, and new/missing category drift.
example_prompt: Compare last quarter's and this quarter's dataset and flag any columns that drifted
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: compute per-column summary stats for both and diff, in-memory.
rationale: Schema and null-rate drift silently breaks pipelines and a side-by-side column profile catches it early.

name: wav-to-aac
description: Encodes a WAV to AAC in an M4A container.
example_prompt: Make an m4a AAC from this wav at 256k
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm encodes AAC and muxes M4A locally.
rationale: AAC/M4A is the default for Apple and mobile delivery, and only ALAC/m4r exports exist today.

name: csv-whitespace-normalizer
description: Trims leading/trailing spaces and collapses internal runs of whitespace in every cell.
example_prompt: Trim and collapse the extra spaces in all cells of this CSV
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM per-cell whitespace pass; entirely in-memory.
rationale: Stray whitespace breaks joins and grouping silently, and bulk-trimming is otherwise scripting work.

name: csv-quote-normalizer
description: Re-emits a CSV with consistent quoting, escaping, and delimiter choices to fix malformed files.
example_prompt: Re-quote this CSV so every field uses standard double-quote escaping
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM tolerant parse + strict re-serialize; client-side.
rationale: Inconsistent quoting from hand-edited CSVs breaks strict parsers, and re-normalizing fixes it cleanly.

name: reindent-json
description: Re-indents JSON to a chosen space/tab width or minifies it, without reordering keys.
example_prompt: reformat this JSON with 4-space indentation
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM serde_json round-trip with a custom formatter; client-side only.
rationale: Switching indentation style or minifying JSON is a constant formatting need.

name: first-difference-calculator
description: Computes first differences or period-over-period deltas of a numeric series, with optional lag and percent-change mode.
example_prompt: Compute the day-over-day change for this revenue series
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sequential subtraction, fully local
rationale: Differencing is the first step in most time-series prep and stationarity checks.

name: mean-center-column
description: Subtracts the column mean (optionally dividing by std for standardization) from every value.
example_prompt: Mean-center the 'temperature' column
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — mean/std + elementwise subtract, fully local
rationale: Centering is a basic preprocessing step that's tedious to do correctly on a single column in a sheet.

name: min-max-rescaler
description: Linearly rescales a numeric column from its observed range onto an arbitrary target [a, b] range.
example_prompt: Rescale this column to the 0–1 range
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — affine min/max mapping, no network
rationale: Min-max scaling to a chosen range is the most common normalization and lacks a precise offline tool.

name: path-extractor
description: Extracts and de-duplicates every file path mentioned in arbitrary text such as build logs, stack traces, or git status output.
example_prompt: Pull all the file paths out of this stack trace
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — regex scanning of pasted text.
rationale: Reproduces PathPicker/fpp's core value of turning messy tool output into a clean, copyable path list.

name: archive-grep
description: Searches every text file inside an uploaded zip/tar archive with a regex and lists file:line matches.
example_prompt: Search this repo.zip for every call to fetchUser
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — unzips and regex-scans in memory; nothing leaves the browser. — via zip crate
rationale: Recursive ripgrep across a whole project archive, fully client-side so private code never gets uploaded.

name: ast-code-search
description: Searches pasted source code by syntactic AST pattern instead of plain text, matching constructs like calls, function signatures, or JSX nodes.
example_prompt: Find every `console.log(...)` call in this JS file and show the surrounding lines
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with tree-sitter grammars compiled in; parsing + pattern matching is pure CPU work on pasted text, no server needed. — via tree-sitter crate
rationale: ast-grep's core value is structural search that regex can't express, and it maps cleanly onto a paste-and-query browser tool.

name: ast-code-rewrite
description: Applies a structural find-and-replace (codemod) to pasted code using AST patterns, e.g. rewriting an old API call shape into a new one everywhere.
example_prompt: Rewrite all `foo.then(cb)` into `await foo` in this TypeScript snippet
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tree-sitter parse + rewrite; transformation runs entirely client-side on the pasted buffer. — via tree-sitter crate
rationale: AST-driven codemods are the highest-leverage half of ast-grep and there is no safe browser tool for them today.

name: sphere-to-wav
description: Converts NIST SPHERE (.sph) speech-corpus files to standard WAV, parsing the ASCII header and byte order.
example_prompt: convert this timit .sph file to wav
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the 1024-byte text header and rewraps the (typically uncompressed) PCM as WAV.
rationale: Speech corpora like TIMIT ship as SPHERE that ASR and editing tools can't open without conversion.

name: ogg-vorbis-to-opus
description: Re-encodes legacy Ogg Vorbis files to Opus, the more efficient modern Ogg codec.
example_prompt: convert my old ogg vorbis files to opus
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader decodes Vorbis and encodes Opus in the same Ogg container, client-side.
rationale: Opus supersedes Vorbis on quality-per-bit, so migrating old Ogg libraries is a real cleanup task.

name: dot-to-mermaid
description: Converts a Graphviz DOT graph into Mermaid flowchart syntax, mapping nodes, edges, labels, and direction.
example_prompt: Convert this Graphviz .dot file to Mermaid
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM DOT parser emitting Mermaid text; runs in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: Mermaid renders natively in Markdown/docs while many existing diagrams are stuck in DOT.

name: markdown-runbook-extractor
description: Extracts named, executable code blocks from a markdown runbook into a single runnable script plus an ordered task list.
example_prompt: Turn this runbook into a runnable script: [paste markdown runbook]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM markdown parsing that pairs headings/annotations with code fences; pure text.
rationale: Runme's runbook-from-markdown idea is genuinely useful, and the extraction half runs fully client-side.

name: jsonl-tool
description: Parse, filter, count, and convert JSON Lines / NDJSON to and from a JSON array.
example_prompt: Convert this JSONL log into a single JSON array
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — line-by-line serde_json parsing in the browser.
rationale: jl demand and the ubiquity of NDJSON logs and exports make line-oriented JSON handling broadly useful.

name: youtube-takeout-stats
description: Parses a Google/YouTube Takeout watch-history file into stats: top channels, videos per month, and viewing patterns.
example_prompt: Analyze my YouTube watch-history.json and show my top channels and monthly counts.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the Takeout JSON/HTML is parsed and aggregated locally, keeping private history off any server.
rationale: Archiving/auditing one's YouTube activity is the appeal of Yark, and Takeout data makes it doable without downloading videos.

name: iir-filter-designer
description: Designs and applies low/high/band-pass and shelving biquad filters to audio with a given cutoff and Q.
example_prompt: Apply a 120Hz high-pass filter to this recording to remove rumble
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — biquad coefficient design and filtering are pure DSP that run in wasmi.
rationale: Designing and applying LTI filters is the core of AudioTK and audiolazy and a constant cleanup need.

name: mfcc-extractor
description: Extracts MFCC coefficients from speech or audio and returns them as a CSV matrix.
example_prompt: Extract MFCCs from this audio as CSV
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM FFT, mel filterbank, and DCT compute MFCCs entirely client-side.
rationale: MFCCs are the most common hand-crafted feature for speech and audio ML pipelines.

name: shader-to-image
description: Runs a fragment shader at a chosen resolution and returns the rendered frame as a PNG.
example_prompt: Render this fragment shader to a 1024x1024 PNG
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute loader compiles and dispatches the shader on the device GPU and reads back pixels, all in-browser. — via wgpu crate
rationale: Shader playgrounds (ShaderToy, GLSL Sandbox, GLSLbin) exist to render shaders to images and a chat-native renderer matches that core use.

name: perceptual-hash-compare
description: Computes aHash/dHash/pHash for two images and reports the Hamming distance plus a same/different verdict.
example_prompt: Are these two photos the same image? Compare their perceptual hashes.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes both images, downscales to a hash grid and computes bit distances entirely in-browser. — via image crate
rationale: A single robust similarity number is the workhorse primitive for spotting re-saves, crops and re-compressions.

name: image-ocr-text-diff
description: OCRs two screenshots or document images and produces a word-level text diff of what was added, removed or changed.
example_prompt: What text changed between these two screenshots of the contract?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime or transformers-js runs an OCR model in the browser, then a Rust text-diff compares the strings.
rationale: Comparing the readable content of two images, not their pixels, is what people actually want when diffing documents or UI text.

name: set-diff-json
description: Performs set operations (union, intersection, difference) on two JSON arrays, optionally matched by a key field.
example_prompt: Which objects are in array A but not array B, keyed on id?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse both arrays and compute set relationships by value or key locally
rationale: Answering membership questions across two record lists is common and awkward without a dedicated tool.

name: elf-macho-info
description: Parses ELF and Mach-O binaries to show sections, symbols, linked libraries, and architecture.
example_prompt: Show me the imports and sections of this Linux binary
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — `goblin` handles ELF/Mach-O in pure Rust — via goblin crate
rationale: Unix/macOS triage (unix_collector, UAC, Fuji) surfaces suspect binaries that need quick static inspection.

name: sigma-rule-matcher
description: Runs Sigma detection rules against parsed Windows event logs and flags matching events as potential threats.
example_prompt: Run these Sigma rules against my EVTX logs and show hits
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Sigma rule evaluation is pure logic over already-parsed records.
rationale: Brings Hayabusa/chainsaw-style detection offline so triage works on air-gapped evidence.

name: model-evaluation-report
description: Builds a confusion matrix, ROC/PR curves, and a precision/recall/F1 report from predictions.
example_prompt: Here are y_true and y_pred — give me the confusion matrix and ROC curve
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs scikit-learn metrics and plots them with matplotlib entirely in-browser.
rationale: Model evaluation plots (the sklearn-evaluation demand) are needed by everyone training models and run offline.

name: linreg-stats
description: Fits an OLS/ridge/lasso regression on a CSV and reports interpretable coefficients, p-values, and R².
example_prompt: Run a linear regression of sales on ad spend and region and show the coefficients.
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs statsmodels/scikit-learn linear models in WASM; the full statistical summary is computed locally.
rationale: An interpretable, classic-stats counterpart to the ML tools that analysts reach for constantly, fully offline.

name: time-series-forecaster
description: Forecasts future points of a univariate time series with exponential smoothing/ARIMA and confidence bands.
example_prompt: Forecast the next 12 months from this monthly sales series.
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs statsmodels ARIMA/ETS in WASM and plots the forecast on-device. — via augurs crate
rationale: Forecasting is a top reason teams adopt these ML stacks and runs comfortably in pyodide without a backend.

name: eda-report
description: Auto-generates an exploratory data analysis report: per-column type, missing-value counts, distribution summaries, and top correlations.
example_prompt: Give me an EDA profile of this dataset
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs pandas/profiling logic on the uploaded CSV with no server round-trip
rationale: Encodes the 'explore the data' core of Practical/Everyday/Exploring Data Science into one automated pass.

name: churn-cohort-retention
description: Builds cohort retention/churn tables and curves from user signup and activity event data.
example_prompt: From this events CSV, show monthly cohort retention
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM groups and aggregates events locally
rationale: Directly operationalizes 'Fighting Churn With Data' into the cohort analysis every growth team runs.

name: email-network-analyzer
description: Builds a sender→recipient communication graph with volume and top-correspondent statistics from a set of emails.
example_prompt: Show me the communication network in these emails
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM address aggregation and edge-list construction, computed locally.
rationale: Email-corpus research (à la Enron studies) centers on who-talks-to-whom, kept private in-browser.

name: timeseries-smoother
description: Applies moving-average, 7-day rolling, or exponential smoothing to a time-series CSV.
example_prompt: Smooth this daily case count with a 7-day average
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM windowed reductions over the parsed series, client-side.
rationale: Covid-style daily counts are noisy and need smoothing before they can be read or compared.

name: pca-visualizer
description: Reduces a high-dimensional dataset to 2D with PCA or t-SNE and plots the points colored by label.
example_prompt: Project this CSV to 2D with PCA and color by the class column
loader_feasibility: pyodide — scikit-learn PCA/t-SNE plus matplotlib run in the browser Python sandbox. — via nalgebra crate
rationale: Dimensionality-reduction visualization is a staple of the ML/dataviz demand for exploring datasets.

name: text-feature-matrix
description: Converts a text collection into bag-of-words or TF-IDF feature matrices exportable as CSV/JSON.
example_prompt: Turn these documents into a TF-IDF matrix I can feed to a model.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; vocabulary building and vectorization run client-side.
rationale: Vectorizing text is the bridge from raw data to ML, matching the scikit-learn workflows across the harvested resources.

name: date-time-extractor
description: Detects and normalizes natural-language dates and times ('next Friday', 'in 2 weeks') to ISO.
example_prompt: Find and normalize all the dates mentioned in this meeting note
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — relative/absolute date grammar evaluated against a supplied reference date. — via chrono crate
rationale: Natural-language date parsing (knwl.js) powers scheduling and calendar extraction without a server.

name: stopword-cleaner
description: Removes stopwords and normalizes whitespace, case, and punctuation for downstream NLP.
example_prompt: Strip the stopwords from this text.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: bundled multilingual stopword lists, pure string processing.
rationale: Standard NLTK/textacy preprocessing step that pairs with frequency and topic tools.

name: tfidf-vectorizer
description: Builds a TF-IDF document-term matrix from multiple documents, exportable as CSV or JSON.
example_prompt: build a tf-idf matrix from these five documents
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM sparse matrix builder; pure compute, offline.
rationale: The text2vec / tm vectorization step that downstream ML and similarity tasks need, fully local.

name: line-operations
description: Bulk line transforms in one place: sort, dedupe, number, reverse, shuffle, trim, and keep/drop lines by regex.
example_prompt: Sort these lines, remove duplicates, and number what's left.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; line manipulation is pure text processing done client-side. — via regex crate
rationale: The sort/uniq/number features editors bundle are constant daily-driver needs and trivially browser-local.

name: email-tracker-pixel-detector
description: Detects tracking pixels and remote images in an email that report when you open it.
example_prompt: Does this email track when I open it?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans for 1x1 and remote-image references locally.
rationale: Privacy-conscious users want to know what's spying before loading remote content.

name: email-semantic-search
description: Semantically searches an mbox by meaning rather than keywords using local embeddings.
example_prompt: Find emails about renewing the contract even if they don't use those words
loader_feasibility: transformers-js embeds messages (all-MiniLM) and ranks by cosine similarity, all in-browser. — model sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
rationale: Meaning-based search over your own mail, fully private, goes beyond what keyword tools can do.

name: ssh-config-formatter
description: Parses, validates, normalizes and pretty-prints an ~/.ssh/config file, flagging duplicate hosts, unknown keywords and shadowed Host patterns.
example_prompt: Clean up and validate this ssh config
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM text parsing of the pasted config; no network or filesystem needed so it runs fully in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: sshto/Wishlist users manage sprawling SSH config files by hand, and a deterministic offline linter/formatter is immediately useful with zero secrets leaving the browser.

name: shamir-secret-recover
description: Reconstructs a secret from a threshold of Shamir shares.
example_prompt: recover the secret from these 3 shares
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Lagrange interpolation over the field runs purely in-memory
rationale: Recombining shares locally is the safe complement to the splitter.

name: newsletter-html-builder
description: Builds responsive, email-client-safe newsletter HTML from simple sections (header, text, button, image).
example_prompt: Build a newsletter HTML with a header, two paragraphs, and a CTA button
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM templating with table-based layout — pure output.
rationale: Hand-coding bulletproof email HTML is painful, and this is the part Mailchimp's editor hides.

name: json-to-graph
description: Visualizes a JSON document's structure as a node-link graph in Mermaid or Graphviz DOT.
example_prompt: Turn this JSON into a node graph like JSON Crack
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM that walks the value tree and emits Mermaid/DOT text — diagram render is client-side.
rationale: The JSON-Crack-style graph view makes relationships in nested data obvious and is a popular, sticky way to inspect JSON.

name: json-key-case-convert
description: Converts all JSON keys between camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, or PascalCase.
example_prompt: Convert all the keys in this JSON from snake_case to camelCase
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM key-walk with case transform; runs on parsed value locally
rationale: Cross-language API boundaries constantly require key-case normalization.

name: json-dedupe-array
description: Removes duplicate elements from a JSON array, with optional key-based dedup for objects.
example_prompt: Remove duplicate objects from this JSON array by the id field
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM hash-based dedup over parsed elements; local-only
rationale: Deduplicating record arrays is a common cleanup step before import or analysis.

name: recovery-code-generator
description: Generates BIP39 mnemonic phrases or one-time backup codes for account recovery.
example_prompt: Generate a 12-word recovery phrase.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the bip39 crate and a CSPRNG; offline, codes never transmitted.
rationale: Backup phrases and one-time codes are the practical mechanics of the 'Secure Account Recovery' demand.

name: multi-hash-digest
description: Computes many digests at once (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256/512, SHA3, BLAKE2b, BLAKE3, RIPEMD-160) in a single pass.
example_prompt: show me every common hash of this string
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the RustCrypto hash family; all algorithms are pure compute and run locally. — via sha2 crate
rationale: A pandect-style one-shot multi-digest saves users from running many tools when verifying downloads.

name: rsa-decrypt
description: Decrypts RSA-OAEP ciphertext using a private key.
example_prompt: decrypt this rsa ciphertext with my private key
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (rsa crate); the private key stays in-page during decryption.
rationale: Pairs with rsa-encrypt and must run locally so the RSA private key is never exposed.

name: svg-security-linter
description: Lints an SVG for XSS-risk constructs: inline script tags, event handlers, external resource refs, and foreignObject.
example_prompt: Check this SVG for security risks before I embed it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the SVG and flags dangerous nodes/attributes without executing anything.
rationale: User-uploaded SVGs are a known XSS vector and a static lint catches script/handler injection.

name: audio-format-conformance-checker
description: Confirms a file's actual codec/container via magic bytes and stream parsing matches its extension and claimed format, exposing mislabeled or renamed files.
example_prompt: Is this really an MP3 or just a renamed file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: magic-byte + container-header inspection on the file bytes, no decoding or server
rationale: Renamed extensions silently break import pipelines; a real-format check catches the mismatch immediately.

name: random-bytes
description: Generate cryptographically secure random bytes as hex, Base64, or a byte array.
example_prompt: give me 32 random bytes as base64
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM via getrandom (browser crypto). — via getrandom crate
rationale: Generating keys/nonces/salts is a frequent dev need not served by password/uuid generators.

name: csv-to-geojson
description: Convert a CSV/JSON table with latitude/longitude columns into GeoJSON points (and back).
example_prompt: Turn this CSV of store locations into GeoJSON
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM transform; offline.
rationale: Standard GIS plumbing step with no existing tool.

name: likert-summary
description: Summarize Likert-scale survey responses with per-item means, distributions, and stacked bars.
example_prompt: Summarize this agree/disagree survey data
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM aggregation plus chart rendering, offline.
rationale: Researchers and PMs analyze Likert surveys often, distinct from generic descriptive stats.

name: diff-highlight
description: Render a unified diff or two texts as a polished, syntax-highlighted side-by-side image for sharing in PRs and chats.
example_prompt: make a shareable image of the diff between these two snippets
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM diff + styled render; local. — via similar crate
rationale: Pretty diff screenshots are popular for reviews and social; text-diff only outputs the textual diff.

name: images-to-animated-webp
description: Combine a set of images into a single animated WebP, far smaller than an equivalent GIF.
example_prompt: make an animated webp from these 12 frames at 10fps
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg/libwebp encoding, already wired; local.
rationale: Animated WebP is the modern sticker/animation format; existing tools only do video-to-webp, not frames-to-webp.

name: data-smooth
description: Smooth a numeric series with a moving average, median filter, or exponential smoothing and plot it.
example_prompt: Smooth this noisy daily-sales column with a 7-day moving average
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust windowed math + plot rendering in-browser.
rationale: Common pre-charting step distinct from full Holt-Winters forecasting.

name: env-var-reference-extractor
description: Finds all environment-variable references ($VAR, ${VAR}, %VAR%) used in shell scripts, Dockerfiles, or configs.
example_prompt: List every environment variable this shell script reads.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; regex scan for the three reference syntaxes, runs in-browser.
rationale: Knowing which env vars a script depends on is essential for writing .env templates and deployment docs.

name: hand-landmark-extractor
description: Detects hands and extracts 21 keypoints per hand as JSON for gesture/sign analysis.
example_prompt: Find the hand keypoints in this photo
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime: a MediaPipe-style hand-landmark model runs inference in-browser on the decoded image. — model opencv/handpose_estimation_mediapipe
rationale: Sign-language, gesture, and HCI projects need per-finger keypoints, a parse no existing tool offers.

name: bpm-key-tag-reader
description: Reads stored tempo and musical-key metadata (TBPM, TKEY, initialkey, and DJ-software variants) from a track's tags.
example_prompt: Show me the BPM and key tags saved in these files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pulls specific tag frames across formats and normalizes the values, no audio decode. — via lofty crate
rationale: DJs and producers rely on stored BPM/key tags, but they live in different frames per format and are easy to lose.

name: flac-picture-extractor

name: geojson-coords-to-csv

name: obj-vertices-to-csv
description: Extracts vertex (v) coordinates from a Wavefront OBJ file into an x,y,z CSV.
example_prompt: Pull the vertices out of this OBJ into CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; line-oriented text parse, no network

name: stl-vertices-to-csv
description: Parses ASCII or binary STL meshes into a CSV of triangle vertex coordinates.
example_prompt: Convert this STL into a CSV of vertices
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; binary and text parsing, fully local

name: video-captions-animated
description: Transcribe speech and burn word-by-word highlighted captions (TikTok/CapCut style) into a video.

name: image-difference-blend

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM does abs(A−B) per channel and re-encodes in-browser
rationale: Difference-blend is the editor's go-to for spotting and aligning duplicate layers.

name: image-cluster-by-similarity
description: Groups a batch of images into visual-similarity clusters and outputs the grouping for organizing or culling.
example_prompt: Group these screenshots into clusters of similar-looking ones
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM hashes images and runs agglomerative clustering locally
rationale: Auto-grouping turns a messy image dump into reviewable sets without any upload.

name: audio-ab-loudness-diff
description: Measures integrated LUFS, true-peak, and RMS for two files and reports the deltas plus the exact gain needed to match them.
example_prompt: Compare the loudness of master_v1.wav and master_v2.wav

rationale: Comparing two masters' loudness is a constant mastering task; single-file meters can't answer 'which is louder and by how much'.

name: json-patch-generate
description: Generates an RFC 6902 JSON Patch describing how to transform the first JSON document into the second.
example_prompt: Generate a JSON Patch from this old object to this new one
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — structural diff emitting add/remove/replace ops, fully local
rationale: Producing a portable patch document is a precise need for APIs and state sync that no generic diff covers.

name: unified-diff-reverse
description: Reverse-applies a unified diff to undo a change or invert hunks for a revert patch.
example_prompt: Reverse this patch so I can undo it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: invert hunk direction then splice, fully local.

name: convert-to-srgb
description: Converts an image with an embedded ICC profile (e.g., Display P3, Adobe RGB) into plain sRGB for consistent web display.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: apply the ICC→sRGB color transform (lcms-style) to each pixel and strip the profile, all local. — via qcms crate

name: audio-lowpass-filter
description: Applies a low-pass filter at a chosen cutoff to tame harsh high-frequency hiss and fizz.
example_prompt: Cut everything above 15 kHz on this track
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg lowpass filter; deterministic, client-side wasm
rationale: Low-pass filtering quickly removes brittle top-end noise without re-recording.

name: audio-bandpass-filter
description: Keeps only a chosen frequency band, removing content above and below it (e.g. telephone/voice band).
example_prompt: Make this sound like an old telephone, 300 Hz to 3 kHz only
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg bandpass filter runs fully in wasm
rationale: Band-limiting is useful for radio/phone effects and for isolating a voice band before analysis.

name: audio-pad-silence
description: Adds a chosen length of silence to the start and/or end of a clip.
example_prompt: Add 2 seconds of silence before this jingle
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg adelay/apad filters; generates silence in wasm

name: audio-voice-suppress
description: Suppresses non-speech background noise on voice recordings using an RNNoise-style speech model.

loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime RNNoise model runs entirely in-browser; speech-tuned, distinct from spectral denoise — model niobures/RNNoise
rationale: Real-time-style voice noise suppression beats generic denoise on speech-over-noise recordings.

name: csv-ragged-row-padder
description: Repairs CSVs where rows have inconsistent field counts by padding short rows with empties and truncating or flagging over-long rows to a uniform width.

name: fiscal-quarter-mapper
description: Maps a date column to fiscal quarter and fiscal year labels given a configurable fiscal-year start month (e.g. April or October).

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: date parsing plus modular month arithmetic, computed in-browser.
rationale: Finance reporting groups by fiscal periods that don't match calendar quarters, and no tool handles the configurable FY-start mapping.

name: toml-to-csv

name: json-pick-fields
description: Keeps only the specified keys from a JSON object (or each object in an array), dropping the rest.
example_prompt: from this JSON keep only id, name and email for each record
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM projects the named paths from the parsed structure locally
rationale: Trimming a fat API response down to the fields you need is a constant data-prep step.

name: json-omit-fields

example_prompt: drop the password and token fields from this JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM deletes the named paths from the parsed structure in-browser
rationale: Scrubbing sensitive or irrelevant keys before sharing a payload is a frequent, sensitive task best done locally.

name: json-trim-strings
description: Trims leading/trailing whitespace from every string value in a JSON document.
example_prompt: trim whitespace off all the string values in this JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM walks the tree and trims string leaves before re-serializing
rationale: Scraped or form-imported JSON is riddled with padded strings that break exact-match lookups.

name: linear-interpolate-gaps
description: Linearly interpolates missing values between known points in an ordered numeric series, with optional max-gap limit.
example_prompt: Interpolate the gaps in this time series of readings
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: segment-wise linear fill, all in-browser
rationale: Gap interpolation is the standard fix for sampled-signal holes and differs from the existing gap-finder that only locates them.

name: accent-stripper
description: Removes diacritics and transliterates accented letters to their closest plain ASCII forms.
example_prompt: Strip the accents from these names so they're plain ASCII
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM NFD decomposition then combining-mark removal; no network — via unicode-normalization crate
rationale: ASCII-only systems (slugs, legacy DBs, sort keys) need accent folding and doing it by hand is error-prone.

name: camera-settings-extractor
description: Surfaces just the exposure triangle and lens data (shutter, aperture, ISO, focal length, flash) in a readable summary.
example_prompt: What camera settings were used for this shot?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM reads the relevant EXIF tags and formats them locally without touching the pixel data. — via kamadak-exif crate
rationale: Photographers studying a shot want the settings cleanly, not a 200-tag EXIF dump.

name: metadata-privacy-scanner
description: Flags privacy-sensitive metadata present in an image — GPS location, device serial numbers, owner name, timestamps.

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM enumerates EXIF/IPTC/XMP fields and matches them against a sensitivity ruleset locally. — via kamadak-exif crate
rationale: People sharing photos online need a quick read on what personal data they're inadvertently publishing.

name: text-encoding-detector
description: Heuristically detects a file's character encoding (UTF-8, UTF-16, Latin-1, Windows-1252) and BOM, flagging decode errors.
example_prompt: What encoding is this text file in?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: BOM checks and byte-pattern heuristics analyze the raw bytes locally — via chardetng crate
rationale: Mojibake from wrong-encoding files is common and identifying the true charset fixes it fast.

name: stack-trace-analyzer
description: Parses a multi-language stack trace into frames, identifies the root exception, and highlights user vs framework code.
example_prompt: Break down this stack trace and find the likely root cause
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: stack-trace formats are regex-parseable text processed locally with no service — via regex crate
rationale: Reading a deep stack trace to separate app code from library noise speeds up debugging.

name: html-outline-analyzer
description: Extracts the heading outline (H1–H6 hierarchy) and element/tag counts from an HTML document.
example_prompt: show the heading outline of this HTML page
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML parser; DOM walked in memory, no rendering needed — via scraper crate
rationale: Checking document structure and heading hierarchy is core to SEO and accessibility review.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — serde_json parse plus a filter/JSONPath evaluator, all in-memory like an embedded NoSQL store. — via serde_json crate
rationale: Mirrors unqlite's embedded document-store use case, letting users query JSON collections without any backend.

name: geojson-wkt
description: Convert geometries between GeoJSON and WKT/WKB in either direction.
example_prompt: Convert this GeoJSON polygon to WKT
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via georust/geo + wkt — format translation only, no server. — via wkt crate
rationale: WKT↔GeoJSON bridging is needed constantly between databases and map libraries.

name: geojson-query
description: Filter and aggregate GeoJSON features with a simple SQL-like spatial query (bbox, contains, property filters).

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via georust/geo + a small query parser — in-memory feature scan, no DB server. — via geo crate
rationale: A lightweight spatial-SQL filter brings sedona-db-style querying to a single file with zero setup.

name: webhook-signature-generator

name: rust-content-summarizer

rationale: Fast, classic denoise for grainy scans and low-light shots.

name: image-concat

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: size the combined canvas and blit each source in order. — via image crate

rationale: The inverse of JSONL export is needed whenever a tool only accepts a single array.

description: Runs object detection across sampled frames and reports which objects appear and when.
example_prompt: What objects appear in this video and at what times?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg extracts frames, onnx-runtime runs a YOLO-class model fully in-browser with no API call. — model Xenova/yolos-tiny
rationale: An object timeline enables content search and auto-tagging of footage entirely on the user's device.

name: mel-spectrogram-generator
description: Produces a mel-scaled spectrogram PNG matching the front-end most ML audio models expect.
example_prompt: Show me the mel spectrogram of this clip
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: rustfft STFT plus a mel filterbank, rendered to PNG locally — via rustfft crate
rationale: Mel spectrograms are the standard perceptual view for speech/music and a precursor for debugging ML pipelines.

name: audio-feature-csv-exporter
description: Exports frame-level audio features (RMS, centroid, ZCR, rolloff, flatness) to a CSV for analysis.
example_prompt: Export per-frame audio features of this file as CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes the feature set per frame and writes CSV entirely client-side — via rustfft crate
rationale: A tidy feature CSV lets users do their own plotting and ML without any audio-DSP setup.

name: stata-dta-to-csv
description: Reads Stata .dta datasets (with value labels and variable labels) into CSV.
example_prompt: Convert this Stata .dta file to CSV
loader_feasibility: pyodide running pandas.read_stata; the whole interpreter and file stay in the browser sandbox.
rationale: Stata files are common in economics/social-science and unreadable without expensive proprietary software.

name: hdf5-to-csv
description: Lists and exports datasets from an HDF5 (.h5) file into CSV tables.
example_prompt: Export the datasets in this .h5 file to CSV
loader_feasibility: pyodide with h5py/pandas reading the file in-memory; no server, decoding stays in WASM.
rationale: HDF5 is the standard scientific bulk-data container and there's no easy way to browse it without code.

name: fasta-to-csv
description: Parses FASTA sequence files into a CSV of id, description, sequence, and length.
example_prompt: Convert this proteins.fasta into a CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM streaming FASTA parser; pure text processing, no server.
rationale: Bioinformatics FASTA files need tabular form for filtering/joins and the parsing edge cases trip people up.

name: dependency-risk-auditor
description: Audits a package.json or lockfile for risky patterns like wildcard versions, git/url deps, and install scripts.
example_prompt: Audit this package.json for supply-chain risks
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies heuristic rules over the parsed manifest; deterministic static analysis runs entirely client-side.
rationale: vet targets supply-chain risk, and a local heuristic auditor gives a fast first pass without sending manifests off-machine.

name: docstring-stub-generator
description: Generates docstring/JSDoc stubs (params, returns, raises) from a pasted function signature.
example_prompt: Generate a Google-style docstring stub for this Python function
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: signature parsing and template emission, fully local.
rationale: Documenting functions is tedious and the param/return scaffolding is mechanical.

name: ascii-table-generator
description: Renders data into a box-drawn ASCII/Unicode table suitable for terminals, READMEs, and code comments.
example_prompt: Render this data as a Unicode box table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: computes column widths and draws border characters as text.
rationale: Pretty terminal-style tables in docs and comments are surprisingly fiddly to produce manually.

name: gantt-mermaid-generator
description: Builds a Mermaid Gantt chart from tasks with start dates, durations, and dependencies.
example_prompt: Generate a Mermaid Gantt chart for this project plan with dependencies
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — date math and Mermaid syntax emission; rendering is handled by the chat UI.
rationale: Project task lists frequently need a timeline view that the CLI tools cannot produce.

name: focus-picker
description: Selects the single most important task from a list by priority, due date, and effort, with a brief justification.
example_prompt: Out of these tasks, what's the one thing I should do right now?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — scoring and ranking over parsed task attributes.
rationale: Directly delivers omm's 'one thing on my mind' philosophy of forcing a single focus.

name: tasks-to-ical
description: Converts dated tasks (todo.txt due:/t: tags) into an importable iCalendar (.ics) feed of VTODO/VEVENT entries.
example_prompt: Export the dated tasks in this todo.txt as an .ics file I can import into my calendar
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — emits RFC 5545 text; no server, just string assembly.
rationale: Bridges CLI todo files into mainstream calendars, a frequently requested but rarely available export.

name: csv-table-aligner
description: Renders CSV/TSV as a cleanly aligned table with column selection and width control.
example_prompt: Show this CSV as an aligned table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSV parsing and column layout, no network
rationale: Making raw delimited data readable is a constant data-wrangling need.

name: ts-type-strip
description: Strips TypeScript type annotations to produce runnable JavaScript.
example_prompt: Strip the types from this TypeScript so it's plain JS.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using an SWC-style parser that erases types; deterministic, offline. — via swc_ecma_parser crate
rationale: Type-stripping is the exact transform Node now uses and a frequent quick conversion need.

name: video-keyframe-timestamp-list
description: Parses the video and outputs the exact timestamps of all I-frames (keyframes) as a text/CSV/JSON list for precise seeking and cut planning.
example_prompt: List all the keyframe timestamps in this MP4 so I know where I can cut losslessly
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader (ffprobe -show_frames / -skip_frame nokey) reads frame metadata directly in the wasm build with no decode of pixel data, fully client-side.
rationale: Lossless cutting and seeking both require knowing keyframe boundaries, and there's no easy way to get them without a tool.

name: video-audio-language-detector
description: Samples the audio and detects the spoken language (and per-track language for multi-track files).
example_prompt: What language is spoken in this video's audio?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg extracts an audio sample; transformers-js (Whisper language ID) classifies it client-side. — model Xenova/whisper-tiny
rationale: Mislabeled or unlabeled audio tracks are common in rips, and knowing the language drives subtitle and routing decisions.

name: k8s-manifest-splitter
description: Splits a multi-document Kubernetes YAML into individual resources indexed by kind and name.
example_prompt: Split this multi-doc Kubernetes YAML into separate resources.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM splits on YAML document markers and parses each manifest locally.
rationale: Big bundled manifests are hard to navigate; a per-resource breakdown speeds review and extraction.

name: csv-numeric-column-extractor
description: Parses a CSV/TSV, detects which columns are fully numeric, and returns those columns as typed arrays with their headers.
example_prompt: From this CSV, give me just the numeric columns as arrays
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — delimiter parsing and per-column type inference, no I/O.
rationale: Isolating the numeric columns is the common first step before any quantitative CSV work.

name: pdf-annotations-extract
description: Collects all comments, highlights, and sticky-note annotations from a PDF with their page numbers and authors.
example_prompt: Give me every comment and highlight in this reviewed PDF
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM iterates each page's /Annots array and decodes markup annotations locally — via lopdf crate
rationale: Reviewers need a flat list of feedback instead of scrolling the whole document.

name: json-to-ddl
description: Infers a table schema from a JSON or CSV sample and generates CREATE TABLE plus INSERT statements.
example_prompt: Generate a CREATE TABLE and inserts from this JSON array of records
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM does type inference and emits SQL text in memory with no server round-trip.
rationale: Bootstrapping a schema from sample data is a universal first step when adopting any SQL store and is trivially local.

name: camera-serial-leak-checker
description: Detects camera body and lens serial numbers embedded in EXIF/MakerNotes that can deanonymize a photographer across uploads.
example_prompt: Does this RAW-derived JPEG leak my camera's serial number?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses EXIF and known MakerNote serial tags in-memory. — via kamadak-exif crate
rationale: Serial numbers are an under-appreciated cross-photo fingerprint that survives most basic scrubbing.

name: jwt-weakness-checker
description: Flags JWT security issues such as alg:none, weak/guessable HMAC secrets, and missing expiry.
example_prompt: Is this JWT misconfigured or signed with a weak secret? <paste token>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — claim inspection plus a small bundled wordlist for HMAC secret testing; all computed locally.
rationale: Maps the authoscope/credential-testing demand into a defensive JWT audit that runs without exposing the token.

name: kanban-board-builder
description: Turns a task list or freeform notes into a structured kanban board with columns in markdown or JSON.
example_prompt: Organize these tasks into a kanban board: design API, write tests, ship docs...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — text parsing and structured formatting, entirely local.
rationale: Maps rust_kanban into a lightweight planning aid that fits naturally into a chat-driven workflow.

name: rust-module-map
description: Parses pasted Rust source (or a lib.rs/main.rs) and renders the mod/struct/fn hierarchy as an indented module tree or Mermaid graph.
example_prompt: Show me the module tree for this Rust file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with a syn-based parser; AST walking over pasted text runs fully client-side — via syn crate
rationale: cargo-modules' value is understanding unfamiliar crate structure, and that only needs the source the user already has.

name: onnx-model-runner
description: Runs an ONNX model you upload on your own input and returns the outputs, all on-device.
example_prompt: Run this ONNX classifier on my input vector.
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime web backend executes the model graph in WASM/WebGPU client-side.
rationale: Letting users run arbitrary small ONNX models privately in the browser unlocks custom-model workflows.

name: pcm-sample-extractor
description: Extracts raw PCM amplitude samples from an audio file as CSV or JSON for analysis or plotting.
example_prompt: Export the PCM samples of this WAV as CSV.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (hound/Symphonia) decodes the file to samples in-runtime. — via symphonia crate
rationale: Feed real audio data into spreadsheets or DSP experiments locally.

name: brotli-decompress
description: Decodes a Brotli-compressed (.br) blob back to its original bytes or text.
example_prompt: Decompress this .br file so I can read the JSON inside
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the brotli decoder is pure Rust and runs client-side, so the file never leaves the browser. — via brotli crate
rationale: Users frequently receive Brotli-encoded payloads (HTTP bodies, asset bundles) and need to inspect them locally.

name: zstd-decompress
description: Decompresses a Zstandard (.zst) blob back to the original bytes or text.
example_prompt: Decompress this .zst archive in the browser
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: zstd-rs's decoder is pure Rust and executes entirely in the browser. — via ruzstd crate
rationale: Zstd files are increasingly common and a private local decoder fills a real gap.

name: gpu-matrix-multiply
description: Multiplies large matrices on the GPU for far higher throughput than CPU on big inputs.
example_prompt: Multiply these two 1024x1024 matrices using the GPU
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute: a WGSL matmul shader (the arrayfire/emu GPU-tensor role) runs on the browser's WebGPU device with no server.
rationale: Large dense matrix multiplies dominate ML and simulation workloads and GPU acceleration makes them practical in-browser.

name: scryptenc-file
description: Encrypts and decrypts data in the scrypt encrypted-data format compatible with the scrypt CLI tool.
example_prompt: open this .enc file made with the scrypt command
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via sorairolake/scryptenc-rs, which reads/writes the standard scrypt header format entirely in-browser. — via scryptenc crate
rationale: Files made by the widely-used `scrypt` CLI need a decryptor, and doing it client-side keeps the protected data private.

name: eth-address-from-key
description: Derives an Ethereum address and EIP-55 checksum form from a secp256k1 private or public key.
example_prompt: what's the ethereum address for this private key?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM combining secp256k1 point math (ecc-rs/k256) with tiny-keccak's keccak256, both wasm32-ready and offline. — via k256 crate
rationale: Mapping a key to its checksummed address is constant Web3 work and revealing a private key to a website is never acceptable.

name: elasticsearch-mapping-generator
description: Infers an Elasticsearch index mapping from a sample JSON document.
example_prompt: generate an Elasticsearch mapping for {"title":"hi","views":10,"tags":["a"]}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM: type inference over the sample JSON, runs in the browser.
rationale: Bootstrapping a mapping from a representative document saves manual type-by-type definition.

name: line-protocol-csv-converter
description: Converts between InfluxDB line protocol and CSV for inspection or bulk import.
example_prompt: convert this InfluxDB line protocol to CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM: pure parse/serialize in both directions.
rationale: Moving time-series data between CSV tools and InfluxDB requires reformatting that is tedious by hand.

name: bson-extended-json-converter
description: Converts MongoDB Extended JSON (with $oid, $date, $numberLong) to and from plain JSON.
example_prompt: convert this MongoDB extended JSON to plain: {"_id":{"$oid":"507f1f77bcf86cd799439011"}}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM: pure JSON transformation, no DB.
rationale: mongoexport output and driver results use Extended JSON that needs flattening for other tools.

name: pdf-resize-pages
description: Changes page size (e.g., A4 to US Letter) and scales content to fit.
example_prompt: Resize this PDF from A4 to US Letter
loader_feasibility: pyodide — pypdf scales each page's media box and content to the target dimensions in-browser. — via lopdf crate
rationale: Cross-region printing constantly requires page-size conversion that desktop tools hide behind menus.

name: json-assertion-runner
description: Runs declarative assertions (JSONPath equals/exists/type/range) against a JSON payload and reports pass/fail.
example_prompt: Assert that $.user.age is a number greater than 18 in this payload
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (jsonpath + rules) — local evaluation — via serde_json_path crate
rationale: This is the most direct mapping of 'automated validation test op' to a reusable browser tool.

name: music-file-renamer
description: Generates a consistent rename/move plan from each file's tags using a chosen pattern like {artist}/{album}/{track} {title}.
example_prompt: Rename these mp3s as Artist - Album - 01 Title based on their tags
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: reads tags and builds the new filenames as text; the user applies the plan, so no filesystem access is required. — via lofty crate
rationale: Pattern-based renaming from tags is the core of beets and the most common library-tidying request.

name: itunes-library-parser
description: Parses an iTunes/Music Library.xml and exports playlists and track metadata as CSV, JSON, or M3U.
example_prompt: Export my playlists from this iTunes Library.xml as m3u files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the library is a local plist XML file parsed entirely in the sandbox. — via plist crate
rationale: itunes-remote users migrating off Apple Music need their playlists and metadata in portable formats.

name: irc-log-parser
description: Parses raw IRC/WeeChat/irssi logs into a structured, readable timeline.
example_prompt: Clean up this weechat log into a readable conversation
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM regex-parses the log format locally; no IRC connection required.
rationale: Turns the un-deployable IRC-client demand into a genuinely local log-cleaning tool.

name: iam-policy-linter
description: Validates AWS IAM policy JSON and flags overly-permissive patterns like Action/Resource wildcards and NotAction.
example_prompt: Check this IAM policy for security problems
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses the JSON and applies rule checks fully in-browser, so sensitive policies never leave the machine. — via serde_json crate
rationale: AWS shell users (SAWS) write IAM policies often, and catching wildcard over-permissioning locally is a genuine security win.

name: red-eye-checker
description: Detects red-eye regions in portrait photos and reports their locations for correction.
example_prompt: Does anyone have red-eye in this flash photo?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes and runs a redness/eye-shape heuristic on candidate regions — fully local. — via image crate
rationale: Red-eye is a common flash artifact, and flagging it lets users fix portraits before sharing or printing.

name: jsonpath-validate
description: Validates JSONPath expression syntax and dry-runs it against a sample document, returning the matched nodes.
example_prompt: Is this JSONPath valid and what does it match here?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using a jsonpath crate; offline
rationale: JSONPath syntax varies by dialect and confirming a query both parses and matches is a common need.

name: openapi-to-curl
description: Generates example curl requests with sample params and bodies for every endpoint in an OpenAPI/Swagger spec.
example_prompt: Give me curl examples for each endpoint in this OpenAPI spec
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the JSON/YAML spec and synthesizes request examples offline. — via openapiv3 crate
rationale: API-client TUIs like ATAC import OpenAPI, and runnable examples from a spec speed up API exploration.

name: issue-export-reporter
description: Parses a Jira or Linear CSV export into a status breakdown, cycle-time, and simple velocity/burndown summary.
example_prompt: Summarize this Linear CSV export — status counts and average cycle time
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — CSV parsing and aggregation run client-side, with no API tokens leaving the browser. — via csv crate
rationale: fjira and linear-tui imply reporting needs; working from exports gives the analytics without API access or credentials.

name: ics-agenda-view
description: Groups parsed calendar events by day into a tidy agenda with free-gap detection between meetings.
example_prompt: Turn this .ics export into a day-by-day agenda and show my free gaps
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sorting and gap computation over parsed events, fully local. — via ical crate
rationale: calcurse's core view is a daily agenda, and gap-finding is what people actually want before booking.

name: portfolio-pnl
description: Calculates profit/loss per position and overall from entry prices and current prices you provide.
example_prompt: Compute my P&L: bought 2 ETH at 1800, now 2400; 0.5 BTC at 30000, now 41000
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — arithmetic on user-supplied prices; no exchange API and thus no server.
rationale: ticker/cointop users constantly check gains, and the calculation works on pasted prices even without live data access.

name: jmespath-query
description: Filters and reshapes a pasted JSON document using a JMESPath expression.
example_prompt: Run JMESPath `people[?age > `30`].name` on this JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the jmespath crate compiles to wasm32 and evaluates expressions over in-memory JSON locally.
rationale: jp brings demand for JMESPath specifically, and it's the query language baked into AWS CLI so users already know it.

name: yaml-query
description: Reads, filters, and transforms YAML with jq-style expressions and converts between YAML and JSON.
example_prompt: Get `.services.web.ports` from this docker-compose YAML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: serde_yaml plus a pure-Rust jq engine (jaq) handle parsing and querying with no server. — via jaq-core crate
rationale: yq and yaml-cli reflect strong demand for querying YAML configs (Kubernetes, CI, compose) directly from chat.

name: config-file-validator
description: Validates the syntax of pasted JSON, YAML, TOML, INI, or XML config files and reports errors with line and column numbers.
example_prompt: is this YAML valid? <paste config>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM bundling serde_json/serde_yaml/toml/quick-xml parsers; all parsing runs in-memory client-side. — via quick-xml crate
rationale: One unified validator across the five formats people actually keep config in saves hunting for format-specific online linters.

name: prefix-suffix-lines
description: Adds a chosen prefix and/or suffix to every non-empty line, useful for quoting, bulleting, or wrapping each line.
example_prompt: Put a '- ' in front of every line and a ',' after
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM per-line string concatenation; runs locally
rationale: Wrapping each line with fixed text (for SQL IN-lists, bullets, quoting) is a constant micro-task with no clean editor path.

name: repeated-word-remover
description: Finds and removes accidental doubled words (e.g. 'the the', 'is is') while ignoring legitimate repeats like 'had had'.
example_prompt: Find any accidentally repeated words in this draft and remove them
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM adjacent-token comparison with a small allow-list; client-side
rationale: Duplicated words are an extremely common typo that spellcheckers miss and that's hard to spot when proofreading.

name: video-rounded-corners
description: Rounds the corners of a video frame to a given radius, producing a card-style clip with transparent or colored corners.
example_prompt: Give this video rounded corners with a 40px radius
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's geq/alphamerge corner mask runs in ffmpeg.wasm; output to a format that supports alpha or a solid backing.
rationale: Rounded-corner clips are ubiquitous in modern UI mockups, app demos, and social embeds.

name: video-dedup-frames
description: Drops consecutive duplicate frames from a video (e.g. screen recordings) to shrink size and clean timing.
example_prompt: Remove the duplicate frames from this screen recording
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's mpdecimate filter detects and drops duplicates in ffmpeg.wasm, fully local.
rationale: Screen captures and slideshow exports are full of repeated frames that waste bytes and confuse editors.

name: video-aspect-ratio-fix
description: Sets the correct display aspect ratio (DAR) tag on a video whose stored aspect metadata is wrong.
example_prompt: This video plays at the wrong aspect ratio — set it to 16:9
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's setdar/setsar with stream copy runs in ffmpeg.wasm, a metadata-only local rewrite.
rationale: Mistagged DAR makes footage look squished or stretched without any pixel problem, and the tag fix is instant.

name: audio-bit-depth-converter
description: Changes PCM bit depth (e.g. 24-bit to 16-bit) with proper dithering on down-conversion.
example_prompt: Convert this 24-bit WAV to dithered 16-bit.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg format/aformat with dither; pure local DSP. — via hound crate
rationale: Correct dithered bit-depth reduction is needed for CD/delivery masters and is easy to get wrong manually.

name: audio-click-remover
description: Removes clicks, pops, and crackle (vinyl or mouth clicks) from audio.
example_prompt: Get rid of the crackle in this digitized vinyl rip.
loader_feasibility: pyodide scipy detects transient outliers and interpolates them out, fully local. — via hound crate
rationale: Declicking is the key restoration step for vinyl/cassette and speech, complementing the existing click detector.

name: csv-to-html-table
description: Renders CSV as a clean, escaped HTML `<table>` with a header row.
example_prompt: make an HTML table from this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parse + HTML escaping/templating; produces a string, no server — via csv crate
rationale: Quick way to drop tabular data into a webpage or email without a build step.

name: toml-formatter
description: Parses and re-emits TOML with normalized spacing, table ordering, and consistent quoting.
example_prompt: format this Cargo.toml fragment nicely
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the toml crate; serialization is local and dependency-free at runtime.
rationale: Config files like Cargo.toml and pyproject.toml benefit from canonical formatting that no current tool provides.

name: url-normalizer
description: Normalizes a URL by lowercasing the host, removing default ports, resolving dot-segments, and sorting query keys.
example_prompt: Normalize this URL to a canonical form
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM URL parse + canonicalize; deterministic, no network — via url crate
rationale: Canonical URLs are needed to dedupe and compare links reliably.

name: toggle-line-comments
description: Comments or uncomments a block of code using the correct line-comment syntax for the language.
example_prompt: comment out this whole block of python code
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM prefixes/removes the language's line-comment token on each line locally
rationale: Bulk comment toggling outside an editor (e.g. on pasted snippets) is otherwise line-by-line tedium.

name: seasonal-difference
description: Computes lag-k (seasonal) differencing of a series, subtracting each value from the one k steps earlier.
example_prompt: Seasonally difference this monthly series with lag 12
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: indexed subtraction pass, pure numeric
rationale: Lag-k differencing removes seasonality and is distinct from the existing first-difference (lag-1) tool.

name: midi-chord-progression-generator
description: Converts a chord-symbol progression (e.g., 'C G Am F') into a MIDI file with voiced chords and timing.
example_prompt: Turn ii-V-I in F major into a MIDI chord progression
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses chord symbols to note sets and writes a MIDI file with bar timing, client-side. — via midly crate
rationale: Songwriters scaffold tracks fast from a chord chart, and MIDI export beats manually placing notes.

name: mp3-to-m4r
description: Converts an MP3 into an iPhone ringtone (.m4r), re-encoding to AAC and trimming to the ringtone length.
example_prompt: turn this mp3 into an iphone ringtone
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader decodes MP3 and encodes AAC into an m4r container in wasm.
rationale: Making a ringtone from a favorite MP3 is a frequent ask blocked by Apple's m4r-only requirement.

name: ip-address-validate
description: Validates IPv4 and IPv6 address syntax, canonicalizes the form, and classifies it (private, loopback, link-local, multicast, documentation).
example_prompt: Is 2001:0db8::1 a valid IPv6 address and what type is it?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM address parsing and classification; offline.
rationale: IPv6 canonicalization and special-range classification are error-prone and useful when debugging configs.

name: zod-to-json-schema
description: Parses a Zod schema definition and emits the equivalent JSON Schema for documentation and interop.
example_prompt: Convert this Zod schema to JSON Schema
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses the Zod expression structurally and renders JSON Schema in-memory.
rationale: Exposing Zod-validated shapes to non-TS consumers requires a standard JSON Schema.

name: xliff-to-json
description: Extracts translation units from an XLIFF file into a flat JSON of source/target pairs by id.
example_prompt: Convert this XLIFF file to JSON key-value pairs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: XLIFF is XML and parses to JSON entirely within the sandbox. — via quick-xml crate
rationale: XLIFF from translation vendors needs flattening to JSON for app i18n bundles.

name: cmyk-jpeg-to-rgb
description: Converts CMYK (often Adobe) JPEGs into standard RGB JPEG/PNG.
example_prompt: This jpg looks inverted/wrong — convert it from CMYK to RGB
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg/Rust image crate handles CMYK + APP14 transform in WASM
rationale: CMYK JPEGs from print workflows display with wrong colors in browsers and need conversion.

name: percentile-rank-calculator
description: Reports the percentile rank of one or more values within a reference dataset, letting you compare where values fall.
example_prompt: What percentile is a score of 82 in this dataset?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: sorted-position lookup over array, runs locally.
rationale: Turns a raw value into a comparable standing within a population, a frequent real-world question.

name: xml-diff
description: Diffs two XML documents by element path and attribute, ignoring insignificant whitespace and attribute ordering.
example_prompt: Compare these two XML feeds and list the element-level differences
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse with an XML reader and compare node trees in-process — via roxmltree crate
rationale: XML configs and feeds need structure-aware comparison that text diff cannot provide cleanly.

name: percent-decimal-converter
description: Converts a column between percentage strings (12.5%) and decimal fractions (0.125) in either direction.
example_prompt: Convert this percentage column to decimals
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse + ×/÷100, fully local
rationale: Percent-vs-decimal mismatches silently corrupt analyses and bulk conversion is fiddly in spreadsheets.

name: color-code-extractor
description: Extracts all hex, rgb(a), and hsl(a) color values from CSS or text and builds a deduplicated palette.
example_prompt: List all the colors used in this stylesheet
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: regex scan plus color normalization, no rendering or server.
rationale: Auditing the real color palette of a stylesheet is a frequent design/cleanup task.

name: css-px-to-rem
description: Converts px length values in CSS to rem against a configurable root font size.
example_prompt: Convert the px values in this CSS to rem using a 16px base
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM regex+arithmetic over declarations; no network involved.
rationale: Switching a stylesheet to scalable rem units by hand is repetitive and easy to get wrong.

name: svg-to-data-uri
description: Encodes an SVG into a URL-escaped or base64 data URI for inline CSS/HTML use.

name: sentence-length-stats

name: particle-overlay-video

name: film-grain-overlay-generator
description: Generates a standalone semi-transparent film-grain overlay clip to composite over footage for an analog look.

name: k8s-manifest-scaffold
description: Scaffolds a Kubernetes Deployment plus Service manifest from image, port, replicas, and resource limits.

name: video-keyframe-extractor
description: Extracts only the video's keyframes (I-frames) as individual images for quick visual inspection.

name: video-duration-validator

name: typescript-interface-from-json

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses JSON and prints TS type syntax; pure transformation, fully local. — via serde_json crate
rationale: A staple of front-end work that developers repeatedly do by hand from API payloads.

name: still-to-clip
description: Turns a single still image into a fixed-duration static video clip at a chosen resolution and frame rate.

loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's image-loop input renders the still to a timed clip entirely within the wasm runtime.

name: video-to-mxf
description: Wraps a video into an MXF container with broadcast-compatible codecs for professional delivery specs.

loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm supports the MXF muxer and pro codecs, producing the deliverable container locally.
rationale: Broadcasters mandate MXF deliverables, and a browser-local wrapper avoids expensive desktop transcoders.

name: docker-compose-generator

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — composes YAML from service templates and a dependency graph, no Docker needed.
rationale: Compose files are verbose and indentation-sensitive; a generator yields a runnable stack quickly.

name: markdown-link-check
description: Checks Markdown for malformed link syntax, broken in-document anchor references, and duplicate reference definitions.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM that parses links and resolves anchors within the document; no network fetch. — via pulldown-cmark crate

name: json-to-toml
description: Serializes a JSON object into valid TOML, ordering tables and arrays correctly.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via serde_json + toml; serialization is fully local. — via toml crate
rationale: Completes TOML round-tripping for config authoring without a server.

name: bibtex-to-csv
description: Convert a BibTeX bibliography into a CSV of references (author, title, year, etc.).

name: image-segmenter

name: latex-compile

name: few-shot-text-classifier

name: quartiles-calculator

name: random-projection-reducer

name: corner-detect

name: stl-format-converter
description: Converts an STL mesh between binary and ASCII encodings in either direction.

name: ply-to-obj

name: child-growth-percentile

name: dna-reverse-complement

name: csr-generator

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM rcgen produces the keypair and CSR locally; the private key never leaves the device. — via x509-cert crate

name: spaced-repetition-scheduler
description: Computes the next review date for each card from its review history using the SM-2 / FSRS algorithm.
example_prompt: Given my last grades on these cards, when should I review each next?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs the SM-2/FSRS math on supplied review logs — deterministic and fully offline.
rationale: hardv/flash-tui demand; the scheduling math is the hard part of any self-study workflow.

name: duplicate-file-finder
description: Finds exact-duplicate files in a selected set by content hash and groups them.
example_prompt: Which of these files are duplicates?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: hashes each file and buckets by digest in-memory.

name: csv-view
description: Load a CSV and interactively sort, filter, and paginate it as a table.
example_prompt: show me this CSV as a sortable table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the `csv` crate parses the uploaded file and renders locally; the data never leaves the browser. — via csv crate

name: port-process-mapper
description: Parses `lsof -i`, `ss -tulpn`, or `netstat -tulpn` output into a port-to-PID-to-process table and flags port conflicts.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses pasted socket listings into a mapping table, client-side only.

name: ris-bibtex-converter

example_prompt: Convert this RIS export from the database into BibTeX.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM bidirectional field mapping over the pasted text — deterministic and local.
rationale: Reference managers export RIS while LaTeX needs BibTeX, so this lossless conversion is a constant chore the cluster's tools handle.

name: shell-script-formatter
description: Reformats and indents a shell script with consistent style (shfmt-like) for readability and diffs.
example_prompt: Format and indent this messy bash script
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses to an AST and pretty-prints; pure text transformation runs entirely in the wasmi runtime.

name: normalize-country

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM fuzzy match against an embedded ISO 3166 table; no external lookups.
rationale: Country normalization is a recurring data-cleaning pain point with a small, embeddable reference table.

name: convert-quotes

example_prompt: Convert all the single-quoted strings in this JS to double quotes.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizing/quote-aware rewriting; pure string transform.
rationale: to-single/to-double-quotes is a frequent code- and prose-cleanup task that maps cleanly to one configurable tool.

name: docker-compose-explainer
description: Parses a docker-compose.yml and summarizes services, images, ports, volumes, and networks in a readable table.
example_prompt: Explain what this docker-compose.yml sets up
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — YAML parsing and summary formatting, no Docker daemon needed. — via serde_yaml crate

name: strip-ansi
description: Removes all ANSI escape codes and control sequences from pasted text to produce clean, plain output.
example_prompt: Clean the color codes out of this log so I can paste it elsewhere <pastes text>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — regex/state-machine removal of escape bytes runs client-side.
rationale: Colored terminal captures are unusable in tickets and docs; stripping ANSI is a constant teetail/log cleanup chore.

name: file-hash-dedupe

rationale: Quick a11y feedback helps developers fix issues early without setting up a full auditing pipeline.

name: format-rust

name: harmony-format-renderer

name: bmi-calc

name: json-search

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — recursive in-memory traversal of the parsed document.

name: json-schema-to-typescript

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — schema walk emits type source text, no toolchain server

name: name-parse

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM rule-based parser; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: Name parsing is a common CRM/data-cleaning task when splitting a single name field.

name: yara-scan

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM via the pure-Rust yara-x engine; rule compilation and matching execute locally with no scanner backend.

name: route-elevation-profile
description: Plot the elevation profile of a GPX track with grade and climb segments.
example_prompt: Show the elevation profile of this GPX ride
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM GPX parse plus chart rendering, offline.
rationale: Cyclists and hikers want a profile chart beyond the GPX summary stats.

name: video-color-temperature
description: Shifts a video warmer or cooler by adjusting its color temperature in kelvin.

loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's colortemperature filter runs in ffmpeg.wasm with local white-balance math.

name: video-auto-levels
description: Automatically stretches a video's histogram per-frame to normalize contrast and color balance.
example_prompt: Auto-correct the levels on this hazy-looking video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's normalize/eq=auto histogram stretch runs in ffmpeg.wasm, fully local.
rationale: A one-click cleanup for low-contrast or color-cast footage where manual tuning is overkill.

name: env-file-diff
description: Compares two .env files and reports added, removed, and changed variables, optionally masking secret values.
example_prompt: Diff my local .env against the example .env and show what's missing
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse KEY=VALUE lines into maps and diff keys in-memory
rationale: Catching missing or drifted environment variables between files is a frequent, error-prone dev task.

name: video-frame-extract-pair
description: Extracts the matching frame from two videos at the same timestamp and saves them as a labeled side-by-side image pair.

loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM seeks and extracts a single frame from each file locally and stacks them with the hstack filter.
rationale: Pulling matched still frames is the simplest, most-requested comparison primitive for spot-checking specific moments.

name: nmf-audio-decompose
