example_prompt: Break this loop into 4 component sounds I can solo.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — non-negative matrix/tensor factorization (NIMFA/NTFLib) is iterative multiplicative-update linear algebra over the magnitude spectrogram, pure compute.
rationale: Component decomposition for sound design, de-humming, and unsupervised separation is a flexible building block with no browser equivalent.

name: timeline-anomaly-finder
description: Scans an event timeline for activity bursts, suspicious gaps, off-hours clusters, and timestamp anomalies.
example_prompt: Find unusual activity bursts and gaps in this timeline
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: histogramming and statistical clustering over event timestamps run locally with no dependencies.
rationale: Mirrors timesketch's analyzers, turning a raw timeline into leads automatically, which is the hardest part of manual review.

name: image-perceptual-diff-score
description: Returns a single 0–100 'how different do these look' score combining luminance, color, and structural deltas, ignoring imperceptible noise.
example_prompt: Give me one number for how different these two images look
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM blends SSIM + ΔE + edge metrics into one score locally
rationale: Non-experts want one human-meaningful number instead of choosing between SSIM/PSNR/ΔE.

name: passport-mrz-reader
description: Reads the machine-readable zone of a passport or ID and decodes name, document number, nationality, and dates with checksum validation.

loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime OCR-B recognition plus plain-Rust MRZ field/checksum decoding run locally — sensitive ID data never leaves the device.
rationale: MRZ parsing has a strict standard format and on-device decoding is essential for privacy with identity documents.

name: api-test-generator
description: Generates an API test workflow in Step CI or Hurl format from an OpenAPI spec or a sample curl command.
example_prompt: Generate a Step CI test for POST /login from this OpenAPI spec
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — emits the YAML/Hurl test file as text, no requests executed.
rationale: Step CI-style API testing needs boilerplate workflows that are tedious to write from scratch.

name: cors-headers-generator
description: Produces the Access-Control-* response header set for a CORS policy given allowed origins, methods, headers, and credentials.
example_prompt: Generate CORS headers allowing GET and POST from https://gizza.ai with credentials
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — derives the correct header set (including credentials caveats) by template, client-side.
rationale: CORS bugs are common and the wildcard-vs-credentials interaction is a frequent footgun a generator can guard.

name: video-color-grade
description: Applies a color LUT or brightness/contrast/saturation grade to a video.
example_prompt: Apply a warm cinematic color grade to this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader runs lut3d/eq/curves filters client-side in WASM
rationale: Color grading is a sought-after look-and-feel recipe in the ffmpeg cookbook space.

name: macro-calculator
description: Splits a daily calorie target into protein, carb, and fat grams based on a chosen diet goal or ratio.
example_prompt: Split 2200 calories into macros for a high-protein cut
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (gram/calorie arithmetic) — no external data required.
rationale: Pairs with the TDEE tool to turn a calorie goal into an actionable macro plan, a staple of fitness apps.

name: json-to-toon
description: Converts JSON into TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation), a compact indentation-based format that uses fewer LLM tokens.
example_prompt: convert this JSON to TOON to save tokens in my prompt
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM serializer implementing the TOON grammar; pure local string output.
rationale: TOON cuts token cost when passing structured data to models — directly valuable inside an AI chat app.

name: ssh-config-builder
description: Builds, or parses and explains, ~/.ssh/config host entries from connection details like host, user, port, jump host, and key.
example_prompt: Make an ssh config entry for user deploy on 10.0.0.5 port 2222 via bastion jump.example.com
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM config generation/parsing; pure text.
rationale: ContainerSSH-style access starts with correct SSH config, which users routinely fumble; generating it offline is a quick win.

name: date-sequence

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM iterating chrono dates; no network or filesystem needed. — via chrono crate
rationale: Directly maps dateutils' dateseq, useful for scheduling, billing cycles, and report ranges.

name: archive-converter
description: Converts an uploaded archive between formats (zip ⇄ tar.gz) preserving paths and permissions where possible.
example_prompt: convert this zip into a tar.gz
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes one format and re-encodes the other entirely in memory; both codecs are pure Rust. — via zip crate
rationale: Cross-format conversion is a recurring chore (TUI Archiver demand) with no good private/offline option today.

name: video-frame-diff
description: Extracts frames from two videos at matching timestamps and produces visual diffs to locate where they diverge.
example_prompt: compare these two video renders and show me at which frames they differ
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg frame extraction + per-frame pixel delta; all client-side WASM
rationale: Verifying that a re-encode or edit only changed intended frames is a real video QA need.

name: yaml-to-properties

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses YAML and emits flattened dotted keys locally — via serde_yaml crate

name: xml-minify

example_prompt: minify this XML document
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with quick-xml streaming rewrite; no external dependencies.
rationale: Useful for trimming verbose XML/RSS/SVG markup before transport or embedding.

name: retirement-calc

rationale: A top personal-finance tool absent from the current finance set.

name: wildcard-mask-converter

rationale: Cisco ACLs use wildcard masks and engineers frequently need to translate between all three notations.

name: moscow-prioritizer

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — keyword/tag-driven classification of text items.

name: sql-syntax-validator

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (sqlparser crate) — parse only, no DB

name: mp3-to-flac
description: Re-wraps MP3 audio into a FLAC container at full decoded resolution for archival/editing workflows.

loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes MPEG audio and encodes FLAC entirely in WASM with no network calls. — via flacenc crate
rationale: Editors and DAWs prefer a lossless container even when the source was lossy, making this a frequent prep step.

name: multipart-parser

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM boundary-splitting parser on pasted body text, no network
rationale: Debugging file-upload and email MIME bodies is hard without a part-by-part view.

name: csv-to-npy

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: writing the .npy magic header plus a contiguous little-endian buffer is pure byte assembly, no runtime needed.
rationale: Lets analysts feed spreadsheet data straight into NumPy/PyTorch without writing a loader script.

name: community-detection-louvain
description: Detects communities in a graph via Louvain modularity optimization and reports clusters and modularity score.
example_prompt: Find communities in this network.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; greedy modularity optimization runs over the pasted edge list locally.

name: random-forest-classifier

name: chinese-sentiment-classifier

example_prompt: How positive is this Chinese customer comment?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — small Chinese sentiment model executes in-browser via WASM/WebGPU.
rationale: Directly serves the SnowNLP sentiment demand with a more robust model and zero server cost.

name: yeo-johnson-transformer

example_prompt: Apply a Yeo-Johnson transform to this column with negatives
loader_feasibility: pyodide — scikit-learn/scipy PowerTransformer in-sandbox, no server
rationale: Yeo-Johnson is the standard normalizer for signed data and is otherwise only in heavyweight stats stacks.

name: key-value-line-parser
description: Parses 'key: value' style line blocks (configs, headers, logfmt) into a JSON object.
example_prompt: Parse these key: value lines into JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM delimiter splitting, client-side
rationale: Many ad-hoc text dumps are colon-delimited and benefit from quick structuring, distinct from .env.

name: waveform-peaks-extractor
description: Generates a downsampled min/max peak array (peaks.json) from an audio file for waveform rendering.
example_prompt: Generate waveform peak data for this audio
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader decodes to PCM in-browser, Rust→WASM downsamples to peak bins — no server.
rationale: Peak data is the standard precomputed input for fast waveform displays in editors and players.

name: logcat-parse
description: Parses Android logcat output into structured rows with timestamp, PID/TID, level, tag, and message.
example_prompt: Turn this logcat dump into a filterable table by tag and level
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM regex/line parsing of the threadtime/brief logcat formats; runs in-browser on pasted logs with no adb needed
rationale: Sifting raw logcat for a specific tag or error level is tedious and a structured view speeds up Android debugging.

name: warc-record-extract

example_prompt: List the captured URLs and statuses in this WARC file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing WARC record headers and content-length framing; reads the archive locally so large crawls aren't uploaded
rationale: WARC is the standard web-archive format yet there's no lightweight browser-local way to peek inside one.

name: vcd-waveform-parse
description: Parses a Value Change Dump (VCD) into its signal definitions and time-ordered value transitions.
example_prompt: List the signals and their transitions in this VCD file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing the $var/$dumpvars sections and value-change records; simulation traces parsed client-side with no server
rationale: Digital-design engineers inspect VCDs from simulators and a quick structural/transition summary beats loading a full waveform viewer.

name: dependency-list-extract
description: Extracts dependency names and versions from package.json, requirements.txt, Cargo.toml, or go.mod.
example_prompt: list all dependencies and versions from this package.json
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM format-specific parsers, offline
rationale: A normalized dependency inventory across formats helps audits and license/security review.

name: tremolo

example_prompt: Add a slow tremolo wobble to this guitar
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: multiply samples by a low-frequency oscillator envelope — trivial DSP.
rationale: Tremolo is a classic modulation effect that's quick to add and commonly requested.

name: semantic-diff
description: Embeds two versions of a text sentence-by-sentence and flags which segments changed in meaning rather than just in wording, separating real semantic edits from harmless paraphrases.

name: base32
description: Encode/decode Base32 (RFC 4648), the encoding used by TOTP secrets and some tokens.
example_prompt: decode this base32 string
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM codec.
rationale: Common encoding (esp. for 2FA secrets) missing alongside base64/base-convert.

name: sql-statement-splitter
description: Splits a SQL script into individual statements, respecting strings, comments, and delimiters.
example_prompt: Split this SQL dump into separate statements
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizer-aware splitting, client-side
rationale: Naive splitting on semicolons breaks on strings/comments; a proper local splitter is genuinely useful.

name: pdf417-decoder

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (rxing) decodes PDF417 rows and codewords entirely client-side, keeping sensitive IDs off any server. — via rxing crate
rationale: PDF417 carries personal data, so local-only decoding is a genuine privacy win.

name: psd-text-extractor
description: Extracts the editable text strings and their styles from a PSD's type layers.
example_prompt: Get all the text content from this PSD
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the PSD type-tool resource blocks in-memory.
rationale: Recovering copy from a layered design file without the editor is a common content task.

name: video-face-thumbnail-extractor
description: Detects faces in sampled frames and exports cropped face thumbnails tagged with their timestamps.
example_prompt: Pull out cropped face thumbnails with timestamps from this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm provides frames and an onnx-runtime face detector crops them in the browser; fully local.
rationale: Extracting face crops (not just counts) supports casting sheets, redaction prep, and dataset building entirely on-device.

name: audio-fileinfo-extractor

example_prompt: Give me the technical specs of this audio file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the container header for most fields; ffmpeg loader confirms codec params when needed — all in-browser.
rationale: A single unified technical summary across formats is one of the most universally requested audio queries.

name: xlsx-formula-extractor

example_prompt: List all the formulas in this Excel workbook
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM ZIP unpack plus sheet XML parse; operates on the uploaded file locally. — via zip crate
rationale: Auditing or migrating spreadsheet logic requires seeing all formulas in one place.

name: fix-message-parse

example_prompt: Decode this FIX 4.4 execution report with the tag names spelled out
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with an embedded FIX tag dictionary; splits on the SOH delimiter entirely client-side so trading data stays local
rationale: Trading-systems engineers read raw FIX logs daily and translating tag numbers to names by hand is error-prone.

name: yarn-lock-parse
description: Parses a yarn.lock (v1 custom or v2+ YAML) into a flat list of resolved packages, versions, and integrity hashes.
example_prompt: List every resolved version in this yarn.lock
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM handling both the v1 grammar and v2 YAML; lockfiles parse locally with no install step
rationale: Auditing exact resolved versions or duplicate packages from a lockfile is a common task with no quick web tool.

name: pkcs7-parse

example_prompt: Parse this PKCS#7 signature and list the certificates inside
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM ASN.1 DER decoder (der/x509 crates); structural decode runs locally so signed payloads stay private — via cms crate
rationale: PKCS#7 blobs (.p7b, .p7s) are common in signing flows yet awkward to inspect without OpenSSL.

name: cose-cwt-decode

example_prompt: Decode this COSE_Sign1 CWT and show the claims
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CBOR decoder mapping COSE label numbers to names; pure decode, no key fetch or network — via coset crate
rationale: COSE/CWT underpin IoT and mDL credentials but there's no easy human-readable local decoder like jwt.io for CBOR.

name: paseto-decode

example_prompt: Decode the payload of this PASETO v4 token
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM base64url + claim parse; structural decode runs entirely client-side like a local jwt-decode
rationale: PASETO is a popular JWT alternative and devs need the same quick local claim-inspection workflow.

name: nifti-header-parse
description: Parses a NIfTI-1/2 neuroimaging header to report dimensions, voxel sizes, datatype, and the affine orientation.
example_prompt: Show me the dimensions and voxel spacing of this .nii file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM fixed-offset binary read of the 348/540-byte NIfTI header; only the header is read so large brain volumes stay local
rationale: Neuroimaging researchers routinely need basic header facts (shape, spacing, orientation) without loading the full volume in Python.

name: p-value-extractor
description: Extracts statistical p-values from text (p<0.05, p = 0.012, p=.003) into a numeric column.
example_prompt: Find every p-value in this results paragraph
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pattern scanning with inequality handling, runs client-side.
rationale: Meta-analysts and reviewers harvest p-values from papers and need them as clean numbers.

name: flanger

loader_feasibility: ffmpeg flanger or Rust modulated delay+feedback — all sample-domain DSP, no server.

name: webvtt-parser

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM timestamp and cue parser.
rationale: Subtitle editing and conversion entirely offline.

name: object-detect

loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs DETR / YOLO-class ONNX models in-browser; boxes drawn onto an output PNG. — model Xenova/detr-resnet-50
rationale: Object detection enables counting, cropping, and downstream automation on images locally.

name: git-log-to-json
description: Parses a pasted `git log` into structured JSON or CSV (hash, author, date, subject, body) you can query or export.
example_prompt: Convert this git log into JSON
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses the log format and serializes it locally.
rationale: Turning log text into structured data unlocks querying and reporting without any extra tooling.

name: autocorrelation
description: Computes and plots ACF and PACF to reveal lag structure in a time series.
example_prompt: Show the ACF and PACF of this time series
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — correlation at lags, no server
rationale: Essential diagnostic for choosing ARIMA orders, supporting the time-series demand.

name: wireguard-config-parser

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; INI-style section parsing with WireGuard's key list, no network.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: dedupe/prune/quantize on parsed glTF (meshopt compiled to wasm). — via gltf crate

name: har-to-curl

loader_feasibility: plain WASM — local JSON parsing of the HAR and string assembly, no network.

name: properties-to-json

example_prompt: Convert this .properties file to JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line parser handling escapes and continuations; fully local.

name: grouped-bar-chart

rationale: Multi-series comparison is a top nvd3/Highcharts use case that single-series tools cannot cover.

name: connection-string-parser

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (url parsing) decomposes the DSN locally
rationale: Supabase/Appwrite users juggle DSNs and need to inspect host/port/db/params safely offline.

rationale: Out-of-sync subtitles are the top complaint in Kodi/OSMC playback and the fix is a trivial offline timing transform.

name: data-plotter

loader_feasibility: pyodide — matplotlib renders charts to PNG entirely in the browser. — via plotters crate
rationale: Quick data visualization is a frequent analysis need that pairs naturally with the stats/fit tools.

name: json-encrypt

rationale: Offline reverse geocoding avoids per-call API costs and keeps location data private in-browser.

name: ai-commit-message
description: Reads a pasted git diff and drafts a clear, conventional commit message describing the change.
example_prompt: Write a commit message for this diff
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a small summarization model over the diff entirely in-browser. — model Xenova/distilbart-cnn-6-6
rationale: AI Git Narrator shows strong demand for AI-authored commits, and doing it locally keeps unpushed code private.

name: email-signature-extractor
description: Strips quoted replies and signatures from email bodies, or extracts the signature block on its own.
example_prompt: Remove the quoted reply and signature from this email
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies signature/quote heuristics locally.
rationale: Clean email bodies feed far better into notes, CRMs, and summaries.

name: log-file-splitter
description: Splits a large uploaded log file into chunks by size, line count, or date boundary for easier review.
example_prompt: Split this 200MB log into daily files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — line/date scanning and chunk emission over the in-memory buffer, no external service
rationale: Oversized logs choke editors and viewers; chunking them locally keeps sensitive log data off any server.

name: double-entry-validator
description: Checks that every transaction in a ledger/beancount journal sums to zero and flags unbalanced or malformed postings.
example_prompt: Validate this ledger — which transactions don't balance?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: line-by-line parse plus exact decimal summation, fully client-side.
rationale: Catching unbalanced entries is the single most common beancount/ledger pain point and is trivially browser-local.

name: list-picker
description: Selects a subset of lines from a pasted list by index, numeric range, or regex, with multi-select support.
example_prompt: From this list keep lines 2-5 and any line matching /error/
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — deterministic line selection and regex, fully offline.
rationale: Maps the deterministic terminal selection menus (smenu, pmenu, cmenu, shmenu, lSel) into a precise, repeatable list-subset tool that complements fuzzy-filter.

name: url-list-normalizer
description: Cleans a list of URLs by deduplicating, normalizing case/trailing slashes, sorting, and optionally stripping tracking query parameters.
example_prompt: dedupe and normalize this list of URLs and strip utm params
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — URL parsing and set operations, runs client-side.
rationale: Tidying crawl/recon URL lists (redive-style discovery output) is a constant, fiddly manual chore.

name: journal-streak-tracker
description: Analyzes dated journal entries to report writing streaks, gaps, and per-period word counts.
example_prompt: Here are my dated diary entries — what's my longest journaling streak?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — date arithmetic and counting, fully client-side
rationale: pdiary/jrnl/TUI-Journal users want habit feedback to stay consistent.

name: availability-finder
description: Reads busy events from one or more .ics calendars and lists open free-time slots within working hours.
example_prompt: Find my free 1-hour slots next week from this calendar
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM interval math over parsed events, no network
rationale: Schedule meetings from a private calendar without sharing it with a third-party scheduling service.

name: semver-compare
description: Compares two semantic version strings and reports which is newer, equal, or older, including prerelease/build precedence.
example_prompt: Is 1.10.0 newer than 1.9.12?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure semver parsing/comparison, no I/O, runs entirely in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: Every version-manager term (mise, lastversion, topgrade) hinges on correct semver precedence, which people routinely get wrong by hand.

name: sbom-parser
description: Parses a CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM and summarizes components, versions, and licenses.
example_prompt: Summarize the components and licenses in this CycloneDX SBOM
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (serde JSON/XML parsing); SBOMs are self-contained documents parsed entirely locally.
rationale: grype workflows start from an SBOM, and parsing/summarizing one needs no network and keeps the dependency manifest private.

name: list-new-lines
description: Outputs only the lines from a new list that don't already appear in an existing list, preserving order and removing duplicates.
example_prompt: Show only the URLs in list B that aren't already in list A
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: hashset membership check over two text blobs, no external state.
rationale: The `anew` append-only-new-lines workflow is a recon/data staple with no convenient browser equivalent.

name: file-filter
description: Filters and sorts a set of uploaded files by name pattern, extension, size, or modified date.
example_prompt: From these uploaded files show only the .csv ones larger than 1 MB, newest first
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM matching glob/size/date metadata of the provided files locally
rationale: Maps zfind's attribute-based find onto the files a user drops into chat, with no filesystem access needed.

name: mask-edit
description: Select only part of each line — by regex match, character range, or delimited field — and apply a transform (replace, case-change, base64, hash) to just that part, leaving the rest untouched.
example_prompt: In this CSV, base64-encode only the 3rd column and leave everything else alone
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; combines field/regex selection with built-in transforms, all client-side
rationale: This is exactly teip's 'edit in place only the selected region' superpower, which has no browser equivalent today and is broadly useful for surgical text edits.

name: todo-txt-sort-filter
description: Sorts and filters a todo.txt list by priority, project, context, or due date and returns the reordered list.
example_prompt: Sort these todo.txt tasks by priority then due date and show only the +work ones
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — in-memory parse, sort, and filter over text lines.
rationale: Sorting/filtering is the single most-used operation across taskwarrior, dstask, and todo.txt workflows.

name: video-meme-maker
description: Overlays top/bottom impact-text captions on a video clip and exports an mp4 or gif.
example_prompt: add the caption 'when the code finally compiles' to the top of this clip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: the drawtext filter renders captions over frames in-browser via ffmpeg.wasm.
rationale: Directly serves the CreateVideoMeme demand and runs without uploading personal clips.

name: manga-text-detector
description: Detects speech-bubble and on-page text regions in a manga or comic image and returns bounding boxes.
example_prompt: Find all the text bubbles in this manga page
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime — a small text/bubble detection model (koharu uses comic-text-detector) runs as ONNX in-browser on the canvas image. — model mayocream/comic-text-detector-onnx
rationale: Locating text is the hard first step of any scanlation workflow and doing it locally avoids uploading copyrighted scans.

name: svg-path-boolean
description: Performs boolean operations (union, intersection, difference, exclusion) on overlapping SVG shapes to make one clean path.
example_prompt: Subtract the circle from the square in this SVG and give me the merged path
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — polygon/bezier boolean clipping is pure computation runnable client-side, mirroring Graphite's vector engine. — via geo crate
rationale: Path boolean ops are a core vector-editing primitive that's tedious to do by hand and missing from lightweight tools.

name: email-permutator
description: Generates likely email-address formats from a person's name and a domain for OSINT and outreach.
example_prompt: Generate possible emails for Jane Smith at example.com
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure string permutation logic; no lookups or network.
rationale: A core OSINT building block (the sn0int theme) that is entirely deterministic and safe to run locally.

name: markdown-todo-extractor
description: Extracts and groups TODO/FIXME/HACK items from pasted markdown or code into an organized list.
example_prompt: Pull all the TODOs out of this file and group them by tag <paste file>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — line scanning and grouping; pure client-side text processing.
rationale: A practical companion to the kanban builder that converts scattered notes into actionable tasks instantly.

name: web-tech-fingerprint
description: Identifies the CMS, frameworks, analytics, and server software powering a site from its pasted HTML source or HTTP response headers.
example_prompt: What technologies is this website built with? Here's the page source
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM running signature/regex rules over the supplied HTML and headers, so no fetching or scanning is required.
rationale: Gives the value of Wappalyzer/observer_ward fingerprinting without a backend, operating only on text the user already has.

name: text-transform
description: Translates, deletes, or squeezes characters and changes case, like tr (e.g. CRLF→LF, upper/lower, strip punctuation).
example_prompt: convert this text to lowercase and strip all punctuation
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: character mapping over the input string, fully local.
rationale: tr-style character surgery is a recurring coreutils need for normalizing pasted text.

name: smart-replace
description: Case-aware find-and-replace that preserves snake_case, camelCase, PascalCase, and kebab-case across all forms at once.
example_prompt: Rename 'oldUserName' to 'accountHolder' everywhere in this code, keeping each casing
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with case-style detection (ruplacer logic); operates on pasted text.
rationale: ruplacer's casing-aware rename avoids the bugs of naive replace and is great for refactoring snippets.

name: dependency-graph
description: Parses Cargo.lock or package.json and emits a Mermaid or Graphviz dependency graph.
example_prompt: Draw the dependency graph for this Cargo.lock
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the lockfile and emits graph source text, pure CPU.
rationale: Visualizes the dependency tree (cargo-depgraph) without installing graphviz or Cargo.

name: fits-to-png-converter
description: Converts a FITS image to PNG with selectable linear, log, or zscale stretch.
example_prompt: Convert this FITS file to a PNG with log stretch.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM FITS parsing feeds pixel data to ffmpeg/image encoding, all client-side. — via fitrs crate
rationale: Sharing FITS data with non-astronomers requires a normal image format and is otherwise script-only (fitsio).

name: dependency-cycle-detector
description: Detects and reports cycles in a dependency graph, naming the offending nodes.
example_prompt: Is there a circular dependency in this module list?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — DFS cycle detection on an in-memory adjacency list.
rationale: Circular dependencies break DAG execution and builds; pinpointing them quickly is valuable (dagrs).

name: string-similarity
description: Computes similarity scores between two strings, or ranks candidates against a target, using Levenshtein, Jaro-Winkler, Sørensen-Dice, and cosine metrics.
example_prompt: How similar are 'Smith & Co.' and 'Smith and Company'?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — strsim-rs is pure string math with no I/O, so it runs entirely in the wasmi sandbox. — via strsim crate
rationale: Name-matching, dedup, and fuzzy-join decisions need a quick offline similarity score without a service round-trip.

name: text-highlight
description: Locates every occurrence of query terms in a document and returns highlighted context snippets.
example_prompt: Show every mention of 'liability' in this contract with surrounding text.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — perlin-style tokenize, match, and snippet-window logic runs in-sandbox with no network.
rationale: Quickly scan long documents for term occurrences with readable context.

name: record-search
description: Typo-tolerant instant search over a JSON array of records with per-field weighting and ranked results.
example_prompt: Search these product records for 'wireless hedphones'.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — MeiliSearch-style ranking rules operate over an in-memory record set, fully offline.
rationale: Search structured data with misspellings and field boosts without a hosted index.

name: image-to-prompt
description: Describe an image as a text-to-image generation prompt (CLIP-interrogate style).
example_prompt: Give me a Stable-Diffusion prompt that would recreate this image
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a BLIP/CLIP-interrogator model in-browser to produce a prompt; no server. — model Xenova/blip-image-captioning-base
rationale: AI-art users heavily use 'interrogate', and it's distinct from the plain image-caption tool.

name: image-diff
description: Compare two images pixel-by-pixel and produce a visual diff highlighting changed regions plus a percent-changed score.
example_prompt: show me what changed between these two screenshots
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (decode both + per-pixel delta, like pixelmatch); pure local compute. — via image crate
rationale: Visual regression/diffing is a common QA and design-review task with no equivalent in the current image set.

name: style-transfer
description: Repaint a photo in an artistic style (e.g. Van Gogh, ukiyo-e, sketch) using fast neural style transfer.
example_prompt: make this photo look like a Van Gogh painting
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime fast-neural-style models (or webgpu-compute shaders); inference is fully local.
rationale: Artistic restyling is a popular creative effect with small pretrained models suited to in-browser inference.

name: text-normalize
description: Clean text by collapsing whitespace, converting smart quotes/dashes to ASCII, stripping zero-width and control characters, and fixing mojibake.
example_prompt: clean up the weird quotes and invisible characters in this pasted text
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: deterministic Unicode normalization, no network.
rationale: Solves a constant copy-paste pain point before publishing or feeding text to code.

name: chapter-generate
description: Generate YouTube-style chapters/timestamps from a transcript by segmenting and labeling topics.
example_prompt: Make chapter timestamps from this video transcript
loader_feasibility: transformers-js segmentation/summarization over transcript text in-browser; local.
rationale: Auto-chaptering is a top creator request and reuses local NLP without uploading the video.

name: json-stringify
description: Wraps arbitrary text or JSON into a single escaped JSON string literal ready to embed in code.
example_prompt: turn this multiline text into a json string
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string-encoding logic, no network.
rationale: Embedding text as an escaped JSON string is a constant copy-paste pain point.

name: url-expand
description: Follow redirects on a shortened or tracking URL and reveal the final destination and the hop chain.
example_prompt: Where does this bit.ly link actually go?
loader_feasibility: web fetch loader — follow redirect responses client-side and record each hop, no external API.
rationale: Unmasking short links is a common safety/transparency check with broad appeal.

name: template-scaffold
description: Renders a boilerplate template, filling `{{placeholder}}` variables from your supplied values.
example_prompt: Scaffold a README from this template with project=Gizza, license=MIT: [paste template]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; mustache-style variable substitution is a local string transform.
rationale: Brings Yeoman/boilr-style scaffolding into the chat with no generator install or filesystem access.

name: log-aggregator
description: Extracts fields from pasted logs with a regex and aggregates them into counts, sums, histograms, or tables.
example_prompt: From this access log, count requests per status code and show a histogram
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using the regex crate plus grouping/aggregation logic; all in-memory over pasted text.
rationale: rare turns raw logs into quick analytics, and that whole workflow is CPU-only and ideal for a browser tool.

name: changelog-generator
description: Generates a grouped changelog (features/fixes/breaking) from pasted git log or conventional-commit history.
example_prompt: Build a changelog from these conventional commits
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM commit parsing and Markdown grouping; fully local.
rationale: git-extras' changelog automation is a common release chore that works entirely from pasted commit text.

name: spoken-language-detect
description: Identify the spoken language of an audio clip.
example_prompt: What language is being spoken in this clip?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a Whisper/SpeechBrain language-ID model in-browser via onnx. — model Xenova/whisper-tiny
rationale: Audio counterpart to text detect-language, useful before transcription/translation.

name: video-crossfade
description: Join multiple clips with smooth crossfade/dissolve transitions (and audio crossfade).
example_prompt: Join these three clips with a half-second crossfade between each
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg xfade + acrossfade; browser-local.
rationale: video-concat only hard-cuts; smooth transitions are the most-requested editing upgrade.

name: csv-melt
description: Unpivot a wide table into long/tidy format (id columns plus variable/value pairs).
example_prompt: Melt this wide sales-by-month table into long format
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM reshape; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: The inverse of csv-pivot and an essential reshape step for charting and analysis.

name: audio-bleep-profanity
description: Transcribe speech, locate profanity by word timestamp, and bleep/mute those moments.
example_prompt: Censor the swearing in this podcast clip
loader_feasibility: transformers-js Whisper word timestamps + ffmpeg mute/bleep; offline. — model Xenova/whisper-tiny
rationale: A real podcaster/streamer need that chains transcription to audio editing.

name: dir-tree
description: Render an ASCII directory tree from an indented list or a set of file paths for READMEs.
example_prompt: Make an ASCII file tree from this list of paths
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM text transform; offline.
rationale: Ubiquitous in documentation with no existing generator.

name: image-palette-remap
description: Remap an image's colors to a target palette (Nord, Solarized, Game Boy, custom).
example_prompt: Recolor this screenshot to the Nord palette
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM nearest-color quantization to a palette, offline. — via image crate
rationale: Theming images/pixel art to a palette is popular and broader than single-color replace or duotone.

name: code-symbol-index
description: Extracts every function, struct, class, and method from pasted source with line numbers, like a ctags index.
example_prompt: List all the functions and types defined in this file with their line numbers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tree-sitter parsing of the pasted text; no compiler or filesystem needed.
rationale: Gives a fast navigable overview of an unfamiliar file without opening an IDE, replacing ptags/ctags for a single snippet.

name: log-window-aggregate
description: Parses a log or event file and computes time-bucketed aggregations like counts, rates, and per-key tallies per interval.
example_prompt: From this access log, count requests per minute and show the top 5 status codes.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — applies the stream-processing windowing model to a static in-memory file.
rationale: Brings windowed stream-analytics (the value behind Arroyo/Arkflow) to ad-hoc local log inspection.

name: json-to-cql-insert
description: Generates Cassandra CQL INSERT statements from a JSON array of records for a target table.
example_prompt: generate CQL inserts into users from this JSON array of records
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM: maps JSON fields to INSERT columns/values deterministically, no DB access.
rationale: Seeding Cassandra tables from JSON fixtures by hand is tedious and easy to get wrong.

name: supernet-aggregator
description: Aggregates a list of CIDR prefixes into the minimal set of supernets for route summarization.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sort plus adjacent-prefix merge on integers, no I/O.
rationale: Route summarization shrinks routing tables and is a standard but fiddly network-engineering chore.

name: slide-frame-extractor
description: Detects slide changes in a talk video and exports one still image per slide.
example_prompt: Pull out each slide as an image from this talk video.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg scene-change detection and frame export run fully in the browser via the ffmpeg loader.
rationale: Recovering slide decks from talk recordings is a genuinely useful, purely local media task.

name: unsubscribe-link-finder
description: Scans an mbox for List-Unsubscribe headers and body links to list every mailing list you can leave.
example_prompt: Find all the unsubscribe links in my mbox
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses headers and bodies locally.
rationale: Bulk-unsubscribing starts with finding the links, and doing it locally keeps your inbox private.

name: llm-bundle-extractor
description: Reverses an LLM-generated PAWS/cats bundle back into individual named files for download as a zip.
example_prompt: Split this bundled text back into the original files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse the path-marker grammar and re-emit a zip with the zip crate entirely in memory
rationale: The natural inverse of bundling; lets users apply an LLM's multi-file edits without manual copy-paste per file.

name: find-query-builder
description: Builds an equivalent find/fd/bfs command from plain-English criteria (name, size, mtime, type) and runs the same filter over a pasted path list.
example_prompt: Find files larger than 1MB modified this week in this list, and give me the fd command
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — criteria parsing, command-string generation, and filtering on provided metadata.
rationale: Serves bfs/friendly-find/Findpick by both teaching the command and producing the result locally.

name: shellcode-format-converter
description: Converts a byte payload between hex, \x-escaped, base64, and C/Python array formats.
example_prompt: Turn this \x-escaped shellcode into a C unsigned char array
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure string/byte encoding with no I/O.
rationale: A constant copy-paste chore in exploit dev and RE that a tiny deterministic tool removes entirely.

name: quiz-response-grader
description: Grades a CSV of quiz responses against a supplied answer key, producing per-respondent scores, percentages, and a per-question correctness breakdown.
example_prompt: Grade this quiz responses CSV against my answer key and give me the scores
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM compares parsed answer cells to the key and tallies; entirely local computation.
rationale: Google Forms and Typeform quiz modes export raw answers, and re-grading or auditing scores outside their UI has no free local option.

name: comment-spam-classifier
description: Classifies a blog or issue comment as spam or legitimate to pre-moderate threads.
example_prompt: Is this comment spam: 'Great post! Buy cheap watches at...'
loader_feasibility: transformers-js zero-shot classification — on-device. — model Xenova/nli-deberta-v3-xsmall
rationale: Comment widgets get drowned in spam, and local pre-filtering keeps moderation cheap.

name: json-schema-ref-resolver
description: Dereferences and bundles all $ref pointers (internal and inline) so a multi-part JSON Schema becomes one self-contained document.
example_prompt: Resolve all the $refs in this JSON Schema into one file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pointer resolution over the in-memory schema; only inline/embedded refs since there's no network fetch
rationale: Directly maps JSON Schema $Ref Parser, a named term, as an offline bundler.

name: annotation-format-converter
description: Converts annotations between brat standoff, CoNLL, doccano JSONL, Label Studio JSON and spaCy formats.
example_prompt: Convert this brat .ann file to doccano JSONL
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing and serialization, offline.
rationale: brat, doccano, Label Studio, INCEpTION and tagtog each use a different format and conversion is constant pain.

name: chinese-word-segmenter
description: Segments continuous Chinese text into words with a dictionary + HMM model (jieba-style).
example_prompt: Segment this Chinese paragraph into words separated by spaces.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — jieba-rs ships its dictionary as a bundled asset and runs in the wasmi runtime. — via jieba-rs crate
rationale: Word segmentation is the prerequisite for all Chinese text work and jieba is the most-requested implementation.

name: spanish-speech-summarizer
description: Summarizes long Spanish speeches or articles into a short abstract.
example_prompt: Summarize this Spanish political speech in a short paragraph.
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — a multilingual summarization model runs locally via WASM/WebGPU.
rationale: Serves the Colombian political-speech corpus demand, giving Spanish users private long-text summarization.

name: corpus-word-frequency
description: Computes word and character frequency lists, n-grams, and type/token statistics over a large text.
example_prompt: Give me the top 50 words and bigrams in this text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: streaming tokenization and counting handles large pasted text in-browser
rationale: Frequency and n-gram analysis of big corpora (like VNTQcorpus) is a core linguistics/SEO need that runs comfortably client-side.

name: persian-lemmatizer
description: Maps Persian words to their dictionary base form (lemma), including irregular verbs.
example_prompt: Give me the lemma of: رفتند، بهترین، خانه‌ها
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with a bundled lemma dictionary loaded into memory — lookup plus morphological fallback runs entirely client-side.
rationale: Lemmatization gives true canonical forms (unlike crude stemming) and underpins accurate frequency analysis and search.

name: persian-keyword-extractor
description: Extracts the most important keywords and keyphrases from a Persian document.
example_prompt: Pull the top 10 keywords from this Persian article
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — graph-based TextRank/Perke-style ranking over tokenized text, no model needed.
rationale: Unsupervised keyphrase extraction (Perke) drives tagging, indexing, and summary previews for Persian content.

name: pitch-detector
description: Tracks the fundamental frequency (pitch) over time and returns a pitch contour.
example_prompt: Plot the pitch contour of this vocal
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM YIN/autocorrelation pitch tracking runs locally with no server.
rationale: Pitch tracking drives intonation feedback for singers, language learners, and melody extraction.

name: midi-transpose
description: Transposes a MIDI or MusicXML file by an interval or into a target key, preserving timing and instrumentation.
example_prompt: Transpose this MIDI down a perfect fourth.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — MIDI parsing and pitch arithmetic on note events is straightforward pure compute (or music21 via pyodide for MusicXML).
rationale: Transposing scores for different instruments or vocal ranges is a frequent, simple task that should not require desktop software.

name: midi-quantize
description: Snaps note start/end times to a rhythmic grid such as 1/8, 1/16, or triplets.
example_prompt: Quantize this MIDI to sixteenth notes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — arithmetic on event timestamps, fully local.
rationale: Tightens sloppily recorded MIDI performances (Pretty-MIDI demand).

name: mesh-thumbnail-renderer
description: Software-rasterizes an OBJ/STL/glTF model to a shaded PNG preview from a chosen camera angle, no GPU required.
example_prompt: Render a 3/4 view thumbnail of this OBJ model
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a software rasterizer shades the mesh to a PNG, no GPU required.
rationale: Previewing a 3D file without standing up a full engine (Babylon/ClayGL/CopperLicht) is exactly what users want before importing.

name: bash-history-analyzer
description: Scans a shell history file for suspicious commands (downloads, reverse shells, credential access, log tampering).
example_prompt: Anything sketchy in this .bash_history?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — rule/regex matching over text
rationale: Shell history is one of the richest intent artifacts unix collectors grab, and pattern-flagging it is quick.

name: bodyfile-timeline
description: Turns a Sleuthkit-style bodyfile into a sorted MACB super-timeline (CSV) you can scan by time.
example_prompt: Build a timeline from this bodyfile
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse, sort, and emit CSV in-browser
rationale: Timelining is the synthesis step of every disk triage, and doing it locally avoids shipping evidence to a server.

name: apple-backup-manifest
description: Reads an iTunes/iOS backup Manifest.db to list backed-up files, domains, and their on-disk hashed names.
example_prompt: List the files in this iPhone backup's Manifest.db
loader_feasibility: pyodide — sqlite3 reads the Manifest.db locally and maps file IDs to original paths
rationale: UFADE/Fuji-style Apple extractions are opaque without resolving Manifest.db's hashed filenames.

name: incident-log-summarizer
description: Summarizes a large collected log or triage-output text into a short timeline of notable events.
example_prompt: Summarize what happened in this 5,000-line log
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — a local summarization model condenses the pasted text in-browser with no upload — model Xenova/distilbart-cnn-6-6
rationale: DFIR-ORC/UAC/Velociraptor collections produce overwhelming text, and a local summarizer speeds first-pass review without leaking data.

name: volatility-lite
description: Runs lightweight Volatility3 plugins (pslist, netscan, cmdline) over a small uploaded memory image.
example_prompt: List the processes in this small memory dump
loader_feasibility: pyodide — Volatility3 is pure Python and runs in the sandbox for modest-sized dumps (browser RAM caps large images)
rationale: Memoryze/Redline/AVML/LiME produce dumps whose analysis usually needs Volatility, and a browser version handles quick small-dump checks.

name: minidump-triage
description: Parses a Windows minidump (.dmp) to list loaded modules, threads, the crash exception, and embedded strings.
example_prompt: What modules and exception are in this crash dump?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the minidump crate is pure-Rust parsing of the uploaded dump.
rationale: Delivers the feasible slice of memory forensics (MemProcFS) for crash/malware triage without a Volatility backend.

name: log-field-analyzer
description: Parses large CSV/JSON/syslog files and reports per-field value distributions, cardinality, and statistical outliers.
example_prompt: Show the value distribution and outliers across fields in this log
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: streaming parse and aggregation handle large files in-sandbox.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses the documented SQLite file format directly from bytes, read-only, no engine, in-browser

name: despeckle-scan

rationale: Scanner speckle is a specific document defect that general denoise tools handle poorly.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — find min/max per channel and linearly rescale, trivial

name: csv-type-coercer

rationale: Inconsistent date formats are a top cause of data-import failures.

name: html-head-inspect
description: Audits an HTML <head>, reporting title length, charset, viewport, canonical, meta count, and missing/duplicated key tags.
example_prompt: check the <head> of this HTML for SEO and missing tags
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML parsing of the pasted markup; no crawl
rationale: A holistic <head> sanity check catches truncated titles and missing canonical/viewport tags in one pass.

name: sample-rate-sanity-check
description: Flags non-standard or unusual sample rates and mismatches between the container-declared rate and the actual decoded stream rate.
example_prompt: Check this file for an unusual or mismatched sample rate
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg exposes container and stream metadata in WASM; comparison and range checks are local.
rationale: Wrong or mislabeled sample rates cause pitch/speed errors that a sanity check catches before further processing.

name: image-dpi-reader
description: Reads the embedded resolution (DPI/PPI) from JFIF, EXIF, or PNG pHYs chunks and warns when it is the meaningless default 72.
example_prompt: What DPI is this scan tagged at?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse the format header bytes directly — trivial and offline.
rationale: Print shops constantly need the tagged DPI and most viewers hide it.

name: changepoint-detector
description: Detects mean and variance change points in a 1-D series using CUSUM/binary-segmentation and reports their indices.
example_prompt: Where does the behavior of this series change? Find the changepoints.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM segmentation algorithm; no server.
rationale: Spotting regime shifts in metrics, sensors, or finance is a common need with no simple client-side tool.

name: timestamp-to-seconds
description: Parses HH:MM:SS, MM:SS, and SS.mmm timestamp strings into total seconds (and the reverse).
example_prompt: Convert 01:23:45 and 4:07.5 to seconds
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — colon-field parsing and arithmetic, no dependencies.
rationale: Subtitle, media, and stopwatch timestamps need numeric seconds for math and sorting.

name: mixed-unit-length-parser
description: Parses compound measurements like '5 ft 7 in' or '1 m 80 cm' into a single value in a chosen base unit.
example_prompt: Convert 5 ft 7 in and 1 m 80 cm both to centimeters
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — multi-unit tokenizing and conversion-factor summation, no network.
rationale: Height, lumber, and fabric measurements come as mixed feet-and-inches that need a single numeric value.

name: strip-eol-whitespace
description: Removes trailing spaces and tabs from the end of every line.
example_prompt: strip trailing whitespace from each line
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM per-line trim, no server needed
rationale: Trailing whitespace causes noisy diffs and trips linters and pre-commit hooks.

name: trim-leading-trailing-blank-lines
description: Strips blank lines only from the very start and end, leaving interior spacing untouched.
example_prompt: remove the empty lines at the top and bottom
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM boundary trim, runs in-browser
rationale: Removes copy-paste padding without altering meaningful paragraph breaks.

name: sentence-per-line
description: Splits prose into one sentence per line using punctuation and abbreviation heuristics.
example_prompt: put each sentence on its own line
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM sentence segmentation, no API
rationale: One-sentence-per-line text yields clean diffs and easier translation alignment.

name: duotone-filter
description: Maps image luminance to a two-color gradient for a branded duotone look.
example_prompt: Apply a blue-and-pink duotone to this photo
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM maps grayscale value to an interpolation between two chosen colors; runs in-browser.
rationale: Duotone is a popular design/branding treatment (distinct from scientific false-color) and trivial to do locally.

name: gradient-banding-dither
description: Adds subtle dithering to smooth visible banding in gradients and skies.
example_prompt: Fix the banding in this sky gradient
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies ordered/blue-noise dithering before output; pure local pixel work.
rationale: Banding in gradients and compressed skies is a common artifact and dithering is the standard cure.

name: video-grid-stack
description: Combines several uploaded videos into a tiled grid (2x2, 3x3, etc.) using xstack into one synchronized output.
example_prompt: Combine these four videos into a 2x2 grid
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader uses scale + xstack on local files entirely in-browser
rationale: Multi-video grid montages are popular for comparisons/collages, distinct from frame previews and two-up compares.

name: telephone-eq
description: Band-limits audio to roughly 300–3400 Hz for a telephone/walkie-talkie effect.
example_prompt: Make this voice sound like it's coming through a phone
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg bandpass or Rust biquads — a fixed band filter applied client-side.
rationale: The phone/radio voice effect is a frequent need for podcasts, games, and film dialogue.

name: mp3-gain-lossless
description: Changes an MP3's volume losslessly by scaling the per-frame global_gain fields with no re-encode.
example_prompt: Turn this MP3 down by 5 dB without re-encoding it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse MP3 frames and adjust global_gain values bit-exactly (MP3Gain-style) — no decode/re-encode.
rationale: Lossless MP3 volume adjustment avoids generation loss that a decode/normalize/re-encode would introduce.

name: audio-pan
description: Sets the stereo pan position of a mono or stereo source using an equal-power law.
example_prompt: Pan this guitar 40% to the left
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: apply equal-power L/R gain coefficients per sample and write a stereo file.
rationale: Precise panning is a basic mixing operation needed to place mono sources in a stereo field.

name: deglitch-dropouts
description: Detects and repairs short digital dropouts or zero-fill gaps in a recording.
example_prompt: Fix the brief audio dropouts in this Bluetooth recording
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: find anomalous silent/zero runs and interpolate across them from surrounding audio.
rationale: Wireless and streamed captures frequently drop samples, and gap interpolation rescues otherwise-unusable takes.

name: normalize-rms
description: Normalizes a file to a target average RMS level rather than peak.
example_prompt: RMS-normalize this to -18 dB so it matches the loudness of my other clips
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: compute RMS, derive a gain to the target, multiply through the buffer.
rationale: RMS normalization matches perceived loudness better than peak for evening out a set of clips.

name: csv-rename-columns
description: Renames columns from an old→new mapping, leaving unmapped columns untouched and warning on misses.
example_prompt: Rename 'cust_nm' to 'customer_name' and 'amt' to 'amount'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM header rewrite; client-side.
rationale: Header renaming to match a downstream schema is constant and error-prone by hand.

name: nan-inf-cleaner
description: Detects NaN, Infinity, and -Infinity tokens in a numeric column and replaces them with a chosen finite value or drops the rows.
example_prompt: Replace any NaN or Inf in this data with 0
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: token detection + substitution, no external calls.
rationale: Exported floats frequently carry NaN/Inf that break downstream math; cleaning them is a precise, common need.

name: video-sharpen
description: Applies an unsharp-mask sharpening filter with adjustable strength to crisp up soft or upscaled footage.
example_prompt: Sharpen this slightly blurry video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader runs the unsharp filter in wasm
rationale: Recovering perceived detail in soft footage is a common enhancement step.

name: label-encoder
description: Maps each distinct category to a stable integer code and emits the encoded column plus the mapping table.
example_prompt: Label-encode this category column to integers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: hash-map of category→code in one pass, no network.
rationale: Integer label encoding is a foundational preprocessing step and pairs naturally with the one-hot tool.

name: lorem-json-generator
description: Generates placeholder JSON of a requested shape, depth, and array length for UI mocking.
example_prompt: Generate a nested placeholder JSON object 3 levels deep
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; synthesizes structure with a local RNG.
rationale: Quick filler payloads for front-end stubs when no schema is handy.

name: video-blockiness-report
description: Estimates macroblocking/compression-blockiness severity over time so over-compressed sections can be found.
example_prompt: How blocky is this video and which parts are worst?
loader_feasibility: Frames are decoded by ffmpeg and a blockiness metric is computed by an onnx model or Rust DCT-edge heuristic locally.
rationale: Blocking is the signature of bitrate starvation, and a per-section score guides where to re-encode.

name: pca-variance-explainer
description: Runs PCA on a numeric matrix and returns explained-variance ratios, cumulative variance, and scree-plot data without performing any transform.
example_prompt: How many principal components explain 95% of variance in this dataset?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via SVD on the centered matrix; no server.
rationale: Dimensionality decisions hinge on the scree/variance curve, which people usually compute in a notebook just to peek.

name: video-audio-bitrate-check
description: Checks the audio bitrate against a minimum/maximum threshold to catch over-compressed or oversized tracks.
example_prompt: Is the audio bitrate on this at least 128kbps?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm reads the audio bitrate locally and threshold logic runs in WASM.
rationale: Under-bitrate audio sounds bad and over-bitrate wastes size; both are checkable only by inspecting the value.

name: sql-create-table-from-json
description: Generates a CREATE TABLE statement from a sample JSON object, mapping field types to SQL column types.
example_prompt: Generate a CREATE TABLE for this JSON record
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — type inference plus DDL string assembly, no database needed.
rationale: Bootstrapping a schema from sample data is a routine, automatable step.

name: video-to-vp8
description: Encodes a video to VP8/WebM for maximum compatibility with older WebRTC and browser stacks.
example_prompt: Give me a VP8 webm of this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader with libvpx — VP8 encode runs client-side in wasm.
rationale: Some legacy WebRTC pipelines and embedded browsers only decode VP8, not VP9 or H.264.

name: ply-to-xyz-converter
description: Converts a PLY point cloud or mesh into plain XYZ coordinates (with optional normals/colors).
example_prompt: Extract XYZ points from this .ply file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the PLY header element/property list then the vertex data
rationale: Point-cloud workflows frequently need bare XYZ extracted from PLY scans.

name: face-crop-safety-checker
description: Detects faces and warns when any face is clipped by the image edges or too small/close to the border for safe cropping.
example_prompt: Will any faces get cut off if I crop this group photo to a square avatar?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a face-detection model in-browser; plain Rust checks bounding boxes against margins.
rationale: Auto-crops that decapitate faces are a common batch-thumbnail failure worth catching before publishing.

name: leading-trailing-silence-check
description: Reports the duration of leading and trailing silence below a chosen threshold so you know how much to trim.
example_prompt: How much silence is at the start and end of this clip?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes to PCM in WASM; threshold scanning from both ends is pure local analysis.
rationale: Stray head/tail silence breaks gapless albums and looped assets, and an exact measurement enables clean trims.

name: image-resize-algorithm-compare
description: Resamples one image with nearest, bilinear, bicubic, and Lanczos and compares the results side metrics (sharpness, SSIM vs. source) to pick the best.
example_prompt: Which resize algorithm looks best for shrinking this logo?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the image crate provides all resamplers; quality metrics computed locally.
rationale: Choosing the right resampler matters for crisp downscales, and seeing the metrics ends the debate.

name: video-diff-heatmap
description: Produces a colorized difference video between two aligned clips, highlighting where and how much pixels changed.
example_prompt: Make a heatmap video showing what changed between these two cuts
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — blend=difference + a false-color LUT in ffmpeg.wasm, no server needed
rationale: Instantly localizes edits, compression artifacts, or watermarks that are hard to spot at full speed.

name: moved-block-diff
description: Diffs two texts and distinguishes blocks that were moved from blocks that were truly added or deleted.
example_prompt: Did I move this section or rewrite it? Diff these two docs detecting moves
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: hash-and-match blocks then reconcile against a plain diff, all in-memory.
rationale: Standard diffs scream 'deleted + added' for a moved paragraph, hiding what really changed.

name: markdown-section-diff
description: Diffs two Markdown documents by heading section so changes are reported per chapter rather than per raw line.
example_prompt: Compare these two versions of my README and tell me which sections changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse heading tree, align sections, diff each, all CPU-bound.
rationale: Section-aware diffs make doc reviews meaningful where flat line diffs scatter changes across the file.

name: sql-ddl-diff
description: Compares two SQL CREATE TABLE definitions and emits the ALTER statements plus added/dropped/changed columns and constraints.
example_prompt: Compare these two table definitions and give me the ALTER TABLE migration
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse DDL into column models and diff, pure computation.
rationale: Hand-writing migrations from two schema snapshots is error-prone and a column-aware diff automates it.

name: histogram-bins-to-csv
description: Converts a list of raw values into binned histogram counts as CSV, and back to bin-center data.
example_prompt: Bin these values into 10 buckets as CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes bin edges and tallies counts in memory
rationale: A reproducible way to turn raw samples into a histogram table for import elsewhere.

name: png-to-ppm
description: Exports PNG to plain PPM/PGM for image-processing toolchains and assignments.
example_prompt: Export this PNG as a binary PPM
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM image crate writes PNM output entirely in the browser
rationale: Many CS courses and C image-processing tools expect raw PPM input, making a precise exporter handy.

name: png-text-chunk-editor
description: Adds, edits, or removes PNG tEXt/iTXt chunks like Title, Author, and Description.
example_prompt: Add an author and copyright text chunk to this PNG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse the PNG chunk stream, insert/rewrite tEXt chunks with CRCs — in-memory only.
rationale: Embedding textual credits/metadata in PNGs has no friendly tool in the browser.

name: number-list-delta
description: Computes element-wise and aggregate deltas between two numeric lists, including absolute and percent change.
example_prompt: Show the change for each value between this month's and last month's numbers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse numbers and compute differences, no external compute
rationale: Comparing two columns of numbers and getting per-row and total deltas is a constant spreadsheet task.

name: image-alignment-offset
description: Estimates the X/Y translation needed to register two near-identical images using phase correlation, then outputs the aligned diff.
example_prompt: How many pixels is this scan shifted from the original, and align them
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: FFT-based phase correlation over pixel buffers runs purely on CPU in wasmi.
rationale: Most diff tools fail on a 2-pixel shift; auto-registering first makes the comparison actually meaningful.

name: video-divergence-point-finder
description: Scans two versions of a video and reports the first timestamp where their frames begin to differ.
example_prompt: Find the exact moment these two exports start to diverge
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — frame-by-frame blend=difference threshold scan in ffmpeg.wasm
rationale: Pinpoints where an edit, trim, or re-render first changed so reviewers jump straight to it.

name: video-bitrate-ladder-report
description: Compares an ABR rendition set, listing each variant resolution, bitrate, and overlap gaps in one table.
example_prompt: Compare the bitrate ladder across these streaming renditions
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — ffprobe over each rendition aggregated by a Rust→WASM tabulator client-side
rationale: Catches redundant or missing rungs in a streaming ladder before publishing.

name: video-keyframe-diff
description: Compares keyframe (GOP) positions between two encodes and reports alignment differences for seeking and ABR.
example_prompt: Do these two renditions have matching keyframe positions?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — ffprobe -skip_frame nokey on both, diffed by a Rust→WASM comparator locally
rationale: Mismatched GOPs break seamless ABR switching, and this surfaces them instantly.

name: video-audio-diff
description: Compares the audio tracks of two videos and reports where they differ, with a per-segment difference timeline.
example_prompt: Where does the audio differ between these two cuts?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — sample-level subtraction and RMS-of-difference timeline computed in ffmpeg.wasm
rationale: Finds re-dubbed lines, added music, or muted sections without listening end to end.

name: video-overlay-diff-locator
description: Compares two versions to locate a persistent added region such as a logo, watermark, or burned-in caption.
example_prompt: Find where a watermark was added between these two versions
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — temporally averaged blend=difference isolates the static overlay box in ffmpeg.wasm
rationale: Pinpoints overlay placement so it can be cropped, blurred, or flagged.

name: format-only-hunk-filter
description: Classifies each hunk of a diff as whitespace/formatting-only versus semantic and can drop the noise.
example_prompt: Filter out the formatting-only changes from this diff
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — per-hunk normalization and comparison runs client-side
rationale: Reformatting commits drown real changes; separating cosmetic hunks focuses review on logic.

name: normalized-diff
description: Diffs two texts after configurable normalization such as lowercasing, punctuation stripping, and whitespace collapse.
example_prompt: Diff these two quotes but ignore case and punctuation differences
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — normalize both sides then run the standard diff engine
rationale: Often only substantive changes matter, and normalizing first removes cosmetic noise from the comparison.

name: audio-stereo-widener
description: Widens or narrows the stereo image via mid/side balance adjustment.
example_prompt: Make this stereo mix sound a bit wider.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg stereotools/extrastereo mid-side processing; runs locally.
rationale: Stereo width control is a common mix-polish transform with no current standalone tool.

name: audio-surround-downmix
description: Downmixes 5.1/7.1 surround audio to stereo with standard coefficients.
example_prompt: Downmix this 5.1 audio track to stereo.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg pan/aresample channel matrix; entirely in-browser.
rationale: Surround-to-stereo is a frequent compatibility conversion for playback and editing with no catalog tool.

name: audio-plosive-remover
description: Detects and attenuates low-frequency plosive 'p'/'b' bursts in vocal recordings.
example_prompt: Soften the popping P sounds in this vocal take.
loader_feasibility: pyodide finds low-band transient bursts and applies a localized high-pass/duck with scipy, all local.
rationale: De-popping plosives is a tedious manual vocal fix that targeted automation makes fast and is unserved by the catalog.

name: anchor-rel-fixer
description: Adds rel="noopener noreferrer" to every target="_blank" anchor missing it.
example_prompt: Fix the target=_blank links in this HTML to add rel=noopener
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM anchor scan + attribute patch; runs in the browser.
rationale: Unprotected _blank links are a known reverse-tabnabbing security hole that should be patched in bulk.

name: counts-to-proportions
description: Converts a counts column into proportions or percentages of the total, with optional grouping key.
example_prompt: Turn these category counts into percentages of the total
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sum + divide, fully local
rationale: Going from raw tallies to a share-of-total is a constant reporting transform.

name: running-extrema
description: Computes expanding or fixed-window rolling minimum, maximum, or range across a numeric series.
example_prompt: Add a 7-row rolling max column for this series
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — monotonic-deque window scan, fully local
rationale: Rolling min/max (drawdown, peaks) is common in finance and sensors but absent from simple tools.

name: numeric-row-deduper
description: Drops near-duplicate numeric rows that match within a chosen absolute or relative tolerance, keeping one representative.
example_prompt: Remove rows that are duplicates within 0.001 of each other
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tolerance bucketing/sort, no network
rationale: Float jitter defeats exact dedup, so tolerant numeric dedup is a real and unmet cleanup need.

name: data-line-chart-animation
description: Generates a video of a line chart being drawn progressively over time from CSV columns.
example_prompt: Animate this CSV's revenue column being drawn out over 8 seconds
loader_feasibility: pyodide renders incremental matplotlib frames in the sandbox and ffmpeg encodes them client-side.
rationale: A reveal-style animated chart makes data slides far more engaging and there is no local one-step generator for it.

name: scrolling-credits-video
description: Generates an end-credits roll video that scrolls a supplied list of names and roles bottom-to-top.
example_prompt: Make a 30-second scrolling credits roll from this cast-and-crew list
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg `drawtext` with a time-based y-position expression scrolls the rendered text over a synthetic background in-browser.
rationale: A proper credits roll is expected on finished videos and building one by hand in an editor is tedious and error-prone.

name: png-to-indexed
description: Quantizes a truecolor image into a palette-indexed PNG (≤256 colors) for smaller files.
example_prompt: Make this PNG an indexed 256-color png to shrink it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: median-cut/neuquant quantization plus indexed PNG encoding run client-side.
rationale: Indexed PNGs are dramatically smaller for flat graphics and UI assets, but no easy local quantizer exists.

name: realaudio-to-wav
description: Decodes legacy RealAudio (.ra/.rm) clips to PCM WAV.
example_prompt: convert this old realaudio .rm file to wav
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader demuxes RealMedia and decodes the audio to WAV entirely client-side.
rationale: Decades of archived RealAudio streams are unplayable without a dedicated, now-rare decoder.

name: wave64-to-wav
description: Converts a Sony Wave64 (.w64) file to a standard RIFF WAV when it fits under 4 GB.
example_prompt: convert this w64 file to a regular wav
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — reads the 64-bit GUID chunk headers and rewrites RIFF chunks, no server.
rationale: Wave64 from pro recorders is rejected by many editors that only accept ordinary WAV.

name: prompt-template-filler
description: Fills {{variable}} placeholders in a prompt template from supplied values and reports missing ones.
example_prompt: Fill this prompt template with my variables
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM template substitution over pasted text; deterministic and local.
rationale: Reflects fabric/AIChat reusable-prompt patterns as a simple offline utility.

name: snippet-template-filler
description: Defines a parameterized command/snippet template with named placeholders and fills them in to produce the final ready-to-run text.
example_prompt: I have a docker run template with {{image}} and {{port}} placeholders — fill it with nginx and 8080.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: placeholder detection and substitution are pure string operations.
rationale: bkmr and sunbeam both center on parameterized snippets, and a safe, local placeholder filler beats hand-editing long commands.

name: format-agnostic-query
description: Run jq-style filters over YAML, TOML, XML, or CSV by parsing them to JSON first.
example_prompt: Query this YAML config with '.services | keys'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — format crates normalize the input to a serde value and the jaq engine applies the filter, all client-side.
rationale: faq/zq demand shows people want jq's power over non-JSON formats without converting by hand first.

name: structural-code-diff
description: Diffs two code snippets by their syntax tree so reordered or reformatted code shows only the real logic changes, ignoring whitespace and line-wrapping noise.
example_prompt: Show me a structural diff of these two versions of my function: <paste A> vs <paste B>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tree-sitter grammars compile to WASM and an AST-alignment pass runs entirely client-side, like Difftastic.
rationale: Line-based diffs drown real changes in formatting noise; a syntax-aware diff is the most-requested diff upgrade and no existing gizza tool does AST-level comparison.

name: rt60-estimator
description: Estimates reverberation time (RT60/RT30/EDT) from a recorded room impulse response.
example_prompt: Estimate the RT60 of this room from my impulse-response recording
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Schroeder backward integration and a linear fit run entirely in wasm.
rationale: RT60 estimation is a primary acoustics/pyroomacoustics task for room and venue characterization.

name: harmonic-percussive-split
description: Separates a recording into its harmonic (melodic) and percussive (drum) layers.
example_prompt: Split this into melody and drums layers.
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM applies median-filter HPSS on the STFT of ffmpeg-decoded audio and resynthesizes both stems locally.
rationale: HPSS is a signature librosa capability useful for remixing, drum extraction, and karaoke-style processing.

name: glsl-image-filter
description: Applies a user-supplied GLSL fragment-shader filter to an uploaded image.
example_prompt: Apply this custom shader filter to my photo: <image> <GLSL>
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute samples the input texture and runs the shader pass on the GPU entirely in-browser.
rationale: WebGL devs prototype post-processing effects on real images, and this gives instant local feedback.

name: stereo-pair-split
description: Splits a side-by-side or over-under stereoscopic VR image into separate left and right eye images.
example_prompt: Split this side-by-side VR photo into left and right images
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM image crop using the image crate; pure pixel ops.
rationale: VR/WebXR content authors regularly need to separate or inspect stereo eye images.

name: lnk-parser
description: Decodes Windows .lnk shortcut files to reveal target paths, volume serials, MAC timestamps, and machine IDs.
example_prompt: What original file and machine does this .lnk shortcut point to?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the Shell Link binary structure is fully parsed from uploaded bytes, no host access required.
rationale: LNK files reveal opened files and removable-media history, a core Zimmerman LECmd use case usable in seconds.

name: jumplist-parser
description: Parses AutomaticDestinations/CustomDestinations jump lists to recover recently opened files per application.
example_prompt: What files were recently opened in Word according to these jump lists?
