loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: jump lists are OLE compound files containing LNK streams, both parsed from the upload with no host access.
rationale: Jump lists tie file access to specific apps and survive deletion, a staple of user-activity analysis (JLECmd).

name: shimcache-parser
description: Decodes the AppCompatCache (Shimcache) from a SYSTEM hive to list executables seen by the system.
example_prompt: Extract the shimcache execution entries from this SYSTEM hive
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Shimcache is a binary value inside the registry hive, parsed in-memory from the upload.
rationale: Shimcache is a key execution-evidence source attackers rarely clean, directly mapping Zimmerman AppCompatCacheParser.

name: recyclebin-parser
description: Parses $I recycle-bin metadata files to recover original deleted-file paths, sizes, and deletion timestamps.
example_prompt: What was the original name and delete time of this $I recycle bin file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: $I files are a tiny fixed binary structure parsed entirely from the upload.
rationale: Deleted-file metadata is routinely needed and the $I format (RBCmd) is trivial to parse browser-local.

name: srum-parser
description: Parses the SRUDB.dat ESE database to report per-application network bytes, app usage, and timing.
example_prompt: Which app sent the most network data according to this SRUM database?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: SRUM is an ESE (EDB) database parsed from the uploaded file with a pure-Rust ESE reader, no host access.
rationale: SRUM uniquely links data exfiltration volumes to applications (SrumECmd), valuable but ESE parsing is involved.

name: windows-timeline-parser
description: Parses the ActivitiesCache.db Windows Timeline to list app/document activities with start and end times.
example_prompt: Show the user's app activity timeline from this ActivitiesCache.db
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the file is a SQLite database read with a pure-Rust SQLite engine compiled to wasm.
rationale: Windows Timeline reconstructs detailed user activity (Zimmerman WxTCmd) and is awkward to query by hand.

name: dedupe-against-reference
description: Removes from one list every line that also appears in a reference list, returning only the unique remainder.
example_prompt: remove from this list anything already in my reference list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM hash-set subtraction; pure computation
rationale: Filtering a list against a known set is a common cleanup task with no native tool.

name: image-stack-median
description: Median-stacks a set of aligned photos of the same scene to remove transient objects like passing people or cars.
example_prompt: Remove the tourists from these 10 shots of the same landmark by median stacking.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes the per-pixel median across the stack entirely in-browser.
rationale: Median stacking is the standard trick for a clean empty-scene plate and there's no client-side tool for it yet.

name: video-perframe-quality-csv
description: Exports per-frame PSNR, SSIM, and VMAF of a distorted video versus its reference as a single CSV for plotting and analysis.
example_prompt: Give me a CSV of per-frame PSNR and SSIM comparing my encode to the master
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM runs the quality filters per frame locally and a plain-Rust block merges the streams into one CSV.
rationale: Per-frame data lets encoders find the exact worst frames, which the existing overall-score reports can't expose.

name: video-ab-montage-export
description: Builds an alternating A/B montage that cuts between two versions every N seconds with on-screen labels for review.
example_prompt: Make a montage that switches between version A and version B every 4 seconds
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM concat/trim and drawtext filters assemble the alternating montage entirely in-browser.
rationale: An alternating-cut review reel is a fast, shareable way to A/B two grades or encodes without a synchronized side-by-side player.

name: video-difference-stats-timeline
description: Computes per-frame mean and max pixel difference between two videos and exports the magnitude timeline as CSV.
example_prompt: Give me a timeline of how big the pixel difference is between these two videos
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM blend-difference plus signalstats produces per-frame difference magnitudes locally, merged to CSV by a plain-Rust block.
rationale: Raw difference magnitude over time complements similarity scores by quantifying *how much* changed at each moment, not just whether it matched.

name: loudness-matched-ab-export
description: Measures the LUFS of two files, applies gain so they match, and exports both for a fair, level-matched A/B comparison.
example_prompt: Loudness-match these two masters so I can A/B them fairly
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM measures LUFS and rescales PCM, re-encoding WAV locally (ffmpeg for compressed output).
rationale: Louder always sounds 'better', so level-matching is the prerequisite for any honest A/B test.

name: sarif-diff
description: Compares two SARIF static-analysis runs and reports newly-introduced, fixed, and persisting findings so a CI baseline can gate only on new issues.
example_prompt: Diff these two SARIF reports and show me which findings are new since the baseline
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses both SARIF JSON files and matches results by rule+location fingerprint entirely in-browser; no scanner or server needed.
rationale: Baseline-vs-new gating is the standard way teams adopt SAST without drowning in legacy findings, and there is no two-run SARIF diff in the catalog (only a single-file parser).

name: vuln-report-diff
description: Compares two dependency-vulnerability reports (npm audit, pip-audit, or OSV JSON) and separates newly-introduced advisories from those that were fixed.
example_prompt: Diff yesterday's npm audit JSON against today's and show only the new vulnerabilities
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses both advisory JSON files and matches by advisory ID + package locally; it is offline report comparison, not a live scan.
rationale: Distinguishing new CVEs from a known backlog is exactly what unblocks audit-gated CI, and this differs from the existing component-level SBOM diff.

name: json-three-way-merge
description: Performs a structural three-way merge of base/yours/theirs JSON documents, auto-merging non-conflicting changes and marking real value conflicts.
example_prompt: Three-way merge these JSON config files: base, mine, and theirs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM walks all three JSON trees and applies path-level merge logic in-browser; it is in-memory data manipulation.
rationale: Git's line-based 3-way merge mangles reformatted JSON; a structural merge resolves config conflicts the text merge can't, and only a text 3-way merge exists.

name: keyed-snapshot-diff
description: Diffs two CSV snapshots joined on an id column, reporting added rows, removed rows, and per-field numeric deltas for changed rows.
example_prompt: Diff yesterday's and today's inventory CSVs by SKU and show the quantity changes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: keyed join and field comparison, fully local
rationale: Comparing two dataset snapshots by key is a frequent ops task that text diff can't do meaningfully for numbers.

name: ioc-format-parser
description: Parses OpenIOC, STIX, and MISP indicator bundles into a flat, readable table of typed indicators.
example_prompt: Show me the indicators inside this OpenIOC file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — XML/JSON parsing only
rationale: Redline exports OpenIOC that feeds Loki/THOR, and reading those bundles without a heavy DFIR suite is genuinely useful.

name: utmp-parser
description: Parses Linux utmp/wtmp/btmp records into a login/logout history with users, terminals, hosts, and times.
example_prompt: Show me the login history from this wtmp file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — fixed-size C-struct record parsing
rationale: Login records are a top artifact unix_collector/UAC grab for building intrusion timelines.

name: macos-unified-log-parser
description: Parses macOS Unified Logging .tracev3 / .logarchive entries into human-readable, timestamped log lines.
example_prompt: Convert this .logarchive into readable log lines
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pure-Rust tracev3 decoding (macos-unifiedlogs) runs entirely client-side.
rationale: Unified logs are the richest macOS timeline source but notoriously hard to read, so mac_apt-grade decoding offline is high value.

name: ios-usage-timeline
description: Analyzes iOS knowledgeC.db and app-usage SQLite to produce a device-activity and app-launch timeline.
example_prompt: Build an app-usage timeline from this knowledgeC.db
loader_feasibility: pyodide: bundled sqlite3 reads the uploaded database and reconstructs the timeline in-sandbox.
rationale: knowledgeC analysis (iLEAPP/ArtEx) is central to iOS investigations and runs fully on-device here.

name: android-usagestats-parser
description: Parses Android usagestats protobuf and app SQLite/XML artifacts into structured app-usage and event records.
example_prompt: Parse these Android usagestats files into an event list
loader_feasibility: pyodide: protobuf and sqlite3 decoding of the uploaded artifacts, all client-side.
rationale: Reproduces ALEAPP's core protobuf/SQLite parsing for Android timelines without a server.

name: semantic-cluster
description: Embeds a list of documents and clusters them into topics, labeling each cluster with representative terms.
example_prompt: Group these 200 article titles into topics.
loader_feasibility: transformers-js sentence embeddings + plain-Rust k-means; both run fully in-browser.
rationale: Topic clustering of text is a marquee modern-DS capability that's still feasible locally on modest corpora.

name: text-augmenter
description: Augments training text with synonym replacement, random swap/deletion, and shuffling (EDA techniques).
example_prompt: Generate 5 augmented variants of this training sentence.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; rule-based transforms over a bundled synonym/WordNet-lite list, fully local.
rationale: Data augmentation expands small labeled sets, a practical need for the 'how to label data' and training-from-scratch demand.

name: chinese-keyword-extractor
description: Extracts top keywords/keyphrases from Chinese text using TF-IDF and TextRank over segmented tokens.
example_prompt: Pull the main keywords out of this Chinese article.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — segmentation plus graph ranking, all computed locally.
rationale: Reproduces jieba.analyse keyword extraction, useful for tagging and SEO entirely in the browser.

name: spanish-profanity-filter
description: Detects and masks Spanish profanity, including leetspeak and obfuscated spellings.
example_prompt: Censor any Spanish swear words in this comment.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bundled bad-word lexicon plus normalization/leet-decoding logic, offline.
rationale: Directly serves the spanlp demand for client-side moderation that never ships user text to a server.

name: vietnamese-diacritic-restorer
description: Adds missing tone marks and diacritics to un-accented Vietnamese text (e.g. 'Toi yeu tieng Viet' → 'Tôi yêu tiếng Việt').
example_prompt: Add Vietnamese accents to: chuc mung nam moi
loader_feasibility: transformers.js: a Vietnamese seq2seq/diacritic-restoration ONNX model runs client-side
rationale: Vietnamese is constantly typed without accents, and restoring them by hand is tedious and error-prone.

name: mbox-search
description: Full-text search across an mbox archive with sender, subject, and date filters.
example_prompt: Search my mbox for emails from alice about invoices
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM builds an in-memory index and queries it client-side.
rationale: Notmuch-style search over your archive without installing Notmuch or exposing your mail.

name: video-set-profile-level
description: Re-encodes H.264 to a specific profile and level (e.g. baseline 3.0) for constrained-device playback.
example_prompt: Encode this to H.264 baseline profile level 3.0
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg-wasm sets -profile:v/-level during a local libx264 encode.
rationale: Old TVs, set-top boxes, and embedded players require specific profile/level limits.

name: video-metadata-tag-editor
description: Edits container metadata fields like title, artist, comment, and description without re-encoding.
example_prompt: Set the title and comment metadata on this mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg-wasm writes container metadata via stream copy locally.
rationale: Stripping exists but there's no tool to set clean, correct tags for organizing a library.

name: video-rotation-metadata-set
description: Sets the display-rotation matrix metadata (90/180/270) so players rotate on playback without re-encoding pixels.
example_prompt: Tag this phone video to rotate 90 degrees on playback
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg-wasm writes the rotate display-matrix via stream copy in-browser.
rationale: Reading and baking rotation exist, but setting the lightweight metadata flag without re-encoding is the cheaper fix.

name: rename-template
description: Renames a name list from a template with placeholders like {name}, {ext}, {num:03}, and {date}.
example_prompt: Rename these using template '{num:03}-{name}{ext}'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM template engine over pasted names; no host access required
rationale: Tempren's template-driven renaming is its whole value proposition and maps cleanly to a client-side string formatter.

name: filename-sequencer
description: Adds zero-padded sequential numbers to a filename list with configurable start, step, prefix, and suffix.
example_prompt: Number these photos as 001, 002, 003 keeping the extension
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM counter logic on pasted text; trivially local
rationale: Sequential numbering is the single most-requested batch-rename operation and is pure text math.

name: media-info-renamer
description: Reads video metadata (resolution, codec, duration) via ffprobe and renames files like 'Title [1080p][h264].mp4'.
example_prompt: Rename these videos to include their resolution and codec
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg/ffprobe loader inspects dropped video bytes client-side without uploading
rationale: Media library managers tag files by stream properties, a deterministic local probe ffmpeg already does.

name: http-from-pcap
description: Reassembles TCP streams in an uploaded pcap to reconstruct full HTTP request/response transactions with timings.
example_prompt: extract the HTTP requests and responses from this pcap capture
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pcap parsing plus TCP stream reassembly of the uploaded file, fully offline.
rationale: Maps Kyanos's application-layer traffic analysis to a privacy-preserving HTTP extractor in the browser.

name: ml-dsa-sign
description: Generates ML-DSA (Dilithium) post-quantum keys and signs or verifies messages.
example_prompt: sign this message with ml-dsa post-quantum
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (RustCrypto ml-dsa crate); lattice signing/verification in-page.
rationale: Post-quantum signatures are the companion to ML-KEM in noble-post-quantum/Flexiprovider and let users try NIST PQC standards offline.

name: rncryptor-decrypt
description: Decrypts an RNCryptor v3 password-encrypted payload back to plaintext after HMAC verification.
example_prompt: decrypt this rncryptor base64 with password pass123
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reimplementing the RNCryptor v3 unwrap with RustCrypto primitives; browser-local.
rationale: Developers migrating off the RNCryptor library need to read its existing ciphertext locally and safely.

name: survey-report-builder
description: Takes a CSV export of survey responses and builds a per-question report with option counts, percentages, text bar charts, and a listing of open-text answers.
example_prompt: Summarize this Google Forms responses CSV question by question
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the CSV and tallies per column; all computation is local, nothing uploaded.
rationale: Google Forms/Typeform/Wufoo/Zoho exports are raw CSVs that nobody wants to hand-pivot into a readable summary.

name: form-to-webhook-formatter
description: Turns submitted form fields into a formatted Slack, Discord, or Telegram webhook payload.
example_prompt: Format these form fields into a Slack message payload: name=Ann, topic=Billing
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON templating — builds the payload string locally; user posts it from their own endpoint.
rationale: Mirrors Form2Channel's core value (form → chat channel) without routing data through a third party.

name: crypto-address-validate
description: Validates and checksums crypto addresses (BTC bech32/legacy, ETH EIP-55) offline and flags malformed or wrong-network ones.
example_prompt: is this a valid checksummed Ethereum address: 0xAbC...?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — base58/bech32 decode and EIP-55 checksum verification, all deterministic math, no network.
rationale: Catching a typo before sending to an address is critical, and the validation is pure local computation.

name: json-join
description: Joins two JSON arrays on a key (inner/left/outer) like a RethinkDB eqJoin and returns the merged records.
example_prompt: Join my users array to my orders array on userId
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM hash-join over serde_json arrays; all in-memory in the browser.
rationale: Joining related JSON collections is exactly what RethinkDB/Mongo $lookup users want and there is no simple browser-local way to do it.

name: jsonselect-query
description: Queries JSON with CSS-style selectors (JSONSelect), e.g. selecting all values of a given type or key.
example_prompt: Use a CSS-like JSONSelect '.name' selector to grab every name in this JSON.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM selector engine over the parsed tree, fully client-side.
rationale: Front-end devs already think in CSS selectors, making this an intuitive JSON query mode.

name: json-template-populate
description: Fills a JSON (or text) template's placeholders from a data object (JSON-populate).
example_prompt: Populate this template {"to":"{{email}}"} with data {"email":"a@b.com"}.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM placeholder substitution over the parsed template, no network.
rationale: Template-driven payload generation is common for emails, requests, and fixtures.

name: exposure-clipping-checker
description: Builds a luminance histogram and reports the percentage of blown-out highlights and crushed shadows (over/under-exposure).
example_prompt: Is this photo over- or under-exposed?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes pixels and bins luminance in-browser.
rationale: Clipped highlights/shadows are unrecoverable and a numeric check is more reliable than eyeballing.

name: color-banding-detector
description: Scans gradients for stair-step quantization (banding) and reports affected regions and severity.
example_prompt: Check this gradient image for color banding
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute runs a gradient/derivative pass over the decoded pixels on the device GPU.
rationale: Banding shows up after compression or 8-bit conversion and a detector quantifies a usually-subjective flaw.

name: letterbox-bar-detector
description: Detects black/solid letterbox or pillarbox bars in an image and reports the true content rectangle.
example_prompt: Does this screenshot have black letterbox bars?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes pixels and scans top/bottom/side rows for solid bars in-browser.
rationale: Letterboxed captures ruin thumbnails and a detector flags them so the real frame can be used.

name: truncated-image-detector
description: Attempts a full decode and reports whether an image is truncated, ending in gray/garbage rows partway down.
example_prompt: Is this image cut off or truncated?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs an in-memory decoder and detects incomplete scan data client-side.
rationale: Half-transferred images decode partially and look fine in thumbnails; a full-decode test catches the cutoff.

name: video-letterbox-detector
description: Detects baked-in black bars and reports the actual active picture crop region and aspect ratio.
example_prompt: Does this video have black bars baked in, and what's the real crop?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: the cropdetect filter measures bar extents in ffmpeg.wasm in-browser.
rationale: Hidden letterboxing wastes resolution and breaks reframing; detecting the true crop is the first step to fixing it.

name: instagram-video-spec-checker
description: Checks a video's aspect ratio, duration, resolution, and codec against Instagram feed and Reels requirements.
example_prompt: Will this video pass Instagram Reels requirements?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: ffprobe properties from ffmpeg.wasm are validated against IG rules client-side.
rationale: Instagram silently crops or rejects off-spec videos, so creators want to verify before posting.

name: streaming-loudness-target-checker
description: Compares a track's integrated LUFS and true-peak against Spotify, YouTube, Apple Music, and Tidal targets and reports how much each platform will turn it up or down.
example_prompt: Is this song too loud for Spotify? What will it get normalized to?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: reuses the BS.1770 loudness measurement and compares to a built-in target table client-side
rationale: Mixing engineers want to predict per-platform normalization without uploading unreleased music anywhere.

name: silence-region-detector
description: Finds leading, trailing, and internal silence regions below a chosen threshold and reports their timestamps and durations.
example_prompt: Find the silent gaps in this recording and the dead air at the start and end
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: RMS-windowed threshold scan over decoded PCM, no server required
rationale: Excess head/tail silence and dead air are common QC issues for podcasts and stems before publishing.

name: audio-spec-validator
description: Checks a file's sample rate, bit depth, channel count, and codec against a required delivery profile and returns per-field pass/fail.
example_prompt: Verify this file is 48kHz 24-bit stereo as required for delivery
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: read stream parameters from the container header and compare to a user-given profile client-side
rationale: Spec-mismatched deliverables get rejected; a quick profile check enforces requirements before submission.

name: id3-tag-linter
description: Lints ID3v1/ID3v2 tags for missing required fields, malformed frames, encoding mismatches, and inconsistent track/disc numbering.
example_prompt: Lint the ID3 tags on this MP3 and list what's missing or broken
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse ID3 frames from the file bytes and apply validation rules, no server needed
rationale: Inconsistent or broken tags break library organization, and a lint pass enumerates exactly what to fix.

name: audio-qc-report
description: Runs a full pre-release QC sweep in one pass — clipping, true-peak, DC offset, loudness, phase, silence, channel balance — and returns a consolidated pass/fail checklist.
example_prompt: Run a full QC check on this master before I release it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a single decode feeding all the individual DSP checks, run entirely client-side
rationale: A one-shot consolidated checklist is what mastering engineers actually want before signing off on a deliverable.

name: ui-screenshot-theme-extractor
description: Extracts an app/website screenshot's color theme — background, surface, text, and accent roles — into design tokens.
example_prompt: Extract the color theme (bg, text, accent) from this app screenshot
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: region sampling plus role heuristics (largest area = background, high-contrast = text) over the pixel buffer runs on CPU.
rationale: Replicating a UI's palette into design tokens is a common front-end task, more structured than a flat dominant-color list.

name: id3v2-frame-dump
description: Lists every ID3v2 frame in an MP3 with its four-character ID, byte size, flags, and a decoded preview, exposing duplicates and unknown frames.
example_prompt: Dump all the ID3v2 frames in this file with their IDs and sizes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — walks the ID3v2 header and frame list by parsing synchsafe sizes, no audio decode.
rationale: A raw frame inventory is the fastest way to diagnose bloated tags, duplicate frames, or non-standard player-specific data.

name: flac-cuesheet-extractor
description: Extracts an embedded FLAC CUESHEET metadata block and converts it back to a standard .cue sheet file.
example_prompt: Export the embedded cue sheet from this flac album
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the binary CUESHEET block (tracks, indices, ISRC) and serializes to cue text.
rationale: Single-file FLAC rips store track boundaries in a CUESHEET block that few tools can export.

name: matroska-tags-reader
description: Reads Matroska \Tags\ SimpleTag entries (title, artist, replaygain, custom fields) into structured JSON with their target scopes.
example_prompt: What tags are stored in this mka file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — locates the Tags EBML element and decodes nested SimpleTag name/value pairs.
rationale: Matroska tagging is scoped and nested unlike ID3/Vorbis, so generic tag readers can't surface it.

name: id3-chapter-reader
description: Parses ID3v2 CHAP and CTOC frames into a nested chapter table with start/end times, titles, and embedded chapter images.
example_prompt: Extract the podcast chapters from this mp3's ID3 tags
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — decodes CHAP/CTOC frames and their nested sub-frames from the ID3v2 tag bytes.
rationale: Podcast chapter markers live in CHAP/CTOC frames that generic chapter tools and tag editors rarely decode.

name: blur-detect
description: Measure image sharpness (variance-of-Laplacian) and flag blurry/out-of-focus photos with a score.
example_prompt: is this photo too blurry to use?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust (image crate) to WASM — fast pure compute.
rationale: Bulk photo culling needs a quick sharpness check and it is trivially feasible locally.

name: whiteboard-enhance
description: Clean up a photo of a whiteboard: remove shadows/glare, boost ink contrast, and flatten to white.
example_prompt: Clean up this whiteboard photo so the writing is readable
loader_feasibility: Plain-Rust adaptive-threshold/illumination correction; offline.
rationale: Classic 'Office Lens' feature complementing the document-scan tool.

name: changelog-from-diff
description: Generates a human-readable changelog of additions, deletions, and edits by diffing two versions of a document.
example_prompt: Write a changelog summarizing what changed between these two versions of my README
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — compute the diff and template the changes into bullet lists in-process
rationale: Auto-deriving a change list from two versions saves manual changelog authoring.

name: image-crossfade-gif
description: Generates a smooth crossfade transition GIF/WebP between two images for before-after reveals.
example_prompt: Crossfade between the original and the retouched version as a gif
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader interpolates and encodes the transition frames in WASM, no server
rationale: Crossfade reveals are a popular shareable format for showing edits.

name: burst-photo-best-pick
description: Compares a burst of near-identical shots and ranks them by sharpness/blur to pick the keeper.
example_prompt: From these 8 burst shots pick the sharpest one
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scores each image's high-frequency energy and ranks them in-browser
rationale: Choosing the sharpest frame from a burst is tedious by eye and a perfect local task.

name: image-compression-artifact-diff
description: Compares an original and a compressed copy to visualize and locate the blocking, ringing, and banding the compression added.
example_prompt: Show me where compression damaged this image versus the original
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM diffs the pair and emphasizes 8×8 block and edge-ringing residuals locally
rationale: Pinpoints which regions a codec hurt so quality settings can be tuned.

name: video-difference-mask-export
description: Thresholds the difference between two videos into a binary black/white mask video marking changed regions.
example_prompt: Export a motion mask of what changed between these two clips
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg difference blend plus a threshold/lutyuv stage produces the mask in-browser.
rationale: A binary change mask feeds downstream compositing or QA without manual rotoscoping.

name: video-frame-similarity-timeline
description: Produces a timeline graph/JSON of per-second similarity between two videos to show where they diverge.
example_prompt: Plot how similar the two cuts stay over time
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg ssim/phash per interval plus Rust→WASM aggregation builds the timeline client-side.
rationale: A divergence timeline pinpoints exactly which moments two versions stop matching.

name: video-quality-regression-flag
description: Flags the timestamps where per-frame SSIM/PSNR against a reference drops below a chosen threshold.
example_prompt: List the moments where the encode quality drops badly versus the master
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg emits per-frame metric logs and Rust→WASM thresholds them into timestamp ranges locally.
rationale: Surfacing only the worst-quality segments turns a metric dump into actionable QA.

name: video-audio-fingerprint-match
description: Computes acoustic fingerprints for two videos' audio and reports whether and where they share the same sound.
example_prompt: Do these two videos contain the same audio track?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes audio and Rust→WASM computes chromaprint-style fingerprints and matches them locally.
rationale: Audio fingerprint matching identifies reused or duplicated soundtracks without exact-byte equality.

name: video-audio-waveform-compare
description: Renders the two videos' audio waveforms overlaid or stacked to visually compare levels and timing.
example_prompt: Show the waveforms of both takes on top of each other
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg showwavespic generates each waveform image and overlays them in the wasm build.
rationale: A side-by-side waveform makes level and timing mismatches obvious before deep analysis.

name: video-color-grade-diff
description: Estimates the tone/color transform between an ungraded and graded version and summarizes the per-channel shift.
example_prompt: What did the colorist change between the raw and final versions?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg samples matched frames and Rust→WASM fits a per-channel transfer curve locally.
rationale: Quantifying a grade as a reusable transform helps replicate or audit color decisions.

name: video-thumbnail-compare-strip
description: Builds a strip of thumbnails sampled at matched timestamps from two videos for quick visual A/B scanning.
example_prompt: Make a thumbnail strip comparing both versions at the same timecodes
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg extracts and tiles matched-timestamp frames from both inputs in the wasm build.
rationale: A matched-timecode strip lets reviewers eyeball whole-video differences in one image.

name: silence-segment-diff
description: Computes voiced/silent segmentation for two recordings and diffs the segment boundaries to reveal edits, trims, or inserted pauses.
example_prompt: Show me where the edited podcast differs in pauses from the raw recording
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: energy-gate VAD on both files, segment-list diff, local
rationale: Detecting cuts/inserts between an edit and its source is a real podcast/QA need with no quick tool.

name: spectrogram-image-diff
description: Renders both files' spectrograms and a difference heatmap so you can see exactly which frequencies/times changed.
example_prompt: Show me a heatmap of what the EQ changed between these two versions
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: STFT both signals, render magnitude diff to an image buffer in-browser
rationale: A visual frequency-domain diff makes processing changes obvious in a way numbers can't.

name: duplicate-across-datasets
description: Finds records that appear in both of two datasets (exact or normalized key match) to detect overlap or double-counting.
example_prompt: Find any records that exist in both of these two CSV exports
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; normalize keys and intersect via hash sets entirely in memory
rationale: Detecting overlap between sources prevents double-counting in merges and is awkward without SQL.

name: jsonl-dataset-diff
description: Diffs two JSONL datasets keyed by a chosen id field, reporting added, removed, and changed records.
example_prompt: Compare these two JSONL files keyed by the id field and show changed records
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: stream-parse both files line by line, key by field, and diff records locally
rationale: Single-document JSON diff can't handle record-keyed JSONL datasets, which ML and data work use heavily.

name: alpha-bbox-cropper
description: Crops a transparent PNG tightly to the bounding box of its non-transparent pixels.
example_prompt: Crop this logo PNG to remove the empty transparent space around it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: scan the alpha channel for min/max non-zero rows/cols and slice the buffer.
rationale: Exported sprites and logos carry transparent padding; tight cropping is a constant asset-prep chore.

name: image-background-color-replacer
description: Replaces a near-uniform background color in an image with a different chosen color.
example_prompt: Change the light gray background of this product shot to pure white
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: flood/color-tolerance mask from the edges, then recolor masked pixels in-memory.
rationale: Standardizing product-shot backgrounds to white is a routine e-commerce task that needs no ML for solid backgrounds.

name: audio-notch-filter
description: Surgically removes a single offending frequency (e.g. a 1 kHz whine) with a narrow notch.
example_prompt: Kill the annoying high-pitched whine around 2.1 kHz
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg equalizer/bandreject with high Q; pure DSP in wasm
rationale: A precise notch removes tonal interference that broadband denoise leaves behind.

name: audio-channel-extract
description: Extracts a single channel (left or right) from a stereo file as a mono output.
example_prompt: Pull just the right channel out of this stereo interview
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg pan to select one channel; plain PCM selection in wasm
rationale: Dual-mono recordings (two mics on L/R) often need one channel isolated.

name: audio-mid-side-convert
description: Encodes L/R into mid-side (or decodes M/S back to L/R) for surgical stereo processing.
example_prompt: Convert this stereo file into mid-side channels
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM M=(L+R)/2, S=(L−R)/2 (and inverse); pure math
rationale: M/S encoding lets users EQ or balance the center vs sides independently.

name: audio-channel-balance-fix
description: Measures and auto-corrects a left/right level imbalance so both channels match.
example_prompt: The left channel is louder than the right — even them out
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM RMS-per-channel measure + gain correction; pure math
rationale: Lopsided stereo from a tilted mic or bad gain is fixed automatically rather than just flagged.

name: plink-ped-to-csv
description: Reads PLINK .ped/.map genotype pairs and emits a tidy CSV of samples × SNPs with optional allele-pair collapsing into 0/1/2 dosages.
example_prompt: Convert this PLINK ped and map pair into a genotype CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: whitespace-delimited genotype text joined against the map file, all in-browser.
rationale: Statistical-genetics newcomers struggle to get PLINK genotypes into a normal dataframe, and the per-SNP allele pairing is hard to do by hand.

name: jsonl-sampler
description: Takes a representative subset of a large JSONL file by head, random reservoir, or per-key stratified sampling with a seed.
example_prompt: Give me a random 1000-line sample of this JSONL file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: single-pass reservoir sampling over the line stream, computed locally.
rationale: Inspecting or testing against a huge NDJSON dataset needs a reproducible sample, and the backlog only samples CSV rows, not JSONL.

name: jsonl-shuffler
description: Randomly reorders the records of a JSONL/NDJSON file with a deterministic seed, for shuffling training data without loading it all into memory.
example_prompt: Shuffle the lines of this JSONL training file with seed 42
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: seeded permutation of line offsets, fully client-side.
rationale: Shuffling ordered NDJSON exports before train/test splits is standard ML prep; only line shuffling for plain text exists, not record-aware JSONL with a seed.

name: json-field-coalescer
description: Merges several alternative keys in each JSON object into one canonical field by taking the first non-null value, then drops the originals.
example_prompt: In this JSON, coalesce email, Email, and e_mail into one email field
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: per-object key resolution over parsed JSON, no server.
rationale: Merged datasets accumulate synonymous keys from different sources, and collapsing them to a canonical field is a frequent cleanup with no current tool.

name: log-strip-timestamps
description: Removes leading timestamps and log-level prefixes so two log runs can be diffed cleanly.
example_prompt: strip the timestamps off these log lines so I can compare runs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM matches common timestamp/level patterns at line start and removes them locally
rationale: Timestamp noise makes log diffs useless; stripping it reveals the real behavioral delta.

name: truncate-decimals
description: Truncates (rounds toward zero) each value to N decimal places without rounding up.
example_prompt: Truncate these values to 2 decimals without rounding
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: scale, trunc, unscale per element, offline
rationale: Truncation differs semantically from rounding and is required for things like financial truncation rules.

name: hex-to-pem
description: Wraps DER hex bytes back into PEM format with a chosen label and 64-char line folding.
example_prompt: wrap this DER hex into a PEM certificate block
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — hex decode, base64 encode, and line wrapping, all in-memory
rationale: Reconstructing PEM from raw bytes is a recurring need for tooling that only outputs DER, and it's privacy-sensitive.

name: quote-extractor
description: Extracts all passages enclosed in quotation marks from a text, with line numbers.
example_prompt: Pull out every quoted sentence in this interview transcript
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: balanced quote-mark scanning over the string, offline
rationale: Journalists and researchers need to isolate quotations quickly, and extraction beats manual highlighting.

name: video-rotation-metadata-reader
description: Reads the display matrix / rotation metadata of a video and reports the intended playback orientation (0/90/180/270).
example_prompt: Does this phone video have a rotation flag set?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses the tkhd display matrix from the file bytes, simple matrix math.
rationale: Sideways phone videos are caused by rotation metadata that most players honor but many tools strip silently.

name: leading-trailing-silence-detector
description: Measures the exact duration of silence at the start and end of a file against a configurable threshold.
example_prompt: How much silence is at the beginning and end of this clip?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM edge scan over PCM (ffmpeg decodes); fully client-side.
rationale: Knowing head/tail silence is the precondition for tight, consistent trims across a batch.

name: dsn-format-converter
description: Converts a database connection string between URL DSN, JDBC, and key=value formats.
example_prompt: convert this JDBC URL into a postgres:// connection string
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bidirectional string transform over parsed connection components, no network.
rationale: Teams move between JDBC (Java/Oracle/MSSQL) and URL-style DSNs (sqlx/Rust) and need a reliable offline converter.

name: geojson-simplify
description: Simplify polygon and line geometries with Douglas-Peucker to reduce vertex count.
example_prompt: Simplify this coastline GeoJSON with tolerance 0.001
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via georust/geo simplify — pure algorithmic compute.
rationale: Geometry simplification cuts map file sizes and render cost and is awkward to do without GIS software.

name: dicom-metadata-viewer
description: Parses a DICOM medical-imaging file and lists its tags — patient, study, series, modality, acquisition parameters — in a readable table.
example_prompt: Show me the metadata and tags inside this DICOM file I'm attaching.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — dicom-rs parses the DICOM data set entirely in Rust with no native deps, so the (often sensitive) scan never leaves the browser.
rationale: Radiologists and devs constantly need to inspect DICOM headers without uploading PHI to a cloud viewer, which a browser-local tool uniquely enables.

name: text-decancer
description: Strips zalgo, homoglyphs, and decorative Unicode from text to recover clean readable plain text.
example_prompt: Clean up this fancy unicode: 𝓗𝓮𝓵𝓵𝓸 wᵒʳˡᵈ
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: decancer is pure Rust, maps confusables in-memory, and needs no network.
rationale: Normalizing obfuscated or stylized usernames and pasted text is valuable for moderation, search, and accessibility.

name: branca-decoder
description: Decodes a Branca token with the supplied 32-byte key, revealing the embedded timestamp and decrypted payload.
example_prompt: Decode this Branca token with key 0x...: 875GH233T7IYrxtgXxlQBYiFobZMQdHAT51vChKsAIYCFxZtL1evV54vYqLyZtQ0ekPHt8kJHQp0a
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the RustCrypto chacha20poly1305 crate (XChaCha20-Poly1305) — pure Rust, wasm-friendly, no native bindings.
rationale: Branca has no public decoder UI; offering one client-side keeps the secret key off any server while satisfying real branca demand.

name: network-config-diff
description: Produces a structural, section-aware diff of two network device configurations, ignoring reordering noise that line diffs flag falsely.
example_prompt: Diff these two switch configs and show what actually changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM hierarchical diffing of two pasted configs; fully offline.
rationale: Comparing before/after device configs is a core change-management task, and a structure-aware diff beats generic line diff for network engineers.

name: audio-ducker
description: Automatically lowers a music/background track whenever a voice track is present (sidechain ducking).
example_prompt: Duck this background music under the narration so the voice stays clear
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — `sidechaincompress` keyed on the voice input drives gain reduction on the music; two-input graph runs in ffmpeg.wasm.
rationale: Voice-over-music ducking is a top podcast/video need and doing it by hand with volume automation is tedious and error-prone.

name: column-value-recoder
description: Applies a find→replace mapping to recode values in a CSV column (e.g. Y/N → true/false).
example_prompt: Recode the status column: A means active, I means inactive
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; dictionary lookup per cell, fully local
rationale: Bulk value remapping is a core cleaning step that's clumsy with spreadsheet find-replace.

name: markdown-trailing-whitespace-stripper
description: Trims trailing spaces from lines (preserving intentional two-space line breaks if requested) and normalizes blank-line runs.
example_prompt: Clean up the trailing whitespace in this Markdown
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans line endings and trims; pure local transform
rationale: Trailing whitespace causes noisy diffs and lint failures across collaborative docs.

name: text-transpose
description: Transposes rows and columns of delimited tabular text.
example_prompt: Transpose this CSV so rows become columns
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — matrix transpose with quoting awareness, local only
rationale: Pivoting small tables between row- and column-orientation is awkward without a tool.

name: yaml-key-sorter
description: Sorts mapping keys in a YAML document recursively while preserving comments where possible.
example_prompt: sort the keys in this YAML alphabetically
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse, reorder mappings, re-emit; in-memory only.
rationale: Ordered YAML keys make large config files (k8s, CI) reviewable and diff-clean.

name: plaintext-outliner
description: Converts indentation-based plain-text notes into a structured, collapsible outline tree (and back).
example_prompt: Turn this indented note into a clean nested outline
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — indentation parsing, local only
rationale: Standard Unix Notes and plain-text purists want structure without leaving plain text.

name: vcard-photo-extractor
description: Extracts embedded base64 contact photos from a vCard file and outputs them as downloadable images.
example_prompt: Pull the photos out of this .vcf file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM base64 decode of PHOTO properties, local only
rationale: Recover contact photos locked inside a contacts export.

name: flamegraph-generator
description: Turns folded/collapsed stack samples (e.g. perf script piped through stackcollapse) into an interactive SVG flamegraph.
example_prompt: Make a flamegraph from these collapsed stacks
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — inferno-style folded-stack parsing emitting a self-contained SVG, runs offline in wasmi.
rationale: Flamegraph generation is a classic local-only transform that maps folded stacks to SVG with no server, exactly fitting the browser sandbox.

name: minisign-sign
description: Signs a file or text with a minisign Ed25519 secret key, producing a minisign signature.
example_prompt: Sign this release file with my minisign key
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (Ed25519 via the `minisign`/`ed25519-dalek` crates); signing is local CPU crypto.
rationale: Minisign is a popular lightweight signing tool whose entire workflow is offline-friendly.

name: log-timeline-builder
description: Normalizes multiple log sources into a single timestamp-sorted timeline with source tagging.
example_prompt: build a unified timeline from these logs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; parsing, timestamp normalization, and sorting all client-side.
rationale: Timeline reconstruction across heterogeneous logs is the heart of intrusion investigations.

name: video-preview-grid
description: Generate a contact-sheet storyboard of evenly-spaced thumbnails summarizing a video at a glance.
example_prompt: Make a thumbnail grid preview of this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: select + tile filters build the sprite sheet inside the WASM runtime.
rationale: Maps ffmpeg-generate-video-preview and gives a fast visual overview of long footage.

name: video-preview-clip
description: Build a short preview montage by sampling a few seconds at intervals across the whole video.
example_prompt: Make a 10-second preview montage of this movie file
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: segment selection and concatenation run locally in the WASM ffmpeg build.
rationale: An alternate ffmpeg-generate-video-preview form useful for quickly skimming long media.

name: pandera-schema-validator
description: Validate a CSV/dataframe against a declared schema: types, ranges, nullability, uniqueness.
example_prompt: Validate this CSV: age must be int 0-120, email must be non-null and unique
loader_feasibility: pyodide + micropip(pandera); pandera is pure-python and installs client-side.
rationale: 'pandera' demand — catch malformed data before it enters a pipeline, all in the browser.

name: datatest-assertions
description: Run datatest-style acceptance assertions on a dataset: allowed values, ordering, completeness.
example_prompt: Check this CSV's status column only contains active or inactive
loader_feasibility: pyodide + micropip(datatest); pure-python, runs client-side.
rationale: 'datatest' demand for test-driven data validation distinct from schema typing.

name: apk-icon-extractor
description: Pulls the launcher icon out of an APK (resolving the manifest's icon reference, including adaptive-icon layers) and exports it as a PNG.
example_prompt: Extract the app icon from this APK as a PNG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM for ZIP/resource resolution plus image decode/encode; ffmpeg can flatten adaptive layers — all browser-local.
rationale: Repo maintainers and icon-pack makers (OpenLauncher/KISS users) need the raw app icon without installing the APK.

name: paste-sanitizer
description: Cleans pasted text by removing zero-width characters, smart quotes, and messy whitespace.
example_prompt: Clean up this pasted text so it's safe to use
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string normalization; no model or network needed
rationale: PasteGuard demand is squarely about sanitizing clipboard text, and this is the fast deterministic core of it.

name: self-decrypting-page
description: Wraps a file into a single standalone HTML page that prompts the recipient for a password and decrypts it in their browser.
example_prompt: Turn this contract into a password-protected HTML file I can send a client
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM builds an HTML document with embedded ciphertext plus a WebCrypto decrypt routine; runs fully offline on both ends
rationale: Offline analog of Firefox Send/Lufi/Blindsend — the recipient needs no app and no server.

name: encrypted-photo-vault
description: Encrypts a set of photos into one password-protected vault file with an embedded encrypted index.
example_prompt: Lock these private photos into one encrypted vault
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; per-photo XChaCha20-Poly1305 + Argon2id, all packed in-browser
rationale: Photok-style private photo storage without a cloud account or app install.

name: telemetry-domain-scanner
description: Scans a pasted config, HAR file, or host list and flags known telemetry, analytics, and tracking endpoints.
example_prompt: Scan this HAR file for any telemetry or tracking domains it contacted
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (bundled tracker-domain database + text matching) — the blocklist ships in-bundle, fully offline.
rationale: Mirrors the No-Telemetry ethos by letting users audit what an app phones home to, without uploading their config anywhere.

name: session-mnemonic-decode
description: Converts a Session 13-word recovery phrase to its hex seed and back using the Monero-style mnemonic wordlist and checksum.
example_prompt: Decode my Session recovery phrase to the seed: kitchen sailor ... (13 words)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — wordlist lookup + CRC32 checksum math, no secrets leave the browser.
rationale: Lets people inspect or migrate a Session identity without trusting a remote decoder with their seed.

name: memos-export-converter
description: Converts a Memos JSON export into dated Markdown notes.
example_prompt: Convert my Memos export to Markdown files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the Memos JSON client-side.
rationale: Memos users moving to file-based apps need their timestamped memos as portable Markdown.

name: markdown-image-inliner
description: Replaces local image references in Markdown with embedded base64 data URIs, or extracts them back out.
example_prompt: Inline all the images in this Markdown as base64
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM base64-encodes and rewrites the references client-side.
rationale: Inlining images makes a note self-contained for sharing across HedgeDoc/Nextcloud Notes without dragging along an attachments folder.

name: video-set-bitrate-cbr
description: Re-encodes to a fixed average/constant bitrate (e.g. 5 Mbps) for predictable streaming-friendly output.
example_prompt: encode this to a constant 5 mbps for streaming
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — -b:v with bufsize/maxrate CBR settings in the WASM build.
rationale: Live-streaming and broadcast targets specify exact bitrates, a different mental model from CRF or file-size targeting.

name: video-extract-elementary-stream
description: Demuxes the raw elementary video or audio stream (e.g. .h264, .aac) out of a container without re-encoding.
example_prompt: extract the raw h.264 stream from this mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — stream-copy to a raw bitstream/ADTS file in the WASM build.
rationale: Bitstream-level workflows and re-muxing need the raw elementary stream, which inspection tools don't produce.

name: video-annexb-convert
description: Converts an H.264 stream between AVCC (MP4-style length-prefixed) and Annex-B (start-code) bitstream formats.
example_prompt: convert this mp4's h.264 to annex-b for my streaming pipeline
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — the h264_mp4toannexb bitstream filter with stream-copy in the WASM runtime.
rationale: Streaming and embedded decoders expect Annex-B while MP4 stores AVCC, a conversion no other tool here handles.

name: float-wav-to-int-pcm
description: Converts an IEEE float32 WAV into integer PCM (16- or 24-bit) with clipping at full scale.
example_prompt: Convert this 32-bit float WAV to 16-bit integer PCM
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: scales the [-1,1] floats to integer range and reformats the fmt chunk locally.
rationale: Many tools export float WAVs that legacy hardware and codecs can't ingest, so integer conversion is constant work.

name: audio-cqt-music-video
description: Creates a musical constant-Q transform visualizer where bars align to piano notes, animated to a supplied audio track.
example_prompt: Generate a piano-keyboard CQT visualizer video from this music file
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg 'showcqt' renders the note-aligned spectrum frames from the audio entirely on-device.
rationale: Note-synced visualizers are prized by music creators and only need the audio plus parameters.

name: spinning-logo-sting-video
description: Turns a supplied logo image into a short 3D-ish spin/zoom-in sting with a configurable color background.
example_prompt: Make a 3-second spinning logo sting from this PNG, white background, gentle bounce
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg rotates/scales the user image with time-based perspective and zoompan expressions; all on-device.
rationale: A quick branded sting from just a logo is a common need distinct from generic intro bumpers.

name: mermaid-class-from-json
description: Generates a Mermaid classDiagram from a JSON object, mapping nested objects to classes and arrays to relationships.
example_prompt: make a Mermaid class diagram from this nested JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; structural walk of parsed JSON to Mermaid syntax, offline.
rationale: Visualizing the shape of a complex JSON payload helps onboarding and design discussions.

name: json-fixture-from-typescript-interface
description: Generates sample JSON fixtures that satisfy a supplied TypeScript interface, filling typed placeholder values for each field.
example_prompt: generate a sample JSON object for this TypeScript interface
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; lightweight interface parsing and value synthesis, no compiler.
rationale: Tests and Storybook stories often need realistic objects matching a type, which is tedious to write manually.

name: media-codec-inspector
description: Reports container, video/audio codecs, resolution, bitrate, and HDR/subtitle tracks of a media file, flagging likely Kodi direct-play issues.
example_prompt: What codecs are in this file and will my Kodi box direct-play it?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (ffmpeg.wasm ffprobe-style) — reads container/stream headers in WASM without uploading the file.
rationale: Before transcoding, OSMC/Kodi users need to know whether a file is already compatible, which is pure local inspection.

name: cost-basis-calculator
description: Matches buy/sell lots with FIFO or LIFO to compute realized capital gains for stocks or crypto.
example_prompt: Compute my FIFO capital gains from these crypto buys and sells
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM lot-matching over the trade list; pure computation, offline.
rationale: Rotki's core is crypto cost-basis/tax accounting, and lot matching is sensitive data best processed locally.

name: image-curves-levels
description: Applies tone curves and levels (black/white/gamma points) to an image.
example_prompt: Apply an S-curve to add punch to this photo
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute shader (or plain Rust→WASM) maps the LUT over every pixel locally
rationale: Advanced darktable editing that browsers lack; WebGPU makes full-res curves real-time.

name: youtube-subscriptions-converter
description: Converts video subscription lists between NewPipe JSON, FreeTube, Invidious, and OPML formats.
example_prompt: Convert my NewPipe subscriptions.json into FreeTube import format
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON/XML transform over uploaded files; entirely local.
rationale: Tubular, FreeTube, and Yattee users switch apps often and each uses an incompatible subscription export format.

name: opml-feed-merger
description: Parses and merges OPML subscription/feed files and removes duplicate entries.
example_prompt: Merge these OPML feed files and dedupe the channels
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML parse + merge; runs on pasted/uploaded OPML.
rationale: OPML is the lingua franca for importing feeds and YouTube subs across privacy clients, and merging lists is common.

name: tiktok-export-analyzer
description: Parses a TikTok user_data.json export to summarize activity, likes, and viewing history offline.
example_prompt: Analyze my TikTok user_data.json export and summarize my activity
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON aggregation over the uploaded export; runs client-side.
rationale: ProxiTok-style privacy users want insight into their own TikTok data without re-uploading it to any service.

name: reddit-export-analyzer
description: Parses a Reddit GDPR export's CSV files (posts, comments, saved) into stats and a searchable view.
example_prompt: Analyze my Reddit data export and show my most active subreddits
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSV parse + aggregation on uploaded files; fully local.
rationale: Libreddit/SaidIt users auditing or leaving Reddit need to mine their export privately and find saved content.

name: firefox-bookmarks-parser
description: Parses a Firefox bookmark-backup .json export into a readable nested Markdown or HTML tree.
example_prompt: Turn my Firefox bookmarks backup into a readable markdown outline
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: JSON parsing and tree formatting only.
rationale: Firefox bookmark backups are opaque JSON; turning them into a browsable outline helps audit and migrate them.

name: pcap-credential-extractor
description: Pulls plaintext credentials and artifacts from HTTP, FTP, Telnet, and DNS traffic in a capture.
example_prompt: find any plaintext credentials in this capture
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; protocol field extraction over packet bytes, fully offline.
rationale: 'Find the leaked password' is a classic network-forensics exercise and a fast win for analysts.

name: caf-to-wav
description: Converts Apple Core Audio Format (.caf) files from GarageBand/iOS to WAV.
example_prompt: convert this caf file from garageband to wav
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader demuxes CAF and writes PCM WAV client-side.
rationale: CAF is GarageBand/iOS-only and unreadable on Windows or non-Apple tools, where WAV is universal.

name: ulaw-alaw-to-wav
description: Decodes G.711 µ-law/A-law telephony recordings into 16-bit linear PCM WAV.
example_prompt: convert this ulaw phone recording to a normal wav
loader_feasibility: G.711 companding is a tiny lookup table, decoded in plain Rust→WASM with no dependencies.
rationale: VoIP/PBX and Asterisk recordings are stored as raw µ-law/A-law and sound like static until expanded to PCM.

name: gsm-to-wav
description: Decodes GSM 6.10 full-rate (.gsm) voicemail/telephony clips to WAV.
example_prompt: convert this .gsm voicemail to wav
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader includes the GSM 6.10 decoder, producing PCM WAV in wasm.
rationale: Old voicemail exports and telephony archives are stored in GSM, unplayable without a dedicated decoder.

name: image-color-namer
description: Identifies the dominant color and maps it to the nearest human-readable name (e.g. 'cornflower blue').
example_prompt: What color is this swatch called?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM finds the dominant color then nearest-neighbors a bundled CSS/X11 name table locally.
rationale: Turning a hex code into a recognizable name is a small but frequently-wanted ergonomic helper.

name: sprite-sheet-grid-detector
description: Detects the cell grid of a sprite sheet or icon atlas by finding periodic transparent or uniform gutters.
example_prompt: Figure out the tile size and grid of this sprite sheet.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM analyzes row/column emptiness periodicity in the alpha/luma channel locally.
rationale: Game and UI devs frequently reverse-engineer atlas layouts, and auto-detecting the grid is a real time-saver.

name: photo-vs-graphic-classifier
description: Classifies an image as a photograph versus a screenshot/illustration to guide format and compression choices.
example_prompt: Is this a photo or a graphic — which format should I save it in?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM derives color-count, edge-sharpness, and flat-region heuristics from the pixels offline.
rationale: The photo-vs-graphic distinction is the key decision between JPEG and PNG/WebP-lossless and is easy to get wrong.

name: video-stream-inventory
description: Summarizes every stream in a container (video/audio/subtitle/data) with codec, language, and disposition.
example_prompt: List all the streams inside this MKV
loader_feasibility: ffprobe enumerates streams from the locally loaded container with no upload.
rationale: A one-glance stream table is the first thing anyone wants before remuxing a multi-track file.

name: json-path-lister
description: Enumerates every unique JSONPath/dotted key path present in a JSON document, with each path's value type.
example_prompt: List all the field paths in this JSON response.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; recursive traversal of the parsed tree, no server.
rationale: Mapping the full set of paths is the fastest way to discover fields in a large API payload.

name: benford-analysis
description: Applies Benford's Law to a numeric column, comparing observed leading-digit frequencies to expected and flagging deviations.
example_prompt: Run a Benford's Law check on these transaction amounts
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM counts leading digits and runs a chi-square goodness-of-fit locally
rationale: Benford screening is a well-known fraud/anomaly-detection heuristic that's simple math over a column.

name: image-quality-score
description: Produces a no-reference perceptual quality score estimating how a viewer would rate the image.
example_prompt: Rate the overall quality of this image.
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a bundled no-reference IQA model (BRISQUE/NIMA-style) on decoded pixels in-browser.
rationale: A single quality score without a reference helps rank and cull large image sets.

name: video-freeze-frame-detector
description: Finds frozen or static segments where the picture stops changing and reports their start/end times.
example_prompt: Does this recording have any frozen/stuck frames? Show me where
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — the `freezedetect` filter flags low-variance runs of frames locally in the wasm runtime.
rationale: Frozen frames are a common capture/encode fault that black-frame detection misses, and they need to be caught before publishing.

name: video-flash-hazard-analyzer
description: Scans a video for rapid luminance flashes that risk triggering photosensitive epilepsy and flags risky timestamps.
example_prompt: Check this clip for flashing lights that could trigger seizures
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg extracts per-frame luminance, then plain Rust→WASM applies a Harding-style flash test; all math runs locally.
rationale: Flash-hazard screening is a real accessibility/compliance need that no off-the-shelf consumer tool offers offline.

name: video-blur-segment-detector
description: Identifies out-of-focus or motion-blurred segments by measuring per-frame sharpness and reports their timecodes.
example_prompt: Find the blurry / out-of-focus parts of this clip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg extracts frames, plain Rust→WASM computes Laplacian-variance sharpness per frame; all local.
rationale: Catching soft footage automatically saves editors from scrubbing long recordings for usable takes.

name: video-stabilization-need-analyzer
description: Analyzes camera shake and reports how unstable each segment is to decide whether stabilization is worthwhile.
example_prompt: How shaky is this video? Does it need stabilizing?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg `vidstabdetect` produces motion-transform data in wasm; the shake report is computed from it locally.
rationale: Knowing shake magnitude before committing to a slow stabilization pass saves time and avoids needless cropping.

name: video-loop-point-finder
description: Finds the best seamless loop points by measuring frame similarity between candidate start/end positions.
example_prompt: Where can I loop this clip seamlessly?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg samples frames, plain Rust→WASM compares perceptual similarity across candidate pairs; all client-side.
rationale: Seamless loops are valuable for backgrounds and GIFs, and picking points by hand is tedious and error-prone.

name: video-speech-music-timeline
description: Classifies each part of a video's audio as speech, music, or silence and outputs a labeled timeline.
example_prompt: Label where this video has talking vs music vs silence
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg extracts audio, transformers-js runs an audio-classification model in-browser to label windows locally.
rationale: A speech/music map drives smart trimming, ducking, and indexing for interviews and podcasts without a server.

name: video-scene-tagger
description: Generates descriptive content tags for each scene of a video using an image-understanding model.
example_prompt: Auto-tag the scenes in this video with keywords
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg samples representative frames, transformers-js runs a CLIP-style zero-shot model in-browser to tag them locally.
rationale: Automatic scene tags make a video library browsable and searchable without any cloud vision service.

name: ndjson-field-stats
description: Computes per-field summary statistics (presence rate, type mix, min/max/distinct) across an NDJSON record stream.
example_prompt: Profile each field across this newline-delimited JSON log.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM streams records and aggregates per-key stats in memory, fully local.
rationale: NDJSON is the default log/event format but lacks a quick way to understand field shape without a query engine.

name: csv-foreign-key-checker
description: Checks referential integrity: verifies every value in one file's column exists in another file's key column, listing orphans.
example_prompt: Check that every customer_id in orders.csv exists in customers.csv.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM builds a hash set from the key file and scans the child file client-side.
rationale: Broken foreign keys are a top data-quality defect; validating them locally catches joins that would drop rows.

name: spss-sav-to-csv
description: Converts SPSS .sav files to CSV, optionally expanding coded values to their labels.
example_prompt: Convert this SPSS .sav survey file to CSV
loader_feasibility: pyodide with pyreadstat/pandas; reads the binary .sav fully offline in WASM.
rationale: Survey data ships as SPSS .sav and researchers without SPSS licenses are stuck.

name: npz-to-csv-bundle
description: Unzips a NumPy .npz archive and emits one CSV per contained named array.
example_prompt: Split this model_weights.npz into separate CSVs for each array
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: .npz is just a ZIP of .npy entries, so an in-WASM unzip plus the npy decoder handles everything locally.
rationale: An .npz can hold dozens of arrays and there's no quick browser way to peek at each one separately.

name: replaygain-analyzer
description: Computes ReplayGain/EBU R128 loudness and true-peak values for a track without altering it.
example_prompt: What's the LUFS loudness and true peak of this song?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's ebur128 filter measures loudness statistics locally in WASM.
rationale: Loudness analysis is what serious music libraries (MusicPlayerPlus-style) rely on for consistent playback, and it runs client-side.

name: podcast-summarizer
description: Transcribes a podcast episode and produces a concise summary with key points and timestamps.
example_prompt: Summarize this podcast episode into bullet points
loader_feasibility: transformers-js chains an on-device Whisper transcription with a local summarization model, all in WASM/WebGPU.
rationale: Episode summaries let listeners triage long shows, directly serving the podcast-CLI demand without sending audio anywhere.

name: line-select
description: Selects lines by range, every Nth line, or lines matching/excluding a pattern, with optional inversion.
example_prompt: Give me lines 50 to 120 of this file, but skip any line containing 'DEBUG'.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line iteration plus regex crate; no I/O.
rationale: Line Select-style slicing is a universal text chore that pairs naturally with the other text tools.

name: markdown-slides-to-video
description: Turns a Markdown deck (slides separated by ---) into a narrated-pace slideshow video with one slide per timed segment.
example_prompt: Turn this markdown presentation into a video with 5 seconds per slide
loader_feasibility: pyodide renders each slide to an image and ffmpeg sequences them with hold times, in-browser.
rationale: Converting a quick Markdown deck into a shareable video is a fast content-repurposing win.

name: openapi-spec-scaffold
description: Scaffolds an OpenAPI 3.1 document skeleton from a list of endpoints, methods, and param hints with reusable components.
example_prompt: Scaffold an OpenAPI spec for GET /users, POST /users, GET /users/{id}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — builds the paths/components tree and serializes to YAML/JSON, fully offline.
rationale: Starting an OpenAPI spec from scratch is verbose; a scaffold gives a valid, fillable structure immediately.

name: taskrunner-graph
description: Builds a Mermaid dependency graph from a task-runner config (Makefile, Taskfile, or rusk file).
example_prompt: Draw a dependency graph of the tasks in this Taskfile
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse dependencies and emit Mermaid graph syntax.
rationale: Visualizing task dependencies makes complex build pipelines (the rusk use case) far easier to reason about.

name: xit-parser
description: Parses the [x]it! plaintext format (open/checked/ongoing/obsolete checkboxes, priority dots, tags, due dates) into structured tasks.
example_prompt: Parse this [x]it! file and list the ongoing and overdue items
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — character-level parsing of the xit grammar, no dependencies.
rationale: xit has no ecosystem of parsers; a browser-local one directly serves the 'xit' demand term.

name: due-date-tracker
description: Flags overdue, due-today, and upcoming tasks from a todo.txt given the current date, sorted by urgency.
example_prompt: Which tasks in my todo.txt are overdue or due this week?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — date comparison against a passed-in today, no network.
rationale: Deadline awareness is the most common reason people open these CLIs daily.

name: syslog-parser
description: Parses RFC5424 and RFC3164 syslog lines into structured fields (priority, facility, severity, timestamp, host, message).
example_prompt: Parse this syslog line: <34>1 2026-06-24T12:00:00Z host app - - - oops
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — syslog framing/parsing (flowgger's core job) is pure string decoding.
rationale: Raw syslog is dense and hard to read by eye; structured field extraction speeds up incident triage.

name: logfmt-parser
description: Parses logfmt key=value log lines (including quoted values) into a structured table or JSON.
example_prompt: Parse this logfmt line: level=info msg="request done" dur=12ms code=200
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — logfmt tokenizing is pure character scanning, a format flowgger ingests.
rationale: logfmt is ubiquitous in Go/Rust services and a one-shot structurer makes ad-hoc log reading far easier.

name: id-card-field-extractor
description: Extracts name, ID number, date of birth, and expiry from a driver's license or ID card image into structured fields.
example_prompt: Pull the name and ID number off this driver's license photo
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime OCR with plain-Rust field heuristics keeps personally identifiable data on the client.
rationale: KYC and onboarding flows benefit from local field extraction that avoids shipping ID scans to a third party.

name: video-bitrate-timeline
description: Extracts per-second (or per-GOP) bitrate over the whole file and outputs it as CSV/JSON for plotting bitrate spikes.
example_prompt: Give me a per-second bitrate breakdown of this video as CSV
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader sums packet sizes per time window via ffprobe -show_packets; no full decode needed, runs client-side.
rationale: Pinpointing bitrate spikes is the first step in diagnosing playback stutter and tuning encoder settings.

name: video-audio-levels-report
description: Reports detailed audio statistics (peak/RMS per channel, DC offset, and clipped-sample count) for the embedded audio.
example_prompt: Check this video's audio for clipping and report peak and RMS levels per channel
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader's astats filter computes per-channel statistics in the wasm runtime.
rationale: Detecting clipping, DC offset, or channel imbalance before publishing prevents distorted, unbroadcastable audio.

name: json-number-path-extractor
description: Walks an arbitrary JSON document and returns every numeric leaf paired with its dotted path, optionally filtered by path pattern.
example_prompt: List every number and its JSON path in this object
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — recursive JSON traversal, no network.
rationale: Auditing or extracting all metrics buried in nested API JSON is otherwise manual and error-prone.

name: log-metric-extractor
description: Scans log lines for numeric metrics with units ("took 123ms", "used 4.2GB") and returns them as a labeled time-ordered series.
example_prompt: Extract all the latency numbers from these log lines into a series
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — per-line pattern scanning and number parsing, runs client-side.
rationale: Turning ad-hoc log numbers into a clean series enables quick local analysis without a pipeline.

name: media-content-hash
description: Computes a content fingerprint of an audio/video file's decoded stream to detect duplicates regardless of container.
example_prompt: Fingerprint this video so I can tell if it's a duplicate of another file.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader decodes the stream and hashes raw samples in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
rationale: Container-agnostic media dedup (dano-style) catches re-encodes and renames that plain file hashes miss.

name: extended-key-decode
description: Decodes an xprv/xpub (and SLIP-132 yprv/zpub variants) into version, depth, fingerprint, chain code, and key bytes.
example_prompt: decode this xpub: xpub661MyMwAqRbcF...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Base58Check parsing only, offline.
rationale: Inspecting extended keys helps wallet developers debug derivation and account structure without trusting a website.

name: ipa-inspector
description: Inspects an uploaded iOS .ipa, parsing Info.plist for bundle id, version, minimum OS, declared permissions, URL schemes and icon list.
example_prompt: What does this .ipa app declare in its Info.plist?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — an .ipa is a ZIP; unzip plus binary/XML plist parsing are pure-Rust crates.
rationale: Understanding an iOS app bundle's metadata is exactly the analysis context behind touchHLE.

name: video-truncation-checker
description: Detects truncated or incomplete files by checking for a missing moov atom, short last packet, or duration mismatch.
example_prompt: Is this MP4 truncated or did it download completely?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses the container index and trailing bytes in the browser to spot truncation.
rationale: Interrupted downloads/exports leave unplayable truncated files that a quick structural check catches.

name: video-av-sync-drift-checker
description: Measures audio-versus-video drift over the duration and reports accumulating sync error, not just the start offset.
example_prompt: Does the audio drift out of sync with the video toward the end?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader probes audio/video stream durations and timestamps in WASM to compute progressive drift locally.
rationale: Sample-rate mismatches cause sync to slip gradually, which a start-offset check alone won't catch.

name: music-tag-linter
description: Lints a library's tags for missing or inconsistent essentials (title, artist, album, track number, year).
example_prompt: Lint this album's tags for anything missing or inconsistent.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — reading and checking tag fields across files is byte parsing, browser-local.
rationale: Incomplete tags break library organization and smart playlists, and a linter surfaces gaps before import.

name: podcast-audio-spec-checker
description: Checks a podcast file against common delivery specs for sample rate, channel count, and bitrate (loudness aside).
example_prompt: Does this episode meet standard podcast delivery specs?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — format/stream probing plus measurements run in the wasm ffmpeg build, no server.
rationale: A one-shot pre-publish spec gate catches the most common podcast format rejections before upload.

name: rust-binary-sbom-extractor
description: Extracts the embedded dependency manifest (cargo-auditable data) from an uploaded Rust binary.
example_prompt: Pull the dependency list out of this compiled Rust binary <upload binary>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — ELF/PE section parsing plus pure-Rust zlib inflate (miniz_oxide); operates on the uploaded file bytes locally.
rationale: Lets anyone recover a precise SBOM from a cargo-auditable binary without trusting an external service with the artifact.

name: sbom-format-converter
description: Converts a software bill of materials between SPDX and CycloneDX JSON formats.
example_prompt: Convert this CycloneDX SBOM to SPDX
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — JSON-to-JSON schema mapping is pure data transformation with no I/O.
rationale: SBOM format friction is real in supply-chain workflows, and a private offline converter avoids uploading inventory data anywhere.
