name: field-extract
description: Extracts and reorders columns from delimited or whitespace/regex-split text like logs and TSV.
example_prompt: From this log, pull columns 1 and 4 split on whitespace
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with regex-based field splitting (hck-style); operates on pasted text.
rationale: hck generalizes cut to regex delimiters, making log/field extraction painless in chat.

name: age-decrypt
description: Decrypts an age-encrypted file or message using a passphrase or identity key.
example_prompt: Decrypt this age file with my key
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: same pure-Rust age crate; decryption runs locally so keys never leave the browser.
rationale: Local decryption preserves the security guarantee that makes age worth using.

name: character-card-reader
description: Extracts the embedded Tavern/RisuAI character-card JSON (name, persona, system prompt, greetings) hidden inside a character-card PNG.
example_prompt: Read the character card data out of this PNG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses PNG tEXt/zTXt chunks and base64-decodes the embedded JSON entirely in memory.
rationale: AI-chat users constantly swap character cards and inspecting one locally avoids uploading prompts to an unknown site.

name: character-card-writer
description: Embeds or updates the character-card JSON inside a PNG, producing a portable card other AI-chat apps can import.
example_prompt: Embed this character JSON into my avatar PNG as a character card
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — re-encodes the PNG with new tEXt/zTXt metadata chunks in memory using the png crate.
rationale: Creators need to package personas as cards; doing it locally keeps custom prompts off third-party servers.

name: video-metadata-inspector
description: Probes an uploaded video and reports container, codecs, resolution, frame rate, bitrate, duration and stream layout.
example_prompt: What codec, resolution and bitrate is this video?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — ffprobe-equivalent stream inspection runs locally in ffmpeg.wasm with no upload.
rationale: Quick technical inspection before editing or sharing, with no command-line ffprobe required.

name: parquet-metadata-inspect
description: Reads a Parquet file's footer to report schema, row count, row groups, compression codecs, and per-column statistics without decoding the data.
example_prompt: What's the schema and row count of this .parquet file?
loader_feasibility: the Rust parquet crate compiles to WASM and reads the footer in-memory; pure compute, no server.
rationale: Quickly inspecting Parquet structure is a core data-engineering need (duckle/DuckDB ETL) that the full-decode parquet-to-csv tool doesn't serve.

name: wasm-optimize
description: Runs size/speed optimization passes on a .wasm module and reports the before/after byte count.
example_prompt: Optimize this wasm binary for size
loader_feasibility: Binaryen's wasm-opt is distributed as a WASM build, so the optimizer runs in the browser on the uploaded module.
rationale: wasm-pack invokes wasm-opt as its key shrink step; exposing it standalone matches direct toolchain demand.

name: rust-trait-mock-generator
description: Parses a pasted Rust trait and generates a mockall-style mock struct skeleton implementing each method.
example_prompt: Generate a mockall mock for this trait
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM; trait-signature parsing plus string codegen, no compiler.
rationale: Hand-writing mock boilerplate from a trait is tedious and mechanical, ideal to generate.

name: chat-template-formatter
description: Applies a chat template (ChatML, Llama, Mistral) to a list of messages to produce the model-ready string.
example_prompt: Format these messages with the ChatML template.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure string templating against built-in template definitions.
rationale: Local/open models each demand a different prompt envelope and mistakes degrade results badly.

name: gpu-array-math
description: Runs elementwise operations and reductions (sum, max, dot product) over large arrays on the GPU.
example_prompt: Compute the dot product of these two million-element vectors on the GPU
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute: parallel WGSL kernels (the emu/collenchyma GPU-compute role) execute on the browser's WebGPU device client-side.
rationale: Massively-parallel array math is the heart of GPU compute and unlocks data-heavy numeric work directly in the browser.

name: abcrypt-file
description: Encrypts and decrypts files in the abcrypt format (scrypt key derivation + XChaCha20-Poly1305).
example_prompt: encrypt this file as abcrypt with a passphrase
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using sorairolake/abcrypt, a pure-Rust container format that operates on in-memory file bytes in the browser.
rationale: abcrypt is a modern portable encrypted-file format and producing/opening it locally avoids ever uploading sensitive files.

name: bls-signature
description: Generates BLS12-381 keypairs and produces, verifies, and aggregates BLS signatures.
example_prompt: aggregate these three bls signatures and verify them
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via dusk-network/bls12-381 pairing arithmetic; pairings are heavy but fully computable in wasmi with no host calls.
rationale: BLS aggregate signatures power Ethereum consensus and threshold schemes, and there are few local tools to inspect or aggregate them.

name: raw-binary-to-numeric-csv
description: Reinterprets a raw binary file as a stream of typed numbers (int8/16/32/64, float32/64) and writes CSV.
example_prompt: Read this .bin as int16 little-endian and show the values
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; dtype- and endianness-aware byte reinterpretation, no decoding libs.
rationale: Sensor dumps and raw buffers need a dtype-aware reader that a hex editor can't give you.

name: wkt-geometry-to-csv
description: Extracts numeric coordinates from WKT geometries (POINT/LINESTRING/POLYGON) into CSV.
example_prompt: Pull the coordinates out of this WKT LINESTRING
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; WKT token parsing.
rationale: WKT is everywhere in spatial databases but its coordinates aren't in a tabular form.

name: product-photo-background-checker
description: Checks whether a product photo has a clean, uniform background (e.g. pure white) as required by e-commerce marketplaces.
example_prompt: Is the background of this product shot clean enough for Amazon?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes and measures edge-region color variance and brightness — fully client-side.
rationale: Marketplaces reject listings with non-uniform backgrounds, and a pre-check avoids rejected uploads.

name: jsonl-validate
description: Validates that every line of a JSONL/NDJSON file is well-formed JSON and reports the line numbers that fail.
example_prompt: Check this JSONL file — which lines aren't valid JSON?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line-by-line parse with serde_json; in-memory
rationale: JSONL is the dataset format for ML/logging and a single bad line can fail an entire import.

name: aria-check
description: Scans an HTML snippet for invalid ARIA roles and attributes and flags missing required ones.
example_prompt: Check this HTML for ARIA mistakes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (HTML parse + ARIA rule table); fully offline
rationale: Misused ARIA actively harms screen-reader users and is easy to get wrong.

name: http-syntax-converter
description: Translates an HTTP request between curl, HTTPie, wget, and raw HTTP request syntaxes.
example_prompt: Convert this HTTPie command to curl: http POST example.com/api name=joe age:=30
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure syntax parsing and regeneration, runs client-side with no network.
rationale: Teams mix curl, HTTPie/curlie, and wget, so converting between syntaxes is constant friction.

name: strip-shell-prompt
description: Cleans pasted shell commands by removing leading $, #, > prompts, line numbers, and copy artifacts.
example_prompt: Strip the $ prompts from this block of commands so I can run them
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM regex/text cleanup; trivial and fully client-side.
rationale: undollar exists purely because pasted commands from docs are full of prompt markers that break when run.

name: nine-patch-generator
description: Wraps an image into an Android 9-patch (.9.png) by adding the black stretch/content guide pixels from chosen regions.
example_prompt: make this button background a 9-patch that stretches the center
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM adds the 1px guide border and writes the .9.png locally from the uploaded image
rationale: 9-patch authoring is fiddly and tied to Android dev — a precise offline generator removes a real pain point.

name: dehyphenate-linebreaks
description: Removes hyphenation introduced at line breaks, rejoining split words (e.g. 'inter-\nnational' to 'international').
example_prompt: Fix the hyphenated words broken across lines in this OCR text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM hyphen+newline pattern join with dictionary-light heuristics; client-side
rationale: Justified print and OCR output splits words with hyphens at line ends, corrupting every downstream search and copy.

name: renumber-ordered-list
description: Renumbers a markdown or plain-text ordered list so the numbers are sequential and consistently formatted, even after edits.
example_prompt: Fix the numbering on this list, it jumps around after I reordered items
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM list-item detection and counter rewrite; client-side
rationale: Reordering or splicing items leaves ordered lists with broken numbering that's tedious to correct manually.

name: indent-to-markdown-list
description: Converts an indentation-based outline (tabs or spaces) into a properly nested markdown bullet list.
example_prompt: Turn this indented outline into a nested markdown bullet list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM indent-depth mapping to bullet nesting; runs locally
rationale: Outlines drafted with raw indentation are common, and converting them to markdown nesting by hand is error-prone.

name: video-audio-mono-to-stereo
description: Duplicates a mono video audio track into both left and right channels to produce centered stereo.
example_prompt: This video's audio only plays in one ear — make it proper stereo
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's pan filter maps the mono channel to L/R in ffmpeg.wasm, fully local.
rationale: One-sided audio from mono mics played as stereo is a classic defect users can't otherwise fix in a browser.

name: video-audio-channel-swap
description: Swaps the left and right channels of a video's stereo audio track.
example_prompt: The left and right audio channels in this video are reversed — swap them
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's pan filter reassigns channels in ffmpeg.wasm with no server step.
rationale: Reversed channels from miswired interfaces are a real and otherwise-annoying capture mistake.

name: video-strip-chapters
description: Removes embedded chapter markers from a video container without re-encoding.
example_prompt: Strip the chapter markers out of this MP4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's -map_chapters -1 with stream copy runs in ffmpeg.wasm, container-only edit.
rationale: Stray chapter metadata from ripping tools shows up as clutter in players and is rarely wanted.

name: video-fix-odd-dimensions
description: Pads a video with odd pixel width/height to even dimensions so yuv420p H.264/H.265 encoding succeeds.
example_prompt: My encode fails because the width is odd — fix the dimensions
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's pad=ceil(iw/2)*2 expression runs in ffmpeg.wasm, a one-pixel local pad.
rationale: The 'height/width not divisible by 2' error blocks countless encodes and this is its precise cure.

name: video-unsqueeze-anamorphic
description: Unsqueezes anamorphic footage with non-square pixels into correct square-pixel proportions.
example_prompt: My anamorphic clip looks stretched — unsqueeze it to the right proportions
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's setsar/scale to apply the pixel aspect runs in ffmpeg.wasm with local rescaling.
rationale: Anamorphic and DVD-era footage plays distorted when SAR is ignored; rescaling to square pixels corrects it.

name: video-inverse-telecine
description: Removes 3:2 pulldown (inverse telecine) from 29.97 fps footage to recover the original 23.976 fps progressive frames.
example_prompt: Inverse-telecine this 29.97 fps video back to 24 fps progressive
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's pullup + fps filters run in ffmpeg.wasm, doing field matching locally.
rationale: Telecined film transfers show combing and judder; IVTC restores clean progressive frames archivists want.

name: audio-breath-remover
description: Detects and attenuates audible breaths between phrases in spoken recordings.
example_prompt: Quiet down all the breath sounds in this voiceover.
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime classifies breath frames and pyodide attenuates them; runs locally.
rationale: Breath reduction is a tedious manual edit that automation makes hugely valuable for voiceover/audiobook work.

name: audio-dc-offset-remover
description: Removes DC bias by centering the waveform around zero.
example_prompt: Fix the DC offset on this recording.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM subtracts the per-channel mean from samples; trivial local math.
rationale: DC offset wastes headroom and causes clicks at edits; the catalog checks for it but never fixes it.

name: audio-polarity-inverter
description: Inverts the polarity (phase flip) of one or all channels.
example_prompt: Flip the polarity of the left channel on this stereo file.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM negates sample values; pure client-side.
rationale: Polarity flipping fixes phase-cancellation problems the catalog's polarity checker only diagnoses.

name: bpm-compare
description: Estimates the tempo of two recordings and reports the BPM difference and any drift.
example_prompt: Are these two loops the same tempo? Compare their BPM
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs onset detection plus autocorrelation on decoded PCM in-browser.
rationale: Confirming two loops/stems share a tempo is essential before layering them in a project.

name: musical-key-compare
description: Detects the musical key of two recordings using chroma analysis and reports whether they match or clash.
example_prompt: Are these two songs in the same key for mashing up?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM builds a chromagram and matches Krumhansl key profiles locally.
rationale: DJs and producers need a fast harmonic-compatibility check between two tracks.

name: bundle-size-diff
description: Compares two webpack/rollup/esbuild bundle-stats files and reports per-chunk and per-module size deltas, flagging regressions and newly-added dependencies.
example_prompt: Diff these two webpack stats.json files and show what grew the bundle
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses both stats JSON files and aggregates module sizes by chunk locally; no bundler execution needed.
rationale: Bundle-size regressions are a top frontend review concern, and the catalog only has a single-file bundle-stats analyzer.

name: qr-payload-diff
description: Decodes two QR-code images and diffs the encoded payloads.
example_prompt: Do these two QR codes contain the same data?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes both images with a QR-reader crate and diffs the payloads locally; offline.
rationale: Verifying whether two printed/screenshot QR codes carry identical content (e.g. tampering checks) needs a decode-then-diff that no current tool offers.

name: video-remux-container
description: Changes a video's container (MP4/MKV/MOV/WebM) by copying all streams, choosing the target from a dropdown.
example_prompt: Rewrap this file into a different container without re-encoding
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM performs a stream-copy remux to the chosen container locally.
rationale: A general-purpose lossless container changer complements the specific converters for arbitrary codec/container combos.

name: midi-to-lilypond
description: Generates LilyPond source from a MIDI file for engraved sheet music.
example_prompt: Turn this MIDI file into LilyPond notation source
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: map MIDI notes/durations to LilyPond pitch/length tokens, text-only
rationale: Bootstraps a publication-quality score from MIDI for the LilyPond engraver.

name: wav-channel-splitter
description: Exports each channel of a multichannel WAV as its own separate mono WAV file.
example_prompt: Split this 5.1 wav into six mono wav files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM deinterleaves channels at the file level and emits one headered mono WAV per channel — client-side
rationale: Stem and surround-channel extraction is a routine editing step that shouldn't require uploading multitrack audio.

name: brotli-codec
description: Compresses and decompresses data with Brotli at a chosen quality level, reporting size and ratio.
example_prompt: brotli compress this text at quality 11
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the brotli crate; the algorithm is self-contained CPU work.
rationale: Brotli is the standard for web asset compression and devs need to test ratios without a build pipeline.

name: image-resolution-compare
description: Tabulates dimensions, aspect ratio, megapixels, DPI and bit depth across a set of images and flags mismatches.
example_prompt: Compare the sizes and aspect ratios of all these assets and tell me which don't match.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads each image header and builds the comparison table locally.
rationale: Asset-prep pipelines need a quick mismatch check before batch processing or upload.

name: jwk-parser
description: Parses a JSON Web Key into readable fields (kty, alg, use, kid, curve) and reports key size and whether it's public or private.
example_prompt: Parse this JWK and tell me the key type, algorithm, and whether it's a private key.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with serde_json; pure structural parsing of the JWK object, no network.
rationale: JWKs are opaque base64url blobs; a parser makes key type, intended use, and visibility immediately clear.

name: audio-wind-noise-removal
description: Removes low-frequency wind rumble and buffeting from outdoor recordings.
example_prompt: Take the wind noise out of this clip filmed outside
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg steep highpass + lowshelf + denoise chain; all client-side wasm
rationale: Wind rumble is the dominant defect in outdoor phone/camera audio and needs a targeted chain.

name: dedent-text
description: Removes the common leading whitespace shared by all lines of a block (textwrap.dedent).
example_prompt: dedent this code block, it's over-indented from where I copied it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM finds the minimum common indent and strips it from each line locally
rationale: Pasted snippets carry context indentation that has to be removed before reuse.

name: yaml-split-documents
description: Splits a multi-document YAML stream (--- separated) into individually labeled documents.
example_prompt: split this multi-doc kubernetes YAML into separate resources
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the document stream and emits each one separately locally
rationale: Kubernetes and CI YAML bundles many docs in one file that you often need to separate.

name: modular-reduce-column
description: Reduces every value in a column modulo N (with true mathematical, non-negative remainder option).
example_prompt: Reduce this column of indices mod 256
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: element-wise modulo with sign handling, pure integer math
rationale: Correct modular reduction (handling negatives) is a common wrap/hash-prep operation with no current tool.

name: swagger-extract
description: Parses an OpenAPI/Swagger spec into a CSV/table of endpoints, methods, params, and response codes.
example_prompt: List every endpoint and method from this OpenAPI spec
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM YAML/JSON parse + traversal; fully local
rationale: Turning a dense API spec into a scannable endpoint inventory is a common, unmet need.

name: ascii-transliterator
description: Folds non-ASCII text to nearest ASCII (ß→ss, æ→ae, curly→straight, …→...) for legacy systems and identifiers.
example_prompt: Transliterate this accented text down to plain ASCII
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: deunicode-style mapping table, pure CPU, no network
rationale: Filenames, URLs, and legacy databases often require ASCII-only text, and naive accent-stripping mishandles ligatures and punctuation.

name: xml-attribute-to-element
description: Rewrites chosen XML attributes into child elements (or the reverse), normalizing inconsistent schemas before downstream parsing.
example_prompt: Convert the id and type attributes in this XML into child elements
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: event-driven XML transform with quick-xml, fully local.
rationale: Mixed attribute/element conventions break naive XML→table mappings, and reshaping one form into the other is a real normalization gap.

name: json-array-fill-keys
description: Normalizes an array of objects so every object has the union of all keys, filling missing ones with null.
example_prompt: make every object in this JSON array have the same keys before I export to CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes the key union and back-fills each object locally
rationale: Ragged object arrays break tabular exports and column-aligned tooling; squaring them up is a common prep.

name: map-range
description: Affine-remaps a numeric column from an explicit input range [a,b] to an output range [c,d], with optional clamping and inversion.
example_prompt: Map these values from range 0-1023 to 0-100
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: single linear interpolation per element, fully offline
rationale: Explicit input/output range remapping is distinct from data-driven min-max rescaling and is what people actually need for sensor/UI value conversion.

name: round-half-even
description: Rounds a column using banker's rounding (round-half-to-even) to reduce cumulative rounding bias.
example_prompt: Round this column with banker's rounding to 2 decimals
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: explicit tie-to-even rounding, pure numeric
rationale: Banker's rounding matters for accounting and statistics where default half-up rounding skews sums.

name: data-sonification-generator
description: Turns a numeric series or CSV column into audio by mapping values to pitch (and optionally amplitude) over time.
example_prompt: Sonify this CSV column of stock prices as a rising/falling pitch
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses numbers, maps to frequency/time, synthesizes tones + WAV encode, no server.
rationale: Sonification gives an accessible, intuitive way to 'hear' trends in data for analysis and accessibility.

name: midi-scale-generator
description: Generates a MIDI file playing a named scale or mode in a chosen key, octave range, and direction.
example_prompt: Make a MIDI of the D dorian scale across two octaves
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: maps scale intervals to note numbers and writes Standard MIDI File bytes, fully local.
rationale: Practicing musicians and producers want scale MIDI to import for warm-ups, ear training, or melodic scaffolding.

name: chord-audio-generator
description: Renders a named chord (e.g., 'Cmaj7', 'F#dim') as a sustained audio tone cluster for reference or ear training.
example_prompt: Play me a Dm9 chord as audio
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: maps the chord symbol to frequencies and sums enveloped sines + WAV encode, client-side.
rationale: Learners and arrangers want to hear a specific named chord instantly without an instrument or app login.

name: sql-query-analyzer
description: Parses a SQL query to list referenced tables, columns, join types, subqueries, and a rough complexity score.
example_prompt: Analyze this SQL query and list the tables and joins
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a SQL parser compiled to WASM analyzes the query string with no database connection
rationale: Understanding an unfamiliar query's table/join footprint is essential before optimizing or modifying it.

name: csv-duplicate-key-check
description: Finds duplicate values in a chosen key column to verify primary-key uniqueness, listing every collision.
example_prompt: Check that the 'id' column in this CSV has no duplicates
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — hashing column values to detect dupes runs in-process
rationale: Duplicate primary keys break joins and upserts, and catching them before load saves debugging downstream.

name: placeholder-image-generator
description: Generates a solid or gradient dummy image of any requested dimensions with the size label drawn in the center, for layout mockups.
example_prompt: make me a 800x600 gray placeholder image with the dimensions written on it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM rasterizes pixels into a PNG buffer and draws text with a bundled bitmap font — pure computation, no network.
rationale: Front-end devs constantly need throwaway sized placeholders and currently hit external services like placeholder.com that require a network round-trip.

name: video-to-mpegts
description: Wraps video into an MPEG transport stream (.ts) for broadcast and streaming ingestion.
example_prompt: convert this mp4 to a .ts transport stream
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm -c copy remux into MPEG-TS in-browser.
rationale: TS is required by many streamers, hardware encoders, and HLS pipelines.

name: duplicate-line-check
description: Detects and reports duplicate lines in a text file, optionally ignoring case and whitespace, with line numbers.
example_prompt: Find any duplicate lines in this list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — hashing lines to find repeats is a single local pass
rationale: Duplicate entries in wordlists, configs, and exports cause subtle bugs and are tedious to spot manually.

name: svg-validator
description: Validates SVG well-formedness, checks required attributes, and flags embedded scripts or external references for safety.
example_prompt: Is this SVG valid and is it safe to inline?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (xml parse + rules); no rendering server
rationale: Inlining SVGs is risky (scripts/XXE) and a structure-plus-safety check is both useful and privacy-preserving.

name: image-psnr-calculator
description: Reports PSNR (dB) and MSE between two same-size images to quantify how lossy an encoding or edit was.
example_prompt: Calculate the PSNR between these before and after JPEGs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM does pure arithmetic over decoded channels, fully client-side
rationale: PSNR is the universal one-number quality yardstick for codec and pipeline tuning.

name: image-channel-diff
description: Splits two images into R, G, B channels and outputs a separate difference image per channel to isolate which channel changed.
example_prompt: Which color channel changed between these two photos?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM separates channels and diffs each, re-encoding three PNGs in-browser
rationale: Channel-isolated diffs pinpoint tints and single-channel artifacts a combined diff hides.

name: image-color-cast-compare
description: Detects and reports the average white-balance/color-cast shift (RGB offset and direction) between two images.
example_prompt: Is there a color cast difference between these two scans?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM averages channel means and computes the shift vector client-side
rationale: Quickly tells whether two captures have a white-balance mismatch before deeper editing.

name: url-status-check
description: Check the HTTP status of a pasted list of URLs and report code, redirects, and timing for each.
example_prompt: Check whether all these links are still alive
loader_feasibility: Fetches each URL via the HTTP host import (as broken-link-check does); in-browser.
rationale: broken-link-check scans one page; bulk-checking an arbitrary URL list is a distinct need.

name: video-set-stream-default-flag
description: Sets which audio or subtitle track is marked default/forced so the right one auto-plays.
example_prompt: make the english audio track the default in this mkv
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — -disposition flags with stream-copy in the WASM build.
rationale: Multi-track files frequently default to the wrong language and fixing the disposition is instant and lossless.

name: dxf-to-svg
description: Renders 2D entities from an AutoCAD DXF drawing (lines, arcs, circles, polylines, text) into a scalable SVG.
example_prompt: Convert this DXF drawing to SVG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (dxf crate) parsing entities and emitting SVG path markup locally.
rationale: Sharing CAD drawings on the web needs SVG, and DXF→SVG normally requires heavyweight CAD software.

name: common-lines
description: Finds the lines that appear in both of two text files, like the intersection mode of the Unix comm tool.
example_prompt: Show me the lines that appear in both of these files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — hash one file's lines and stream-match the other locally
rationale: Identifying shared entries between two lists is a common deduplication and reconciliation step.

name: bom-stripper
description: Detects and removes a leading UTF-8/UTF-16 byte-order mark, or optionally adds one.
example_prompt: Remove the BOM at the start of this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM byte-prefix check; fully client-side
rationale: A stray BOM silently corrupts the first field of CSVs and the first line of scripts, and it's invisible until something breaks.

name: jpeg-artifact-remover
description: Reduces blocky JPEG compression artifacts and ringing around edges.
example_prompt: Clean up the blocky compression artifacts in this JPEG
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime — a compact deblocking restoration model (e.g. FBCNN) runs locally on tiles
rationale: Deblocking heavily-compressed images is a distinct restoration need beyond generic denoise.

name: csv-boolean-normalizer
description: Maps varied truthy/falsy strings (Y/N, yes/no, 1/0, true/false) to a canonical boolean representation.
example_prompt: Normalize the 'active' column so Y, yes, and 1 all become true
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM lookup mapping over column values; local string work.
rationale: Mixed boolean encodings silently corrupt filters and need consistent normalization.

name: l2-row-normalizer
description: Normalizes each row of a numeric matrix to unit norm using L2, L1, or max norm.
example_prompt: L2-normalize each row of this feature matrix
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — per-row norm + divide, fully local
rationale: Row normalization is a ubiquitous ML preprocessing step with no offline single-purpose tool.

name: ics-builder
description: Builds a valid iCalendar (.ics) VEVENT from title, start/end, location, and description with proper escaping and line folding.
example_prompt: make an .ics event for a meeting next Tuesday 3-4pm
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; iCal text encoding, escaping, and 75-octet folding are local ops.
rationale: Generating add-to-calendar files requires fussy escaping and folding rules that hand-writing gets wrong.

name: opml-to-json
description: Parses an OPML subscription export into a flat JSON list of feed titles and URLs.
example_prompt: Turn this OPML file into a JSON list of feeds
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM OPML outline parser; pure local transform.
rationale: Migrating between feed readers means reshaping OPML, which is awkward to do by hand.

name: probability-normalizer
description: Rescales a vector of nonnegative numbers so they sum exactly to 1 (or 100%), reporting the original total.
example_prompt: Normalize these weights so they add up to 1
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sum + divide, no network
rationale: Turning raw weights or counts into a valid probability distribution is a tiny but constant need.

name: detrend-series
description: Removes a fitted linear or low-order polynomial trend from a numeric series, returning the residual.
example_prompt: Detrend this time series with a linear fit
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — least-squares fit + subtract, no network
rationale: Detrending before seasonality/spectral analysis is standard and currently requires a stats package.

name: rule-of-thirds-analyzer
description: Maps an image's visual-energy distribution onto rule-of-thirds gridlines and scores compositional placement.
example_prompt: Does this photo follow the rule of thirds?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes an edge/contrast energy map and evaluates thirds alignment in-browser.
rationale: Composition feedback is valuable for photographers and social-media croppers.

name: lower-third-generator
description: Generates a transparent (alpha) lower-third name-and-title graphic clip that animates in and out for compositing over footage.
example_prompt: Generate a transparent lower-third for 'Dr. Sarah Lin / Lead Researcher' that slides in
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg renders a ProRes-4444/WebM-alpha lower-third from `drawtext`/`drawbox` with no input footage in wasm.
rationale: Lower thirds are one of the most-used overlay assets and an alpha-channel generator lets users composite them in any editor.

name: fixture-array-generator
description: Generates an array of N objects from one example object, varying ids and selected fields.
example_prompt: Take this one example object and make an array of 25 with unique ids and varied names.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: cloning a template and mutating fields per index is pure local work.
rationale: Expanding a single hand-built example into a fixture set is a frequent test-setup chore.

name: sql-migration-scaffold
description: Generates paired up/down SQL migration file skeletons from a described change.
example_prompt: Scaffold up/down migrations to add a nullable 'phone' column to users.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: templating ALTER/CREATE statements with reversals is pure local computation.
rationale: Writing reversible migrations is repetitive and forgetting the down-step is a common bug.

name: png-integrity-check
description: Parses every PNG chunk and verifies CRC32 checksums to report corruption, truncation, or invalid chunk ordering.
example_prompt: Check if this PNG is corrupted or has bad chunks
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM walks the PNG byte stream and recomputes CRCs entirely in-memory, no decode or network needed.
rationale: Corrupt PNGs fail silently in many viewers; a hard chunk/CRC check tells you exactly where the file broke.

name: jpeg-structure-validator
description: Validates JPEG marker sequence (SOI/SOF/SOS/EOI), flags missing EOI, and detects premature truncation.
example_prompt: Is this JPEG file complete and valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans JPEG markers byte-by-byte client-side without decoding pixels.
rationale: Partially-downloaded or half-saved JPEGs are common and a marker check catches them before they ship.

name: svg-animation-to-video
description: Renders an animated SVG (SMIL or CSS keyframes) to an MP4 at a chosen duration, resolution, and frame rate.
example_prompt: Render this animated logo.svg to a 5-second transparent-background video
loader_feasibility: webgpu/canvas rasterizes each SVG animation frame in the browser and ffmpeg encodes the sequence locally.
rationale: Designers build motion graphics as SVG but need a video file to use them in editors, and no local SVG-to-video tool exists.

name: faker-dataset-generator
description: Generates locale-aware synthetic datasets using Python's Faker library in a sandbox.
example_prompt: Use Faker to generate 50 fake German customers with address and phone.
loader_feasibility: pyodide: bundles the Faker package and runs it entirely in the Python-in-WASM sandbox.
rationale: Faker is the de-facto standard for synthetic data and exposing it browser-local needs zero install.

name: synthetic-regression-dataset
description: Generates a synthetic regression dataset from a chosen linear or polynomial ground-truth function with configurable Gaussian noise and feature count.
example_prompt: Generate 200 points from y = 3x + 2 with noise sd 0.5
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — seeded sampling and noise injection, emits CSV in-browser.
rationale: Reproducible labeled regression data is essential for demos and teaching and is awkward to hand-build with known parameters.

name: component-boilerplate-generator
description: Generates a UI component skeleton (props interface, file, and basic markup) for React, Vue, or Svelte from a name and prop list.
example_prompt: Scaffold a React component called Button with variant and disabled props
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM templating per framework; emits source text locally
rationale: Spinning up components with consistent prop typing and structure is a constant front-end chore.

name: spx-to-wav
description: Decodes legacy Speex (.spx) voice files to WAV.
example_prompt: convert this old speex .spx recording to wav
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader has the Speex decoder, producing PCM WAV in-browser.
rationale: Older VoIP and podcast recordings used Speex, now deprecated and unplayable in current apps without conversion.

name: matrix-market-to-csv
description: Expands a MatrixMarket .mtx sparse-matrix file into a dense CSV grid (or a row/col/value triplet CSV).
example_prompt: Turn this .mtx sparse matrix into a dense CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the MatrixMarket header and coordinate entries are line-oriented ASCII, trivially parsed and reassembled in WASM.
rationale: Scientific/graph datasets ship as .mtx and most tools can't open them without a converter.

name: endian-swap-float-binary
description: Byte-swaps a raw binary array of fixed-width floats/ints between little- and big-endian.
example_prompt: Swap this big-endian float32 file to little-endian
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: reversing bytes per element is a tight local loop over the buffer in WASM memory.
rationale: Cross-platform binary data breaks silently on endianness mismatch and a swap fixes it instantly.

name: number-base-csv-converter
description: Converts a chosen column of integers in a CSV between bases (binary, octal, decimal, hex, or arbitrary radix).
example_prompt: Convert the hex ID column in this CSV to decimal
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parsing and re-emitting integers in any radix is standard big-integer-safe arithmetic done client-side.
rationale: Mixed-base data (hex IDs, binary flags) needs uniform decimal for analysis without per-cell manual edits.

name: tensor-reshape-file
description: Reshapes a flat numeric array file into a target N-D shape (row/column-major) and re-serializes it.
example_prompt: Reshape this 784-length vector into a 28x28 grid CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: validating element counts and re-indexing by stride order is pure integer/memory work done client-side.
rationale: Flattened model tensors (e.g. MNIST rows) are unintelligible until reshaped into their real dimensions.

name: whitespace-lint
description: Flags trailing whitespace, mixed tabs/spaces, and missing final newline.
example_prompt: Show me the whitespace problems in this file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line scanning; client-side
rationale: Whitespace issues cause noisy diffs and broken indentation-sensitive formats.

name: cpf-cnpj-validator
description: Validates Brazilian CPF and CNPJ taxpayer numbers using their two weighted mod-11 check digits.
example_prompt: Is CPF 111.444.777-35 valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: double weighted-mod-11 computation, no government API call.
rationale: Brazilian signup and billing forms validate CPF/CNPJ constantly and want it fully offline.

name: sql-explain
description: Parse a SQL query and describe in plain English what it selects, joins, filters, and groups.
example_prompt: explain this query: SELECT u.name, COUNT(*) FROM users u JOIN orders o ON o.uid=u.id GROUP BY u.name
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM SQL parser walks the AST and narrates it; complement to existing text-to-sql.
rationale: Reading unfamiliar SQL is a daily task and the reverse of text-to-sql is missing.

name: bleu-rouge-scorer
description: Scores generated text against reference text using BLEU and ROUGE-N/L for translation and summarization eval.
example_prompt: Compute BLEU and ROUGE between this machine translation and the reference
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizes and computes n-gram overlap locally
rationale: BLEU/ROUGE are the bread-and-butter metrics for the MT (Vamshi Ambati) and LLM-eval (Maxim AI) crowds.

name: social-text-cleaner
description: Cleans social-media text by stripping URLs, mentions, hashtags, and emoji, with optional tokenization.
example_prompt: Clean these tweets for analysis — remove links, mentions, and emoji
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies regex/unicode normalization locally
rationale: Pre-cleaning noisy social text is the unavoidable first step in Mining the Social Web-style analysis.

name: json-to-ini
description: Flattens a two-level JSON object into INI sections and key=value pairs.
example_prompt: Convert this JSON into an INI config
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string-building from serde_json; fully local.
rationale: Lets users author INI from structured data without round-tripping through a website.

name: flac-to-alac
description: Repackages lossless FLAC into Apple Lossless (ALAC) in an .m4a container with no quality loss.
example_prompt: convert my flac album to alac for apple music
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader decodes FLAC and re-encodes to ALAC (lossless) in wasm.
rationale: iTunes/Apple Music and iOS won't import FLAC, so audiophiles must move their lossless libraries to ALAC.

name: midi-to-csv
description: Exports a MIDI file's events to a human-readable CSV (time, track, type, note, velocity).
example_prompt: dump this midi file's notes to a csv
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM (midly) decodes events and writes CSV rows, no dependencies or server.
rationale: Researchers and devs analyze or diff MIDI in spreadsheets/scripts, which is impossible with the binary format.

name: bcrypt-verify
description: Checks whether a plaintext password matches a given bcrypt hash.
example_prompt: Does the password 'hunter2' match this bcrypt hash?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the bcrypt crate; the compare is local constant-time computation.
rationale: Verifying a stored bcrypt hash is a frequent auth-debugging step that must stay private.

name: video-shader-transition
description: Applies a GL-style transition (wipe, morph, dissolve) between two clips by shading each boundary frame.
example_prompt: Blend these two clips with a swirl GL transition
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader decodes/encodes frames while webgpu-compute renders the transition shader, all in-browser
rationale: Directly realizes the ffmpeg-gl-transition demand with the actual shader path rather than a flat crossfade.

name: motion-photo-splitter
description: Splits an Android/Google Motion Photo (a JPEG with an appended MP4) into the still image and the embedded video clip.
example_prompt: Split this motion photo into the still and the video
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM locates the embedded MP4 via the XMP offset and slices the bytes locally; ffmpeg can remux the clip.
rationale: Aves surfaces motion photos and users want to recover the hidden video, which most galleries hide or discard.

name: blob-counter
description: Detects and counts distinct blobs or objects (e.g. cells, dots, particles) in an image.
example_prompt: Count the cells in this microscope image
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs scikit-image's blob_log/blob_dog detectors locally on the decoded image.
rationale: Automated object counting is a high-value lab/QA task that scikit-image solves and nobody offers free in-browser.

name: seaborn-plot
description: Executes Seaborn statistical-plot code (regression, pairplot, distribution) over pasted data and returns a PNG.
example_prompt: Seaborn pairplot of this iris-style dataset colored by species
loader_feasibility: pyodide loads pandas+seaborn via micropip and renders with Agg to PNG entirely in the browser.
rationale: Maps Seaborn (and ggplot2-style statistical graphics) demand to a true Python statistical-viz environment.

name: news-category-classifier
description: Classifies a news article into topic categories (politics, sports, economy, tech, etc.) on-device.
example_prompt: What category does this news article belong to?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a zero-shot/text-classification model in WASM on the article text locally.
rationale: Directly serves the categorized-news demand (NAYN.CO Turkish News) without sending articles to a server.

name: feed-convert
description: Convert a feed between RSS 2.0, Atom, and JSON Feed formats.
example_prompt: Convert this Atom feed to JSON Feed
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust parse + re-serialize in-browser (input fetched client-side).
rationale: Format conversion distinct from rss-parse (which only reads) and sitemap tools.

name: python-nlp-sandbox
description: Runs Python NLP snippets (regex, scikit-learn, textstat, numpy) in an in-browser Pyodide sandbox.
example_prompt: Run this Python: vectorize these docs with sklearn TfidfVectorizer and print the vocab.
loader_feasibility: pyodide; CPython compiled to WASM runs the code locally with bundled pure-Python/scientific packages, no server.
rationale: An offline Python sandbox directly serves the 'NLP in Python' / NLTK-tutorial demand and lets learners experiment without setup.

name: rule-based-entity-matcher
description: Extracts entities and spans using human-readable pattern rules instead of a model.
example_prompt: Find every dosage and drug name in these clinical notes using pattern rules.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM compiles a small RITA-style rule DSL into matchers over tokenized text; deterministic and local.
rationale: RITA DSL exists for exactly this transparent, trainless pattern extraction, which complements the statistical NER tool for domain-specific spans.

name: thai-text-normalizer
description: Normalizes Thai text by fixing character ordering, collapsing repeats, and expanding the maiyamok (ๆ) repetition mark.
example_prompt: Normalize this messy Thai text so it's clean for search: ทำงานๆๆ
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: deterministic normalization rules with no external dependency
rationale: Raw Thai input from the web is full of malformed sequences that break search and matching unless normalized first.

name: octave-band-analyzer
description: Computes 1/1 and 1/3-octave band sound levels (A/C/Z-weighted) from an audio signal.
example_prompt: Give me the 1/3-octave band levels for this noise recording
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — octave-band filtering and weighting are pure DSP that run in wasmi.
rationale: Octave-band analysis is a staple of the acoustics package for noise and room measurements.

name: room-impulse-response-sim
description: Simulates a room impulse response from room dimensions, absorption, and source/mic positions via the image-source method.
example_prompt: Simulate the impulse response of a 5x4x3m room with the mic in the corner
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the image-source geometry math is pure compute and runs in wasmi.
rationale: RIR simulation is pyroomacoustics' headline feature, valuable for auralization and AR/VR audio.

name: phoneme-transcriber
description: Transcribes speech into a phoneme (IPA) sequence rather than words.
example_prompt: Give me the phonemes spoken in this clip
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a wav2vec2 phoneme-recognition model in the browser.
rationale: Phoneme transcription supports pronunciation training and low-resource linguistic work that word ASR can't.

name: violin-plot
description: Generates SVG violin plots showing the kernel-density distribution shape for each group.
example_prompt: Violin plot comparing salary distributions by department
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM does KDE estimation and mirrored-path SVG output locally.
rationale: A richer Seaborn distribution view than box plots when shape and multimodality matter.

name: cowrie-log-parser
description: Parse Cowrie/SSH honeypot JSON logs into attacker session timelines with commands run and downloaded payload IOCs.
example_prompt: Summarize the attacker sessions in this Cowrie log
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: JSON-line parsing and aggregation over the pasted log, fully local.
rationale: Turns noisy honeypot output into readable threat intel without a backend.

name: download-url-extractor
description: Extracts and de-duplicates all downloadable links by extension or pattern from pasted HTML or text.
example_prompt: Pull every PDF and zip link out of this page's HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML/text scan with regex, no fetching
rationale: Feeds batch download managers like uGet/Persepolis a clean URL list.

name: abc-to-midi

name: list-transform

name: markdown-to-email

example_prompt: convert this markdown newsletter to email-ready HTML

rationale: Email HTML needs inline styles and quirks handling that generic markdown-to-html ignores, making this a distinct newsletter tool.

name: glitch-art

loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute — channel offsets and pixel-sort passes run as local GPU shaders.
rationale: A trendy aesthetic for album art and social posts with no offline equivalent.

name: plus-code
description: Encode coordinates to a Google Plus Code (Open Location Code) and decode one back.
example_prompt: What's the Plus Code for 48.8584, 2.2945?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM OLC algorithm; offline.

name: dechunk-http-response

Dechunk this body: 4
Wiki
5
pedia
0

name: mojibake-fixer

name: invisible-text-encoder

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: encodes bytes as zero-width codepoint sequences interleaved in cover text, fully offline.

name: text-similarity
description: Compute the semantic similarity score between two pieces of text using sentence embeddings and cosine distance.

name: latex-ocr
description: Convert a photo/screenshot of a math formula into LaTeX source.
example_prompt: extract the LaTeX from this equation screenshot
loader_feasibility: transformers.js/ONNX vision-encoder-decoder (Texify/pix2tex class); WASM/WebGPU.
rationale: Hugely useful for students/researchers and not covered by plain OCR.

name: settle-up
description: Given who-paid-what in a group, compute the minimal set of repayments to settle everyone up.
example_prompt: We split a trip — here's who paid what; who owes whom?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM debt-minimization; offline.
rationale: Splitwise-style settlement is far beyond the single-bill tip-split tool.

name: home-affordability
description: Estimate the home price you can afford from income, debts, down payment, and rate (DTI-based).
example_prompt: What house price can I afford on $120k income, $500 debts, 20% down?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM DTI and payment math, offline.
rationale: A flagship real-estate calculator distinct from computing a known mortgage payment.

name: image-extend
description: Outpaint an image beyond its original borders, generating plausible new content to extend the scene.
example_prompt: extend this photo to a 16:9 frame by filling in the sides
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute diffusion, the same WebGPU path the existing imagine tool uses; runs in-browser.
rationale: Outpainting/uncrop is one of the most popular generative-image features and reuses proven WebGPU infrastructure.

name: depth-estimate
description: Produce a depth map from a single photo.
example_prompt: Make a depth map of this photo: <image url or ref>
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs DPT/Depth-Anything ONNX models in-browser; outputs a grayscale PNG.
rationale: Enables fun and practical effects (parallax, bokeh) entirely client-side.

name: image-steganography
description: Hide a secret message inside an image (LSB) and extract hidden messages back out.
example_prompt: hide 'meet at 8' inside this picture
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM least-significant-bit encode/decode.
rationale: Fun + privacy use case that's a classic CyberChef-style tool absent here.

name: video-interpolate
description: Generate smooth slow-motion by interpolating intermediate frames.
example_prompt: make this 30fps clip smooth 120fps slow motion
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime frame-interpolation model (RIFE-class) in-browser.
rationale: AI slow-mo is a sought-after effect distinct from frame-dropping speed changes.

name: readability-scorer
description: Computes Flesch–Kincaid and related readability scores and flags long or complex sentences.
example_prompt: how readable is this paragraph and which sentences are too long?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM counts syllables/words/sentences and applies the formulas locally.
rationale: PolishMyWriting demand maps to objective, instant writing-quality feedback.

name: ambient-mixer
description: Layers multiple looping sound files into a single soundscape with per-track volume.
example_prompt: Mix rain, thunder, and a fireplace loop into one ambient track
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg amix combines and weights several decoded inputs locally.
rationale: Directly mirrors Ambient Mixer's layered-loop product and runs offline on uploaded loops.

name: charset-encoder
description: Encodes text into a chosen character set (UTF-8/16, Latin-1, Windows-1252, Shift-JIS, etc.) and shows the resulting bytes as hex.
example_prompt: encode "café" as Windows-1252 and show the bytes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via encoding_rs — all codecs are pure Rust tables that compile to wasm32
rationale: Debugging cross-locale text bugs requires seeing exact byte output per charset, which no built-in browser API exposes cleanly.

name: count-occurrences
description: Counts how many times a substring, word, or pattern appears in the text.
example_prompt: count how many times 'TODO' appears in this file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: scanning and tallying matches is a pure single-pass computation with no I/O.
rationale: Counting a specific term (distinct from total word count) is a frequent quick-answer query in chat.

name: sql-to-graphql-schema
description: Generates a GraphQL SDL schema (types, queries, relations) from SQL table definitions.
example_prompt: generate a GraphQL schema from these database tables
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the DDL and maps columns/foreign keys to GraphQL types client-side.
rationale: This is precisely what seaography does (SQL→GraphQL), and the mapping is deterministic and browser-friendly.

name: sql-to-typescript-types
description: Generates TypeScript interfaces/types from SQL CREATE TABLE statements with correct nullable and type mapping.
example_prompt: give me TypeScript types for this database schema
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — DDL parse plus a type map to TS, no execution needed.
rationale: Front-end and full-stack devs constantly need type-safe shapes matching their DB, a quick deterministic transform.

name: email-auth-record-explainer
description: Parses and validates SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MTA-STS, and BIMI DNS TXT records, explaining each mechanism and flagging misconfigurations.
example_prompt: Explain this SPF record and tell me if it's set up correctly: v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via mail-auth record parsers — the user pastes the record text, so no DNS/server is involved
rationale: Email-deliverability setup is confusing and a local explainer turns cryptic record syntax into plain guidance without any infrastructure.

name: gdscript-formatter
description: Auto-formats GDScript source to the canonical Godot style using the gdtoolkit gdformat rules.
example_prompt: Format this GDScript file with standard Godot indentation and spacing.
loader_feasibility: pyodide — gdtoolkit's gdformat is pure Python, so it runs in the in-browser Python sandbox with the file never leaving the page.
rationale: GDScript has no built-in editor formatter for many setups and gdtoolkit is the de facto standard, so a zero-install browser formatter has real pull.

name: texture-power-of-two-resizer
description: Resizes or pads a texture to the nearest power-of-two dimensions to satisfy GPU mipmap and compression constraints.
example_prompt: Pad this 600x400 texture to the next power of two.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — scale and pad filters handle power-of-two adjustment locally on the supplied image.
rationale: Many engines and older GPUs still require POT textures, and getting the right padding/scaling by hand is fiddly.

name: mvt-decode
description: Decode a Mapbox Vector Tile (.pbf/.mvt) into readable GeoJSON.
example_prompt: Decode this .mvt tile to GeoJSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via geozero/mvt — protobuf decode and geometry rebuild are pure compute.
rationale: Inspecting vector tiles is painful without tooling; decoding offline aids map debugging.

name: cidr-overlap-detector
description: Checks a list of CIDR blocks for overlaps, containment, and adjacency to catch conflicting routes or rules.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pairwise prefix comparison on integers, fully local.
rationale: Overlapping CIDRs are a frequent cause of routing and firewall bugs that are easy to miss manually.

name: proto-file-formatter
description: Parses, validates, and pretty-prints a .proto file, flagging syntax errors and inconsistent formatting.
example_prompt: Format and lint this .proto file for me.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — protobuf IDL tokenizer/formatter over text, fully local.
rationale: Consistent .proto formatting and quick validation help gRPC developers without running protoc locally.

name: rust-perf-lint
description: Scans Rust source for common performance anti-patterns (needless clone, collect-then-iterate, allocation in hot loops, String concat in loops) and suggests fixes.
example_prompt: Check this Rust function for performance problems.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: syn AST walk with heuristic lint rules, fully offline.
rationale: Operationalizes 'The Rust Performance Book' / 'Performance of Rust' guidance as an actionable linter.

name: rust-doc-comment-generator
description: Parses a Rust function or type signature and scaffolds a /// doc comment with Arguments, Returns, Errors, Panics, and Examples sections.
example_prompt: Generate a doc comment template for this Rust function signature.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: syn extracts params and return type, then fills a template locally.
rationale: Supports the documentation discipline in 'Rust Guidelines' / 'Rust for professionals' with zero setup.

name: rust-test-scaffolder
description: Given a Rust function, generates a #[test] skeleton with arrange/act/assert structure and edge-case stubs derived from the signature.
example_prompt: Write a test scaffold for this Rust function.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: syn parses the signature and emits a test template, no compiler involved.
rationale: Encourages the testing habits behind 'Rust for professionals' directly from a pasted function.

name: text-tone-analyzer
description: Classifies the tone and emotion of a passage (formal, casual, joyful, angry, etc.) with confidence scores.
example_prompt: What tone does this email come across as?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — emotion/tone classification model executes client-side
rationale: Toney-style tone checking helps writers calibrate messages before sending.

name: agenda-builder
description: Turns a list of tasks with durations and priorities into a time-blocked daily agenda.
example_prompt: Schedule these 6 tasks into my 9-5 with breaks
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — greedy scheduling math, no server
rationale: lazyorg-style agenda planning is a common need that's pure computation.

name: ics-todo-extractor
description: Extracts VTODO tasks from an iCalendar file into a checklist with due dates and priorities.
example_prompt: Pull the to-dos out of this .ics file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM VTODO parsing, local only
rationale: Many task apps export ICS; this surfaces the buried tasks as a usable list.

name: conventional-commit-versioner
description: Reads a list of conventional-commit messages and computes the next semantic version (feat→minor, fix→patch, BREAKING→major) with a generated release summary.
example_prompt: Given these commit messages, what should the next version be? [pastes commits]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses commit prefixes and applies semver bump rules, no I/O.
rationale: Release-automation behind these update tools depends on conventional-commits version inference, which is fully deterministic locally.

name: kdbx-reader
description: Open a KeePass .kdbx database with its master password (and optional key file) and search or list entry titles, usernames, URLs, and revealed passwords.
example_prompt: open this .kdbx with my master password and find the github entry
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the pure-Rust `keepass` crate; AES/ChaCha20 + Argon2/AES-KDF decryption runs in the wasmi sandbox so the vault is never uploaded.
rationale: Maps directly to kpcli/kpxhs — letting people read their KeePass vault on any device without installing a client and without the vault ever leaving the browser.

name: text-to-flowchart
description: Turns a numbered list of steps and decisions into Mermaid flowchart syntax.
example_prompt: Make a flowchart: user submits form, validate, if valid save else show error
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM text transformation emitting Mermaid; no runtime dependencies
rationale: Going from prose steps to a diagram spec by hand is tedious and error-prone.

name: output-diff-checker
description: Compares actual program output against expected output with optional regex/wildcard lines and ignore rules, reporting pass/fail and the differing lines.
example_prompt: Does this actual output match the expected output (treat lines with [NUM] as regex)?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: line diffing and pattern matching are pure string operations
rationale: pvcheck (and Scrut) demand maps to a flexible expected-vs-actual checker useful for graders and CLI test authoring.

name: wifi-passphrase-strength
description: Scores a Wi-Fi/WPA passphrase for entropy, length, and resistance to common cracking dictionaries.
example_prompt: How strong is this Wi-Fi password: latte123
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes entropy and checks against a small bundled common-password list; pure local math, no transmission.
rationale: passphrase strength is the defensive flip side of wifi-password recovery, and checking it must stay offline to be safe.

name: shell-command-formatter
description: Reformats long piped shell one-liners into readable multi-line form with line continuations and aligned pipes.
example_prompt: Format this into readable multi-line: cat x | grep foo | awk '{print $2}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — shell-aware tokenization and pretty-printing of the command string, entirely local.
rationale: inshellisense-style help is about understanding commands, and reflowing a dense pipeline into readable steps is the fastest way to grasp one.

name: timeblock-scheduler
description: Packs a task list with estimates into time blocks across a working day given start time, work hours, and breaks.
example_prompt: Time-block my day from 9am to 5pm with a lunch break for these tasks and estimates
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — greedy bin-packing over a time window, pure computation.
rationale: Time-blocking is the planning step the CLI task tools leave to the user; automating it is high-value.

name: task-dependency-sort
description: Topologically orders tasks by their dependencies and detects and reports any dependency cycles.
example_prompt: Order these tasks so dependencies come first, and tell me if there's a cycle
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — graph build plus Kahn's algorithm, all in memory.
rationale: dstask and grit model dependencies but few tools compute a safe execution order or catch cycles.

name: wrong-layout-decoder
description: Recovers text that was typed while the OS was set to the wrong keyboard layout by re-mapping it between QWERTY, Dvorak, Colemak, and other layouts.
example_prompt: I typed this with my keyboard in Dvorak by mistake — convert it back to what I meant on QWERTY
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM character-position remapping using bundled layout tables; deterministic offline transform
rationale: Solves a real, common annoyance (passwords/notes garbled by a stray layout switch) and reuses the layout maps from the analyzer tools.

name: char-inspect
description: Lists every character in a string with its codepoint, name, category and width, exposing hidden or invisible characters.
example_prompt: Inspect every character in this string for hidden ones
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: iterates the string and looks up Unicode metadata locally.
rationale: Reveals zero-width, combining or look-alike characters that break copy-pasted code or data.

name: text-snapshot-diff
description: Diffs two pasted text snapshots (e.g. before/after command output) and highlights exactly what changed between them.
example_prompt: What changed between these two outputs? <pastes version A> <pastes version B>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a Myers/LCS diff over two strings runs entirely client-side.
rationale: This is the browser-local realization of watch/sasqwatch: spot the delta between two captures of the same thing.

name: minify-css
description: Minifies and optionally autoprefixes CSS, reporting the size savings.
example_prompt: Minify this CSS and tell me how many bytes I saved
loader_feasibility: lightningcss is pure Rust with a WASM build, so minification happens entirely in the browser.
rationale: Asset minification rounds out the prettier/dprint formatting demand with the size-reduction side dev tooling cares about.

name: knn-classifier
description: Classifies new rows by majority vote of their k nearest neighbors in your CSV training data.
example_prompt: Use k-NN to predict the category of these new samples.
loader_feasibility: smartcore/rustlearn k-NN in plain Rust→WASM; distance computation runs client-side.
rationale: k-NN is a simple, training-free classifier that's ideal for small local datasets.

name: matrix-multiply
description: Multiplies two matrices and returns the product with shape validation.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: dimforge/nalgebra (or faer-rs) provides BLAS-style dense matmul that compiles to WASM and runs in-browser.
rationale: Matrix multiplication is the most-requested linear-algebra operation and runs instantly client-side.

name: polynomial-tool
description: Finds roots, fits, differentiates, and evaluates polynomials.
example_prompt: Find the roots of x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: polynomial algorithms are pure math that run in wasmi.
rationale: Polynomial manipulation spans algebra homework to signal design and benefits from instant answers.

name: verbal-regex-builder
description: Builds a regex from a structured, human-readable specification of constraints (starts with, digits, optional, etc.).
example_prompt: Build a regex: starts with https, then ://, then any non-space characters until end
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; deterministic mapping of a constraint grammar to regex syntax, fully local string assembly.
rationale: Captures VerbalExpressions, Super Expressive, and js-regex as one fluent builder for people who think in intent, not syntax.

name: multi-pattern-matcher
description: Matches many regex patterns against the same text at once and reports which patterns hit and where.
example_prompt: Which of these patterns match 'ERROR 500 at /api': ERROR\s\d+, WARN, /api/\w+
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using the `regex` crate's `RegexSet` for simultaneous linear-time matching, all in-sandbox.
rationale: Brings Hyperscan-style multi-pattern scanning (rules engines, log triage) to the browser without its native dependency.

name: regex-code-snippet
description: Wraps a tested regex into ready-to-paste code for Python re, JavaScript, Java, Go, grep, and sed.
example_prompt: Give me Python and grep code that uses the regex ^ERROR.*timeout$
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string templating per language; fully client-side.
rationale: Bridges the gap from a working pattern to usable code across the exact languages the demand terms name.

name: regex-recipe-library
description: A searchable library of vetted regex recipes (email, URL, IPv4/6, dates, phone, hex color, UUID) you can test and copy.
example_prompt: Give me a reliable regex for matching ISO-8601 dates and let me test it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM serves static recipes plus the local tester; no network.
rationale: Direct mapping of 'Regular Expressions Cookbook' and 'Pocket Reference' into copy-and-test recipes.

name: analytics-csv-summary
description: Ingests a Google Analytics / Simple Analytics CSV export and produces a clean summary: sessions, top pages, sources, conversion and bounce rates.
example_prompt: Summarize this Google Analytics export — top traffic sources and pages
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — CSV parsing and metric rollups run locally.
rationale: Turns raw analytics exports into readable insight client-side, no third-party processing.

name: sessionize-events
description: Groups a raw pageview/event log into user sessions by user id and inactivity timeout, then reports session counts, duration, and paths.
example_prompt: Sessionize this event log with a 30-minute timeout and show average session length
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sorting and windowing over rows is deterministic and local.
rationale: Core product-analytics transform (raw events → sessions) that normally requires a hosted pipeline.

name: jsonp-unwrap
description: Strips the callback wrapper from a JSONP response to recover the raw JSON payload.
example_prompt: Extract the JSON from this JSONP callback response
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — trims the leading callback identifier and trailing parens, pure text op.
rationale: Legacy JSONP endpoints still exist and unwrapping the padding by hand is exactly the kind of small chore a tool should own.

name: json-pointer-resolve
description: Resolves an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer against a document and returns the referenced value.
example_prompt: What value does the JSON Pointer /items/0/price point to in this JSON?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM pointer parser + lookup; client-side
rationale: JSON Pointers appear in JSON Schema $ref and patches; resolving them by hand is fiddly.

name: json-circular-refs
description: Encodes/decodes JSON containing circular or shared references using $ref pointers (CircularJSON).
example_prompt: Serialize this object graph that has a circular reference into safe JSON with $ref pointers.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tracks visited nodes and rewrites cycles as JSON Pointers locally.
rationale: Logging or persisting object graphs with cycles otherwise throws, and the fix is pure logic.

name: 3des-encrypt-decrypt
description: Encrypts and decrypts with legacy Triple DES (3DES) for interop with older systems.
example_prompt: Decrypt this 3DES ciphertext for me.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the des crate; fully local.
rationale: 3DES appears explicitly in demand because legacy payment and enterprise systems still emit it and need decoding.

name: openapi-to-types
description: Generate typed client models (TypeScript/Rust/Go/Python) from an OpenAPI/Swagger spec.
example_prompt: Generate TypeScript interfaces from this OpenAPI schema
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — local spec parsing and code emission, no codegen server.
rationale: API client typing is a frequent dev chore and a step beyond json-to-types' single-sample inference.

name: mel-spectrogram
description: Produces a mel-scaled spectrogram (and optional MFCCs) suitable for ML feature extraction.
example_prompt: Give me the mel spectrogram and MFCCs for this voice sample
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — FFT plus a mel filterbank computed in wasm, no server.
rationale: Mel features are the standard front end for audio ML, so on-device extraction is broadly useful.

name: loudness-meter
description: Measures integrated/short-term LUFS loudness, true peak, RMS, and dynamic range of a track.
example_prompt: What's the LUFS and true peak of this master?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader — the ebur128 filter computes loudness statistics in wasm.
rationale: Loudness/level metering (acoustics, pyfar) is essential before publishing audio to any platform.

name: signal-wavelet-decompose
description: Decomposes any uploaded numeric time series into wavelet approximation and detail bands for denoising or trend extraction.
example_prompt: Wavelet-decompose this sensor CSV and remove the noise band
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM discrete wavelet transform processes the CSV locally; no data leaves the browser.
rationale: Wavelet decomposition is a go-to for denoising and multiresolution analysis of sensor, finance, and biomedical series.

name: speaker-verify
description: Compares two voice clips and reports whether they are the same speaker with a similarity score.
example_prompt: Are these two recordings the same person speaking?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime loader — a small speaker-embedding model (ECAPA-TDNN/x-vector) runs in onnxruntime-web; cosine similarity of the two embeddings is pure arithmetic.
rationale: Voice-match verification without sending biometric audio to a cloud service is exactly the kind of privacy-sensitive task that belongs client-side.

name: dtw-audio-align
description: Aligns two recordings of the same piece via dynamic time warping and reports the warp path.
example_prompt: Align these two takes of the same song
loader_feasibility: pyodide computes chroma features and runs DTW entirely in-browser.
rationale: Compares performances and syncs a cover to the original (Fundamentals of Music Processing demand).

name: image-convolve
description: Applies a custom or preset convolution kernel (blur, sharpen, emboss, edge) to an image.
example_prompt: Sharpen this photo.
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute runs the convolution as a GPU shader over the image on the user's device.
rationale: Kernel convolution is the foundation of WebGL image processing and gives one tool a whole family of fast filters.

name: glsl-to-spirv
description: Compiles a GLSL shader to a SPIR-V binary module and shows the hex/word output.
example_prompt: Compile this GLSL compute shader to SPIR-V
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via naga's GLSL frontend and SPIR-V backend, all compiled to WASM and run client-side.
rationale: SPIR-V is the common intermediate for Vulkan/WebGPU toolchains and there's no good zero-install browser compiler for it.

name: equirectangular-to-cubemap
description: Converts a 360° equirectangular panorama into the six cubemap face images for WebGL skyboxes.
example_prompt: Convert this 360 panorama into cubemap faces
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute samples the panorama per cube face on the GPU and returns the six images, all in-browser.
rationale: Skyboxes and WebVR environments need cubemaps, and converting from equirectangular sources is otherwise a desktop-tool chore.

name: geohash-converter
description: Encodes lat/lon to a geohash at chosen precision and decodes geohashes back to a bounding box.
example_prompt: Geohash for lat 37.77 lon -122.42 at precision 8
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: geohash bit-interleave, pure math.
rationale: Geohashing is a standard spatial-indexing primitive for map data pipelines that lacks a quick chat tool.

name: procedural-texture-generator
description: Generates tileable noise, gradient, checker, and Voronoi textures via GPU shaders at a chosen size.
example_prompt: Generate a 512px seamless Perlin noise texture
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute: noise/voronoi shaders run on the local GPU.
rationale: Procedural textures feed materials in every 3D engine and a one-prompt generator beats hunting for asset packs.

name: game-texture-converter
description: Inspects and converts game texture formats (DDS, KTX2, PNG) including mip and compression details.
example_prompt: Convert this DDS texture to PNG and show its mip levels
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: container parsing and transcoding run over the uploaded texture in-browser.
rationale: DDS/KTX2 handling is a constant graphics-pipeline need and a local converter avoids heavyweight tooling.

name: hash-wordlist-cracker
description: Cracks a single supplied hash against a user-provided wordlist using GPU-accelerated hashing, for CTF and password-strength auditing.
example_prompt: Try to crack this MD5 hash with this wordlist for my CTF challenge
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute: hash kernels run thousands of candidates per dispatch on the local GPU; wordlist stays in memory, nothing leaves the device.
rationale: Brings John the Ripper's dictionary attack to the browser for legitimate CTF and self-audit use, with no candidate or hash ever uploaded.

name: ole-structure-viewer
description: Browses the storage/stream tree of an OLE/CFB compound file and lets you dump any stream as hex or text.
example_prompt: Show me the internal streams of this .doc compound file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the CFB directory and FAT structures parse directly from file bytes in memory.
rationale: Gives oletools' structural view of legacy Office and MSI files, the foundation for understanding embedded objects and payloads.

name: noun-phrase-extractor
description: Extracts noun phrases and base chunks from text for terminology and concept mining.
example_prompt: Extract the key noun phrases from this abstract.
loader_feasibility: transformers-js for POS tags + plain Rust→WASM chunking rules, all client-side.
rationale: Noun-phrase chunking is a standard shallow-parsing step and a practical way to surface concepts from documents.

name: ner-preannotator
description: Auto-pre-annotates text with entity labels and exports in CoNLL/BIO for import into labeling tools.
example_prompt: Pre-label these sentences with entities and give me CoNLL output
loader_feasibility: transformers-js NER plus Rust→WASM BIO formatting, browser-local.
rationale: Model-assisted pre-annotation is the top productivity feature of doccano, Label Studio, UBIAI and prodigy.

name: privacy-policy-analyzer
description: Summarizes a privacy policy and flags clauses about data collection, sharing, and retention.
example_prompt: analyze this privacy policy for what data they collect
loader_feasibility: transformers-js zero-shot-classification and summarization run locally, so the policy text never leaves the device.
rationale: Privee-style consumer protection where running locally is the entire point — analyzing privacy without sacrificing it.

name: chinese-script-converter
description: Converts between Simplified and Traditional Chinese, including region phrase variants.
example_prompt: Convert this Simplified Chinese text to Traditional.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — OpenCC-style mapping dictionaries bundled into the WASM module.
rationale: Simplified⇄Traditional conversion (a HanLP feature) is constantly needed across CN/TW/HK audiences with no API call.

name: german-compound-splitter
