description: Splits long German compound nouns into their constituent words.
example_prompt: Split Donaudampfschifffahrtsgesellschaft into its parts.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — dictionary-driven longest-match splitting with a bundled German wordlist, offline.
rationale: Compound splitting is the signature German-NLP problem that wrecks search and TTS, solvable fully client-side.

name: polish-stemmer
description: Reduces Polish words to stems to group inflected forms for search and analysis.
example_prompt: Stem these Polish words.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Stempel-style stemming table bundled into the module (Snowball lacks Polish), offline.
rationale: Polish's heavy inflection makes stemming essential for recall, and it's absent from common stemmer libraries (Polish-NLP demand).

name: polish-diacritics-folder
description: Folds Polish diacritics to base Latin letters (ł→l, ż→z, ą→a) and back-maps for matching.
example_prompt: Remove the Polish diacritics from these surnames.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — fixed character-mapping table, runs offline.
rationale: Diacritic folding is the standard way to make Polish names searchable in ASCII systems.

name: devanagari-normalizer
description: Normalizes Indic Unicode text — canonical nukta forms, ZWJ/ZWNJ cleanup, and native↔Western digit conversion.
example_prompt: Normalize this Devanagari text and convert the digits to Western.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM Unicode table operations; normalization is rule-based and deterministic, running entirely in the browser.
rationale: The IIT Bombay Indic NLP Resources include exactly this normalization step, and inconsistent Indic Unicode silently breaks search, dedup, and embeddings.

name: thai-word-segmenter
description: Splits unspaced Thai text into words using a bundled dictionary with maximal-matching (newmm-style) plus character-cluster awareness.
example_prompt: Split this Thai sentence into words: สวัสดีครับยินดีต้อนรับ
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: longest/maximal dictionary matching over a bundled Thai wordlist is a pure algorithm with no network call
rationale: Thai has no spaces between words, so segmentation is the mandatory first step before search, translation, or any analysis and browsers have no native support.

name: factor-expression
description: Factors polynomials over the integers/rationals, including multivariable expressions.
example_prompt: factor x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6
loader_feasibility: pyodide + SymPy factor() is pure-Python, no server
rationale: College Algebra factoring is a top precalc task solvable exactly client-side.

name: convex-hull-2d
description: Computes the convex hull of a set of 2D points.
example_prompt: Find the convex hull of these points: <list>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM Andrew's monotone-chain algorithm; pure CPU.
rationale: Hulls are the simplest valid physics collider and a frequent building block for game-dev geometry.

name: factor-analyzer
description: Performs exploratory factor analysis on survey or tabular data, returning factor loadings and explained variance.
example_prompt: Find the underlying factors in these survey responses
loader_feasibility: pyodide — scikit-learn's FactorAnalysis runs locally on the pasted numeric table.
rationale: Researchers and product teams routinely run factor analysis on Likert-scale surveys and want it without uploading sensitive responses.

name: active-learning-sampler
description: Ranks unlabeled rows by model uncertainty to suggest which examples to label next.
example_prompt: Which of these unlabeled rows should I label next?
loader_feasibility: pyodide trains a scikit-learn model and computes uncertainty (margin/entropy) sampling client-side.
rationale: Active learning (the modAL demand) cuts labeling cost and works fully on the user's local data.

name: vega-lite-spec-generator
description: Turns a plain-language chart request plus data into a valid Vega-Lite JSON spec.
example_prompt: Give me a Vega-Lite spec for a grouped bar chart of sales by region and quarter
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM templates the JSON spec from parsed intent; pure text transformation runs offline.
rationale: Altair is Vega-Lite under the hood, so a spec generator serves the entire declarative-viz crowd.

name: stopword-tokenize
description: Tokenizes text and applies a cleaning pipeline: lowercase, strip punctuation, remove stopwords, optional stemming.
example_prompt: Clean and tokenize this text, removing stopwords.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with an embedded stopword list and stemmer; local only.
rationale: Text preprocessing is the unavoidable first step in every NLP tutorial and is purely local.

name: notebook-output-stripper
description: Strips outputs, execution counts, and metadata from a notebook for clean diffs and sharing.
example_prompt: clear all outputs from this notebook so I can commit it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM edits the notebook JSON in place without executing anything.
rationale: nbshare/git workflows need output-stripped notebooks to avoid huge noisy diffs.

name: image-augmenter
description: Generates augmented variants of an image (flip, rotate, brightness, noise) for ML training data.
example_prompt: create augmented versions of this training image
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (WASM) applies the transform filters to the image entirely client-side.
rationale: From adversarial/competition ML demand — data augmentation is a standard way to boost models.

name: clothing-image-classifier
description: Classifies a clothing photo into garment categories (shirt, dress, shoe, bag, etc.) with a small ONNX vision model.
example_prompt: What kind of clothing is in this image?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a quantized image classifier in WASM/WebGPU on the local image pixels.
rationale: Maps the '5000 Images of Clothes' demand into on-device fashion tagging with no upload.

name: comic-panel-composer
description: Arranges uploaded images into a multi-panel comic strip grid with gutters and borders.
example_prompt: Lay these 4 screenshots out as a 2x2 comic strip with white gutters
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm — hstack/vstack/pad filters composite the panels client-side.
rationale: Maps the 'comic compilation' demand to a real layout tool people lack a quick browser option for.

name: dose-response-ic50-fitter
description: Fits a four-parameter logistic curve to dose-response data and reports IC50/EC50, Hill slope and the fitted curve.
example_prompt: Fit a dose-response curve and give me the IC50 from these concentrations and responses.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; nonlinear least-squares (Levenberg-Marquardt) and plotting run client-side.
rationale: IC50 estimation is the quantitative backbone of drug-interaction studies and is otherwise stuck in desktop software.

name: duplicate-json-key-detector
description: Parses JSON while preserving every key occurrence and reports duplicate keys within the same object that standard parsers silently drop.
example_prompt: Does this JSON have any duplicate keys in the same object?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM streaming JSON tokenizer tracks duplicate keys per object locally
rationale: Duplicate JSON keys cause data loss that JSON.parse hides, and only a duplicate-aware parser can surface them.

name: image-dimension-spec-checker
description: Checks an image's pixel dimensions against a required width/height (exact, min, or max) and reports pass/fail.
example_prompt: Make sure this image is exactly 1080x1080
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads dimensions from the header without full decode, client-side.
rationale: Platforms reject off-spec dimensions and a quick gate avoids the rejection round-trip.

name: social-og-image-validator
description: Verifies an image meets Open Graph / social-card specs (e.g. 1200x630, min size, ratio) and reports compliance per platform.
example_prompt: Is this a valid Open Graph share image?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM checks header dimensions and byte size against platform spec tables locally.
rationale: Wrong OG dimensions produce ugly link previews; validating beats guessing each platform's rules.

name: exif-orientation-checker
description: Reads the EXIF orientation flag and warns when an image will appear rotated/flipped in viewers that honor (or ignore) it.
example_prompt: Will this photo show up sideways because of its orientation flag?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the single EXIF orientation tag in-browser.
rationale: Orientation-flag mismatches are the classic 'why is my photo rotated' bug and this pinpoints it.

name: video-silent-track-checker
description: Determines whether a video's audio track is entirely (or near-entirely) silent, catching accidentally muted or dead-channel exports.
example_prompt: Does this video actually have any audio?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: astats/volumedetect measure track-wide levels in ffmpeg.wasm client-side.
rationale: Exports with a silent audio track look fine until played, a frequent and embarrassing mistake.

name: video-vfr-detector
description: Inspects packet timestamps to determine whether a video is constant or variable frame rate and reports the range of frame intervals.
example_prompt: Is this screen recording variable frame rate?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: ffprobe frame/packet timestamps from ffmpeg.wasm are analyzed client-side.
rationale: VFR sources (screen and phone recordings) desync audio in many editors, so detecting VFR early prevents wasted work.

name: video-resolution-validator
description: Verifies a video's pixel dimensions match an expected target (e.g. exactly 1920x1080) and flags any deviation.
example_prompt: Confirm this video is exactly 1080p
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: ffprobe width/height from ffmpeg.wasm checked against the target in-browser.
rationale: Off-by-a-few-pixel or wrong-resolution exports fail automated ingest, so a precise check saves a re-upload.

name: mp3-frame-integrity-checker
description: Walks MP3 frame sync words and headers to detect missing sync, truncated frames, junk data, and stream corruption.
example_prompt: Check this MP3 for corruption or broken frames
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: byte-level frame-sync parser over the file, no codec or server required
rationale: Corrupt frames cause skips and player errors; a structural integrity scan locates the damage precisely.

name: duration-metadata-mismatch-checker
description: Compares the duration reported in the container/tags against the actual decoded sample count and flags discrepancies.
example_prompt: Does this file's reported length match how long it actually is?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: read header duration, count decoded samples, and compare client-side
rationale: Mismatched durations break seeking and gapless playback and usually mean a corrupt or wrongly-tagged header.

name: toml-validate
description: Checks TOML syntax and reports parse errors with line and column.
example_prompt: Is this pyproject.toml valid? Point me at any syntax errors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the toml crate; parse-only, runs locally
rationale: TOML is now ubiquitous in tooling configs and a quick syntax check saves debugging.

name: mermaid-syntax-check
description: Validates Mermaid diagram source for syntax errors and unsupported directives before rendering.
example_prompt: is this mermaid diagram syntax valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM Mermaid grammar parser; validates text without rendering or a server.
rationale: Mermaid errors only show as a blank render and a syntax checker reports the actual problem line.

name: data-uri-validator
description: Validates and parses a data: URI, checking the MIME type, base64 flag, and payload integrity.
example_prompt: Is this data URI valid and what's its MIME type?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing the URI grammar and attempting a base64 decode; local
rationale: Inline data URIs are common in CSS and emails and a malformed one fails silently without a validator.

name: protobuf-from-json
description: Generates a Protocol Buffers message definition from a sample JSON object.
example_prompt: generate a .proto message from this JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: walks parsed JSON and emits proto3 fields with numbered tags locally.
rationale: Bootstrapping proto schemas from existing JSON saves manual field-numbering work.

name: ffmpeg-concat-list-generator
description: Generates a valid ffmpeg concat-demuxer file list from a set of filenames (and optional per-clip durations).
example_prompt: Build a concat list for clip1.mp4, clip2.mp4, clip3.mp4
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM string templating produces the properly-escaped concat file text with no runtime dependency.
rationale: The concat demuxer file is finicky to format by hand and getting the escaping wrong is a common joining failure.

name: id3-tag-template-generator
description: Generates a fill-in ID3 metadata template (title/artist/album/track/year) across a list of filenames for batch tagging.
example_prompt: Make an ID3 tagging template for this album's 10 tracks
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM emits a structured template (CSV/JSON) of tag fields per file as text in-browser.
rationale: Batch-tagging a whole album is faster from a pre-filled template than entering each file in a tag editor.

name: typescript-to-zod
description: Generates Zod schemas from TypeScript interface/type declarations.
example_prompt: Convert these TypeScript interfaces into Zod schemas.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a TS type-declaration parser plus Zod emission needs only local string processing.
rationale: Keeping runtime Zod validators in sync with TS types is a common, automatable chore.

name: synthetic-cluster-dataset
description: Generates labeled Gaussian-blob clusters with controllable centers, spreads, and class balance (a make_blobs equivalent) as CSV.
example_prompt: Generate 3 clusters of 100 points each in 2D for clustering practice
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — seeded multivariate-normal sampling per cluster, no dependencies.
rationale: Synthetic clustered data is the standard input for testing k-means/DBSCAN demos entirely client-side.

name: latin-hypercube-sampler
description: Generates a Latin hypercube sample over given variable ranges so each dimension is evenly stratified, with optional maximin optimization.
example_prompt: Generate a 20-point Latin hypercube over x in [0,1] and y in [10,20]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — stratified permutation sampling, seeded and fully local.
rationale: LHS is the workhorse of space-filling design and simulation sampling and benefits from a quick reproducible generator.

name: bibtex-to-json
description: Parses BibTeX entries into a structured JSON array of citation objects.
example_prompt: Convert my .bib file into JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizing BibTeX braces/fields; pure local parsing.
rationale: Researchers move references between tools and BibTeX parsing is fiddly enough to warrant a dedicated tool.

name: fb2-to-text
description: Extracts reading text from FictionBook (.fb2) XML ebooks.
example_prompt: Get the text out of this .fb2 ebook
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing the FB2 XML body sections; local only.
rationale: FB2 is a popular ebook format in Eastern Europe with almost no client-side converters.

name: video-audio-transcode-aac
description: Re-encodes only the audio track of a video to AAC while stream-copying the video, fixing unsupported-audio playback.
example_prompt: This video has no sound on my phone—re-encode just the audio to AAC
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm copies the video stream and re-encodes audio to AAC in one local pass, avoiding a full transcode.
rationale: Files with AC-3/DTS/Opus audio play silently on many devices; swapping only the audio codec is the efficient fix.

name: tta-to-flac
description: Converts True Audio (.tta) lossless files to FLAC.
example_prompt: convert this tta album to flac
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader has a TTA decoder plus FLAC encoder, all wasm-side.
rationale: TTA shows up in older lossless rips and needs converting to FLAC for any modern library tool.

name: shorten-to-flac
description: Converts legacy Shorten (.shn) live-concert archives to FLAC.
example_prompt: convert these shn files from a concert tape to flac
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader decodes Shorten and encodes FLAC losslessly in wasm.
rationale: Tape-trading and Live Music Archive sets are full of .shn that no current player opens; FLAC revives them.

name: mat-to-json
description: Reads a MATLAB .mat file and dumps its variables (arrays, matrices, structs) as JSON.
example_prompt: Extract the variables from this results.mat file as JSON
loader_feasibility: pyodide: scipy.io.loadmat reads MAT v5/v7 in the Pyodide sandbox and serializes arrays to JSON, all in-browser.
rationale: MATLAB .mat data is opaque to anyone without a MATLAB license, and scipy already solves the parsing.

name: dms-to-decimal-csv
description: Converts a CSV column of degrees-minutes-seconds coordinates into decimal degrees.
example_prompt: Convert the DMS latitude/longitude column in this CSV to decimal degrees
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parsing the D°M'S" pattern and computing D + M/60 + S/3600 is trivial arithmetic per row in WASM.
rationale: Surveying/GPS exports use DMS, but every mapping and analysis tool wants decimal degrees.

name: sklearn-classifier-trainer
description: Train a scikit-learn classifier or regressor on an uploaded CSV and report accuracy and metrics.
example_prompt: Train a random forest on this CSV to predict churn and show the accuracy
loader_feasibility: pyodide + scikit-learn (prebuilt pyodide package) trains the model in-browser.
rationale: Directly serves the 'Python For Data Science - Scikit-Learn' demand with an end-to-end train/evaluate flow.

name: news-headline-generator
description: Generate a single concise headline from a news article body.
example_prompt: Write a headline for this news story
loader_feasibility: transformers-js summarization model with short-output constraints, client-side.
rationale: 'Annotated English Gigaword' is the standard headline-generation corpus — distinct one-line output.

name: lsa-topic-summarizer
description: Extract latent topics from a document with LSA (truncated SVD over a TF-IDF matrix).
example_prompt: What are the main latent topics in this document?
loader_feasibility: pyodide + scikit-learn TruncatedSVD reproduces gensim's LSI client-side without C extensions.
rationale: 'gensim models.lsimodel' demand — LSA topic extraction with no server and no heavy gensim dependency.

name: summary-rouge-scorer
description: Score a candidate summary against one or more reference summaries with ROUGE-1/2/L.
example_prompt: Score my summary against this reference using ROUGE
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — ROUGE is n-gram overlap and longest-common-subsequence, pure computation.
rationale: 'DUC 2004' is a summarization benchmark whose standard metric is ROUGE — needed to evaluate the summarizer tools.

name: article-read-aloud
description: Takes pasted article or document text and narrates the whole thing into a single audio file.
example_prompt: Narrate this article so I can listen to it
loader_feasibility: transformers-js TTS synthesizes chunk-by-chunk in-browser; ffmpeg (WASM) concatenates the chunks into one file
rationale: Listen-to-articles is the dominant consumer use of Piper/Kokoro and is fully offline-capable.

name: bookmark-tag-suggester
description: Suggests tags and categories for bookmarks by zero-shot-classifying their titles and descriptions.
example_prompt: Suggest tags for these 40 bookmark titles
loader_feasibility: transformers-js zero-shot classification runs the model fully in-browser on the pasted titles.
rationale: Karakeep/Hoarder's headline feature is AI auto-tagging, but it needs a server and an API key — this gives the same value privately and offline.

name: sd-prompt-cleaner
description: Parses and normalizes Stable Diffusion prompt weighting syntax and splits positive from negative prompts.
example_prompt: Clean up and split this messy SD prompt
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizes the weighting/attention syntax; pure text processing.
rationale: Sharing and tweaking InvokeAI prompts is hard when weights and emphasis markers are tangled, and there's no standard cleaner.

name: image-adversarial-cloak
description: Adds Fawkes-style adversarial perturbation to a photo to resist facial-recognition matching.
example_prompt: Cloak this photo against face recognition
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute (or onnx-runtime) computes the perturbation against an in-browser feature extractor; the original image never leaves the device.
rationale: Fawkes/CloakMe exist exactly for this, and running it locally is essential — uploading your face to a cloud 'privacy' tool defeats the purpose.

name: font-glyph-coverage-checker
description: Checks whether an uploaded font covers a given text string, character set, or language and lists missing glyphs.
example_prompt: Does this font support Polish? Check: ąćęłńóśźż
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (cmap inspection via ttf-parser) — reads the font locally, no rendering server.
rationale: Libre fonts from foundries like Velvetyne often have partial coverage, so verifying glyphs before adoption is essential.

name: form-submission-validator
description: Validates a form submission payload against a JSON Schema and reports each failing field with the reason.
example_prompt: Validate this submission against my schema and tell me what's wrong
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (jsonschema validation engine) — runs entirely offline on the provided data.
rationale: Closes the form loop by letting users check responses locally, completing the self-hosted form toolkit.

name: video-remux-for-kodi
description: Remuxes a video into an MKV/MP4 container and transcodes only incompatible audio so it streams cleanly on a Kodi/OSMC box.
example_prompt: Remux this AVI into an MKV that Kodi can direct-play.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (ffmpeg.wasm) — container remux and selective audio transcode run in WebAssembly entirely on-device.
rationale: Direct-play failures on low-power OSMC devices are usually a container/audio mismatch that a quick offline remux fixes without re-encoding video.

name: redirect-url-unwrapper
description: Unwraps redirect/outbound wrappers (google.com/url?q=, l.facebook.com, out.reddit, t.co-style query wrappers) to reveal the real destination URL.
example_prompt: What's the real URL behind this google.com/url redirect?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: decodes and extracts the embedded target from the query string locally (no following of HTTP redirects required for the query-encoded case).
rationale: De-googling links is squarely in the Whoogle/SearXNG privacy-search demand and works fully offline for query-encoded wrappers.

name: apriori-association-rules
description: Mines frequent itemsets and association rules with support, confidence, and lift from transaction/basket data.
example_prompt: Which items are frequently bought together in these baskets?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Apriori candidate generation and support counting are pure set/array operations.
rationale: Market-basket analysis is a classic, immediately practical business task that runs comfortably on client-side transaction logs.

name: video-noise-level-estimator
description: Estimates per-segment film grain/noise level so you know how much denoising a clip needs.
example_prompt: How noisy is this footage?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg samples frames, plain Rust→WASM measures high-frequency variance in flat regions; all local.
rationale: A noise estimate guides denoise and encoder settings and flags low-light capture problems.

name: video-credits-detector
description: Detects the start of end-credits by spotting scrolling text over a dark background and reports the timestamp.
example_prompt: When do the end credits start in this video?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg samples late frames, plain Rust→WASM detects vertical text motion + low brightness locally.
rationale: An automatic credits marker enables 'skip credits' chaptering and accurate runtime-without-credits measurement.

name: audio-codec-identifier
description: Identifies the true container and codec of an audio file from its bytes regardless of extension.
example_prompt: What format is this file really?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM probes magic bytes and container headers locally with no network call
rationale: Mislabeled extensions are common; byte-level identification prevents failed imports.

name: embedding-similarity-inspector
description: Loads a set of vectors (CSV/NPY) and reports nearest neighbors, cosine-similarity ranges, and duplicate clusters.
example_prompt: Find the nearest neighbors for each row in this embeddings file.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (or transformers-js for on-the-fly embedding) computes cosine similarity locally.
rationale: Inspecting raw embeddings is otherwise notebook-only; a local NN/similarity tool demystifies vector data.

name: html-encoding-issue-detector
description: Scans HTML or text for mojibake and double-encoding artifacts (e.g. Ã©, â€™) and identifies the likely encoding mismatch.
example_prompt: This page shows weird characters like â€" everywhere, what's the encoding problem?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM byte/character pattern matching against known mojibake signatures; fully local.
rationale: Mojibake is common after bad encoding conversions and identifying the mismatch points straight to the fix.

name: png-chunk-inspector
description: Lists every PNG chunk (IHDR, PLTE, tEXt, etc.) with length, type, CRC validity, and decoded key fields.
example_prompt: Show me all the chunks in this PNG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: PNG is a length-prefixed chunk stream parsed by byte offset, no decoder, in-browser
rationale: Diagnosing color profiles, metadata, or corruption requires a chunk-level view a viewer won't give.

name: jpeg-segment-inspector
description: Walks a JPEG's marker segments (SOI, APPn, DQT, SOF, DHT, SOS) and reports each marker's offset, size, and decoded basics.
example_prompt: List the JPEG markers and where the image data starts
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: JPEG marker scanning is sequential byte parsing, no decode, fully client-side
rationale: Understanding JPEG segment layout helps with metadata stripping, progressive vs baseline, and corruption.

name: datetime-format-convert
description: Reformats a date/time from one pattern or standard to another (ISO 8601 ↔ RFC 2822 ↔ US MM/DD/YYYY ↔ custom strftime).
example_prompt: convert 06/03/2026 to YYYY-MM-DD
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; parse-then-format string work, no network or filesystem.
rationale: Directly serves the 'Translate DateTime Format' demand and the universal copy-paste reformatting chore.

name: media-library-renamer
description: Generates clean Plex/Jellyfin-style filenames for a list of movie or show files.
example_prompt: Suggest Plex-friendly names for these movie files
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM reformats parsed names into the chosen library convention locally.
rationale: Practical media-organization helper that keeps the user's file list private.

name: text-to-sequence-diagram
description: Converts a description of actor interactions into a Mermaid sequence diagram.
example_prompt: Sequence diagram: client calls API, API queries DB, DB returns rows, API responds
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM text-to-Mermaid transformation; no dependencies
rationale: Sequence diagrams clarify request flows but are tedious to hand-author.

name: asciidoc-to-markdown
description: Converts AsciiDoc source into Markdown, handling headings, lists, admonitions, and links.
example_prompt: Convert this AsciiDoc to Markdown
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (AsciiDoc subset parser → Markdown writer); deterministic, offline.
rationale: Teams moving docs off AsciiDoc toolchains onto Markdown platforms need a quick converter.

name: png-to-bmp
description: Exports a PNG/JPEG as an uncompressed 24-bit BMP for legacy software and embedded toolchains.
example_prompt: I need this as a 24-bit bmp for my microcontroller IDE
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: BMP encoding via the `image` crate runs in-browser.
rationale: Old industrial and embedded tools often only ingest BMP, an awkward gap with no easy converter.

name: video-to-wmv
description: Encodes video to WMV (WMV2/WMA) for legacy Windows Media workflows.
example_prompt: convert this to wmv
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm encodes WMV2 plus WMA into an ASF/WMV container locally.
rationale: Some legacy Windows apps and projectors still require WMV input.

name: transparent-padding-checker
description: Detects unnecessary fully-transparent border padding around an image and reports how much could be trimmed.
example_prompt: Is there wasted transparent padding around this icon?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM inspects the alpha channel of edge rows/columns to find the tight bounding box locally.
rationale: Transparent padding inflates icon/sprite sizes and misaligns layouts, and it's invisible against a transparent canvas.

name: video-container-extension-mismatch-checker
description: Probes the real container format and warns when the file extension (e.g., .mp4) doesn't match the actual format (e.g., Matroska).
example_prompt: This is named .mp4 — is it actually an MP4 inside?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader probes the format via ffprobe in WASM and compares to the filename extension locally.
rationale: Mismatched extensions cause silent playback/tooling failures that a format-vs-extension check prevents.

name: nginx-config-linter
description: Parses nginx.conf for unbalanced blocks, missing semicolons, and directives used in the wrong context.
example_prompt: Lint my nginx config
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM recursive-descent parser of nginx syntax; no server needed
rationale: Context/semicolon errors fail nginx -t and a fast browser check saves a reload cycle.

name: rsa-key-parameter-validator
description: Validates RSA parameters by checking p and q are prime, n=p·q, and e is invertible mod φ(n) with the right d.
example_prompt: Are p=61, q=53, e=17, d=2753 valid RSA parameters?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: primality tests and modular-inverse checks on big integers, runs locally.
rationale: End-to-end sanity check for crypto key setups that no existing tool offers.

name: redline-doc
description: Produces a legal-style redline of two document versions with strikethrough deletions and underlined insertions.
example_prompt: Create a redline showing the changes between these two contract versions
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — word-level diff rendered with redline markup runs locally
rationale: Redline/track-changes output is the expected format for legal and editorial review.

name: image-luminance-diff
description: Diffs only the luminance (brightness) of two images, ignoring color, to isolate tonal/structural changes.
example_prompt: Compare just the brightness between these two shots, ignore color
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes luma and diffs it without any external call
rationale: Separating tonal change from color change is essential for grading and retouch review.

name: image-saturation-compare
description: Compares the saturation distribution of two images and reports whether one is more/less vivid and by how much.
example_prompt: Which of these two edits is more saturated?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM converts to HSV and compares saturation stats in-browser
rationale: Vividness comparisons matter for grading consistency across a set.

name: image-sharpness-compare
description: Compares the focus/sharpness of two images and reports which is sharper, with a per-region sharpness difference map.
example_prompt: Tell me which of these two shots is in better focus
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM measures gradient/high-frequency energy on each and diffs it locally
rationale: Comparing focus across takes is a frequent culling decision that's hard to judge by eye.

name: palette-diff
description: Compares the color palettes of two images and reports matched, added, and removed swatches with ΔE distances.
example_prompt: Compare the color palettes of these two designs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM quantizes each image and matches swatches by ΔE client-side
rationale: Brand-consistency checks need a swatch-level palette comparison, not a side-by-side glance.

name: histogram-compare
description: Overlays the RGB/luminance histograms of two images and reports a distribution-distance score (e.g. EMD/chi-square).
example_prompt: Compare the histograms of these two photos and tell me how close they are
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM builds both histograms and computes the distance metric locally, rendering an overlay chart
rationale: Histogram comparison quantifies tonal/exposure matching for grading consistency.

name: video-frame-count-diff
description: Counts decoded frames in two videos and reports any mismatch with the likely cause (drops, fps change).
example_prompt: Do these two versions have the same number of frames?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg frame counting runs in the wasm build and Rust→WASM compares the totals, no network.
rationale: Frame-count mismatches reveal silent dropped frames a duration check can miss.

name: dynamic-range-diff
description: Computes the DR (crest-factor) value for two masters and reports which is more dynamically squashed.
example_prompt: Which of these two masters is more compressed?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: peak-vs-RMS crest analysis per channel on both files, local
rationale: DR comparison is the standard 'loudness war' check when choosing between two masters.

name: business-card-to-vcard
description: Reads a business card image and extracts name, title, company, phone, email, and address into a downloadable vCard.
example_prompt: Turn this business card photo into a contact I can import
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime OCR plus plain-Rust field heuristics and vCard serialization all run locally in wasmi.
rationale: Manually retyping cards into contacts is tedious and a clean offline parser saves real time.

name: nutrition-label-parser
description: Parses a photo of a nutrition facts panel into structured per-serving values for calories, fats, carbs, protein, and more.
example_prompt: Read this nutrition label and give me the macros as JSON
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime OCR plus plain-Rust table parsing handle the fixed label layout entirely in the browser.
rationale: Diet and fitness apps want machine-readable nutrition data from packaging without manual entry.

name: svg-path-extractor
description: Parses an SVG and lists all path/shape elements with their `d` data, IDs, and bounding boxes.
example_prompt: Extract all the path data from this SVG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust parses the SVG XML and geometry in WASM — pure text/structure parsing.
rationale: Devs and icon authors need to pull specific paths out of a bundled SVG to reuse or animate them.

name: video-frame-timestamps-export
description: Exports the PTS/DTS presentation and decode timestamps of every frame as CSV for diagnosing timing and A/V sync issues.
example_prompt: Export the PTS and DTS of every frame in this file as a CSV
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader reads frame timing via ffprobe -show_frames; pure metadata, client-side.
rationale: Stutter and lip-sync bugs are debugged by inspecting raw frame timestamps that no player surfaces.

name: checkerboard-pattern-generator
description: Builds a checkerboard image with configurable cell size and two colors, including a transparency-style alpha checker for compositing backdrops.
example_prompt: make a 1000x1000 transparency checkerboard with 20px squares
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM fills alternating cells into a PNG — trivial pixel math, fully local.
rationale: A precise checker backdrop is constantly needed for previewing transparency and tiling, with no current single-purpose generator.

name: progress-bar-overlay-video
description: Creates a transparent animated progress/loading bar video that fills from 0–100% over a set duration for overlaying on footage.
example_prompt: Generate a transparent 10-second progress bar that fills left-to-right, blue, 1920 wide
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg draws a growing rectangle (drawbox with a time expression) over a transparent source; on-device only.
rationale: Tutorial and timer videos constantly need a clean fill bar and there's no off-the-shelf transparent generator.

name: interval-ear-training-generator
description: Generates audio of musical interval pairs (ascending/descending/harmonic) for ear-training drills.
example_prompt: Make ear-training audio for perfect fifths and major thirds
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: synthesizes two-note sequences at chosen intervals + WAV encode, fully offline.
rationale: Self-study ear training needs precise, repeatable interval audio that learners can export and loop.

name: ogv-to-mp4
description: Converts Ogg Theora (.ogv) video to MP4 for playback on modern devices.
example_prompt: turn this ogv into mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm decodes Theora/Vorbis and re-encodes to H.264/AAC client-side.
rationale: Old Wikipedia/Theora exports need MP4 to play anywhere today.

name: lrc-to-srt
description: Converts time-tagged LRC lyrics into SRT subtitles, deriving each cue's end time from the next line's timestamp.
example_prompt: convert these lrc lyrics to an srt subtitle file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — timestamp arithmetic and text reformatting only, fully offline.
rationale: Karaoke/lyric LRC files are everywhere but video tools want SRT cues with start and end times.

name: lrc-to-vtt
description: Converts LRC lyrics into WebVTT cues for HTML5 audio/video lyric display.
example_prompt: convert this lrc to a webvtt file for my html player
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — timestamp conversion and VTT cue formatting in-browser.
rationale: Web players use VTT, not LRC, so lyric files must be re-encoded for browser playback.

name: abc-to-musicxml
description: Converts ABC text notation into MusicXML for import into MuseScore, Sibelius, or Finale.
example_prompt: convert this abc tune to musicxml
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tokenizes the ABC grammar and emits MusicXML, no network.
rationale: ABC collections are huge but professional engravers only import MusicXML.

name: m4a-tags-to-id3
description: Transfers iTunes-style MP4 atom metadata from an M4A onto an MP3 as ID3v2 frames.
example_prompt: copy the tags from this m4a onto my mp3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (lofty) — reads MP4 ilst atoms and writes equivalent ID3v2 frames locally.
rationale: Converting Apple M4A files to MP3 loses tags unless they are explicitly mapped to ID3.

name: graphql-sdl-to-json
description: Parses a GraphQL SDL schema into a structured JSON AST of types, fields, arguments, and directives.
example_prompt: Convert this GraphQL schema SDL into JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM GraphQL parser (graphql-parser crate) producing JSON locally.
rationale: Tooling and codegen often need the schema as machine-readable JSON rather than SDL text.

name: image-bit-depth-reducer
description: Down-converts 16-bit-per-channel images to 8-bit (or 8 to lower) with optional dithering control.
example_prompt: Convert this 16-bit png to 8-bit
loader_feasibility: Rust image crate decodes high-bit-depth and re-encodes at 8-bit in WASM
rationale: 16-bit scientific/camera PNGs break many tools and printers that expect 8-bit.

name: png-color-type-converter
description: Converts a PNG between truecolor, palette/indexed, and grayscale encodings.
example_prompt: Make this png an indexed 256-color file
loader_feasibility: Rust png crate re-encodes with the target color type in WASM
rationale: Choosing the right PNG color type can shrink files dramatically and fix tool compatibility, but it's buried in pro editors.

name: image-dpi-setter
description: Sets the print DPI/PPI metadata (pHYs / JFIF density) without resampling pixels.
example_prompt: Set this image to 300 dpi for printing
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM edit of the density header bytes
rationale: Print shops reject images without correct DPI tags, and changing it shouldn't require re-rendering.

name: csv-to-wav
description: Renders numeric sample values from a CSV into a playable WAV at a chosen sample rate.
example_prompt: Turn this CSV of samples into a WAV at 48 kHz
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses numbers, clamps/scales them, and writes a WAV container in the browser.
rationale: Lets people sonify generated or measured data directly without a DAW or scripting setup.

name: id3-tag-stripper
description: Removes all ID3v1 and ID3v2 metadata from an MP3, leaving only the audio frames.
example_prompt: Strip all ID3 tags from this MP3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: locates and excises the tag regions at file head/tail, no decoding required.
rationale: Stripping tags reduces size and removes embedded art or stale metadata before distribution.

name: utf-byte-reencoder
description: Re-encodes text between UTF-8, UTF-16LE/BE, and UTF-32 and shows the resulting byte sequences with optional BOM.
example_prompt: show this text as UTF-16LE bytes with a BOM
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; native string encoding to byte buffers, fully in-process.
rationale: Cross-encoding byte inspection is needed when files open as garbage in the wrong codec.

name: css-minify-beautify
description: Minifies or pretty-prints CSS, collapsing/expanding whitespace, comments, and rule blocks.
example_prompt: minify this CSS for production
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; CSS tokenization and re-serialization, fully local.
rationale: Quick CSS minify/beautify without a build pipeline is broadly useful.

name: number-deformatter
description: Strips currency symbols, separators, percent signs, and parentheses to recover the raw numeric value.
example_prompt: turn '$ (1,234.50)' into a plain number
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — character filtering and sign inference, deterministic and local.
rationale: Pasted financial text is rarely machine-readable; this normalizes it for further math.

name: csv-scientific-notation-formatter
description: Reformats a selected CSV numeric column into scientific notation with a fixed significant-figure count.
example_prompt: convert the measurement column to scientific notation, 3 sig figs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — CSV parse + scientific formatting per cell, local.
rationale: Useful for wide-magnitude datasets where uniform exponential display aids readability.

name: alpha-channel-extract
description: Exports the alpha channel of an image as a standalone grayscale mask.
example_prompt: Extract the transparency mask from this PNG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — copy alpha to RGB grayscale output, trivial
rationale: Designers often need the mask itself for compositing pipelines, which no tool currently outputs.

name: audio-seamless-looper
description: Creates a seamless loop by crossfading the tail into the head at the wrap point.
example_prompt: Turn this ambient clip into a seamless loop.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg acrossfade wrap plus trim; entirely client-side DSP.
rationale: Seamless background-loop creation for games/apps/streams is a specific transform unaddressed in the catalog.

name: json-array-explode
description: Explodes an array-valued field into multiple records, one per array element, copying sibling fields.
example_prompt: Explode this JSON so each order with multiple items becomes one row per item
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM record expansion over parsed JSON; no server.
rationale: Flattening one-to-many array fields into rows is a key normalization step for analysis.

name: csv-explode-delimited
description: Splits delimited values within a single cell into separate rows, duplicating the other columns.
example_prompt: For each row, split the semicolon-separated 'tags' cell into its own row
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM row expansion over parsed cells; in-memory.
rationale: Cells packing multiple values are unanalyzable until exploded into atomic rows.

name: csv-phone-normalizer
description: Parses and reformats phone numbers in a column to a consistent E.164 or national format with a default region.
example_prompt: Normalize the phone numbers in this CSV to E.164 assuming US for numbers without a country code
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM phone parsing/formatting (phonenumber-style) per cell; client-side.
rationale: Phone columns arrive in dozens of formats and must be canonicalized before dialing, matching, or import.

name: markdown-link-reference-converter
description: Converts Markdown between inline links and reference-style link definitions in either direction.
example_prompt: Convert the inline links in this Markdown to reference style
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM Markdown link parser + rewrite; pure local transform.
rationale: Reference-style links keep long-form prose readable, but switching styles by hand is error-prone.

name: winsorize-outliers
description: Caps a column's extreme values at chosen lower/upper percentiles (e.g. 5th/95th) instead of removing rows.
example_prompt: Winsorize this column at the 1st and 99th percentiles
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — percentile sort + clamp, fully local
rationale: Winsorizing is the preferred robust outlier treatment in stats and there's no client-side tool for it.

name: log-transformer
description: Applies log, log10, log1p, or exp transforms to a numeric column with safe handling of zeros and negatives.
example_prompt: Log10-transform the 'population' column
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — elementwise math functions, no network
rationale: Log-transforming skewed data is a routine analysis step and easy to get wrong with zeros present.

name: rank-transformer
description: Replaces a column's values with their ranks or percentile ranks, with configurable tie handling (average/min/dense).
example_prompt: Convert this column to percentile ranks
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — argsort + rank assignment, no network
rationale: Rank transforms power nonparametric stats and feature scaling but require careful tie logic users get wrong.

name: cumulative-to-incremental
description: Inverts a cumulative / running-total column back into the per-step increments that produced it.
example_prompt: These are cumulative totals — give me the per-day amounts
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — adjacent differencing, no network
rationale: Cumulative dashboards and APIs often only expose totals and recovering deltas is a recurring need.

name: acronym-glossary-builder
description: Extracts acronyms from a document, pairs each with its first parenthetical expansion if present, and lists undefined ones.
example_prompt: Build a glossary of acronyms used in this report
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: regex-style scan for capitalized initialisms plus expansion lookup, runs locally
rationale: Long technical docs accumulate undefined acronyms, and an auto-built glossary both documents and flags missing definitions.

name: heading-outline-extractor
description: Builds the heading hierarchy of a markdown or text document as an outline and flags skipped heading levels.
example_prompt: Show me the outline of this document and any skipped heading levels
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse heading markers and validate level transitions locally
rationale: A clean heading tree aids navigation and accessibility, and detecting skipped levels catches structural mistakes.

name: video-motion-intensity-timeline
description: Estimates per-frame motion magnitude and returns a timeline showing high-action vs static segments.
example_prompt: Where is the most motion in this video?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: motion is estimated from decoded-frame differences locally, no model or server.
rationale: A motion curve helps pick highlight moments and tune encoder settings without watching the whole clip.

name: arrow-ipc-inspector
description: Inspects an Apache Arrow IPC file/stream reporting schema fields, types, record batches, and row counts.
example_prompt: Show the schema and batches in this Arrow file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Arrow IPC headers and flatbuffer schema parse locally without loading full columns
rationale: Arrow IPC is common in analytics pipelines and a schema peek avoids loading the whole dataset.

name: dockerfile-analyzer
description: Parses a Dockerfile reporting stages, layer count, base images, and flags common anti-patterns like missing pinned versions.
example_prompt: Review this Dockerfile and flag bad practices
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Dockerfile instructions are line-parsed and rule-checked locally with no Docker engine
rationale: A quick Dockerfile lint catches layer bloat and unpinned bases that hurt build reproducibility.

name: asn1-der-decoder
description: Decodes generic ASN.1 DER/BER into a tag-length-value tree with OID resolution and printable value previews.
example_prompt: Decode this DER blob and show the ASN.1 structure
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM TLV parser with an OID table; pure byte parsing in-sandbox.
rationale: A general ASN.1 viewer unlocks inspection of keys, certs, and PKCS structures entirely offline.

name: video-color-histogram-timeline
description: Extracts per-frame luma/chroma histogram and signal statistics over time as CSV/JSON for color analysis.
example_prompt: Give me the brightness histogram over time for this clip as CSV
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader's signalstats/histogram filters compute stats during decode, all client-side.
rationale: Colorists and QC engineers use luminance/chroma trends over time to spot grading drift and exposure problems.

name: embedded-lyrics-extractor
description: Extracts unsynchronized lyrics from ID3 USLT frames, FLAC/Vorbis LYRICS fields, or MP4 ©lyr atoms into plain text.
example_prompt: Get the lyrics stored inside this song file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — reads the lyrics frame/field for each format directly from the tag area, no decoding
rationale: Lyrics baked into files are easy to lose on re-encode, and there's no single tool to pull them across formats.

name: embedded-json-extractor
description: Extracts JSON embedded in inline <script type="application/json"> blocks such as __NEXT_DATA__ or Redux state.
example_prompt: Pull the __NEXT_DATA__ JSON out of this page source
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM locates script tags and parses their text content.
rationale: SPA data lives in inline JSON, not the rendered DOM, so this is often the only way to read it.

name: tfstate-parser
description: Parses a Terraform .tfstate file to list managed resources, their types, providers, and key attributes.
example_prompt: List the resources tracked in this terraform.tfstate.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the tfstate JSON and walks the resource/instance tree locally.
rationale: Reading state files by hand is painful, and a local resource inventory helps audits without exposing secrets.

name: numeric-literal-base-parser
description: Scans text for numeric literals in any base (0x1F, 0b1010, 0o17, 1_000, 42) and returns each parsed to decimal with its detected radix.
example_prompt: Parse all the numbers in '0x1F, 0b1010, 0o17, 1_000' to decimal
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — prefix detection and radix conversion, no external deps.
rationale: Source code and hex dumps mix literal bases that are tedious to convert by hand.

name: stacktrace-parse
description: Parses a Java/Python/JS/Rust stack trace into structured frames with file, line, function, and exception cause chain.
example_prompt: Break this stack trace into structured frames
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM matches per-language frame patterns locally
rationale: Structured frames make it far easier to triage and group crash reports.

name: vat-number-validator
description: Validates EU VAT number format and country-specific checksum offline.
example_prompt: Is this German VAT number formatted correctly?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — format + checksum rules, no VIES lookup
rationale: Format/checksum pre-validation catches most bad VAT entries before any online lookup is needed.

name: color-gradient
description: Generates a smooth color gradient or N-step palette between chosen colors and outputs swatches, hex codes, and CSS.
example_prompt: Make a 7-color gradient from teal to orange with CSS
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using colorgrad-rs to interpolate in perceptual color space, rendering swatches as SVG.
rationale: Designers and data-viz users constantly need palette/gradient generation, and color interpolation is pure offline math.

name: pug-to-html
description: Compiles Pug (Jade) template markup into rendered HTML.
example_prompt: Compile this Pug template to HTML.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a Pug parser/compiler runs against the template string with no runtime services.
rationale: Front-end devs frequently need to preview or convert Pug without a Node toolchain.

name: json-schema-to-openapi
description: Wraps a JSON Schema as an OpenAPI 3.1 component schema and emits a stub path/request-body referencing it.
example_prompt: Turn this JSON Schema into an OpenAPI component
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — schema embedding and YAML/JSON emission, no network
rationale: Bridges the prmd API-doc demand to the dominant OpenAPI ecosystem with a fully offline conversion.

name: saml-decode
description: Decodes a base64/deflated SAML request or response and pretty-prints the XML assertions and attributes.
example_prompt: decode this SAMLResponse parameter
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM combining base64, miniz_oxide inflate and an XML pretty-printer; runs fully local.
rationale: Debugging Keycloak/pac4j SSO requires inspecting SAML payloads, which often carry sensitive claims best kept offline.

name: sql-minify
description: Collapses formatted SQL into a single compact line for embedding in code or logs.
example_prompt: minify this SQL statement
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM whitespace/comment-stripping tokenizer; fully local.
rationale: Compacting SQL for one-line embedding in source or config is a frequent chore.

name: sql-string-escape
description: Escapes a literal string for safe inclusion in a SQL statement (doubling quotes, per dialect).
example_prompt: escape this text so I can paste it into a SQL string literal
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies dialect-specific quote-doubling/escaping rules in-browser
rationale: Hand-escaping quotes for an ad-hoc SQL literal is exactly where injection-style breakage creeps in.

name: graphql-minify
description: Strips comments and insignificant whitespace from a GraphQL query/schema to a compact one-liner.
example_prompt: minify this graphql query so it fits on one line for a fetch call
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizes GraphQL and re-emits without redundant whitespace locally
rationale: Embedding queries in code or URLs benefits from a compact form that pretty-printers don't give.

name: wav-to-caf
description: Wraps PCM WAV audio in an Apple Core Audio Format (CAF) container, which supports files larger than the 4 GB WAV limit.
example_prompt: Convert this long 5GB wav into a CAF file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM writes CAF 'desc'/'data' chunks around the existing samples — no decode/encode, just container framing
rationale: CAF is the standard way to carry multi-hour or >4 GB PCM that WAV's 32-bit size field can't represent.

name: digit-group-formatter
description: Adds thousands separators and decimal styling to numbers using selectable grouping conventions (1,000 / 1.000 / 1 000 / lakh-crore).
example_prompt: format 1234567.89 with Indian grouping
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; digit-grouping logic, fully local.
rationale: Locale-style digit grouping (incl. lakh/crore) is fiddly and worth a precise tool.

name: jxl-to-png
description: Decodes a JPEG XL (.jxl) image into a widely-supported PNG.
example_prompt: convert these jxl photos to png
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: `jxl-oxide` is a pure-Rust JXL decoder that compiles to wasm
rationale: JPEG XL adoption is growing but most browsers and apps still can't display it.

name: video-to-apng
description: Converts a short clip into an animated PNG (APNG) for lossless, alpha-capable looping animations.
example_prompt: Convert this clip to an apng with transparency
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm's apng encoder writes the animated PNG from decoded frames entirely in the browser.
rationale: APNG offers lossless, alpha-aware looping that GIF can't, valued for crisp UI animations and stickers.

name: dsd-to-flac
description: Converts DSD/SACD rips (.dsf/.dff) to high-resolution PCM FLAC.
example_prompt: convert this dsf sacd rip to a 24-bit flac
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader demuxes DSF/DFF and decodes DSD to PCM, then encodes FLAC, all in wasm.
rationale: DSD/SACD files won't play on PCM-only DACs or most software, so audiophiles down-convert them to hi-res FLAC.

name: image-stereo-disparity-depth
description: Takes a left/right stereo image pair and computes a disparity/depth map showing how far each pixel shifted between views.
example_prompt: Make a depth map from this stereo image pair.
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a stereo-matching model (or plain Rust block matching) on the pair fully in-browser.
rationale: Disparity between two viewpoints is the canonical pair-comparison task and yields useful 3D depth for free.

name: mml-to-midi
description: Compiles Music Macro Language (MML) text into a Standard MIDI File.
example_prompt: Convert this MML string to a MIDI file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: tokenize MML notes/octave/tempo commands and encode SMF
rationale: Turns the popular retro/chiptune MML notation into standard MIDI offline.

name: id3v1-to-id3v2-upgrader
description: Reads an MP3's legacy 128-byte ID3v1 tail and writes an equivalent ID3v2 header, mapping title/artist/album/year/genre.
example_prompt: Upgrade the old ID3v1 tags on this track.mp3 to ID3v2
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the fixed ID3v1 block and prepends a built ID3v2 frame to the MP3 stream — byte work only
rationale: Modern players and stores prefer ID3v2; migrating legacy v1-only files preserves metadata that would otherwise be lost.

name: js-string-escaper
description: Escapes text for safe inclusion in single-quoted, double-quoted, or template JavaScript string literals.
example_prompt: Escape this snippet so it's a valid JS string literal
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: context-specific escaping is a deterministic local transform.
rationale: Inlining text into JS literals safely avoids syntax errors and injection footguns.

name: requirements-to-pyproject
description: Converts a pip requirements.txt into a pyproject.toml dependencies block.
example_prompt: Convert this requirements.txt into pyproject.toml dependencies
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; parse pinned/ranged specs and emit TOML, no package index access.
rationale: Migrating Python projects to PEP 621 pyproject is common and the dependency reformat is fiddly by hand.

name: audio-autotune
description: Pitch-correct a vocal to the nearest note in a chosen key/scale (subtle tuning or hard auto-tune effect).
example_prompt: auto-tune this vocal to C major
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust DSP or ffmpeg+rubberband, client-side.
rationale: Pitch correction is a sought-after music effect with no current equivalent.

name: k8s-manifest-validate
description: Validates a Kubernetes manifest against built-in resource schemas, flagging unknown fields, bad apiVersion/kind, and missing required keys.
example_prompt: Validate this Kubernetes deployment manifest
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM YAML parser plus embedded core resource schemas; offline (no cluster access)
rationale: Manifest typos fail apply at deploy time and a schema check catches them before the cluster does.

name: z-score-outlier-flagger
description: Flags values whose absolute z-score exceeds a threshold and reports each value's standardized score.
example_prompt: Flag z-score outliers above 2.5 in this data: [paste numbers]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: mean/std then per-point standardization, no network.
rationale: Z-score flagging is the parametric counterpart to IQR and useful when normality is assumed.

name: cron-expression-validate
description: Validates a cron expression, reports syntax errors, and explains the next few run times in plain English.
example_prompt: Is '0 */3 * * 1-5' a valid cron and when does it run?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using a cron parser plus a deterministic next-time calculator; no clock dependency beyond a supplied base time
rationale: Cron syntax is error-prone and people constantly second-guess what an expression actually does.

name: graphql-query-check
description: Validates a GraphQL query or mutation against a supplied schema, reporting unknown fields and bad argument types.
example_prompt: Does this query match my GraphQL schema?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing both schema and query and validating selection sets locally
rationale: Catching invalid queries before hitting the API saves a network round-trip and a confusing error.

name: srt-subtitle-scaffold
description: Generates a blank SRT or VTT subtitle skeleton with evenly spaced empty cues spanning a video's duration, ready to fill in.
example_prompt: Make me an empty SRT scaffold with 3-second cues for this 2-minute video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg reads the duration and a plain-Rust step emits the timed empty cues locally.
rationale: Hand-captioners want a pre-timed template instead of typing every timestamp from scratch.

name: sql-ddl-from-csv
description: Samples a CSV's columns to guess SQL types (INT/REAL/TEXT/DATE/BOOL) and emits a CREATE TABLE statement.
example_prompt: Generate a CREATE TABLE for this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: CSV streaming parse plus type heuristics and DDL emission, all in-browser.
rationale: Bootstrapping a table for a CSV import is one of the most common data chores and is fully deterministic.

name: python-stub-generator
description: Generates .pyi type stub files from Python source by extracting function and class signatures with annotations.
example_prompt: Generate a .pyi stub for this Python module
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses defs and emits stub signatures, no Python interpreter required.
rationale: Hand-maintaining stub files for typed libraries is laborious; extracting them from source keeps them in sync.

name: video-audio-channel-remap
description: Remaps audio channels — downmix 5.1 to stereo, mono to stereo, or pick a single channel.
example_prompt: downmix this video's 5.1 audio to stereo
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm pan/aresample channel layout runs locally
rationale: Surround tracks play silent or wrong on stereo devices and remapping is the standard fix.

name: css-empty-rule-remover
description: Removes CSS rules that contain no declarations, including empty at-rule blocks.
example_prompt: Strip out the empty rules from this CSS
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSS parse + filter; local only
rationale: Generated or refactored CSS often leaves dead empty rules that bloat the file.

name: isotonic-regression
description: Fits a monotonic (non-decreasing or non-increasing) step function to a series via pool-adjacent-violators, smoothing noisy ordered data.
example_prompt: Make this calibration curve monotonically increasing
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: PAVA algorithm in a single pass, fully client-side
rationale: Isotonic regression is the standard monotonic-fit/calibration smoother and is genuinely different from a running max.

name: trailing-whitespace-trimmer
description: Strips trailing spaces and tabs from every line and normalizes the file to a single final newline.
example_prompt: Trim trailing whitespace and fix the final newline on this text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM per-line trim; trivial client-side string pass
rationale: Trailing whitespace and missing/extra final newlines trip pre-commit hooks and pollute git diffs.

name: dns-zone-validator
description: Parses a BIND-style DNS zone file, validates record syntax and TTLs, and flags common mistakes like missing trailing dots and duplicate records.
example_prompt: validate this zone file and point out any errors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — zone-file grammar parsing, no DNS queries, fully local.
rationale: Zone-file mistakes are easy to make and a local linter (recon/DNS-adjacent) avoids round-trips.

name: graphql-type-from-json
description: Generates a GraphQL type definition from a JSON sample, mapping scalars and lists.
example_prompt: create a GraphQL type from this JSON object
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: JSON parse plus SDL string generation, no external service.
rationale: Speeds up schema-first GraphQL work when starting from existing JSON shapes.

name: dead-pixel-detector
description: Finds stuck, hot, or dead pixels by locating isolated outliers against their neighborhood.
example_prompt: Find any dead or hot pixels in this sensor test image.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans decoded pixels for local outliers against a neighbor median locally.
rationale: Sensor defect mapping is a real need for camera testing and astrophotography.

name: snr-estimator
description: Estimates signal-to-noise ratio by separating active signal segments from noise-only segments.
example_prompt: Estimate the SNR of this field recording
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM uses energy-based VAD plus RMS ratios on decoded PCM, fully local
rationale: SNR is a core objective quality metric for evaluating microphones and denoising results.

name: paragraph-stats
description: Reports per-paragraph word, sentence, and character counts plus longest/shortest and the overall average.
example_prompt: Give me word and sentence counts for each paragraph in this draft.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM text segmentation and counting; runs locally.
rationale: Per-paragraph metrics help writers find bloated or stubby sections quickly during revision.

name: round-to-nearest-fraction
description: Rounds decimals to the nearest 1/N fraction (e.g. 1/16, 1/8) and returns the result as a reduced fraction.
example_prompt: round 0.31 to the nearest 1/16 inch as a fraction
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — scale, round, reduce with integer math, no I/O.
rationale: Woodworking, machining, and imperial measurements need snapping to fractional increments expressed as fractions, which decimal-step rounding can't give.

name: stacked-area-chart-svg
description: Plots multiple series as a stacked area chart SVG over a shared x-axis.
example_prompt: Stacked area chart of revenue by product over 4 quarters
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM accumulates series and emits filled SVG polygons locally.
rationale: Stacked areas show composition-over-time, a frequent Bokeh/Altair use case.

name: frontmatter-stripper
description: Removes YAML/TOML frontmatter blocks from the top of a document.
example_prompt: Remove the YAML frontmatter from this markdown file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — delimiter detection at file head, local only
rationale: Reusing static-site content elsewhere requires dropping the metadata block first.

name: image-bilateral-smooth
description: Smooths flat regions while keeping sharp edges using an edge-preserving bilateral filter.
example_prompt: Smooth the skin in this portrait without losing edges
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: spatial+range Gaussian weighting per pixel, runs locally.
rationale: Edge-aware smoothing for portrait cleanup and cartoon-style prep.

name: image-film-negative-invert
description: Inverts scanned color film negatives and removes the orange base mask to recover a positive.
example_prompt: Convert this scanned 35mm negative into a normal positive photo
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: per-channel inversion plus orange-mask white-balance correction.
rationale: Digitizes film scans correctly, which naive inversion gets wrong.

name: audio-expander
description: Applies downward expansion to push quiet sections lower and restore dynamic contrast.
example_prompt: Expand the dynamics on this over-compressed clip to make it less flat
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — `compand`/`agate` range expansion with transfer-curve parameters in ffmpeg.wasm.
rationale: Expansion is the inverse of compression and the right tool for taming low-level noise or undoing a squashed recording, complementing the gate.

name: html-tag-case-lowercaser
description: Lowercases all element and attribute names in legacy uppercase HTML without touching text or attribute values.
example_prompt: Convert all the uppercase tags in this old HTML to lowercase
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizes and lowercases only name positions; pure local rewrite
rationale: Modernizing inherited UPPERCASE markup by hand is error-prone because you must avoid touching content.

name: html-empty-attribute-pruner
description: Removes attributes whose value is empty when emptiness is meaningless, like class="" or style="", leaving meaningful ones intact.
example_prompt: Drop the empty class and style attributes from this generated HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM checks attribute values against an allow-list of safe-to-drop names; pure local edit
rationale: Component frameworks emit reams of empty class/style attributes that clutter output.

name: html-deprecated-attribute-stripper
description: Strips presentational legacy attributes such as align, bgcolor, border, and cellpadding from markup.
example_prompt: Remove the old presentational attributes like bgcolor and align from this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM matches a known deprecated-attribute set and removes them; runs entirely in-browser
rationale: Cleaning up table-era presentational attributes is the first step in any HTML modernization.

name: svg-editor-metadata-stripper
description: Removes editor cruft from SVGs — inkscape/sodipodi/sketch namespaces, <metadata>, comments, and empty defs.
example_prompt: Strip the Inkscape and editor metadata out of this SVG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the XML tree and drops known editor namespaces/nodes; fully client-side
rationale: Vector editors bloat exported SVGs with metadata that doubles file size and leaks tool info.

name: set-cookie-attribute-normalizer
description: Canonicalizes a Set-Cookie header's attributes — casing, attribute order, and SameSite/Secure defaults — for consistent diffs.
example_prompt: Normalize the attributes in this Set-Cookie header
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses cookie attributes and re-emits canonically; local text transform
rationale: Inconsistent Set-Cookie formatting across services makes security review and diffing harder than it should be.

name: metric-suffix-expander
description: Expands human shorthand counts like 1.5k, 2M, 3.2B, 4T into their full numeric values.
example_prompt: turn 1.5k, 2.3M and 0.8B into plain numbers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — suffix lookup and multiply per token, entirely client-side; distinct from byte-size (KB/MB) parsing.
rationale: Scraped analytics and social-stats use k/M/B shorthand that must be expanded before any aggregation, and no count-suffix expander exists yet.

name: line-numberer
description: Adds or removes leading line numbers with configurable start, width, and separator.
example_prompt: add line numbers to this code snippet
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; line counting and prefix formatting, fully local
rationale: Numbering lines for reviews or removing pasted numbers is a quick, frequent edit.

name: json-number-string-guard
description: Converts oversized integers in JSON to strings to prevent precision loss in JavaScript consumers.
example_prompt: Quote the big integer IDs in this JSON so they don't lose precision
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM number-aware JSON rewrite preserving structure; offline
rationale: 64-bit IDs silently corrupt when parsed as JS numbers, and stringifying them at the source prevents data loss.

name: boxcox-transformer
description: Fits and applies a Box-Cox power transform (estimating lambda) to make a positive-valued column more normal.
example_prompt: Box-Cox transform this skewed column and report the lambda
loader_feasibility: pyodide — uses scipy.stats.boxcox in the Python sandbox, fully client-side
rationale: Box-Cox is a go-to normality fix in statistics and requires real ML-fitting unavailable client-side today.

name: threshold-to-bw
description: Converts to pure black-and-white at a chosen or automatic luminance threshold.
example_prompt: Threshold this logo to pure black and white at 50%
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — single comparison per pixel after luminance conversion
rationale: Cleanly binarizes logos and line work, which compression and grayscale tools can't do.

name: chroma-key-quality-checker
description: Assesses a green/blue-screen frame for backdrop uniformity, spill, and shadows that will hurt keying.
example_prompt: Is my green screen evenly lit enough to key cleanly?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM measures backdrop hue/luminance variance and edge spill from pixel data offline.
rationale: Catching uneven lighting or spill before shooting/compositing saves hours of cleanup.

name: video-blur-sharpness-timeline
description: Computes a focus/sharpness score per frame to chart which sections are soft or out of focus.
example_prompt: Show me which parts of my video are out of focus
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes frames and a Rust Laplacian-variance pass scores sharpness in-browser.
rationale: A sharpness timeline finds soft autofocus hunts and bad takes far faster than scrubbing manually.

name: video-duplicate-frame-detector
description: Finds runs of consecutive identical/near-identical frames that pad a stream or signal bad frame-rate conversion.
example_prompt: Does my export have duplicated frames from a frame-rate conversion?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's mpdecimate analysis marks droppable duplicate frames decoded in-browser.
rationale: Duplicate frames reveal botched 24→30 conversions and let editors reclaim a true cadence.

name: video-codec-profile-level-reader
description: Reads the exact codec profile and level (e.g. H.264 High@4.1) and explains decoder compatibility implications.
example_prompt: What H.264 profile and level is my file?
loader_feasibility: ffprobe parses profile/level fields from the locally loaded bitstream headers.
rationale: Profile/level decides whether old TVs and phones can play a file, a frequent compatibility question.

name: audio-spectral-centroid-tracker
description: Computes the spectral centroid (brightness) over time and exports the curve as CSV or a plot.
example_prompt: Plot the brightness (spectral centroid) of this mix over time
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: per-frame magnitude-weighted mean frequency from FFT; trivial local math.
rationale: Brightness tracking is a compact descriptor for tone/timbre changes and mastering decisions.

name: audio-spectrum-peak-finder
description: Identifies the dominant spectral peaks (resonances/tones) in a file with their frequencies and levels.
example_prompt: What are the loudest resonant frequencies in this room recording?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: averaged FFT spectrum with peak picking and interpolation; pure CPU.
rationale: Pinpointing peak frequencies guides corrective EQ and reveals problem resonances.

name: sql-lineage-extractor
description: Statically parses a SQL query and extracts referenced tables, columns, joins, and output-to-source column lineage.
example_prompt: What tables and columns does this SQL query read from?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the SQL into an AST and traces references without executing against any database
rationale: Understanding a complex query's data lineage is essential for impact analysis and runs purely on the query text.

name: normality-test
description: Runs Shapiro-Wilk, Anderson-Darling, and skewness/kurtosis tests on a sample and reports whether normality is plausible.
example_prompt: Is this sample normally distributed?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes the test statistics and p-values over the values locally
rationale: Checking normality is a prerequisite for many parametric methods and is a self-contained statistical computation.

name: quantile-calculator
description: Computes arbitrary percentiles and quantiles from a dataset using all nine standard interpolation methods so results match R, Excel, or NumPy.
example_prompt: What's the 90th percentile of 4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42 using the Excel method?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; sort plus interpolation index math, entirely client-side.
rationale: Percentile values silently differ across software because of interpolation method, and exposing the method choice prevents reproducibility bugs.

name: image-difference-stats
description: Outputs a numeric difference report between two images: RMSE, mean/max absolute diff, percent changed pixels and per-channel breakdown.
example_prompt: Give me the numbers on how different these two exports are.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM subtracts the images and aggregates statistics locally.
rationale: A compact numeric verdict is what scripts and QA checklists need, where a heatmap image isn't actionable.

name: image-changed-region-bbox
description: Diffs two images and returns the tight bounding box(es) of changed areas as JSON coordinates plus an annotated preview.
example_prompt: Where exactly did these two screenshots differ? Give me the coordinates.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM thresholds the diff and computes connected-component bounds in-browser.
rationale: Machine-readable change coordinates let developers auto-crop or assert on the exact region that changed.

name: image-template-match
description: Locates where a small template image appears inside a larger image and reports match positions with confidence scores.
example_prompt: Find where this icon appears in the screenshot.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs normalized cross-correlation over the search image locally.
rationale: Sub-image search is a core comparison task for UI testing, sprite location and 'is this logo present' checks.

name: image-difference-mask-export
description: Diffs two images and exports a clean binary (or alpha) mask of exactly which pixels changed, ready for compositing.
example_prompt: Give me a transparent mask of just the pixels that changed between these two frames.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM thresholds the diff and writes a 1-bit/alpha PNG client-side.
rationale: A reusable change mask feeds straight into editing pipelines, unlike a baked-in heatmap visualization.

name: video-ssim-heatmap-render
description: Renders a per-pixel SSIM difference heatmap as a video so quality loss can be seen spatially over time.
example_prompt: Make a heatmap video showing where my encode loses the most quality
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM decodes both streams and a WebGPU compute shader produces the per-pixel SSIM map per frame locally.
