rationale: A spatial heatmap reveals *where* artifacts concentrate (faces, motion, gradients) far better than a single overall SSIM number.

name: waveform-overlay-image
description: Renders two waveforms overlaid (or stacked) in one image for direct visual comparison of edits and dynamics.
example_prompt: Overlay the waveforms of these two takes into one picture
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM downsamples PCM peaks and draws a PNG locally.
rationale: Overlaid waveforms quickly reveal trims, level changes, and timing shifts between two files.

name: json-contract-diff
description: Compares an API JSON response against a golden reference while ignoring volatile fields (ids, timestamps, ordering) to surface only real contract drift.
example_prompt: Compare this API response to the golden one but ignore the id and createdAt fields
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies ignore-path masking and order normalization then deep-diffs the two JSON docs in-browser; pure data processing.
rationale: Snapshot/contract testing constantly trips on noisy fields; a masking-aware diff is meaningfully different from a plain JSON diff.

name: diff-context-resize
description: Re-renders a unified diff with a different number of surrounding context lines, given the two original files.
example_prompt: Regenerate this diff with 10 lines of context instead of 3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: recompute hunks from the two inputs at the requested context width locally
rationale: More or fewer context lines greatly affect reviewability, and regenerating context normally needs the source files and git.

name: loan-offer-compare
description: Compares two loan offers by APR, monthly payment, and total interest over the term.
example_prompt: Which is cheaper: $20k at 6% over 5 years, or $20k at 5.5% over 6 years?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes amortization for both offers locally; pure arithmetic, fully offline.
rationale: People weighing financing decisions want an apples-to-apples total-cost comparison, not two separate calculators.

name: gitconfig-parser
description: Parses a git config file (INI-with-subsections) into structured sections, including [remote "x"] and conditional includes.
example_prompt: Parse this .gitconfig and show me the sections and values.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; handles git's subsection quoting in the INI grammar, no network.
rationale: Git's subsection syntax breaks generic INI parsers; a git-aware one reliably surfaces remotes and aliases.

name: video-frame-count-extractor
description: Decodes the stream to report the exact total frame count, distinguishing it from container estimates.
example_prompt: How many frames are actually in this video?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (loaded) counts decoded frames via -count_frames; runs in wasm ffmpeg locally
rationale: VFR and broken-header files report wrong frame counts, and exact counts matter for frame-accurate workflows.

name: markdown-table-number-extractor
description: Extracts the numeric columns from a Markdown table into clean CSV.
example_prompt: Pull the numbers out of this markdown table as CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; pipe-table parser, no dependencies
rationale: Numbers locked in Markdown tables can't be charted or summed until extracted.

name: fixed-width-number-extractor
description: Parses fixed-width / column-aligned text reports and extracts numeric columns by character position.
example_prompt: Extract the numeric columns from this fixed-width report
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; column slicing plus parsing, no network
rationale: Legacy mainframe and accounting reports are column-aligned, not delimited, so CSV tools fail.

name: wav-to-aiff
description: Converts a WAV to AIFF preserving sample rate and bit depth.
example_prompt: Export this wav as aiff
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm muxes AIFF client-side.
rationale: Round-tripping into Logic/Pro Tools sessions needs the WAV→AIFF direction that isn't covered.

name: unwrap-phase-series
description: Unwraps a wrapped phase/angle series by adding multiples of 2π (or 360°) to remove discontinuous jumps.
example_prompt: Unwrap this phase series so it's continuous
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — jump-detect + offset accumulation, no network
rationale: Phase unwrapping is essential in DSP and interferometry and is otherwise a numpy-only function.

name: font-identifier
description: Identifies the most likely font(s) from an uploaded image of text.
example_prompt: what font is used in this screenshot?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a font-classification vision model on the decoded image entirely in-browser.
rationale: WhatTheFont is high-demand and currently requires uploading images to a third party.

name: convert-naming-case
description: Converts an identifier between camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, PascalCase, and CONSTANT_CASE.
example_prompt: convert myVariableName to snake_case
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: tokenizing and re-joining identifier words is pure string manipulation done entirely in the browser.
rationale: Renaming identifiers between conventions is a constant coding need with very high search demand.

name: json-schema-infer
description: Infers a JSON Schema from one or more sample JSON documents, detecting types, required keys, and enums.
example_prompt: Generate a JSON Schema from this sample JSON payload
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM analyzes the sample structure locally.
rationale: Schema inference saves real effort when documenting or validating API responses, fully offline.

name: git-branch-cleanup
description: Parses `git branch -vv` / `--merged` output to flag fully-merged and gone-upstream branches, then emits safe `git branch -d/-D` cleanup commands.
example_prompt: From this `git branch -vv` output, tell me which branches are safe to delete and give me the commands
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM text parsing of git output; pure compute, offline.
rationale: Pruning stale/dead branches (the deadbranch demand) is a recurring repo-hygiene chore with no generator today.

name: pregnancy-due-date
description: Calculate due date, current gestational age, and trimester from the last menstrual period or conception date.
example_prompt: My last period started March 1 — when is my due date?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM date math; browser-local and private.
rationale: Due-date calculators are extremely high-traffic and benefit from staying private/on-device.

name: chinese-pinyin-converter
description: Converts Chinese characters to pinyin with tone marks or tone numbers, handling common polyphones.
example_prompt: Give me the pinyin for 中文输入法.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bundled character→pinyin table, no network.
rationale: Pinyin transcription (a SnowNLP/HanLP staple) is widely needed for learning, sorting, and TTS prep, fully offline.

name: mka-to-mp3
description: Extracts and converts audio from a Matroska Audio (.mka) container to MP3.
example_prompt: convert this mka file to mp3
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader demuxes the Matroska container, decodes the stream, and encodes MP3 client-side.
rationale: MKA containers from rips and recordings won't play on most devices, where MP3 is universally supported.

name: redline-html
description: Generates tracked-changes redline HTML showing insertions and deletions between two document versions.
example_prompt: Make a redline showing the edits between version 1 and version 2 of this contract
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — word-diff then emit ins/del-tagged HTML string
rationale: Legal and editorial workflows live on redlines, and producing one locally keeps confidential text private.

name: readability-compare
description: Computes readability metrics (Flesch, grade level, average sentence length) for two texts and shows them side by side.
example_prompt: Is my rewrite easier to read than the original?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — syllable and sentence heuristics computed locally for both inputs
rationale: Editors revising for clarity need a direct readability comparison to confirm a rewrite actually simplified the text.

name: video-scene-similarity-search
description: Embeds a query clip and a longer video with CLIP to find where the long video best matches the query scene.
example_prompt: Find where in this long video the scene from my short clip appears
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — CLIP frame embeddings with a similarity scan, all client-side and cached
rationale: Locates a remembered moment in long footage without manual scrubbing or a server.

name: audio-format-diff
description: Diffs the technical specs (sample rate, bit depth, channels, codec, duration) of two audio files in a side-by-side table.
example_prompt: What technical specs differ between these two audio files?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses both headers and renders the spec comparison with no server.
rationale: Instantly explains why two 'same' files behave differently in a pipeline.

name: image-metadata-diff
description: Compares EXIF/IPTC/XMP metadata of two images and reports added, removed, and changed tags.
example_prompt: What metadata differs between the original and the edited photo?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse metadata blocks from both files and diff tags, no network.
rationale: Spotting stripped or altered metadata between an original and an export matters for provenance and privacy.

name: two-sample-stats-comparator
description: Produces a side-by-side comparison of mean, median, SD, quartiles, and range for two datasets with deltas.
example_prompt: Compare descriptive stats of [3,5,7,9] and [4,4,6,12] side by side.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; descriptive statistics over two arrays, fully client-side.
rationale: A one-shot side-by-side stats table with deltas is exactly what people build manually when eyeballing two samples.

name: vector-delta-table
description: Produces an elementwise difference and percent-change table between two equal-length vectors.
example_prompt: Show the elementwise delta and percent change from [100,200,300] to [110,180,330].
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; per-element subtraction and ratio over arrays, fully local.
rationale: A clean per-element diff with percent change is what people want when comparing before/after vectors and spreadsheets are overkill.

name: video-to-flac
description: Extracts a video's audio into lossless FLAC.
example_prompt: Rip the audio from this concert video to FLAC
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader — native FLAC encoder runs in wasm.
rationale: Audiophiles and archivists want lossless audio extraction, which most online tools never offer.

name: base64-float-array-converter
description: Converts a base64-encoded raw float buffer to/from a JSON number array, with selectable dtype.
example_prompt: Decode this base64 Float32Array into numbers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM base64-decodes then reinterprets bytes as floats
rationale: Typed-array buffers shipped over JSON/protobuf are base64 blobs that need decoding to read.

name: mp4-to-avi
description: Repackages an MP4 into an AVI container for legacy editors and players that require it.
example_prompt: I need this mp4 as an .avi for an old program
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader — container rewrap/transcode to AVI runs locally in wasm.
rationale: Some industrial and legacy Windows tools only ingest AVI, and no good local converter exists.

name: stopword-remove
description: Strip common stopwords from text in a chosen language to keep only content-bearing words.
example_prompt: Remove stopwords from this paragraph for a keyword index
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — bundled per-language stopword lists applied with local tokenization, no network.
rationale: A common cleaning step for search/embedding pipelines that pairs with the existing keyword and chunk tools.

name: markdown-to-ansi
description: Renders Markdown into styled, colorized terminal-ready text (headings, bold, lists, code).
example_prompt: Show this markdown formatted for the terminal
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing Markdown and emitting ANSI escape sequences; pure string output
rationale: People want a readable terminal/preview rendering of Markdown without an HTML viewer, the way glow and mdv do it.

name: json-tree-viewer
description: Render a JSON document as a collapsible, navigable tree for exploring large or deeply nested payloads.
example_prompt: Let me explore this big JSON as a collapsible tree
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the JSON into a node model and the tool page renders the tree in the browser, mirroring jless/jqview without a server.
rationale: Read-only exploration of deep JSON (jless/jqview/jid demand) is a distinct need from querying and is painful in a plain text box.

name: bash-explain
description: Explain a shell command and each of its flags in plain English (explainshell-style).
example_prompt: explain this command: tar -xzvf archive.tar.gz -C /tmp
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: rule-based parser over a bundled flag/man reference, no network or model needed.
rationale: explainshell is one of the most-used dev reference tools and there is no offline equivalent in chat.

name: semver-bump
description: Recommends the next semantic version from the current version and the kinds of changes made.
example_prompt: Current version is 2.4.1 and I added a feature plus a breaking change—what's next?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; semver increment rules are deterministic arithmetic with no external calls.
rationale: Encodes semantic-release/np versioning rules so teams bump consistently without standing up CI.

name: redaction-coverage-checker
description: Runs OCR under blackbox/blur redactions in a screenshot to confirm no text remains readable through them.
example_prompt: Did my black boxes actually hide all the text in this screenshot before I share it?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js/onnx-runtime runs an OCR model in-browser, then plain Rust checks detected text against redaction regions.
rationale: Incomplete or semi-transparent redactions leak sensitive data and are impossible to verify by eye at full opacity.

name: http-header-validator
description: Validates HTTP header field names and values for legal characters, folding, and known-header value formats (Cache-Control, ETag, etc.).
example_prompt: Are these response headers syntactically valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM RFC 7230 token/field-value rules, client-side
rationale: Illegal header characters cause servers/proxies to reject or strip headers in confusing ways.

name: json-ld-validator
description: Validates a Schema.org JSON-LD block for valid JSON, recognized @type/@context, and presence of required properties for common types.
example_prompt: Validate the JSON-LD structured data on my product page
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON parse plus Schema.org type requirement tables, offline
rationale: Bad structured data costs rich-result eligibility and Google's tester is online-only and rate-limited.

name: residual-analyzer
description: Compares predicted versus actual values, returning residuals plus RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and R².
example_prompt: Compare predicted [2.1,3.9,6.2] vs actual [2,4,6] — give residuals, RMSE and R².
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; residual and error-metric arithmetic over two arrays, no external libs.
rationale: Comparing predictions to ground truth with the standard regression error metrics in one shot is a constant modeling task.

name: covariance-matrix-validator
description: Validates a covariance matrix is symmetric and positive semidefinite, flagging negative eigenvalues.
example_prompt: Check whether this covariance matrix is valid (symmetric PSD)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — symmetry check and PSD test via Cholesky/eigen-sign, pure numeric.
rationale: A PSD covariance is a precondition for many statistical methods; validating it offline prevents silent garbage results.

name: video-scanlines-overlay-generator
description: Generates a transparent CRT scanline / RGB-mask overlay clip for a retro monitor look.
example_prompt: make a CRT scanline overlay with alpha at 1080p
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — a geq/drawgrid procedural pattern on a transparent source, encoded in the browser.
rationale: Retro/CRT aesthetic is popular and reusable as a drop-in overlay.

name: video-bokeh-background-generator
description: Generates an animated soft-bokeh particle background loop.
example_prompt: make a warm bokeh background, 12s, 1080p
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute (or pyodide) renders the particle frames in the browser; the ffmpeg loader encodes the result.
rationale: Elegant motion backdrop for titles, weddings, and lifestyle content.

name: video-encode-command-generator
description: Generates a target-tuned ffmpeg encode command (codec, bitrate, flags) for a chosen platform or size goal.
example_prompt: give me an ffmpeg command to make a 1080p H.264 under 25MB
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — rule-based command assembly from the target spec, no media touched.
rationale: Encodes platform best-practices into a single copy-paste command.

name: swagger-ui-html-generator
description: Generates a self-contained Swagger UI HTML page that renders an embedded OpenAPI spec.
example_prompt: wrap this OpenAPI spec in a standalone Swagger UI page
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: embed the spec into an HTML template referencing the CDN bundle, fully local
rationale: Sharing a browsable API doc as one HTML file is handy and there's no Swagger-UI page generator in the catalog.

name: graphql-to-types
description: Generate typed models (TypeScript/Rust/Go/Python) from a GraphQL SDL schema.
example_prompt: generate TypeScript types from this GraphQL schema
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust codegen to WASM — pure compute.
rationale: Codegen from GraphQL schemas is widely used; openapi-to-types covers only REST.

name: histogram-kde
description: Builds a histogram with an overlaid kernel density estimate from raw values.
example_prompt: Make a histogram with a density curve for these numbers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — binning plus Gaussian KDE, local
rationale: Basic data visualization that every data-science primer in the demand starts with.

name: gradient-animation-video
description: Generates a seamless looping animated gradient background clip in chosen colors and dimensions.
example_prompt: Generate a 10-second looping purple-to-teal animated gradient at 1080x1920
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute renders the gradient per frame on the GPU and ffmpeg encodes the loop, all client-side.
rationale: Animated gradient backdrops are heavily used behind titles and shorts and a generator avoids paid stock loops.

name: prime-tools
description: Generates large random primes and runs Miller-Rabin primality tests.
example_prompt: Generate a random 512-bit prime.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM big-integer math with host entropy; local.
rationale: Prime generation and testing is the building block behind RSA keys and a recurring exercise in the harvested crypto texts.

name: cap-table-dilution
description: Model equity dilution across a funding round and show pre/post ownership percentages for each holder.
example_prompt: if we raise $2M at $8M pre on a 1M-share table, what's my dilution?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM cap-table math; local.
rationale: Founders and employees constantly model dilution; nothing here does cap-table math.

name: torrent-file-creator
description: Builds a .torrent file from an uploaded file, computing piece SHA-1 hashes and embedding a user-supplied tracker list.
example_prompt: Make a .torrent for this file with tracker udp://tracker.example:6969
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — piece hashing and bencode encoding run on the in-browser file bytes; output is a downloadable .torrent.
rationale: Creating a torrent normally requires a desktop client; doing it from an uploaded file in-browser is a genuinely novel convenience.

name: audio-spectral-compare
description: Compares two audio clips by their spectral content and reports a similarity score plus a difference spectrogram.
example_prompt: How similar are these two audio takes? Show me where they differ spectrally
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes both clips to PCM in-browser, then a plain-Rust FFT computes spectra and the diff locally
rationale: Comparing recordings (takes, encodings) perceptually needs spectral analysis, not byte comparison.

name: bundle-stats-analyzer
description: Parses a webpack/rollup stats.json to list the largest modules, chunk sizes, and biggest contributors to bundle weight.
example_prompt: What modules are bloating my webpack bundle? Here's stats.json
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON parse + sort/aggregate in-sandbox.
rationale: Bundle-size investigation is a frequent frontend task and stats.json can be huge and private.

name: apr-to-apy
description: Convert between APR and APY and between nominal and effective rates at any compounding frequency.
example_prompt: what's the APY for 5% APR compounded monthly?
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM.
rationale: A specific, frequently-confused finance conversion not covered by finance-calc.

name: vlsm-subnet-planner
description: Splits a parent network into variable-length subnets sized to each requested host count and reports the allocation map.
example_prompt: Subnet 10.0.0.0/16 into subnets needing 500, 200, 50, and 10 hosts
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust VLSM allocator in WASM; purely computational, no network.
rationale: VLSM planning is a classic, error-prone networking task that benefits from an instant offline solver.

name: image-brightness-meter
description: Computes mean luminance, perceived brightness, and an EV-style estimate for the whole frame or a region.
example_prompt: What's the average brightness of this image?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: average luminance over decoded pixels — offline arithmetic.
rationale: Useful for normalizing batches and checking thumbnail visibility.

name: image-saturation-analyzer
description: Reports the saturation distribution and the percentage of oversaturated (clipped-chroma) pixels.
example_prompt: Is this image oversaturated?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: convert to HSV and tally saturation — offline arithmetic.
rationale: Catches over-vivid edits before publishing.

name: audio-leading-trailing-silence-detector
description: Reports exactly how much silence pads the beginning and end of a clip in samples, milliseconds, and dB threshold used.
example_prompt: How much silence is at the start and end of this clip?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes to PCM, Rust→WASM scans inward from both ends, client-side.
rationale: Trimming edge silence consistently across files requires knowing the exact padding amounts first.

name: time-gap-detector
description: Scans a timestamp column for missing intervals, irregular sampling, and duplicate timestamps given an expected cadence.
example_prompt: Find the gaps and irregular intervals in this log's timestamps
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — timestamp parsing and interval diffing is simple arithmetic.
rationale: Detecting holes in a series is critical before charting or aggregating and is a different problem from imputation.

name: sourcemap-inspect
description: Parses a .map source map and lists original source files, embedded sources presence, and basic mapping/version sanity checks.
example_prompt: what original files does this source map cover?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON + VLQ decode of the mappings field; entirely local
rationale: Confirming a source map points at the right originals (and whether sourcesContent leaks code) is a real debugging and security task.

name: id3-tag-inspector
description: Decodes ID3v1/ID3v2 tags from an MP3 to list frames like title, artist, album art presence, and encoder.
example_prompt: Show me the ID3 tags in this mp3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: ID3 frames are length-prefixed text/binary fields parsed without decoding audio.
rationale: Reading/verifying music metadata without a media player is a small constant utility.

name: matrix-condition-number
description: Computes the condition number and singular-value spread of a matrix from CSV to flag ill-conditioning before solving or inverting it.
example_prompt: What's the condition number of this matrix.csv? Is it ill-conditioned?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with an SVD routine (nalgebra); pure numeric work, no server needed.
rationale: Numerical stability is invisible until a solve blows up; a quick conditioning check is a standard diagnostic people lack a client-side tool for.

name: folder-structure-to-mermaid
description: Turns an uploaded folder or path list into a Mermaid graph/flowchart of the directory structure for docs and diagrams.
example_prompt: Make a Mermaid diagram of this project's folder structure
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM text generation — emits Mermaid source from parsed paths, no rendering needed in-tool.
rationale: Bridges directory listing to the diagram workflows teams actually keep in docs, a distinct output from plain trees.

name: fixed-point-to-float-csv
description: Converts a column of Qm.n fixed-point integers into decimal floats (and the reverse).
example_prompt: Convert this Q15 fixed-point sensor column to floating point
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: dividing/scaling integers by 2^n per the Q format is exact local arithmetic in WASM.
rationale: DSP and embedded logs store fixed-point values that are meaningless until scaled to real units.

name: linear-system-solver
description: Solves a system of linear equations Ax = b for the unknown vector x.
example_prompt: Solve 2x+y=5 and x-3y=-1
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: faer-rs/nalgebra perform LU/QR solves (the LAPACK gesv role) entirely in the browser.
rationale: Solving linear systems is core to engineering and economics homework and modeling, and runs instantly offline.

name: blue-noise-texture-generator
description: Generates a blue-noise (void-and-cluster) point or tiling texture for high-quality dithering and stochastic sampling.
example_prompt: give me a 64x64 blue noise tile for dithering
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs the void-and-cluster algorithm into a PNG — CPU-only iterative computation.
rationale: Blue-noise tiles are hard to find at arbitrary sizes and are essential for renderers and dither pipelines, making a local generator valuable.

name: dummy-pdf-generator
description: Generates a multi-page placeholder PDF with page numbers, headings, and lorem text at a chosen page size and count.
example_prompt: make a 5-page A4 dummy PDF for upload testing
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (printpdf); constructs the PDF bytes in-browser, no service.
rationale: Testing file uploads, viewers, and page-count handling needs throwaway PDFs of a precise size.

name: html-form-scaffold
description: Generates an accessible HTML form (labels, types, required, ARIA) from a list of field specs.
example_prompt: Scaffold a signup form with name, email, password, and a terms checkbox
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM builds semantic HTML from field definitions, client-side
rationale: Correct, accessible form markup is repetitive and frequently shipped without labels/ARIA.

name: spf-record-generator
description: Builds an SPF TXT record from allowed senders, includes, and the chosen all-qualifier.
example_prompt: Generate an SPF record allowing Google and Mailgun with a soft-fail default
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM mechanism concatenation, no network
rationale: SPF syntax (includes, qualifiers, 10-lookup limit) is commonly misconfigured.

name: css-class-selector-extractor
description: Extracts the deduplicated list of class and id names defined in a stylesheet.
example_prompt: List all the class names defined in this CSS
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM selector tokenizer; runs client-side
rationale: Auditing or reusing a stylesheet's class vocabulary needs a clean extracted list.

name: ip-info
description: Parse and classify an IP: v4/v6, private vs public, loopback/reserved, expanded/compressed forms, reverse-DNS name.
example_prompt: Is 172.16.5.4 a private IP, and what class is it?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM IP math; pure compute, browser-local (no geolocation API).
rationale: IP classification/expansion is a distinct everyday networking need from CIDR subnet math.

name: scientific-notation-formatter
description: Formats a plain number into scientific notation with a chosen number of significant figures, or expands it back.
example_prompt: show 0.00004507 in scientific notation with 3 sig figs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — exponent/mantissa arithmetic, no dependencies, local.
rationale: Frequent formatting chore for scientific writing that the catalog doesn't yet cover.

name: significant-figures-rounder
description: Rounds a number (or a list) to a specified count of significant figures, preserving correct zeros.
example_prompt: round 0.0034567 to 2 significant figures
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — log/round arithmetic with careful zero handling, fully local.
rationale: Sig-fig rounding is error-prone by hand and not the same as decimal-place rounding.

name: number-locale-reformatter
description: Converts numbers between locale formats, e.g. US "1,234.56" ↔ EU "1.234,56".
example_prompt: convert 1.234.567,89 from German format to US format
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — separator swap with disambiguation rules, fully local.
rationale: Cross-locale data exchange routinely corrupts numbers; a dedicated converter prevents that.

name: intro-bumper-generator
description: Generates a short branded intro bumper from a channel name and accent color with a simple animated reveal.
example_prompt: Create a 3-second intro bumper for 'PixelForge' with an orange accent
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg builds the animated reveal from `drawtext`/`drawbox` keyframed expressions over a synthetic background in wasm.
rationale: A consistent short bumper is core channel branding and a one-prompt generator beats reusing the same template project.

name: video-bitrate-calculator
description: Computes the target video and audio bitrate needed to hit a desired file size for a given duration and resolution.
example_prompt: What bitrate do I need to fit a 12-minute 1080p clip into 200 MB with 128k audio?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM does the arithmetic locally with no input file or service.
rationale: Hitting an upload or attachment size cap is a constant encoding chore and the math is easy to get subtly wrong.

name: hearing-test-tone-generator
description: Produces a sequence of calibrated pure tones at standard audiometric frequencies and decreasing levels for a DIY hearing screen.
example_prompt: Generate a hearing test tone sequence from 250 Hz to 8 kHz
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM steps through the audiometric frequency/level grid generating each tone burst and concatenating to a WAV locally.
rationale: A reproducible self-screening tool set people can run with headphones, no app or clinic.

name: json-to-avro-schema
description: Generates an Apache Avro schema (record with inferred field types) from a JSON sample.
example_prompt: Produce an Avro schema for this JSON record.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Avro schema emission from inferred JSON types is deterministic local computation.
rationale: Kafka/data-pipeline users need Avro schemas for their JSON events and hand-authoring them is brittle.

name: cookie-consent-banner-generator
description: Scaffolds a self-contained, dependency-free cookie consent banner (HTML+CSS+JS) with accept/reject and localStorage persistence.
example_prompt: Make a simple cookie consent banner with accept and reject buttons, no libraries
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — emits inline HTML/CSS/JS from a template; no runtime execution needed.
rationale: Most consent banners pull heavy third-party scripts; a minimal self-hosted one is privacy-friendlier and lighter.

name: random-spd-matrix-generator
description: Generates a random symmetric positive-definite matrix of given size and target condition number via A = LLᵀ from a random lower-triangular factor.
example_prompt: Generate a 4x4 symmetric positive-definite matrix with condition number around 10
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — seeded random fill plus a Cholesky product, no external solver.
rationale: SPD test matrices with controlled conditioning are exactly what people need to exercise solvers and optimizers.

name: fraction-calculator
description: Does exact rational arithmetic with fractions and mixed numbers, auto-simplifying to lowest terms.
example_prompt: compute 3/4 + 5/6 and simplify 18/24
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — big-integer rational arithmetic is pure computation that runs in wasmi.
rationale: Maps genius/kalc/Speedcrunch exact-arithmetic demand; floating-point calculators silently lose fraction precision.

name: github-folder-download
description: Downloads the files under a specific GitHub repo path and packages them into a single zip.
example_prompt: Download just the src/utils folder from this GitHub repo as a zip
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM calls the CORS-enabled GitHub API / raw.githubusercontent.com and zips the files in the browser.
rationale: github-dlr exists precisely because you can't normally grab one subfolder, and GitHub's API is browser-accessible.

name: mbox-to-maildir
description: Converts an mbox archive into a Maildir folder structure delivered as a zip.
example_prompt: Convert my mbox to maildir
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads mbox and emits the cur/new/tmp layout into a client-side zip.
rationale: Maildir is what Mutt, mbsync, and Notmuch expect, and the conversion is pure file manipulation.

name: extension-normalizer
description: Bulk-changes or normalizes file extensions in a list (e.g. .JPEG→.jpg, add or strip an extension).
example_prompt: Normalize all .jpeg and .JPG extensions to .jpg in this list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM suffix manipulation; no host access
rationale: Inconsistent extensions are a perennial cleanup task that batch-rename tools handle and is pure string work.

name: midi-to-audio
description: Synthesize a MIDI file into rendered audio (WAV/MP3) using a built-in soundfont.
example_prompt: Render this MIDI file to an MP3
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — a lightweight soundfont synth (TinySoundFont-style) renders samples locally.
rationale: Completes the round-trip with the existing audio-to-midi tool and is handy for musicians.

name: xpath-test
description: Evaluate an XPath expression against XML/HTML and show matching nodes, text, or attributes.
example_prompt: test this XPath against my XML and show matches
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust (sxd-xpath/libxml-wasm) to WASM — pure compute.
rationale: XPath testing complements the existing CSS-selector and jq-style tools.

name: color-mixer
description: Mix two or more colors at given ratios (additive or subtractive) and show the resulting swatch and codes.
example_prompt: Mix 70% #3366FF with 30% white and give me the hex
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM color math; browser-local.
rationale: Color mixing is a common design need distinct from harmony/shade palette generation.

name: bubble-chart
description: Render a bubble chart encoding x, y, and a size dimension (with optional color/labels).
example_prompt: Make a bubble chart of GDP vs life-expectancy sized by population
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust plotting to a PNG/SVG image; no server.
rationale: A standard chart type not present in the large existing chart catalog.

name: sql-in-clause
description: Turn a pasted list of values into a SQL IN (...) clause or a quoted/delimited list.
example_prompt: turn these into a SQL IN clause: 12, 15, 99, 102
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM list transform with quoting/dedup options.
rationale: Tiny but extremely common database/dev productivity chore.

name: age-estimate
description: Estimate a person's age range from a face photo (for fun/demographics).
example_prompt: How old does this person look?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime age-estimation model in-browser.
rationale: Viral, lightweight demo that complements the existing face-emotion tool.

name: dna-translate
description: Translate a DNA/RNA sequence into amino acids across reading frames using the codon table.
example_prompt: Translate this mRNA sequence to protein
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM codon lookup; offline.
rationale: Core molecular-biology tool pairing with dna-revcomp.

name: keyword-density
description: Analyze keyword and phrase density of a page or text and flag over/under-optimization for a target keyword.
example_prompt: check the keyword density of this article for 'cold brew coffee'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenization + counts; can fetch via web-fetch; local.
rationale: Keyword density is a core SEO check framed differently from generic word-frequency or RAKE extraction.

name: openapi-to-postman
description: Generate a ready-to-import Postman collection from an OpenAPI/Swagger spec.
example_prompt: convert this OpenAPI spec into a Postman collection
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM spec parsing + JSON emit; local.
rationale: Bootstrapping API testing from a spec is a frequent dev task; existing OpenAPI tools emit types/docs, not collections.

name: convert-data-units
description: Converts digital storage sizes between decimal (KB/MB/GB) and binary (KiB/MiB/GiB) units and bits/bytes.
example_prompt: how many MiB is 3.5 GB
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; power-of-ten/two arithmetic runs locally.
rationale: The KB-vs-KiB ambiguity makes a precise data-size converter genuinely useful to developers.

name: css-beautify
description: Expands and indents CSS rules and declarations into a clean, readable format.
example_prompt: beautify this CSS
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using lightningcss to parse and pretty-print; runs entirely in the browser.
rationale: Designers and devs constantly inherit minified CSS that needs to be made editable.

name: invert-image
description: Inverts the colours of an image to produce a photo negative.
example_prompt: Invert the colors of this picture
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies a per-pixel inversion, no network.
rationale: Quick negatives and accessibility previews are a one-tap need.

name: text-encoding-brute-force
description: Tries decoding bytes across many character sets and ranks the candidates by readability to identify the correct encoding.
example_prompt: brute force the encoding of these mystery bytes and tell me which charset is right
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via encoding_rs + chardetng — detection heuristics are pure Rust, no network
rationale: Fixing garbled text from unknown sources is painful without an automated charset guesser, and it runs instantly offline.

name: oid-name-lookup
description: Maps a dotted OID to its friendly name (and vice versa) using an embedded dictionary of common X.509/PKCS/crypto OIDs.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with a compiled-in OID table; a pure in-memory lookup with no network calls.
rationale: Turns opaque OIDs from certificate dumps into meaningful names, saving constant reference-table lookups.

name: convert-speed
description: Converts a speed value between units (m/s, km/h, mph, knots, ft/s).
example_prompt: convert 100 km/h to mph
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; pure arithmetic conversion in-browser.
rationale: Speed conversion is routinely needed for travel, physics, and sports contexts.

name: video-boomerang
description: Create a forward-then-reverse looping 'boomerang' clip from a short video.
example_prompt: make this clip into a boomerang
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (reverse + concat); already wired.
rationale: Wildly popular social format distinct from a plain reverse.

name: mindmap-generate
description: Turn an indented outline or bullet list into a rendered mind-map / tree diagram image.
example_prompt: Make a mind map from this outline of my project plan
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — local tree layout and SVG/PNG rendering, same browser-local pattern as graphviz-render.
rationale: Visualizing outlines as mind maps is popular for studying and planning and pairs well with AI-generated outlines.

name: body-fat-calc
description: Estimate body-fat percentage using the U.S. Navy circumference method.
example_prompt: body fat for a 180cm male, neck 38cm, waist 90cm
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM.
rationale: A top fitness calculator distinct from BMI/TDEE/ideal-weight.

name: email-header-analyze
description: Parse raw email headers into the Received hop chain with delays, plus SPF/DKIM/DMARC results.
example_prompt: Analyze these email headers — why did this go to spam?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM header parsing; offline.
rationale: Go-to debugging tool for deliverability, distinct from the DNS-based spf-dmarc-check.

name: black-scholes-pricer
description: Prices European call and put options via the Black-Scholes formula from spot, strike, vol, rate, and time.
example_prompt: Price a 3-month call: spot 100, strike 105, vol 25%, rate 4%
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; closed-form math on entered numbers, no server.
rationale: Option pricing is a high-demand quant task that reduces to a pure function ideal for browser-local execution.

name: magic-byte-detector
description: Identifies a file format or wire protocol from its leading bytes or a pasted hex dump, the same first-byte sniffing sslh uses to demux SSH vs TLS vs HTTP.
example_prompt: What kind of file is this? hex: 89504e47...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM signature matching against a magic-number table; pure byte inspection runs entirely client-side.
rationale: Identifying an unknown blob or protocol from its header is a daily reverse-engineering and forensics need that maps cleanly to sslh's core trick.

name: web-vitals-scorer
description: Scores entered LCP, CLS, INP, and TTFB values as good/needs-improvement/poor against current thresholds with targeted advice.
example_prompt: My LCP is 3.4s and CLS is 0.18, how bad is that and how do I fix it?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — threshold comparison and advice lookup on a handful of inputs, client-side.
rationale: The 'vitals' demand maps cleanly to Web Vitals scoring, which developers check constantly and is a simple deterministic rubric.

name: css-class-sorter
description: Sorts, deduplicates, and groups CSS/Tailwind utility class lists in pasted markup.
example_prompt: Sort and dedupe these Tailwind classes: p-4 flex p-4 text-sm flex items-center
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string parsing and ordering; no network or DOM access needed
rationale: Messy, duplicated class attributes are a constant readability pain in component code.

name: business-days-counter
description: Counts working days between two dates, optionally skipping listed holidays.
example_prompt: How many business days are between March 2 and April 15, excluding April 3?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM calendar math; no external data required beyond user-supplied holidays.
rationale: Deadlines, SLAs, and payroll all run on working-day counts that calendars don't give directly.

name: countdown-to-date
description: Shows the remaining time (days, hours, minutes) from now until a future date or event.
example_prompt: how long until 2026-12-25
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM delta math over the current epoch supplied by the JS host (Date.now()); no network.
rationale: Common 'how long until' lookup that complements the delta tool with a live reference point.

name: critical-points-finder
description: Finds critical points, classifies maxima/minima/saddles, and reports extrema of a function.
example_prompt: find and classify the critical points of x^3 - 3x
loader_feasibility: pyodide + SymPy solve(diff()) with second-derivative test runs in-browser
rationale: Calculus 1 optimization is a heavily taught topic across the listed channels.

name: song-structure-segmenter
description: Segments a song into structural sections (intro, verse, chorus, bridge) with boundary timestamps.
example_prompt: Map out the sections of this song with timings.

name: audio-fingerprint

loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM builds a chroma-based fingerprint from ffmpeg-decoded PCM and hashes it on-device.

name: survival-curve-estimator

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes the Kaplan-Meier estimator and confidence bands over the parsed table locally.

name: ab-test-significance
description: Runs frequentist significance tests (two-proportion z-test, t-test, chi-square) with p-values and confidence intervals.
example_prompt: Is the difference between these two conversion rates statistically significant?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM statistical functions run client-side
rationale: The classic complement to the Bayesian test, covering the most common experiment-analysis question.

name: distribution-comparator
description: Compares two numeric columns with a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test and overlaid histograms.
example_prompt: compare the distributions of these two columns
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs scipy.stats and matplotlib entirely client-side.
rationale: Comparing distributions is core to statistics-collaboration and feature analysis demand.

name: image-watermark-extractor
description: Subtracts a clean image from its watermarked counterpart to reconstruct and reveal the embedded watermark.
example_prompt: Extract the watermark by comparing the marked and clean versions
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM diffs and amplifies the residual between the pair locally
rationale: Recovering a watermark pattern from a known pair is a precise diff task with no API needed.

name: query-string-diff
description: Compares the parameters of two URL query strings and reports added, removed, and changed values.
example_prompt: Diff the query params between these two URLs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — query parse + param map comparison, no network
rationale: Comparing tracking or API params between two URLs is a quick debugging task with no server needed.

name: magic-square-generator
description: Generates a magic square of any order with the construction method shown.
example_prompt: Generate a 5x5 magic square
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM Siamese/LUX construction algorithms — pure deterministic computation.
rationale: Directly serves the 'Magic Squares and Cubes' demand with a clean, self-contained generator.

name: protobuf-diff
description: Compares two .proto files and reports field number reuse, type changes, and removed messages that break wire compatibility.
example_prompt: Are there wire-breaking changes between these two proto files?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse proto syntax and compare message/field tables locally
rationale: Protobuf wire compatibility hinges on field-number rules that are easy to violate and hard to eyeball.

name: csp-directive-linter
description: Lints a Content-Security-Policy header directive by directive, flagging unsafe-inline, wildcard sources, and missing key directives.
example_prompt: Lint this Content-Security-Policy header for weaknesses.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSP grammar parse and rule evaluation — fully client-side.
rationale: Deep per-directive CSP analysis catches the weak spots a presence-only header check misses.

name: confusion-matrix-analyzer
description: Takes a confusion matrix and computes accuracy, precision, recall, F1, specificity, and Matthews correlation coefficient per class and overall.
example_prompt: From this confusion matrix TP=40 FP=5 FN=10 TN=45 give me all the metrics
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; classification metrics are direct arithmetic on counts, no server involved.

name: set-prediction-scorer
description: Scores a predicted set against a reference set with precision, recall, F1, and Jaccard.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; overlap counting over two sets, no dependencies.
rationale: Quickly scoring a predicted set against ground truth is a constant need in IR and ML eval and the four metrics together tell the full story.

name: confusion-matrix-validator
description: Checks that a confusion matrix is square, nonnegative-integer, and that its totals reconcile with provided support counts.
example_prompt: Is this 3x3 confusion matrix internally consistent?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — shape, integrality, and marginal-sum checks in one pass, all local.
rationale: Catches malformed classification reports (non-integer, wrong totals) before metrics are computed from them.

name: balanced-delimiters-checker
description: Scans code or text for unbalanced brackets, braces, parentheses, and quotes, reporting the line and column of the first mismatch.
example_prompt: Find the unbalanced bracket in this snippet
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM stack-based scanner with string/comment awareness, client-side
rationale: A single missing brace causes baffling parser errors far from the real location, which this pinpoints.

name: kolmogorov-smirnov-test
description: Runs one-sample (vs a reference distribution) and two-sample KS tests to compare distributions and reports the D statistic and p-value.
example_prompt: Do these two samples come from the same distribution? Run a KS test.
loader_feasibility: pyodide with scipy.stats; runs locally in the Python sandbox.
rationale: Distribution comparison is a distinct, widely needed test not covered by chi-square.

name: markdown-ordered-to-unordered

example_prompt: change this numbered list into bullet points
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM list rewrite, client-side

name: normalize-heading-case

example_prompt: fix the capitalization of these headings to title case
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with a built-in stop-word list, fully local
rationale: Enforces consistent heading style across a document.

name: video-white-balance
description: Corrects color casts and color temperature using colortemperature/colorbalance filters to neutralize orange or blue tints.
example_prompt: Fix the orange tint in this indoor video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader runs colortemperature/colorbalance filters in wasm
rationale: Wrong white balance from indoor/mixed lighting is a distinct, common correction.

name: loudness-match
description: Adjusts a target file's gain so its loudness matches a reference file.
example_prompt: Make this clip the same loudness as my reference track
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: measure LUFS/RMS of both files and apply the difference as a gain to the target — local math.
rationale: Loudness-matching multiple sources to a reference is common when assembling interviews or compilations.

name: json-rename-keys
description: Renames JSON keys throughout a document from an old→new mapping at any nesting depth.
example_prompt: Rename every 'userId' key to 'user_id' in this JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM recursive walk with mapping; client-side.
rationale: Schema migrations on captured JSON payloads need bulk, depth-aware key renaming.

name: relative-to-absolute-url-resolver
description: Resolves a list of relative URLs (./img, ../a, /root, page.html) against a given base URL into fully absolute URLs.
example_prompt: Resolve ../images/logo.png and /about against base https://example.com/blog/post/
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; RFC 3986 reference resolution, pure computation.
rationale: Turning scraped relative links into absolute ones is a constant pre-processing step.

name: ordinal-encoder
description: Encodes an ordered categorical column to integers following a user-supplied category order (e.g. low<med<high).
example_prompt: Encode this column as ordinals where low=0, medium=1, high=2
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: order map lookup per value, fully local.
rationale: Ordinal data needs order-preserving codes, which label encoding can't guarantee on its own.

name: threshold-binarizer
description: Converts a numeric column to 0/1 (or custom labels) based on a chosen threshold and comparison direction.
example_prompt: Binarize this column to 1 if above 50 else 0
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: per-value comparison, fully local.
rationale: Thresholding into a binary indicator is a basic but missing feature-engineering and gating step.

name: version-list-sort
description: Sorts a pasted list of version tags/strings in true version order (not lexical) and flags the latest stable vs prerelease.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — natural-version sort over text input, no network needed.
rationale: Picking the latest version from a messy tag list is the core job of lastversion/getghrel and trivially done offline.

name: summation-calculator
description: Evaluates finite and infinite series and closed-form summations symbolically.
example_prompt: sum of 1/n^2 from n=1 to infinity
loader_feasibility: pyodide + SymPy Sum().doit() computes closed forms locally
rationale: Calculus 2 series convergence (Mathematical Monk) needs exact summation.

name: trend-significance
description: Runs a Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope to assess whether a time-series trend is statistically significant.
example_prompt: Is the warming trend in this climate series statistically significant?
loader_feasibility: pyodide with scipy/numpy computes the non-parametric test locally.
rationale: Climate analysis (NCEI, ClimateData.us, SEDAC) hinges on testing trend significance, not just plotting.

name: morse-code-audio-generator
description: Converts text into a Morse-code WAV of dots and dashes at a chosen tone frequency and words-per-minute.
example_prompt: Turn 'SOS HELP' into Morse code audio at 15 wpm
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM maps characters to timed sine bursts using standard Morse timing and writes the WAV client-side.
rationale: Hobbyists, ham-radio learners, and puzzle makers need an exact-timing Morse audio file from text.

name: bash-syntax-check
description: Parses a shell script and reports syntax errors, unclosed quotes/blocks, and a structural outline of commands.
example_prompt: Is there a syntax error in this bash script?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using a Rust shell parser (brush-shell's lineage) to parse the script text locally without executing it.
rationale: Catches shell-script mistakes before running them, derived from brush-shell's parser, with no code execution risk in the browser.

name: jsonschema-to-types
description: Generate typed models (TypeScript/Rust/Go/Python) from a JSON Schema document.
example_prompt: generate TypeScript interfaces from this JSON Schema
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust codegen to WASM — pure compute.
rationale: Many APIs ship JSON Schema; json-to-types only infers from sample data.

name: dockerfile-diff
description: Instruction-level diff of two Dockerfiles, highlighting base-image, layer, ENV, EXPOSE, and copy/run changes.
example_prompt: What changed between these two Dockerfiles?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse both into instruction lists and diff them, no network
rationale: Dockerfile edits change build behavior subtly; an instruction-aware diff makes review fast and local.

name: partial-fraction-decomposer
description: Decomposes a rational function into its partial-fraction sum to simplify integration.
example_prompt: decompose (3x+5)/((x+1)(x+2)) into partial fractions
loader_feasibility: pyodide + sympy.apart runs the decomposition algorithm locally in WASM.
rationale: A high-frequency integration prerequisite taught explicitly by PatrickJMT and Calculus.org.

name: text-similarity-percent
description: Reports an overall percentage similarity between two documents based on matched content.
example_prompt: how much overlap is there between these two essays as a percentage
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM diff ratio over tokens; pure computation
rationale: A single headline number is what people want when comparing drafts or checking overlap.

name: skewness-kurtosis-calculator
description: Calculates sample skewness and excess kurtosis for a dataset and interprets the shape (left/right skew, heavy/light tails).
example_prompt: What are the skewness and kurtosis of 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 10?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: third- and fourth-moment computation over a numeric list, no server required.
rationale: Distribution-shape diagnostics are commonly needed yet rarely available without statistical software.

name: regex-validator
description: Checks that a regular expression compiles and surfaces the precise syntax error and supported flags.
example_prompt: Why is this regex invalid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (regex crate compile step); runs locally.
rationale: Quickly diagnosing a broken pattern is a constant need that requires only an in-browser compile.

name: vin-decode

example_prompt: Decode VIN 1HGCM82633A004352
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM WMI/year tables plus check-digit math, offline.
rationale: VIN decoding is a popular consumer/automotive lookup with no current tool.

name: sql-table-extractor
description: Parses SQL statements to extract referenced table and column names and classifies each as read or write.
example_prompt: List every table this SQL query touches
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a SQL tokenizer/parser walks the statements locally, no database connection.
rationale: Understanding a query's footprint for migrations or impact analysis is valuable and purely static.

name: ip-cidr-parser
description: Parses an IPv4/IPv6 CIDR like "192.168.0.0/24" into network/broadcast addresses, host count, and the integer range bounds.
example_prompt: What range and how many hosts does 192.168.0.0/24 cover?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bitmask arithmetic on parsed addresses, fully local.
rationale: Network subnet math is error-prone and a quick deterministic parser saves real mistakes.

name: imei-validator
description: Validates a 15-digit IMEI via its Luhn check digit and decodes the TAC reporting-body prefix.
example_prompt: Check if IMEI 490154203237518 is valid
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Luhn over 15 digits plus a static prefix lookup, entirely local.
rationale: Phone resellers and IT inventory staff regularly verify IMEIs and want a quick offline check.

name: image-entropy-calculator
description: Calculates Shannon entropy of an image as a measure of visual complexity and compressibility.
example_prompt: How complex or compressible is this image?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM builds an intensity histogram and computes entropy locally.
rationale: Entropy predicts how well an image will compress and flags near-blank or texture-heavy content.

name: video-waveform-monitor-image
description: Generates a luma/RGB waveform monitor image to read exact brightness levels across the picture width.
example_prompt: Show me the waveform monitor for this frame
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg `waveform` filter builds the scope from decoded pixels locally with no server.
rationale: Waveform monitors are essential for verifying legal video levels and matching shots, here usable offline.

name: image-clone-detector
description: Detects copy-move forgery by finding duplicated image regions via block/feature matching and overlays the matched pairs.
example_prompt: Check if part of this image was cloned to cover something
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute: block descriptor matching is GPU-parallel and runs locally on the decoded pixels.
rationale: Copy-move detection is sherloq's hardest, most convincing tamper check and is unavailable in most quick web tools.

name: rss-feed-filter
description: Parses a pasted RSS/Atom feed and filters or transforms entries by keyword, date or count, emitting a new feed.
example_prompt: Filter this RSS feed down to only items mentioning Rust
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — XML parse, filter and re-serialize all happen in memory with no fetching.
rationale: Recreates rss-funnel's core feed-shaping on a pasted feed without needing a hosted middleware service.

name: semver-version-bumper
description: Computes the next semantic version for a given current version and bump type (major/minor/patch/pre/build) and rewrites the version field in a pasted Cargo.toml or package.json.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM doing semver arithmetic and a single manifest field edit; entirely deterministic and offline
rationale: cargo-release's version step is pure semver math that's easy to get wrong by hand and trivial to do client-side.

name: xml-tree-viewer
description: Pretty-prints and renders any XML (including GObject-introspection .gir files) as a collapsible tree with attribute search.
example_prompt: Render this .gir XML as a browsable tree
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — an XML parser producing a tree structure, pure in-memory compute.
rationale: gtk-rs/gir consumes large .gir XML files that are unreadable when flat, and a local tree viewer makes them navigable.

name: shell-history-dedup
description: Cleans and deduplicates a shell history file, collapsing repeats while preserving most-recent order.
example_prompt: Dedupe my bash history, keeping the latest occurrence of each command
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure line processing, no filesystem or network.
rationale: Readline tools (rustyline/liner) maintain history, and cleaning a bloated history file is a real browser-local chore.

name: arbitrary-precision-calculator
description: Performs exact arbitrary-precision decimal and integer arithmetic with no floating-point rounding error.
example_prompt: Compute 0.1 + 0.2 exactly and also 2^200
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the fastnum crate provides fixed-precision decimals and big integers that run client-side.
rationale: Exact decimal math matters for finance and crypto where float rounding is unacceptable, and it runs instantly locally.

name: timeseries-plot

example_prompt: Plot this CSV of daily temperatures over time
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: date parsing plus plotters time-axis rendering to SVG, no server.
rationale: Time-series visualization (the rerun use case, minus the heavy 3D) is extremely common and runs fully client-side as SVG.

name: kmeans-cluster
description: Groups a set of numeric points into k clusters and reports centroids and assignments.
example_prompt: Cluster these 2D points into 3 groups
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: k-means is iterative arithmetic over the input vectors, no backend or GPU required.
rationale: Clustering is a staple exploratory-analysis tool and runs comfortably client-side for typical paste-in datasets.

name: kelly-criterion
description: Compute the optimal bet/position size from win probability and odds via the Kelly criterion.
example_prompt: Kelly stake for a 55% edge at even odds?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM arithmetic, offline.
rationale: A well-known sizing formula for betting/investing not covered by existing finance tools.

name: area-under-curve
description: Numerically integrate a function over an interval and shade the area on a plot.
example_prompt: Integrate sin(x) from 0 to pi and show the area
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM quadrature plus plotting, offline.
rationale: A visual numerical companion to the symbolic equation solver for students.

name: weighted-average
description: Computes a weighted mean from value/weight pairs, e.g. for grades or portfolio allocations.
example_prompt: My grades are 90 (weight 0.3), 80 (weight 0.5), 70 (weight 0.2) — what's my weighted average?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sum-of-products over weight divided by total weight, purely local.
rationale: Weighted averages are a common real-world variant of the mean demand (grades, GPAs, weighted scores) with no quick interactive tool.

name: running-pace

example_prompt: what pace do I need to run a sub-4-hour marathon?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust to WASM — pure compute.
rationale: Pace calculators are a staple for runners.

name: github-actions-validator

example_prompt: Validate this GitHub Actions workflow file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — YAML parse + schema check, no network
rationale: CI config breakage is costly to discover late, so a local pre-commit check has clear value.

name: lyrics-format-converter
description: Converts lyrics between plain text, LRC, and SRT and shifts the timing offset of synced lyrics.
example_prompt: Shift this LRC file 0.5 seconds later and save it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pure parsing and timestamp arithmetic over text, no I/O.
rationale: Lyrics arrive in mismatched formats and with drifting offsets; converting and nudging them is a small but frequent need.

name: dependency-range-auditor

example_prompt: How loose is each dependency range in this package.json?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; range parsing and classification need no network, just the pasted manifest.
rationale: Gives the local half of npm-check-updates—how much version drift you've allowed—without contacting the registry.

name: overtime-calculator

example_prompt: I'm contracted 40h/week but worked 47h this week — how much overtime at 1.5x?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — rule evaluation and arithmetic only.
rationale: Directly maps the 'OverTime' demand term to a precise, privacy-preserving payroll calculation.

name: birthday-reminder

example_prompt: From this list of birthdays, tell me whose is coming up next and their age
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure date arithmetic over the pasted list, fully offline.
rationale: the birthday tool is exactly this calculation, and it is trivially browser-local while genuinely handy.

name: bird-call-id

loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a BirdNET-Lite model on a locally computed mel-spectrogram; inference is in-browser.
rationale: birda-style bird ID from sound is a delightful on-device ML use that needs no upload.

name: audio-to-flac

example_prompt: Convert this song.mp3 to FLAC
loader_feasibility: the ffmpeg loader decodes and re-encodes to FLAC fully client-side, carrying over tags (transflac).

name: audiobook-generator

example_prompt: Make an audiobook from this story text
loader_feasibility: transformers-js TTS streams long text in chunks client-side; ffmpeg (WASM) stitches segments with chapter markers
rationale: Long-form narration is a recurring Piper/MeloTTS power-user request and is feasible without a server.

name: m3u-playlist-tool

example_prompt: Clean up this M3U playlist and remove duplicate entries
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM line parser/writer; pure text processing.

name: wikilink-converter

name: apng-to-mp4

name: webp-animation-to-mp4

example_prompt: Convert this animated webp to mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm decodes animated WebP via libwebp and encodes H.264 MP4 in the browser.
rationale: Animated WebP downloads often need to become MP4 for editing or posting, a gap generic tools miss.

name: edgelist-to-adjacency-matrix
description: Builds a dense adjacency matrix CSV from a graph edge list, with optional weights and directedness.
example_prompt: Turn this edge list into an adjacency matrix
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: mapping node labels to indices and filling a matrix is in-memory integer work with no deps.
rationale: Graph-theory and linear-algebra tools want a matrix while most graph data arrives as edge pairs.

name: csv-slugify-column

example_prompt: Make a 'slug' column from the article titles in this CSV
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM transliteration + slug rules per cell; local string work.
rationale: Generating consistent slugs in bulk is a routine content/SEO data prep need.

name: degrees-radians-converter

example_prompt: Convert this column of radians to degrees
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — constant scaling, fully local
rationale: Angle-unit mismatches are a constant source of bugs in geometry, robotics, and graphics data.

name: png-to-tiff
description: Converts a PNG/JPEG into a TIFF with selectable LZW or no compression for print and archival.
example_prompt: Save this image as an uncompressed tiff for the printer
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: TIFF encoding via the `tiff`/`image` crate runs client-side.
rationale: Print shops and archives often demand TIFF, completing the round-trip with the existing tiff-to-png tool.

name: softmax-normalizer

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: max-subtraction, exp, and normalize in one pass, pure float math
rationale: Softmax over logits is a distinct exponential transform that simple proportion/probability normalizers don't provide.

name: protobuf-message-scaffold

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — emits proto3 syntax from structured inputs, no protoc required.

name: combination-enumerator

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — combinatorial-number-system iteration, deterministic and dependency-free.
rationale: A reliable scaffold for test-case matrices and subset enumeration that is error-prone to write by hand.

name: permutation-enumerator

example_prompt: List all permutations of 1, 2, 3, 4
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Heap's / next-permutation algorithm, runs fully client-side.
rationale: Exhaustive permutation lists scaffold brute-force search, scheduling, and puzzle generation without a server.

name: weighted-random-picker

example_prompt: Pick a winner from this list where Alice has weight 3 and the rest weight 1
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: builds a cumulative weight table and samples with the host RNG.
rationale: Fair weighted draws (raffles, A/B picks) are common and the cumulative-weight logic is easy to get wrong.

name: list-shuffler

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Fisher-Yates over the input lines using host RNG; fully local.
rationale: Unbiased shuffling for playlists, prompts, or running orders is wanted often and naive methods skew results.

name: xml-comment-stripper
description: Removes XML comments and optional processing-instruction cruft while keeping the document well-formed.
example_prompt: Strip all the comments out of this XML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM walks the node tree dropping comment nodes; deterministic in-browser pass
rationale: Generated XML often carries verbose tool comments that bloat feeds and config files.

name: wav-bit-depth-converter
description: Re-quantizes an integer WAV between bit depths (e.g. 24→16) with optional truncation control.
example_prompt: Downconvert this 24-bit wav to 16-bit

example_prompt: Sort the attributes on every tag in this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parse + re-emit with sorted attribute lists; browser-local.
rationale: Stable attribute order makes generated-HTML diffs reviewable instead of full of reorder noise.

name: inline-style-linter
description: Reports inline style attributes in HTML, flagging !important usage and properties that conflict with a CSP style-src.
example_prompt: List all inline styles in this HTML and flag the risky ones
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM attribute scan of pasted markup.
rationale: Inline styles break under strict CSP and resist theming; surfacing them is the first step to removing them.

name: weasel-word-finder
description: Highlights vague qualifiers and weasel words like 'several', 'often', and 'arguably'.
example_prompt: Point out the weasel words in this report.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a curated wordlist matched against tokens, no network needed.
rationale: Removing vague qualifiers sharpens persuasive and academic prose.

name: numeric-dtype-recommender
description: Analyzes each numeric column's range and required precision and recommends the smallest lossless integer/float dtype.
example_prompt: What's the smallest dtype I can store each column in without losing data?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM range/precision scan; no server.
rationale: Right-sizing dtypes shrinks datasets dramatically and is otherwise a manual, error-prone judgment call.

name: wav-header-validator
description: Validates a WAV RIFF header: chunk sizes, fmt fields, and whether declared data length matches the actual file.
example_prompt: Check whether this WAV file's header matches its data
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: RIFF header fields are read directly from the byte buffer.
rationale: Mismatched WAV headers cause playback glitches and truncation that a header check catches immediately.

name: deprecated-html-element-checker
description: Scans HTML for obsolete elements (center, font, marquee, big, frame, acronym) and suggests modern replacements.
example_prompt: Find deprecated HTML tags in this markup
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tag scan against a built-in obsolete-element list.
rationale: Legacy markup pasted from old templates still uses dead elements; a checker modernizes it quickly.

name: floating-point-allclose-comparator
description: Compares two numeric arrays elementwise within relative and absolute tolerances and lists mismatching indices.
example_prompt: Are these two arrays equal within 1e-6 tolerance?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — numpy-style allclose comparison over pairs, deterministic and local.
rationale: Tolerance-aware array comparison is the core check for numerical test assertions and result reproducibility.

name: image-bit-depth-inspector
description: Reports bit depth, color type, channel count, and whether an alpha channel exists from the file header.
example_prompt: Is this PNG 8-bit or 16-bit, and does it have alpha?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse PNG IHDR / JPEG SOF / WebP headers — byte-level reads, no decode required.
rationale: Bit depth and channel layout decide whether a pipeline will clip or banding-fail.

name: image-spectral-analyzer
description: Computes and visualizes the 2D FFT magnitude spectrum to reveal periodic noise, screening, or resampling traces.
example_prompt: Show me the frequency spectrum of this image.
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute or plain Rust→WASM (rustfft): the 2D FFT runs on-device with no server.
rationale: Frequency view exposes halftone screens, moiré, and resampling artifacts invisible in pixel space.

name: image-snr-calculator
description: Estimates single-image signal-to-noise ratio by separating low-frequency signal from high-frequency noise.
example_prompt: What's the signal-to-noise ratio of this image?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: frequency separation and power-ratio math on decoded pixels — local.
rationale: Gives a single quality figure for comparing capture or denoise settings.

name: image-dimensions-from-header
description: Reads just the header bytes of PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/AVIF to report dimensions, color type, and animation flag without full decode.
example_prompt: what are the dimensions of these images from their headers?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM header byte parsing (imagesize-style); fast and fully local, no decode
rationale: Getting dimensions and format from bytes alone is instant and avoids decoding large images.

name: avro-ocf-inspector
description: Reads an Avro Object Container File's header to extract the embedded writer schema, codec, and block count.
example_prompt: What schema and codec is this .avro file using?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the OCF header (magic, metadata map, sync marker) is parsed from raw bytes client-side.
rationale: Recovering the embedded schema is the first step in debugging any Avro data pipeline.

name: matrix-rank-analyzer
description: Reports the numerical rank, nullity, and rank-deficiency of a matrix from CSV with a configurable singular-value tolerance.
example_prompt: What is the rank of this matrix and is it full rank?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via SVD with thresholding; no external services.
rationale: Rank deficiency silently breaks least-squares and inverses; a dedicated tolerance-aware checker catches it early.

name: multicollinearity-vif
description: Computes Variance Inflation Factors for each numeric predictor column to detect multicollinearity before regression.
example_prompt: Check these features for multicollinearity — give me the VIFs.
loader_feasibility: pyodide with numpy/statsmodels regression; in-browser Python.
rationale: Collinearity quietly destabilizes regression coefficients, and VIF is the standard diagnostic few can run offline.

name: rolling-correlation-analyzer
description: Computes windowed (rolling) correlation between two series to reveal how their relationship changes over time.
example_prompt: Show me the 30-day rolling correlation between these two columns.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM sliding-window pass; fully local.
rationale: Static correlation hides regime changes; rolling correlation exposes them and isn't covered by moving-average tools.

name: ecdf-calculator
description: Computes the empirical cumulative distribution function of a numeric column and returns the step-function points.
example_prompt: Give me the empirical CDF of this column.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM sort + cumulative count; entirely local.
rationale: The ECDF is the most honest distribution view and a clean building block for plotting and comparison.

name: stationarity-test
description: Runs Augmented Dickey-Fuller and KPSS tests on a series to assess stationarity and reports statistics, p-values, and critical values.
example_prompt: Is this time series stationary? Run an ADF test.
loader_feasibility: pyodide with statsmodels; executes in the in-browser Python sandbox.
rationale: Stationarity gates nearly all time-series modeling and is hard to test without a stats library.

name: seasonality-detector
description: Detects the dominant seasonal period(s) of a time series via autocorrelation peaks and periodogram analysis.
example_prompt: What seasonal period does this sales series have?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM ACF + periodogram scan; fully local.
rationale: Knowing the seasonal period is a prerequisite for forecasting and decomposition, and isn't trivially eyeballed.

name: vector-norm-calculator
description: Computes L1, L2, L-infinity, and arbitrary p-norms of vectors or each row of a CSV.
example_prompt: Compute the L2 norm of each row in this CSV.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM elementwise reduction; fully local.
rationale: Norms are a constant utility in ML and geometry that's surprisingly fiddly to do across a whole file.

name: aztec-code-decoder
description: Detects and decodes Aztec 2D codes (transit/event tickets) into their text payload.
example_prompt: Decode the Aztec code on this train ticket
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (rxing) does the bullseye-locator and Galois-field decode in-memory.
rationale: Ticketing systems use Aztec codes and there's no easy offline reader.

name: pixel-art-grid-extractor
description: Detects the pixel grid in pixel art and exports it as a downscaled-to-true-resolution color matrix (JSON/CSV).
example_prompt: Extract the true pixel grid from this scaled-up pixel art
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM detects the repeat period and samples cell centers in-memory.
rationale: Pixel artists frequently need to recover the real grid from upscaled sprites.

name: cpio-archive-list
description: Lists the entries, modes, sizes, and types in a cpio archive (newc/odc formats) without extracting.
example_prompt: What files are inside this cpio archive?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reading cpio header magic and entry records; archive walked in-memory with no server
rationale: cpio archives (initramfs, RPM payloads) have no everyday listing tool the way zip/tar do.

name: wsdl-parse
