description: Parses a WSDL document into its services, ports, operations, and message/part definitions.
example_prompt: List all the operations and their input/output messages in this WSDL
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML walk of the definitions/portType/binding tree; pure parsing of SOAP service descriptions in-browser
rationale: Devs integrating legacy SOAP services need a fast operation summary without firing up an enterprise IDE.

name: source-map-resolver
description: Given a JS source map and a generated line/column, resolves the original source file, line, and symbol name.
example_prompt: Use this source map to find the original location of line 1, column 8423
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decoding the Base64 VLQ mappings; pure computation, no network.
rationale: De-minifying a production stack frame locally avoids uploading source maps to third-party services.

name: enum-lookup-table-generator
description: Generates a lookup/enum table (id, code, label) as SQL INSERTs or CSV from a list of values.
example_prompt: Make a lookup table for these order status values
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; list parsing plus templated output.
rationale: Reference tables are common and tedious to hand-write consistently.

name: video-audio-channel-layout-check
description: Reports the audio channel layout (mono/stereo/5.1) and flags layouts that don't match the expected delivery spec.
example_prompt: Is this audio stereo or accidentally mono/5.1?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm reads channel_layout from the audio stream in-browser.
rationale: An accidentally-mono or surprise-5.1 track fails ingest and is invisible without checking the layout tag.

name: duplicate-id-checker
description: Parses HTML and reports any id value used on more than one element, with the line of each occurrence.
example_prompt: Check this HTML for duplicate id attributes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML parsing of pasted markup — purely local.
rationale: Duplicate IDs break getElementById, label[for], and anchor links in ways no validator output makes obvious otherwise.

name: sine-wave-generator
description: Generates a sampled sine wave CSV from frequency, amplitude, phase, sample rate, and duration.
example_prompt: Generate a 440 Hz sine wave sampled at 8000 Hz for 0.1 seconds
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sin over time steps, no audio backend required
rationale: A reusable signal scaffold for DSP demos, test tones, and plot data without spinning up Python.

name: image-to-lqip
description: Produces a low-quality image placeholder: a tiny blurred base64 thumbnail plus a CSS snippet.
example_prompt: Make an LQIP placeholder for this hero image
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: downscale, blur, encode tiny JPEG, base64, emit CSS — all local.
rationale: LQIP blur-up is a popular perceived-performance trick that's fiddly to generate by hand.

name: audio-phase-aligner
description: Time-aligns two channels or two tracks by cross-correlation and shifting to fix phase/timing offsets.
example_prompt: Align these two mic recordings of the same source so they're phase-coherent
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — cross-correlate decoded PCM to find the lag, then sample-shift one track; pure computation, no server.
rationale: Multi-mic and dual-take recordings comb-filter when out of phase, and automatic alignment is a precise fix that's painful to do by ear.

name: audio-soft-clipper
description: Applies musical soft clipping/saturation to round off peaks and tame transients without harsh digital clipping.
example_prompt: Soft-clip the peaks on this drum loop to make it punchier without distortion
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — `asoftclip` offers several soft-clip transfer curves; runs in ffmpeg.wasm.
rationale: Soft clipping squeezes a few more dB and adds warmth where a brickwall limiter would sound clamped, and it has no equivalent in the catalog.

name: audiogram-video
description: Generates a square or vertical podcast audiogram with an animated waveform drawn over a cover image and the audio track.
example_prompt: Make an audiogram clip of this 30s podcast quote with our show artwork
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg showwaves overlays the live waveform onto the image, fully local.
rationale: Audiograms are the standard way to promote podcasts on social and currently require paid SaaS tools.

name: lsb-steganalysis
description: Runs a chi-square/LSB statistical test to estimate whether data is hidden in an image's least-significant bits.
example_prompt: Could there be hidden data steganographically embedded in this PNG?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes LSB pair-value statistics across pixels offline.
rationale: A privacy-preserving way to screen images for steganography without trusting a remote analyzer.

name: rule-of-thirds-checker
description: Estimates the main subject's position via saliency and reports how well it aligns with rule-of-thirds intersections.
example_prompt: Is the subject well-placed by the rule of thirds in this shot?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a small saliency model on the decoded image entirely in-browser.
rationale: Composition feedback helps users pick and crop stronger photos without manual eyeballing.

name: text-encoding-linter
description: Detects mixed line endings, trailing whitespace, BOM markers, tab/space mixing, and invalid UTF-8 bytes in a text file.
example_prompt: Lint this file for line-ending and whitespace issues
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scanning bytes directly; pure byte inspection, fully offline.
rationale: Invisible encoding/whitespace problems cause diff noise and parse failures, and a byte-level linter makes them visible.

name: raw-embedded-preview
description: Extracts the full-size JPEG preview embedded in a camera RAW without full demosaicing.
example_prompt: Pull the jpeg preview out of this .cr2
loader_feasibility: Parsing the RAW/TIFF IFDs to locate and copy the embedded JPEG is lightweight pure-Rust work in wasm.
rationale: Grabbing the camera's own preview is instant and avoids the heavy cost of a full RAW develop.

name: homoglyph-detect
description: Detects confusable/homoglyph characters used to spoof domains, brand names, or text.
example_prompt: Does this domain use any look-alike characters?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (unicode confusables table); pure local lookup
rationale: Homoglyph spoofing drives phishing and is invisible to the naked eye.

name: video-semantic-frame-diff
description: Uses image embeddings to find frames whose semantic content changed between two versions, beyond pixel-level differences.
example_prompt: Find the frames where something meaningfully different appears between these two cuts
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs a CLIP-style image encoder in-browser (WASM/WebGPU) to embed sampled frames and compare them locally.
rationale: Semantic diffing catches added/removed objects or text overlays that pixel-difference tools flag as noise or miss entirely.

name: lighthouse-report-diff
description: Compares two Lighthouse JSON reports and shows score deltas and Core Web Vitals (LCP/CLS/TBT) movement between runs.
example_prompt: Compare these two Lighthouse reports and tell me if performance regressed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads both Lighthouse JSON files and diffs the category scores and audit metrics in-browser; the reports are self-contained JSON.
rationale: Web-perf regression tracking needs run-to-run comparison; the catalog has a single-report analyzer but no two-report diff.

name: po-to-json
description: Converts a gettext .po translation catalog into a JSON message map.
example_prompt: Convert this .po file to a JSON translation map
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM .po parser handling msgid/msgstr and plurals, no network.
rationale: Front-end i18n libraries consume JSON while translators ship .po, a frequent pipeline conversion.

name: video-set-timecode
description: Embeds a starting SMPTE timecode (HH:MM:SS:FF) into the video for editing/broadcast workflows.
example_prompt: Set this clip's start timecode to 01:00:00:00
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg-wasm writes the -timecode metadata via stream copy locally.
rationale: NLEs and broadcast tools rely on embedded timecode and there's no way to set it currently.

name: video-mjpeg-encode
description: Encodes video to Motion JPEG, where every frame is an independent intraframe JPEG.
example_prompt: Encode this to Motion JPEG for frame-accurate editing
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg-wasm's mjpeg encoder runs entirely in-browser.
rationale: MJPEG is needed for editing tools and hardware that require all-intraframe footage; only mjpeg decoding exists today.

name: matroska-chapters-extractor
description: Extracts Matroska Chapters (ChapterAtom timestamps and titles) from an MKA file into JSON or a cue sheet.
example_prompt: Pull the chapter list out of this mka audiobook
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the EBML Chapters element and reads ChapterTimeStart/ChapterDisplay entries.
rationale: Matroska chapter markers are stored as nested EBML and are inaccessible to format-agnostic chapter tools.

name: matroska-attachment-extractor
description: Extracts attached files (cover art, fonts, cue sheets) embedded in a Matroska/MKA AttachedFile element.
example_prompt: Extract the cover image attached to this mka
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — walks the Attachments EBML element and copies each FileData payload out.
rationale: Matroska attachments are a common way to bundle artwork that no ID3/FLAC art tool can reach.

name: video-deblock
description: Smooths blocky compression artifacts from heavily re-encoded or low-bitrate video.
example_prompt: reduce the blocky compression artifacts in this clip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm deblock/pp filters run in-browser
rationale: Re-shared social videos accumulate blocking that deblocking visibly improves.

name: audio-mono-bass
description: Sums low frequencies to mono below a crossover while keeping highs in stereo, for vinyl/club-safe masters.
example_prompt: Make everything below 120 Hz mono on this track
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg crossover + per-band pan, or plain Rust→WASM band split; client-side
rationale: Mono-ing the bass prevents vinyl cutting problems and tightens club playback.

name: audio-true-peak-limit
description: Limits inter-sample (true) peaks using oversampling so the file passes streaming true-peak specs.
example_prompt: Make sure this master never exceeds -1 dBTP
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg alimiter with oversampling for true-peak detection; runs in wasm
rationale: True-peak (not just sample-peak) limiting is required to pass Spotify/Apple delivery checks.

name: decimate-series
description: Downsamples a series by keeping every Nth sample (with optional anti-alias pre-averaging).
example_prompt: Downsample this signal keeping every 4th point
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: stride selection and optional block-mean, in-browser
rationale: Decimation shrinks oversampled data for plotting/storage and isn't covered by reshape or resample tools.

name: signed-log-transform
description: Applies sign(x)·log(1+|x|) to compress heavy-tailed columns while preserving sign and zero.
example_prompt: Apply a signed log transform to this column with large positive and negative values
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: element-wise symmetric log, fully offline
rationale: Signed-log compresses two-sided heavy tails where plain log fails, and differs from Yeo-Johnson by needing no fitted parameter.

name: python-docstring-extractor
description: Extracts module/class/function docstrings from Python source, paired with their owning symbol, for doc audits.
example_prompt: Extract all the docstrings from this Python module with the functions they belong to.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; scans `def`/`class` headers and the following triple-quoted strings, no network.
rationale: Auditing which symbols lack docstrings or pulling docs for review is common and tedious by hand.

name: netrc-parser
description: Parses a ~/.netrc file into machine/login/password/account entries and flags duplicate or default-only hosts.
example_prompt: Parse my .netrc and show the machines and logins (mask the passwords).
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; the netrc token grammar is small and parsed entirely in-browser.
rationale: Reviewing which hosts have credentials configured is useful and safer done locally than pasted to a server.

name: dynamic-range-meter
description: Calculates the official DR (dynamic range) value of a track using the Pleasurize Music Foundation algorithm.
example_prompt: Compute the DR value of this song
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM implements the DR algorithm on PCM (ffmpeg pre-decodes); fully local.
rationale: The DR metric is the de facto standard for rating loudness-war compression on a release.

name: video-chapter-embed
description: Adds named chapter markers to an MP4/MKV from a timestamp list for seekable navigation.
example_prompt: add chapter markers to this mp4 from this list of timestamps
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm writes a chapters metadata file during remux locally
rationale: Chapter-marked videos navigate far better and few free tools embed chapters offline.

name: resample-series
description: Resamples a series to a target number of evenly-spaced points via linear interpolation.
example_prompt: Resample this 317-point series to exactly 100 points
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: interpolation onto a new grid, fully client-side
rationale: Length normalization by interpolation is needed to align series of different lengths and has no existing equivalent.

name: currency-amount-extractor
description: Extracts monetary amounts with currency symbols or codes and lists them with context.
example_prompt: List all the dollar amounts in this contract
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pattern match on currency symbols/codes plus numerals, offline
rationale: Pulling every money figure from a contract or invoice is tedious manually and trivial for a targeted extractor.

name: heading-hierarchy-checker
description: Flags skipped or out-of-order heading levels in Markdown or HTML documents.
example_prompt: Does this document skip any heading levels?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM heading parse; no network.
rationale: Proper heading order matters for accessibility and SEO, and validating it is purely structural.

name: license-header-checker
description: Checks source files for a required license/SPDX header and reports files that are missing or have a mismatched header.
example_prompt: Check these files for missing license headers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM text comparison against a user-supplied header template; runs locally on pasted/loaded files
rationale: License-header compliance is tedious to enforce by hand across many files.

name: voc-to-wav
description: Converts Creative Voice File (.voc) DOS-era audio, including its multi-block structure, into a single WAV.
example_prompt: convert this old creative .voc sound to wav
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — walks the VOC data blocks and concatenates the PCM into a WAV container.
rationale: Sound Blaster / DOS game audio assets are stored as .voc that modern editors no longer read.

name: aac-adts-to-m4a
description: Remuxes a raw ADTS AAC stream (.aac) into an MP4/M4A container without re-encoding.
example_prompt: wrap this raw aac stream into an m4a
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader copies the AAC stream (codec copy) into an m4a container in wasm.
rationale: Raw ADTS dumps from streams and DVRs need an M4A container to seek, tag, and play normally.

name: fits-table-to-csv
description: Reads a FITS file's binary or ASCII table extension and exports its columns as CSV.
example_prompt: Convert the table in this .fits file to CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: FITS uses fixed 2880-byte blocks with a card-image header and big-endian columns, all decodable with pure byte parsing in-browser.
rationale: Astronomy catalogs are distributed as FITS tables and researchers routinely need them as CSV without installing astropy.

name: video-difference-blend
description: Renders the absolute pixel difference between two aligned videos as a new video where identical areas are black.
example_prompt: Show me the difference video between source.mp4 and recompressed.mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg blend=difference computes per-pixel deltas directly in the client wasm build.
rationale: A pure difference pass instantly localizes where two encodes or edits diverge.

name: video-encode-quality-ladder
description: Compares several encodes of the same source on size versus SSIM to chart the quality-per-byte ladder.
example_prompt: Compare my three bitrate encodes for the best size-to-quality tradeoff
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg measures SSIM and file size for each encode and Rust→WASM builds the comparison table client-side.
rationale: A rate-distortion ladder turns guesswork about bitrate choice into an evidence-based pick.

name: wav-null-test
description: Phase-inverts one file, sums it with another, and reports the residual RMS/peak to prove whether two renders are bit-for-bit or audibly identical.
example_prompt: Null-test these two WAV exports and tell me if the processing was transparent
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: decode/align PCM, invert, sum, compute residual energy — pure DSP, no network
rationale: The classic engineer's transparency check (did this plugin/bounce actually change anything?) has no easy browser tool.

name: package-json-dep-diff
description: Compares the dependency blocks of two package.json files and reports added, removed, and version-bumped packages.
example_prompt: What dependencies changed between these two package.json files?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — JSON parse of dependency maps + semver comparison, fully local
rationale: Dependency-delta review is routine in PR auditing and clearer than diffing the whole file by line.

name: openapi-validate
description: Validates an OpenAPI 3.x document for structural correctness — missing required fields, bad refs, and invalid types.
example_prompt: Validate this OpenAPI spec and list the structural errors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the spec's schema and $ref resolution are checked in-process over the parsed document
rationale: Broken OpenAPI specs silently fail codegen and docs tooling, and structural validation catches the cause.

name: jsonl-to-csv
description: Converts a JSON Lines / NDJSON stream into a single CSV with a unified header.
example_prompt: Convert this JSONL log into a CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (line-by-line serde_json + csv writer); streams locally with no upload.
rationale: NDJSON exports from log/event systems are unwieldy until flattened into a spreadsheet.

name: video-ffv1-archive
description: Encodes a video to lossless FFV1 in a Matroska container for long-term archival masters.
example_prompt: make a lossless ffv1 archival copy of this footage
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — the FFV1 encoder + mkv muxer run client-side in the WASM build.
rationale: FFV1/MKV is the standard preservation format for archives and libraries, complementing the lossy/intermediate encoders already built.

name: audio-embedding-similarity
description: Generates audio embeddings for two clips and reports cosine similarity to judge whether they sound semantically alike (same instrument, scene, or sound class).
example_prompt: Do these two sound effects sound like the same kind of thing?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime: run a small CLAP/PANNs audio encoder in-browser, cosine-compare the vectors locally
rationale: Perceptual 'do these sound similar' comparison enables sample-pack curation without a cloud API.

name: playlist-diff
description: Diffs two M3U/PLS playlists and reports added, removed, and reordered tracks.
example_prompt: What changed between my old and new playlist files?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse both playlist formats and compute an ordered set diff, local
rationale: Reconciling playlist edits across exports is a small but real chore with no quick tool.

name: sitemap-diff
description: Compares two XML sitemaps and lists URLs added, removed, or with changed lastmod dates.
example_prompt: What URLs were added or removed between these two sitemaps?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — XML parse of URL entries + set comparison, no fetching
rationale: Tracking which pages appeared or vanished between crawls is a real SEO task done entirely from two files.

name: graphql-schema-diff
description: Compares two GraphQL SDL schemas and reports added, removed, and changed types and fields with breaking-change flags.
example_prompt: What changed between these two GraphQL schemas?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — SDL parser builds type maps, comparison runs locally
rationale: Schema-evolution review is a core GraphQL workflow and entirely computable from two SDL files.

name: currency-string-parser
description: Parses currency strings like "$1,234.56", "€1.234,56", "USD 99" into {amount, currency} with the symbol/code resolved.
example_prompt: Parse $1,234.56 and €1.234,56 into amount and currency
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — symbol/code table plus locale number parsing, no exchange-rate lookups.
rationale: Extracting clean amounts from formatted prices is the first step before any financial math.

name: ligature-expander
description: Expands typographic ligatures (ﬁ, ﬂ, ﬀ, ﬃ) and similar presentation-form glyphs back to their plain letter sequences.
example_prompt: Expand the fi and fl ligatures in this copied text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM Unicode presentation-form mapping; no server
rationale: PDF and font ligatures sneak single glyphs into copied text that break search and word counts in ways users can't see.

name: video-deflicker
description: Removes brightness flicker from time-lapse or LED-lit video by averaging luminance across frames.
example_prompt: Remove the flicker from this time-lapse
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's deflicker filter runs in ffmpeg.wasm, analyzing a frame window locally.
rationale: Time-lapses and footage shot under LED/fluorescent lights flicker badly, and deflicker is the targeted fix.

name: maxabs-scaler
description: Scales a column by its maximum absolute value into [-1, 1], preserving sign and sparsity.
example_prompt: Scale this column to [-1,1] by max absolute value
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — divide by max|x|, no network
rationale: MaxAbs scaling is the standard choice for sparse/signed features and is missing offline.

name: unit-quantity-parser
description: Parses physical-quantity strings like "12.5 kg", "3 m/s", "450 mL" into separate {value, unit} fields across a list.
example_prompt: Split these quantities into value and unit: 12.5 kg, 3 m/s, 450 mL
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — number+unit tokenizing, fully local string work.
rationale: Separating magnitude from unit is the prerequisite step for any downstream unit conversion or computation.

name: isbn-extractor
description: Finds ISBN-10 and ISBN-13 numbers in text, validates their check digits, and normalizes formatting.
example_prompt: Pull the valid ISBNs out of this book list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: regex plus check-digit arithmetic, fully local.
rationale: Catalogers and resellers need clean, validated ISBNs and check-digit math is easy to get wrong by hand.

name: fullwidth-halfwidth-converter
description: Converts fullwidth Latin letters, digits, and punctuation to halfwidth (and back) for cleaning CJK-input text.
example_prompt: Convert the fullwidth letters and numbers in this to normal halfwidth
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM fullwidth/halfwidth codepoint offset mapping; client-side
rationale: Text typed with CJK IMEs mixes fullwidth ASCII that breaks parsing and search, and normalizing it is a routine cleanup step.

name: video-sepia
description: Applies a warm sepia/vintage tone to a video via a color matrix.
example_prompt: Give this video an old-film sepia look
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's colorchannelmixer matrix runs in ffmpeg.wasm, fully client-side.
rationale: Vintage tinting is a popular, deterministic stylistic effect that needs no creative judgment.

name: inline-style-extractor
description: Pulls inline style attributes out of HTML into a stylesheet with generated class names.
example_prompt: Extract the inline styles from this HTML into a CSS block with classes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML+CSS parsing; deterministic refactor with no server.
rationale: Email and CMS exports are riddled with inline styles that are impossible to maintain until extracted.

name: html-class-prefixer
description: Adds a namespace prefix to every class name in HTML and the matching CSS selectors together.
example_prompt: Prefix all classes in this HTML and CSS with myapp-
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM coordinated HTML+CSS rewrite; deterministic, browser-local.
rationale: Embedding a widget into another site needs class isolation, which manual find-replace can't do safely.

name: requirements-txt-sort
description: Sorts, deduplicates, and normalizes spacing in a Python requirements.txt file.
example_prompt: sort and clean up this requirements.txt
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line parse of pinned specs; client-side only.
rationale: Tidy, sorted requirements reduce merge conflicts and duplicate pins.

name: fixed-decimal-formatter
description: Formats a numeric column with fixed decimal places, zero-padding, and fixed total width for aligned output.
example_prompt: Format this column to always show 3 decimals, zero-padded
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — printf-style formatting, no network
rationale: Presentation-grade fixed formatting (invoices, reports) is finicky to do uniformly across a column.

name: adverb-counter
description: Counts and lists -ly adverbs and reports their density to flag adverb-heavy prose.
example_prompt: How many adverbs am I using in this essay?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; suffix-based token matching locally.
rationale: Adverb density is a quick lever for tightening writing per common style advice.

name: edge-density-analyzer
description: Measures overall edge/detail density to classify an image as flat, moderate, or busy.
example_prompt: How much fine detail is in this image?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs a Sobel pass and aggregates edge magnitude over decoded pixels.
rationale: Detail density informs sharpening, compression, and thumbnail-legibility decisions.

name: video-motion-intensity-graph
description: Quantifies how much motion occurs in each part of a video and graphs motion intensity over time.
example_prompt: Where are the high-action parts of this video?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes frames and computes inter-frame difference magnitude in wasm; the graph is rendered from those values.
rationale: A motion profile helps find action peaks, choose encode settings, or pick highlight moments offline.

name: progress-ring-video
description: Generates a transparent animated circular progress-ring clip filling from 0% to 100% over a set duration.
example_prompt: Make a transparent 10-second progress ring filling from empty to full in teal
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute draws the arc per frame on the GPU with an alpha channel and ffmpeg encodes it client-side.
rationale: A clean animated progress ring is a frequent UI/loading and timer overlay that creators otherwise screen-record.

name: plantuml-url-encoder
description: Encodes PlantUML diagram source into the deflate+base64 form used in PlantUML server URLs.
example_prompt: Encode this PlantUML source into a shareable URL fragment
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with a deflate implementation and PlantUML's custom base64; runs locally
rationale: The PlantUML URL encoding is non-standard and nearly impossible to produce without a dedicated tool.

name: audio-dropout-detector
description: Detects sudden glitches, dropouts, and sample discontinuities (abrupt amplitude jumps) and reports their timestamps.
example_prompt: Find any glitches or dropouts in this audio file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: first-difference / energy-spike scan over decoded PCM, runs in-browser
rationale: Streaming, USB, and disk-buffer dropouts are intermittent and hard to spot by ear across a long file.

name: requirements-from-imports
description: Scans Python source for top-level imports and emits a requirements.txt of third-party packages.
example_prompt: Build a requirements.txt from the imports in this Python file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — lexes import statements and maps known import names to PyPI names via a bundled table, offline.
rationale: Recovering dependencies from inherited scripts that lack a requirements file is a frequent, annoying task.

name: isin-validator
description: Validates a 12-character ISIN security identifier using its Luhn-based mod-10 check digit after letter expansion.
example_prompt: Is ISIN US0378331005 valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: alphanumeric-to-digit expansion plus Luhn, fully offline.
rationale: Traders and back-office staff verify ISINs constantly and benefit from an instant private check.

name: ass-to-srt
description: Converts Advanced SubStation Alpha (.ass/.ssa) subtitles to plain SRT, dropping styling tags.
example_prompt: Convert this .ass subtitle file to SRT
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing the [Events] dialogue lines and stripping override tags; local only.
rationale: Anime/fansub subtitles ship as ASS but most players/editors want SRT, with no good offline converter.

name: video-to-dash
description: Packages a video into MPEG-DASH segments with an .mpd manifest for standards-based adaptive streaming.
example_prompt: Package this clip as MPEG-DASH for my player
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm's dash muxer generates the init/media segments and manifest in the virtual filesystem client-side.
rationale: DASH is the open streaming standard, and browser-local packaging removes the need for an encoding backend.

name: apk-tracker-scanner
description: Scans an Android APK for known third-party trackers and reports which ones it embeds.
example_prompt: Scan this APK and tell me what trackers it contains
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: unzip the APK and match classes.dex strings against a bundled εxodus signature DB, all in memory
rationale: Exact mapping of εxodus/ClassyShark3xodus/Exodus Privacy — a beloved privacy audit with no web equivalent.

name: video-chapter-marker-generator
description: Turns a list of timestamps and titles into YouTube-style chapter markers and a WebVTT chapters file.
example_prompt: Make chapter markers from these timestamps: 0:00 Intro, 2:30 Setup, 8:10 Demo
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM text/time parsing and formatting; no network.
rationale: Creators publishing to FreeTube/Yattee/Owncast audiences need chapter markers in both description and WebVTT form.

name: thai-spell-checker
description: Flags misspelled Thai words and suggests corrections from a bundled dictionary.
example_prompt: Check the Thai spelling in this paragraph and suggest fixes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: edit-distance ranking over a bundled Thai dictionary, runs client-side
rationale: Thai spell-check is rarely available offline and is genuinely useful for writers and form input.

name: vietnamese-word-segmenter
description: Joins space-separated Vietnamese syllables into multi-syllable words using dictionary longest-matching.
example_prompt: Segment the Vietnamese words in: học sinh trường đại học
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: dictionary longest-matching over a bundled Vietnamese wordlist, no network
rationale: Vietnamese words span multiple space-separated syllables, so word segmentation is required before search or analysis.

name: persian-digit-converter
description: Converts between Persian, Arabic-Indic, and Latin digits and spells numbers out in Persian words.
example_prompt: Convert ۱۲۳۴ to English digits and also spell it in Persian words
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — deterministic digit mapping plus a number-to-words algorithm, fully offline.
rationale: Mixed digit systems are a constant headache in Persian data entry, invoices, and search normalization.

name: formant-analyzer
description: Extracts vowel formant frequencies (F1–F4) over time from a voice recording.
example_prompt: Show the formants in this vowel
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM LPC analysis computes formants locally with no server.
rationale: Formants are central to phonetics, accent training, and speech-therapy analysis.

name: music-theory-analyzer
description: Parses a MIDI or MusicXML file and reports key, time signature, chords, and Roman-numeral harmonic analysis.
example_prompt: Analyze the harmony in this MIDI file.
loader_feasibility: pyodide loader — music21 is pure Python and runs under Pyodide via micropip, doing full symbolic analysis on the uploaded score in-browser.
rationale: Composers and students want harmonic analysis of their scores and music21-in-Pyodide brings that whole toolkit client-side.

name: jams-converter
description: Reads and converts JAMS annotation files to and from CSV and JSON.
example_prompt: Convert this JAMS file to CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON handling, fully local.
rationale: Interop glue for the JAMS-based MIR dataset ecosystem (mirdata demand).

name: shadertoy-to-standalone
description: Rewrites a ShaderToy-style mainImage shader into a standalone WebGL/WebGPU fragment shader with proper uniforms.
example_prompt: Convert this ShaderToy shader into a standalone WebGL fragment shader
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM that rewrites mainImage()/iResolution/iTime/iMouse conventions into a normal entry point; pure text transform.
rationale: ShaderToy's huge shader library uses nonstandard uniform conventions that block direct reuse, and porting them by hand is fiddly.

name: map-tile-calculator
description: Converts between lat/lon/zoom and XYZ slippy tiles, quadkeys, and tile bounding boxes.
example_prompt: What XYZ tile and quadkey contains lat 40.7 lon -74.0 at zoom 12?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: slippy-tile/quadkey arithmetic, pure math.
rationale: Every WebGL map stack (MapMetrics GL, Deck.gl) needs tile-index math when debugging layers and viewports.

name: mesh-recenter-scale
description: Recenters a model to the origin and normalizes its size to a unit bounding box.
example_prompt: Recenter this model.obj at the origin and scale it to fit a 1-unit box
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM vertex transform; simple matrix math over the mesh, fully local.
rationale: Imported assets land at arbitrary offsets/scales, and recentering is a universal prep step before loading into a scene.

name: macho-analyzer
description: Parses macOS Mach-O binaries (incl. fat/universal) for load commands, segments, linked libs, and code-sign info.
example_prompt: What dynamic libraries does this Mach-O binary link against?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Mach-O structures are decoded from the uploaded file with a pure-Rust parser.
rationale: macOS malware analysis is underserved and the format parses cleanly with no host dependency.

name: scatter-matrix
description: Builds an SVG scatter-plot matrix (SPLOM) showing every pairwise relationship among CSV numeric columns.
example_prompt: Scatter matrix of all numeric columns in this dataset
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM iterates column pairs and tiles small SVG scatter cells locally.
rationale: Glue's linked multidimensional exploration distilled into a single fast pairwise overview.

name: postal-code-validator
description: Validates and formats postal/ZIP codes for many countries using embedded format rules (no external lookup).
example_prompt: Is 90210 a valid US ZIP, and what's the UK postcode format?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM regex matching against an embedded per-country format table, no network.
rationale: Maps the ZipCheckup demand to a format-based validator that needs no server or dataset download.

name: c2-beacon-detector
description: Detects periodic beaconing by computing connection-interval regularity and jitter from logs or PCAP flows.
example_prompt: find any C2 beaconing pattern in these connection logs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; timing/statistics over parsed records, all client-side.
rationale: Beacon-interval analysis is a core network-security-monitoring skill and rarely available as a simple browser tool.

name: stego-detector
description: Scans an image for steganography signs: appended data after EOF, bit-plane anomalies, and embedded archives.
example_prompt: is there hidden data in this image?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; statistical and signature checks over image bytes, fully local.
rationale: A quick 'is anything hidden here' triage saves time before committing to extraction in CTFs.

name: archive-repacker
description: Converts archives between formats (e.g. ZIP⇄TAR.GZ) and re-compresses with a chosen level, all without leaving the page.
example_prompt: Convert this zip into a tar.gz
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: decompress then recompress using Rust archive crates entirely in-memory.
rationale: File-manager users frequently need a cross-platform archive format for sharing and lack a quick, private repacker.

name: comment-thread-to-markdown
description: Renders a nested comment thread JSON into readable indented Markdown.
example_prompt: Turn this comment thread JSON into a readable Markdown transcript
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM recursive tree-to-Markdown rendering; local only.
rationale: Archiving or quoting a discussion from Remark42/Commento exports is easier when the thread is flattened into plain Markdown.

name: opml-markdown-outline
description: Converts between OPML outlines and nested Markdown bullet lists.
example_prompt: Turn this OPML outline into a Markdown list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses OPML/Markdown client-side.
rationale: Outliner-style apps (Logseq, AppFlowy) and mind-map tools exchange data as OPML that users want as plain Markdown outlines.

name: logseq-to-obsidian
description: Converts Logseq Markdown (block properties, block refs, page properties) to Obsidian-flavored Markdown.
example_prompt: Convert my Logseq notes to Obsidian format
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses and rewrites the Markdown locally.
rationale: Logseq-to-Obsidian is one of the most common note migrations and it mangles block refs and properties without a dedicated converter.

name: linux-log-summarizer
description: Summarizes a pasted journalctl/dmesg/boot log into the key errors, warnings, and likely root cause for troubleshooting.
example_prompt: Summarize this journalctl output and tell me what failed at boot.
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — a small summarization model runs in-browser over the pasted log, no server inference.
rationale: Fedora/Mint/Qubes users debugging boot or service failures face overwhelming logs, and on-device summarization keeps potentially sensitive system data private.

name: rule-list-classifier
description: Learns an interpretable if-then rule list from labeled CSV so predictions come with human-readable reasons.
example_prompt: Build a simple rule-based classifier I can read for this loan-approval data
loader_feasibility: pyodide — a decision-rule/greedy rule-list learner over scikit-learn primitives runs entirely in the sandbox.
rationale: sklearn-expertsys demand for transparent rule lists serves the strong interest in interpretable, explainable models.

name: jsonapi-build
description: Builds and validates JSON:API resource objects, relationships, and compound documents.
example_prompt: Wrap this record as a JSON:API resource document
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — constructs/validates the JSON:API shape with serde_json, all local.
rationale: JSON:API's strict envelope (type/id/attributes/relationships) is easy to get wrong, and a generator/validator speeds API work.

name: rule-lemmatizer
description: Lemmatizes English words to their dictionary base form using morphological rules and an exception list.
example_prompt: Lemmatize: geese, was, better, studies.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; morphology rules + bundled exception table run locally.
rationale: Lemmatization (vs. stemming) is a distinct, more accurate normalization taught alongside WordNet in NLTK material.

name: topic-segmenter
description: Segments a long document into topical sections using TextTiling lexical-cohesion analysis.
example_prompt: Split this transcript into its distinct topic sections.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; lexical-cohesion scoring over sliding windows runs locally.
rationale: Topic segmentation is a well-known discourse-analysis technique with real utility for long transcripts and no good local tool.

name: relation-extractor
description: Extracts subject–relation–object triples linking the entities found in text.
example_prompt: Extract the relationships between people and companies mentioned here as triples.
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs NER plus a relation-classification model over entity pairs entirely in-browser.
rationale: Binary relation extraction is the distinctive feature of the MIT Information Extraction Toolkit (MITIE) and turns prose into a small knowledge graph.

name: word-semantic-clusterer
description: Groups a list of words or short phrases into clusters by meaning.
example_prompt: Cluster these 40 product tags into meaning-based groups.
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — embeds each item with a multilingual model and clusters in-browser.
rationale: A concrete, useful application of word-embedding demand for taxonomy and tag cleanup with no backend.

name: persian-stemmer
description: Reduces Persian words to their stems by stripping inflectional prefixes and suffixes.
example_prompt: Find the stem of each Persian word: کتاب‌ها، می‌روند، زیباترین
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Perstem-style affix-stripping rules, no model download required.
rationale: Stemming collapses morphological variants for search and indexing, and Persian's rich affixation makes a dedicated rule set valuable.

name: persian-pos-tagger
description: Tags each word in a Persian sentence with its part of speech.
example_prompt: Tag the parts of speech in: علی کتاب جدیدی خرید
loader_feasibility: transformers-js token-classification with an ONNX-converted Persian BERT model, executed in-browser via onnxruntime-web.
rationale: PoS tags (the demand behind Bijankhan/PANL10N tagging work) feed chunking, parsing, and grammar tooling for Persian.

name: chroma-features
description: Computes a chromagram (energy per pitch class) over time for harmonic analysis.
example_prompt: Give me the chroma features of this track
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM maps FFT bins onto 12 pitch classes locally with no server.
rationale: Chroma features underpin chord recognition, key detection, and cover-song matching.

name: spectral-features
description: Computes frame-level spectral descriptors (centroid, rolloff, bandwidth, flatness, zero-crossing rate) as a CSV.
example_prompt: Export spectral centroid and rolloff for this clip
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM FFT computes the descriptors frame by frame in the browser.
rationale: These low-level descriptors feed classic audio classifiers and timbre analysis.

name: voice-quality
description: Measures voice-quality metrics — jitter, shimmer, and harmonics-to-noise ratio — from a sustained vowel.
example_prompt: Measure jitter and shimmer in this recording
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM pitch-period analysis computes the perturbation metrics in the browser.
rationale: Jitter, shimmer, and HNR are standard clinical and vocal-coaching indicators of voice health.

name: beat-tracker
description: Detects beat positions and exports beat times or a click track.
example_prompt: Find the beats in this song
loader_feasibility: pyodide numpy/scipy onset+tempo tracking on ffmpeg-decoded PCM, no server.
rationale: Lets editors sync cuts and overdubs to the beat (FMP/MIR Notebooks demand).

name: numpy-calculator
description: Evaluates NumPy array expressions and returns results, shapes, and stats.
example_prompt: Compute the mean and std of [3,1,4,1,5,9] with numpy
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs numpy entirely in-browser.
rationale: Hands-on numeric helper that mirrors intro tutorials (Introduction to Numpy and Scipy demand).

name: sprite-sheet-builder
description: Combines animation frames into a sprite sheet plus frame metadata for particle and billboard effects.
example_prompt: Build a sprite sheet from these animation frames
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg composites frames; grid layout computed in plain Rust→WASM
rationale: Serves the particle-billboard demand and reduces per-frame texture binds.

name: gltf-validator
description: Validates a glTF/GLB file against the spec and reports structural errors and warnings.
example_prompt: Is this glTF valid? Show me any spec violations
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: schema/spec checks on parsed glTF, local.
rationale: Broken glTF exports are a frequent cause of 'model won't load' across every engine, and validation is normally a separate web service.

name: threat-report-summarizer
description: Summarizes long security advisories or threat reports into key findings, affected systems, and recommended actions.
example_prompt: Summarize this 20-page APT report into the key TTPs and IOCs
loader_feasibility: transformers-js: runs a summarization model entirely in the browser over pasted text, no API calls.
rationale: Analysts drown in long reports and local summarization keeps sensitive intel off third-party services.

name: dependency-parser
description: Parses sentences into a dependency tree showing grammatical relations.
example_prompt: Show the dependency parse of this sentence.
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime: a small biaffine dependency-parser model runs in-browser, with a tree rendered to SVG.
rationale: spaCy, jPTDP, and AllenNLP dependency-parsing demand, visualized fully client-side.

name: json-merge-patch
description: Applies an RFC 7396 JSON Merge Patch to a document, including null-key deletion and recursive object merging.
example_prompt: Apply this merge patch to my JSON: {settings:{theme:'dark', legacy:null}}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM merge-patch implementation over serde_json; fully in-browser.
rationale: Merge-patch is the update/sync semantic behind Kinto/CouchDB-style clients and is distinct from positional RFC 6902 patches.

name: jsonapi-flatten
description: Parses a JSON:API document and resolves its included resources into flat, denormalized objects.
example_prompt: flatten this JSON:API response with its included resources
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM resource linker over the parsed document; relationship resolution is local.
rationale: jsonapi-consumer demand reflects how painful manual resolution of JSON:API includes/relationships is.

name: json-translate
description: Translates only the string values of a JSON document to a target language while preserving keys and structure.
example_prompt: Translate the values in this i18n JSON file to Spanish, keep the keys
loader_feasibility: transformers-js translation model (opus-mt/NLLB) running in WASM/WebGPU; runs fully in-browser, no API.
rationale: Maps 'trans' (translate) demand to localization JSON, a real i18n workflow that keeps source strings off third-party servers.

name: render-3d-model
description: Renders a static preview image of a glTF/GLB model from a chosen camera angle with basic lighting.
example_prompt: Render a front-view preview PNG of this GLB model
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute — rasterizes the mesh on the GPU in-browser, no server-side rendering.
rationale: Generates Sketchfab-style thumbnails for 3D assets entirely client-side.

name: video-timecode-overlay
description: Burn a running timecode or frame-counter overlay onto a video.
example_prompt: Add a timecode overlay to this clip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg drawtext with the timecode filter, fully in-browser.
rationale: Standard editorial/review need distinct from the progress-bar overlay.

name: mongo-aggregate
description: Runs a MongoDB aggregation pipeline ($match/$group/$sort/$project/$limit) over a JSON array of documents and returns the aggregated result.
example_prompt: Run this aggregation pipeline on my JSON: [{$group:{_id:'$dept', total:{$sum:'$salary'}}},{$sort:{total:-1}}]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM implementing the core aggregation stages over serde_json; all computation in wasmi.
rationale: Aggregation pipelines are where Mongo users do real analytics and there is no browser-local way to try one without a server today.

name: geojson-summary
description: Summarizes a GeoJSON: feature count, geometry types, bounding box, and properties, with coords exportable to CSV.
example_prompt: summarize this GeoJSON and give me the bounding box
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (geojson crate) — local computation, no network or map tiles
rationale: Inspecting large GeoJSON without loading it into a mapping app saves time for GIS users.

name: caesar-cipher
description: Encrypts or decrypts text with a Caesar/ROT-N shift, including ROT13.
example_prompt: rot13 this sentence
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM character shift — trivial transform, client-side
rationale: The Caesar cipher is the entry point of every crypto course and a perennially searched utility.

name: lua-linter
description: Statically analyzes Lua code for undefined globals, unused variables, shadowing, and common mistakes, like a browser-local Selene.
example_prompt: Lint this Lua script and tell me about unused variables: `local x = 1 local y = 2 print(x)`
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Selene is pure Rust on top of `full_moon` and compiles to wasm32; analysis is fully in-memory.
rationale: embedded-Lua hosts (mlua, hlua, td_rlua) want to catch script errors before runtime, and a static linter does that without executing untrusted code.

name: vcf-parser
description: Parses VCF variant lines into a readable table of chromosome, position, ref/alt alleles, quality, filters, and INFO fields.
example_prompt: Parse these VCF records into a table.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: tab-delimited and INFO-field parsing, pure text processing as in Rust-Bio's vcf support.
rationale: Inspecting variant records is a routine genomics task and local parsing avoids sending clinical/genomic data anywhere.

name: crash-report-formatter
description: Turns a stack trace plus environment details into a clean, shareable markdown bug report.
example_prompt: Format this panic and my OS/version info into a bug report
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — text templating only.
rationale: Mirrors human-panic's job of converting raw crashes into reports humans can actually file.

name: lucene-query-builder
description: Builds and validates Lucene/Elasticsearch query-string syntax including fields, ranges, booleans, and wildcards.
example_prompt: build a Lucene query: title contains rust, year after 2020, not draft
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM: string assembly plus syntax validation, all local.
rationale: Lucene query-string operators are terse and error-prone to type by hand.

name: database-schema-docs
description: Generates clean Markdown documentation (tables, columns, types, keys, relationships) from SQL schema DDL.
example_prompt: generate markdown docs for this CREATE TABLE schema
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — AST walk over parsed DDL emitting Markdown, all client-side.
rationale: Schema documentation derived from sea-schema-style introspection is tedious by hand and perfect for a deterministic local tool.

name: sql-to-orm-entities
description: Generates ORM model/entity code (SeaORM, Diesel, or rbatis style) from CREATE TABLE statements.
example_prompt: generate SeaORM entity structs from this schema
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the DDL and templates out Rust entity code; no codegen toolchain or DB required.
rationale: Entity scaffolding is the top reason people reach for sea-orm/diesel/rbatis/njord/rustorm/taitan-orm and is templatable offline.

name: orm-entities-to-sql
description: Reverses ORM model definitions (SeaORM/Diesel/rbatis structs) back into CREATE TABLE DDL.
example_prompt: turn these Diesel model structs into CREATE TABLE statements
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the struct/attribute syntax and emits DDL, fully in-memory text work.
rationale: Going model-first then needing the matching schema (for migrations or review) is common and has no offline tool today.

name: heightmap-erosion-simulator
description: Applies hydraulic and thermal erosion passes to a heightmap to produce realistic terrain, with adjustable droplet and erosion parameters.
example_prompt: Run hydraulic erosion on this heightmap for more natural terrain.
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute — droplet erosion is a parallel compute-shader simulation that runs locally on the GPU via WebGPU.
rationale: RTS/open-world terrain (the oxidator demand) needs eroded heightmaps and a GPU-accelerated browser simulator replaces specialized paid software.

name: find-image-in-screenshot
description: Locates a smaller template image inside a larger screenshot via template matching and returns its bounding-box coordinates.
example_prompt: Find where this button icon appears in the full screenshot
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — normalized cross-correlation over decoded pixel buffers in-WASM.
rationale: Directly mirrors autopilot-rs's image-search feature, useful for UI testing and locating elements in mockups.

name: log-level-histogram
description: Counts log entries by severity level and renders the distribution as a bar chart.
example_prompt: How many errors vs warnings are in this log?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tallies levels from the parsed text and emits chart data locally
rationale: Quick triage signal for any log dump, cheap to build from the same parsing primitives.

name: bazel-build-formatter
description: Parses and pretty-prints Bazel BUILD and .bzl files to a canonical style, like a browser-local buildifier.
example_prompt: Format this BUILD file for me (pasted below)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — starlark-rust parses to an AST and re-emits formatted source with no I/O, runnable fully in-browser.
rationale: Teams want consistent BUILD-file formatting in review without installing the Go buildifier toolchain.

name: mcp-config-validator
description: Validates and lints an MCP server configuration JSON, flagging missing fields, bad transports, and schema errors.
example_prompt: Check my MCP servers config for mistakes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (serde + schema check) parses and validates the JSON string entirely client-side
rationale: mcp-manager demand maps to a deterministic config linter that catches setup errors without running any server.

name: vocabulary-extractor
description: Pulls the key/rare vocabulary from a foreign-language text and gives a frequency-ranked list with translations.
example_prompt: Pull the hard vocabulary out of this Spanish article and translate each word.
loader_feasibility: transformers-js: local tokenizer/frequency pass plus a small translation model run entirely client-side.
rationale: Directly serves vocage's language-learning use case — building study lists from real reading material.

name: binary-diff
description: Creates a compact binary delta between two file versions and can apply the patch to reconstruct the new file.
example_prompt: Make a binary patch between these two versions of my file.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a bsdiff/rsync-style rolling-hash delta runs over both buffers in-memory.
rationale: The incremental-delta core of rdiff-backup and duplicity, exposed as a general diff/patch tool.

name: text-similarity-minhash
description: Estimates how similar two documents are using MinHash/Jaccard over text shingles.
example_prompt: How similar are these two articles?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM MinHash computes the estimate on the pasted text locally.
rationale: mash (MinHash) demand maps to fast near-duplicate text detection without sending content anywhere.

name: shell-alias-generator
description: Analyzes a pasted shell history to suggest aliases/abbreviations for frequent commands and flags name conflicts with existing ones.
example_prompt: Here's my zsh history — suggest aliases for my most-repeated commands.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: frequency counting, alias naming heuristics, and conflict checks are pure text analysis.
rationale: alman is dedicated to alias management, and turning real history into a tuned alias set is an easy, high-value local transform.

name: bookmark-organizer
description: Parses a Netscape bookmarks HTML export to dedupe, sort, group by domain, and re-tag entries, then emits a cleaned export.
example_prompt: Clean up my exported browser bookmarks — remove duplicates and group them by site.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: HTML bookmark parsing and reorganization run on the uploaded file in-memory with no network calls.
rationale: bkmr-style bookmark management is private data users want to tidy locally rather than upload to a third-party service.

name: shell-history-analyzer
description: Summarizes a shell history file: top commands, most-used flags, command-length distribution, and usage patterns.
example_prompt: Analyze my shell history and show my top commands: [paste history]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM aggregation and counting over pasted text; no external data needed.
rationale: Pairs with alias suggestion to give users insight into their own habits, entirely client-side and private.

name: snippet-format-converter
description: Converts command-snippet collections between pet (TOML), Nap, JSON, and plain markdown formats.
example_prompt: Convert my pet snippets to Nap format: [paste pet snippet.toml]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parse/serialize between known snippet schemas; pure data transformation.
rationale: Users migrating between pet, Nap, snipt and rsnip have no easy converter; this removes lock-in offline.

name: browser-storage-report
description: Reports how much origin storage the browser is using vs its quota, broken down across caches/IndexedDB/local storage.
example_prompt: How much storage is this site using in my browser and how close am I to the limit?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM formats the figures the host passes from navigator.storage.estimate() — a browser-native, client-side API.
rationale: It's the browser-local analog of dfc/df (free-vs-used reporting) and is the only filesystem a web app can truthfully measure.

name: email-thread-visualizer
description: Groups mbox messages into conversation threads using References/In-Reply-To and shows the tree.
example_prompt: Show the conversation threads in this mbox
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM builds the thread graph from headers locally.
rationale: Flat archives hide the conversation structure that threading reveals.

name: email-volume-chart
description: Charts email volume over time (per day/week/month) from an mbox.
example_prompt: Chart how many emails I got per month from this mbox
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM buckets Date headers and renders the chart client-side.
rationale: A time-series of your own mail is a quick, private analytic with no upload.

name: email-archive-builder
description: Packages selected emails into a browsable offline archive (zip of .eml plus a searchable HTML index).
example_prompt: Build a browsable archive from these emails
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM assembles the zip and index client-side — an Open Archiver-style local export.
rationale: Long-term email archiving shouldn't require standing up a server.

name: pretty-ls
description: Renders uploaded files/folder as a rich `ls -l`-style table with human-readable sizes, type icons, modified dates, and sortable columns.
example_prompt: List this folder like exa with sizes and dates, sorted by size
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM over file metadata from the browser file/directory picker — formatting only.
rationale: Delivers the exa/colorls/pretty-ls modern-ls experience as a flat detailed view, complementing the tree view.

name: archive-lister
description: Lists the contents (names, sizes, paths) of a dropped zip/tar/tar.gz archive without extracting it.
example_prompt: What's inside this zip file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM zip/tar/flate2 parsing of the dropped bytes; nothing leaves the browser
rationale: Previewing archive contents is a standard file-manager feature (hunter/lf previews) and runs safely client-side.

name: cash-flow-projector
description: Projects month-by-month cash balance from starting balance, recurring income, and recurring/one-off expenses.
example_prompt: Project my cash for the next 12 months from $3,000 with these incomes and bills.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: iterative monthly accumulation on entered figures, runs locally.
rationale: Cloudcash/Finance Tracker demand shows forward-looking cash projection is wanted and is pure arithmetic.

name: json-resume-renderer
description: Renders a JSON Resume (jsonresume.org schema) into a polished, themeable HTML or Markdown resume.
example_prompt: Render this JSON Resume as a clean one-page markdown resume
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — deserializes the JSON and templates HTML/Markdown output, fully client-side.
rationale: ancv exists to render JSON Resume nicely, and a browser renderer keeps the resume private on-device while producing shareable output.

name: json-resume-validator
description: Validates a JSON Resume document against the official schema and reports missing, malformed, or deprecated fields.
example_prompt: Check if my resume.json is valid JSON Resume and tell me what's wrong
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — schema validation of pasted JSON in the sandbox, no network.
rationale: JSON Resume tooling fails silently on schema errors, so a quick local validator saves users from broken renders downstream.

name: todo-comment-scanner
description: Scans pasted code for TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX comments, lists them with line numbers, and flags ones that lack an issue reference.
example_prompt: Find all the TODO and FIXME comments in this file and flag the ones with no ticket link
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure regex scan over the pasted buffer, no filesystem or network, runs fully client-side.
rationale: todocheck exists because dangling TODOs rot; surfacing and triaging them inline is a tiny but high-value habit tool.

name: sed-tester
description: Applies a sed-style s/// substitution or address expression to pasted text and shows the result.
example_prompt: Apply sed 's/foo/bar/g' to this text and show me the output
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM implements the substitution via the regex crate; pure text transformation in the wasmi runtime.
rationale: sed expressions are notoriously trial-and-error, and an instant local preview beats running them blindly on real files.

name: cue-sheet-parser
description: Parses a CUE sheet into a structured JSON track list with titles, performers, start times, and ISRC codes.
example_prompt: parse this cue sheet into a clean track listing
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — text parse of the CUE grammar, no I/O.
rationale: Lets people inspect or convert CUE metadata or feed it into other audio tools.

name: sql-migration-linter
description: Lints SQL migration files for irreversible operations, missing down-migrations, and locking statements that block production.
example_prompt: Review this database migration for anything risky to run in production
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: SQL statement parsing plus a bundled risk ruleset, no database connection required.
rationale: A single unguarded ALTER can lock a prod table for minutes; trek-style migration tooling demand confirms the need for pre-flight checks.

name: log-template-extract
description: Clusters raw log lines into templates by masking variable tokens, showing each pattern with its count.
example_prompt: Group these log lines into their underlying patterns and show how often each pattern occurs.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM Drain-style tokenization/clustering; pure computation on the input.
rationale: logu-style template extraction turns noisy logs into a digest and is exactly the kind of sensitive data users want kept local.

name: org-mode-converter
description: Converts between Emacs org-mode TODO trees and markdown checklists, preserving TODO/DONE states and nesting.
example_prompt: Convert this org-mode TODO outline to a markdown checklist
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — two-way text grammar transformation.
rationale: org-mode users frequently need to share tasks as markdown and back, with no good offline converter.

name: task-deduplicator
description: Merges multiple todo.txt lists and removes near-duplicate tasks by normalized text, keeping the richest-tagged version.
example_prompt: Merge these two todo.txt files and drop duplicate tasks
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — normalization and similarity matching over lines, no I/O.
rationale: Syncing task lists across devices/tools produces dupes; cleaning them is a clear local utility.

name: junit-xml-summarizer
description: Parses JUnit/xUnit test-result XML into a pass/fail/skip summary with the failing tests and messages listed.
example_prompt: Summarize this JUnit XML — which tests failed?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML parse over pasted results; all aggregation is local.
rationale: Clustered test runners like maelstrom emit JUnit XML, and a quick local summary beats scrolling raw CI output.

name: markdown-i18n-extract
description: Extracts translatable strings from a Markdown document into a gettext POT template, skipping code and links.
example_prompt: Pull the translatable strings out of this Markdown into a POT file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses Markdown (pulldown-cmark) and serializes message entries client-side.
rationale: This is the core function of mdbook-i18n-helpers and is pure text processing that fits the browser sandbox perfectly.

name: gelf-converter
description: Converts plain or syslog log lines to and from Graylog GELF JSON, normalizing levels and timestamps.
example_prompt: Convert this log line to GELF JSON: 2026-06-24 ERROR db timeout
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — GELF is a JSON schema mapping, pure text transformation flowgger performs.
rationale: Teams piping logs into Graylog need quick GELF shaping without spinning up a forwarder.

name: content-address-file
description: Computes a content-addressed identifier (BLAKE3/SHA-256 multihash) for an uploaded file for dedup and integrity checks.
example_prompt: Give me the content hash of this file for deduplication
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — hashing runs on the in-memory file bytes, mirroring MaidSafe's self-encryption content addressing.
rationale: Content addressing underpins dedup and verification, and doing it client-side keeps the file off any server.

name: podcast-chapter-extractor
description: Extracts embedded chapter markers and titles from a podcast audio file.
example_prompt: List the chapters in this podcast file. [uploads show.m4a]
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — reads chapter metadata atoms from the container locally and emits a structured list.
rationale: Pinepods and podcast clients rely on chapter data for navigation, and pulling it out is a fast, useful utility.

name: bitcoin-address-validator
description: Validates a Bitcoin address and reports its type (P2PKH, P2SH, Bech32/SegWit) and network.
example_prompt: Is bc1qar0srrr7xfkvy5l643lydnw9re59gtzzwf5mdq a valid Bitcoin address?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Base58Check and Bech32 checksum verification run entirely client-side.
rationale: BSV/Electrum wallets demand address validation before sending; catching a malformed address locally prevents lost funds.

name: sql-schema-diff
description: Diffs two SQL CREATE TABLE schemas and outputs the ALTER statements needed to migrate from one to the other.
example_prompt: Diff these two CREATE TABLE definitions and give me the migration ALTERs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — SQL DDL parsing and structural comparison run entirely on parsed ASTs client-side.
rationale: Hand-writing migrations between schema versions is error-prone, and this is squarely the data-transfer/migration demand the corpus signals.

name: image-to-mono-bitmap
description: Converts an image into a 1-bit monochrome bitmap array for OLED/e-paper microcontroller displays.
example_prompt: Turn this logo into a 128x64 monochrome bitmap array for an SSD1306
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes the image, plain Rust→WASM applies thresholding/dithering and packs bits — fully client-side.
rationale: Distinct from RGB565 (1-bit OLED/e-paper), this serves the same embassy/waveshare embedded crowd with their other common display type.

name: nes-chr-to-png
description: Extracts the CHR pattern tables from an NES ROM and renders the full tile sheet as a PNG using a chosen NES palette.
example_prompt: Show me the sprite tiles inside this NES ROM as an image
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — CHR is 2bpp planar tile data decoded with arithmetic; the image crate emits PNG bytes in-browser.
rationale: Visualizing a ROM's graphics is a core NES-romhacking workflow surfaced by pinky/sprocketnes demand.

name: doom-flat-to-png
description: Extracts DOOM textures, flats and sprites from a WAD and renders them as PNGs using the embedded PLAYPAL palette.
example_prompt: Export the textures from this DOOM WAD as images
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Doom's column/post and flat formats decode with the palette LUT; PNG written via the image crate.
rationale: Doom's picture format is unreadable by image viewers, making in-browser extraction genuinely useful for modders.

name: minecraft-nbt-viewer
description: Decodes Minecraft NBT files (level.dat, schematics, player data) into readable JSON.
example_prompt: Read this level.dat and show me the seed and game rules
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — NBT plus gzip decoding is pure Rust (fastnbt-style), no server needed.
rationale: World tooling like arnis and ferium revolves around NBT, and players can't otherwise inspect these binary files.

name: dlt-log-parser
description: Parses AUTOSAR DLT automotive log files into readable ECU, app ID, context, and payload columns.
example_prompt: Parse this DLT log and show me the messages from the ENGINE ECU
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the DLT binary format (as handled by chipmunk) is pure byte parsing that runs entirely in-browser.
rationale: Automotive developers have very few free tools to read DLT logs, making a browser-local parser genuinely valuable.

name: statsd-aggregator
description: Parses pasted StatsD metric lines and aggregates them into counts, gauges, timers, and percentiles.
example_prompt: Aggregate these StatsD lines and show me the p95 for each timer
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — StatsD line parsing and aggregation (à la bioyino) is pure computation runnable client-side.
rationale: Developers debugging metrics pipelines benefit from quickly summarizing raw StatsD streams without standing up a server.

name: trace-critical-path
description: Analyzes an OTLP trace to surface the critical path, slowest spans and self-time per service.
example_prompt: What's the critical path and slowest span in this trace?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: span-tree traversal and timing math are pure CPU work on the parsed trace.
rationale: Finding where latency actually goes is the whole reason people instrument with OpenTelemetry.

name: emv-tlv-decoder
description: Decodes EMV TLV-encoded card data into named tags and human-readable values.
example_prompt: Decode this EMV TLV string into its tags
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: TLV walking plus a static EMV tag dictionary, all in memory.
rationale: Card-present payment debugging in the Hyperswitch space involves reading raw EMV tags.

name: json-to-form-schema
description: Infers an HTML form schema (field types, labels, validation) from a sample JSON object.
example_prompt: Generate a form schema from this JSON record
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — type inference over parsed JSON is pure logic with no runtime dependency.
rationale: Low-code internal-tool builders like illa show demand for going from data shape to an editable form quickly.

name: insecure-c-function-finder
description: Scans pasted C/C++ source for calls to dangerous functions like strcpy, gets, and sprintf.
example_prompt: Find any unsafe C functions in this code <paste C source>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tokenizing and pattern-matching source text runs fully in-browser.
rationale: Directly mirrors rhabdomancer's banned-function locator, giving a fast first-pass vuln triage on any code snippet.

name: shellcode-disassembler
description: Disassembles a hex or byte-array shellcode blob into commented x86/x64 assembly.
example_prompt: Disassemble this shellcode: \x31\xc0\x50\x68...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a pure-Rust x86 decoder (iced-x86/yaxpeax) turns bytes into mnemonics with no external dependency.
rationale: Essential for malware analysis and CTF, and a perfect fit for offline computation on arbitrary byte input.

name: bad-char-finder
description: Detects bad characters in a payload against a supplied badchar set for exploit reliability.
example_prompt: Does this payload contain any of these bad chars 00 0a 0d? <paste bytes>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — byte-set membership testing, purely local.
rationale: A standard exploit-dev/CTF step that is faster and more private as an in-chat client-side utility.

name: username-osint-links
description: Generates candidate profile URLs for a given username across 100+ social, dev, and gaming platforms for OSINT research.
example_prompt: Give me profile links for the username 'kpcyrd' across major sites
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM that fills URL templates from a bundled site list; it only constructs links (no cross-origin fetching, which the browser would block anyway).
rationale: Delivers Sherlock's enumeration value as a link list, sidestepping the CORS wall that prevents in-browser checking while staying fully local.

name: dependency-lister
description: Extracts the imports/requires from a source file, separates standard-library from third-party from local modules, and links third-party ones to their registry page.
example_prompt: List the external dependencies imported in this file: <paste code>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM import parsing plus registry-URL construction (no fetch); fully local.
rationale: Module Linker exists to connect imports to their sources, and listing/classifying a file's dependencies is a useful local analog.

name: code-spell-checker
description: Spell-checks identifiers, comments, and strings in source code and flags likely typos with suggested corrections.
example_prompt: Find and fix the typos in this Rust file: <paste code>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — ships an embedded word list plus a Levenshtein matcher (typos-style) and runs as pure CPU text work with no network or filesystem.
rationale: Catches embarrassing misspellings in code, comments, and docs that compilers never flag, entirely offline.

name: unused-crate-finder
description: Cross-references the dependency table of a pasted Cargo.toml against use/extern-crate references in pasted source to flag dependencies that appear unused.
example_prompt: Which dependencies in this Cargo.toml don't seem to be used in my code?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizing source for crate paths and diffing against parsed manifest; all inputs are pasted text
rationale: cargo-udeps normally needs a nightly compiler, but a heuristic source-vs-manifest scan delivers most of the value offline.

name: rust-backtrace-cleaner
description: Parses a RUST_BACKTRACE dump, demangles frames, strips std/runtime noise, and shows a compact stack of just your crate's frames.
example_prompt: Clean up this Rust panic backtrace and show only my crate's frames
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — regex line parsing plus rustc-demangle, all pure text processing that runs entirely client-side.
rationale: Raw Rust backtraces from panics and debuggers are painful to read, and a local cleaner makes them legible without uploading stack traces anywhere.

name: wasm-size-profile
description: Breaks down a .wasm binary's size by function and section so you can see what is bloating the module.
example_prompt: Why is this wasm file so big — show me the size breakdown
loader_feasibility: twiggy is a pure-Rust size profiler that compiles to WASM and analyzes the bytes locally.
rationale: Code size is the dominant pain point for wasm-pack/wasm-bindgen users and twiggy was built by that same team.

name: cargo-audit-report-parser
description: Parses cargo-audit JSON output and summarizes advisories by severity and affected crate.
example_prompt: summarize this cargo audit output
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: serde_json parses and groups the report locally
rationale: Turns noisy audit output into an actionable triage list, the local part of deps.rs security checks.

name: folded-stack-collapser
description: Converts perf script or DTrace stack output into the folded-stack format flamegraphs require.
example_prompt: collapse this perf script output into folded stacks
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: line-oriented text parsing, local
rationale: Supplies the missing preprocessing step before flamegraph rendering.

name: rust-module-dependency-graph
description: Parses `mod` and `use` statements across pasted Rust files and emits the inter-module coupling as edges plus a Mermaid graph.
example_prompt: Map the module coupling in these Rust files and draw the dependency graph
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM; string parsing of use/mod paths into a graph, fully local.
rationale: Surfaces tight coupling and cycles between modules the way cargo-coupling does, but instantly in chat.

name: rust-panic-risk-linter
description: Scans pasted Rust for panic-prone patterns (`.unwrap()`, `.expect()`, slice indexing, `panic!`, integer arithmetic that can overflow) and lists each with its line.
example_prompt: Find all the panic risks in this Rust code
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM; pattern-based lexical analysis of source, no abstract interpreter or toolchain required.
rationale: Captures the highest-value slice of MIRAI/RAPx-style analysis as a fast browser-local lint.

name: harmony-format-parser
description: Parses Harmony-formatted completion text back into structured role/channel messages.
example_prompt: Parse this harmony-formatted completion into separate analysis and final messages.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a state-machine parser over the Harmony token grammar, fully local.
rationale: Consumers of gpt-oss output need to split analysis vs final channels reliably (openai/harmony).

name: surrealql-playground
description: Runs SurrealQL statements against an in-browser SurrealDB instance with no server.
example_prompt: run these SurrealQL statements and show the result
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM: the surrealdb crate compiles to wasm32 with the in-memory kv-mem engine, so the full query engine runs client-side.
