rationale: Learning and prototyping SurrealQL without spinning up a server is exactly what a browser-local DB enables.

name: csv-geocode
description: Geocode an address column across a whole CSV into latitude/longitude.
example_prompt: Add lat/lng columns by geocoding the 'address' column
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM issuing batched HTTP calls to a keyless geocoder, like the existing geocode tool.
rationale: Bulk geocoding a spreadsheet is far more useful than single-address lookup for mapping data.

name: text-to-calendar
description: Parse a natural-language event description into a downloadable .ics calendar invite.
example_prompt: make a calendar invite: lunch with Sam next Friday 1-2pm at Cafe Roma
loader_feasibility: transformers-js/regex date parsing + plain Rust ICS writer; local.
rationale: Turning 'dinner Thursday 7pm' into an .ics is a delightfully common need that the structured ical-generate tool can't do from prose.

name: device-mockup
description: Place a screenshot inside a realistic device bezel (iPhone, MacBook, browser window).
example_prompt: put this screenshot in an iPhone frame
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM perspective composite onto bundled device frames.
rationale: Marketing/portfolio mockups are a popular product; differs from generic chrome beautify by using true device bezels.

name: scss-compile
description: Compile SCSS/Sass source into plain CSS.
example_prompt: Compile this SCSS with nesting and variables into plain CSS
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM via the grass Sass compiler (Rust-native); fully browser-local.
rationale: A no-toolchain Sass compiler is genuinely useful and feasible with a pure-Rust compiler.

name: face-compare
description: Estimate whether two face photos are the same person via face-embedding similarity.
example_prompt: Do these two photos show the same person?
loader_feasibility: onnx face-recognition embedding model runs in-browser; cosine similarity in Rust. Privacy-friendly (no upload).
rationale: Real verification use case, privacy-preserving precisely because it stays browser-local.

name: json-to-zod
description: Infer a Zod validation schema from a JSON sample.
example_prompt: make a Zod schema from {"id":1,"name":"a","tags":["x"]}
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM type inference, same engine family as json-to-types.
rationale: Zod is the dominant TS validation library and is a different target than the existing json-to-types (TS/Rust/Go/Python).

name: typographic-fix
description: Apply smart typography: straight quotes to curly, -- to en/em dashes, ... to an ellipsis (a 'smartypants' pass).
example_prompt: Fix the typography in this paragraph for publishing
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM string transform; offline.
rationale: Inverse of the existing text-normalize tool and a real publishing/writing need.

name: font-preview
description: Render the same sample text in several Google Fonts side-by-side as a comparison image.
example_prompt: Show 'Hello World' in Inter, Roboto, and Lora
loader_feasibility: Fetches font files via the HTTP host import and rasterizes glyphs in WASM; in-browser.
rationale: Visual font comparison is a frequent design step and produces a shareable image.

name: fuzzy-hash-compare
description: Compares two SSDEEP/CTPH hashes and returns a 0–100 similarity score indicating how alike the original inputs are.
example_prompt: how similar are these two ssdeep hashes?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the SSDEEP comparison is a pure edit-distance computation over the two fingerprint strings, fully offline.
rationale: Generating a fuzzy hash is only useful if you can score similarity, so the compare step completes the CTPH workflow for malware triage and dedup.

name: xxtea-cipher
description: Encrypts or decrypts data with the XXTEA block cipher using a 128-bit key.
example_prompt: Decrypt this XXTEA ciphertext with key 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure integer arithmetic XXTEA implementation, no deps or network.
rationale: XXTEA is widely embedded in games and IoT firmware; covers both encrypt and decrypt demand.

name: flask-session-verify
description: Verifies a Flask session cookie's signature against a supplied secret key and reports validity plus the decoded payload and timestamp.
example_prompt: Is this Flask session cookie validly signed with secret 'dev-key-123'? eyJ1c2VyIjoxfQ.aBcDeF...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: signature verification is HMAC recomputation and constant-time comparison over base64url data, pure Rust with no external calls.
rationale: Confirming a cookie's integrity is a routine debugging and security-check task that benefits from running entirely client-side.

name: sm2-sign
description: Produces an SM2 digital signature (r,s) over a message, computing the ZA user-identity hash with SM3 as the spec requires.
example_prompt: Sign this message with SM2 using my private key and user ID 1234567812345678
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via RustCrypto `sm2`/`sm3`; the per-signature nonce comes from the host secure-random import or RFC6979-style derivation, rest is pure compute in wasmi.
rationale: SM2 signing (not just encryption) is required for ShangMi-compliant auth and document signing, and the ZA pre-hashing trips people up enough to want a turnkey tool.

name: kubeconfig-redactor
description: Redacts cluster server URLs, tokens, and certificate data from a kubeconfig so it can be shared safely.
example_prompt: Redact the secrets from this kubeconfig so I can post it
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses the YAML structure and masks sensitive fields locally, preserving shape.
rationale: k9s users share kubeconfig context when troubleshooting, and structure-aware masking beats hoping a generic redactor catches the right fields.

name: cooklang-recipe-parser
description: Parses CookLang recipe markup into a structured ingredient list, cookware list, timers, and numbered steps.
example_prompt: Parse this CookLang recipe into ingredients and steps: Crack @eggs{3} into a #bowl{} and whisk for ~{2%minutes}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — CookLang is a small deterministic grammar, ideal for a Rust parser.
rationale: Directly implements CookCLI's core value (the CookLang spec) as a browser-local parser with zero install.

name: recipe-scaler
description: Rescales every ingredient quantity in a recipe up or down for a target number of servings.
example_prompt: Scale this 4-serving recipe to 10 servings: 200g flour, 3 eggs, 150ml milk
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — quantity extraction and proportional math run offline.
rationale: Recipe scaling is the most-requested cooking utility and complements the CookCLI-derived parser.

name: task-urgency-ranker
description: Scores and ranks a task list using Taskwarrior-style urgency from priority, due date, age, and tags.
example_prompt: Rank these tasks by Taskwarrior urgency and tell me what to do first
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the urgency coefficients are a fixed formula computed offline.
rationale: Reproduces Taskwarrior's signature 'what's most urgent' algorithm as an instant, install-free ranking.

name: note-tag-indexer
description: Collects #tags and YAML frontmatter tags across a note collection and builds a tag-to-notes index with counts.
example_prompt: Index all the #tags in these notes and show which notes use each
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tag scanning and inverted-index building run offline.
rationale: Tag-based retrieval is the primary navigation model in geeknote/nb-style tools and is missing without their backend.

name: netscape-bookmarks-parser
description: Parses a browser-exported bookmarks HTML file (Netscape format) into structured JSON or a clean Markdown link list with folders.
example_prompt: Convert my exported bookmarks.html into a tidy Markdown list by folder
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — HTML bookmark export is a fixed nested structure parsed entirely offline.
rationale: Buku and nb manage bookmarks; importing the universal browser export format makes the data portable without a CLI.

name: billable-hours-rounder
description: Rounds tracked time entries to a chosen billing increment (e.g. 6 or 15 minutes) and totals the billable time.
example_prompt: Round these entries to 15-minute increments and total them: 0:08, 0:22, 1:03
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — increment rounding and summation are simple offline arithmetic.
rationale: Consultants using Timetrap/utt must bill in fixed increments; precise local rounding avoids spreadsheet errors.

name: transliterate
description: Transliterates text between scripts such as Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, and Han-to-pinyin and the Latin alphabet.
example_prompt: romanize this Russian text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM ICU-style mapping tables and a bundled pinyin dictionary run locally.
rationale: Script romanization is a frequent companion to translation and a deterministic mapping task.

name: fix-shell-command
description: Detects common mistakes in a shell command (typos, missing sudo, wrong flag, swapped args) and returns a corrected version with the reason.
example_prompt: Fix this command: `git pus origin main`
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a rule/edit-distance engine over a known-command table needs no execution and runs locally.
rationale: The Fuck is a hugely popular utility and the correction rules are pure pattern-matching that ports cleanly to a sandboxed tool.

name: csv-frequency-table
description: Produces a value-count / frequency table for one or more columns of a pasted CSV, sorted by count.
example_prompt: Count the distinct values in the `status` column of this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a single hash-map pass over parsed rows runs locally with no server.
rationale: Frequency analysis is VisiData's single most-used operation and is trivially fast in-browser.

name: groq-query
description: Queries a pasted JSON document with a subset of GROQ (filters, projections, ordering) — Sanity's graph-relational query language.
example_prompt: Run GROQ `*[_type == 'post']{title, author}` on this JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a GROQ-subset parser and evaluator over the in-memory document runs entirely client-side.
rationale: GROQ has a devoted Sanity user base with no convenient offline playground, so a browser-local evaluator fills a real gap.

name: multi-format-data-query
description: Selects or updates a value by a unified path selector across JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, or CSV without converting formats first.
example_prompt: Get `.database.host` from this TOML config
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a single selector engine over a serde-normalized in-memory tree runs locally for every format.
rationale: dasel's unique value is one selector syntax for every format, which no single-format jq/yq tool offers.

name: json-gron
description: Flattens JSON into discrete greppable `path = value` assignment lines and reconstructs the original JSON back from them.
example_prompt: gron this JSON so I can grep the nested fields: {"a":{"b":[1,2]}}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with serde_json; pure parsing/string emission, no network or filesystem needed.
rationale: Makes deeply nested JSON line-greppable and diff-able, a constant pain point for anyone inspecting API payloads.

name: rclone-password-reveal
description: Reveals or obscures an rclone config password using rclone's fixed AES-CTR scheme, so you can read or generate obscured secrets.
example_prompt: Decode this rclone obscured password: <token>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — rclone's reveal/obscure uses a known static key and AES-CTR, fully reproducible offline.
rationale: rclone users hit obscured passwords in configs and need to recover or generate them; it's a small, exact, genuinely-requested transform.

name: archive-tree
description: Renders the contents of an uploaded zip or tar archive as a directory tree with per-file sizes and type indicators.
example_prompt: Show me a tree view of the files inside this project.zip
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — zip/tar are parsed from the uploaded bytes entirely in memory, no filesystem or network needed.
rationale: Lets users inspect an archive's structure (the eza/lsd/alder use case) without unzipping it to disk first.

name: ls-long
description: Produces an ls -l style long listing from an uploaded archive — size, modified time, type indicator, and name — sortable by any column.
example_prompt: Give me a long listing of this archive sorted by size
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — reads archive entry metadata from the uploaded bytes.
rationale: Directly serves the ll/lla/pls/eza long-format use case for archives, with sorting the browser can't do natively.

name: scoped-replace
description: Performs search-and-replace limited to language-aware scopes — e.g. only inside comments, only inside string literals, or only within a function body.
example_prompt: Replace the word 'TODO' with 'FIXME' but only inside comments in this file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using tree-sitter to identify scopes then apply regex within them; fully local text processing.
rationale: srgn's surgical scoping prevents the classic 'replaced it inside a string by accident' bug that plain find-replace can't avoid.

name: ascii-line-chart
description: Plots a numeric series as an ASCII/braille line chart.
example_prompt: Plot this series as a line chart: 1 4 9 16 25 36
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM rasterizes the series into a braille grid with pure math, no server.
rationale: Rounds out lowcharts demand with trend visualization for pasted data.

name: nostr-event-verifier
description: Recomputes a Nostr event id and verifies its BIP-340 schnorr signature against the author pubkey.
example_prompt: is this nostr event signature valid? {paste event JSON}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sha256 + secp256k1 schnorr verify compile to WASM with no host services needed.
rationale: Lets people confirm an event is authentic without trusting whatever relay handed it to them.

name: perceptual-image-hash
description: Generates aHash/pHash/dHash fingerprints for an image so you can compare or index it elsewhere.
example_prompt: Give me the perceptual hash of this image
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: grayscale downscale plus DCT/average over decoded pixels is pure local math.
rationale: A reusable primitive behind image dedup demand that's also useful standalone for content indexing.

name: image-sorter
description: Embeds images and clusters them into visually coherent groups (e.g. screenshots, people, landscapes) for organizing.
example_prompt: Sort these photos into groups by what's in them
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime (or transformers-js) runs a CLIP/MobileNet image encoder in-browser, then plain-Rust clustering groups the embeddings — all local.
rationale: Direct realization of the 'image-sorter' demand with no upload of personal photos.

name: file-inventory-generator
description: Produces a manifest CSV of dropped files listing name, size, type, and content hash.
example_prompt: Make an inventory CSV of all these files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: reads file metadata and hashes bytes locally, then emits CSV.
rationale: Direct map of the 'inventory' demand and a natural companion to the duplicate finders.

name: shell-command-safety-linter
description: Scans a command or script for dangerous patterns like `rm -rf /`, `curl | sh`, fork bombs and unquoted variables before you run it.
example_prompt: Is this safe to run: curl example.com/i.sh | bash
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM pattern and structural checks; no execution, no network.
rationale: AI-shell tools generate commands users paste blindly, so a local footgun-catcher is a natural safety layer.

name: nestedtext-convert
description: Converts between NestedText and JSON, YAML, or TOML in either direction.
example_prompt: Convert this NestedText to JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (or pyodide's pure-Python nestedtext) parses and re-emits each format client-side (NestedTextTo).
rationale: NestedText avoids YAML's footguns, and users need lossless conversion to mainstream config formats.

name: kubeconfig-editor
description: Parses a kubeconfig and lets you rename, set the current-context, or strip clusters, emitting the edited YAML.
example_prompt: Set the current-context in this kubeconfig to staging and remove the dev cluster.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: kubeconfig is YAML edited entirely in memory with no API calls.
rationale: Context switching/cleanup is a frequent kubectx chore that is pure config manipulation.

name: eml-to-standalone-html
description: Renders an .eml email into a single self-contained HTML file with inline images for portable viewing or printing.
example_prompt: Make a standalone HTML version of this email I can print
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM inlines MIME-related images as data URIs locally.
rationale: A portable, printable email should need no mail client and no upload.

name: mbox-stats
description: Summarizes an mbox: top senders/recipients, volume over time, busiest hours, and total size.
example_prompt: Give me stats on this mbox archive
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM aggregates message metadata locally.
rationale: Understanding a large archive at a glance is genuinely useful and stays private.

name: mutt-alias-converter
description: Converts between Mutt aliases, abook databases, and vCard contact formats.
example_prompt: Convert my mutt aliases to vCard
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads and writes the three text formats locally.
rationale: Switching email clients means migrating address books between exactly these formats.

name: vim-motion-text-cutter
description: Slices unstructured text into columns or fields using vim-style motions, producing TSV/CSV.
example_prompt: Cut these log lines into columns by word motions
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies motion-based extraction locally — a vicut port.
rationale: Turns messy text into clean tables the way vicut does, but in the browser.

name: download-organizer
description: Takes a messy list of filenames and proposes a tidy folder structure plus a rename/move plan grouped by type, date, or project.
example_prompt: Organize this list of files from my Downloads folder into sensible folders
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — extension/date pattern classification over a list of strings, fully local
rationale: Everyone's Downloads folder is chaos and a deterministic sort plan is a quick, high-value win.

name: flatten-paths
description: Converts a list of nested paths into flat filenames by joining directory segments, for flattening a tree into one folder.
example_prompt: Flatten 'a/b/c.txt' style paths into 'a_b_c.txt' filenames
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM path-string manipulation; no I/O
rationale: Flattening a directory tree into unique names is a recurring file-manager chore that is pure string work.

name: hash-rename
description: Computes a content hash (SHA-256/MD5) of dropped files and proposes hash-based filenames while flagging duplicate content.
example_prompt: Rename these files to their SHA-256 hash and tell me which are duplicates
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM hashing over dropped file bytes; no network
rationale: Content-hash renaming and dedup is a common archival/file-manager task that is pure local computation.

name: filename-metadata-extractor
description: Extracts structured fields (dates, sequence numbers, tags, resolution) from a list of filenames into a clean table.
example_prompt: Pull the dates and tags out of these photo filenames into a table.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: regex extraction over pasted filenames producing a table, entirely client-side.
rationale: TMSU/wutag/VisioNomicon tagging demand maps to turning messy filenames into organized, queryable metadata without any database.

name: sudoku
description: Generates uniquely-solvable Sudoku puzzles at chosen difficulty and lets you play with pencil marks and validation.
example_prompt: give me a hard sudoku puzzle to solve
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — backtracking generator with uniqueness check plus grid UI, all client-side
rationale: Maps the 'nudoku' demand into a polished playable puzzle that works fully offline.

name: snake
description: The arrow-key Snake game with growing tail, wraparound option, and high-score tracking.
example_prompt: let me play snake
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — simple game loop and grid rendering on canvas, no server
rationale: Covers two harvested terms (Micro Snake, nSnake) with one of the most recognizable casual games.

name: commit-absorb-suggester
description: Suggests which recent commit each hunk of a diff should be squashed into, based on the files and lines each commit last touched.
example_prompt: Which of my recent commits should each part of this diff be absorbed into?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM matches diff hunks against a pasted `git log -p` / blame locally.
rationale: git-absorb automates fixup commits and the matching heuristic runs fine on pasted history.

name: git-log-sql
description: Loads a pasted formatted `git log` into an in-memory SQLite table so you can query commit history with SQL.
example_prompt: From this git log, SQL-query the top 5 authors by commit count: <pasted log>
loader_feasibility: pyodide ships sqlite3; it parses the log into rows and runs your SQL fully in the browser sandbox.
rationale: Ad-hoc analytics over commit history (top authors, busiest files) is far easier in SQL than shell pipelines.

name: image-emboss
description: Applies a bevel/emboss effect to an image, producing a raised metallic or carved-stone look with adjustable depth and light angle.
example_prompt: Give this logo a beveled embossed look
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies a directional convolution kernel over the decoded pixels client-side.
rationale: Bevel demand maps to a quick, popular image effect that's otherwise buried in heavyweight editors.

name: cloze-generator
description: Turns a passage into fill-in-the-blank cloze exercises by blanking out key vocabulary for study and language learning.
example_prompt: Make cloze flashcards from this paragraph for French study
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using stopword/frequency heuristics to pick blanks; entirely local text processing
rationale: directly serves the minicloze language-learning demand and feeds spaced-repetition study workflows.

name: xoauth2-builder
description: Builds and decodes the SASL XOAUTH2 base64 string from a username and OAuth2 access token for IMAP/SMTP authentication.
example_prompt: build the XOAUTH2 SASL string for user@example.com with this access token
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — string assembly and base64 encode/decode, runs client-side.
rationale: Directly maps oama's purpose (OAuth2 for mail) — a fiddly encoding people otherwise hand-craft.

name: recovery-codes
description: Generate a set of one-time backup/recovery codes (configurable count, length, and grouping) for 2FA fallback.
example_prompt: generate 10 backup recovery codes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using the browser CSPRNG; pure local randomness with no server involvement.
rationale: Backup codes complement the existing TOTP/HOTP tooling and must be generated locally so they are never exposed to a third party.

name: audio-echo
description: Add a tunable echo/delay effect (delay time, decay, repeats) to an audio file.
example_prompt: Add a slap-back echo to this guitar take
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — aecho filter computes the delay taps locally.
rationale: Echo/delay is a fundamental creative audio effect with broad appeal.

name: outline-generate
description: Produce a structured hierarchical outline from a long document or a topic.
example_prompt: Make an outline from this 2000-word essay
loader_feasibility: transformers-js summarization/text-gen model client-side; browser-local inference.
rationale: Useful for studying, repurposing content, and planning, and works on local text without upload.

name: image-color-isolate
description: Keep a chosen color and desaturate everything else (color-splash / selective color).
example_prompt: Keep only the red in this photo and make the rest black and white
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM HSV masking per pixel; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: The selective-color/color-splash effect is a recognizable, frequently-requested edit.

name: image-tilt-shift
description: Apply a tilt-shift miniature-faking blur gradient with adjustable focus band.
example_prompt: Apply a tilt-shift effect to this cityscape so it looks like a miniature
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute or plain Rust graduated blur; browser-local.
rationale: Tilt-shift is a distinctive, popular photo effect not covered by portrait-blur.

name: decision-matrix
description: Score options against weighted criteria and rank them (weighted decision matrix).
example_prompt: decision matrix: options A,B,C scored on cost(0.5), speed(0.3), risk(0.2)
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM scoring + table render.
rationale: A widely-used decision-making aid with no equivalent in the data tools.

name: voice-emotion
description: Classify the emotion conveyed in a speech clip (happy, angry, sad, neutral…) with confidence scores.
example_prompt: what emotion is in this voice recording?
loader_feasibility: onnx/transformers audio classification model in-browser.
rationale: Speech-emotion analysis serves call-center and UX research; existing emotion tools cover only text and faces.

name: rison-to-json
description: Decodes a Rison string from a URL into readable JSON.
example_prompt: decode this Rison: (a:1,b:!t,c:!(x,y))
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure recursive-descent parse of the Rison grammar, fully offline
rationale: Reverse-engineering shared Kibana/OpenSearch dashboard URLs requires reading their Rison-encoded state.

name: gost-signature
description: Generates GOST R 34.10-2012 keypairs and signs or verifies messages over GOST elliptic curves.
example_prompt: Sign this message with my GOST private key, then verify the signature
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using elliptic-curve/bigint crates for GOST R 34.10-2012 — keygen, sign and verify are pure CPU math with no network calls.
rationale: Covers both the GOST Sign and GOST Verify demand in one tool, with no existing offline browser option.

name: strip-http-headers
description: Removes the header block from a raw HTTP message and returns just the body.
example_prompt: Strip the headers from this HTTP response and show only the body
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust split-on-CRLFCRLF logic in WASM; deterministic and local.
rationale: Isolating an HTTP body is a quick, frequently needed cleanup step.

name: line-pad
description: Pads every line to a fixed width using a chosen character, aligning left or right.
example_prompt: pad each of these lines to 20 characters on the right with dots
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; per-line string padding with zero dependencies.
rationale: Column alignment for logs, tables, and fixed-width formats is a common formatting chore.

name: key-detect
description: Estimate the musical key/scale of a song from its chroma profile.
example_prompt: what key is this track in?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: FFT chroma extraction + key-template matching, no network.
rationale: Pairs with bpm-detect for the musician/DJ audience using browser-local DSP.

name: headline-generate
description: Generate several catchy title/headline options for an article, blog post, or topic.
example_prompt: Give me 5 headline options for an article about browser-based AI tools
loader_feasibility: transformers-js small text-generation model in-browser; runs fully local with no API.
rationale: Title/headline generators are among the most-used standalone copywriting utilities.

name: playlist-converter
description: Parses and converts internet-radio and music playlists between M3U/M3U8, PLS, and JSON.
example_prompt: Convert this M3U radio playlist into a PLS file
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM text parser; pure format conversion with no streaming.
rationale: Internet Radio / Jango / Radio Garden listeners shuffle station playlists between players that demand different formats.

name: json-to-rison
description: Encodes JSON into compact URL-safe Rison, the format used in Kibana/OpenSearch query state.
example_prompt: encode this JSON as Rison for a Kibana URL
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure string serialization following the Rison grammar, no network
rationale: Kibana/OpenSearch users hand-build Rison query state and a local encoder removes the guesswork.

name: polodb-playground
description: Runs MongoDB-style queries against an in-browser PoloDB document store loaded with your sample JSON.
example_prompt: load these documents into PoloDB and run find({active:true})
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM: PoloDB is a pure-Rust embedded database whose in-memory backend compiles to wasm32 and runs fully client-side.
rationale: Prototyping document queries with real Mongo-like semantics and zero server is a strong browser-local fit.

name: spf-dkim-dmarc-record-builder
description: Generates and validates SPF, DKIM, and DMARC DNS TXT records from guided inputs for email authentication setup.
example_prompt: build SPF and DMARC records for my domain that allows Google and SendGrid
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM assembling and lint-checking record strings; record generation is pure text, no DNS query needed.
rationale: Email-auth DNS records are error-prone to hand-write and underpin the whole transactional-email cluster.

name: json-to-ron
description: Converts JSON into Rusty Object Notation (RON), the format used by Bevy and many Rust tools.
example_prompt: Convert this JSON into RON.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (serde_json + ron) emits RON locally.
rationale: Bevy/Rust game and app developers regularly author RON assets from JSON data.

name: matchmaking-team-balancer
description: Splits a list of rated players into the most evenly-matched teams by minimizing the rating gap between sides.
example_prompt: Split these 10 players with these Elo ratings into two balanced 5v5 teams.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — partitioning by rating is a bounded combinatorial search that fits easily in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: Anyone organizing scrims or pickup games needs fair teams and currently does it by eyeball, so an instant balancer is broadly wanted.

name: pixel-art-upscaler
description: Scales pixel art up by integer factors using nearest-neighbor sampling so edges stay crisp with no blurring.
example_prompt: Upscale this 32x32 sprite 8x with no smoothing.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — nearest-neighbor scaling is a single ffmpeg scale flag applied to the local image.
rationale: Default image resizers blur pixel art; a guaranteed nearest-neighbor upscaler is a constant need for retro game and icon work.

name: morphology-ops
description: Applies morphological operations (erode, dilate, open, close) to a binary or grayscale image.
example_prompt: Dilate the white regions in this binary mask.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — imageproc provides morphology kernels that run locally over image-rs buffers.
rationale: Morphology is essential for cleaning up masks in CV pipelines and is trivially browser-local.

name: feature-keypoint-detector
description: Detects scale-invariant feature keypoints (AKAZE/ORB-style) in an image and returns descriptors and positions.
example_prompt: Extract feature keypoints from this image.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the rust-cv (cv/akaze) crates are pure Rust and compile to WASM.
rationale: Feature detection is the foundation of image matching and stitching, and a local version lets users experiment without OpenCV.

name: asm-diff
description: Diffs two assembly or object-file functions and highlights matching and differing instructions, decompilation-project style.
example_prompt: Diff these two assembly functions and show what changed (both pasted below)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — objdiff's diff core already targets WASM and operates purely on the inputs you provide.
rationale: Decompilation and matching-decomp communities rely on exactly this kind of side-by-side asm comparison.

name: column-align
description: Aligns tab- or space-separated rows into evenly-spaced columns using elastic tabstops.
example_prompt:
Align these into clean columns:
name	age
Ada	36
Bob	5
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: tabwriter is pure Rust and formats text buffers in-memory with no I/O.
rationale: Turning ragged TSV or log output into aligned tables is a common terminal and documentation need.

name: rust-idiom-lint
description: A clippy-style idiom linter that flags non-idiomatic Rust (redundant matches that could be if-let, manual map loops, unnecessary unwrap, verbose conversions) and proposes the idiomatic form.
example_prompt: Make this Rust code more idiomatic and tell me what you changed.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: syn AST analysis with a rule set, runs client-side without clippy/rustc.
rationale: Captures 'Refactoring to Rust' and 'Rust Guidelines' demand for nudging code toward idiomatic style offline.

name: markdown-form-builder
description: Generates an HTML form or JSON schema from a concise field specification.
example_prompt: Build a contact form with name, email, and a message textarea
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — emits HTML/JSON strings locally, no backend
rationale: bashform shows demand for spinning up forms fast without standing up a server.

name: doc-to-slide-outline
description: Condenses a long document into a structured slide outline of titles and bullet points.
example_prompt: Turn this report into a 10-slide outline with titles and bullets
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — runs a summarization model entirely in-browser to compress each section into bullets.
rationale: The hardest part of making slides is deciding structure, and local summarization does it without sending content out.

name: remind-to-ics
description: Converts a remind-format calendar file (as used by Wyrd and remind) into a standard .ics calendar.
example_prompt: Convert my remind file into an .ics calendar
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM remind-syntax parser plus iCal emitter, no network
rationale: Migrate off the niche remind format into mainstream calendar apps.

name: outdated-upgrade-planner
description: Takes pasted `npm outdated` / `pip list --outdated` / `cargo outdated` output and groups upgrades by risk (patch vs minor vs major semver jump).
example_prompt: Prioritize these upgrades by how risky they are [pastes npm outdated table]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the outdated report and classifies semver deltas locally.
rationale: topgrade upgrades everything blindly; the missing piece is triaging which bumps are safe, which is pure local semver math.

name: bitwarden-export-viewer
description: Parses an unencrypted Bitwarden JSON export and renders a clean, searchable view of items, folders, and custom fields.
example_prompt: Show me a readable view of my Bitwarden export [pastes JSON]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — JSON parsing/rendering with no network, keeping the export local.
rationale: Browsing a Bitwarden export is awkward as raw JSON and is exactly the kind of sensitive file that must stay client-side.

name: wgsl-compute-run
description: Run a user-supplied WGSL compute shader over an input buffer and return the output buffer, for quickly testing GPU kernels.
example_prompt: run this wgsl compute shader over these 1024 floats
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute loader compiles and dispatches the WGSL on the local GPU and reads the result buffer back; all execution is on-device.
rationale: Gives GPU/shader developers a zero-setup scratchpad to validate compute kernels locally, leaning fully into the webgpu-compute capability the GPU demand cluster implies.

name: flamegraph-diff
description: Compares two folded-stack profiles (before/after) and renders a differential flamegraph highlighting regressions and improvements.
example_prompt: Diff these two profile stacks and show me what got slower
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — computes per-frame deltas between two pasted profiles and emits a colored SVG, fully client-side.
rationale: Differential flamegraphs are the most actionable profiling artifact for confirming a fix, and they are pure data-to-SVG work that runs locally.

name: lighthouse-report-analyzer
description: Parses an uploaded Lighthouse JSON report into a Core Web Vitals summary, score breakdown, and ranked optimization opportunities.
example_prompt: Upload my lighthouse.json and tell me the top three things slowing my page
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the report JSON and ranks audits, no network access.
rationale: Lighthouse JSON is verbose and the actionable opportunities are buried, so a focused summary of page vitals is genuinely useful.

name: heightmap-hillshade
description: Produces a hillshade/relief-shaded image from a grayscale elevation map with adjustable sun azimuth and angle.
example_prompt: Generate a hillshade from this DEM with the sun coming from the northwest
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes per-pixel illumination and emits a PNG; no GIS server needed.
rationale: A second DEM use case that turns raw elevation rasters into readable terrain imagery offline.

name: bibtex-to-citation
description: Renders BibTeX entries as formatted reference-list citations in APA, MLA, Chicago, or IEEE style.
example_prompt: Turn these BibTeX entries into an APA reference list.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applying bundled style rules to the parsed entries — deterministic formatting, no network.
rationale: Researchers need ready-to-paste citations in a target style, and the major styles are rule-driven enough to run locally.

name: bibliography-deduplicate
description: Deduplicates a reference list by DOI and fuzzy title/author match, a core systematic-review step.
example_prompt: Remove duplicate references from this BibTeX list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: normalize DOIs/titles and Levenshtein-match — pure computation on the pasted list.
rationale: Deduping merged search exports is the first chore of any systematic literature review (slr-kit demand).

name: paper-backup
description: Encrypts text with a passphrase and renders a printable page with a QR code and armored ciphertext for paper cold storage.
example_prompt: Make a paper backup of my seed phrase with this passphrase
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (age + qrcode + a pure-Rust PDF writer); all encryption and rendering happen in-tab with no server.
rationale: PaperAge-style offline backups are only trustworthy if the secret is encrypted locally before it ever hits paper.

name: powershell-decoder
description: Decodes a PowerShell -EncodedCommand base64/UTF-16LE payload back into readable script for analysis.
example_prompt: Decode this PowerShell encoded command: cABvAHcAZQByAHMAaABlAGwAbAA...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM base64-decodes then UTF-16LE-decodes the payload; pure encoding work, ideal for browser-local malware triage.
rationale: encoded PowerShell is a top malware/incident-response artifact, and decoding it locally avoids feeding live threats to web services.

name: ssh-reachability-mapper
description: Builds a lateral-movement graph from pasted known_hosts, authorized_keys, and SSH config files to reveal who can reach whom.
example_prompt: From these known_hosts and authorized_keys files, map which hosts can SSH into which
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the artifacts, builds an adjacency graph, and emits Mermaid/DOT text; all in-memory, no scanning.
rationale: this turns SSH-Snake's offensive idea into a defensive self-audit you can run on sensitive key material entirely client-side.

name: sound-event-tagger
description: Identifies non-speech sounds and events in a recording (e.g. applause, music, dog bark).
example_prompt: What sounds are in this recording?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a YAMNet-style audio event model on the decoded waveform in WASM.
rationale: Tagging ambient sounds is useful for editing and indexing field recordings and runs entirely client-side.

name: cue-sheet-editor
description: Creates, validates, and edits .cue sheets (track titles, performers, indices) for an album file.
example_prompt: Build a cue sheet for this album with these track times and titles
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM generates and validates the cue text format in memory.
rationale: Cue sheets are core to lossless album archiving and editing them is a simple local text operation.

name: claude-usage-analyzer
description: Parses Claude Code / ccusage JSONL logs into token totals, cost, per-day burn rate, and per-session breakdown.
example_prompt: Analyze my Claude Code usage JSONL and show daily cost and token burn
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — JSONL parsing plus pricing math; logs stay on the user's machine.
rationale: Cloud Code Usage Monitor demand is directly on-brand for gizza; analyzing local usage logs answers 'how much am I spending' without uploading them.

name: terminal-theme-from-image
description: Extracts a cohesive 16-color ANSI terminal palette from an uploaded wallpaper or screenshot and emits it as a ready-to-use terminal theme.
example_prompt: Make me a kitty color theme based on this wallpaper
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the `image` crate decodes the PNG/JPEG and k-means/median-cut quantization runs in-browser, so the photo never leaves the device.
rationale: Matching a terminal palette to a desktop wallpaper is a hugely popular ricing workflow that today requires Python scripts like pywal.

name: systemd-unit-linter
description: Parses a pasted systemd unit file and flags syntax errors, deprecated directives, and security/hardening improvements.
example_prompt: Review this systemd service file and tell me what's wrong or unsafe
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: unit-file parsing plus a bundled directive/best-practice ruleset, no network needed.
rationale: Misconfigured units fail silently at boot and most users never run systemd-analyze to catch hardening gaps.

name: firewall-rule-explainer
description: Parses iptables, nftables, or ufw rules and explains in plain English exactly what traffic each rule permits or blocks.
example_prompt: Explain what this iptables ruleset actually does
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: rule-syntax parsing and human-readable summarization run entirely client-side.
rationale: Inherited firewall rulesets are notoriously opaque and one wrong reading causes outages or exposure.

name: paragraph-grep
description: Searches text by record and returns whole matching paragraphs or blank-line-separated blocks instead of single lines.
example_prompt: Show me every paragraph in this doc that mentions 'rollback'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM splitting on record separators then regex-matching each block locally
rationale: Reproduces paragrep's block-oriented search, which is far more useful than line grep for prose and config stanzas.

name: standup-notes-formatter
description: Formats a task list into standup notes split into Done, Doing, and Blockers sections.
example_prompt: Turn my task list into standup notes for tomorrow
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — grouping by status flags and templated text output.
rationale: Daily standup prep is a recurring chore that maps cleanly onto any tracked task list.

name: taskpaper-converter
description: Parses TaskPaper-format projects, tasks, and tags and converts to or from markdown and JSON.
example_prompt: Convert this TaskPaper file to JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — TaskPaper indentation/tag grammar parsing into a data model.
rationale: TaskPaper is a popular plain-text task format (close to Taskline) that lacks lightweight converters.

name: taskwarrior-export-converter
description: Converts a taskwarrior 'task export' JSON dump into markdown, CSV, or todo.txt.
example_prompt: Turn this taskwarrior export JSON into a markdown task list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — JSON parsing and reformatting, fully offline.
rationale: taskwarrior and taskwarrior-tui users want to share or migrate their data without scripting an exporter.

name: accomplishments-summary
description: Turns a completed-task log into a grouped weekly-review or brag-doc summary with counts by project and date.
example_prompt: Summarize what I finished this week from this done-task log
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — grouping, counting, and templated formatting over dated done entries.
rationale: Reviewing what got done (the Redo/done-log use case) supports retros and performance reviews that task tools ignore.

name: todotxt-to-markdown
description: Renders a todo.txt list as a grouped GitHub-flavored markdown checklist (sectioned by project or context).
example_prompt: Turn this todo.txt into a markdown checklist grouped by project
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — text transformation only.
rationale: Lets people move tasks from CLI tools into README/issue checklists, a common export request.

name: todotxt-archive-splitter
description: Splits completed tasks out of a todo.txt into a done.txt archive, preserving the standard archive workflow.
example_prompt: Move all done tasks in this todo.txt into a separate done.txt
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — line partitioning, fully local.
rationale: The canonical todo.txt 'archive' command, reproduced offline for users without the CLI installed.

name: strategy-backtester
description: Backtests a simple rule (e.g. moving-average crossover) over OHLCV data and reports returns, max drawdown, win rate and an equity curve.
example_prompt: Backtest a 50/200 MA crossover on this price CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — simulating trades over the series and tallying P&L is pure compute.
rationale: Backtesting is the explicit purpose of nautilus_trader; a zero-setup browser version is broadly useful.

name: matrix-decomposition
description: Factors a matrix via LU, QR, Cholesky, or SVD and returns the component matrices.
example_prompt: Give me the QR decomposition of this matrix
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: faer-rs provides all four decompositions (LAPACK-equivalent routines) compiled to WASM and run client-side.
rationale: Decompositions are the backbone of numerical linear algebra and are tedious to do by hand.

name: bond-pricer
description: Prices a fixed-coupon bond and computes yield-to-maturity, duration, and convexity.
example_prompt: Price a bond: 5% annual coupon, face 1000, 7 years, market yield 4.2% — and give YTM and duration
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; discounted-cashflow math plus a YTM solver on entered terms, offline.
rationale: Bond valuation and yield metrics are core fixed-income tasks that fit entirely in a client-side calculator.

name: particle-simulator
description: Simulates an N-body / particle system on the GPU and renders animation frames from initial conditions.
example_prompt: Simulate 50,000 gravitating particles for 200 steps and animate it
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute loader; compute shaders integrate particle state each step on-device and render frames.
rationale: Large particle/ECS-style simulations are exactly what WebGPU compute unlocks locally and what the game-dev terms ask for.

name: translate-comments
description: Translates code comments or documentation between languages.
example_prompt: Translate the comments in this snippet to Spanish: <paste>
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — runs a client-side MT model (e.g. opus-mt/NLLB) in WASM.
rationale: Makes Rust learning resources accessible across languages, fully offline.

name: likert-scale-encoder
description: Maps Likert text answers (Strongly disagree through Strongly agree, etc.) in a survey CSV to consistent numeric scores so columns can be averaged or charted.
example_prompt: Convert the agree/disagree answers in this survey CSV to a 1-5 scale
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies a configurable text→number mapping across parsed columns; deterministic and local.
rationale: Likert questions are the staple of Wufoo/Google Forms/Zoho surveys but export as text, blocking any quantitative analysis until encoded.

name: email-css-inliner
description: Inlines a stylesheet into HTML email so styles render in clients that strip <style> blocks.
example_prompt: Inline the CSS in this HTML email
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML/CSS parsing and inlining — runs locally.
rationale: CSS inlining is a mandatory, fiddly step for every hand-built campaign.

name: email-preheader-generator
description: Generates concise preheader/preview text that summarizes an email's content.
example_prompt: Write preview text for this newsletter
loader_feasibility: transformers-js summarization (distilbart) — model runs on-device via WASM/WebGPU.
rationale: Preheaders strongly affect open rates but are usually an afterthought.

name: crypto-payment-uri
description: Builds a BIP21/EIP-681 payment URI and matching QR code for receiving BTC, ETH or token payments to an address and amount.
example_prompt: make a payment QR for 0.005 BTC to bc1q... with a label 'Invoice 42'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — URI string assembly plus a local QR encoder, the receive-payment half of MoneyButton, no network.
rationale: Generating a correct payment-request URI and QR is error-prone by hand and entirely offline-computable.

name: jsonstat-to-csv
description: Unrolls a JSON-stat dataset's dimensions into a tidy CSV or Markdown table.
example_prompt: Turn this JSON-stat dataset into a CSV table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — decodes the JSON-stat dimension/value arrays and emits rows, no network.
rationale: Official statistics agencies publish JSON-stat, and its packed dimension encoding is unreadable until unrolled into a table.

name: jsonnet-eval
description: Evaluates a Jsonnet template with variables and imports into final JSON output.
example_prompt: Evaluate this Jsonnet and give me the resulting JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the jrsonnet pure-Rust interpreter; self-contained, no network.
rationale: 'Jsonnet' is widely used for config templating (k8s, Grafana); a browser-local evaluator removes the CLI-install barrier.

name: json-denormalize
description: Rebuilds nested JSON from normalized entity tables and a root reference.
example_prompt: Denormalize these entity tables back into nested JSON starting from post 1.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM resolves id references back into a tree, fully local.
rationale: The inverse of normalize, needed to reconstruct API-shaped payloads from a normalized store.

name: json-schema-examples
description: Produces annotated valid and deliberately-invalid example documents that demonstrate each constraint in a JSON Schema.
example_prompt: Show me example documents that pass and fail this JSON Schema
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — derives boundary cases from the schema constraints, no external data
rationale: Turns the Understanding JSON Schema learning intent into hands-on examples, distinct from bulk fake data.

name: json-schema-draft-upgrade
description: Migrates a JSON Schema between drafts (e.g. draft-04 to 2020-12), rewriting renamed and restructured keywords.
example_prompt: Upgrade this draft-04 schema to JSON Schema 2020-12
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — keyword rewriting over the parsed schema, offline
rationale: Cross-draft differences are a recurring pain point in the JSON Schema docs ecosystem with no easy converter.

name: kangarootwelve-hash
description: Hashes large inputs with KangarooTwelve/TurboSHAKE for very fast Keccak-family integrity digests.
example_prompt: compute the KangarooTwelve hash of this file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the `k12` crate; CPU-only streaming hash with no I/O, ideal for wasmi.
rationale: K12 is XKCP's flagship high-speed hash for big payloads and is otherwise unavailable in the browser.

name: cart-totals
description: Computes subtotal, line discounts, coupon, tax and shipping into a fully itemized cart grand total.
example_prompt: compute the cart total: 3 items at $19.99, 10% off, 8.25% tax, $5 flat shipping
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — money-safe decimal arithmetic over line items, the cart math Snipcart/Foxy run, no server.
rationale: Order-total math with discounts and tax is fiddly and rounding-sensitive, so a precise tool prevents off-by-a-cent bugs.

name: chat-sentiment-analyzer
description: Scores the sentiment and tone of each message in a conversation and flags the most negative or heated exchanges.
example_prompt: analyze the tone of this chat — where did it get tense?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — text-classification model runs client-side over pasted messages.
rationale: Tone analysis helps with moderation and self-review, and keeping it local respects the sensitivity of chat content.

name: markdown-stats
description: Reports word count, reading time, heading structure, and code/link counts for a Markdown document.
example_prompt: How long will this markdown article take to read?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenization and counting; pure local computation
rationale: reading-time and structure metrics are a common blogging/writing need that fits the markdown demand cluster.

name: process-tree-visualizer
description: Builds an indented or SVG process tree from pasted `ps -ef` or pstree output with CPU and memory rolled up per subtree.
example_prompt: Turn this ps -ef output into a process tree and show me the heaviest subtree
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — reconstructs the PID/PPID hierarchy and renders text/SVG, no OS access.
rationale: pshunt/PCtrl users need to see process lineage and resource rollups, which is a clean tree-building transform on pasted data.

name: fuzzing-wordlist
description: Generates a content-discovery wordlist with common paths, extensions, case/permutation variants for web fuzzing.
example_prompt: Generate a directory fuzzing wordlist with php and bak extensions
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM expanding seed words and rules into a list; pure local text generation.
rationale: feroxbuster's effectiveness depends on good wordlists, and generating one is a self-contained local task.

name: danish-lemmatizer
description: Reduces Danish words to their dictionary base form (lemma).
example_prompt: Give the lemmas for the words in this Danish sentence
loader_feasibility: transformers.js: a Danish lemmatization ONNX model (DaNLP-style) runs client-side
rationale: Lemmatization is essential for Danish search, frequency counts, and study, and isn't available in-browser.

name: dutch-pos-lemmatizer
description: Tags Dutch words with parts of speech and reduces them to lemmas.
example_prompt: Give me POS tags and lemmas for this Dutch sentence
loader_feasibility: transformers.js: Dutch POS + lemmatization ONNX models run client-side
rationale: Replicates Frog's core Dutch POS/lemma functionality locally for search and grammar tooling.

name: urdu-text-normalizer
description: Normalizes Urdu text: unifies Arabic/Urdu character variants, fixes diacritics and spacing, and standardizes digits.
example_prompt: Normalize this Urdu text and standardize the characters
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Unicode normalization and character-mapping rules for the Perso-Arabic Urdu script, fully offline.
rationale: Urdu corpora are notoriously noisy in encoding, so normalization is the essential first step for any Urdu dataset work.

name: urdu-word-segmenter
description: Inserts correct word boundaries into Urdu text where spaces are missing or wrongly placed.
example_prompt: Add proper word boundaries to this run-together Urdu text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — dictionary plus statistical/ZWNJ heuristics over the bundled Urdu lexicon, in memory.
rationale: Urdu's inconsistent space usage breaks tokenization, and reliable segmentation is a prerequisite for all Urdu NLP.

name: onset-detector
description: Finds note and percussion onset times in an audio clip and returns timestamps.
example_prompt: List the onset times in this drum loop
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM spectral-flux onset detection runs fully in the browser.
rationale: Onset times are the basis for slicing samples, transcription, and rhythmic analysis.

name: chorus-finder
description: Finds the single most repeated, catchiest section of a song (the chorus/hook) and returns its time range for use as a preview clip.
example_prompt: Find the chorus of this song so I can make a 15-second preview.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — repetition analysis on the chroma self-similarity matrix (the Catchy/thumbnailing idea) is pure DSP over decoded audio.
rationale: Auto-generating the catchy preview snippet is exactly what social/teaser workflows need and is otherwise manual scrubbing.

name: bloom-glow
description: Adds a cinematic bloom/glow around bright areas of an image.
example_prompt: Add a soft glow to the bright parts of this image.
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute thresholds, blurs, and composites highlights in shader passes on the GPU locally.
rationale: Bloom is a signature real-time-rendering post effect and gives photos and renders an instant polished look.

name: image-displace-warp
description: Warps an image using a displacement map to create distortion and glitch effects.
example_prompt: Warp this image using this displacement map.
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute resamples the source image per-pixel by the displacement texture in a shader, locally.
rationale: Displacement warping is a flexible WebGL-style effect used for glitch art, liquify, and motion fakery.

name: glsl-to-wgsl
description: Transpiles a GLSL vertex or fragment shader into WebGPU's WGSL shading language.
example_prompt: Convert this GLSL fragment shader to WGSL so I can use it in WebGPU
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using the naga crate (pure-Rust GLSL frontend + WGSL backend), so the whole cross-compile runs in the wasmi sandbox with no server.
rationale: Porting the huge body of existing GLSL/WebGL shaders to WebGPU is the #1 friction point in the 'next-gen 3D graphics on the web' migration.

name: webgpu-capability-report
description: Queries the current device's WebGPU adapter and reports its features, limits, and vendor/architecture info.
example_prompt: Show me what my GPU supports in WebGPU
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute loader exposes the WebGPU adapter, so the tool reads real device features/limits client-side.
rationale: WebGL Report/support-stats sites are heavily used for capability detection, and the WebGPU equivalent is now the relevant target.

name: shader-uniform-extractor
description: Extracts a shader's uniforms, attributes, and varyings with their types as a JSON binding interface.
example_prompt: List all the uniforms and attributes in this shader
loader_feasibility: naga reflection / plain Rust parser in WASM; CPU-only
rationale: Generates the JS binding contract devs otherwise hand-write when wiring shaders to buffers.

name: webgl1-to-webgl2-shader
description: Upgrades GLSL ES 1.00 shaders to 3.00 (attribute/varying→in/out, gl_FragColor→out, texture2D→texture).
example_prompt: Port this WebGL 1 shader to WebGL 2
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM source rewriter; pure text transform
rationale: Directly serves the heavy WebGL-2 migration interest in the demand set.

name: obj-compute-normals
description: Generates smooth or flat per-vertex normals for an OBJ mesh that lacks them.
example_prompt: This OBJ has no normals — generate smooth normals and give me the updated file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM geometry math over the parsed mesh; pure CPU.
rationale: Many downloaded meshes ship without normals and render black under lighting, a common WebGL frustration.

name: panorama-perspective-view
description: Renders a flat rectilinear view from an equirectangular panorama at a given yaw/pitch/field-of-view.
example_prompt: From this 360 image, render the view looking at yaw 90, pitch 10, 75° fov
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg v360 (input e, output flat with yaw/pitch/h_fov) runs locally in ffmpeg.wasm.
rationale: Extracting a normal photo from a panorama is a common need for the WebXR/360-content audience.

name: point-cloud-downsampler
description: Voxel-grid downsamples a PLY or XYZ point cloud to a target density, reporting before/after counts.
example_prompt: Downsample this XYZ point cloud with a 5cm voxel grid
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: voxel-hash downsample, pure math.
rationale: Massive point clouds choke WebGL viewers (xeokit/Deck.gl point layers), so local thinning is a real performance win.

name: heightmap-to-mesh
description: Converts a grayscale heightmap image into a 3D terrain mesh (OBJ/glTF) with adjustable height scale and resolution.
example_prompt: Turn this grayscale heightmap into a terrain OBJ with 50x height
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: decode grayscale image + grid triangulation, local.
rationale: Heightmap-to-terrain is a recurring 3D/geo need bridging the image and 3D-engine demand without any server round-trip.

name: equirect-thumbnail
description: Reprojects a 360 equirectangular panorama into a flat perspective snapshot or stereographic 'little planet' view.
example_prompt: Make a little-planet thumbnail from this 360 panorama
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: v360 stereographic/flat projection of a 360 image, local.
rationale: 360 content (React 360 era) needs flat previews for thumbnails and sharing, which this produces in one shot.

name: recompute-normals
description: Recomputes vertex normals for a mesh with selectable smooth or flat shading.
example_prompt: Recompute smooth normals for this model.obj
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM per-face/vertex normal accumulation; pure geometry math, local.
rationale: Models with missing or broken normals render with wrong lighting in every WebGL engine, and fixing them is a common rescue.

name: prefetch-parser
description: Parses Windows .pf prefetch files to show program execution history, run counts, and last-run timestamps.
example_prompt: Parse this prefetch file and tell me when this program last ran
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: prefetch is a self-contained binary format (MAM/SCCA), decompressed and parsed entirely from the uploaded bytes with no OS or network access.
rationale: Prefetch is a top execution-evidence artifact in every Windows DFIR exam (Eric Zimmerman PECmd) and currently needs a desktop tool.

name: windows-logon-timeline
description: Analyzes Windows security logs to build a logon timeline and a user-to-host graph for spotting lateral movement.
example_prompt: Build a logon graph from these event logs to find lateral movement
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: timeline and graph construction is pure data processing on parsed events.
rationale: Reproduces LogonTracer/Blauhaunt's lateral-movement view without a server or database.

name: ese-db-parser
description: Parses Microsoft ESE/EDB databases (WebCacheV01.dat, Windows.edb, IE history) and exports their tables to viewable rows.
example_prompt: Extract the browsing history table from this WebCacheV01.dat file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the ESE page/B-tree format is fully documented and parses from the raw file bytes in memory.
rationale: One engine covers both IE10Analyzer and WinSearchDBAnalyzer demand, unlocking Windows artifact data that normally requires Windows-only tooling.

name: office-doc-ioc-scanner
description: Scans an Office document's macros and structure for suspicious indicators: auto-exec triggers, shell/CreateObject calls, URLs, and obfuscation.
example_prompt: Is this Excel file's macro malicious? Scan it for red flags.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: extraction plus heuristic/regex scoring runs locally on the document bytes.
rationale: Captures oletools' mraptor-style verdict so a user gets a fast malicious/benign signal on a document client-side, without detonating it.

name: text-clusterer
description: Groups sentences or documents into clusters using embeddings and k-means.
example_prompt: Cluster these 50 survey responses into themes.
loader_feasibility: transformers-js embeddings + plain Rust→WASM k-means, all client-side.
rationale: Unsupervised text clustering is a common exploratory-analysis need that benefits from staying fully local and private.

name: text-simplifier
description: Suggests simpler replacements for complex or jargon words to improve plain-language writing.
example_prompt: Simplify the complex words in this policy document
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — retext-simplify replacement dictionary applied offline.
rationale: Plain-language rewriting (retext-simplify) is valuable for accessibility and gov/healthcare writing.

name: filler-word-detector
description: Detects weasel words, hedges, and fillers ('very', 'just', 'really') that weaken writing.
example_prompt: Find the filler and weasel words in this paragraph
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — curated weasel/intensify word lists matched offline.
rationale: Filler-word linting (retext-intensify) is a quick, high-value tightening check for writers.

name: token-regex-matcher
description: Matches token-level patterns over words and POS tags — regex across linguistic tokens.
example_prompt: find all 'adjective + noun' sequences in this text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM token-pattern engine over tokenized/POS-tagged input; offline.
rationale: Browser-local OpenRegex-style linguistic pattern search for extraction and annotation.

name: japanese-tokenizer
description: Performs Japanese morphological analysis, splitting text into words with readings and parts of speech.
example_prompt: Tokenize this Japanese sentence and show the reading of each word: 東京都に住んでいます。
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM compiling the `lindera` morphological analyzer with a bundled dictionary, fully offline (large download).
rationale: jProcessing is direct demand for Japanese NLP and lindera gives proper segmentation that whitespace tokenizers cannot.

name: indic-tokenizer
description: Splits Indic-language text into sentences and words with script-aware rules for Hindi, Bangla, and related scripts.
example_prompt: Tokenize this Bengali paragraph into sentences and words.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Indic sentence/word segmentation uses deterministic danda/punctuation and script rules, no model or network.
rationale: Whitespace tokenizers mishandle Indic punctuation (danda, conjuncts); this packages the IIT Bombay / Indic-NLP tokenization demand into a correct local primitive.

name: regression-diagnostics
description: Runs residual analysis, Q-Q and residual-vs-fitted plots, Durbin-Watson, and multicollinearity (VIF) checks to validate a fitted regression's assumptions.
example_prompt: Check the residuals and multicollinearity for my regression on this data
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — residuals, VIF, and Durbin-Watson are simple post-fit statistics computed in-memory.
rationale: Fitting a regression is only trustworthy once its assumptions are checked, a step users often skip for lack of a tool.

name: label-propagation
description: Spreads a handful of labels across a similarity graph using Laplacian-regularized label propagation for semi-supervised labeling.
example_prompt: I labeled 5 of these points—label the rest
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — iterative propagation over the graph Laplacian is sparse matrix math.
rationale: Lets users bootstrap a full labeling from a few examples, a high-value workflow that keeps unlabeled data private.

name: uplift-effect-analyzer
description: Estimates treatment effect / uplift from experiment data using a two-model (T-learner) approach.
example_prompt: Estimate the uplift of the treatment in this experiment CSV
loader_feasibility: pyodide trains two scikit-learn models and computes per-row uplift entirely in-browser.
rationale: Uplift modeling (the causalml demand) answers 'who does this treatment actually help' and runs offline.

name: geo-heatmap
description: Renders a density heatmap SVG from a set of lat/long points over a normalized grid.
example_prompt: Make a heatmap of these pickup coordinates.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM grid binning + color-mapped SVG; rendered in-browser, no map tiles needed.
rationale: Spatial density visualization is the headline NYC-taxi-blog use case, doable without external tiles.

name: tidy-data-validator
description: Checks a CSV against tidy-data rules (one variable per column, one observation per row) and flags violations.
example_prompt: is this spreadsheet tidy data?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM inspects headers, merged-header patterns, and shapes locally.
rationale: Directly from 'How to Share Data with a Statistician' — tidy-data hygiene is widely taught and rarely tooled.

name: index-rebaser
description: Rebases a time series to a chosen base period set to 100 for comparable indexing.
example_prompt: Rebase these price series to 2020=100
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM arithmetic over the series; offline.
rationale: Comparing economic indicators (FRED, NZIER) requires rebasing to a common index base.

name: salary-string-normalizer
description: Parses messy salary strings ($80k–100k/yr, £45,000 pa) into normalized annual min/max ranges and currency.
example_prompt: Normalize these salary strings into yearly numbers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizing and unit/period normalization on the input, client-side.
rationale: Job-posting salaries are unstructured text that must be normalized before any comparison or analysis.

name: drug-synergy-scorer
description: Computes Bliss, Loewe and ZIP synergy scores from a pasted dose-response combination matrix and renders a synergy heatmap.
example_prompt: Score the synergy of this drug-combination dose-response grid.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; reference-model math and SVG heatmap rendering run locally on pasted data.
rationale: Directly serves the drug-synergy demand with the field's standard quantitative analysis, fully offline.

name: choropleth-map
description: Colors regions of a user-supplied GeoJSON by a data value and renders it as a projected SVG choropleth.
example_prompt: Choropleth map shading these US states by population using this GeoJSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM projects polygons and maps values to colors locally; no map tiles or network needed.
rationale: Delivers the CartoDB geographic-data demand without any tile server or external mapping service.

name: arima-forecast
description: Fits an ARIMA model and forecasts future values with confidence intervals.
example_prompt: Fit ARIMA to this series and forecast the next 12 points
loader_feasibility: pyodide — statsmodels ARIMA in the browser sandbox
rationale: The headline modelling technique behind the time-series demand term.

name: dna-toolkit
description: Parses FASTA sequences and computes GC content, reverse complement, ORFs, and DNA-to-protein translation.
example_prompt: Translate this DNA sequence to protein and give me the GC content
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM sequence processing; runs fully offline.
rationale: Genomic reference data is distributed as FASTA, and basic sequence operations are constantly needed.

name: image-file-size-budget-checker
description: Checks an image's byte size against a performance budget and reports by how much it's over or under.
example_prompt: Is this hero image under my 200KB budget?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the file length directly in the browser.
rationale: Page-weight budgets are easy to blow and a simple gate keeps assets honest.

name: image-format-recommendation-checker
description: Analyzes an image's content (photo vs flat/graphic, transparency) and recommends the optimal format among PNG/JPEG/WebP.
example_prompt: Should this be a PNG, JPEG, or WebP?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes and measures color complexity/alpha usage to pick a format, all local.
rationale: Wrong-format assets are routinely 2-5x too large and a content-aware check gives a clear recommendation.

name: sprite-sheet-grid-checker
description: Checks that a sprite sheet's content aligns to a given cell grid and reports misaligned or bleeding cells.
example_prompt: Do the sprites in this sheet line up on a 32x32 grid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes pixels and analyzes per-cell content bounds against the grid locally.
rationale: Off-grid sprites cause clipping/bleeding in games and a checker pinpoints the bad cells.

name: embedded-thumbnail-mismatch-checker
description: Compares a JPEG's embedded EXIF thumbnail to the full image to flag edited photos whose thumbnail wasn't updated (tamper hint).
example_prompt: Does this photo's embedded thumbnail match the actual image?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM extracts the EXIF thumbnail, decodes both, and compares scaled versions locally.
rationale: A stale embedded thumbnail is a classic sign of post-capture editing and is invisible in normal viewers.

name: out-of-gamut-color-checker
description: Flags pixels whose colors fall outside the sRGB gamut (or another target) and reports the percentage affected.
example_prompt: Does this image have colors outside the sRGB gamut?
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute runs a per-pixel gamut test on the GPU entirely in-browser.
rationale: Out-of-gamut colors clip unpredictably when converted to sRGB and a check warns before the shift.

name: audio-clipping-detector
description: Analyzes a video's audio track for clipped samples and 0 dBFS peaks and reports where the audio is distorting.
example_prompt: Check if the sound in this clip is clipping
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: the astats filter surfaces peak/clip statistics in ffmpeg.wasm in-browser.
rationale: Clipped audio sounds harsh and is unfixable post-export, so catching it early matters.

name: video-interlace-detector
description: Analyzes frames to determine whether a video is interlaced or progressive and reports the detected field order.
example_prompt: Is this footage interlaced or progressive?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: the idet filter performs interlace detection in ffmpeg.wasm client-side.
rationale: Treating interlaced footage as progressive (or vice versa) causes combing artifacts; knowing first guides correct handling.

name: video-corrupt-frame-detector
description: Decodes a video while capturing decoder errors and reports the timestamps of corrupt or undecodable frames and packets.
example_prompt: Scan this video for corrupted frames
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: decoding with error-flagging runs in ffmpeg.wasm fully in-browser.
rationale: Recovered or partially-downloaded files often have localized corruption that only surfaces on a full decode pass.

name: click-pop-detector
description: Detects impulsive clicks, pops, and crackle (digitization errors or vinyl artifacts) using high-frequency transient analysis.
example_prompt: Find the clicks and pops in this vinyl rip
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: high-pass + median-deviation transient detector over decoded PCM, fully client-side
rationale: Click/pop locations let users target de-click repair instead of hunting a whole transfer by ear.

name: flac-integrity-verifier
description: Decodes a FLAC stream and compares the recomputed MD5 signature against the one stored in STREAMINFO to verify bit-exact integrity.
example_prompt: Verify that this FLAC isn't corrupted
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: claxon/symphonia decodes FLAC and an MD5 of the PCM compares to the embedded hash, all client-side
rationale: FLAC's own integrity check (flac -t) requires a desktop tool; this brings verified-decode QC into the browser.

name: inter-channel-delay-checker
description: Cross-correlates stereo channels to detect time misalignment (one channel delayed by samples), flagging accidental offsets.
example_prompt: Are the two channels of this file time-aligned or is one delayed?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: short-lag cross-correlation over decoded stereo PCM, pure DSP client-side
rationale: Sample-level channel delay smears the stereo image and comes from bad routing; correlation pinpoints the offset.

name: polarity-checker
description: Estimates absolute signal polarity from asymmetric transients and flags likely inverted-polarity recordings.
example_prompt: Is this kick-drum recording polarity-inverted?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: transient asymmetry analysis over decoded PCM, computed in-browser
rationale: Inverted polarity weakens transients when combined with other mics and is otherwise inaudible in isolation.

name: dither-detector
description: Analyzes least-significant-bit behavior to detect whether a bit-depth reduction was dithered or truncated, flagging undithered requantization.
example_prompt: Was this 16-bit file properly dithered or just truncated from 24-bit?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: LSB histogram and noise-floor statistics on decoded PCM, all client-side
rationale: Undithered truncation adds quantization distortion in quiet passages; detecting it guides a re-export with dither.

name: abrupt-cut-detector
description: Detects audio that ends (or begins) abruptly at a non-zero level with no fade, indicating a truncated or improperly trimmed file.
example_prompt: Does this track get cut off abruptly at the end?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: check head/tail sample levels and slope over decoded PCM, a few lines in WASM
rationale: Hard cuts cause audible clicks and signal incomplete exports; a boundary-level check flags them before publishing.

name: replaygain-tag-validator
description: Checks for presence of ReplayGain/R128 gain tags and recomputes loudness to verify the stored values are accurate, not stale.
example_prompt: Are the ReplayGain tags on this file correct?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse gain tags plus a BS.1770 loudness recompute on decoded PCM, compared in-browser
rationale: Stale or missing ReplayGain tags defeat volume normalization in players; verification catches drift after edits.

name: editorconfig-check
description: Verifies that pasted files conform to a given .editorconfig (indent, charset, final newline).
example_prompt: Does this file follow my .editorconfig rules?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM matching glob rules and inspecting text; runs client-side
rationale: Catches formatting drift across a team without running a full linter toolchain.

name: bsn-validator
description: Validates a Dutch BSN national identifier using the eleven-test (elfproef) weighted modulo check.
example_prompt: Check if BSN 111222333 passes the eleven-test
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: weighted sum with the final negative weight, no network.
rationale: Dutch identity-sensitive forms need a private, exact elfproef validator.

name: vin-validator
description: Validates a 17-character VIN by transliterating letters and computing the position-9 mod-11 check digit.
example_prompt: Check if VIN 1HGCM82633A004352 is valid
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: letter-to-value table, weighted sum, and mod-11, no lookups needed.
rationale: Car buyers and dealers want to confirm a VIN's check digit before trusting a listing.

name: image-noise-estimator
description: Estimates per-channel sensor/grain noise (sigma) in flat regions to gauge how noisy an image is.
example_prompt: How much noise is in this night photo?
