loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM finds low-gradient patches and computes local standard deviation locally.
rationale: Quantifying noise tells users whether denoising or a reshoot is worthwhile.

name: exposure-clipping-analyzer
description: Reports the percentage of blown-out (clipped white) and crushed (clipped black) pixels to flag exposure problems.
example_prompt: Are the highlights blown out in this shot?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tallies clipped luminance values from decoded pixels locally.
rationale: Clipping detection is a precise exposure check that a generic histogram render doesn't quantify.

name: image-channel-stats
description: Computes min, max, mean, and standard deviation for each RGB/alpha channel of an image.
example_prompt: Give me the per-channel statistics for this image.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM iterates decoded pixels and accumulates per-channel statistics in-browser.
rationale: Channel-level numbers help diagnose color casts, dead channels, and dynamic-range issues.

name: color-temperature-estimator
description: Estimates the overall white-balance color temperature of a photo in Kelvin.
example_prompt: What's the color temperature of this photo?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM derives correlated color temperature from average chromaticity locally.
rationale: A Kelvin estimate helps match white balance across a set of images.

name: public-key-from-certificate
description: Extracts the subject public key from an X.509 certificate and outputs it as PEM (and optionally JWK).
example_prompt: Extract the public key from this certificate as PEM
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via x509-parser + spki; a local extraction and re-encoding with no network.
rationale: Pulling the public key out of a cert is a frequent setup step for signature verification and JWKS publishing.

name: video-edl-generator
description: Generates a CMX3600 EDL from a list of source-name and in/out timecode cut points.
example_prompt: Make a CMX3600 EDL from these in/out timecodes for reel A001
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust computes the timecode math and formats the fixed-width EDL records entirely in WASM.
rationale: EDLs remain the lingua franca for moving cut lists between editors and a generator avoids error-prone manual formatting.

name: otio-timeline-generator
description: Generates an OpenTimelineIO JSON timeline from a simple clip-and-cut list for interchange between editors.
example_prompt: Generate an OTIO timeline for these three clips at 24fps with their in/out points
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust serializes the OTIO JSON schema with computed rational-time values, no external library needed.
rationale: OTIO is the emerging open standard for timeline interchange and a local generator seeds it without installing the Python toolkit.

name: ticker-tape-video
description: Generates a transparent horizontally-scrolling news-ticker strip clip from a line of text for compositing.
example_prompt: Make a transparent bottom news ticker that scrolls 'BREAKING: gizza ships 40 new tools'
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg `drawbox`/`drawtext` with an x-position-over-time expression renders the ticker on an alpha source in wasm.
rationale: A scrolling ticker is a recognizable broadcast element creators want to overlay and currently fake with manual keyframes.

name: vinyl-crackle-generator
description: Synthesizes procedural vinyl crackle, pops, and surface hiss as a WAV texture for lo-fi production.
example_prompt: Generate 60 seconds of warm vinyl crackle to layer under my beat
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM models random impulse pops plus filtered noise to produce the texture entirely in-browser.
rationale: Lo-fi and hip-hop producers want authentic, royalty-free vinyl noise without sampling a record.

name: backing-track-generator
description: Generates a full practice backing track (drums, bass, simple comping) as a WAV from a key, chord progression, and tempo.
example_prompt: Make a 12-bar blues backing track in A at 80 bpm
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM sequences and synthesizes the parts then mixes them to a single WAV entirely client-side.
rationale: Instrumentalists need jam-along tracks for any key/progression and generating one beats searching for the right one online.

name: video-to-ogv
description: Converts a video into an Ogg Theora/Vorbis OGV file for fully open-format, patent-free distribution.
example_prompt: Convert this clip to .ogv for a Wikipedia upload
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm bundles the Theora and Vorbis encoders, producing OGV locally with no server.
rationale: Wikimedia and open-source projects require Theora/OGV, a niche but unmet conversion need.

name: video-pixel-format-convert
description: Re-encodes a video into yuv420p (or a chosen pixel format) so it plays on devices that reject 4:4:4/4:2:2.
example_prompt: Convert this to yuv420p so QuickTime stops showing a black screen
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm applies -pix_fmt yuv420p during a local re-encode, fixing the pixel layout in-browser.
rationale: Non-420 pixel formats silently fail on many players, and this targeted fix resolves 'black video' complaints.

name: video-color-range-convert
description: Converts a video between full-range (PC, 0–255) and limited-range (TV, 16–235) to fix washed-out or crushed levels.
example_prompt: Fix the washed-out colors by converting this to limited TV range
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm applies the scale/colorspace range filters during a local re-encode in the browser.
rationale: Range mismatches cause grey blacks or blown highlights, a precise technical fix users rarely know how to do.

name: video-chroma-subsample-convert
description: Converts a video's chroma subsampling (e.g. 4:2:2 or 4:4:4 to 4:2:0) for editor and web-player compatibility.
example_prompt: Convert this 4:2:2 footage to 4:2:0 for web upload
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm re-encodes with the target pixel format that encodes the chosen subsampling, fully local.
rationale: Capture cards and pro cameras produce 4:2:2/4:4:4 that web players choke on, needing a subsampling downconvert.

name: dv-to-mp4
description: Converts raw DV/DVCAM camcorder footage (.dv/.avi) into a modern H.264 MP4 for editing and sharing.
example_prompt: Convert this old DV camcorder capture to mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm includes the DV decoder and H.264 encoder, transcoding the tape capture entirely client-side.
rationale: Digitized MiniDV tapes arrive as bulky DV streams that need transcoding before they're usable on modern devices.

name: timeline-extractor
description: Build a chronological timeline of events from a long article or set of stories.
example_prompt: Make a dated timeline of events from this article
loader_feasibility: transformers-js sentence extraction + Rust→WASM date parsing/sorting, all client-side.
rationale: '17 Timelines' demand for timeline summarization — a structured output not covered by plain summarizers.

name: wordlist-frequency-builder
description: Builds a frequency-sorted wordlist/dictionary from a pasted text corpus, with options for min-count, case folding, and stop-word removal.
example_prompt: Build a frequency wordlist from this text for a custom keyboard dictionary
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: tokenization and counting over the corpus in-memory.
rationale: Open keyboards (AnySoftKeyboard, OpenBoard) let users import custom prediction dictionaries, and a corpus-derived wordlist is the raw material.

name: wallabag-export-converter
description: Converts a Wallabag JSON export into Markdown, plaintext, or a bundle of EPUBs.
example_prompt: Convert my Wallabag export to Markdown files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON parsing and reformatting of the export payload.
rationale: People leaving or backing up Wallabag have no easy way to liberate their archive into portable formats.

name: hypothesis-annotations-to-markdown
description: Converts a Hypothesis annotation/highlight JSON export into Markdown notes grouped by source page.
example_prompt: Turn my Hypothesis highlights export into Markdown notes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON-to-Markdown transform on the export file.
rationale: Hypothesis users want their web highlights inside Obsidian/notes, and the only path today is brittle third-party scripts.

name: deniable-encrypted-vault
description: Creates a vault with two compartments — a decoy and a hidden real one — each unlocked by a different password for plausible deniability.
example_prompt: Make an encrypted file with a decoy password and a hidden real one
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; two independently keyed XChaCha20-Poly1305 payloads packed to look indistinguishable from random data
rationale: Browser-local take on VeraCrypt/Shufflecake hidden volumes for coercion resistance.

name: medical-abbreviation-decoder
description: Expands medical abbreviations and shorthand in a pasted note using a bundled clinical-abbreviation dictionary.
example_prompt: Decode the abbreviations in: pt c/o SOB, hx of CHF, BID dosing
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (embedded abbreviation dictionary + tokenized replacement) — offline text lookup.
rationale: Makes personal health records human-readable locally, a practical companion to the record summarizer.

name: self-host-fonts-css-generator
description: Generates @font-face CSS and preload tags for a set of uploaded font files so they can be served from your own domain.
example_prompt: Generate @font-face CSS for these two woff2 weights
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (reads font metadata, emits CSS text) — pure offline string generation.
rationale: Turns self-hosted fonts into drop-in CSS, eliminating the Google Fonts CDN call that privacy proxies like coolLabs/Bunny route around.

name: simplex-link-parse
description: Decodes a SimpleX invitation/contact link into its server queue address, version, and key parameters.
example_prompt: What's inside this SimpleX link? https://simplex.chat/invitation#/?v=2&smp=...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — URL-fragment and base64url parsing, no server contact.
rationale: SimpleX links are opaque blobs; surfacing the queue server and version helps users vet who they're connecting through.

name: matrix-megolm-export-decrypt
description: Decrypts a Matrix encrypted room-keys export blob with the user's passphrase using PBKDF2-SHA512, AES-256-CTR, and HMAC-SHA256.
example_prompt: Decrypt my Matrix key export with passphrase 'hunter2': -----BEGIN MEGOLM SESSION DATA-----...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — RustCrypto PBKDF2/AES/HMAC run locally so the passphrase and keys never leave the device.
rationale: Recovering Megolm keys offline avoids handing an encrypted key backup to any web service.

name: lesspass-stateless-derive
description: Recreates LessPass deterministic derivation: site + login + master password + counter run through PBKDF2 to regenerate a site password with no vault stored.
example_prompt: Derive my LessPass password for github.com login alice.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (pbkdf2 + sha256 crates) — the entire LessPass algorithm is deterministic math done in-browser.
rationale: Directly serves LessPass demand — a stateless manager whose whole value is recomputing passwords offline from a master secret.

name: apk-google-dependency-checker
description: Checks an APK for Google Play Services/Firebase dependencies to predict de-Googled compatibility.
example_prompt: Will this APK work without Google Play Services?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: scan dex strings for com.google.android.gms/firebase references in memory
rationale: Direct mapping of Plexus — de-Googled users constantly need to know if an app will run before installing.

name: privacy-frontend-redirector
description: Rewrites a YouTube/Twitter/Reddit/Medium/Quora/Instagram URL into an equivalent privacy-frontend URL (Invidious, Piped, Nitter, Teddit, Scribe, Quetre, Pixelfed).
example_prompt: Convert this YouTube link to an Invidious link: https://youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pure string/host parsing and template substitution against an embedded mapping table, no network needed.
rationale: This is the core LibRedirect behavior the entire Scribe/Quetre/Invidious/Piped/Librarian demand cluster wants, and it runs entirely offline.

name: mastodon-archive-analyzer
description: Parses a Mastodon data export outbox.json and reports posting frequency, top hashtags, and reply ratios.
example_prompt: Analyze my Mastodon export outbox.json and show my posting stats
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON parse + aggregation over the uploaded archive; runs entirely client-side for privacy.
rationale: Users leaving or auditing an instance want offline insight into their own archive without uploading it anywhere.

name: fediverse-follow-list-merger
description: Merges and dedupes Mastodon following_accounts.csv files for clean migration between instances.
example_prompt: Merge these two following_accounts.csv files and remove duplicates
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSV parse/merge; operates on uploaded files only.
rationale: Instance migration is a core fediverse pain point and Mastodon's CSV import needs a single deduped list.

name: mastodon-blocklist-merger
description: Combines multiple Mastodon domain/account block CSV lists into one deduplicated import file.
example_prompt: Combine these fediblock domain CSVs into one import-ready list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSV merge/dedupe; no network.
rationale: Fediverse moderators routinely share and combine blocklists and need them merged without conflicts.

name: zulip-export-analyzer
description: Parses a Zulip export JSON to report stream/topic activity and search messages offline.
example_prompt: Analyze my Zulip export and show the busiest streams
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON aggregation over the uploaded export; fully client-side.
rationale: Teams migrating off or auditing Zulip need to explore their export without standing up a server.

name: kfold-cross-validation-splitter
description: Generates k-fold or stratified k-fold index splits from a CSV for cross-validation.
example_prompt: Make 5 stratified folds from this dataset.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes fold indices locally.
rationale: Cross-validation is fundamental to honest model evaluation in every ML course.

name: model-leaderboard
description: Trains several algorithms (linear, tree, KNN, SVM, forest, boosting) on your dataset with cross-validation and ranks them by score.
example_prompt: Try several ML models on this CSV and tell me which performs best
loader_feasibility: pyodide — runs a cross-validated scikit-learn bake-off entirely in the browser sandbox.
rationale: Turns the generic 'which model / ensemble learning' demand into a practical one-shot auto-comparison.

name: image-vignette-detector
description: Detects lens vignetting by comparing corner brightness to the center and reports the falloff amount.
example_prompt: Does this image have vignetting in the corners?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM samples radial luminance from center to corners over decoded pixels.
rationale: Quantified vignette falloff guides correction and flags unintended darkening.

name: video-brightness-timeline
description: Plots average frame brightness over the whole video so dark or blown-out stretches are easy to spot.
example_prompt: Graph the brightness over time for this footage
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg `signalstats` emits per-frame YAVG metadata in wasm; the graph is drawn from that data locally.
rationale: A brightness curve reveals exposure problems and lighting changes at a glance for colorists and QC.

name: video-saturation-timeline
description: Plots average color saturation over time to reveal washed-out or oversaturated segments.
example_prompt: Show me how saturated the colors are across this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg `signalstats` outputs per-frame SATAVG locally; plotting happens client-side from the metadata.
rationale: Saturation drift is a frequent grading issue that a timeline exposes without frame-by-frame inspection.

name: video-fade-detector
description: Detects fade-in and fade-out transitions and reports their start/end timestamps and direction.
example_prompt: Find the fade-ins and fade-outs in this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg extracts luminance over time, plain Rust→WASM detects monotonic brightness ramps to/from black; local.
rationale: Fade boundaries mark natural segment edges for chaptering and trimming and are easy to miss in a cut list.

name: video-duplicate-segment-finder
description: Scans a video for repeated or duplicate segments (e.g. reused B-roll) using perceptual hashing.
example_prompt: Are any parts of this video repeated?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg samples frames, plain Rust→WASM computes per-segment perceptual hashes and matches them locally.
rationale: Detecting accidental reuse or padded duplicate footage is useful for QC and originality checks offline.

name: video-face-count-timeline
description: Counts visible faces in each sampled frame and graphs how many people are on screen over time.
example_prompt: Graph how many faces are on screen throughout this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg samples frames, onnx-runtime runs a face-detection model locally; nothing leaves the browser.
rationale: A face-count curve helps find group shots, solo segments, and crowd scenes while keeping faces private on-device.

name: spectral-flatness-analyzer
description: Measures spectral flatness (tonal versus noise-like) over time to characterize a signal.
example_prompt: Is this signal more tonal or more noisy?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes the geometric/arithmetic mean ratio per FFT frame client-side
rationale: Flatness distinguishes pitched content from noise for sound design and segmentation.

name: spectral-rolloff-analyzer
description: Reports the frequency below which a chosen percentage of spectral energy lies, over time.
example_prompt: Show the 95% spectral rolloff for this clip
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM accumulates per-frame FFT energy and finds the rolloff bin in-browser
rationale: Rolloff summarizes high-frequency content for comparing recordings and detecting muffling.

name: zero-crossing-rate-analyzer
description: Computes the zero-crossing rate over time to help separate voiced, unvoiced, and percussive sounds.
example_prompt: Give me the zero-crossing rate of this speech clip
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM counts sign changes per window on decoded PCM, fully client-side
rationale: ZCR is a cheap, classic feature for speech/percussion segmentation and noise detection.

name: speaking-rate-analyzer
description: Computes words-per-minute speaking rate over time from a speech recording.
example_prompt: How fast am I talking in this voiceover?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs Whisper locally and divides word counts by segment durations
rationale: Pacing feedback improves narration, language practice, and podcast clarity.

name: yaml-to-toml
description: Converts a YAML document into equivalent TOML.
example_prompt: convert this yaml config to toml
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — serde_yaml parse then toml serialization, fully in-memory.
rationale: Moving config between ecosystems (e.g. into Rust/Cargo-style TOML) is awkward by hand and ideal for automation.

name: git-identity-config
description: Generates conditional `includeIf` gitconfig blocks so the right name, email, and signing key are used per directory or remote host.
example_prompt: Set git to use my work email under ~/work and personal under ~/personal
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM emits the gitconfig INI text locally.
rationale: Juggling work/personal identities is a common pain and includeIf snippets are fiddly to hand-write correctly.

name: packet-header-decoder
description: Decodes a hex dump of a frame into Ethernet/IP/TCP/UDP/ICMP header fields with flags, ports and checksum verification.
example_prompt: decode this hex packet dump into its header fields
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — byte parsing of well-known header layouts, no network, client-side.
rationale: Maps packemon's packet-inspection demand and is a great learning/debugging aid for hand-pasted captures.

name: glob-to-regex
description: Converts shell glob patterns like src/**/*.{js,ts} into equivalent regular expressions and tests them against sample paths.
example_prompt: convert the glob src/**/*.{js,ts} into a regex and test it on src/app/main.ts
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure string parsing of glob syntax into a regex, no I/O or network.
rationale: Glob↔regex translation is a recurring pain point for shell, CI, and gitignore authors.

name: id3v2-tag-reader
description: Parses the ID3v2 header of an MP3/AIFF file and lists every frame (title, artist, album, year, comments, TXXX, etc.) with raw values.
example_prompt: Read all the ID3v2 tags out of this song.mp3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — ID3v2 is a documented byte structure at the file head, parsed entirely in-memory with no decoding or network
rationale: ID3v2 holds dozens of frame types most players hide, and a faithful dump is the basis for any tag audit or migration.

name: encoded-polyline-decoder
description: Decodes a Google-encoded polyline string into the original list of latitude/longitude points.
example_prompt: Decode this encoded polyline into lat/long points
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the standard varint/zigzag decode algorithm, fully offline.
rationale: Route polylines from mapping APIs are opaque until decoded, with no good browser-local tool.

name: title-case-formatter
description: Applies title case following AP or Chicago rules, keeping small words and acronyms correct.
example_prompt: Title-case this headline using Chicago style: 'the war of the worlds'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bundled stop-word lists + capitalization rules, client-side
rationale: Naive capitalize-every-word is wrong for headlines, and proper style-guide title casing is genuinely fiddly.

name: accounting-format-formatter
description: Renders numbers in accounting style with negatives in parentheses and aligned currency symbols.
example_prompt: show -2450.5 and 1200 in accounting format
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sign and alignment formatting, deterministic and local.
rationale: Accounting display conventions differ from plain currency and are tedious to apply by hand.

name: char-diff
description: Shows a character-level diff between two short strings, useful for spotting typos, IDs, or hash mismatches.
example_prompt: Which characters differ between these two API keys?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — character-array LCS is trivial to run locally
rationale: Precise per-character comparison is essential for debugging near-identical identifiers and tokens.

name: hex-diff
description: Renders a byte-level hex diff of two binary or text inputs, highlighting differing offsets and bytes.
example_prompt: Show me a hex diff of these two files and which bytes differ
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — compare byte arrays and format aligned hex columns in-process
rationale: Byte-precise comparison is indispensable for debugging encoding and binary-format issues.

name: video-pts-dts-validator
description: Validates packet PTS/DTS for negative values, non-monotonic ordering, and unexpected gaps across the stream.
example_prompt: Check the PTS/DTS timestamps in this file for ordering or gap problems.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader reads packet timestamps via ffprobe in WASM and analyzes ordering locally.
rationale: Broken presentation/decode timestamps cause seeking and sync failures that only packet-level validation reveals.

name: video-embedded-captions-checker
description: Detects whether the stream carries EIA-608/CEA-708 closed captions and reports which caption services are present.
example_prompt: Does this file have embedded 608/708 closed captions?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader probes for caption side-data/streams in WASM and enumerates services locally.
rationale: Embedded captions (distinct from subtitle tracks) are legally required for broadcast and easy to lose in transcode.

name: loudness-range-meter
description: Reports EBU R128 loudness range (LRA) to quantify how much loudness varies across a program.
example_prompt: Measure the loudness range (LRA) of this audiobook chapter.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — the ebur128 filter computes integrated loudness and LRA fully in-browser.
rationale: LRA is a delivery metric distinct from a single loudness target, telling editors if dynamics are too wide or too flat.

name: lossless-reencode-verifier
description: Decodes two lossless files (e.g. original vs re-encoded) and confirms their PCM is bit-for-bit identical.
example_prompt: Confirm my re-encoded FLAC decodes to exactly the same audio as the WAV.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — decoding both to PCM and hashing/comparing samples is fully client-side.
rationale: Proving a lossless re-encode is truly bit-identical is the only way to trust a format migration before deleting originals.

name: image-dimension-attr-checker
description: Lists img and picture tags missing explicit width/height attributes, the leading cause of layout shift (CLS).
example_prompt: Which images in this HTML are missing width/height attributes?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tag scan; local.
rationale: Setting width/height is the cheapest Core Web Vitals win and easy to miss across many templates.

name: passage-overlap-detector
description: Detects and highlights overlapping passages shared between two documents and reports the overlap percentage.
example_prompt: How much of this essay overlaps word-for-word with this source?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — n-gram matching and longest-common-substring search run in-memory
rationale: Quantifying shared text supports plagiarism screening and citation checks fully offline.

name: sentence-align
description: Aligns the sentences of two related documents (versions or translations) into matched pairs, marking unmatched insertions and deletions.
example_prompt: Align the sentences of my original and edited draft so I can compare them one to one
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — length-and-overlap alignment (Gale-Church style) runs locally
rationale: Sentence alignment is the foundation for careful version and translation comparison.

name: ab-text-metrics-compare
description: Compares two text variants on length, readability, sentiment-neutral keyword coverage, and structure to support A/B copy decisions.
example_prompt: Compare these two versions of my landing-page copy on readability and length
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — compute readability indices and counts for both texts locally
rationale: Side-by-side objective metrics help writers choose between competing copy variants without guesswork.

name: alpha-mask-diff
description: Compares the alpha/transparency channels of two PNGs and highlights where the cutout or mask differs.
example_prompt: Did the transparency mask change between these two cutouts?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the alpha plane of both images and diffs it locally
rationale: Designers iterating on cutouts need to verify only the matte changed, not the RGB.

name: image-brightness-shift-detector
description: Measures the overall exposure/gamma shift between two images and reports it as a stops/gamma estimate.
example_prompt: How many stops brighter is the second photo than the first?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM fits a brightness/gamma curve from histograms locally
rationale: Photographers comparing brackets want the exposure delta quantified, not eyeballed.

name: image-onion-skin
description: Overlays two aligned images at an adjustable opacity blend so subtle shifts can be inspected.
example_prompt: Overlay these two frames at 50% so I can see what moved
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM alpha-blends the two layers and outputs one image client-side
rationale: Onion-skinning is the classic animator/registration check for small positional drift.

name: image-checkerboard-compare
description: Interleaves two images in a checkerboard tile pattern so seams reveal exactly where they diverge.
example_prompt: Compare these two textures in a checkerboard pattern
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tiles pixels from each source by cell and re-encodes locally
rationale: Checkerboard interleave exposes alignment and tone mismatches a slider can miss.

name: video-split-wipe-compare
description: Shows video A on the left half and video B on the right half of one frame, split by a movable wipe line.
example_prompt: Make a split-screen wipe comparing the original and color-graded versions
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg crop+overlay filters slice and recombine the two streams locally in wasmi-driven ffmpeg.
rationale: Wipe comparisons reveal grading/encoding differences that side-by-side hides.

name: video-bitrate-compare
description: Overlays the per-second bitrate timelines of two videos to compare encoder allocation strategies.
example_prompt: Compare how the two encoders allocated bitrate over time
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg packet-size sampling for both files in wasm plus Rust→WASM merges the two timelines client-side.
rationale: Seeing two bitrate curves together explains quality differences in motion-heavy scenes.

name: video-color-histogram-diff
description: Compares the RGB/luma histograms of two videos and quantifies how their tonal distributions differ.
example_prompt: How different is the color distribution between these two grades?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg histogram stats per file plus Rust→WASM distance metrics run entirely client-side.
rationale: Histogram distance objectively measures grading or exposure shifts between versions.

name: audio-clipping-compare
description: Counts clipped/0dBFS-pinned samples in two files and reports which version clips more and where.
example_prompt: Which of these two bounces clips more?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: threshold-run sample analysis on both signals, no server
rationale: Catching a louder master that introduced clipping is a common, cheap regression check.

name: channel-correlation-diff
description: Compares the two channels of a stereo file (or two mono files) to detect mono, dual-mono, polarity-inverted, or fake-stereo content.
example_prompt: Is this file real stereo or just fake/dual-mono?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: inter-channel correlation and L−R energy analysis on PCM, no server
rationale: Identifying fake-stereo or accidentally mono files saves storage and catches mixing mistakes.

name: onset-timing-diff
description: Extracts onset/transient times from two takes and diffs them to measure rhythmic tightness and timing drift.
example_prompt: How tight is the second drum take against the first?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: spectral-flux onset detection on both, matched-onset timing deltas, local
rationale: Quantifying performance timing differences supports comping and groove analysis with no equivalent tool.

name: three-way-text-merge
description: Performs a three-way merge of a base, mine, and theirs text, emitting conflict markers where they disagree.
example_prompt: Three-way merge these base, mine, and theirs versions
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — diff3 algorithm over three buffers, fully local
rationale: Resolving merges without git tooling is genuinely useful for snippets, configs, and translated content.

name: directory-manifest-diff
description: Compares two file-tree listings (find/ls -R/tree output) and reports added, removed, and moved paths.
example_prompt: Diff these two directory listings and tell me what files were added or moved
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse path sets from both listings and compute set and rename diffs locally
rationale: Comparing before/after file inventories is common and a path-aware diff detects moves a line diff misses.

name: har-diff
description: Request-level diff of two HAR captures, surfacing added/removed endpoints and status, size, and timing deltas.
example_prompt: Compare these two HAR files and tell me which requests or timings changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: both HARs are JSON; key entries by method+URL and diff fields locally
rationale: Perf and regression debugging across two captures needs an entry-matched diff, which the many HAR tools lack.

name: indexed-palette-extractor
description: Reads the actual stored color palette table from an indexed GIF or PNG and exports the exact hex list.
example_prompt: Extract the palette table from this indexed GIF
loader_feasibility: plain Rust parses the PLTE/palette block directly in WASM — exact values, not clustered approximations.
rationale: Pixel artists and retro-game devs need the precise stored palette, which clustering tools don't give them.

name: comic-panel-splitter
description: Detects panel boundaries on a comic or manga page and exports each panel as a separate image in reading order.
example_prompt: Split this comic page into its individual panels
loader_feasibility: plain Rust gutter detection (optionally onnx for tricky layouts) segments and crops panels in WASM.
rationale: Webtoon creators and readers want panels split out for reformatting and there's no convenient private tool.

name: apng-frame-extractor
description: Splits an animated PNG (APNG) into its individual frame images with per-frame delay metadata.
example_prompt: Extract all the frames from this APNG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust parses the APNG fcTL/fdAT chunks and reconstructs each frame in WASM.
rationale: APNG tooling is scarce and people who hit one need a way to break it into frames they can edit.

name: video-loudness-report
description: Runs EBU R128 analysis on the audio track and reports integrated LUFS, loudness range, and true-peak without modifying the file.
example_prompt: What's the integrated LUFS and true peak of this video's audio?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader's ebur128/loudnorm-print filter computes loudness stats entirely in the wasm runtime.
rationale: Broadcasters and podcasters must hit platform loudness targets, and a read-only measurement is needed before deciding whether to normalize.

name: video-telecine-detector
description: Detects 3:2 pulldown / telecine cadence and reports the pattern so you know whether inverse telecine is needed.
example_prompt: Does this video have 3:2 pulldown telecine applied?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader analyzes field cadence with idet/fieldmatch metrics client-side.
rationale: Restoring film-sourced video to 24fps requires confirming the pulldown cadence first, which is hard to eyeball.

name: mp4-atom-tree
description: Parses an MP4/MOV file and renders its box/atom hierarchy (ftyp, moov, trak, mdat…) with sizes and offsets.
example_prompt: Show me the atom/box structure tree of this MP4
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM MP4 box parser walks the container structure with no decode, entirely client-side.
rationale: Diagnosing corrupt or non-standard MP4s requires seeing the box layout, and uploading media to an online inspector is a privacy risk.

name: fixed-width-validate
description: Validates a fixed-width text file against a supplied column spec (offsets/widths/types), flagging misaligned rows.
example_prompt: Validate this fixed-width file — columns are 0-10 name, 10-18 date, 18-25 amount
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — slicing rows by byte offset and type-checking runs locally
rationale: Legacy mainframe and banking feeds are fixed-width and a single shifted field corrupts everything downstream.

name: ical-validator
description: Checks .ics calendar files for required VEVENT properties, valid DTSTART/DTEND, and correct line-folding.
example_prompt: Validate this .ics calendar file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM RFC 5545 line parser; fully offline
rationale: Subtle iCalendar errors cause events to silently vanish in some clients.

name: running-clock-overlay-video
description: Generates a transparent or solid-background video of a live ticking digital clock (HH:MM:SS) for compositing or stream overlays.
example_prompt: Make a 5-minute running clock overlay starting at 09:00:00, white text on transparent
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg drawtext with the 'pts' timecode expression renders the incrementing clock per frame; fully client-side.
rationale: Stream and edit overlays often need a clean ticking clock and it's distinct from the existing countdown timer.

name: callout-annotation-overlay-video
description: Generates a transparent animated callout (arrow + label box that pops in then fades) for pointing at on-screen elements.
example_prompt: Make a callout arrow pointing top-right with label 'Click here', pops in at 1s, transparent overlay
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg drawbox/drawtext plus a drawn arrow with fade/scale time expressions over a transparent source; all local.
rationale: Tutorial creators add callouts constantly and currently rely on heavy editors to do it.

name: audio-vectorscope-video
description: Renders an audio stereo-vectorscope (Lissajous) visualizer video from a supplied stereo track.
example_prompt: Make a stereo vectorscope visualizer from this track, glowing green, 720x720
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg 'avectorscope' plots L/R correlation per frame from the audio in the WASM ffmpeg loader.
rationale: A striking, unusual audio visual distinct from existing video-domain vectorscope image tools.

name: latex-matrix-scaffold
description: Converts a grid of numbers or symbols into a LaTeX matrix environment (pmatrix/bmatrix/vmatrix) with alignment.
example_prompt: Turn 1 2 3 / 4 5 6 into a LaTeX bmatrix
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — text parsing and template assembly, no external compiler
rationale: Hand-typing LaTeX matrices with correct ampersands and row breaks is tedious and a frequent source of typos.

name: qcp-to-wav
description: Decodes Qualcomm PureVoice (.qcp) QCELP/EVRC recordings from old phones into PCM WAV.
example_prompt: convert this old .qcp phone recording to wav
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader includes the QCELP/EVRC decoders and writes WAV in wasm.
rationale: Recordings from legacy CDMA handsets are stuck in QCP and play in almost nothing today.

name: iff-8svx-to-wav
description: Converts Amiga IFF/8SVX sampled-sound files (including Fibonacci-delta compressed ones) to WAV.
example_prompt: convert this amiga 8svx sample to wav
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses IFF chunks and decodes 8-bit/Fibonacci-delta samples to PCM locally.
rationale: Amiga demoscene and game sample archives are full of 8SVX that no current player opens.

name: id3-to-vorbis-comment
description: Copies ID3v2 tag fields from an MP3 onto a FLAC/Ogg file as Vorbis comments, mapping field names.
example_prompt: copy the id3 tags from this mp3 onto my flac
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (lofty) — reads ID3 frames and writes the Vorbis comment block without touching audio.
rationale: Transcoding MP3 to FLAC usually drops tags; this preserves metadata across the container change.

name: gguf-header-to-json
description: Parses a GGUF (llama.cpp) file header and metadata key-values into readable JSON, including tensor dimensions and quantization types.
example_prompt: Read the metadata header of this GGUF model file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: GGUF's binary metadata block has a well-defined typed-KV structure parsed by reading a few kilobytes of the front of the file, client-side.
rationale: Local-LLM users need to know a GGUF's quant type, context length, and tensor list without running an inference engine.

name: video-strip-attachments
description: Removes embedded font and file attachments from an MKV, keeping only the media streams.
example_prompt: strip the embedded fonts and attachments out of this mkv
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — maps out attachment streams with -map -0:t and stream-copy in the WASM runtime.
rationale: Fan-subbed MKVs carry megabytes of fonts/attachments that bloat files, the write-side counterpart to attachment extraction.

name: alaw-encoder
description: Encodes 16-bit PCM WAV into G.711 A-law companded audio.
example_prompt: Encode this WAV to G.711 A-law
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: applies the standard A-law compression table per sample, no server.
rationale: A-law is the European telephony standard and a distinct companding scheme from mu-law for VoIP/PBX assets.

name: ima-adpcm-encoder
description: Encodes PCM WAV into IMA/DVI ADPCM (4-bit) compressed WAV.
example_prompt: Compress this WAV to IMA ADPCM
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: runs the IMA ADPCM step-size predictor state machine per nibble, no external codec.
rationale: IMA ADPCM is the classic 4:1 game/embedded audio format with no clean browser encoder available.

name: g726-adpcm-codec
description: Encodes and decodes G.726 ADPCM (16/24/32/40 kbps) telephony audio.
example_prompt: Convert this PCM to 32 kbps G.726 ADPCM
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: implements the G.726 adaptive quantizer/predictor in pure Rust, no server.
rationale: G.726 is a widely deployed VoIP/DECT codec with few self-contained, browser-runnable implementations.

name: gsm-0610-codec
description: Encodes and decodes GSM 06.10 full-rate audio between PCM WAV and GSM frames.
example_prompt: Encode this WAV to GSM 06.10
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (wasm) supports the gsm codec, so encode/decode runs entirely in the browser sandbox.
rationale: GSM 06.10 is the canonical mobile-voice format for archival and telephony interoperability.

name: ltc-timecode-decoder
description: Decodes SMPTE Linear Timecode (LTC) from an audio track into HH:MM:SS:FF values over time.
example_prompt: Read the SMPTE timecode off this LTC audio track
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: decodes the biphase-mark LTC bitstream from PCM samples, no server.
rationale: Film/video sync workflows depend on extracting timecode that's encoded as an audio signal.

name: wav-info-tag-writer
description: Writes a LIST/INFO metadata chunk (artist, title, comment, copyright) into a WAV file.
example_prompt: Add title and copyright INFO tags to this WAV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: inserts a well-formed LIST INFO chunk into the RIFF structure, client-side.
rationale: WAV deliverables for broadcast and libraries often require embedded INFO metadata.

name: wav-cue-chunk-writer
description: Adds a 'cue ' chunk of marker points (with optional labels) at specified sample positions in a WAV.
example_prompt: Add cue markers at 2s and 5s to this WAV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: encodes cue points and an associated labl list into the RIFF tree locally.
rationale: Editors and samplers read embedded cue markers, which most generators don't write.

name: flac-vorbis-comment-writer
description: Writes or edits Vorbis comment metadata fields on FLAC and Ogg files.
example_prompt: Set the ARTIST and TITLE Vorbis comments on this FLAC
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: rewrites the Vorbis comment metadata block without touching audio frames, no server.
rationale: FLAC/Ogg tagging complements the existing read-only reader and is essential for library curation.

name: wav-channel-mapping-rewriter
description: Reorders or remaps channels in a multichannel WAV (e.g. swap L/R or reorder 5.1 streams).
example_prompt: Swap the left and right channels in this WAV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: permutes channel slots within each interleaved frame, no decoding libs.
rationale: Surround and multitrack files frequently arrive with the wrong channel order for the target system.

name: ellipsis-dash-normalizer
description: Normalizes ellipses ('...' ↔ '…') and dashes ('--' ↔ '—', spaced hyphens ↔ en dashes) to a chosen consistent style.
example_prompt: Make all the dashes and ellipses in this consistent as em dashes and …
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM punctuation pattern rewrite; runs locally
rationale: Mixed dash and ellipsis conventions look unprofessional, and standardizing them by hand is finicky.

name: video-vignette
description: Applies a soft darkened vignette around the edges of a video to draw focus to the center.
example_prompt: Add a subtle vignette to this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's vignette filter runs in ffmpeg.wasm, processing frames locally.
rationale: Vignetting is a one-knob cinematic polish people apply to otherwise flat footage.

name: audio-wav-header-repair
description: Repairs corrupt or incorrect WAV headers (wrong size fields, missing fmt chunk).
example_prompt: This WAV won't open — fix its broken header.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM rewrites RIFF/fmt/data chunk fields from the actual byte stream.
rationale: Truncated-transfer or aborted-recording WAVs are common and a header fix often fully recovers them.

name: html-id-deduplicator
description: Finds duplicate id attributes in HTML and renames collisions to make ids unique.
example_prompt: Find and fix the duplicate IDs in this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tree scan + rename pass; fully local logic.
rationale: Duplicate ids silently break anchors, label-for, and scripts, and they're invisible until something fails.

name: json-number-round
description: Rounds every numeric value in a JSON document to a chosen number of decimal places.
example_prompt: round all the numbers in this JSON to 2 decimals
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tree walk over serde_json values; in-memory, client-side.
rationale: Long floating-point tails bloat JSON and obscure diffs; rounding cleans them up.

name: csv-value-clamper
description: Clamps a numeric column so every value falls within a specified [min, max] range.
example_prompt: Clamp the 'score' column to between 0 and 100
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — elementwise min/max, no network
rationale: Bounding sensor or score data into a valid range is a one-line transform users currently script by hand.

name: iptc-metadata-viewer
description: Extracts IPTC-IIM fields (caption, keywords, byline, copyright, location) from a JPEG's photoshop resource block.
example_prompt: What IPTC keywords and caption are in this JPEG?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM scans the APP13/Photoshop marker and decodes IPTC records locally with no decode of the image itself.
rationale: Stock/press photos carry IPTC that EXIF tools ignore, so it fills a real metadata gap.

name: xmp-metadata-extractor
description: Locates and pretty-prints the embedded XMP (RDF/XML) packet from an image, listing every namespace and property.
example_prompt: Pull out the XMP metadata from this image
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM finds the XMP packet markers in the byte stream and parses the XML locally.
rationale: Editing apps store ratings, edit history and rights in XMP that no EXIF tool surfaces.

name: video-creation-time-reader
description: Reports the container creation and modification timestamps from the mvhd/mdhd atoms in human-readable form.
example_prompt: When was this mp4 actually created according to its metadata?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: decodes the 1904-epoch fields from mvhd directly, pure integer conversion.
rationale: Filesystem dates lie after copying; the embedded creation time is the reliable record and easy to miss.

name: subtitle-format-detector
description: Identifies whether a subtitle file is SRT, WebVTT, ASS/SSA, SAMI, or SBV from its structure regardless of extension.
example_prompt: What subtitle format is this file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pattern-matches the text header/structure locally with no network.
rationale: Mislabeled or extensionless subtitle files break players, and a reliable detector tells you what you actually have.

name: wav-cue-reader
description: Reads WAV cue points and associated labels/notes from the cue and LIST/adtl chunks and lists them with timestamps.
example_prompt: List the marker cue points stored in this wav
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the cue and adtl chunks from raw bytes; runs in-browser.
rationale: Markers carry edit/loop information that's otherwise invisible without a DAW.

name: sibilance-analyzer
description: Measures energy in the 5–10 kHz sibilance band over time to locate harsh 's'/'sh' sounds for de-essing.
example_prompt: Find the sibilant spots in this vocal recording
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM band-energy FFT DSP on PCM (ffmpeg decodes); fully local.
rationale: Pinpointing sibilance lets editors de-ess surgically instead of dulling the whole track.

name: subtitle-timing-analyzer
description: Analyzes SRT/VTT subtitles for overlapping cues, large gaps, and reading-speed (chars-per-second) violations.
example_prompt: check this srt file for timing and reading-speed problems
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM subtitle parser; timing math is local
rationale: Subtitlers need to catch unreadable or overlapping cues before publishing.

name: video-frame-difference-report
description: Computes a frame-to-frame change metric across the video and outputs the curve as CSV/JSON to find motion and activity peaks.
example_prompt: Give me a per-frame motion/change curve for this surveillance clip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader's tblend/signalstats difference computation runs during decode, client-side.
rationale: A raw change-over-time signal lets users find activity in long static footage without a full scene-detection cut list.

name: number-range-expander
description: Expands compact range expressions like '1-5,8,10-12' into a full list, and collapses lists back into ranges.
example_prompt: Expand the page range 3-7,9,12-14 into individual page numbers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — integer parsing and set math only.
rationale: smenu interprets numeric ranges; expanding/collapsing ranges is a recurring need for page selections, ID lists, and batch jobs.

name: webgpu-benchmark
description: Run a GPU compute shader workload and report throughput (GFLOPS) and memory bandwidth for the user's graphics device.
example_prompt: benchmark my gpu's compute performance
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute loader dispatches an FMA/matmul shader on the local adapter and times it; runs entirely on the user's GPU via the browser WebGPU stack.
rationale: Captures the amdgpu-top spirit (knowing your GPU's real-world performance) using the one system resource a browser tool can actually exercise.

name: forwarded-header-parser
description: Parses X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Proto/Host, and RFC 7239 Forwarded header chains into the real client IP and an ordered list of proxy hops.
example_prompt: Who's the real client IP behind these proxy headers? X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7, 70.41.3.18, 150.172.238.178
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string parsing of header chains; pure compute, fully offline.
rationale: Recovering the true client identity behind reverse proxies (pingora/rama/g3proxy) is a constant ops debugging chore with no existing tool.

name: to-ci-regex
description: Converts a literal string into a case-insensitive regex pattern (e.g. cat → [Cc][Aa][Tt]).
example_prompt: turn 'error' into a case-insensitive regex
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: building the character-class pattern is pure string assembly with no external regex engine needed.
rationale: Hand-writing case-insensitive patterns for engines without an /i flag is tedious and error-prone.

name: duration-humanizer
description: Converts between human durations (e.g. '1h30m') and raw seconds/milliseconds, in both directions.
example_prompt: how many seconds is 2h 15m 30s
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; duration parsing and formatting are pure computation.
rationale: Translating timeouts, delays, and durations between formats is a frequent dev and config task.

name: tlv-parser
description: Parses generic Type-Length-Value (BER-TLV / EMV-style) hex into a nested tag tree with decoded lengths.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — recursive length-prefixed byte walker, fully client-side
rationale: Smartcard/EMV and protocol engineers debug TLV blobs constantly, and a local parser avoids leaking payment data.

name: adsb-message-decoder
description: Decodes raw Mode-S/ADS-B hex messages into aircraft ICAO address, callsign, altitude, and position.
example_prompt: Decode this ADS-B message: 8D4840D6202CC371C32CE0576098
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM bit-field/CPR decoding; runs in-browser.
rationale: ADS-B Exchange feeds raw frames that hobbyists need decoded without a server-side decoder.

name: sql-keyword-case
description: Uppercases (or lowercases) only the reserved keywords in a SQL statement while leaving identifiers and strings untouched.
example_prompt: make all the sql keywords uppercase but leave my table names alone
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizes SQL and case-folds keyword tokens locally
rationale: Enforces a house style on SQL without a full reformatter that may rewrite layout.

name: non-ascii-escape
description: Escapes every non-ASCII character in text to its \uXXXX (or \xNN) form, or reverses it.
example_prompt: escape all the non-ascii characters in this string to unicode escapes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans code points above 0x7F and rewrites them as escapes in-browser
rationale: ASCII-only channels (some configs, legacy tooling) require escaped Unicode that's tedious to produce.

name: valgrind-output-parser
description: Parses Valgrind/Memcheck output into structured errors (kind, message, stack) and a leak summary by category.
example_prompt: Parse this Valgrind output and summarize the memory leaks.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; parses the ==pid== prefixed error/leak blocks textually, fully client-side.
rationale: Valgrind dumps are verbose; a structured error/leak summary turns noise into a prioritized fix list.

name: rdfa-extractor
description: Extracts RDFa annotations (vocab, typeof, property) from an HTML page into a structured JSON-LD-style object graph.
example_prompt: Pull the RDFa data out of this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML parse plus RDFa attribute resolution; runs entirely in the sandbox on the pasted markup.
rationale: RDFa is a distinct structured-data format from microdata/JSON-LD with no extractor in the catalog, and reading it by eye is error-prone.

name: qoi-encoder
description: Encodes a PNG or JPEG into the fast lossless QOI format.
example_prompt: convert this image to qoi
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM qoi crate; the format is trivially simple and pure-byte
rationale: QOI encodes near-instantly and is popular in game/graphics tooling with almost no existing converters.

name: uuid-format-converter
description: Converts a UUID between hyphenated, raw hex, URN, Base64, and 128-bit integer forms and reports its version and variant.
example_prompt: convert this uuid to its raw bytes and tell me the version
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; UUID parsing and reformatting is local string/byte manipulation.
rationale: Devs constantly reshape UUIDs for DBs, URLs, and APIs, and decoding version/variant is genuinely fiddly by hand.

name: permissions-policy-generator
description: Generates a Permissions-Policy (formerly Feature-Policy) header controlling camera, geolocation, microphone, and other features per origin.
example_prompt: Make a Permissions-Policy that disables geolocation and camera but allows fullscreen self
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — maps feature/allowlist pairs to the structured-header syntax, offline.
rationale: The structured allowlist syntax is unintuitive and a generator prevents subtle quoting mistakes.

name: video-motion-difference-compare
description: Compares the per-segment motion-intensity profiles of two videos to show where motion energy differs between versions.
example_prompt: Compare the motion intensity over time between the original and the stabilized version
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM extracts inter-frame difference energy per file locally and a plain-Rust block diffs the two profiles.
rationale: Comparing motion profiles reveals the effect of stabilization, frame-blending, or interpolation that a single-file graph can't contextualize.

name: docker-compose-diff
description: Diffs two docker-compose files and reports added/removed services and per-service changes to image, ports, environment, volumes, and depends_on.
example_prompt: Compare these two docker-compose.yml files and summarize the service changes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses both YAML files into the compose schema and diffs structurally in-browser; no Docker engine involved.
rationale: Compose-file review is error-prone (ports/env drift), and the catalog only has compose validators/visualizers, not a two-file diff.

name: nginx-config-diff
description: Diffs two nginx configurations and reports changes at the server-block, location, and directive level rather than as raw text lines.
example_prompt: Compare these two nginx.conf files and show what routing changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizes both configs into the nginx directive tree and diffs semantically in-browser; it is pure text parsing.
rationale: A semantic nginx diff catches real routing/upstream changes that a line diff buries, and only single-file nginx parsers/linters exist today.

name: pdf-form-diff
description: Compares the AcroForm field values of two filled PDFs and reports which form fields changed, were added, or were cleared.
example_prompt: Compare the filled fields in these two PDF forms and show what changed
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs pypdf to extract form-field dictionaries from both PDFs and diffs them by field name in the browser sandbox; no server upload.
rationale: Comparing two versions of a filled form (contracts, applications) is common, and the catalog has single-PDF form extractors but no field-level diff.

name: csv-to-libsvm-converter
description: Converts a dense numeric CSV with a label column into sparse LIBSVM format.
example_prompt: Convert this CSV to LIBSVM with column 1 as the label
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; non-zero extraction and 1-based index emission.
rationale: Feeding tabular data to LIBSVM or XGBoost CLIs needs exact sparse formatting.

name: jpeg-comment-editor
description: Reads and sets the JPEG COM comment marker without re-encoding pixels.
example_prompt: read the embedded comment in this jpeg
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans JPEG markers and rewrites the COM segment in place
rationale: The JPEG comment marker carries notes and watermark text that no existing tool can view or edit losslessly.

name: icc-profile-embed
description: Embeds a supplied ICC color profile into an image without altering pixel values.
example_prompt: tag this image with the Display P3 profile
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM injects the ICC payload into the appropriate marker/chunk
rationale: Assigning the correct color profile is essential for accurate print/wide-gamut output and no tool offers it client-side.

name: svg-currentcolor
description: Replaces hardcoded fill/stroke colors in an SVG with currentColor for CSS theming.
example_prompt: make this svg icon inherit text color via currentColor
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM rewrites color attributes in the SVG text
rationale: Themeable icons must use currentColor, and converting fixed-color exports is a frequent, finicky design-system task.

name: video-color-range-tag
description: Tags a video as full (PC) or limited (TV) color range without re-encoding pixels.
example_prompt: Tag this video as limited (TV) color range
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg-wasm rewrites the color-range metadata flag via stream copy in-browser.
rationale: Mistagged color range causes washed-out or crushed playback and is a pure metadata fix.

name: video-color-primaries-tag
description: Sets color primaries, transfer characteristics, and matrix coefficients (e.g. bt709, bt2020) metadata.
example_prompt: Tag this video with bt709 color metadata
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg-wasm writes the color-description flags during a local copy/encode.
rationale: Untagged color metadata leads to wrong-gamut playback; setting it correctly is essential and absent.

name: video-set-bframes
description: Re-encodes with a chosen number of B-frames (including zero) in the GOP structure.
example_prompt: Re-encode this with zero B-frames for low-latency
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg-wasm passes -bf during a local encode.
rationale: B-frames affect latency and decoder compatibility; controlling them is a distinct encoding knob not yet exposed.

name: video-set-sample-aspect-ratio
description: Sets the pixel/sample aspect ratio (SAR) flag to mark anamorphic content correctly.
example_prompt: Set this DVD rip's pixel aspect ratio to anamorphic
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg-wasm applies setsar metadata via stream copy locally.
rationale: Anamorphic DVD/broadcast footage looks squished without the right SAR flag.

name: video-language-tag-set
description: Sets ISO language tags on audio and subtitle tracks so players label them correctly.
example_prompt: Tag the second audio track in this mkv as Spanish
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg-wasm writes per-stream language metadata via stream copy locally.
rationale: Untagged tracks show as 'unknown' and break audio/subtitle auto-selection.

name: video-creation-time-set
description: Sets or corrects the creation_time metadata field on a video file.
example_prompt: Set this clip's creation date to 2024-01-15
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg-wasm writes the creation_time tag via stream copy locally.
rationale: Correct creation dates matter for chronological sorting in photo/video libraries.

name: mediawiki-to-markdown
description: Converts MediaWiki markup (headings, links, templates, lists, tables) into Markdown.
example_prompt: convert this Wikipedia wikitext to markdown
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM wikitext tokenizer → Markdown emitter; fully client-side
rationale: Migrating wiki content to Markdown repos/docs is common and otherwise manual.

name: hmm-sequence-decoder
description: Fits a hidden Markov model to an observation sequence and decodes the most-likely hidden states with Viterbi.
example_prompt: Find the hidden states behind this observation sequence
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — forward-backward, Baum-Welch, and Viterbi are small dynamic-programming routines.
rationale: HMM decoding is the standard tool for sequence segmentation (bioinformatics, sensor states, finance regimes) and runs fast locally.

name: wcag-image-contrast-checker
description: Detects text regions in an image and checks their text/background contrast ratio against WCAG AA/AAA thresholds.
example_prompt: Does the text on this banner meet WCAG contrast?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime locates text and plain Rust→WASM computes WCAG contrast ratios, all client-side.
rationale: Text baked into images escapes normal accessibility tooling and a dedicated checker closes that gap.

name: eth-tx-decoder
description: Decodes a raw signed Ethereum transaction into its fields (nonce, gas, to, value, calldata, signature).
example_prompt: Decode this raw transaction: 0x02f86b01...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — RLP-decodes the envelope and parses typed (EIP-1559/2930) fields locally.
rationale: Inspecting a broadcast-ready raw tx before sending is a key safety/debug step that should never require a remote node.

name: video-web-playback-compatibility-checker
description: Flags codecs, containers, pixel formats, and color ranges (HEVC, ProRes, yuv422p, 10-bit, MKV) that won't play natively in mainstream browsers.
example_prompt: Will this video play in a browser, or do I need to re-encode it?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm probes streams and a rules table maps them to browser support matrices; all evaluation happens in the browser.
rationale: Creators repeatedly ship videos that fail in browsers, and a one-shot compatibility verdict saves the re-encode round-trip.

name: video-audio-video-duration-mismatch-checker
description: Compares the audio and video track durations and flags mismatches beyond a tolerance that indicate truncation or sync problems.
example_prompt: Do the audio and video tracks in this file have the same duration?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm probes each track's duration and the tool diffs them; metadata comparison, fully in the browser.
rationale: A track-duration mismatch is a clear, cheap signal of a botched export or truncated capture that otherwise only shows up at the very end of playback.

name: video-chapter-coverage-checker
description: Validates that chapter markers span the full timeline in order with no gaps, overlaps, out-of-range, or zero-length chapters.
example_prompt: Do the chapters in this video cover the whole timeline without gaps or overlaps?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (or ffmpeg.wasm chapter probe) reads chapter start/end times and checks ordering and coverage; client-side.
rationale: Broken chapter ranges produce confusing player navigation, and validating coverage is distinct from merely reading or extracting chapters.

name: video-subtitle-cue-overlap-checker
description: Inspects an embedded subtitle/caption track for cues whose times overlap, run out of order, or have zero/negative duration.
example_prompt: Check this video's embedded subtitle track for overlapping or out-of-order cues.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM extracts the subtitle track samples and validates cue timing intervals; pure parsing, browser-local.
rationale: Overlapping cues flash or stack incorrectly during playback, and validating cue timing inside the container is distinct from comparing or detecting tracks.

name: robots-txt-validator
description: Validates robots.txt syntax and answers whether a given URL path is allowed or disallowed for a specified user-agent.
example_prompt: Is /admin/ blocked for Googlebot in this robots.txt?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM implementing the robots.txt grammar and longest-match precedence rules; pure parsing.
rationale: robots.txt precedence rules are subtle and a validator-plus-tester prevents accidental crawl blocking or exposure.

name: rut-validator
description: Validates a Chilean RUT/RUN tax ID's mod-11 verifier digit (0-9 or K).
example_prompt: Is RUT 12.345.678-5 valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: cyclic 2-7 weight sum mod 11, pure integer math.
rationale: RUT entry is ubiquitous in Chilean systems and the mod-11 rule is error-prone to do by hand.

name: macos-iconset-generator
description: Generates a macOS .iconset folder (all @1x/@2x sizes) from a single source image, ready to compile into an .icns.
example_prompt: Make a macOS iconset from this 1024 image
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — produce the named-size PNG set and zip it; resampling done client-side.
rationale: macOS app developers need the exact .iconset naming and currently script it by hand.

name: maskable-pwa-icon-generator
description: Generates Android/PWA maskable icons by fitting a source logo inside the safe zone with a chosen background, at all manifest sizes.
example_prompt: Make maskable PWA icons from this logo with a white safe-zone background
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pad to the maskable safe zone and resample to each size; offline.
rationale: Maskable icons are a specific PWA correctness requirement that favicon packages don't satisfy.

name: app-store-screenshot-framer
description: Generates App Store / Play Store listing screenshots: device-framed screenshot plus a headline caption on a branded background, at required store sizes.
example_prompt: Make a 6.7-inch App Store screenshot: this screen framed with caption 'Track everything'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — frame the screenshot, render the caption, and emit each required store dimension; offline.
rationale: Store-listing screenshots are a real chore with strict size specs and no offline generator exists.

name: punctuation-deduplicator
description: Collapses runs of repeated punctuation (e.g. '!!!' → '!', ',,' → ',') to a single mark.
example_prompt: Tone down the repeated exclamation marks in this text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: regex collapse of punctuation runs, no network
rationale: Cleaning informal or scraped text for publishing means normalizing exaggerated punctuation.

name: clustal-to-fasta
description: Converts CLUSTAL .aln multiple-alignment output (with its conservation lines and wrapped blocks) into aligned FASTA preserving gaps.
example_prompt: Convert this Clustal .aln file to aligned FASTA
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses the wrapped CLUSTAL block layout and reassembles per-sequence rows locally.
rationale: ClustalW/Omega output is the most common alignment format students paste, but downstream tools want FASTA, and the conservation-line stripping is fiddly.

name: las-well-log-to-csv
description: Parses LAS 2.0 ASCII well-log files (Version/Well/Curve/ASCII sections) into a CSV of depth-indexed curve readings with NULL sentinel handling.
example_prompt: Convert this LAS well log file to CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: sectioned-text parser that reads the ~CURVE header and ~ASCII data block locally.
rationale: Geoscience and petrophysics LAS logs are plain text but the sentinel-null and curve-mnemonic handling makes naive CSV exports wrong; no tool covers it.

name: gaussian-quantile-transformer
description: Maps a numeric column to a standard normal distribution via its empirical quantiles (rank-to-normal transform).
example_prompt: Quantile-transform this column to a normal distribution
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: sort, compute empirical CDF, apply inverse-normal CDF approximation, all in-memory
rationale: Quantile normalization to Gaussian is a robust nonparametric transform used heavily in ML feature prep and is not a percentile-rank lookup.

name: clip-to-range
description: Clamps every value in a column into a user-specified [min,max] interval without rescaling.
example_prompt: Clamp this column to between 0 and 255
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: element-wise min/max clamp, no dependencies
rationale: Hard clamping to fixed bounds is a common, distinct cleanup step from percentile winsorizing or rescaling.

name: hampel-despike
description: Despikes a 1-D series with a Hampel filter, replacing points that deviate >k·MAD from a rolling median.
example_prompt: Despike this sensor series with a Hampel filter, window 7
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: sliding-window median and MAD, pure numeric loops
rationale: The Hampel filter is the go-to robust spike remover for noisy time series and no existing smoother does median+MAD detection.

name: lag-shift-column
description: Shifts a column forward or backward by k positions to create lag/lead features, with configurable fill value.
example_prompt: Add a lag-1 version of the sales column
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: index shift and pad, all in-memory
rationale: Lag/lead feature creation is a core time-series preprocessing step missing from the catalog.

name: pad-or-truncate-series
description: Forces a numeric sequence to a fixed length by padding (with a value, edge, or reflection) or truncating.
example_prompt: Pad this list to length 128 with zeros
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: append or slice, no dependencies
rationale: Fixed-length padding/truncation is a routine prep step for batched ML input that nothing in the catalog handles.

name: html-toc-generator
description: Generates a nested table-of-contents list with anchor links and injects matching id slugs into the headings.
example_prompt: build a table of contents from the headings in this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML parsing of h1-h6 and slug generation; distinct from the heading-outline viewer.
rationale: Long docs need a clickable ToC and doing it by hand keeps anchors and slugs out of sync.

name: fake-person-generator
description: Generates synthetic identities (name, email, phone, address, birthdate) for testing, in batches and locales.
example_prompt: Generate 20 fake US identities with name, email, and address
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: embeds locale name/street lists and composes records with host RNG; nothing leaves the browser.
rationale: Realistic test personas are needed for QA and demos, and privacy means they must never touch a server.

name: json-highlight
description: Renders JSON as syntax-highlighted HTML with colored keys, strings, numbers, and structure.
example_prompt: show this JSON with syntax highlighting
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizer emitting span-wrapped HTML (JsonHilo-style); no rendering engine needed beyond the chat's HTML.
rationale: Colorized output makes large JSON readable in chat and mirrors the JsonHilo highlighter demand.

name: serp-preview
description: Render a Google search-result (SERP) snippet preview from a title, URL, and meta description, flagging length truncation.
example_prompt: preview how this title and description will look in Google results
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM render to image/HTML; local.
rationale: SEOs constantly preview SERP snippets; existing tools render OG/social cards, not search results.

name: gpx-validate
description: Validates GPX file structure and sanity-checks tracks, segments, and waypoints.
example_prompt: Is this GPX file valid? Flag any malformed tracks
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML parse plus schema checks; client-side
rationale: Complements the existing GPX merge/split tools with an integrity gate.

name: arxiv-citation-formatter
description: Parses a pasted arXiv abstract or metadata block into a BibTeX, APA, or MLA citation.
example_prompt: Make a BibTeX entry from this arXiv abstract page
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM extracts title, authors, ID, and year from the pasted text and formats citations locally.
rationale: cli-arxiv users grab papers to cite them, and citation formatting works fully offline on provided metadata.

name: json-to-sequence-diagram
description: Turns a JSON array of events or messages into a Mermaid sequence diagram.
example_prompt: Make a sequence diagram from this JSON list of API calls
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM mapping event records to Mermaid syntax — rendered client-side, no network.
rationale: Visualizing a captured request/event log as an interaction diagram makes traces far easier to reason about.

name: long-line-finder
description: Lists every line that exceeds a configurable character or display-width limit, with the overflow amount.
example_prompt: Find all lines longer than 80 characters in this code.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; counts grapheme/column width per line locally.
rationale: Enforcing line-length limits before a linter run or print/PDF export is a constant code-and-docs chore.

name: magic-number-finder
description: Flags unnamed numeric literals in source code that should likely be named constants.
example_prompt: find the magic numbers in this code
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM lexing the source and filtering literals; no runtime.
rationale: A focused readability lint distinct from broad complexity scoring.

name: naming-convention-linter
description: Checks identifier casing consistency (camelCase, snake_case, etc.) and reports outliers.
example_prompt: check naming consistency in this file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM extracting identifiers and classifying their casing.
rationale: Catches style drift in code that no formatter normalizes for naming.

name: json-size-analyzer
description: Ranks JSON keys, arrays, and values by serialized byte size to find what bloats a payload.
example_prompt: what's taking up the most space in this json?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM measuring each subtree's serialized length.
rationale: Pinpoints payload-shrinking opportunities for APIs and configs.

name: xml-attribute-sorter
description: Sorts attributes on every XML element into canonical order for stable, diff-friendly documents.
example_prompt: Sort the attributes on each element in this XML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses elements and re-emits attributes sorted, preserving namespaces; client-side only
rationale: Canonicalizing attribute order makes machine-generated XML (configs, feeds) reviewable in version control.

name: lottie-to-gif
description: Render a Lottie (Bodymovin JSON) animation to an animated GIF, MP4, or WebM.
example_prompt: convert this Lottie animation JSON to a GIF
loader_feasibility: rlottie-wasm frame rendering plus ffmpeg encoding, client-side.
rationale: Designers share Lottie files but often need a GIF/video fallback.

name: end-screen-generator
description: Generates a YouTube-style end-screen template clip with placeholder boxes for a subscribe button and recommended videos.
example_prompt: Make a 20-second end screen with two video boxes and a subscribe area on a soft gradient
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg composes the layout from `color`, `drawbox`, and `drawtext` lavfi filters procedurally in-browser.
rationale: A correctly-timed 20-second end screen is required for YouTube interactive cards and is tedious to build by hand each upload.

name: countdown-to-date-video
description: Generates a clip showing a fixed days/hours/minutes/seconds countdown ticking toward a target event.
example_prompt: Make a 60-second countdown video ending at zero for our product launch reveal
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust computes the per-second labels and ffmpeg renders them with `drawtext` over a chosen background in-browser.
rationale: Launch and event countdowns are a recurring promo asset and a generator beats stitching one together by hand each time.

name: hash-commitment
description: Creates a hash commitment to a value with a random nonce and later verifies a reveal against it.
example_prompt: make a commitment to the value "7" and give me the nonce to reveal later
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using RustCrypto hashes + CSPRNG nonce; pure local computation.
rationale: Commit-reveal is the practical browser-local slice of the cryptoballot demand and useful for fair draws, auctions, and games.

name: cross-validation-scorer
description: Runs k-fold cross-validation for a chosen sklearn model and reports per-fold and mean scores with variance.
example_prompt: Run 5-fold cross-validation of a random forest on this dataset
loader_feasibility: pyodide with scikit-learn; cross_val_score executes in the Pyodide WASM sandbox.
rationale: Cross-validation is the central honest-evaluation practice from 'Managing ML Projects'.

name: latam-id-validator
description: Validates Latin American national/tax IDs (Brazil CPF/CNPJ, Chile RUT, Mexico CURP) via their check digits.
example_prompt: Validate this Brazilian CPF number
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM checksum logic per ID scheme, entirely client-side.
rationale: latamdata-py demand maps to identity validation that is pure checksum logic, ideal in-browser.

name: dockerfile-layer-analyzer
description: Statically estimates image layer count and ordering from a Dockerfile and flags cache-busting sequences and oversized COPYs.
example_prompt: Analyze the layers and caching in this Dockerfile: [paste Dockerfile]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM static parse and heuristic layer model; no daemon or image pull needed.
rationale: dive's layer insight requires a built image; a static approximation gives most of the value before you ever build.

name: soft-hyphen-remover
description: Removes soft hyphens and optional-break characters left over from justified PDF or Word text.
example_prompt: Strip the soft hyphens out of this copied PDF text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — targeted U+00AD removal, fully local
