rationale: Soft hyphens from justified layouts split words invisibly and wreck search and copy-paste.

name: image-feather-edges
description: Fades the image edges to transparency for soft-edge compositing and badges.
example_prompt: Feather the edges of this cutout so it blends smoothly
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: distance-to-edge alpha ramp applied to the buffer.
rationale: Soft vignette-free edge blending for overlays and stickers.

name: audio-speed-changer
description: Changes playback speed varispeed-style so both tempo and pitch shift together (like a record at the wrong RPM).
example_prompt: Speed this clip up by 10% with the chipmunk pitch effect
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — `asetrate` resamples to change speed and pitch in lockstep; runs in ffmpeg.wasm.
rationale: Varispeed is distinct from pitch-preserving stretch and is exactly what people want for tape-style speed effects or RPM correction.

name: audio-volume-envelope
description: Applies a user-defined volume automation curve (keyframed gain over time) across a clip.
example_prompt: Fade this clip down to -10dB at 0:15, hold, then back up at 0:25
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — time-keyed `volume` expression / chained `afade` segments, or a plain Rust→WASM gain-curve pass on PCM; both client-side.
rationale: Multi-point volume rides go beyond a single fade and let users shape level changes anywhere in a clip without a full DAW.

name: audio-bpm-fit
description: Time-stretches a clip to a target BPM (from a known source BPM) without changing pitch.
example_prompt: Stretch this 120 BPM loop to match my 128 BPM track
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — compute the tempo ratio and apply chained `atempo`, all in ffmpeg.wasm.
rationale: Matching a sample/loop to a project tempo is a core DJ/producer task and BPM-parameterized stretching is far handier than a raw percentage.

name: audio-dropout-repair
description: Detects short dropouts and digital glitches and fills the gaps by interpolating surrounding samples.
example_prompt: Fix the brief audio dropouts in this Bluetooth recording
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — locate near-zero/discontinuity gaps in decoded PCM and patch with interpolation/short crossfades; deterministic and local.
rationale: Wireless and streaming captures suffer momentary dropouts, and gap interpolation salvages otherwise-ruined takes — distinct from declick/declip.

name: quote-unwrapper
description: Removes surrounding quotes from each line and unescapes inner escaped quotes and characters.
example_prompt: Strip the surrounding quotes off each of these quoted strings
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM per-line quote detection and unescape; in-sandbox
rationale: Lists copied as quoted string literals need de-quoting before reuse, a fiddly manual task at scale.

name: quantile-normalizer
description: Quantile-normalizes several numeric columns so they share an identical reference value distribution.
example_prompt: Quantile-normalize these sample columns to the same distribution
loader_feasibility: pyodide — numpy rank+interp in the Python sandbox, client-side
rationale: Quantile normalization is essential in genomics/benchmarking and has no lightweight browser tool.

name: reciprocal-transformer
description: Applies a reciprocal (1/x) or general power (x^p) transform to a column with configurable zero handling.
example_prompt: Take the reciprocal of this column, treating zeros as blank
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — elementwise power, fully local
rationale: Reciprocal/power transforms are common in physics and regression with no safe bulk tool for zeros.

name: cumulative-product-builder
description: Computes a running cumulative product or cumulative max/min along a numeric column.
example_prompt: Compute the cumulative product of these growth factors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sequential accumulation, no network
rationale: Compounding returns and survival curves need cumulative products that spreadsheets handle clumsily.

name: wrap-angle-normalizer
description: Wraps an angle column into a canonical range such as [0,360), [-180,180), or [0,2π).
example_prompt: Wrap these headings into the 0–360 degree range
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — modulo wrapping, fully local
rationale: Heading/bearing data drifts outside its range and needs normalization in navigation and robotics.

name: tsne-projector
description: Projects high-dimensional CSV rows or vectors down to a 2-D t-SNE embedding for visualization.
example_prompt: Make a t-SNE plot of this dataset
loader_feasibility: pyodide — scikit-learn's TSNE runs entirely in the in-browser Python sandbox on numpy arrays.
rationale: t-SNE is the go-to method for seeing cluster structure in high-dimensional data and has no good privacy-preserving local option today.

name: pixelation-region-detector
description: Locates deliberately pixelated or mosaic-censored regions by finding areas of unnaturally uniform blocks.
example_prompt: Which parts of this screenshot have been pixelated/censored?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM detects block-aligned uniform regions distinct from the surrounding detail locally.
rationale: Useful for auditing whether sensitive areas were actually redacted and where, fully privately.

name: alpha-edge-fringe-detector
description: Inspects semi-transparent edges for color fringing or halos left by bad matting against a wrong background.
example_prompt: Does this cutout PNG have ugly edge fringing?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM examines color values at partial-alpha boundary pixels locally.
rationale: Fringe halos are a common cutout-quality defect that's easy to miss until placed on a new background.

name: video-xmp-metadata-extractor
description: Extracts the embedded XMP packet from a video and presents its fields as readable key/value pairs.
example_prompt: Pull the XMP metadata out of this video file
loader_feasibility: A Rust parser locates and decodes the XMP UUID/box payload from the in-browser buffer.
rationale: XMP carries authorship, edit history, and rights data that standard tag readers ignore.

name: subtitle-reading-speed-checker
description: Computes characters-per-second for each subtitle cue and flags ones that exceed readability guidelines.
example_prompt: Are any of my subtitles too fast to read?
loader_feasibility: A Rust parser reads SRT/VTT/ASS timings and text and computes CPS entirely in WASM.
rationale: Over-fast cues are the top accessibility note from QC reviewers and are trivial to flag automatically.

name: image-stack-mean
description: Averages a burst of aligned images to reduce random noise and produce a cleaner composite.
example_prompt: Average these handheld night shots to cut down the noise.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM accumulates and divides per-pixel sums across the stack locally.
rationale: Frame averaging is the simplest, most reliable noise reduction for a steady burst and runs fine in WASM.

name: video-content-trim-detector
description: Detects leading and trailing trims between two cuts of the same footage by matching audio/frame fingerprints at the boundaries.
example_prompt: Figure out how much was trimmed off the start and end of edit-v2 compared to edit-v1
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM extracts boundary fingerprints locally and a plain-Rust block aligns them to report trim amounts.
rationale: Editors constantly need to know exactly where one cut was shortened relative to another, which no single-file tool can answer.

name: video-perceptual-hash-timeline-diff
description: Computes a perceptual hash per frame for two videos and plots their per-frame Hamming distance over time to localize where content diverges.
example_prompt: Show me a timeline of where these two cuts start to differ
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM extracts frames locally and a plain-Rust DCT-based pHash plus Hamming-distance computation runs in-browser.
rationale: A per-frame divergence timeline pinpoints exactly when two versions stop matching, which a single similarity score can't localize.

name: replaygain-compare
description: Calculates ReplayGain track gain and peak for two files and compares their normalized loudness.
example_prompt: Compute and compare the ReplayGain of these two tracks
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies the ReplayGain loudness model to decoded PCM in-browser.
rationale: ReplayGain comparison shows how a player would normalize two tracks relative to each other.

name: coverage-report-diff
description: Diffs two code-coverage reports (lcov, cobertura, or coverage.json) and shows per-file line and branch coverage deltas plus newly-uncovered lines.
example_prompt: Compare coverage.xml from main against my branch and tell me if coverage dropped
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses both coverage files and computes per-file deltas locally; coverage data is just text/XML/JSON so it runs fully client-side.
rationale: "Did my PR lower coverage?" is a constant review question and the catalog only has single-report coverage viewers, not a run-to-run delta.

name: junit-results-diff
description: Compares two JUnit XML test reports and lists newly-failing, newly-fixed, and newly-skipped tests along with per-test duration changes.
example_prompt: Diff these two junit.xml files and show which tests started failing
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses both JUnit XML trees and matches testcases by classname+name in-browser; no test runner required.
rationale: Pinpointing which tests flipped between two runs is far faster than re-reading logs, and only single-file JUnit viewers/summarizers exist today.

name: iam-policy-diff
description: Diffs two IAM policy documents (AWS/GCP JSON) and reports statements, actions, resources, and conditions added or removed, flagging privilege escalations.
example_prompt: Compare these two IAM policies and tell me if the new one grants more access
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses both policy JSON documents and diffs the statement/action sets in-browser; policy evaluation is offline.
rationale: "Does this change widen permissions?" is a security-critical review, and the catalog has only single-policy linters/explainers.

name: effective-config-diff
description: Resolves two layered configuration sets (each base + overrides, with precedence) into their effective values and diffs the resolved results.
example_prompt: Resolve and compare the effective config for staging vs prod from these layered files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM merges each layer stack by precedence then diffs the flattened key/value maps in-browser; pure data merging.
rationale: Comparing raw config files misses overrides; diffing the *effective* result is what actually answers "why does prod behave differently?"

name: budget-variance-report
description: Compares a budget CSV against an actuals CSV by line item and produces absolute and percentage variances with over/under-budget flags.
example_prompt: Compare my budget vs actuals spreadsheets and show the biggest variances
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM joins both CSVs on the account/line key and computes variances in-browser; it is arithmetic over uploaded files.
rationale: Budget-vs-actual variance is a core finance task with no dedicated tool, distinct from generic numeric diffing.

name: ap-three-way-match
description: Matches purchase-order, goods-receipt, and invoice line items and flags quantity, price, and missing-document discrepancies for accounts-payable review.
example_prompt: Three-way match my PO, receipt, and invoice CSVs and show the discrepancies
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM joins all three datasets on PO/line key and applies match tolerances in-browser; it is keyed reconciliation over uploaded files.
rationale: Three-way match is the canonical AP control and is genuinely absent from the catalog's two-source reconciliation tools.

name: json-shape-diff
description: Compares only the key/type structure of two JSON objects, ignoring scalar values, to show schema-shape changes.
example_prompt: Compare the shape of these two JSON objects and ignore the actual values
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON parse + recursive shape comparison; no server
rationale: Shape-only diffing reveals structural API changes without drowning in value noise.

name: vcard-contact-diff
description: Diffs two vCard contacts field by field, highlighting changed phones, emails, and addresses.
example_prompt: What changed between these two vCard files?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses both vCards and field-diffs locally; the vcard-parse tool proves parsing works client-side.
rationale: Merging address-book exports needs to see which contact fields actually changed, with no upload of personal data.

name: todo-list-progress-diff
description: Compares two Markdown checklists and reports newly completed, newly added, and removed tasks.
example_prompt: What got checked off between these two versions of my TODO?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses task-list syntax and diffs checkbox states locally; offline.
rationale: Tracking progress between checklist snapshots is more useful than a raw line diff that obscures completion changes.

name: image-contour-extractor
description: Detects edges/contours in an image and exports them as SVG outline paths or a polyline JSON.
example_prompt: Trace the outlines in this image and give me an SVG of the contours
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Canny/Suzuki contour tracing (e.g. via `imageproc`) runs on CPU over the decoded buffer.
rationale: CNC, laser-cut, and design users need crisp vector contours from raster art, a distinct extraction task not covered by the listed filters.

name: video-timed-id3-extractor
description: Extracts timed ID3 metadata frames from HLS/MPEG-TS segments with their associated timestamps.
example_prompt: Get the timed ID3 tags out of this HLS segment
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the TS PES/ID3 packets; pure parsing, no network, client-side
rationale: Streaming workflows embed timed ID3 for ad markers and now-playing data that needs to be read back exactly.

name: replaygain-tag-reader
description: Extracts ReplayGain track/album gain and peak values from ID3, Vorbis, MP4, or APE tags and reports them in dB and linear form.
example_prompt: What ReplayGain values are stored in this track?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — reads named tag frames/comments and parses their numeric strings, no signal analysis.
rationale: Loudness-normalization metadata is invisible in most tag editors yet critical for consistent playback levels.

name: pagination-rel-link-extractor
description: Extracts rel=next, rel=prev, and rel=first/last navigation links from an HTML head or Link header to reconstruct a paginated sequence.
example_prompt: Find the next/prev pagination links in this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM head/link parsing; operates only on supplied text.
rationale: Walking a paginated archive or API requires the rel-link chain, which is tedious to spot manually across pages.

name: mp3-xing-header-writer
description: Computes and writes a correct Xing/Info VBR header so players show accurate duration and can seek.
example_prompt: Fix the duration on this VBR mp3 by adding a Xing header
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans frames, builds the Xing/Info frame, and prepends it; no re-encoding.
rationale: MP3s concatenated or cut without a Xing header show wrong length, and rewriting the header repairs it losslessly.

name: coordinate-precision-trimmer
description: Trims latitude/longitude columns to a chosen number of decimal places to shrink GeoJSON/CSV size with a stated accuracy.
example_prompt: Trim these lat/long pairs to 5 decimals
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — coordinate rounding + size report, fully local
rationale: Over-precise coordinates bloat map files and trimming to a known accuracy is a common GIS cleanup.

name: protobuf-encode
description: Encodes a simple field spec (field number, wire type, value) into Protocol Buffers wire bytes.
example_prompt: Encode field 1 as varint 150 and field 2 as string 'hi' into protobuf bytes
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust wire-format writer in WASM; no dependencies, runs locally.
rationale: Crafting protobuf payloads by hand for testing is otherwise tedious and error-prone.

name: extract-audio-metadata
description: Reads tags and technical info (bitrate, sample rate, channels, duration) from MP3/FLAC/OGG/M4A/WAV.
example_prompt: What's the bitrate and duration of this flac?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via lofty reading container headers only; no full decode, fully offline.
rationale: Generalizes ID3 to every common audio format, covering the broad 'audio metadata' demand in one tool.

name: option-greeks-calculator
description: Computes Delta, Gamma, Theta, Vega, and Rho for a European option.
example_prompt: Give me the Greeks for a put: spot 50, strike 48, vol 30%, rate 3%, 60 days to expiry
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; closed-form derivatives of Black-Scholes on user input, fully offline.
rationale: Traders routinely need the Greeks alongside price, and they are deterministic closed-form computations.

name: pdf-inspector
description: Inspects a PDF's structure and metadata: version, page count and sizes, fonts, embedded files, encryption status, and producer/title info.
example_prompt: What's inside this PDF — how many pages, is it encrypted, what fonts does it embed?
loader_feasibility: pyodide running pypdf reads the uploaded bytes inside the Python sandbox; no upload to any server.
rationale: Maps the pdf-inspector demand into a privacy-safe way to audit PDFs (often sensitive documents) for metadata leaks and structure issues.

name: periodic-table
description: Looks up element properties including atomic number, mass, electron configuration, group, state, and discovery.
example_prompt: tell me everything about tungsten
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with a bundled element dataset; static lookup, no network.
rationale: periodic-table-cli demand maps to a self-contained reference every student reaches for.

name: natural-date-parser
description: Parses natural-language date/time phrases into an exact ISO-8601 timestamp.
example_prompt: What's the exact date and time for 'next Friday at 3pm'?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using a temps-style NL date grammar; pure string parsing, no network or server needed.
rationale: Turning fuzzy human date phrases into machine timestamps is a constant need for scheduling, reminders, and data cleanup.

name: json-path-finder
description: Given a JSON document and a target key or value, return the JSONPath(s) that locate it.
example_prompt: Find the JSON path to the value 'expired' in this API response
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM recursive traversal; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: Locating the path to a deep value is the inverse of json-query and a real debugging convenience.

name: curl-builder
description: Build a curl command from method, URL, headers, query, and JSON/body.
example_prompt: build a curl POST to /api/login with JSON {user,pass} and a bearer token
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM string assembly; the reverse of the existing curl-convert.
rationale: Constructing curl by hand is error-prone; curl-convert only goes curl→code.

name: image-paint-by-numbers
description: Convert a photo into a paint-by-numbers template with outlined regions, numbers, and a color legend.
example_prompt: make a paint-by-numbers template from this photo with 16 colors
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM color quantization + region labeling.
rationale: A popular craft/print tool distinct from posterize and edge-detect.

name: loess-smoother
description: Applies LOESS/LOWESS local regression to smooth a noisy x,y scatter and returns the fitted trend curve with a confidence band.
example_prompt: Smooth this x,y scatter data with LOWESS and give me the trend line
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — local weighted least-squares at each query point is a small loop with no external dependencies.
rationale: Non-parametric smoothing is widely used to reveal trends in noisy data without assuming a global form.

name: binary-struct-unpacker
description: Interprets a raw byte sequence as typed fields (signed/unsigned ints, floats, widths) in chosen endianness via a format spec.
example_prompt: Read these bytes as a little-endian u32 followed by an f64
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via BurntSushi/byteorder — endian-aware reads are pure arithmetic with no server
rationale: Decoding binary protocol/file headers by hand is error-prone, and a struct unpacker gives instant correct field values offline.

name: telegram-message-builder
description: Builds a Telegram Bot API sendMessage request URL and JSON body with the chosen parse mode and keyboard.
example_prompt: build a Telegram sendMessage request with MarkdownV2 text and an inline button
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — assembles the API URL and JSON payload as strings client-side
rationale: Maps the teloxide/tbot demand: constructing Bot API calls by hand is tedious and easy to misformat.

name: script-readme-generator
description: Scans a set of uploaded scripts and builds an index README from their header comments, shebangs, and detected usage.
example_prompt: Make an index README for these scripts: [upload several .sh files]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing of leading comment blocks and usage strings across files; pure text.
rationale: tome organizes scattered scripts into a searchable collection; auto-documenting them is the offline, shareable counterpart.

name: merkle-root-calculator
description: Computes a Merkle tree root from a list of leaf hashes or values.
example_prompt: Compute the Merkle root of these hashes: 0xaa..., 0xbb..., 0xcc...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — iterative SHA-256/Keccak pairwise hashing of the leaf list runs locally.
rationale: Merkle roots back airdrops, allowlists, and block construction across Bitcoin and Ethereum; computing one offline is a recurring dev need.

name: nes-screenshot
description: Runs an uploaded NES ROM for a chosen number of frames and captures a PNG screenshot of the PPU output.
example_prompt: Boot this NES ROM and screenshot the title screen
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Rust NES cores (CPU+PPU+mappers, as in pinky/sprocketnes) compile to WASM and a one-shot run dumps a framebuffer to PNG.
rationale: Generating a ROM preview thumbnail without an interactive emulator is precisely what a one-shot chat tool can do that pinky/sprocketnes can't.

name: ms-script-decoder
description: Decodes Microsoft Script Encoder (#@~^ / screnc) encoded VBScript and JScript back to source.
example_prompt: decode this encoded VBScript
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM implementing the published screnc substitution algorithm; no external calls.
rationale: Reversing encoded legacy/malware scripts is a real forensics need with no good in-browser option.

name: ecdsa-signature-convert
description: Converts an ECDSA signature between DER (ASN.1) and raw fixed-length r||s (IEEE P1363/JOSE) formats in either direction.
example_prompt: Convert this DER ECDSA signature to raw r||s format
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the ecdsa/der crates; a pure byte reformatting with no network.
rationale: DER↔raw signature mismatches are a notorious JWT/WebAuthn interop bug and a dedicated converter fixes them fast.

name: xml-escape-unescape
description: Escapes or unescapes XML/HTML entities like &, <, and numeric character references.
example_prompt: unescape the XML entities in this string
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a small character-substitution pass, no dependencies, fully client-side.
rationale: A quick, high-frequency utility for anyone hand-editing XML or embedding markup in attributes.

name: swiss-pairing-generator
description: Generates Swiss-system pairings for the next round given current standings and prior matchups.
example_prompt: Pair round 4 of my Swiss tournament from these standings, avoid rematches
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; pairing/matching algorithm over entered standings, no server.
rationale: Swiss pairing is fiddly to do by hand and is exactly the kind of deterministic logic that belongs client-side.

name: set-cookie-builder
description: Builds a correct Set-Cookie header from a name, value, and flags (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, Max-Age).
example_prompt: build a Set-Cookie header for a secure session cookie that expires in 7 days
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — assembles and validates the header string locally
rationale: Getting SameSite/Secure/HttpOnly combinations right is error-prone and worth automating.

name: serverless-config-validator
description: Validates a serverless.yml or SAM/CloudFormation template's structure, listing functions, events, and resources plus any schema errors.
example_prompt: Validate my serverless.yml and list the functions and their triggers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: YAML/JSON parsing and structural checks run locally with no AWS calls
rationale: sls-dev-tools demand maps to catching serverless config mistakes before deploy, entirely offline.

name: gzip-base64-codec
description: Compresses text with gzip/deflate and emits it as base64, and decompresses base64 gzip back to text.
example_prompt: Gzip-compress this JSON and give me a base64 string I can share
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM via flate2 — DEFLATE runs entirely in the WASM sandbox, no network
rationale: Sharing compressed payloads in URLs or configs and decoding them is a real need with no trusted local tool.

name: arxiv-id-linker
description: Finds arXiv IDs in text and builds canonical abstract, PDF, and HTML links for each.
example_prompt: Find the arXiv IDs in this text and give me PDF links
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM regex-matches arXiv IDs in the pasted text and constructs deterministic URLs; no fetch required.
rationale: Mirrors cli-arxiv's lookup convenience by turning bare IDs scattered in notes into ready-to-open links.

name: chiptune-melody-generator
description: Renders an 8-bit chiptune melody WAV from a note list or key/scale using square and triangle waveforms.
example_prompt: Generate a cheerful 8-bit melody in C major, 8 bars
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM band-limited square/triangle oscillators produce the samples and emit a WAV file fully client-side.
rationale: Indie game devs need royalty-free chiptune stingers without firing up a tracker.

name: word-count-delta
description: Compares word, sentence, paragraph, and character counts between two texts and reports the differences.
example_prompt: How did the length stats change between my first and final draft?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — count tokens for each input and subtract
rationale: Writers tracking how a revision grew or shrank want side-by-side count deltas, not a content diff.

name: image-motion-diff
description: Frame-differences two photos of the same scene to isolate and highlight what moved, with a noise threshold to suppress sensor grain.
example_prompt: Highlight what moved between these two security-camera frames
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: thresholded absolute difference with morphological cleanup, all CPU-local.
rationale: Isolating motion between two stills is the core of any DIY surveillance or time-lapse change check.

name: image-bit-depth-diff
description: Quantizes an image to a target bit depth and diffs against the original to visualize banding and posterization before exporting.
example_prompt: Show me the banding if I drop this gradient to 8-bit
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: quantize channels, diff, and amplify the residual locally.
rationale: Previewing quantization banding prevents shipping gradients that posterize on lower-depth targets.

name: video-triptych-diff
description: Builds an A | B | difference triptych video so reviewers see both versions and the pixel delta in one synced frame.
example_prompt: Show version A, version B, and their difference all in one video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — hstack of two inputs plus a blend=difference pane, all in ffmpeg.wasm
rationale: Combines visual comparison with an explicit diff lane so subtle changes are not missed.

name: video-subtitle-diff
description: Diffs the text content of two subtitle files line-by-line, showing added, removed, and reworded captions.
example_prompt: Show me what changed between these two SRT files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse both SRT/VTT/ASS files and run a line diff entirely in-browser
rationale: Translators and editors need a clean changelog of caption edits across revisions.

name: onset-alignment-compare
description: Detects note/beat onsets in two performances and reports per-onset timing deviations.
example_prompt: How tight is the timing of take 2 versus take 1?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM does onset detection and alignment on both decoded files in the browser.
rationale: Quantifies rhythmic tightness between takes, which a global tempo compare cannot show.

name: merge-conflict-extractor
description: Parses a file containing git conflict markers and extracts each conflicting hunk's ours/base/theirs sides into a structured list.
example_prompt: pull out all the conflict hunks from this file with merge markers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM marker scanner; offline text parsing
rationale: Isolating just the conflicting regions makes resolving a messy merge far easier.

name: multiset-comparator
description: Compares two multisets (bags) showing shared, added, and removed elements with their count differences.
example_prompt: Compare the bags [a,a,b,c,c,c] and [a,b,b,c,c] and show count diffs.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; count-map differencing over parsed lists, fully local.
rationale: Comparing collections that allow duplicates (inventories, word counts) needs count-aware diffing that plain set ops can't give.

name: common-phrase-extractor
description: Finds the longest and most frequent phrases shared between two texts.
example_prompt: What phrases do these two articles have in common?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — suffix/n-gram matching across the two token streams
rationale: Shared-phrase detection helps spot reuse, boilerplate, or copying between documents.

name: thd-compare
description: Measures total harmonic distortion from a test tone in two files and reports the THD delta.
example_prompt: Which of these two test-tone recordings has more harmonic distortion?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM runs the FFT and harmonic-bin summation on both files in the browser.
rationale: Lets engineers A/B the distortion of two converters, codecs, or gain stages quantitatively.

name: snapshot-test-diff
description: Compares two Jest-style snapshot files and groups changed, added, and removed snapshots by test name.
example_prompt: Diff my old and new __snapshots__ files and group the changes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — snapshot block parse keyed by test name then compare, no network
rationale: Large snapshot churn is hard to review; grouping by test makes intentional vs accidental changes clear.

name: font-metrics-compare
description: Compares two fonts' metrics — ascent, descent, line-gap, x-height, and advance widths — to gauge swap-in compatibility.
example_prompt: Compare the metrics of these two fonts to see if I can swap one for the other
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — ttf-parser extracts metric tables and the comparison runs in-browser
rationale: Knowing whether a font substitution will reflow layout is a real typography/web-perf concern.

name: video-exposure-report
description: Detects over- and under-exposed segments by analyzing luminance and clipping, outputting a timestamped QC list.
example_prompt: Flag the over-exposed and under-exposed parts of this clip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader's signalstats luma stats identify exposure extremes during decode, client-side.
rationale: Exposure QC catches blown highlights and crushed shadows that ruin shots, before committing to a grade or re-shoot.

name: meta-tags-diff
description: Compares the meta, Open Graph, and Twitter tags of two HTML documents and reports what changed.
example_prompt: Diff the meta and Open Graph tags between these two page versions
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse head tags into maps and compare, fully local
rationale: SEO regressions often hide in changed meta/OG tags, and a targeted diff catches them faster than a full-page diff.

name: video-to-opus
description: Extracts a video's audio into an efficient Opus file.
example_prompt: Extract the audio as opus
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader with libopus — Opus encode runs locally in wasm.
rationale: Opus gives the best quality-per-byte for voice and music, ideal for messaging and storage.

name: dictionary-define
description: Look up a word's definitions, part of speech, and usage examples from an offline dictionary.
example_prompt: Define "ephemeral"
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — bundled WordNet/Wiktionary gloss data, lookups are local map reads with no API.
rationale: Dictionary lookup is one of the most common everyday text needs and works great offline.

name: font-pairing
description: Suggest harmonious Google Font pairings for a given font or vibe, with usage notes.
example_prompt: What pairs well with Playfair Display for a heading?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM over a curated pairing dataset; offline.
rationale: Common design decision with strong demand and no current tool.

name: pdf-stats
description: Reports page count, word count, fonts used, and image count for a PDF.
example_prompt: How many pages and words are in this PDF?
loader_feasibility: pyodide — pypdf and pdfplumber gather structural and text statistics in the sandbox.
rationale: Document metrics help writers and reviewers gauge length and complexity at a glance.

name: orf-finder
description: Finds open reading frames in all six frames of a DNA sequence, reporting start/stop positions and length.
example_prompt: Find all ORFs longer than 100bp in this sequence.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: scan for start/stop codons across frames, pure compute as in Rust-Bio.
rationale: ORF identification is a standard gene-prediction step that benefits from running on sequences without uploading them.

name: ssh-config-parser
description: Parses ~/.ssh/config into per-host blocks, resolves which options apply to a given host, and flags conflicts.
example_prompt: Which settings apply when I ssh to 'prod' given this ssh config?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM config parser plus Host pattern-match logic; pure text, fully local.
rationale: ssh config Host pattern resolution is confusing and sshuttle-style users live in this file.

name: daily-note-template
description: Generates a dated daily-note or bullet-journal template with configurable sections.
example_prompt: Make me a daily journal template for today with gratitude, tasks, and reflection sections
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — templated string building with host-provided date, no server
rationale: jrnl/tdo/Diary users start every day from a template, and generating it removes friction.

name: cpu-benchmark
description: Run integer, floating-point, and hashing workloads in WASM and report ops/sec plus a rough single-thread score for the device.
example_prompt: benchmark this device's single-thread cpu speed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tight-loop workloads timed in the wasmi sandbox; runs purely on the local CPU with no server.
rationale: Offers the 'how fast is this machine' angle of the *top monitor cluster using the one CPU measurement a sandboxed browser tool can legitimately make.

name: pe-header-parser
description: Parses a PE/COFF executable (EXE/DLL/EFI) header showing machine type, sections, imports, and subsystem.
example_prompt: Parse the headers of this .efi file
loader_feasibility: The object/goblin crate parses PE binaries in plain Rust→WASM; the file is read locally.
rationale: uefi-rs apps are PE binaries, and PE inspection is a broadly useful malware-triage and dev tool that runs safely offline.

name: broken-image-check
description: Fetch a page and verify each image URL, reporting broken or oversized images.
example_prompt: Find any broken images on this page
loader_feasibility: Fetches page + each image via the HTTP host import; in-browser.
rationale: broken-link-check covers hyperlinks; broken images are a separate common QA task.

name: call-log-analyzer
description: Analyzes an exported call-log CSV to surface top contacts, total/average talk time, missed-call counts, and call activity by hour and weekday.
example_prompt: Analyze my exported call log and show my most-called contacts and total minutes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: CSV parsing and aggregation in-memory, with private data never leaving the device.
rationale: Privacy-focused dialer users (Fossify Phone) export logs and want insights without sending them to a cloud analytics service.

name: connected-components
description: Finds connected components and reports each node's community in an undirected edge list.
example_prompt: How many connected groups are in this graph?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM uses union-find over the edges, a small fully-local computation.
rationale: Community/component detection is a foundational graph-science operation and cheap to ship.

name: ndjson-validator
description: Validates newline-delimited JSON, reporting the exact line of any record that fails to parse and any blank/trailing-line issues.
example_prompt: Validate this NDJSON log file — which lines aren't valid JSON?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses each line independently and reports per-line errors client-side
rationale: Streaming/log pipelines use NDJSON heavily and one bad line aborts ingestion; per-line validation isolates it.

name: protobuf-lint
description: Lints .proto files for syntax errors, naming-convention violations, and reserved-field conflicts.
example_prompt: lint my protobuf schema
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM proto parser; text-only analysis runs client-side.
rationale: Protobuf style and reserved-field mistakes break wire compatibility and a local linter catches them early.

name: rust-doc-extractor
description: Extracts doc comments and public signatures from Rust source into Markdown API docs.
example_prompt: generate markdown docs from this Rust file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the syn crate parses Rust to an AST entirely locally
rationale: A lightweight deepwiki-rs that works on a single pasted file.

name: mime-header-decode
description: Decodes RFC 2047 MIME encoded-words (=?charset?B/Q?...?=) in email headers into readable Unicode text.
example_prompt: Decode this email subject: =?UTF-8?B?SGVsbG8gV29ybGQ=?=
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: base64/quoted-printable decode plus charset transcoding to UTF-8, all pure computation runnable client-side.
rationale: Garbled =?...?= subject and From lines are a constant pain when reading raw email, and decoding them locally keeps the contents private.

name: conventional-commit-builder
description: Builds and validates a Conventional Commit message from type/scope/description fields and lints a pasted message against the spec.
example_prompt: Make a conventional commit message for a bug fix in the auth module about expired tokens
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string templating and validation; no external calls.
rationale: semantic-git-commit-cli's structured-commit flow is pure formatting/validation that fits a quick browser tool.

name: exif-thumbnail-extractor
description: Extracts the embedded JPEG preview thumbnail stored inside a photo's EXIF metadata as a separate image.
example_prompt: Pull out the embedded EXIF thumbnail from this JPEG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust parses the EXIF APP1 segment and writes out the embedded thumbnail bytes — pure parsing, no model.
rationale: Forensics and recovery workflows sometimes need the original-camera thumbnail when the full image is altered or missing.

name: graphql-syntax-validator
description: Parses a GraphQL query/mutation/schema document and reports syntax errors (bad selection sets, unterminated strings) with positions.
example_prompt: Is this GraphQL query syntactically valid? Find the error
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM GraphQL parser (graphql-parser/apollo-parser) validates document syntax offline
rationale: GraphQL syntax errors are common during hand-editing and a local parser flags them without hitting a server.

name: trig-identity-simplifier
description: Simplifies and verifies trigonometric expressions and identities.
example_prompt: simplify sin(x)^2 + cos(x)^2 and verify it equals 1
loader_feasibility: pyodide + SymPy trigsimp()/simplify() runs locally
rationale: Precalculus/Trigonometry identity practice is a recurring College Algebra search.

name: social-safe-area-checker
description: Checks that key content stays inside platform safe-margins for thumbnails and social crops, flagging subjects too close to edges.
example_prompt: Will the important part of this thumbnail get cropped on different feeds?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM detects content bounds via edge/saliency heuristics and compares to margin templates.
rationale: Edge-hugging subjects get cut off across platforms' varying crops, costing engagement.

name: video-variable-framerate-check
description: Measures per-frame durations to detect variable frame rate and reports the min/avg/max effective fps.
example_prompt: Is this screen recording VFR or constant frame rate?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm reads frame PTS deltas in-browser; no conversion is performed, only measurement.
rationale: VFR sources desync audio and confuse editors, and the variability is undetectable without timestamp analysis.

name: video-container-codec-mismatch-check
description: Flags when the file extension or container brand disagrees with the actual codecs inside (e.g. VP9 in a .mp4).
example_prompt: This is named .mp4 — does it actually contain MP4-compatible codecs?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm probes real codecs locally and compares against the container brand in WASM.
rationale: Extension/codec mismatches cause confusing 'unsupported' errors that look like corruption.

name: video-even-dimension-check
description: Checks that width and height are divisible by 2 (and optionally 16) to satisfy common encoder block requirements.
example_prompt: Are this clip's dimensions encoder-safe (divisible by 2)?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm reads resolution locally and the divisibility test runs in WASM.
rationale: Odd dimensions hard-fail many encoders and the constraint is easy to violate after a crop.

name: css-zindex-auditor
description: Extracts all z-index values from CSS, groups them by stacking context, and flags duplicates, magic numbers, and gaps.
example_prompt: Audit the z-index values in my stylesheet
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSS parsing of the pasted stylesheet.
rationale: Sprawling z-index values cause unwinnable stacking wars; an audit gives the map needed to flatten them.

name: matrix-dimension-consistency-checker
description: Checks that all rows of a parsed matrix/CSV have equal length and reports ragged rows and inferred shape.
example_prompt: Are all rows in this matrix the same length?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — row-length tally over parsed input, deterministic and in-browser.
rationale: Ragged rows are the most common cause of matrix-load failures; a fast linter saves debugging time.

name: cross-foot-checker
description: Validates that a table's row totals and column totals reconcile with the grand total (accounting cross-footing).
example_prompt: Do the row and column totals in this spreadsheet reconcile?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — independent row/column summation and comparison, deterministic and offline.
rationale: Cross-footing is a standard financial-statement integrity check that catches totals that don't tie out.

name: set-cookie-linter
description: Lints one or more Set-Cookie header values for missing Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite, oversized cookies, and conflicting attributes.
example_prompt: Lint this Set-Cookie: sid=abc; Path=/; SameSite=None
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM cookie-string parsing per RFC 6265 — fully local.
rationale: SameSite=None without Secure is rejected by browsers and is a common bug a quick linter surfaces instantly.

name: worley-noise-texture-generator
description: Produces Worley/cellular (Voronoi-distance) noise textures useful for stone, water-caustic, and organic-cell looks.
example_prompt: create a 512x512 cellular noise texture that looks like cracked stone
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scatters feature points and computes nearest-neighbor distances per pixel — entirely offline.
rationale: Worley noise covers a texture family Perlin can't, and procedural texture authoring is a high-demand client-side use case.

name: svg-background-pattern-generator
description: Generates tileable geometric SVG backgrounds (dots, crosses, diagonal lines, chevrons) with adjustable color and scale.
example_prompt: generate a subtle diagonal-line SVG background pattern in light gray
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM emits a small repeating SVG pattern tile entirely client-side, no rasterization or network
rationale: Lightweight CSS-ready background patterns are widely wanted and stay crisp as vectors at any size.

name: license-report-diff
description: Compares the dependency-license inventories of two builds and flags newly-introduced, removed, or changed licenses, highlighting copyleft additions.
example_prompt: Compare the license lists from these two builds and warn me about any new GPL deps
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses both license-report files (license-checker JSON/CSV) and diffs by package, classifying SPDX IDs in-browser.
rationale: Legal/compliance teams care specifically about license changes between releases, which a generic SBOM diff does not surface.

name: photo-mosaic-generator
description: Builds a photographic mosaic of a target image out of many small tile images.
example_prompt: Turn this portrait into a mosaic made of these 200 thumbnails
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: matches tile average colors to target cells and composites the result entirely in-WASM.
rationale: Photo mosaics are a delightful, share-worthy effect that normally requires a desktop tool.

name: video-countdown-leader-generator
description: Generates an animated numeric countdown (e.g. 5→1) leader clip with an optional beep on each second.
example_prompt: make a 5 second countdown intro clip at 1080p
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — drawtext with a per-frame time expression plus a sine beep, all synthesized in wasm with no input.
rationale: Common pre-roll for talks, livestream starts, and edits.

name: video-black-filler-generator
description: Generates a black, optionally silent-audio, filler clip to bridge gaps or pad a timeline.
example_prompt: make a 3-second black clip with silent stereo audio
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — color=black plus an anullsrc audio source, synthesized in the browser.
rationale: Padding and gap clips are a frequent timeline-assembly need.

name: video-glitch-overlay-generator
description: Generates a transparent digital-glitch (RGB-shift / block) overlay clip.
example_prompt: make a 3-second glitch overlay with alpha
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — geq/rgbashift/noise procedural effects on a transparent canvas, all client-side.
rationale: Stylized transition asset usable across many edits.

name: video-vignette-overlay-generator
description: Generates a transparent vignette overlay clip (darkened edges) for compositing.
example_prompt: make a soft vignette overlay with alpha at 1080p
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — a geq radial-falloff on a transparent canvas, rendered in the browser.
rationale: Reusable framing/mood asset that avoids re-baking a vignette per clip.

name: barcode-number-generator
description: Generates valid EAN-13, UPC-A, and ISBN-13 numbers with correct check digits.
example_prompt: Generate 10 valid EAN-13 barcode numbers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; check-digit math, no network.
rationale: Populating product test catalogs with scannable-valid codes.

name: linspace-generator
description: Generates N evenly spaced floating-point values between a start and stop bound, like NumPy linspace.
example_prompt: Generate 100 evenly spaced points between 0 and 6.28
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — single division and a loop, fully deterministic offline
rationale: Constantly needed to scaffold plot axes, sampling grids, and lookup-table inputs without booting Python.

name: math-to-latex
description: Convert plain or ASCIIMath expressions into LaTeX source.
example_prompt: Convert 'integral of x^2 dx from 0 to 1' to LaTeX
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust ASCIIMath→LaTeX parser in-browser.
rationale: Text→LaTeX is distinct from latex-render (renders) and latex-ocr (image input).

name: struct-decode
description: Decodes raw hex/bytes into typed fields (u8/u16/u32/u64, signed, f32/f64, LE/BE) given a struct layout.
example_prompt: Decode '0A000000FF7F' as { count: u32 LE, flags: u16 BE }.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — zerocopy-style typed byte reinterpretation is pure computation in the sandbox.
rationale: Inspect binary formats, packet payloads, and embedded data without a desktop hex editor.

name: magnet-from-torrent
description: Generates a magnet link from an uploaded .torrent file by computing its info hash and embedding name and trackers.
example_prompt: Make a magnet link from this .torrent file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bencode parse plus SHA-1 info-hash computation, then URI assembly, fully client-side.
rationale: A frequently wanted conversion (torrent file → shareable magnet) that requires no downloading and runs purely locally.

name: self-training-classifier
description: Semi-supervised low-density-separation classifier that pseudo-labels confident unlabeled rows and iteratively retrains.
example_prompt: Train a classifier from mostly-unlabeled data
loader_feasibility: pyodide — scikit-learn's SelfTrainingClassifier wraps a base estimator in the sandbox.
rationale: Exploits the low-density-separation assumption to get good classifiers when labels are scarce, a common real-world constraint.

name: rust-syntax-check
description: Parses Rust source with a real parser and reports syntax errors and unbalanced delimiters without compiling.
example_prompt: Is this Rust syntactically valid? Point at any errors.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the syn parser compiles to WASM and reports parse errors; no rustc or network needed.
rationale: Gives instant syntax feedback (a cargo-check subset) without a Rust toolchain installed.

name: vesting-calc
description: Generate an equity vesting schedule with cliff and monthly vesting, showing vested shares over time.
example_prompt: vesting schedule for 48,000 options, 4-year vest, 1-year cliff
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM date/share math; local.
rationale: Employees and HR routinely need vesting schedules; no current tool produces them.

name: kubernetes-manifest-diff
description: Field-level diff of two Kubernetes YAML manifests that ignores status, generation, and other server-noise fields.
example_prompt: Diff these two Deployment manifests and skip the noisy status fields
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse both YAML docs to maps, strip known noise paths, and diff key paths locally
rationale: Raw YAML diffs of k8s objects drown real changes in metadata churn; a manifest-aware diff is far cleaner.

name: sdf-to-csv
description: Splits an SDF/MOL chemical structure file into records and tabulates the molecule name plus all data-field properties as CSV.
example_prompt: Extract the property fields from this SDF file into a CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing the SDF record delimiters and data-field tags locally; no chemistry server.
rationale: Chemists pull property tables out of vendor SDF files constantly and want a quick offline tabular export.

name: shellcode-analyzer
description: Analyzes shellcode for syscalls/API hashes, decoder stubs, and egg hunters, summarizing behavior.
example_prompt: analyze what this shellcode does
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; pattern detection over disassembled bytes, runs in-browser.
rationale: Turning raw shellcode into a behavior summary saves significant manual RE time in CTFs.

name: graph-force-layout-svg
description: Renders an edge list as a force-directed graph layout SVG with optional node sizing by degree.
example_prompt: Visualize this edge list as a network diagram.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; force-simulation positions and SVG output computed locally.
rationale: Seeing the graph is the first step of explainable graph reasoning and there's no quick local visualizer.

name: cli-args-to-json
description: Builds a JSON object from key=value and --flag style arguments, with type and array inference.
example_prompt: Make JSON from: name=Joris admin=true tags=a,b
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tokenizes the arguments and assembles JSON locally.
rationale: Quickly composing JSON payloads from shorthand args is exactly what jarg does.

name: hex-to-oid
description: Converts the DER hex encoding of an ASN.1 OBJECT IDENTIFIER into its dotted-decimal OID string.
example_prompt: What OID is the hex 06 03 55 04 03?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; trivial byte-level base-128 decoding with no dependencies or network.
rationale: A frequent ASN.1 debugging need that is tiny to implement and individually searched for.

name: yaml-anchor-expander
description: Inlines all YAML anchors and aliases so the output is fully expanded with no &/* references.
example_prompt: expand all the anchors in this YAML so there are no aliases left
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (serde_yaml) resolves anchors during parse and re-emits expanded YAML in-browser
rationale: Tools that don't support YAML merge keys need flattened config, and manual expansion is tedious.

name: image-dust-spot-detector
description: Finds sensor dust spots and scan blemishes as small dark/light blobs in smooth areas and maps them.
example_prompt: Find the dust spots on this scanned slide.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: blob detection over low-frequency regions — local scan.
rationale: Locating dust spots speeds retouching of scans and clear-sky shots.

name: video-banding-detector
description: Samples frames and scores visible color banding in gradients, flagging clips that need dithering or higher bit depth.
example_prompt: Does this video have visible color banding?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes frames and an onnx-runtime/heuristic banding metric scores gradient discontinuities, all in-browser.
rationale: Banding in skies and gradients is a common 8-bit compression artifact that's hard to spot manually but quantifiable.

name: video-rgb-parade-export
description: Exports an RGB parade / waveform-scope image so channel levels and clipping can be inspected.
example_prompt: Give me an RGB parade scope image for this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's waveform filter renders the parade to a PNG entirely within the browser WASM build.
rationale: The RGB parade is the primary scope for diagnosing color casts and crushed/blown channels.

name: video-static-logo-locator
description: Finds a persistent overlay/logo region in a single video by locating areas that stay temporally constant across scenes.
example_prompt: Where is the watermark/logo in this video?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes sampled frames and a Rust temporal-variance pass (or small onnx model) locates static regions in WASM.
rationale: Identifying a burned-in logo's location is the prerequisite to cropping or masking it, and it works on a single file unlike diff tools.

name: video-white-balance-analyzer
description: Estimates the overall color cast / white balance of the footage and reports an approximate color temperature.
example_prompt: Does this footage have a color cast? What's the white balance?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes sampled frames and a Rust gray-world/illuminant estimator computes the cast locally in WASM.
rationale: A white-balance read-out tells a colorist how far off-neutral a clip is before any correction, distinct from the temperature adjuster.

name: pickle-disassembler
description: Disassembles a Python pickle into its opcode stream and flags dangerous reduce/global opcodes for security review.
example_prompt: Disassemble this pickle file and flag any unsafe opcodes
loader_feasibility: pyodide: runs the stdlib pickletools module in the Python sandbox fully client-side.
rationale: Auditing untrusted pickles for arbitrary-code-execution opcodes is a real security need before unpickling.

name: constant-near-constant-detector
description: Flags zero-variance and near-constant numeric columns (low unique-value ratio or tiny spread) that add no information.
example_prompt: Which columns in this dataset are constant or near-constant?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM variance + unique-ratio scan; fully local.
rationale: Useless near-constant features waste model capacity and storage; spotting them is a quick, valuable cleanup step.

name: asciicast-player
description: Plays back and inspects an asciinema .cast terminal recording with scrubbing, and exports any frame as selectable text.
example_prompt: Play this asciinema recording and let me copy the text at the end
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM parsing of the JSONL .cast format driving an in-page terminal renderer; playback is fully local.
rationale: termishare/TStream/sshx share terminal sessions as recordings, and an offline player/extractor makes those captures viewable and copyable anywhere.

name: json-server-db-generator
description: Generates a json-server db.json with N fake records per named resource.
example_prompt: Create a json-server db.json with 20 users and 50 posts.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: resource-spec parsing and fake-record assembly are deterministic and offline.
rationale: json-server is a popular mock-API tool and seeding its db.json by hand is tedious.

name: image-spot-the-difference-marker
description: Auto-detects the differences between two near-identical images and annotates each one with a circle or numbered box.
example_prompt: Circle all the differences between these two cartoon pictures.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM clusters the diff into regions and draws annotations onto a copy in-browser.
rationale: An annotated 'here are the changes' image is the most human-readable diff output for reviews and puzzles.

name: iana-timezone-validator
description: Checks whether timezone identifiers are valid current IANA tz database names and suggests fixes for deprecated aliases.
example_prompt: Are 'America/New_York' and 'US/Eastern' valid IANA timezones?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with an embedded list of canonical and alias tz names; small static table, no lookups.
rationale: Invalid or deprecated tz names silently break scheduling and date math, and this validates them without a server.

name: redis-rdb-viewer
description: Parses a Redis RDB dump file and lists its keys, types, TTLs, and values.
example_prompt: Show me the keys and values inside this dump.rdb
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with an rdb-parser crate; reads the binary blob in-memory with no Redis connection.
rationale: Gives Redis Viewer/redis_tui users offline inspection of a backup without standing up a server.

name: jwk-inspector
description: Parses a JWK or JWKS document and displays each key's type, use, algorithm, and thumbprint.
example_prompt: Show me the keys in this JWKS: {"keys":[...]}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — JWK parsing and RFC7638 thumbprint hashing are pure JSON/crypto operations.
rationale: Debugging OIDC signature validation means understanding a provider's JWKS, which this lays out clearly offline.

name: lipinski-druglikeness
description: Evaluates Lipinski's Rule of Five and related descriptors (MW, logP, H-donors/acceptors) for a molecule.
example_prompt: Does ibuprofen pass Lipinski's Rule of Five? SMILES: CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O
loader_feasibility: pyodide; RDKit computes the descriptors from SMILES in the browser sandbox.
rationale: Drug-likeness screening is a core polypharmacy/interaction-prediction prerequisite mapped from that demand term.

name: csv-to-matrix-market
description: Writes a CSV matrix out as a MatrixMarket .mtx file, auto-detecting sparsity and symmetry.
example_prompt: Export this adjacency CSV as a MatrixMarket .mtx file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: counting nonzeros and emitting the coordinate format is pure text generation, fully client-side.
rationale: Numerical-solver and graph libraries expect .mtx, and hand-writing the header is error-prone.

name: temperature-converter
description: Convert temperatures between Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin.
example_prompt: convert 98.6F to celsius
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: affine arithmetic only.
rationale: Everyday conversion that belongs in a quick-tools chat.

name: vigenere-cipher
description: Encodes or decodes text with the Vigenère keyword cipher.
example_prompt: Decode 'LXFOPVEFRNHR' with the Vigenère key LEMON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — keyword-driven shift arithmetic, deterministic and client-side.
rationale: Covers both Vigenère Encode and Decode demand in one tool; a classic-crypto mainstay.

name: hexdump-to-binary
description: Reconstructs the original binary file from an xxd/hexdump-style hex listing, ignoring offsets and ASCII gutters.
example_prompt: Rebuild the binary file from this xxd hexdump
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses hex columns and emits the bytes for download locally.
rationale: Reverse-engineering and forensics workflows produce hexdumps that need turning back into runnable/loadable files.

name: calibration-tone-generator
description: Produces a precise reference tone at a chosen frequency and exact dBFS level for gain-staging and meter calibration.
example_prompt: Make a 1kHz tone at exactly -18 dBFS for calibration
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: amplitude-accurate sine synthesis at a target dBFS + WAV encode, deterministic client-side.
rationale: Engineers align meters and gain structure to known reference levels (-18/-20 dBFS), needing bit-exact tones.

name: css-theme-variables-generator
description: Turns a color palette and scale into a :root block of CSS custom properties with light/dark variants.
example_prompt: Make CSS variables for a theme with primary #3366ff, neutrals, and a dark mode override
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes shades and emits :root vars, no network
rationale: Design-token scaffolding standardizes theming and removes manual color bookkeeping.

name: dmarc-record-generator
description: Generates a DMARC TXT record from policy, reporting addresses, percentage, and alignment options.
example_prompt: Make a DMARC record with quarantine policy and reports to dmarc@example.com
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tag-value string assembly, offline
rationale: Distinct from the excluded explainer — building a valid DMARC string from scratch is tricky.

name: graphql-resolver-stub-generator
description: Scaffolds resolver function stubs from a GraphQL SDL schema's types and fields.
example_prompt: Generate resolver stubs for the Query and Mutation types in this schema
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — SDL parse + resolver-skeleton emission
rationale: Wiring one stub per field is mechanical work that scales painfully with schema size.

name: pytest-scaffold
description: Scaffolds a pytest test module with fixtures, parametrize stubs, and arrange-act-assert skeletons from a function signature.
example_prompt: Scaffold pytest tests for a function add(a, b) with parametrized cases
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust to WASM; parses the signature and emits Python test source text, no interpreter.
rationale: Starting a test file with fixtures and parametrize boilerplate is repetitive and a scaffold standardizes it.

name: test-stub-from-signature
description: Generates unit-test stubs (happy path, edge cases, error case) from a pasted function signature in JS, TS, Python, or Rust.
example_prompt: Generate test stubs for this TypeScript function signature
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust to WASM; parses the signature and emits language-appropriate test skeletons as text, no compiler.
rationale: Scaffolding test cases from a signature nudges coverage of edge and error paths people otherwise skip.

name: csv-to-toml
description: Builds a TOML array-of-tables from CSV rows, inferring scalar types so the output is valid, human-editable config.
example_prompt: Convert this CSV of config entries into a TOML array of tables
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: row parsing with type inference and TOML serialization, fully in-browser.
rationale: Turning a spreadsheet of settings into editable TOML config is a real authoring need that the backlog's csv-to-yaml/json don't cover for TOML.

name: html-boolean-attribute-normalizer
description: Normalizes boolean attributes (checked, disabled, selected) to their canonical bare form.
example_prompt: Normalize the boolean attributes in this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM attribute rewrite; deterministic local transform
rationale: Inconsistent boolean attribute styles (checked="checked" vs checked) clutter diffs.

name: diff-strip-markers
description: Strips +/-/space and @@ hunk markers from a unified diff to recover the clean post-change file.
example_prompt: give me just the final file from this git diff, no diff symbols
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM filters out removed lines and unprefixes the rest locally
rationale: Pulling the resulting source out of a pasted diff for re-use is otherwise line-by-line cleanup.

name: base64-line-wrap
description: Wraps or unwraps a Base64 string to fixed-width MIME lines (default 64 columns).
example_prompt: wrap this base64 blob to 64-character lines for a PEM file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM inserts/removes newlines at the column boundary in-browser
rationale: PEM and MIME formats require column-wrapped Base64 that one-line encoders don't produce.

name: tga-converter
description: Converts images to or from Truevision TGA (with optional RLE).
example_prompt: Export this as a tga
loader_feasibility: Rust image crate encodes/decodes TGA locally
rationale: TGA is a staple of game-engine and 3D pipelines that browsers can't open.

name: netpbm-converter
description: Converts to/from Netpbm PPM/PGM/PBM (ASCII or binary).
example_prompt: Give me a binary ppm of this image
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM; Netpbm is a trivial header+raster format
rationale: Netpbm is the lingua franca of CV/scientific pipelines and command-line image tools.

name: chroma-subsampling-converter
description: Re-encodes a JPEG with a chosen chroma subsampling mode (4:4:4, 4:2:2, 4:2:0).
example_prompt: Re-save this jpg as 4:4:4 for sharper text
loader_feasibility: jpeg-encoder in WASM controls subsampling on re-encode locally
rationale: Subsampling is the key quality/size lever for JPEGs with text or fine color edges and is normally inaccessible.

name: title-card-generator
description: Generates a standalone intro title-card clip with headline and subtitle text fading in over a chosen background.
example_prompt: Make a 4-second title card that says 'Episode 12 — The Reveal' fading in on navy
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg `color`/`drawtext` with `fade` builds the card from text and synthetic background entirely client-side.
rationale: Creators need quick branded title cards to drop on the front of clips without opening a full motion-graphics editor.

name: matrix-rain-video
description: Generates a Matrix-style digital falling-character rain background clip in a chosen color and density.
example_prompt: Make a 12-second green Matrix digital rain background loop
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute renders the cascading glyph columns per frame on the GPU before ffmpeg encodes them locally.
rationale: The digital-rain look is endlessly requested for tech content and a local generator beats reusing the same stock clip.

name: tinnitus-masking-noise-generator
description: Generates notched or narrow-band masking noise tuned to a user's tinnitus frequency as a WAV.
example_prompt: Make 5 minutes of notched noise around my 7 kHz tinnitus tone
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies a FIR notch/band filter to white noise and writes the WAV in-browser.
rationale: Notched-noise masking is a recognized tinnitus relief technique that needs a per-user custom frequency.

name: crontab-annotator
description: Parses a crontab file and annotates each line with a plain-English description of its schedule.
example_prompt: Explain each line of this crontab in plain English
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM cron parsing and humanization; entirely client-side
rationale: Auditing inherited crontabs is hard and inline descriptions catch surprising schedules.

name: extract-images
description: Fetch a web page and list all image URLs (with alt text and dimensions where available).
example_prompt: Get all the image URLs from this article
loader_feasibility: web fetch loader — parse /srcset/og:image from fetched HTML locally.
rationale: Harvesting page images is distinct from extract-links and useful for archiving and audits.

name: mermaid-render
description: Render a Mermaid diagram definition (flowchart, sequence, ER, gantt) to an SVG/PNG image.
example_prompt: Render this mermaid flowchart to an image
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — a Rust/WASM diagram renderer rasterizes the parsed Mermaid graph locally, the same browser-local pattern as the existing graphviz-render tool.
rationale: Mermaid is hugely popular for docs and AI-generated diagrams, and there's only a DOT renderer today.

name: distance-calculator
description: Computes the Euclidean distance between two points in 2D or 3D.
example_prompt: distance from (0,0) to (3,4)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — square-root distance math runs locally with no backend.
rationale: A natural geometry companion to the midpoint tool with everyday coursework use.

name: json-from-fields
description: Build a JSON object or array from simple key=value pairs with typed numbers, booleans, and nesting.
example_prompt: Make JSON from name=Ada age=36 admin=true
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure string parsing and serde_json serialization, no external calls.
rationale: jo/jf demand: hand-writing JSON is error-prone, and assembling it from flat pairs is a fast, popular shortcut.

name: path-tagger
description: Assigns tag labels to a file/path list by rule or manually and outputs a tag→files index plus an optional grouping plan.
example_prompt: Tag these paths by top-level folder and give me a tag-to-files index
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — rule matching and index generation over provided paths.
rationale: Captures the crtag tagging concept in a stateless, browser-local form that produces a usable organization plan.

name: sound-classify
description: Identify the dominant sounds/events in an audio clip (speech, dog, music, applause, siren…).
example_prompt: What sounds are in this recording?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime — a YAMNet-style model classifies log-mel frames entirely in-browser.
rationale: General audio event detection enables tagging and search and has no current equivalent.

name: wayback-snapshot
description: Find the latest or closest-to-a-date archived version of a URL via the Internet Archive Wayback API.
example_prompt: Show me the archived version of example.com from 2015
loader_feasibility: A single client-side fetch to the free, key-less archive.org availability API.
rationale: Common research/recovery task with a public no-auth endpoint.

name: cidr-merge
description: Summarize a list of IPs/ranges into the minimal set of CIDR blocks (and expand back).
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM IP math.
rationale: Network/firewall admins need range summarization; subnet-calc only handles a single CIDR.

name: before-after-image
description: Build a before/after comparison image or slider GIF from two photos.
example_prompt: Make a before/after slider from these two edits
loader_feasibility: Plain-Rust compositing or ffmpeg for the animated variant; offline.
rationale: Shareable format editors and marketers ask for constantly.

name: playfair-cipher
description: Encrypt or decrypt text with the Playfair digraph cipher using a keyword.
example_prompt: Encrypt 'meet at dawn' with Playfair key MONARCHY
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM grid cipher, offline.
rationale: A classic cipher missing from the ROT/Caesar/Vigenère/rail-fence set.

name: vigenere-keylength
description: Estimates the likely key length of a Vigenère cipher by computing the Index of Coincidence across candidate periods.
example_prompt: guess the vigenere key length for this ciphertext
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — slices text into columns and runs IoC per period, all in-memory
rationale: Key-length estimation is the hard step in breaking Vigenère ciphers and directly applies the IoC demand signal.

name: curl-convert
description: Convert a curl command into equivalent code (fetch/JavaScript, Python requests, Go, or HTTPie).
example_prompt: convert this curl command to Python requests: curl -X POST ...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (parse curl flags → emit code); pure string transform.
rationale: curl-to-code is a hugely popular developer utility (curlconverter) that's purely deterministic parsing.

name: data-cluster
description: Cluster rows of a numeric CSV with k-means (auto-k option), label each row, and plot the clusters.
example_prompt: cluster these customers into groups and show a scatter
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust (linfa) to WASM — pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: Unsupervised segmentation of tabular data is a core analytics task; text-cluster only covers text.

name: label-sheet-generate
description: Lay out an Avery-style label sheet PDF (addresses, names) from a CSV.
example_prompt: Make Avery 5160 address labels from this CSV
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM PDF layout to label templates, offline.
rationale: Mail-merge label sheets are a common office/print task with nothing equivalent yet.

name: json-mapreduce
description: Runs a CouchDB-style map/reduce over a JSON array using small user-supplied Python map and reduce functions and returns grouped results.
example_prompt: Map/reduce these orders to sum total revenue per customer
loader_feasibility: pyodide sandbox executes the user's map/reduce Python over the JSON in-browser with no server; only the standard library is exposed.
rationale: Map/reduce is the core CouchDB/RethinkDB compute model and pyodide lets users express it naturally without a database.

name: json-to-swift-codable
description: Generates Swift Codable structs from a sample JSON document.
example_prompt: Generate Swift Codable structs for this JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM inference→Swift emitter; no network
rationale: Directly maps 'codables' — Swift Codable struct generation is its exact concern.

name: json-to-python-dataclass
description: Generates Python dataclasses (with type hints) from a sample JSON document.
example_prompt: make Python dataclasses for this JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM inference emitting Python source; no runtime needed for generation.
rationale: simplejson/jsonpickle users want typed Python models from JSON, and dataclass scaffolding is the modern shape.

name: json-humanize
description: Transforms JSON into a human-readable nested table/definition-list view instead of raw braces (json.human.js).
example_prompt: Turn this JSON into a human-friendly table: {"order":{"items":2,"total":19.99}}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM walks the value tree and emits semantic HTML; rendered client-side.
rationale: Non-developers and reviewers want structured data as readable tables, not punctuation.

name: xxhash-checksum
description: Produces ultra-fast non-cryptographic XXH32, XXH64, XXH3-64 and XXH3-128 checksums of text or files.
example_prompt: what's the xxh3 checksum of this file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via `xxhash-rust`/`twox-hash`; pure arithmetic, no dependencies on the host.
rationale: xxHash is the fastest checksum for dedup and integrity checks and is a frequent developer ask with no native support.

name: confluent-wire-decoder
description: Decodes the Confluent Schema Registry wire format (magic byte + schema ID + payload) and optionally decodes the Avro body with a supplied schema.
example_prompt: decode this Confluent-wrapped Kafka message bytes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing the fixed 5-byte header then schema_registry_converter-style payload decode; pure byte parsing offline.
rationale: Reading Confluent-framed Kafka messages requires knowing the wire layout that few tools expose.

name: contour-detection
description: Finds connected components/contours in a binary image and reports their bounding boxes and areas.
example_prompt: Find and outline the shapes in this binary image.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — imageproc labels connected components in Rust with no native deps.
rationale: Contour/blob analysis is a common counting-and-measuring task that runs perfectly as a local tool.

name: image-feature-match
description: Detects and matches keypoints between two images, reporting correspondences and an estimated homography/overlap.
example_prompt: Match the features between these two photos to see how they overlap.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — rust-cv handles detection, descriptor matching, and RANSAC fully in Rust client-side.
rationale: Pairwise image matching powers panorama/alignment and duplicate-frame detection, valuable as a private, no-install tool.

name: sdp-parser
description: Parses an SDP blob (WebRTC offer/answer or SIP body) into media sections, codecs, ICE candidates, and DTLS fingerprints.
example_prompt: Parse this WebRTC SDP offer and list the codecs and ICE candidates
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line parser (shared with the SIP stack); fully client-side text processing.
rationale: SDP is central to both VoIP (rsipstack) and WebRTC debugging, and reading it by hand is error-prone.

name: system-info-parser
description: Parses pasted system output like /proc/cpuinfo, /proc/meminfo, lscpu, or free into a clean, structured summary.
example_prompt: Summarize this lscpu output for me (pasted below)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parsing is pure text processing (the core of sysinfo/procsys/nixinfo) needing no host access, which the browser sandbox cannot provide anyway.
rationale: People share raw /proc and lscpu dumps for support and want them turned into a readable summary.

name: graphql-schema-explorer
description: Parses a GraphQL SDL schema and lists its types, fields, arguments, queries, mutations, and relationships.
example_prompt: Show me all the types and queries defined in this schema.graphql
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: graphql-parser builds the type system in-memory and we walk it locally — no introspection endpoint needed.
rationale: Gives a quick map of an unfamiliar API surface without spinning up a GraphQL playground server.

name: graphql-request-builder
description: Turns a GraphQL query plus variables into a ready-to-run curl or fetch POST request.
