example_prompt: build a curl command for this GraphQL query against https://api.example.com/graphql
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — JSON-encodes the query/variables into an HTTP body as text, all client-side
rationale: Hand-escaping GraphQL into a JSON POST body is fiddly and error-prone; automating it saves real time.

name: rust-edition-migrator
description: Rewrites legacy Rust idioms to modern editions (try! → ?, removed extern crate, explicit dyn, 2015→2021 closures) via AST transforms.
example_prompt: Modernize this old Rust 2015 code to the 2021 edition.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: syn parse plus targeted rewrites re-emitted with prettyplease, all local.
rationale: Serves the 'Refactoring to Rust' demand for mechanically updating dated code without running cargo fix.

name: traceroute-visualizer
description: Parses traceroute, tracepath or mtr output and renders per-hop latency and packet-loss bars to spot where a path degrades.
example_prompt: Visualize this mtr output and show me where latency spikes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM parsing of pasted CLI output plus a rendered chart; no live probing needed so it runs client-side.
rationale: trippy/mtr produce dense text that's hard to read; turning saved output into a hop-by-hop visual helps diagnose where a route hurts.

name: docker-stats-parser
description: Parses `docker stats` output into a per-container CPU, memory, network, and block-IO table and flags resource hogs.
example_prompt: Which container is using the most memory in this docker stats output?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the stats table and ranks containers, fully offline.
rationale: docker stats is a live stream that's hard to read, so analyzing a captured snapshot to find the hog is a practical container-monitoring aid.

name: feed-timeline-merger
description: Merges multiple pasted RSS/Atom feeds into one deduplicated, reverse-chronological timeline of items.
example_prompt: Merge these three feeds into one timeline sorted newest-first and drop duplicates
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parsing, dedup by link/title, and date sorting are pure in-memory operations over pasted text, running client-side.
rationale: Aggregator-style readers like nom and Newsraft exist to unify many feeds, and a merge-and-dedupe timeline delivers that combined view without a backend.

name: bible-lookup
description: Looks up Bible passages by reference from bundled public-domain translations (KJV English and the Latin Vulgate) and can keyword-search the text.
example_prompt: Show me John 3:16-18 in both KJV and the Latin Vulgate.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the public-domain translations embedded as compressed assets; all reference resolution and search is in-memory, no network.
rationale: bbl, bible, Bible TUI, The Rock, and CatenaVetus are all evidence of strong demand for an instant, offline scripture reader.

name: literature-term-frequency
description: Extracts and clusters recurring topics/keywords across a set of pasted abstracts to scope a literature review.
example_prompt: Find the main themes across these 20 abstracts
loader_feasibility: transformers-js: embed each abstract with a small in-browser sentence model (or TF-IDF in Rust→WASM) and cluster locally.
rationale: Turns the slr-kit screening/keywording step into an offline tool, keeping unpublished abstracts private.

name: powershell-script-analyzer
description: Scans a PowerShell script for suspicious patterns like download cradles, IEX, hidden windows, and obfuscation.
example_prompt: Is this PowerShell script malicious? <paste script>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies a signature/heuristic ruleset over the script text; static analysis only, runs fully client-side.
rationale: defenders need to triage PowerShell quickly and offline, since the scripts under review are by definition untrusted.

name: ssh-config-linter
description: Parses an SSH client config and lints it for weak ciphers, risky options, and overlapping Host blocks.
example_prompt: Review my ~/.ssh/config for security issues: <paste config>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the config grammar and applies best-practice rules; static text analysis, no SSH connection made.
rationale: SSH-Snake-style risks start with sloppy client config, and linting it locally avoids exposing host inventory to a server.

name: podcast-chapter-editor
description: Adds or edits chapter markers (titles and start times) in an MP3/M4A file's metadata.
example_prompt: Add chapters to this podcast mp3 at 0:00 Intro, 3:30 Topic, 40:00 Outro
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM writes ID3 chapter (CHAP/CTOC) frames in memory, no server required.
rationale: Chaptered podcasts greatly improve navigation, a clear win for the podcast-client cluster and done fully client-side.

name: adblock-list-converter
description: Converts and validates adblock filter lists and /etc/hosts blocklists between formats.
example_prompt: Convert this hosts file into a uBlock/AdGuard filter list.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust parses and re-emits the filter syntaxes entirely in the browser.
rationale: Maps AdGuardian — people maintain blocklists and switching between hosts/AdGuard/uBlock formats is error-prone by hand.

name: dotfile-template-renderer
description: Renders a mustache-style config/dotfile template against user-provided variables to produce the final file.
example_prompt: render this config template with hostname=server1 and port=8080
loader_feasibility: A small templating engine compiled to Rust→WASM; deterministic substitution with no external data.
rationale: chezmoi's templated dotfiles are its standout feature, and offline template rendering lets users generate per-machine configs without installing the tool.

name: systemd-unit-generator
description: Generates a valid systemd .service, .timer, or .socket unit file from a plain-language description of the service.
example_prompt: Make a systemd service that runs /opt/app/run.sh as user deploy and restarts on failure
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: it emits a structured INI-style unit file from inputs, fully client-side text generation.
rationale: Writing unit files from memory is fiddly and demand for systemctl TUIs shows people want easier service management.

name: log-highlight
description: Colorizes plain log or command output by pattern (errors, IPs, timestamps, numbers) into styled HTML.
example_prompt: Highlight the errors and IPs in this log
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: regex rules map matches to colored spans in-memory.
rationale: Generic colourising of dull output (grc) makes logs scannable, and doing it client-side keeps log data private.

name: dictionary-tagger
description: Finds and highlights every occurrence of a supplied word/phrase list in text, returning counts and positions.
example_prompt: Highlight every occurrence of these 40 banned terms in this document and tell me how many of each.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM Aho-Corasick multi-pattern matching; in-memory only.
rationale: lexmatch-style bulk lexicon matching powers content moderation, glossary checks, and NLP tagging without sending text anywhere.

name: wip-limit-checker
description: Checks a kanban board against per-column work-in-progress limits and flags any columns over capacity.
example_prompt: My Doing column limit is 3 — does this board violate any WIP limits?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — counting per column against supplied limits.
rationale: WIP-limit enforcement is a core lean/kanban discipline that the source tools surface but rarely validate.

name: frontmatter-query
description: Queries and filters YAML/TOML frontmatter fields across a set of pasted Markdown documents.
example_prompt: List the frontmatter tags and dates from these markdown files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM frontmatter parsing and filtering, no network
rationale: Querying note/blog metadata (Obsidian-style) is a clear demand and purely local.

name: load-test-data-generator
description: Generates parameterization CSV/JSON of fake users, tokens, and payloads for data-driven load tests.
example_prompt: Make a CSV of 1000 fake test users with email and password for a load test
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM fake-data engine with seedable RNG; produces the dataset entirely client-side.
rationale: Parameterized load tests need bulk fake input rows, and generating them locally is faster and keeps no PII risk.

name: liquid-template-renderer
description: Renders a Shopify/Jekyll Liquid template against provided JSON data and shows the output.
example_prompt: Render this Liquid snippet with this product JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM liquid crate; compiles and renders pasted template+data locally with no network.
rationale: Shopify theme development is Liquid-heavy, and previewing template output against sample data is a core dev loop.

name: zone-file-formatter
description: Parses, validates, and canonically reformats a BIND zone file, flagging malformed records and missing TTLs.
example_prompt: Validate and tidy up this BIND zone file: $ORIGIN example.com. ...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — zone-file lexing/serialization is pure text processing.
rationale: Hand-edited zone files are error-prone and a client-side validator catches typos before a deploy breaks resolution.

name: m3u-playlist-parser
description: Parses M3U/M3U8 playlists into a structured list of tracks, durations, and stream URLs.
example_prompt: Parse this radio playlist into a track list. [uploads stations.m3u]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — straightforward text parsing of the M3U format with no external dependencies.
rationale: tunein-cli and music daemons exchange M3U files constantly; turning them into readable, editable lists is broadly handy.

name: eth-function-selector
description: Computes the 4-byte function selector and 32-byte event topic from a Solidity signature.
example_prompt: What's the selector for balanceOf(address)?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — keccak256 over the canonical signature string, computed instantly client-side.
rationale: Selectors are needed constantly for calldata, proxies, and 4byte lookups, and Foundry's `cast sig` proves the demand.

name: ipfs-cid-inspector
description: Parses an IPFS/Filecoin CID, decoding its version, multicodec, multihash, and base encoding.
example_prompt: What's inside this CID: bafybeigdyrzt5sfp7udm7hu76uh7y26nf3efuylqabf3oclgtqy55fbzdi
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — multibase/multihash/CID parsing is pure decoding with no network lookup.
rationale: Forest (Filecoin) and IPFS users hit opaque CIDs constantly; decoding the structure aids debugging without contacting a gateway.

name: eth-abi-encode
description: ABI-encodes a function call into calldata from a signature and argument values.
example_prompt: abi encode transfer(address,uint256) with 0xabc... and 1000000
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — deterministic ABI serialization, offline.
rationale: Hand-crafting calldata is a frequent dev task for raw transactions and debugging.

name: cvss-calculator
description: Computes a CVSS v3.1 base and temporal score and severity rating from a vector string.
example_prompt: What's the CVSS score for AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM; the CVSS formula is pure arithmetic over a parsed vector, no data fetch needed.
rationale: Security teams score vulnerabilities daily and the official calculator is just a formula that fits client-side.

name: venn-diagram
description: Render a 2-3 set Venn diagram with labels and region counts.
example_prompt: Draw a Venn diagram of 120 cat owners, 90 dog owners, 30 both
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM SVG geometry; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: Venn diagrams are a frequent explanatory visual not covered by the existing chart set.

name: chord-diagram
description: Render a circular chord diagram showing flows/relationships between categories from a matrix or edge list.
example_prompt: make a chord diagram of migration flows between these regions
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM SVG generation; local.
rationale: Chord diagrams are a distinctive, popular relationship viz not covered by network-graph or sankey.

name: persian-informal-to-formal
description: Rewrites colloquial/spoken Persian into standard written form (e.g. می‌رم→می‌روم, نمی‌دونم→نمی‌دانم).
example_prompt: Convert this informal Persian text to formal written Persian: نمی‌دونم کجا می‌رن
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — rule and lexicon-based mapping of common colloquial verb endings and contractions (Large-Scale Colloquial Persian patterns), fully offline.
rationale: Social-media and chat Persian is overwhelmingly colloquial, so normalizing it to formal form unlocks standard NLP and clean publishing.

name: self-similarity-matrix
description: Computes a self-similarity matrix to reveal song structure such as verse and chorus.
example_prompt: Show the structure of this song as an SSM
loader_feasibility: pyodide computes features + matrix and renders with matplotlib, all local.
rationale: Makes musical form visible at a glance (Fundamentals of Music Processing demand).

name: anaglyph-3d-maker
description: Combines a left/right stereo image pair into a red-cyan anaglyph 3D image.
example_prompt: Make a red-cyan 3D anaglyph from these two stereo photos
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (channel mixing) or plain Rust→WASM compositing runs the merge client-side.
rationale: Stereoscopic/anaglyph 3D is a recurring WebVR-adjacent want and red-cyan glasses make it universally viewable.

name: mvp-matrix-calculator
description: Builds perspective/orthographic projection, lookAt view, and model matrices for WebGL.
example_prompt: Give me a perspective matrix for 60° fov, 16:9, near 0.1 far 100
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM linear algebra; deterministic math
rationale: Matrix setup is the single biggest stumbling block for WebGL learners.

name: projection-matrix
description: Computes a perspective or orthographic projection matrix from fov/aspect/near/far or frustum bounds.
example_prompt: Perspective projection matrix for 60° fov, aspect 1.777, near 0.1, far 100
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM closed-form matrix math; pure numeric.
rationale: Getting the projection matrix right is a classic WebGL stumbling block and a dedicated calculator removes guesswork.

name: polygon-triangulate
description: Triangulates a 2D polygon (with holes) into a vertex/index list for WebGL/PixiJS rendering.
example_prompt: Triangulate this polygon outline into triangles for WebGL: <points>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM ear-clipping (earcut-style) algorithm; pure CPU geometry.
rationale: Filling arbitrary shapes in WebGL/PixiJS requires triangulation, a frequent need with no built-in browser API.

name: trs-matrix-builder
description: Builds a 4x4 model matrix from translation/rotation/scale and decomposes any 4x4 back into TRS components.
example_prompt: Build a model matrix with position 1,2,3, rotation 45deg around Y, and scale 2
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: 4x4 matrix compose/decompose is pure math.
rationale: Composing and reading back TRS matrices is core to every scene-graph engine (Babylon, ClayGL, Hilo3d, GLBoost).

name: h3-hex-index
description: Maps lat/lon to an H3 hexagon cell at a given resolution and returns its boundary, center, and neighbors.
example_prompt: Give me the H3 cell at resolution 9 for lat 51.5 lon -0.12 and its 6 neighbors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the h3o crate (pure-Rust H3 port) compiles to wasm32.
rationale: Deck.gl's HexagonLayer popularized H3 aggregation, and a local indexer lets users bin geo data without a server.

name: tensor-inspector
description: Reports shape, dtype, min/max/mean/std, NaN/Inf counts, and a value histogram for a pasted array or .npy.
example_prompt: Inspect this numpy array — give me stats and a histogram
loader_feasibility: pyodide loads numpy to analyze the array in-browser
rationale: Captures TensorWatch's tensor-debugging demand with a lightweight stats inspector.

name: onnx-model-graph
description: Parses an ONNX model and renders its layer/operator graph with shapes and parameter counts.
example_prompt: Visualize the architecture of this .onnx model
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime/plain Rust parses the ONNX protobuf and emits an SVG graph locally
rationale: Serves torchvista/TensorWatch model-visualization demand entirely in-browser with no Netron upload.

name: graph-centrality
description: Computes degree, closeness, and betweenness centrality for every node in a graph.
example_prompt: Which node is most central in this network?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs BFS-based centrality computations over the adjacency list in-browser.
rationale: Centrality drives network analysis throughout the graph-algorithms demand source.

name: propensity-score-matching
description: Estimates an average treatment effect by fitting propensity scores and matching treated to control units.
example_prompt: Estimate the treatment effect in this dataset using propensity score matching
loader_feasibility: pyodide with scikit-learn for the logistic propensity model plus nearest-neighbor matching, all in the WASM sandbox.
rationale: PSM is a headline technique of 'Causal Inference for Data Science' that sklearn-in-Pyodide makes browser-local.

name: jingle-loop-maker
description: Loops and crossfades a short audio snippet into a seamless repeating jingle.
example_prompt: loop this 4-second clip into a smooth 30-second jingle
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (WASM) applies aloop and acrossfade filters locally.
rationale: Direct demand from the 'Jingles' term for making short looping audio brand cues.

name: model-metrics-comparator

name: bin-packing-optimizer
description: Packs a list of weighted/sized items into the fewest bins or containers (1D/2D) and reports utilization.

rationale: Directly serves the Packrift packaging-optimization benchmark demand with a real solver.

name: growth-rate-calculator
description: Estimates growth rate, doubling time, and an effective reproduction proxy from a case/value time series.
example_prompt: What's the doubling time of these case numbers?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM regression/ratio math over the input series, no server.
rationale: The core question for any epidemic or growth series, computed instantly offline.

name: json-schema-docs
description: Renders browsable HTML/Markdown reference documentation for a JSON Schema, listing every property, type, constraint, and description.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — schema traversal emits HTML/Markdown, no server rendering

name: syllable-count

loader_feasibility: plain WASM — Liang hyphenation patterns + a pronunciation dictionary do syllabification locally.
rationale: Needed for poetry, lyrics, typesetting, and readability work that the existing readability tool doesn't cover.

name: graphql-query-parser

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM GraphQL parser.

name: ics-calendar-diff

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse VEVENT blocks into a map keyed by UID and diff locally
rationale: Reconciling two calendar exports to find moved or cancelled events is a concrete personal-data task.

name: image-mask-iou
description: Computes IoU and Dice overlap between two binary masks or segmentations and renders the agreement/disagreement map.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM counts intersection/union per pixel and colorizes the overlap locally
rationale: Anyone evaluating segmentation outputs needs IoU/Dice without spinning up a Python stack.

name: video-blink-comparator
description: Rapidly alternates between two aligned videos at a chosen interval so any changed pixels appear to flicker.

loader_feasibility: ffmpeg interleaves frames from both inputs on a timer pattern, all in the wasm ffmpeg runtime.

name: video-metadata-diff
description: Diffs the full metadata of two video files and highlights every field that changed.
example_prompt: Show me what metadata differs between these two exports
loader_feasibility: ffprobe metadata extraction in wasm ffmpeg plus Rust→WASM field comparison, no server.
rationale: A focused metadata diff catches unintended tag/codec changes between exports.

name: video-resolution-compare
description: Compares two videos' resolution, display aspect ratio, and sample aspect ratio and flags scaling/stretch differences.
example_prompt: Are these two clips the same resolution and aspect ratio?
loader_feasibility: ffprobe geometry fields from both files in wasm ffmpeg, compared in Rust→WASM.
rationale: Hidden SAR/DAR mismatches cause stretching that a pixel-resolution check alone misses.

name: mfcc-distance-compare
description: Extracts MFCCs from two clips and reports a DTW-aligned timbral distance, quantifying how similar they sound in tone color.
example_prompt: How timbrally similar are these two vocal takes?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: mel filterbank + DCT + DTW distance on decoded PCM, fully local
rationale: Tempo-robust timbre comparison underpins take-selection and reference-matching, with no equivalent browser tool.

name: rms-envelope-compare
description: Computes windowed RMS/loudness envelopes for two files and diffs them over time to show where levels diverge.
example_prompt: Show me where the remaster gets louder than the original over time
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: sliding-window RMS on both decoded signals, returns a difference curve, local
rationale: Time-resolved level comparison reveals automation/limiting changes that a single integrated number hides.

name: pitch-contour-diff
description: Extracts fundamental-frequency contours from two monophonic takes and overlays/diffs them to compare intonation and pitch drift.
example_prompt: Compare the tuning of these two vocal takes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: autocorrelation/YIN pitch tracking on both clips then contour diff, no network
rationale: Intonation comparison for take-selection or tuning QA has no client-side equivalent.

name: lossless-verify
description: Decodes a FLAC/ALAC file and bit-compares its PCM against a reference WAV to prove the lossless copy is truly identical.
example_prompt: Verify this FLAC is a perfect lossless copy of my WAV

rationale: Archivists need proof a lossless transcode is exact, not just 'probably fine'.

name: snr-improvement-estimate
description: Estimates the noise floor of a noisy and a cleaned version and reports the achieved SNR/noise-reduction in dB.
example_prompt: How much noise did my denoiser actually remove?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: quietest-percentile noise-floor estimation on both signals, dB delta, local
rationale: Quantifying how much a denoise pass helped (and at what cost) needs an objective before/after number.

name: geojson-feature-diff
description: Diffs two GeoJSON feature collections by feature id, reporting added, removed, and geometry/property-changed features.
example_prompt: Compare these two GeoJSON files and tell me which features moved or changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; parse both collections and diff geometries/properties by feature id locally
rationale: Map data updates frequently and seeing exactly which features changed is valuable for GIS work.

name: cookie-set-diff
description: Compares two sets of cookies and reports added, removed, and changed cookies including attribute differences.
example_prompt: Diff the cookies set by these two responses
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse Set-Cookie / cookie strings and compare maps, local
rationale: Comparing cookie attributes (SameSite, Secure, expiry) across responses helps debug session and auth issues.

name: two-sample-compare
description: Side-by-side descriptive comparison of two numeric samples: difference in mean, median, SD, IQR, and range.
example_prompt: Compare the summary stats of group A vs group B
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: quantile and moment computation over arrays, no server.
rationale: A fast descriptive head-to-head of two datasets without firing up a stats package.

name: mean-difference-ci
description: Estimates the confidence interval for the difference between two sample means (Welch and pooled).
example_prompt: Give me the 95% confidence interval for the difference in means between these two samples
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: t-quantile approximation plus standard-error math, client-side.
rationale: Estimating the magnitude and uncertainty of a difference is the practical question after comparing two groups.

name: odds-ratio-calculator
description: From a 2×2 contingency table computes odds ratio, relative risk, risk difference, and their confidence intervals.
example_prompt: Compute the odds ratio and relative risk for this 2x2 table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: closed-form ratios and log-SE intervals, runs locally.
rationale: The standard way to compare two groups' outcome rates in epidemiology and A/B analysis.

name: bland-altman-analyzer
description: Compares two measurement methods via Bland-Altman statistics: bias, limits of agreement, and per-point differences.
example_prompt: Run a Bland-Altman comparison on these paired measurements from two devices
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: paired-difference means and SD over arrays, client-side.
rationale: The gold-standard method-agreement analysis that correlation alone can't provide.

name: distance-matrix-builder
description: Computes the full pairwise distance matrix among a set of points under a chosen metric.
example_prompt: Give me the pairwise Euclidean distance matrix for these points
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: O(n²) metric evaluation over coordinate arrays, client-side.
rationale: A reusable input for clustering and nearest-neighbor work that's painful to assemble by hand.

name: archive-listing-diff
description: Compares the file listings of two archives (zip/tar), showing added, removed, and size-changed entries.
example_prompt: What files differ between these two zip archives?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: read central directories/headers (no extraction) then compare, local.
rationale: Comparing two release archives or backups for content changes is a practical, no-extract task.

name: low-dynamic-range-checker
description: Flags images whose pixel values occupy only a narrow tonal range, indicating washed-out, hazy, or under-contrasted content.
example_prompt: Is this photo low-contrast or washed out?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes the min/max/spread of luminance from decoded pixels locally.
rationale: Narrow dynamic range is a fast objective signal that an image needs a levels/contrast pass.

name: video-dropped-frame-detector
description: Flags dropped or duplicated frames in a stream by comparing frame durations against the nominal frame rate.
example_prompt: Check whether this video has dropped or duplicated frames.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader uses mpdecimate/showinfo statistics in WASM to detect duplicate and missing frames locally.
rationale: Capture and transcode pipelines silently drop frames, causing stutter that needs detection before delivery.

name: video-resolution-standard-checker
description: Validates the resolution against a list of accepted standard frame sizes (e.g., 1920x1080, 1280x720, 3840x2160).
example_prompt: Is this 1080p exactly, or some off-spec resolution?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader reads dimensions via ffprobe in WASM and compares to the spec list locally.
rationale: Off-by-a-few-pixels resolutions slip through and fail platform ingest unless explicitly checked.

name: video-profile-level-validator
description: Validates the H.264/HEVC profile and level against a configured maximum (e.g., High@4.0) and flags streams that exceed it.
example_prompt: Is this within H.264 High Profile Level 4.0?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader reads codec profile/level via ffprobe in WASM and compares against the ceiling locally.
rationale: Devices decode only up to a profile/level ceiling, so validating it prevents playback failures on target hardware.

name: stereo-correlation-timeline-compare
description: Computes the L/R Pearson correlation over time for two files and diffs the resulting timelines to flag mono-compatibility differences.
example_prompt: Compare how the stereo correlation changes over time between these two mixes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM windows PCM and computes per-frame correlation coefficients locally.
rationale: A correlation timeline reveals time-varying width/phase issues that a single balance number misses.

name: id3-cover-art-compare
description: Extracts embedded cover art from two MP3 files and compares dimensions, format, and content hash.
example_prompt: Do these two MP3s have the same embedded album art?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the ID3 APIC frames and hashes the image bytes locally.
rationale: Cover-art differences are invisible to text-tag diffs but matter for catalog consistency.

name: redirect-chain-diff
description: Compares two redirect chains step by step, highlighting changed hops, status codes, and a different final destination.
example_prompt: Diff these two redirect chains and tell me where they diverge
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing of hop lists + step comparison; fully local
rationale: Redirect changes after a migration can break SEO or loops; a hop-level diff isolates the regression.

name: audio-spectral-diff
description: Compares two audio files and reports spectral and loudness differences with a summary of where they diverge.
example_prompt: How different do these two audio clips sound?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader decodes both clips to PCM, then FFT-based spectral comparison runs in WASM
rationale: Quantifies audio changes from re-encoding or editing without uploading potentially sensitive recordings.

name: word-frequency-diff
description: Compares the word/token frequency distributions of two texts and reports the biggest relative shifts.
example_prompt: What words got more or less common between these two drafts?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: tokenize, count, and compare frequency maps entirely in-memory
rationale: Reveals thematic and emphasis shifts between document versions that a line diff completely misses.

name: timeseries-align-diff
description: Aligns two timestamped series by their time keys (inner/outer join) and reports per-timestamp value differences.
example_prompt: Align these two timestamped series and show the value differences
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: timestamp parsing and keyed join, no network
rationale: Diffing two real-world series requires alignment on irregular timestamps before differencing, which nothing here covers.

name: tolerance-band-checker
description: Checks each measured value against a reference ± tolerance band (absolute or percent) and flags pass/fail with margins.
example_prompt: Which of these readings fall outside 100 ± 2%?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: bounds comparison over arrays, runs locally
rationale: QA/spec conformance checks compare values to a target band, a common task with no dedicated tool.

name: residual-calculator
description: Computes residuals (observed − predicted) between two series plus residual summary stats and a normality hint.
example_prompt: Give me the residuals between these observed and fitted values
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: elementwise subtraction and stats, fully sandboxed
rationale: Residual analysis between two series is a core model-diagnostic step distinct from scalar error metrics.

name: image-opaque-alpha-checker
description: Decodes an RGBA image and checks whether the alpha channel is fully opaque, meaning it can be dropped to a smaller RGB file.
example_prompt: Does this PNG actually use transparency or is the alpha wasted?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes pixels and scans the alpha channel — no network, fully local.
rationale: A fully-opaque alpha channel is pure wasted bytes, and flagging it lets users save real file size by switching to RGB.

name: image-palettizable-checker
description: Counts unique colors and reports whether an image can be losslessly reduced to a ≤256-color PNG-8 palette.
example_prompt: Can this PNG be saved as an indexed 256-color file without loss?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes and tallies unique colors in a hashset — fully client-side.
rationale: Many UI graphics secretly fit in 256 colors, and knowing this enables a large lossless size reduction to PNG-8.

name: video-start-time-offset-checker
description: Detects a non-zero or negative initial timestamp/start_time on any stream that can desync concatenation, trimming, or muxing.
example_prompt: Does this video start at timestamp zero or is there an offset?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm probes each stream's start_time and first PTS; analysis only, runs entirely in the browser.
rationale: Non-zero start offsets silently break concat and sync workflows, and surfacing them early prevents mysterious downstream drift.

name: video-color-tag-consistency-checker
description: Specifically lints the color primaries, transfer characteristics, matrix coefficients, and range tags for 'unspecified' or internally contradictory values.
example_prompt: Are this video's color primaries/transfer/matrix tags fully specified and consistent?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm probes the four color tags and the tool applies a known-good combination table; analysis only, client-side.
rationale: Unspecified or mismatched color tags cause washed-out or oversaturated playback across players, and a focused color-tag lint pinpoints exactly which tag is wrong.

name: video-audio-sample-rate-checker
description: Flags non-standard or delivery-inappropriate audio sample rates (e.g. 44.1 kHz where 48 kHz is required for broadcast/NLE) across all audio tracks.
example_prompt: Are all audio tracks in this video at 48 kHz?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm probes each audio stream's sample rate and the tool checks it against the target; metadata-only, client-side.
rationale: Mismatched sample rates force silent resampling in editors and break broadcast specs, a constraint easy to validate but easy to forget.

name: video-audio-dropout-checker
description: Scans the audio track for mid-stream silent gaps or dropouts that interrupt otherwise-continuous sound.
example_prompt: Are there any audio dropouts in the middle of this video?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm's silencedetect filter locates silent intervals and the tool filters out expected leading/trailing pauses; client-side.
rationale: Audio dropouts from buffer underruns or bad muxes are easy to miss on a quick listen but obvious to an automated gap scan.

name: video-dropframe-timecode-checker
description: Verifies that an embedded timecode's drop-frame flag is consistent with the video frame rate (drop-frame only valid for 29.97/59.94).
example_prompt: Is the drop-frame timecode flag correct for this video's frame rate?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the tmcd flags and frame rate and applies the drop-frame rule; arithmetic in the browser.
rationale: A wrong drop-frame flag throws off clock-accurate timecode in broadcast, a subtle spec error this check makes explicit.

name: tag-encoding-checker

example_prompt: Are the tags in these files showing as garbled text?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads tag text frames and runs encoding heuristics locally.
rationale: Encoding mismatches produce unreadable artist/title fields, and pinpointing them is far easier than guessing.

name: conflicting-tags-detector
description: Detects files carrying multiple competing tag systems (ID3v1 vs ID3v2, ID3 vs APE) and reports where their values disagree.
example_prompt: Does this file have conflicting tag systems?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM locates each tag block and diffs the overlapping fields locally.
rationale: Different players read different tag blocks, so conflicting tags cause inconsistent metadata that this flags directly.

name: album-metadata-consistency-check
description: Across a set of album tracks, checks that album, album-artist, year, genre, and disc tags agree and reports any outliers.
example_prompt: Check that all tracks in this album folder have consistent album tags
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads tags from each provided file and cross-compares them locally.
rationale: One mismatched album-artist splits an album into pieces in every music app, and this catches the stray track.

name: track-number-sequence-check
description: Validates a set of tracks for a contiguous track-number sequence, flagging gaps, duplicates, and missing total-track counts.
example_prompt: Are the track numbers in this album complete and in order?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads track-number tags and checks the sequence locally.
rationale: Gaps or duplicate track numbers reveal a missing or mis-tagged file before you notice it on playback.

name: filename-tag-mismatch-check
description: Compares each file's name against its title/artist/track tags and reports mismatches per a chosen naming pattern.
example_prompt: Do my filenames match the artist and title tags?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses filenames and tag values and compares them against a pattern locally.
rationale: Filename/tag drift breaks both file-based and tag-based browsing, and this reconciles the two without renaming anything.

name: color-value-validator
description: Validates and normalizes CSS color values across hex, rgb(a), hsl(a), and named forms, flagging out-of-range channels.
example_prompt: Validate these color values and normalize them to hex
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing each color syntax and checking channel ranges; pure parsing.
rationale: Design-token and theme files accumulate malformed colors and a validator normalizes a whole palette consistently.

name: robots-meta-checker
description: Scans HTML for robots meta tags and X-Robots equivalents, flagging conflicting or accidental noindex/nofollow directives.
example_prompt: Check this page's robots meta tags for accidental noindex.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML parse and directive reconciliation — fully client-side.
rationale: Accidental noindex meta tags silently kill SEO and a focused checker surfaces them fast.

name: html-table-accessibility-validator

example_prompt: Audit the accessibility of the tables in this HTML.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML parse and table-structure analysis — fully local.
rationale: Table accessibility is a frequent WCAG failure not covered by alt-text or ARIA checkers and needs dedicated rules.

name: http-cache-header-auditor
description: Audits Cache-Control, ETag, Expires, and Pragma headers together, flagging contradictions and missing revalidation settings.
example_prompt: Audit these response headers for caching mistakes.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM header parse and cross-directive reasoning — no network.
rationale: Caching headers interact in non-obvious ways and a holistic auditor prevents stale or uncacheable responses.

name: json-pointer-validate

example_prompt: Does the JSON Pointer /a/0/b resolve in this document?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM RFC 6901 parser plus resolver; in-memory
rationale: JSON Pointers appear in JSON Schema and Patch, and verifying they actually resolve saves debugging.

name: exif-software-detector

example_prompt: Was this image edited, and by what software?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the EXIF software tags from the bytes, fully offline.
rationale: A quick forensics/provenance signal for spotting whether a 'straight from camera' photo was actually processed.

name: dynamic-range-estimator
description: Estimates the captured dynamic range in stops from luminance percentiles and flags clipped highlights/shadows.
example_prompt: How many stops of dynamic range does this photo use?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM builds a luminance histogram and computes percentile EV spread offline.
rationale: Photographers gauging exposure latitude and HDR needs want a concrete range figure, not just an exposure verdict.

name: video-audio-track-loudness-compare

example_prompt: Are the English and Spanish dubs in my file at the same loudness?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg meters each audio track with ebur128 from the locally loaded multi-track file.
rationale: Dub/alternate tracks at different loudness jar viewers who switch languages, and no offline tool compares them.

name: video-frame-size-timeline
description: Charts the encoded byte size of each individual frame to expose oversized frames and rate spikes.

name: audio-spectral-cutoff-finder

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: averaged FFT spectrum, locate the upper edge where energy drops to noise; local compute.
rationale: The cutoff frequency reveals true quality/bitrate of a file independent of its claimed format.

name: audio-tempo-stability-analyzer
description: Tracks tempo over time to reveal drift, rubato, or speed inconsistencies across a recording.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: windowed tempo estimation across the file, output a BPM-vs-time curve; local FFT/autocorrelation.
rationale: Tempo drift detection helps decide if a take needs warping and isn't covered by single-value BPM tools.

name: audio-noise-type-classifier

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: compare the noise-floor spectral slope/peaks against known noise profiles; local FFT math.
rationale: Identifying noise type tells the user which specific filter or denoise approach to use.

name: npy-header-inspector

example_prompt: what's the dtype and shape of this npy file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing the small .npy header preamble from bytes.
rationale: Quickly vets array files for ML pipelines without reading gigabytes of data.

name: ngram-overlap

example_prompt: What's the trigram overlap between these two essays?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — build n-gram multisets and compute overlap, fully local
rationale: N-gram overlap is a standard, interpretable measure of textual closeness for reuse and similarity checks.

name: chord-progression-diff

example_prompt: Compare the chord progressions of these two song versions.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM does chroma-based chord recognition on both decoded tracks client-side.
rationale: Reveals harmonic edits or reharmonizations between two versions of a song.

name: transparent-background-checker
description: Verifies that an asset's background is genuinely transparent rather than a solid white/colored fill mistaken for transparency.
example_prompt: Is this logo's background actually transparent or just white?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM checks for an alpha channel and zero-alpha border regions.
rationale: Logos with baked-white backgrounds break on dark themes and are a constant asset-handoff mistake.

name: midi-note-range-checker

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses note-on events and compares pitches to range tables, no synthesis needed.
rationale: Out-of-range notes sound wrong or silent on real instruments, and an arranger-focused checker prevents that.

name: date-range-overlap

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM date arithmetic; pure offline computation
rationale: Detecting schedule conflicts and overlaps comes up constantly in planning and booking work.

name: percentile-rank-comparator

example_prompt: Where does a score of 85 rank in dataset A vs dataset B?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; sorting and rank lookup over two arrays, all in-memory.
rationale: Comparing how a value ranks across two populations (benchmarks, cohorts) makes relative standing concrete.

name: toeplitz-matrix-checker

example_prompt: Verify this matrix is Toeplitz
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — diagonal-constancy comparison across cells, all computed locally.
rationale: Toeplitz structure underlies signal-processing and convolution data; validating it catches malformed kernels.

name: histogram-sum-validator

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sum and nonnegativity check over bins, pure arithmetic in-browser.
rationale: Confirms a histogram accounts for every sample, catching dropped/double-counted bins in binned data.

name: image-megapixel-calculator

example_prompt: How big can I print this photo at 300 DPI?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: read dimensions and do arithmetic — entirely offline.
rationale: Answers the constant 'will it print big enough' question without a calculator.

name: extract-questions

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM sentence splitting + punctuation/interrogative heuristics, local

rationale: Defends against Trojan-Source-style hidden text and pasted bidi cruft.

name: strip-list-numbering

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM per-line trim, no server

name: video-colorspace-convert
