example_prompt: Convert this clip from BT.601 to BT.709 so the colors look right
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader uses colorspace/zscale filters with proper tagging in wasm
rationale: Mismatched color matrices cause washed/oversaturated playback; converting is a real fix, not just a report.

name: remove-inter-channel-delay
description: Estimates and corrects timing offset between left and right channels to re-align them.
example_prompt: The left channel lags the right slightly — align the two channels
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: cross-correlate the channels to find the lag, then shift one to compensate.
rationale: Inter-channel delay from mic spacing or routing smears stereo; auto-alignment restores a tight image.

name: series-bucket-aggregator
description: Splits an ordered numeric series into N equal-width buckets and aggregates each (mean/sum/min/max) into one row.
example_prompt: Aggregate this series into 100 buckets using the mean of each
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: index bucketing + per-bucket aggregate, all in-memory.
rationale: Bucket-aggregating a huge series down to a fixed size is a common downsample-for-analysis task not covered by histogram counting.

name: left-trim-lines
description: Removes leading whitespace from each line while leaving trailing content intact.
example_prompt: remove the leading indentation from every line
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM per-line trim_start, client-side
rationale: Flattens inconsistently-indented pasted snippets without disturbing line ends.

name: dockerfile-generate
description: Generate a sensible multi-stage Dockerfile for a chosen stack (Node, Rust, Python, Go).
example_prompt: write a Dockerfile for a Node 20 app with pnpm
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM templates per stack.
rationale: High-traffic scaffold request; pairs with the new dockerfile-lint.

name: frequency-response-plot
description: Plots magnitude and phase frequency response of a filter or measured impulse response (Bode-style).
example_prompt: Plot the frequency response of this speaker measurement
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — FFT plus an image encoder produce the plot fully client-side.
rationale: Transfer-function/frequency-response visualization is central to pyfar and audio-engineering work.

name: cohort-retention-heatmap
description: Converts cohort-by-period retention data into a triangular retention heatmap with percentage labels.
example_prompt: Turn this signup cohort table into a retention heatmap
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM normalizes retention rates and renders the staircase SVG grid locally, no server needed.
rationale: Retention heatmaps are a core growth/analytics artifact that founders and PMs request frequently.

name: path-normalizer
description: Normalizes and inspects file paths: collapses ./.. segments, splits components, and extracts parent, stem, and extension.
example_prompt: Normalize and break down this path: ./a/../b/c.tar.gz
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (camino/std path logic) manipulates UTF-8 paths in-browser.
rationale: Reasoning about messy relative paths is error-prone by hand and useful across scripting tasks.

name: solana-address-validator
description: Validates a Solana address, checking Base58 length and whether the key lies on the ed25519 curve.
example_prompt: Is this a valid Solana wallet address: 9WzDXwBbmkg8ZTbNMqUxvQRAyrZzDsGYdLVL9zYtAWWM?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Base58 decode plus an ed25519 on-curve check runs locally with no RPC call.
rationale: Anchor/Solana developers need to distinguish wallet keys from PDAs (off-curve) and reject typos before submitting transactions.

name: ascii-diagram-to-svg
description: Converts hand-drawn ASCII-art box/arrow diagrams into clean rendered SVG.
example_prompt: Turn this ASCII diagram into an SVG: +--+  -->  +--+
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — svgbob is a pure-Rust crate with no I/O, so it compiles to wasmi and renders entirely client-side.
rationale: Devs constantly sketch ASCII diagrams in READMEs and want presentable SVGs without a server round-trip.

name: mp2-to-mp3
description: Converts MPEG-1 Layer II (.mp2) broadcast audio to MP3.
example_prompt: convert this mp2 broadcast file to mp3
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader decodes MP2 and encodes MP3 in wasm, no upload.
rationale: Radio automation and DVB systems output MP2, which consumer players and editors rarely accept.

name: video-color-tag-fix
description: Sets or corrects color primaries, transfer, and matrix metadata without re-encoding pixels.
example_prompt: tag this clip as bt709 so the colors stop looking off
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm writes color metadata via bitstream flags locally
rationale: Missing or wrong color tags cause players to misinterpret colors and a metadata fix is lossless.

name: dns-query-builder
description: Builds a DNS query in wire format (and the DoH base64url GET form) for a given name and record type.
example_prompt: Build a DNS query for the AAAA record of example.com and give me the DoH base64url
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust wire-format encoder plus base64url in WASM; constructs bytes only, no request sent.
rationale: Generating a correct DNS/DoH query payload is the offline-computable core of the DNS-over-HTTPS demand.

name: js-ast-explorer
description: Parses JavaScript and returns its abstract syntax tree as inspectable JSON.
example_prompt: show me the AST of this JS code
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using swc_ecma_parser to emit a serializable AST; entirely in-browser.
rationale: An AST view helps developers understand parsing, tooling, and codemods without external playgrounds.

name: graphql-schema-stats
description: Counts types, fields, enums, and interfaces in a GraphQL SDL and flags unreferenced types.
example_prompt: give me stats on this graphql schema
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing the SDL into an AST and tallying definitions.
rationale: Quantifies schema size and surface area for API design review.

name: heading-level-shifter
description: Promotes or demotes every Markdown heading by a fixed number of levels.
example_prompt: Shift all the headings in this markdown down one level
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — line-prefix adjustment, no I/O
rationale: Embedding one document inside another requires rebalancing all heading levels at once.

name: oauth2-url-builder
description: Builds a correctly encoded OAuth2 authorization request URL from client ID, scopes, redirect, state, and PKCE params.
example_prompt: Build the OAuth2 authorize URL for this client ID, these scopes, and PKCE
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM doing URL/query encoding; pure string assembly, no network call needed.
rationale: OAuth2c's core help is constructing valid authorize URLs, which is just deterministic local encoding.

name: uint256-calculator
description: Performs exact arbitrary-precision arithmetic on 256-bit unsigned integers with hex/decimal I/O.
example_prompt: What is 2**256 - 1 minus 1000000 in hex?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — big-integer arithmetic avoids JavaScript's 53-bit float limit entirely in the sandbox.
rationale: Token amounts and EVM math overflow normal calculators; exact uint256 math is a constant requirement when working with Foundry/EVM.

name: astro-coordinate-converter
description: Converts between equatorial, horizontal, and galactic astronomical coordinate systems.
example_prompt: Convert RA 10h 0m, Dec +20° to galactic coordinates.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — rotation-matrix math from astro-rust, fully offline.
rationale: Coordinate conversion is a daily chore for observers and is the math behind Aladin-style viewers.

name: sudoku-image-reader
description: Detects a Sudoku grid in a photo and extracts the given digits into a solvable 9x9 grid.
example_prompt: Read this Sudoku puzzle photo into a grid I can solve
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime digit recognition plus plain-Rust grid detection run locally in wasmi.
rationale: Puzzlers want to lift printed Sudoku into digital form without retyping every cell.

name: set-similarity-calculator
description: Computes Jaccard, Dice/Sørensen, and overlap-coefficient similarity between two sets of items or numbers.
example_prompt: Jaccard similarity between these two sets of tags?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: set intersection/union counting, client-side.
rationale: The standard family of set-overlap measures, useful for tags, keywords, and feature sets.

name: ascii-only-checker
description: Reports any non-ASCII characters in text along with their positions and code points.
example_prompt: Tell me which characters here aren't ASCII
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scan; client-side.
rationale: Verifying ASCII-only constraints (identifiers, legacy systems) is a frequent, instant offline check.

name: rms-level-compare
description: Reports the overall and per-channel RMS levels of two files and the difference in dB.
example_prompt: Which of these two clips is louder on average, and by how many dB?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM sums squared PCM samples per file in the browser.
rationale: A simple energy-level delta is the fastest fair-volume check before any subjective A/B.

name: day-of-week
description: Returns the weekday name for any given past or future date.
example_prompt: what day of the week was 1995-07-12
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM calendar math, fully offline.
rationale: Perennial 'what day was I born / what day will it fall on' query that derives directly from date parsing.

name: seven-segment-display-reader
description: Reads the digits on a seven-segment LCD/LED display (meters, clocks, scales) into a number.
example_prompt: Read the number on this digital meter photo
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime (or classical segment thresholding in Rust): operates on the cropped display region client-side.
rationale: Logging readings from instruments/meters by photo is a frequent industrial and home need with no catalog equivalent.

name: braille-image-decoder
description: Detects Braille dot cells in an image and decodes them into the corresponding text.
example_prompt: Decode the Braille shown in this picture into text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: dot-grid detection over the binarized pixel buffer plus a Braille lookup table runs fully on CPU.
rationale: Accessibility and education use cases need to read Braille from images, an extraction the OCR tools don't handle.

name: flac-seektable-reader
description: Parses the FLAC SEEKTABLE metadata block into a JSON list of seekpoints with sample number, byte offset, and frame size.
example_prompt: Dump the seektable from this flac
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — reads fixed-width 18-byte seekpoint entries from the SEEKTABLE block.
rationale: Inspecting seekpoints helps diagnose seeking problems and verify a file was encoded with usable seek metadata.

name: opus-header-reader
description: Decodes the binary OpusHead identification header (version, channels, pre-skip, input sample rate, output gain, channel mapping).
example_prompt: Read the OpusHead fields from this opus file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — locates the OpusHead packet on the first Ogg page and parses its fixed binary layout.
rationale: OpusHead binary fields like pre-skip and output gain govern gapless playback yet are unreadable by tag tools.

name: mp3-frame-header-table
description: Walks every MPEG audio frame in an MP3 and tabulates each frame's bitrate, sample rate, channel mode, and CRC flag.
example_prompt: Build a per-frame header table for this mp3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — syncs on 0xFFE frame markers and decodes the 32-bit header bitfields, no audio decode.
rationale: A frame-by-frame header table exposes free-format frames, mid-file bitrate switches, and stream corruption.

name: hex-dump-to-bytes
description: Parses a hex dump (xxd/hexdump style) back into raw byte values as a decimal CSV array.
example_prompt: Convert this hexdump into a list of byte values
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; hex parsing and offset stripping, fully local
rationale: Reverse-engineering and forensics need numeric byte arrays out of pasted hex dumps.

name: video-color-bars-detector
description: Detects the presence of SMPTE/EBU color-bar test patterns at the head of a clip and reports their duration.
example_prompt: Does this clip start with color bars, and how long do they last?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader samples head frames in WASM and plain-Rust pattern analysis identifies bar layouts locally.
rationale: Leftover or required color-bar slates are part of broadcast QC, and detecting them automates a manual check.

name: css-duplicate-property-finder
description: Parses CSS and flags duplicate or overridden declarations within a rule and rules that fully shadow earlier ones.
example_prompt: Find duplicate or overridden properties in this CSS
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSS parser and per-rule declaration diffing; local.
rationale: Accidental duplicate declarations cause hard-to-spot override bugs and easy cleanup wins.

name: yaml-duplicate-key-detector
description: Finds duplicate mapping keys and conflicting anchors in YAML that cause silent value overrides.
example_prompt: Check this YAML for duplicate keys
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM YAML event parser tracking key occurrences; offline
rationale: Duplicate YAML keys silently overwrite config and are a common production footgun.

name: latlong-coordinate-validator
description: Validates latitude/longitude ranges, parses multiple notations (DMS, decimal), and normalizes to decimal degrees.
example_prompt: Is 91.5, -200 a valid coordinate, and convert 40°26′46″N to decimal
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; range checks + format parsing
rationale: Coordinate range/format errors are common in data pipelines and trivial to validate offline.

name: video-container-format-detector
description: Identifies the true container format (MP4, MKV, MOV, AVI, FLV, MPEG-TS, WebM) from magic bytes regardless of file extension.
example_prompt: What container format is this file really, the extension says .mov
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: signature sniffing reads only the first few hundred bytes locally.
rationale: Mislabeled extensions break pipelines, and a reliable magic-byte detector resolves it instantly without uploading.

name: partitioned-cookie-analyzer
description: Parses a Set-Cookie line and reports whether it is correctly partitioned under CHIPS, checking the Partitioned attribute alongside Secure and SameSite.
example_prompt: Is Set-Cookie: id=1; Secure; Partitioned; SameSite=None a valid CHIPS cookie?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Set-Cookie attribute parsing plus CHIPS requirement checks, no server
rationale: CHIPS partitioned cookies are required as third-party cookies are phased out and have strict co-requirements people miss.

name: lang-attribute-checker
description: Checks every lang attribute in an HTML document for a valid BCP-47 tag and warns when the document root is missing a language declaration.
example_prompt: Are the lang attributes in my HTML valid, and is <html lang> set?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — HTML parse plus BCP-47 subtag validation, fully local
rationale: A correct lang attribute is a core accessibility/SEO requirement and invalid tags like lang="english" are common.

name: flac-metadata-block-inspector
description: Lists every FLAC metadata block (STREAMINFO, SEEKTABLE, CUESHEET, PICTURE, APPLICATION, PADDING) with sizes and STREAMINFO details like MD5 and total samples.
example_prompt: What metadata blocks does this flac file contain?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — FLAC metadata blocks are a length-prefixed list at the file head, parsed before any audio frames
rationale: FLAC packs seektables, cuesheets and embedded art in distinct blocks that no Vorbis-comment reader surfaces.

name: synced-lyrics-extractor
description: Extracts synchronized lyrics from an ID3 SYLT frame and exports them as a timestamped LRC file.
example_prompt: Export the synced lyrics from this mp3 as an LRC
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses SYLT timestamp/text pairs and reformats them into LRC syntax entirely in-memory
rationale: SYLT karaoke timing is locked inside the file binary; converting it to portable LRC has no off-the-shelf option.

name: app-store-screenshot-validator
description: Validates a screenshot's dimensions and aspect against App Store / Play Store device-class requirements and reports failures.
example_prompt: Check if this screenshot meets App Store requirements
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM compares header dimensions against a built-in spec table, no network.
rationale: Store submissions get rejected for tiny dimension mismatches; pre-checking saves a review cycle.

name: png-color-type-checker
description: Reports a PNG's color type (grayscale, palette, RGB, RGBA) and bit depth and recommends a more efficient type when applicable.
example_prompt: What color type is this PNG and could it be smaller?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the IHDR chunk and samples pixels in-browser.
rationale: Mis-chosen PNG color types waste bytes and a quick read points at a cheaper encoding.

name: png-gamma-chunk-checker
description: Detects gAMA/cHRM chunks in a PNG that cause cross-browser color shifts and recommends stripping or normalizing them.
example_prompt: Why does this PNG look different across browsers — check its gamma chunk
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the gAMA/cHRM chunks from the PNG client-side.
rationale: Stray gAMA chunks are a well-known source of browser color inconsistency and are easy to overlook.

name: video-pixel-format-checker
description: Reports a video's pixel format and flags non-yuv420p or 10-bit formats that may break compatibility with a target.
example_prompt: Is this video yuv420p for maximum compatibility?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: ffprobe pix_fmt read in ffmpeg.wasm and checked against the target locally.
rationale: yuv444p or 10-bit exports silently fail to play on many devices and web players that only accept yuv420p.

name: video-color-space-checker
description: Reports a video's color primaries, transfer characteristics, and matrix coefficients and flags missing or non-BT.709 tagging.
example_prompt: Check the color space tags on this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: ffprobe color metadata from ffmpeg.wasm is evaluated client-side.
rationale: Untagged or wrong color metadata makes colors shift between players, a subtle and widespread bug.

name: video-sample-rate-checker
description: Verifies a video's audio sample rate matches a required value such as 48 kHz for broadcast.
example_prompt: Is this video's audio at 48kHz?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: ffprobe sample_rate read in ffmpeg.wasm and checked locally.
rationale: Broadcast and many platforms mandate 48 kHz; a 44.1 kHz track triggers resampling or rejection.

name: digital-silence-checker
description: Detects fully digital-silent (all-zero or below true-silence floor) files or channels, catching dead channels and empty exports.
example_prompt: Is the right channel of this file completely silent?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: scan decoded PCM for any non-zero sample per channel, trivially WASM
rationale: A silently-dead channel from a bad export or cable is easy to ship and embarrassing; this catches it instantly.

name: frequency-balance-checker
description: Computes the long-term average spectrum, splits it into standard bands, and flags muddy, harsh, or thin tonal balance against a reference target curve.
example_prompt: Check the tonal balance of this mix — is it too bass-heavy or harsh?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: averaged FFT spectrum binned into bands on decoded PCM, compared to a built-in curve client-side
rationale: Objective spectral balance against a reference curve catches frequency problems that monitors and ears can mask.

name: semver-validate
description: Validates a semantic version string and can compare two versions for ordering.
example_prompt: Is '1.2.0-rc.1+build5' valid semver, and is it newer than 1.1.9?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the semver crate; pure parsing/comparison
rationale: Version handling in release tooling and manifests is error-prone.

name: roman-numeral-validator
description: Checks whether a Roman numeral is well-formed under standard subtractive rules and reports its integer value.
example_prompt: Is MCMXCIV a valid Roman numeral?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: rule-based parsing of the numeral grammar, no network.
rationale: Many parsers silently accept malformed numerals like IIII or VX, so a strict validator is genuinely useful.

name: iso8601-datetime-validator
description: Validates ISO 8601 dates, times, intervals, and durations and explains which component is malformed.
example_prompt: Is 'P1Y2M10DT2H30M' a valid ISO 8601 duration?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with chrono/iso8601 parsing; no clock needed
rationale: ISO 8601 has many corner cases and a strict validator catches the malformed strings that break date parsers.

name: image-saliency-detector
description: Predicts where viewers look first and renders a saliency/attention heatmap over the image.
example_prompt: Where will people look first in this design?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime runs a bundled saliency model on decoded pixels in-browser.
rationale: Attention maps guide cropping, layout, and ad/thumbnail design decisions.

name: video-color-histogram
description: Computes RGB and luma histograms for a chosen frame or the whole clip to inspect tonal distribution.
example_prompt: Show the RGB histogram for this video frame
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg `histogram` filter renders the distribution directly from decoded pixels in wasm.
rationale: Histograms are the standard tool for judging exposure and clipping, and there's no offline browser equivalent.

name: instrument-classifier
description: Identifies the dominant instrument(s) present in a short audio clip.
example_prompt: Which instruments are playing in this loop?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js runs an instrument-recognition model entirely in the browser on log-mel input
rationale: Instrument tags speed up sample-library organization and stem identification.

name: java-class-inspector
description: Parses a Java .class file and shows its constant pool, version, access flags, fields, and methods.
example_prompt: Inspect this .class file and list its methods
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the class file format is a byte-offset parse with no JVM required, fully client-side
rationale: Reverse-engineering or verifying compiled Java without a decompiler or toolchain install.

name: pem-validator
description: Validates a PEM block's BEGIN/END markers, label consistency, and base64 body without parsing key material.
example_prompt: Is this PEM block structurally valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM checking markers and decoding the base64 body; key data stays in the browser
rationale: Copy-pasted certificates and keys often have broken wrapping that a structural check catches without exposing the secret.

name: ntfs-volume-inspector
description: Parses an NTFS boot sector / $Boot to report cluster and sector size, MFT location, volume serial, and geometry.
example_prompt: What's the cluster size and MFT offset of this NTFS image?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: reads fixed on-disk structures from the uploaded image header.
rationale: NTFSTool's volume-info pass orients every other NTFS artifact and is trivially local.

name: image-noise-map
description: Generates a noise/luminance-gradient map to reveal inconsistent sensor noise that betrays pasted or manipulated regions.
example_prompt: Show the noise map of this image to find spliced areas
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute: per-pixel high-pass and variance filters run as shaders on the local GPU.
rationale: Complements ELA from the sherloq toolkit, catching edits ELA misses, all without server-side image processing.

name: nft-metadata-validate
description: Validates ERC-721/ERC-1155 token metadata JSON against the standard schema and flags missing or malformed fields.
example_prompt: validate this NFT metadata json
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — JSON schema validation, offline.
rationale: Marketplaces like OpenSea reject malformed metadata, so creators benefit from local pre-flight validation.

name: chip8-assembler
description: Assembles CHIP-8 assembly source into a runnable binary ROM.
example_prompt: Assemble this CHIP-8 program into a ROM
loader_feasibility: Text-to-bytecode assembly is pure logic in plain Rust→WASM with a downloadable output.
rationale: Completes the CHIP-8 dev loop alongside the disassembler for the active CHIP-8 hacking community.

name: ast-explorer
description: Parses code with tree-sitter and shows its concrete syntax tree, letting you inspect node types and ranges.
example_prompt: show me the syntax tree for this JavaScript function
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: tree-sitter and its grammars compile to wasm32 and run inside wasmi; heavier because grammars are bundled, but fully local.
rationale: ki-editor is built on tree-sitter, and an AST viewer is invaluable for writing queries, linters, and codemods.

name: webhook-signature-verifier
description: Verifies an HMAC webhook signature (GitHub, Stripe or Svix style) against a payload and secret.
example_prompt: Verify this GitHub webhook signature against the payload
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — HMAC-SHA256 over the payload with constant-time compare, no network.
rationale: Debugging webhook delivery means checking signatures, and doing it locally keeps the signing secret off the wire.

name: nix-expression-formatter
description: Parses and pretty-prints a pasted Nix expression with consistent indentation and attribute alignment, reporting syntax errors with positions.
example_prompt: Format this Nix expression
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with a Nix grammar parser and pretty-printer; formatting is a pure source-to-source transform
rationale: Nix code is notoriously hard to format by hand and a deterministic formatter is exactly the kind of offline transform browsers can run.

name: js-import-graph
description: Analyzes import/export statements across pasted JS/TS modules to build a dependency graph and flag circular imports and unresolved specifiers.
example_prompt: Map the import graph for these JS modules and find any circular dependencies
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizing ESM import/export syntax; static analysis over pasted files, no bundling or execution
rationale: rolldown's bundler ecosystem cares about module graphs, and circular-import detection is a high-value static check that runs locally.

name: elf-binary-size-analyzer
description: Parses an uploaded ELF binary and breaks down its size by section (.text/.data/.rodata) and largest symbols, like a local cargo-bloat.
example_prompt: Analyze the section sizes of this compiled Rust binary
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the object/goblin crate parses ELF in WASM and the file is read via the browser File API, nothing leaves the device.
rationale: mini-docker-rust and musl-builder users obsess over binary size, and a local analyzer shows where the bytes go without extra tooling.

name: allocation-profile-summary
description: Summarizes allocation samples by call site, showing the top allocators and total bytes.
example_prompt: summarize these allocation samples
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse and aggregate the dump locally
rationale: Delivers the Bytehound triage view — find the biggest allocators fast.

name: rust-unsafe-block-auditor
description: Finds every `unsafe` block/fn in pasted Rust, shows its surrounding context, and attaches a soundness-review checklist per occurrence.
example_prompt: List every unsafe block in this Rust file so I can review them
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM; brace-matched text parsing only, fully local.
rationale: Concentrating review attention on unsafe sites is the practical core of static-analysis safety auditing.

name: sql-seed-generator
description: Generates SQL INSERT statements populated with fake data for a given table schema.
example_prompt: Generate 50 INSERT rows for table users(id, name, email, created_at)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — column parsing and SQL string emission with fake values run entirely in-sandbox.
rationale: Seeding dev/test databases is a constant chore that fake-data plus SQL output eliminates.

name: openapi-mock-data
description: Generates mock response payloads for the endpoints defined in an OpenAPI/Swagger spec.
example_prompt: From this OpenAPI spec, generate mock responses for the GET endpoints
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — YAML/JSON parsing and schema-to-sample generation run without any server.
rationale: httpmock/mockito users mock APIs constantly; instant payloads straight from a spec save hours of setup.

name: decision-tree-to-rules
description: Converts a trained decision tree into human-readable if/then rules and equivalent code.
example_prompt: Turn this trained decision tree into plain if/else rules
loader_feasibility: pyodide — scikit-learn tree traversal runs in the browser Python sandbox with no server round-trip.
rationale: Like m2cgen, readable rules make ML models auditable and deployable as plain, dependency-free code.

name: route-optimizer
description: Finds a near-optimal visiting order for a set of locations (traveling-salesman) via genetic and 2-opt search.
example_prompt: Given these 12 city coordinates, find the shortest route visiting all of them
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — distance-matrix computation and the GA loop run entirely in the sandbox.
rationale: TSP-style route ordering is a classic, widely-needed optimization for delivery and trip planning.

name: symbolic-regression
description: Discovers a compact math formula that fits your x/y data using genetic programming.
example_prompt: Find a formula that fits this table of measurements.
loader_feasibility: radiate genetic-programming in plain Rust→WASM; program evolution is pure compute in wasmi.
rationale: Symbolic regression recovers interpretable equations from data, valuable in science and rare in consumer tools.

name: qr-video-decoder
description: Decodes a QR-code video back into the original text or data.
example_prompt: Decode the text from this QR video.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg extracts frames and a plain Rust→WASM QR decoder (rqrr) reconstructs the payload locally.
rationale: The decode side is the necessary complement to QR-video archival and must reconstruct data privately (memvid).

name: fastq-quality-stats
description: Parses FASTQ reads and summarizes Phred quality scores, per-position quality, read-length distribution, and GC content.
example_prompt: Summarize the read quality in this FASTQ file.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: text parsing plus Phred decoding and aggregation, no network needed and keeps raw reads local.
rationale: A lightweight FastQC-style summary that runs without uploading sequencing reads is genuinely useful and privacy-preserving.

name: dna-motif-search
description: Searches a sequence for a motif expressed with IUPAC ambiguity codes or a regex, returning all match positions on both strands.
example_prompt: Find all GGNCC motifs in this sequence on both strands.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: IUPAC-to-pattern expansion plus scanning, pure compute like Rust-Bio's pattern matching.
rationale: Locating binding sites and degenerate motifs is a frequent task that is easy to get wrong by eye.

name: docopt-parser
description: Parses a docopt-style usage/help string into a structured JSON schema of commands, options, and positional arguments.
example_prompt: Turn this docopt usage block into a JSON schema of its flags and arguments
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure text parsing of the usage grammar, no network or filesystem, runs fully in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: docopt's whole value is deriving structure from a usage string, so a one-shot parser makes that reusable in any toolchain.

name: bech32-encode
description: Encodes and decodes Bech32/Bech32m strings used by Bitcoin SegWit and Cosmos addresses.
example_prompt: decode this bc1 segwit address to its witness program
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the bech32 crate, a pure checksum/charset transform that runs entirely in wasmi.
rationale: Bech32 is the modern address format across multiple chains and developers need to inspect or build these addresses locally.

name: cql-schema-generator
description: Generates valid Cassandra CREATE KEYSPACE/TABLE DDL from a table name, column list, and partition/clustering keys.
example_prompt: create a Cassandra table events with id uuid, ts timestamp, payload text, partition key id, clustering key ts
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM: assembles the DDL string from structured inputs, fully deterministic and local.
rationale: Hand-writing CQL DDL with correct PRIMARY KEY and clustering syntax is error-prone; structured generation removes mistakes.

name: influx-line-protocol-validator
description: Validates and formats InfluxDB line protocol, checking measurement, tag, field, and timestamp structure.
example_prompt: validate this line protocol: cpu,host=a usage=0.6 1620000000000000000
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM: parses and checks line-protocol text with no server.
rationale: Malformed line protocol silently drops writes, so offline validation catches issues before ingest.

name: mongodb-schema-validator-generator
description: Generates a MongoDB $jsonSchema collection validator from a sample document.
example_prompt: generate a MongoDB schema validator for {name:'a', age:30, tags:['x']}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM: infers types into $jsonSchema and runs locally.
rationale: Authoring $jsonSchema by hand is verbose, and inference from a sample is far faster.

name: julian-date
description: Convert between calendar dates and astronomical Julian Date / Julian Day Number.
example_prompt: What is the Julian Date for 2026-06-17 12:00 UTC?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM date math, offline.
rationale: Astronomy and some software use JD; distinct from epoch/ISO timestamp tools.

name: email-signature-generator
description: Builds an HTML email signature block from contact and role details.
example_prompt: Create an email signature for me as Head of Product at Acme
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM templates the HTML locally; copy-paste ready.
rationale: Recurring Communication need that existing tools monetize with watermarks.

name: snapshot-comparator
description: Compares actual program output against an expected snapshot and highlights mismatches.
example_prompt: Does this output match my expected snapshot?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — normalize + diff, local
rationale: Snapshot/golden-file testing is the literal 'validation test op' and needs no server.

name: shell-test-scaffold
description: Generates a bats-core or shellspec test skeleton from a shell script, with stubbed cases per function.
example_prompt: Create bats tests for this bash script
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the script and emits a test-file template offline.
rationale: bats-core and shellspec require repetitive scaffolding, and auto-stubbing lowers the barrier to testing shell code.

name: slide-speaker-notes-extractor
description: Pulls presenter notes out of a Marp/reveal-style deck and outputs them as a per-slide speaker script.
example_prompt: Extract just the speaker notes from this slide markdown
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — comment/notes-block parsing over the deck text, no server.
rationale: Presenters (decktape/marp users) need a clean rehearsal script separate from the slides themselves.

name: domain-permutator
description: Generates domain-name variations from a keyword — TLD swaps, typos, hyphenations, prefixes/suffixes — for brainstorming or typosquat audits.
example_prompt: Generate domain name variations for 'gizza' across common TLDs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string generation; tldx's permutation core needs no network, only availability lookup does.
rationale: tldx's permutation engine is browser-local and the brandable/typosquat ideas are the genuinely hard part.

name: symbolic-equation-solver
description: Solves single equations or systems symbolically and shows exact solutions.
example_prompt: Solve x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0 and this system for x and y.
loader_feasibility: pyodide: SymPy runs in the in-browser Python sandbox, no compute server.
rationale: The headline capability of AngouriMathCLI, delivered fully client-side via SymPy.

name: notepad-tape-calculator
description: Soulver-style multi-line calculator: write text with inline math, named variables, and a running total per line.
example_prompt:
rent = 1800
food = 400
total = rent + food
20% of total
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — line-by-line parsing, variable binding, and evaluation are pure computation in wasmi.
rationale: Maps Nota/TuringTape demand; the running-tape notepad model is a genuinely different and popular calculation UX.

name: regex-test-runner
description: Runs a regex against a labelled list of should-match and should-not-match cases and reports pass/fail like a unit test.
example_prompt: Run my regex /^[a-z0-9_]{3,16}$/ against these usernames and tell me which fail
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM evaluates each case locally and tallies results.
rationale: Embodies 'treat regular expressions as code, not magic' and mirrors the HackerRank/Regex-Exercises challenge-verification loop.

name: form-validation-rules
description: Generates HTML5 validation attributes plus matching regex patterns and inline error messages for a described set of form fields (email, phone, postcode, etc.).
example_prompt: Give me validation rules and patterns for a checkout form with email, phone, and a US zip code
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM maps field types to known patterns and constraints; static lookup and string assembly, fully local.
rationale: Hosted form builders bury validation behind their UI; developers wiring their own forms need the constraint set directly.

name: share-link-builder
description: Generates ready-to-use share URLs and button HTML for X, Facebook, LinkedIn, Reddit, WhatsApp and email from a URL and title.
example_prompt: make share links and buttons for https://example.com/post 'My new article'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure URL templating and percent-encoding per network, the core of ShareThis, entirely local.
rationale: Hand-building per-network share URLs is fiddly and a deterministic generator removes the guesswork.

name: word-inflector
description: Pluralizes, singularizes, and converts case/format (camelCase, snake_case, title case) of words and identifiers.
example_prompt: Pluralize "person" and "octopus", and singularize "data".
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM port of inflection rules (like Infections-clj), purely rule-based and offline.
rationale: Inflections-clj is direct demand evidence and inflection helpers are constantly needed for codegen and copy.

name: session-bounce-analyzer
description: Sessionizes pageview events and reports session count, bounce rate, and average session duration.
example_prompt: Sessionize these pageviews and give me the bounce rate: <paste>
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM event sorting and gap-based sessionization; offline.
rationale: Bounce rate and session metrics are core analytics KPIs derivable purely from the user's own event stream.

name: license-detector
description: Identifies the open-source license of a LICENSE file and summarizes its key obligations.
example_prompt: What license is this and what are its terms? <paste LICENSE text>
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM normalized-text matching against bundled SPDX license texts; offline.
rationale: License identification is a common compliance need when evaluating GitHub and F-Droid projects.

name: apk-signature-info
description: Reads an APK's v1 JAR signature (PKCS#7 cert in META-INF) and extracts the signing certificate subject, validity, and SHA-256 fingerprint.
example_prompt: Show me the signing certificate fingerprint of this APK
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: ZIP extraction plus PKCS#7/X.509 parsing via Rust crypto crates, all computed locally with no key material leaving the browser.
rationale: Accrescent/Obtainium users verify that an update is signed by the same key as the installed app to avoid signature-spoof attacks.

name: adb-debloat-command-generator
description: Takes a list of package names (or a checklist of common OEM bloat) and emits ready-to-run `adb shell pm uninstall --user 0` or disable commands.
example_prompt: Give me adb commands to remove these stock packages without root
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pure text templating over the input package list, no execution and no network.
rationale: Universal Android Debloater users want copy-paste, user-0 removal commands without installing the desktop tool.

name: bounding-box-tool
description: Computes the bounding box and center point of a set of coordinates or a GeoJSON/GPX file.
example_prompt: What's the bounding box and center of this GPX track?
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM min/max scan over parsed coordinates; offline.
rationale: Bounding boxes are needed to define OSM extract regions, offline map downloads, and map viewports.

name: gpx-heatmap-image
description: Renders a GPX track or set of points as a PNG heatmap/track image with adjustable intensity.
example_prompt: Make a heatmap image from all my GPX runs in this folder
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM raster (image crate) or webgpu-compute accumulation; renders to a PNG buffer in-browser.
rationale: Personal-tracking users love Strava-style heatmaps but won't upload their full history to make one.

name: streaming-export-to-playlist
description: Converts an exported Spotify/streaming playlist (CSV or JSON) into M3U or XSPF.
example_prompt: Convert my exported Spotify playlist CSV to an M3U
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses and re-serializes the text client-side.
rationale: Users migrating off Spotify via Spotube/psst to self-hosted players need their playlists in a standard, server-agnostic format.

name: mastodon-thread-splitter
description: Splits a long text into a numbered thread of posts that each respect a character limit, breaking on word/sentence boundaries.
example_prompt: Split this essay into a Mastodon thread of 500-character posts
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: greedy boundary-aware chunking on the input string, fully local.
rationale: Fediverse posters (Mastodon/Pixelfed/Plume) constantly need to thread long text under per-post limits and it is pure string work.

name: chat-export-analyzer
description: Parses Revolt/Discord/Twake chat export JSON into per-channel stats and a searchable message view.
example_prompt: Search my Revolt export for messages from last month about deploys
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON parse + aggregation on uploaded files; entirely local.
rationale: Chat-platform users need private, searchable analysis of their own exported history without re-uploading it.

name: discord-export-analyzer
description: Computes activity stats (top posters, busiest hours, message/word counts) from a DiscordChatExporter JSON export.
example_prompt: Give me stats on who talks most in this Discord export
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses the export JSON and aggregates metrics entirely in-browser.
rationale: Discord mods and community managers want server analytics without handing chat history to a third-party bot.

name: gitlab-ci-validator
description: Validates a .gitlab-ci.yml file's structure, stages, and job references and flags common mistakes.
example_prompt: Check my .gitlab-ci.yml for errors
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses the YAML and applies GitLab CI schema/structural checks locally.
rationale: Catching CI config errors before a push saves slow pipeline round-trips and is a direct GitLab demand.

name: eval-metrics-calculator
description: Computes NLP/LLM evaluation metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, METEOR, exact-match, token F1) between predictions and references.
example_prompt: Score these model outputs against the references with BLEU and ROUGE
loader_feasibility: pyodide: runs standard metric implementations (sacrebleu/rouge) in a Python sandbox locally.
rationale: Anyone doing ai-evaluation needs these metrics constantly, and a local calculator avoids spinning up a Python environment.

name: metaheuristic-optimizer
description: Minimizes or maximizes a user-defined objective over parameters using a genetic algorithm or simulated annealing.
example_prompt: Find parameters that minimize this function
loader_feasibility: pyodide — evaluates the user's Python objective in the sandbox while the search loop drives it.
rationale: A general-purpose heuristic search for problems with no closed-form solution, entirely local and arbitrary-objective.

name: high-utility-pattern-miner
description: Finds high-utility and periodic itemsets from quantity/price-weighted transactions, surfacing the most profitable recurring patterns.
example_prompt: Which item combinations drive the most revenue in this sales log?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — utility-list pruning (TPU-style) is pure combinatorial computation, runs entirely client-side.
rationale: Extends plain frequency mining with profit/recurrence weighting that retailers and analysts actually ask for.

name: ieee754-hex-to-float-csv
description: Decodes a column of IEEE-754 hex words (32/64-bit) into their exact decimal float values.
example_prompt: Decode these 32-bit hex floats into decimal numbers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: bit-reinterpreting hex into f32/f64 is a native, exact operation in WASM.
rationale: Firmware/register dumps log floats as hex and engineers need the real value without manual bit math.

name: morphological-analyzer
description: Returns a word's lemma plus morphological features — POS, gender, number, case, tense — for morphologically rich languages.
example_prompt: Give the morphological analysis of the Hindi word 'लड़कियों'.
loader_feasibility: transformers-js / onnx-runtime runs a seq2seq morphological-analysis ONNX model in-browser; decoding of feature tags is local.
rationale: Directly realizes the Multi-Task Deep Morphological Analyzer demand, which is far more valuable interactive than as a research artifact.

name: openapi-skeleton-generator
description: Scaffolds an OpenAPI 3 spec from a list of path and method entries with stub responses.
example_prompt: scaffold an OpenAPI spec for GET /users, POST /users, GET /users/{id}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: builds the paths object and serializes YAML/JSON locally, no server.
rationale: Bootstrapping a valid OpenAPI document by hand is slow and indentation-heavy.

name: flatten-transparency
description: Composites a transparent image onto a chosen solid background color to remove the alpha channel.
example_prompt: Flatten this PNG onto a white background
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — alpha-over blend against a constant color per pixel
rationale: Needed whenever transparent PNGs must become solid JPEGs without dark fringing.

name: remove-vignette
description: Corrects lens-induced edge darkening by flattening the radial brightness falloff.
example_prompt: Fix the dark corners on this wide-angle photo
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — estimate radial gain curve from corner-vs-center luminance and divide it out
rationale: Lens vignetting is a real defect in phone and action-cam shots with no dedicated fix.

name: lens-distortion-correct
description: Removes barrel or pincushion distortion with an adjustable radial distortion coefficient.
example_prompt: Fix the fisheye bulge in this wide-angle shot
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — radial remap function with interpolation, pure math
rationale: Action-cam and wide-angle bulge is a real defect users want straightened locally.

name: css-vendor-prefix-stripper
description: Removes obsolete vendor-prefixed (-webkit-, -moz-, -ms-) declarations when an unprefixed rule exists.
example_prompt: Strip the unneeded vendor prefixes from this CSS
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM declaration matching; deterministic, no external data needed.
rationale: Legacy prefixes accumulate in copied snippets and bloat modern stylesheets that no longer need them.

name: srcset-builder
description: Generates a responsive srcset and sizes attribute from a base filename and a list of widths.
example_prompt: Build a srcset for hero.jpg at 480, 768, and 1200 widths
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string templating; deterministic, no assets fetched.
rationale: Hand-writing srcset descriptors is finicky and a generator prevents typos in width descriptors.

name: musicxml-to-mxl
description: Compresses a plain MusicXML document into the standard zipped MXL container with the proper META-INF manifest.
example_prompt: compress this musicxml into an mxl file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — builds the ZIP container and container.xml manifest client-side.
rationale: MXL is the compact distribution format score editors expect for sharing and upload.

name: hjson-to-json
description: Converts human-friendly Hjson (optional quotes, comments, multiline strings) into strict JSON.
example_prompt: Convert this Hjson to standard JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Hjson tokenizing and JSON emit are pure in-memory operations.
rationale: Hjson is used for hand-edited config but needs strict JSON before machine consumption.

name: dense-to-coo-sparse
description: Scans a dense CSV matrix and emits the COO triplet list (row,col,value) of its nonzeros.
example_prompt: Give me the sparse COO triplets for this dense matrix
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a single pass over CSV cells collecting nonzeros — no dependencies, runs locally.
rationale: Turning a dense export into a sparse triplet list is the first step before loading huge matrices into sparse tooling.

name: csr-to-dense-matrix
description: Expands CSR sparse arrays (indptr, indices, data) back into a full dense CSV matrix.
example_prompt: Rebuild the dense matrix from these CSR arrays
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: scattering values into a zero-filled grid is pure indexing math, fully in-browser.
rationale: Inspecting or visualizing a sparse matrix often requires materializing the dense form first.

name: ply-ascii-binary-converter
description: Converts a Stanford PLY mesh/point-cloud between ASCII and binary (little/big-endian) encodings, preserving all properties.
example_prompt: Convert this ASCII PLY to little-endian binary
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parsing the PLY element/property header and re-packing the body is pure byte handling, in-browser.
rationale: Binary PLY loads far faster in viewers while ASCII is debuggable, and reliable round-tripping is surprisingly fiddly.

name: yaml-flow-block-converter
description: Converts YAML between compact flow style ({a: 1, b: [2,3]}) and expanded block style.
example_prompt: expand this inline flow-style YAML into normal block style
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses YAML and re-emits in the requested style client-side
rationale: Flow-style YAML pasted from logs/tools is hard to read; expanding it aids review and editing.

name: css-sort-properties
description: Sorts the declarations within each CSS rule (alphabetical or a concentric/grouped order).
example_prompt: sort the properties inside each CSS rule alphabetically
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses declarations per selector and reorders them locally
rationale: Consistent property order makes stylesheets scannable and reduces noisy diffs.

name: float-noise-rounder
description: Cleans binary floating-point representation noise (e.g. 0.30000000000000004) by rounding to the shortest exact decimal.
example_prompt: Clean up the float noise in these computed values
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: shortest-round-trip decimal formatting, fully offline
rationale: Float artifact cleanup makes computed columns human-readable and is something no formatter or scaler currently addresses.

name: multipart-form-data-builder
description: Assembles a complete multipart/form-data body with boundary, part headers, and content for fields and faux file uploads.
example_prompt: Build a multipart/form-data body with a text field and a file part
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: concatenates parts and a random-ish boundary as bytes; nothing is transmitted.
rationale: Crafting valid multipart bodies for API testing is notoriously tricky and the spec details are easy to botch.

name: wordcloud
description: Generate a word-cloud image sized by word frequency, with color/shape options.
example_prompt: make a word cloud from this text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (tokenize + layout + raster via the image crate).
rationale: Perennially-requested visualization for reports, slides, and social with no current tool.

name: light-leak-overlay-video
description: Generates an animated light-leak / lens-flare overlay clip for retro transitions and color washes.
example_prompt: Generate a warm orange light-leak overlay for a transition
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg animated gradients with blur and screen-blend math produce the leak frames locally.
rationale: Light leaks are a staple transition effect that creators repeatedly hunt for as stock assets.

name: animated-noise-background-video
description: Generates an abstract animated background loop from procedural noise (Perlin/plasma) in chosen colors.
example_prompt: Make a 20-second looping abstract noise background in teal
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute renders the procedural noise per frame and ffmpeg encodes it, fully client-side.
rationale: Procedural motion backgrounds are useful for titles and livestreams and aren't covered by gradient/starfield generators.

name: beat-flash-video
description: Analyzes an audio track and generates a video that flashes or pulses a color/image on each detected beat.
example_prompt: Make a video that flashes white on every beat of this song
loader_feasibility: pyodide (librosa) detects beat times and ffmpeg renders the keyed flashes, both fully local.
rationale: Beat-synced flashing visuals are popular for music shorts and need both audio analysis and rendering, all doable offline.

name: drawtext-filter-builder
description: Builds a correctly escaped FFmpeg drawtext filter string from plain options (text, font, size, color, position, box, timing).
example_prompt: Give me the ffmpeg drawtext filter for centered yellow 48px text from 2s to 5s
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM assembles and escapes the filter expression with no network.
rationale: drawtext escaping and positioning syntax is a notorious footgun that a generator removes.

name: video-seo-metadata-generator
description: Generates schema.org VideoObject JSON-LD plus Open Graph and Twitter video meta tags from a video's probed duration, dimensions, and supplied title/thumbnail.
example_prompt: Make the JSON-LD and OG tags to embed this video on my site for SEO
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg probes the technical fields and a plain-Rust step renders the markup locally.
rationale: Correct video structured-data markup boosts search/preview behavior and is painful to author by hand.

name: midi-from-note-list
description: Converts a plain list of notes with start times, durations, and velocities into a Standard MIDI File.
example_prompt: Turn this note list into a MIDI file: C4 0 1, E4 1 1, G4 2 2
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the rows into timed events and writes the SMF entirely client-side
rationale: It's the simplest bridge from a textual/AI-generated melody to a usable MIDI file.

name: prisma-schema-from-json
description: Generates a Prisma model block with field types and optional markers from a JSON sample record.
example_prompt: Create a Prisma model from this JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: JSON parse plus Prisma DSL emission as text, no Prisma CLI.
rationale: Prisma is a leading TS ORM and scaffolding a model from existing data shape accelerates schema design.

name: mongoose-schema-from-json
description: Generates a Mongoose Schema definition with typed paths and nested subdocuments from a JSON document.
example_prompt: Make a Mongoose schema from this JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: structural inference plus JS Schema emission as text, no Node runtime.
rationale: MongoDB/Node devs define schemas from existing documents constantly and hand-typing them is repetitive.

name: breadcrumb-nav-generator
description: Generates accessible breadcrumb HTML (nav, ol, aria-current) from a path or page list.
example_prompt: make breadcrumb nav HTML for Home > Blog > This Post
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML templating with ARIA attributes; distinct from the JSON-LD breadcrumb tool.
rationale: The visible breadcrumb markup (separate from schema) has accessibility rules people routinely miss.

name: test-scaffold-generator
description: Generates Jest or Vitest test stubs (describe/it blocks with arrange-act-assert TODOs) from function signatures.
example_prompt: Scaffold Vitest tests for these three exported functions
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses signatures and emits structured test skeletons, no test runner needed.
rationale: Boilerplate test structure is the friction that stops people writing tests; scaffolding lowers that barrier.

name: jsdoc-scaffold
description: Generates JSDoc comment blocks with @param, @returns, and type placeholders from a JS/TS function signature.
example_prompt: Add a JSDoc block for this function signature
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — lightweight signature parse and comment emission, pure text transform.
rationale: Consistent JSDoc is tedious to type for every function; generating the skeleton from the signature is fast and accurate.

name: ini-formatter
description: Normalizes INI/properties files with consistent section ordering, key spacing, and comment handling.
example_prompt: tidy up this messy ini config
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; INI parsing and re-emission are local string processing.
rationale: INI and .properties files remain common and lack any canonical formatter in the catalog.

name: currency-minor-units-converter
description: Converts decimal money amounts to integer minor units (cents) and back using each ISO 4217 currency's defined exponent.
example_prompt: Convert 19.99 USD and 1000 JPY to minor units
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: per-currency exponent table and integer scaling
rationale: Storing money as integer minor units is best practice; this avoids per-currency exponent mistakes.

name: harwell-boeing-to-csv
description: Parses a Harwell-Boeing sparse-matrix file and emits CSV triplets or a dense grid.
example_prompt: Read this Harwell-Boeing matrix file and give me CSV triplets
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; fixed-format Fortran-style column parsing of the header and column pointers.
rationale: Legacy numerical datasets ship in Harwell-Boeing and have almost no modern readers.

name: html-void-element-normalizer
description: Normalizes void elements like br, img, and input to either the bare HTML5 form or the self-closing XHTML form.
example_prompt:
Strip the trailing slashes off all the void tags like
in this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM recognizes the void-element set and rewrites their closing syntax; deterministic local pass
rationale: Self-closing-slash inconsistency is a frequent style-guide violation across migrated codebases.

name: css-zero-unit-normalizer
description: Strips redundant units from zero values, turning 0px, 0em, and 0% into a bare 0 where valid.
example_prompt: Normalize all the zero values in this CSS to drop their units
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizes declaration values and rewrites zero lengths; deterministic in-browser pass
rationale: A classic minification optimization that's tedious and error-prone to do safely by hand.

name: css-leading-zero-normalizer
description: Normalizes fractional numbers in CSS to either always-have or always-drop a leading zero (0.5 vs .5).
example_prompt: Strip the leading zeros from the decimals in this CSS
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM rewrites numeric tokens consistently; deterministic in-browser pass
rationale: Leading-zero style is a common lint rule and minifier optimization that's fiddly to apply globally.

name: markdown-heading-style-converter
description: Converts between Setext (underlined) and ATX (#) heading styles consistently throughout a document.
example_prompt: Convert the underlined headings in this Markdown to # style
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM detects heading forms and rewrites them; deterministic in-browser pass
rationale: Inherited docs mix heading styles, and standardizing on ATX is a common cleanup pass.

name: number-to-metric-suffix
description: Abbreviates large numbers into compact k/M/B/T shorthand with a chosen number of significant digits.
example_prompt: abbreviate 1532000 and 9800000000 with k/M/B suffixes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — magnitude bucketing and rounding, pure local math.
rationale: The reverse direction is needed for compact labels and dashboards, and abbreviating counts cleanly (with rounding) is fiddly by hand.

name: empirical-cdf-transformer
description: Maps each value in a list to its empirical CDF value (probability integral transform) producing a near-uniform [0,1] series.
example_prompt: transform these to their empirical CDF values: 3, 8, 1, 8, 5
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — rank-then-normalize over the sorted array, no model.
rationale: The probability integral transform is the foundational step for copulas and uniformization, and differs from a gaussian-quantile (rank-gauss) transform.

name: pcm-deinterleaver
description: Splits an interleaved stereo/multichannel WAV into separate per-channel mono WAVs.
example_prompt: Split this stereo wav into left and right mono files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM strides through interleaved samples and writes one file per channel.
rationale: Per-channel mono stems are needed for analysis and DAW import, and channel-mask rewriting doesn't produce them.

name: string-escape-converter
description: Escapes and unescapes string literals for JSON, C, shell, SQL, and regex contexts.
example_prompt: escape this multi-line string for a JSON value
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; per-context escaping rules computed in-process.
rationale: Pasting strings across languages constantly breaks on quoting; one tool covers every target.

name: aac-to-flac
description: Decodes a raw AAC or M4A stream to a lossless FLAC file at full decoded resolution.
example_prompt: Convert this aac to flac
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's AAC decoder plus FLAC encoder run entirely client-side in WASM.
rationale: Archivists want a lossless container for streamed/downloaded AAC even though it can't restore lost data.

name: checklist-from-outline
description: Converts a plain or indented outline into a nested GitHub-flavored markdown task checklist.
example_prompt: Turn these steps into a markdown checklist
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — indentation parse and checkbox emission, no dependencies.
rationale: Spinning quick notes into trackable checklists is a small but frequent productivity win.

name: solid-color-png

name: address-dataset-generator

name: kustomization-generator

name: citation-format-checker

name: cohens-d-calculator

name: perlin-noise-image

name: compound-interest

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes the closed-form/iterated growth locally.

name: image-cross-stitch

loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM downscale + palette mapping + grid render.
rationale: A dedicated crafting tool not covered by pixel-art or dither.

name: graphql-query-linter

description: Draws a uniformly random orthogonal matrix from the Haar measure via QR of a Gaussian matrix.

name: power-set-generator

name: common-denominator-converter

example_prompt: make a .gitignore for Node, Rust, and macOS
