rationale: gitignore.io-style generator is a daily-use dev convenience.

name: graphql-schema-validator
description: Validates a GraphQL SDL schema for syntax and type-resolution errors.
example_prompt: Is this GraphQL schema valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (graphql parser) — local
rationale: Schema breakage is a common GraphQL failure mode that a fast validator catches early.

name: plaintext-to-slides
description: Turns a sent-style file (blank-line-separated paragraphs, one idea per slide) into a minimal big-text HTML deck.
example_prompt: Make simple big-text slides from this plain text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — splits on blank lines and emits styled HTML slides, no dependencies.
rationale: sent's minimalist one-thought-per-slide style has a dedicated following but produces nothing shareable on its own.

name: oh-my-posh-theme-preview
description: Renders a visual preview of an oh-my-posh prompt theme from its JSON/YAML config and lets you tweak segments.
example_prompt: Show me what this oh-my-posh theme JSON looks like
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the config and rasterizes an SVG/PNG preview locally.
rationale: You normally can't see an oh-my-posh theme without applying it to a live shell first.

name: chem-equation-balancer
description: Balances chemical equations and reports the stoichiometric coefficients.
example_prompt: balance C2H6 + O2 -> CO2 + H2O
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM solves the null space of the element matrix over rationals; fully local.
rationale: Equation balancing is a frequent, deterministic chemistry-homework ask.

name: git-log-stats
description: Computes contributor and activity statistics — commits per author, additions/deletions, busiest days — from pasted `git log` output.
example_prompt: Paste git log: who are the top committers and what's the commit-by-weekday breakdown?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parser over the pasted log text; no repo access or network required.
rationale: git-stats gives instantly useful repo insight and only needs the log text the user can paste.

name: units-calculator
description: Computes with physical units and does dimensional analysis (e.g. 60 mph in m/s, 3 kWh / 12 V).
example_prompt: convert 2.5 cups of flour to grams and 60 miles/hour to km/h
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a bundled units database plus dimensional-analysis math runs fully client-side in wasmi.
rationale: Directly maps to Numbat/ka/numio-cli demand; unit-aware math prevents the dimension errors plain calculators miss.

name: rpn-calculator
description: A reverse-Polish (HP-35 style) stack calculator that pushes operands and applies operators to the stack.
example_prompt: in RPN compute 5 1 2 + 4 * + 3 -
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a stack machine evaluating RPN tokens is trivial pure computation in wasmi.
rationale: Maps HIP35 demand; RPN has a devoted user base and a distinct interaction model worth a dedicated tool.

name: tweet-thread-formatter
description: Formats a set of tweets into a clean numbered thread, expands t.co stubs you supply, and counts weighted characters.
example_prompt: format these 5 tweets into a clean reading thread with numbering
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — text segmentation and grapheme-aware counting are pure operations.
rationale: Drafting and reviewing threads is a constant social-media chore that benefits from instant local formatting.

name: social-post-char-counter
description: Counts a post's length against platform limits (X 280 weighted, Mastodon 500, Bluesky 300) with emoji/URL weighting.
example_prompt: will this fit in a tweet and a bluesky post?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — grapheme-aware counting and weighting rules are pure computation.
rationale: Cross-posting means juggling different limits and weighting quirks, which a local counter resolves instantly.

name: animated-sticker-converter
description: Converts animated webp/webm stickers (Telegram/WhatsApp) to gif, mp4, or a still png frame.
example_prompt: turn this animated webp sticker into a gif
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — handles webp/webm decode and gif/mp4/png encode client-side.
rationale: Sharing stickers outside their app means reformatting them, and doing it locally is quick with no upload.

name: tweet-character-counter
description: Counts a tweet's length using Twitter's weighted rules (URLs count as 23, CJK as 2) and shows remaining space.
example_prompt: How many characters is this tweet with the link?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: implements Twitter's documented weighted counting algorithm purely on the input string.
rationale: Closes the gap that naive character counts get wrong, serving the same tweet-composing demand precisely.

name: compose-to-podman
description: Converts a docker-compose.yml into equivalent podman run commands or Quadlet unit files.
example_prompt: Convert this docker-compose.yml to podman commands
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the compose YAML and templates the podman/Quadlet output client-side (podman/toolbox demand).
rationale: Podman users migrating off Docker Compose have a real, recurring translation pain point.

name: wpm-calculator
description: Computes words-per-minute, characters-per-minute, net WPM, and accuracy from a typed sample plus elapsed time or a target/typed text pair.
example_prompt: I typed 420 characters in 90 seconds with 6 errors — what's my WPM?
loader_feasibility: trivial plain Rust→WASM arithmetic on supplied numbers/text; fully offline one-shot computation
rationale: A quick standalone calculation for people who already have their numbers and don't want to run a full interactive test.

name: text-shadow-css
description: Generate CSS text-shadow code, including layered, 3D, and neon glow presets, with preview.
example_prompt: generate a neon glow text-shadow in cyan
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM string assembly plus an inline preview.
rationale: text-shadow is distinct from the existing box-shadow-css and a common design ask.

name: ratio-calc
description: Solve proportions (A:B = C:x), simplify ratios, and split a quantity by a ratio.
example_prompt: If 3 eggs make 12 cookies, how many eggs for 30 cookies?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM arithmetic; offline.
rationale: Everyday proportion math distinct from aspect-ratio-calc.

name: gauge-chart
description: Render a KPI gauge/dial chart showing a value against a range and thresholds.
example_prompt: Make a gauge showing 72 out of 100 with green/amber/red zones
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust arc rendering to PNG/SVG in-browser.
rationale: Dashboard staple absent from the chart catalog.

name: mailto-link-generate
description: Build a mailto: link with recipients, cc/bcc, subject, and body, properly encoded.
example_prompt: mailto link to a@b.com, subject 'Hi', body 'Let's chat'
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM URL encoding.
rationale: Common web-dev snippet that's easy to get encoding wrong.

name: rust-ownership-annotator
description: Annotates a Rust snippet with educational notes on moves, borrows (&/&mut), clones, and end-of-scope drops to teach ownership flow (heuristic, not a full borrow checker).
example_prompt: Annotate where ownership moves and borrows happen in this Rust code.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: syn AST walk applies ownership heuristics and inlines annotations, fully offline.
rationale: Targets the hardest beginner concept behind 'rust-learning' and 'Rust in Action' with visual ownership feedback.

name: prime-factorization
description: Factors an integer into its prime powers and lists divisors.
example_prompt: prime factorization of 360
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — trial division/Pollard-rho compiles to a tiny fast WASM module, fully local.
rationale: A classic Mathematica number-theory primitive that is fast, exact, and lightweight in Rust.

name: truth-table-generator
description: Builds the full truth table for a boolean expression using AND, OR, NOT, XOR, and implication.
example_prompt: Generate the truth table for (A AND B) OR (NOT C)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a small boolean expression parser/evaluator over all input rows, deterministic and local.
rationale: Truth tables are a staple of digital-logic and CS courses and a frequent search, with no convenient browser tool that takes an arbitrary expression.

name: world-clock
description: Show the current time across multiple named time zones at once, with UTC offsets and day differences.
example_prompt: What time is it right now in Tokyo, London, and New York?
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — bundled IANA tz database plus the current instant, computed locally.
rationale: Remote teams check multiple zones constantly; timestamp-convert handles one conversion, not a live board.

name: projectile-motion
description: Solve 2D projectile motion (range, max height, flight time) and plot the trajectory.
example_prompt: Plot the trajectory for a launch at 30 m/s and 45 degrees
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM physics plus plot rendering, offline.
rationale: A core physics-class problem with a visual answer, beyond the 1D kinematics solver.

name: fraction-calc
description: Add, subtract, multiply, divide, and simplify fractions, with mixed-number and decimal conversion.
example_prompt: Simplify 3/4 + 5/6 as a fraction
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — exact rational arithmetic with integer math, no network.
rationale: Exact fraction arithmetic avoids floating-point error and is common in education and cooking/recipes.

name: polynomial-roots
description: Find all real and complex roots of a polynomial from its coefficients.
example_prompt: find the roots of x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust numerics to WASM — pure compute.
rationale: Root-finding is a common algebra task beyond what solve-equation handles symbolically.

name: noise-generate
description: Generate white, pink, or brown noise of a given duration for focus, sleep, or testing.
example_prompt: Generate 10 minutes of brown noise
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust sample synthesis → WAV, optionally encoded via ffmpeg, in-browser.
rationale: Popular focus/sleep utility not covered by tone-generate (single tones).

name: sales-tax-calc
description: Add or remove VAT/sales tax and convert between gross and net for a given rate.
example_prompt: Remove 20% VAT from £120
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust arithmetic in-browser.
rationale: Frequent everyday/finance calc more specific than generic percentage-calc.

name: monte-carlo-stock-sim
description: Simulates Geometric Brownian Motion price paths via Monte Carlo and summarizes the outcome distribution.
example_prompt: Simulate 10,000 GBM paths for a stock at 100 with 20% vol, 6% drift, over 1 year
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; RNG-driven path simulation and statistics, no server needed.
rationale: Monte Carlo forecasting of asset paths is a popular quant exercise that is embarrassingly local compute.

name: tic-tac-toe
description: Noughts & Crosses against an unbeatable minimax AI or a second human player.
example_prompt: play tic tac toe against the computer
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — full minimax search is trivial on a 3x3 board, runs instantly client-side
rationale: Maps the explicit 'Noughts & Crosses (Tic Tac Toe)' demand with a perfect-play local opponent.

name: vietnamese-sentiment-analyzer
description: Classifies the sentiment of Vietnamese text.
example_prompt: Is this Vietnamese product review positive or negative?
loader_feasibility: transformers.js: a Vietnamese sentiment classification ONNX model runs client-side
rationale: Local sentiment scoring of Vietnamese reviews and feedback keeps the text private.

name: portuguese-verb-conjugator
description: Conjugates Portuguese verbs across all tenses and persons, handling regular and irregular forms.
example_prompt: conjugate the verb 'fazer' in all tenses
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM encodes conjugation rules plus an irregular-verb table, running fully in-browser.
rationale: A staple of Portuguese-nlp and language learning with no good offline browser tool today.

name: sequence-series-analyzer
description: Identifies arithmetic/geometric sequences, finds the nth term, and computes partial/infinite sums.
example_prompt: find the nth term and sum of 2, 6, 18, 54
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM pattern detection and closed-form sums run client-side
rationale: Precalculus sequences-and-series unit with fast deterministic answers.

name: beam-deflection-calculator
description: Computes deflection, bending moment, and shear for common beam loading cases.
example_prompt: max deflection of a simply supported beam, 4m span, 10kN center load, steel I-beam
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — closed-form beam equations run locally; no engineering server.
rationale: Maps the SEPCO structural-engineering-tools demand to a precise, offline structural calculator.

name: moment-of-inertia-calculator
description: Computes area, centroid, and second moment of area for standard cross-sections (rectangle, circle, I-beam, T).
example_prompt: moment of inertia of a 200x300mm rectangular section
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — section-property formulas run instantly client-side.
rationale: A core structural-engineering computation that feeds the beam tool and matches the SEPCO demand.

name: dtmf-decoder
description: Detects DTMF touch-tones in an audio clip and decodes them back into the dialed digit sequence.
example_prompt: Decode the phone tones in this audio into numbers
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes to PCM and a Rust→WASM Goertzel filter detects the tone pairs locally.
rationale: Decoding DTMF is a recurring Sonic-Visualiser CTF task that's tedious by hand; an automated local decoder nails it instantly.

name: css-box-shadow-generator
description: Generates box-shadow CSS (including multi-layer and inset) from offset, blur, spread, and color inputs.
example_prompt: give me a soft elevated box-shadow css for a card
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM template generation, no runtime dependencies.
rationale: Covers another high-traffic CSS Matic generator with natural-language inputs.

name: css-border-radius-generator
description: Produces border-radius CSS including asymmetric blob shapes from up to eight radius values.
example_prompt: create an organic blob border-radius in css
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string output; pure computation.
rationale: Rounds out the CSS Matic toolset for shape styling without a GUI.

name: csp-analyzer
description: Parse a Content-Security-Policy and flag unsafe-inline, wildcards, missing fallbacks, and bypassable sources.
example_prompt: Audit this CSP header for weaknesses
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: directive parsing and ruleset evaluation over the pasted policy.
rationale: CSP misconfig is a common AppSec finding; this explains it offline in plain language.

name: ha-yaml-validate
description: Parses and validates Home Assistant YAML config or automation snippets, reporting syntax errors and unknown top-level keys.
example_prompt: Check this Home Assistant automation YAML for errors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — YAML parsing and structural checks, no network.
rationale: HA users edit YAML by hand and a quick offline check prevents a bad reload of their whole config.

name: savings-goal
description: Calculates the monthly contribution needed to reach a savings goal by a target date, accounting for interest.
example_prompt: How much must I save monthly to reach $20k in 3 years at 4% interest?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM time-value-of-money math; deterministic, offline.
rationale: Savings goals are a headline feature of Budget Zen/Sure and reduce cleanly to an offline annuity calculation.

name: dividend-projector
description: Projects annual dividend income and yield-on-cost from holdings and per-share dividend rates.
example_prompt: Project my yearly dividend income from these positions
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM arithmetic over the holdings list; offline.
rationale: Dividend tracking is a prominent Ghostfolio feature and is a simple, private local calculation.

name: mcp-tool-schema-validator
description: Validates an MCP tool definition's JSON Schema (inputSchema) for correctness and common authoring mistakes.
example_prompt: Is the inputSchema for my MCP tool valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: JSON Schema structural validation in pure code.
rationale: Malformed tool schemas cause silent tool-call failures, and authors need fast offline feedback while building MCP servers.

name: bootstrap-ci
description: Estimates a bootstrap confidence interval for a statistic (mean, median, etc.) from a sample.
example_prompt: Give me a 95% bootstrap CI for the mean of these values
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM resamples and computes the interval with no dependencies.
rationale: Bootstrapping is a key non-parametric technique that's tedious to do by hand.

name: recommender-collaborative
description: Builds item-item and user-user collaborative-filtering recommendations from a ratings matrix.
example_prompt: Given this user-movie ratings table, recommend 3 movies for user Bob
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — cosine/Pearson similarity over a sparse ratings matrix is pure numeric, fully local.
rationale: Directly serves the Minnesota Recommender Systems Specialization demand term with a hands-on browser tool.

name: adaboost-classifier
description: Trains an AdaBoost ensemble of weak learners, showing how sample weights evolve across rounds, and reports the boosted accuracy.
example_prompt: Run AdaBoost on this dataset and show me the final accuracy
loader_feasibility: pyodide — scikit-learn's AdaBoost is bundled; stump fitting and reweighting are light CPU work in the sandbox.
rationale: AdaBoost is a named, distinct boosting method whose weight-evolution view is genuinely instructive.

name: model-stacking
description: Builds a stacked ensemble that trains a meta-model on the cross-validated predictions of several base models and reports the lift over each base.
example_prompt: Stack a logistic regression, SVM, and random forest with a meta-learner on this data
loader_feasibility: pyodide — scikit-learn's StackingClassifier runs all base and meta fits in the browser Python sandbox.
rationale: Stacking squeezes extra accuracy out of combined models and is a clearly named demand term.

name: fuzzy-cmeans-clustering
description: Fuzzy c-means soft clustering that assigns each point a membership degree to every cluster instead of a single hard label.
example_prompt: Run fuzzy c-means and tell me each point's membership across 3 clusters
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the alternating membership/centroid update is small matrix math with no dependencies.
rationale: Soft cluster memberships are useful when points genuinely belong partly to several groups.

name: falling-words-typing-game
description: Arcade typing game where words fall from the top and you must type them before they hit the bottom, with rising difficulty and a score.
example_prompt: let me play a falling-words typing game
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM drives word spawning, collision/scoring, and difficulty ramp; rendering and key capture happen on the tool page in-browser with no backend
rationale: Distinct gameplay loop covers the Typespeed / typeinc / typing-game-cli demand, which is a game rather than a measured test.

name: tga-to-png
description: Converts Truevision TGA game/texture assets to PNG.
example_prompt: convert these .tga textures to png
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the `image` crate decodes TGA (incl. RLE) client-side
rationale: TGA is ubiquitous in game asset pipelines but unviewable in browsers or most editors.

name: quaternion-to-euler-csv
description: Converts a CSV of unit quaternions into Euler angles in a chosen rotation order.
example_prompt: Convert these quaternion rows to roll/pitch/yaw
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: quaternion-to-Euler trig (with gimbal-lock handling) is closed-form math computed per row in WASM.
rationale: IMU/robotics logs store quaternions but humans and many controllers reason in Euler angles.

name: webvtt-validator
description: Validates WebVTT files for the required header, correct cue timing format, and valid settings/region syntax.
example_prompt: Is this .vtt file valid WebVTT?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM WebVTT parser checks the spec grammar entirely in-browser
rationale: WebVTT must be byte-correct for browsers to render captions and a quick validator prevents silent caption failures.

name: isochronic-tones-generator
description: Creates isochronic tones — a single tone amplitude-gated at a chosen brainwave rate — as a WAV, distinct from binaural beats.
example_prompt: Generate 10 minutes of 10 Hz isochronic tones at 200 Hz carrier
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM modulates a carrier sine with a pulse envelope and renders the WAV locally with no streaming.
rationale: Isochronic tones work over speakers (unlike binaural) and are a popular focus/relaxation aid people want to self-generate.

name: github-actions-scaffolder
description: Generates a GitHub Actions CI workflow YAML for a given language, with cache and matrix steps.
example_prompt: Scaffold a GitHub Actions workflow that tests a Python package on 3.10–3.12
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — composes YAML from step templates and a version matrix; no API calls.
rationale: CI YAML is verbose and easy to misindent; a curated scaffold saves a lot of trial-and-error pushes.

name: eslint-config-generator
description: Scaffolds a flat ESLint config for a chosen framework and style preset with common rule sets.
example_prompt: Scaffold an ESLint flat config for a React + TypeScript project
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — emits the config module text from per-stack templates, no install step.
rationale: The flat-config migration confused many; a generated starting point removes setup friction.

name: penrose-tiling-generator
description: Generates an aperiodic Penrose (rhombus) tiling as an SVG at a chosen subdivision depth.
example_prompt: Generate a Penrose tiling at depth 5
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM deflation subdivision emitting SVG polygons — fully client-side.
rationale: Aperiodic tilings are a celebrated Bridges/Recreations-in-Math subject and visually compelling.

name: photo-to-coloring-page
description: Reduces a photo to clean black outlines on white, ready to print and color in.
example_prompt: Make a coloring book page from this picture
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — edge detection followed by thresholding and line cleanup
rationale: Parents and teachers want printable coloring pages from photos, a clear unmet niche.

name: oil-paint-effect
description: Applies an oil-painting stylization by replacing each pixel with the dominant intensity bin in its neighborhood.
example_prompt: Give this landscape an oil painting look
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — local intensity-histogram per window, pure CPU computation
rationale: A distinctive painterly effect that broadens the artistic-transform options without a server.

name: cosine-similarity-calculator
description: Computes cosine similarity and the angle between two vectors.
example_prompt: Cosine similarity between these two embedding vectors?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: dot product and norms only, runs locally.
rationale: The default similarity measure for embeddings and feature vectors, useful without uploading data anywhere.

name: bipartite-graph-checker
description: Checks whether an undirected graph is bipartite via two-coloring and returns the partition.
example_prompt: Is the graph with edges 1-2,2-3,3-4,4-1 bipartite?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: BFS/DFS two-coloring, runs locally.
rationale: Useful for matching and scheduling problems, no existing tool covers it.

name: cors-policy-validate
description: Given a sample request (origin, method, headers) and a server's CORS response headers, checks whether the browser would actually allow the request and explains any failure.
example_prompt: Would Origin https://app.io with credentials pass these CORS headers: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM implementation of the Fetch CORS check algorithm; no live request, purely local reasoning.
rationale: CORS failures are notoriously opaque; simulating the browser's allow/deny decision saves hours of guesswork.

name: dns-zone-file-generator
description: Builds a BIND-format DNS zone file from A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/TXT/SRV record inputs.
example_prompt: Generate a zone file for example.com with an A record, MX for Google, and an SPF TXT
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM formats records with correct TTL/serial layout, client-side
rationale: Zone file column formatting and serial conventions are error-prone by hand.

name: gauss-legendre-quadrature-generator
description: Computes Gauss–Legendre quadrature nodes and weights of a given order for numerical integration.
example_prompt: Gauss-Legendre nodes and weights for n=5
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Newton iteration on Legendre polynomials, fully local numerics
rationale: Accurate quadrature tables are essential for numerical integration and the root-finding behind them is non-trivial to do by hand.

name: dns-record-decoder
description: Parses DNS zone-file records or wire-format responses and explains each record type.
example_prompt: Parse and explain these DNS records
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizes zone-file/wire formats locally
rationale: DNS demystification is squarely in Julia Evans' wheelhouse and runs fully offline.

name: anagram-solver
description: Finds all dictionary words and sub-words that can be formed from a set of letters.
example_prompt: What words can I make from the letters TPALEN?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM lookup against an embedded sorted dictionary; pure compute, no server.
rationale: Word games like word-blazer drive steady demand for fast letter unscrambling.

name: lorem-ipsum-generator
description:
Generates placeholder text by words, sentences, or paragraphs with optional HTML

wrapping.
example_prompt: Give me 3 paragraphs of lorem ipsum wrapped in p tags
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM from an embedded word bank, no network
rationale: Filler text for mockups is a universal need and trivially offline.

name: hamming-distance-calculator
description: Computes the Hamming distance between two equal-length sequences (bit strings, hex, or symbol vectors).
example_prompt: How many positions differ between 11010 and 10011?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: positional comparison and popcount, runs locally
rationale: Hamming distance is the core comparison metric for codes and fingerprints with no single-purpose tool.

name: word-unscrambler
description: Finds all valid words (and best-scoring ones) that can be made from a set of scrambled letters.
example_prompt: what words can I make from the letters R A T S E P?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — anagram lookup over a bundled dictionary index runs locally with no API
rationale: Generalizes the word-game demand (guess-word, Language-games) into an everyday anagram/Scrabble helper.

name: finance-calc
description: Compute loan payments, compound interest, and savings growth from principal/rate/term inputs.
example_prompt: What's the monthly payment on a $30,000 loan at 6% for 5 years?
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM financial formulas; instant and offline.
rationale: Loan/interest math is a high-traffic consumer calculation that goes beyond the existing plain calculator.

name: mandala-generator
description: Generates a radially symmetric mandala from a seed, with adjustable symmetry order, layers, and color scheme.
example_prompt: Generate an 12-fold symmetry mandala in teal and gold
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — draw one wedge and rotate-copy around the center into a raster; deterministic from seed.
rationale: Mandala art is a high-demand decorative and coloring-page generator that runs trivially offline.

name: lagrange-interpolator
description: Builds the Lagrange interpolating polynomial through a set of points and evaluates it at requested x-values, returning the polynomial coefficients.
example_prompt: Interpolate through (0,1),(1,3),(2,7) and evaluate at x=1.5
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; basis-polynomial construction and evaluation are local arithmetic over the point set.
rationale: Exact interpolation through known points is distinct from least-squares fitting and Bézier sampling already in the catalog.

name: cubic-spline-interpolator
description: Fits a natural or clamped cubic spline through data points and evaluates the smooth curve and its slope at any x.
example_prompt: Fit a natural cubic spline through (0,0),(1,1),(2,0),(3,1) and evaluate at 1.5
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; solving the tridiagonal spline system is a small local linear solve in WASM.
rationale: Smooth interpolation without polynomial oscillation is the standard tool for clean curves through data and is not yet covered.

name: matrix-norm-calculator
description: Computes the 1-norm, infinity-norm, Frobenius norm, and (via power iteration) spectral norm of a matrix in one report.
example_prompt: Compute all the norms of [[1,2],[3,4]].
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: column/row sum maxima, Frobenius sum, and power iteration for the spectral norm, all local.
rationale: Matrix norms quantify sensitivity and error bounds, and gathering several at once saves repeated manual work.

name: kl-divergence-calculator
description: Computes KL divergence (both directions) and symmetric Jensen-Shannon divergence between two discrete probability distributions.
example_prompt: KL divergence between distribution [0.2,0.5,0.3] and [0.1,0.6,0.3]?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: log-ratio sums over normalized arrays, client-side.
rationale: Core measure for comparing distributions in ML/stats with no good single-purpose calculator available offline.

name: unit-vector-checker
description: Checks whether a vector has unit length within tolerance and reports its computed magnitude.
example_prompt: Is (0.6, 0.8, 0) a unit vector?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: norm computation and tolerance comparison, pure arithmetic.
rationale: Normalization bugs are common in graphics/physics and an exact magnitude readout makes them obvious.

name: combinations-generator
description: Enumerates all k-element combinations of a list (with or without repetition) as CSV rows.
example_prompt: Give all 3-element combinations of 1,2,3,4,5,6
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — lexicographic combination iteration, fully client-side
rationale: Common scaffolding for A/B test buckets, lottery-style enumeration, and parameter sweeps without a script.

name: emoji-inventory
description: Counts and lists every emoji in the text with its name and frequency.
example_prompt: Which emojis and how many appear in this chat log?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: emoji ranges and the name table bundle into the binary, fully offline.
rationale: Social and moderation workflows need a quick inventory of emoji usage.

name: othello
description: Reversi/Othello against an alpha-beta AI with selectable strength, showing legal-move hints and disc counts.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the GGUF binary header/metadata block in-buffer; no model execution needed so it's instant and offline
rationale: ollama/LamaCLI users constantly inspect local model files, and header parsing is a small, exact, fully-local job.

name: srt-index-sequence-checker
description: Verifies that an SRT file's cue index numbers are present, sequential, and unduplicated, listing any gaps or repeats.
example_prompt: Check that the cue numbers in this SRT are sequential
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses the numeric index lines and checks ordering entirely in-memory.
rationale: Out-of-order or duplicate SRT indices silently drop cues in strict players, and the defect is easy to overlook.

name: srt-subtitle-validator
description: Validates SRT subtitles for sequential numbering, well-formed timecodes, non-overlapping/negative durations, and empty cues.
example_prompt: Validate this SRT file — are there any overlapping or backwards timestamps?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses subtitle blocks and checks timing invariants offline
rationale: Subtitle timing errors are invisible until playback; a validator catches overlaps and gaps before publishing.

name: video-encode-quality-compare
description: Compares two versions of a video and reports objective PSNR and SSIM quality metrics per frame and overall.
example_prompt: Compare the quality of my original and compressed video with PSNR and SSIM
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg `psnr`/`ssim` filters compute the metrics between the two decoded streams entirely in wasm.
rationale: Objective quality metrics let creators tune compression settings with numbers instead of guesswork, fully offline.

name: forensic-article-summarizer
description: Summarizes long forensics blog posts and research papers into key findings, tools, and IOCs.
example_prompt: summarize this SANS forensics article into key takeaways
loader_feasibility: transformers-js loader runs a summarization model in the browser, no API call.
rationale: Keeping up with sources like SANS, Zena Forensics, and This Week in 4n6 is easier with local summarization.

name: allergen-scanner
description: Scans a pasted ingredients list and flags the major regulated allergens and their hidden synonyms.
example_prompt: Check this ingredient list for allergens: wheat flour, casein, lecithin, almonds
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (bundled allergen synonym dictionary + text matching) — runs offline on the pasted text.
rationale: Allergen detection is health-critical and privacy-sensitive, perfect for a local tool that never sees a server.

name: plist-validator
description: Validates Apple plist (XML or binary) structure, type tags, and key/value pairing inside dict elements.
example_prompt: Validate this plist file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML/bplist parser; fully local
rationale: A misplaced key or wrong type tag silently corrupts macOS/iOS config files.

name: country-code-validator
description: Validates ISO 3166-1 country codes (alpha-2, alpha-3, numeric) and shows the canonical name and other forms.
example_prompt: Is 'UK' a valid ISO country code?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with bundled ISO 3166 table; lookup only
rationale: Country-code mistakes (UK vs GB) are pervasive in data and a bundled validator settles them instantly.

name: midi-to-musicxml
description: Converts a MIDI performance into MusicXML sheet-music notation for score editors.
example_prompt: convert this midi into musicxml so i can open it in musescore
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses MIDI (midly) and emits MusicXML; pure data transformation, no server.
rationale: Composers want to engrave MIDI in MuseScore/Sibelius/Finale, which import MusicXML, not raw MIDI events.

name: csh-to-bash-converter
description: Translates common tcsh/csh constructs (setenv, alias, set, if, foreach) in a script into POSIX/bash equivalents and flags non-translatable parts.
example_prompt: convert this .tcshrc to a bash-compatible file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — line-oriented parse and rule-based rewrite, no execution needed.
rationale: People migrating off tcsh to bash or zsh need a mechanical first-pass converter.

name: hex-grid-generator
description: Generates an SVG hex grid with axial/cube coordinate labels for board-game and map design.
example_prompt: Make a 10x8 flat-top hex grid SVG with coordinate labels
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure string/geometry generation emitting SVG, fully client-side.
rationale: Hex strategy games (zemeroth, Zone of Control, rhex) drive demand for designer-friendly hex grids.

name: time-unit-converter
description: Converts a quantity between time units — seconds, minutes, hours, days, and weeks.
example_prompt: convert 36 hours to days
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — unit scaling is trivial arithmetic with no external dependency.
rationale: Collapses convert-days-to-hours and convert-hours-to-days (and more) into one tool that answers many related searches.

name: play-doom
description: Play a playable port of the classic DOOM first level rendered to the browser via raycasting.
example_prompt: let me play doom
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the engine and a bundled shareware-style level run as pure computation, rendering frames to a canvas with no server.
rationale: The 'DOOM-ASCII' demand term taps enduring DOOM nostalgia, and a browser-local port is a high-impact showcase tool.

name: audio-waveform-viewer
description: Decodes audio and renders an interactive waveform with amplitude, clipping, silence, and channel statistics.
example_prompt: Show me the waveform and any silent gaps in this recording
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes the audio to PCM locally and the waveform is drawn from in-memory samples.
rationale: A quick local waveform covers Sonic Visualiser's most basic inspection need and pairs with the spectrogram tool for fast audio triage.

name: classical-cipher-solver
description: Decode or brute-force Caesar/ROT-N, Vigenère, Atbash, and substitution ciphers using frequency analysis.
example_prompt: Solve this Vigenère ciphertext
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: cipher logic and frequency scoring run in-process.
rationale: Covers a huge share of CTF crypto challenges and security-education exercises.

name: pascals-triangle-generator
description: Generates the first N rows of Pascal's triangle as exact big integers, optionally reduced mod p to reveal Sierpiński patterns.
example_prompt: Show me 12 rows of Pascal's triangle
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — additive big-integer row construction, no external libraries.
rationale: Pascal's triangle is a frequent teaching artifact and the mod-p mode adds genuine exploratory value.

name: dimensional-consistency-checker
description: Parses a physics-style equation with units and checks that both sides reduce to the same SI base dimensions.
example_prompt: Is F = m·a dimensionally consistent, and what about E = m·c²/2?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: unit parsing into base-dimension exponent vectors and comparison, no network.
rationale: Dimensional analysis is the fastest sanity check on a formula, and an automated linter catches unit mistakes instantly.

name: minecraft-color-code-converter
description: Converts Minecraft text between legacy section-sign codes, ampersand codes, hex colors, and MiniMessage tag formats.
example_prompt: Convert &cHello &lWorld to MiniMessage format.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — it is a bidirectional string transform with no dependencies.
rationale: Plugin and server configs mix several incompatible color-code dialects and authors waste time hand-translating between them.

name: rust-cheatsheet-lookup
description: Given a concept like 'iterate a hashmap' or 'split a string', returns the idiomatic Rust syntax snippet from an embedded cheat sheet via fuzzy keyword match.
example_prompt: Rust cheat sheet: how do I collect an iterator into a Vec?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: fuzzy match over an embedded snippet table, fully offline.
rationale: Maps the 'Rust Language Cheat Sheet' demand into instant, searchable snippet lookup inside chat.

name: molarity-calc
description: Compute molarity, mass, or volume of a solution from any two known values.
example_prompt: Molarity of 11.7g NaCl in 0.5L of water?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM arithmetic; offline.
rationale: Standard chemistry-class calculation complementing dilution-calc.

name: swim-pace
description: Compute swim pace, critical swim speed, and interval splits per 100m/100yd.
example_prompt: My 400m took 6:40 — what's my pace per 100m?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM arithmetic, offline.
rationale: Swimmers track pace differently from runners; the running-pace tool doesn't fit.

name: dc-offset-check
description: Measures per-channel DC offset of a decoded file and flags channels whose mean exceeds a threshold.
example_prompt: Does this recording have a DC offset problem?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes to PCM in WASM; the mean per channel is a trivial local computation.
rationale: DC offset wastes headroom and causes clicks on edits, and a quick check tells you whether to high-pass.

name: mono-fold-clip-check
description: Checks whether summing a stereo file to mono would clip, reporting the peak of the mono fold-down and required gain reduction.
example_prompt: Will this stereo track clip when folded to mono?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes to PCM in WASM; computing the L+R sum peak is a local pass.
rationale: Mono fold-down clipping ruins playback on phone speakers and club PA, and a check warns before it ships.

name: audio-truncation-check
description: Detects likely truncated files by checking for an abrupt non-zero ending and comparing declared vs decodable duration.
example_prompt: Was this audio file cut off or truncated?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes to PCM in WASM and compares decode length to the container's declared duration locally.
rationale: Interrupted downloads leave files that play until they abruptly stop, and this distinguishes truncation from intended endings.

name: channel-layout-validator
description: Verifies the declared channel count/layout matches the decoded channels and flags empty or dead channels carrying no signal.
example_prompt: Check whether this multichannel file has any dead or mislabeled channels
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes to PCM in WASM; per-channel energy and layout checks run client-side.
rationale: Surround and stems deliveries fail QC for empty or misordered channels, which this validator detects.

name: waveform-asymmetry-check
description: Measures positive-vs-negative peak asymmetry of a decoded waveform to flag likely polarity issues or strong asymmetric distortion.
example_prompt: Check this recording for waveform asymmetry or polarity problems
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes to PCM in WASM; comparing positive and negative peak/RMS is a local computation.
rationale: Asymmetric waveforms waste headroom and hint at processing errors, which this lint surfaces objectively.

name: css-shorthand-conflict-finder
description: Detects shorthand/longhand ordering conflicts in CSS rules (e.g. margin after margin-top resetting it) and reports the masked declaration.
example_prompt: Does my CSS have shorthand properties overriding longhand ones?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSS parsing with a shorthand-expansion map.
rationale: Shorthand-after-longhand bugs are a classic source of 'my style isn't applying' and are invisible without expansion logic.

name: css-unused-keyframes-finder
description: Cross-references @keyframes definitions against animation/animation-name usage and reports keyframe blocks that are never referenced.
example_prompt: Which @keyframes in my CSS are never used?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parse of both keyframe defs and animation references in the same stylesheet.
rationale: Orphaned keyframes bloat CSS after components are deleted; matching defs to usage finds them precisely.

name: meta-charset-position-checker
description: Checks that a document's <meta charset> appears within the first 1024 bytes of the head and is not preceded by content that forces a fallback encoding.
example_prompt: Is my meta charset early enough in this HTML?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM byte-offset scan of the pasted document.
rationale: A late charset declaration is ignored by browsers and reintroduces encoding bugs; position is what matters and is easy to miss.

name: console-statement-detector
description: Detects leftover debug output (console.log/debugger in JS, print/breakpoint in Python, fmt.Println in Go, dbg! in Rust) and reports their locations.
example_prompt: Find any leftover console.log or debugger statements in this code
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: language-aware pattern matching over the pasted source, local.
rationale: Stray debug statements routinely sneak into commits and a quick detector keeps them out.

name: decimal-precision-consistency-checker
description: Checks that all numbers in a column use a consistent number of decimal places and flags inconsistent or over-precise values.
example_prompt: Are all the prices in this column formatted to 2 decimals?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — string decimal-place tally per value, deterministic and in-sandbox.
rationale: Inconsistent decimal precision signals data-entry or rounding errors; a linter surfaces them quickly.

name: image-zone-system-analyzer
description: Maps the tonal distribution onto Ansel Adams' 11 zones and reports which zones are empty or crowded.
example_prompt: Show me the zone-system tonal breakdown of this black-and-white photo.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: bucket luminance into 11 ranges — pure local computation.
rationale: Photographers use zone analysis to judge tonal range and exposure intent.

name: image-grain-analyzer
description: Measures film/sensor grain size and intensity using autocorrelation of high-frequency residuals.
example_prompt: How coarse is the grain in this scanned film photo?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: high-pass filter then autocorrelation — pure local computation.
rationale: Quantifying grain helps match looks and decide on denoising strength.

name: image-periodicity-detector
description: Detects repeating patterns such as halftone screens or textile weaves and reports their dominant frequency/period.
example_prompt: What's the halftone screen frequency in this scanned print?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: autocorrelation/FFT peak analysis — local computation.
rationale: Knowing the screen period lets users descreen scans or spot synthetic textures.

name: video-aspect-ratio-report
description: Reports storage vs display aspect ratio and flags anamorphic encoding where SAR differs from 1:1.
example_prompt: Is this video anamorphic? What's its display aspect ratio?
loader_feasibility: Container/stream header fields (SAR, DAR, coded dimensions) are read by the ffmpeg/Rust loader without decoding.
rationale: Anamorphic mismatches make video play stretched, and confirming SAR/DAR is a frequent debugging need.

name: video-resolution-change-detector
description: Scans the stream for mid-file resolution or pixel-format changes that break many editors and players.
example_prompt: Does the resolution change partway through this video?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg reports per-packet/parameter-set dimensions that a Rust pass compares across the stream, in-browser.
rationale: Concatenated or adaptive captures can switch resolution mid-stream, a subtle corruption that this surfaces directly.

name: video-rate-control-analyzer
description: Classifies the encode's rate-control mode (CBR vs VBR) by measuring per-window bitrate variance and reports the spread.
example_prompt: Is this video CBR or VBR encoded?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg packet sizes are aggregated into per-window bitrates and analyzed by Rust locally; no server.
rationale: Knowing CBR vs VBR matters for streaming/CDN budgeting and is not derivable from the container's nominal bitrate alone.

name: video-no-reference-quality
description: Computes a no-reference perceptual quality score (BRISQUE/NIQE-style) per interval so quality can be judged without an original.
example_prompt: Score the visual quality of this video without a reference
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes sampled frames and a small onnx-runtime model produces the no-reference score entirely in the browser.
rationale: No-reference quality scoring fills the gap that PSNR/SSIM can't (no original available), enabling absolute quality QC.

name: video-mp4-track-timescale-report
description: Reports each track's timescale, duration, and implied length, flagging mismatches that cause A/V drift.
example_prompt: Show the per-track timescales and durations in this mp4
loader_feasibility: A Rust ISO-BMFF parser reads mvhd/tkhd/mdhd fields straight from the bytes, fully client-side.
rationale: Timescale/duration mismatches between tracks are a classic root cause of gradual sync drift that this exposes cleanly.

name: audio-stereo-correlation-meter
description: Computes the stereo phase-correlation coefficient (-1 to +1) overall and over time to reveal out-of-phase content.
example_prompt: Check the stereo phase correlation of this mix
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes to stereo PCM, Rust→WASM correlates L and R, client-side.
rationale: Phase correlation is the key indicator of mono-collapse problems and isn't currently measurable in-app.

name: audio-channel-balance-meter
description: Measures the average level difference between left and right channels in dB to detect a lopsided mix or mic placement.
example_prompt: Is the left/right balance even in this recording?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes to stereo PCM, Rust→WASM compares per-channel RMS, in-browser.
rationale: A small persistent L/R imbalance is easy to miss by ear but obvious as a single dB figure.

name: lossy-source-detector
description: Analyzes a lossless file's spectrum for lowpass cutoffs and missing high-frequency content to flag audio that was transcoded from a lossy source.
example_prompt: Was this FLAC really lossless or made from an MP3?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes to PCM, Rust→WASM runs a long-term average FFT and detects encoder cutoff signatures, in-browser.
rationale: Transcoded-from-lossy files are common in music libraries and only spectral analysis exposes the deception.

name: cbor-inspect
description: Decodes a CBOR binary blob into a readable JSON-like tree with type and tag annotations.
example_prompt: What's inside this CBOR file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the ciborium crate decodes CBOR with no external dependency.
rationale: CBOR shows up in COSE/WebAuthn/IoT payloads that developers regularly need to inspect.

name: geojson-inspector
description: Analyzes a GeoJSON file: feature count, geometry-type breakdown, property keys, coordinate bounding box, and validity issues.
example_prompt: Summarize this GeoJSON — how many features and what's the bounding box?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the geojson crate parses and tallies geometries entirely offline.
rationale: Understanding an unfamiliar GeoJSON's contents is a frequent GIS step with no current inspector.

name: npz-archive-inspector
description: Lists every array inside a .npz (zip) archive with its name, shape, and dtype without decompressing the data.
example_prompt: List the arrays and shapes inside this data.npz.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the zip directory + each npy header; local.
rationale: An .npz can hold many arrays; a manifest view is the natural first inspection step and nothing offers it.

name: measurement-extractor
description: Finds numbers paired with units (kg, m, °C, GB, etc.) and returns structured value+unit pairs.
example_prompt: Pull out all the measurements and their units from this spec sheet
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM regex + unit dictionary, no network
rationale: Spec sheets and recipes are full of measurements worth extracting into a clean table.

name: icns-contents-extractor
description: Parses a macOS .icns file and extracts each contained icon size as a separate PNG.
example_prompt: Extract all the icons from this .icns file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM walks the icns type chunks and decodes the embedded images locally.
rationale: Recovering individual icons from a macOS bundle is impossible for most users without tooling.

name: ogg-chapter-extractor
description: Extracts CHAPTERnnn / CHAPTERnnnNAME comment-style chapter markers from an Ogg/Opus/Vorbis file.
example_prompt: List the chapter marks in this ogg file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: reads the comment header fields, no decode, client-side.
rationale: Ogg chapters use a comment convention that generic tag readers don't surface as a timeline.

name: musicxml-part-extractor
description: Lists the parts/instruments, staves, and tunings declared in a MusicXML score.
example_prompt: What instruments and parts are in this musicxml file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: reads the part-list header of the XML, fully client-side.
rationale: A quick instrumentation overview is useful before importing or arranging a score.

name: edifact-parse
description: Parses a UN/EDIFACT interchange into its UNB/UNH segments, data elements, and composite components.
example_prompt: Break down this EDIFACT ORDERS message into segments
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizing on the EDIFACT service characters (UNA-defined); pure parsing, no server needed for supply-chain documents
rationale: EDI documents are everywhere in logistics and a quick structural view beats squinting at a wall of apostrophes and plus signs.

name: x12-edi-parse
description: Parses an ANSI X12 EDI document (ISA/GS/ST envelopes) into segments and elements with separator detection.
example_prompt: Parse this X12 850 purchase order into readable segments
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reading the ISA segment to detect delimiters, then splitting; fully client-side for B2B documents that often contain sensitive trade data
rationale: X12 is the dominant US EDI standard and developers need a no-upload way to inspect interchanges.

name: pnpm-lock-parse
description: Parses a pnpm-lock.yaml into its packages, importers, and dependency graph entries.
example_prompt: Show me the resolved dependency list from this pnpm-lock.yaml
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM YAML parse of the pnpm lock schema; fully client-side dependency inspection
rationale: pnpm's lock layout differs from npm/yarn and devs need a clear view of what actually got resolved.

name: composer-lock-parse
description: Extracts package names, versions, and sources from a PHP composer.lock file.
example_prompt: List all packages and versions in this composer.lock
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON parse of the packages array; runs in-browser with no PHP toolchain required
rationale: PHP devs reviewing pinned dependencies have no fast offline way to summarize a composer.lock.

name: poetry-lock-parse
description: Parses a Python poetry.lock (TOML) into packages, versions, and marker/extras metadata.
example_prompt: Summarize the locked dependencies in this poetry.lock
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM TOML parse of the [[package]] tables; client-side, no Python environment needed
rationale: Reading a poetry.lock to confirm pinned versions or markers currently means scrolling raw TOML.

name: geotiff-tags-parse
description: Reads the GeoTIFF/TIFF tags from an image header to report the pixel grid, geo-keys, model transform, and projection.
example_prompt: What's the geospatial extent and projection of this GeoTIFF?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM TIFF IFD walk plus GeoKeyDirectory decode; reads only the header so large rasters never upload
rationale: GIS users frequently need the CRS and bounds of a GeoTIFF and there's no quick header-only browser tool.

name: iges-entity-parse
description: Parses an IGES CAD file's Start/Global/Directory/Parameter sections into entity records with type names.
example_prompt: Break down the entities in this IGES file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reading the fixed 80-column IGES section layout; deterministic text parse with no server
rationale: IGES is still exchanged in manufacturing and its column-based format is painful to read without a dedicated parser.

name: raml-parse
description: Parses a RAML API spec (YAML) into its resources, methods, query params, and response bodies.
example_prompt: List the endpoints and methods defined in this RAML file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM YAML parse plus RAML resource-tree flattening; runs in-browser with no API tooling install
rationale: RAML specs are still maintained in many orgs and a quick endpoint overview helps without a RAML-aware editor.

name: openexr-header-parse
description: Reads an OpenEXR file header to report channels, data/display windows, compression, and custom attributes.
example_prompt: What channels and resolution does this EXR file have?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parse of the EXR magic and attribute list; only the header is read so heavy VFX frames stay local
rationale: VFX and 3D artists need to know an EXR's channels (e.g. AOVs) and compression without opening a compositor.

name: dpx-header-parse
description: Parses a DPX film-frame header to report resolution, bit depth, colorimetry, and timecode/film metadata.
example_prompt: Show me the resolution and bit depth of this DPX frame
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM fixed-offset read of the DPX file/image/orientation/film headers (endian-aware); header-only, runs client-side
rationale: DI and scanning workflows rely on DPX and there's no easy browser-local way to confirm a frame's format.

name: lcov-parser
description: Parses an LCOV coverage report (.info) into per-file line/function/branch coverage percentages with a total.
example_prompt: Parse this lcov.info and show me coverage per file.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; LCOV's SF/DA/FN/BRDA record format is simple line parsing, fully local.
rationale: Reading raw LCOV is painful; a per-file coverage table makes gaps visible without a coverage server.

name: bibtex-to-csl-json
description: Parses a BibTeX/BibLaTeX file into CSL-JSON, mapping entry types and author name parts correctly.
example_prompt: Convert my .bib file to CSL-JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; BibTeX tokenizer plus field mapping, no API.
rationale: Moving references between LaTeX and Zotero/Pandoc requires CSL-JSON, and author-name parsing is exactly what a dedicated tool should get right.

name: htaccess-parser
description: Parses an Apache .htaccess file into structured rules (RewriteRule, headers, auth, redirects).
example_prompt: Explain the rules in this .htaccess file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM directive parser.
rationale: Decodes legacy rewrite and redirect logic into readable form.

name: nhs-number-validator
description: Validates a UK NHS number using its 10-9-8…2 weighted mod-11 check digit.
example_prompt: Check if NHS number 943 476 5919 is valid
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: weighted modular sum over nine digits, no network.
rationale: NHS-facing tooling needs to validate patient numbers locally for privacy and to catch typos.

name: license-compatibility-checker
description: Checks a set of SPDX license identifiers for distribution compatibility and surfaces conflicts.
example_prompt: Can I ship a binary that combines MIT, Apache-2.0, and GPL-3.0?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a bundled license-compatibility matrix evaluated with pure logic; no external calls.
rationale: Answers a recurring legal-engineering question deterministically, complementing the cargo license auditor.

name: dependency-diff
description: Diffs two Cargo.lock or Cargo.toml files and shows added, removed, and upgraded crates.
example_prompt: diff these two Cargo.lock files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses both files and compares with the semver crate locally
rationale: Makes dependency-bump PRs reviewable at a glance, the local half of deps.rs.

name: flaky-test-detector
description: Compares multiple JUnit XML runs and identifies tests whose pass/fail result is inconsistent across runs.
example_prompt: Here are three test runs — which tests are flaky?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM; parses several reports and cross-references results locally.
rationale: Flakiness is a major CI pain and cross-run comparison is exactly how you confirm it.

name: thesaurus
description: Find synonyms, antonyms, and related words for a given word using a bundled WordNet lexicon.
example_prompt: Give me synonyms for "happy"
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — a compressed WordNet dictionary ships in the block and lookups are pure in-memory string matching, no network.
rationale: Writers and copy editors reach for a thesaurus constantly and a fully offline one is a clear win.

name: number-format
description: Format numbers with thousands separators, fixed decimals, currency, percent, or scientific notation by locale.
example_prompt: format 1234567.5 as USD currency
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM number formatting.
rationale: Quick, frequent formatting need for reports and copy.

name: pluralize
description: Pluralize or singularize English nouns, including irregular forms, optionally with a count.
example_prompt: What's the plural of "cactus"? And singular of "geese"?
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — inflection rule tables plus irregular-word lists run as pure local string transforms.
rationale: Useful for both writing and code/data generation where correct inflection matters.

name: furigana
description: Annotate Japanese kanji with their hiragana readings as ruby/inline furigana.
example_prompt: Add furigana readings to 漢字を勉強する
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM with a bundled kanji-reading dictionary; offline.
rationale: Heavily requested by Japanese learners and distinct from kana conversion.

name: cloudformation-graph
description: Parses a CloudFormation/SAM template and renders a Mermaid graph of resource dependencies via Ref and GetAtt links.
example_prompt: Draw the resource dependency graph for this CloudFormation template
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: YAML/JSON parse plus Mermaid emission, pure computation
rationale: Extends the sls-dev-tools demand into visualizing infra dependencies, which is hard to grasp from raw YAML.

name: rot47
description: Applies the ROT47 cipher across the printable ASCII range, covering letters, digits and punctuation (its own inverse).
example_prompt: ROT47 decode: %96 BF:4< 3C@H?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — fixed-range codepoint rotation, deterministic and client-side.
rationale: A common alternative to ROT13 that also scrambles punctuation and digits.

name: list-formatter
description: Joins a list of items into a sentence with a chosen separator and an Oxford-comma conjunction.
example_prompt: Join these with 'and': apples, pears, figs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pure string joining (joinery-style) with no I/O.
rationale: Formatting lists into grammatical sentences is a small but frequent text chore.

name: ps-parser
description: Parse pasted `ps aux` or `top` output into a structured table sortable by CPU, memory, or PID, with optional per-user aggregation.
example_prompt: sort this ps aux output by memory and show the top 10
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM column parsing of the pasted text; deterministic local transform, no network.
rationale: Recreates the process-inspection value of bottom/bpytop/htop for a captured snapshot, letting users quickly find the hungriest processes from a copied dump.

name: disk-usage-visualizer
description: Parses `df -h` output into per-mount usage bars and flags filesystems above a configurable fullness threshold.
example_prompt: Show me which mounts are almost full from this df -h output
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the table and emits bar/SVG output in the sandbox.
rationale: Spotting the near-full mount is a daily ops glance and a quick visual beats scanning columns of percentages.

name: tone-synth
description: Synthesizes piano or instrument notes and chords from note names into an audio file.
example_prompt: Play C-E-G as a piano chord.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust wavetable/additive synthesis writes a WAV directly in the browser.
rationale: Maps the upiano demand — sketching notes and chords without any external instrument or DAW.

name: sentence-aligner
description: Aligns sentences between two parallel (source/target) texts to build bitext for translation data.
example_prompt: Align the sentences between this English text and its German translation.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; length/anchor-based dynamic-programming alignment runs client-side.
rationale: Bitext alignment is a foundational MT data-prep step from the JHU/Penn NLP tradition, feasible without a server.

name: expand-expression
description: Expands products, powers, and binomials into fully distributed polynomial form.
example_prompt: expand (2x - 3)^4
loader_feasibility: pyodide + SymPy expand() runs in-browser
rationale: Pairs with factoring as a core algebra manipulation people repeatedly look up.

name: midi-arpeggiator
description: Turns input chords into an arpeggiated MIDI sequence with selectable pattern, rate, and octave range.
example_prompt: Arpeggiate Cmaj Am F G up-down at 1/16 notes as MIDI
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM expands each chord into the chosen step pattern and writes a Standard MIDI File in-browser.
rationale: Arps are everywhere in electronic music and generating editable MIDI beats programming a hardware arp by hand.

name: changelog-parser
description: Parses a Keep-a-Changelog markdown file into structured entries by version, date, and change type.
example_prompt: Parse this CHANGELOG and show what changed in the last 3 releases
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM markdown parser, local only
rationale: Extract release notes programmatically for dashboards, diffs, or release tooling.

name: restriction-sites
description: Find restriction-enzyme cut sites in a DNA sequence and report fragment sizes.
example_prompt: Where does EcoRI cut this DNA sequence?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM pattern search over a bundled enzyme table, offline.
rationale: A molecular-biology staple complementing the existing DNA reverse-complement/translate tools.

name: text-to-svg
description: Convert text in a chosen font into editable SVG outline paths (for logos, laser cutters, Cricut).
example_prompt: convert the word 'MAKER' to SVG paths in a bold font
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM font shaping to vector paths; local.
rationale: Makers and designers need text-as-paths for cutting/engraving; vectorize only traces raster images.

name: python-trace-visualizer
description: Runs Python line by line and returns a step-by-step trace of variable values and the call stack at each step.
example_prompt: Show me a step-by-step execution trace of this Python function
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs CPython in WASM and sys.settrace captures per-line variable state locally, reproducing PythonTutor with no server.
rationale: PythonTutor's step-through visualization is a popular learning aid that maps directly onto pyodide's in-browser tracing.

name: package-json-linter
description: Lints a pasted package.json for missing or invalid fields, malformed version ranges, and common mistakes.
example_prompt: Check this package.json for problems: { "name": "My App", "version": "v1" }
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; JSON parsing plus field-level rule checks run entirely locally.
rationale: Surfaces metadata and dependency-range errors offline before they cause a failed publish.

name: fits-image-viewer
description: Parses a FITS astronomy file and renders its image with adjustable brightness/contrast stretch.
example_prompt: Open this .fits file and show the image.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a fitsio-style parser reads the binary table/image, pixels drawn to a local canvas.
rationale: FITS is unviewable in normal image tools, so a browser-local viewer fills a real gap (fitsio).

name: image-to-ansi-art
description: Converts an image into color terminal art using Unicode half-blocks and 24-bit ANSI color codes, preserving the original palette.
example_prompt: Make a colored ANSI block version of this logo for my terminal: <upload logo.png>
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes/resizes the image and plain Rust→WASM emits half-block glyphs with ANSI truecolor escapes, fully local.
rationale: Distinct from monochrome ASCII, colored block art (chafa-style) is what people actually want for terminal banners and runs offline.

name: dehaze-image
description: Reduces atmospheric haze and fog to recover contrast and color using dark-channel prior.
example_prompt: Remove the haze from this foggy landscape shot
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — dark-channel prior estimation and transmission-map division, pure math
rationale: Haze removal noticeably rescues outdoor photos and has no dedicated tool in the catalog.

name: doi-extractor
description: Extracts and validates DOI identifiers from text and emits resolvable doi.org links.
example_prompt: Find all the DOIs in this reference list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: regex match plus checksum/format validation, no resolver call.
rationale: Researchers collecting DOIs from messy bibliographies want a quick, offline harvest.

name: chessboard-to-fen
description: Reads a chess position from a board photo or diagram and outputs the FEN string.
example_prompt: Give me the FEN for this chessboard screenshot
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime classifies each square's piece and plain Rust assembles the FEN — no network needed.
rationale: Chess players want to analyze positions from books and screenshots by importing them into an engine.

name: channel-pack-texture
description: Packs separate grayscale maps into the R/G/B/A channels of one texture (e.g. ORM packing).
example_prompt: Pack these AO, roughness and metallic maps into one rgba texture
loader_feasibility: Rust image crate composites single channels in WASM
rationale: Game and 3D artists routinely channel-pack PBR maps and currently script it manually.

name: png-to-tga
description: Encodes a PNG as a 32-bit TGA texture for game engines and 3D tools.
example_prompt: Export this png as a tga texture
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: TGA encoding via the `image` crate runs locally.
rationale: Game artists frequently need PNGs back in TGA form for engine import, with no good local tool today.

name: sentence-length-distribution
description: Builds a histogram of sentence lengths and flags overly long or very short sentences.
example_prompt: Analyze the sentence-length variety in this essay
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: sentence splitting plus word counting, fully client-side
rationale: Sentence-length variety is a key prose-rhythm signal that a quick distribution makes visible without manual counting.

name: svg-inspector
description: Reports an SVG's viewBox, dimensions, element counts, path node complexity, and any embedded raster data.
example_prompt: inspect the structure of this SVG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML parser; SVG is text parsed locally
rationale: Designers and devs need to gauge SVG complexity and find bloat before shipping.

name: fasta-stats
description: Parses FASTA input and reports per-record and total sequence counts, lengths, GC content, and N50.
example_prompt: Give me sequence stats for this FASTA file.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: streaming text parse and counting, the core of Rust-Bio, with no system access.
rationale: Quick FASTA summaries are a daily bioinformatics chore that normally requires installing a toolkit.

name: audio-nightcore
description: Make a nightcore (sped-up + higher pitch) or slowed+reverb remix of a track.
example_prompt: Make a slowed and reverb version of this song
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg asetrate/atempo (+aecho/areverb); browser-local.
rationale: Nightcore and slowed+reverb edits are massively popular and trivial with ffmpeg.

name: mixed-content-check
description: Fetch an HTTPS page and flag insecure http:// scripts, images, and other subresources.
example_prompt: Does this page load any insecure HTTP resources?
loader_feasibility: Fetches the page via the HTTP host import and scans the HTML in plain Rust; in-browser.
rationale: Targeted security check the broad seo/a11y/security audits don't isolate.

name: battery-life-calc
description: Estimate device runtime from battery capacity, load current, and efficiency.
example_prompt: How long will a 2000mAh battery last at 150mA draw?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM arithmetic, offline.
rationale: Useful for IoT/maker projects and absent from the electronics calculators.

name: disk-free-table
description: Formats raw df -h output into a clean, color-coded mount table with usage bars and highlights nearly-full filesystems.
example_prompt: Make this df output readable: <pasted df -h>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — splits columns and emits an HTML table from the user's pasted df text; fully offline.
rationale: duf's appeal is purely presentational, which a browser formatter reproduces exactly from pasted df output.

name: glsl-to-msl
description: Cross-compiles a GLSL shader to Apple Metal Shading Language.
example_prompt: Convert this fragment shader from GLSL to Metal MSL
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via naga's GLSL frontend and MSL backend; pure Rust so it runs in the browser sandbox.
rationale: Devs porting WebGL shaders to native iOS/macOS need an MSL version and have no easy browser tool for it.

name: wgsl-formatter
description: Reformats and indents WGSL shader source consistently.
example_prompt: Tidy up the formatting of this WGSL shader
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM token reformatter operating on WGSL text in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: WGSL tooling is immature and a consistent formatter is a missing basic for WebGPU developers.

name: blend-map-generator
description: Builds an RGBA splat/blend map from per-channel layer masks for terrain multitexturing.
example_prompt: Combine these four terrain masks into a blend map
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg/plain Rust channel packing in WASM; local pixels
rationale: Directly serves the multitexturing-with-a-blendmap demand term.

name: design-tokens-converter
description: Converts design tokens between CSS custom properties, W3C/Style-Dictionary JSON, and SCSS variables.
example_prompt: Convert these CSS variables into Style Dictionary JSON tokens
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse one token format and re-serialize to another, no I/O.
rationale: Teams using shadcn/Flutter/native toolkits constantly move tokens between formats and there's no quick browser tool for it.

name: align-assignments
description: Vertically aligns the = signs across a block of assignment or key=value lines.
example_prompt: line up the equals signs in this block of variable assignments
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes column widths and pads each line in-browser
rationale: Aligned assignment blocks read far better in config and constants, and aligning by hand is tedious.

name: sarif-parser
description: Parses a SARIF static-analysis report into a flat table of findings (rule, severity, file, line, message) grouped by tool.
example_prompt: Parse this SARIF file and show me the findings sorted by severity.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with serde_json; walks the SARIF runs/results structure locally, no network.
rationale: SARIF is the common output of linters/scanners but is deeply nested; flattening it makes findings actionable.

name: mel-cepstral-distortion
description: Computes mel-cepstral distortion (MCD) between a reference and a synthesized/test speech file as an objective quality metric.
example_prompt: Measure the MCD between my reference voice and the TTS output
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM extracts MFCCs and computes the cepstral distance on decoded PCM.
rationale: MCD is the standard objective metric for TTS/voice-conversion fidelity and has no browser-local tool yet.

name: stack-trace-diff
description: Compares two stack traces and pinpoints the first divergent frame.
example_prompt: Where do these two crash stack traces start to differ?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM normalizes frames (stripping addresses/line noise) and aligns them locally; offline.
rationale: Triaging whether two crashes share a root cause is faster when the first divergent frame is called out automatically.

name: jp2-to-png
description: Decodes JPEG 2000 (.jp2/.j2k) images to PNG.
example_prompt: Convert this archival .jp2 to png
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg or pyodide (imagecodecs/openjpeg wasm) decodes JPEG 2000 locally; PNG encode follows.
rationale: Libraries, GIS, and archives store JPEG 2000 masters that few consumer apps can open.

name: task-time-summer
description: Sums per-task time estimates (e.g. est:2h, 30m tags) across a list and rolls them up by project and context.
example_prompt: Total the time estimates in this task list and break it down by project
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — duration parsing and arithmetic, fully local.
rationale: Effort estimation/rollup is a project-management need none of the harvested tools compute automatically.

name: directory-index-parser
description: Parses an HTML directory-listing/autoindex page (Apache, nginx, miniserve, etc.) into a structured table of file names, sizes, and modified dates.
example_prompt: Extract the file list from this nginx 'Index of /' HTML page
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML parsing; pure compute, no server.
rationale: Turning a file server's index page into structured data is a common scraping/inventory task directly motivated by miniserve/skyfolder/binserve.

name: darwin-core-validator
description: Validates a GBIF/Darwin Core occurrence CSV for required terms, coordinate ranges, and ISO date formats.
example_prompt: Validate my species occurrence file against Darwin Core
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM field/range checks against embedded Darwin Core term definitions, no network.
rationale: GBIF rejects malformed occurrence records, so researchers need to catch errors locally first.

name: resource-log-summary
description: Parse the text output of system monitors (atop, sar, vmstat, dstat, free) and produce CPU/memory/IO summary stats plus an SVG trend chart.
example_prompt: summarize this atop log and chart the cpu and memory over time
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line parsing + plotters SVG rendering; pure text-to-chart compute with no server.
rationale: Browsers can't watch a live host, but turning the captured output of atop/below/bottom/bpytop into a readable summary and chart is the genuinely portable, on-theme version of those monitors.

name: disk-usage-treemap
description: Parses `du` output (or any path-with-size listing) and renders an interactive treemap plus a sorted breakdown of what is consuming space.
example_prompt: visualize this `du -ah` output and show me the biggest space hogs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the listing and emits an SVG treemap; rendering is computed client-side from pasted text.
rationale: It brings the diskonaut/dua insight — seeing where space goes — to anyone who can paste `du` output, with no TUI.

name: discount-code-generator
description: Generates a batch of unique, hard-to-guess coupon/discount codes in a chosen format with optional prefix and checksum.
example_prompt: generate 500 unique 8-character coupon codes with prefix SALE-
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — deterministic pseudo-random code generation with collision checking in memory, no network.
rationale: Bulk unique coupon codes are a routine ecommerce need that store backends make surprisingly awkward.

name: rlp-decoder
description: Decodes RLP-encoded data (the serialization used for Ethereum transactions and state) into nested structures.
example_prompt: Decode this RLP blob: 0xc88363617483646f67
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — RLP is a self-describing length-prefixed format parsed purely in-memory.
