rationale: RLP underlies raw transactions and Merkle-Patricia proofs; a local decoder is a frequent low-level debugging need.

name: sprite-sheet
description: Pack multiple images into a single sprite-sheet atlas plus a JSON coordinate map.
example_prompt: pack these 12 icons into a sprite sheet
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM bin-packing + composite + JSON emit.
rationale: Common asset-pipeline step for web/game devs that's tedious to do by hand.

name: moderation-spam-classifier
description: Classifies a post as spam, toxic, or benign to assist fediverse moderation decisions.
example_prompt: Is this comment spam or toxic? '<paste comment>'
loader_feasibility: transformers-js text-classification model runs locally; no server call.
rationale: Volunteer Lemmy/Mastodon/Kbin moderators triage reports manually and a local classifier speeds up obvious cases.

name: gtfs-feed-validator
description: Validates a GTFS transit feed (stops, routes, trips, stop_times) for required fields and broken cross-references.
example_prompt: Validate this transit GTFS zip
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM unzip plus CSV referential-integrity checks, entirely in-browser.
rationale: Municipal open portals like Istanbul's IBB publish GTFS, and feeds must pass validation to be usable.

name: acronym-finder
description: Lists acronyms used in a document and pairs each with its first parenthetical or nearby expansion.
example_prompt: What acronyms does this document define, and what do they stand for?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM pattern matching over the text; no external glossary needed.
rationale: Building an acronym glossary for a long technical doc is exactly the dull work tools should automate.

name: function-length-report
description: Lists functions/methods in a source file ranked by line count, flagging those over a threshold.
example_prompt: Which functions in this file are the longest?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM lightweight brace/indent parsing per language; runs locally.
rationale: Spotting overgrown functions is a quick refactoring-priority signal during review.

name: manifest-v2-to-v3
description: Migrates a Chrome/Firefox extension manifest from MV2 to MV3, converting background scripts to a service worker, browser_action to action, and splitting host permissions.
example_prompt: Upgrade this MV2 extension manifest to Manifest V3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: deterministic JSON-to-JSON rewrite with known mapping rules.
rationale: MV2 is being phased out and the migration is mechanical but error-prone, so automating the boilerplate saves real time.

name: burndown-chart-data
description: Computes a burndown series (remaining open tasks over time) from completion dates (done:YYYY-MM-DD) and emits a Mermaid/CSV chart.
example_prompt: Build a burndown chart from the completed dates in this todo.txt
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — date bucketing and cumulative counting, no server.
rationale: Turns the completion history these tools already record into a progress visualization they don't provide.

name: quoted-printable-decode
description: Decodes quoted-printable text (=XX escapes and soft line breaks) back to its original UTF-8 bytes.
example_prompt: Decode this quoted-printable: Hello=20World=21
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: a simple byte-level state machine that runs fully local.
rationale: Quoted-printable is everywhere in email and form posts, and decoding it inline saves a trip to a sketchy web converter.

name: path-parts-extractor
description: Splits each path in a list into directory, stem, and extension columns (dirname/basename/ext).
example_prompt: Extract the folder, base name, and extension from each of these paths
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM path parsing on pasted text; no I/O
rationale: Decomposing paths is a building block scripters constantly need and is a clean deterministic local tool.

name: package-command-translator
description: Translates a package-manager command between apt, dnf, pacman, brew, zypper, apk, and others (install/remove/search/update).
example_prompt: What's the dnf and pacman equivalent of `apt install ripgrep`?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a static cross-PM command mapping table evaluated client-side, exactly upt's model.
rationale: upt's entire value is cross-distro command translation, a self-contained lookup that runs offline far faster than searching docs.

name: chm-extractor
description: Parses a Microsoft Compiled HTML Help (.chm) file and extracts its HTML pages and readable text.
example_prompt: Extract the help pages from this old .chm manual
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the ITSF container plus LZX decompression have pure-Rust implementations (lzxd) that run on bytes in memory
rationale: Legacy .chm help files are otherwise unreadable on modern systems and no good browser-local viewer exists.

name: intel-hex-decode
description: Decode Intel HEX firmware files into raw bytes with address ranges, and re-encode bytes.
example_prompt: extract the bytes from this intel hex file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; record parsing and checksum verification, no I/O
rationale: Firmware ships as Intel HEX and inspecting it needs a record parser.

name: srec-decode
description: Decode Motorola S-record (SREC) firmware into raw bytes and an address map.
example_prompt: parse this s-record file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; record-type and checksum handling done locally
rationale: S-record is the other dominant firmware format with no browser viewer.

name: habit-heatmap
description: Render a GitHub-style contribution heatmap (SVG/PNG) from a list of dates or a date,count log of habit completions.
example_prompt: Make a year heatmap from these workout dates
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM draws the calendar grid as SVG client-side; no rendering server
rationale: habitmap/dijo demand is fundamentally about the visual calendar view, which is a pure offline render of data the user supplies.

name: cooking-convert
description: Convert recipe measurements (cups, grams, ml, tbsp, oz) using ingredient densities, and scale recipes up or down.
example_prompt: How many grams is 2 cups of flour, and scale the recipe to 6 servings?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM with a bundled ingredient-density table; browser-local.
rationale: Ingredient-aware cooking conversions are hugely popular and distinct from physical unit-convert.

name: dmarc-report-parser
description: Parses a DMARC aggregate XML report (often gzipped) into a readable pass/fail table by source IP.
example_prompt: Parse this DMARC report for me
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM unzips and parses the XML locally.
rationale: DMARC reports are unreadable XML that admins need digested into something actionable.

name: makefile-graph
description: Parses a pasted Makefile and renders its target/prerequisite dependencies as a readable graph plus a flattened build order.
example_prompt: Show me the dependency graph for this Makefile
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Makefile parsing and Mermaid/text graph emission is deterministic text processing that needs no shell, matching the umake demand without actually executing builds.
rationale: umake-style universal build tooling is sought after because Makefiles get tangled; visualizing the target graph makes a confusing build instantly legible.

name: bible-reference-parser
description: Detects, normalizes, and expands scripture references in arbitrary text (e.g. "Jn 3.16–18" → "John 3:16-18" and an enumerated verse list).
example_prompt: Find and normalize every Bible reference in this paragraph: ...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM regex/parsing over the input text — no data bundle or network required.
rationale: Citation-heavy study notes and sermons need consistent, machine-readable scripture references, which this produces instantly offline.

name: flash-swf-player
description: Plays a Flash SWF animation or game in the browser using a Ruffle-based WASM player.
example_prompt: Play this old Flash .swf game
loader_feasibility: Ruffle is itself a Rust→WASM Flash player that runs entirely in the browser with no plugin.
rationale: Ruffle is the marquee browser-WASM emulator and revives an enormous archive of otherwise-dead Flash content.

name: video-thumbnail-track
description: Generate a sprite sheet of evenly-spaced thumbnails plus a WebVTT track for scrubbing previews in video players.
example_prompt: make a scrubbing thumbnail sprite and VTT for this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg frame sampling plus plain Rust sprite packing, in-browser.
rationale: Web developers need preview thumbnails for custom players and no tool produces the VTT.

name: quadrant-chart
description: Render a labeled 2x2 quadrant scatter (priority/effort-impact matrix).
example_prompt: plot these items on an effort vs impact 2x2: <data>
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM SVG/PNG render.
rationale: A staple product/strategy diagram not covered by the generic scatter.

name: glsl-formatter
description: Pretty-prints and re-indents messy GLSL source with consistent style.
example_prompt: Format and indent this GLSL shader nicely
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM token-based reformatter; runs entirely client-side on text.
rationale: Shaders copy-pasted from playgrounds like GLSL Sandbox or SHDR are usually unformatted and hard to read.

name: japanese-address-parser
description: Parses Japanese addresses into prefecture, city/ward, district, and block components and extracts postal codes.
example_prompt: Parse 〒150-0001 東京都渋谷区神宮前1-2-3 into structured parts
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM with an embedded prefecture/ward table; fully local.
rationale: Japan Neighborhoods data needs address normalization that English geocoders handle poorly.

name: exr-to-png
description: Decodes and tone-maps an OpenEXR float image to a standard PNG.
example_prompt: convert this render.exr to png
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the `exr` crate decodes OpenEXR; tone-map runs client-side
rationale: VFX and 3D renders ship as EXR and need conversion to share or review quickly.

name: unused-css-check
description: Cross-checks CSS selectors against pasted HTML to flag rules that match no elements.
example_prompt: Which CSS selectors in this stylesheet aren't used by this HTML?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSS parse plus DOM-less selector matching against parsed HTML; fully local
rationale: Dead CSS bloats pages and is hard to find manually; a local checker keeps private markup off external tools.

name: edn-converter
description: Converts EDN (Clojure/Datomic data notation) to JSON and back, with validation and pretty-printing.
example_prompt: Convert this EDN map to JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via edn-rs — EDN parsing/serialization is pure local text work, no server
rationale: Clojure and Datomic users routinely bridge EDN and JSON, and no mainstream converter exists for this niche.

name: audio-null-test
description: Inverts and sums two aligned audio files to report the residual difference level and where they diverge.
example_prompt: Null test these two renders to see if they're identical
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes both files, aligns and subtracts, and measures residual RMS in-browser
rationale: Null testing is the definitive way to prove two files match or to isolate exactly what changed.

name: comment-thread-renderer
description: Renders a JSON or markdown list of comments into a styled, threaded, static HTML comment section you can drop into any page.
example_prompt: Turn this JSON of blog comments into an HTML comment thread
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the input and emits nested HTML with markdown bodies; no backend, matching the static-site use case.
rationale: giscus and utterances exist to add comment threads to static sites; a backend-free renderer covers the common case of pre-collected or exported comments.

name: image-text-behind-subject
description: Place text between the background and a segmented foreground subject (the trendy text-behind-photo effect).
example_prompt: Put the word SUMMER behind the person in this beach photo
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime subject segmentation (same as background-remove) + canvas compositing; browser-local.
rationale: This effect went viral on social/design tools in 2024-25 and reuses the existing segmentation loader.

name: movie-filename-parser
description: Parses messy media filenames into title, year, resolution, codec, and group.
example_prompt: Parse 'The.Film.2021.1080p.x265-GRP.mkv' into fields
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM applies scene-naming regex locally; no metadata lookups needed.
rationale: The browser-local core of moviemon-style library tooling, no API keys required.

name: japanese-word-segmenter
description: Segments space-free Japanese text into words with POS and base forms.
example_prompt: Split this Japanese sentence into words and show the reading of each.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (lindera/vibrato-style) with a compressed IPADIC dictionary loaded once into the browser, fully offline.
rationale: Japanese word segmentation is precisely what MeCab does and is a hard, high-value problem with no good built-in browser support.

name: normal-matrix-calculator
description: Computes the normal matrix (inverse-transpose of the upper-left 3×3) from a model matrix.
example_prompt: Compute the normal matrix for this model matrix
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM math
rationale: Wrong normal matrices are a classic, hard-to-spot lighting bug for WebGL beginners.

name: video-attachment-extractor
description: Extracts embedded attachments (subtitle fonts, cover images, arbitrary files) stored inside MKV/WebM containers.
example_prompt: Pull out the embedded fonts attached to this MKV file
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader's -dump_attachment extracts MKV attachment tracks directly in the wasm runtime.
rationale: Styled subtitles break without their embedded fonts, and there's no native way to retrieve attachments from a container.

name: npm-lockfile-tree
description: Extracts the resolved dependency tree (name, version, resolved URL) from a package-lock.json or yarn.lock into a flat table.
example_prompt: List every resolved package and version from this package-lock.json
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON/yarn-lock parsing; the lockfile is read locally
rationale: Auditing exactly which versions a lockfile pins (for supply-chain or duplicate checks) needs a flattened view.

name: comment-export-migrator
description: Converts comment exports between Commento, Comentario, Isso, Remark42, and Cusdis formats.
example_prompt: Migrate my Isso comments export into Remark42's import format
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON/SQL-dump reshaping; all the named tools export plain structured files.
rationale: Self-hosters switch comment engines often, and no neutral converter exists between these overlapping but incompatible schemas.

name: viewport-meta-validate
description: Validates the viewport meta tag, warning about user-scalable=no, fixed widths, and other anti-patterns that hurt mobile usability and accessibility.
example_prompt: Check my viewport meta tag for mobile-friendliness issues
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM content-attribute parser with a fixed ruleset; local.
rationale: A bad viewport tag breaks mobile layout or zoom accessibility and is a single, checkable line.

name: yubikey-otp-parse
description: Splits a 44-character YubiKey OTP into its Modhex public ID and token, and optionally decrypts the token with a supplied AES-128 key to reveal the private ID, counters, timestamp, and CRC.
example_prompt: Parse this yubikey OTP ccccccibhbfflnjvjfbnjuvkhfthjvfvfclr with AES key 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: Modhex decode plus a single AES-128-ECB block decrypt via the pure-Rust `aes` crate, all done locally so the secret key never leaves the browser.
rationale: Lets security engineers validate and inspect YubiKey OTPs offline without sending secret keys to a server.

name: parse-http2-frame
description: Decodes HTTP/2 binary frames (length, type, flags, stream id) and the payloads of structured frames like SETTINGS, WINDOW_UPDATE, RST_STREAM, and PING.
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust frame parser in WASM; deterministic and local (HEADERS payloads are surfaced as raw HPACK).
rationale: HTTP/2 is binary and hard to read by hand, so an offline frame decoder fills a real gap.

name: chromatic-aberration-detector
description: Detects color fringing at high-contrast edges by measuring R/B channel misalignment.
example_prompt: Is there chromatic aberration in this photo?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM measures per-channel edge offsets on decoded pixels in-browser.
rationale: Detecting fringing tells photographers whether lens correction is needed.

name: video-dominant-color-timeline
description: Extracts the dominant color palette for each scene and renders a color barcode across the video's duration.
example_prompt: Make a color timeline / barcode of this movie
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg samples frames, plain Rust→WASM clusters colors; the barcode is composed locally with no API.
rationale: Color barcodes are popular for analyzing a film's visual mood and grading consistency.

name: crest-factor-analyzer
description: Reports peak-to-RMS crest factor over the whole file and per segment as a punchiness/compression indicator.
example_prompt: Measure the crest factor of this drum bus
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes peak and RMS from decoded PCM in-browser
rationale: Crest factor quickly quantifies how heavily a signal has been compressed or limited.

name: noise-floor-estimator
description: Estimates the noise-floor level (dBFS) of a recording from its quietest passages.
example_prompt: What's the noise floor of this voiceover?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM analyzes the low-percentile RMS distribution of decoded samples client-side
rationale: Noise-floor numbers tell you whether a recording is clean enough to publish.

name: image-contrast-compare
description: Computes contrast and dynamic-range metrics (RMS contrast, min/max, histogram spread) for several images and tabulates the differences.
example_prompt: Which of these edits has the most contrast?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: statistical passes over luminance buffers, no server.
rationale: Quantifying contrast across versions removes the subjectivity from 'which one pops more'.

name: chroma-similarity
description: Computes chroma (pitch-class) profiles for two tracks and reports their harmonic similarity.
example_prompt: Are these two tracks harmonically similar enough to be a cover?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM does the FFT and chroma binning on both decoded tracks locally.
rationale: Surfaces cover-song and version relationships through harmonic content rather than raw waveform.

name: audio-edit-diff
description: Aligns two versions of a recording and locates the time regions where they diverge, flagging inserted, deleted, or altered sections.
example_prompt: Find the edits between these two versions of the master.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM cross-correlates and walks both PCM streams to find divergence points locally.
rationale: Acts like a 'diff' for audio, pinpointing exactly what changed between two takes.

name: a-weighted-level-compare
description: Computes the A-weighted level of two files and reports the perceived-loudness difference in dB(A).
example_prompt: Which of these two clips sounds louder by A-weighting?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM applies the A-weighting filter and integrates the level for both files in-browser.
rationale: Compares perceived loudness with a weighting curve distinct from LUFS or raw RMS.

name: video-audio-track-compare
description: Compares the audio tracks of two videos by count, codec, channel layout, sample rate, and language tags.
example_prompt: Do both files have the same audio tracks and channel layouts?
loader_feasibility: ffprobe enumerates audio streams for both files in wasm ffmpeg, diffed in Rust→WASM.
rationale: Catching a dropped or down-mixed audio track between exports prevents shipping the wrong mix.

name: protobuf-varint-decoder
description: Decodes a raw protobuf varint/zigzag byte stream into the original integers.
example_prompt: Decode these protobuf varints to integers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies 7-bit continuation and zigzag decoding
rationale: Reverse-engineering protobuf wire data requires manual varint decoding that's easy to get wrong.

name: cooking-substitute
description: Suggest ingredient substitutions with quantities (e.g. buttermilk, eggs, baking powder).
example_prompt: What can I use instead of buttermilk for 1 cup?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM lookup over a bundled substitution database, offline.
rationale: A daily kitchen rescue not covered by measurement conversion or recipe extraction.

name: glsl-to-hlsl
description: Cross-compiles a GLSL shader to Direct3D HLSL, the way Google's ANGLE does at runtime.
example_prompt: Translate this GLSL shader to HLSL like ANGLE would
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using naga's GLSL frontend and HLSL backend, fully client-side.
rationale: Cross-platform shader authors and ANGLE users need to preview the D3D translation without a Windows toolchain.

name: type-token-ratio
description: Computes lexical-diversity metrics (type-token ratio, MTLD, hapax counts) for a text.
example_prompt: How lexically diverse is this essay?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM counts types and tokens and derives the metrics locally.
rationale: Lexical-diversity measures are a standard quantitative tool in the corpus-linguistics curriculum.

name: frequency-sweep-generator
description: Generates a linear or logarithmic frequency sweep (chirp) WAV between two frequencies over a chosen duration.
example_prompt: Make a log sweep from 20 Hz to 20 kHz over 10 seconds
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes the swept-sine phase integral and writes PCM samples to a WAV entirely client-side.
rationale: Sweeps are the standard test signal for speaker/room measurement and audio QA, and people need them on demand.

name: excel-formula-explain
description: Explain an Excel/Sheets formula in plain English, breaking down each function.
example_prompt: explain =VLOOKUP(A2,Sheet2!A:C,3,FALSE)
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM formula parser; complement to spreadsheet-formula-eval.
rationale: Spreadsheet users constantly need to decode inherited formulas; only evaluation exists today.

name: download-batch-generator
description: Turns a pasted list of URLs into a ready-to-run wget, curl, or aria2 batch-download command or input file.
example_prompt: Make an aria2 input file to download all these image URLs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; it only transforms a URL list into shell/config text, no actual downloading.
rationale: Assembling correct multi-file download commands is tedious and easy to botch quoting on.

name: bibtex-lint
description: Validates and normalizes a BibTeX file, flagging duplicate keys, missing required fields, and inconsistent casing.
example_prompt: check this .bib file for errors and duplicate keys
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parser plus rule checks operate only on the pasted file.
rationale: Keeping a clean .bib is a chronic pain for papis/pubs users and is a deterministic lint task.

name: canonical-url-checker
description: Inspects rel=canonical declarations in HTML (and matching Link headers) for absolute-URL correctness, self-reference, and conflicts.
example_prompt: Check the canonical URL setup in this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tag/header parsing and URL normalization; offline.
rationale: Wrong or relative canonicals quietly de-index pages and are easy to misconfigure.

name: metalink-parse
description: Parses .metalink/.meta4 files into mirror URLs, file sizes, hashes, and chunk info.
example_prompt: List the mirrors and hashes in this .meta4 file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML parsing in the sandbox
rationale: Metalink is the format Motrix/aria2 consume; this makes it human-readable.

name: fake-hires-detector
description: Checks whether a hi-res file (96/192 kHz, 24-bit) carries real ultrasonic content or was merely upsampled from CD quality, by inspecting spectral cutoff and effective bit depth.
example_prompt: Is this 24-bit/96kHz file genuine hi-res or just upsampled?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: FFT spectral-cutoff analysis plus least-significant-bit usage histogram on decoded PCM
rationale: Padded 'hi-res' downloads waste storage and bandwidth; this verifies the format actually carries the resolution it claims.

name: cue-sheet-validator
description: Validates a .cue sheet's syntax, required commands, and track INDEX times, and checks that times fall within the referenced audio's duration.
example_prompt: Validate this cue sheet against the FLAC it points to
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse the cue text and compare track times to the decoded audio length client-side
rationale: Broken cue sheets desync album track splits, and validating against actual duration catches out-of-range indexes.

name: opus-stream-validator
description: Validates Ogg Opus structure: OpusHead/OpusTags headers, page sequence numbers, granule positions, and pre-skip, flagging stream defects.
example_prompt: Check this .opus file's stream structure is valid
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse Ogg pages and Opus headers from the file bytes, no decode or server
rationale: Malformed Opus pages cause seeking and gapless-playback bugs that only structural validation can reveal.

name: aliasing-detector
description: Detects resampling and synthesis aliasing by finding mirror-image spectral components folded back below Nyquist.
example_prompt: Does this resampled file have aliasing artifacts?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: FFT spectrum analysis on decoded PCM with mirror-frequency detection, client-side
rationale: Cheap sample-rate conversion and soft-synths leave audible aliasing that spectral analysis can objectively confirm.

name: html-iframe-inventory
description: Extracts every iframe with its src, sandbox, allow, and referrerpolicy attributes so embeds can be audited at a glance.
example_prompt: List the iframes and their sandbox attributes in this page
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM attribute extraction over the pasted HTML.
rationale: Embedded third-party frames are a security surface, and seeing their sandbox/allow flags in one list speeds review.

name: video-mp4-box-validator
description: Walks the MP4 box tree to validate required boxes, sizes, and ordering, reporting structural corruption or truncation.
example_prompt: Validate the box structure of this MP4 — is it well-formed?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses the atom hierarchy directly from bytes; no decode needed.
rationale: A structurally broken MP4 fails differently across players, and box-level validation pinpoints the actual defect.

name: envelope-difference-compare
description: Extracts the amplitude envelopes of two recordings and highlights the regions where their dynamics differ most.
example_prompt: Show me where the dynamics differ between these two takes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes RMS/peak envelopes and diffs them locally.
rationale: Envelope diffing localizes where compression or performance changed, not just whether it did.

name: tap-results-diff
description: Compares two TAP (Test Anything Protocol) outputs and reports which assertions changed status, were added, or were removed between runs.
example_prompt: Here are two TAP outputs from before and after my change — what changed?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the line-oriented TAP format and aligns tests by number/description locally; it is pure text processing.
rationale: TAP is ubiquitous in Node/Perl/embedded ecosystems and has no diff tool in the catalog, unlike JUnit.

name: har-response-diff
description: Diffs two HTTP responses captured in HAR files, comparing status, headers, and JSON bodies.
example_prompt: Compare the API responses in these two HAR captures
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse HAR JSON, select entries, and diff headers/bodies in-memory
rationale: Debugging API regressions across captures needs a structured response diff rather than eyeballing raw HAR.

name: video-static-noise-generator
description: Generates a TV-static / analog-noise clip at a chosen intensity and duration.
example_prompt: make 5 seconds of TV static noise at 720p
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — a nullsrc plus the noise filter (or geq) generates the frames locally.
rationale: Glitch transitions and 'no signal' looks are frequently needed.

name: pdf-booklet
description: Reorders pages into booklet imposition for folded, saddle-stitched printing.
example_prompt: Arrange this PDF as a printable booklet
loader_feasibility: pyodide — pypdf computes the imposition order and writes 2-up signatures client-side.
rationale: Booklet printing is fiddly to set up manually and a satisfying one-click win.

name: prolog-query
description: Loads a Prolog program and evaluates queries against it, returning all solutions and variable bindings, in-browser.
example_prompt: Given `parent(tom,bob). parent(bob,ann).`, query `?- parent(tom,X), parent(X,Y).`
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: scryer-prolog is pure Rust with an experimental wasm32 target (it powers a web playground), so the engine runs client-side in wasmi.
rationale: mthom/scryer-prolog maps to an actual logic engine, and a browser-local Prolog REPL is a genuinely novel tool for learning and quick reasoning tasks.

name: pesel-validator
description: Validates a Polish PESEL number's weighted checksum and decodes the embedded birth date and sex.
example_prompt: Validate PESEL 44051401359
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: weighted mod-10 plus date parsing, entirely client-side.
rationale: PESEL encodes both a checksum and a birthdate, so a combined validate-and-decode tool is genuinely useful.

name: slate-generator
description: Generates a production slate/clapperboard card clip with scene, take, date, and project fields before a shot.
example_prompt: Make a 3-second slate for Scene 12 Take 4, project 'Aurora', dated today
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg lays out the slate fields with `drawbox`/`drawtext` over a synthetic source entirely client-side.
rationale: A consistent head slate keeps footage organized for editorial and a one-prompt generator removes a repetitive setup step.

name: package-json-analyzer
description: Parses a package.json and reports dependency counts, duplicate dev/prod deps, missing fields, and risky version ranges.
example_prompt: Analyze this package.json for issues
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON parsing of pasted text; no registry calls, fully local.
rationale: awesome-nodejs CLI users want quick package.json hygiene checks without installing anything.

name: strip-line-numbers
description: Removes leading line-number prefixes from each line.
example_prompt: strip the line numbers off this pasted code
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a per-line regex/prefix strip runs entirely client-side with no dependencies.
rationale: Copying numbered code from docs/editors leaves prefixes that must be removed before reuse.

name: near-duplicate-detector
description: Uses SimHash/MinHash fingerprints to find near-duplicate paragraphs or documents within or across two inputs.
example_prompt: Find paragraphs in these two drafts that are almost identical
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — shingle, hash, and compare fingerprints with Hamming distance locally
rationale: Near-duplicate detection catches copy-paste and boilerplate that exact diffing misses.

name: onion-address-validator
description: Validates and decodes a Tor v3 .onion address, checking its ed25519 key, version byte and checksum.
example_prompt: Is this .onion address valid? Check its checksum
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM base32 decode + SHA3 checksum verification — no Tor connection, just math on the string.
rationale: OnionShare demand brings .onion handling; validating address integrity is a genuinely local security utility.

name: dmesg-analyzer
description: Scans pasted dmesg/kernel-log output and highlights OOM kills, segfaults, I/O errors, and hardware warnings grouped by severity.
example_prompt: Look through this dmesg and tell me why the process got killed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pattern-matching and grouping over pasted kernel log text, client-side only.
rationale: Kernel logs are huge and scary, and surfacing the OOM-killer or hardware fault lines is exactly the triage users need.

name: journal-log-analyzer
description: Parses journalctl output to filter by unit and priority, build an error timeline, and surface the noisiest units.
example_prompt: Analyze this journalctl dump and show me the errors from the last boot by service
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — structured parsing and aggregation of pasted journal text, no systemd access.
rationale: systemd journals are dense and per-unit filtering plus an error timeline is the common diagnostic task, fully doable on pasted text.

name: kdl-validate
description: Parses, validates, and pretty-formats KDL document files (the config format used by Zellij and other tools), reporting syntax errors with line numbers.
example_prompt: Check my Zellij layout.kdl for syntax errors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the `kdl` crate compiles to WASM and parses entirely in-memory.
rationale: KDL has no mainstream online validator yet Zellij/config users frequently hand-edit it and hit cryptic parse failures.

name: erlang-term-codec
description: Decodes Erlang External Term Format (ETF) binaries into readable terms and re-encodes terms back to ETF bytes.
example_prompt: Decode this Erlang ETF binary (hex): `83 6C 00 00 00 01 61 01 6A`
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: ETF is a documented binary format; encoding/decoding is straightforward byte-level parsing with no external runtime.
rationale: rustler bridges Rust and the BEAM, and developers debugging NIF data exchange need to inspect the ETF payloads crossing that boundary.

name: stereo-vectorscope
description: Renders a goniometer/vectorscope PNG of the stereo signal so phase and width are visible at a glance.
example_prompt: Generate a vectorscope image for this stereo file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM plots L/R sample pairs to a PNG on PCM (ffmpeg decodes); runs entirely in-browser.
rationale: The vectorscope is the standard visual for diagnosing stereo phase and image at a glance.

name: shake-xof
description: Generates SHAKE128/SHAKE256 extendable-output (XOF) digests of a chosen output length.
example_prompt: shake256 of "seed" with 64 bytes output
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the sha3 crate's SHAKE XOF reader is pure-Rust and produces arbitrary-length output offline.
rationale: SHAKE's variable-length output is a unique capability no fixed-digest tool offers, useful for key/nonce derivation.

name: quoted-printable-codec
description: Encodes and decodes MIME Quoted-Printable, the =XX hex escaping used in email bodies and headers.
example_prompt: decode this quoted-printable: =C3=A9t=C3=A9
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — QP is a deterministic byte-escaping scheme with no I/O.
rationale: Anyone inspecting raw email or MIME parts needs to decode Quoted-Printable, and few clean browser tools exist.

name: video-color-metadata-extractor
description: Extracts the color primaries, transfer characteristics, matrix coefficients, and range tags from a video stream.
example_prompt: What color primaries and transfer function does this video use?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg/ffprobe (loaded) reads colr/VUI tags without decoding; runs in wasm ffmpeg locally
rationale: Wrong or missing color tags cause washed-out or oversaturated playback, and users need to read them to fix it.

name: video-encoder-tag-extractor
description: Reads the encoder, software, and handler tags that identify what produced a video file.
example_prompt: What software or encoder created this video?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the udta/meta and stream metadata tags; byte-level read, no upload
rationale: Encoder fingerprints reveal provenance and help reproduce or audit an encode.

name: video-vmaf-report
description: Computes Netflix VMAF perceptual quality scores between a reference and a distorted/re-encoded video and reports mean, min, and harmonic-mean scores.
example_prompt: Compare the VMAF quality of my re-encode against the master.mp4 original
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM libvmaf filter with the VMAF model JSON bundled in the tool runs the whole comparison client-side with no upload.
rationale: VMAF is the industry-standard perceptual metric and is distinct from the already-built PSNR/SSIM tools, giving encoders a much better quality signal.

name: log-spectral-distance
description: Computes the log-spectral distance (LSD) between a reference and a degraded audio file frame-by-frame.
example_prompt: What's the log-spectral distance between the clean and codec'd version?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs FFTs and averages log-magnitude differences locally.
rationale: LSD is a compact objective measure of codec/enhancement spectral fidelity against a reference.

name: vtk-points-to-csv
description: Reads legacy VTK polydata/unstructured-grid point and scalar data into CSV.
example_prompt: Convert the points in this .vtk file to CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; legacy VTK ASCII section parsing.
rationale: Scientific-visualization VTK files trap data that researchers want in spreadsheets.

name: tiled-map-inspector
description: Parses a Tiled .tmx/.tsx map into a readable summary of layers, tilesets, object groups, and properties, with optional JSON export.
example_prompt: Summarize the layers and tilesets in this Tiled .tmx map.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — .tmx/.tsx are XML files parseable with a pure-Rust XML reader in the sandbox.
rationale: Tiled maps drive levels in ggez/Bevy/Godot projects and inspecting or converting them to JSON is a frequent, fiddly chore.

name: tracing-span-timeline
description: Parses `tracing`/structured span logs and renders a timeline of span start/end durations.
example_prompt: Visualize the spans in this tracing JSON output
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — span events are parsed and laid out into an SVG timeline locally
rationale: Directly serves tokio-rs/tracing users who otherwise need a separate collector to see span timing.

name: kcl-renderer
description: Compiles KCL configuration code and renders the output to YAML or JSON.
example_prompt: Render this KCL config to YAML (pasted below)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the KCL compiler ships an official wasm target, so config evaluation runs client-side.
rationale: KCL is growing for Kubernetes config-as-code and users want to preview rendered manifests instantly.

name: flac-stream-validator
description: Structurally validates a FLAC stream: STREAMINFO consistency, frame sync codes, and metadata block ordering, without full decode.
example_prompt: Is this FLAC file structurally valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses FLAC metadata blocks and frame headers locally with no network.
rationale: Quickly flags malformed FLAC files that fail silently or only error deep into playback.

name: bloom-filter
description: Builds a Bloom filter from a set and tests membership with a tunable false-positive rate.
example_prompt: Build a bloom filter from these IDs and test if X is present
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM implements the bit-array and hash functions locally.
rationale: Probabilistic membership is a core space-efficiency structure from Mining Massive Datasets.

name: nominalization-detector
description: Finds nominalizations ('zombie nouns' like 'utilization', 'implementation') that bury verbs.
example_prompt: Flag the zombie nouns in this paragraph.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: suffix-pattern heuristics over tokens, no model required.
rationale: Converting nominalizations back to verbs is a core clarity-editing technique.

name: image-focus-peak-map
description: Generates a heatmap highlighting the sharpest, in-focus regions of an image.
example_prompt: Show me which parts of this macro shot are actually in focus.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: per-region high-frequency energy mapped to a heat overlay — local pixel math.
rationale: Focus peaking reveals depth-of-field and confirms the subject is sharp.

name: video-gamut-coverage-report
description: Measures how much of a target gamut (BT.709 / BT.2020 / P3) the content's colors actually occupy.
example_prompt: How much of the BT.2020 gamut does this footage use?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes frames and a Rust/onnx pass maps pixel chromaticities against gamut boundaries in WASM.
rationale: Gamut coverage tells whether wide-gamut delivery is justified and flags content that barely exceeds Rec.709.

name: dmarc-record-parse
description: Parses a DMARC TXT record and explains the policy, subdomain policy, alignment modes, and reporting addresses.
example_prompt: explain what p=quarantine pct=50 means in this DMARC record
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tag parsing of the record string; fully local
rationale: DMARC tags are cryptic and misconfigured policies quietly fail to protect a domain.

name: point-cloud-bounds
description: Computes the axis-aligned bounding box, centroid, and per-axis extents of a 2-D/3-D point set from CSV.
example_prompt: What's the bounding box and centroid of these 3D points?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM min/max/mean scan; no server.
rationale: Bounds and centroid are the first things you need when sizing or normalizing point data.

name: gdb-backtrace-parser
description: Parses a GDB backtrace into structured frames (frame number, function, args, source file, line) for easier triage.
example_prompt: Parse this gdb backtrace into a clean list of frames with files and lines.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; pattern-matches GDB's `#N func (args) at file:line` frame lines locally.
rationale: Crash triage means reading backtraces fast; structuring frames highlights the relevant call path.

name: two-column-percent-change
description: Computes row-wise percent change between a baseline column and a new column and outputs an augmented table.
example_prompt: Add a percent-change column comparing last month vs this month in this table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: tabular parsing and division, runs locally
rationale: Period-over-period comparison is everyday spreadsheet work that benefits from a precise, locale-safe helper.

name: bazel-build-explainer
description: Parses pasted Bazel/Starlark BUILD files, lists each rule and target, and maps their declared dependencies as a graph.
example_prompt: Explain the targets and their dependencies in this BUILD file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Starlark rule/attr extraction is text parsing with no evaluation needed, so it runs client-side in wasmi.
rationale: blaze/Bazel BUILD files are notoriously opaque to newcomers, so a paste-and-understand explainer addresses real onboarding demand.

name: chapter-metadata-generator
description: Builds an ffmpeg/QuickTime chapter-metadata file from a pasted list of chapter titles and timestamps.
example_prompt: make a chapter metadata file from this list of times and titles
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse timestamps and emit the chapter metadata format, no I/O.
rationale: Feeds clean chapter info into audiobook and podcast tools without hand-formatting.

name: nomad-job-validator
description: Validates a Nomad job spec (HCL) for required blocks, common misconfigurations, and resource sanity.
example_prompt: Check this Nomad job file for problems before I submit it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: HCL parsing plus a bundled Nomad schema ruleset, all client-side.
rationale: Wander-style demand shows Nomad users want help with job specs, which fail late with cryptic scheduler errors.

name: cargo-license-auditor
description: Analyzes dependency licenses from Cargo metadata and flags copyleft or policy-violating licenses.
example_prompt: Audit the licenses in my Cargo dependencies and warn me about anything GPL: <paste cargo metadata>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — JSON/TOML parsing and SPDX expression evaluation are pure computation that runs entirely client-side.
rationale: cargo-deny's license gate is the most-used policy check; running it on pasted metadata helps devs vet dependencies before committing.

name: melody-to-regex
description: Compiles the readable Melody DSL into a standard regular expression.
example_prompt: Compile this Melody source into a regex: 5 of "a"; <space>;
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Melody is itself a Rust compiler, so it ports directly to wasm with no runtime deps.
rationale: Melody makes regex authoring approachable; a browser compiler turns an intimidating syntax into plain language.

name: xor-key-breaker
description: Recovers single-byte and repeating-key XOR keys from ciphertext using frequency scoring.
example_prompt: find the xor key for this hex ciphertext
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM keysize/Hamming-distance search + scoring — CPU-only
rationale: Repeating-key XOR breaking is the signature Cryptopals-style challenge and a strong cryptanalysis demo.

name: honeypot-spam-guard
description: Generates a hidden honeypot field plus a time-trap and the client-side check logic to silently reject bot form submissions without a CAPTCHA.
example_prompt: Add anti-spam protection to my contact form without reCAPTCHA
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM emits the markup and guard snippet; static code, no external anti-spam service.

name: choropleth-data-binner

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM classification algorithms; no network.
rationale: Mapping census/crime data requires good break points, which generic tools don't provide.

name: tei-xml-reader

name: video-subtitle-track-compare
description: Compares which subtitle tracks (language, format, forced flag) exist in two videos and flags missing ones.

name: zalgo-cleaner
description: Strips excessive combining diacritical marks ("zalgo" glitch text) back to clean base characters.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — strip combining-mark code points, no deps

name: set-operations
description: Computes union, intersection, difference, and symmetric difference of sets and renders a Venn diagram.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM set math plus SVG Venn rendering — fully client-side.
rationale: Set operations and Venn diagrams are foundational discrete-math concepts that benefit from visualization.

name: license-generator
description: Generates a LICENSE file from an SPDX identifier, author name, and year, with proper placeholder substitution.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: bundled license templates with field substitution.

name: pcd-to-xyz-pointcloud
description: Parses a PCL .pcd point-cloud file (ASCII or binary) and exports the XYZ coordinates as a plain point list.
example_prompt: Convert this .pcd point cloud to a simple XYZ file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: PCD has a fixed text header followed by ASCII or packed binary points, decoded client-side with no native libs.
rationale: ROS/PCL pipelines emit .pcd but most lightweight viewers and tools only read plain XYZ.

name: bayer-matrix-generator
description: Outputs an ordered Bayer dither threshold matrix as a grayscale image at a chosen order (2x2 up to 16x16).
example_prompt: generate an 8x8 bayer matrix image
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes the recursive Bayer pattern and scales it into a PNG — deterministic math.
rationale: The ordered-dither matrix is a reusable building block for shaders and dithering and is distinct from the excluded dither-image transform.

name: plasma-fractal-generator
description: Creates a cloud-like plasma image using the diamond-square midpoint-displacement algorithm with a chosen roughness and palette.
example_prompt: make a colorful plasma cloud texture 800x800
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM performs diamond-square subdivision into a PNG — iterative CPU math, no deps.
rationale: Plasma/cloud textures are a distinct fractal family widely used as backgrounds and as a base for further effects.

name: loopback-latency-signal-generator
description: Generates a sharp click pattern designed for measuring round-trip audio latency through a loopback path.
example_prompt: Generate a loopback latency test click train
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: emits precisely-spaced impulses with known offsets + WAV encode, client-side.
rationale: Setting up low-latency monitoring/recording requires a known stimulus to measure system round-trip delay.

name: adsr-envelope-tone-generator
description: Synthesizes a tone shaped by user-defined attack/decay/sustain/release envelope parameters.
example_prompt: Make a 220Hz tone with a 10ms attack, 200ms decay, 60% sustain, 500ms release
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: oscillator multiplied by a computed ADSR gain curve + WAV encode, deterministic local.
rationale: Producers want quick enveloped one-shots for sound-design sketches without opening a full synth.

name: additive-harmonic-tone-generator
description: Builds a timbre by summing a fundamental and harmonics with user-specified amplitudes/phases.
example_prompt: Make a sawtooth-like tone from the first 12 harmonics at 1/n amplitude
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: additive synthesis over a harmonic series + WAV encode, fully deterministic offline.
rationale: Additive control lets users craft exact spectra (and band-limited classic waveforms) for synthesis and testing.

name: stereo-channel-id-tone-generator
description: Generates alternating left-then-right identification tones to verify speaker/headphone wiring and channel mapping.
example_prompt: Make a left/right channel check tone
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: writes tone bursts to one channel at a time in a stereo WAV, deterministic client-side.
rationale: A quick, reliable way to confirm L/R polarity and routing when setting up speakers or testing a new interface.

name: video-field-order-fix
description: Swaps top/bottom field order to fix juddery or torn interlaced footage.
example_prompt: fix the field order on this interlaced capture, it judders
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm setfield/field filters run locally
rationale: Wrong field order produces a distinctive judder that only a field-order swap corrects.

name: css-keyframes-extractor
description: Pulls all @keyframes animation blocks out of a stylesheet into a standalone file.
example_prompt: Extract all the @keyframes from this CSS
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM at-rule parse + collection; no server
rationale: Isolating animation definitions makes them easy to reuse or move into one place.

name: png-interlace-converter
description: Adds or removes Adam7 interlacing in a PNG.
example_prompt: Remove interlacing from this png
loader_feasibility: Rust png crate re-encodes with the chosen interlace setting in WASM
rationale: Interlacing affects load behavior and file size and is otherwise only adjustable in heavy editors.

name: pcm-interleave-deinterleave
description: Converts multichannel PCM between interleaved (LRLR) and planar (LLL…RRR) channel layouts.
example_prompt: Deinterleave this stereo PCM into separate channel blocks
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: reshuffles sample frames by channel, pure indexing work in the browser.
rationale: GPU/ML audio buffers expect planar layout while files store interleaved, so reshaping is a frequent need.

name: ltc-timecode-encoder
description: Generates an LTC audio track from a start timecode, frame rate, and duration.
example_prompt: Make a 30-second LTC track starting at 01:00:00:00 at 25 fps
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: synthesizes the biphase-mark-coded timecode waveform as PCM locally.
rationale: Productions need to lay down reference timecode tracks for multi-device synchronization.

name: sample-rate-header-rewriter
description: Changes only the declared sample rate in a WAV header (varispeed) without resampling the audio.
example_prompt: Re-tag this 44100 Hz WAV as 48000 Hz without resampling
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: edits the fmt chunk's sample-rate and byte-rate fields in place, client-side.
rationale: Intentional pitch/speed shifts and fixing mistagged rates are quick header-only operations.

name: starfield-background-video
description: Generates an animated flying-through-space starfield background loop with adjustable density and speed.
example_prompt: Generate a 20-second starfield background flying forward at medium speed
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute simulates and draws the moving stars on the GPU, with ffmpeg encoding the result in-browser.
rationale: Starfields are an iconic intro/background motion asset and a parameterized generator gives endless royalty-free variants.

name: two-pass-encode-script-generator
description: Generates the matched pair of ffmpeg commands for a two-pass encode targeting a specific bitrate.

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM templates the first-pass (null mux) and second-pass commands with consistent stats-file naming.
rationale: Two-pass encoding requires two carefully-aligned commands and a generator removes the easy-to-mismatch boilerplate.

name: safe-area-overlay-template
description: Generates a transparent broadcast/title-safe guide overlay clip showing action-safe and title-safe margins.
example_prompt: Make a transparent 16:9 title-safe and action-safe guide overlay at 1080p
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg draws the nested safe-area rectangles with `drawbox` on an alpha source, fully in wasm.
rationale: Overlaying a safe-area guide while editing keeps text and logos inside broadcast margins and there is no quick generator for one.

name: lrc-lyrics-scaffold
description: Creates a timestamped LRC lyric file skeleton from plain lyrics and a song duration, evenly distributing line cues for tweaking.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM splits the lyrics into lines, spreads timestamps across the duration, and formats valid LRC text client-side.
rationale: Hand-typing LRC timestamps from scratch is painful; a scaffold gives a near-aligned starting point to nudge.

name: netlify-headers-generator
description: Generates a Netlify/Cloudflare-Pages _headers file mapping path patterns to custom HTTP response headers.
example_prompt: Build a _headers file: /* gets HSTS and X-Frame-Options, /assets/* gets long cache
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — path-indented header formatting, fully offline.
rationale: JAMstack hosts use this exact indentation-sensitive format that silently fails when malformed.

name: responsive-iframe-generator

example_prompt: Make a responsive 16:9 iframe embed for this map URL
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — templates the wrapper markup and aspect-ratio CSS, client-side.
rationale: Fluid iframes need a wrapper/padding trick that people repeatedly look up.

name: youtube-embed-builder
description: Builds a privacy-enhanced YouTube embed snippet (youtube-nocookie, lazy loading, start time, params) from a video URL.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the video ID and templates an iframe with chosen params; no API call.
rationale: Default YouTube embeds set cookies and load eagerly; a builder produces the privacy/perf-tuned version.

name: route-match
description: Tests a request path against route patterns (e.g. /users/{id}/posts/{slug}) and reports which matches plus the extracted path parameters.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — actix-web-style pattern compilation and matching is pure string work in the sandbox.
rationale: Debug API routing and parameter extraction offline before deploying.

name: thai-romanizer

example_prompt: Romanize ภูเก็ต into English letters
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: rule-based grapheme-to-Latin mapping with no model or API needed
rationale: Lets non-Thai readers pronounce names and places, a constant need for travel, contacts, and search.

name: vietnamese-telex-converter
description: Converts Telex/VNI keystroke sequences (e.g. 'Vieejt Nam') into proper Unicode Vietnamese.
example_prompt: Convert this Telex typing to real Vietnamese: tieesng Vieejt
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: rule-based input-method transformation, no model required
rationale: Lets people on any keyboard produce correct Vietnamese without installing an input method.

name: recfile-to-json

example_prompt: Convert this .rec file into a JSON array
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line-oriented parser; the rec format is plain text, fully client-side.
rationale: Unlocks the niche-but-loyal GNU Recutils format for users who want it in mainstream tooling.

name: column-block-editor

example_prompt: Add `// ` to the start of every line and align these assignments on the `=`.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; pure text-grid manipulation runs entirely in-browser.
rationale: Multi-cursor/column editing (Amp, ox, aretext) is what people reach modal editors for, and it works great as a one-shot batch transform.

name: structural-regex
description: Applies sam/vis-style structural regular expressions (x/y/g/v commands) to transform text.
example_prompt: Use structural regex to wrap every quoted string in this text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM implements the structural-regex engine locally.
rationale: A uniquely powerful text transform from the vis editor that has no web equivalent.

name: compression-ratio-comparator
description: Compresses an uploaded file with gzip, deflate, and brotli and reports each output size and ratio so you can pick the best codec.
example_prompt: Which compression gives the smallest size for this log file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — miniz_oxide and the pure-Rust brotli crate compress the in-memory buffer with no native deps
rationale: Picking a codec for an asset usually means guessing; measuring actual ratios locally settles it instantly.

name: archive-symlink-auditor
description: Scans an uploaded zip/tar for dangerous entries — symlinks pointing outside the archive, absolute paths, and ../ traversal (zip-slip).
example_prompt: is it safe to extract this zip? check for any path-traversal or symlink tricks
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM inspects entry names and symlink targets in the archive metadata; pure parsing, no extraction or FS access.
rationale: Reinterprets the symlinks demand as a real security check, catching the zip-slip/tar-symlink attacks that bite people who extract untrusted archives.

name: duplicate-name-resolver
description: Detects colliding filenames (including case-insensitive collisions) in a list and appends (1)/(2) suffixes to make them unique.
example_prompt: Find duplicate filenames in this list and de-duplicate them
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM set logic on pasted names; runs locally
rationale: Name collisions break every batch move/rename, and resolving them deterministically is a quick local win.

name: tax-bracket-calculator
description: Computes marginal and effective income tax from user-supplied bracket thresholds and rates.
example_prompt: With these brackets, what's the tax on $85,000 and my effective rate?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: piecewise bracket arithmetic on entered numbers, no external tax service.
rationale: paycon/wfh demand shows interest in pay-after-tax reasoning; user-supplied brackets keep it accurate and offline.

name: git-blob-hash

example_prompt: What git blob hash would this file have?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM does the object framing and SHA-1 locally on the supplied bytes — no checkout required.
rationale: Lets developers verify object identity or locate an object without a repo, a small but frequently-wanted lookup.

name: git-error-explainer
description: Explains a pasted git error message and suggests the exact commands to recover from it.
example_prompt: What does this git error mean and how do I fix it?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM matches the message against a curated error→explanation→fix table bundled in the WASM, all offline.
rationale: Decoding cryptic git errors is one of the most common developer questions and works on just the pasted message.

name: svg-layer-split
description: Extracts named layers/groups from a layered SVG and exports each as a standalone SVG or sequential animation frame.
example_prompt: Split this layered SVG into separate files per layer
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM walks the SVG group/Inkscape-layer tree and emits per-layer documents in the browser.
rationale: inklayers demand reflects a real need to decompose layered SVGs for animation or asset pipelines without proprietary tools.

name: escape-sequence-expander
description: Expands or escapes backslash sequences (\n, \t, \xNN, \uNNNN, ANSI codes) the way echo -e and printf do.
example_prompt: expand this echo -e string: "line1\tcol\nline2"
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — character-level escape processing of input text, fully local.
rationale: Maps echo to the genuinely useful escape/unescape conversion people repeatedly hand-decode.

name: gost-streebog-hash
description: Computes the GOST R 34.11-2012 Streebog cryptographic hash (256-bit and 512-bit) of text or hex input.
example_prompt: Give me the Streebog-256 hash of 'hello world'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the RustCrypto `streebog` crate — pure hashing, no I/O, runs entirely in the browser runtime.
rationale: Streebog is the GOST digest used for signatures and integrity checks and has no convenient browser-local implementation.

name: citrix-ctx1-cipher
description: Encodes and decodes Citrix CTX1 obfuscated passwords as found in legacy ICA/connection files.
example_prompt: Decode this Citrix CTX1 password: NBA2EOLEEDGBEK
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the fixed XOR/transform scheme is pure byte math with no dependencies.
rationale: A specific, recurring admin/forensics need with steady search demand and almost no maintained tooling.

name: sm3-hash
description: Computes the SM3 (GM/T 0004) 256-bit cryptographic hash of arbitrary text or hex/base64 input.
example_prompt: Compute the SM3 hash of 'hello world'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via RustCrypto `sm3`; streaming hash over CPU only, no I/O, runs in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: SM3 underpins SM2's KDF/ZA and is mandated alongside it in ShangMi stacks, so a standalone digest tool rounds out the suite and has independent demand.

name: take-nth-bytes
description: Keeps every Nth byte of the input (with optional start offset), useful for de-interleaving data.
example_prompt: take every 2nd byte from this hex string
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; deterministic stride extraction, no external calls.
rationale: De-interleaving byte streams is a recurring reverse-engineering and forensics task.

name: drop-nth-bytes
description: Removes every Nth byte of the input (with optional start offset), the complement of take-nth-bytes.
example_prompt: drop every 3rd byte from this data
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; pure stride filtering, runs entirely in the browser.
rationale: Pairs with take-nth-bytes to manipulate interleaved or padded binary streams.

name: lrc-timing-shifter
description: Offsets every timestamp in an LRC lyric file by a number of milliseconds to re-sync it.
example_prompt: Shift this LRC file 500ms earlier
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM arithmetic over the parsed timestamps; fully local.
rationale: Synced lyrics are almost always slightly off and a one-shot offset is the standard fix.

name: jsonml-to-html
description: Converts between JsonML array-encoded markup and HTML/XML.
example_prompt: Convert this JsonML to HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — recursive walk of the JsonML arrays emitting markup via quick-xml, all local.
rationale: JsonML lets JSON pipelines carry markup, and round-tripping to real HTML/XML is the practical step users need.

name: jsonld-to-table
description: Expands inline-context JSON-LD and flattens entities into a readable property/value table.
example_prompt: Show the fields in this JSON-LD as a table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — applies embedded @context locally (no remote context fetch) and flattens entities.
rationale: JSON-LD's nesting and context aliases obscure the actual data; a flattened table makes schema.org records human-readable.

name: fractured-json
description: Formats JSON in 'fractured' style — small arrays/objects kept inline and column-aligned while large ones expand — for human-readable diffs.
example_prompt: format this JSON the compact fractured way so it's easy to scan
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM custom pretty-printer implementing the FracturedJson algorithm; pure string output.
rationale: FracturedJson is a distinctive, well-loved formatting style that standard pretty-printers can't produce.

name: defiantjs-xpath
description: Queries JSON using XPath by internally converting it to XML (DefiantJS approach).
example_prompt: Run XPath '//book[price<10]/title' against this JSON using DefiantJS-style search.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: JSON→XML shim plus the sxd-xpath engine, evaluated in-sandbox.
rationale: XPath veterans get a familiar query surface over JSON without leaving the browser.

name: json-to-scss-map
description: Converts a JSON object into an SCSS map or variable set for use in stylesheets (SassyJSON).
example_prompt: Convert this JSON of breakpoints into an SCSS map.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string-builds SCSS syntax from the parsed value, no network.
rationale: Designers share tokens as JSON but need them as Sass maps, a clean one-way text transform.

name: orderly-to-json-schema
description: Compiles an Orderly schema DSL definition into standard JSON Schema.
example_prompt: Compile this Orderly schema into JSON Schema
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a small Orderly-syntax parser emits JSON Schema, no toolchain server
rationale: Directly serves the Orderly JSON demand term, which has no maintained browser-local compiler.

name: ron-formatter
description: Formats and validates RON (Rusty Object Notation) documents, reporting parse errors.
example_prompt: Format and validate this RON file.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (ron crate) parses and re-emits RON in-browser.
rationale: Bevy and Rust asset authors need quick RON validation without a build step.

name: storage-uri-parser
description: Parses cloud storage URIs (s3://, gs://, azblob://) into bucket/key/region and converts between provider forms.
example_prompt: Parse s3://my-bucket/logs/2026/app.log and show me the gs:// and https equivalents
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; pure URI string parsing, no network calls to the storage backends.
rationale: Devs juggling multiple object stores need to decode and translate storage URIs without hitting any API.

name: gdscript-linter
description: Lints GDScript and reports style, naming, and design warnings using gdtoolkit's gdlint ruleset.
example_prompt: Lint this GDScript and tell me what's wrong with it.
loader_feasibility: pyodide — gdlint is the same pure-Python gdtoolkit package, runnable entirely client-side in Pyodide.
rationale: Godot devs want quick style/lint feedback without wiring up a Python toolchain, and a paste-and-check tool delivers that instantly.

name: hurl-to-curl-converter
description: Converts the requests in a Hurl (.hurl) file into equivalent curl commands.
example_prompt: Convert this .hurl file's requests into curl commands.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Hurl syntax parsing and curl string generation over text, fully local.
rationale: Hurl is popular for HTTP testing and devs often need the curl equivalent to share or debug a single call.

name: authenticode-inspector
description: Extracts the Authenticode signature from a PE binary, shows the signer certificate chain and digest algorithm, and verifies the embedded hash matches the computed file hash.
example_prompt: Is this installer signed? Show me who signed it and whether the hash checks out
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the PKCS#7 SignedData in the cert table and recomputes the Authenticode SHA-256 locally; all crypto runs client-side.
rationale: Directly maps the pe-sign demand into a useful integrity check for verifying downloaded executables without trusting a remote service.

name: cargo-lock-deps
description: Lists every resolved dependency and version from a Cargo.lock file.
example_prompt: List all dependencies and versions from this Cargo.lock
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Cargo.lock is TOML, parsed locally with the toml crate.
rationale: Auditing the full locked dependency set is a frequent registry/security chore for Rust teams.

name: rust-bounds-check-analyzer
description: Flags indexing patterns in a Rust snippet that incur runtime bounds checks and rewrites them into iterator/slice idioms that elide the checks without unsafe.
example_prompt: Find the bounds checks in this loop and show me how to remove them safely.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: syn AST scan for index expressions plus rewrite suggestions, no compiler needed.
rationale: Directly serves the niche-but-specific 'How to avoid bounds checks in Rust (without unsafe!)' demand.

name: rust-type-diagram
description: Parses Rust structs, enums, and trait impls and emits a Mermaid class diagram of the type relationships.
example_prompt: Draw a diagram of the structs and enums in this Rust module.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: syn parses the items and generates Mermaid text rendered client-side.
rationale: Helps 'rust-learning' users visualize how types relate without any external diagramming tool.

name: rust-cargo-toml-doctor
description: Parses a Cargo.toml and explains/validates its dependencies, features, edition, and lint sections, flagging common mistakes.
example_prompt: Review my Cargo.toml and explain what each dependency and feature does.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the pure-Rust toml crate parses and validates locally, no registry calls.
rationale: Demystifies project setup for the 'rust-how-do-i-start' audience without needing cargo installed.

name: rust-docs-translator

loader_feasibility: transformers-js: an in-browser translation model (e.g. opus-mt/m2m100) runs client-side with no API.
rationale: Directly serves 'Rust Tiếng Việt' and the broader non-English Rust audience locally and privately.

name: journal-recap-summarizer
description: Summarizes a batch of dated journal entries into a weekly or monthly recap.
example_prompt: Summarize my journal entries from this week into a recap
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — a summarization model runs in-browser, entries stay local
rationale: pdiary/Diary users want periodic reflection without re-reading every entry.

name: lotus-123-to-csv
description: Opens legacy Lotus 1-2-3 .wk1/.wks/.wk3 files and exports their cells as CSV.
example_prompt: Read this old Lotus .wk1 file and give me a CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a custom parser for the documented WK binary record format runs entirely client-side.
rationale: Directly answers the 'Lotus 1-2-3 for Linux' demand for recovering decades-old data no modern app reads.

name: changelog-summarizer
description: Summarizes long release notes or a CHANGELOG into the handful of breaking changes and notable fixes that matter before upgrading.
example_prompt: Summarize the breaking changes in these release notes [pastes changelog]
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — runs a summarization model fully in-browser on pasted changelog text.
rationale: Deciding whether to take an upgrade (the human side of topgrade/mise) means reading dense changelogs that a local model can distill.

name: ps-table-formatter
description: Reformats raw `ps aux`/`ps -ef` output into a clean, sortable, colorized table with optional tree view, like procs.
example_prompt: Format this ps aux dump sorted by memory and group child processes under their parents
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure text-in/text-out reformatting of pasted process listings, fully client-side.
rationale: procs is popular precisely because raw ps output is hard to read; the formatting value travels even without live process access.

name: gpu-status-parser
description: Parses nvidia-smi, rocm-smi, intel_gpu_top, or tegrastats output into a unified table of GPU utilization, VRAM, temperature, power, and per-process usage.
example_prompt: Parse this nvidia-smi output and tell me which process is holding the most VRAM
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses pasted vendor tool text into a normalized structure, no driver or hardware access required.
rationale: nvtop/nvitop/radeontop/gputop/tegratop users all stare at vendor dumps that are inconsistent and noisy; a unified parser is useful across all GPU vendors.

name: io-stats-parser
description: Parses iostat or iotop output into per-device and per-process throughput, %util, and await latency, flagging I/O bottlenecks.
example_prompt: Read this iostat -x output and tell me which disk is saturated
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tabular parsing and threshold analysis of pasted text, no syscalls needed.
rationale: iotop/iostat output is dense and column-heavy, and spotting the saturated device is exactly the analysis users want help with.

name: nmon-analyzer
description: Parses an uploaded nmon capture file into time-series charts and summaries for CPU, memory, disk, and network as inline SVG.
example_prompt: Upload: server.nmon — chart the CPU and disk usage over the capture window
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — reads the nmon CSV-style file and emits SVG charts as text output, fully offline.
rationale: nmon files are routinely collected on Linux/AIX servers but the official analyzers are clunky spreadsheets, so a browser charting tool is a real upgrade.

name: pprof-parser
description: Parses `go tool pprof -top` or pprof text output into a ranked function table by flat and cumulative cost with percentages.
example_prompt: Here's my pprof top output, which functions are the real hot spots?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the pprof text report and ranks entries, fully client-side.
rationale: pproftui exists because raw pprof output is hard to triage, and ranking the true hot spots is useful without any live profiling session.

name: perf-stat-parser
description: Parses `perf stat` output into IPC, cache-miss rate, branch-misprediction rate, and frontend/backend stalls with plain-language interpretation.
example_prompt: Explain this perf stat output, is my code memory-bound or compute-bound?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses counters and derives ratios from pasted text, no perf or kernel access needed.
rationale: perf stat numbers are meaningless to most developers until turned into IPC and miss-rate intuition, which is a pure calculation on the pasted figures.

name: strace-summarizer
description: Summarizes raw strace output into a syscall count and time histogram like `strace -c`, flagging the slowest and most error-prone calls.
example_prompt: Summarize this strace log and tell me where the time is going
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — aggregates pasted strace lines into per-syscall stats, fully offline.
rationale: Developers often capture strace without `-c` and then need the aggregate view, which is a deterministic reduction of the log text.

name: asciinema-cast-to-svg
description: Converts an asciinema v2 .cast recording into a self-contained, animated SVG terminal playback.
example_prompt: Turn this asciinema cast into an animated SVG I can embed in my README
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a .cast is line-delimited JSON; parse it and emit an SVG with CSS/SMIL frame animation — pure text generation, no rendering backend.
rationale: Lightweight, embeddable terminal demos for docs (the termtosvg use case) with zero external dependency.

name: dmesg-colorizer
description: Parses kernel dmesg/ring-buffer output, colorizes by severity, and converts monotonic timestamps to wall-clock time.
example_prompt: Colorize this dmesg dump and convert the [12345.678] timestamps to real times given boot at 09:00
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — line parsing, severity tagging, and time arithmetic are pure text processing.
rationale: kmon demand is about making kernel logs readable; turning cryptic dmesg into a colorized, time-resolved view is a frequent triage need.

name: otel-trace-waterfall
description: Renders an OTLP JSON trace export as a span waterfall with durations and parent/child nesting.
example_prompt: Show this OTLP trace export as a waterfall and tell me the slowest span
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses OTLP JSON and lays out an SVG/text timeline, no collector needed.
rationale: otel-tui demand is about reading traces interactively; a browser waterfall visualizes a single exported trace without standing up an observability stack.

name: sysctl-conf-explainer
description: Parses a sysctl.conf and explains what each kernel parameter does, its default, and whether the value is risky.
example_prompt: Explain what each setting in my sysctl.conf does
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: line parsing against a bundled kernel-parameter knowledge base, fully offline.
rationale: Copy-pasted sysctl tuning snippets are applied without understanding, and systeroid-style demand shows people want them demystified.

name: ufw-rule-generator
description: Turns a plain-language firewall intent into the exact sequence of ufw commands, with comments.
example_prompt: Give me ufw commands to allow SSH from 10.0.0.0/24 and HTTPS from anywhere, deny everything else
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: it maps intent to ufw command strings locally; nothing touches a real firewall.
rationale: ufw is meant to be simple but users still misorder allow/deny rules and lock themselves out; tufw demand confirms the pain.

name: task-tree-rollup
description: Parses an indented task outline into a tree and rolls up completion status and counts from children to parents.
example_prompt: From this nested task outline, tell me which parent tasks are fully done
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — indentation parsing and recursive aggregation.
rationale: Reproduces grit's tree-of-tasks model and answers the question hierarchical task tools make hard to see.

name: todotxt-stats
description: Summarizes a todo.txt list: counts by project, context and priority, plus open/done and overdue totals.
example_prompt: Give me a breakdown of my todo.txt by project and how many are overdue
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — aggregation over parsed lines, no network.
rationale: A dashboard/summary view is what TUI managers like Ultralist add on top of the file, and it's a quick local win.

name: task-dependency-graph
description: Builds a Mermaid dependency graph from tasks using id:/dep:/blocks: tags (as in topydo) to show blockers and ordering.
example_prompt: Draw the dependency graph for these topydo tasks with dep: tags
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — graph assembly and Mermaid text emission, fully offline.
rationale: topydo and Yokadi support task dependencies but cannot visualize them; this fills that gap locally.

name: wasm-to-wat
description: Disassembles a binary .wasm module into readable WebAssembly text (WAT).
example_prompt: Disassemble this .wasm file so I can read the instructions.
