loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using wasmparser/wabt-style decoding; byte-level parsing with no server.
rationale: Inspecting compiled WASM is awkward without tooling, and gizza itself runs WASM so the audience is built-in.

name: eth-signed-message-hash
description: Computes the EIP-191 personal_sign hash and EIP-712 typed-data hash for a given message or struct.
example_prompt: compute the EIP-712 hash for this typed data JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Keccak-256 over the encoded message, offline.
rationale: EIP-191/712 hashing is needed to verify wallet signatures, permits, and Seaport/OpenSea orders without a backend.

name: ss58-address-codec
description: Encodes and decodes Polkadot/Substrate SS58 addresses and re-encodes a public key for any network prefix.
example_prompt: convert this Polkadot address to the Kusama format
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Blake2b checksum + Base58 encoding, offline.
rationale: The same key has different SS58 addresses per Substrate chain, so conversion and validation are constant needs.

name: eth-deposit-data-decode
description: Decodes a beacon-chain deposit_data record (pubkey, withdrawal credentials, signature, deposit root) from JSON or hex.
example_prompt: decode this validator deposit_data hex
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — fixed-layout byte parsing, offline.
rationale: Verifying deposit data before sending 32 ETH is a critical, high-stakes check best done locally.

name: multilingual-readability-scorer
description: Scores text readability (Flesch and language-adapted formulas) for Portuguese, Hungarian and English.
example_prompt: how readable is this Portuguese paragraph
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes syllable counts and readability indices locally with per-language coefficients.
rationale: Readability tooling is a common ask in Portuguese-nlp/hungarian-nlp ecosystems and for course-material grading.

name: binaural-spatializer
description: Places a mono sound at a chosen 3D direction (azimuth/elevation) and outputs binaural stereo for headphone 3D audio.
example_prompt: Make this voice sound like it's coming from 45 degrees to my left.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — HRTF convolution against a bundled HRIR set (the sound-field-synthesis idea) is pure DSP, optionally accelerated with webgpu-compute.
rationale: Headphone 3D/spatial audio for games, ASMR, and immersive content is in demand and works perfectly offline once an HRTF set is bundled.

name: tempogram
description: Visualizes how tempo and pulse strength change over the course of a performance.
example_prompt: Make a tempogram of this performance
loader_feasibility: pyodide onset-envelope autocorrelation rendered in-browser.
rationale: Lets musicians study expressive tempo variation (FMP/MIR Notebooks demand).

name: speaker-counter
description: Estimates how many distinct speakers are present in a recording.
example_prompt: How many different people speak in this audio?
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime extracts speaker embeddings per segment and clusters them locally to count speakers.
rationale: A quick speaker count helps triage interviews and calls before committing to full diarization.

name: mesh-decimator
description: Reduces a mesh's triangle count to a target budget while preserving its shape.
example_prompt: Cut this model down to 10k triangles.
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM runs quadric edge-collapse simplification on the parsed mesh entirely in the browser.
rationale: Decimation is the central technique for optimizing scenes for WebGL performance and a frequent asset-prep need.

name: spirv-to-wgsl
description: Decompiles a SPIR-V binary back into readable WGSL source.
example_prompt: Turn this SPIR-V blob into WGSL I can read and edit
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using naga's SPIR-V frontend and WGSL backend; SPIR-V parsing is pure Rust so it runs entirely browser-local.
rationale: Devs often only have a precompiled SPIR-V asset and need editable WGSL to integrate it into a WebGPU project.

name: mipmap-generator
description: Generates a full mipmap chain for a texture and returns the levels as a stacked image or zip.
example_prompt: Generate the mipmap chain for this texture
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg or webgpu-compute downsamples each level in-browser; pure client-side image work.
rationale: Precomputing mipmaps (especially for compressed/NPOT textures) is a common WebGL asset-pipeline step with no easy browser tool.

name: stereoscopic-pair-maker
description: Generates a side-by-side stereoscopic image pair from a photo plus a depth map for VR viewers.
example_prompt: Make a side-by-side VR stereo pair from this photo and depth map
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute (or plain Rust→WASM) applies a depth-based horizontal parallax shift per eye in-browser.
rationale: WebVR/headset viewers consume side-by-side stereo and converting flat images with a depth map is a niche with no easy tool.

name: vertex-buffer-interleaver
description: Interleaves separate position/normal/UV arrays into one VBO with correct stride and byte offsets.
example_prompt: Interleave these position and uv arrays into a single buffer
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM array packing
rationale: Interleaving and computing strides routinely trips up WebGL learners configuring attributes.

name: chrome-trace-analyzer
description: Parses a Chrome/Web-Tracing-Framework trace JSON and reports frame times, long tasks, and jank.
example_prompt: Analyze this performance trace and tell me where the frame drops are
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON parser; CPU analysis only
rationale: Serves the Web-Tracing-Framework and devtools-profiling demand by turning trace dumps into a readable timing report.

name: look-at-matrix
description: Computes a lookAt view matrix from eye, target, and up vectors.
example_prompt: lookAt view matrix for eye (0,0,5), target (0,0,0), up (0,1,0)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM vector math; pure numeric.
rationale: Camera setup is required in every WebGL 2 scene and a correct lookAt is a frequent source of bugs.

name: normal-matrix
description: Derives the 3x3 normal matrix (inverse-transpose of the upper-left model matrix) for correct lighting under non-uniform scale.
example_prompt: Compute the normal matrix for this model matrix: <16 floats>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM matrix inverse/transpose; pure numeric.
rationale: Lighting breaks under scaling without the normal matrix, and most tutorials gloss over computing it.

name: convex-decompose
description: Decomposes a concave 2D polygon into convex pieces for p2.js/Planck.js physics colliders.
example_prompt: Break this concave shape into convex parts for a Planck.js body: <points>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM Bayazit/Hertel-Mehlhorn decomposition; pure CPU geometry.
rationale: 2D physics engines require convex colliders, and decomposing hand-drawn shapes is a known pain point for p2/Planck users.

name: kpi-card
description: Generates a polished SVG KPI/stat card with a headline number, delta vs prior, and a sparkline.
example_prompt: Make a KPI card: Revenue $1.2M, up 8% vs last month, with this trend
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM composes the number, delta, and sparkline into one SVG in-sandbox.
rationale: Captures the vida/Slemma dashboard-tile demand as a shareable single-stat infographic.

name: trip-stats
description: Summarizes trip/event records into distributions of duration, distance, and speed, with by-hour breakdowns.
example_prompt: Summarize trip durations and speeds in this taxi dataset by hour of day.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM aggregation over parsed rows; no server.
rationale: Mobility-data summarization directly answers the NYC Taxi Visualization demand term.

name: hxl-tag-validator
description: Validates the Humanitarian Exchange Language (HXL) hashtag row in a CSV against the HXL standard.
example_prompt: Check the HXL tags in this humanitarian dataset
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing of the tag row against an embedded HXL attribute list, client-side.
rationale: The Humanitarian Data Exchange requires valid HXL tags and contributors must verify them before upload.

name: waterfall-chart
description: Render a financial waterfall chart showing cumulative increases and decreases.
example_prompt: Make a waterfall chart of revenue minus each cost category
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM SVG/raster plotting; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: Waterfall charts are a finance/analytics standard not in the existing chart set.

name: kana-convert
description: Convert Japanese text between hiragana, katakana, and romaji.
example_prompt: Turn コンピューター into romaji
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM with a small kana mapping table; pure compute.
rationale: Common, deterministic Japanese-learner utility not covered by transliterate.

name: dockerfile-parser
description: Parses a Dockerfile into an ordered table of instructions, build stages, base images, exposed ports, and ARGs.
example_prompt: Parse this Dockerfile and list its stages and base images
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizing the Dockerfile grammar (line continuations, here-docs); local text work
rationale: Auditing or summarizing a Dockerfile's stages and bases is a common review and security task.

name: nginx-config-parser
description: Parses an nginx configuration into a nested directive tree of http/server/location blocks with their settings.
example_prompt: Parse this nginx config and show all the server blocks and their listen/root directives
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM recursive-descent parsing of the brace-block grammar; pure text
rationale: Understanding a sprawling nginx config's structure is a frequent ops need with no good lightweight viewer.

name: link-header-parser
description: Parses an HTTP Link header into structured entries (URL, rel, and parameters) for pagination and preload hints.
example_prompt: Parse this Link header into its rel relationships
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM bracket and parameter parser.
rationale: API pagination and resource-hint debugging.

name: word-frequency-compare
description: Compares the word-frequency distributions of two texts and reports the terms that rose, fell, or are unique to each.
example_prompt: Compare the vocabulary of these two articles and tell me which words each emphasizes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — build frequency maps and compute per-term deltas in-memory
rationale: Contrasting term frequencies reveals topical and stylistic differences between documents.

name: translation-pair-diff
description: Compares two translations of the same source text and highlights where they diverge in wording or meaning.
example_prompt: Compare these two translations of the same paragraph and show where they differ
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — sentence embeddings score divergence in-browser, no API needed
rationale: Reviewers and translators need to spot disagreements between alternative translations offline.

name: image-blink-comparator
description: Builds an animated GIF that rapidly alternates between two aligned images so changes 'pop' the way astronomers spot moving objects.
example_prompt: Make a blinking GIF that flips between these two images
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM encodes a 2-frame looping GIF with the image crate, fully local
rationale: Blink comparison is the most sensitive human method for spotting small changes.

name: image-similarity-matrix
description: Computes a pairwise visual-similarity matrix across a set of images and renders it as a labeled grid/heatmap.
example_prompt: Show how similar each of these images is to the others
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM hashes/feature-vectors each image and tabulates distances client-side
rationale: A similarity matrix surfaces clusters and outliers in a set at a glance.

name: image-filesize-efficiency-compare
description: Compares two encodings of the same picture by bytes, bytes-per-pixel, and quality metric to show which is the better trade-off.
example_prompt: Which of these two compressed versions is the better size/quality trade-off?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM measures byte sizes and computes SSIM/PSNR locally to weigh them
rationale: Picking the right compression setting needs size and quality compared together, not separately.

name: image-format-roundtrip-diff
description: Re-encodes an image to a chosen format/quality and diffs it against the original to visualize and quantify the loss introduced.
example_prompt: Show me what I'd lose by saving this PNG as quality-70 JPEG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (or ffmpeg) re-encodes then diffs against the source entirely in-browser
rationale: Lets people preview compression damage before committing to a lossy save.

name: image-noise-diff
description: Compares the noise/grain levels of two images and reports which is noisier and where, after removing structural content.
example_prompt: Which of these two photos has more sensor noise?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM estimates per-region noise variance on both and compares client-side
rationale: Quantifies denoiser effectiveness or ISO differences objectively.

name: image-edge-diff
description: Extracts edge maps from two images and diffs them to show structural outline changes while ignoring color/lighting.
example_prompt: Compare just the outlines/edges of these two images
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs Sobel/Canny on both and diffs the edge images in-browser
rationale: Edge-only diffing isolates shape changes from tonal noise for structural review.

name: video-onion-skin-compare
description: Overlays two videos at adjustable opacity so shifts in framing, motion, or color are visible as ghosting.
example_prompt: Overlay the two takes at 50% opacity so I can see how the camera moved
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg blend=average / opacity overlay composites both decoded streams in-browser.
rationale: Onion-skinning is the standard way to spot alignment and motion drift between versions.

name: video-spec-diff
description: Compares two videos' core specs (resolution, fps, codec, profile, pixel format, bitrate) in a side-by-side table.
example_prompt: Tabulate the spec differences between fileA and fileB
loader_feasibility: ffprobe reads both streams' parameters in the wasm build and Rust→WASM renders the comparison table.
rationale: A spec table instantly explains why two visually-similar files behave differently.

name: video-duration-diff
description: Compares two videos' exact durations and reports the drift in frames and milliseconds.
example_prompt: How much shorter is the edited cut than the original?
loader_feasibility: ffprobe duration/timebase from both files in wasm ffmpeg, differenced in Rust→WASM locally.
rationale: Sub-frame duration drift after re-encoding causes sync issues this catches early.

name: video-fps-compare
description: Compares two videos' frame rates and CFR/VFR character, flagging conversions that may cause judder.
example_prompt: Did the frame rate change between these two versions?
loader_feasibility: ffprobe frame-timing analysis on both files runs in the wasm ffmpeg build and Rust→WASM diffs the results.
rationale: Frame-rate or CFR/VFR shifts between versions are a common cause of playback judder.

name: video-gop-structure-compare
description: Compares the GOP size and I/P/B frame patterns of two videos to reveal encoder configuration differences.
example_prompt: Show how the GOP structure differs between these two encodes
loader_feasibility: ffprobe frame-type extraction for both files runs in wasm and Rust→WASM summarizes the GOP patterns.
rationale: GOP-structure differences explain seek behavior and size gaps between otherwise-equal encodes.

name: chroma-cover-match
description: Cross-correlates the chroma sequences of two recordings to detect whether one is a cover/alternate version of the other despite key or tempo shifts.
example_prompt: Is this a cover of the other track I uploaded?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: chromagram + transposition-invariant cross-correlation, no server
rationale: Harmonic-progression matching for cover detection is a niche but genuinely useful client-side capability.

name: stereo-phase-correlation-compare
description: Computes the stereo phase-correlation coefficient and width for two mixes and reports which is more mono-compatible.
example_prompt: Which of these two mixes will collapse worse in mono?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: mid/side and L/R correlation math on PCM, no server
rationale: Mono-compatibility regressions between mix versions are easy to miss and cheap to compute objectively.

name: tempo-curve-compare
description: Beat-tracks two performances and compares their tempo-over-time curves to reveal rushing, dragging, or click-vs-human drift.
example_prompt: Did the second take drag the tempo compared to the first?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: onset-envelope beat tracking on both signals, tempo-curve diff, local
rationale: Comparing groove/tempo stability between takes is valuable for editing and has no browser tool.

name: transcode-cutoff-compare
description: Detects the high-frequency lowpass cutoff of two files and compares them to expose upsampled or re-encoded fakes.
example_prompt: Is the 'lossless' file actually a transcode of the lossy one?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: averaged FFT spectrum + cutoff detection on both files, local
rationale: Spotting fake-lossless/transcoded uploads by spectral ceiling is a popular audiophile QA check.

name: mid-side-balance-diff
description: Compares the mid/side energy balance and stereo width of two mixes across the frequency range.
example_prompt: Is the new mix wider than the old one, and where?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: M/S decomposition + banded energy on both files, no server
rationale: Stereo-width regressions between mix revisions are easy to overlook and cheap to quantify.

name: loudness-range-compare
description: Computes EBU R128 loudness range (LRA) for two files and compares how much dynamic spread each retains.
example_prompt: Compare the loudness range of these two versions
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: gated short-term loudness distribution + LRA percentiles on both, no server
rationale: LRA is the broadcast-standard dynamics metric; comparing two deliverables is a real compliance task.

name: resample-artifact-compare
description: Compares two sample-rate-converted versions of a source for aliasing and imaging artifacts above/below Nyquist.
example_prompt: Which resampler gave fewer aliasing artifacts on this file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: high-frequency spectral analysis of both outputs, artifact-energy scoring, local
rationale: Comparing SRC quality between two converters is an audiophile/engineering need that's purely spectral.

name: phase-coherence-diff
description: Computes inter-channel phase coherence across frequency for two stereo files and diffs them to expose phase problems introduced by processing.
example_prompt: Did the new processing chain introduce phase issues vs the old one?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: cross-spectral coherence per band on both files, difference curve, local
rationale: Frequency-dependent phase regressions are subtle and need a per-band comparison to catch.

name: duplicate-frame-checker
description: Detects identical or near-identical consecutive frames in an animated image that waste file size and could be merged with longer delays.
example_prompt: Are there redundant duplicate frames in this GIF I could drop?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader decodes frames locally and the tool hashes/diffs adjacent frames in WASM memory.
rationale: Redundant frames bloat animation file size and are invisible without frame-by-frame inspection.

name: edge-bleed-checker
description: Flags when the main subject's non-background content runs into the image edges, signaling a crop that may clip important detail.
example_prompt: Is my subject getting cut off at the edges of this photo?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM analyzes edge-pixel activity versus interior content locally.
rationale: Edge-bleeding crops look unprofessional and break safe-area requirements for thumbnails and prints.

name: video-ftyp-brand-checker
description: Reads the MP4 ftyp box and reports the major brand and compatible brands, flagging missing or incompatible brand sets.
example_prompt: What ftyp brands does this MP4 declare?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses the ftyp box bytes in the browser without decoding the media.
rationale: Wrong or missing brand declarations cause some players and devices to reject otherwise-valid MP4s.

name: video-fragmented-mp4-checker
description: Verifies fragmented-MP4 structure (moof/mfra/sidx presence and ordering) and flags malformed fMP4 used for streaming.
example_prompt: Is this a valid fragmented MP4 for DASH streaming?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM walks the box tree in the browser to validate fragment layout without a server.
rationale: fMP4 streaming requires specific fragment structure that a plain box-validator can't confirm without fMP4-aware checks.

name: video-mp4-free-atom-checker
description: Reports the size of free/skip/wide padding atoms in an MP4 and flags bloated unused space that wastes bytes.
example_prompt: How much wasted free-atom padding is in this MP4?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM sums free/skip atom sizes from the box tree in the browser.
rationale: Leftover padding atoms bloat files needlessly, and surfacing them lets users reclaim space before publishing.

name: video-edit-list-warning-checker
description: Inspects the MP4 edit list (elst) for non-trivial entries that cause A/V offset or trimming surprises in some players.
example_prompt: Does this MP4 have a tricky edit list that could throw off sync?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses elst entries in the browser and evaluates them against safe defaults.
rationale: Edit lists are honored inconsistently across players, so warning on non-trivial ones prevents sync bugs.

name: video-bitrate-cap-checker
description: Measures average and peak bitrate over a sliding window and flags any segment exceeding a configured cap.
example_prompt: Does this video ever spike above 8 Mbps?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader reads packet sizes/timestamps via ffprobe in WASM and computes windowed bitrate locally.
rationale: Platform and device specs impose hard bitrate ceilings that a peak-window check enforces before upload.

name: video-chapter-timestamp-validator
description: Validates embedded chapter markers are time-ordered, within the file duration, and non-overlapping.
example_prompt: Are the chapter markers in this file valid and in order?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader reads chapter metadata via ffprobe in WASM and checks ordering/bounds locally.
rationale: Malformed chapter timestamps break navigation in players, so validating them protects the viewer experience.

name: haproxy-config-parser
description: Parses an HAProxy haproxy.cfg into structured global/defaults/frontend/backend/listen sections with their options.
example_prompt: Parse this haproxy.cfg and list the frontends and the backends they route to.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; section-and-keyword text parsing, runs in-browser.
rationale: Mapping frontends to backends from a flat config is error-prone by eye; structured output clarifies routing.

name: resolv-conf-parser
description: Parses /etc/resolv.conf into nameservers, search domains, and options (ndots, timeout, attempts).
example_prompt: Parse this resolv.conf and show the nameservers and the ndots option.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; small keyword-line grammar parsed in-browser.
rationale: DNS resolution quirks (especially ndots) hide in resolv.conf; a structured read makes them obvious.

name: mailto-link-parser
description: Parses a mailto: URI into to/cc/bcc/subject/body fields, URL-decoding each, for inspection or editing.
example_prompt: Decode this mailto: link and show me the subject and body it pre-fills.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; splits the mailto target and query and percent-decodes locally.
rationale: Marketing and support mailto links carry encoded subjects/bodies that are unreadable until decoded.

name: true-peak-compare
description: Oversamples two files to estimate inter-sample (true) peaks and reports which exceeds 0 dBTP and by how much.
example_prompt: Compare the true-peak levels of these two masters for streaming compliance
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM 4× upsamples PCM and finds reconstructed peaks locally.
rationale: True-peak compliance differs from sample peak, and comparing two masters guides which passes streaming specs.

name: onset-density-compare
description: Counts transient onsets per second in two recordings to compare their rhythmic/percussive density.
example_prompt: Which of these two takes is busier rhythmically?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs spectral-flux onset detection on PCM with no server.
rationale: Onset density objectively compares performance energy between alternate takes.

name: duration-mismatch-report
description: Compares the exact sample count and duration of two audio files and reports any length drift down to the sample.
example_prompt: Are these two stems exactly the same length?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads format headers and sample counts directly in-browser.
rationale: Sub-sample length mismatches between stems cause sync drift and are otherwise hard to spot.

name: mono-compatibility-compare
description: Sums a stereo file to mono and compares it against the stereo version to quantify level loss from phase cancellation.
example_prompt: Will this mix survive mono playback? Compare stereo vs mono-summed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM downmixes and measures band-wise energy loss on PCM in-browser.
rationale: Mono-fold cancellation breaks club/phone playback, and a self-comparison surfaces it before release.

name: pitch-cents-compare
description: Detects the fundamental pitch of two single-note recordings and reports the tuning difference in cents.
example_prompt: How many cents apart are these two recorded notes?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs a YIN pitch estimator on decoded PCM locally.
rationale: Comparing intonation in cents is exactly what's needed to match tuning between instruments or takes.

name: feature-flag-diff
description: Compares two feature-flag config snapshots (LaunchDarkly/Flagsmith/Unleash export JSON) and reports flags added, removed, toggled, or with changed targeting rules.
example_prompt: Diff these two flag exports and show which flags changed targeting
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses both flag-export JSON files and diffs by flag key and rule structure locally; no flag service contacted.
rationale: Flag drift between environments causes real incidents and there is no flag-config diff in the catalog.

name: gpx-track-deviation
description: Compares two GPX tracks and reports max/average deviation between the routes.
example_prompt: How far apart are these two GPX tracks?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses GPX XML and computes haversine distances point-to-segment locally; location data never leaves the browser.
rationale: Athletes and hikers compare a planned vs actual route; gpx-merge exists but there's no deviation comparison, and GPS traces are privacy-sensitive.

name: subscription-cost-compare
description: Normalizes two subscription plans to the same billing period and compares effective cost.
example_prompt: Is $99/year or $12/month the better deal?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM does the period normalization math locally; no network required.
rationale: Annual-vs-monthly and tier comparisons are a constant consumer decision that a focused tool answers instantly.

name: image-decode-bomb-checker
description: Flags decompression-bomb images where a tiny file declares enormous dimensions that would exhaust memory on decode.
example_prompt: Is this small image file safe to open or is it a decode bomb?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads only the dimension header and compares declared pixels to file size — no decode, fully local.
rationale: Decompression bombs are a real DoS vector for image pipelines, and a header-only check screens uploads before they ever decode.

name: webp-feature-checker
description: Reports which WebP features a file uses (lossy, lossless, alpha, animation) and flags ones unsupported by a chosen target.
example_prompt: What WebP features does this file use and will old browsers render it?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the RIFF/VP8X chunks — header-only, fully client-side.
rationale: Animated or alpha WebP silently breaks on older clients, and a feature scan tells you whether a fallback is needed.

name: avif-heic-compatibility-checker
description: Detects AVIF and HEIC images that won't render in older browsers and recommends a fallback format.
example_prompt: Will this AVIF image work in browsers, or do I need a fallback?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the ISOBMFF box structure to identify the codec brand — no decode, runs locally.
rationale: Next-gen formats break on a meaningful slice of clients, and a compatibility check prevents shipping images that show as blanks.

name: image-upscale-detector
description: Detects whether an image was interpolated up from a smaller source, lacking true detail at its stated resolution.
example_prompt: Is this image real 4K detail or upscaled from something smaller?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM analyzes high-frequency energy and edge sharpness vs resolution — CPU-only, in-browser.
rationale: Fake-resolution upscales mislead asset buyers and print jobs, and a detector catches them before they're trusted.

name: logo-clearspace-checker
description: Verifies a transparent logo PNG has the brand-required clear-space padding around its visible bounding box.
example_prompt: Does this logo have enough transparent padding around it per the brand guide?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes alpha, computes the content bounding box, and measures margins — fully local.
rationale: Brand guidelines mandate logo clear-space, and an automated check enforces it across asset batches.

name: texture-colorspace-encoding-checker
description: Detects whether a data texture (normal/roughness/metallic) was mistakenly saved sRGB-encoded when it should be linear.
example_prompt: Is this roughness map sRGB-encoded by mistake?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM inspects the embedded color profile and pixel histogram for gamma signatures — fully local.
rationale: sRGB-tagged data maps render with wrong material response, and catching the encoding mistake prevents broken PBR materials.

name: heightmap-range-checker
description: Checks whether a heightmap or depth image uses its full value range, flagging clipped or low-contrast data.
example_prompt: Does this heightmap use the full 16-bit range or is it clipped?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes and computes min/max/histogram of values — trivial local computation.
rationale: Under-ranged heightmaps lose terrain detail, and a range check tells you whether to re-normalize before use.

name: pixel-art-grid-checker
description: Verifies pixel art sits on a clean integer pixel grid with no anti-aliasing or fractional scaling artifacts.
example_prompt: Is this pixel art on a clean grid or was it accidentally resampled?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes and detects sub-pixel edges and color-count inflation — CPU-only, in-browser.
rationale: Resampled pixel art picks up blur and stray colors, and a grid check confirms it's still crisp and properly scaled.

name: print-bleed-checker
description: Given a trim size, verifies a print image extends content into the required bleed margin instead of stopping at the edge.
example_prompt: Does this flyer have the 3mm bleed my printer requires?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes and inspects edge regions against the supplied trim/bleed spec — fully client-side.
rationale: Missing bleed causes white slivers after trimming, and a pre-flight check avoids a costly reprint.

name: favicon-ico-spec-validator
description: Validates an .ico file contains the recommended browser sizes (16/32/48) in proper format and reports any missing ones.
example_prompt: Does my favicon.ico have all the sizes browsers expect?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the ICO directory and per-image headers — no decode, runs locally.
rationale: Incomplete ICO bundles render blurry favicons in some browsers, and a spec check confirms full coverage.

name: image-moire-detector
description: Detects moiré and aliasing interference patterns from rephotographed screens or fine-pattern subjects.
example_prompt: Does this photo of a screen have moiré patterns?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs an FFT and looks for off-axis frequency peaks — CPU-heavy but fully client-side.
rationale: Moiré ruins photos of screens and textiles, and objective detection flags shots that need reshooting or filtering.

name: mp4-required-box-checker
description: Validates that an MP4 contains all mandatory boxes (ftyp, moov, mvhd, at least one trak/mdia/minf/stbl) and flags any that are missing or empty.
example_prompt: Check this mp4 for any missing required atoms.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM traverses the ISO-BMFF box tree and asserts the required-box checklist; purely structural, runs in the browser.
rationale: Tools that emit malformed MP4s often drop required boxes, and an explicit presence check pinpoints why a file won't open.

name: video-chunk-offset-validity-checker
description: Verifies that every stco/co64 chunk offset and sample-table entry points to a valid in-file location and that sample counts are internally consistent.
example_prompt: Check whether this mp4's chunk offsets actually point inside the file.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM cross-validates stbl tables (stco/co64/stsc/stsz) against file length; arithmetic on parsed boxes, fully local.
rationale: Corrupted or rewritten offset tables make players seek into garbage, and this catches the corruption deterministically without playback.

name: video-track-id-collision-checker
description: Flags duplicate or zero track IDs and a next_track_id field that doesn't exceed all existing IDs, which violate the MP4 spec.
example_prompt: Are any track IDs duplicated in this mp4?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads each tkhd track_id plus the mvhd next_track_id and checks uniqueness; trivial structural validation in the browser.
rationale: Muxers that splice tracks sometimes collide IDs, which breaks track selection in strict demuxers and is hard to spot otherwise.

name: video-empty-track-checker
description: Detects tracks declared in the header that contain zero samples (empty stsz/stco), often leftover audio/subtitle stubs.
example_prompt: Does this video have any empty tracks with no actual samples?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM inspects each track's sample tables for zero entries; pure parsing, no decode, client-side.
rationale: Empty tracks show up as selectable-but-silent options in players and bloat metadata; flagging them lets editors strip them.

name: video-orphan-data-stream-checker
description: Identifies data/metadata streams that have no recognized handler or decoder mapping and would be ignored or error in playback.
example_prompt: Are there any orphan data streams in this video that nothing can decode?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm probes stream/handler types and the plain-Rust parser checks hdlr/codec mappings; both run in-browser.
rationale: Orphan streams from screen recorders and DV captures cause spurious decode warnings and confuse downstream tools.

name: video-interleaving-checker
description: Measures how well audio and video samples are interleaved on disk and flags poorly-interleaved files that cause excessive seeking and buffering.
example_prompt: Is the audio and video in this file well interleaved for streaming?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM derives per-sample file offsets from the sample tables and measures the read-distance between A/V samples; client-side computation.
rationale: Badly interleaved files stream poorly and stutter on low-end players, a real problem that no surface-level metadata reveals.

name: video-timestamp-gap-checker
description: Scans packet timestamps for gaps or discontinuities larger than one frame interval, indicating dropped frames or stitched recordings.
example_prompt: Are there any timestamp gaps or dropped frames in this recording?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm reads packet PTS/DTS and the tool diffs consecutive timestamps against the expected interval; demux-only, no upload.
rationale: Capture cards and screen recorders drop frames invisibly, and gap detection turns that into a concrete report.

name: video-sync-sample-table-checker
description: Validates the stss sync-sample (keyframe) table against actual frame types and flags an all-intra-but-no-stss or out-of-range entries.
example_prompt: Does this mp4's keyframe table match its real keyframes?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses stss and cross-checks indices against sample counts, with optional ffmpeg.wasm frame-type confirmation; client-side.
rationale: A wrong or missing sync-sample table makes seeking land on non-keyframes and produces decode artifacts that are otherwise unexplained.

name: video-gop-structure-validator
description: Analyzes GOP length and open-vs-closed GOP structure across the file and flags irregular or open GOPs that hurt seeking and segmentation.
example_prompt: Analyze the GOP structure of this video and tell me if any GOPs are open or irregular.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm exposes frame types and keyframe flags so the tool can reconstruct GOP boundaries and openness; decode-light, runs locally.
rationale: Open and irregular GOPs are a top cause of seek glitches and broken adaptive-streaming segments, invisible without per-frame inspection.

name: video-frame-size-anomaly-checker
description: Flags abnormally large or near-zero encoded frame sizes that indicate encoder glitches, dropped frames, or corruption.
example_prompt: Are there any abnormally sized frames in this video that suggest an encode glitch?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm exposes per-packet sizes and the tool computes statistical outliers against the local distribution; client-side.
rationale: Outlier frame sizes are an early, codec-agnostic signal of encoding faults that frame-by-frame visual review would take far longer to find.

name: video-fake-stereo-checker
description: Detects stereo audio tracks whose left and right channels are identical (true mono encoded as stereo), wasting bitrate.
example_prompt: Is the stereo audio in this video actually just dual-mono?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm decodes the audio and the tool compares L/R channel samples for equality; decode and compare in-browser.
rationale: Dual-mono-as-stereo is common from screen recorders and doubles audio bitrate for no benefit, which this exposes so it can be downmixed.

name: video-timecode-track-checker
description: Detects the presence and validity of an embedded SMPTE timecode track (tmcd) and reports its start timecode and frame rate basis.
example_prompt: Does this video carry an embedded SMPTE timecode track?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the tmcd sample description and timecode media sample; pure box reading, client-side.
rationale: NLE and broadcast workflows depend on embedded timecode, and confirming its presence and start value avoids conform errors downstream.

name: ogg-crc-validator
description: Recomputes the CRC32 checksum of every Ogg page and reports any page whose stored checksum doesn't match.
example_prompt: Check the page checksums in this ogg file for corruption
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses Ogg pages and computes the CRC32 locally with no server.
rationale: Per-page CRC failure is the definitive signal that an Ogg/Opus/Vorbis file was corrupted in transfer.

name: opus-header-validator
description: Validates the OpusHead and OpusTags identification packets for correct magic, version, channel mapping, and pre-skip fields.
example_prompt: Validate the Opus header packets in this file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the first Ogg pages and checks the Opus packet structure locally.
rationale: Malformed OpusHead packets break channel mapping and gapless playback, and the spec rules are easy to check exactly.

name: mp4-audio-box-validator
description: Validates the MP4/M4A box hierarchy for an audio file, checking moov/trak/mdat sizes and required sample-table atoms are present and consistent.
example_prompt: Validate the atom structure of this m4a
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM walks the ISO-BMFF box tree by length prefixes, no decoding needed.
rationale: Missing or mis-sized atoms are a top cause of M4A files that play on one device but not another.

name: wav-smpl-loop-validator
description: Checks a WAV's smpl chunk loop points for in-range, non-overlapping, and correctly-ordered start/end sample positions.
example_prompt: Validate the sampler loop points in this wav
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the smpl chunk and compares loop offsets to the data length locally.
rationale: Out-of-range loop points crash or mis-loop hardware samplers, and this catches them before loading into an instrument.

name: tag-whitespace-linter
description: Lints tag values for leading/trailing spaces, double spaces, stray tabs, and trailing null padding that corrupt sorting and display.
example_prompt: Lint my track tags for stray whitespace
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads tag strings and applies whitespace rules locally.
rationale: Invisible whitespace fragments artist/album grouping in libraries, and a linter surfaces it cleanly.

name: script-async-defer-auditor
description: Audits script tags for render-blocking loading, flagging external scripts missing async or defer and inline scripts placed in head.
example_prompt: Which scripts in this HTML are render-blocking?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML parse and attribute analysis — pure local logic.
rationale: Render-blocking scripts are a leading cause of slow page loads and an auditor pinpoints the offenders.

name: htaccess-rewrite-tester
description: Given .htaccess RewriteRules and a request URL, reports which rule matches and the resulting rewritten URL.
example_prompt: Which RewriteRule matches /blog/2024/post and what does it rewrite to?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM regex-based rule evaluation mirroring mod_rewrite semantics — pure logic.
rationale: RewriteRule behavior is hard to predict and a tester lets you verify redirects without deploying to a server.

name: numeric-range-validator
description: Checks that every value in a list lies within a given [min, max] bound and lists the out-of-range entries.
example_prompt: Are all these between 0 and 100: 12, 99, 105, 47, -3?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: comparison sweep over parsed numbers, fully offline.
rationale: Range linting is a basic but constant data-cleaning need and is trivially exact to compute.

name: saturation-vibrance-meter
description: Measures an image's mean and distribution of saturation to report how muted or vivid it is.
example_prompt: How saturated is this image overall?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM converts pixels to HSV and computes saturation statistics offline.
rationale: Helps grade a photo set for consistency and decide whether a vibrance adjustment is warranted.

name: monochrome-tint-detector
description: Detects whether an image is monochrome with a single-hue tone (sepia, cyanotype, duotone) and reports the tint.
example_prompt: Is this photo sepia-toned, and what tint exactly?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM checks whether hues collapse to one value while luminance varies, all locally.
rationale: Distinguishing a true grayscale from a tinted monochrome matters for restoration and faithful conversion.

name: video-blockiness-detector
description: Scores per-frame compression blocking artifacts and reports the worst-affected timestamps.
example_prompt: Where is my video the most blocky from over-compression?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes frames and a Rust DCT-edge metric scores blockiness fully client-side.
rationale: Blockiness pinpoints where a higher bitrate is needed, turning a vague 'looks bad' into actionable timestamps.

name: audio-sweep-frequency-response-analyzer
description: Derives a frequency-response curve from a recorded sine-sweep (or noise) measurement signal.
example_prompt: Turn this sine-sweep recording into a frequency response curve
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: deconvolve/FFT the sweep response into magnitude-per-frequency and emit CSV/PNG; CPU-only.
rationale: Lets users measure speakers/rooms from a single sweep without lab software.

name: audio-loop-point-finder
description: Finds seamless loop start/end points in ambient or game audio by matching waveform and spectral continuity.
example_prompt: Find good seamless loop points in this ambient pad
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: zero-crossing + cross-correlation similarity search across candidate boundaries; CPU-only.
rationale: Loop-point discovery is tedious by hand and essential for game/ambient sound design.

name: image-text-match-score
description: Scores how well an image matches a text description using CLIP image-text similarity, ranking multiple captions if given.
example_prompt: Does this image match the caption 'a red bicycle by the sea'? Score it
loader_feasibility: transformers-js: CLIP's joint image/text encoders run client-side to produce a match score.
rationale: Verifying image-caption fit is useful for alt-text QA and dataset cleaning without sending images anywhere.

name: image-anaglyph-overlay
description: Maps one image to the red channel and the other to cyan, so differences appear as colored ghosting in a single composite.
example_prompt: Make a red/cyan overlay of these two scans so I can see the shift
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: channel remap and composite over two buffers, encoded locally.
rationale: Red/cyan ghosting is an intuitive single-image way to perceive offset between two near-identical images.

name: image-color-chart-deltae
description: Reads the patches of a photographed color chart (e.g. ColorChecker) and reports per-patch Delta-E against reference values to grade color accuracy.
example_prompt: Measure how accurate the colors are in this photo of my color chart
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: locate patch grid, average each patch, convert to Lab, compute ΔE — all local math.
rationale: Photographers and printers need objective Delta-E numbers to calibrate, and the chart never leaves the device.

name: video-subtitle-timing-diff
description: Compares cue timings between two subtitle tracks and reports per-line drift and total offset trend.
example_prompt: How much has the timing drifted between these two subtitle versions?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse cue timecodes from both files and compute deltas locally
rationale: Separates timing regressions from text edits when resyncing subtitles to a recut.

name: video-perceptual-quality-lpips
description: Scores perceptual quality between a reference and test video using an LPIPS model for human-aligned diffs.
example_prompt: Give me a perceptual quality score comparing my encode to the source
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime — a bundled LPIPS model runs over sampled frame pairs in-browser
rationale: LPIPS correlates with human judgment better than PSNR/SSIM for modern codec artifacts.

name: bit-exact-audio-comparator
description: Decodes two audio files of any container/codec to PCM and reports whether the underlying samples are bit-identical.
example_prompt: Are these FLAC and WAV files bit-identical after decoding?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes both to raw PCM, plain Rust hashes and compares the streams in the browser.
rationale: Verifies a transcode or container remux preserved the audio data exactly across different formats.

name: cue-marker-diff
description: Diffs the cue/marker positions stored in two WAV files and reports added, removed, or moved markers.
example_prompt: Did the cue markers change between these two WAV files?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM reads the RIFF cue chunks of both files and compares them in-browser.
rationale: Verifies marker edits survived a round-trip through an editor.

name: tuning-offset-compare
description: Detects the tuning reference (A=Hz) of two recordings and reports the difference in cents.
example_prompt: How many cents apart are these two recordings in tuning?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM runs pitch-histogram tuning estimation on both files client-side.
rationale: Tells you whether two tracks can be layered without a tuning clash.

name: zcr-compare
description: Computes the zero-crossing rate of two clips and reports the difference as a quick noisiness/texture proxy.
example_prompt: Compare the zero-crossing rate of these two clips.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM counts sign changes per window on both decoded clips locally.
rationale: A cheap first-pass texture comparison between two signals before heavier analysis.

name: comb-filter-summation-check
description: Sums two near-identical files and detects comb-filtering notches caused by timing or phase misalignment.
example_prompt: Will summing these two mic tracks cause comb filtering?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM sums the PCM and runs an FFT to find periodic notches in the browser.
rationale: Predicts phase problems before combining two correlated mic recordings.

name: mic-polarity-compare
description: Determines whether two recordings of the same source are in or out of polarity (180°) with each other.
example_prompt: Are these two mic tracks in polarity with each other?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM cross-correlates the two aligned signals and checks the sign client-side.
rationale: Catches a flipped-polarity mic that would cancel when the two tracks are mixed.

name: waveform-similarity-score
description: Aligns two waveforms and reports a normalized cross-correlation similarity score from 0 to 1.
example_prompt: Give me a similarity score between these two audio files.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM normalizes, aligns, and correlates the two PCM streams in-browser.
rationale: A single quick 'how alike are these' number for triaging duplicate or near-duplicate files.

name: gain-delta-detector
description: Aligns two otherwise-identical files and measures the constant gain difference in dB between them.
example_prompt: How many dB louder is the second file than the first?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM aligns and computes the per-sample ratio on both PCM streams locally.
rationale: Reveals exactly how much one copy was normalized or gained relative to the other from the signal itself.

name: envelope-follower-diff
description: Extracts the amplitude envelopes of two files and diffs them over time to compare dynamics processing.
example_prompt: Show how the dynamics differ between the compressed and uncompressed versions.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM computes RMS/peak envelopes for both files and diffs them in-browser.
rationale: Visualizes exactly where and how much a compressor or limiter altered the dynamics.

name: loudness-over-time-delta
description: Computes the short-term LUFS curves of two files and plots their loudness delta over time.
example_prompt: Compare the moment-to-moment loudness of these two masters.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM measures windowed LUFS on both files and diffs the time series client-side.
rationale: Shows where two masters diverge in dynamics, beyond a single integrated-loudness number.

name: rt60-reverb-compare
description: Estimates the RT60 reverb decay time of two recordings and reports the difference.
example_prompt: Which of these two rooms is more reverberant?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM runs Schroeder-integration decay estimation on both files in the browser.
rationale: Quantifies room/space differences between two recordings for matching or QC.

name: pprof-diff
description: Computes a differential profile between two pprof samples, showing per-function delta time/allocations.
example_prompt: Diff these two pprof profiles and show what got slower
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — protobuf profile parse and sample aggregation run client-side
rationale: Differential profiling isolates a regression's hotspots far better than reading two profiles separately.

name: video-color-range-check
description: Detects whether the video signal is tagged limited (TV) or full (PC) range and flags mismatched/missing range tags.
example_prompt: Does this video use full or limited color range?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm reads color_range stream metadata locally with no decode required.
rationale: Wrong range tagging produces washed-out or crushed playback that is hard to diagnose without the tag value.

name: video-negative-timestamp-check
description: Flags negative or pre-roll PTS/DTS values and priming offsets that cause clicks or sync errors at the head of playback.
example_prompt: Check this file for negative timestamps at the start.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm reads initial packet timestamps in-browser; just measurement.
rationale: Negative-timestamp edge cases break web players unpredictably and aren't surfaced by normal media info.

name: video-luma-range-check
description: Builds a luma histogram to detect crushed blacks or blown highlights from clipped exposure or bad levels.
example_prompt: Are the blacks crushed or highlights blown out in this footage?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm computes luma histogram stats over sampled frames locally.
rationale: Clipped tonal range is unrecoverable detail loss that's hard to confirm without histogram data.

name: video-duration-mismatch-check
description: Compares container-declared duration against the actual decoded stream length to detect truncated or padded files.
example_prompt: Is this download truncated — does the real length match the header?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm reads the header duration and counts decoded packets in-browser to compare.
rationale: A truncated download often still has a full-length header, so only a decoded comparison reveals the missing tail.

name: video-audio-video-duration-sync-check
description: Compares audio and video stream durations and flags large differences that indicate one track ends early.
example_prompt: Do the audio and video tracks in this file end at the same time?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm reads per-stream durations locally and the diff check runs in WASM.
rationale: A short audio or video stream causes silent endings or frozen tails that no single-track inspection catches.

name: video-missing-audio-check
description: Detects files that have no audio stream or whose audio is effectively silent throughout.
example_prompt: Does this export actually have audio, or is it silent?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm checks for an audio stream and measures RMS over decoded audio in-browser.
rationale: A silently-muted or audio-less export is a common mistake that's only noticed after upload without this check.

name: wav-fmt-chunk-validator
description: Validates that a WAV fmt chunk is internally consistent (byteRate equals sampleRate×blockAlign, blockAlign equals channels×bitsPerSample/8, valid format tag).
example_prompt: Check whether the fmt header in this WAV file is self-consistent
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses the RIFF fmt chunk bytes and checks arithmetic relations, no decoding or network needed.
rationale: Mislabeled byteRate/blockAlign silently corrupts playback speed and a quick lint catches it before files ship.

name: rf64-wave64-validator
description: Validates large-file WAV variants (RF64 ds64 chunk and Sony Wave64 GUID chunks) for correct 64-bit size fields and structure.
example_prompt: Validate this RF64 / Wave64 large WAV file header
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses the ds64 / Wave64 chunk headers from bytes, no decode required.
rationale: Over-4GB recordings use RF64/Wave64 and broken 64-bit size fields make the entire file unreadable.

name: ac3-frame-header-validator
description: Validates AC-3 (Dolby Digital) sync frames: syncword, CRC presence, sample-rate code, frame-size code, and bitstream id consistency.
example_prompt: Check the AC-3 frame headers in this audio stream
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: scans for 0x0B77 syncwords and parses the bitstream-info bits directly.
rationale: AC-3 streams extracted from video often have truncated frames, and header validation confirms playable audio.

name: dts-frame-header-validator
description: Validates DTS Coherent Acoustics frame headers: syncword, frame size, sample-rate index, and channel arrangement code.
example_prompt: Validate the DTS frame headers in this file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: detects DTS syncwords and parses the fixed header bitfields locally.
rationale: DTS streams demuxed from discs frequently lose frame alignment, which a syncword validator detects.

name: ogg-page-sequence-validator
description: Validates Ogg logical-stream integrity: continuous page sequence numbers, monotonic granule positions, and a correct end-of-stream flag.
example_prompt: Check this Ogg file for page sequence or granule errors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: walks Ogg page headers and compares sequence/granule fields, no codec decode.
rationale: Out-of-order or missing Ogg pages cause skips and seek failures that CRC checks alone miss.

name: mp3-cbr-consistency-check
description: Scans all MP3 frames and verifies a CBR-labeled file actually uses one constant bitrate (flagging hidden VBR or mixed frames).
example_prompt: Is this MP3 really constant bitrate, or secretly VBR?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: reads each frame header's bitrate index by walking sync words, pure parsing.
rationale: Tools sometimes mislabel VBR as CBR, breaking byte-offset seeking, and a frame-by-frame lint exposes it.

name: musicxml-wellformed-validator
description: Checks a MusicXML score for well-formedness and required structural elements (part-list, parts, measures, attributes), reporting missing pieces.
example_prompt: Check whether this MusicXML score is well-formed and complete
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: XML parsing plus structural element checks run entirely in the browser.
rationale: Hand-edited or exported MusicXML often omits required nodes, breaking import into notation tools.

name: midi-overlapping-note-linter
description: Detects overlapping same-pitch notes on the same channel (a second note-on before the first note-off), which cause stuck or doubled notes.
example_prompt: Find overlapping same-pitch notes in this MIDI file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: tracks per-pitch note state while parsing events, pure computation.
rationale: Overlapping same-pitch notes produce hanging-note glitches on many synths that this lint isolates.

name: midi-tempo-sanity-check
description: Checks MIDI tempo metadata: presence of an initial tempo, BPM values within a sane range, and no conflicting tempo events at time zero.
example_prompt: Sanity-check the tempo events in this MIDI file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: reads Set-Tempo meta events and validates values/positions offline.
rationale: A missing or absurd initial tempo makes DAWs default to 120 BPM and ruins imported timing.

name: clipping-sample-detector
description: Decodes audio and counts clipped (full-scale) samples plus contiguous clip regions per channel, reporting total clip duration.
example_prompt: How many clipped samples are in this track?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes to PCM in WASM, then plain analysis counts full-scale runs, all in-browser.
rationale: Digital clipping is the most common mastering defect, and a precise per-sample count guides re-gain decisions.

name: whitespace-diff-checker
description: Determines whether two texts differ only in whitespace, line endings, or trailing spaces, and shows where.
example_prompt: Are these two files actually different or just whitespace/line-ending changes?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — normalize whitespace and compare, flagging invisible diffs
rationale: Whitespace-only changes cause spurious diffs and confusing reviews that this tool can rule in or out instantly.

name: audio-tag-diff
description: Diffs the metadata tags (ID3, Vorbis comments, MP4 atoms) of two audio files, listing added, removed, and changed fields.
example_prompt: Show me what tags differ between these two MP3 versions.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses the tag containers of both files and renders a field-level diff with no network.
rationale: Catches accidental metadata drift between an original and a re-tagged copy at a glance.

name: mp3-frame-diff
description: Compares the MPEG frame-header sequences of two MP3s and reports where bitrate, mode, or framing diverge.
example_prompt: Where do these two MP3 files differ at the frame level?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses both files' frame headers and walks them in parallel client-side.
rationale: Detects re-encodes, splices, or edits between two MP3s without decoding audio.

name: phase-spectrum-diff
description: Compares the phase spectra of two files at matched frequencies to reveal all-pass or phase-rotating processing.
example_prompt: Did any phase processing change between these two files?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM runs FFTs on both files and diffs the unwrapped phase per bin in-browser.
rationale: Detects phase-only changes that a magnitude frequency-response compare is blind to.

name: beat-grid-diff
description: Detects the beat grid of two tracks and diffs the beat positions to show tempo or phase drift between them.
example_prompt: Compare the beat grids of these two tracks.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM runs beat tracking on both files and aligns the grids client-side.
rationale: Shows whether two tracks share a stable beat relationship for layering or mashups.

name: benchmark-diff
description: Compares two benchmark JSON outputs and flags statistically meaningful regressions and improvements.
example_prompt: Compare these two benchmark result files and tell me what regressed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — JSON parse and percentage-delta computation, no server
rationale: Manually eyeballing benchmark numbers misses regressions a threshold-based diff catches.

name: cross-correlation-calculator
description: Computes the cross-correlation of two signals across lags and reports the lag of maximum correlation.
example_prompt: Cross-correlate [1,2,1,0] and [0,1,2,1] and tell me the best lag.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; shift-and-multiply sums over arrays, all in-memory.
rationale: Finding the lag that best aligns two signals is a core comparison task in DSP, finance, and synchronization.

name: rand-index-calculator
description: Compares two clusterings of the same items using the Rand index and adjusted Rand index.
example_prompt: Compare clusterings A=[1,1,2,2,3] and B=[1,1,2,3,3] with the adjusted Rand index.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; pair-counting over label arrays, fully client-side.
rationale: Measuring how much two clusterings agree is the standard way to evaluate clustering results and ARI corrects for chance.

name: cramers-v-calculator
description: Measures association between two categorical variables via chi-square and Cramér's V from a contingency table.
example_prompt: Cramér's V for the table [[20,30],[25,25]]?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; chi-square computation over the table, all in-memory.
rationale: Cramér's V is the standard normalized effect size for categorical-vs-categorical comparisons and is rarely a one-click tool.

name: qr-code-quality-checker
description: Checks a rendered QR code for scannability: quiet-zone margin, module sharpness, contrast ratio, and error-correction headroom.
example_prompt: Will this QR code on my poster actually scan reliably?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes the QR and measures geometry/contrast locally.
rationale: QR codes that decode in a debugger still fail in the field when quiet zones or contrast are too tight.

name: double-jpeg-compression-detector
description: Detects signs that a JPEG was decoded and re-saved (double compression), indicating editing or quality loss.
example_prompt: Has this JPEG been re-saved/edited rather than being an original?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM analyzes DCT-coefficient histograms for double-quantization artifacts.
rationale: Double-compression is a key forensic and provenance signal that an image isn't an untouched original.

name: brand-color-compliance-checker
description: Checks whether an image's dominant colors match a supplied brand palette within tolerance and lists off-brand colors.
example_prompt: Do the colors in this banner match our brand palette #1A73E8 and #FF6F00?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM clusters image colors and compares them to user-supplied palette values.
rationale: Brand-color drift across assets is a routine compliance check that's painstaking to do by eyedropper.

name: flac-seektable-validator
description: Validates a FLAC SEEKTABLE metadata block: seekpoints sorted ascending, sample numbers within stream length, and placeholder-point rules.
example_prompt: Check the FLAC seektable in this file for invalid seekpoints
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses the SEEKTABLE block bytes and verifies ordering invariants locally.
rationale: Broken seektables cause players to scrub to the wrong position, a subtle bug a dedicated validator pins down.

name: flac-metadata-block-order-validator
description: Enforces FLAC's metadata-block ordering rules (STREAMINFO must be first, last-block flag set exactly once, no duplicate singleton blocks).
example_prompt: Verify the FLAC metadata block ordering is spec-compliant
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: iterates the metadata block headers and checks ordering flags, pure byte parsing.
rationale: Out-of-order metadata blocks are a common tagger bug that some decoders reject outright.

name: atom-feed-validator
description: Validates an Atom 1.0 feed: required id/title/updated elements, entry constraints, and RFC 3339 timestamps.
example_prompt: Check whether this Atom feed is valid
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Atom validation is XML parsing plus rule checks, all local.
rationale: Atom has stricter requirements than RSS and a local validator catches publish-time mistakes.

name: gzip-integrity-checker
description: Validates a gzip stream's trailing CRC32 and ISIZE against the decompressed output.
example_prompt: Check whether this .gz file is corrupted
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: inflate plus CRC32/ISIZE comparison is pure local computation.
rationale: Corrupted gzip files fail mid-pipeline and an integrity check confirms them before processing.

name: content-type-header-validator
description: Validates a Content-Type header for a known MIME type, correct charset parameter, and mismatches like text/* without a charset.
example_prompt: Validate this Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf8
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM media-type parsing with an embedded MIME registry subset.
rationale: A wrong charset or 'utf8' vs 'utf-8' typo causes mojibake; a validator catches the header-level cause.

name: set-cookie-validate
description: Validates a Set-Cookie header for attribute correctness, SameSite/Secure conflicts, oversized values, and __Host-/__Secure- prefix rule violations.
example_prompt: Validate this Set-Cookie header
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: header tokenization and attribute rule checks, local.
rationale: Cookie prefix and SameSite rules are easy to violate and break auth, so a checker catches real bugs.

name: winding-order-checker
description: Determines whether a polygon's vertices are ordered clockwise or counter-clockwise via the signed shoelace area.
example_prompt: Is this polygon wound clockwise or counter-clockwise?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — signed shoelace-area sum, deterministic and offline.
rationale: Winding order drives front/back-face and fill conventions; validating it fixes inside-out polygons in geometry data.

name: trailing-whitespace-linter
description: Reports lines with trailing whitespace, mixed tabs-and-spaces indentation, and over-long lines past a configurable limit.
example_prompt: Lint this file for trailing whitespace and mixed indentation
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM per-line scan, offline
rationale: These whitespace issues create noisy diffs and trip strict linters; catching them pre-commit is handy.

name: video-bits-per-pixel-report
description: Computes bits-per-pixel and bitrate efficiency from resolution, frame rate, and bitrate to judge encode quality.
example_prompt: What's the bits-per-pixel of this encode? Is it under-allocated?
loader_feasibility: Pure arithmetic over header-derived metadata in Rust→WASM; nothing leaves the browser.
rationale: Bits-per-pixel is the quick sanity metric for whether a clip is over- or under-compressed for its resolution.

name: video-nal-unit-histogram
description: Counts the NAL units in an H.264/H.265 elementary stream by type to summarize the bitstream's composition.
example_prompt: Break down the NAL units in this h264 stream by type
loader_feasibility: Rust scans Annex-B/AVCC NAL start codes and tallies types in WASM, fully local.
rationale: NAL histograms expose missing SPS/PPS, SEI usage, and slice structure for low-level bitstream debugging.

name: flac-streaminfo-reader
description: Decodes the FLAC STREAMINFO block into sample rate, channels, bit depth, total samples, min/max frame and block sizes, and the stored MD5 of the PCM.
example_prompt: Show the STREAMINFO fields of this FLAC
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bit-unpacks the 34-byte STREAMINFO struct, runs locally with no dependencies.
rationale: The stored PCM MD5 and exact sample count are key integrity fields that are otherwise hidden inside the binary.

name: subtitle-inspect
description: Parses an SRT or WebVTT file to report cue count, total duration, and timing problems like overlaps, gaps, or out-of-order cues.
example_prompt: check this SRT file for overlapping or out-of-order subtitles
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM text parsing of the subtitle format; no media decode needed
rationale: Subtitle timing errors are common after edits and a validator beats scrubbing through video.

name: woff2-inspector
description: Parses a WOFF/WOFF2 web-font wrapper header to report the embedded SFNT flavor, table count, and total/compressed sizes.
example_prompt: Inspect this woff2 and show the original font size vs compressed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the WOFF2 header and table directory are read from raw bytes (decompression optional).
rationale: Web-font size budgeting and flavor checks are a frequent front-end performance task.

name: series-entropy-calculator
description: Computes Shannon, sample, and permutation entropy of a numeric series to quantify its complexity and predictability.
example_prompt: How complex/random is this series? Compute its entropy.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM probability + embedding calculations; local.
rationale: Entropy measures are used in physiology, finance, and anomaly detection and have no easy offline calculator.

name: m4a-itunes-metadata-reader
description: Reads iTunes-style metadata from an M4A/AAC file's ilst atom (title, artist, album, track, compilation, gapless, etc.).
example_prompt: Read the iTunes tags from this m4a
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses the moov/udta/meta/ilst atom chain, no decode, client-side.
rationale: M4A metadata uses a wholly different box scheme than ID3 and has no general client-side reader yet.

name: mp3-duration-from-frames
description: Computes accurate MP3 duration by scanning every frame header instead of trusting the (often wrong) tag or VBR estimate.
example_prompt: Calculate the real duration of this mp3 by counting frames
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: iterates frame headers summing sample counts, no full decode, client-side.
rationale: Damaged or VBR files report wrong lengths, and frame-accurate counting is the only reliable fix.

name: midi-cc-extractor
description: Extracts control-change automation for chosen CC numbers from a MIDI file as time/value series.
example_prompt: Extract the CC11 expression automation from this MIDI
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: filters control-change events per channel/CC, fully client-side.
rationale: Isolating modulation/expression curves is useful for analysis and re-targeting automation.

name: morse-audio-decoder
description: Detects a CW tone in an audio file and decodes the Morse code timing into text.
example_prompt: Decode the Morse code beeps in this audio into text
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes to PCM, Rust→WASM does tone envelope detection + dot/dash timing analysis — fully client-side.
rationale: Morse decoding from audio is a classic, satisfying, fully local DSP task with real hobbyist demand.

name: ocsp-response-parse
description: Decodes an OCSP response into cert status, this/next-update times, and revocation reason.
example_prompt: Decode this OCSP response and tell me the cert status
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM ASN.1 DER decode of the OCSP structure; the bytes are parsed locally with no live OCSP call
rationale: Debugging TLS revocation issues means reading raw OCSP responses, which no browser-local tool currently does.

name: ensure-single-final-newline
description: Normalizes the end of the text to exactly one trailing newline, or to none.
example_prompt: make sure this file ends with a single newline
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tail normalization, fully local
rationale: POSIX tools, linters, and many parsers expect a single terminating newline.

name: lyrics-video-generator
description: Generates a karaoke-style lyrics video from an LRC timing file and an audio track, revealing each line on cue.
example_prompt: Turn this LRC file and MP3 into a lyrics video with white text on black
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust parses the LRC timestamps into per-line `drawtext` enable windows, then ffmpeg muxes them with the audio client-side.
rationale: Musicians want shareable lyric videos for uploads and there is no fully local tool that turns an LRC + audio pair into one.

name: quoted-printable-encode
description: Encodes arbitrary text into quoted-printable with proper =XX escaping and 76-column soft line wraps.
example_prompt: Quoted-printable encode: naïve café — résumé
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: deterministic byte-by-byte escaping with no network.
rationale: Round-trips with the decoder so users can both produce and read MIME bodies when crafting or testing emails.

name: premultiply-alpha
description: Converts an RGBA image between straight and premultiplied alpha.
example_prompt: Premultiply the alpha on this png
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM per-pixel multiply of color by alpha
rationale: GPU/compositing pipelines expect premultiplied alpha and getting it wrong causes dark fringing.

name: video-to-mpeg2
description: Encodes video to an MPEG-2 program stream for DVD authoring and legacy hardware.
example_prompt: make a DVD-compatible mpeg2 from this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm's mpeg2video encoder writes DVD-spec MPEG-2/MP2 streams locally.
rationale: DVD authoring and broadcast pipelines still consume MPEG-2.

name: petition-analyzer
description: Analyzes petition or advocacy text for readability, key demands, tone, and a short summary.
example_prompt: Break down this petition: what is it actually asking for and how readable is it?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM for readability/keyphrase extraction; optional transformers-js summary — all client-side.
rationale: Serves the 'petitions' demand by helping organizers and signers quickly grasp and improve petition text.

name: cliche-detector
description: Flags overused clichés and stock phrases against a bundled list, with positions.
example_prompt: Point out any clichés in this cover letter
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: multi-word phrase matching against an embedded dictionary, no network
rationale: Clichés dull writing and are hard to self-spot, so a curated local matcher adds real editorial value.

name: long-term-average-spectrum
description: Computes the long-term average spectrum (LTAS) of a file as a frequency-response curve for tonal-balance checks.
example_prompt: Plot the average frequency spectrum of this track
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM FFT-averaging over PCM (ffmpeg decodes); runs in-browser.
rationale: An averaged spectrum is the standard way to compare tonal balance against reference tracks.

name: tangent-space-calculator
description: Computes per-vertex tangents and bitangents from positions, UVs, and normals for normal mapping.
example_prompt: Generate tangents for this mesh data so I can do normal mapping
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM math over vertex arrays
rationale: Tangent generation is required for normal/bump mapping and notoriously tedious to get right.

name: jsonlogic-eval
description: Evaluates a JSONLogic rule expression against a JSON data object and returns the result, with a step-by-step trace.
example_prompt: Apply this JSONLogic rule {"and":[{">":[{"var":"age"},18]}]} to {"age":21}.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — datalogic-rs is a pure-Rust JSONLogic evaluator with no I/O, trivially wasm-compatible.
rationale: JSONLogic powers portable business rules and developers need a quick way to test rules against sample data.

name: decision-table-eval
description: Evaluates a decision table (rows of conditions mapping to outcomes) against an input record and returns the matched outcome.
example_prompt: Given this decision table and a customer with spend=5000, tier=gold, what discount applies?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — built on datalogic-rs rule evaluation, runs fully in-memory.
rationale: Decision tables are a common business-rules format and evaluating them by hand is error-prone.

name: starlark-evaluator
description: Runs Starlark (the Python-like config language behind Bazel and Buck) and shows the resulting values.
example_prompt: Run this Starlark and show x: x = [i*i for i in range(5)]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Facebook's starlark-rust is pure Rust with no system access, so the interpreter sandboxes naturally in wasmi.
rationale: Bazel and Buck users need to prototype build logic and macros without spinning up a full build.

name: release-asset-picker
description: Given a pasted list of GitHub release asset filenames and your OS/architecture, picks the right binary and builds its download URL.
example_prompt: I'm on an Apple Silicon Mac — which of these release assets should I grab? [pastes asset list]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — replicates eget's OS/arch matching as pure pattern logic; no live fetch, the user supplies the asset list.
rationale: eget/godyl/stew/getghrel all exist solely to match the correct asset to your platform, the one part of that job that needs no network.

name: rust-to-csharp-bindings
description: Reads Rust `extern "C"` functions and `#[repr(C)]` structs and emits matching C# `DllImport` methods plus `[StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)]` structs.
