example_prompt: Make C# interop bindings for `#[repr(C)] pub struct Color { r: u8, g: u8, b: u8 } extern "C" fn blend(a: Color, b: Color) -> Color`
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse a Rust FFI subset and template the C# side via a fixed type-mapping; no native runtime involved.
rationale: this is csbindgen's exact job (Rust→C#), valuable for Unity/.NET developers who want bindings without running the native generator locally.

name: conversational-form-generator
description: Generates a self-contained Typeform-style HTML form that shows one question at a time with a progress indicator and keyboard navigation.
example_prompt: Build a one-question-at-a-time onboarding form like Typeform with 5 steps
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM emits HTML plus a small vanilla-JS step controller; runs fully in the page with no service.
rationale: Typeform's whole appeal is the one-question conversational flow, which people want without the subscription or hosted dependency.

name: codec-artifact-compare
description: Decodes two lossy encodes of the same source and measures quantization, pre-echo, and birdie artifacts to rank which encoder did better.
example_prompt: Compare the MP3 vs AAC encode of this track for artifacts
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (wasm) decode both to PCM, then plain-Rust artifact metrics vs the source — all in-browser
rationale: Encoder/bitrate A/B comparison is a frequent listening-test decision that an objective metric can sharpen.

name: octave-text-matrix-to-csv
description: Reads an Octave/MATLAB -ascii text matrix dump and converts it to CSV.
example_prompt: Convert this Octave -ascii matrix file to CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the Octave text format is whitespace-delimited numbers with a small header, parsed entirely client-side.
rationale: Octave's `save -ascii` output is awkward to import elsewhere and a clean CSV makes it portable.

name: video-language-tag-checker
description: Checks that every audio and subtitle stream has a valid ISO language tag and flags untagged or 'und' streams.
example_prompt: Do all the audio and subtitle tracks have proper language tags?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader reads per-stream language metadata via ffprobe in WASM and validates locally.
rationale: Missing language tags break player track selection and fail most platform ingest QC.

name: video-default-track-checker
description: Verifies exactly one default audio and one default subtitle track are flagged, flagging zero or multiple defaults.
example_prompt: Check that only one default audio track is set on this file.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader inspects stream disposition flags via ffprobe in WASM and counts defaults locally.
rationale: Multiple or missing default flags cause unpredictable track selection across players.

name: audio-container-validator
description: Confirms the container actually matches its codec and profile (e.g. .m4a is AAC, .wav is PCM, not a surprise codec).
example_prompt: Make sure this .wav is genuine PCM and not some weird compressed codec.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — container/codec cross-checking uses the in-browser demuxer with no server round-trip.
rationale: Non-standard codec-in-container combos pass loosely but are rejected by hardware players and broadcast ingest.

name: favicon-link-checker
description: Checks an HTML head for the recommended favicon/apple-touch-icon/manifest link set across modern browsers and platforms and lists what's missing.
example_prompt: Does this page declare all the recommended favicon and touch-icon links?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM head scan against a fixed recommended-link checklist; offline.
rationale: The cross-platform favicon set is fiddly and almost always partially wrong.

name: video-audio-channel-checker
description: Verifies a video's audio channel count and layout (mono, stereo, 5.1) match an expected configuration.
example_prompt: Confirm this video has a proper stereo audio track
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: ffprobe channel_layout/channels from ffmpeg.wasm are compared client-side.
rationale: Wrong channel layout (e.g. mono delivered where stereo is required) is a routine delivery rejection.

name: gameboy-emulator
description: Load a Game Boy ROM file and play it in the browser with on-screen controls and save states.
example_prompt: run this gameboy rom in an emulator
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a CPU/PPU/APU emulator core steps the loaded ROM entirely in-memory under wasmi; the ROM never leaves the device (interpreter speed is the main constraint).
rationale: The 'Gameboy Emulator' demand term is a marquee capability that demonstrates gizza can run real retro hardware fully client-side and privately.

name: image-wipe-compare-gif
description: Generates an animated GIF with a vertical wipe sweeping between a before and after image for a clean reveal.
example_prompt: Make a before/after wipe animation from these two edits.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM renders each wipe frame and encodes the GIF locally.
rationale: A slider-style wipe is the most engaging way to present before/after edits and differs from a crossfade dissolve.

name: video-banding-compare
description: Measures color banding severity in two encodes and reports which one exhibits more visible gradient banding.
example_prompt: Which of these two encodes has worse banding in the sky gradients?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM extracts smooth-region gradients locally and a plain-Rust block scores step-discontinuities per file.
rationale: Banding is the most common low-bitrate artifact and a quantified A/B comparison guides dithering/bit-depth decisions.

name: video-sharpness-diff
description: Compares high-frequency detail/sharpness between two videos to detect softening from re-encoding or scaling.
example_prompt: Did my downscale lose sharpness compared to the original?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM extracts frames locally and a plain-Rust block measures high-frequency energy (Laplacian variance) for each.
rationale: Quantifying detail loss is the clearest way to catch over-aggressive denoise or scaling that quality scores can understate.

name: video-noise-level-diff
description: Estimates and compares the noise floor of two videos to verify a denoise pass or detect added grain.
example_prompt: How much noise did my denoise filter actually remove?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM samples flat regions locally and a plain-Rust block estimates noise variance for each file in-browser.
rationale: Measuring before/after noise levels validates denoising effort objectively instead of by eye.

name: video-luma-range-diff
description: Compares the luma and chroma value ranges (full vs limited / TV vs PC range) of two videos to catch level-mismatch crush or wash-out.
example_prompt: Did the encode change my video from full range to limited range?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM signalstats reports min/max luma per file locally and a plain-Rust block compares the ranges.
rationale: Full-vs-limited range mismatches are an extremely common and easy-to-miss cause of washed-out or crushed output.

name: video-pixel-format-diff
description: Compares pixel format, bit depth, and chroma subsampling of two videos and flags any change.
example_prompt: Compare the pixel format and bit depth of source.mov and export.mp4
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM probes each file locally and a plain-Rust block diffs the format fields.
rationale: Silent 10-bit-to-8-bit or 4:2:2-to-4:2:0 conversions cause real quality loss that a focused diff surfaces instantly.

name: video-roi-compare
description: Compares only a user-specified cropped region of interest between two videos using PSNR/SSIM, ignoring the rest of the frame.
example_prompt: Compare just the lower-third logo area between these two encodes
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM crops both inputs to the ROI and runs the quality filters locally.
rationale: Region-limited comparison answers targeted questions (did the watermark/text degrade?) that whole-frame metrics dilute.

name: video-rendition-content-match-check
description: Verifies that an ABR rendition is genuinely the same content as the source (not corrupted, swapped, or misaligned) via downscaled frame matching.
example_prompt: Confirm my 480p rendition is actually the same content as the master
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM downscales and samples both locally and a plain-Rust block matches frame fingerprints in-browser.
rationale: Packaging pipelines occasionally mislabel or swap renditions, and a content-match check catches it before publishing.

name: video-tonemap-compare
description: Compares an HDR source against its SDR tonemapped output to report highlight clipping and color shift introduced by the tonemap.
example_prompt: How much highlight detail did I lose tonemapping this HDR clip to SDR?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM applies/reads both signals locally and a plain-Rust block measures clipped-highlight and saturation deltas.
rationale: Tonemapping quality is hard to judge by eye, and quantifying highlight loss guides curve selection for HDR-to-SDR delivery.

name: frequency-response-compare
description: Derives the EQ/frequency-response delta curve between two versions of the same audio (e.g., before vs after EQ).
example_prompt: What EQ curve was applied between the dry and EQ'd version of this track?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM averages FFT magnitude ratios across the files entirely in-browser.
rationale: Reverse-engineering the applied EQ from a before/after pair is a frequent mixing and mastering need.

name: integrated-loudness-delta
description: Measures ITU-R BS.1770 integrated LUFS for two files and reports the loudness difference between them.
example_prompt: How many LUFS louder is master B than master A?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies the K-weighting filter and gating to decoded PCM locally.
rationale: Integrated-LUFS difference is the exact number needed to loudness-match versions before judging them, distinct from loudness range.

name: peak-to-loudness-ratio-compare
description: Computes the peak-to-loudness ratio (PLR) of two masters and compares how much headroom/dynamics each retains.
example_prompt: Compare the PLR of these two masters to see which is more squashed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM derives true peak and integrated LUFS from PCM with no server.
rationale: PLR is a concise loudness-war indicator that lets users pick the less-crushed master.

name: noise-floor-compare
description: Estimates the noise-floor level of the quietest sustained segment in each of two recordings and reports the difference.
example_prompt: Which of these two recordings has the lower noise floor?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM finds the minimum-energy window and measures dBFS per file locally.
rationale: Comparing noise floors picks the cleaner of two mic/preamp setups without a full SNR study.

name: voronoi-diagram
description: Generate a Voronoi cell pattern image from random or supplied seed points.
example_prompt: Make a colorful Voronoi pattern with 40 cells
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM computes nearest-seed regions per pixel, offline.
rationale: A versatile generative-art and data-viz primitive not currently available.

name: fluent-ftl-parser
description: Parses Mozilla Fluent (.ftl) localization files into messages, terms, attributes, and placeables for translation tooling.
example_prompt: Parse this Fluent .ftl file and list all the message IDs and their placeables.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; implements the Fluent message/term grammar locally, fully client-side.
rationale: Fluent is gaining adoption for i18n but lacks lightweight inspection tools outside its JS runtime.

name: nbib-parser
description: Parses PubMed .nbib citation records into structured fields (authors, title, journal, DOI, PMID, MeSH terms).
example_prompt: Parse this .nbib file from PubMed and show me the title, authors, and DOI.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; the nbib tag-prefixed (PMID-, TI-, AU-) format is straightforward line parsing, fully local.
rationale: Researchers export PubMed citations as .nbib; parsing them locally feeds reference managers without a server round-trip.

name: image-histogram-extractor
description: Computes per-channel and luminance histograms and exports them as CSV/JSON plus a rendered histogram chart.
example_prompt: Give me the RGB histogram data for this image as CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: histogram binning over the decoded pixel buffer is a single CPU pass in Rust.
rationale: Exposure analysis and dataset QA need numeric histogram data, not just a visual readout, and nothing in the catalog provides it.

name: pixel-art-resolution-detector
description: Detects the native pixel grid of an upscaled pixel-art image and downsamples it back to its true 1:1 resolution.
example_prompt: This pixel art was scaled up — recover the original small version
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: autocorrelation/edge-period analysis on the pixel buffer finds the block size and snaps to it in Rust.
rationale: Pixel artists and emulator users often only have a blurry upscaled sprite and need the clean original grid back, which no catalog tool recovers.

name: video-sps-pps-decoder
description: Extracts the H.264/HEVC SPS/PPS parameter sets and decodes resolution, profile, level, chroma format, and bit depth.
example_prompt: Decode the SPS/PPS from this video and tell me its profile and level
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM bitstream reader parses the parameter-set RBSP with exp-Golomb decoding; no media decode, fully local
rationale: The real encoding parameters live in the SPS/PPS, and container metadata often lies about them.

name: video-klv-metadata-extractor
description: Extracts KLV/MISB timed metadata from an MPEG-TS data stream and decodes the universal-key packets.
example_prompt: Extract the KLV metadata stream from this drone TS file
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg (loaded) demuxes the data stream, then plain Rust→WASM parses KLV triplets; fully client-side
rationale: Drone and aerial footage embeds KLV telemetry that specialist tools cost money to read and never run in-browser.

name: video-codec-extradata-extractor
description: Extracts the codec extradata/private bytes (avcC, hvcC, vpcC, esds) and presents them as annotated hex.
example_prompt: Dump the avcC extradata from this mp4 as hex
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the sample-entry config box; pure byte extraction, client-side
rationale: Remuxing and WebCodecs initialization require the exact extradata, which no GUI tool exposes.

name: asf-header-parser
description: Parses the ASF/WMA header objects (File Properties, Stream Properties, Content Description, Extended Content) into JSON.
example_prompt: Read the metadata and stream info out of this wma file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — ASF is a GUID-tagged object list with little-endian sizes, parsed directly from bytes.
rationale: WMA/ASF metadata uses GUID-keyed objects that ID3/Vorbis tools cannot read at all.

name: wav-inst-chunk-reader
description: Reads the WAV \inst\ chunk for unshifted note, fine tune, gain, and low/high note and velocity ranges.
example_prompt: Read the instrument chunk from this wav sample
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the inst chunk is a fixed 7-byte record parsed directly from the RIFF structure.
rationale: Sampler key/velocity mapping is stored in inst and needed when importing one-shots into instruments.

name: acid-chunk-reader
description: Parses the ACIDized WAV \acid\ chunk to report loop tempo, beat count, root note, and one-shot/loop flags.
example_prompt: What tempo and key are in this acidized wav loop?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — reads the proprietary but documented fixed-size acid chunk from the RIFF tree.
rationale: ACIDized loop libraries embed authoritative tempo/key data that DAWs use for time-stretching.

name: cart-chunk-reader
description: Reads the broadcast \cart\ chunk (AES46) from a WAV: title, artist, cut ID, category, timers, and start/end dates.
example_prompt: Read the radio cart metadata from this wav
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the cart chunk is a fixed-layout struct of ASCII fields parsed from RIFF bytes.
rationale: Radio-automation systems depend on cart metadata that ordinary audio tools never expose.

name: bext-metadata-reader
description: Reads the Broadcast Wave \bext\ chunk into structured fields: description, originator, origination date/time, and time reference.
example_prompt: Read the BWF bext metadata and timecode from this wav
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bext is a fixed-layout ASCII+integer struct read directly from the RIFF tree.
rationale: The bext time reference is the sync anchor for broadcast/film audio and is buried in a non-tag chunk.

name: lame-info-tag-reader
description: Reads the Xing/Info/LAME header from an MP3: encoder version, VBR method, quality, encoder delay/padding, and stated track gain.
example_prompt: Read the LAME Info header from this mp3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the Info tag inside the first MP3 frame's side-info region by byte offset.
rationale: The LAME tag holds the encoder fingerprint and gapless delay/padding that determine seamless playback.

name: sfz-instrument-parser
description: Parses an SFZ instrument definition into structured JSON of regions, groups, and opcodes with their key/velocity ranges and sample paths.
example_prompt: Parse this sfz file into a region/opcode JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — SFZ is a text opcode format with header sections, parsed line-by-line.
rationale: SFZ mappings are plain text but hierarchical, and a structured view makes them auditable and editable.

name: ris-parse
description: Parses RIS reference-manager records into structured JSON/CSV.
example_prompt: Convert this RIS export from PubMed into a CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line-tag parser; deterministic local transform
rationale: RIS is the other dominant citation format with no client-side converter.

name: igc-parse
description: Parses IGC glider/paraglider flight logs into a CSV/GeoJSON track with altitude and time.
example_prompt: Turn this IGC flight log into a track CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line parser over B-records; fully local
rationale: Free-flight pilots have IGC files with no convenient client-side extractor.

name: ttml-caption-parser
description: Parses a TTML/DFXP caption file into a flat cue list with begin/end times and text, ready for conversion or review.
example_prompt: Parse this TTML caption file into a cue list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML parse and time-expression normalization, fully local.
rationale: TTML's XML and varied time formats make it the hardest caption format to read, yet it's common in broadcast exports.

name: timestamp-chapter-extractor
description: Extracts timestamped chapter markers (e.g. 00:00 Intro) from a pasted description into a structured chapter list with durations.
example_prompt: Pull the chapters out of this video description
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM timestamp-line parsing and duration diffing over the text.
rationale: Converting a description's timestamp list into structured chapters with durations is a repetitive editing chore.

name: matroska-ebml-parser
description: Parses MKV/WebM EBML elements to list tracks, codecs, languages, and segment metadata.
example_prompt: What tracks and codecs are in this .mkv file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; EBML is a variable-length-integer tagged tree decoded directly from bytes.
rationale: MKV/WebM container inspection (track/codec/subtitle layout) is a frequent media-dev need with no good in-browser tool.

name: video-metadata-tag-linter
description: Lints container metadata against a required-tags checklist (title, encoder, copyright, etc.) and lists what's missing.
example_prompt: Does this file have all the required metadata tags for delivery?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader reads all format/stream tags via ffprobe in WASM and checks them against the rule set locally.
rationale: Delivery specs mandate metadata fields, and a linter prevents rejections from forgotten title/copyright tags.

name: video-frame-checksum-verify
description: Recomputes per-frame checksums and verifies them against a sidecar framemd5 list to confirm lossless integrity.
example_prompt: Verify this video against its framemd5 sidecar file.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader regenerates framemd5 hashes in WASM and diffs them against the provided list locally.
rationale: Archival and lossless workflows rely on frame-hash verification to prove a copy is bit-exact.

name: video-alignment-tone-detector
description: Detects a 1 kHz alignment tone in the head of the audio and reports its level and duration against slate requirements.
example_prompt: Is there a 1kHz line-up tone at the start of this file?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader runs aspectralstats/astats in WASM to find the dominant head-of-file frequency locally.
rationale: Broadcast slates pair bars with a reference tone, so detecting it completes automated slate conformance.

name: truncated-audio-detector
description: Compares the header/tag-declared duration against the actually decodable length to flag cut-off or incomplete files.
example_prompt: Did this podcast file get cut short during download?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — decodes to the real end-of-stream and diffs against the container's stated duration, all in-browser.
rationale: Truncated files pass casual playback but fail in archives and CMS uploads, so an explicit check saves re-downloads.

name: silent-file-detector
description: Flags files that are entirely silent or below an audible threshold from start to end.
example_prompt: Is this recording completely silent? My mic might have been muted.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — volumedetect/silencedetect confirm an all-silence stream client-side.
rationale: Dead-silent captures (muted mic, wrong input) are a common batch failure that's worth auto-flagging.

name: subsonic-rumble-detector
description: Measures inaudible sub-20Hz energy (HVAC rumble, handling, DC drift) that wastes headroom.
example_prompt: Check this field recording for subsonic rumble.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a low-band FFT energy measurement on PCM runs entirely in-browser.
rationale: Subsonic energy is inaudible on most monitors yet eats headroom and pumps limiters, so flagging it pre-master is valuable.

name: id3-tag-validator
description: Validates ID3v1/ID3v2 structure, frame sizes, text encodings, and version conformance.
example_prompt: Validate the ID3 tags on this MP3 — some players show garbage.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — ID3 frame parsing is pure byte work, no decode or network.
rationale: Malformed ID3 frames cause garbled metadata and rejected uploads that a structural check pinpoints.

name: audio-quality-mos-estimator
description: Runs a no-reference quality model to estimate a perceptual MOS score for speech/music recordings.
example_prompt: Give me a perceptual quality score for this voice recording.
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime — a NISQA-style no-reference MOS model runs in-browser on decoded audio frames.
rationale: A single perceptual score lets non-engineers rank takes and reject low-quality recordings without expert listening.

name: inline-event-handler-scanner
description: Finds inline event-handler attributes (onclick, onload, etc.) and inline style/script that block a strict CSP, listing each location for migration.
example_prompt: List inline event handlers in this HTML that would violate a strict CSP
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM attribute scan over parsed HTML; no network.
rationale: Adopting a strict CSP requires removing exactly these, and a complete inventory makes the migration tractable.

name: duplicate-meta-tag-detector
description: Finds duplicate or conflicting head elements — multiple title, description, canonical, charset, or viewport tags — that confuse crawlers.
example_prompt: Are there any duplicate or conflicting meta tags in this HTML head?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM head scan and grouping by tag identity; offline.
rationale: Duplicate canonicals/descriptions cause real SEO problems and are invisible without tooling.

name: corporate-buzzword-detector
description: Flags business jargon and buzzwords (synergy, leverage, circle back) against a built-in glossary.
example_prompt: Find the corporate buzzwords in this email
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: phrase matching against an embedded buzzword list, fully offline
rationale: Buzzword-heavy text reads as empty, and surfacing the offenders helps tighten professional writing.

name: markdown-table-validator
description: Checks markdown tables for consistent column counts, valid alignment rows, and ragged cells.
example_prompt: Is this markdown table well-formed?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse pipe-delimited rows and compare widths locally
rationale: Malformed markdown tables render as garbage, and a focused validator pinpoints the bad row faster than a full linter.

name: capitalization-consistency-checker
description: Flags recurring terms spelled with inconsistent capitalization (e.g. JavaScript vs Javascript).
example_prompt: Am I capitalizing product names consistently in this doc?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: case-insensitive token grouping and variant comparison locally
rationale: Inconsistent capitalization of brand and technical terms looks unprofessional and is hard to catch by eye across a long doc.

name: word-count-by-section
description: Reports word counts under each heading or section of a document.
example_prompt: How many words are in each section of this report?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: section splitting on headings plus word counting, offline
rationale: Authors balance section lengths, and per-section counts make imbalance obvious without manual tallying.

name: redundant-phrase-detector
description: Flags tautological redundancies such as 'ATM machine' or 'free gift' against a built-in pair list.
example_prompt: Find redundant phrases in this paragraph
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: phrase matching against an embedded redundancy dictionary, no network
rationale: Redundant phrasing slips past authors and a curated detector tightens writing in one pass.

name: mp4-codec-string-extractor
description: Extracts the RFC 6381 codecs string (e.g. avc1.640028,mp4a.40.2) needed for HTML5 MediaSource and canPlayType checks.
example_prompt: Give me the MSE codecs string for this mp4
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: reads sample-description boxes and SPS profile/level bytes directly from the file.
rationale: Web devs building MSE players need this exact string and assembling it by hand from SPS bytes is error-prone.

name: mpegts-pid-inspector
description: Scans an MPEG-TS stream and lists all PIDs, packet counts per PID, PAT/PMT program mappings, and stream types.
example_prompt: List the PIDs and programs in this .ts file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: 188-byte TS packets are parsed in a tight loop over the byte buffer, no decode.
rationale: Broadcast and HLS segment debugging needs a PID/program map and there's no lightweight browser tool for it.

name: webm-cue-points-inspector
description: Extracts a WebM/MKV file's Cues (seek index) and lists cue timestamps and the byte positions they point to.
example_prompt: Show the seek cue points in this webm
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: EBML Cues elements are parsed directly from the byte stream.
rationale: Missing or sparse cue points are why some WebM files seek slowly, and inspecting them pinpoints the issue.

name: av1-obu-inspector
description: Parses an AV1 bitstream into its Open Bitstream Units (OBUs) and lists OBU types, sizes, and sequence-header parameters.
example_prompt: Inspect the OBUs in this AV1 stream
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: OBU framing and the sequence header are bit-parsed from the byte buffer without decoding frames.
rationale: AV1 adoption is rising and there's no accessible browser tool to inspect its bitstream structure.

name: vp9-frame-header-inspector
description: Reads VP9 (super)frame headers and reports frame types, profile, color config, and show-frame flags.
example_prompt: Decode the VP9 frame headers in this file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: VP9 uncompressed headers are bit-parsed from the stream, no full decode required.
rationale: VP9 powers most WebM video and its frame/superframe structure is hard to inspect without specialized tooling.

name: h264-sei-message-extractor
description: Extracts H.264 SEI messages (caption data, picture timing, HDR, user data) and lists their payload types and sizes.
example_prompt: Pull the SEI messages out of this h264 stream
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: SEI NAL units are located and their payload types parsed directly from the bitstream bytes.
rationale: SEI carries CEA-608/708 captions and HDR hints that are otherwise invisible and frequently mishandled in transcodes.

name: video-camera-metadata-extractor
description: Pulls camera make, model, and software/firmware strings from a video's QuickTime/MP4 metadata atoms.
example_prompt: What camera or phone recorded this video?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: the WASM demuxer surfaces udta/meta tag dictionaries parsed locally from the file.
rationale: Provenance checks and asset organization need the recording device, which is buried in container metadata.

name: video-hdr-metadata-inspector
description: Reads HDR10 static metadata (mastering display primaries, MaxCLL, MaxFALL) and HDR transfer characteristics from the stream.
example_prompt: Show the HDR10 mastering metadata for this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: HDR side-data and VUI/SEI fields are parsed by the WASM build from the file locally.
rationale: Missing or wrong HDR metadata is the top cause of washed-out HDR playback and is hard to verify by eye.

name: video-chroma-subsampling-checker
description: Reports the chroma subsampling (4:2:0, 4:2:2, 4:4:4) of a video stream and flags formats unsuitable for chroma-key or print.
example_prompt: What chroma subsampling does this clip use?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: subsampling is encoded in the pixel format read from codec parameters locally.
rationale: 4:2:0 footage keys and grades poorly, so editors need to confirm subsampling before committing to a workflow.

name: subtitle-empty-cue-detector
description: Finds subtitle cues that have valid timing but no text (or only whitespace/markup), which flash blank on screen.
example_prompt: Are there any empty subtitle cues in this file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: scans parsed cue bodies for emptiness locally.
rationale: Empty cues create distracting blank flashes and are a common artifact of automated subtitle pipelines.

name: ixml-reader
description: Locates and pretty-prints the iXML production-metadata chunk from a WAV file (scene, take, track names, project).
example_prompt: Show the iXML production metadata in this field recording
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM extracts and formats the embedded iXML chunk from bytes, fully client-side.
rationale: Location-sound recorders embed iXML that editors need but most apps can't display.

name: upsampled-audio-detector
description: Flags files whose sample rate was inflated (e.g. 44.1k upsampled to 96k) by detecting no energy above the original Nyquist.
example_prompt: Was this 96kHz file genuinely recorded that high or upsampled?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM FFT high-band energy check on PCM (ffmpeg decodes); browser-local.
rationale: Hi-res audio stores are full of upsampled fakes and buyers want to verify what they paid for.

name: stereo-field-balance-meter
description: Reports left/right RMS balance and mid/side energy ratio to quantify how centered and wide a stereo mix is.
example_prompt: Is this mix balanced between left and right, and how wide is it?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM channel-energy DSP on PCM (ffmpeg decodes); browser-local.
rationale: A quick balance/width readout catches lopsided mixes and over-widening before mastering.

name: tuning-reference-detector
description: Estimates the concert-pitch reference (e.g. A4=440 vs 432 Hz) a recording is tuned to from its pitch content.
example_prompt: Is this song tuned to A=440 or A=432?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM pitch-histogram FFT analysis on PCM (ffmpeg decodes); fully local.
rationale: Musicians playing along or remastering need to know a track's true tuning reference.

name: package-lock-analyzer
description: Analyzes an npm/yarn lockfile reporting dependency count, tree depth, duplicate versions, and heaviest subtrees.
example_prompt: Analyze this package-lock.json for duplicate dependencies
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: lockfile JSON/text parsing and graph analysis run on the pasted file client-side
rationale: Spotting duplicated or deeply nested dependencies helps shrink node_modules and audit supply chain.

name: form-autocomplete-auditor
description: Scans HTML form inputs and validates each autocomplete attribute against the spec's token vocabulary, flagging typos and missing tokens on common fields.
example_prompt: Audit the autocomplete attributes on my checkout form's input fields.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — HTML parse plus token validation against the WHATWG autofill list, offline
rationale: Correct autocomplete tokens are an accessibility and UX win that almost everyone sets wrong or omits.

name: tabindex-auditor
description: Scans HTML for tabindex attributes and flags positive values that hijack focus order plus redundant tabindex on natively focusable elements.
example_prompt: Find any tabindex problems in this HTML that would break keyboard navigation.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — HTML attribute scan with rule checks, no server
rationale: Positive tabindex is a classic accessibility anti-pattern that screen-reader users feel immediately.

name: picture-source-analyzer
description: Analyzes a <picture> element's <source> children for media query / type ordering bugs and overlapping or unreachable source conditions.
example_prompt: Check my <picture> with AVIF, WebP, and a JPEG fallback — will the sources match correctly?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — HTML parse plus media-query/type ordering analysis, offline
rationale: Responsive <picture> markup silently picks the wrong source when type/media ordering is off, and it's hard to spot by eye.

name: loading-attribute-auditor
description: Scans img and iframe elements for loading and decoding attributes and flags lazy-loading above-the-fold images or eager loading that hurts LCP.
example_prompt: Audit loading="lazy" usage in my HTML — am I lazy-loading the hero image?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — HTML scan with positional heuristics, no network
rationale: Lazy-loading the LCP image is one of the most common Core Web Vitals regressions and is trivially detectable in markup.

name: theme-color-meta-checker
description: Parses theme-color and color-scheme meta tags, validates the colors, and reports light/dark media-variant coverage for browser UI theming.
example_prompt: Check my <meta name="theme-color"> tags — do I cover both light and dark mode?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — HTML meta parse plus CSS color and media-query validation, fully local
rationale: theme-color and color-scheme drive native browser/PWA chrome theming and are commonly set without the dark-mode variant.

name: exposure-analyzer
description: Analyzes an image's tonal distribution and reports clipped highlights, crushed shadows, and exposure bias.
example_prompt: Is this photo over- or under-exposed? Show me the clipping
loader_feasibility: plain Rust computes the luminance histogram and clip percentages in WASM.
rationale: Photographers want an objective exposure read on a shot before deciding whether to keep or reshoot.

name: video-frame-md5-list
description: Computes a per-frame MD5 hash list (framemd5) for integrity verification and frame-accurate diffing of two encodes.
example_prompt: Generate the per-frame MD5 list for this video so I can verify a re-encode
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader's framemd5 muxer hashes decoded frames in the wasm runtime, no server.
rationale: Per-frame hashes are the canonical way to prove two videos are bit-identical or locate the exact frame where they diverge.

name: kml-placemark-extractor
description: Extracts placemarks, coordinates, and descriptions from a KML file into a structured table.
example_prompt: List all the placemarks and their coordinates from this KML file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML parsing of the KML schema; runs on the local file
rationale: KML exports from Google Earth/Maps are common and users need the raw points as a table for analysis.

name: microdata-extractor
description: Walks itemscope/itemprop microdata in HTML and serializes it to a nested JSON tree.
example_prompt: Turn the schema.org microdata in this HTML into JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM attribute traversal of the supplied DOM tree, no fetch.
rationale: Many sites still use microdata rather than JSON-LD; this surfaces it.

name: microformats2-extractor
description: Parses microformats2 (h-card, h-entry, h-event) markup into the canonical mf2 JSON structure.
example_prompt: Parse the h-card and h-entry microformats from this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM class/property parsing of pasted markup.
rationale: IndieWeb feeds and contact cards rely on mf2 and few tools decode it offline.

name: gha-workflow-parser
description: Parses a GitHub Actions workflow YAML into its triggers, jobs, steps, and the action dependency list.
example_prompt: Break down the jobs and steps in this GitHub Actions workflow.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the workflow YAML and extracts uses/run steps locally.
rationale: Understanding what a CI workflow actually runs (and which third-party actions it pulls) is a frequent review need.

name: safetensors-header-reader
description: Reads a .safetensors file's JSON header to list every tensor with its dtype, shape, and byte offsets.
example_prompt: List the tensors, shapes, and dtypes in this safetensors model file.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads only the leading length-prefixed JSON header, never loading the weights.
rationale: ML practitioners need a model file's tensor map fast, and reading just the header keeps it instant and local.

name: latex-matrix-to-csv
description: Parses a LaTeX bmatrix/pmatrix/array environment into CSV or a numeric 2D array.
example_prompt: Extract the numbers from this \begin{bmatrix}...\end{bmatrix} as CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — string scanning of LaTeX delimiters, no TeX engine needed.
rationale: Pulling a matrix out of a paper or homework PDF into a computable form is otherwise tedious retyping.

name: xkcd-chart
description: Renders your data as a hand-drawn, XKCD-style chart with sketchy lines and jittered axes.
example_prompt: Make an xkcd-style line chart of these monthly signups: Jan 120, Feb 150, Mar 90, Apr 240
loader_feasibility: pyodide — matplotlib's plt.xkcd() context renders to PNG entirely inside the in-browser Python WASM sandbox, no server.
rationale: Directly serves the 'Data Science: The XKCD Edition' / cartoon demand with a fun, shareable, genuinely useful chart style.

name: awesome-list-formatter
description: Parses an awesome-list markdown file, deduplicates entries, and sorts links alphabetically within each section.
example_prompt: Clean up and alphabetize the links in this awesome-list README
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure markdown parsing and string sorting, no network needed.
rationale: Every 'awesome-*' demand term is a curated markdown list that constantly needs tidy/dedup maintenance.

name: smiles-molecule-viewer
description: Parses a SMILES string and draws the 2D molecular structure with atom and bond labels.
example_prompt: Draw the molecule for CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O.
loader_feasibility: pyodide; the RDKit WASM build parses SMILES and emits 2D depiction SVG entirely in-browser.
rationale: Molecule visualization is the entry point for the drug-synergy/polypharmacy demand and is hard to do offline.

name: merge-conflict-marker-finder
description: Scans text/code for leftover Git merge-conflict markers (<<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>) and lists every line that still contains them.
example_prompt: Did I leave any merge conflict markers in this file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line scan for the marker patterns runs client-side
rationale: Accidentally committed conflict markers break builds; a quick scan before pasting/committing catches them.

name: line-ending-checker
description: Reports a file's line-ending style (LF, CRLF, CR, or mixed) and whether it has a UTF-8/UTF-16 BOM, flagging inconsistencies.
example_prompt: Does this file have mixed line endings or a BOM?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM byte scan classifies newline and BOM bytes locally
rationale: Mixed CRLF/LF and stray BOMs cause cross-platform diff noise and shell-script failures that are hard to spot.

name: mixed-indentation-detector
description: Detects lines that mix tabs and spaces, inconsistent indent widths, and indentation that doesn't match the file's dominant style.
example_prompt: Find lines with mixed tabs and spaces in this code
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM per-line leading-whitespace analysis runs in-browser
rationale: Mixed indentation breaks Python and Makefiles outright and a fast detector pinpoints the offending lines.

name: megapixel-limit-checker
description: Computes total megapixels and flags images that exceed a service's decode/upload pixel limit.
example_prompt: Is this image under the 25 megapixel upload limit?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads dimensions from the header and multiplies, no decode needed.
rationale: Pixel-count caps cause opaque upload failures; a megapixel gate explains the rejection in advance.

name: cmyk-jpeg-detector
description: Detects CMYK or YCCK JPEGs (which render wrong or inverted in browsers) and flags them for RGB conversion.
example_prompt: Is this JPEG in CMYK instead of RGB?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the JPEG component/Adobe markers without decoding pixels.
rationale: CMYK JPEGs display with wrong colors on the web and the cause is invisible until checked.

name: icc-profile-checker
description: Detects presence and type of an embedded ICC color profile and flags non-sRGB profiles that may shift colors on the web.
example_prompt: Does this image have a color profile that could shift its colors online?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans the file for ICC profile markers/atoms locally.
rationale: Non-sRGB profiles cause colors to look different in browsers and the culprit is invisible without inspection.

name: image-bit-depth-checker
description: Reports an image's per-channel bit depth and checks whether 16-bit data can be reduced to 8-bit without visible loss.
example_prompt: Is this a 16-bit image, and can I safely make it 8-bit?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads bit depth from the header and samples for value spread client-side.
rationale: Unneeded 16-bit depth doubles file size and detecting it enables a safe reduction.

name: jpeg-blockiness-detector
description: Measures 8x8 DCT block-edge discontinuities to score JPEG compression blockiness/artifact level.
example_prompt: How blocky is this JPEG from compression?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes pixels and computes block-boundary energy client-side.
rationale: An objective blockiness score flags over-compressed images that need a higher-quality source.

name: seamless-tile-checker
description: Compares opposite edges of a texture to score how seamlessly it tiles and highlights visible seams.
example_prompt: Will this texture tile seamlessly?
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute samples and compares wrapped edge pixels on the GPU client-side.
rationale: Seam detection is tedious by hand and an objective edge-match score saves trial-and-error tiling.

name: normal-map-validator
description: Validates that an image is a usable tangent-space normal map by checking it's bluish and that vectors are near-unit-length.
example_prompt: Is this actually a valid normal map?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes pixels and computes vector magnitudes per texel in-browser.
rationale: Mislabeled or unnormalized normal maps cause wrong lighting and a validator catches them before import.

name: video-faststart-checker
description: Inspects an MP4's box order to report whether the moov atom precedes mdat, i.e. whether the file is web fast-start ready.
example_prompt: Is this MP4 ready to stream progressively from the web?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: only the ISO-BMFF box headers need parsing, no full decode, so it is instant in-browser.
rationale: A trailing moov atom forces full download before playback starts; checking is far cheaper than blindly remuxing.

name: video-dual-mono-checker
description: Detects when a stereo track is actually dual-mono (left and right channels identical), which usually signals a routing mistake.
example_prompt: Is this stereo video really just mono in both channels?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: astats per-channel correlation runs in ffmpeg.wasm in-browser.
rationale: Dual-mono masquerading as stereo wastes bitrate and indicates a broken mixdown that should be fixed.

name: broadcast-levels-checker
description: Scans luma and chroma signal statistics to flag out-of-gamut or broadcast-illegal levels that exceed legal range.
example_prompt: Is this video broadcast-safe on its color levels?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: the signalstats filter computes min/max/range per frame in ffmpeg.wasm client-side.
rationale: Broadcast QC rejects out-of-range levels, and creators rarely have a tool to check before delivery.

name: video-codec-compliance-checker
description: Validates a video's codec, profile, level, and pixel format against a target delivery spec and lists every mismatch.
example_prompt: Does this file meet H.264 High profile, Level 4.0?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: ffprobe codec/profile/level fields from ffmpeg.wasm are compared client-side.
rationale: Profile/level mismatches cause playback failures on constrained devices and fail strict ingest pipelines.

name: hdr10-metadata-validator
description: Checks an HDR video for required HDR10 mastering-display metadata and MaxCLL/MaxFALL values and reports what's missing.
example_prompt: Validate the HDR10 metadata on this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: ffprobe side_data for mastering display and content light is read in ffmpeg.wasm client-side.
rationale: Incomplete HDR10 metadata makes HDR content tone-map incorrectly or fall back to SDR on TVs.

name: video-keyframe-interval-checker
description: Measures the spacing between keyframes (GOP length) across a video and flags intervals that violate a streaming requirement.
example_prompt: Check this video's keyframe interval for HLS streaming
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: ffprobe frame pict_type data from ffmpeg.wasm is analyzed client-side.
rationale: Adaptive streaming requires regular keyframe spacing for clean segment boundaries, and irregular GOPs break it.

name: video-timecode-continuity-checker
description: Reads embedded SMPTE timecode and verifies it starts where expected and increments continuously without jumps.
example_prompt: Verify the embedded timecode on this clip is continuous
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: ffprobe timecode metadata and frame counts from ffmpeg.wasm are checked client-side.
rationale: Broken or discontinuous timecode breaks conform and round-trip workflows in professional post.

name: phase-correlation-checker
description: Computes the stereo phase-correlation coefficient over time and flags sustained out-of-phase regions that risk cancellation.
example_prompt: Check this stereo file for phase problems
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: windowed L·R correlation over decoded stereo PCM, simple per-block math client-side
rationale: Out-of-phase stereo cancels on mono playback (clubs, phones) and is a top mastering reject reason.

name: fake-stereo-detector
description: Detects dual-mono and fake-stereo files where both channels are identical or near-identical, reporting the inter-channel difference level.
example_prompt: Is this 'stereo' file actually just mono duplicated?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: L−R difference energy over decoded PCM, a few lines of arithmetic client-side
rationale: Many 'stereo' downloads are upmixed mono; a quick check exposes wasted file size and false labeling.

name: mains-hum-detector
description: Detects 50/60 Hz mains hum and its harmonics via FFT and reports hum level relative to program audio.
example_prompt: Does this recording have electrical hum, 50 or 60 Hz?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: FFT (rustfft) on decoded PCM, then peak-energy check at mains frequencies, no server
rationale: Ground-loop hum ruins recordings and identifying 50 vs 60 Hz tells the user exactly what notch filter to apply.

name: bwf-metadata-validator
description: Validates Broadcast Wave Format bext-chunk fields (timecode origin, coding history, UMID, loudness fields) for completeness and broadcast-delivery conformance.
example_prompt: Check the BWF metadata on this file meets delivery spec
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse and validate the bext chunk fields from raw bytes client-side
rationale: Broadcast and film delivery rejects WAVs with missing or malformed BWF fields; this verifies them before handoff.

name: vbr-header-validator
description: Checks an MP3 for a Xing/Info/VBRI header and verifies its frame count and byte fields match the actual stream so seeking and duration stay accurate.
example_prompt: Does this VBR MP3 have a valid Xing header for accurate seeking?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: locate and parse the VBR header, then walk frames to confirm counts, all on the file bytes
rationale: A missing or wrong Xing header makes VBR MP3s report wrong length and seek inaccurately in every player.

name: gapless-metadata-checker
description: Verifies gapless-playback metadata (encoder delay/padding, iTunSMPB, LAME info tag) is present and consistent so album tracks join seamlessly.
example_prompt: Check whether this album's tracks have proper gapless playback metadata
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse encoder-delay tags from headers and cross-check against frame counts client-side
rationale: Missing delay/padding metadata inserts audible gaps between continuous-album tracks; this verifies it before publishing.

name: stereo-width-checker
description: Measures mid/side energy ratio and per-band stereo width, flagging mixes that are too narrow (collapsing to mono) or too wide (phase risk).
example_prompt: Measure the stereo width of this master and flag any problem bands
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: mid/side decomposition + per-band energy over decoded PCM, pure DSP in WASM
rationale: Excessive or collapsed stereo width fails on different playback systems, and a per-band width report quantifies it.

name: markdown-image-alt-checker
description: Finds markdown images that are missing or have empty alt text and reports their locations.
example_prompt: Which images in this markdown are missing alt text?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; parse image syntax and inspect alt fields locally.
rationale: An easy accessibility win that's tedious to audit manually in long documents.

name: image-symmetry-analyzer
description: Scores horizontal, vertical, and rotational symmetry of an image.
example_prompt: How symmetric is this logo?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM mirrors and diffs decoded pixels to compute symmetry scores locally.
rationale: Symmetry scoring helps validate logos, patterns, and balanced compositions.

name: video-bitrate-timeline-graph
description: Graphs instantaneous bitrate over the video's duration to reveal spikes that can stall playback.
example_prompt: Plot the bitrate over time and show me the spikes
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg reports per-packet sizes/timestamps in wasm; plain Rust bins them into a per-second curve locally.
rationale: A bitrate curve exposes streaming-hostile spikes that a single average-bitrate check cannot.

name: video-vectorscope-image
description: Renders a vectorscope from a frame or segment to inspect hue and saturation distribution.
example_prompt: Generate a vectorscope for this clip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg `vectorscope` filter produces the scope image from decoded chroma entirely in wasm.
rationale: Colorists rely on vectorscopes to check skin-tone lines and color balance, and this brings that scope to the browser.

name: video-shot-type-classifier
description: Classifies each shot as close-up, medium, or wide based on subject scale and reports the breakdown.
example_prompt: Classify the shots in this video as close-up, medium, or wide
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg samples one frame per shot, onnx-runtime runs a small classifier/face-scale model in-browser; all local.
rationale: A shot-type breakdown gives filmmakers and editors quick coverage analysis without manual logging.

name: effective-bit-depth-analyzer
description: Detects the true used bit depth of PCM audio, exposing 16-bit content padded into a 24-bit container.
example_prompt: Is this 24-bit file actually using all 24 bits?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM inspects the least-significant-bit activity across samples directly in the browser
rationale: Reveals fake high-res masters and wasted storage from upconverted files.

name: wav-chunk-inspector
description: Lists every RIFF chunk in a WAV file with sizes and decodes fmt/fact/cue/list metadata.
example_prompt: Show me all the chunks inside this WAV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the RIFF container structure byte-by-byte with no server
rationale: Exposes nonstandard chunks, broken sizes, and hidden metadata that break some players.

name: vorbis-comment-reader
description: Dumps all Vorbis comment key/value tags from FLAC/Ogg/Opus files as structured JSON.
example_prompt: List every tag in this Opus file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the Vorbis comment block without decoding audio, fully client-side
rationale: Vorbis comments are free-form, so a faithful raw dump catches nonstandard tags that editors hide.

name: channel-polarity-checker
description: Detects inverted polarity between the two channels of a stereo file or between two takes.
example_prompt: Is one channel of this file polarity-inverted?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM cross-correlates channels at zero lag on decoded PCM locally
rationale: A flipped channel causes hollow mono sound and is easy to fix once detected.

name: vibrato-analyzer
description: Measures vibrato rate (Hz) and depth (cents) from a sustained pitched note.
example_prompt: Analyze the vibrato in this violin note
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tracks the pitch contour then analyzes its modulation spectrum in-browser
rationale: Objective vibrato metrics help singers and instrumentalists evaluate technique.

name: sample-value-histogram
description: Plots a histogram of PCM sample amplitudes to reveal clipping plateaus, DC bias, and quantization.
example_prompt: Show me the sample amplitude histogram for this WAV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM bins decoded sample values and renders the histogram PNG client-side
rationale: The amplitude distribution exposes truncation, dithering, and clipping that level meters miss.

name: gzip-member-inspector
description: Parses gzip member headers to report original filename, modification time, OS byte, extra fields, and stored CRC/size.
example_prompt: What metadata is in this .gz file's header?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: gzip header is a small fixed structure, parsed without decompressing, client-side
rationale: Gzip headers carry metadata (mtime, original name) that is otherwise invisible.

name: tiff-tag-inspector
description: Parses a TIFF file's IFD chain and lists all directory tags with IDs, types, counts, and decoded values.
example_prompt: Dump all the IFD tags in this TIFF
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: TIFF IFD parsing is endian-aware byte-offset work, no codec, runs client-side
rationale: TIFF tags carry critical scanning/geo metadata that is opaque without an IFD reader.

name: ifc-inspector
description: Parses an IFC/STEP BIM model and lists building elements (walls, doors, spaces) with counts and properties.
example_prompt: What's in this IFC file — how many walls, doors, and storeys?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: IFC/STEP is a text schema parsed locally (large but CPU-only).
rationale: xeokit's core audience is BIM/IFC, and a private offline IFC summary is valuable since these models are confidential.

name: stix-bundle-inspector
description: Parses STIX 2.x JSON bundles into a readable list of indicators, relationships, and threat objects.
example_prompt: Summarize the indicators and relationships in this STIX bundle
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: STIX is JSON parsed and graphed from the upload, fully local.
rationale: STIX is the lingua franca of threat intel (IntelMQ) and a quick inspector beats reading raw JSON.

name: wifi-capture-analyzer
description: Parses Kismet netxml and wardriving captures to list detected access points, SSIDs, channels, encryption, and GPS coordinates.
example_prompt: List the access points and encryption from this kismet capture
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: XML/log parsing of the uploaded file, no radio access needed.
rationale: Turns Kismet survey output into a readable AP inventory without standing up the Kismet stack.

name: apfs-volume-parser
description: Parses an APFS container superblock and volume metadata to list volumes, snapshots, and file records read-only.
example_prompt: List the volumes and snapshots in this APFS image
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: APFS on-disk structures are parsed directly, with no mounting or FUSE.
rationale: Brings APFS-Fuse's read access to macOS images into the browser without kernel mounts.

name: hyperloglog
description: Estimates the number of distinct elements in a large stream with HyperLogLog.
example_prompt: Approximate the distinct-user count from this big id list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM maintains the register array and computes the cardinality estimate locally.
rationale: Cardinality estimation is a key streaming algorithm from Mining Massive Datasets / Streaming Systems.

name: cosmos-address-convert
description: Re-encodes a Cosmos bech32 address to a different chain prefix (e.g. cosmos→osmo) while preserving the underlying key.
example_prompt: convert cosmos1abc... to an osmosis address
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bech32 decode then re-encode with a new HRP, offline.
rationale: The same account has different addresses per Cosmos chain, so prefix conversion is a frequent IBC-era need.

name: streaming-window-aggregate
description: Computes tumbling and sliding window aggregations (counts, sums, averages) over a time-series CSV.
example_prompt: Give me 5-minute tumbling-window sums of this event log's amount column
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM streams the rows and maintains window state in memory; no streaming engine required.
rationale: Materialize/noria/RisingWave demand centers on windowed rollups, which are perfectly computable locally over an uploaded series.

name: nes-rom-info
description: Parses an uploaded .nes ROM's iNES/NES 2.0 header and reports mapper, PRG/CHR sizes, mirroring, region and trainer flags.
example_prompt: What mapper and sizes does this NES ROM use?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — reads a 16-byte header from the uploaded file buffer, no decoding pipeline.
rationale: Identifying ROM mapper/region is the first question every NES emulation/dev task needs answered.

name: n64-rom-header
description: Parses an N64 ROM header (title, region, version, CIC/checksum) and detects byte order, offering z64/v64/n64 conversion.
example_prompt: Identify this N64 ROM and tell me its byte order
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — header parsing and 16/32-bit byte-swapping are pure buffer operations.
rationale: N64 ROM byte-order confusion (z64 vs v64) is a constant pain point that gopher64 users hit.

name: doom-wad-inspector
description: Parses a DOOM WAD and lists its lumps, maps, textures, flats, sprites and music with sizes and offsets.
example_prompt: List everything inside this DOOM WAD
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the WAD directory is a flat lump table read straight from the uploaded file.
rationale: WAD spelunking is core to the active Doom-modding scene that cristicbz/rust-doom taps into.

name: mrpack-inspector
description: Parses a Modrinth .mrpack modpack and lists its mods, versions, dependencies, and download sizes.
example_prompt: What mods are in this .mrpack file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a .mrpack is just a ZIP with a JSON index; zip+serde decoding runs entirely client-side.
rationale: Minecraft players want to audit a modpack's contents before installing it, motivated by tools like Ferium.

name: vox-to-obj
description: Converts a MagicaVoxel .vox model into a greedy-meshed OBJ with per-voxel colors.
example_prompt: Convert this .vox model to an OBJ mesh
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — dot_vox parsing plus mesh emission is pure compute, fully client-side.
rationale: Voxel artists (Veloren-style worlds) need their models in OBJ for engines that don't read .vox.

name: quake-pak-extractor
description: Lists and extracts files from a Quake/Half-Life .pak archive without external tools.
example_prompt: List the files inside this .pak archive
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the PAK directory format is parsed with simple binary reads, fully client-side.
rationale: Retro-FPS modders (rust-quake) need to peek inside and unpack legacy game archives in the browser.

name: rop-gadget-finder
description: Scans a binary or hex blob for ROP gadgets ending in ret/jmp and lists their addresses.
example_prompt: Find ROP gadgets in this binary
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: disassembly plus gadget scanning are pure CPU work over uploaded bytes.
rationale: Gadget discovery is core to binary exploitation, the research area 0xdea's tools serve, and works fully offline.

name: ldif-parser
description: Parses and validates LDIF, rendering users, groups, and attributes as a readable table.
example_prompt: Parse this LDIF and show me the users and their groups
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — LDIF is a line-oriented text format parsed entirely on CPU.
rationale: LDAP/LLDAP admins need a quick offline way to inspect directory exports without uploading sensitive data.

name: cargo-lock-vuln-checker
description: Parses a Cargo.lock and flags dependencies with known vulnerabilities against a bundled RustSec advisory snapshot.
example_prompt: Check this Cargo.lock for vulnerable crate versions: <paste lock file>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — TOML parsing plus an embedded RustSec advisory dataset; no network or server needed, the advisory DB ships inside the WASM module.
rationale: Brings cargo-audit's core value (vuln detection) to anyone pasting a lockfile, with zero install and full privacy.

name: hashcat-rule-applier
description: Applies hashcat-style mangling rules to a wordlist to expand it into candidate passwords.
example_prompt: Apply these hashcat rules to my wordlist <paste rules and words>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure string-transformation rule engine over the pasted inputs.
rationale: A common credential-testing prep step (the authoscope theme) that is pure deterministic computation, ideal for offline use.

name: openapi-security-linter
description: Lints an OpenAPI/Swagger spec for security problems like missing auth, no rate limiting, and weak schemes.
example_prompt: Audit this OpenAPI spec for security issues <paste spec>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — YAML/JSON parsing and rule evaluation; the whole spec stays in the browser.
rationale: Directly reproduces Cherrybomb's spec-audit value with no server, perfect for reviewing specs privately.

name: file-dedup-analyzer
description: Splits uploaded files into content-defined chunks via a rolling hash and reports shared/duplicate regions and dedup ratio, the way restic dedups backups.
example_prompt: Find the duplicate chunks across these two backup archives and tell me the dedup ratio
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — rolling-hash (buzhash) chunking plus SHA-256 are pure CPU over uploaded bytes with no I/O or daemon.
rationale: Lets users see storage redundancy and dedup potential without installing restic or running a backup server.

name: cargo-toml-editor
description: Adds, removes, renames, or version-bumps dependencies in a pasted Cargo.toml and returns the rewritten file with formatting preserved.
example_prompt: Add serde 1.0 with the derive feature and bump tokio to 1.40 in this Cargo.toml
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using a TOML parser/serializer; pure in-memory text edit, no registry or network call needed
rationale: cargo-edit's most-used operation is hand-editing dependency tables, which is error-prone to do manually and trivially local.

name: license-text-identifier
description: Identifies the SPDX license of a pasted LICENSE file by fingerprinting it against bundled license templates and returns the SPDX id plus confidence.
example_prompt: What license is this LICENSE file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with normalized-text similarity against an embedded SPDX template set; offline corpus, no registry lookup
rationale: cargo-license's core need — knowing what a license actually is — reduces to local text matching when given the file.

name: strace-log-summarizer
description: Parses strace/tracexec-style syscall or exec logs and summarizes which files, processes, and network calls a program made.
example_prompt: Summarize what this strace log accessed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM for the line parsing and aggregation, with optional transformers-js for a natural-language summary — all runs in the browser.
rationale: tracexec and strace output is verbose, and a local summary of files, execs, and sockets touched is far more actionable than scrolling raw lines.

name: c-header-to-rust-ffi
description: Parses C declarations from a header and emits matching Rust `extern "C"` function bindings, `#[repr(C)]` structs, enums, and type aliases.
example_prompt: Generate Rust FFI bindings for this C header: `typedef struct { int x; int y; } Point; int dist(const Point* a, const Point* b);`
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a hand-rolled C-declaration parser does text-in/text-out codegen, so it runs fully client-side without libclang (which bindgen normally needs); covers the common declaration subset.
rationale: rust-bindgen is the single most-demanded term here, and a browser-local 'paste a C header, get Rust bindings' tool removes a heavy native toolchain dependency.

name: jni-header-generator
description: Generates `javah`-style C JNI function prototypes (correct `Java_pkg_Class_method` name mangling and `JNIEXPORT`/`JNICALL` signatures) from a Java class with native methods.
example_prompt: Generate the JNI C prototypes for `package com.app; class Crypto { native byte[] hash(String input); }`
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse the Java method declarations and apply the documented JNI name-mangling rules (`_1`, `_0xxxx`) to emit C prototypes; pure text codegen.
rationale: modern JDKs dropped the standalone `javah` tool, so devs binding Rust to Java (rjni, j4rs, drrb/java-rust-example) need exactly this prototype scaffolding.

name: csharp-pinvoke-generator
description: Turns a C function signature into a C# `[DllImport]` P/Invoke declaration with correctly marshalled parameter and return types.
example_prompt: Generate a C# P/Invoke for `int compress(const unsigned char* src, size_t len, unsigned char* dst);`
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: map C primitive/pointer types to .NET marshalling types via a lookup table and emit the attribute; pure text transformation.
rationale: csbindgen exists precisely because hand-writing P/Invoke signatures with correct marshalling is error-prone, and a quick in-browser generator covers the common cases.

name: model-to-code
description: Converts a trained scikit-learn model (linear, tree, or boosting) into standalone code with no ML dependencies.
example_prompt: Convert this trained sklearn LogisticRegression into plain Python code
loader_feasibility: pyodide — m2cgen and scikit-learn run in the in-browser Python WASM sandbox so model weights never upload.
rationale: m2cgen lets you ship models as pure code, and doing it client-side keeps proprietary weights private.

name: token-cost-estimator
description: Estimates the API dollar cost of a request from input/output token counts and a model's pricing.
example_prompt: Estimate the cost of 50k input and 10k output tokens on gpt-4o.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure arithmetic against an embedded pricing table, no calls out.
rationale: Cost forecasting is a constant need for anyone scripting LLM calls (async-openai users).

name: onnx-model-inspector
description: Inspects an ONNX model's inputs, outputs, op set, and parameter count without running it.
example_prompt: What are the input shapes and op set of this .onnx model?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the ONNX protobuf graph metadata, no inference required.
rationale: Developers integrating models constantly need to check tensor shapes and ops before wiring inference (tensorflow/rust).

name: midi-piano-roll-image
description: Renders a MIDI file as a piano-roll PNG showing notes laid out across pitch and time.
example_prompt: Render this MIDI file as a piano-roll image.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (nodi to parse plus a Rust image encoder) draws the roll in memory.
rationale: Gives a visual overview of a MIDI composition with no external software.

name: genomic-interval-overlap
description: Computes intersections, unions, and overlap counts between two sets of genomic intervals (BED-style start/end coordinates).
example_prompt: Find which intervals in set A overlap set B from these two BED lists.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: interval-tree/sort-sweep computation, the browser-local equivalent of polars-bio operations.
rationale: Interval overlap (bedtools-style intersect) is one of the most common genomics operations and maps directly to polars-bio demand.

name: schnorr-sign
description: Generates sr25519/Ristretto Schnorr keypairs and produces or verifies Schnorr signatures.
example_prompt: sign this message with an sr25519 schnorr key
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via schnorrkel, the Ristretto-based Schnorr crate (used by Polkadot/Substrate) that targets wasm32 natively.
rationale: sr25519 is the signature scheme for Substrate/Polkadot accounts, so chain developers need local sign/verify tooling.

name: grid-transform
description: Transposes, rotates, flips, or reshapes a 2D grid/table of values.
example_prompt: Transpose this table so rows become columns.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a becheran/grid-style 2D structure manipulated in-memory.
rationale: Reorienting tabular/grid data is a frequent need that's surprisingly fiddly to do manually.

name: identicon-generator
description: Generates a deterministic geometric avatar/identicon from any username, email or string.
example_prompt: Make an identicon avatar for 'joris@suppers.ai'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM hashes the input and draws the pattern locally.
rationale: Default avatars for apps and profiles are widely needed and fully deterministic offline.

name: parse-user-agent
description: Parses a User-Agent string into structured browser, engine, OS, and device fields.
example_prompt: Parse this user agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0 Safari/537.36
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM with bundled UA pattern tables; pure string matching, no network or model, so it runs fully in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: User-agent parsing is a constant log-analysis and analytics chore that is fully deterministic offline.

name: justfile-generator
description: Scaffolds a justfile (or Makefile) from a list of described tasks.
example_prompt: Make a justfile with build, test, and deploy recipes
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM emits the recipe syntax from structured input locally.
rationale: Turns the 'just'/foy task-runner demand into a quick scaffolding helper.

name: fake-log-generator
description: Generates synthetic log lines in Apache CLF/combined, Nginx, syslog (RFC5424), and JSON formats for testing.
example_prompt: Generate 200 fake Apache combined log lines
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM uses a seeded RNG and format templates to emit lines with no external service.
rationale: flog's whole purpose is seeding log pipelines/parsers under test, and a local generator is instant and reproducible.

name: wikilink-graph
description: Reads a set of notes, extracts [[wikilinks]], and renders the note-to-note link structure as a Mermaid graph.
example_prompt: Build a link graph of my Obsidian-style notes from these files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — link extraction and Mermaid string emission are pure text operations with no server.
rationale: rucola's whole value is visualizing a wikilinked knowledge base, which is impossible from the CLI alone but trivial to render in chat.

name: broken-wikilink-finder
description: Cross-checks every [[wikilink]] in a note set against existing note titles and reports the dangling ones.
example_prompt: Find broken wikilinks across these markdown notes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — set membership over parsed link targets, no I/O beyond the pasted notes.
rationale: Link rot silently breaks rucola/notesmd vaults, and there is no built-in validator in the CLIs.

name: slide-outline-extractor
description: Reads a markdown or HTML deck and returns a numbered outline of every slide title.
example_prompt: Give me the outline of this presentation
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — slide-boundary and heading detection over pasted text, fully local.
rationale: mdp/slides users review structure and ordering, and an outline is the fastest way to sanity-check a deck.

name: command-cheatsheet
description: Looks up a command and shows the handful of practical example invocations people actually use, tldr-style.
example_prompt: Show me practical examples for the `ffmpeg` command
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a bundled tldr/cheat corpus as a static asset with an in-WASM lookup index — no network access needed.
rationale: tldr, navi, and Linux Command Library all express the same demand for example-first command reference, and a bundled corpus is fully offline.

name: content-chunk-dedup
description: Runs content-defined chunking over files to report how much space deduplication would save and which chunks repeat.
example_prompt: How much would these files dedupe against each other?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: FastCDC chunking plus chunk hashing over the buffers, no external service.
rationale: The deduplication engine shared by Restic, Borg, bup, bupstash, and zbackup, turned into an analyzer.

name: language-flashcards
description: Builds a quiz from your vocabulary list, auto-translating terms into a target language and drilling you with spaced prompts.
example_prompt: quiz me on these English words translated to Spanish: dog, house, water
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — runs an opus-mt translation model in-browser to generate cards, then a local quiz loop, no server
rationale: Maps the vague 'Language-games' demand into a concrete, genuinely useful study tool using on-device translation.

name: regex-flavor-converter
description: Translates a regex between PCRE, ECMAScript, Python re, Java Pattern, Perl, and Go flavors, fixing syntax differences.
example_prompt: Convert this Python regex (?P<year>\d{4}) to Java and JavaScript syntax
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses the AST and re-serializes per flavor's grammar (named-group syntax, escapes, flags); pure transform.
rationale: Maps the PCRE / ECMAScript 6 / Perl / Java Pattern / Scala Regex / Python re cluster into one genuinely useful porting tool.

name: disqus-export-convert
description: Converts a Disqus comment XML export into clean JSON or Markdown for migration.
example_prompt: Convert my Disqus export XML into JSON I can import elsewhere
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML parser (quick-xml) reshaping the export locally
rationale: Leaving Disqus is a real, frequent task, and converting the export locally keeps the comment archive off third-party servers.

name: form-response-completeness-checker
description: Scans a responses CSV against a list of required questions and flags incomplete, blank, or partially answered submissions row by row.
example_prompt: Find the responses in this survey CSV that skipped required questions
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM checks parsed rows for empty required cells; all logic local, nothing uploaded.
rationale: Required-field enforcement on hosted forms is imperfect, and cleaning incomplete responses before analysis is a recurring manual chore.

name: payout-splitter
description: Splits a payout pool across recipients by fixed shares, percentages or weights, applying per-recipient fees and rounding remainders fairly.
example_prompt: split $1,000 among 3 contractors at 50/30/20 with a 2% fee each
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — money-safe weighted division with remainder allocation, the payout math Trolley does, no server.
rationale: Fairly splitting a total without rounding leftover cents is a recurring marketplace/payout problem best handled deterministically.

name: cheatsheet-card-maker
description: Turns a list of command-to-description pairs into a grouped, printable cheatsheet card in Markdown or HTML.
example_prompt: Make a printable git cheatsheet from these commands and descriptions, grouped by topic.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: grouping and layout of user-supplied entries is pure formatting with no reference database needed.
rationale: cheatshh, cmdCompass, and gocheat show steady demand for personal cheatsheets, and formatting user content avoids any bundled-data feasibility problem.

name: acronym-extractor
description: Detects acronyms and matches them to their in-text expansions.
example_prompt: List the acronyms in this report and what they stand for
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — capitalization and parenthetical-definition pattern matching, offline.
rationale: Acronym/definition extraction is a recurring need for technical and scientific document readers.

name: conll-folia-converter
description: Converts linguistic annotations between CoNLL-U, FoLiA XML, and JSON.
example_prompt: Convert this CoNLL-U file to JSON.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: deterministic format parsers and serializers, no dependencies.
rationale: foliapy, PyNLPl, and jPTDP interoperability demand for linguistic annotation pipelines.

name: ngram-collocation-analyzer
description: Computes n-gram frequencies and statistically significant word collocations in a corpus.
example_prompt: Show the most common bigrams and trigrams in this text.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM counts n-grams and computes PMI/log-likelihood scores locally; pure computation.
