rationale: N-gram and collocation analysis is a core MeTA feature, useful for corpus linguistics, SEO and phrase mining without any backend.

name: script-detector
description: Identifies the writing systems (Latin, Cyrillic, Han, Arabic, Devanagari, etc.) present in a text and their proportions.
example_prompt: Which scripts are mixed in this string: 'Hello мир 世界 مرحبا'?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM walking Unicode script blocks per code point, no model or network needed.
rationale: Script detection is distinct from language ID and is essential for routing multilingual content to the right downstream tool.

name: corpus-keyness-comparison
description: Compares two corpora and reports words that are statistically over- or under-represented in one versus the other.
example_prompt: Compare these two sets of tweets and tell me which words distinguish them.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM log-likelihood/keyness computation over two frequency tables, no network.
rationale: Keyness comparison is exactly the comparative corpus analysis corporaexplorer enables, all doable locally.

name: nlp-dataset-inspector
description: Validates an NLP dataset file and summarizes token counts and label distribution.
example_prompt: give me stats on this JSONL training set
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing and aggregation over the uploaded file, entirely in-browser.
rationale: Quick dataset QA before training, motivated by nlp-datasets/gensim-data demand.

name: korean-pos-tagger
description: Tokenizes Korean text into morphemes and tags their parts of speech.
example_prompt: tag the morphemes in 나는 학교에 갔다
loader_feasibility: transformers-js token-classification with a Korean (KLUE/KoBERT-derived) ONNX model runs client-side; exporting the model is the main effort.
rationale: Brings KoNLPy/Mecab-style Korean morphological analysis to the browser with no server dependency.

name: apk-size-breakdown
description: Analyzes an APK's ZIP entries and groups them by type (dex code, resources, assets, native libs, META-INF) with per-group and per-ABI size totals.
example_prompt: Break down what's taking up space inside this APK
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pure ZIP central-directory walk and byte tallying, no decompression of payloads required and no server.
rationale: App-store and debloat users care about download size and want to know whether native libs or assets dominate before installing.

name: aab-bundle-lister
description: Lists the contents and split configuration of an Android App Bundle (.aab) or split-APK set (.apks), showing base, density, language, and ABI splits.
example_prompt: What splits are inside this .apks file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: both formats are ZIP containers, so listing entries and reading split metadata is a local ZIP walk.
rationale: Accrescent and Aurora Store deliver split bundles, and users want to understand which device-specific pieces a set contains.

name: type-specimen-generator
description: Renders a specimen sheet (waterfall sizes and pangrams) as an SVG from an uploaded font file.
example_prompt: Make a specimen sheet for this OTF showing it at several sizes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (ttf-parser glyph outlines emitted as SVG paths) — renders vector specimens offline without system font installation.
rationale: Lets designers preview a downloaded libre font without installing it, the showcase that font foundries provide online.

name: conversational-form-flow-builder
description: Builds a TypeBot-style conversational form flow as structured JSON with branching steps from a described question sequence.
example_prompt: Build a chatbot flow that asks for name, then budget, then branches on budget over 1000
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (flow-graph construction from the step spec) — offline JSON generation, no TypeBot server.
rationale: Directly reproduces TypeBot's conversational-form output as a portable JSON flow you own and can host anywhere.

name: hosts-blocklist-merger
description: Merges, deduplicates, and normalizes multiple hosts-format blocklists into a single clean Pi-hole-ready file.
example_prompt: Merge these three hosts blocklists and remove duplicates and comments
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (text parsing, dedup, normalization) — pure offline text processing.
rationale: The anti-telemetry/self-hosted crowd assembles blocklists constantly, and merging them is a deterministic local text job.

name: threema-contact-parse
description: Parses a Threema contact QR payload into its 8-character Threema ID and 32-byte public key, validating both.
example_prompt: Parse this Threema contact code: 3mid:ECHOECHO,xxxxxxxx...publickey
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — splits the QR string and hex-validates the key locally.
rationale: Verifying a scanned Threema contact's key by hand is otherwise error-prone.

name: xmpp-stanza-format
description: Validates and pretty-prints an XMPP XML stanza (message/presence/iq), flagging malformed XML and missing required attributes.
example_prompt: Format and check this XMPP stanza: <message to='a@b'><body>hi</body></message>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — XML parsing and indentation done in-browser.
rationale: Debugging raw XMPP streams is painful without a stanza-aware formatter.

name: deltachat-invite-parse
description: Parses a DeltaChat OPENPGP4FPR / i.delta.chat invite link into its fingerprint, address, and group-join parameters.
example_prompt: What does this Delta Chat invite link contain? https://i.delta.chat/#FINGERPRINT&a=alice@example.org
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — URL/fragment parsing only, fully offline.
rationale: Lets users verify which key fingerprint and address an invite actually encodes before scanning it.

name: signal-safety-number
description: Computes a Signal-style 60-digit safety number from two identity public keys and stable identifiers using Signal's iterated SHA-512 fingerprint scheme.
example_prompt: Generate the Signal safety number for these two identity keys and UUIDs ...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — 5200-round SHA-512 hashing runs locally, no keys uploaded.
rationale: Reproducing the safety-number algorithm offline lets developers and auditors verify Signal's key-comparison code.

name: ens-namehash
description: Normalizes an ENS name and computes its keccak256 namehash node, the value used by Status and Ethereum resolvers.
example_prompt: What's the ENS namehash of alice.eth?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — UTS-46 normalization + keccak256 hashing run in-browser.
rationale: Status usernames and any ENS integration need the namehash, and computing it locally avoids trusting a remote resolver.

name: autocrypt-header-parse
description: Parses and validates an Autocrypt email header into its address, prefer-encrypt setting, and decoded key material.
example_prompt: Decode this Autocrypt header: addr=a@b.com; prefer-encrypt=mutual; keydata=...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — header attribute parsing + base64 decode, no network.
rationale: Autocrypt drives DeltaChat's opportunistic encryption, and developers need to inspect these headers when debugging key exchange.

name: osm-poi-extractor
description: Parses an OSM XML export and extracts points of interest (amenities, shops, etc.) as a list or GeoJSON.
example_prompt: Pull all the cafes and restaurants out of this OSM export as GeoJSON
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM XML parse + tag filtering; runs on the uploaded file directly.
rationale: OSM XML extracts are bulky and tag-heavy; turning them into a filtered POI list is a common offline GIS task.

name: privacy-video-embed-builder
description: Generates a no-cookie privacy embed iframe (Invidious/Piped) for a given video URL with options for autoplay, start time, and size.
example_prompt: Make me a Piped embed iframe for this video that starts at 1:30
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: builds an HTML/iframe string from parsed parameters, no network.
rationale: Bloggers and PeerTube/Invidious users embedding video want a tracking-free embed snippet, which is a pure URL-to-markup transform.

name: lemmy-community-export-analyzer
description: Parses a Lemmy/Kbin subscription or settings export to list communities for migration.
example_prompt: List all the communities in my Lemmy settings export
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON parse on the uploaded export; fully local.
rationale: Lemmy/Kbin users switching instances need to extract and re-subscribe to their community list.

name: adblock-filter-dedupe
description: Dedupes, sorts, and compacts an adblock filter list, detecting redundant or fully-overlapping rules.
example_prompt: Remove duplicate and redundant rules from my merged filter list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: set/prefix analysis over parsed filter rules, all in-memory.
rationale: Users who merge multiple lists end up with bloated, conflicting rule sets that slow the blocker and are tedious to clean by hand.

name: tor-bridge-parser
description: Parses and validates Tor bridge lines (obfs4, webtunnel, snowflake), extracting transport, address, port, and fingerprint.
example_prompt: Parse this obfs4 bridge line and check it's well-formed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: tokenizing a fixed line grammar, no network.
rationale: Bridge lines are copy-pasted from chat and email where they get mangled; validating them offline avoids silent connection failures.

name: fingerprint-entropy-analyzer
description: Analyzes a browser-fingerprint attribute set (canvas, webgl, fonts, headers) and estimates uniqueness in bits of entropy.
example_prompt: How identifying is this browser fingerprint?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Shannon-entropy math over provided attributes against a bundled reference distribution.
rationale: Privacy-focused browser users (Mullvad, Tor) want to quantify how trackable their configuration is, and there is no offline tool for it.

name: single-file-asset-extractor
description: Extracts embedded data: URI assets (images, fonts, CSS) from a SingleFile-saved HTML page and lists or decodes each one.
example_prompt: Pull all the embedded images out of this SingleFile HTML page
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: HTML scanning plus base64 decoding of data: URIs, fully local.
rationale: SingleFile archives inline every asset as a giant data URI, and there is no easy way to get the original files back out.

name: mds-projector
description: Turns a distance or similarity matrix into 2-D coordinates with classical multidimensional scaling.
example_prompt: Turn this distance matrix into a 2D map
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — classical MDS is a double-centering plus eigen-decomposition of the Gram matrix.
rationale: Lets users visualize any pairwise-distance data (genetic, survey, perceptual) without sending it to a server.

name: video-to-animated-avif
description: Converts a short clip into an animated AVIF, the most space-efficient modern looping-image format.
example_prompt: Make an animated avif from this short video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm with libaom encodes animated AVIF frames client-side (heavy but fully local).
rationale: Animated AVIF beats GIF and WebP on size and is the emerging web standard for looping clips.

name: video-to-y4m
description: Exports a video's raw frames as uncompressed YUV4MPEG (.y4m) for codec testing and pipeline analysis.
example_prompt: Export this clip to raw y4m for encoder benchmarking
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm decodes to raw YUV and writes the .y4m stream to the virtual filesystem locally.
rationale: Codec researchers and encoder-tuners need raw Y4M input, a precise format no consumer tool exposes.

name: au-to-wav
description: Converts legacy Sun/NeXT .au/.snd audio files to WAV.
example_prompt: convert this old .au sound file to wav
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader demuxes the .au/.snd format and outputs WAV in wasm.
rationale: Decades-old Unix and Java sound assets ship as .au, which modern editors no longer open.

name: vox-to-wav
description: Converts headerless Dialogic ADPCM (.vox) IVR audio to WAV given a sample rate.
example_prompt: convert this 8khz dialogic vox file to wav
loader_feasibility: 4-bit Dialogic ADPCM decode is implemented in plain Rust→WASM; user supplies the rate the format omits.
rationale: Legacy IVR/auto-attendant systems store prompts as raw .vox that needs the right rate and ADPCM table to play.

name: audio-container-remux
description: Changes an audio file's container (e.g. m4a↔aac, mka↔ogg) without re-encoding, preserving exact quality.
example_prompt: rewrap this m4a into a different container without re-encoding
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader stream-copies the codec into a new container in wasm; no decode/encode, just a remux.
rationale: When a player rejects the container but supports the codec, a lossless remux fixes playback instantly without quality loss.

name: libsvm-to-csv
description: Expands a LIBSVM/SVMlight sparse `label index:value` file into a dense feature CSV with a header.
example_prompt: Convert this libsvm training file to a normal CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parsing the per-line index:value tokens and filling a dense row is straightforward text processing in WASM.
rationale: LIBSVM is a dominant ML dataset format but unreadable in spreadsheets or pandas without conversion.

name: graphml-to-edgelist
description: Parses a GraphML XML file into a flat edge-list CSV with node and edge attributes preserved.
example_prompt: Flatten this .graphml network into an edge list CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: an in-WASM XML reader walks the GraphML nodes/edges and emits CSV rows, no network needed.
rationale: GraphML is verbose XML that pandas/spreadsheets can't read, but the underlying graph is just edges.

name: dot-to-edgelist
description: Extracts the edges (and labels) from a Graphviz DOT file into a tabular edge list.
example_prompt: Pull the edges out of this Graphviz .dot file as a CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a small DOT tokenizer/parser handles the `a -> b` statements entirely in WASM.
rationale: DOT files encode graphs as visual layout; extracting the raw edges lets people analyze them as data.

name: dimacs-to-edgelist
description: Converts a DIMACS graph (`p`/`e` lines) into a plain edge list or adjacency CSV.
example_prompt: Convert this DIMACS .col graph into an edge list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: DIMACS is line-oriented ASCII, parsed and re-emitted entirely client-side.
rationale: Graph-coloring/SAT benchmark datasets ship in DIMACS, which no general tool reads natively.

name: pajek-net-to-edgelist
description: Reads a Pajek .net network file (vertices + arcs/edges) and outputs a labeled edge list CSV.
example_prompt: Convert this Pajek .net file to an edge list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the *Vertices/*Edges section format is simple ASCII parsed in WASM with no external calls.
rationale: Social-network datasets are often distributed only as Pajek files that modern tools can't load.

name: hebrew-prefix-segmenter
description: Splits attached Hebrew prefixes (ב ה ו כ ל מ ש) off word stems for searching and analysis.
example_prompt: Segment the prefixes off these Hebrew words.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — rule-based morphological prefix splitting with a bundled lexicon, runs offline.
rationale: Hebrew agglutinated prefixes break naive search; an RFTokenizer-style segmenter restores recall entirely client-side.

name: chinese-pos-tagger
description: Tags each Chinese word with its part of speech after segmentation.
example_prompt: Tag the parts of speech in this Chinese sentence.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — jieba posseg-style tagging with bundled dictionary, runs offline.
rationale: POS tagging (FudanNLP/HanLP) underpins grammar analysis and information extraction for Chinese, fully local.

name: spanish-word-similarity
description: Finds the most semantically similar Spanish words or ranks how close two Spanish terms are.
example_prompt: Which words are most similar in meaning to 'feliz' in Spanish?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js — multilingual embedding model computes vectors and cosine similarity in-browser.
rationale: Delivers the Spanish word-embeddings/word2vec demand as an interactive semantic tool with no backend.

name: cross-lingual-match
description: Given a word or phrase, finds its closest matches in another language from a candidate list using shared multilingual embeddings.
example_prompt: Which English word is closest to the Hindi 'किताब' from this list?
loader_feasibility: transformers-js embeds both-language items with one multilingual sentence-transformer ONNX model and ranks by cosine locally.
rationale: Maps the IIT Patna Hi-En bilingual word-embeddings demand into a concrete cross-lingual lookup that runs entirely in the browser.

name: thai-syllable-segmenter
description: Breaks Thai text into pronounceable syllables.
example_prompt: Break ประเทศไทย into syllables
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: rule-based Thai syllable grammar runs entirely client-side
rationale: Syllable units are needed for text-to-speech, rhyme, and pronunciation help that word segmentation alone can't give.

name: shields-badge-generator
description: Builds shields.io badge markdown (or HTML) from label, message, color, and link.
example_prompt: make a green 'build passing' badge that links to my CI
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: URL-encodes the fields into the shields template string locally.
rationale: README badges are everywhere and constructing the URL by hand is fiddly.

name: arabic-text-normalizer
description: Normalizes Arabic letter variants (alef forms, hamza seats, teh marbuta, alef maqsura) and folds tatweel for consistent matching.
example_prompt: Normalize these Arabic names so the different alef spellings match.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — deterministic character-mapping table, runs entirely in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: Reproduces PyArabic's normalization that every Arabic NLP pipeline depends on for reliable string matching.

name: css-media-query-merger
description: Combines duplicate @media blocks with identical conditions into a single grouped block.
example_prompt: Merge the repeated media queries in this stylesheet
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM at-rule grouping over the parsed tree; fully local.
rationale: Component-authored CSS scatters identical breakpoints everywhere and merging them shrinks and clarifies the file.

name: bbcode-to-html
description: Converts forum BBCode tags ([b], [url], [quote], [code]) into safe HTML.
example_prompt: Convert this BBCode post to HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (bbcode parser) tokenizes and emits HTML in the sandbox.
rationale: Old forum and game-community content lives in BBCode and migrating it to HTML/CMS platforms needs exactly this.

name: images-to-multipage-tiff
description: Bundles several images into a single multi-page TIFF for document/archival systems.
example_prompt: Pack these scans into one multi-page tiff
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the `tiff` encoder writes successive image directories in-browser.
rationale: Archival and fax systems require multi-page TIFF, with essentially no friendly local builder available.

name: sf2-to-sfz
description: Converts a SoundFont 2 (.sf2) bank into an SFZ instrument definition plus extracted sample WAVs.
example_prompt: convert this sf2 soundfont into an sfz instrument
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the RIFF sfbk structure, writes SFZ opcodes, and dumps samples as WAV locally.
rationale: SFZ-based samplers can't load SF2 banks directly, so musicians need this format bridge.

name: dls-to-sf2
description: Converts a DLS (Downloadable Sounds) instrument bank into the SoundFont 2 format.
example_prompt: convert this dls bank to sf2
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — maps DLS regions/articulations to SF2 generators and rewrites the RIFF bank in-browser.
rationale: DLS banks from old games/GM hardware are unusable in the SF2-only synths most people run today.

name: simplify-ratio
description: Reduces a multi-term ratio (e.g. 1920:1080 or 4:6:8) to its simplest integer form using the GCD.
example_prompt: Simplify the ratio 1920:1080 to lowest terms
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: multi-term GCD reduction, offline
rationale: Ratio/aspect-ratio simplification is a frequent practical need (screens, mixes) with no existing tool.

name: package-json-sorter
description: Reorders package.json into conventional top-level key order and alphabetizes dependency blocks.
example_prompt: sort this package.json into the standard order
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — serde_json with a fixed key ordering; local only.
rationale: Conventional package.json ordering reduces merge conflicts across a team.

name: multibase-codec
description: Encodes/decodes self-describing Multibase strings (the prefixed format used across IPFS/IPLD).
example_prompt: decode multibase string zQmYwAP...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — prefix dispatch over baseN tables, all local.
rationale: IPFS CIDs are Multibase-encoded and devs need to resolve the prefix and base offline.

name: deep-zoom-tiler
description: Generates a Deep Zoom (DZI) tile pyramid for OpenSeadragon/Leaflet panning of huge images.
example_prompt: make deep zoom tiles from this giant scan
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM repeatedly downsamples and tiles each pyramid level, emitting the DZI descriptor
rationale: Serving gigapixel images interactively requires a tile pyramid that is laborious to produce without dedicated tooling.

name: subtitle-fps-retime
description: Rescales subtitle timings for a frame-rate change (e.g. 23.976 ↔ 25 fps PAL speedup).
example_prompt: Retime these subs from 25fps to 23.976fps
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM multiplies the timecodes by the fps ratio with no media access.
rationale: PAL/NTSC subtitle drift accumulates over a movie and needs ratio retiming, not a flat offset.

name: mu-law-wav-codec
description: Encodes 16-bit PCM WAV to G.711 µ-law (8-bit) or decodes µ-law back to PCM.
example_prompt: Encode this voice clip to mu-law wav for a phone system
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies the deterministic µ-law companding lookup per sample — no external codec library
rationale: µ-law is the telephony/IVR standard and the companding math is a tiny, well-defined table that runs instantly client-side.

name: cue-to-chapter-list
description: Converts a .cue sheet into MP4/Matroska chapter metadata (and ffmetadata) with timestamped chapter marks.
example_prompt: Turn this album.cue into chapter markers I can mux into an m4b
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses cue INDEX times and emits ffmetadata/chapters text — client-side reformatting
rationale: Audiobook and long-mix containers use chapter atoms, not cue sheets, so a converter bridges ripping to packaging.

name: blake2-hash
description: Computes BLAKE2b and BLAKE2s digests of text or a file with optional output length.
example_prompt: blake2b hash of this file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the blake2 RustCrypto crate is pure-Rust, deterministic and offline.
rationale: BLAKE2 is a fast, widely-adopted modern hash (used by argon2, libsodium, many CLIs) with real standalone demand.

name: circle-packing-art-generator
description: Generates non-overlapping circle-packing art that fills a canvas (or an image mask) with sized circles.
example_prompt: Make circle-packing art inside this logo silhouette
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — greedy growth/collision packing over the canvas or alpha mask; CPU only.
rationale: A popular generative-art technique that doubles as a mask-aware decorative fill, with no catalog twin.

name: sql-seed-from-json
description: Generates idempotent seed SQL (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT / UPSERT) from a JSON array against a named table.
example_prompt: Make idempotent seed SQL from this JSON for the products table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: JSON parse plus dialect-aware upsert string emission, deterministic and offline.
rationale: Repeatable seed scripts are scaffolding every project needs and hand-writing upserts is error-prone.

name: frictionless-table-schema
description: Generates a Frictionless Table Schema descriptor (field names, types, formats, constraints) from a CSV sample.
example_prompt: Generate a Table Schema descriptor for this CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: CSV parse plus type/format inference emitted as the standard JSON descriptor, offline.
rationale: Open-data publishers need standards-compliant Table Schemas and inferring one from data is otherwise manual.

name: terraform-vars-from-json
description: Generates Terraform variable declarations (type, default, description) from a JSON configuration object.
example_prompt: Generate Terraform variables from this JSON config
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: JSON parse plus HCL variable-block emission as text, no Terraform binary.
rationale: Translating an existing config object into typed Terraform variables is repetitive IaC scaffolding.

name: datalist-generator
description: Generates an <input> with an associated <datalist> autocomplete from a pasted list of options.
example_prompt: make a datalist autocomplete input from this list of countries
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML templating over the option list; fully client-side.
rationale: Native autocomplete via datalist is underused and wiring the list/input id pair is mechanical busywork.

name: details-accordion-generator
description: Generates a no-JS accordion using <details>/<summary> elements from a list of title/content pairs.
example_prompt: turn this FAQ into a details/summary accordion
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML templating; no JavaScript runtime needed.
rationale: Disclosure widgets are common and the native <details> approach avoids shipping accordion JS.

name: word-elongation-normalizer
description: Normalizes stretched words ("sooo goood") down to standard spelling.
example_prompt: Normalize the stretched-out words in this social media text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — repeated-letter reduction heuristic, in-browser
rationale: Elongated spellings in social text defeat search, dedup, and dictionary lookups.

name: hashtag-splitter
description: Splits camelCase or run-together hashtags (#ThisIsGreat) into separate readable words.
example_prompt: Split these hashtags into readable words
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — case-boundary and dictionary-assisted segmentation, in-browser
rationale: Hashtags compress phrases into one token that must be split to read or index them.

name: video-strip-cover-art
description: Removes an embedded cover/thumbnail image stream that some containers carry as an attached picture.
example_prompt: Remove the embedded cover image from this video file
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader drops the attached_pic stream with selective -map and -c copy in ffmpeg.wasm.
rationale: Embedded cover art can confuse players and editors, and clean removal is otherwise obscure.

name: video-reorder-audio-tracks
description: Reorders the audio streams so a chosen track comes first in the file.
example_prompt: Move the English audio track to be first in this video
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader re-maps streams in the desired order with -c copy in ffmpeg.wasm.
rationale: Players that pick the first audio track need reordering, which is otherwise a command-line chore.

name: video-sample-aspect-normalize
description: Bakes a non-square pixel aspect ratio into square pixels so the video displays correctly everywhere.
example_prompt: Fix this anamorphic DVD rip so it isn't stretched
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader scales by the SAR and resets it to 1:1 in ffmpeg.wasm, client-side.
rationale: Anamorphic/DVD sources show stretched in dumb players, and squaring pixels is the canonical fix.

name: audio-emphasis-filter
description: Applies or removes standard pre/de-emphasis curves (RIAA, 50µs, CD pre-emphasis) for correct playback EQ.
example_prompt: Apply RIAA de-emphasis to this raw phono transfer
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — `aemphasis` implements the standard emphasis filter modes; runs client-side.
rationale: Vinyl rips and pre-emphasized CDs sound wrong until the correct emphasis curve is applied, and the standard curves are otherwise hard to reproduce.

name: html-quote-style-normalizer
description: Converts all attribute quoting to a single consistent style (double or single) and quotes unquoted values.
example_prompt: Make every attribute in this HTML use double quotes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM re-emits attribute values with chosen delimiter and proper escaping; client-side only
rationale: Mixed and missing attribute quotes are a common lint failure that's annoying to fix manually.

name: enhanced-lrc-to-plain-lrc
description: Flattens word-level enhanced (A2) LRC lyrics into standard line-level LRC.
example_prompt: Strip the per-word timings from this enhanced LRC to a plain LRC
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: drop inline <mm:ss.xx> word tags, keep the line timestamp, text-only
rationale: Makes karaoke-style enhanced LRCs compatible with players that only read line timing.

name: ass-to-lrc
description: Extracts dialogue lines and start times from an ASS/SSA subtitle file into an LRC lyrics file.
example_prompt: Convert this .ass karaoke subtitle to an LRC
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse [Events] Dialogue rows, strip override tags, emit LRC timestamps
rationale: Recovers timed lyrics from anime/karaoke ASS subtitles for music players.

name: json-schema-to-markdown-table
description: Flattens a JSON Schema's properties into a Markdown table of field, type, required, and description for README embedding.
example_prompt: Make a Markdown table of the fields in this JSON Schema
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — schema flattening plus Markdown emission, offline
rationale: A lightweight, frequently-wanted slice of the prmd/Docson documentation demand.

name: css-custom-property-extractor
description: Lists every CSS custom property (variable) and its value found in a stylesheet.
example_prompt: Pull out all the CSS variables defined in this file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scan for --name declarations; pure parsing, browser-local.
rationale: Auditing a design-token system means seeing every variable at once, which scrolling can't give you.

name: image-to-1bit-bmp
description: Floyd–Steinberg dithers an image to 1-bit black-and-white and saves it as a monochrome BMP.
example_prompt: Convert this image to a 1-bit dithered BMP for my receipt printer
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: grayscale, error-diffuse, pack 1bpp into a BMP — pure CPU.
rationale: Thermal/e-ink printers need true 1-bit monochrome and dithering preserves perceived detail.

name: image-palette-to-gpl
description: Extracts an image's dominant colors and exports them as a GIMP .gpl palette file.
example_prompt: Export the palette of this artwork as a GIMP palette
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: quantize to N colors then write the .gpl text format — pure local processing.
rationale: Artists pulling a palette from reference art need it in a tool-importable format, not just swatches.

name: video-timestamp-rebase
description: Resets a clip's PTS/DTS so timestamps start cleanly at zero, fixing negative or offset start times.
example_prompt: Reset the timestamps on this clip to start at zero
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM applies setpts/-output_ts_offset locally with no upload.
rationale: Trimmed segments often carry nonzero start PTS that breaks concatenation and players.

name: ms-adpcm-to-pcm-wav
description: Decodes Microsoft ADPCM WAV files into linear PCM WAV.
example_prompt: Convert this MS ADPCM wav to pcm
loader_feasibility: MS-ADPCM uses fixed coefficient tables and per-block prediction, decodable in plain Rust→WASM.
rationale: Legacy Windows and game-asset WAVs use MS-ADPCM and silently fail to decode in modern tools.

name: native-flac-to-ogg-flac
description: Re-encapsulates a native .flac stream into Ogg-FLAC for players and pipelines that require Ogg framing.
example_prompt: Wrap this flac into an ogg-flac file
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg remuxes FLAC into an Ogg container by stream copy in WASM.
rationale: Some streaming and embedded players only accept Ogg-framed FLAC, and remuxing keeps it lossless.

name: gcode-path-extractor
description: Extracts G0/G1 motion coordinates from a G-code file into a CSV toolpath of XYZ points.
example_prompt: Extract the XYZ toolpath from this gcode
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizes G-code coordinate words and tracks modal position
rationale: Makers want to inspect or plot a machine's actual path without slicer software.

name: video-resolution-test-chart-generator
description: Generates a lens/codec resolution test chart (zone-plate / star-style) clip.
example_prompt: make a zone-plate resolution test chart clip at 4K
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — the zoneplate/testsrc2 procedural source is synthesized in wasm with no input.
rationale: Needed for lens, focus, and codec-sharpness testing.

name: video-frame-counter-clip-generator
description: Generates a clip with a burned-in running frame number and timecode for QA and sync work.
example_prompt: make a 10s 30fps clip with frame numbers and timecode burned in
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — testsrc2/drawtext using frame_num and timecode expressions, no input file.
rationale: Essential reference for frame-accuracy and round-trip testing.

name: absolute-to-relative-url
description: Rewrites a set of absolute URLs as relative paths against a base URL, useful for portable static-site output.
example_prompt: Make https://example.com/blog/post/img.png relative to https://example.com/blog/post/
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; path-segment diffing between two parsed URLs, no network.
rationale: Relative links keep a site portable across domains and previews; manual conversion is error-prone.

name: html-entity-minimizer
description: Replaces unnecessary numeric/named HTML entities with their literal UTF-8 characters, keeping only the ones that must stay escaped.
example_prompt: Decode the unnecessary entities in Café & co <b>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; entity table lookup + selective decode, no network.
rationale: Over-escaped HTML from old editors is hard to read; minimizing entities cleans it up safely.

name: css-hex-color-shortener
description: Shortens 6-digit hex colors to their 3-digit equivalent where lossless (and 8→4 for alpha), across a stylesheet.
example_prompt: Shorten the hex colors in this CSS where possible
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; hex pattern detection and rewrite, local only.
rationale: A small, safe byte-saving cleanup that also makes palettes more readable.

name: signum-encoder
description: Replaces each value with its sign as -1, 0, or +1 (signum), optionally as text labels.
example_prompt: Convert these numbers to just their sign
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: sign test per value, no I/O.
rationale: Sign extraction is a common feature-engineering and direction-of-change step distinct from absolute value.

name: dkim-record-parse
description: Parses a DKIM DNS TXT record, reporting the key type, public key presence, flags, and any deprecated settings.
example_prompt: is this DKIM record using a valid RSA key and what's the version?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tag parsing plus base64 key length check; self-contained
rationale: Verifying a DKIM record's key and flags without a separate tool helps debug email signing.

name: adjacency-matrix-analyzer
description: From an adjacency matrix, reports degree distribution, graph density, and the number and sizes of connected components.
example_prompt: Analyze this adjacency matrix — degree distribution and connected components.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (matrix scan + union-find); fully local.
rationale: Quick structural inspection of a graph encoded as a matrix is common in network/data work and has no simple offline tool.

name: yaml-frontmatter-builder
description: Generates a YAML frontmatter block for static-site posts from title, date, tags, and custom key-value fields.
example_prompt: Make Jekyll frontmatter with title, today's date, and tags rust, wasm
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — serializes user fields into valid YAML locally.
rationale: Bloggers repeatedly hand-write frontmatter and get quoting/indentation wrong.

name: chord-symbol-to-midi
description: Generates a single-chord Standard MIDI File from a chord symbol with optional voicing and inversion.
example_prompt: Make a MIDI file of a Bbmaj9 chord in root position
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses the chord symbol to pitch classes and writes a one-chord SMF, no network
rationale: A quick chord-to-MIDI export is handy for dropping reference voicings into a DAW and isn't covered by note-list tools.

name: spiral-coordinates-generator
description: Generates points along an Archimedean or logarithmic spiral over a chosen turn count.
example_prompt: Generate 300 points on an Archimedean spiral with 5 turns
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parametric r(θ) evaluation, deterministic in wasmi
rationale: Useful coordinate scaffold for art, antenna/spiral layouts, and visualizations that are awkward to hand-derive.

name: motion-blur-detector
description: Detects directional motion blur and reports its angle and severity, distinguishing it from general softness.
example_prompt: Does this photo have motion blur, and which direction?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs frequency/gradient-direction analysis on decoded pixels.
rationale: Motion blur from camera shake is a distinct, fixable defect worth flagging separately from focus blur.

name: cache-control-linter
description: Lints a Cache-Control header for contradictory directives (no-store with max-age, public with private) and missing freshness hints.
example_prompt: Are these directives contradictory? no-store, max-age=600, public
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM directive tokenization and rule checks — no server.
rationale: Conflicting cache directives cause unpredictable CDN behavior; a linter pins down the actual effective policy.

name: triangular-matrix-checker
description: Determines whether a matrix is upper-, lower-, or non-triangular by scanning off-triangle entries against a tolerance.
example_prompt: Is this matrix upper triangular?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — single pass over off-diagonal entries, deterministic and offline.
rationale: Triangularity validation is a quick structural check for decomposed/factorized matrices.

name: adjacency-matrix-validator
description: Validates a graph adjacency matrix is square, binary (or nonnegative-weighted), with a chosen self-loop and symmetry policy.
example_prompt: Is this a valid undirected adjacency matrix?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — squareness, entry-domain, and symmetry checks in one pass, offline.
rationale: Catches malformed graph matrices (non-square, asymmetric for undirected) before graph algorithms run.

name: m3u-to-csv
description: Parses an M3U/M3U8 playlist into a CSV of track titles, durations, and file paths.
example_prompt: convert this m3u playlist to CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM #EXTINF line parser; runs on the pasted playlist locally
rationale: Playlists are easier to audit and edit as a spreadsheet.

name: asset-depreciation-calculator
description: Builds straight-line and declining-balance depreciation schedules from cost, salvage value, and useful life.
example_prompt: Make a depreciation schedule for a $50k asset over 5 years
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM iterative arithmetic; no data leaves the browser.
rationale: The IBM Asset Dataset demand reflects routine accounting math well suited to offline computation.

name: grade-calc
description: Compute a weighted course grade or the final-exam score needed to hit a target grade.
example_prompt: What do I need on the final to get a B if I have 78% going in and it's worth 30%?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM arithmetic; browser-local.
rationale: Final-grade and 'what do I need' calculators are heavily used by students each semester.

name: flooring-calculator
description: Estimate flooring/tiles needed for a room including a waste allowance and box counts.
example_prompt: Tiles needed for a 3.5x4m floor with 10% waste, 0.5x0.5m tiles?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM arithmetic, offline.
rationale: A common renovation estimate distinct from generic geometry area.

name: bignum-calc
description: Arbitrary-precision integer and decimal arithmetic (huge factorials, exact division, mod).
example_prompt: compute 200! exactly
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM big-integer/decimal crate.
rationale: The float-based calculator can't do exact big-number math that students and devs often need.

name: animated-gif-frame-validator
description: Validates an animated GIF or APNG's frame count, per-frame delays, and loop setting, flagging too-fast delays or a missing loop count.
example_prompt: Check the frame timing and loop settings on this animated GIF.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the GIF graphic-control extensions / APNG fcTL chunks — pure header walk, client-side.
rationale: Sub-2cs frame delays and missing loop flags cause janky or non-looping animations, and a validator surfaces them before publishing.

name: vorbis-comment-validator
description: Lints Vorbis comments (FLAC/Ogg tags) for RFC-compliant field-name characters, valid UTF-8 values, and the required vendor string.
example_prompt: Are the tags in this flac valid Vorbis comments?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the comment block and applies the Vorbis-comment spec rules locally.
rationale: Non-compliant field names silently drop in some players, and a strict validator prevents lost metadata.

name: playwright-script-generator
description: Generates a Playwright automation script from a described sequence of navigate/click/fill/assert steps.
example_prompt: Write a Playwright script that logs in, clicks Settings, and checks the page title
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM templating into JS/TS source; produces the script as text locally (it runs later under Playwright, not in-browser).
rationale: Browser-automation tools like beachpatrol drive Playwright, and scaffolding a correct script from plain steps removes boilerplate.

name: graph-analyzer
description: Analyzes a graph from an edge list and reports connected components, degrees, cycles, and node centrality.
example_prompt: Analyze this edge list and tell me the connected components and most central nodes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM graph algorithms (hypergraph/gust-style) operate purely on the in-memory adjacency structure.
rationale: Graph metrics are valuable for network/dependency inspection and need only CPU-bound traversal, ideal for browser-local.

name: analog-clock-video
description: Generates a standalone animated analog clock-face video sweeping over a chosen time span, exportable with transparency.
example_prompt: Make a 60-second analog clock animation counting one minute
loader_feasibility: pyodide (Pillow) draws each clock-hand frame and ffmpeg encodes them, all in-browser.
rationale: A reusable animated clock graphic is useful for timers and explainers and differs from overlaying a clock on existing footage.

name: brown-noise-generator
description: Generates deep, low-rumble Brownian (red) noise as a WAV for focus and sleep use.
example_prompt: Generate 10 minutes of brown noise
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM integrates white noise into a Brownian walk and writes WAV without any backend
rationale: Brown noise has a distinct, much-requested deeper character than white/pink and deserves its own one-shot.

name: arrow-schema-from-json
description: Infers an Apache Arrow / Parquet logical schema (field names and Arrow types) from a JSON array of records.
example_prompt: Make an Arrow schema from this JSON array
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: JSON parse plus Arrow type inference emitted as text, no Arrow runtime needed.
rationale: Columnar pipelines need an explicit schema before writing Parquet and inferring it from JSON is a real gap.

name: json-skeleton-from-schema
description: Produces an empty structural template document (all properties present with null/default placeholders) from a JSON Schema.
example_prompt: Give me a blank JSON skeleton matching this schema
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: JSON Schema parse plus structural template emission, no value randomization or network.
rationale: Authors filling in a config or request body need the exact shape with no values, which mock generators don't provide.

name: plantuml-class-from-json
description: Generates a PlantUML class diagram (classes, fields, and composition edges) from a nested JSON document.
example_prompt: Make a PlantUML class diagram from this JSON structure
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: JSON parse plus PlantUML source emission as text, fully client-side.
rationale: Visualizing the structure of an unfamiliar JSON payload as a class diagram aids comprehension and docs.

name: pacman
description: Maze-chase arcade game with pellets, power-ups, and four ghosts driven by distinct chase/scatter AI.
example_prompt: play a pacman game
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tile maze, pathfinding ghost AI, and canvas animation all run locally
rationale: Covers two harvested terms (MyMan, NCurses Pacman) with a marquee arcade title.

name: midi-orphan-note-detector
description: Scans a MIDI file for note-on events without a matching note-off (and vice versa), reporting stuck or orphaned notes.
example_prompt: Find stuck notes in this MIDI file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tracks note on/off pairs per channel locally.
rationale: Orphaned note-ons cause notes that ring forever on synths, and pairing analysis pinpoints the offending event.

name: raw-pcm-sanity-check
description: Interprets a headerless PCM file under a declared format and flags likely wrong sample rate, bit depth, endianness, or channel count.
example_prompt: Does my raw PCM dump match 16-bit 44.1k stereo little-endian?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg reads the raw stream under the stated format and statistics are computed in WASM to test plausibility.
rationale: Wrongly-interpreted raw PCM sounds like noise, and a sanity check confirms the format parameters before further processing.

name: gif-metadata-inspector
description: Reports a GIF's frame count, per-frame delays, loop count, palette size, and transparency without exporting frames.
example_prompt: How many frames and what loop/delay settings does this GIF have?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the GIF logical screen descriptor and graphic control extensions locally.
rationale: Animators and web devs need timing and loop info to debug playback without unpacking every frame.

name: python-ast-explorer
description: Shows the abstract syntax tree of a Python snippet as a readable node hierarchy.
example_prompt: show me the AST for this python code
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs the stdlib ast module locally to parse and dump the tree.
rationale: Indispensable for writing linters, codemods, and understanding parse behavior.

name: residual-diagnostics
description: Takes observed and predicted values and reports residual diagnostics: R², adjusted R², RMSE, MAE, Durbin-Watson, and a residual-normality check.
example_prompt: Diagnose residuals: observed 10,20,30,40 predicted 11,19,32,38
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; residual statistics and autocorrelation tests are arithmetic over two parsed arrays, no server.
rationale: Fitting a model is only half the job; checking residual quality catches bad fits, and the existing curve-fit tools stop at producing coefficients.

name: vscode-launch-generator
description: Generates a .vscode/launch.json with debug configurations for a chosen runtime (Node, Python, Go, Rust).
example_prompt: Generate a VS Code launch.json to debug a Node app entry at src/index.js
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — emits the configurations array per debugger type, no editor needed.
rationale: launch.json debug-type fields and per-language keys are easy to forget; a generator removes the lookup.

name: express-route-scaffold
description: Generates Express route handler boilerplate (router, async handlers, validation, error wrapping) from a route spec.
example_prompt: Scaffold Express routes for a CRUD /tasks resource
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — template emission of router and handler functions from the spec, entirely local.
rationale: CRUD route boilerplate with consistent async/error handling is repetitive setup well-suited to generation.

name: fastapi-endpoint-scaffold
description: Generates FastAPI endpoint stubs with path operations, Pydantic request/response models, and status codes from a spec.
example_prompt: Scaffold FastAPI endpoints for a /items resource with create and list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — emits decorated route functions and model classes as Python text, no server.
rationale: Getting FastAPI's response_model and status_code wiring right is boilerplate that a scaffold standardizes.

name: svg-path-precision-reducer
description: Rounds path and coordinate numbers in an SVG to a chosen precision, shrinking file size with negligible visual change.
example_prompt: Reduce the coordinate precision in this SVG to 2 decimals
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses path data and numeric attributes and reformats them; local math transform
rationale: Over-precise float coordinates are the largest avoidable cost in exported SVG payloads.

name: uniform-decimal-formatter
description: Forces every number in a list to the same fixed number of decimal places by padding or rounding to a chosen width.
example_prompt: make these all show 2 decimals: 3.1, 4, 5.25, 6.7
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — per-element format to N places, pure local arithmetic/string work.
rationale: Mixed decimal widths make columns unreadable and break naive string sorting; equalizing them is a constant pre-display chore.

name: arcsine-transform
description: Applies the variance-stabilizing arcsine (or arcsine-square-root) transform to a list of proportions in [0,1].
example_prompt: arcsine-sqrt transform these proportions: 0.04, 0.5, 0.96
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — elementwise asin(sqrt(x)), pure local math.
rationale: The arcsine transform is the classic fix for proportion/percentage data before analysis and is distinct from log/Box-Cox power transforms.

name: initial-bearing-calculator
description: Computes the initial great-circle bearing (forward azimuth) from one latitude/longitude to another.
example_prompt: what bearing do I start on going from 40.7,-74.0 to 51.5,-0.1?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — spherical-trig azimuth on doubles, no network or geocoding.
rationale: The starting heading between two coordinates is a core navigation value that the existing haversine-distance and midpoint tools don't compute.

name: byte-size-report
description: Reports total and per-line UTF-8 byte size alongside character count, flagging where bytes ≫ characters.
example_prompt: How many bytes is this text and which lines are heaviest?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; UTF-8 byte counting needs no external resources.
rationale: Byte budgets matter for column limits, SMS, tweet, and DB-field constraints where multibyte chars surprise users.

name: json-depth-analyzer
description: Reports the maximum nesting depth of a JSON document and the path to the deepest node.
example_prompt: how deeply nested is this json?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM walking the parsed JSON tree.
rationale: Helps catch pathological nesting that breaks parsers or recursion limits.

name: python-bytecode-disassembler
description: Disassembles a Python function or snippet into CPython bytecode opcodes.
example_prompt: disassemble this python function
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs the stdlib dis module entirely in the browser sandbox.
rationale: Helps performance and behavior debugging without a local Python install.

name: makefile-scaffold
description: Scaffolds a Makefile with common phony targets (build, test, lint, clean, run) for a chosen stack.
example_prompt: Scaffold a Makefile for a Go project
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: tab-aware template emission from options, fully local.
rationale: Makefiles are tab-sensitive and a correct starting scaffold avoids a classic pitfall.

name: code-typing-video
description: Renders a video of a code snippet being typed out line-by-line with monospace styling and a blinking cursor.
example_prompt: Make a coding video that types out this Python function
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg drawtext reveals the snippet progressively from a generated frame schedule, in-browser.
rationale: Dev creators need typed-code clips for tutorials and shorts and have no offline tool for it.

name: midi-click-track-generator
description: Produces a MIDI metronome/click track (with accents) for a tempo map and time signature, for DAW import.
example_prompt: Generate a MIDI click track for 32 bars of 6/8 at 80 BPM
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM emits accented/unaccented note events on a percussion channel and writes the SMF locally
rationale: A MIDI click syncs cleanly to a DAW's tempo grid in a way an audio click can't.

name: llms-txt-generator
description: Generates an /llms.txt file listing a site's key pages and summaries for AI crawlers, in the proposed Markdown format.
example_prompt: generate an llms.txt for my docs site with these main pages
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM Markdown templating; no network.
rationale: llms.txt is a fast-emerging convention and a generator captures fresh demand the existing robots-AI tool doesn't cover.

name: news-sitemap-generator
description: Generates a Google News XML sitemap with publication name, language, and per-URL publication dates.
example_prompt: make a Google News sitemap for these 12 article URLs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML templating with the news: namespace; no network.
rationale: News publishers need the specialized news-namespace sitemap that the generic sitemap generator doesn't produce.

name: image-sitemap-generator
description: Generates an image XML sitemap, grouping image entries under their page URLs with the image: namespace.
example_prompt: build an image sitemap from this list of pages and their images
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML templating; fully client-side.
rationale: Image SEO benefits from a dedicated image sitemap whose namespaced structure is awkward to author by hand.

name: gitlab-ci-scaffold
description: Generates a .gitlab-ci.yml with stages, jobs, and cache/artifact blocks for a selected language and pipeline shape.
example_prompt: Create a GitLab CI config with build, test, and deploy stages for a Go service
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — deterministic YAML templating from inputs, no server needed.
rationale: GitLab pipeline syntax differs enough from Actions that a dedicated scaffold prevents copy-paste mistakes.

name: sparse-matrix-generator
description: Generates a random sparse matrix at a target density and emits it in COO and CSR formats.
example_prompt: Generate a 100x100 sparse matrix with 2% density in CSR format
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with seeded PRNG — sample nonzeros, sort, and pack index arrays, no external libraries.
rationale: Quickly scaffolds test inputs for sparse solvers and graph algorithms in the exact storage layout downstream code expects.

name: requirements-txt-validator
description: Validates a pip requirements.txt for malformed PEP 508 specifiers and reports duplicate or conflicting pins.
example_prompt: Check my requirements.txt for invalid version specifiers and conflicts
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the `pep508_rs` parser; pure text/version analysis, no index access.
rationale: Bad specifiers and silent duplicate pins cause confusing resolver errors that a local validator catches up front.

name: doi-validate
description: Checks a DOI string's syntax and normalizes it to canonical form.
example_prompt: Is this a valid DOI and what's its canonical form?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (regex + normalization); pure text
rationale: Reference managers frequently encounter malformed or wrapped DOIs that need cleaning.

name: numerical-optimizer
description: Minimizes a user-supplied function using Nelder-Mead or gradient descent.
example_prompt: Minimize (x-3)^2 + (y+1)^2
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: gradient-free and gradient optimizers (Peroxide optimization) are CPU math suited to wasmi.
rationale: Optimization is central to ML and engineering and rarely available as a quick private tool.

name: geometry-solver
description: Solves common geometry problems — triangle sides/angles, circle and polygon area and perimeter, and point-to-point distance.
example_prompt: A triangle has sides 3, 4, and 5 — give me its area, angles, and perimeter
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — closed-form trig and area formulas are pure floating-point math with no dependencies, ideal for the wasmi runtime.
rationale: Bare-word geometry demand maps cleanly to a reliable client-side calculator that avoids the arithmetic slips of free-form LLM answers.

name: css-selector-test
description: Test a CSS selector against pasted HTML and show which elements match.
example_prompt: Which elements does 'div.card > h2' match in this HTML?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM HTML parse + selector engine (scraper); browser-local.
rationale: Testing selectors against pasted HTML differs from css-select-extract (which fetches a URL) and aids scraping/styling.

name: certificate-fingerprint
description: Computes the SHA-256, SHA-1, and MD5 fingerprints of an X.509 certificate (over the full DER) for trust comparison.
example_prompt: Give me the SHA-256 fingerprint of this certificate
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via PEM/DER decode + sha2/sha1; deterministic hashing performed entirely locally.
rationale: Fingerprint matching is the everyday way to pin or verify a certificate and is trivial yet frequently searched.

name: phred-quality-converter
description: Converts FASTQ Phred quality characters to and from integer scores and error probabilities.
example_prompt: Decode this FASTQ quality string to Phred scores
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; ASCII-offset mapping and 10^(-Q/10) math.
rationale: Bioinformatics QC needs Phred scores pulled out of the packed ASCII quality line.

name: row-major-col-major-converter
description: Reorders a flattened matrix between row-major (C) and column-major (Fortran) layouts.
example_prompt: Convert this row-major 3x3 buffer to column-major
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; transpose-style reindexing.
rationale: C/Fortran/BLAS interop breaks silently on layout mismatch; this fixes it explicitly.

name: image-color-temperature-compare
description: Estimates the white-balance / correlated color temperature of two images and reports the Kelvin and tint difference between them.
example_prompt: Are these two photos the same white balance? Compare their color temperature.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes gray-world/illuminant estimates per image and diffs them locally.
rationale: Matching white balance across a shoot is a constant editing task and a Kelvin delta is far more useful than eyeballing.

name: image-noise-level-compare
description: Estimates the noise floor (sigma) of two images and reports which is noisier and by how much, per channel.
example_prompt: Which of these two ISO settings produced less noise?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM estimates noise via high-pass/MAD on flat regions of each image client-side.
rationale: Objectively comparing noise between camera/setting choices beats squinting at 100% crops.

name: midi-cc-diff
description: Diffs the continuous-controller (CC) automation between two MIDI files, reporting changed controllers and value curves.
example_prompt: What CC automation changed between these two MIDI files?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses CC events per track and compares them locally.
rationale: Expression/modulation edits live in CC data that note-level MIDI diffs ignore entirely.

name: midi-program-change-diff
description: Compares program-change/instrument assignments per channel between two MIDI files.
example_prompt: Did the instrument assignments change between these two MIDI files?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans program-change events per channel in-browser.
rationale: Instrument reassignment changes playback drastically and is easy to overlook without a focused diff.

name: flac-metadata-compare
description: Compares STREAMINFO fields and Vorbis comments between two FLAC files and reports the differences.
example_prompt: Compare the metadata and stream info of these two FLAC files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses FLAC metadata blocks directly in-browser.
rationale: Verifying that a re-encode preserved sample rate, depth, and tags needs a focused FLAC diff.

name: dns-zone-diff
description: Compares two BIND-style DNS zone files and reports added, removed, and changed records plus whether the SOA serial was correctly bumped.
example_prompt: Diff these two zone files and tell me which DNS records changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses both zone files (RFC 1035 master format) and diffs by name+type+rdata locally; no DNS server needed.
rationale: Zone-edit review needs record-level diffing and serial-bump checks, and the catalog has only zone parsers/validators/generators.

name: forecast-accuracy-report
description: Compares a forecast series against actuals and computes MAPE, MAE, RMSE, and bias overall and per period to grade forecast quality.
example_prompt: Compare my forecast vs actual sales and tell me how accurate the forecast was
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM aligns both series on the time key and computes error metrics locally; standard numeric work in WASM.
rationale: Forecast scoring is a recurring analytics need with specific error metrics that a generic series diff doesn't compute.

name: population-stability-index
description: Computes the Population Stability Index (and per-bin contributions) between an expected and an actual distribution to quantify model-input drift.
example_prompt: Compute the PSI between my training distribution and this month's scoring data
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM bins both numeric/categorical columns and sums the PSI formula in-browser; it is pure statistics on uploaded data.
rationale: PSI is the industry-standard model-monitoring drift metric with a specific binned formula not covered by the existing KS/Wasserstein tools.

name: rss-feed-diff
description: Compares two snapshots of an RSS/Atom feed and lists new, removed, and edited items by GUID/link with title and date deltas.
example_prompt: Diff these two RSS feed snapshots and show me the new and removed items
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM feed XML parsing + item-keyed comparison; runs locally
rationale: Detecting feed changes offline is useful for archiving, monitoring, and content audits.

name: structured-data-diff
description: Compares JSON-LD structured data between two HTML pages, showing changed schema.org types and property values.
example_prompt: Diff the JSON-LD structured data on these two pages and show what changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML script extraction + JSON-LD comparison; client-side
rationale: Rich-result eligibility breaks when structured data drifts, and a diff pinpoints the regressed property.

name: head-elements-diff
description: Compares the document <head> of two HTML pages, reporting added/removed scripts, stylesheets, preloads, and meta tags.
example_prompt: Compare the <head> of these two HTML pages and show added or removed scripts and links
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM head parsing + element-set comparison; runs locally
rationale: Head changes (new trackers, dropped preloads) affect performance and privacy and are easy to overlook.

name: git-range-diff
description: Compares two patch series (sets of commits as diffs) and shows how the patches themselves changed, like git range-diff.
example_prompt: Compare these two versions of my patch series
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse both diff sets, match patches by similarity, and diff the diffs in-memory
rationale: Reviewing how a rebased or amended branch changed is hard, and a range-diff makes the meta-diff legible.

name: matrix-elementwise-diff
description: Computes A−B element-wise for two same-shape matrices, plus relative difference and the location of the largest deviation.
example_prompt: Subtract matrix B from matrix A element by element and tell me the biggest difference
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: matrix parsing and elementwise arithmetic, fully client-side
rationale: Comparing two numeric matrices (expected vs actual) is a constant need in numerics and there's no single-purpose diff for it yet.

name: qq-quantile-comparison
description: Computes matched quantiles of two samples for Q-Q comparison and reports the quantile-by-quantile differences.
example_prompt: Compare the distributions of these two samples with a Q-Q table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: sorting and quantile interpolation, fully local
rationale: Q-Q comparison reveals distributional differences beyond means and needs paired-quantile output.

name: nearest-neighbor-matcher
description: For each point in set A, finds its nearest point in set B (Euclidean) and reports the match and distance.
example_prompt: Match each point in list A to its closest point in list B
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pairwise distance scan, fully sandboxed
rationale: Comparing two point sets by nearest-neighbor matching is common in geometry and record linkage with no tool.

name: mutual-information-calculator
description: Computes the mutual information (and normalized MI) between two discrete variables from their paired samples.
example_prompt: Compute the mutual information between these two columns of categories
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: joint/marginal histogram and log arithmetic, no network
rationale: MI captures nonlinear dependence between two variables that correlation misses and has no client-side tool.

name: aspect-ratio-compare
description: Compares two width×height pairs, reporting simplified ratios and the crop/letterbox needed to match.
example_prompt: How do 1920x1080 and 1280x1024 compare in aspect ratio?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reduces ratios and computes fit math locally; pure arithmetic, offline.
rationale: Designers and video editors need to know fit/crop between two formats — distinct from raw dimension comparison.

name: wcag-contrast-compare
description: Compares two foreground/background color pairs against WCAG AA/AAA contrast thresholds.
example_prompt: Which of these two text/background color pairs passes WCAG AA?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes relative-luminance contrast ratios locally; offline.
rationale: Accessibility decisions need a direct pass/fail comparison of candidate color pairs, which perceptual delta-E tools don't give.

name: us-uk-spelling-diff
description: Compares two texts and flags words that differ only by US vs UK spelling conventions.
example_prompt: Show me the US/UK spelling differences between these two drafts
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM uses a bundled US↔UK spelling map to align and diff locally; offline.
rationale: Editors localizing content need to isolate dialect differences from real content changes, which a raw diff buries.

name: unit-magnitude-compare
description: Compares two physical quantities given in different units by converting to a common base.
example_prompt: Which is larger, 5 miles or 8 kilometers?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses units and converts via a bundled factor table locally; offline.
rationale: Comparing magnitudes across unit systems is a frequent everyday question distinct from price-per-unit comparison.

name: color-blindness-compare
description: Simulates how two colors appear under common color-vision deficiencies and reports whether they stay distinguishable.
example_prompt: Will these two chart colors be confusable for deuteranopia?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies CVD transform matrices and computes the resulting distance locally; offline.
rationale: Accessible data-viz requires checking that two key colors remain distinct for color-blind users.

name: pgp-key-compare
description: Compares two PGP/GPG public keys by fingerprint, user IDs, algorithm, and expiry.
example_prompt: Are these two PGP public keys the same identity?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the OpenPGP packets and diffs key metadata locally; offline.
rationale: Confirming whether two key blocks represent the same key/identity is a trust-critical task best done locally.

name: column-formatter
description: Formats a flat list into aligned multi-column output like `ls -C` or `column -t`, fitting a chosen terminal width.
example_prompt: Lay out these filenames in aligned columns for an 80-char terminal
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — width measurement and column packing, no IO.
rationale: The column-layout core of lscoltui/pretty-ls/colorls is a clean, reusable text utility.

name: gear-ratio
description: Compute gear/sprocket ratios and resulting RPM, torque, and speed.
example_prompt: What's the ratio and output RPM for a 14T to 50T sprocket at 3000 RPM?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM arithmetic, offline.
rationale: Useful for cycling, machining, and robotics with no existing equivalent.

name: language-code-converter
description: Converts between language names and ISO 639-1/639-2/639-3 codes (and back) for a value or a whole column.
example_prompt: Convert these language names to ISO 639-1 codes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: embedded ISO 639 lookup tables, no network.
rationale: Localization and NLP datasets need consistent language codes, and while country codes are covered, language codes are not.

name: css-important-finder
description: Lists every !important declaration in a stylesheet with its selector and line for cleanup.
example_prompt: Find all the !important rules in this CSS
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM declaration scan; runs entirely in-browser
rationale: Specificity-war cleanup starts with locating every !important override.

name: toml-key-sorter
description: Sorts keys within each TOML table (and optionally orders tables) while preserving values.
example_prompt: alphabetize the keys in my Cargo.toml dependencies
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses TOML and re-emits with sorted keys per table client-side
rationale: Sorted dependency tables produce clean diffs and avoid merge conflicts in lockfile-adjacent files.

name: collapse-consecutive-duplicates
description: Run-length-collapses a numeric sequence so consecutive repeated values become one, optionally emitting run lengths.
example_prompt: Collapse repeated consecutive values in this sequence
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: single linear pass, no dependencies
rationale: Collapsing runs is a distinct sequence-cleanup operation (e.g. for state logs) that full-set dedup doesn't do.

name: wav-to-c-header-array
description: Exports a WAV's PCM samples as a C/C++ header file with a const byte array and length macro for embedding in firmware.
example_prompt: Turn this alert.wav into a C header array for my microcontroller
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the sample bytes and formats them as a comma-separated C array literal — pure text generation
rationale: Embedded audio playback on MCUs needs samples compiled in as arrays, and hand-converting is tedious and error-prone.

name: rot13-rot47-cipher
description: Applies ROT13 and ROT47 substitution to obfuscate or reveal text (self-inverse).
example_prompt: rot13 decode Uryyb Jbeyq
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; fixed character rotation is trivial local computation.
rationale: ROT13/ROT47 appear in CTFs and spoiler text and there is no rotation cipher in the catalog.

name: integer-to-hex-bytes
description: Encodes an integer as a hex/binary byte sequence at a chosen width and endianness, and decodes byte sequences back to a number.
example_prompt: Show 305419896 as little-endian 4-byte hex
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: integer-to-bytes serialization with endianness swap
rationale: Reading/writing binary buffers needs explicit endianness control that the catalog lacks.

name: markdown-definition-list-parser
description: Parses Markdown/PHP-Markdown-Extra definition lists (term + ': ' definition) into structured term→definitions JSON.
example_prompt: Turn this markdown definition list into a JSON object of terms and their definitions.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; pure text parsing of the term/`:`-prefixed-definition grammar, fully client-side.
rationale: Definition lists are common in glossaries and docs but have no easy extractor to reuse the data elsewhere.

name: markdown-blockquote-extractor
description: Extracts all blockquotes from Markdown (with nesting depth and source line numbers) into a clean list.
example_prompt: Extract every blockquote from this markdown article as a plain list.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; scans for `>`-prefixed lines and groups contiguous/nested quotes, no server needed.
rationale: Pulling quotes/callouts out of docs for review or reuse is a frequent manual chore.

name: gradle-dependency-extractor
description: Extracts dependency declarations (group:artifact:version, configuration) from a Gradle build.gradle/.kts file.
example_prompt: List all the dependencies declared in this build.gradle.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; pattern-matches `implementation`/`api`/`testImplementation` coordinate strings locally.
rationale: Gradle files mix DSL and config; pulling just the dependency coordinates is a frequent need.

name: tel-link-parser
description: Parses a tel: URI into its number, extension, and parameters, and reports whether it's in valid RFC 3966 form.
example_prompt: Parse this tel: link and show the number and extension.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; RFC 3966 tel-URI grammar parsing, fully client-side.
rationale: Click-to-call links are easy to malform; validating the tel: URI prevents broken mobile links.

name: css-import-extractor
description: Extracts all @import rules (URLs, media queries, layer) from CSS to map a stylesheet's dependency graph.
example_prompt: Pull all the @import statements out of this CSS and show their media conditions.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; parses @import at-rules with their optional media/layer parts locally.
rationale: @import chains affect load order and performance; listing them surfaces hidden CSS dependencies.

name: aria-role-extractor
description: Inventories explicit and implicit ARIA roles plus aria-* attributes per element, producing a role map of the document.
example_prompt: Extract the ARIA roles and attributes used in this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM DOM parse with a static implicit-role table; no scoring, just extraction, all local.
rationale: Understanding a page's accessibility tree starts with knowing which roles are declared, a pure extraction step distinct from any audit.

name: html-class-id-inventory
description: Lists all unique class names and IDs used in an HTML document with usage counts, surfacing duplicate IDs.
example_prompt: List every class and id used in this HTML with counts
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM attribute scan over the pasted markup.
rationale: A class/ID census is the starting point for CSS dead-code hunts and catches accidental duplicate IDs.

name: structured-field-parser
description: Parses an RFC 8941 HTTP structured field (list, dictionary, or item) into a typed JSON structure with parameters.
example_prompt: Parse this structured header: a=1, b=(x y);q=0.5
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM grammar parse of the field value string; local only.
rationale: Modern headers (Accept-CH, Cache-Status, Priority) use structured fields whose nested syntax is hard to read raw.

name: ordinal-converter
description: Converts cardinal numbers to ordinals (1→1st, 22→22nd) or spelled-out ordinals, in bulk.
example_prompt: Turn these numbers into ordinals like 1st, 2nd, 3rd
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: suffix rules with teen exceptions, fully local
rationale: Generating ranked lists and dates correctly handles the 11th/21st/22nd edge cases that trip people up.

name: longest-line-finder
description: Lists the longest lines and any lines exceeding a chosen character-width threshold.
example_prompt: Find all lines over 100 characters in this file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: measures line lengths locally, no I/O
rationale: Width limits matter for code style and terminal output, and pinpointing overruns beats scrolling manually.

name: thd-analyzer
description: Measures total harmonic distortion (THD and THD+N) of a recorded single-frequency test tone.
example_prompt: Compute the THD of this 1kHz test tone recording
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM FFT harmonic-summation on PCM (ffmpeg decodes); runs in-browser.
rationale: THD is the core bench measurement for testing audio gear, amps, and converters.

name: rrule-builder
description: Builds and explains iCalendar RRULE recurrence rules and previews upcoming dates.
example_prompt: Give me an RRULE for every second Tuesday of the month and list the next 5 dates
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM recurrence expander; all date math is computed in-process.
rationale: Recurring scheduling (zenplanner/Booking.js territory) hinges on RRULE syntax that is notoriously hard to author by hand.

name: protein-properties
description: Compute a protein's molecular weight, isoelectric point, and amino-acid composition from its sequence.
example_prompt: Molecular weight and pI of MKTAYIAKQR...
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM residue tables and pK math, offline.
rationale: Biochemists routinely compute these, and only DNA/chemical-formula tools exist.

name: license-file-generator
description: Produces a complete LICENSE file (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, GPL, etc.) with author name and year substituted in.
example_prompt: give me an MIT license for 2026, author Jane Doe
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with bundled full license texts and token substitution; fully local.
rationale: The exact legal text matters and people routinely fetch it from a website — bundling it makes it instant and offline.

name: plantuml-class-scaffold
description: Generates PlantUML class-diagram source from a spec of classes, fields, methods, and relationships.
example_prompt: PlantUML class diagram for User, Order with a 1-to-many relation
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM templating emitting PlantUML text; client-side.
rationale: Lets users author class diagrams from a concise spec without memorizing PlantUML notation.

name: sstv-image-encoder
description: Encodes an image into an SSTV (slow-scan TV) audio transmission in a chosen mode (e.g., Martin, Scottie, Robot).
example_prompt: Encode this image as Martin M1 SSTV audio
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: maps pixel rows to FM-modulated tone sequences per the SSTV mode spec + WAV encode, local.
rationale: The inverse of the existing SSTV decoder, this lets ham operators and hobbyists prepare image transmissions offline.

name: mojibake-detect
