description: Detects double-encoded UTF-8 (mojibake) such as 'Ã©' for 'é' and reports the suspect spans.
example_prompt: Is this text mojibake — does it look like double-encoded UTF-8?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — encoding-pattern heuristics run in-process over the string
rationale: Mojibake silently corrupts imported text and identifying it is the first step to recovering the original.

name: preload-hint-validator
description: Validates <link rel=preload/preconnect/prefetch> hints for required as/type/crossorigin attributes and flags unused or duplicate hints.
example_prompt: Validate the resource hints in this HTML head
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tag validation against the rel=preload spec rules; local.
rationale: A preload without a correct `as` is ignored or double-fetched, wasting the optimization silently.

name: graphql-schema-lint
description: Lints a GraphQL SDL schema for convention issues — naming, missing descriptions, nullable list anti-patterns, and unused types.
example_prompt: Lint my GraphQL schema for style and design issues
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM SDL parser plus a configurable ruleset; local.
rationale: Schema design conventions are easy to drift from across a team and a linter enforces consistency.

name: editorconfig-validator
description: Validates .editorconfig syntax, flags unknown properties, conflicting/duplicate sections, and invalid glob patterns.
example_prompt: Check this .editorconfig for errors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM INI-style parser with a bundled property table; fully offline
rationale: Bad editorconfig rules silently fail to apply across an editor team.

name: tsconfig-validator
description: Validates tsconfig.json compilerOptions against known keys and enum values, flagging deprecated, conflicting, or mistyped options.
example_prompt: Is my tsconfig.json valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON parse against a bundled compilerOptions schema; offline
rationale: Typo'd compiler options are silently ignored by tsc, causing confusing build behavior.

name: circleci-config-validator
description: Checks .circleci/config.yml for version, orbs/jobs/workflows wiring, and references to undefined jobs or executors.
example_prompt: Check my CircleCI config for undefined job references
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM YAML parse + cross-reference resolution; offline
rationale: Catches broken workflow wiring before burning a CI run.

name: codeowners-validator
description: Lints CODEOWNERS for malformed path patterns, invalid owner handles, and duplicate or overshadowed rules.
example_prompt: Lint my CODEOWNERS file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM pattern/line parsing; pure local rules
rationale: A shadowed or malformed line silently leaves files with no required reviewer.

name: pyproject-validator
description: Validates pyproject.toml [build-system] and [project] tables for PEP 621 fields and dependency-specifier syntax.
example_prompt: Validate my pyproject.toml
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM TOML parser + PEP 508 specifier checker; offline
rationale: Bad project metadata or specifiers break pip builds with unclear errors.

name: eslintrc-validator
description: Checks ESLint config (legacy rc or flat) for unknown rule severities, malformed extends/plugins, and invalid env keys.
example_prompt: Validate my eslint config
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON/YAML parse against a bundled schema; offline
rationale: A malformed ESLint config can crash the linter or silently disable rules.

name: linear-constraint-feasibility-checker
description: Checks whether a candidate point satisfies a set of linear equality and inequality constraints and lists violations.
example_prompt: Does x=2, y=3 satisfy x+y<=4 and x>=0?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: evaluates each constraint row against the point, offline.
rationale: Quick feasibility lint for LP/optimization inputs with no existing counterpart.

name: text-box
description: Draws a Unicode/ASCII box or frame around a block of text with selectable border styles.
example_prompt: put this in a double-line box: SHIP IT
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — width measurement and border composition only.
rationale: The 'boxes' CLI utility from awesome-shell, handy for callouts and ASCII diagrams.

name: clustered-heatmap
description: Reorders matrix rows and columns via hierarchical clustering before rendering the heatmap so similar groups sit together.
example_prompt: Cluster and draw a heatmap of this gene-expression matrix
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs agglomerative clustering on distances then emits the reordered SVG heatmap — all CPU-side, no server.
rationale: Clustered heatmaps are the standard view in bioinformatics and analytics, and the clustering step adds real value over a plain heatmap.

name: ip-address-group
description: Groups a list of IPv4/IPv6 addresses into their containing subnets at a chosen CIDR prefix length.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — masking each address to the prefix and bucketing is integer math on parsed octets, fully local.
rationale: Collapsing scattered log IPs into networks is a core triage step for analysts and directly fulfills the harvested 'Group IP addresses' demand.

name: sbv-to-srt
description: Converts YouTube SBV caption files into SubRip .srt.
example_prompt: Convert this YouTube .sbv captions file to SRT
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (simple line/timestamp parser); no network needed.
rationale: SBV is a YouTube-only format that almost every other tool rejects, so a converter unblocks reuse.

name: ttml-to-srt
description: Converts TTML/DFXP caption XML into SubRip .srt.
example_prompt: Convert this TTML captions file to SRT
loader_feasibility:
plain Rust→WASM (quick-xml over

timing attrs); deterministic, browser-local.
rationale: Broadcast and streaming platforms emit TTML/DFXP that consumer tools can't read.

name: pcx-to-png
description: Decodes a vintage PCX image (RLE-compressed, palettized) into a PNG.
example_prompt: Convert this old .pcx image to png
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a PCX decoder expands the RLE/palette data and encodes PNG in-browser.
rationale: PCX is a common format in retro game assets and DOS-era archives that modern tools refuse to open.

name: xspf-to-m3u
description: Flattens an XSPF XML playlist into an extended M3U with locations and titles.
example_prompt: convert this xspf playlist to m3u
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — XML parse of track locations, emit M3U lines locally.
rationale: XSPF exports from VLC often need to feed M3U-only tools and embedded players.

name: mxl-to-musicxml
description: Decompresses a zipped MXL score into its plain uncompressed MusicXML document.
example_prompt: unzip this mxl file into plain musicxml
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the zip crate reads the MXL container and extracts the root XML entirely in-browser.
rationale: MXL is just a ZIP and many parsers and diff tools need the raw MusicXML inside it.

name: properties-to-yaml
description: Converts a Java .properties file into nested YAML by expanding dotted keys into a tree.
example_prompt: Convert this application.properties into YAML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: line parsing plus tree-building and YAML emit, all in-memory.
rationale: Spring Boot devs constantly switch between flat .properties and nested application.yml.

name: csv-to-wav-pcm
description: Synthesizes a WAV file from a CSV of numeric samples at a chosen sample rate and bit depth.
example_prompt: Render this CSV of samples to a 44.1kHz WAV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: clamping/quantizing samples and writing a RIFF/PCM header is pure byte assembly, in-browser.
rationale: Lets users hear a generated or edited waveform without any DAW or server-side encoder.

name: markdown-table-diff
description: Compares two Markdown tables cell-by-cell using a key column, reporting changed, added, and removed rows.
example_prompt: Compare these two Markdown tables and highlight the rows that changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse pipe-delimited table rows and diff by key column locally
rationale: Docs and README maintainers edit Markdown tables and need precise cell-level change tracking.

name: subtitle-diff
description: Compares two subtitle files (SRT/VTT) and reports text edits and timing shifts cue-by-cue.
example_prompt: Compare these two subtitle files and show which captions changed text or timing
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse cues into timestamp+text records and diff them locally
rationale: Subtitle editors need to track per-cue text and timing changes between revisions.

name: html-dom-diff
description: Parses two HTML documents into DOM trees and reports added, removed, and modified nodes.
example_prompt: Diff these two HTML pages at the DOM level so formatting noise is ignored
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML parser; tree diff over normalized DOM nodes runs client-side
rationale: Comparing scraped or rendered HTML by raw text is hopeless; DOM-level diff surfaces real changes.

name: font-glyph-coverage-diff
description: Compares the glyph coverage of two font files and lists which codepoints each supports that the other doesn't.
example_prompt: Compare these two fonts and tell me which characters one supports but the other lacks
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM ttf-parser reads both fonts' cmap tables; codepoint set diff is local
rationale: Choosing between fonts or validating a subset requires knowing exactly which glyphs differ.

name: wordlist-overlap-matrix
description: Compares three or more lists pairwise and outputs an overlap/Jaccard matrix showing how similar each pair is.
example_prompt: I have five keyword lists — show me a Jaccard similarity matrix of how much they overlap
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; pairwise set intersection and Jaccard scores over hash sets are local
rationale: Comparing many lists at once (audiences, tag sets, keyword groups) needs a matrix, not pairwise diffs.

name: robots-txt-diff
description: Compares two robots.txt files by user-agent group and reports changed allow/disallow rules.
example_prompt: Diff these two robots.txt files and show rule changes per agent
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — robots grammar parse + grouped rule comparison, local
rationale: A flipped Disallow can deindex a site, so per-agent rule diffing catches dangerous changes line diffs bury.

name: changelog-new-entries
description: Diffs two CHANGELOG files and extracts only the entries present in the newer one.
example_prompt: What entries were added in the new changelog versus the old one?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse changelog sections and set-difference entries, local
rationale: Pulling just the new changelog entries is a frequent release-notes task done from two files.

name: avro-schema-compat-diff
description: Checks whether one Avro schema is BACKWARD, FORWARD, or FULL compatible with another per Avro resolution rules.
example_prompt: Are these two Avro schemas backward compatible? Show me what changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: both schemas are JSON; apply Avro resolution rules in-memory, fully offline
rationale: Schema-registry compatibility decisions are error-prone by eye and there is no Avro diff in the catalog.

name: hosts-file-diff
description: Reports added, removed, and remapped host entries between two /etc/hosts files, normalizing whitespace and comments.
example_prompt: Diff these two hosts files and tell me which mappings changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse IP→hostname pairs from both files and set-diff them locally
rationale: Hosts-file drift causes baffling routing bugs; a normalized entry diff pinpoints the change instantly.

name: crontab-diff
description: Diffs two crontab files job-by-job, matching on command and showing added, removed, and reschedule changes.
example_prompt: Compare these two crontabs and show what schedules changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse cron lines into schedule+command pairs and diff them, no network
rationale: Reordered cron lines defeat text diff; a job-matched diff reveals real schedule changes and is distinct from overlap checks.

name: dts-api-diff
description: Compares two TypeScript .d.ts declaration files and reports added, removed, and changed exported types, functions, and signatures.
example_prompt: Diff the public API between these two .d.ts files and flag breaking changes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a compiled TS/JS declaration parser builds export tables and diffs signatures locally
rationale: Library maintainers need a public-API breaking-change report and no tool diffs declaration surfaces.

name: eslint-config-diff
description: Resolves two ESLint configs to effective rule sets and reports which rules were enabled, disabled, or re-severitied.
example_prompt: Diff these two eslint configs and show me the effective rule changes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse both JSON/YAML configs, flatten rules, and diff rule→severity maps offline
rationale: Lint-config drift across projects or upgrades is hard to audit by raw file diff.

name: tsconfig-diff
description: Compares two tsconfig.json files by effective compilerOptions, including include/exclude and strictness flags.
example_prompt: Compare these two tsconfig files and tell me which compiler options differ
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse both JSON configs and diff the options maps in-browser
rationale: Mismatched compiler options cause confusing build differences that a focused diff resolves fast.

name: notebook-diff
description: Diffs two Jupyter .ipynb notebooks by cell source, ignoring volatile outputs, execution counts, and metadata.
example_prompt: Compare these two notebooks but ignore the outputs and execution counts
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: both notebooks are JSON; strip noise fields and diff cell sources locally
rationale: Raw ipynb JSON diffs are unreadable; a cell-aware, output-stripped diff is what data scientists actually need.

name: parquet-schema-diff
description: Compares the schemas of two Parquet files and reports added, removed, and type-changed columns and nesting.
example_prompt: Diff the schemas of these two Parquet files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: read the footer metadata of both Parquet files and diff the column schemas in-browser
rationale: Data-pipeline breakages often stem from a column type or nullability change that a schema diff catches early.

name: relative-error-calculator
description: Given measured-vs-reference value pairs, computes absolute error, relative error, MAE, RMSE, and MAPE.
example_prompt: Compute the RMSE and MAPE between my predictions and the actual values
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: per-pair error aggregation, runs locally.
rationale: The standard accuracy summary for comparing estimates to ground truth, with no spreadsheet needed.

name: histogram-distance
description: Compares two histograms via chi-square distance, intersection, Bhattacharyya, and earth-mover (binned) measures.
example_prompt: Compare these two histograms and tell me how different they are
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: bin-wise distance formulas over arrays, fully client-side.
rationale: Picking the right histogram-distance is non-obvious; offering several side-by-side is genuinely useful.

name: pcm-signed-unsigned-converter
description: Converts 8-bit PCM between signed and unsigned representations by toggling the sign bias.
example_prompt: Convert this unsigned 8-bit WAV to signed PCM
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: adds or subtracts 128 per byte, trivial and fully client-side.
rationale: 8-bit PCM disagreements between signed and unsigned conventions cause a loud DC click until corrected.

name: uri-template-expand
description: Expands an RFC 6570 URI Template against supplied variables, supporting all operator levels.
example_prompt: expand /users/{id}{?fields*} with id=7 and fields=name,email
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; template parsing and variable substitution are pure string ops.
rationale: Many APIs (GitHub, hypermedia) publish URI templates and expanding them correctly by hand is hard.

name: etag-generator
description: Computes a strong or weak ETag (content hash) for given text or bytes.
example_prompt: generate an ETag for this response body
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; sha2 hashing compiles to WASM and runs locally.
rationale: Setting deterministic ETags for static caching needs a content hash, which has no current tool.

name: tel-uri-builder
description: Builds and validates tel:, sms:, and facetime: URIs from a phone number, normalizing to E.164.
example_prompt: make a tel: link for +1 (415) 555-0132
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; number normalization and URI assembly run locally.
rationale: Click-to-call links need clean E.164 formatting that people routinely format incorrectly.

name: relative-time-formatter
description: Formats a timestamp (or two timestamps) into a relative phrase like '3 days ago' or 'in 2 hours'.
example_prompt: how long ago was 2026-06-20T08:00:00Z?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; difference computation and unit selection are local (now supplied by host).
rationale: Turning timestamps into human-friendly relative text is a constant UI and writing need.

name: iso7064-mod97-checkdigit
description: Computes and validates ISO 7064 mod-97-10 check digits used by IBAN and similar identifiers.
example_prompt: validate IBAN GB82WEST12345698765432
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: rearrange, base-36 expand, and take mod 97, all client-side.
rationale: IBAN/mod-97 validation is needed for finance test fixtures and has no privacy-safe local tool.

name: zigzag-encoder
description: Applies and reverses Protocol Buffers zigzag encoding that maps signed ints to small unsigned ints.
example_prompt: zigzag encode -3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — shift/XOR integer ops, fully local.
rationale: Developers debugging protobuf/varint wire data need this exact transform.

name: leb128-encoder
description: Encodes and decodes integers in unsigned/signed LEB128 variable-length byte form.
example_prompt: LEB128 encode 624485
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — 7-bit grouping with continuation bits, deterministic and local.
rationale: LEB128 is everywhere in WASM/DWARF/protobuf and tedious to compute manually.

name: emoji-shortcode
description: Convert between :shortcode: aliases and actual emoji characters in text.
example_prompt: replace :rocket: and :tada: with the actual emoji
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM shortcode lookup table; no network.
rationale: Round-tripping emoji shortcodes is common when moving text between platforms with different conventions.

name: markdown-footnote-extractor
description: Collects all footnote definitions and their references from Markdown and reports orphans or duplicates.
example_prompt: List every footnote in this article and flag any unused ones
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: regex/scan for [^id] markers and definitions over the string, no server.
rationale: Long-form writers lose track of footnotes; a local audit catches broken references instantly.

name: conventional-commit-parser
description: Parses Conventional Commit messages into type, scope, breaking-change flag, subject, and footer trailers.
example_prompt: Parse these git commit messages into type and scope
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: grammar regex over each message line, runs fully in-browser.
rationale: Structuring commit messages drives changelogs and version bumps and is easy to validate locally.

name: id3v1-tag-reader
description: Reads the fixed 128-byte ID3v1/ID3v1.1 trailer at the end of an MP3 and reports title, artist, album, year, comment, track and genre.
example_prompt: Does this mp3 have a legacy ID3v1 tag, and what's in it?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — only the last 128 bytes are inspected as a fixed-offset struct, trivially browser-local
rationale: Old rips and hardware players still rely on ID3v1, and users need to see it separately from ID3v2 to reconcile mismatches.

name: midi-tempo-map-extractor
description: Extracts all tempo-change meta events from a MIDI file and produces a tempo map listing tick position, time, and BPM.
example_prompt: Show me the tempo changes in this midi file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — scans for FF 51 set-tempo meta events and converts microseconds-per-quarter to BPM in-memory
rationale: Tempo maps are needed to align MIDI with audio or click tracks, and they're scattered through the file as raw meta events.

name: pdb-structure-parser
description: Extracts chains, residues, atom counts, and header metadata from a PDB protein structure file into a summary table.
example_prompt: Parse this PDB file and tell me how many chains and residues it has
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM fixed-column record parsing of the PDB format; runs on the local file
rationale: Structural biologists routinely need a quick chain/residue inventory of a structure without loading a molecular viewer.

name: robots-txt-parser
description: Parses robots.txt into structured per-user-agent allow/disallow rules plus sitemap references.
example_prompt: Parse this robots.txt and show the rules per crawler
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line parser; pure text processing.
rationale: Makes crawl directives readable at a glance.

name: svg-path-parser
description: Parses an SVG path 'd' attribute into a normalized list of commands and absolute coordinates.
example_prompt: Break down this SVG path data into its commands and points.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizes the path mini-language and resolves relative-to-absolute coords locally.
rationale: Editing or analyzing SVG paths by hand is error-prone; a structured command list makes it tractable.

name: complex-number-parser
description: Parses complex-number strings ("3+4i", "2-5j", "-i", "5") into {real, imaginary} plus modulus and argument.
example_prompt: Parse 3+4i into real and imaginary parts and give its modulus
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — string parsing and basic trig, runs in wasmi.
rationale: Engineering/EE notes mix i and j conventions and need reliable parsing into components.

name: math-equation-extractor
description: Scans a document for inline and display math ($...$, \(...\), \[...\], $$...$$) and returns each LaTeX equation as a list.
example_prompt: Pull out all the LaTeX equations from this document
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — delimiter scanning over text, no TeX engine.
rationale: Collecting every formula from a paper for review or reuse is otherwise a manual hunt.

name: wkt-geometry-parser
description: Parses WKT geometry (POINT/LINESTRING/POLYGON) into coordinate arrays and computes length/area.
example_prompt: Parse this WKT POLYGON and give me its area
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — recursive coordinate parsing plus shoelace/haversine math, client-side.
rationale: WKT is a common GIS exchange string but reading its geometry and measuring it needs a parser.

name: sepia-convert
description: Applies a tunable sepia tone for a warm vintage look.
example_prompt: Give this photo a sepia tone
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — fixed 3x3 color matrix multiply per pixel
rationale: A specific, popular single-purpose effect that the excluded generic filter tool doesn't expose directly.

name: daltonize-image
description: Adjusts colors to be more distinguishable for a chosen type of color blindness.
example_prompt: Daltonize this chart for protanopia
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — fixed color-space matrices remap and redistribute error per pixel
rationale: Making charts and UI accessible to color-blind viewers is valuable and distinct from simulation.

name: css-color-normalizer
description: Rewrites every color in a stylesheet to one chosen format (hex, rgb, or hsl).
example_prompt: Convert all the colors in this CSS to hex
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM color parser/converter; deterministic math, fully client-side.
rationale: Mixed color notations make stylesheets inconsistent and hard to grep; one canonical form fixes it.

name: chess-best-move
description: Analyzes a chess position (FEN) and returns the engine's best move and evaluation.
example_prompt: What's the best move in this position: rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 2
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a minimax/alpha-beta chess engine compiles to WASM and runs locally.
rationale: SparkChess/Miniclip demand reflects interest in chess analysis, which a small local engine can satisfy without multiplayer servers.

name: unicode-normalize
description: Normalizes text between Unicode NFC, NFD, NFKC, and NFKD forms.
example_prompt: normalize this text to NFC: café
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the `unicode-normalization` crate ships its tables into the wasm binary, running offline.
rationale: Normalization fixes invisible duplicate-glyph and combining-mark bugs that break search, dedup, and string comparison.

name: percentage-calc
description: Solve common percentage problems: X% of Y, percent change, what-percent-is, markup/discount, and tip.
example_prompt: What's the percentage increase from 80 to 120?
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — direct arithmetic, fully local.
rationale: Percentage questions are among the most common everyday math tasks and easy to get subtly wrong by hand.

name: probability-calc
description: Compute PDF/CDF/quantiles and sample stats for common distributions (normal, binomial, Poisson, t, etc.).
example_prompt: what's the probability of getting 8+ heads in 10 coin flips?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust (statrs) to WASM — pure compute.
rationale: Distribution calculations are a frequent stats need beyond hypothesis-test.

name: permutations-generate
description: List all permutations (or k-combinations) of a set of items.
example_prompt: list all permutations of [a, b, c]
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM enumeration.
rationale: combinatorics counts arrangements; actually generating them is a separate, frequent need.

name: h264-nal-unit-inspector
description: Parses an H.264 elementary stream and lists its NAL units with types, SPS/PPS parameters, and slice info.
example_prompt: Break down the NAL units in this H.264 stream
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans start codes and decodes NAL/SPS/PPS headers from the byte stream; pure parsing, local.
rationale: Low-level NAL inspection is the go-to tool for diagnosing decode failures and verifying encoder output.

name: gif-color-usage-analyzer
description: Analyzes an animated GIF's global/local palettes and reports color counts and palette efficiency.
example_prompt: How many colors does this GIF actually use?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the GIF palette tables and tallies used colors across frames locally.
rationale: Understanding palette usage guides GIF optimization and quantization decisions without any tooling install.

name: mp3-frame-analyzer
description: Parses MP3 frame headers to report CBR/VBR, real average bitrate, frame count, and Xing/Info header presence.
example_prompt: Analyze the MP3 frames in audio.mp3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM walks the MPEG frame sync headers byte-by-byte, no decoding or server required
rationale: Frame-level truth catches mislabeled bitrates and missing VBR headers that break seeking.

name: json-numeric-precision-check
description: Scans JSON for numbers that lose precision when parsed as IEEE-754 doubles or exceed safe integer range.
example_prompt: Do any numbers in this JSON lose precision as floats?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM re-parses numeric literals with arbitrary-precision comparison client-side.
rationale: Silent precision loss on large IDs and money values causes real bugs that this catches before they ship.

name: readme-generate
description: Generate a structured project README skeleton (badges, install, usage, license sections) from a few inputs.
example_prompt: generate a README for a CLI tool called gizza that resizes images
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM templating; optional transformers-js for prose.
rationale: Project-bootstrap staple distinct from generic template-render.

name: tsconfig-generator
description: Generates a tsconfig.json from target, module, strictness, and output-dir choices.
example_prompt: make a strict tsconfig targeting ES2022 with outDir dist
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: maps options into a compilerOptions object and serializes JSON locally.
rationale: TypeScript config has many interacting flags that are easy to misconfigure manually.

name: quote-card-video
description: Generates a short animated quote-card clip with the quote text, an attribution line, and a styled background.
example_prompt: Make a 6-second quote card: 'Stay hungry, stay foolish' — Steve Jobs, on a gradient
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg `color`/`drawtext`/`fade` lays out and animates the card from text inputs alone in the browser.
rationale: Quote cards are everyday social content and a video version with gentle motion outperforms static images on most feeds.

name: euclidean-rhythm-midi-generator
description: Generates Euclidean rhythm patterns (k hits evenly spread over n steps) as MIDI for drums or melodic gates.
example_prompt: Make a Euclidean rhythm of 5 hits in 8 steps as MIDI
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs the Bjorklund algorithm and writes the resulting note grid to a Standard MIDI File locally.
rationale: Euclidean rhythms are a popular generative-music building block musicians want exported to their DAW.

name: hilbert-matrix-generator
description: Generates the N×N Hilbert matrix (entries 1/(i+j−1)) as exact fractions and reports its notoriously large condition number.
example_prompt: Generate a 6x6 Hilbert matrix with its condition number
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — exact rational entry construction with no dependencies.
rationale: The Hilbert matrix is the canonical ill-conditioned test case for numerical methods and is useful to produce exactly.

name: luhn-test-number-generator
description: Generates Luhn-valid test card numbers for a chosen scheme prefix, clearly labeled as non-real test data.
example_prompt: Generate 5 Luhn-valid Visa test numbers for my checkout tests
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM Luhn check-digit computation with seeded RNG; fully local
rationale: Payment-form tests need valid-format dummy numbers and generating them locally avoids any real-data risk.

name: webp-validator
description: Validates RIFF/WebP container structure and VP8/VP8L/VP8X chunks, reporting whether it's lossy, lossless, or animated.
example_prompt: Validate this WebP file and tell me if it's lossy or lossless
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the RIFF chunk tree directly in the browser.
rationale: WebP support varies and a structural check confirms a file is well-formed before relying on it.

name: gif-structure-validator
description: Validates GIF header, logical screen descriptor, and image/extension blocks, reporting frame count and any malformed blocks.
example_prompt: Check that this GIF is structurally valid
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads GIF block structure in-memory with no decode required.
rationale: Broken GIF block chains crash some decoders; structural validation flags them up front.

name: power-of-two-texture-checker
description: Checks whether a texture's dimensions are power-of-two (and optionally square) for GPU mipmapping compatibility.
example_prompt: Are this texture's dimensions power-of-two?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads dimensions from the header and does bit math client-side.
rationale: Non-POT textures break mipmaps/tiling in many engines and a quick gate prevents runtime surprises.

name: subtitle-encoding-checker
description: Detects non-UTF-8 bytes, stray BOMs, and likely mojibake in a subtitle file and reports the offending lines.
example_prompt: Why do accents look broken in my subtitle file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: byte-level encoding inspection runs entirely client-side.
rationale: Mis-encoded subtitle files render garbled accented characters, a frequent and confusing failure.

name: midi-conformance-validator
description: Validates a Standard MIDI File against the SMF spec: header format, track chunk integrity, running-status correctness, and unbalanced note-on/note-off pairs.
example_prompt: Validate this MIDI file for spec violations and stuck notes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse MThd/MTrk chunks and event stream from the file bytes and apply conformance rules
rationale: Out-of-spec or unbalanced MIDI causes stuck notes and load failures in DAWs that strict validation catches up front.

name: open-graph-validate
description: Validates Open Graph meta tags for required properties and correct types so link previews render.
example_prompt: Check my page's Open Graph tags — why is my preview broken?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML head parse with OG rule set; runs on pasted markup locally
rationale: Missing or malformed OG tags are the top cause of broken social-share previews and are tedious to debug.

name: bom-detect
description: Detects and identifies byte-order marks (UTF-8, UTF-16 LE/BE) at the start of a file that can break parsers.
example_prompt: does this file start with a BOM?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM inspecting leading bytes; fully client-side.
rationale: A stray BOM silently breaks JSON parsers and shell scripts and detecting it explains otherwise baffling errors.

name: graphviz-dot-validate
description: Validates Graphviz DOT source for syntax errors, unbalanced braces, and malformed attribute lists.
example_prompt: check this DOT graph for syntax errors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM DOT grammar parser; text-only validation, fully local.
rationale: DOT errors are cryptic and a local validator gives a precise location instead of a rendering failure.

name: simple-polygon-checker
description: Checks whether a polygon's edges are non-self-intersecting (a simple polygon) and reports any crossing edge pair.
example_prompt: Does this list of vertices form a simple, non-self-intersecting polygon?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pairwise segment-intersection tests, entirely client-side.
rationale: GIS and graphics pipelines reject self-intersecting polygons, so a dedicated validity check saves debugging.

name: float-equality-checker
description: Compares two floating-point numbers by absolute, relative, and ULP distance and explains why a naive == fails.
example_prompt: Why isn't 0.1 + 0.2 equal to 0.3, and how close are they in ULPs?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: IEEE-754 bit inspection and tolerance math, entirely client-side.
rationale: Float-equality bugs are a perennial trap, and a tool that quantifies the gap teaches the right comparison.

name: currency-code-validator
description: Validates ISO 4217 currency codes and returns the currency name and minor-unit precision.
example_prompt: Is 'XBT' a valid ISO 4217 currency code?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the bundled ISO 4217 table; no lookups
rationale: Financial data and invoices require valid currency codes with correct decimal precision.

name: mime-type-validator
description: Validates a MIME type's syntax and parameters and flags unregistered or deprecated types.
example_prompt: Is 'application/json; charset=utf-8' a well-formed MIME type?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing per RFC 6838 grammar; local
rationale: Content-Type mistakes cause silent rendering and parsing failures that a syntax check prevents.

name: hdr-to-png
description: Tone-maps a Radiance .hdr high-dynamic-range image down to a viewable 8-bit PNG.
example_prompt: convert this hdr environment map to a normal png
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the `image` crate decodes HDR and applies tone-mapping in wasmi
rationale: HDR environment maps from 3D/photography pipelines can't be previewed without tone-mapping.

name: geojson-to-kml
description: Renders GeoJSON features as KML for opening in Google Earth.
example_prompt: Turn this GeoJSON into a KML for Google Earth
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML emitter over parsed GeoJSON geometries; deterministic local output.
rationale: The reverse trip is needed to visualize web-mapping data in Google Earth, and no listed tool does it.

name: hyperparameter-grid-search
description: Runs grid search over a user-defined scoring function and returns the best config with a heatmap.
example_prompt: Grid search learning rate [0.01,0.1] x batch [16,32,64] maximizing this score table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM evaluates the grid and renders the score heatmap locally.
rationale: Hyperas/Talos demand is about tuning; a local grid-search visualizer covers the common case.

name: random-search-sampler
description: Samples hyperparameter configurations from specified ranges/distributions for a tuning run.
example_prompt: Sample 20 random configs: lr log-uniform 1e-4..1e-1, dropout 0..0.5, units {64,128,256}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM draws samples with a seeded PRNG and tabulates them offline.
rationale: Random search often beats grid search and Talos users need quick config generation.

name: graph-laplacian-analyzer
description: Computes degree, adjacency, and Laplacian matrices plus spectral metrics for a graph, with an SVG layout.
example_prompt: For edges A-B, B-C, C-A, A-D give me the Laplacian and number of components
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM builds the matrices and runs small-graph eigen analysis client-side.
rationale: Spektral demand is graph neural networks; the underlying graph-spectral math is a reusable offline tool.

name: count-min-sketch
description: Estimates element frequencies in a stream using a Count-Min Sketch and reports heavy hitters.
example_prompt: Find the most frequent items in this large event log
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM maintains the sketch matrix and queries counts in-browser.
rationale: Frequency estimation over streams is a central Streaming Systems / Mining Massive Datasets technique.

name: diff-in-diff
description: Estimates a treatment effect via difference-in-differences from pre/post treatment and control groups.
example_prompt: Run a difference-in-differences on these before/after treatment and control numbers
loader_feasibility: pyodide fits the interaction regression with statsmodels in the browser sandbox.
rationale: Difference-in-differences is a headline method from the Causal Inference demand term.

name: mcmc-sampler
description: Samples from a user-specified target density using Metropolis-Hastings and returns the chain, acceptance rate, and summary stats.

name: gameboy-rom-info

name: gba-rom-info

name: chip8-disassembler

name: gamemaker-data-info
description: Inspects a GameMaker data.win file, listing its sprites, rooms, scripts, and metadata.

name: keyboard-keymap-visualizer

loader_feasibility: Keymap parsing and SVG generation run in plain Rust→WASM with no backend.
rationale: rmk is keyboard firmware; visualizing layers/keymaps is the chief pain point for mechanical-keyboard builders.

name: zx-spectrum-screen-to-png
description: Converts a ZX Spectrum 6912-byte SCR screen dump into a PNG, correctly expanding the interleaved bitmap and attribute color blocks.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the SCR layout is a fixed bit/attr decode; the image crate writes PNG locally.

name: prometheus-metrics-parser
description: Parses Prometheus/OpenMetrics exposition text into a table with HELP/TYPE metadata and per-series summaries.
example_prompt: Parse this /metrics output and show me the top counters
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the exposition format is a line grammar parsed entirely in memory.
rationale: OpenObserve and Vector both ingest Prometheus exposition, which engineers often eyeball raw.

name: prompt-library-organizer

rationale: Skill/prompt managers like skills-manager show demand for keeping a growing prompt library navigable.

name: bgp-update-decoder

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure parsing of the BGP wire format from pasted hex; no live peering.
rationale: Captures the analyzable core of RustyBGP/Holo for routing engineers debugging captures, without running a daemon.

name: fuzz-input-mutator
description: Generates mutated test inputs from a seed using bit flips, havoc, and splicing strategies.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — deterministic (index-seeded) mutation logic running fully in-browser.
rationale: Brings LibAFL-style input mutation to anyone preparing a fuzzing corpus, no harness or install required.

name: graphql-persisted-query-hash

rationale: Apollo/Hasura APQ setups need the exact query hash and there's no convenient offline tool for it.

name: lua-ast-explorer
description: Parses Lua into a labeled syntax tree / token stream so tooling authors can inspect exactly how the parser sees their code.

name: gherkin-feature-linter

name: property-test-generator

rationale: quickcheck/proptest workflows need input generation; this brings that capability to any language or tester.

name: wav-file-inspector

name: special-functions

name: holidays-calc

name: audio-loudness-meter

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM contrast math + color search; browser-local.

name: openapi-diff

name: eth-abi-decode

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM ABI decoding; offline.
rationale: Core web3 debugging tool not covered by the existing eth-unit/address tools.

name: chess-fen-render

name: adler32-checksum

name: heading-anchor-generator

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM slugification rules; pure string transform, browser-local.
rationale: Consistent anchor labels matter for deep-linking docs and are fiddly to produce by hand.

name: endianness-swapper

rationale: Reverse-engineering binary formats and network protocols constantly requires flipping endianness by hand otherwise.

name: prng-generator

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — seeded PRNG state advances deterministically on-device with no entropy source needed.
rationale: Reproducible seeded randomness is handy for testing and simulations, and existing web generators aren't deterministic or private.

name: venn-counts

rationale: Region counts for two- and three-way overlaps are exactly what people need for audience/segment analysis and Venn diagrams, beyond simple two-set boolean ops.

name: parse-client-hints

loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM header tokenizer; purely computational, runs in-browser.

name: food-identify

loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime food classifier + bundled nutrition table; offline.

name: speed-reader

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM tokenizes and paces the text; rendering is purely client-side.
rationale: Direct browser-local realization of SpeedRead with no account or extension needed.

foo

name: htaccess-to-nginx

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses the directives and emits Nginx syntax via pure text transformation.

name: ipfs-cid-generator
description: Computes the IPFS content identifier (CIDv0 and CIDv1) for a file locally without uploading it anywhere.
example_prompt: What's the IPFS CID for this file?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM hashes the bytes (SHA-256) and encodes multihash + base32/base58 — the CID is deterministic and needs no node.
rationale: ipfs-deploy/Discharge users want content-addressing, and verifying a file's CID before/after pinning is a real local need.

name: bench-stats

example_prompt: Give me the stats for these benchmark times: 12, 15, 11, 30, 14, 13
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; arithmetic over the supplied numbers runs entirely locally.
rationale: Delivers a rigorous summary of micro-benchmark runs without opening a spreadsheet.

name: python-benchmark

loader_feasibility: pyodide — executes and times the snippet in the in-browser Python sandbox, no server.
rationale: cmdperf-style micro-benchmarking is valuable, and pyodide makes it safe and instant in the browser.

name: project-scaffold-generator

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — outputs the file set as text, fully client-side.
rationale: scaffold-static and mevn-cli bootstrap front-end starters, and an instant skeleton beats a CLI install plus config.

name: css-dark-mode-generator

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; CSS color parsing and luminance-aware remapping are deterministic text transforms.
rationale: Retrofitting dark mode is a tedious manual job that a smart color-flip can bootstrap in seconds.

name: frecency-ranker

name: git-standup-summary

example_prompt: Make a standup summary from this git log of the last 3 days
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing and grouping of the pasted log; entirely local.
rationale: git-standup automates a chore everyone does manually, and the input is just pasted commit text.

name: asciinema-to-gif

rationale: ttygif and ttystudio fill a real need for shareable terminal demos in READMEs and tutorials.

name: emoji-semantic-search

rationale: Identifier/permalink formats trip people up constantly, and validating them locally is instant and private.

name: xmpp-jid-parser

rationale: JID escaping rules are subtle and a common bug source for XMPP client and bot developers.

name: man-page-summarizer

name: grid-pathfinder

name: git-command-builder

name: model-3d-viewer

name: map-projection-convert

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM evaluates the closed-form projection math locally with no dependencies.
rationale: Mercator demand maps to a precise, frequently-needed geo conversion that developers otherwise hunt for in scattered references.

name: obj-render
description: Loads a 3D .obj mesh and renders it from a chosen camera angle as a shaded image or ASCII view.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the OBJ and runs a software rasterizer (or webgpu-compute), no GPU server required.

name: inflation-calc

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM with a bundled CPI table; browser-local.

name: css-filter-generate
description: Build and preview a CSS filter chain (blur, brightness, contrast, saturate, hue-rotate, drop-shadow).

loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM code emit with preview; produces CSS rather than rasterizing.
rationale: Generates CSS code (unlike the raster image-filter tool) and is a routine front-end task.

name: text-to-regex
description: Generate a regular expression from a plain-English description of the pattern to match.

loader_feasibility: transformers-js small code model runs in-browser; best-effort output the user can verify with regex-test.

name: contrast-matrix
description: Build a contrast-ratio matrix for a palette, showing every foreground/background pair's WCAG AA/AAA pass/fail.
example_prompt: check all color combinations in this 5-color palette for WCAG contrast
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM contrast math + table render; local.
rationale: Design systems need full pairwise contrast grids; contrast-check only evaluates a single pair.

name: imap-protocol-parser
description: Parses and explains raw IMAP client commands and server responses, labeling tags, commands, and data items.

name: godot-scene-inspector
description: Parses a Godot .tscn or .tres resource file into a readable node tree with scripts, resources, and external dependencies listed.

name: obj-model-inspector
description: Parses a Wavefront OBJ model and reports vertex, face, and material counts, bounding box, and any non-triangulated or missing-normal issues.
example_prompt: Inspect this .obj and tell me its triangle count and bounding box.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — OBJ is a plain-text mesh format parseable entirely in the sandbox with no renderer.
rationale: Kiss3d/raylib developers need quick mesh stats and validity checks before loading a model, without firing up a 3D editor.

name: graph-analyze
description: Report graph metrics: connected components, node degrees, cycles, and PageRank/centrality.

rationale: Quick structural metrics on a graph save spinning up Neo4j for one-off questions.

name: varint-codec

name: sip-message-parser

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM text parser modeled on rsipstack; SIP is line-based text, parsed entirely in the browser.
rationale: VoIP engineers debug raw SIP traces constantly and need them dissected without pasting call metadata into a web service.

name: fill-mask
description: Predicts the most likely tokens to fill a [MASK] in a sentence (BERT-style cloze).

name: embedding-projector
description: Reduces high-dimensional embeddings to 2D via PCA for visual inspection of text relationships.

loader_feasibility: transformers-js embeddings + plain Rust→WASM PCA, rendered client-side.
rationale: Visualizing the embedding space makes representation learning intuitive, mirroring the explanatory blogs in the demand list.

name: ngram-language-model

rationale: N-gram LMs with perplexity are the foundational 'train a language model from scratch' exercise, fully feasible offline.

name: word-forms-generator
description: Generates all inflections of a word: plurals, verb tenses, and adjective/adverb forms.

rationale: Direct map of the Word Forms library demand, useful for search expansion and writing.

name: topic-model-explorer
description: Renders an interactive view of topics, their top terms, and per-document weights from a topic model.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM generates HTML/SVG from a topic-document matrix; fully client-side.
rationale: A self-contained dfr-browser-style topic exploration UI that needs no hosted service.

name: label-distribution-analyzer
description: Reports class balance and label distribution for a labeled dataset.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tallying, offline.
rationale: Class-imbalance audits matter before training and produce an instant local report.

name: word-sense-disambiguator
description: Determines which sense of an ambiguous word is intended in a given context.

loader_feasibility: transformers-js embeds the in-context word and candidate sense glosses, ranking by similarity in WASM.
rationale: Adaptive-skip-gram-style sense resolution improves translation, search, and reading comprehension.

name: korean-jamo-tool
description: Decomposes Hangul syllable blocks into individual jamo and recomposes them back.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure Unicode Hangul algorithm, no data needed.
rationale: Jamo decomposition powers Korean typo-tolerant search, IME logic, and linguistics teaching, all client-side.

name: thai-character-cluster

name: prefill-form-link-builder

name: captcha-image-generator

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM image rasterization (image + ab_glyph) — draws the PNG entirely in the browser.

name: security-headers-generator

name: fractal-generate

name: broken-link-check

name: crossword-generate

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM grid placement plus PNG/PDF rendering, offline.

name: robots-check

loader_feasibility: web fetch of robots.txt + plain-Rust rule matching.
rationale: Useful SEO/crawler check that pairs with the existing sitemap/seo tools.

name: vector-calc

example_prompt: what's the cross product of (1,2,3) and (4,5,6)?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust to WASM — pure compute.
rationale: Vector math is core to physics/graphics and isn't covered by matrix-calc.

name: balance-equation

name: electricity-cost

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM arithmetic; browser-local.

name: glsl-lint

name: loss-calculator

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — direct formulas, no server

name: yara-rule-lint

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM writes the SMF header and empty named tracks with meta-events in-memory.
