name: audacity-label-track-generator
description: Generates an Audacity label-track text file from a list of timestamps and labels for importing as markers.
example_prompt: Make an Audacity label track from these section timestamps
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM writes the tab-separated start/end/label rows Audacity imports, as text client-side.
rationale: Importing markers in bulk is far faster than placing each label by hand in Audacity.

name: csv-template-generator
description: Generates an empty CSV with headers plus one example row from a described field list.
example_prompt: Make a CSV template with columns name, email, age, and one sample row.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: header and example-row emission from a field spec is pure local string work.
rationale: Handing collaborators a correctly-shaped blank CSV reduces import errors and back-and-forth.

name: responsive-email-template-generator
description: Generates a bulletproof table-based responsive HTML email scaffold with inline-style-friendly structure and a preheader.
example_prompt: Make a responsive HTML email template with a header, one CTA button, and a footer
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — emits the nested-table HTML from a layout template, fully offline.
rationale: HTML email requires arcane table layouts for client compatibility that a scaffold gets right.

name: package-json-scaffolder
description: Scaffolds a package.json with name, scripts, type, and engines for a chosen project kind.
example_prompt: Scaffold a package.json for an ESM CLI tool named widgetize
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — JSON assembly from field inputs and script presets, no npm calls.
rationale: Sets up the manifest correctly (type, bin, scripts) so a new package builds without manual fixes.

name: pyproject-toml-generator
description: Generates a pyproject.toml with build-system, project metadata, and optional tool sections.
example_prompt: Generate a pyproject.toml for a hatchling-built package called dataflow
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — TOML assembly from a metadata form and build-backend templates, offline.
rationale: The PEP 621 layout is finicky; a generator avoids the trial-and-error of getting a packageable file.

name: vandermonde-matrix-generator
description: Builds the Vandermonde matrix from a list of nodes for polynomial interpolation, with optional transpose and determinant of node differences.
example_prompt: Build a Vandermonde matrix for the points 1, 2, 3, 5
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — power-table construction, exact in big-rational or float, runs in-browser.
rationale: Vandermonde matrices are the scaffold for interpolation and curve fitting and are commonly assembled by hand wrongly.

name: toeplitz-matrix-builder
description: Builds a Toeplitz matrix from a specified first row and first column (constant diagonals), with a Hermitian/symmetric option.
example_prompt: Build a Toeplitz matrix with first row 1,2,3,4 and first column 1,5,6,7
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — index-difference fill, trivial and fully local.
rationale: Toeplitz matrices model convolutions and time series and are error-prone to lay out manually.

name: circulant-matrix-builder
description: Builds a circulant matrix from a generator vector and reports its eigenvalues as the DFT of that vector.
example_prompt: Build the circulant matrix generated by 2,1,0,1 and give its eigenvalues
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — cyclic-shift fill plus a small FFT, all client-side.
rationale: Circulant matrices diagonalize via the DFT and the bundled eigenvalues make this a genuinely insightful generator.

name: full-factorial-design
description: Generates a full or fractional (2^(k−p)) factorial design matrix with coded and natural factor levels and the alias structure for fractional runs.
example_prompt: Generate a 2^4 full factorial design matrix
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — combinatorial level enumeration with generator-based aliasing, pure computation.
rationale: Factorial designs are foundational to experiments and the alias structure is error-prone to derive manually.

name: central-composite-design
description: Generates a central composite design (factorial + axial star + center points) with configurable axial distance for rotatability.
example_prompt: Generate a rotatable central composite design for 2 factors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — factorial enumeration plus axial-point math, all client-side.
rationale: CCD is the standard second-order experimental design and the rotatability math is easy to get wrong by hand.

name: plackett-burman-design
description: Generates a Plackett–Burman screening design for up to N−1 factors in N runs from the appropriate cyclic generating row.
example_prompt: Generate a 12-run Plackett-Burman design
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — cyclic-shift construction from known generators, pure integer fill.
rationale: Plackett–Burman is the go-to for cheap main-effect screening and a generator removes lookup-table tedium.

name: halton-sequence-generator
description: Generates Halton low-discrepancy quasi-random points in D dimensions using coprime prime bases, with optional Owen scrambling.
example_prompt: Generate 256 Halton points in 2D
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — radical-inverse computation per coordinate, deterministic and local.
rationale: Halton points give far better coverage than pseudo-random for quasi-Monte-Carlo integration and sampling.

name: sobol-sequence-generator
description: Generates Sobol low-discrepancy points in D dimensions from direction numbers, offering superior uniformity for high-dimensional sampling.
example_prompt: Generate 512 Sobol points in 3 dimensions
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bitwise Gray-code recurrence over embedded direction numbers, fully client-side.
rationale: Sobol sequences are the standard for quasi-Monte-Carlo in finance and graphics and need careful direction-number handling a tool can bundle.

name: fantasy-name-generator
description: Generates names for characters, places, and factions by chosen culture or style.
example_prompt: Give me 10 dwarven fortress names
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM composes names from bundled syllable/phoneme tables; deterministic and offline.
rationale: Worldbuilding staple for Dwarf Fortress / NetHack fans and tabletop GMs.

name: implied-volatility-solver
description: Solves the implied volatility of an option given its market price by iterative root-finding.
example_prompt: What implied vol gives a call price of 6.20 at spot 100, strike 100, rate 4%, 90 days?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; Newton/bisection loop over the pricing function, no network.
rationale: Implied vol is the inverse problem traders actually care about and it runs as a tight local numerical loop.

name: chord-finder
description: Names the chord formed by a set of notes and lists the notes for a named chord.
example_prompt: What chord is C E G B flat?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM implements interval/chord theory tables with no network or server.
rationale: Directly realizes the kord music-theory tool as an instant offline reference for musicians.

name: transfer-time-calculator
description: Computes transfer time, throughput, and ETA from any two of size, bandwidth, and duration, with unit conversion (bits/bytes, SI/IEC).
example_prompt: how long to transfer 4.7 GB over a 50 Mbps connection?
loader_feasibility: Simple arithmetic and unit handling in Rust→WASM; no I/O required.
rationale: pv's core value is throughput/ETA math, which translates directly into a handy offline calculator for backups, downloads, and uploads.

name: prisma-flow-diagram
description: Generates a standards-compliant PRISMA systematic-review flow diagram (identification→screening→included) from record counts.
example_prompt: Make a PRISMA diagram: 1200 identified, 300 duplicates, 80 screened out, 42 included.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; deterministic box-and-arrow SVG layout produced client-side.
rationale: Every evidence-synthesis paper needs this exact diagram and authors hand-draw it today.

name: wavelength-convert
description: Convert between wavelength, frequency, and photon energy for EM and sound waves.
example_prompt: What's the frequency of 500nm green light?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM arithmetic; offline.
rationale: Handy physics conversion not in the unit-convert set.

name: iso-week-number
description: Returns the ISO-8601 week number, day-of-year, and calendar quarter for a given date.
example_prompt: what ISO week is 2026-06-19
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM calendar math, no I/O.
rationale: Useful for sprint planning, payroll, and reporting that index time by ISO week or quarter.

name: latin-square-generator
description: Generates a random valid N×N Latin square (each symbol once per row and column) with optional reduced/normalized form.
example_prompt: Generate a random 6x6 Latin square
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — seeded backtracking fill, deterministic and tiny, fully in-browser.
rationale: Latin squares underpin experiment design and puzzles; an instant generator saves manual construction.

name: semver-range-parser
description: Parses a semver range (^, ~, ranges, ||) into its normalized comparator set and tests a list of versions for membership.
example_prompt: Does version 2.3.1 satisfy the range '>=2.0.0 <3.0.0 || ^4.1'?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the semver crate; pure version arithmetic
rationale: Reasoning about which versions a dependency range actually allows is a common, error-prone developer question.

name: reverse-lines
description: Reverses the order of lines in a document (last line first), with an option to also reverse characters within lines.
example_prompt: Reverse the line order of this log so newest is on top
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line reversal; no network
rationale: Flipping log or list order top-to-bottom is a frequent quick transform that's awkward by hand.

name: gradient-map
description: Recolors an image by mapping its luminance through a user-defined multi-stop gradient.
example_prompt: Apply a sunset gradient map to this photo
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — luminance indexes an interpolated gradient LUT, pure lookup
rationale: Gradient maps are a powerful color-grading technique not covered by any current tool.

name: scientific-engineering-notation-converter
description: Converts a numeric column between plain decimal, scientific (1.2e3), and engineering (1.2×10³, exponent multiple of 3) notation.
example_prompt: Convert these values to engineering notation
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure float formatting, no dependencies
rationale: Engineering and lab data constantly needs notation normalization that spreadsheets can't target per-column.

name: float-precision-reducer
description: Round-trips a numeric column through float16, bfloat16, or float32 to simulate and quantify precision loss.
example_prompt: Show what happens to these values at float16 precision
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — `half` crate float conversions, fully local
rationale: ML engineers need to preview quantization error before committing to lower-precision storage.

name: twos-complement-converter
description: Converts a column of signed integers to and from two's-complement binary/hex at a chosen bit width.
example_prompt: Show -42 in 8-bit two's complement hex
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bitwise integer math, no network
rationale: Firmware and protocol debugging constantly needs signed↔two's-complement views the calculator app omits.

name: fixed-width-number-aligner
description: Right-aligns a column of numbers on the decimal point and pads to a fixed width for monospaced display.
example_prompt: align these numbers on the decimal point: 3.5, 12, 0.75, 100.125
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — padding and decimal-position math, fully local.
rationale: Decimal alignment in plain-text tables is fiddly and worth automating.

name: excel-column-converter
description: Converts spreadsheet column labels to numbers and back (A↔1, Z↔26, AA↔27).
example_prompt: what column number is 'AZ'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bijective base-26 arithmetic, deterministic and local.
rationale: Bijective base-26 is non-obvious and constantly needed when scripting spreadsheets.

name: avro-schema-validator
description: Parses and lints an Avro .avsc schema, flagging invalid types, missing fields, and naming issues.
example_prompt: is this Avro schema valid? {paste avsc}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using apache-avro schema parsing; structural validation only, runs client-side.
rationale: Kafka/schema-registry users frequently need to sanity-check Avro schemas before publishing.

name: objectid-parser
description: Parses a MongoDB ObjectId into its embedded timestamp, machine, process, and counter components.
example_prompt: what timestamp is in this ObjectId 507f1f77bcf86cd799439011
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; hex decoding and field extraction are pure computation.
rationale: Extracting the creation time from an ObjectId is a frequent backend debugging task.

name: repeating-decimal-to-fraction
description: Converts repeating decimals (e.g. 0.1(6) or 0.333…) into their exact rational fraction.
example_prompt: What fraction is 0.142857 repeating?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — repeating-block algebra, fully local
rationale: Recovering the exact fraction behind a repeating decimal is a classic task with no quick client-side tool.

name: fips-code-lookup
description: Decodes US FIPS state and county codes to place names and vice versa.
example_prompt: What county is FIPS 06037 and give me the code for Cook County, IL
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM with an embedded compact FIPS table; fully local.
rationale: Census, FARS, and data.gov tables key on FIPS codes that mean nothing without a lookup.

name: png-color-intent-chunk-checker
description: Reports whether a PNG carries color-management intent via sRGB or iCCP chunks, warning when neither is present for color-critical work.
example_prompt: Does this PNG declare an sRGB color intent?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM enumerates PNG ancillary chunks for sRGB/iCCP presence without decoding pixels.
rationale: Missing color-intent chunks cause inconsistent rendering across browsers and print pipelines.

name: exif-timestamp-consistency-checker
description: Compares DateTimeOriginal, DateTimeDigitized, and modify timestamps in EXIF and flags inconsistencies that suggest editing or tampering.
example_prompt: Do the timestamps in this photo's metadata line up?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the three EXIF date fields and diffs them locally.
rationale: Timestamp mismatches are a simple authenticity signal useful for provenance and journalism checks.

name: video-audio-bitdepth-checker
description: Reports the audio sample format/bit depth (e.g., 16-bit vs 24-bit) and flags it against a required depth.
example_prompt: What bit depth is the audio in this file — is it 24-bit?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader reads sample_fmt via ffprobe in WASM and validates the bit depth locally.
rationale: Mastering specs mandate a specific audio bit depth, and silent downconversion is easy to miss without a check.

name: video-head-tail-silence-checker
description: Verifies head/tail audio silence (slate padding) is within a required range and flags too-short or too-long silence.
example_prompt: Check that there's the required 2 seconds of silence at the start and end.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader runs silencedetect at the file boundaries in WASM and measures padding locally.
rationale: Broadcast slates require exact head/tail silence, and getting it wrong is a common rejection reason.

name: audio-chapter-validator
description: Validates podcast/audiobook chapter markers for ordering, non-overlap, and bounds within the file.
example_prompt: Check the chapter markers on this m4b for overlaps or out-of-range times.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — chapter metadata extraction plus duration come from the in-browser demuxer.
rationale: Out-of-order or out-of-bounds chapters break navigation in podcast apps and audiobook players.

name: cache-control-validate
description: Parses a Cache-Control header, validates directive names and values, and warns about contradictory combinations like no-store with max-age.
example_prompt: Check this Cache-Control: private, no-store, max-age=3600, must-revaliate
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM directive parser; no I/O.
rationale: Caching bugs from contradictory directives are subtle and expensive; a linter surfaces them instantly.

name: terraform-resource-scaffold
description: Generates a Terraform resource block skeleton with required and common attributes for a chosen resource type.
example_prompt: scaffold an aws_s3_bucket terraform resource
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HCL templating from bundled resource attribute lists; client-side.
rationale: HCL resource arguments are many and provider-specific; a scaffold seeds the correct attribute keys.

name: julia-set-generator
description: Renders a Julia-set fractal for a user-supplied complex constant with adjustable zoom and coloring.
example_prompt: generate a Julia set fractal for c = -0.8 + 0.156i
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs the per-pixel iteration like Mandelbrot — pure computation.
rationale: Julia sets give endlessly varied art from a single parameter and complement the Mandelbrot tool without overlapping it.

name: flow-field-art-generator
description: Creates flow-field (vector-field-guided particle trail) generative art seeded by noise, with tunable particle count and stroke style.
example_prompt: make a flowing flow-field artwork in warm colors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM advects particles through a noise-derived vector field and accumulates strokes into a PNG — CPU-only.
rationale: Flow-field art is a flagship generative-art style and produces unique high-value outputs entirely offline.

name: reaction-diffusion-generator
description: Simulates a Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion system to produce Turing-pattern textures (spots, stripes, mazes).
example_prompt: generate a reaction-diffusion coral pattern texture
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM iterates the Gray-Scott PDE on a grid and colorizes the result into a PNG — heavy but pure CPU math.
rationale: Turing patterns yield organic textures impossible to get from simple noise and showcase real simulation client-side.

name: grid-overlay-generator
description: Creates a transparent PNG composition-guide overlay (rule-of-thirds, golden ratio, golden spiral, or custom grid) at a target resolution.
example_prompt: make a transparent rule-of-thirds and golden-spiral overlay for 1920x1080
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM draws guide lines on a transparent PNG — pure offline drawing.
rationale: Photographers and designers reuse composition overlays constantly and need them at exact aspect ratios.

name: sierpinski-fractal-video
description: Produces an animated Sierpinski carpet/triangle motion clip with drifting offsets for use as a generative background.
example_prompt: Make a 10s looping Sierpinski triangle background video at 720p
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg 'sierpinski' source filter renders the fractal motion frames directly in the WASM ffmpeg runtime.
rationale: A distinct generative pattern not covered by existing fractal tools, trivial to scaffold from one source filter.

name: bouncing-logo-screensaver-video
description: Makes a retro DVD-style screensaver where a supplied logo/image bounces around the frame and changes color on each wall hit.
example_prompt: Turn this PNG into a 30-second bouncing-DVD-logo screensaver video at 1080p
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg overlays the user image with a sine/modulo motion expression over a color source; pure on-device compositing.
rationale: A nostalgic, instantly recognizable effect people make from their own logo with zero design effort.

name: voronoi-cells-video
description: Renders an animated Voronoi/cellular pattern motion background with drifting seed points.
example_prompt: Create an animated Voronoi cell background, pastel colors, seamless 10-second loop
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute evaluates nearest-seed Voronoi per pixel each frame on the GPU; encoded locally with ffmpeg.
rationale: Voronoi motion backgrounds are widely used in motion graphics and map cleanly to a compute shader.

name: lava-lamp-video
description: Creates a slow-flowing lava-lamp blob animation as a calming looping background video.
example_prompt: Generate a warm orange lava-lamp background loop, 20 seconds, 1080x1920 vertical
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute simulates the rising/falling blob field in a shader per frame; ffmpeg encodes on-device.
rationale: Ambient lava-lamp loops are a frequent request for chill streams and vertical reels.

name: obs-scene-json-generator
description: Builds an OBS Studio scene-collection JSON scaffold from a list of scenes and source types (display, image, text, browser).
example_prompt: Generate an OBS scene collection with a 'Starting Soon' scene, a webcam scene, and a 'BRB' scene
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM serializes the OBS scene-collection JSON schema locally; no OBS or server involved.
rationale: New streamers struggle to build scene collections and a local JSON scaffold jump-starts their setup.

name: white-noise-generator
description: Produces flat-spectrum white noise as a WAV at a chosen duration and level.
example_prompt: Make 2 minutes of white noise for a sleep loop
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: seeded PRNG samples + WAV encode, no external resources required.
rationale: White noise is widely used for masking, baby-sleep, and audio system testing, and people want it without ads or sign-ups.

name: vite-config-scaffold
description: Generates a vite.config.ts with framework plugin, aliases, server proxy, and build options.
example_prompt: vite.config for React with an @ alias and a /api proxy to localhost:8080
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — emits TS config text from selections
rationale: Proxy and alias resolve blocks are repetitive boilerplate across every Vite project.

name: changelog-entry-generator
description: Formats a Keep a Changelog entry block from a version, date, and grouped change list.
example_prompt: Format these changes as a Keep a Changelog 1.2.0 entry
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — section/heading templating
rationale: Consistent Added/Changed/Fixed grouping and date format is easy to mess up by hand.

name: poisson-disk-sampler
description: Generates blue-noise points with a minimum spacing in a 2D region via Bridson's Poisson-disk algorithm.
example_prompt: Poisson disk samples in a 500x500 area with min distance 30
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — grid-accelerated Bridson sampling with seeded PRNG, offline
rationale: Blue-noise point sets are essential for procedural scattering and stippling and require a non-trivial algorithm most people lack.

name: bash-script-scaffold
description: Scaffolds a robust bash script with a strict-mode header, arg parsing, usage function, and a logging helper.
example_prompt: Scaffold a bash script that takes an input file and output dir with usage help
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust to WASM; assembles the script skeleton from chosen options as text, no shell execution.
rationale: Most scripts skip set -euo pipefail and arg validation; a scaffold bakes in safe defaults.

name: graphql-schema-scaffold
description: Scaffolds a GraphQL SDL with types, Query and Mutation roots, and input types from a described entity list.
example_prompt: Scaffold a GraphQL schema for a Book entity with CRUD queries and mutations
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust to WASM; generates the SDL text from entity inputs, no server validation.
rationale: Bootstrapping a GraphQL schema with matching inputs and resolvers stubs is verbose and rule-based.

name: markov-chain-analyzer
description: Analyzes a finite Markov chain: stationary distribution, hitting/absorption probabilities, and sample trajectories.
example_prompt: Find the stationary distribution of this transition matrix
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — eigenvector/linear-solve and simulation run in wasmi with no network.
rationale: Markov chains span probability and theoretical CS and are a frequent homework and modeling tool.

name: react-component-scaffold
description: Scaffolds a React function component file from a name and a list of props.
example_prompt: scaffold a React component Button with props label and onClick
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: string templating with prop destructuring generated locally, no build server.
rationale: New-component boilerplate is repetitive and benefits from a consistent shape.

name: tmux-config-generator
description: Generates a .tmux.conf from choices like prefix key, mouse mode, vi copy mode, status-bar layout, and plugin list.
example_prompt: Generate a tmux config with Ctrl-a prefix, mouse on, vi keys, and a clean status bar
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: it templates a tmux config from structured inputs, no multiplexer required.
rationale: tmux/byobu newcomers spend hours assembling a usable config from scattered gists.

name: story-beat-sheet
description: Generates a structured beat sheet (three-act or Save-the-Cat) scaffold from a logline and genre.
example_prompt: Make a Save-the-Cat beat sheet for a heist comedy about a retired chef
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM fills deterministic structural templates from the user's inputs; no LLM call required.
rationale: storycraftr shows novelists want structured planning scaffolds, and the structure itself is rule-based not generative.

name: comment-density-analyzer
description: Computes the ratio of comment lines to code lines for a source file, with per-block breakdown.
example_prompt: How well-commented is this code?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: language-aware comment detection and line counting locally
rationale: Comment density is a maintainability signal in reviews, and an objective ratio replaces a subjective gut check.

name: bullet-list-consistency-checker
description: Flags mixed bullet markers and inconsistent terminal punctuation or capitalization within a list.
example_prompt: Are my bullet points formatted consistently?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: list-item parsing and style comparison locally
rationale: List inconsistency is a subtle polish issue that a targeted checker surfaces without a heavyweight style tool.

name: subtitle-word-counter
description: Counts total words, unique words, and characters across a subtitle file and reports per-cue averages.
example_prompt: How many words are in this subtitle file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: tokenizes the stripped cue text locally with no network.
rationale: Translators and localizers quote and budget by word count, and pulling it from raw subtitles otherwise needs cleanup.

name: gif-disposal-method-inspector
description: Reports each GIF frame's disposal method and transparency flags to diagnose ghosting and trailing-artifact bugs.
example_prompt: Why does this GIF leave trails — check its frame disposal methods
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses the graphic control extension of each frame from the byte stream.
rationale: GIF ghosting and smearing are almost always wrong disposal methods, which only a per-frame readout exposes.

name: webp-chunk-inspector
description: Reports a WebP file's RIFF chunks, format (lossy/lossless/extended), dimensions, alpha, and animation flags.
example_prompt: Is this WebP lossless and does it have animation?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: WebP is a RIFF container whose chunks parse from bytes with no decode, fully client-side
rationale: Web devs need to confirm a WebP's mode and features before serving it in production.

name: vary-header-analyzer
description: Parses a Vary header, flags caching footguns like Vary: * or Vary: User-Agent, and explains how each listed header fragments the cache key.
example_prompt: Is Vary: Accept-Encoding, User-Agent going to wreck my CDN cache hit rate?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — header list parsing plus a static high-cardinality warning set, no server
rationale: Misused Vary values quietly destroy cache efficiency and this catches the classic mistakes.

name: accept-encoding-analyzer
description: Parses an Accept-Encoding header, ranks the offered codecs by q-value, and flags whether modern compressions like br and zstd are advertised.
example_prompt: Does Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br;q=0.9 mean the client supports Brotli?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — q-value parsing and sorting, fully local
rationale: Knowing which clients advertise br/zstd drives compression strategy and the q-value ordering trips people up.

name: importmap-validator
description: Validates an import map's imports and scopes JSON, checking for trailing-slash mapping rules, duplicate specifiers, and resolvable scope keys.
example_prompt: Is this <script type="importmap"> JSON valid — I'm mapping react and a scoped lodash?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — JSON parse plus import-map resolution rule checks, no server
rationale: Import maps fail silently with bad trailing-slash semantics and there's no friendly local validator for them.

name: caa-record-parser
description: Parses DNS CAA records into flags, tags (issue/issuewild/iodef), and values and explains which certificate authorities are allowed to issue for the domain.
example_prompt: Parse 0 issue "letsencrypt.org" and 0 iodef "mailto:sec@x.com" — what CAs can issue my certs?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — CAA RDATA string parsing, user pastes records so no DNS lookup needed
rationale: CAA records control who can mint certificates for a domain and their flag/tag syntax is poorly understood.

name: dns-soa-record-explainer
description: Parses a DNS SOA record's seven fields and explains serial format, refresh/retry/expire timers, and the negative-cache TTL in human terms.
example_prompt: Explain my SOA: ns1.x.com hostmaster.x.com 2026061801 7200 3600 1209600 300.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — fixed-field parse with TTL humanization, no server
rationale: SOA timers drive zone propagation and negative caching but the bare seven numbers mean nothing to most people.

name: dns-srv-record-parser
description: Parses DNS SRV records into priority, weight, port, and target and explains the load-balancing/failover behavior they encode for a service.
example_prompt: Parse _sip._tcp 10 60 5060 sipserver.example.com and tell me how clients pick a host.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — field parse plus weight-distribution explanation, fully local
rationale: SRV records configure service discovery (SIP, XMPP, Minecraft, _matrix) and their priority/weight selection is widely misunderstood.

name: ulid-generator
description: Generates ULIDs (lexicographically sortable, timestamp-prefixed unique identifiers).
example_prompt: generate 5 ulids
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — combines the host clock and crypto randomness with Crockford base32 encoding, all local.
rationale: ULIDs are an increasingly popular UUID alternative and developers want them generated without a server.

name: finite-difference-table
description: Builds the full finite-difference table for a sequence, exposing the constant difference row that reveals the underlying polynomial degree.
example_prompt: Show the finite-difference table for 1, 8, 27, 64, 125.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: successive-difference computation across rows of the input, fully local.
rationale: The difference table is the standard way to find a closed form for tabulated data and is laborious by hand.

name: longest-common-subsequence
description: Finds the longest common subsequence of two sequences of characters or tokens.
example_prompt: find the longest common subsequence of these two strings
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM LCS dynamic programming; pure computation
rationale: LCS underlies diffing and is a useful standalone primitive for comparison tasks.

name: user-agent-diff
description: Parses two User-Agent strings into structured components (browser, version, OS, engine, device) and reports the differences.
example_prompt: Compare these two User-Agent strings and tell me what differs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM UA tokenizer + field comparison; runs locally
rationale: Field-level UA comparison is handy for analytics, fingerprint audits, and bug-repro matching.

name: matrix-norm-distance
description: Computes the distance between two same-shape matrices in L1, Frobenius, and max norms of A−B.
example_prompt: How far apart are these two matrices in Frobenius norm?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: elementwise norm aggregation, runs locally
rationale: A scalar norm-based distance between two matrices is a distinct, frequently-wanted summary of their difference.

name: acronym-builder
description: Builds acronyms and initialisms from a phrase, with options to skip stopwords or keep specific words.
example_prompt: Make an acronym from 'Self Organizing List Index'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: tokenize and select initials, no network.
rationale: Naming projects and systems often needs a tidy acronym, which is a pure text operation.

name: video-sitemap-generator
description: Generates a video XML sitemap with thumbnail, title, description, duration, and content/player URLs.
example_prompt: generate a video sitemap for my tutorial pages
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML templating with the video: namespace and ISO-8601 durations; no API.
rationale: Video pages need this rich, error-prone sitemap variant to surface in video search results.

name: importmap-generator
description: Generates a JSON <script type="importmap"> from a list of bare module specifiers and their CDN/local URLs.
example_prompt: build an import map mapping react and lodash to esm.sh
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON building with imports/scopes; a validator exists but no generator.
rationale: Native import maps let people skip bundlers and the imports/scopes structure is easy to misnest.

name: podcast-rss-generator
description: Generates a podcast RSS feed with the iTunes/Apple Podcasts namespace, episodes, enclosures, and channel art.
example_prompt: generate a podcast RSS feed for my show with these 5 episodes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML templating with the itunes: namespace; a validator exists but no generator.
rationale: Self-hosting a podcast requires a correct iTunes-namespaced feed that is notoriously fussy to hand-write.

name: metric-prefix-converter
description: Restates a quantity from one SI prefix to another (e.g. 3.3 kΩ → 3300 Ω → 0.0033 MΩ).
example_prompt: express 2200 microfarads in millifarads
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: power-of-ten scaling between named prefixes, runs locally.
rationale: Component datasheets and lab measurements force constant rescaling across kilo/milli/micro/nano prefixes.

name: semver-diff
description: Classifies the bump type between two semver strings as major, minor, patch, or prerelease.
example_prompt: Is going from 1.4.2 to 1.5.0 a minor or major bump?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — semver parse and component comparison run locally
rationale: Confirming the release-impact level of a version change is a constant CI and changelog question.

name: aliquot-sequence-generator
description: Generates the aliquot sequence from a starting number (iterated proper-divisor sum), detecting termination, perfect, amicable, or sociable cycles.
example_prompt: Generate the aliquot sequence starting at 276
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — divisor-sum iteration with big integers and cycle detection, no server.
rationale: Aliquot sequences reveal sociable cycles and open problems and are tedious to iterate by hand.

name: triangle-inequality-checker
description: Determines whether three side lengths can form a valid triangle and classifies it as acute, right, or obtuse.
example_prompt: Can sides 3, 4, 8 form a triangle?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: three comparisons and a law-of-cosines sign test, no network.
rationale: It's a precise validity check (not a solver) that geometry students and CAD users hit constantly.

name: grid-template-areas-generator
description: Converts an ASCII layout sketch into a CSS grid-template-areas rule plus matching named-area class stubs.
example_prompt: turn this ASCII layout into CSS grid: header header / nav main / footer footer
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM grid parsing and CSS emission; no network.
rationale: Named grid areas are powerful but the area-string/class pairing is fiddly to write by hand.

name: gemfile-scaffold
description: Scaffolds a Ruby Gemfile with source, ruby version, and gem entries (with groups).
example_prompt: scaffold a Gemfile with rails and rspec in the test group
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: template the gem/group DSL, client-side
rationale: Ruby projects start from a Gemfile and the group/version DSL is exactly the boilerplate people look up.

name: play-solitaire
description: Play Klondike solitaire with draw-1/draw-3 options, undo, and auto-complete.
example_prompt: deal me a game of klondike solitaire
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — shuffle, move-legality, and tableau state are pure logic; no backend needed.
rationale: Maps the 'csol' demand term to the single most familiar card game, broadening reach beyond niche terminal users.

name: inversion-counter
description: Counts inversions between two orderings of the same items (the minimum adjacent swaps to turn one into the other).
example_prompt: How many swaps to turn this ordering into that one?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: merge-sort inversion count, runs locally.
rationale: A concrete edit-distance for permutations useful for sorting analysis and ranking change.

name: lode-runner
description: Platformer where you dig holes, dodge guards, and collect all the gold across handcrafted levels (Oldrunner-style).
example_prompt: play a lode runner style game
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tile physics, digging timers, and guard AI all run client-side on canvas
rationale: Maps the 'Oldrunner' demand into a strategic action-puzzle platformer with lasting replay value.

name: shebang-detector
description: Reads the first line of a script and reports the interpreter, args, and whether it uses /usr/bin/env, flagging non-portable shebangs.
example_prompt: What interpreter does this script use, and is the shebang portable?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; parses the `#!` line, no execution and no network.
rationale: Hard-coded interpreter paths break portability; a quick check encourages `/usr/bin/env` usage.

name: barcode-quietzone-checker
description: Checks a 1D barcode image for adequate quiet-zone margins and module width so scanners can read it reliably.
example_prompt: Will this barcode scan, or is the quiet zone too small?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes the barcode and measures border whitespace and bar widths locally.
rationale: Insufficient quiet zones are the top cause of unscannable printed barcodes, and a check catches them pre-press.

name: jsonschema-meta-validate
description: Checks that a JSON Schema document is itself well-formed against the appropriate meta-schema and flags illegal keywords or type mismatches.
example_prompt: Is this JSON Schema I wrote actually valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM bundling the Draft meta-schemas; fully offline
rationale: Authors frequently write subtly broken schemas and have no quick way to confirm the schema itself is legal.

name: psnr-calculator
description: Computes Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio between a reference and a test numeric array given a peak/max value.
example_prompt: Compute the PSNR between these reference and reconstructed sample arrays
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: MSE and log arithmetic over arrays, runs in-browser
rationale: PSNR is the standard fidelity comparison for reconstructed signals/data and has no numeric-array tool here.

name: percentage-point-difference
description: Computes the percentage-point difference and the relative percent change between two percentage values.
example_prompt: Approval went from 42% to 47% — how many percentage points and what relative change?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: trivial arithmetic, no external calls
rationale: People constantly conflate percentage points with percent change; a precise comparator avoids that error.

name: monotonic-trend-compare
description: Compares the monotonic trend direction (Mann-Kendall sign) of two series and reports whether they trend the same way.
example_prompt: Do these two series trend in the same direction over time?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pairwise sign tallying, no external calls
rationale: Asking whether two series move together directionally is a useful, distinct comparison not covered by correlation tools.

name: graphql-query-scaffolder
description: Generates a sample query or mutation with all fields expanded for each operation in a GraphQL SDL.
example_prompt: From this GraphQL schema, scaffold a full query for the getUser operation.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: SDL parsing and recursive selection-set emission are pure local work.
rationale: Writing exhaustive GraphQL queries by hand is tedious and easy to leave fields out.

name: bernoulli-number-generator
description: Generates Bernoulli numbers B_0 through B_n as exact rational fractions via the Akiyama–Tanigawa algorithm.
example_prompt: Generate the first 16 Bernoulli numbers as fractions
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — exact rational arithmetic on big integers, no symbolic backend required.
rationale: Exact Bernoulli numbers are needed for sums of powers and series expansions and are hard to compute by hand.

name: stirling-number-table
description: Generates a triangular table of Stirling numbers of the first or second kind up to a given N using exact big-integer recurrences.
example_prompt: Make a Stirling numbers of the second kind table up to n=8
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — additive big-integer recurrence over a triangle, fully local.
rationale: Stirling tables are core to combinatorics and partition counting and rarely available as an instant generator.

name: premultiplied-alpha-detector
description: Analyzes alpha vs color values to detect whether an image uses premultiplied or straight alpha, flagging likely mismatches.
example_prompt: Is this texture premultiplied or straight alpha?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes pixels and inspects color/alpha relationships in the browser.
rationale: Premultiplied/straight mismatch causes dark halos in compositing and is hard to diagnose by eye.

name: delaunay-lowpoly-generator
description: Produces an abstract low-poly background by triangulating random points and shading each triangle from a gradient.
example_prompt: generate a low-poly triangle background in blue tones, 1920x1080
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM does Delaunay triangulation and flat-fills triangles into a PNG — pure geometry.
rationale: Low-poly geometric backdrops remain a sought-after design asset and there is no current generative gizza tool for them.

name: dot-grid-paper-generator
description: Creates dot-grid (bullet-journal style) paper at configurable dot spacing, size, and color for printing.
example_prompt: generate Letter-size dot grid paper with 5mm dots
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM stamps the dot lattice into a PNG/SVG — trivial pixel math.
rationale: Dot-grid templates are wildly popular for journaling and planners and are quick to produce locally.

name: ruled-notebook-paper-generator
description: Produces lined notebook paper (college/wide rule, with optional margin line and Cornell-note layout) for printing.
example_prompt: make wide-ruled notebook paper with a red margin line
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM draws horizontal rules and margins into a PNG/SVG at print resolution — fully offline.
rationale: Printable lined paper in exact rulings is a common everyday need with no current generator.

name: halftone-screen-generator
description: Generates a halftone dot-screen pattern image at a chosen dot pitch, angle, and dot shape for print and retro effects.
example_prompt: make a 45-degree halftone dot screen, medium dots, in cyan
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tiles angled dots into a PNG — deterministic geometry, no deps.
rationale: Halftone screens are a distinct print/retro asset and generating the pattern itself differs from dithering an image.

name: ffmpeg-watermark-command-builder
description: Builds an ffmpeg overlay command to place a watermark image at a chosen corner, margin, opacity, and scale.
example_prompt: Command to watermark my video with logo.png bottom-right, 20px margin, 60% opacity
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM templates the overlay/format/colorchannelmixer chain into a command; pure text.
rationale: Watermarking is one of the most common ffmpeg lookups and the opacity/position syntax is non-obvious.

name: isochronic-tone-generator
description: Produces a single tone pulsed on and off at a chosen beat rate with adjustable envelope shape.
example_prompt: Create an isochronic tone at 432Hz pulsing 8 times per second
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: amplitude-gated sine with a smoothing envelope + WAV encode, deterministic offline.
rationale: Isochronic tones differ from binaural beats (mono, works on speakers) and are a distinct, commonly requested generator.

name: companion-matrix-generator
description: Builds the companion matrix of a monic polynomial from its coefficients for eigenvalue/root work.
example_prompt: Companion matrix for x^3 - 2x^2 + 5x - 1
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — coefficients placed into a fixed sparse pattern, fully local
rationale: Companion matrices bridge polynomials and eigenvalue solvers, and the layout is easy to get wrong by hand.

name: hilbert-curve-generator
description: Generates the order-N Hilbert space-filling curve as an ordered list of grid coordinates and SVG path.
example_prompt: Generate an order-4 Hilbert curve
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — recursive L-system/bit-twiddling mapping, fully local
rationale: Hilbert curves drive spatial indexing and dithering, and generating the exact traversal order by hand is infeasible.

name: superellipse-generator
description: Generates superellipse (Lamé curve) boundary points from semi-axes and the exponent n.
example_prompt: Superellipse points with a=2, b=1, exponent 2.5
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parametric Lamé-curve sampling computed locally
rationale: Superellipses (squircles) appear in UI design and typography and need exact boundary coordinates for tooling.

name: webmanifest-validate
description: Validates a PWA web app manifest for required fields, icon sizes, and installability criteria.
example_prompt: Check my manifest.json — is my PWA installable?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON parse with W3C manifest rules; fully local
rationale: Missing icon sizes or display fields silently block PWA installation and are easy to overlook.

name: code39-mod43-validator
description: Validates the optional Code 39 mod-43 check character over its alphanumeric symbol set.
example_prompt: Is the mod-43 check character on CODE39 correct?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: symbol-value table and modulo-43 sum, no scanner.
rationale: Industrial label makers using Code 39 with check digits need a precise offline verifier.

name: accept-header-parser
description: Parses an Accept header into media types with their quality and parameters, sorted by precedence.
example_prompt: sort the media types in this Accept header by priority
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; media-range parsing and q/specificity ranking are pure computation.
rationale: Diagnosing why a server returns the wrong representation requires reading Accept precedence correctly.

name: content-type-parse
description: Parses a MIME Content-Type/media-type string into type, subtype, and parameters.
example_prompt: parse text/html; charset=utf-8; boundary=xyz
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: media-type grammar tokenizing, fully in-sandbox.
rationale: Correctly splitting media-type parameters (charset, boundary) avoids subtle HTTP handling bugs.

name: repeating-decimal-formatter
description: Converts a fraction to its decimal with explicit repetend notation and reports the period length.
example_prompt: show 1/7 as a repeating decimal
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — long-division with remainder cycle detection, local.
rationale: Detecting and marking the repeating block is non-trivial and uniquely useful.

name: pythagorean-triple-validator
description: Checks whether three integers form a Pythagorean triple and reports whether it is primitive and its generating parameters.
example_prompt: Is (8, 15, 17) a Pythagorean triple, and is it primitive?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: integer square test plus GCD and Euclid-parameter recovery, no network.
rationale: It's a precise integer-checking task useful for number-theory learners and procedural geometry that isn't covered by solvers.

name: extended-euclidean
description: Computes the GCD and the modular multiplicative inverse via the extended Euclidean algorithm.
example_prompt: modular inverse of 17 mod 3120
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM big-int Euclid — deterministic, client-side
rationale: Computing modular inverses is the step learners stumble on when deriving RSA private keys.

name: korean-romanizer
description: Transliterates Korean Hangul into Latin script using Revised Romanization rules.
example_prompt: romanize 안녕하세요
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM rule-based Hangul decomposition and mapping; fully deterministic and offline.
rationale: Clearly browser-local and broadly useful for travelers and Korean learners; from the Korean-NLP demand.

name: multi-armed-bandit-sim
description: Simulates epsilon-greedy, UCB, and Thompson-sampling bandits and plots cumulative regret.
example_prompt: Compare epsilon-greedy vs UCB on a 5-armed bandit over 1000 pulls
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs the simulation and emits the regret-curve SVG client-side.
rationale: Bandit algorithms are the entry point to reinforcement learning and ideal for browser-local demos.

name: astar-pathfind
description: Finds an optimal path through a grid with obstacles using A* search and shows the route.
example_prompt: Find the shortest path through this maze grid
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs A* over the grid with a heap, a small deterministic computation.
rationale: Heuristic search is the centerpiece of Artificial Intelligence: Foundations of Computational Agents.

name: version-string-compare
description: Naturally compares two arbitrary dotted or mixed version strings, ordering them correctly despite non-semver formats.
example_prompt: Which is newer: 'v1.10.2-beta' or 'v1.9.20'?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tokenize into numeric/alpha segments and compare
rationale: Lexical comparison mis-orders versions (1.9 vs 1.10) and a natural comparator fixes a common pitfall.

name: fletcher-checksum-validator
description: Computes Fletcher-16/32 checksums of input data and checks them against an expected value.
example_prompt: Validate the Fletcher-16 checksum of 'abcde'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — paired modular accumulators over bytes, deterministic and offline.
rationale: Fletcher checksums appear in protocols and embedded data and are a distinct verification scheme.

name: polygon-area-calculator
description: Computes the area, perimeter, and centroid of a polygon from its vertex coordinates using the shoelace formula.
example_prompt: What's the area and centroid of the polygon with these vertices?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM shoelace + centroid math; entirely local.
rationale: Polygon area/centroid is a frequent GIS and CAD calculation distinct from convex-hull tools.

name: extract-emoji
description: Extracts every emoji from text with counts and Unicode codepoints.
example_prompt: Which emojis appear in this chat export and how often
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM Unicode scan over codepoints, runs in browser
rationale: Quick emoji inventory of chat/social text is fun and useful for content analysis.

name: capacitor-code-decoder
description: Decodes 3-digit ceramic capacitor codes like '104' into capacitance in farads/pF/nF.
example_prompt: What capacitance is the code 104 and 223?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — digit-multiplier formula, no dependencies.
rationale: Capacitor markings are a compact code most people must look up every single time.

name: mixed-content-url-upgrader
description: Rewrites insecure http:// resource URLs (src/href) in an HTML snippet to https:// to eliminate mixed-content warnings.
example_prompt: Upgrade all the http:// asset links in this HTML to https
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; attribute-aware string rewrite of the markup, no network.
rationale: Mixed content silently blocks assets on HTTPS pages; bulk-upgrading is tedious by hand.

name: affine-rescale-column
description: Applies a user-specified linear transform y = a·x + b to a numeric column (e.g. unit conversions or calibration).
example_prompt: Multiply this column by 1.8 and add 32
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: per-value multiply-add, fully local.
rationale: A general affine rescale covers countless ad-hoc unit/calibration adjustments in one tool.

name: video-codec-container-compatibility-checker
description: Tells you which codecs a target container (mp4/webm/mkv/mov) legally supports before you mux.
example_prompt: Can I put VP9 video and AAC audio in an mp4?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM compatibility-table lookup, no media, in-browser.
rationale: Illegal codec/container combos fail muxing late and this answers it up front.

name: wav-to-rf64
description: Promotes an oversized WAV to RF64/BW64 with a ds64 chunk so the size fields stay valid.
example_prompt: My wav is over 4GB and broken — make it RF64
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM injects the ds64 chunk and 0xFFFFFFFF size markers; no re-encoding.
rationale: Recorders that crash past 4 GB leave broken RIFF size fields that an RF64 rewrite repairs losslessly.

name: polynomial-format-converter
description: Converts a polynomial between coefficient-list, root-factored, and expanded-string forms.
example_prompt: Convert these roots to expanded polynomial coefficients
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM multiplies factors and parses/prints terms
rationale: Moving between roots and coefficients is exactly the kind of exact algebra a tool should automate.

name: aztec-code-generator
description: Generates an Aztec 2D barcode image from text, useful for tickets and transit passes.
example_prompt: Create an Aztec code for my ticket reference 'TKT-88231'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a pure-Rust Aztec encoder produces the matrix and renders PNG in-WASM.
rationale: Aztec codes dominate transit/ticketing and round out the catalog's 2D-code generators.

name: scale-tone-generator
description: Plays a musical scale (major, minor, modes, pentatonic) ascending and descending as a WAV from a chosen root.
example_prompt: Generate an A harmonic minor scale ascending and descending as a WAV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: maps scale intervals to frequencies and sequences enveloped sines into PCM
rationale: A scale-by-name renderer is a practical ear-training and reference tool distinct from the arbitrary frequency-list sequencer.

name: hsts-header-generator
description: Builds a Strict-Transport-Security header from max-age, includeSubDomains, and preload choices and warns about preload requirements.
example_prompt: Generate an HSTS header for 1 year with subdomains and preload
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM formats the header and checks preload constraints locally
rationale: Getting HSTS preload eligibility right matters because mistakes can lock users out of a domain.

name: error-page-generator
description: Generates a self-contained static error page (404, 500, 503) with inline styles and a customizable message.
example_prompt: Make a clean static 404 page that links back home
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM emits the standalone HTML document locally
rationale: A polished, dependency-free error page is a small touch every static host needs but few bother to craft.

name: open-graph-tag-deduplicator
description: Removes duplicate Open Graph / Twitter meta tags from an HTML <head>, keeping the last (or first) of each property.
example_prompt: Dedupe the duplicate og: meta tags in this head HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; meta-tag parse keyed by property, no network.
rationale: CMS/plugin stacks often emit conflicting duplicate OG tags that confuse scrapers; dedup fixes previews.

name: box-packing-3d
description: Fits 3D boxes into a container to minimize wasted volume and returns a placement layout.
example_prompt: Fit these carton dimensions into a 120x100x150 cm container
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute or plain Rust→WASM 3D packing heuristics run in-browser; webgpu accelerates the search.
rationale: 3D bin packing is the hard core of the Packrift packaging benchmark and has real logistics value.

name: loot-drop-simulator
description: Computes expected attempts and probability curves for hitting a target drop given per-attempt rates (incl. gacha pity).
example_prompt: If a drop is 2% per kill, what's the chance I get it within 50 kills?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; closed-form geometric/negative-binomial math runs locally.
rationale: Drop-rate math is a perennial game-dataset and game-design question with no reliable quick tool.

name: bill-split-itemized
description: Splits an itemized restaurant bill by per-item assignment with proportional tax and tip.
example_prompt: Split this dinner bill: itemize who ordered what, add 8% tax and 20% tip
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM arithmetic over the item list; offline.
rationale: Itemized fairness (not just even splits) is exactly what SplitPro/MoneyBuster users want at the table.

name: discord-emoji-checker
description: Checks whether an image meets Discord custom-emoji constraints (square aspect, ≤256KB, supported format) before upload.
example_prompt: Will this image work as a Discord custom emoji?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads dimensions, format, and byte size locally.
rationale: Platform emoji limits are fiddly and uploads fail without explanation, so a local validator saves trial and error.

name: ads-txt-validate
description: Validates an ads.txt / app-ads.txt file's record format (domain, publisher ID, relationship, optional cert authority) and flags malformed or duplicate lines.
example_prompt: Validate this ads.txt file's format
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line/field parser per the IAB spec; offline.
rationale: Malformed ads.txt lines are ignored by buyers, costing ad revenue, and are tedious to audit by hand.

name: chemical-equation-balance-checker
description: Checks whether a chemical equation is balanced by comparing per-element atom counts on each side.
example_prompt: Is 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O balanced?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: formula parsing and integer atom tallying, fully offline.
rationale: Conservation-of-mass check (a linear-algebra balancing problem) not in the catalog.

name: groebner-basis-calculator
description: Computes Groebner bases and reduces polynomial ideals for algebraic geometry.
example_prompt: groebner basis of x^2+y^2-1 and x-y in x,y
loader_feasibility: pyodide + SymPy groebner() runs in the wasm Python sandbox
rationale: Captures Macaulay2/Singular/Magma demand for ideal computation with a free browser tool.

name: lambda-calculus-reducer
description: Beta-reduces lambda-calculus terms to normal form with optional step-by-step and Church-numeral output.
example_prompt: Reduce (\x.\y.x) a b step by step
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — substitution and reduction are pure term-rewriting that run in wasmi.
rationale: Lambda calculus is foundational TCS/PL material that benefits from a precise interactive evaluator.

name: helm-chart-scaffold
description: Scaffolds a Helm chart skeleton (Chart.yaml, values.yaml, and templated deployment/service/ingress) from inputs.
example_prompt: Scaffold a Helm chart for a web app with a deployment, service, and ingress
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — emits the chart directory files with Go-template placeholders as text, entirely local.
rationale: Helm's templating directory conventions are easy to misplace, and a scaffold gives a lint-clean starting chart.

name: kronecker-product-builder
description: Computes the Kronecker (tensor) product of two input matrices into the full block matrix.
example_prompt: Compute the Kronecker product of [[1,2],[3,4]] and [[0,1],[1,0]]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — nested multiply-and-tile loops over small dense matrices, no libraries needed.
rationale: Kronecker products scaffold quantum gates, 2D operators, and DoE arrays but blow up quickly when done manually.

name: finite-difference-stencil-generator
description: Generates finite-difference coefficients for a chosen derivative order and accuracy at arbitrary grid points.
example_prompt: Generate the central 4th-order finite-difference stencil for the first derivative
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — solve the small Vandermonde-like coefficient system via in-WASM Gaussian elimination, no deps.
rationale: Fornberg-style stencil generation scaffolds custom PDE discretizations without re-deriving coefficients by hand.

name: fps-frame-time-converter
description: Converts between frame rate and per-frame time budget and checks how much headroom a given workload leaves at a target FPS.
example_prompt: At 60 fps how many milliseconds per frame do I have, and is 9ms of logic safe?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the conversions are trivial arithmetic with no I/O.
rationale: Performance budgeting in frame-time terms is a constant reference for game programmers and a quick converter saves repeated mental math.

name: win32-error-decoder
description: Decodes a Windows HRESULT or Win32 error code into its symbolic name and message.
example_prompt: what is error 0x80070005?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with an embedded code table; a pure local lookup.
rationale: The windows-rs demand maps to a genuinely useful offline error-code lookup for Windows devs.

name: data-structure-diagram
description: Renders linked lists, trees, and graphs as SVG from a textual spec.
example_prompt: Draw a linked list 1 -> 2 -> 3 as a diagram
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — builds SVG strings in-memory with no DOM or server.
rationale: Directly serves 'Too Many Linked Lists'-style learning by visualizing structures.

name: pace-speed-converter
description: Converts between running/cycling pace (min per km or mile) and speed (km/h, mph, m/s).
example_prompt: Convert a 5:00 min/km pace to km/h
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; reciprocal unit arithmetic.
rationale: Athletes and route data constantly switch between pace and speed units.

name: iso8601-duration-calculator

rationale: Ramps, roofs, and roads spec slope in inconsistent units that need cross-conversion.

name: mixed-number-converter
description: Converts between improper fractions and mixed numbers and reduces them to lowest terms.
example_prompt: Convert 17/5 to a mixed number
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: integer division and GCD reduction
rationale: A basic fraction-formatting task distinct from the excluded fraction calculator/decimal-to-fraction.

name: trailing-zero-trimmer
description: Strips insignificant trailing zeros (and a bare trailing decimal point) from a list of decimal numbers without rounding.
