loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — purely lexical string trimming of parsed numerics, no I/O so it runs fully in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: Exported and computed values often carry noise zeros that clutter tables, and this trims them losslessly unlike a precision-rounder.

name: run-length-encoding-formatter
description: Run-length encodes and decodes a string or numeric sequence into count-symbol pairs.
example_prompt: run-length encode AAAABBBCCDAA
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a single linear scan over the input, no dependencies.
rationale: A foundational compression demo and a quick way to compact repetitive sequences for sharing.

name: gcd-lcm-table
description: Builds a square GCD or LCM table for a list of integers or a 1..N range.
example_prompt: Make a GCD table for the numbers 6, 8, 12, 15
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Euclidean algorithm in a nested loop, deterministic in wasmi
rationale: Quick reference matrix for fraction reduction and scheduling problems that beats computing each pair by hand.

name: translation-drift-checker
description: Compares two language versions of the same content structurally, flagging mismatched placeholders, line counts, and untranslated segments.
example_prompt: Check whether the Spanish version of these UI strings drifted from the English source structure
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — align keys/lines and compare placeholder tokens and counts locally
rationale: Localization files drift silently (missing keys, broken placeholders) and a structural cross-check catches it without a translation API.

name: video-pts-delta-report
description: Builds a histogram of inter-frame presentation-timestamp deltas to reveal frame-timing jitter and duplicated/dropped timestamps.
example_prompt: Show me the frame timing jitter in this video
loader_feasibility: PTS deltas come from the ffmpeg demuxer and are histogrammed in Rust locally, no network.
rationale: PTS jitter pinpoints capture glitches and muxing faults that a simple frame-rate number hides.

name: htaccess-linter
description: Lints an Apache .htaccess file for unknown directives, unbalanced section tags, and common RewriteRule mistakes.
example_prompt: Lint this .htaccess file.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM directive parser following Apache config grammar — fully local.
rationale: A broken .htaccess can take a whole site down with a 500, so static linting prevents costly outages.

name: traktor-nml-to-m3u
description: Extracts the track file paths from a Traktor NML collection/playlist and writes a portable M3U.
example_prompt: Export this Traktor .nml playlist to a normal M3U
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse the NML XML <ENTRY><LOCATION> nodes, decode DIR/FILE, emit M3U
rationale: Frees DJ playlists from Traktor's proprietary XML so they work in any player.

name: base62-id-encoder
description: Encodes large integers into compact Base58/Base62/Base36 strings (and decodes them) using configurable alphabets for short IDs.
example_prompt: Encode the number 1000000 as a Base62 short ID
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: big-integer base conversion with custom alphabets
rationale: Short-ID and URL-slug generation from integers is common and has no offline tool here.

name: srt-timestamps-to-seconds
description: Parses SRT/VTT subtitle cue timestamps into start/end seconds and durations as CSV.
example_prompt: Extract every subtitle's start and end time in seconds from this SRT
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; timestamp parsing only, no dependencies
rationale: Subtitle timing analysis and re-sync need numeric seconds, not HH:MM:SS,mmm strings.

name: aiff-chunk-inspector
description: Lists the chunks of an AIFF/AIFF-C file (COMM, SSND, MARK, INST, APPL, ID3) with their sizes and key fields like sample rate and bit depth.
example_prompt: Break down the chunks inside this .aiff file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — AIFF is IFF/big-endian chunked format read by walking chunk headers in the buffer
rationale: AIFF is the Mac/pro-audio counterpart to WAV and has no dedicated structural reader despite WAV having three.

name: www-authenticate-parser
description: Parses WWW-Authenticate and Authorization challenge headers into scheme and parameters.
example_prompt: Parse this WWW-Authenticate header
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM challenge tokenizer.
rationale: Auth-flow debugging across Basic, Bearer, and Digest schemes.

name: nutri-score-calculator
description: Computes the Nutri-Score grade (A–E) from per-100g nutrition facts using the official point system.
example_prompt: What Nutri-Score for a food with 450 kcal, 12g sugar, 1.2g salt, 3g fiber, 8g protein per 100g?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (Nutri-Score point algorithm) — pure scoring math, the offline half of OpenFoodFacts.
rationale: Reproduces OpenFoodFacts' headline score locally so users can grade any product or recipe from its label.

name: math-worksheet-generator
description: Generates a set of practice problems on a chosen topic with an answer key.
example_prompt: generate 10 quadratic equation practice problems with answers
loader_feasibility: pyodide — SymPy synthesizes problems and solutions client-side, no server.
rationale: Captures the Free Math/Mathcheap teacher-and-student demand for endless graded practice material.

name: cowsay-box
description: Wraps any message in a classic cowsay-style ASCII speech bubble with a selectable character.
example_prompt: Make a cowsay of 'build passing' with a dragon
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bubble wrapping and bundled ASCII art are pure text assembly with no dependencies, running fully client-side.
rationale: cowsay is a staple of MOTD and welcome-script culture surfaced by these terms, and it is a cheap, delightful, self-contained tool.

name: chess-pgn-to-gif
description: Animate a chess game from PGN into a GIF or MP4 of the moves.
example_prompt: Turn this PGN game into an animated GIF
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM PGN parse + board frames + ffmpeg GIF; offline.
rationale: Shareable game replays building on chess-fen-render.

name: emoji-favicon
description: Turn an emoji (or short text) into a multi-size favicon set and .ico file.
example_prompt: make a favicon from the rocket emoji
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust emoji render plus ico encoding to WASM — fully local.
rationale: Emoji favicons are a popular quick way to brand a site; favicon-generate needs a source image.

name: json-to-jsx
description: Scaffolds a React/JSX component that renders a given JSON data object.
example_prompt: turn this JSON into a React component that displays it
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM template generation from the parsed structure; emits JSX text locally.
rationale: json2react demand shows people want UI scaffolding straight from data shapes.

name: quaternion-tool
description: Converts between quaternions, Euler angles, and axis-angle, and interpolates with slerp.
example_prompt: Convert euler angles 30,45,0 to a quaternion
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM math
rationale: Rotation math is error-prone and needed for animating any 3D scene.

name: shader-art-video
description: Renders a user-supplied fragment shader (Shadertoy-style) to a fixed-length MP4 at a chosen resolution and fps.
example_prompt: Render this WGSL fragment shader to a 10-second 1080p video
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute runs the shader each frame on the GPU and ffmpeg encodes the frame sequence entirely in-browser.
rationale: Shader artists need an offline-quality render of their code to a clean video file, which browsers can now do locally via WebGPU.

name: box-behnken-design
description: Generates a Box–Behnken response-surface design for K factors with center points, listing all runs in coded and natural units.
example_prompt: Generate a Box-Behnken design for 3 factors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — fixed block patterns combined per factor pair, no dependencies.
rationale: Box–Behnken designs efficiently fit quadratic models and few tools generate them offline.

name: ffmpeg-command-builder
description: Generate a ready-to-run ffmpeg command line from a plain-language description of the desired operation.
example_prompt: Give me the ffmpeg command to crop and convert this to a 720p mp4
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a deterministic builder maps requested operations to ffmpeg flags; pure text generation, no execution.
rationale: Turns the ffmpeg CLI-flags/fluent-ffmpeg/man-page maze into a single copyable command.

name: named-graph-generator
description: Emits the edge list and adjacency matrix for standard graph families (complete, cycle, path, Petersen, hypercube, wheel).
example_prompt: Give me the edge list of the Petersen graph
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — combinatorial construction rules computed offline
rationale: Textbook graph families are referenced constantly but their exact edge sets are easy to misremember.

name: shepard-tone-generator
description: Synthesizes a Shepard tone — the auditory illusion of an endlessly rising or falling pitch — as a seamless looping WAV.
example_prompt: Generate a 30-second endlessly rising Shepard tone
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM stacks octave-spaced sines under a Gaussian amplitude envelope and renders the loop in the browser.
rationale: A specific, hard-to-make illusion useful for sound design, tension cues, and music demos.

name: mp4-fragment-detector
description: Detects whether an MP4 is fragmented (moof/mfra) or progressive and summarizes the fragment layout.
example_prompt: Is this mp4 fragmented or a regular progressive file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans for moof boxes in the byte stream, fully in-browser.
rationale: Fragmented vs progressive MP4 determines compatibility and is otherwise invisible to users.

name: ffmpeg-thumbnail-extract-command-builder
description: Generates an ffmpeg command to extract a poster frame or N evenly-spaced thumbnails from a video.
example_prompt: Command to grab 10 evenly spaced thumbnails from a 6-minute video as JPGs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM emits the select/fps/thumbnail command from the parameters; no media processed.
rationale: Thumbnail extraction is constantly needed and the even-spacing select expression is hard to remember.

name: repeating-decimal-notation-formatter
description: Detects the repeating cycle of a decimal expansion and formats it with overbar or parenthesis notation (0.1666… → 0.1(6)).
example_prompt: write 4/7 as a decimal with its repeating part marked
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — long-division cycle detection with integer remainders, fully offline.
rationale: Showing the actual repeating block is a distinct presentation problem from converting a repeating decimal back into a fraction.

name: minecraft-server-properties-generator
description: Builds and validates a server.properties file from guided options, flagging invalid values and explaining each setting.
example_prompt: Generate a server.properties for a hardcore survival server on port 25566 with 10 max players.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — key/value generation and range validation are pure text logic requiring no runtime.
rationale: New server operators frequently misconfigure server.properties; a validating generator that explains each key reduces broken-server support churn.

name: ascii-progress-bar
description: Renders a text/ASCII progress bar from a percentage or value/total with configurable width and style.
example_prompt: Show a 40-char progress bar at 73%
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: builds the bar string from numbers locally.
rationale: Drop-in progress visuals for READMEs, logs and CLI mockups (the ProgressLine use case).

name: video-to-ascii
description: Turns a short video clip into an ASCII-art animation, frame by frame.
example_prompt: Make an ASCII animation from this video clip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes frames in WASM and each frame is mapped to ASCII, all in-browser
rationale: A fun, distinctive media toy with no privacy-safe browser equivalent.

name: systemd-unit-generate
description: Generate a systemd service unit file from command, user, restart, and dependency options.
example_prompt: Make a systemd service that runs /opt/app on boot and restarts on failure
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM templating, offline.
rationale: Self-hosters write these constantly; fits the existing nginx/dockerfile/htaccess generators.

name: esp32-partition-table-generator
description: Generates and validates an ESP-IDF partition table CSV (offsets, sizes, types) and flags overlaps or flash-size overflow.
example_prompt: Make an ESP32 partition table with OTA, NVS, and a 1MB SPIFFS for a 4MB flash
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — CSV generation plus range-overlap checks, pure compute.
rationale: esp-rs developers hand-edit partition CSVs where one wrong offset bricks the flash layout, so local validation catches it early.

name: ulam-spiral-generator
description: Generates the Ulam prime spiral as a grid plus prime coordinates, revealing the diagonal clustering of primes for a given size.
example_prompt: Generate a 51x51 Ulam spiral
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — spiral coordinate walk plus a prime sieve, no external resources.
rationale: The Ulam spiral is a striking visual of prime distribution that requires programmatic grid generation.

name: option-payoff
description: Plot the payoff diagram of an options strategy (covered call, spread, straddle).
example_prompt: Plot the payoff of a bull call spread, strikes 100/110, premium 3
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM payoff math plus plotting, offline.
rationale: Traders visualize strategy payoffs; the Black-Scholes tool only prices single options.

name: timestamp-log-align
description: Aligns two log files by timestamp and diffs entries to surface where their event sequences diverge.
example_prompt: Compare these two run logs and show where they started behaving differently
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse timestamps, merge by time, and diff aligned entries
rationale: Comparing a good run against a failing run by aligned time is a powerful, manual-heavy debugging move.

name: spectral-flatness-compare
description: Computes spectral flatness (tonal-vs-noise character) of two clips and reports the difference.
example_prompt: Which of these two recordings is noisier versus more tonal?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM runs the FFT and geometric/arithmetic-mean ratio on both files in-browser.
rationale: Distinguishes noise-like versus tonal content between two takes in one number.

name: spectral-rolloff-compare
description: Measures the spectral rolloff frequency of two files and reports the delta to compare high-frequency content.
example_prompt: Compare the high-frequency extension of these two files.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM computes the cumulative-energy rolloff point on both decoded files locally.
rationale: Reveals whether one file is rolled off or band-limited relative to another.

name: video-matroska-element-validator
description: Parses the MKV/WebM EBML element tree to validate required elements, sizes, and nesting for spec conformance.
example_prompt: Is this MKV's element structure valid?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses EBML from file bytes entirely client-side.
rationale: Malformed EBML from buggy muxers causes seek/playback failures that only structural validation explains.

name: video-360-metadata-check
description: Detects spherical/360 spatial-media metadata and reports projection type so 360 players treat the file correctly.
example_prompt: Is this video tagged as 360/spherical?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses the spherical-video metadata boxes from file bytes client-side.
rationale: Missing 360 metadata makes platforms render an equirectangular blob flat, a tagging issue invisible in normal info.

name: ape-tag-validator
description: Validates an APEv2 tag footer/header pair, item-key legality, value lengths, and flags for files (often MP3 or Monkey's Audio).
example_prompt: Check the APEv2 tag at the end of this file for problems
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: reads the fixed-layout APE footer and item list from file bytes, no codec needed.
rationale: APE tags coexist with ID3 and are easy to corrupt, so a targeted lint avoids silent metadata loss.

name: caf-chunk-validator
description: Validates an Apple CAF file's chunk structure: required Audio Description chunk, valid chunk sizes, and presence of a Data chunk.
example_prompt: Is this CAF audio file's chunk layout valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: CAF is a simple big-endian chunked container parsed directly from bytes.
rationale: CAF files exported from macOS tools sometimes omit required chunks, breaking cross-platform players.

name: au-snd-header-validator
description: Validates a Sun/NeXT .au (.snd) header: '.snd' magic, data offset, encoding code, sample rate, and channel field sanity.
example_prompt: Validate this .au audio file header
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the .au header is a fixed 24-byte big-endian struct trivially parsed offline.
rationale: Legacy .au files still appear in academic and telephony datasets and need a basic integrity gate.

name: dsf-dsd-header-validator
description: Validates a DSF (DSD) file's DSD/fmt chunk header: format version, channel type, sampling frequency, bits-per-sample, and block size.
example_prompt: Check whether this DSF DSD file has a valid header
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: DSF headers are fixed-layout chunks read straight from file bytes.
rationale: High-res DSD purchases occasionally have mismatched header fields that confuse DACs, and this flags them.

name: speex-header-validator
description: Validates a Speex Ogg packet header: 'Speex   ' magic, version, rate, mode, and channel fields against spec ranges.
example_prompt: Check whether this Speex audio file has a valid header
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses the Speex header packet bytes from the first Ogg page, fully offline.
rationale: Voice/VoIP archives still hold Speex files and a header lint guards against malformed legacy encodes.

name: wavpack-block-validator
description: Validates WavPack block headers: 'wvpk' ID, block size, version, sample counts, and flag-field consistency across blocks.
example_prompt: Validate the WavPack block headers in this .wv file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: iterates WavPack block headers from file bytes without decoding samples.
rationale: WavPack's per-block headers can desync after partial transfers, and block-level validation finds the break.

name: requirements-txt-lint
description: Lints a Python requirements.txt for duplicate/conflicting pins, unpinned packages, invalid PEP 440 version specifiers, and editable/URL line issues.
example_prompt: Lint this requirements.txt
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: line parsing against PEP 440 grammar, fully local.
rationale: Conflicting or unpinned requirements cause non-reproducible builds and a linter flags them before install.

name: ogg-vorbis-comment-reader
description: Extracts the Vorbis comment block (vendor string plus all FIELD=value entries) from an Ogg Vorbis stream.
example_prompt: Show the Vorbis comments in this .ogg
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — locates the comment header packet and reads its length-prefixed strings, client-side.
rationale: Vorbis comments hold all OGG tagging and need a focused reader separate from container inspection.

name: ar-archive-inspector
description: Lists members, sizes, and timestamps inside a Unix ar archive (.a static library or .deb).
example_prompt: List the object files inside this .a static library
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the ar format is a simple text-header + payload sequence parsed in pure Rust.
rationale: Inspecting static-lib or .deb contents without extracting is a frequent build-debugging task.

name: mp4-sample-table-parser
description: Extracts an MP4 track's sample table (stts/stsz/stsc/stco/ctts) into a CSV of per-sample size, file offset, and duration.
example_prompt: Export the sample table of the video track in this mp4 as CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the stbl sub-boxes and expands the run-length tables in memory; no decoding.
rationale: Per-sample offsets/sizes are needed for byte-range streaming, repair, and verifying interleave without any external tool.

name: mp4-edit-list-parser
description: Reads the MP4 edit list (elst) entries per track, showing media-time mappings, offsets, and rates.
example_prompt: Does this mp4 have an edit list? Show the elst entries
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the small elst box directly; trivial in-browser computation.
rationale: Edit lists silently shift A/V sync and trim playback start, and they are invisible in most metadata views.

name: fmp4-fragment-index-parser
description: Parses a fragmented MP4's sidx/moof/tfdt boxes into a table of fragment offsets, durations, and decode times.
example_prompt: List the fragments and their timestamps in this fragmented mp4
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM walks the segment index and movie-fragment boxes; structural parse, runs locally.
rationale: DASH/HLS fMP4 debugging needs the fragment index to spot gaps or wrong baseMediaDecodeTime values.

name: mpegts-program-table-parser
description: Parses MPEG-TS PAT/PMT tables into a JSON map of programs, elementary PIDs, stream types, and descriptors.
example_prompt: Show me the PAT and PMT program map of this .ts file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM demultiplexes 188-byte TS packets and parses the PSI sections; pure parsing, client-side.
rationale: Understanding which PIDs carry which streams is essential for broadcast/HLS TS troubleshooting and there is no TS PSI tool yet.

name: video-scte35-marker-parser
description: Extracts SCTE-35 ad-insertion cue messages from an MPEG-TS stream into a timestamped JSON list.
example_prompt: Pull all the SCTE-35 ad markers out of this transport stream
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM filters the SCTE-35 PID and decodes the splice_info sections; no network, runs in-browser.
rationale: Ad-break cue auditing is a real broadcast/streaming workflow with no existing client-side parser.

name: video-spherical-360-metadata-parser
description: Parses 360/VR spherical-video metadata (Google ST3D/SV3D, equirectangular projection, stereo layout) into JSON.
example_prompt: Is this a 360 video? Show me its spherical/projection metadata
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the spherical metadata boxes/XML in the MP4; structural parse, fully local.
rationale: 360 players rely on this metadata and authors need to verify it is present and correct before publishing.

name: avi-riff-chunk-parser
description: Parses an AVI file's RIFF chunk hierarchy, stream headers (strh/strf), and index (idx1) into JSON.
example_prompt: Show the RIFF chunk structure and stream headers of this .avi
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the RIFF/LIST chunk tree directly; structural parse, runs locally.
rationale: AVI is still produced by capture cards and a RIFF tree view is the only way to diagnose codec/index issues.

name: mxf-partition-parser
description: Parses MXF partition packs, the primer pack, and essence descriptors into a readable structural summary.
example_prompt: Parse the partitions and essence descriptors in this MXF file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the KLV-coded MXF partitions and metadata sets; structural parse, fully client-side.
rationale: Broadcast/cinema MXF interchange frequently fails on partition/descriptor issues that no browser tool currently surfaces.

name: video-gop-structure-parser
description: Lists every frame's picture type (I/P/B) and marks GOP boundaries and open/closed GOP status.
example_prompt: Show me the I/P/B frame pattern and GOP structure of this video
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses slice/picture headers in the elementary stream to classify frames; no full decode required.
rationale: Full frame-type sequencing (beyond just keyframe timestamps) reveals encoder GOP settings that affect seeking and editing.

name: abc-notation-parser
description: Parses ABC notation into structured tune data: headers (title, key, meter, tempo) and a decoded note sequence.
example_prompt: Parse this ABC tune into notes and headers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: ABC grammar tokenizer/parser, fully client-side.
rationale: ABC is the dominant folk-tune text format and a structured parse unlocks playback and conversion.

name: audacity-label-parser
description: Parses an Audacity label-track export (TSV of start, end, label) into structured region JSON.
example_prompt: Parse this Audacity labels.txt into regions
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: tab-separated text parse, fully client-side.
rationale: Audacity labels are a common hand-made source of region/marker data for splitting and subtitling.

name: midi-marker-extractor
description: Extracts marker and cue-point meta events (with tick/time) from a MIDI file into a timeline.
example_prompt: List the markers in this MIDI file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: reads marker/cue meta events, fully client-side.
rationale: Section markers structure arrangements and are needed when porting between DAWs.

name: resx-parse
description: Flattens a .NET .resx resource XML into a key/value/comment table.
example_prompt: Show me all the strings in this resx file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML parse of the <data> nodes; pure text, no server, works on localization files directly in chat
rationale: Translators and .NET devs need to read resx strings without opening Visual Studio.

name: xcstrings-parse
description: Flattens an Apple String Catalog (.xcstrings) JSON into a per-language translation table with state flags.
example_prompt: List every key and its translations from this xcstrings file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON traversal of the localizations tree; runs in-browser so iOS string catalogs need no tooling install
rationale: The new .xcstrings format is hard to read raw and there's no lightweight viewer outside Xcode.

name: touchstone-sparam-parse
description: Parses a Touchstone .sNp S-parameter file into a frequency table of complex parameters with the option-line settings.
example_prompt: Parse this .s2p file into a frequency vs S21 table
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reading the option line (# GHz S RI/MA) and numeric rows; pure numeric parsing in-browser
rationale: RF engineers exchange Touchstone files constantly and need a fast local way to read magnitudes/phases without MATLAB.

name: guitar-pro-tab-parse
description: Parses a Guitar Pro file (.gp5 binary or .gp/.gpx zip) into its track list, tunings, tempo, and measure count.
example_prompt: List the tracks and tunings in this Guitar Pro file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (binary read for gp5, zip+XML for gpx); pure parsing of tablature files entirely in-browser
rationale: Musicians want to inspect a tab's instruments and tuning without installing Guitar Pro.

name: dtd-element-parse
description: Parses an XML DTD into its element, attribute-list, and entity declarations with content models.
example_prompt: Show me the elements and attributes declared in this DTD
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizing the <!ELEMENT/<!ATTLIST/<!ENTITY declarations; pure text analysis client-side
rationale: Understanding an unfamiliar XML vocabulary from its DTD is common and there's no lightweight local viewer.

name: go-sum-parser
description: Parses go.sum into modules with versions and hash types, flagging modules with only go.mod hashes.
example_prompt: Parse this go.sum and list the modules and hashes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line-parsing the simple go.sum format; offline text processing.
rationale: Auditing Go module hashes/versions is straightforward but tedious by hand.

name: q-format-fixed-point-parser
description: Parses Qm.n fixed-point hex/integer values into their real floating-point equivalents.
example_prompt: Interpret 0x4000 as Q1.15 fixed point
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — scaling by 2^-n with sign handling, fully local.
rationale: DSP and embedded data is stored in Q-format that has no readable decimal without this conversion.

name: ordinal-number-parser
description: Parses ordinals in digit ('21st') and word ('twenty-first') forms into their cardinal integer.
example_prompt: Convert 'twenty-third' and '101st' to numbers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — suffix stripping and word-number tables, no network.
rationale: Ranked lists and dates use ordinals that need cardinal integers for sorting and arithmetic.

name: sparkline
description: Generate a compact inline sparkline (Unicode or tiny SVG) from a list of numbers.
example_prompt: sparkline for 5, 9, 3, 12, 7, 15
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM render.
rationale: Tiny trend visuals for dashboards/READMEs/chat with no current tool.

name: ssh-fingerprint
description: Compute the SHA256/MD5 fingerprint and randomart of an SSH public key.
example_prompt: What's the fingerprint of this SSH public key?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM hashing/parse; offline.
rationale: Standard verification step when adding/trusting keys.

name: vcard-generator

example_prompt: Make a vCard for Jane Doe, jane@acme.com, +1 555 0100
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM emits the vCard text format directly.
rationale: Lightweight Communication tool that's surprisingly fiddly to do by hand.

name: isbn-validator
description: Validates an ISBN and converts between ISBN-10 and ISBN-13.
example_prompt: Is 978-3-16-148410-0 a valid ISBN, and what's its ISBN-10?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; check-digit math and conversion run entirely in-process.
rationale: Goodreads/Open Library demand centers on book identifiers, and validation/conversion is pure arithmetic.

name: jsonapi-validator
description: Validates a document against the JSON:API specification and flags structural violations.
example_prompt: is this response a valid JSON:API document?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with serde_json — checks the JSON:API structural rules in-memory

name: npi-validator

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: prefix-augmented Luhn, fully local with no PHI exposure.

name: abn-validator

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: weighted sum and modulo, no external register call.
rationale: Australian invoicing and onboarding flows need offline ABN format validation before any registry lookup.

name: viewport-meta-normalizer

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; key=value content parsing, pure computation.

name: integer-fraction-splitter
description: Splits each decimal value into separate integer-part and fractional-part columns.
example_prompt: Split these decimals into whole-number and fractional columns
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: truncation + subtraction, all in-memory.
rationale: Separating integer and fractional parts is a tidy preprocessing step for currency, time, and feature engineering.

name: csp-violation-report-parse
description: Parses a CSP violation report (report-uri JSON or Reporting API body) and summarizes the blocked URI, directive, and source.
example_prompt: which directive blocked this resource in my CSP report?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON parsing of the posted report body; no policy fetching
rationale: CSP reports arrive as terse JSON and pinpointing the offending directive speeds policy tuning.

name: html-form-inspect
description: Inspects an HTML form, listing its action, method, enctype, and every field's name, type, required state, and validation attributes.
example_prompt: list all the fields and required ones in this form HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML parsing of the pasted form; no submission
rationale: Understanding a form's exact fields and validation is key for testing and integration without guessing.

name: points-on-circle-generator
description: Generates N evenly spaced points on a circle of given radius and center as CSV coordinates.
example_prompt: Place 12 points evenly around a circle of radius 5
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — angular stepping with sin/cos, fully client-side
rationale: Handy for clock faces, radial layouts, and sampling points for plotting without manual trig.

name: sixel-to-png
description: Decodes terminal Sixel graphics data into a PNG image.
example_prompt: Turn this Sixel terminal output into a PNG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM sixel decoder parses the escape stream and renders PNG locally

name: brightness-compare
description: Computes the average spectral centroid of two clips and reports which is brighter and by how many Hz.
example_prompt: Which of these two mixes sounds brighter?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM performs FFT and centroid averaging on both clips client-side.
rationale: Gives a single objective tonal-brightness comparison useful for matching mixes or masters.

name: changelog-version-diff
description: Parses a Keep-a-Changelog file and extracts the combined set of changes between two specified versions.
example_prompt: What changed between v1.2.0 and v1.5.0 in this CHANGELOG?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse version sections and merge entries in range, text-only.
rationale: Summarizing what changed across several releases means manually stitching changelog sections today.

name: video-mime-codecs-string-validator
description: Validates a provided RFC 6381 codecs= MIME parameter string (e.g. avc1.640028, mp4a.40.2) for correct syntax and consistency with the file.
example_prompt: Is this codecs string valid: avc1.640028,mp4a.40.2 — and does it match my file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the codecs grammar and optionally cross-checks the file's actual codecs; pure string/box logic, client-side.
rationale: A wrong codecs= string breaks Media Source Extensions playback entirely, and there's no easy way to verify it by hand.

name: adts-aac-header-validator
description: Validates ADTS AAC frame headers for consistent profile, sample-rate index, channel config, and frame-length fields across the stream.
example_prompt: Check the AAC ADTS headers in this .aac file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses each 7/9-byte ADTS header in sequence, fully client-side.
rationale: Inconsistent ADTS headers cause hardware decoders to reject otherwise-playable AAC streams.

name: aiff-chunk-validator
description: Validates an AIFF/AIFF-C file's FORM, COMM, and SSND chunk sizes and confirms the declared frame count matches the sound data.
example_prompt: Is this AIFF file's chunk structure valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the IFF chunk layout locally with no network.
rationale: AIFF is common in pro audio and broadcast, and chunk-size errors break import in editors that strictly parse COMM/SSND.

name: jpeg-quality-estimator
description: Reverse-engineers the approximate JPEG quality factor from the embedded quantization tables.
example_prompt: What quality was this JPEG saved at?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the DQT tables and matches them to standard quality curves client-side.
rationale: Knowing the original quality prevents pointless re-compression and reveals over-compressed assets.

name: line-stats
description: Reports line, word, byte, and character counts plus longest/shortest line and blank-line totals for text.
example_prompt: Give me line, word, and character counts for this text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM byte-wise line iteration (bytelines-style efficiency); pure in-memory scan.
rationale: bytelines is about fast line processing; a wc-plus tool is a simple, universally useful text utility.

name: pgp-word-list-converter
description: Converts bytes/hex to and from the PGP (RFC 1751) word list used to read transfer codes and fingerprints aloud.
example_prompt: Convert this hex fingerprint into PGP words so I can read it over the phone
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM table lookup mapping in both directions — entirely local.
rationale: Magic Wormhole's human-readable codes rely on exactly this encoding, useful for verbally verifying any transfer.

name: unit-price-compare
description: Compare unit prices ($/100g, $/oz, $/unit) across package sizes to find the best deal.
example_prompt: Which is cheaper: 500g for $4.20 or 750g for $6.10?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM arithmetic + unit normalization; browser-local.
rationale: Unit-price comparison is a practical everyday shopping aid not covered by generic calculators.

name: houndstooth-pattern-generator
description: Generates a classic two-tone houndstooth tile at a chosen scale and color pair, output as a seamless PNG.
example_prompt: Generate a black-and-white houndstooth pattern, 64px tile
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — stamp the houndstooth motif into a tile buffer; pure raster math.
rationale: Specific named-pattern generators are exactly the precise single-purpose tools requested and have no catalog entry.

name: herringbone-pattern-generator
description: Generates a tileable herringbone brick/parquet pattern with configurable plank size, gap, and colors.
example_prompt: Make a herringbone wood-floor pattern, 120x30 planks
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — place rotated rectangles on the herringbone lattice and PNG-encode.
rationale: Herringbone backgrounds are common in design mockups but absent from the existing pattern set.

name: crosshatch-pattern-generator
description: Generates a tileable crosshatch/engraving line pattern with adjustable angles, spacing, and stroke weight.
example_prompt: Make a crosshatch pattern at 30 and 120 degrees, fine lines
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — draw two stroked line families into a seamless tile; pure raster.
rationale: Crosshatch fills are a specific, frequently wanted texture absent from the existing pattern tools.

name: color-swatch-sheet-generator
description: Renders a provided list of colors into a labeled swatch sheet image with hex/RGB captions for sharing or print.
example_prompt: Make a swatch sheet image from #1b1b2f #e94560 #0f3460 with hex labels
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — lay out captioned color tiles into a raster; pure drawing.
rationale: Turning a palette into a shareable labeled image is distinct from generating shades and is genuinely handy.

name: thrift-from-json
description: Generates Apache Thrift struct definitions with numbered fields from a JSON sample document.
example_prompt: Make Thrift struct definitions from this JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: JSON parse plus Thrift IDL string emission, no thrift compiler.
rationale: Thrift IDLs require explicit field IDs and types; scaffolding them from existing JSON is a clear time-saver.

name: referrer-policy-generator
description: Generates the Referrer-Policy header and the equivalent meta tag, with a plain-language effect summary.
example_prompt: give me a privacy-friendly Referrer-Policy header
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM enum mapping and output formatting; no network.
rationale: There are eight referrer-policy values with subtle cross-origin differences that most people pick blindly.

name: skip-link-generator
description: Generates a 'skip to main content' link plus the CSS to visually hide it until focused.
example_prompt: add an accessible skip-to-content link to my page
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML + CSS templating; fully local.
rationale: Skip links are a baseline WCAG requirement and the visually-hidden-until-focus CSS trips people up.

name: native-dialog-generator
description: Scaffolds a native HTML <dialog> modal with open/close JS, backdrop styling, and focus handling.
example_prompt: scaffold a native dialog modal with a close button
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML/CSS/JS templating; no framework or network.
rationale: The <dialog> element replaces ad-hoc modal libraries but the showModal/backdrop/focus pattern needs a correct starter.

name: general-midi-compliance-check
description: Checks a MIDI file for General MIDI compliance: program numbers in range, percussion on channel 10, and recognized controller usage.
example_prompt: Is this MIDI file General MIDI compliant?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads program-change and channel events and applies GM rules locally.
rationale: Non-GM files play with wrong instruments on GM hardware, and a compliance check tells you what to remap.

name: smpte-timecode-validator
description: Validates SMPTE timecode strings or a list of them for legal HH:MM:SS:FF ranges at a given frame rate, flagging drop-frame errors.
example_prompt: Validate these SMPTE timecodes at 29.97 drop-frame
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses each timecode and checks frame/drop-frame rules locally.
rationale: Illegal or wrong-rate timecodes desync audio-to-picture, and validation catches them before a sync session.

name: meta-refresh-checker
description: Detects meta http-equiv=refresh redirects in HTML and warns about the delay value and accessibility/SEO drawbacks.
example_prompt: Does this HTML use a meta refresh redirect?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML parse for the meta refresh pattern — pure local scan.
rationale: Meta refresh redirects hurt accessibility and SEO and should be flagged so they can be replaced with HTTP redirects.

name: unicode-script-breakdown
description: Counts how many characters belong to each Unicode script and block (Latin, Cyrillic, CJK, emoji, etc.).
example_prompt: What scripts and Unicode blocks appear in this text?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with bundled Unicode property tables; lookups run offline.
rationale: Mixed-script strings reveal homoglyph spoofing, encoding mishaps, and unexpected foreign-language content.

name: animated-image-frame-counter
description: Detects whether a GIF, APNG, or animated WebP is animated and counts its frames and total duration.
example_prompt: Is this image animated, and how many frames does it have?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM inspects the container of GIF/APNG/WebP frame structures from the bytes.
rationale: A single 'is it animated and how long' check spans three formats people commonly confuse for static images.

name: video-audio-dc-offset-report
description: Computes the DC bias (mean amplitude offset) of each audio channel in the video.
example_prompt: Is there a DC offset on my video's audio?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg's astats filter reports per-channel mean amplitude from locally decoded PCM.
rationale: DC offset wastes headroom and causes pops; a quick read tells whether a correction filter is needed.

name: video-frame-type-histogram
description: Counts I, P, and B frames and reports their ratio to characterize the encode's GOP economy.
example_prompt: How many I, P, and B frames does my video have?
loader_feasibility: ffprobe reads per-frame picture types from the locally parsed stream.
rationale: The I/P/B mix instantly explains a file's size and seekability and flags wasteful all-intra encodes.

name: mp4-track-duration-vs-samples-checker
description: Compares each track's declared duration against the sum of its sample durations to catch header inconsistencies.
example_prompt: Does my MP4's declared duration match its actual samples?
loader_feasibility: A Rust parser reads mvhd/tkhd/stts from the in-browser file and recomputes sample totals.
rationale: Mismatched declared vs real duration causes wrong progress bars and seeking, and is otherwise invisible.

name: audio-gapless-info-reader
description: Reports encoder delay and end padding (iTunSMPB / LAME) used for gapless playback alignment.
example_prompt: Show the gapless playback delay and padding for this track
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse the relevant header/atom fields; pure byte-level reading, no decode.
rationale: Gapless metadata is critical for correct album playback and seamless concatenation.

name: linear-recurrence-generator
description: Generates terms of a linear recurrence from its coefficients and initial seed values.
example_prompt: Generate 20 terms of a_n = a_{n-1} + a_{n-2} starting 2, 1
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — big-integer rolling evaluation of the recurrence, no deps.
rationale: A general scaffold covering Fibonacci, Lucas, Padovan, and custom sequences without special-casing each.

name: image-swap-channels
description: Reorders color channels (e.g. RGB→BGR or red↔blue) to fix mis-decoded images.
example_prompt: Fix this image where the red and blue channels are swapped
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: permute channel bytes in the pixel buffer.
rationale: Repairs the common BGR/RGB channel-order bug from misread formats.

name: excess-k-converter
description: Converts integers to and from biased/excess-K (offset-binary) representation for a chosen bias and width.
example_prompt: encode -3 in excess-127 with 8 bits
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — add bias then format bits, pure local math.
rationale: Biased exponents (excess-127/1023) underpin IEEE floats and many ADC formats, and decoding them by hand is mistake-prone.

name: morton-zorder-encoder
description: Interleaves the bits of 2D (or 3D) integer coordinates into a single Morton/Z-order index and decodes it back.
example_prompt: morton encode the coordinate x=5, y=3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bit-interleaving loops, deterministic and local.
rationale: Z-order curves are a standard way to linearize spatial data for indexing/caching, and bit-interleaving by hand is tedious and bug-prone.

name: destination-point-calculator
description: Computes the destination latitude/longitude from a start point given a bearing and distance (great-circle dead reckoning).
example_prompt: from 51.5,-0.12 go 10km on bearing 90 degrees — where do I land?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — spherical trig (direct geodesic) on doubles, no geocoding call.
rationale: Plotting a destination from a heading and distance is core navigation math that the existing distance/format coordinate tools don't provide.

name: list-to-quoted-csv
description: Wraps each line in quotes and joins them into a comma-separated list for SQL IN clauses or arrays.
example_prompt: turn this list of ids into a quoted comma-separated list for a SQL IN
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; per-line quoting and joining, no I/O
rationale: Building IN-clause and array literals from a pasted column is a daily query task.

name: tartan-pattern-generator
description: Generates a tileable tartan/plaid weave from a thread-count sett string (e.g. "K24 R4 K24 G24").
example_prompt: Make a tartan from sett K24 R4 K24 G24 W2
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — expand the sett into warp/weft stripes with twill over-under blending; PNG output.
rationale: Encodes real tartan rules into a precise generator that fashion and craft users want and can't find browser-local.

name: frequency-list-to-tone-sequence
description: Turns a list of frequencies (or note names) and durations into a sequential melody/test WAV.
example_prompt: Play 440 Hz, 554 Hz, 659 Hz each for 0.5s as one audio clip
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM concatenates per-step oscillator segments and emits a single WAV locally
rationale: A scriptable tone-sequence builder is useful for jingles, alerts, and data-to-sound sketches.

name: pls-playlist-generator
description: Creates a PLS-format playlist (FileN/TitleN/LengthN entries) from a track list for legacy players and streams.
example_prompt: Generate a PLS playlist for these three stream URLs with titles
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM writes the INI-style PLS sections from the inputs entirely local
rationale: PLS is still required by many radio players and is annoying to format manually.

name: json-feed-generator
description: Generates a JSON Feed 1.1 document from a list of items with titles, URLs, dates, and content.
example_prompt: generate a JSON Feed from my latest 10 blog posts
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON building per the jsonfeed.org spec; fully offline.
rationale: JSON Feed is a clean alternative to RSS/Atom and no existing tool emits it despite the format's growing support.

name: changelog-linter
description: Validates a CHANGELOG against the Keep a Changelog format, checking version order, date formats, and section headings.
example_prompt: Lint my CHANGELOG.md against Keep a Changelog
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing Markdown structure and semver ordering; fully offline.
rationale: Hand-maintained changelogs drift from the standard and a structural linter keeps release notes machine-parseable.

name: asyncapi-validate
description: Validates an AsyncAPI 2.x/3.x document structure and channel/message references against the spec.
example_prompt: Is this AsyncAPI document valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parser with the AsyncAPI schema and ref checks; offline
rationale: Event-driven API specs are increasingly common but lack convenient client-side validators.

name: cipher-identifier
description: Analyzes an unknown ciphertext and ranks the most likely classical ciphers (Caesar, affine, Atbash, A1Z26, rail fence, substitution, etc.).
example_prompt: What kind of cipher is 'Gsrh rh z hvxivg' likely to be?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — frequency-analysis and character-set heuristics run entirely on-device.
rationale: Turns the cluster of classical-cipher demand into a high-value first step users reach for before decoding.

name: video-to-uncompressed-avi
description: Exports a video as raw uncompressed (rawvideo) frames in an AVI container for legacy editors.
example_prompt: Give me an uncompressed AVI of this clip
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM writes rawvideo packets into an AVI container client-side.
rationale: A handful of old editing/analysis tools only ingest uncompressed AVI, and no current tool produces it.

name: rekordbox-xml-to-m3u
description: Converts a Pioneer rekordbox collection/playlist XML into a standard M3U playlist.
example_prompt: Turn my rekordbox.xml playlist into an M3U
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse the rekordbox <TRACK Location=...> file URIs and write M3U paths
rationale: Migrates DJ libraries off rekordbox into open tooling with no cloud upload.

name: serato-crate-to-m3u
description: Decodes a Serato .crate binary file and lists its track paths as an M3U playlist.
example_prompt: Convert this Serato crate file to an M3U playlist
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse the Serato tagged binary (ptrk/otrk) records and write M3U
rationale: Opens Serato's opaque crate format so DJs can move sets to other software.

name: matrix-csv-to-mathml
description: Renders a numeric CSV matrix as a MathML matrix expression for docs and web pages.
example_prompt: Turn this CSV into a MathML matrix
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; CSV parse then MathML string emission.
rationale: Embedding real data as proper MathML matrices otherwise means hand-writing the markup.

name: image-color-profile-compare
description: Reads the embedded ICC color profiles of two images and reports differences in color space, gamma and white point.
example_prompt: Are these two images in the same color profile? Compare their ICC data.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses each ICC profile header and diffs the tagged fields client-side.
rationale: Mismatched profiles (sRGB vs Display P3) silently shift colors; comparing them catches the cause of inconsistent rendering.

name: video-mp4-atom-diff
description: Parses the MP4/MOV box (atom) tree of two files and diffs the structure to reveal muxing differences like faststart, edit lists, or extra boxes.
example_prompt: Diff the MP4 atom structure of these two files to see why one won't stream
loader_feasibility: MP4 box parsing is straightforward byte-offset walking that runs as a self-contained plain-Rust WASM block.
rationale: Container-structure diffs catch faststart/moov-placement and edit-list bugs that metadata-level inspection completely misses.

name: video-blockiness-compare
description: Compares blocking-artifact levels between two encodes by measuring edge energy on the 8x8 DCT grid.
example_prompt: Compare the blocking artifacts between my CRF 23 and CRF 28 encodes
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM decodes frames locally and a plain-Rust block computes the grid-aligned blockiness metric per file.
rationale: Blockiness is the classic visible compression failure and a direct comparison helps pick the right bitrate ceiling.

name: video-color-tag-diff
description: Compares the color primaries, transfer characteristics, and matrix coefficients tags of two videos to catch BT.709-vs-BT.2020 mismatches.
example_prompt: Did my export change the color space tags from BT.2020 to BT.709?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM reads the color metadata of each file locally and a plain-Rust block diffs the tags.
rationale: Wrong color tags cause incorrect playback rendering, and this targeted diff catches the most common HDR/SDR tagging mistake.

name: video-container-overhead-compare
description: Compares container overhead (header/index bytes vs payload) of two files to show which muxing is more efficient.
example_prompt: Compare how much container overhead MKV vs MP4 adds to my video
loader_feasibility: Box/element size walking of each container compiles to a self-contained plain-Rust WASM block.
rationale: Container efficiency matters for bandwidth-tight delivery and is invisible to bitrate-level comparison.

name: video-encoder-fingerprint-diff
description: Extracts and compares embedded encoder signatures and settings (e.g. x264 SEI strings) from two files to reveal which tool and settings produced each.
example_prompt: What encoder settings differ between these two files?
loader_feasibility: Parsing SEI/metadata strings from the bitstream is plain byte scanning that runs in a plain-Rust WASM block.
rationale: Recovering the actual encode recipe from two files explains quality/size gaps that metadata alone can't account for.

name: video-audio-bitrate-diff
description: Compares audio codec, bitrate, sample rate, and channel count of two videos and flags any downgrade.
example_prompt: Did my export downgrade the audio bitrate or sample rate?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM probes each file's audio streams locally and a plain-Rust block diffs the parameters.
rationale: Audio quality silently dropping during a video re-encode is common and a focused diff surfaces it immediately.

name: video-chapter-diff
description: Compares chapter markers (count, timestamps, titles) between two video files.
example_prompt: Compare the chapter markers in these two versions of my film
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM reads chapter metadata from each file locally and a plain-Rust block diffs the lists.
rationale: Chapter loss or drift during editing/remuxing is easy to miss and matters for navigable long-form video.

name: video-hdr-metadata-diff
description: Compares HDR static and dynamic metadata (MaxCLL, MaxFALL, mastering-display values) between two files to detect lost or altered HDR signaling.
example_prompt: Did my export preserve the HDR10 mastering metadata?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg WASM reads side-data HDR metadata per file locally and a plain-Rust block diffs the values.
rationale: Stripped HDR metadata causes wrong tone mapping on displays, and this is the only quick way to verify it survived an encode.

name: crest-factor-compare
description: Computes the crest factor (peak÷RMS) of two recordings to compare how much dynamic punch each preserves.
example_prompt: Compare the crest factor of the limited vs unlimited mix
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM derives peak and RMS from PCM arrays locally.
rationale: Crest factor exposes compression/limiting differences that loudness numbers alone hide.

name: dc-offset-compare
description: Measures the DC offset of two files per channel and reports which has more baseline bias.
example_prompt: Do either of these recordings have a DC offset, and which is worse?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM averages PCM samples per channel in-browser.
rationale: DC offset wastes headroom and causes clicks; a two-file check flags a faulty interface quickly.

name: codec-delay-compare
description: Reads encoder delay and padding (gapless info) from two encoded files and reports the difference for playback alignment.
example_prompt: Compare the encoder delay/padding between these two MP3s
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses LAME/iTunSMPB gapless headers without decoding audio.
rationale: Mismatched encoder delay causes gapless-playback glitches, and a diff explains alignment problems.

name: musicxml-diff
description: Diffs two MusicXML scores and reports changed notes, measures, and parts.
example_prompt: What changed between these two versions of the score?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the MusicXML and walks the note trees in-browser.
rationale: Score versioning lacks a readable diff, and comparing notes/measures helps composers track revisions.

name: bitrate-profile-compare
description: Compares the per-frame bitrate profiles of two MP3 files to show their CBR/VBR distribution differences.
example_prompt: Compare the bitrate profiles of these two MP3s
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM walks MP3 frame headers and bins bitrates without decoding audio.
rationale: Bitrate-profile comparison reveals which of two encodes allocated more data and where.

name: maven-dependency-diff
description: Compares the dependency sets of two Maven pom.xml files and reports version, scope, and exclusion changes plus added/removed artifacts.
example_prompt: Compare the dependencies in these two pom.xml files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses both POM XML files and diffs by groupId:artifactId locally; it is XML processing with no Maven invocation.
rationale: Java dependency review needs POM-aware diffing (scope/exclusions), which the npm-focused package-json diff does not cover.

name: epub-toc-diff
description: Compares the table-of-contents and chapter structure of two EPUB files and reports added, removed, renamed, and reordered sections.
example_prompt: Compare the chapters in these two EPUB editions and show what changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM unzips both EPUBs and diffs the NCX/nav XML in-browser; EPUB is just a ZIP of XML, handled fully client-side.
rationale: Comparing book editions/revisions by structure is a real editorial need with no EPUB-aware diff in the catalog.

name: cache-control-diff
description: Parses and compares the Cache-Control directives of two responses, showing changed max-age, added/removed directives, and stricter/looser caching.
example_prompt: Compare the Cache-Control headers of these two responses and explain what changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM directive parsing + comparison; client-side
rationale: A subtle Cache-Control change can cause stale assets or cache stampedes, and a directive diff makes it obvious.

name: unix-permissions-compare
description: Compares two file permission specs (symbolic rwx vs octal) and explains the differences.
example_prompt: What's the difference between 0755 and rwxr-x---?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses both notations and diffs the bits locally; offline.
rationale: Mixed octal/symbolic permissions confuse people, and a side-by-side bit comparison removes the guesswork.

name: license-text-diff
description: Compares two open-source license texts and highlights clause-level differences and likely license identity.
example_prompt: How does this LICENSE file differ from the standard MIT text?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizes and diffs against bundled canonical license texts locally; offline.
rationale: Detecting modified or non-standard license text matters for compliance and is awkward with a generic text diff.

name: fuel-economy-compare
description: Compares two vehicles' fuel economy across mpg and L/100km and projects annual fuel cost.
example_prompt: Compare a 32 mpg car with a 7 L/100km car over 15,000 km
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM converts units and computes cost locally; pure arithmetic, offline.
rationale: Car shoppers face mixed mpg/L-per-100km figures and want a normalized cost comparison.

name: mgrs-coordinate-converter
description: Converts between decimal-degree lat/lon and MGRS military grid reference strings at a chosen precision, for single values or a CSV column.
example_prompt: Convert these lat/lon points to MGRS grid references
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: UTM/UPS plus 100km grid-square lettering math, computed locally.
rationale: MGRS is standard in defense, search-and-rescue, and field surveys, and no existing tool handles the lat/lon↔MGRS round trip.

name: class-attribute-dedupe
description: Deduplicates and optionally sorts the class names inside HTML class attributes.
example_prompt: clean up duplicate classes in these class= attributes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizes class attribute values and removes repeats locally
rationale: Templating and utility-CSS workflows accumulate duplicate classes that bloat markup.

name: deduplicate-floats-with-tolerance
description: Collapses near-equal floating-point values that fall within an absolute or relative tolerance into a single representative.
example_prompt: Dedupe these floats treating anything within 1e-6 as equal
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: sort and merge within epsilon, pure numeric
rationale: Tolerance-based merging handles float jitter that exact row-dedup tools miss entirely.

name: xxencode-codec
description: Encodes and decodes the classic xxencode binary-to-text format (a Uuencode sibling).
example_prompt: xxencode this text block
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — fixed alphabet block transform, no network.
rationale: Legacy Usenet/email archives still contain xxencoded blobs that need decoding.

name: wav-endianness-swapper
description: Byte-swaps the PCM sample data of a WAV between little-endian and big-endian and updates the format markers.
example_prompt: Swap this wav to big-endian bytes for my DSP board
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reverses bytes per sample word based on bit depth — pure byte manipulation
rationale: Embedded and cross-platform PCM pipelines often expect the opposite byte order, producing static otherwise.

name: enhanced-lrc-to-simple
description: Strips word-level A2 timestamps from an Enhanced LRC file down to standard line-timed LRC.
example_prompt: Convert this karaoke enhanced lrc to a plain line-timed lrc
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM removes inline <mm:ss.xx> word tags while keeping line tags — pure text filtering
rationale: Many players choke on Enhanced LRC word timing and need the simpler line-only variant for display.

name: markdown-admonition-parser
description: Parses admonition/callout blocks (GitHub `> [!NOTE]`, MkDocs `!!! warning`, Docusaurus `:::tip`) into typed, structured entries.
example_prompt: Find all the note/warning/tip callouts in this markdown and list them by type.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; recognizes the three callout syntaxes via text patterns, runs entirely in-browser.
rationale: Different doc tools use different callout syntaxes; one parser to inventory them helps migration and review.

name: gemfile-lock-parser
description: Parses a Ruby Gemfile.lock into a structured dependency tree with resolved versions and platforms.
example_prompt: Parse this Gemfile.lock and show me the resolved gem versions.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; the Gemfile.lock format is a simple indented text grammar, parsed locally.
rationale: Inspecting locked Ruby dependency versions and platforms without a Ruby toolchain is genuinely useful.

name: pipfile-parser
description: Parses a Pipenv Pipfile (TOML) into structured package, dev-package, and source sections with version specifiers.
example_prompt: Show me the packages and version constraints in this Pipfile.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via a TOML parser; pure text, no network.
rationale: Quickly reading a Python project's declared deps and constraints without installing Pipenv.

name: pom-dependency-extractor
description: Extracts Maven <dependency> entries (groupId/artifactId/version/scope) from a pom.xml into a table.
example_prompt: Extract the Maven dependencies from this pom.xml as a table.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML parsing of the POM dependency elements, fully client-side.
rationale: POM files are verbose; a clean dependency table speeds up audits and version reviews.

name: apache-config-parser
description: Parses Apache httpd config into a directive/section tree (VirtualHost, Directory, Location) for inspection.
example_prompt: Parse this Apache config and show the VirtualHosts and their directives.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; recursive parse of the directive/`<Section>` grammar, fully local.
rationale: Apache configs nest deeply; a structured tree makes auditing vhosts and directives far easier.

name: desktop-entry-parser
description: Parses a freedesktop .desktop entry into structured fields (Name, Exec, Icon, Categories, MimeType, Actions).
example_prompt: Parse this .desktop file and show the Exec command and categories.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; the .desktop format is INI-like with localized keys, parsed locally.
rationale: Linux app launchers and broken menu entries are easiest to debug by reading a structured view of the entry.

name: procfile-parser
description: Parses a Procfile into process-type → command entries and flags duplicate types or empty commands.
example_prompt: Parse this Procfile and list each process type and its command.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; simple `name: command` line parsing, fully client-side.
rationale: Procfiles drive Heroku/Foreman-style deploys; a quick structured check catches typos before a deploy.

name: tap-output-parser
description: Parses Test Anything Protocol (TAP) output into structured pass/fail/skip/todo results with diagnostics and a summary.
example_prompt: Parse this TAP test output and give me a pass/fail summary.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; line-based TAP grammar parsing, runs entirely client-side.
rationale: TAP is emitted by many test runners; a structured summary is far more readable than raw streams.

name: dig-output-parser
description: Parses dig DNS query output into structured sections (question, answer, authority records, flags, query time).
example_prompt: Parse this dig output and just show me the answer records.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; section-and-record text parsing of dig's standard format, no network.
rationale: Extracting just the answer records and flags from verbose dig output speeds up DNS debugging.

name: video-dolby-vision-rpu-extractor
description: Detects and extracts Dolby Vision configuration and RPU metadata, reporting the profile and BL/EL/RPU layout.
example_prompt: Does this file have Dolby Vision metadata, and what profile?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the dvcC/dvvC box and RPU NAL side-data; pure parsing, no decode, local
rationale: Dolby Vision profile/RPU presence determines compatibility, and it is distinct from and invisible alongside HDR10.

name: ogg-page-dump
description: Parses an Ogg bitstream into a page-by-page report of serial number, granule position, segment count, and BOS/EOS/continuation flags.
example_prompt: Dump the Ogg page structure of this file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — scans for OggS page captures and reads the fixed 27-byte page header plus segment table.
rationale: Page-level structure reveals multiplexed streams, broken granule positions, and truncated files invisible to codec tools.

name: css-media-query-parser
description: Parses a CSS media query string into structured feature conditions (type, min/max-width, orientation, prefers-*) with logical operators.
example_prompt: Break down this media query: (min-width: 768px) and (orientation: landscape)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM grammar parse of the query string; no network.
rationale: Media-query syntax nests conditions in ways that are easy to misread, and a structured breakdown removes ambiguity.

name: mixed-script-detector
description: Flags individual words or tokens that mix Unicode scripts (e.g. Latin + Cyrillic within one word).
example_prompt: Does any word here mix alphabets?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: classifies each char's Unicode script block per token, offline
rationale: Single-token script mixing is a strong spoofing signal distinct from look-alikes and worth surfacing on its own.

name: server-timing-parser
description: Parses a Server-Timing header into named metrics with their durations and descriptions and renders a ranked breakdown of backend phases.
example_prompt: Parse Server-Timing: db;dur=53, app;dur=47.2;desc="Render", cache;desc="Hit" and show me where the time went.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — structured metric parsing and sorting, no network
rationale: Server-Timing is the standard way to surface backend latency to devtools but pasted values are unreadable raw.

name: tunnel-effect-video
description: Generates a classic demoscene-style infinite tunnel flythrough with a textured or colored pattern.
example_prompt: Make a psychedelic infinite tunnel video, 15 seconds, looping, 1080p
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute runs the polar tunnel-mapping shader per frame on the GPU, then ffmpeg encodes it locally.
rationale: A beloved retro effect that's hard to author by hand but ideal as a parametric shader generator.

name: gif-loop-count-checker
description: Reads the Netscape application extension of an animated GIF and reports whether it loops infinitely, once, or a fixed number of times.
example_prompt: Does this banner.gif loop forever or just play once?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the GIF block structure and the NETSCAPE2.0 extension entirely in-memory, no decoding or network needed.
rationale: A GIF that silently plays only once is a common, hard-to-spot bug when exporting from editors that drop the loop flag.

name: ttml-subtitle-validator
description: Validates a TTML/DFXP subtitle document for well-formed XML, required namespaces, and time-ordered, in-bounds cues.
example_prompt: Check this TTML subtitle file for structural errors.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM parses the XML and validates timing/structure fully in the browser.
rationale: TTML/DFXP is the streaming-industry caption standard (Netflix/IMSC) with no validator in the catalog yet.

name: subresource-integrity-checker
description: Scans script and link tags in HTML for the integrity attribute, validates hash format and crossorigin pairing, and flags external resources lacking SRI.
example_prompt: Check SRI coverage on the script and stylesheet tags in this HTML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML tag scan and base64/hash-format validation; no fetching required.
rationale: CDN supply-chain attacks make SRI important, and missing/malformed integrity attributes are easy to overlook.

name: broken-fragment-link-checker
description: Checks every in-page #fragment link in an HTML document against the set of element ids/name anchors and reports dangling anchors.
example_prompt: Do all the #anchor links in this HTML point to real ids?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: collect ids, resolve hrefs starting with #; no network.
rationale: Broken table-of-contents anchors are common after refactors and not caught by URL link checkers.

name: security-txt-validate
description: Validates a /.well-known/security.txt file against RFC 9116 — required Contact and Expires fields, field syntax, and expiry freshness.
example_prompt: Validate my security.txt against RFC 9116
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line parser with the RFC's field rules; expiry checked against a user-supplied date, fully local.
rationale: security.txt has exact required fields and an expiry that lapses silently; a validator keeps it compliant.

name: amf-codec
description: Decodes and encodes Action Message Format (AMF0/AMF3) binary payloads to and from readable JSON.
example_prompt: decode this AMF0 payload (hex): 020005 68656c6c6f
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — AMF is a self-contained binary serialization format parsed from bytes in-memory, no runtime needed.
rationale: AMF round-tripping is nearly impossible to find in-browser yet still appears in legacy Flash/RTMP and game traffic analysis.

name: bench-compare
description: Compares two benchmark result sets and reports percent change plus whether the difference is statistically significant.
example_prompt: Did performance regress? baseline: 12,13,11,14 vs new: 18,17,19,16
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs the t-test and summary statistics in-browser via a sandboxed Python environment, no server.
rationale: Tells you whether a benchmark change is real signal or noise, the core value of Bencher, fully offline.

name: wbmp-to-png
description: Decodes a legacy Wireless Bitmap (.wbmp) into a modern PNG.
example_prompt: What's in this .wbmp file? Convert it to png
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a small WBMP parser decodes the 1-bit format and encodes PNG locally.
rationale: WBMP files surface in old mobile and embedded archives and have essentially no surviving viewers.

name: video-to-dv
description: Encodes video to DV/DVCPRO for legacy tape and camcorder editing workflows.
example_prompt: convert this to DV for an old editor
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm's dvvideo encoder writes DV in an AVI/MOV container client-side.
rationale: DV-based NLEs and capture devices still require DV-format input.

name: pls-to-m3u
description: Converts a PLS playlist back into an extended M3U with #EXTINF title/duration lines.
example_prompt: turn this pls into an extended m3u
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure text key/value parse and M3U serialization, fully client-side.
rationale: M3U is the near-universal playlist format and PLS files frequently need migrating into it.

name: asx-to-m3u
description: Extracts stream/file references from an ASX (Advanced Stream Redirector) file into an M3U playlist.
example_prompt: pull the urls from this asx into an m3u
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the ASX XML <ref href> entries and emits M3U, no network.
rationale: Legacy ASX redirector files hide stream URLs that users want as a plain modern playlist.

name: lrc-to-plain-lyrics
description: Strips all [mm:ss.xx] timestamps and metadata tags from an LRC file to produce clean plain-text lyrics.
example_prompt: remove the timestamps from this lrc and give me plain lyrics
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — line filtering and tag stripping, pure computation.
rationale: People often want the readable lyric text out of a synced LRC without any timing markup.

name: midi-format1-to-format0
description: Merges a multi-track MIDI Format 1 file into a single-track Format 0 file with a unified event stream.
example_prompt: flatten this multitrack midi into a type 0 file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (midly) — merges and re-sorts events by absolute time, then rewrites the header locally.
rationale: Some hardware sequencers and embedded players only accept Format 0 single-track MIDI.

name: ini-to-toml
description: Converts an INI/config file into equivalent TOML, mapping sections to tables and inferring value types.
example_prompt: Convert this INI config to TOML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: INI parse + TOML serialize are pure string/value transforms with no I/O, so it runs entirely in the wasmi sandbox.
rationale: Devs migrating tools from INI to TOML (Rust/Python ecosystems) need a quick faithful section→table mapping.

name: toml-to-ini
description: Flattens a TOML document back into INI sections, emitting dotted keys for nested tables.
example_prompt: Turn this TOML into an old-style INI file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: deterministic parse-and-emit over text, no network or filesystem.
rationale: Useful when feeding modern TOML config into legacy tools that only read INI.

name: android-strings-to-ios-strings
description: Converts an Android strings.xml resource into an iOS Localizable.strings file, mapping placeholders.
example_prompt: Convert this Android strings.xml to iOS .strings
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: XML parse plus key=value emission with format-specifier mapping, all in-memory.
rationale: Cross-platform apps must keep Android and iOS localization files in sync, format placeholders and all.

name: toml-diff
description: Reports key and table-level differences between two TOML config files, normalizing ordering and comments.
example_prompt: Show what changed between these two Cargo.toml files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse with the toml crate into a value map and diff keys
rationale: Developers frequently compare TOML manifests and want semantic, not textual, change reports.

name: image-bit-depth-compare
description: Compares the effective color precision/bit-depth of two images and flags posterization or banding introduced by one.
example_prompt: Did the second image lose color depth compared to the first?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM analyzes unique-value counts and gradients per channel locally
rationale: Detects silent precision loss from 8-bit conversions or aggressive palettes.

name: icon-set-diff
description: Compares two folders of named icons and reports which icons were added, removed, or visually changed.
example_prompt: What changed between these two versions of my icon set?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM matches by filename then pixel-diffs each pair in-browser
rationale: Design-system maintainers need a per-icon changelog across releases.

name: logo-similarity-check
description: Compares two logos and returns a similarity score plus the regions that drive the difference, useful for trademark or version checks.
example_prompt: How similar are these two logos?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM normalizes scale/color then computes structural similarity in-browser
rationale: Brand teams want a quick objective similarity read between logo variants or competitors.

name: image-scale-detector
description: Detects whether one image is a resampled (up/down-scaled) version of another and estimates the scale factor and resampling quality.
example_prompt: Was this image upscaled from the smaller one, and by how much?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM compares frequency content and downscale-match error in-browser
rationale: Reveals hidden upscaling that fakes resolution between asset versions.

name: midi-diff
description: Diffs two MIDI files and lists added/removed/changed notes, tempo, time signature, and track-name differences.
example_prompt: Show me what changed between arrangement_v1.mid and arrangement_v2.mid
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse both SMF byte streams and structurally diff events — no decoding or server needed
rationale: Composers iterate on MIDI constantly but have no git-style diff for note-level changes.

name: id3-tag-diff
description: Compares ID3v2 tags of two MP3 files field-by-field (title, artist, album, art, comments) and highlights the differences.
example_prompt: What metadata differs between these two MP3 copies?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse ID3 frames from both files and diff fields, fully local
rationale: Library de-duplication and tag-merge decisions need a quick side-by-side of two near-identical files.

name: wav-header-diff
description: Compares the fmt chunks of two WAV files (sample rate, bit depth, channels, codec, byte rate) and flags any mismatch.
example_prompt: Do these two WAVs have the same format?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: read RIFF headers only, no decode, instant and local
