rationale: Format mismatches silently break concatenation/batch pipelines; a one-shot header compare catches them.

name: midi-velocity-diff
description: Compares note velocities between two MIDI performances and reports per-note and overall dynamics differences.
example_prompt: How do the dynamics differ between these two MIDI takes?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse both SMF files, match notes, diff velocities, local
rationale: Velocity/dynamics comparison helps choose or humanize between performance variants.

name: midi-timing-groove-diff
description: Measures each MIDI file's deviation from the grid and diffs the groove/quantization between two performances.
example_prompt: Compare the groove feel of these two MIDI drum loops
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse tempo map, compute per-note grid offsets, diff groove templates, local
rationale: Groove comparison is how producers decide which take feels better, with no existing browser tool.

name: wav-chunk-diff
description: Diffs all RIFF chunks (bext, cue, LIST, iXML, smpl) between two WAV files to reveal differing broadcast metadata and markers.
example_prompt: What chunk-level metadata differs between these two broadcast WAVs?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: enumerate and compare every RIFF chunk in both files, local
rationale: Broadcast/production WAVs carry rich chunk metadata that needs a structural diff, not just header fields.

name: i18n-locale-diff
description: Compares two translation files (JSON locale or PO) and reports missing keys, extra keys, and changed strings.
example_prompt: Diff my en.json and fr.json locales and tell me which keys are untranslated
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; parses both locale formats and set-diffs the key/value maps locally
rationale: Keeping translation files in sync is a constant chore in localized apps with no quick local tool.

name: css-rule-diff
description: Diffs two stylesheets selector-by-selector, reporting added rules, removed rules, and changed declarations.
example_prompt: Compare these two CSS files and tell me which rules and properties changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSS parser; selector/declaration map comparison is local
rationale: Tracking what a stylesheet refactor actually altered is hard with line diff but easy rule-by-rule.

name: plist-diff
description: Compares two Apple property-list files (XML or binary plist) key-by-key and reports value and type changes.
example_prompt: Compare these two Info.plist files and show me what's different
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: decode XML and binary plist formats and diff the resulting key trees locally
rationale: macOS/iOS devs need plist diffs and binary plists can't be diffed as text at all.

name: helm-values-diff
description: Diffs two Helm values.yaml files by key path, showing exactly which overrides were added, removed, or changed.
example_prompt: Compare these two Helm values files and list the key changes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse both YAML files into key trees and diff by dotted path, offline
rationale: Helm release debugging hinges on knowing which values changed and there is no values-aware diff yet.

name: wasm-module-diff
description: Diffs two WebAssembly modules by imports, exports, function signatures, and section sizes.
example_prompt: Compare these two wasm modules and show me which exports and imports changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse both module binaries' sections and diff the symbol tables in-browser
rationale: Verifying a rebuilt wasm module's ABI didn't drift is a real need and nothing in the catalog covers it.

name: package-json-script-diff
description: Diffs the npm scripts blocks of two package.json files, reporting added, removed, and changed script commands.
example_prompt: Compare the scripts in these two package.json files
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse both files and diff the scripts objects locally, no network
rationale: Dependency diffs exist but script changes (build/test commands) are equally impactful and uncovered.

name: dot-graph-diff
description: Diffs two Graphviz DOT graphs by nodes and edges, reporting additions, removals, and attribute changes.
example_prompt: Compare these two DOT graphs and tell me which nodes and edges changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse both DOT files into node/edge sets and diff them in-browser
rationale: Generated dependency or state graphs change subtly; a graph-aware diff beats comparing DOT text.

name: angle-difference-calculator
description: Computes the smallest signed and unsigned difference between two angles or compass bearings with correct wraparound.
example_prompt: What's the difference between bearing 350° and 20°?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: modular angle arithmetic, runs locally.
rationale: Angle wraparound trips people up constantly; a dedicated tool removes the off-by-360 errors.

name: unicode-normalization-diff
description: Reveals differences between two strings that are masked by Unicode normalization or homoglyph substitution.
example_prompt: These two strings look the same but aren't equal—show me why
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: NFC/NFD normalization + codepoint comparison, local.
rationale: Homoglyph and normalization mismatches cause baffling 'identical but unequal' bugs and security issues.

name: dds-texture-encoder
description: Encodes an image into a GPU-compressed DDS texture (BC1/BC3) with mipmaps.
example_prompt: Export this as a bc3 dds with mipmaps
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute (or pure Rust block compression) generates BCn data client-side
rationale: Game engines consume DDS/BCn textures and there's no convenient browser-local encoder.

name: audio-hex-dumper
description: Produces an annotated hex dump of an audio file with chunk/frame boundaries labeled.
example_prompt: Show me a hex dump of this WAV with the chunks labeled
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: formats bytes as offset/hex/ASCII columns and tags known headers, client-side.
rationale: Inspecting raw bytes is the fastest way to diagnose a malformed or unexpected audio container.

name: kcs-tape-encoder
description: Encodes arbitrary bytes into Kansas City Standard FSK audio for cassette-style storage.
example_prompt: Encode this file as Kansas City Standard tape audio
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: generates the 1200/2400 Hz FSK bit tones per byte frame as PCM, client-side.
rationale: Retro-computing enthusiasts archive and transfer programs via the KCS cassette audio format.

name: pcm-audio-hash
description: Computes an MD5/SHA-256 hash of the decoded PCM samples, ignoring container and metadata differences.
example_prompt: Hash the actual audio of this file, ignoring tags
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: decodes to PCM and hashes the sample bytes locally, no upload.
rationale: A format-agnostic audio hash verifies that two differently-tagged files contain identical sound.

name: yenc-decode
description: Decodes yEnc-encoded Usenet binaries, handling the =y headers, escape bytes, and CRC32 trailer check.
example_prompt: decode this yenc post back to bytes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; single-byte offset/escape decode plus a CRC32 verify, no I/O.
rationale: yEnc is the dominant binary Usenet format and has essentially no browser-side decoder.

name: http-date-formatter
description: Parses and formats HTTP-date values (RFC 7231 IMF-fixdate) and converts to/from ISO 8601 and epoch.
example_prompt: convert 'Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT' to ISO 8601
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; calendar/date math is self-contained (current time supplied by host).
rationale: Date, Last-Modified, and Expires headers use a fixed GMT format that's awkward to read or produce by hand.

name: geo-uri-parser
description: Parses and builds RFC 5870 geo: URIs into latitude, longitude, altitude, and uncertainty.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; coordinate parsing/formatting is pure arithmetic.
rationale: geo: URIs in QR codes and contacts need decoding, and there's no tool for them.

name: signed-number-formatter
description: Forces an explicit +/− sign on numbers with optional fixed-width padding for tables.
example_prompt: format 5, -3, 0 with explicit signs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sign prefixing and padding, no I/O, local.
rationale: Deltas and diffs read clearer with forced signs; a small but genuinely missing utility.

name: vlq-encoder
description: Encodes and decodes MIDI-style variable-length quantities (big-endian 7-bit groups).
example_prompt: encode 0x3FFF as a MIDI VLQ
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — 7-bit big-endian grouping, fully local.
rationale: Needed when hand-authoring or debugging MIDI and source-map VLQ data.

name: hex-float-formatter
description: Formats a float as a C99 hexadecimal float literal (e.g. 0x1.91eb86p+1) and parses such literals back.
example_prompt: give the C hex float for 3.14
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — mantissa/exponent extraction and hex formatting, local.
rationale: Exact, round-trip-safe float notation that C/Rust programmers need and can't write by hand.

name: binary-grouping-formatter
description: Reformats long binary or hex strings into readable nibble/byte groups with chosen separators.
example_prompt: group 11010010111 into 4-bit nibbles
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — string chunking from the right, deterministic and local.
rationale: Improves readability of bitmasks and register dumps with zero risk of miscounting.

name: uudecode
description: Decode classic uuencoded blocks back into the original binary bytes.
example_prompt: uudecode this block back to a file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM uudecode over text input; offline.
rationale: Old email attachments and Usenet posts still use uuencoding that modern tools rarely handle.

name: riff-info-tag-reader
description: Extracts the LIST/INFO chunk metadata (IART, INAM, ICMT, ICRD, ISFT, etc.) embedded in WAV/AVI RIFF files.
example_prompt: Pull the artist and title from the INFO chunk of this wav
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — walks RIFF chunk headers to the INFO list and reads its sub-fields, no audio decode needed
rationale: RIFF INFO is where many DAWs and recorders stash WAV metadata, and it's distinct from BWF/bext fields no existing tool surfaces.

name: wma-metadata-reader
description: Parses the ASF Content Description and Extended Content Description objects of a WMA/ASF file to list title, author, and custom attributes.
example_prompt: What metadata is stored in this .wma file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — ASF is a GUID-prefixed object list parsed by walking object headers in the buffer
rationale: WMA tagging uses ASF objects that no ID3/Vorbis tool can read, leaving legacy Windows libraries opaque.

name: amr-frame-parser
description: Parses an AMR-NB/AMR-WB voice file's frame headers to report the codec mode per frame, bitrate distribution and total duration.
example_prompt: Analyze the frame modes in this .amr voicemail
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — AMR frames are self-describing with a mode byte each, walked sequentially after the magic header
rationale: AMR voicemail/recordings carry per-frame mode data that reveals quality and lets users estimate length without decoding.

name: aac-adts-header-parser
description: Walks the ADTS frame headers of a raw .aac stream to report profile (AAC-LC/HE), sample rate index, channel config and frame count.
example_prompt: Parse the ADTS headers in this raw aac file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — each ADTS frame begins with a fixed syncword+bitfield header scanned directly from bytes
rationale: Raw ADTS streams have no container metadata, so frame-header parsing is the only way to learn their format.

name: dj-cue-point-extractor
description: Decodes Serato/Rekordbox/Traktor cue points and hot cues stored in ID3 GEOB/private frames into a readable position+color+name list.
example_prompt: Extract the Serato cue points from this track
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the base64/binary payloads of the DJ-software GEOB frames directly from the tag bytes
rationale: DJs lose hours of cue work when migrating software, and these proprietary markers are otherwise unreadable.

name: wav-smpl-loop-extractor
description: Parses the WAV 'smpl' chunk to report MIDI root note, fine tuning and all sustain/release loop start-end points for samplers.
example_prompt: What loop points and root note are in this sampler wav?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the smpl chunk is a fixed struct with a loop array, read directly from the buffer
rationale: Sampler instrument metadata (root key, loops) is critical for instrument builders and invisible in normal players.

name: pls-playlist-parser
description: Parses a PLS playlist (INI-style File/Title/Length entries) into an ordered list of tracks with titles and durations.
example_prompt: Read the entries out of this .pls file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — PLS is an INI-format text file parsed entirely from the provided content
rationale: PLS is the radio/stream playlist standard whose numbered-key format trips up naive parsers, so a dedicated reader helps.

name: xspf-playlist-parser
description: Parses an XSPF (XML Shareable Playlist Format) file into a structured track list with title, creator, album, duration and location.
example_prompt: Extract the tracks from this xspf playlist
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — XSPF is XML parsed in-memory with a Rust XML reader, no network
rationale: XSPF carries richer per-track metadata than M3U, and converting it to a table is the first step of any library import.

name: bell202-caller-id-decoder
description: Decodes the Bell 202 FSK Caller ID burst found between phone rings into the calling number, name and timestamp.
example_prompt: Extract the caller ID data from this phone line recording
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — 1200/2200 Hz FSK demod plus the SDMF/MDMF message parser run on PCM samples in-browser
rationale: Telephony hobbyists and PBX debuggers capture CID tones and have no simple offline way to read the embedded data.

name: midi-lyrics-extractor
description: Extracts lyric/text meta events from a karaoke MIDI (.kar/.mid) and outputs the timed lyrics, optionally as an LRC-style list.
example_prompt: Pull the karaoke lyrics out of this .kar file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — collects FF 05 lyric (and FF 01 text) meta events with their tick times and formats them in-memory
rationale: Karaoke MIDIs embed timed lyrics no normal player surfaces, and extracting them enables lyric sheets or LRC conversion.

name: meta-refresh-extractor
description: Extracts <meta http-equiv="refresh"> directives from HTML, returning the delay and target URL.
example_prompt: Does this HTML have a meta-refresh redirect, and where to?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tag scan of the pasted markup.
rationale: Detects client-side redirects hidden in saved pages.

name: timecode-parser
description: Parses SMPTE timecode "HH:MM:SS:FF" or "HH:MM:SS.mmm" into total seconds and frame counts given a frame rate.
example_prompt: Convert timecode 00:01:23:12 at 24fps to seconds and frames
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — arithmetic over parsed fields, no media decoding required.
rationale: Video/audio editors need fast frame-accurate timecode math that web tools rarely get right (drop-frame aware).

name: unicode-fraction-parser
description: Parses Unicode vulgar fractions and mixed forms ("½", "3¾", "⅝") into decimals or improper fractions.
example_prompt: Convert ½, 3¾ and ⅝ into decimals
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Unicode codepoint mapping table, no rendering needed.
rationale: Recipe and measurement text full of glyph fractions is unparseable to most numeric tools.

name: ratio-parser
description: Parses ratio strings like "16:9", "3:2:1" into decimals, percentages, and the reduced integer ratio.
example_prompt: Reduce and decimalize the ratio 1920:1080
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — GCD reduction and division, runs client-side.
rationale: Aspect ratios and mix proportions need quick reduction/decimal conversion all the time.

name: polynomial-coefficient-extractor
description: Parses a polynomial written as "3x^2 + 2x - 1" (any variable, unsorted terms) into a dense coefficient vector and degree.
example_prompt: Extract the coefficient array from 3x^2 + 2x - 1
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — term tokenizing and exponent bucketing, fully client-side.
rationale: Coefficient vectors are the input format every numeric polynomial routine actually needs.

name: superscript-subscript-normalizer
description: Converts Unicode super/subscript digits (x², H₂O, 10⁻³) into ASCII caret/underscore notation and back.
example_prompt: Normalize 'x² + H₂O' into plain ASCII math
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Unicode codepoint mapping, no rendering needed.
rationale: Copied formulas with glyph super/subscripts break in code and search until normalized.

name: classic-cipher
description: Apply or break classic ciphers (ROT13, Caesar, Atbash, Vigenère) on a string.
example_prompt: decode this Caesar cipher shifted by 3: 'Khoor Zruog'
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: pure character arithmetic, runs instantly in-browser.
rationale: Common puzzle/CTF/learning tool found in every developer toolbox.

name: signature-generate
description: Turn a typed name into a realistic cursive signature PNG with a transparent background.
example_prompt: Make a cursive signature image for 'Jordan Lee'
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM renders text in a bundled handwriting font to a transparent raster, offline.
rationale: E-signing a typed name is a common need distinct from full-page handwriting or photo extraction.

name: cors-test
description: Fetch a URL and report its CORS headers and whether a given origin/method would be allowed.
example_prompt: Does api.example.com allow CORS requests from my site?
loader_feasibility: Client-side fetch inspecting Access-Control-* response headers.
rationale: Targeted CORS debugging beyond the generic http-headers/security-headers tools.

name: number-base-convert
description: Converts a number between binary, octal, decimal, hexadecimal, and any arbitrary radix from 2 to 36.
example_prompt: convert 255 to binary and hex
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — integer parsing and radix output are pure arithmetic, no external runtime.
rationale: A programmer's base calculator covers the To/From Decimal, Binary, and Octal demand in a single high-utility tool.

name: unicode-block-report
description: Reports which Unicode scripts and blocks appear in the text and the proportion of each.
example_prompt: What scripts and Unicode blocks are used in this document?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; maps each codepoint to its block locally.
rationale: Quickly reveals unexpected CJK, emoji, or symbol contamination in supposedly plain text.

name: mixed-line-ending-detector
description: Reports the mix of CRLF, LF, and CR line endings and lists lines that differ from the dominant style.
example_prompt: Does this file have mixed line endings?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; counts line-ending bytes in a single pass.
rationale: Mixed EOLs cause whole-file diffs and cross-platform script failures.

name: hapax-legomena-finder
description: Lists words that appear exactly once in the text (hapax legomena).
example_prompt: Which words occur only once in this manuscript?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; build a frequency map and filter to count one.
rationale: Once-only words highlight rare terms, possible typos, and stylistic fingerprints.

name: gif-frame-timing-inspector
description: Lists every frame of an animated GIF with its delay, disposal method, and transparency flags.
example_prompt: Show me the per-frame delays and disposal methods of this GIF
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the GIF graphic-control extensions and image descriptors from the bytes locally.
rationale: Per-frame timing and disposal details explain janky playback and are needed to fix or re-time a GIF.

name: font-face-extractor
description: Extracts @font-face declarations from CSS and lists family names, weights, styles, formats, and source URLs.
example_prompt: List every web font this CSS loads and in what formats
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM at-rule parsing; local on the pasted CSS.
rationale: Web fonts are a top performance cost and an inventory shows redundant weights and missing formats.

name: redirect-chain-analyzer
description: Takes a pasted sequence of redirect responses (status + Location) and analyzes the hop chain for loops, protocol downgrades, and excessive hops.
example_prompt: Analyze this redirect chain: 301 -> http://..., 302 -> https://..., 200
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM URL resolution and chain analysis over pasted hops; no live fetching needed.
rationale: Long or insecure redirect chains hurt SEO and security and visualizing the hops makes the problem obvious.

name: starfield-generator
description: Generates a procedural starfield/night-sky background with adjustable density, star sizes, and color temperature.
example_prompt: make a 1920x1080 starfield wallpaper with a few bright stars
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scatters and renders stars from a seeded RNG straight to a canvas, no assets fetched
rationale: Star backgrounds are constantly needed for games and slides and are trivial to do well offline.

name: bassline-midi-generator
description: Generates a MIDI bassline that follows a chord progression in a chosen style (walking, root-fifth, syncopated).
example_prompt: Write a walking bass MIDI line over Dm7 G7 Cmaj7
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM derives notes from the chord tones and rhythmic template and writes a Standard MIDI File entirely client-side.
rationale: Songwriters have chords but want an idiomatic bassline scaffold to edit rather than start blank.

name: melody-midi-generator
description: Generates a singable MIDI melody constrained to a key, scale, and contour shape as a starting sketch.
example_prompt: Generate an 8-bar uplifting melody in G major as MIDI
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM samples scale-degree motion under contour rules and writes a Standard MIDI File locally.
rationale: Beating writer's block with an editable melodic seed is a high-value, repeatable need.

name: http-link-header-generator
description: Generates an HTTP Link response header for preload/prefetch/preconnect and other rel relationships with as/type params.
example_prompt: Build a Link header preloading /app.css as style and preconnecting to fonts.gizza.ai
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — comma-joins parameterized link-values per RFC 8288, offline.
rationale: Early-hints/preload via the Link header is high-impact for performance but its grammar is obscure.

name: resource-hints-generator
description: Generates <link rel=preload|prefetch|preconnect|dns-prefetch> tags from a list of resources with correct as/type/crossorigin.
example_prompt: Make resource hint tags: preconnect to cdn.gizza.ai, preload hero.jpg, prefetch /next-page
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — infers the `as` attribute from extensions and templates the tags, client-side.
rationale: Resource hints meaningfully speed pages but the per-type attribute rules are easy to get subtly wrong.

name: image-interlace-checker
description: Detects whether a PNG (Adam7) or GIF is interlaced/progressive and reports the interlace method.
example_prompt: Is this PNG interlaced?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the interlace flag from the header in the browser.
rationale: Interlacing changes file size and load behavior and isn't visible in a normal viewer.

name: icon-transparent-padding-linter
description: Checks an app/launcher icon for the consistent transparent safe-area padding platforms require and reports the actual margins.
example_prompt: Does this app icon have the right transparent padding?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes the alpha channel and measures the opaque content bounding box client-side.
rationale: Icons with wrong padding get clipped or float oddly in launchers and a margin lint enforces the spec.

name: ass-subtitle-validator
description: Checks an Advanced SubStation Alpha (.ass/.ssa) file for undefined styles, malformed dialogue lines, and bad timing fields.
example_prompt: Validate this .ass subtitle file's styles and events
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: ASS is a structured text format parsed entirely client-side.
rationale: ASS files reference named styles that, when missing, render with wrong fonts; a validator catches it before muxing.

name: subtitle-overlap-checker
description: Scans SRT/VTT cues for time ranges that overlap each other and reports every colliding pair.
example_prompt: Do any captions in this file overlap in time?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses cue timecodes as text and compares intervals locally.
rationale: Overlapping cues cause flickering double-subtitles, a common artifact after machine translation or merging.

name: subtitle-line-length-linter
description: Reports cues that exceed a maximum characters-per-line or allowed number of lines (e.g. 42 chars, 2 lines).
example_prompt: Check if any subtitle lines are too long for the screen
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: line-length rules are simple text measurements done in the browser.
rationale: Over-long lines wrap awkwardly or get cut off, and broadcasters enforce strict line limits.

name: subtitle-gap-checker
description: Detects cue-to-cue gaps shorter than a minimum frame count, which professional standards require between consecutive subtitles.
example_prompt: Make sure my subtitles have enough gap between them
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: gap computation from timecodes is pure arithmetic on parsed text.
rationale: Sub-frame gaps make subtitles appear to merge; the minimum-gap rule is part of every delivery spec.

name: subtitle-duration-checker
description: Flags cues displayed for less than a minimum or more than a maximum duration so nothing flashes or lingers.
example_prompt: List captions that are on screen too briefly or too long
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: duration thresholds checked from parsed timecodes locally.
rationale: Cues under ~1s are unreadable and cues over ~7s feel stale; both are spec violations.

name: dash-mpd-validator
description: Validates a DASH MPD manifest's structure — periods, adaptation sets, representations, and segment templates — and flags missing or inconsistent fields.
example_prompt: Validate my DASH .mpd manifest
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the MPD is XML, parsed and checked entirely client-side.
rationale: A malformed MPD breaks adaptive playback in ways that are hard to debug from the player side.

name: sfv-verify
description: Verifies a set of files against the CRC32 entries in an .sfv manifest.
example_prompt: Verify these files against my checksums.sfv
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CRC32 over local files plus .sfv parse; client-side
rationale: Batch integrity verification of archives/downloads with a standard manifest format.

name: html-deprecated-tags
description: Flags deprecated/obsolete HTML tags and attributes (center, font, align, etc.) with modern replacements.
example_prompt: Find deprecated HTML in this page and suggest replacements
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM HTML parse with a deprecation rule set; fully local
rationale: Legacy HTML lingers in old templates and flagging it helps modernization and standards compliance.

name: po-file-lint
description: Lints gettext .po translation files for untranslated/fuzzy entries, mismatched printf placeholders, and duplicate msgids.
example_prompt: Lint this .po file for placeholder mismatches and fuzzy strings
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM gettext parser; runs on pasted catalog locally
rationale: Placeholder mismatches in translations crash apps at runtime and are easy to introduce during localization.

name: issn-validator
description: Validates an 8-digit ISSN serial number using its mod-11 check digit including the X case.
example_prompt: Validate ISSN 0378-5955
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: weighted mod-11 over seven digits, fully client-side.
rationale: Researchers and catalogers handle ISSNs separately from ISBNs and need a dedicated checksum check.

name: cusip-validator
description: Validates a 9-character CUSIP via its modulo-10 double-add-double check digit with letter and special-character weighting.
example_prompt: Validate CUSIP 037833100
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: per-character value mapping and modular sum, no network.
rationale: US/Canada securities workflows hinge on CUSIPs and a dedicated checker catches transcription errors locally.

name: sedol-validator
description: Validates a 7-character SEDOL security code using its weighted mod-10 check digit.
example_prompt: Is SEDOL B0WNLY7 valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: fixed weight vector and modular sum, entirely client-side.
rationale: UK/Irish market data handling needs SEDOL validation distinct from ISIN/CUSIP.

name: figi-validator
description: Validates a 12-character Bloomberg FIGI identifier via its mod-10 double-add-double check digit.
example_prompt: Validate FIGI BBG000BLNQ16
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: character-value expansion plus modular sum, no API.
rationale: FIGIs are increasingly used as open security IDs and lack a common offline validator.

name: orcid-validator
description: Validates a 16-digit ORCID researcher ID using the ISO 7064 mod-11-2 check digit including the X case.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: running mod-11-2 computation over digits, fully offline.
rationale: Academics and repositories verify ORCIDs and benefit from a quick standalone checker.

name: siren-validator
description: Validates French SIREN and SIRET company numbers using the Luhn algorithm with the SIRET edge cases.
example_prompt: Validate SIRET 73282932000074
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Luhn plus a special-case rule, fully local.
rationale: French B2B and accounting tools verify SIREN/SIRET routinely and want it offline.

name: frames-to-apng
description: Assembles a sequence of PNG frames into a single looping APNG animation.
example_prompt: stitch these numbered pngs into an apng at 12 fps
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the `png` crate's APNG encoder writes frames in-memory
rationale: APNG output (full color + alpha) is missing from GIF-only frame-combiners.

name: tracker-module-to-wav
description: Renders tracker module music (.mod/.xm/.it/.s3m) to a standard WAV file.
example_prompt: render this .xm tracker module to a wav
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader built with libopenmpt synthesizes the module to PCM WAV entirely in wasm.
rationale: Demoscene/chiptune .mod/.xm files are score+sample formats that need rendering before any normal player can use them.

name: gaussian-process-fit
description: Fits a Gaussian-process regression to (x,y) data and plots the mean curve with uncertainty bands.
example_prompt: Fit a curve with uncertainty to these noisy data points.
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs scikit-learn GaussianProcessRegressor in WASM, computing kernels and posteriors locally.
rationale: Maps the GPyTorch demand to its signature use case — uncertainty-aware regression — without any GPU/server.

name: bayesian-ab-test
description: Runs a Bayesian A/B test from conversion counts and reports the posterior probability that B beats A.
example_prompt: Variant A: 120/2000, Variant B: 145/2050 — is B actually better?
loader_feasibility: pyodide samples Beta posteriors with numpy in WASM; everything is computed client-side.
rationale: Maps the Pyro/PyVarInf probabilistic-inference demand to a concrete, widely-needed decision tool that runs locally.

name: causal-dag-analyzer
description: Parses a causal DAG specification and identifies confounders, colliders, backdoor paths, and a valid adjustment set.
example_prompt: Given X->Y, Z->X, Z->Y, what do I need to adjust for to estimate X on Y?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; graph traversal and d-separation logic over an adjacency list, fully local.
rationale: Identification via DAGs is the central skill in 'Causal Machine Learning' with no good in-browser tool.

name: stylometry-analyzer
description: Computes stylometric features (average word/sentence length, function-word frequencies, lexical diversity) for authorship analysis.
example_prompt: Analyze the writing style of this text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes the lexical statistics locally
rationale: Stylometry is a signature Digital-Humanities technique with no privacy-respecting browser tool today.

name: doi-metadata-fetch
description: Resolves a DOI to formatted citation metadata via DataCite/Crossref content negotiation.
example_prompt: Get the citation for DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.12345678
loader_feasibility: Browser fetch to the CORS-enabled DataCite/Crossref content-negotiation endpoints; no backend of our own.
rationale: Citing figshare/DataCite datasets requires pulling their public, CORS-friendly metadata.

name: dcat-catalog-parser
description: Parses a DCAT-US/DCAT-AP data catalog JSON and lists datasets, distributions, formats, and licenses.
example_prompt: List every dataset and download URL in this data.gov catalog JSON
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM JSON-LD/DCAT parsing of the uploaded catalog; fully local.
rationale: data.gov and the European data portal both publish giant DCAT catalogs that are unwieldy to browse raw.

name: congressional-trade-parser
description: Parses US congressional STOCK Act periodic transaction reports (pasted text/CSV) into structured trades with ticker, side, amount range, and dates.
example_prompt: Turn this PTR disclosure text into a clean table of trades
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM text/CSV parsing and normalization; no server.
rationale: The Congressional Stock Brain demand is for structuring messy disclosure filings into analyzable rows.

name: session-id-validate
description: Validates a Session account ID, confirming it is 66 hex chars and begins with the 05 X25519 prefix.
example_prompt: Check if this Session ID is well-formed: 05abc123...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — format/prefix/hex checks only, fully offline.
rationale: Session has no usernames, so the long hex ID is the only handle people share and mistype.

name: translation-glossary-checker
description: Verifies that a translated text uses required glossary terms consistently and flags mismatches.
example_prompt: Check that my Catalan translation uses these glossary terms consistently
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM matches source/target term pairs against the translation locally — no model or network.
rationale: Professional and OSS localizers (Apertium/Softcatalà) need term-consistency QA that hosted translators don't provide.

name: webextension-manifest-validator
description: Validates a browser-extension manifest.json (MV2 or MV3) against the WebExtension schema and flags missing or invalid keys.
example_prompt: Check my extension manifest.json for errors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: JSON parse plus a bundled schema check, no runtime required.
rationale: Manifest mistakes are the most common reason an extension silently fails to load, and store reviewers reject them late.

name: model-calibration-curve
description: Plots a probability calibration (reliability) diagram from predicted probabilities and reports the Brier score.
example_prompt: Show the calibration curve for these predicted probabilities.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM bins probabilities and renders an SVG reliability plot.
rationale: Calibration is a key but often-overlooked ML-observability concern.

name: scatterplot-matrix
description: Renders a pairwise scatter-matrix (pairplot) of numeric columns with histograms on the diagonal.
example_prompt: Show a pairplot of these features.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM lays out the grid and renders SVG in-browser.
rationale: The pairplot is a standard multivariate EDA visualization for spotting relationships.

name: process-variant-analysis
description: Extracts and ranks the distinct trace variants (activity sequences) in an event log by frequency.
example_prompt: What are the most common process variants in this log?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM groups traces by sequence in-browser.
rationale: Variant analysis is a core process-mining task for understanding real behavior.

name: art-online-clustering
description: Clusters tabular or streaming data online with Adaptive Resonance Theory, spawning new clusters when the vigilance threshold is exceeded.
example_prompt: Cluster this data with adaptive resonance theory
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — ART1/ART2 are lightweight incremental match-and-update loops.
rationale: ART handles 'unknown number of clusters' and incremental data, a niche but genuinely useful capability missing elsewhere.

name: indic-transliterator
description: Transliterates text between Latin schemes (IAST, ITRANS, Harvard-Kyoto) and Indic scripts like Devanagari.
example_prompt: Transliterate 'namaste' into Devanagari using IAST.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM scheme-mapping tables (Aksharamukha-style), fully rule-based and offline.
rationale: The Vedika/Sanskrit demand points to Indic transliteration, a real need with no good privacy-preserving browser tool.

name: arabic-root-stemmer
description: Light-stems Arabic words by stripping prefixes/suffixes to approximate the triliteral root for grouping and search.
example_prompt: Stem these Arabic words down to their roots.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — rule-based affix stripping (the jsastem/ISRI approach) with bundled affix lists, no network.
rationale: Root stemming massively improves Arabic recall in search and clustering and has no good browser-side equivalent.

name: thai-pos-tagger
description: Tags each Thai word with its part of speech.
example_prompt: Show the part-of-speech tags for this Thai sentence
loader_feasibility: transformers.js: Thai POS token-classification ONNX model runs client-side
rationale: POS tags are a building block for grammar checking, parsing, and language learning, and aren't available natively in-browser.

name: speech-quality-pesq
description: Computes a PESQ perceptual speech-quality score by comparing a clean reference to a degraded recording.
example_prompt: Score the call quality of this recording against the reference
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM implements the PESQ algorithm and runs the comparison locally.
rationale: PESQ is the standard objective measure for codec, VoIP, and speech-enhancement quality testing.

name: speech-intelligibility-stoi
description: Computes the STOI short-time objective intelligibility score between a reference and a processed or degraded signal.
example_prompt: Compute the STOI between these two recordings
loader_feasibility: Rust→WASM implements STOI and compares the two signals client-side.
rationale: STOI predicts how understandable enhanced or noisy speech is, a key metric for evaluating denoisers.

name: fm-synth
description: Generates FM-synthesis tones from carrier and modulator settings.
example_prompt: Make an FM bell tone
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes FM samples, ffmpeg encodes — fully client-side.
rationale: Classic synth timbres explorable in the browser (PYO/Jupylet demand).

name: glsl-validator
description: Parses a GLSL shader and reports syntax and type errors with line numbers.
example_prompt: Check this GLSL fragment shader for errors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using naga's validating GLSL frontend, which surfaces parse/type diagnostics without a GPU or server.
rationale: Editors like SHDR and ShaderFrog exist mainly to catch shader compile errors early, and a chat-native validator fills the same need offline.

name: ubjson-json
description: Converts JSON to and from UBJSON (Universal Binary JSON).
example_prompt: Encode this JSON as UBJSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a UBJSON codec serializes and parses locally.
rationale: UBJSON is a real but niche binary JSON format with no easy in-browser converter.

name: json-to-jsonx
description: Converts between JSON and JSONX, the XML representation of JSON used by IBM DataPower.
example_prompt: Convert this JSON to JSONX XML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with quick-xml + serde_json — pure structural mapping, no services.
rationale: Enterprise integration buses still require JSONX and there is almost no free, private converter for it.

name: cson-json
description: Converts CoffeeScript Object Notation (CSON) to JSON and back, preserving comments where possible.
example_prompt: Convert this CSON config file to JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSON tokenizer/emitter; pure text transform, no server.
rationale: Direct match for 'CSON' demand; CSON configs (Atom, Hexo) frequently need JSON interop.

name: archieml-to-json
description: Parses ArchieML markup into structured JSON, supporting nested objects, arrays, and freeform blocks.
example_prompt: Parse this ArchieML document into JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line-based ArchieML state machine; pure parsing, browser-local.
rationale: Serves 'ArchieML' demand directly — the NYT-style writer-friendly format that journalists hand-author and devs consume as JSON.

name: chat-response-time-analyzer
description: Computes first-response and average reply times, plus message counts, from a timestamped transcript.
example_prompt: Calculate response-time stats from this chat log
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM timestamp parsing and math — runs locally.
rationale: Response-time analytics is a paid dashboard metric in every live-chat product.

name: product-feed-builder
description: Converts a product list into a platform import feed (Ecwid CSV, Google Merchant, or generic catalog CSV/XML).
example_prompt: turn this product JSON into a Google Merchant product feed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — field mapping and CSV/XML emission from an in-memory list, no network.
rationale: Catalog import feeds have strict required columns and a generator saves hours of manual spreadsheet wrangling.

name: throughput-calculator
description: Computes ops/sec and bytes/sec with KB/MB/GB scaling from counts and elapsed time.
example_prompt: 1.2M requests in 8.5s — what's the throughput?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: arithmetic with unit scaling, local
rationale: Produces the headline number from g3bench and load tests in one step.

name: j1939-pgn-decoder
description: Splits a 29-bit J1939 extended CAN ID into priority, PGN, PDU format/specific, and source address with PGN name lookup.
example_prompt: What does J1939 CAN ID 0x18FEF100 mean?

name: gltf-inspector

name: railroad-diagram

name: repeated-substring-finder

name: telegram-message-link-parser

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM URL parsing of the Telegram link grammar — no API calls, pure string logic.

name: du-output-chart

name: molecule-ascii-viewer

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse atomic coordinates and project to a character grid; no external chem libs or network needed.

name: zettel-id-generator

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — string and host-provided-time formatting, no server
rationale: zk/meudeus users need consistent unique IDs and slugs to keep their note graph linkable.

name: wiki-infobox-extractor
description: Extracts structured key/value data from a Wikipedia infobox template into JSON or a table.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM template parser, no network
rationale: Scrape structured facts out of wiki markup for datasets and research.

name: pypi-metadata-viewer
description: Parses a pasted PyPI JSON response or a wheel METADATA file and shows dependencies, Python version requirements, license, and classifiers.
example_prompt: Summarize this package's requirements from its PyPI metadata [pastes JSON]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the metadata text the user supplies; no live PyPI query.
rationale: pypi-command-line's `info`/`show` output is just structured metadata that parses fine offline once you have it.

name: sensors-thermal-parser
description: Parses lm-sensors `sensors` output into a table of CPU/GPU temperatures, fan speeds, and voltages, flagging anything running hot.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — text parsing with threshold checks on pasted sensor readings, client-side only.

name: smartctl-health-parser
description: Parses `smartctl -a` output into a drive-health verdict covering reallocated sectors, wear level, temperature, and error logs.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — extracts SMART attributes from pasted text and applies health heuristics, client-side.
rationale: SMART attributes are cryptic and the 'should I replace this disk' verdict is exactly what users want from the raw dump.

name: kubectl-top-parser
description: Parses `kubectl top pods`/`nodes` output into a resource table and, if requests/limits are pasted, flags over- and under-provisioned workloads.
example_prompt: Parse this kubectl top pods output and show me which pods are near their limits
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — table parsing and comparison of pasted text, no cluster access.
rationale: Cluster operators read kubectl top constantly and the requests-vs-usage comparison is a high-value reduction of the raw output.

name: bandwidth-log-parser
description: Parses vnstat, iftop, or nload output into network usage totals, top talkers, and a transfer-rate chart.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses pasted network stats into totals and an SVG rate chart, no network access.
rationale: Network monitors expose the gotop/network-pane data, and summarizing usage and peaks from their text output is straightforward and handy.

name: go-mod-analyzer

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the go.mod syntax; fully client-side.
rationale: Interprets the gup demand as Go-module inspection, giving Go devs a quick dependency overview.

name: jsonrpc-inspector

rationale: Complements the MCP inspector demand by debugging the raw protocol frames developers actually paste in.

name: pester-results-viewer

example_prompt: Summarize this Pester test results XML
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: quick-xml parses the report and aggregates counts in-process
rationale: PesterExplorer demand maps to making CI test output legible without a PowerShell environment.

name: torah-hebrew-lookup

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the WLC text embedded as a compressed asset; lookups are local indexing with no server call.

name: parsha-calendar

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM implementing the Hebrew calendar arithmetic and a small bundled triennial/annual reading table — pure computation, no network.

name: minisign-verify

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (Ed25519 verification); deterministic local check, no network.
rationale: Verifying signed releases is a frequent security chore that needs nothing but the file and public key.

name: png-zip-polyglot

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM concatenating valid PNG and ZIP structures; pure byte assembly in-tab.

name: discogs-collection-analyzer

example_prompt: analyze my discogs collection csv and show me a breakdown by genre and decade
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — CSV parse and aggregation, no network and no account access.
rationale: discodos-style insight into a vinyl/record collection straight from the official Discogs export.

name: prometheus-rule-linter
description: Validates Prometheus alerting/recording rule YAML and basic PromQL syntax.
example_prompt: Check this Prometheus alert rules file for errors.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust parses YAML and PromQL expressions entirely in WASM.
rationale: Maps amtui (Alertmanager) — catching rule mistakes before deploy is a common ops need with no server dependency.

name: bash-bookmark-generator
description: Generates shell functions and aliases for quick directory jumping from a list of paths.
example_prompt: Turn these project paths into 'cd' bookmark functions for my shell.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust emits the shell snippet text fully client-side.
rationale: Maps Bashmark — generating tidy shell bookmarks is a pure text-generation task that saves repetitive config writing.

name: smbios-decoder

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — SMBIOS is a fixed byte-structure format, fully parseable from the pasted bytes with no system calls.
rationale: dmidecode demand reflects a real need to read DMI tables; doing it in-browser means sensitive hardware dumps never leave the machine.

name: edid-decoder

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — EDID is a 128/256-byte binary spec parsed purely from input bytes.
rationale: Hardware-decode demand (dmidecode/inxi) extends naturally to EDID, a common display-troubleshooting need with no good quick web tool.

name: df-parser

example_prompt: Format this df -h output as a readable table and flag anything over 90% full
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — tabular text parsing and gauge rendering, pure string work.
rationale: dysk's df-replacement appeal is readable mount usage; a quick formatter highlights at-risk volumes from any pasted df dump.

name: fstab-parser

rationale: bashmount targets filesystem mounting, and an fstab explainer/linter delivers the safe, educational kernel of that need entirely client-side.

name: hardware-info-summarizer

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — text/structured parsing of the tool output into a normalized summary, no hardware access needed.
rationale: lshw output is verbose and hard to skim, and a local summarizer turns it into the few facts people actually want.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the roff/man macros and emits Markdown/HTML, no external man system needed.
rationale: qman exists because raw man pages are hard to read, and turning roff into clean Markdown makes them usable anywhere.

name: terminal-color-scheme-converter

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pure text parse/serialize of color config formats, no OS or network needed so it runs fully client-side.
rationale: Terminal users constantly port the same palette across alacritty/kitty/ghostty/st and currently hand-edit it every time.

name: ngram-extractor

example_prompt: Find the most common 3-word phrases in this text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: sliding-window counting over tokens, fully local.
rationale: N-gram/pattern extraction (Colibri Core's core feature) underpins phrase-mining and corpus analysis and is rare as a browser tool.

name: cjk-scan

example_prompt: Tell me which lines in this file contain Chinese or Japanese characters
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM inspecting Unicode code-point ranges locally
rationale: Implements nocjk for the common encoding-cleanup and i18n-auditing need.

name: velocity-forecaster

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — averaging and division over supplied numbers.
rationale: Forecasting from velocity is a common planning question with no offline calculator in these tools.

name: keyboard-heatmap

example_prompt: make a heatmap of which keys this code uses the most
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM counts character frequencies and emits an SVG keyboard image as a string; no external rendering service needed
rationale: A shareable visual of typing/key usage that complements the layout analyzer and serves writers, programmers, and keyboard hobbyists.

name: image-to-sixel

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM builds a Sixel palette and emits the escape-sequence stream locally; pure encoding step.
rationale: Sixel is exactly how timg/viu/w3m display true images in a terminal, and no easy in-browser sixel encoder exists.

name: whois-parser
description: Parses a pasted raw WHOIS response into structured fields: registrar, creation/expiry dates, nameservers, and status.
example_prompt: Parse this WHOIS output into a clean summary
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM multi-registrar field parser over pasted text; the lookup is done elsewhere, parsing is fully local.
rationale: WHOIS output is inconsistent across registrars, so a normalizing parser makes domain-check data actually readable.

name: wasm-inspect

example_prompt: What functions does this .wasm module import and export?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing the module header/sections; no execution or network needed.
rationale: Quickly understanding an unknown WASM binary's interface and bloat is a real debugging need.

name: glicol-music-synth

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Glicol's engine already runs in-browser via WASM, so synthesis is fully client-side.
rationale: Glicol's graph-oriented audio DSL is browser-native and lets users sketch music from text in chat.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bech32 + tagged-field parsing, fully offline.
rationale: Inspecting a Lightning invoice before paying is a common need and currently relies on online decoders.

name: near-account-validate

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — rule-based string validation, offline.

name: near-amount-converter

name: ckb-address-codec

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bech32m + lock-script parsing, offline.
rationale: CKB addresses encode a lock script, and decoding it is essential for understanding ownership conditions.

name: cardano-address-inspect

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bech32/Base58 + header-byte parsing (the amaru ecosystem's address rules), offline.
rationale: Cardano addresses pack payment and staking credentials that users and devs frequently need to inspect safely.

name: cardano-ada-converter

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — fixed-point math, offline.
rationale: Lovelace/ADA conversion is a routine, error-prone task that benefits from exact tooling.

name: eth-beacon-slot-converter

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — arithmetic over genesis time and slot duration, offline.
rationale: Validators and stakers (Lighthouse users) constantly map slots/epochs to wall-clock time.

name: cairo-felt-converter

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — modular big-integer math over the Stark prime (cairo-vm field), offline.
rationale: felt252 short-string encoding is ubiquitous in Cairo/Starknet dev and tedious to compute by hand.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Keccak with Starknet's high-bit masking, offline.
rationale: Starknet calls are addressed by selector, so devs need to derive them to build or decode invocations.

name: ibc-denom-hash

name: swf-info

loader_feasibility: SWF header/tag decoding (Ruffle's own swf crate) compiles to plain Rust→WASM and reads the file locally.
rationale: Ruffle drives Flash-preservation interest; inspecting SWF metadata is a quick, useful triage tool for archivists.

name: petscii-converter

loader_feasibility: A static character-mapping table runs in plain Rust→WASM, fully offline.

loader_feasibility: BASIC token tables and the PRG layout are decoded in plain Rust→WASM with no external calls.

name: svd-register-explorer

loader_feasibility: SVD is XML; parsing and indexing run in plain Rust→WASM with no network access.
rationale: embassy and rtic users live in SVD/PAC register maps, and a searchable register explorer saves constant datasheet hunting.

name: path-tracer

rationale: Browser-local physically-based rendering (the tray_rust/rs_pbrt niche) lets users learn and experiment with ray tracing without any install.

name: papercraft-unfolder

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — mesh unwrapping and net layout are pure geometry that compute in-browser and emit an SVG/PDF sheet.
rationale: Turning a 3D model into a buildable paper model is a beloved maker workflow with no good free web tool.

name: opcua-message-decoder
description: Decodes OPC UA binary messages into their node IDs, data types, and structured field values.
example_prompt: Decode this OPC UA binary message and show the node IDs and values
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — OPC UA binary encoding is deterministic byte parsing (per the opcua crate) that runs fully client-side.
rationale: OPC UA is ubiquitous in industrial automation and has almost no accessible browser-based decoding tools.

name: device-tree-parser

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the FDT binary format is parsed purely in memory from uploaded bytes.
rationale: RISC-V/ARM kernels (DragonOS, tock) boot from device trees that devs need to read and verify.

name: cyclic-pattern-offset

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: De Bruijn sequence generation and substring search are pure compute.
rationale: 0xdea's exploitation tooling reflects active demand for this pwntools-style staple in CTFs and research.

name: cargo-lock-dupe-finder

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure TOML graph analysis; deterministic and offline.
rationale: Maps cargo-deny's 'bans/duplicates' check into a quick build-bloat diagnostic developers reach for constantly.

name: tcp-os-fingerprinter

rationale: Directly reflects huginn-net's passive fingerprinting in a form that runs offline on captured signatures.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with the regex crate applying patterns to the pasted log text locally.

name: episode-filename-parser

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: heuristic regex extraction over text, fully local.
rationale: tv-renamer's core job is decoding messy episode filenames; exposing just the parser is a quick, reusable win.

name: nix-derivation-generator
