loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: template-driven text generation with no fetching.
rationale: nix-init's core value—scaffolding derivations—maps cleanly to local templating for Nix users.

name: nix-fetcher-snippet
description: Generates a fetchFromGitHub/fetchurl/fetchgit Nix snippet from a repo URL and ref, with a placeholder SRI hash to fill in.
example_prompt: Make a fetchFromGitHub snippet for github.com/foo/bar at v1.0
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: URL parsing and text templating; the hash is left as a placeholder since fetching is out of scope.
rationale: nurl's snippet structure is the tedious part packagers want generated, and that piece is fully local.

name: nix-hash-converter
description: Converts Nix hashes between formats (base16, base32/nix32, base64, and SRI like sha256-...).
example_prompt: Convert this base32 nix hash to SRI format
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: deterministic base-encoding math, no I/O.
rationale: Nix users (nurl/nix-init audience) constantly juggle hash formats and this is pure local computation.

name: proxy-protocol-decoder
description: Decodes a HAProxy PROXY protocol v1 (text) or v2 (binary) header into source/destination address, port, and transport family.
example_prompt: Decode this PROXY protocol header: PROXY TCP4 192.168.0.1 192.168.0.11 56324 443
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM byte/text parsing of the header; no network required.
rationale: The PROXY protocol carries the original client address through L4 proxies and is opaque binary without a dedicated decoder.

name: rust-symbol-outline
description: Extracts functions, structs, enums, traits, and impl blocks from a Rust file into a navigable outline/tag list.
example_prompt: Give me an outline of all the items in this Rust file: <paste code>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the syn parser compiled to WASM; pure AST walk, no server.
rationale: rusty-tags-style symbol indexing helps users orient in pasted code and runs entirely on the AST.

name: rust-unsafe-scanner
description: Scans Rust source for unsafe blocks, functions, traits, and impls and reports their locations and a total count.
example_prompt: Find all the unsafe usage in this Rust code: <paste code>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via syn AST traversal; fully local analysis.
rationale: geiger-style unsafe auditing is a real security/code-review aid that is pure static analysis.

name: git-graph-diagram
description: Converts git log output into a Mermaid gitGraph diagram so branch and merge history can be visualized.
example_prompt: Turn this git log into a visual branch diagram: <paste git log --graph>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM log parsing and Mermaid emission; pure compute.
rationale: git-time-machine-style history visualization is high-value and can be rendered locally as a Mermaid graph.

name: debian-control-generator
description: Generates a Debian control file and packaging metadata from a pasted Cargo.toml.
example_prompt: Make a debian/control file from this Cargo.toml
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses the TOML and fills a template; pure text transform.
rationale: Bootstraps .deb packaging straight from crate metadata, like cargo-deb, with no toolchain.

name: rust-doc-to-readme
description: Extracts crate-level //! doc comments from a pasted lib.rs and emits a formatted README.md, expanding doc-test fences into code blocks.
example_prompt: Turn the //! docs in this lib.rs into a README
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM doing line-oriented comment extraction and markdown assembly; no toolchain required
rationale: cargo-rdme keeps README and rustdoc in sync, a pure text transform that's perfect for browser-local execution.

name: cargo-lock-tree-inspector
description: Parses a pasted Cargo.lock and renders the full dependency tree while flagging crates resolved to multiple distinct versions (duplicate-version bloat).
example_prompt: Show the dependency tree from this Cargo.lock and highlight any duplicated crate versions
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing the lockfile's TOML and building the graph in memory; the lockfile already contains every resolved version
rationale: Duplicate-version detection and tree visualization are common pre-release hygiene checks that need only the lockfile.

name: cmake-lists-analyzer
description: Parses a pasted CMakeLists.txt to list defined targets, their source files, link dependencies, and declared options/variables.
example_prompt: List the targets and link libraries in this CMakeLists.txt
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM with a CMake command tokenizer; reads the build script as text without invoking cmake
rationale: The CMakeRust/RustCMake demand is about understanding mixed CMake builds, and target/dependency extraction from the file is purely local.

name: rust-symbol-demangler
description: Demangles Rust legacy and v0 mangled symbol names from compiler, linker, or debugger output into readable function paths.
example_prompt: Demangle this symbol: _ZN4core3fmt9Formatter3pad17h2c3f0a1b9e8d7c6dE
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the rustc-demangle crate compiles to WASM and the operation is a pure in-memory string transform with no I/O.
rationale: Output from BugStalker, CodeLLDB, and gdbgui is full of mangled names, and instant local demangling is a constant developer need.

name: healthcheck-probe-generator
description: Generates a Docker HEALTHCHECK directive or Kubernetes readiness/liveness probe from a host:port or URL and timing parameters.
example_prompt: Generate a k8s readiness probe and Docker HEALTHCHECK for http://localhost:8080/health
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — template-driven text generation, no network access.
rationale: is_ready and Komodo both exist to answer 'is the service up?', and generating the probe config locally is a quick win.

name: jni-descriptor-converter
description: Converts between human-readable Java type/method signatures and JNI field/method descriptor strings in both directions.
example_prompt: What's the JNI descriptor for `String format(int code, byte[] data)`?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: descriptor encoding is a deterministic character mapping (e.g. `[Ljava/lang/String;` ↔ `String[]`); a few hundred lines of pure string logic.
rationale: Every JNI demand term (jni, jni-sys, rjni, j4rs, rucaja) forces developers to hand-write these cryptic descriptors, and getting them wrong fails silently at runtime.

name: cpp-name-demangler
description: Decodes Itanium-ABI mangled C++ symbols (e.g. `_ZN3foo3barEv`) into readable function signatures.
example_prompt: Demangle this symbol: `_ZNSt6vectorIiSaIiEE9push_backEOi`
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the `cpp_demangle` crate is `no_std`-friendly pure Rust and compiles cleanly to wasm32; computation only, no I/O.
rationale: anyone using cxx or rust-cpp routinely reads mangled C++ symbols out of linker errors and stack traces and needs to translate them quickly.

name: rust-to-typescript-defs
description: Converts Rust function signatures and `#[repr(C)]`/serde-style structs into TypeScript type declarations (`.d.ts`) for a native Node addon.
example_prompt: Generate TypeScript declarations for `pub fn parse(input: String) -> Vec<Token>` where `Token { kind: String, span: (u32, u32) }`
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse the Rust types and map them to TS types via a fixed table; pure text transformation, client-side.
rationale: neon and node-bindgen produce native Node modules whose JS consumers need accurate `.d.ts` typings, which authors otherwise hand-maintain.

name: c-to-node-ffi-def
description: Turns a C function signature into a node-ffi-rs / ffi-napi definition object with the correct retType and paramsType descriptors.
example_prompt: Give me the node-ffi-rs definition for `double pow(double base, double exp);`
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: map C types to the library's type-descriptor enum and emit the JS object literal; pure lookup-and-format.
rationale: node-ffi-rs callers hand-write these type-descriptor objects per function, and a generator eliminates a common source of wrong-arity / wrong-type crashes.

name: rust-code-metrics
description: Reports LOC, function/struct/enum counts, unsafe blocks, and the longest functions for pasted Rust.
example_prompt: give me code metrics for this Rust file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a syn AST walk, local
rationale: Gives the quick complexity read an IDE outline does, in chat.

name: criterion-report-parser
description: Parses criterion's text and estimates output into a per-benchmark summary with regression flags.
example_prompt: summarize this criterion benchmark output
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: text parsing plus serde_json for estimates.json, local
rationale: Turns criterion.rs's verbose output into a quick pass/regression table.

name: testdox-name-humanizer
description: Converts snake_case/camelCase test function names (e.g. `it_returns_error_when_empty`) into readable specification sentences.
example_prompt: Turn these test names into a readable spec list
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM; pure string tokenization and casing transforms, fully local.
rationale: Reproduces cargo-testdox's value of turning test names into living documentation, language-agnostically.

name: fits-header-reader
description: Extracts and displays the header keyword/value metadata from a FITS file.
example_prompt: Show the FITS header keywords for this file.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — reads only the fixed-format 80-char header cards, no full decode needed.
rationale: Inspecting FITS metadata (exposure, instrument, WCS) is a constant need that's tedious without tooling (fitsio).

name: metronome-click-track
description: Generates a click-track WAV at a given BPM, beats-per-bar, and length.
example_prompt: Make a 2-minute 120 BPM metronome click track in 4/4.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (hound) synthesizes the click PCM and encodes the WAV client-side.
rationale: A practice and recording aid produced entirely offline.

name: kmer-counter
description: Counts all k-mers of a chosen length in a sequence and reports frequencies and the most common motifs.
example_prompt: Count 4-mers in this DNA sequence and show the top 10.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a sliding-window hashmap count, pure computation with no I/O.
rationale: K-mer profiles underpin assembly and composition analysis and are a fast, common local operation.

name: function-minimizer
description: Finds a local minimum of a user-supplied scalar or multivariate function.
example_prompt: Minimize f(x,y) = (x-3)^2 + (y+1)^2
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: argmin-rs/argmin (gradient-descent, L-BFGS, Nelder-Mead) compiles to WASM and optimizes in-browser.
rationale: Numerical minimization is widely needed for fitting and design problems and has no easy browser-local tool.

name: pgfplots-codegen
description: Converts pasted data into ready-to-paste LaTeX pgfplots/TikZ code for publication-quality figures.
example_prompt: Generate pgfplots LaTeX for a line chart of this data
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string templating; it only emits LaTeX text, so it runs entirely in-browser.
rationale: Academics writing LaTeX need pgfplots boilerplate generated from raw data, a pure text transform that is trivially browser-local.

name: partiql-formatter
description: Formats PartiQL statements used by DynamoDB and other PartiQL engines.
example_prompt: format this PartiQL: select id,name from Users where active=true
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM: SQL-like tokenizer and pretty-printer, fully local.
rationale: PartiQL queries pasted from code need consistent formatting and it is purely textual.

name: influxql-formatter
description: Formats InfluxQL and Flux time-series queries with a consistent, readable layout.
example_prompt: format this InfluxQL: select mean(usage) from cpu where time>now()-1h group by time(5m)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM: tokenizer and pretty-printer, local.
rationale: Time-series queries get long, and readable formatting aids review and debugging.

name: redis-glob-tester
description: Tests Redis KEYS/SCAN glob patterns against sample keys to preview which keys match.
example_prompt: which of user:1, user:2, order:1 match the Redis pattern user:*
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM: implements Redis glob matching locally.
rationale: Running KEYS in production is dangerous, so testing patterns offline avoids surprises.

name: surrealql-formatter
description: Formats SurrealDB SurrealQL queries with consistent indentation and keyword casing.
example_prompt: format this SurrealQL: select * from user where age>18 fetch posts
loader_feasibility: plain Rust->WASM: tokenizer and pretty-printer, local.
rationale: SurrealQL is new and editors lack formatters, so deterministic layout helps adoption.

name: emmet-expand
description: Expand an Emmet abbreviation (e.g. ul>li*3>a) into full HTML/CSS.
example_prompt: Expand this Emmet: nav>ul>li*4>a
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM Emmet parser; pure compute, browser-local.
rationale: Emmet expansion is a quick scaffolding aid for anyone writing HTML outside an editor.

name: gravatar-url
description: Generate a Gravatar (and Libravatar) image URL from an email by hashing it.
example_prompt: gravatar url for joris@suppers.ai at 200px
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM email normalization + md5/sha256.
rationale: A standard avatar-bootstrap snippet developers repeatedly hand-build.

name: image-emoji-mosaic
description: Rebuild an image as a mosaic made of emoji.
example_prompt: turn this photo into an emoji mosaic
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM: tile-average matching against an emoji color table, rendered on canvas.
rationale: A viral creative effect distinct from photomosaic (which uses tiles of the image itself).

name: carbon-footprint
description: Estimate CO2 emissions for a flight, drive, or trip from distance and mode.
example_prompt: How much CO2 for a round-trip flight London to New York?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM with bundled emission factors; offline.
rationale: Widely searched and trivially offline with standard factors.

name: runway-calc
description: Compute a startup's cash runway (months remaining) from current cash, monthly burn, and revenue.
example_prompt: $400k in the bank, burning $35k/month net — how many months of runway?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM arithmetic; local.
rationale: Runway is a core founder/operator metric not covered by the generic finance calculators.

name: print-size-calc
description: Convert between pixels and physical print size at a chosen DPI and report max print size.
example_prompt: How big can I print a 6000x4000 photo at 300 DPI?
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust arithmetic in-browser.
rationale: Common photo/print question distinct from aspect-ratio-calc.

name: sketch-to-icon
description: Recognizes a rough doodle and returns the matching clean icon.
example_prompt: Guess what this doodle is and give me a clean icon
loader_feasibility: onnx-runtime running a small QuickDraw classifier model in-browser.
rationale: Reproduces AutoDraw's magic with an offline ML model.

name: lrc-lyrics-editor
description: Creates and edits synced LRC lyric files, attaching timestamps to each line.
example_prompt: Turn these lyrics into a timed LRC file
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM text formatting of timestamps and lines; no I/O.
rationale: MusixHub demand is about lyrics, and synced LRC files are what karaoke and music players consume.

name: musicxml-parser
description: Parses a MusicXML sheet-music file into a readable summary of measures, notes, and parts.
example_prompt: Summarize the notes in this MusicXML score
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM XML parser on the uploaded score; no server.
rationale: MusicXML is NoteFlight's interchange format and a quick readable digest has no local tool today.

name: css-typography-scale
description: Generates a modular typographic scale (font sizes and line-heights as CSS variables) from a base size and ratio.
example_prompt: make a modular type scale starting at 16px with a 1.25 ratio
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM arithmetic and CSS string output, browser-local.
rationale: Maps CSS Typeset's typography focus into a reusable design-token generator.

name: ssh-hassh-fingerprint
description: Computes HASSH (client) and HASSHServer fingerprints from SSH KEXINIT algorithm lists for SSH client/server identification.
example_prompt: Generate the HASSH fingerprint for this SSH client: kex=curve25519-sha256,ecdh-sha2-nistp256 enc=aes128-ctr,aes256-ctr mac=hmac-sha2-256 comp=none
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — HASSH is just an MD5 hash of the semicolon-joined kex/encryption/mac/compression algorithm strings; pure string + hash work, no network.
rationale: HASSH is a standard SSH fingerprinting method used in threat hunting and asset inventory, and analysts currently bounce to CyberChef to compute it.

name: shuffle-lines
description: Randomly reorders the lines of text.
example_prompt: shuffle these lines into a random order
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a pure-Rust seeded PRNG (Fisher–Yates) shuffles the line vector entirely client-side with an optional user seed.
rationale: Randomizing a list (names, questions, picks) is a frequent need and works fully offline with a seed.

name: windows-filetime-to-unix
description: Converts a Windows FILETIME value (100-nanosecond intervals since 1601-01-01) to a Unix timestamp and a readable date.
example_prompt: convert FILETIME 133000000000000000 to a normal date
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM 64-bit integer math, fully offline.
rationale: A zero-substitute need in Windows log and forensic analysis that maps the demand term exactly.

name: murmurhash3
description: Computes the non-cryptographic MurmurHash3 (x86 32-bit and x64 128-bit) of input with an optional seed.
example_prompt: Give me the murmurhash3 128-bit of this string
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the murmur3 crate; it is a few rounds of integer mixing, entirely client-side.
rationale: MurmurHash3 underpins many hash tables, bloom filters, and sharding schemes that developers need to reproduce.

name: colormap-preview
description: Generates gradient swatches and legends for scientific colormaps (viridis, magma, plasma, turbo) with hex stops.
example_prompt: Show me the viridis and magma colormaps as gradient swatches
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM evaluates colormap functions and emits SVG/PNG swatches entirely client-side.
rationale: Choosing a perceptually-uniform colormap is a recurring need for anyone building heatmaps or data viz.

name: decimal-codec
description: Encodes text into space-separated decimal byte values and reconstructs text from a list of decimal byte values.
example_prompt: give me the decimal byte values for "OK"
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — byte enumeration and decimal formatting are pure in-memory work.
rationale: Decimal byte encoding is a distinct, searched operation that complements the charcode and binary codecs.

name: base92-codec
description: Encodes binary/text to and decodes from Base92, a high-density ASCII-safe encoding.
example_prompt: encode the word hello to base92
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a fixed-alphabet big-integer base conversion done in-memory.
rationale: Base92 is requested but rarely available outside CyberChef, so a browser-local version fills a real gap.

name: ls47-cipher
description: Encrypts or decrypts text with the LS47 pen-and-paper cipher over its 7x7 character grid.
example_prompt: Encrypt 'attack at dawn' with LS47 using the password 'rosebud'
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM with a small hand-written LS47 implementation; it's pure character-grid arithmetic, ideal for the sandbox.
rationale: LS47 is a niche but beloved human-computable cipher with no good browser-local tool today.

name: gost-key-wrap
description: Wraps or unwraps a symmetric key under a key-encryption key using the GOST 28147-89 key-wrap scheme (RFC 4357).
example_prompt: Unwrap this GOST-wrapped key blob with my KEK
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM built on the Magma cipher plus its MAC (imitovstavka) — deterministic byte math, runs client-side.
rationale: Covers GOST Key Wrap and Unwrap; secure key transport is required wherever GOST ciphers are deployed.

name: sm2-encrypt
description: Encrypts a message with an SM2 public key, producing C1C3C2 ciphertext in hex or ASN.1 DER form.
example_prompt: Encrypt this message with SM2 using this public key: 04a1b2...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via RustCrypto `sm2` (+`sm3` KDF); needs one ephemeral random scalar from the host secure-random import or a user seed, otherwise pure in-sandbox compute.
rationale: Directly maps the harvested 'SM2 Encrypt' demand and serves the large base of developers integrating with Chinese government/banking APIs that mandate ShangMi.

name: sm2-verify
description: Verifies an SM2 signature against a public key and message, handling the SM3-based ZA identity hashing.
example_prompt: Verify this SM2 signature against this public key and message
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via RustCrypto `sm2`/`sm3`; deterministic verification with no randomness or network, runs client-side in wasmi.
rationale: The natural companion to sm2-sign, letting developers check ShangMi signatures without standing up a Chinese-crypto backend.

name: offset-checker
description: Compares two or more inputs character-by-character and highlights the offsets where they match or diverge.
example_prompt: check the offsets where these three hashes differ
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; positional comparison is pure computation, no server.
rationale: Spotting where similar strings, hashes, or hex blobs start to differ speeds up debugging.

name: image-histogram
description: Compute and render an RGB/luminance histogram for an image to inspect exposure and tone.
example_prompt: show the histogram of this photo
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (image crate) for analysis + plotting.
rationale: Standard photo-editing diagnostic that complements the existing image filters.

name: normal-map
description: Generate a tangent-space normal map from a heightmap or photo for 3D/game materials.
example_prompt: make a normal map from this brick texture
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (or WebGPU) Sobel-gradient to RGB normals.
rationale: Gamedev/3D staple with no in-catalog equivalent and clean local compute.

name: vim-regex-converter
description: Converts between Vim regex syntax and PCRE/JavaScript regex in either direction.
example_prompt: Convert this Vim pattern to JavaScript regex: \v(\d+)-(\d+)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — a deterministic syntax transform between regex dialects, fully local.
rationale: Vim's regex flavor trips up users moving patterns to/from other tools, a recurring need across the editor-term cluster.

name: loadtest-config-generator
description: Generates a k6, artillery, or vegeta load-test script from a target endpoint, request shape, and load profile.
example_prompt: Generate a k6 script to load test POST /checkout at 200 RPS for 5 minutes
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — emits the script text from parameters, offline.
rationale: loadtest tools need correct config, and generating it from a plain description removes a common setup hurdle.

name: cooking-timeline-planner
description: Builds a back-timed cooking schedule from recipe step durations so multiple dishes finish at the same target serving time.
example_prompt: I want dinner ready at 19:00 — schedule these three dishes with their cook times
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — critical-path scheduling over durations, no external data.
rationale: Coordinating dish timing is the hardest part of cooking and a natural extension of the recipe-parsing cluster.

name: checksum-list-diff
description: Compares two checksum manifests (e.g. an old and new sha256sum list) to flag added, removed, and silently-changed/corrupted files for bit-rot detection.
example_prompt: Diff these two sha256sum outputs and tell me which files changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses and set-diffs the two pasted manifests; offline.
rationale: chkbit's whole point is spotting bit rot by comparing stored hashes; a manifest differ delivers that with nothing to install.

name: shell-config-linter
description: Lints pasted .zshrc/.bashrc for duplicate PATH entries, unquoted variables, and slow startup patterns.
example_prompt: Lint my .zshrc for problems
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line parsing of the pasted config; entirely text analysis, runs client-side.
rationale: Directly serves the awesome-zsh-plugins crowd who accumulate messy dotfiles over years.

name: matrix-event-formatter
description: Pretty-prints a Matrix event JSON and explains its type, content fields, and relations (edits, replies, reactions).
example_prompt: what does this matrix event mean? {paste m.room.message JSON}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — JSON parse plus a Matrix event-type dictionary, no homeserver call required.
rationale: Matrix event JSON is verbose and nested; a local explainer helps client devs and power users inspect events privately.

name: mxc-uri-parser
description: Decomposes Matrix mxc:// media URIs into server name and media id and builds the corresponding download/thumbnail API paths.
example_prompt: turn mxc://matrix.org/abc123 into a download URL path
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure string manipulation against the documented media API path template.
rationale: Resolving mxc URIs by hand is error-prone; a tool removes guesswork for client builders and bot authors.

name: fediverse-handle-parser
description: Validates @user@instance fediverse handles and derives the WebFinger acct: URI and expected actor URL pattern.
example_prompt: what's the webfinger acct uri for @gargron@mastodon.social?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — handle parsing and URI templating are pure string logic.
rationale: Mapping handles to WebFinger/actor endpoints is a recurring need when building or debugging fediverse integrations.

name: emote-frequency-counter
description: Counts and ranks emotes and emoji in a chat log to show which ones a community uses most.
example_prompt: Which emotes show up most in this Twitch chat log?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizes the log and tallies emote/emoji tokens locally.
rationale: A fun, fast tool tapping Twitch/chat-client culture from the ttchat/twitch-tui demand, fully offline.

name: command-batch-expander
description: Expands a command template over a list or numeric range of inputs to preview every generated command, mimicking GNU parallel/xargs.
example_prompt: Show me the commands `convert {}.png {}.jpg` would run over files a, b, c, d.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: template substitution across an input list is pure string expansion, generating preview text only (never executing).
rationale: parallel/xargs users want to verify the exact expanded commands before running them, which is a safe, deterministic local preview.

name: lxc-incus-profile-linter
description: Validates and explains an LXC/Incus YAML container profile, flagging unknown or risky configuration keys.
example_prompt: Check this Incus profile and explain its keys: [paste profile YAML]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM YAML parse with key explanation; no hypervisor contact needed.
rationale: Incus and lxc configs are error-prone and sparsely documented, so an offline linter/explainer fills a real gap.

name: jitter-latency-calculator
description: Parses ping/traceroute output and computes average, min/max, standard deviation, jitter and packet loss.
example_prompt: Paste of my ping results — calculate the jitter and packet loss
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM numeric parsing and statistics over pasted text — no measurement performed, just analysis.
rationale: The 'Jitter' demand maps directly to a network-diagnostics stat users currently eyeball from ping logs.

name: edit-script
description: Outputs the minimal shortest edit script — the exact ordered list of insert, delete, and substitute operations — that transforms one string into another.
example_prompt: What's the minimal sequence of edits to turn 'kitten' into 'sitting'?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — backtracks the Levenshtein DP matrix to emit the operation transcript; runs fully in-browser.
rationale: The existing edit-distance tool gives only a number; spell-checking, fuzzy matching, and linguistics work need the actual operation sequence (sesdiff), which nothing in the catalog provides.

name: tree-to-scaffold
description: Takes an ASCII directory tree and emits a downloadable zip of empty folders/files plus an equivalent mkdir/touch shell script.
example_prompt: scaffold this project structure into a zip I can unpack
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the tree and writes the empty-file zip in memory; both steps are pure computation.
rationale: The literal treegen use case — turning a sketched layout into a ready-to-fill project skeleton in one step.

name: junk-file-detector
description: Scans a pasted file list or uploaded archive for junk and build artifacts (node_modules, .DS_Store, __pycache__, *.log, target/, .tmp) and totals the reclaimable space.
example_prompt: which of these files are junk I should delete?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM matches paths against rule patterns and sums sizes; rule evaluation is pure and instant in-page.
rationale: Maps the trash/del demand to a useful 'what's safe to throw away' classifier instead of an FS-dependent trash bin.

name: git-vanity-hash
description: Brute-forces commit metadata (author/committer timestamps and a nonce) until the resulting SHA-1 commit hash begins with a chosen prefix.
example_prompt: Find a commit whose hash starts with cafe for this commit object
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute parallelizes the SHA-1 search on the GPU entirely in-browser (plain Rust→WASM fallback for short prefixes); it works on the pasted commit object so no repo or network is needed.
rationale: Vanity commit hashes are a popular bragging-rights task and the search is pure local compute that the GPU accelerates dramatically.

name: mtr-report-parser
description: Parses pasted mtr or traceroute output into a clean per-hop table with loss, latency, and jitter columns.
example_prompt: turn this mtr report into a readable hop-by-hop latency table

name: camelcase-hashtag-fixer

name: webfinger-resolver-formatter

name: ublock-filter-linter
description: Validates and lints uBlock Origin / Adblock Plus filter-list syntax, flagging errors, unknown options, and deprecated directives.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pure text/grammar parsing of ABP filter syntax, no network or DOM needed.

name: ip-address-generator

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — deterministic/seeded integer generation, no server needed.
rationale: Directly maps the generate-ip demand and is useful for test fixtures, mock data, and load-test address lists.

name: phonetic-encode

loader_feasibility: Plain Rust (rphonetic) to WASM — no network or model, pure compute.

name: svg-to-ico
description: Rasterizes an SVG at multiple sizes and packs them into a multi-resolution favicon.ico.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: `resvg` renders sizes, the `image` crate writes the ICO container

name: matlab-to-numpy
description: Translates common MATLAB expressions and functions into equivalent NumPy code.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies a rule-based mapping of common MATLAB↔NumPy equivalences locally.

name: sudoku-validator

name: h264-stream-to-mp4

name: newick-to-json

example_prompt: Convert this Newick tree into nested JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM recursive-descent parser; small, deterministic, fully local.
rationale: Newick is the standard tree format but unusable in JS visualizations until turned into a JSON hierarchy.

name: xyz-to-ply-pointcloud
description: Wraps a plain XYZ (optionally XYZRGB) point file into a proper PLY point cloud with a header.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: counting points and writing the PLY element header plus the data block is simple client-side text/byte work.
rationale: Point-cloud viewers need PLY structure that bare XYZ dumps lack.

name: color-namer
description: Maps any hex or RGB value to the closest human-readable color name and reports the perceptual delta.
example_prompt: What color is #4a7ba6 called?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM nearest-neighbor search over an embedded named-color table; no network needed.
rationale: NTC (Name That Color) demand reflects how often designers and devs need a name for a raw hex value.

name: sleep-cycle-calc
description: Compute optimal bedtimes or wake times around 90-minute sleep cycles.
example_prompt: I want to wake at 6:30am — when should I go to sleep?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM time math; offline.
rationale: Popular consumer wellness tool absent from the health set.

name: l-system-renderer

example_prompt: render the L-system F→F+F−F−F+F at 90 degrees, 4 iterations
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM does string rewriting then turtle interpretation to SVG, all in-browser
rationale: L-systems are a core generative-art and procedural-plant technique with no clean single-purpose web tool.

name: bidi-trojan-source-detector
description: Detects Unicode bidirectional-override characters used in Trojan Source attacks that make source code read differently than it executes.
example_prompt: Scan this source code for hidden bidi override / Trojan Source characters
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans for the specific Unicode Bidi control code points locally

name: progressive-jpeg-checker
description: Reports whether a JPEG is baseline or progressive, which affects perceived load behavior and decoder compatibility.
example_prompt: Is this JPEG baseline or progressive?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads the SOF marker type client-side.
rationale: Progressive vs baseline matters for load UX and some older decoders, and it's not visible otherwise.

name: graphql-query-complexity
description: Analyzes a GraphQL query for depth, field count, and estimated complexity to flag potentially abusive or expensive requests.
example_prompt: How deep and complex is this GraphQL query?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM GraphQL document parsing and traversal; entirely local.
rationale: Query depth and complexity drive GraphQL DoS risk and a local analyzer helps set sane limits.

name: color-clip-generator
description: Generates a solid single-color (default black) video clip of a given duration, resolution, and frame rate.
example_prompt: Give me 8 seconds of solid black at 1920x1080 30fps for padding
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg `color` lavfi source produces the clip with no input file inside the wasm runtime.
rationale: Editors constantly need black/solid spacer clips for padding, transitions, and timeline gaps and otherwise improvise them.

name: wavetable-generator
description: Creates single-cycle wavetable WAV files from harmonic recipes or waveform blends for import into synths.
example_prompt: Generate a single-cycle wavetable that morphs saw to square
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM additively builds the harmonic content and exports correctly-sized single-cycle WAVs locally.
rationale: Sound designers feed custom single-cycle wavetables into Serum/Vital and need a precise generator.

name: silence-wav-generator
description: Creates a WAV file of pure digital silence with chosen duration, sample rate, bit depth, and channel count.
example_prompt: Generate 3 seconds of stereo 48 kHz silence
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM writes a valid WAV header plus zero-filled PCM entirely in-memory.
rationale: Editors need exact-spec silent spacers for padding, gaps, and format-conformance testing.

name: kick-drum-synth-generator
description: Synthesizes a custom kick drum from pitch-envelope, click, and decay parameters as a one-shot WAV.

loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies a pitch-swept sine plus a click transient and amplitude envelope to render the one-shot WAV in-browser.
rationale: Designing a kick from scratch is a daily producer task and a parametric generator beats digging through sample packs.

name: 808-bass-generator
description: Generates a tuned 808-style sub-bass one-shot with glide, saturation, and decay at a chosen note, as WAV.
example_prompt: Generate an 808 bass on F1 with a slow glide and some distortion
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM synthesizes the pitched sub sine with optional waveshaping and writes the note-tuned WAV client-side.
rationale: Trap/hip-hop tracks are built on tuned 808s and producers want them generated at an exact pitch.

name: cue-sheet-generator
description: Generates a CUE sheet from a track list with titles, performers, and start times for a single long audio file.
example_prompt: Build a .cue file for my DJ mix from these track timestamps
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM formats the CUE syntax (FILE/TRACK/INDEX) as text entirely client-side.
rationale: DJ mixes and concert recordings need CUE sheets for chaptering and the syntax is fiddly to hand-write.

name: podcast-chapters-json-generator
description: Generates a Podcasting 2.0 chapters JSON file from titles, start times, and optional links/images.
example_prompt: Make a podcast chapters.json from my episode segment list
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM builds the spec-compliant chapters JSON structure in-memory with no network call.
rationale: Modern podcast players read chapters JSON and producers need a valid file without a hosting tool.

name: reaper-project-scaffold
description: Generates a REAPER .RPP project file pre-populated with named tracks, tempo, and time signature from a spec.
example_prompt: Scaffold a REAPER project with 6 named tracks at 95 bpm
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM writes the .RPP text chunk structure (TRACK/TEMPO blocks) entirely client-side.
rationale: Spinning up a templated session with the right track layout saves repetitive setup before every project.

name: regular-polygon-vertices
description: Generates the vertices of a regular N-gon or star polygon {N/k} given radius and rotation, with edge connectivity for star forms.
example_prompt: Generate the vertices of a regular 7-pointed star
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — evenly-spaced trig point placement, instant in-browser.
rationale: Exact polygon and star vertex coordinates are constantly needed for geometry, SVG, and CNC layout.

name: platonic-solid-mesh
description: Generates the vertices, edges, and faces of a chosen Platonic solid at unit edge length, with optional OBJ/PLY-style output.
example_prompt: Generate the vertices and faces of an icosahedron
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — closed-form vertex coordinates and face tables, pure math.
rationale: Exact Platonic solid meshes are needed for 3D demos and geometry teaching and are tedious to hand-enter.

name: png-to-icns
description: Builds a macOS .icns icon set from source PNGs at the standard Apple sizes.
example_prompt: make an app icon.icns from this 1024px png
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM via the `icns` crate, which assembles the .icns container in-memory
rationale: macOS app/dock icons require the proprietary .icns format that no simple online tool builds offline.

name: pnm-to-png
description: Converts Netpbm PBM/PGM/PPM images into PNG.
example_prompt: convert this ppm output to png
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the `image` crate decodes the PNM family in-memory
rationale: Scientific and CLI tools emit Netpbm that nothing on the web can open.

name: poseidon-hash
description: Computes the zk-friendly Poseidon hash of field elements.
example_prompt: Poseidon hash of [1, 2, 3]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the Poseidon permutation (arkworks/circom-compat) is pure field arithmetic.
rationale: Poseidon is the standard hash in zk circuits and developers need a quick local way to compute it.

name: process-compose-validator
description: Validates a process-compose.yaml and visualizes process startup order, depends_on conditions, and health checks as a Mermaid graph.
example_prompt: Check this process-compose.yaml for dependency cycles and draw the startup order.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM: schema validation, cycle detection, and diagram generation are pure in-memory operations.
rationale: process-compose and procmux users juggle multi-process orchestration files where a missed cycle or bad health check is hard to spot by eye.

name: image-to-braille-art
description: Renders an image as high-resolution monochrome art using Unicode braille characters, packing a 2×4 dot grid into every glyph.
example_prompt: Convert this drawing to braille-dot ASCII art: <upload sketch.png>
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes/thresholds the image and plain Rust→WASM packs dot patterns into braille code points, no server involved.
rationale: Braille gives ~8× the resolution of plain ASCII for the same width, a meaningfully different and impressive output mode.

name: awg-wire
description: Look up AWG wire gauge diameter, resistance, and current capacity (and the reverse).
example_prompt: What's the ampacity and diameter of 12 AWG copper?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM tables and formulas, offline.
rationale: Electricians and makers need wire-gauge specs with no current tool.

name: radar-chart-svg

example_prompt: Radar chart comparing two phones on Camera 8, Battery 7, Speed 9, Price 6
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM converts axis angles to coordinates with trig and emits SVG polygons.
rationale: Radar charts are a signature amCharts/AnyChart type ideal for side-by-side comparisons.

name: ean-upc-validator
description: Validates EAN-8/EAN-13 and UPC-A barcode numbers via their check digit and reports the failing entries.
example_prompt: Validate these barcode numbers — which check digits are wrong?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM modulo check-digit computation runs client-side with no API
rationale: Retail/inventory feeds carry mistyped barcodes that silently mismatch products; a checksum pass catches them.

name: correlation-matrix-validator
description: Checks whether a matrix is a valid correlation matrix: symmetric, unit diagonal, entries in [-1,1], and positive semidefinite.
example_prompt: Is this 3x3 matrix a valid correlation matrix?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: symmetry/range tests plus an eigenvalue-sign check, client-side.
rationale: Risk and portfolio tools require valid correlation matrices, and hand-entered ones often violate the PSD constraint.

name: probability-distribution-validator

example_prompt: Do these probabilities form a valid distribution: 0.2, 0.5, 0.4?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a sum and range scan, fully on-device.
rationale: ML and stats users frequently pass malformed PMFs into samplers and a quick validity check prevents silent bugs.

name: elliptic-curve-calculator

example_prompt: on curve y^2=x^3+2x+3 mod 97, compute 5 times point (3,6)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: num-bigint field arithmetic implements the group law in pure Rust, offline.
rationale: Directly fulfills the 'Elliptic Curve Calculator' demand term, which has few good interactive tools.

name: rate-limit-simulator
description: Simulates token-bucket, leaky-bucket, and sliding-window rate limiters against a request pattern and reports which requests are allowed or throttled.
example_prompt: Simulate a 100 req/min token bucket against this burst of 250 requests
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the simulation is deterministic arithmetic over a request timeline, fully client-side.
rationale: Tuning rate-limit parameters (the redis-shield demand) before deploying is much safer to explore in a local simulator.

name: sfx-generator
description: Synthesizes retro 8-bit game sound effects (jump, laser, pickup, explosion) as WAV.
example_prompt: Generate a retro coin pickup sound effect
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM DSP synthesizes waveforms and writes a WAV buffer, no assets needed.
rationale: Directly answers the 'bfxr' demand term for indie game-dev sound effects.

name: inequality-prover
description: Checks polynomial/algebraic inequalities (AM-GM-style) symbolically and by dense numeric sampling.
example_prompt: Is a^2+b^2+c^2 >= ab+bc+ca for all reals? Check it
loader_feasibility: pyodide loader — sympy runs in a client-side Python sandbox; numeric sampling backs up the symbolic check.
rationale: Evan Chen's audience wants fast sanity-checks on olympiad inequalities, which this delivers offline.

name: pac-file-generator
description: Generates a valid proxy auto-config (FindProxyForURL) PAC file from a list of host/domain/CIDR → proxy rules with a default fallback.
example_prompt: Make a PAC file that sends *.internal.example.com direct and everything else through proxy.corp:8080
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM template/text generation; deterministic and offline.
rationale: Hand-writing PAC JavaScript is error-prone, and generating it from simple rules serves the broad proxy-config demand.

name: x402-payment-header

example_prompt: Decode this x402 payment-required header
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: header/JSON parsing and construction of the x402 envelope.
rationale: The x402 micropayment scheme (Spraay-style gateways) is emerging and developers need to inspect its headers while integrating.

name: terminal-string-width
description: Computes the true display width (in terminal cells) of strings, correctly handling wide CJK, combining marks, and emoji.
example_prompt: How many terminal columns wide is this string with emoji and Japanese text?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: uses the unicode-width algorithm over bundled tables, fully offline.
rationale: TUI and status-bar authors constantly misalign columns because `len()` ≠ display width for CJK/emoji.

name: content-disposition-parser
description: Parses a Content-Disposition header to extract the disposition type and RFC 5987-encoded filename.
example_prompt: What filename does this Content-Disposition header set?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM header parser handling filename* extended encoding.
rationale: Download-naming and header debugging.

name: hosts-file-parser
description: Parses an /etc/hosts file into structured IP→hostname mappings and flags duplicates.
example_prompt: Parse this hosts file and flag duplicate hostnames
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line parser.
rationale: DNS-override review and conflict detection.

name: solarize-image
description: Inverts tones above a threshold to create the classic solarization effect.
example_prompt: Solarize this photo above 60% brightness
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — conditional per-channel inversion above a cutoff
rationale: A specific darkroom effect with no equivalent in the existing catalog.

name: css-shorthand-expander
description: Expands CSS shorthand properties like margin or background into their explicit longhand declarations.
example_prompt: Expand the shorthand margin and font rules in this CSS to longhand
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM property-mapping logic; deterministic, no server needed.
rationale: Longhand is clearer for debugging cascade conflicts and for diffing why two rules collide.

name: css-shorthand-collapser
description: Merges adjacent longhand CSS declarations into equivalent shorthand to cut rule size.
example_prompt: Collapse these margin-top/right/bottom/left rules into shorthand
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM declaration grouping; purely local string analysis.
rationale: Hand-written longhand bloats stylesheets and collapsing it is tedious and error-prone manually.

name: picture-element-builder
description: Wraps an img into a <picture> with AVIF/WebP source fallbacks from a single base path.
example_prompt: Wrap photo.jpg in a picture element with webp and avif sources
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM markup templating; pure string output, browser-local.
rationale: Modern responsive image markup is verbose boilerplate that's faster to generate than to type.

name: content-type-parser
description: Splits a Content-Type value into type, subtype, suffix, and parameters like charset and boundary.
example_prompt: what charset and boundary does this Content-Type declare?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; MIME parameter parsing is local string work.
rationale: Pulling charset/boundary out of a media type is a frequent need that the generic header tools don't isolate.

name: generative-art-poster
description: Produces algorithmic generative art (flow fields, noise, tilings) from a seed and a few parameters.
example_prompt: Generate a flow-field generative art poster with a blue and gold palette
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — valora-style generative art is pure computation that renders to a canvas/PNG buffer entirely in-browser.
rationale: Seed-based generative art gives users unique, downloadable wallpapers and prints with no design skill required.

name: qoi-to-png
description: Decodes the Quite-OK-Image (QOI) format into PNG.
example_prompt: convert these .qoi files to png
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: the `image`/`qoi` crate decodes QOI in-memory
rationale: QOI is increasingly used by indie game engines but viewers don't support it yet.

name: rot13-brute-force
description: Shows all 25 Caesar/ROT rotations of a message so you can spot the readable plaintext.
example_prompt: Brute force this ROT cipher: Khoor zruog
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — 25 deterministic shifts computed in-memory, no I/O.
rationale: Cracks unknown-shift Caesar/ROT messages in one step, a staple of puzzle and CTF solving.

name: m3u-playlist-builder
description: Builds an M3U/M3U8 playlist from a list of media URLs with optional titles and durations.
example_prompt: Make an M3U playlist from these PeerTube video links
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: emits M3U text from the provided entries locally.
rationale: Watching PeerTube/Odysee/Invidious media in an external player needs an M3U, and generating it is pure text output.

name: bash-menu-generator
description: Generates a ready-to-run bash `select` menu script from a list of options and the action for each.
example_prompt: Make me a bash menu to choose between deploy, rollback, and status
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string templating produces the script with no external calls.
rationale: climenu and menu.sh demand maps to pure codegen of an interactive shell menu.

name: animated-webp-frame-checker
description: Confirms an animated WebP's ANIM/ANMF chunk structure is complete and counts frames, flagging files that decode as a single still image.
example_prompt: Is this WebP actually animated or just one frame?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the RIFF/WebP container chunks locally; only header walking is required.
rationale: Converters frequently flatten animated WebP to a still and this catches it before publishing.

name: copyright-metadata-checker
description: Checks whether an image declares copyright, author, and licensing metadata in EXIF/IPTC/XMP, warning when attribution fields are empty.
example_prompt: Does this image have copyright info embedded?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM inspects the relevant attribution tags across metadata blocks in-memory.
rationale: Stock and agency workflows require attribution metadata, and missing fields cause rejections downstream.

name: photosensitive-flash-checker
description: Analyzes an animated image's per-frame luminance to flag rapid flashing that risks triggering photosensitive seizures (WCAG 2.3.1).
example_prompt: Is this animated GIF safe for photosensitive viewers?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg decodes frames locally and the tool measures frame-to-frame luminance deltas and flash frequency in WASM.
rationale: Flashing-content accessibility is a real legal and safety requirement that almost no editor checks automatically.

name: transparent-pixel-color-consistency-checker
description: Checks the hidden RGB values beneath fully-transparent pixels and flags inconsistent or noisy color that can cause edge bleeding during scaling.
example_prompt: Are the RGB values under my transparent pixels clean?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads RGB of alpha-zero pixels and measures their variance locally.
rationale: Garbage RGB under transparent pixels bleeds in when textures are filtered or mipmapped, producing edge halos.

name: svg-external-reference-checker
description: Flags external references in an SVG (remote image hrefs, fonts, stylesheets, use links) that break offline rendering or leak requests.
example_prompt: Does this SVG pull in any external resources?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses href/url() attributes and classifies them as internal vs external locally.
rationale: External refs cause broken icons offline and privacy-leaking network calls, both invisible until deployed.

name: video-closed-gop-checker
description: Determines whether the stream uses closed GOPs (each starting at an IDR) and flags open GOPs that hinder clean splicing.
example_prompt: Are the GOPs in this file closed or open?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader reads frame/IDR types via ffprobe in WASM and classifies GOP closure locally.
rationale: Open GOPs break ad-insertion and clean cutting, so broadcast specs require a closed-GOP conformance check.

name: video-bframe-policy-checker
description: Checks whether the stream contains B-frames and flags violations of profiles (e.g., Baseline) that forbid them.
example_prompt: Does this H.264 use B-frames? It needs to be Baseline-compatible.
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader reads per-frame picture types via ffprobe in WASM and applies the no-B-frame policy locally.
rationale: Low-latency and legacy-device targets forbid B-frames, so a policy check guards device compatibility.

name: video-first-frame-keyframe-checker
description: Confirms the first decoded frame is a keyframe (IDR), which streaming and seeking require for clean startup.
example_prompt: Does this stream start on a keyframe?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader reads the first frame's key flag via ffprobe in WASM and checks it locally.
rationale: A non-keyframe start breaks adaptive streaming and seek-to-zero, making this a quick but vital gate.

name: video-audio-phase-checker
description: Measures stereo correlation/phase and flags out-of-phase content that collapses or cancels in mono playback.
example_prompt: Is the stereo audio on this video out of phase?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader runs the aphasemeter/astats filters in WASM to compute correlation locally.
rationale: Out-of-phase stereo disappears on mono devices, a defect only a phase-correlation check reliably catches.

name: video-font-attachment-checker
description: Checks that fonts referenced by embedded ASS/SSA subtitles are attached to the container, flagging missing fonts.
example_prompt: Are all the subtitle fonts attached to this MKV?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg loader lists attachments and parses ASS style fonts in WASM, cross-checking them locally.
rationale: Missing attached fonts make styled subtitles render with wrong typefaces, a frequent MKV delivery defect.

name: subtitle-markup-linter
description: Lints subtitle cue text for unsupported or malformed markup (HTML/ASS override tags) that target players won't render.
example_prompt: Are there any unsupported formatting tags in these subtitles?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM scans cue text against an allowed-tag set entirely in the browser.
rationale: Unsupported markup renders as literal garbage on many players, a content-quality issue a tag linter catches.

name: subtitle-line-count-linter
description: Flags subtitle cues exceeding the maximum allowed lines (typically 2) per the target broadcast or platform style guide.
example_prompt: Do any subtitle cues have more than two lines?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM counts lines per cue in the browser against the configured limit.
rationale: Too many lines per cue violate readability standards distinct from line-length, requiring a dedicated check.

name: scc-caption-validator
description: Validates a Scenarist Closed Caption (.scc) file for correct timecode format, byte-pair parity, and control-code sequences.
example_prompt: Validate this SCC caption file for errors.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM decodes and checks the SCC hex/byte-pair structure entirely in the browser.
rationale: SCC is the US broadcast caption standard with strict parity rules that only a format-specific validator can enforce.

name: wood-grain-texture-generator
description: Synthesizes a seamless procedural wood-grain texture from turbulent noise rings with adjustable color and ring frequency.
example_prompt: make a seamless oak wood grain texture 512x512
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM warps concentric rings with noise and colorizes into a PNG — CPU-only math.
rationale: Tileable material textures like wood are core 3D/UI assets and procedural generation gives infinite variation offline.

name: radar-sweep-video
description: Renders a rotating radar/sonar sweep animation with concentric rings as a looping overlay or background.
example_prompt: Create a green radar sweep loop, 8 seconds, transparent background, 720x720
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg geq/rotate expressions draw the sweeping wedge and rings procedurally per frame; no assets needed.
rationale: A common HUD/sci-fi motif that's tedious to make by hand but easy to parametrize.

name: metaballs-background-video
description: Generates an organic blobby metaballs motion background as a looping video from color and blob-count parameters.
example_prompt: Make a 12-second looping metaballs background, blue blobs on dark, 1080p
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute runs a metaball distance-field shader per frame, encoded via ffmpeg; all browser-local.
rationale: Smooth metaball motion is a popular modern background and a natural shader job distinct from existing shader art.

name: handbrake-preset-generator
description: Produces an importable HandBrake preset JSON from chosen codec, quality, resolution, and audio settings.
example_prompt: Make a HandBrake preset for 1080p H.265, RF 22, AAC stereo, web-optimized
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM templates the HandBrake preset JSON schema locally; nothing encoded or uploaded.
rationale: HandBrake presets are JSON that almost nobody writes by hand, and a generator standardizes team encoding.

name: log-sweep-ir-measurement-generator
description: Produces a paired exponential sine sweep and its inverse filter for impulse-response measurement via deconvolution.
example_prompt: Make me an ESS sweep and inverse filter to measure a room impulse response
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: Farina-method sweep + time-reversed amplitude-corrected inverse, both WAVs computed in-memory.
rationale: Acoustic measurement needs the matched sweep/inverse pair, which is tedious to derive by hand and unavailable in casual tools.

name: tuning-reference-generator
description: Generates a sustained reference tone for any note at a chosen concert-pitch standard (e.g., A=432/440/442).
example_prompt: Give me a sustained A note reference at A=442Hz
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: maps note + tuning standard to a frequency and synthesizes a sine + WAV encode, offline.
rationale: Players who tune by ear want a precise pitch reference at non-standard concert pitches that generic apps don't offer.

name: multitone-test-signal-generator
description: Builds a sum-of-sines multitone signal with user-chosen frequencies and levels for distortion/linearity testing.
example_prompt: Make a multitone test signal with tones at 100, 1k, and 10kHz
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: additively sums sines with crest-factor control + WAV encode, no external compute.
rationale: Multitone stimuli reveal nonlinear distortion across the band in one pass, a staple of audio bench testing.

name: two-tone-imd-generator
description: Generates a two-tone test signal (e.g., 19kHz + 20kHz or SMPTE 60Hz + 7kHz) for intermodulation-distortion measurement.
example_prompt: Create a CCIF 19kHz + 20kHz IMD test tone
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: sums two precisely-spaced sines at a set ratio + WAV encode, deterministic offline.
rationale: Standard IMD test pairs are needed to characterize amplifier/converter nonlinearity and aren't trivial to craft by ear.

name: two-pop-sync-generator
description: Generates a single 1kHz 2-pop beep at a precise offset (e.g., 2 seconds before start) for audio/video alignment.
example_prompt: Make a 2-pop sync beep 2 seconds before a 30-second slate
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: places a short tone burst at an exact sample offset in silence + WAV encode, offline.
rationale: The 2-pop is the standard sync marker for lining up audio and picture in post, and editors need it placed sample-accurately.

name: impulse-click-generator
description: Creates a single-sample impulse or short click for impulse-response capture and timing tests.
example_prompt: Make a single-sample impulse WAV at 48kHz
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: writes one full-scale sample (or band-limited click) in silence + WAV encode, offline.
rationale: A clean impulse is the simplest excitation for capturing reverb/IR and verifying delay, and must be exactly one sample wide.

name: subwoofer-sweep-generator
description: Generates a slow low-frequency sweep (e.g., 10–120Hz) tailored for testing subwoofers and room modes.
example_prompt: Make a 20Hz to 100Hz subwoofer test sweep over 30 seconds
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: band-limited low-frequency chirp synthesis + WAV encode, deterministic offline.
rationale: Hunting for rattles, port noise, and room nulls in the low end needs a slow dedicated sub sweep, not a full-range one.

name: synthetic-geojson-generator
description: Generates random points, lines, or polygons within a bounding box as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection with optional properties.
example_prompt: make 100 random GeoJSON points inside this bounding box
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; seeded coordinate synthesis and GeoJSON assembly, no map service.
rationale: Map-rendering and spatial-query tests need throwaway geo features that this produces on demand.

name: redirect-rules-generator
description: Converts an old→new URL mapping into 301 redirect rules for Apache, nginx, Netlify, or Vercel.
example_prompt: Turn this list of moved page URLs into nginx 301 redirect rules
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM maps pairs into platform-specific syntax, offline
rationale: Site migrations need bulk redirects and each platform's format differs subtly.

name: chebyshev-nodes-generator
description: Generates Chebyshev interpolation nodes (first/second kind) on a chosen interval to avoid Runge oscillation.
example_prompt: Give me 8 Chebyshev nodes on [-1, 1]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — cosine node formula evaluated locally
rationale: Chebyshev nodes are the correct sampling points for stable interpolation, frequently needed when scaffolding numerical experiments.

name: maze-solver
description: Finds and overlays the shortest path through a maze you provide as an ASCII grid or image.
example_prompt: Solve this maze and show me the path
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the grid and runs BFS/A*, drawing the solution path — fully client-side.
rationale: Directly serves the 'Maze Solver' demand and doubles as a pathfinding demo.

name: terrain-generator
description: Generates procedural terrain heightmaps from layered Perlin/simplex noise, output as grayscale heightmap or colored relief.
example_prompt: Generate a 512x512 terrain heightmap with mountains and valleys
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute evaluates noise octaves per-pixel in parallel (plain Rust→WASM fallback), fully client-side.
rationale: TerrainGenerator demand reflects game-dev/worldbuilding need for quick, parameterized heightmaps without installing tooling.

name: cargo-feature-explorer
description: Parses the [features] and [dependencies] tables of a pasted Cargo.toml and visualizes which features enable which optional deps and other features, including default-feature chains.
example_prompt: Explain what each feature in this Cargo.toml turns on
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM resolving the feature graph from the manifest tables; everything needed is in the pasted file
rationale: cargo-info surfaces feature relationships, and tracing the feature graph from a manifest is a common confusion point solvable offline.

name: ipv6-ula-generator
description: Generates a unique-local IPv6 (ULA) prefix per RFC 4193 from random entropy.
example_prompt: generate an ipv6 unique local address prefix
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using getrandom (crypto.getRandomValues) for the 40-bit global ID plus SHA-1 hashing; all client-side.
rationale: Self-hosters need a properly-randomized ULA prefix, and generating it locally is both correct and private.

name: from-ci-regex
description: Collapses a case-insensitive character-class regex back to its plain-text literal.
example_prompt: convert [Cc][Aa][Tt] back to plain text
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parsing the bracketed classes and emitting one letter each is pure local computation.
rationale: Reverses the case-insensitive regex form to make verbose patterns readable again.

name: legacy-md-hash
description: Computes the obsolete MD2 and MD4 digests for legacy interoperability and forensic analysis.
example_prompt: md4 hash of this NTLM input
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the md2 and md4 RustCrypto crates are pure-Rust and run offline.
rationale: MD4 underpins NTLM password hashes and MD2 still appears in old certificates, so security/forensics users need them despite being deprecated.

name: genbank-feature-extractor
description: Extracts the feature table (genes, CDS, locations, qualifiers) and metadata from a GenBank flat file into structured rows.
example_prompt: Pull all the CDS features and their locations out of this GenBank file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing of the GenBank record/feature grammar; local-only
rationale: GenBank's dense feature syntax is hard to read raw, and a structured feature table is what researchers actually want.

name: integer-partition-generator
description: Generates all integer partitions of N (optionally with a fixed number of parts or maximum part size) in lexicographic order, plus the partition count.
example_prompt: List all partitions of 7 into at most 3 parts
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — successor-rule enumeration with no recursion blowup, fully local.
rationale: Enumerating partitions (not just counting) is a distinct combinatorial generation task used in optimization and number theory.

name: sentence-opener-variety-analyzer
description: Analyzes how sentences begin and flags repetitive opening words or structures.
example_prompt: Do too many of my sentences start the same way?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: first-token tallying across sentences locally
rationale: Repetitive sentence openers make prose monotonous and the pattern is invisible to the author without a tally.

name: dialogue-tag-analyzer
description: For fiction, counts dialogue tags and flags overused or adverb-laden attributions like 'said angrily'.
example_prompt: Analyze the dialogue tags in this story excerpt
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: detect quoted speech plus adjacent attribution verbs locally
rationale: Tag overuse and adverbial attributions are common fiction-writing weaknesses a dedicated analyzer can surface.

name: transition-word-analyzer
description: Measures use of transition words and phrases between sentences and paragraphs and flags gaps or overuse.
example_prompt: Am I using enough transitions in this essay?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: match against a bundled transition-word list per sentence boundary, offline
rationale: Transition usage drives readability scores and coherence, and quantifying it guides revision.

name: highlight-shadow-clipping-detector
description: Reports the percentage of blown-out highlights and crushed shadows and overlays the clipped regions as a mask.
example_prompt: How much of this photo has clipped highlights or shadows?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM thresholds luminance at 0/255 over decoded pixels locally — pure pixel math.
rationale: Clipping warnings tell a photographer whether detail is recoverable before they invest in editing.

name: flv-tag-inspector
description: Parses an FLV file's tag stream and reports the sequence of audio, video, and script-data tags with timestamps and codec IDs.
example_prompt: Break down the tags in this .flv recording
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: FLV tags are a simple sequential binary format parsed from the file bytes.
rationale: FLV is still produced by old RTMP recorders and capture tools, and its tag layout is otherwise opaque.

name: mxf-header-metadata-inspector
description: Reads MXF header metadata and reports essence descriptors, operational pattern, and track/timecode information.
example_prompt: What's in the header of this broadcast .mxf file?
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: the WASM ffmpeg demuxer parses MXF KLV structures locally and exposes the metadata.
rationale: MXF is the broadcast/post delivery standard and its metadata is otherwise locked behind expensive desktop tools.

name: video-packet-size-timeline
description: Charts individual packet sizes across the stream to expose oversized keyframes and pacing irregularities.
example_prompt: Plot the packet sizes for this video stream
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg: packet metadata is read without decoding and plotted locally in WASM.
rationale: Huge keyframe packets cause buffer underruns on constrained networks and stand out instantly in a packet plot.

name: vtt-cue-settings-inspector
description: Lists each WebVTT cue's positioning settings (line, position, align, size, vertical) to audit on-screen caption placement.
example_prompt: Show the positioning settings on each cue in this VTT
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parses cue setting tokens from the text file locally.
rationale: Misplaced captions usually trace to stray cue-setting tokens that are invisible until you list them out.

name: ordered-list-diff
description: Diffs two ordered numeric lists into added, removed, and changed entries with positional alignment.
example_prompt: What changed between these two lists of numbers, in order?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: sequence parsing and LCS-style alignment, fully sandboxed
rationale: Distinct from per-element series deltas — this aligns and reports insertions/deletions between two whole lists.

name: concordance-correlation-coefficient
description: Computes Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) measuring agreement between two continuous series.
example_prompt: Compute Lin's CCC between method A and method B measurements
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: means, variances, and covariance, no network
rationale: CCC measures agreement (not just correlation) between two methods and complements existing agreement tools.

name: keyboard-layout-diff
description: Compares two keyboard layout definitions and lists remapped, added, and removed key bindings.
example_prompt: What keys differ between these two XKB/KLC layout files?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the layout format and diffs key maps locally; offline.
rationale: Custom-layout authors need to see exactly which keys changed between revisions.

name: regex-to-dfa
description: Converts a regular expression to an NFA and minimized DFA, draws the state diagram, and tests strings against it.
example_prompt: Build the DFA for (ab)*c and tell me if 'ababc' is accepted
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Thompson construction, subset construction, and a diagram encoder run in wasmi.
rationale: Theoretical CS courses lean on regex↔automata conversion; an interactive visual tool is high-value and offline.

name: erdos-renyi-graph-generator
description: Generates a random G(n,p) Erdős–Rényi graph and returns its adjacency matrix and edge list.
example_prompt: Random graph with 8 nodes and edge probability 0.3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — seeded Bernoulli trials over node pairs, fully local
rationale: Random graphs are the standard input for testing graph algorithms and network demos, and seeding makes results reproducible.

name: keycode-lookup
description: Looks up JavaScript key/code values and HID usage codes for a named key or pressed input.
example_prompt: What are the JS key and code values for the left arrow key?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM static lookup table of key/code/HID mappings; pure reference data, no server.
rationale: kbt is a keyboard tester; a keycode reference is a small but frequently-needed dev lookup that ports cleanly offline.

name: xirr-calculator
description: Computes money-weighted return (XIRR) from a series of dated cash flows.
example_prompt: Compute the XIRR of these dated investment cashflows
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM Newton-Raphson root-finding on the cashflow series; deterministic, offline.
rationale: XIRR is PortfolioPerformance's headline metric and is a self-contained numeric routine ideal for the browser.

name: isin-validate
description: Validates a securities ISIN check digit and shows the issuing country prefix.
example_prompt: Is US0378331005 a valid ISIN?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (Luhn over alphanumerics); pure local
rationale: Traders and finance ops verify ISINs against data-entry errors regularly.

name: number-counter-video
description: Animates a number counting up or down from one value to another over a set duration, with optional thousands separators and prefix/suffix.
example_prompt: Animate a counter from 0 to 10,000 subscribers over 4 seconds
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg drawtext evaluates the interpolated value per frame, fully local.
rationale: Stat-reveal counters are everywhere in milestone and marketing videos.

name: siren-sound-generator
description: Synthesizes emergency/alarm sirens (wail, yelp, hi-lo, two-tone) with adjustable speed as a WAV.
example_prompt: Generate a police 'wail' siren that sweeps up and down for 8 seconds
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM modulates an oscillator frequency along the siren pattern and writes WAV locally
rationale: Siren SFX are commonly needed for video/game projects and are tedious to source royalty-free.

name: image-to-spectrogram-audio
description: Encodes an image into audio so the picture appears in the sound's spectrogram (Aphex-style spectral art).
example_prompt: Hide this image inside the spectrogram of a WAV file
loader_feasibility: pyodide runs numpy inverse-STFT to map image rows to frequencies and writes WAV fully in-browser
rationale: A fun, shareable creative-coding toy that's surprisingly hard to find as a one-click tool.

name: product-schema-generator
description: Builds a schema.org Product JSON-LD block with offers, price, availability, brand, and aggregate rating fields.
example_prompt: generate Product structured data for a $39 wireless mouse, in stock, 4.6 stars from 210 reviews
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string/JSON templating with field validation; no network needed.
rationale: Product rich results are one of the highest-demand SEO markups and the generic json-ld tool doesn't enforce Product's required fields.

name: local-business-schema-generator
description: Builds a schema.org LocalBusiness JSON-LD block with address, geo, opening hours, and phone.
example_prompt: generate LocalBusiness structured data for my cafe open Mon-Fri 8-5
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM templating with openingHoursSpecification formatting; fully local.
rationale: Local SEO markup is a top small-business need and the opening-hours syntax is error-prone by hand.

name: article-schema-generator
description: Builds a schema.org Article/NewsArticle/BlogPosting JSON-LD block with headline, author, dates, and image.
example_prompt: generate BlogPosting JSON-LD for this post by Jane published today
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM templating with ISO-8601 date handling; no API.
rationale: Article markup is required for Top Stories and Discover eligibility and the date/author fields are commonly malformed.

name: css-utility-class-generator
description: Generates a set of atomic utility classes (spacing, display, text) on a configurable scale.
example_prompt: generate Tailwind-style margin and padding utilities on a 4px scale up to 64px
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string generation over a numeric scale; no build tools.
rationale: Teams who want utilities without a full framework need a quick way to emit a consistent scale.

name: opml-generator
description: Generates an OPML outline file from a list of feed titles and URLs for import into feed readers.
example_prompt: turn this list of blog feed URLs into an OPML file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML templating; the opml-to-json tool covers the reverse only.
rationale: Sharing or migrating feed subscriptions needs OPML and only the parse direction exists today.

name: permutation-matrix-generator
description: Turns a permutation given in one-line or cycle notation into its 0/1 permutation matrix.
example_prompt: Make the permutation matrix for the permutation (3 1 4 2)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — index parsing and one-hot row placement, fully deterministic client-side.
rationale: Useful for row swaps in LU, group theory demos, and routing problems where hand-building the matrix is fiddly.

name: tls-cipher-suite-analyzer
description: Parses TLS cipher-suite names and rates their key exchange, cipher and MAC against modern hardening guidance.
example_prompt: is TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA secure
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: a static suite registry plus scoring rules in pure Rust, fully offline.
rationale: Turns the 'Applied Crypto Hardening' demand into an actionable, no-network suite-strength checker.

name: regex-equivalence-checker
description: Checks whether two regexes match the same language and shows a distinguishing string when they differ.
example_prompt: Do /colou?r/ and /color|colour/ match exactly the same strings?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM converts backreference-free patterns to DFAs for exact comparison and falls back to sampling otherwise — all local.
rationale: Lets users verify that an optimized rewrite ('The Bad, the Better, and the Best') is truly equivalent, closing the loop on the optimizer tool.

name: reddit-markdown-preview
description: Renders Reddit-flavored markdown including superscript, spoiler tags, and its table restrictions so you can preview a post before submitting.
example_prompt: Preview how this r/rust post will render on Reddit.
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM markdown renderer implementing Reddit's dialect rules; local text rendering only.
rationale: People drafting subreddit posts want an accurate local preview of Reddit's quirky markdown.

name: static-map
description: Render a static map image for a place or bounding box with optional markers.
example_prompt: Show me a map image of Kyoto with a pin on the station
loader_feasibility: Fetches OSM raster tiles via the runtime HTTP host import and composites them in plain Rust; in-browser.
rationale: Inline map images are broadly useful and there is no mapping render tool yet.

name: life-pattern-converter
description: Parses and converts Game of Life pattern files between RLE, Life 1.06, plaintext, and a normalized cell list.
