example_prompt: Convert this RLE pattern to plaintext and tell me its bounding box and population.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing of the pasted pattern text — purely local format conversion.
rationale: Game of Life tooling (gol-tui, gof-rs) revolves around RLE/Life pattern files, and converting between these formats is a common friction point.

name: favicon-link-generator
description: Generates the full set of favicon/apple-touch-icon <link> and manifest tags for given icon paths and sizes.
example_prompt: give me all the favicon link tags for my site icons
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; emitting the standard tag block is deterministic string output.
rationale: The modern favicon tag set is large and fiddly, and copying a correct boilerplate saves time.

name: drum-fill-midi-generator
description: Generates short MIDI drum fills (tom rolls, snare builds) to drop in at the end of phrases at a given tempo.
example_prompt: Generate a 1-bar snare-build drum fill MIDI at 120 bpm
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM sequences the fill notes on General-MIDI drum mappings and writes the MIDI file client-side.
rationale: Programmed drums sound static without fills, and a generator gives instant transition variety.

name: bcrypt-inspect
description: Parses a bcrypt hash into its version, cost factor, and salt without verifying any password.
example_prompt: What cost factor and version does this bcrypt hash use?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; parsing the modular-crypt format is pure string decoding.
rationale: Auditing the cost factor of legacy bcrypt hashes is a real security-review need.

name: browserslist-resolver
description: Resolves a Browserslist query into the concrete list of browser versions it targets.
example_prompt: Which browsers does '> 0.5%, last 2 versions, not dead' actually include?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — uses the same embedded caniuse/browser-data tables to evaluate the query locally.
rationale: Build-config opacity ('what does my browserslist actually cover?') is a real source of bugs and shares the caniuse data.

name: ruff-config-generator
description: Generates a ruff configuration (pyproject or ruff.toml) from selected rule sets and options.
example_prompt: generate a ruff config with line length 100 and the import rules enabled
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: template the [tool.ruff] table from inputs, client-side
rationale: Ruff is now the dominant Python linter and a guided config beats memorizing its rule codes.

name: biome-config-generator
description: Generates a biome.json with formatter/linter rules and language settings from a checklist.
example_prompt: generate a Biome config with tab indentation and recommended lint rules
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: template the JSON config, fully local
rationale: Biome is a fast-rising ESLint/Prettier replacement and a config scaffold lowers the adoption barrier.

name: dependabot-config-generator
description: Generates a .github/dependabot.yml from chosen package ecosystems, schedules, and grouping.
example_prompt: generate a dependabot config for npm and cargo updated weekly
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: template the YAML update blocks, client-side
rationale: Dependabot config is per-ecosystem boilerplate that's easy to mis-indent and a generator gets it right first time.

name: ulid-inspector
description: Decodes a ULID into its millisecond timestamp and 80-bit randomness, and verifies Crockford base32 validity.
example_prompt: Decode this ULID and tell me when it was created
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: ULID is base32-decoded and bit-split with pure logic client-side.
rationale: Extracting the creation time from a ULID is handy for sorting/debugging event records.

name: matrix-sparsity-profiler
description: Profiles a matrix's nonzero count, density, per-row/column nonzero distribution, and bandwidth to guide sparse-format and solver choice.
example_prompt: How sparse is this matrix.csv and what's its bandwidth?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM counting/scan pass; trivially local.
rationale: Choosing CSR vs banded vs dense storage depends on these stats, which nothing currently surfaces client-side.

name: mac-to-eui64
description: Derives the IPv6 EUI-64 interface identifier and link-local (fe80::) address from a 48-bit MAC address.
example_prompt: What is the IPv6 link-local address for MAC 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — EUI-64 is a fixed bit-flip-and-insert transform on the MAC bytes; deterministic local arithmetic.
rationale: Mapping a MAC to its auto-configured IPv6 identifier is a recurring need for network troubleshooting and a clean extension of the MAC-formatting demand.

name: image-frequency-domain-diff
description: Compares the 2D FFT magnitude spectra of two images to reveal periodic, halftone or texture differences invisible in the spatial domain.
example_prompt: Compare these two scans in the frequency domain to find the moiré pattern difference.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (or webgpu-compute for large images) runs the FFT and diffs the spectra client-side.
rationale: Periodic artifacts like screening, moiré and watermark grids only show up clearly as a spectral diff.

name: fraction-comparator
description: Exactly compares two fractions (and orders a list of them) using cross-multiplication without float error.
example_prompt: Which is larger, 17/24 or 5/7?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; big-integer cross multiplication, no I/O.
rationale: Comparing fractions exactly avoids the rounding mistakes that decimal conversion introduces.

name: hashcash-generator
description: Generates a Hashcash proof-of-work stamp for a given resource string and difficulty.
example_prompt: Make a hashcash stamp for user@example.com at 20 bits
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM SHA-1/SHA-256 minting loop; entirely local CPU work.
rationale: Hashcash is the original PoW anti-spam stamp that mCaptcha/Altcha descend from, and self-hosters still use it for email and form gating.

name: expression-equivalence-checker
description: Tests whether two math expressions are algebraically equivalent and explains the result.
example_prompt: is (x+1)^2 the same as x^2 + 2x + 1?
loader_feasibility: pyodide — SymPy simplify(a-b) determines equivalence locally in the sandbox.
rationale: Directly serves the Free Math/Mathcheap homework-checking demand for verifying a student's steps.

name: rbac-policy-checker
description: Evaluates whether a role/actor may perform an action on a resource given a defined role-permission policy.
example_prompt: given these roles and permissions, can an 'editor' delete a 'post'?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the policy is parsed and evaluated as in-memory rules, no policy server needed
rationale: Maps the oso authorization demand to a concrete, testable access-decision tool that's fully self-contained.

name: limit-calculator
description: Evaluates symbolic limits, including one-sided limits and limits at infinity.
example_prompt: What's the limit of sin(x)/x as x approaches 0?
loader_feasibility: pyodide: SymPy's limit runs locally with no external compute.
rationale: Completes the symbolic-calculus toolkit AngouriMathCLI represents, fully browser-local.

name: nostr-event-formatter
description: Pretty-prints a raw Nostr event and explains its kind, tags, and timestamps in plain language.
example_prompt: explain this nostr event: {paste JSON}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — JSON parsing plus a static kind/tag dictionary, fully offline.
rationale: Raw Nostr JSON is cryptic; decoding kinds and tag semantics makes debugging and learning the protocol approachable.

name: activitypub-object-formatter
description: Pretty-prints and explains ActivityPub/ActivityStreams JSON objects (Note, Create, Follow, Actor).
example_prompt: explain this activitypub Create object: {paste JSON}
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — JSON parse plus an ActivityStreams vocabulary map, offline.
rationale: Fediverse devs debug raw AP payloads often, and a local decoder beats squinting at nested JSON-LD.

name: man-to-html
description: Renders a roff/troff/mdoc man page into standalone, styled HTML suitable for publishing or offline reading.
example_prompt: Render this man page as a webpage: [paste of `man grep` source]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM roff parser emitting self-contained HTML+CSS; no external resources required.
rationale: ManWEB is named demand and an HTML rendering is the most shareable form of a manual page.

name: man-to-pdf
description: Renders a man page as a styled, paginated PDF document.
example_prompt: Make a PDF of this man page: [paste of `man ssh` source]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM using a pure-Rust PDF writer (printpdf) with the standard 14 fonts; roff parse + manual layout, fully offline.
rationale: ManPDF is explicit demand and PDF export of documentation has no browser-local equivalent today.

name: bit-difference-analyzer
description: Compares two integers bit-for-bit, reporting Hamming distance and exactly which bit positions were set or cleared.
example_prompt: Which bits differ between 0b10110 and 0b11010?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: XOR and popcount on integers, no server.
rationale: Quick diff for flags, registers, and hashes that is fiddly to do mentally.

name: dtw-distance
description: Computes dynamic time warping distance between two time series, aligning them even when shifted or stretched in time.
example_prompt: How similar are these two signals using DTW?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: dynamic-programming cost matrix over arrays, client-side.
rationale: The go-to similarity for time series of differing speed/length that simple distance metrics get wrong.

name: hausdorff-distance
description: Computes directed and symmetric Hausdorff distance between two sets of points.
example_prompt: Hausdorff distance between these two point sets?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: nearest-neighbor max-min over coordinate arrays, no network.
rationale: Standard worst-case shape/point-cloud comparison metric for geometry and contour matching.

name: wasserstein-distance-1d
description: Computes the 1-D Wasserstein (earth mover's) distance between two empirical distributions or sample sets.
example_prompt: Earth mover's distance between these two samples?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: sorted CDF integration, runs locally.
rationale: A robust distribution comparison that, unlike KL, handles non-overlapping supports and is hard to compute manually.

name: weighted-mean-comparison
description: Compares two weighted datasets by computing and differencing their weighted means, variances, and effective sample sizes.
example_prompt: Compare the weighted averages of these two weighted datasets
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: weighted moment sums over arrays, no network.
rationale: Weighted comparisons (survey, portfolio, grade weights) are common and easy to get subtly wrong manually.

name: line-ending-compare
description: Detects and compares line-ending styles (LF/CRLF/CR) and BOM presence between two files.
example_prompt: Do these two files use the same line endings?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: byte scan for EOL/BOM markers, instant and local.
rationale: CRLF/LF and BOM mismatches break tooling and diffs across OSes; a quick check saves debugging.

name: css-breakpoint-extractor
description: Extracts all @media query conditions from CSS and lists the distinct responsive breakpoints in use.
example_prompt: What breakpoints does this stylesheet define?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM @media rule scanning; runs locally on the pasted CSS.
rationale: Inconsistent breakpoints across a stylesheet cause layout gaps and listing them reveals the drift.

name: git-status-humanizer
description: Turns `git status --porcelain` output into a readable, categorized summary of staged, modified, untracked, and renamed files.
example_prompt: Explain this git status --porcelain output
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM decodes the porcelain status codes locally.
rationale: Porcelain codes are cryptic and a plain-English summary is a quick, common win.

name: git-hook-generator
description: Generates ready-to-use git hook scripts (pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push) for common checks like linting and message validation.
example_prompt: Generate a pre-commit hook that runs cargo fmt and blocks if files change
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM script templating; produced locally for the user to drop into .git/hooks.
rationale: Hooks enforce quality gates but writing the shell plumbing correctly is fiddly and rarely remembered.

name: hsts-header-parser
description: Parses a Strict-Transport-Security header into max-age (with human duration), includeSubDomains, and preload flags.
example_prompt: Parse this HSTS header: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM directive parse of the header string, fully offline.
rationale: HSTS misconfiguration is a common security finding, and decoding max-age into a readable duration prevents footguns.

name: wasm-import-export-lister
description: Parses a WebAssembly binary and lists its imports, exports, memory/table definitions, and custom-section names.
example_prompt: List the imports and exports of this .wasm file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM module parsing with a wasm-parser crate; inspects the uploaded bytes locally.
rationale: Auditing what host functions a wasm module needs and what it exposes is a security/interop step with no browser tool.

name: metrics-snapshot-diff
description: Diffs two Prometheus/OpenMetrics text-exposition snapshots and reports per-series value deltas plus newly-appeared and disappeared series.
example_prompt: Compare these two /metrics dumps and show which counters changed the most
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses both exposition-format snapshots and aligns series by name+labels in-browser; it is text parsing, no scraping.
rationale: Comparing two captured metrics dumps is a common debugging step with no tool, distinct from the existing single-file OpenMetrics parser.

name: k6-summary-diff
description: Compares two k6 load-test summary JSON files and reports deltas in p95/p99 latency, throughput, and error rate between runs.
example_prompt: Diff these two k6 summary.json files and tell me if latency regressed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM reads both k6 summary JSONs and diffs the metric aggregates locally; the summaries are self-contained.
rationale: Load-test runs are only meaningful against a baseline, and there is no k6 (or generic load-test) result diff in the catalog.

name: pls-playlist-validator
description: Validates a PLS playlist's [playlist] header, NumberOfEntries count, and contiguous FileN/TitleN/LengthN key numbering.
example_prompt: Check this .pls playlist for errors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the INI-style PLS text and checks key consistency locally.
rationale: Mismatched NumberOfEntries and gapped keys cause players to drop entries, and validation keeps the playlist intact.

name: css-vendor-prefix-auditor
description: Flags vendor-prefixed CSS properties that are no longer needed given current baseline browser support, plus missing prefixes still required.
example_prompt: Which vendor prefixes in this CSS are now redundant?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM CSS parse against a bundled support table — no network.
rationale: Stale prefixes bloat stylesheets while a few are still required, and an auditor cleans up without breaking support.

name: math-expression-syntax-validator
description: Validates that an arithmetic expression is syntactically well-formed (operators, operands, parentheses) without evaluating it.
example_prompt: Is the expression 3 + * (4 - 2) syntactically valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: tokenizer plus shunting-yard/grammar check, no network.
rationale: Catches malformed formulas before they're fed to a calculator, complementing the existing equation extractor.

name: confidence-interval-sanity-checker
description: Checks that a reported confidence interval is well-formed: lower ≤ point estimate ≤ upper and the margin is non-negative.
example_prompt: Is the CI 'estimate 5.2, [5.5, 4.9]' well-formed?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: ordering and margin comparisons, pure arithmetic.
rationale: Swapped or inconsistent CI bounds slip into reports often and a quick local lint catches them.

name: webmanifest-diff
description: Compares two web app manifest.json files, highlighting changes to name, icons, theme/background color, display mode, and shortcuts.
example_prompt: Diff these two web app manifests and show what install metadata changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON parsing + field comparison; client-side
rationale: PWA install metadata regressions (missing icon sizes, changed scope) are easy to miss without a structured diff.

name: cipher-suite-diff
description: Compares two TLS cipher-suite lists, showing added/removed suites and flagging newly enabled weak or deprecated ciphers.
example_prompt: Diff these two TLS cipher suite lists and flag any weak ciphers that were added
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM cipher-name parsing + set comparison against a bundled weak-suite table; client-side
rationale: Cipher policy changes between server configs are security-relevant and a flagged diff catches downgrades.

name: tailwind-config-diff
description: Compares the resolved theme objects of two Tailwind configs, showing changed colors, spacing, breakpoints, and font scales.
example_prompt: Diff these two Tailwind config theme objects and show what design tokens changed
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM JSON theme parsing + token-map comparison; client-side
rationale: Design-token drift between Tailwind configs is hard to spot and a token-level diff surfaces it cleanly.

name: eigenvalue-spectrum-compare
description: Computes and compares the sorted eigenvalue spectra of two symmetric matrices, reporting per-eigenvalue gaps.
example_prompt: Compare the eigenvalue spectra of these two symmetric matrices
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: symmetric eigen-solver (Jacobi) plus sorted comparison, no network
rationale: Comparing two matrices' spectra is a meaningful structural diff that requires a self-contained eigen routine.

name: mqtt-packet-decoder
description: Decodes raw MQTT control packet bytes (hex) into packet type, flags, topic, QoS, and payload fields.
example_prompt: decode this MQTT packet hex: 30 0c 00 04 74 65 73 74 68 65 6c 6c 6f
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — binary protocol parsing of pasted hex, fully offline.
rationale: Maps MQTT TUI to a wire-level debugging aid that has no privacy-safe equivalent online.

name: pre-commit-config-generator
description: Generates a .pre-commit-config.yaml from a selection of common hooks and their repos/versions.
example_prompt: make a pre-commit config with black, ruff, and trailing-whitespace
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: composes hook entries from a bundled catalog into YAML locally.
rationale: Knowing each hook's repo URL and rev by heart is impractical; a catalog-backed scaffold helps.

name: uv-checker-texture
description: Generates a numbered/colored UV checker texture for debugging UV mapping and seams on 3D models.
example_prompt: make a 2048 UV checker texture with row/column labels
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM draws the colored grid and labels with a bundled font to a power-of-two canvas locally
rationale: Every 3D artist needs a UV checker and a parameterized offline generator beats hunting for one online.

name: camera-calibration-pattern
description: Generates printable camera-calibration targets — checkerboard, asymmetric circle grid, or ChArUco — with exact square sizes.
example_prompt: make a 9x6 checkerboard calibration target with 25mm squares
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM draws the geometrically exact pattern to a print-scaled SVG/PDF entirely in-browser
rationale: OpenCV/photogrammetry workflows require precisely-dimensioned calibration boards that must be generated exactly.

name: sorting-algorithm-video
description: Generates a video visualizing how a sorting algorithm reorders an array step by step.
example_prompt: Make a video showing quicksort on 50 random bars
loader_feasibility: pyodide simulates the algorithm and draws each step with matplotlib, then ffmpeg encodes the frames in-browser.
rationale: Algorithm visualizations are popular teaching content and a prompt-driven generator removes all the rendering boilerplate.

name: midi-cc-automation-generator
description: Generates MIDI CC automation curves (LFO, ramp, envelope) for volume, filter, or any controller number.
example_prompt: Make a slow MIDI CC1 sine LFO over 4 bars at 100 bpm
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM samples the chosen curve into CC events and writes a Standard MIDI File entirely in-browser.
rationale: Drawing smooth automation by hand is tedious and a curve generator produces clean, precise MIDI CC data.

name: twitter-card-generator
description: Produces Twitter/X Card meta tags (summary or summary_large_image) with the right twitter:* properties for a given page.
example_prompt: Make twitter card meta tags, large image, for @gizza linking to mypost with this image url
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — deterministic template fill-in with attribute escaping, fully offline.
rationale: Card markup has fragile property names that a generator gets right every time.

name: sitemap-index-generator
description: Builds a sitemapindex XML that references multiple child sitemap files with lastmod timestamps.
example_prompt: Make a sitemap index for sitemap-posts.xml, sitemap-pages.xml, sitemap-tags.xml
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — template-based XML generation, fully offline.
rationale: Large sites split sitemaps and the index format is distinct and easy to get wrong.

name: rss-feed-builder
description: Constructs a valid RSS 2.0 feed XML from scratch given channel metadata and a list of items you type or paste.
example_prompt: Build an RSS feed for my changelog, channel title 'Gizza Updates', with these 5 entries
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — assembles channel/item XML with CDATA and date formatting; no fetching involved.
rationale: Static sites without a CMS still want a feed, and authoring RSS XML by hand is tedious and break-prone.

name: prime-sieve-list
description: Generates every prime up to a bound N (or the first K primes) using a segmented sieve of Eratosthenes, with optional twin/cousin filtering.
example_prompt: List all primes below 10000
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — segmented sieve is cache-friendly bit manipulation that runs to millions in-browser.
rationale: Listing primes up to N is a distinct generation task from factoring a single number and is constantly needed.

name: pythagorean-triple-generator
description: Generates all primitive (and optionally non-primitive) Pythagorean triples whose hypotenuse or perimeter is below a given bound using Euclid's parametrization.
example_prompt: List all primitive Pythagorean triples with hypotenuse under 100
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Euclid m,n enumeration with gcd checks, pure integer math.
rationale: Enumerating triples is a distinct generation task from validating one, useful for geometry teaching and number-theory exploration.

name: rose-curve-generator
description: Generates polar rose curve points r = a·cos(kθ) (or sin), reporting petal count and converting to Cartesian coordinates.
example_prompt: Generate a rose curve with 5 petals
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — polar sampling and Cartesian conversion, no dependencies.
rationale: Rose curves are a common parametric-art and trigonometry exercise that benefits from instant coordinate output.

name: bibtex-validator
description: Validates BibTeX entries for required fields per entry type, duplicate keys, and unbalanced braces, flagging each problem.
example_prompt: Check my .bib file — are any entries missing required fields?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM BibTeX parser walks entries and applies field rules entirely offline
rationale: Academics fight LaTeX bibliography errors constantly and a local validator catches missing fields before compile.

name: m3u-playlist-linter
description: Validates M3U/M3U8/PLS playlist syntax, EXTINF directives, duration fields, and entry consistency, flagging malformed or duplicate entries.
example_prompt: Lint this M3U playlist for formatting errors
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: parse the playlist text and apply per-format structure rules client-side
rationale: Broken EXTINF lines and bad encodings cause players to skip tracks, and a linter pinpoints the offending entries.

name: aba-routing-validate
description: Validates a US ABA routing number using its weighted checksum.
example_prompt: Is 021000021 a valid routing number?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM checksum arithmetic; no network
rationale: Useful for cleaning payments and banking CSVs client-side.

name: bic-swift-validate
description: Validates SWIFT/BIC code format and reports bank/country/branch components.
example_prompt: Validate this BIC: DEUTDEFF500
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM structural checks plus country table; local
rationale: Complements IBAN checks for international payment data validation.

name: phyllotaxis-spiral-generator
description: Generates a sunflower-style phyllotaxis dot spiral using the golden angle with adjustable point count and dot scaling.
example_prompt: make a phyllotaxis spiral with 1500 dots
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM places dots by polar golden-angle math into a PNG — pure computation.
rationale: Phyllotaxis patterns are visually compelling and a common generative-art and math-teaching artifact.

name: fcpxml-timeline-generator
description: Builds a Final Cut Pro XML (FCPXML) timeline scaffold from a list of clips, durations, and timeline order.
example_prompt: Make an FCPXML timeline placing these 5 clips back-to-back at 30fps, 1080p
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM emits the FCPXML resource/sequence tree as a string; no app or server required.
rationale: FCPXML is the lingua-franca import format and generating a valid scaffold saves huge manual effort.

name: premiere-marker-csv-generator
description: Generates a marker CSV (name, in, out, comment, color) importable as timeline markers in Premiere Pro.
example_prompt: Turn these review notes with timecodes into a Premiere marker CSV
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM formats the marker CSV columns and timecodes locally; pure text output.
rationale: Round-tripping review notes into editor markers is a real workflow gap a local generator fills.

name: video-batch-rename-script-generator
description: Generates a shell/PowerShell rename script that applies a naming convention (project_scene_take, zero-padding) to a list of clip filenames.
example_prompt: Make a rename script to turn my GoPro clips into projectX_scene01_take03 format
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the supplied filenames and emits the rename commands as text; nothing executed.
rationale: Footage organization is a constant pain and a generated, reviewable script is safer than a black-box renamer.

name: ffmpeg-speed-ramp-command-builder
description: Builds an ffmpeg command for speed changes (slow-mo/fast-forward) with correct setpts and atempo chaining for audio.
example_prompt: Command to play my clip at 0.5x speed including the audio
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes the setpts factor and chained atempo steps (for out-of-range tempos) as text.
rationale: Speed changes are common and the audio atempo chaining (capped at 0.5–2.0 per stage) routinely trips people up.

name: devcontainer-scaffolder
description: Generates a .devcontainer/devcontainer.json with a base image, features, and post-create commands for a chosen stack.
example_prompt: scaffold a devcontainer for a Rust project with the rust feature and clippy
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; JSON template assembly, no container runtime needed.
rationale: Codespaces/Dev Containers configs are reference-heavy, and a scaffold gets a working environment faster.

name: dockerignore-generator
description: Builds a .dockerignore from project type, excluding build artifacts, VCS, and secrets to shrink the build context.
example_prompt: Generate a .dockerignore for a Go service so node_modules and .git don't bloat the image
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — rule templates assembled as text
rationale: A missing .dockerignore silently balloons build context; few people remember the right patterns.

name: jest-config-generator
description: Scaffolds a jest.config.js with testEnvironment, transform, coverage, and moduleNameMapper presets.
example_prompt: Jest config for a TypeScript project with ts-jest and coverage thresholds
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — config object emitted as JS text
rationale: ts-jest/jsdom transform wiring is fiddly and commonly copied wrong.

name: circulant-matrix-generator
description: Generates a circulant matrix by cyclically shifting a single generator row.
example_prompt: Make a circulant matrix from 1, 2, 3, 4
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure cyclic-shift fill, deterministic and offline
rationale: Circulant matrices are central to FFT-based linear algebra and make a clean reusable scaffold for coursework and demos.

name: dft-matrix-generator
description: Produces the N×N discrete Fourier transform matrix with complex roots-of-unity entries in rectangular or polar form.
example_prompt: Give me the 4-point DFT matrix
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — evaluates exp(-2πi·jk/N) with local trig, no server
rationale: Writing out the DFT matrix entry by entry is a common, mistake-prone task in signals courses.

name: tridiagonal-matrix-generator
description: Builds a tridiagonal matrix from sub-, main-, and super-diagonal vectors (e.g. discretized PDE operators).
example_prompt: Tridiagonal matrix with -1 on off-diagonals and 2 on the diagonal, size 5
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — three-vector band fill, no server needed
rationale: The 1D Laplacian and Thomas-algorithm setups all start from a tridiagonal matrix that is tedious to type out.

name: bspline-knot-vector-generator
description: Generates clamped, open, or periodic B-spline knot vectors for a given degree and control-point count.
example_prompt: Clamped knot vector for a cubic B-spline with 7 control points
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — integer/uniform knot layout rules computed offline
rationale: Correct knot vectors are a notorious source of CAD/graphics bugs and the clamping rules are easy to get wrong.

name: wolfram-rule-automaton-generator
description: Generates the spacetime grid of a 1D elementary cellular automaton for any Wolfram rule 0–255.
example_prompt: Run elementary cellular automaton rule 30 for 40 steps from a single cell
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — 3-cell neighborhood lookup iterated locally, no network
rationale: Elementary CA like Rule 30/110 are iconic complexity demos and the evolution grid is impractical to compute by hand.

name: clap-cli-scaffold
description: Scaffolds a Rust clap derive CLI with subcommands, flags, and arguments from a described command structure.
example_prompt: Scaffold a clap CLI with subcommands add, list, and remove each taking an id
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust to WASM; generates the derive structs and enums as Rust source text, no compiler.
rationale: Setting up clap derive boilerplate for multi-subcommand CLIs is repetitive and mechanical to generate.

name: frontmatter-validate
description: Validates YAML/TOML front matter in a Markdown file and checks required keys for static-site generators.
example_prompt: Check the front matter in this Hugo post for missing fields
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM front-matter splitter plus YAML/TOML parse; fully local
rationale: Broken front matter is the top cause of failed static-site builds and bad post metadata.

name: wkt-validate
description: Validates Well-Known Text geometry strings and reports malformed POINT/POLYGON/MULTIPOLYGON syntax.
example_prompt: Is this WKT POLYGON valid?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM WKT grammar parser; pure string parsing locally
rationale: WKT is hand-typed in GIS/SQL contexts and a single missing paren breaks the whole geometry.

name: verhoeff-checksum-validator
description: Validates or generates a Verhoeff check digit using its dihedral-group permutation tables (as used by Aadhaar).
example_prompt: Check the Verhoeff digit on 2363
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: small lookup tables for the D5 group, fully local.
rationale: Verhoeff catches more transposition errors than mod-10 and is the basis of national IDs, yet rarely available as a tool.

name: stochastic-matrix-validator
description: Validates a Markov transition matrix by checking non-negativity and that each row (or column) sums to one within tolerance.
example_prompt: Is this a valid row-stochastic transition matrix?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: per-row sums and range checks, no network.
rationale: Anyone modeling Markov chains needs to confirm their transition matrix is well-formed before iterating it.

name: monotonic-sequence-checker
description: Checks whether a numeric sequence is strictly/weakly increasing or decreasing and pinpoints the first violation.
example_prompt: Is 1, 3, 3, 7, 6, 9 monotonically increasing?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: single linear pass comparing adjacent terms, fully local.
rationale: Validating monotonicity (e.g. sorted keys, cumulative totals, calibration curves) is a frequent data-integrity check.

name: image-to-xbm
description: Exports a 1-bit image as XBM (X BitMap) C source.
example_prompt: Make an xbm of this monochrome icon
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM threshold-to-1bpp plus XBM text emit
rationale: XBM is still used for e-ink and monochrome display assets and has no browser tooling.

name: css-identifier-escape
description: Escapes arbitrary strings into safe CSS identifiers/selectors per CSS.escape() rules.
example_prompt: escape '#my id.123' so I can use it as a CSS selector
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; the CSSOM serialization rules are a fixed character-class transform run locally.
rationale: Building selectors from dynamic class/ID names is error-prone, and no tool implements the official escaping rules.

name: content-disposition-builder
description: Builds a correct Content-Disposition header for a given filename, including RFC 5987 filename* for non-ASCII names.
example_prompt: build a Content-Disposition attachment header for 'Отчёт 2026.pdf'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; ASCII fallback plus percent-encoding is deterministic string assembly.
rationale: Serving non-ASCII download filenames safely requires the dual filename/filename* form most people don't remember.

name: content-range-parser
description: Parses Content-Range and Range headers into start, end, total, and computed byte length for partial responses.
example_prompt: parse 'bytes 200-1023/2048' into start/end/total
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; numeric range parsing is pure arithmetic.
rationale: Debugging resumable downloads and 206 responses needs the byte ranges decoded clearly.

name: wifi-channel-calculator
description: Converts between Wi-Fi channel numbers and center frequencies across 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz bands and flags overlaps.
example_prompt: what frequency is wifi channel 149 and which 2.4GHz channels don't overlap
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — frequency-table math on the chosen band/channel, fully local.
rationale: Maps impala's Wi-Fi domain to a quick channel-planning calculator with no radio needed.

name: midi-track-name-extractor
description: Lists every track in a MIDI file with its track-name and instrument-name meta events and the MIDI channels it uses.
example_prompt: What are the track names in this midi arrangement?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — reads FF 03/FF 04 meta events per track header from the byte buffer
rationale: Track naming is how arrangers orient themselves, and a quick index saves opening the file in a DAW just to read labels.

name: smiles-formula-parser
description: Parses a SMILES chemical string into its molecular formula, atom counts, ring count, and approximate molecular weight.
example_prompt: What's the molecular formula and weight for the SMILES 'CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O'?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM SMILES tokenizing plus atom/valence bookkeeping; pure computation
rationale: Chemistry students and researchers want to derive a formula and weight from a SMILES string without a chem suite.

name: pgn-chess-parser
description: Parses a PGN chess game into its header tags, full move list (SAN), and result, supporting multi-game files.
example_prompt: Parse this PGN and list the players, opening moves, and result
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizing of the PGN move/tag grammar; pure text parsing
rationale: Players and tooling builders need to extract moves and metadata from PGN exports for analysis or conversion.

name: dimensional-analysis-parser
description: Parses a unit expression like "kg*m/s^2" into its base-SI dimension exponents (mass, length, time, …) for dimensional checking.
example_prompt: What are the base SI dimensions of kg*m/s^2?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — unit-to-dimension table and exponent algebra, runs in wasmi.
rationale: Verifying that an equation's units balance is a core physics/engineering sanity check.

name: weight-quantizer
description: Quantizes a float array to N-bit fixed point and reports the quantization error.
example_prompt: Quantize these weights to 4 bits and tell me the mean error: 0.12 -0.84 0.33 0.91
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM does the scale/round/dequantize math locally.
rationale: QKeras demand is about quantization; simulating it teaches the accuracy/size tradeoff instantly.

name: lr-schedule-visualizer
description: Plots learning-rate schedules (step, exponential, cosine, warmup) over training steps.
example_prompt: Show a cosine learning-rate schedule with warmup over 1000 steps
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM evaluates the schedule formula per step and renders the SVG locally.
rationale: LR scheduling is a key Keras callback knob and visualizing it prevents common training mistakes.

name: regex-match-diff
description: Runs two regex patterns over the same sample text and shows which lines each matches differently.
example_prompt: How do these two regexes differ in what they match across this sample?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — compile both patterns with the regex crate and compare match sets locally
rationale: Refactoring a regex risks silent behavior changes, and a match-difference view verifies equivalence empirically.

name: rrule-validate
description: Validates an RFC 5545 RRULE recurrence string, flags invalid BY* combinations and out-of-range values, and previews the next few occurrences.
example_prompt: Validate this RRULE and show me the next occurrences
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: RRULE parsing and occurrence expansion computed locally.
rationale: Recurrence rules are dense and error-prone, and a validator with a preview makes correctness obvious.

name: heic-box-inspector
description: Parses a HEIC/HEIF file's ISOBMFF box tree and reports item, grid, and metadata structure.
example_prompt: Show me the box structure of this HEIC photo
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the nested ISOBMFF boxes locally.
rationale: HEIC's container is complex and there's no simple offline structural viewer.

name: gif-comment-extractor
description: Extracts text from a GIF's comment extension blocks.
example_prompt: Are there any hidden comments in this GIF?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM scans for 0xFE comment-extension blocks locally.
rationale: GIF comment blocks often hide authorship or notes that no viewer surfaces.

name: smf-structure-parser
description: Reports a MIDI file's header chunk (format, track count, division) and per-track byte sizes and event counts.
example_prompt: Show the chunk structure of this MIDI file
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: reads MThd/MTrk chunk framing, fully client-side.
rationale: A structural overview quickly diagnoses malformed or unexpectedly multi-track MIDI files.

name: scientific-notation-expander
description: Expands E-notation and Fortran D-notation (1.5e6, 2.3D-4) into plain decimal strings without precision loss.
example_prompt: Expand 6.022e23 and 1.5D-4 to plain decimals
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — big-decimal style digit shifting, avoids float rounding, no network.
rationale: Exported scientific data uses exponent notation that's unreadable and breaks naive integer parsers.

name: video-bitrate-ladder-generator
description: Generates an adaptive-streaming bitrate ladder (resolution/bitrate rungs) from a source resolution.
example_prompt: Give me an ABR bitrate ladder for a 4K source for HLS
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes the rung table from heuristics, client-side only.
rationale: Building a sensible ABR ladder is a standard streaming task that has clear, codifiable rules.

name: thumbnail-sprite-vtt-index-generator
description: Generates the WebVTT timing index that maps scrub-bar timestamps to tiles of an existing thumbnail sprite sheet.
example_prompt: Make a WebVTT thumbnail index for my 10x10 sprite sheet at 5-second intervals
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes tile coordinates and writes the .vtt text, no media.
rationale: Players need a WebVTT sprite index for scrub previews and hand-writing the #xywh cues is tedious.

name: wav-to-w64
description: Wraps PCM data from a WAV into the Sony Wave64 container to bypass the 4 GB RIFF limit.
example_prompt: Convert this big wav to Wave64 so it isn't size-limited
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM swaps 32-bit RIFF chunk sizes for 64-bit GUID chunks; pure byte surgery.
rationale: Multi-hour stereo/multitrack recordings exceed RIFF's 4 GB cap and need W64 to stay valid.

name: musepack-to-wav
description: Decodes a Musepack (.mpc) file to PCM WAV.
example_prompt: Convert this mpc to wav
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg.wasm decodes Musepack in-browser.
rationale: Musepack is a niche audiophile lossy format whose files are otherwise unplayable in mainstream apps.

name: wav-bext-chunk-writer
description: Writes or updates the Broadcast Wave (bext) chunk including originator, date, and timecode reference.
example_prompt: Add BWF originator and timecode metadata to this wav
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM inserts/rewrites the bext chunk and fixes RIFF sizes; pure byte editing.
rationale: Field recordings need correct bext timecode for DAW sync, and no tool currently writes this chunk.

name: texture-atlas-packer
description: Bin-packs many irregularly sized images into a compact power-of-two atlas with a coordinate map.
example_prompt: Pack these UI icons into the smallest atlas with a coordinate JSON
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: runs a rectangle-packing algorithm and composites the atlas plus JSON map in-WASM.
rationale: Atlas packing minimizes draw calls and download size, and a local packer keeps assets private.

name: video-bars-and-tone-generator
description: Generates a broadcast alignment clip pairing color bars with a 1 kHz reference tone.
example_prompt: generate 30s of color bars with a 1kHz tone for alignment
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — smptebars video plus a sine audio source combined entirely by the in-browser ffmpeg.
rationale: Standard ingest/broadcast leader that supplies both a visual and audio reference.

name: video-pluge-pattern-generator
description: Generates a PLUGE black-level / brightness calibration pattern clip.
example_prompt: make a PLUGE calibration pattern at 1080p
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg — drawbox/geq grayscale bars on a generated canvas, all client-side.
rationale: Display black-level calibration without external test gear.

name: midi-arpeggio-generator
description: Builds a Standard MIDI File arpeggiating a given chord with a chosen pattern (up, down, up-down) and rate.
example_prompt: Arpeggiate Am7 as eighth notes, up-down, over 4 bars, to MIDI
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: expands chord notes into timed MIDI events written as SMF bytes, client-side
rationale: Arpeggio MIDI generation from a chord and pattern is a frequent producer task distinct from any catalog tool.

name: id3-chapter-frame-scaffold
description: Generates the ID3v2 CHAP/CTOC chapter frames bytes from a chapter list for embedding podcast chapters into MP3.
example_prompt: Build ID3 chapter frames from these podcast chapter times and titles
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: serializes CHAP and CTOC frame structures per the ID3v2 spec, fully client-side
rationale: Embedded MP3 chapters require correctly nested CHAP/CTOC frames that no catalog tool generates, a genuine podcast-production gap.

name: typescript-union-from-list
description: Generates a TypeScript string-literal union type (or const enum) from a plain list of values.
example_prompt: make a TS union type from these status values
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: split list + emit union/enum text, no network
rationale: Turning a column's allowed values into a literal union is a tiny but constant task with no dedicated tool.

name: meshgrid-generator
description: Generates all (x,y) coordinate pairs from two ranges as a flat CSV grid, like NumPy meshgrid.
example_prompt: Make a meshgrid of x from 0 to 4 and y from 0 to 2, step 1
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Cartesian product of two ranges, deterministic offline
rationale: Scaffolds 2D sampling grids for heatmaps, surface plots, and function evaluation without writing loops.

name: protocol-relative-url-converter
description: Converts protocol-relative URLs (//cdn.example.com/x.js) to explicit https:// (or back) across a block of HTML or a list.
example_prompt: Make all the //cdn... links in this HTML explicitly https
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; regex/string rewrite over the input, fully local.
rationale: Protocol-relative URLs are deprecated and break in non-HTTP contexts; explicit https is the fix.

name: beta-binomial-updater
description: Updates a Beta prior with observed successes and failures and reports the posterior mean, mode, and credible interval.
example_prompt: Start with Beta(1,1) and update with 8 successes out of 20 trials
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; conjugate update is closed-form arithmetic, no dependencies.
rationale: Concrete hands-on Bayesian-updating tool that makes the 'Grokking Bayes' conjugate-prior lesson tangible.

name: pronunciation-audio
description: Generates spoken audio for a word or phrase in a chosen language for language-learning practice.
example_prompt: How do you pronounce 'bonjour tout le monde' — give me the audio
loader_feasibility: transformers-js multilingual TTS voices render the phrase in-browser with no external pronunciation API
rationale: Multilingual local TTS (MeloTTS) is heavily used for pronunciation drills.

name: food-additive-lookup
description: Looks up E-number food additives by code or name, returning purpose, common uses, and notes from a bundled dataset.
example_prompt: What is E621 and is it controversial?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM (embedded additives dataset) — the curated E-number table ships in-bundle, no OpenFoodFacts API.
rationale: Decoding additive codes on a label is a top OpenFoodFacts use case and the dataset is small enough to embed.

name: rdp-connection-file-generator
description: Generates a Windows .rdp connection file from host, username, resolution, and display/redirection options.
example_prompt: Generate an .rdp file for 192.168.1.50 at 1920x1080 with clipboard sharing
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: emits the key/value .rdp text from form inputs, no network.
rationale: Remmina/UltraVNC/RDP users need correctly formatted connection files and producing one is a pure config-generation task.

name: rtmp-stream-command-builder
description: Generates a correct ffmpeg command for RTMP/HLS live streaming from chosen resolution, bitrate, and codec options.
example_prompt: Give me an ffmpeg command to stream 1080p30 to my Owncast RTMP endpoint
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM string templating of flags; no execution or network.
rationale: Owncast/livego operators struggle to assemble correct ffmpeg streaming flags by hand.

name: librewolf-userjs-linter
description: Parses and validates a Firefox/LibreWolf user.js, flagging malformed pref lines, unknown prefs, and conflicting overrides.
example_prompt: Check my user.js for invalid or conflicting Firefox prefs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: text parsing of user_pref() statements against a bundled pref list.
rationale: Privacy-hardened Firefox forks rely on hand-edited user.js files where one typo silently drops a setting.

name: robots-ai-blocker
description: Generates a robots.txt that blocks AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, etc.) with an up-to-date agent list.
example_prompt: Make me a robots.txt that blocks AI scrapers
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: template generation from a bundled bot-agent list.
rationale: Site owners increasingly want to opt out of AI training crawls but can't remember the ever-growing list of bot user-agents.

name: genetic-algorithm-solver
description: Solves optimization problems (TSP, knapsack, function minimization) with a configurable genetic algorithm and shows fitness over generations.
example_prompt: Use a genetic algorithm to solve this 20-city TSP
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs the GA loop (selection/crossover/mutation) entirely in-browser.
rationale: Directly serves the multiple harvested genetic-algorithm courses with a runnable solver.

name: dutch-number-to-words
description: Spells out numbers, currency amounts, and ordinals as Dutch words.
example_prompt: Write 1234,56 euro in Dutch words
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — deterministic Dutch number-realization rules (a SimpleNLG-NL capability), fully offline.
rationale: Number realization is the most reusable piece of Dutch NLG, useful for invoices, cheques, and TTS preprocessing.

name: web-safe-palette-checker
description: Checks whether every color in an image falls within the 216-color web-safe palette, useful for retro and constrained-display targets.
example_prompt: Are all colors in this sprite web-safe?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM decodes pixels and tests each against the 6×6×6 web-safe cube locally.
rationale: Retro/embedded UI work needs strict palette conformance that's tedious to verify by eye.

name: slack-emoji-checker
description: Validates an image against Slack custom-emoji rules (recommended 128×128, ≤128KB, GIF/PNG/JPG).
example_prompt: Is this good to upload as a Slack emoji?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM checks dimensions, format, and size from the file bytes locally.
rationale: Slack emoji silently downscale or reject, and confirming constraints up front avoids fuzzy results.

name: svg-viewbox-checker
description: Checks whether an SVG declares a viewBox and a consistent width/height, the prerequisite for clean responsive scaling.
example_prompt: Does this SVG have a proper viewBox for responsive scaling?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses the SVG XML root attributes locally with no rendering needed.
rationale: A missing or mismatched viewBox is the single most common reason SVGs scale or crop incorrectly on the web.

name: svg-id-collision-checker
description: Detects duplicate element IDs within an SVG that cause gradient and clip-path conflicts when multiple SVGs are inlined on one page.
example_prompt: Will inlining these SVGs cause ID conflicts?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM collects all id attributes during XML parse and reports duplicates locally.
rationale: Duplicate IDs are the classic cause of gradients and clips bleeding between inlined SVG icons.

name: svg-precision-linter
description: Flags excessive decimal precision in SVG path coordinates that bloats file size with no visible benefit.
example_prompt: Is this SVG carrying way too many decimal places in its paths?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM tokenizes path data and measures coordinate decimal lengths locally.
rationale: Editor-exported SVGs often carry 6+ decimal places, needlessly enlarging files that ship to every page load.

name: embedded-lyrics-checker
description: Detects presence of unsynced (USLT) or synced lyrics frames and reports which tracks lack them.
example_prompt: Which of these songs are missing embedded lyrics?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — lyric-frame detection is byte-level tag parsing, browser-local.
rationale: A quick lyrics-coverage report tells curators which tracks still need lyric data before publishing.

name: permissions-policy-lint
description: Parses a Permissions-Policy header, validates feature names and allowlist syntax, and flags unknown or deprecated features.
example_prompt: Lint this Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(self), camera=*, fullscren=()
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parser with a built-in feature registry; offline.
rationale: The structured-field syntax and feature list are easy to typo and most editors give no feedback.

name: podcast-feed-validate
description: Validates a podcast RSS feed for Apple Podcasts requirements — required itunes:* tags, enclosure URLs/types, GUID uniqueness, and image dimensions.
example_prompt: Will this podcast RSS feed be accepted by Apple Podcasts?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM XML parse against the Apple/iTunes namespace ruleset; local.
rationale: Podcast directories reject feeds for precise missing tags that generic RSS tools don't check.

name: runs-test-randomness-checker
description: Applies the Wald–Wolfowitz runs test to assess whether a binary or sign sequence is random.
example_prompt: Is the sequence HHTTHTHTTTH random by the runs test?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: run counting and normal-approximation z-score, runs locally.
rationale: Quick randomness diagnostic for sequences with no existing counterpart.

name: persian-romanizer
description: Transliterates Persian/Farsi script to Latin romanization and back using rule-based mapping.
example_prompt: romanize this Farsi sentence
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM applies deterministic Perso-Arabic↔Latin transliteration rules entirely client-side.
rationale: Directly serves the Hamshahri (Persian corpus) demand and helps learners read Farsi text.

name: slope-field-plotter
description: Draws the direction (slope) field of a first-order ODE with optional solution trajectories.
example_prompt: plot the slope field of y' = x - y
loader_feasibility: pyodide + Matplotlib quiver renders the field to a PNG client-side
rationale: Differential Equations direction fields are course-central and rarely available free.

name: neural-forward-pass
description: Computes the forward pass of a small multilayer perceptron from entered weights, biases, and inputs.
example_prompt: Compute the output of a 2-3-1 MLP given these weights and input [0.5, 0.8]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM matrix-vector math plus activations — deterministic arithmetic, no runtime model.
rationale: Tracing a forward pass by the numbers demystifies neural nets for the math-behind-AI audience.

name: cyk-parser
description: Parses a string against a context-free grammar using the CYK algorithm and shows the parse table and tree.
example_prompt: Does this grammar generate 'aabb'? Show the CYK parse
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the dynamic-programming parse runs entirely in wasmi.
rationale: CFG membership/parsing is core formal-language material and a natural homework helper.

name: srgb-linear-converter
description: Converts colors and texture values between sRGB and linear space for correct WebGL lighting.
example_prompt: Convert this sRGB color #aabbcc to linear
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM math
rationale: Gamma/linear confusion is a pervasive cause of wrong-looking WebGL output.

name: affine-cipher
description: Encrypts/decrypts affine ciphers and can brute-force valid (a,b) key pairs.
example_prompt: break this affine cipher: Ihhotruqkj
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pure modular arithmetic over the alphabet, no network.
rationale: Standard classical cipher on the cited tool sites and a teaching staple for modular inverses.

name: redos-analyzer
description: Analyzes a regex for catastrophic-backtracking / ReDoS risk and flags the vulnerable nested-quantifier constructs.
example_prompt: Is this regex vulnerable to ReDoS? ^(a+)+$
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM walks the regex-syntax AST detecting nested/overlapping quantifiers; static analysis, fully local.
rationale: A security-grade differentiator no listed tester offers, valuable to any dev shipping user-facing regexes.

name: regex-tutor
description: Walks through interactive regex lessons with live testing, from literals to lookaround.
example_prompt: Teach me regex starting from the basics with exercises I can run
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM bundles lesson content and the live matcher; runs entirely offline.
rationale: Captures the heavy learning-oriented demand ('the complete tutorial', 'Introducing/Beginning Regular Expressions') in one interactive tool.

name: voronoi-stained-glass-generator
description: Generates a stained-glass mosaic by Voronoi-partitioning random seed points and filling each cell with a palette color and dark leading.
example_prompt: Make a stained-glass image, 60 cells, autumn palette
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — compute the Voronoi diagram and rasterize colored cells with stroked edges.
rationale: A distinctive decorative generator (colored cells + leading) that no existing noise tool produces.

name: terraform-module-scaffold
description: Scaffolds a Terraform module skeleton (main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, versions.tf) from a resource and variable spec.
example_prompt: Scaffold a Terraform module for an S3 bucket with a name variable and an arn output
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — emits HCL files from the spec as text, no terraform binary needed.
rationale: A consistent module file layout with declared variables and outputs is standard practice worth scaffolding cleanly.

name: band-matrix-builder
description: Builds a banded matrix with a specified number of lower and upper diagonals from supplied values.
example_prompt: Make a 6x6 banded matrix with bandwidth 2 above and below
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bounded-offset diagonal fill, no libraries, runs client-side.
rationale: Banded structures arise in splines and PDEs and a quick generator gives a ready scaffold for solvers and tests.

name: block-diagonal-matrix-builder
description: Stacks several input blocks into a single block-diagonal matrix with zero off-diagonal regions.
example_prompt: Build a block-diagonal matrix from [[1,2],[3,4]] and [[9]]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — offset block copy into a zero-initialized grid, deterministic client-side.
rationale: Block-diagonal scaffolds model decoupled subsystems and ensemble operators that are tedious to lay out by hand.

name: gram-matrix-builder
description: Computes the Gram matrix of pairwise inner products from a list of input vectors.
example_prompt: Build the Gram matrix of vectors [1,0,1], [0,1,1], and [1,1,0]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — dense dot-product loops over the vector set, fully client-side.
rationale: Gram matrices underpin kernels, least squares, and linear-independence checks and are tedious to fill manually.

name: incidence-matrix-builder
description: Builds the node–edge incidence matrix of a graph from its edge list, oriented or unoriented.
example_prompt: Build the oriented incidence matrix for edges 1->2, 2->3, 1->3
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — column-per-edge ±1 placement, deterministic client-side.
rationale: Incidence matrices scaffold flow networks and algebraic graph theory exercises that are awkward to write by hand.

name: range-header-builder
description: Builds and parses HTTP Range and Content-Range headers, validating byte ranges and computing the satisfied length.
example_prompt: Build a Range header for bytes 0-1023 and explain the matching Content-Range
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: range arithmetic and grammar parsing are pure local computation.
rationale: Partial-content requests are easy to misformat and the off-by-one byte math trips people up.

name: percent-basis-point-converter
description: Converts freely between percentages, decimal fractions, basis points, and per-mille, with rounding control.
example_prompt: How many basis points is 0.35%?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: scalar arithmetic and formatting
rationale: Finance users constantly juggle bps/percent/decimal; a precise converter avoids mental-math errors.

name: flatbuffers-schema-explorer
description: Parses a FlatBuffers .fbs schema and lists its tables, structs, enums, and fields with types, defaults, and validation warnings.
example_prompt: Explain the tables and fields in this FlatBuffers .fbs schema
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM grammar parser for .fbs text (FlatBuffers/flatc-rust ecosystem) — pure text parsing, no codegen or server
rationale: Understanding an unfamiliar FlatBuffers schema is hard without tooling, and a local explorer clarifies the data model offline.

name: rust-struct-to-typescript
description: Converts Rust structs and enums into matching TypeScript interfaces and union types for FFI boundaries.
example_prompt: Generate TypeScript interfaces from these Rust structs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse Rust type definitions and emit TypeScript as strings.
rationale: dioxus-fullstack and flutter_rust_bridge demand shows people crossing the Rust↔TS/Dart type boundary and needing the shapes to match.

name: tcp-flags-decoder
description: Decodes a TCP flags byte (or hex) into SYN/ACK/FIN/RST/PSH/URG/ECE/CWR and explains common combinations.
example_prompt: What flags are set in TCP flags value 0x12?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — single-byte bitfield decode, fully local.
rationale: Reading TCP flag combinations during connection-state debugging is constant and easy to get wrong by memory.

name: ip-checksum-calculator
description: Computes and verifies IPv4 header, TCP, and UDP checksums from header/payload hex including the pseudo-header.
example_prompt: Verify the IPv4 header checksum for these header bytes: 4500003c1c4640004006...
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — ones'-complement sum over byte arrays, no network.
rationale: Hand-checking checksums when crafting or debugging packets is exactly what smoltcp/libpnet users do and it's error-prone.

name: zmq-frame-decoder
description: Decodes a ZeroMQ/ZMTP frame from hex into its flags, length, multipart structure, and body.
example_prompt: Decode this ZMTP frame from hex and tell me if it's multipart
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing of the ZMTP wire format; pure byte processing in the browser.
rationale: Maps the rust-zmq demand into a debugging aid for the ZMTP framing that ZeroMQ developers occasionally need to inspect by hand.

name: handlebars-linter
description: Lints a Handlebars template for syntax errors and lists every variable, helper, partial, and block it references.
example_prompt: Check this Handlebars template for errors and list all the variables it uses.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: handlebars-rust parses the template to an AST locally; we report diagnostics and referenced names.
rationale: Surfacing required data keys and unclosed blocks up front prevents silent render failures in template-driven apps.

name: url-shortcode
description: Generates a deterministic base62 short code for a long URL entirely offline.
example_prompt: Give me a short base62 code for this URL
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: hashing the URL and base62-encoding it is pure math, no shortening service involved.
rationale: Maps urlshortener-rs into something genuinely browser-local — a stable short token without any backend.

name: rust-ast-explore
description: Parses a Rust snippet and shows its syntax tree.
example_prompt: Show the AST for: let v = vec![1, 2, 3];
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the `syn` crate parses Rust to an in-memory AST with zero external dependencies.
rationale: Seeing the AST helps learners understand how Rust syntax is actually structured.

name: welcome-script-generator
description: Generates a customizable terminal login/MOTD script that combines an ASCII header, a quote line, and placeholder system-info fields.
example_prompt: Generate a welcome.sh login banner with my hostname, an ASCII title, and a random quote
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — the script is produced by pure templating; it emits shell text for the user to run rather than reading their machine, so it stays sandbox-safe.
rationale: welcome.sh and synth-shell login screens are popular personalizations, and scaffolding the script saves users from assembling escape codes and layout by hand.

name: cpuid-decoder
description: Decodes a CPUID leaf hex dump or feature-flag string into named CPU capabilities (SSE/AVX/AES, etc.).
example_prompt: Decode the feature flags from this CPUID leaf 1 / leaf 7 hex output
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — bit-field decoding against a known CPUID map is pure table lookup.
rationale: CoreFreq/macmon demand around CPU internals extends to decoding CPUID; it answers 'does my CPU support X' from a pasted dump, locally.

name: story-point-poker
description: Suggests a planning-poker estimate by mapping rough effort to the nearest Fibonacci point value and reconciling a set of votes.
example_prompt: Votes are 3, 5, 5, 8 — what's the consensus story point?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — Fibonacci snapping and simple consensus statistics.
rationale: Estimation is a frequent agile ritual and a quick consensus helper saves meeting time.

name: rrule-explainer
description: Translates an iCal RRULE string into a plain-English description of its recurrence pattern.
example_prompt: Explain RRULE:FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=2MO in plain English
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parses RRULE fields and templates a sentence.
rationale: RRULE strings are opaque and a human-readable explanation is a common debugging need.

name: oidc-discovery-parser
description: Parses an OIDC .well-known discovery document and lists endpoints, supported scopes, grant types, and signing algorithms.
example_prompt: Summarize this OIDC discovery JSON for me
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — it's structured JSON summarization of a provider config like Rauthy's, no network needed.
rationale: OIDC discovery documents are large and noisy, and a focused summary speeds up integration work.

name: engine-sound-generator
description: Procedurally synthesizes a car/motor engine sound from RPM and cylinder parameters into a WAV.
example_prompt: Generate a 4-cylinder engine sound revving from 1000 to 6000 RPM.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM DSP (enginesound-style) generating PCM samples; pure computation, offline.
rationale: Game and video makers want quick royalty-free engine SFX without recording or licensing.

name: zx-tap-tzx-inspector
description: Lists the blocks and files inside a ZX Spectrum TAP or TZX tape image with their types, sizes and load addresses.
example_prompt: What's inside this .tzx tape file?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — TAP/TZX are simple length-prefixed block streams parsed from the file buffer.
rationale: Tape archive contents are opaque; cataloguing them is a basic need for the rustzx/preservation crowd.

name: raytrace-render
description: Renders a 3D scene of spheres and planes with reflections and shadows from a simple text scene description.
example_prompt: Raytrace a red sphere on a checkered floor with a light above it
loader_feasibility: webgpu-compute — the ray loop runs as a GPU compute shader in the browser, no server GPU required.
rationale: A live in-chat raytracer is a striking demo of client-side GPU compute and answers real 'render this scene' asks.

name: datacenter-pue-calculator
description: Computes PUE, annual energy cost and carbon footprint from facility power and IT-load figures.
example_prompt: Compute PUE and yearly cost for 1.2MW IT load and 1.9MW total at $0.12/kWh
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: straightforward ratio and cost math done locally.
rationale: Energy-monitoring interest (Scaphandre) extends to facility-level efficiency planning, a common spreadsheet task.

name: rustc-error-explainer
description: Parses raw cargo/rustc compiler output into a structured, deduplicated list of errors grouped by file with the error code highlighted.
example_prompt: Make sense of this cargo error output: <paste errors>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM diagnostic-output parser; pure text processing, no server.
rationale: bacon-style fast feedback shows demand for digesting compiler noise, and parsing pasted output is fully browser-local.

name: precommit-config-explainer
description: Parses a .pre-commit-config.yaml and lists each repo, hook, language, and stage in a readable table, flagging obvious misconfigurations.
example_prompt: Explain what this pre-commit config runs: <paste .pre-commit-config.yaml>
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM YAML parse plus structural checks; entirely in-browser.
rationale: prek's fast pre-commit runner drives interest in these configs, and making an opaque hook file legible is pure local parsing.

name: feature-combo-generator
description: Generates the set of feature-flag combinations to test from a list of Cargo features, like cargo-all-features.
example_prompt: Generate all the feature combinations I should test for these Cargo features
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — pure combinatorics over the pasted feature list.
rationale: Enumerates a feature test matrix instantly without writing a script.

name: midi-note-histogram
description: Computes a distribution of note pitches, durations, and velocities across a MIDI file for compositional analysis.
example_prompt: Give me a histogram of the notes used in this midi
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses MIDI events and aggregates counts locally, no server.
rationale: Pitch/duration distributions reveal range, density, and tonal tendencies useful to composers and educators.

name: content-digest-parser
description: Parses a Content-Digest / Repr-Digest header (RFC 9530), decodes the base64 digest, and identifies the algorithm and byte length.
example_prompt: Decode Content-Digest: sha-256=:X48E9qOokqqrvdts8nOJRJN3OWDUoyWxBf7kbu9DBPE=: and tell me the algorithm and digest length.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — structured-field + base64 decode, no network
rationale: Integrity-digest headers are spreading in API security specs but tooling to read the new RFC 9530 format barely exists.

name: http-method-safety-explainer
description: Given an HTTP method, reports whether it is safe, idempotent, and cacheable and what a correct Allow header for that resource should advertise.
example_prompt: Is PATCH idempotent, and should it be safe to retry automatically?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — static method-property table lookup, no network
rationale: Retry logic and caching correctness hinge on these method properties that developers routinely misremember.

name: mta-sts-policy-validator
description: Validates an MTA-STS policy file (version, mode, mx patterns, max_age) and flags issues like testing mode or overly short max_age.
example_prompt: Validate my MTA-STS policy: version STSv1, mode enforce, mx *.mail.example.com, max_age 604800.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — line-based policy parse with field validation, fully local
rationale: MTA-STS enforces SMTP TLS but a mode:testing or malformed mx silently leaves mail downgrade-attackable.

name: svcb-https-record-parser
description: Parses DNS SVCB/HTTPS resource records into priority, target, and SvcParams (alpn, port, ipv4hint, ech) and explains the connection hints.
example_prompt: Decode my HTTPS record: 1 . alpn="h3,h2" ipv4hint=192.0.2.1 ech=… — what does it advertise?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — SvcParam key/value parsing with base64 ech decode, offline
