example_prompt: Validate this SPF record and warn me about lookup limits
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing mechanisms and counting include/a/mx terms; no live DNS resolution
rationale: SPF records easily exceed the DNS-lookup limit and a static analyzer flags that before it breaks mail delivery.

name: html5-boilerplate-generator
description: Emits a complete HTML5 starter document with charset, viewport, title, and linked stylesheet.
example_prompt: give me an HTML5 boilerplate with the title 'My Page'
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: fixed template with a few substituted fields, fully offline.
rationale: The standard starting point for any web page, generated correctly every time.

name: datamatrix-generator
description: Encodes short text into a DataMatrix 2D barcode, the compact square code used on electronics and industrial labels.
example_prompt: make a DataMatrix code for serial SN-4471
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM implements Reed-Solomon ECC and the DataMatrix placement algorithm with no external service
rationale: DataMatrix is standard on small-part marking yet rarely available in offline tools, filling a real gap.

name: islamic-geometric-pattern
description: Constructs traditional Islamic star-and-polygon tessellations from a chosen symmetry and renders them as SVG.
example_prompt: generate an 8-fold Islamic star pattern as SVG
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes the polar grid and line intersections geometrically and outputs vector paths in-browser
rationale: These ornaments are widely wanted for design/laser-cutting and require exact construction not freehand drawing.

name: guilloche-pattern-generator
description: Draws guilloché security-rosette line art from layered sinusoidal/spirograph parameters as fine SVG paths.
example_prompt: generate a guilloche rosette like on a banknote
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM evaluates the parametric curve equations and writes the path, a pure-math render that runs locally
rationale: Guilloché ornament is prized for certificates and packaging yet has essentially no free offline generator.

name: breadcrumb-schema-generator
description: Generates schema.org BreadcrumbList JSON-LD from an ordered list of crumb names and URLs.
example_prompt: Generate breadcrumb JSON-LD: Home / Blog / Rust in the Browser with their urls
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — serializes an itemListElement array with correct positions, offline.
rationale: Breadcrumb markup improves SERP display and the position/itemListElement shape is fiddly by hand.

name: service-worker-generator
description: Scaffolds a service-worker.js with a chosen caching strategy (cache-first, network-first, stale-while-revalidate) and a precache list.
example_prompt: Generate a service worker, stale-while-revalidate, precache index.html and app.css
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — emits JS source from parameterized templates; no execution, just text generation.
rationale: Offline-capable PWAs need a correct SW and getting install/activate/fetch handlers right is a common stumbling block.

name: security-txt-generator
description: Generates an RFC 9116 .well-known/security.txt with Contact, Expires, Encryption, and Policy fields.
example_prompt: Make a security.txt, contact mailto:security@gizza.ai, expires in 1 year
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — formats required/optional fields and computes the Expires timestamp offline.
rationale: security.txt is increasingly expected and the RFC's field ordering/format trips people up.

name: kenken-puzzle-generator
description: Generates a KenKen/Calcudoku puzzle by partitioning a Latin square into cages with arithmetic target clues that yield a unique solution.
example_prompt: Make a 5x5 KenKen puzzle with addition and multiplication cages
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — cage partitioning plus a uniqueness-checking solver, all pure computation.
rationale: KenKen generators are scarce and the cage-uniqueness logic is exactly what a deterministic local tool excels at.

name: cayley-table-generator
description: Generates the Cayley (operation) table for Z_n under addition or multiplication, or a small cyclic/dihedral group, flagging identity and inverses.
example_prompt: Generate the multiplication Cayley table for Z mod 7
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — modular arithmetic table fill, fully deterministic and local.
rationale: Cayley tables are the core teaching object of group theory and an instant generator beats hand-tabulating them.

name: rational-approximation
description: Finds the best rational p/q approximating a decimal within a tolerance or maximum-denominator bound.
example_prompt: Best fraction for 3.14159 with denominator under 1000
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — continued-fraction convergents, fully local
rationale: Gear ratios, color mixes, and unit conversions need compact rational approximations no calculator gives.

name: rtty-decoder
description: Demodulates an RTTY (radioteletype) FSK audio signal into decoded Baudot/ASCII text, with configurable baud and shift.
example_prompt: Decode the RTTY text in this shortwave clip
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — mark/space tone discrimination and bit-timing recovery run as DSP over PCM samples in-browser
rationale: RTTY is still active on HF bands and decoding it from a captured clip currently requires installed SDR software.

name: balanced-ternary-converter
description: Converts integers to and from balanced ternary using digits −1, 0, +1.
example_prompt: show 17 in balanced ternary
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — adjusted base-3 division loop, fully local.
rationale: Balanced ternary is a distinct signed positional system not handled by ordinary base conversion.

name: interval-notation-formatter
description: Converts between interval notations like [a,b], (a,b], and set-builder/inequality form.
example_prompt: write 2 <= x < 9 in interval notation
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — parse bounds and render alternate notations, deterministic and local.
rationale: Translating between inequality and interval forms is a recurring math-class and spec-writing chore.

name: routh-hurwitz-stability-checker
description: Determines whether all roots of a polynomial lie in the left half-plane using the Routh-Hurwitz table.
example_prompt: Is the system s^3 + 2s^2 + 3s + 4 stable?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: builds the Routh array and counts sign changes, offline.
rationale: Control-systems stability test with no need to compute roots, missing from the catalog.

name: commitlint-config-generator
description: Produces a commitlint config with rule overrides (type-enum, scope, header length).
example_prompt: commitlint config extending conventional with a 72-char header limit
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — emits config module text
rationale: Rule tuple severity/level syntax ([2,'always',72]) is unintuitive to recall.

name: peano-curve-generator
description: Generates the Peano space-filling curve of order N as ordered grid coordinates and an SVG path.
example_prompt: Order-3 Peano curve coordinates
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — recursive ternary subdivision computed offline
rationale: The Peano curve is a foundational space-filling example distinct from Hilbert's and is just as tedious to trace by hand.

name: lcg-sequence-generator
description: Generates a linear-congruential PRNG stream from chosen modulus/multiplier/increment/seed and reports its period.
example_prompt: First 30 outputs of the LCG with a=1664525, c=1013904223, m=2^32, seed 7
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — modular recurrence with period detection, all local
rationale: LCGs are the textbook PRNG for teaching randomness quality, and an explicit configurable stream generator aids that study.

name: jacobi-symbol-calculator
description: Computes the Jacobi symbol (a/n) for odd n using the reciprocity algorithm, showing each reduction step.
example_prompt: Compute the Jacobi symbol (1001/9907).
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: iterative reciprocity and reduction rules with integer arithmetic, fully client-side.
rationale: Essential for quadratic-residue work and Solovay-Strassen testing; the step trace is hard to do by hand.

name: polynomial-discriminant-calculator
description: Computes the discriminant of a polynomial from its coefficients and interprets what it reveals about repeated and real-vs-complex roots.
example_prompt: What is the discriminant of 2x² + 3x - 5?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: discriminant via the resultant of the polynomial and its derivative using integer/float arithmetic, local.
rationale: The discriminant summarizes root structure in one number and is error-prone to compute by hand beyond quadratics.

name: humans-txt-generator
description: Generates a humans.txt credits file from team, site, and tech-stack details.
example_prompt: make a humans.txt crediting our 3-person team and tech stack
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM text templating; fully offline.
rationale: humans.txt is a small but recurring site-launch checklist item with a loose format people format inconsistently.

name: egyptian-fraction-generator
description: Decomposes a fraction into a sum of distinct unit fractions using the greedy and optional shortest method.
example_prompt: Express 5/7 as a sum of distinct unit fractions
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — greedy big-integer Fibonacci–Sylvester expansion, no external deps.
rationale: Egyptian-fraction decomposition is a classic recreational and number-theory exercise generated exactly client-side.

name: matrix-sparsity-analyzer
description: Reports a matrix's sparsity ratio, number of nonzeros, bandwidth, and whether it is diagonal, triangular, or banded.
example_prompt: Analyze the sparsity of [[1,0,0],[0,2,0],[0,0,3]]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; nonzero counting and bandwidth measurement are single passes over the matrix, no server.
rationale: Sparsity structure drives storage and solver choice for large matrices, and there is no existing tool that profiles it.

name: graph-isomorphism-checker
description: Determines whether two small graphs are isomorphic and returns a vertex mapping if they are.
example_prompt: Are these two graphs isomorphic: edges {1-2,2-3,3-1} and {a-b,b-c,c-a}?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; degree-sequence pruning plus backtracking on small adjacency lists, fully local.
rationale: Checking whether two graphs are structurally the same is a classic, hard-by-hand comparison with no easy quick tool.

name: nvmrc-generator
description: Generates an .nvmrc (or .node-version) file from a chosen or LTS-aligned Node version.
example_prompt: create an .nvmrc pinned to Node 22
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: emit the version string in the right format, client-side
rationale: Pinning Node versions per repo is standard hygiene and a tiny, frequently-needed file to produce correctly.

name: divisor-table-generator
description: Lists all divisors, divisor count, and divisor sum for each integer from 1 to N.
example_prompt: List divisors and divisor counts for numbers 1 to 100
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — trial-division sieve, no network, exact integers
rationale: Generates a handy reference for perfect/abundant number exploration and factor lookups in one shot.

name: binomial-coefficient-table
description: Generates a C(n,k) lookup table over given ranges of n and k using exact big integers.
example_prompt: Build a binomial coefficient table for n up to 12
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — multiplicative big-integer formula, deterministic in wasmi
rationale: A reusable probability/combinatorics reference that avoids overflow bugs from naive factorial code.

name: pong
description: Two-paddle Pong against an AI opponent with adjustable ball speed and first-to-N scoring.
example_prompt: play ping pong with me
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: physics step, paddle AI, and collision run in wasmi at frame rate, rendered to an in-browser canvas with keyboard input.
rationale: Terminal Ping Pong demand maps to the archetypal arcade game, ideal as a lightweight real-time local block.

name: asteroids
description: Vector-style Asteroids: rotate, thrust, and shoot to break drifting rocks into smaller fragments with wraparound space.
example_prompt: play asteroids
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: vector physics, rock splitting, and collision are deterministic compute in wasmi, rendered client-side with keyboard control.
rationale: term-asteroids demand maps to a beloved arcade classic that runs comfortably as a self-contained client-side block.

name: http-status-explainer
description: Explains any HTTP status code with its meaning, typical causes, and whether it's retryable.
example_prompt: What does HTTP 425 mean and should I retry it?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM lookup table; static data baked into the WASM, no fetch.
rationale: A quick, trustworthy status-code reference is a frequent need while building services.

name: emoji-translate
description: Rewrite a sentence by inserting or replacing key words with matching emoji.
example_prompt: Add emoji to: "I love pizza and sunny beach days"
loader_feasibility: plain WASM — keyword→emoji mapping table applied with local tokenization, no network.
rationale: Popular for social posts and messaging, and trivially correct to do offline.

name: water-intake-calc
description: Recommend daily water intake from body weight, activity, and climate.
example_prompt: how much water should an 80kg active person drink?
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM.
rationale: Common wellness calculator with no current entry.

name: bingo-card-generate
description: Generate a set of unique printable bingo cards from a word/number list.
example_prompt: Make 20 unique bingo cards from these phrases
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM randomized layout to PDF, offline.
rationale: A popular classroom/party printable with no current tool.

name: regex-crossword-solver
description: Solves a regex crossword by finding the grid of letters satisfying the row and column regex constraints.
example_prompt: Solve this regex crossword: rows [HE|LL|O+], columns [[PLEASE]+, [^SPEAK]+]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM runs a constraint/backtracking search over the small grid — fully local.
rationale: Directly serves the recurring 'Regex Crossword' / 'Regular Expression Crossword Puzzle' demand with an actual solver.

name: scrabble-score
description: Score a word in Scrabble or Words With Friends, including blanks and bonus squares.
example_prompt: What's 'quixotic' worth in Scrabble on a double-word?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM scoring; offline.
rationale: Game utility distinct from the existing anagram-solver.

name: tron-lightcycle
description: Tron-style light-cycle duel against an AI opponent on a walled arena where crashing into any trail loses.
example_prompt: let's play tron, me vs the computer
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: single-player AI pathing + collision are pure compute in wasmi; the SSH multiplayer transport is dropped, the cycle mechanic is fully local.
rationale: SSHTron and sshattrick show demand for the light-cycle mechanic, distinct from snake by the head-to-head AI duel.

name: space-shooter
description: Real-time top-down space shooter with waves of enemies, power-ups, and escalating difficulty.
example_prompt: play a space shooter game
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: enemy waves, bullet pools, and collision are deterministic per-frame compute in wasmi, rendered and controlled in-browser.
rationale: Terminal Phase demand maps to an action shooter that exercises the runtime's real-time rendering path entirely client-side.

name: checkers
description: Play draughts/checkers against an AI with forced-capture rules, kinging, and selectable difficulty.
example_prompt: play checkers against me
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: move generation and minimax search are pure compute in wasmi, board renders and accepts input in-browser.
rationale: terminal_board_games demand includes checkers — a distinct board game with a solvable AI, ideal as an offline block.

name: hebrew-gematria-calculator
description: Computes the gematria (numeric) value of Hebrew words or phrases across standard, ordinal, and reduced methods.
example_prompt: What are the gematria values of חיים in standard and ordinal methods?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM mapping Hebrew letters to values over the input text — no data bundle or network.
rationale: ltorah/Torah-study demand includes gematria analysis, a self-contained character-to-number computation ideal for browser-local execution.

name: wordle-solver
description: Suggests optimal next guesses from green/yellow/gray clues against a word list.
example_prompt: wordle helper: green C in slot 1, yellow R, gray A E O
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM filters a bundled word list by the constraints locally.
rationale: Wordle demand is enormous and a solver is a natural, self-contained companion tool.

name: parity-bit
description: Computes the even or odd parity bit for a byte, hex value, or bit string.
example_prompt: What's the even parity bit for 0b1011001?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; population-count parity is a single local operation.
rationale: Parity is a teaching staple and a real check in serial/UART and memory contexts.

name: collatz-sequence-explorer
description: Generates the Collatz (3n+1) trajectory for a starting integer and reports its length and peak value.
example_prompt: show the Collatz sequence starting at 27
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM iterates the sequence locally, trivially handling large step counts.
rationale: A signature Numberphile demand term that makes an engaging, demonstrably-requested exploratory tool.

name: discord-ansi-colorizer
description: Wraps text in Discord-supported ANSI escape codes to produce colored code-block messages.
example_prompt: Make this text show up red and bold in a Discord code block
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM string templating injects ANSI codes; no network required.
rationale: Colored Discord messages are a known power-user trick that's painful to type by hand.

name: discord-theme-css
description: Generates a BetterDiscord/Vencord-compatible theme CSS file from a chosen accent color, background, and font.
example_prompt: Generate a dark purple Discord theme CSS for BetterDiscord
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust→WASM templates CSS variables into a stylesheet string locally.
rationale: Theme creation is the central activity of the BetterDiscord/Vencord/Replugged communities.

name: linear-transform-visualizer
description: Renders how a 2x2 matrix warps a grid of basis vectors to illustrate linear transformations geometrically.
example_prompt: Show me how the matrix [[2,1],[0,1]] transforms the plane
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM computes the transformed lattice and draws to canvas — purely local geometry, no server.
rationale: Directly serves Strang's 'A 2020 Vision of Linear Algebra', whose entire pedagogy is the geometric view of transformations.

name: punnett-square
description: Generate a Punnett square and offspring genotype/phenotype ratios for a genetic cross.
example_prompt: Punnett square for a Bb x Bb cross
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM + table/image render; offline.
rationale: Classic biology-teaching visual with no existing equivalent.

name: mocking-spongebob
description: Convert text to alternating-case 'mocking' text (aLtErNaTiNg cApS).
example_prompt: mock this: that's a great idea
loader_feasibility: Pure Rust→WASM.
rationale: A widely-used meme transform distinct from the camel/snake-style case-convert.

name: java-cheatsheet
description: Renders a Java quick-reference cheat sheet covering syntax, types, collections, and common idioms.
example_prompt: Show me a Java cheat sheet for collections and streams
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM serves static formatted reference content; client-side only.
rationale: Maps the 'Java Cheat Sheet' and 'Java 101' demand directly, since Java can't run in-browser but a reference can.

name: constellation-viewer
description: Shows an ASCII star chart plus facts (stars, mythology, best viewing month) for a named constellation.
example_prompt: Show me the constellation Orion
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: an embedded star/constellation dataset renders the ASCII chart and facts with no network.
rationale: A delightful, self-contained reference (the starfetch demand) that needs only bundled data.

name: power-budget-calculator
description: Sums component wattages into total draw and estimates battery runtime or PSU headroom.
example_prompt: Given these component wattages and a 90Wh battery, estimate my runtime
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — energy/power arithmetic with no device access.
rationale: powertop demand is about understanding power use; a planning calculator lets users size batteries and PSUs without measuring live hardware.

name: resistor-color-code
description: Decode resistor color bands to resistance/tolerance and encode a value back to bands (4/5/6-band).
example_prompt: What resistance is brown-black-red-gold?
loader_feasibility: Pure-Rust lookup tables + a rendered band image; no network.
rationale: Beloved by makers/EE students and absent despite the existing ohms-law tool.

name: voltage-divider-calc
description: Solve a resistive voltage divider for output voltage or a missing resistor.
example_prompt: Voltage divider: 10k and 4.7k on 5V — what's Vout?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM arithmetic; offline.
rationale: Fundamental EE calculation distinct from the existing ohms-law tool.

name: led-resistor-calc
description: Compute the series resistor for an LED from supply voltage, forward voltage, and current (with nearest E-series value).
example_prompt: What resistor for a 2V red LED at 20mA on 5V?
loader_feasibility: Plain Rust/WASM arithmetic; offline.
rationale: One of the most-used hobby-electronics calculators; pairs with resistor-color-code.

name: gray-code-converter
description: Converts integers between standard binary and reflected Gray code in either direction.
example_prompt: convert 0b1011 to gray code
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; the conversion is a couple of XOR/shift operations.
rationale: Gray code shows up in encoders and Karnaugh maps and has no quick converter available.

name: prime-factorization-verifier
description: Checks a claimed prime factorization by multiplying the factors back and confirming each factor is prime.
example_prompt: Verify that 2^3 * 3 * 7 equals 168 and all factors are prime
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: big-integer multiply plus primality test, offline.
rationale: Validates user/AI-supplied factorizations end to end, a checking task not yet covered.

name: fibonacci-number-checker
description: Checks whether an integer is a Fibonacci number using the 5n²±4 perfect-square test.
example_prompt: Is 832040 a Fibonacci number?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: integer square-root test, fully client-side.
rationale: O(1) membership test that's a clean single-purpose checker.

name: function-parity-checker
description: Determines whether a function is even, odd, or neither by comparing f(x) with f(−x) symbolically and showing the simplified comparison.
example_prompt: Is f(x) = x³ + sin(x) even, odd, or neither?
loader_feasibility: pyodide: sympy parses the expression and simplifies f(x)±f(−x) symbolically in the local Python sandbox.
rationale: Parity is a common preliminary step in integration and Fourier work, and symbolic comparison avoids sampling errors.

name: symmetric-matrix-checker
description: Reports whether a square matrix equals its transpose within tolerance and lists the asymmetric entry positions.
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: pairwise element comparison, fully local.
rationale: Symmetry is a precondition for many algorithms (covariance, eigendecomposition) and worth verifying exactly.

name: jacobian-evaluator
description: Computes the Jacobian matrix of a vector-valued function at a point and reports its determinant and rank.
example_prompt: Jacobian of [x*y, x+y] at (2,3)
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; expression parsing and finite-difference partials of each component are local numeric work.
rationale: The Jacobian governs local linearization, change of variables, and Newton solvers, and evaluating it by hand is error-prone.

name: euler-totient-table
description: Generates a table of Euler's totient φ(n) for every integer from 1 to N.
example_prompt: Make a totient table for 1 through 200
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — sieve-based factorization in pure Rust, client-side
rationale: A reusable number-theory reference for cryptography study and modular-arithmetic work that's tedious to compute repeatedly.

name: continued-fraction-evaluator
description: Parses continued-fraction notation [a0; a1, a2, ...] and evaluates it to a rational and decimal value.
example_prompt: Evaluate the continued fraction [3; 7, 15, 1, 292]
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — backward recurrence over integer terms, exact rational output, fully client-side.
rationale: Continued fractions show up in number theory and approximation work but have no quick evaluator.

name: position-size-calculator
description: Computes position size, share count and risk/reward from account size, risk percentage, entry, stop and target.
example_prompt: Risking 1% of a $25k account, entry 50 stop 47 — what's my size?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — position sizing is a handful of arithmetic formulas.
rationale: Risk-based position sizing is a daily trader necessity surfaced by the trading-terminal demand.

name: app-ads-txt-generator
description: Generates an app-ads.txt authorized-sellers file for mobile/CTV app monetization with correct relationship fields.
example_prompt: generate app-ads.txt for these ad network seller IDs
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM line templating and relationship-field validation; distinct from the web ads.txt tool.
rationale: App publishers need app-ads.txt specifically and the DIRECT/RESELLER syntax is identical-but-separate from ads.txt.

name: interval-overlap-calculator
description: Compares two numeric intervals and reports overlap length, gap, containment, and Allen interval relation.
example_prompt: Do [3,8] and [6,12] overlap, and by how much?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: min/max comparisons, fully client-side.
rationale: Ranges come up everywhere (schedules, bins, tolerances) and their relations are error-prone to compute by hand.

name: chord-progression-compare
description: Compares two chord progressions (typed or per-bar lists) and reports substitutions, additions, and key-relative differences.
example_prompt: Compare these two chord progressions and tell me where they diverge
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parses chord symbols and aligns the sequences locally.
rationale: Comparing a reharmonization against the original is a common songwriting/analysis task.

name: smpte-bars-generator
description: Generates a calibration clip of SMPTE color bars paired with a 1kHz reference tone at a chosen resolution, fps, and duration.
example_prompt: Make me 10 seconds of SMPTE color bars with a 1kHz tone at 1080p
loader_feasibility: ffmpeg lavfi `smptebars`/`sine` sources synthesize both video and audio entirely in the wasm ffmpeg build, no input file or server needed.
rationale: Editors and streamers constantly need a standard bars-and-tone leader for calibration and slate, and there is no client-side generator for it.

name: cas-number-validator
description: Validates a chemical CAS Registry Number using its reverse-weighted mod-10 check digit.
example_prompt: Is CAS 7732-18-5 (water) a valid registry number?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM: positional weighted sum and modulo, no database needed.
rationale: Chemists and lab software verify CAS numbers and there's no common offline checker for them.

name: arduino-json-sizer
description: Computes the ArduinoJson document capacity (bytes) needed to parse or build a given JSON payload.
example_prompt: How much StaticJsonDocument capacity does ArduinoJson need for this JSON?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM walks the parsed value applying ArduinoJson's nesting/overhead formula; local computation
rationale: Directly maps ArduinoJson — its official assistant computes exactly this capacity sizing for embedded targets.

name: midi-program-list-extractor
description: Scans a MIDI file's program-change events and reports which General MIDI instruments are used on each channel.
example_prompt: Which instruments does this midi file use?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM — gathers Cn program-change events per channel and maps them to GM instrument names in-memory
rationale: Knowing the instrument palette helps when re-orchestrating or choosing a soundfont, without loading the file into a sequencer.

name: codeowners-parser
description: Parses a CODEOWNERS file and, given a path, resolves which rule matches and which owners apply.
example_prompt: Given this CODEOWNERS file, who owns src/api/server.ts?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM implementing the gitignore-style glob matching from text; offline evaluation.
rationale: CODEOWNERS precedence (last match wins) is error-prone; resolving ownership for a path locally is genuinely useful.

name: cargo-make-task-graph
description: Parses a cargo-make Makefile.toml and renders the task dependency graph plus an execution-order listing, surfacing cycles and dangling task references.
example_prompt: Visualize the task dependencies in this Makefile.toml
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM parsing the TOML task definitions and topo-sorting them client-side
rationale: cargo-make task files grow tangled, and a dependency graph from the file alone makes them comprehensible.

name: video-stream-map-command-builder
description: Builds ffmpeg -map selectors to keep, drop, or reorder specific video/audio/subtitle streams by index.
example_prompt: ffmpeg -map flags to keep video plus only the English audio track
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM assembles -map tokens from a track spec, no media read.
rationale: -map syntax is unintuitive and easy to invert, so a generator prevents dropped-track mistakes.

name: color-delta-e
description: Computes the perceptual color difference (CIEDE2000 Delta-E) between two colors in CIELAB.
example_prompt: How perceptually different are #FF0000 and #FE0A05?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM evaluates the Delta-E formula; fully local.
rationale: Maps the `lab` demand to a precise design/QA metric for judging whether two colors are distinguishable.

name: npm-name-validator
description: Validates a proposed npm package name against npm's naming rules and explains any violations.
example_prompt: Is `React_Helper!` a valid npm package name?
loader_feasibility: plain Rust→WASM; length, case, character, and scope rules are checked locally (validity only, not registry availability).
rationale: Catches names npm will reject before you ever attempt to publish, with no registry round-trip.

name: distribution-explorer
description: Plots PDF/CDF and computes probabilities for normal, binomial, Poisson, and other distributions.
example_prompt: Plot a normal distribution with mean 10 and sd 2 and tell me P(X<8)
